title: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Mexico and United States: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a United States citizen dies in Mexico (whether in a hospital, private residence, hotel, or public space), medical certification and civil registration must first be completed before local Mexican authorities before the body or ashes can be transported to the United States and the federal consular report of death can be issued [1][2].

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Death Certificate (in or outside a hospital) and verify sanitary deadlines
steps.html:
Ask the attending physician or hospital administration to issue the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción) on the Ministry of Health (Secretaría de Salud) form [1][3]. Provide the deceased person's U.S. passport before the certificate is finalized so that their full legal name, date of birth, and nationality match their official identification exactly; any discrepancy can delay registration with the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) and consular processing [1].

  • Hospital death versus residence, hotel, or public space: When death occurs in a hospital from natural causes certified by the attending physician, the hospital issues the Certificado Médico de Defunción directly once hospital administrative steps are completed [1]. If the death occurs in a hotel, temporary accommodation, private residence without an attending physician, or public space (or is classified as sudden, accidental, or subject to investigation), call the national emergency number 911 immediately so local authorities, the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público), and the Forensic Medical Service (Servicio Médico Forense - SEMEFO) of the relevant Mexican state can conduct the legal removal and authorize the release of the body before a funeral home can intervene [1].
  • 12-to-48-hour sanitary window in Mexico: Under the Regulation of the General Health Law on Sanitary Control of the Disposition of Organs, Tissues, and Cadavers of Human Beings, overseen at the federal level by the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (Federal Commission for the Protection against Sanitary Risk - COFEPRIS, phone: +52 800 033 5050) and the state sanitary commissions (COEPRIS), burial, cremation, or embalming must take place between 12 and 48 hours after death, unless specific sanitary authorization or an order from the Ministerio Público applies [3].

steps.title: Check assistance insurance and appoint a funeral home in Mexico and in the United States
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member had travel insurance, international medical evacuation coverage, or travel assistance benefits linked to bank cards [2]. Where active coverage exists, the insurer's assistance center typically appoints the coordinating funeral agency directly and covers authorized repatriation costs [2].

If the family is arranging the service independently, you will need to coordinate an authorized funeral home in the Mexican municipality where the death occurred and, for full-body repatriation, a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state [1][2]:

  • Funeral home in Mexico: The Embajada y Consulados de los Estados Unidos en México (U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Mexico, phone from Mexico: 55 2579 2000; from the United States: +1 301 985 8843 or 011 52 55 2579 2000) publish regional lists of local funeral homes experienced in international procedures across each consular district (for example, Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Mérida, or Tijuana) [1].
  • Receiving funeral home in the United States: You can locate a licensed funeral home in the destination U.S. state and city through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (phone: +1 262 789 1880; email: nfda@nfda.org) [4]. Clarvia provides directory information for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific funeral providers.

steps.title: Register the death with the Civil Registry and arrange international transport or local cremation
steps.html:
The appointed Mexican funeral home typically submits the Certificado Médico de Defunción, the deceased person's U.S. passport, and the declarant's identification to the Civil Registry Office (Oficialía del Registro Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred (for example, the Mexico City Civil Registry or the corresponding municipal office) to obtain certified copies of the official Civil Death Certificate (Acta de Defunción) and the burial, cremation, or transit permit (boleta de inhumación, cremación o traslado) [1][3].

Subsequent sanitary permits depend on whether the family chooses repatriation of the body or local cremation in Mexico:

  • International repatriation of the body to the United States: The Mexican funeral home performs official embalming, places the body in a hermetically sealed casket with a sealed metal liner for air or land border transport, and obtains the international sanitary transit permit (permiso sanitario de traslado internacional de cadáveres) from the state sanitary authority (COEPRIS / Secretaría de Salud) or the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios, together with the certificate of embalming and certificate of absence of communicable disease [1][3]. Under the rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (phone: +1 800 232 4636) for importing human remains into the United States, no special CDC quarantine permit is required when the cause of death is not a quarantinable communicable disease and the body enters embalmed with official cause-of-death documentation [5].
  • Local cremation in Mexico and transport of ashes: Once cremation is authorized by the Registro Civil and the sanitary authority, the licensed crematory issues the official cremation certificate [1][3]. Cremated remains are treated as inert material under Mexican sanitary rules and the regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [3][5]. A family member may carry the ashes on a flight to the United States as carry-on luggage in a non-metallic urn suitable for X-ray screening, bringing the Acta de Defunción and the cremation certificate after verifying the airline's specific rules [1][5].

steps.title: Apply for the consular mortuary certificate and CRDA with the U.S. Embassy or Consulate
steps.html:
Contact the American Citizens Services (ACS) unit of the Embajada y Consulados de los Estados Unidos en México with jurisdiction over the place of death (the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City or the Consulates General in Guadalajara, Monterrey, Mérida, Tijuana, Ciudad Juárez, Hermosillo, Matamoros, Nogales, or Nuevo Laredo) [1][2].

  • Consular mortuary certificate for shipment of remains: For repatriation of the body, the Mexican funeral home submits the Acta de Defunción, the sanitary transit permit, and the embalming certificate (with state apostille and translation as required by the local jurisdiction) to the consulate, which issues the English-language Consular Mortuary Certificate needed for air cargo and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) clearance [1][2].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Once the Mexican Acta de Defunción is issued, submit the original certificate and your family member's U.S. passport to the consulate so the passport can be canceled and the CRDA (Form DS-2060) issued to the next of kin or legal representative [1][2]. The CRDA serves across all U.S. states as official English-language proof of death for probate courts, banks, and insurers; additional certified copies can later be requested from the U.S. Department of State using Form DS-5542 [2].

steps.title: Coordinate reception in the United States and notifications to the Social Security Administration (SSA)
steps.html:
When the casket arrives at the U.S. airport or land port of entry, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the documentation with U.S. Customs and Border Protection, obtains the state burial-transit permit under the laws of the destination state (for example, in California, Texas, Illinois, or New York), and coordinates the local funeral service [1][4].

For initial administrative formalities in the United States:

  • Social Security Administration notification and survivor benefits: Contact the Social Security Administration (phone: +1 800 772 1213; TTY: +1 800 325 0778) to report the death abroad [6]. Although the consulate typically reports the death when processing the CRDA, the family should confirm directly with the Social Security Administration that monthly payments have been stopped (any payment received for the month of death or later must be returned) and inquire about eligibility for the $255 lump-sum death payment and monthly survivor benefits, which depend on the family relationship to the deceased (such as a surviving spouse, eligible former spouse, minor or disabled child, or dependent parent) [6].
  • Probate, bank accounts, and insurance in the United States: Use the CRDA (and, where requested by an institution, apostilled copies of the Mexican Acta de Defunción) to notify banks, life insurance companies, pension or retirement plan administrators, and the county probate court where your family member resided in the United States [1][2].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide the exact consular district details and local requirements, in which municipality and state of Mexico did the death occur, and in which U.S. state did your family member reside or will the remains be received?
caseDependentItems: Exact Mexican state and municipality Registro Civil deadlines, translation, and Apostille requirements
Specific U.S. Consular District jurisdiction (Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Merida, Tijuana, etc.) and CRDA turnaround

contacts.note: Mexico's federal sanitary authority (COFEPRIS), which regulates, together with the state commissions (COEPRIS), sanitary permits for the transit, entry, or export of human remains.

contacts.note: National professional funeral services association in the United States with a public directory to locate a licensed receiving funeral home in any U.S. state.

contacts.note: United States federal public health authority that sets sanitary and quarantine requirements for the importation of human remains and cremated ashes.

contacts.name: Social Security Administration
contacts.note: United States federal agency for reporting the death of an insured person, stopping monthly payments, and applying for survivor benefits based on family relationship.

es.title: Qué hacer cuando un ciudadano estadounidense fallece en México: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Pasos oficiales para el Certificado Médico de Defunción en México, inscripción en el Registro Civil, traslado internacional (COFEPRIS/COEPRIS) o cremación local, reporte consular ante la Embajada de EE. UU. (CRDA) y trámites ante la Administración del Seguro Social (SSA).
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía de los Estados Unidos fallece en México (ya sea en un hospital, domicilio particular, hotel o espacio público), la certificación médica y el registro civil deben completarse primero ante las autoridades mexicanas locales antes de poder trasladar el cuerpo o las cenizas a los Estados Unidos y obtener el reporte consular federal de defunción [1][2].

steps.title: Obtener el Certificado Médico de Defunción (en hospital o fuera de él) y verificar los plazos sanitarios
steps.html:
Solicite al médico tratante o a la administración del hospital la expedición del Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial en el formato de la Secretaría de Salud [1][3]. Entregue el pasaporte estadounidense de la persona fallecida antes de que se cierre el documento para que su nombre legal completo, fecha de nacimiento y nacionalidad coincidan exactamente con su identificación oficial; cualquier discrepancia puede retrasar la inscripción en el Registro Civil y los trámites consulares [1].

  • Fallecimiento en hospital frente a domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Cuando el fallecimiento ocurre en un hospital por causas naturales certificadas por el médico tratante, el hospital entrega el Certificado Médico de Defunción directamente una vez cubiertos los trámites administrativos hospitalarios [1]. Si el deceso ocurre en un hotel, alojamiento temporal, domicilio particular sin médico tratante o en la vía pública (o si se clasifica como súbito, accidental o sujeto a investigación), llame de inmediato al número nacional de emergencias 911 para que intervengan las autoridades locales, el Ministerio Público y el Servicio Médico Forense (SEMEFO) de la entidad federativa correspondiente a fin de realizar el levantamiento legal y autorizar la entrega del cuerpo antes de que una funeraria pueda intervenir [1].
  • Plazo sanitario de 12 a 48 horas en México: Conforme al Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Control Sanitario de la Disposición de Órganos, Tejidos y Cadáveres de Seres Humanos, supervisado a nivel federal por la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (teléfono: +52 800 033 5050) y las comisiones estatales (COEPRIS), la inhumación, cremación o embalsamamiento debe realizarse entre las 12 y las 48 horas posteriores al fallecimiento, salvo autorización sanitaria expresa o disposición del Ministerio Público [3].

steps.title: Verificar seguros de asistencia y designar una funeraria en México y en los Estados Unidos
steps.html:
Antes de firmar un contrato funerario de forma independiente, verifique si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, cobertura de evacuación médica internacional o beneficios de asistencia en viaje vinculados a tarjetas bancarias [2]. Cuando existe cobertura activa, la central de asistencia de la aseguradora suele designar directamente a la agencia funeraria coordinadora y cubrir los costos autorizados de repatriación [2].

Si la familia gestiona el servicio por cuenta propia, deberá coordinar una agencia funeraria autorizada en el municipio mexicano donde ocurrió el deceso y, en caso de traslado de cuerpo completo, una funeraria receptora con licencia en el estado correspondiente de los Estados Unidos [1][2]:

  • Agencia funeraria en México: La Embajada y Consulados de los Estados Unidos en México (teléfono desde México: 55 2579 2000; desde los Estados Unidos: +1 301 985 8843 o 011 52 55 2579 2000) publican listas regionales de agencias funerarias locales con experiencia en trámites internacionales en cada distrito consular (por ejemplo, Ciudad de México, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Mérida o Tijuana) [1].
  • Funeraria receptora en los Estados Unidos: Puede localizar una funeraria con licencia en el estado y ciudad de destino de los Estados Unidos a través del directorio de la National Funeral Directors Association (teléfono: +1 262 789 1880; correo electrónico: nfda@nfda.org) [4]. Clarvia facilita información de directorios únicamente a título orientativo y no avala, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores funerarios concretos.

steps.title: Inscribir la defunción en el Registro Civil y tramitar el traslado internacional o la cremación local
steps.html:
La agencia funeraria mexicana designada presenta habitualmente el Certificado Médico de Defunción, el pasaporte estadounidense de la persona fallecida y la identificación del declarante ante la Oficialía del Registro Civil del municipio donde ocurrió el fallecimiento (por ejemplo, ante el Registro Civil de la Ciudad de México o del municipio estatal correspondiente) para obtener copias certificadas del Acta de Defunción oficial y la boleta de inhumación, cremación o traslado [1][3].

Los permisos sanitarios posteriores dependen de si la familia opta por la repatriación del cuerpo o por la cremación en México:

  • Traslado internacional del cuerpo a los Estados Unidos: La funeraria mexicana realiza el embalsamamiento oficial, coloca el cuerpo en un féretro hermético con caja metálica sellada para transporte aéreo o fronterizo y tramita el permiso sanitario de traslado internacional de cadáveres ante la autoridad sanitaria estatal (COEPRIS / Secretaría de Salud) o la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios, junto con el certificado de embalsamamiento y de no enfermedad infectocontagiosa [1][3]. Conforme a las normas de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (teléfono: +1 800 232 4636) para la importación de restos humanos a los Estados Unidos, no se exige un permiso especial de cuarentena de los CDC cuando la causa de muerte no es una enfermedad cuarentenable y el cuerpo ingresa embalsamado con la documentación oficial de causa de defunción [5].
  • Cremación local en México y traslado de cenizas: Una vez autorizada la cremación por el Registro Civil y la autoridad sanitaria, el crematorio autorizado entrega el certificado oficial de cremación [1][3]. Las cenizas se consideran material inerte según las normas sanitarias mexicanas y de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [3][5]. Un familiar puede transportarlas en avión hacia los Estados Unidos como equipaje de mano en una urna no metálica apta para escaneo por rayos X, llevando consigo el Acta de Defunción y el certificado de cremación, previa verificación de las normas de la aerolínea [1][5].

steps.title: Tramitar el certificado mortuorio consular y el CRDA ante la Embajada o Consulado de los Estados Unidos
steps.html:
Comuníquese con la unidad de Servicios a Ciudadanos Estadounidenses (American Citizens Services - ACS) de la Embajada y Consulados de los Estados Unidos en México con jurisdicción sobre el lugar del fallecimiento (la Embajada en la Ciudad de México o los Consulados Generales en Guadalajara, Monterrey, Mérida, Tijuana, Ciudad Juárez, Hermosillo, Matamoros, Nogales o Nuevo Laredo) [1][2].

  • Certificado mortuorio consular para envío de restos: Para la repatriación del cuerpo, la funeraria mexicana presenta el Acta de Defunción, el permiso sanitario de traslado y el certificado de embalsamamiento (con apostilla estatal y traducción según lo requiera la jurisdicción local) ante el consulado, el cual expide en inglés el Consular Mortuary Certificate necesario para el despacho de carga aérea y de la Oficina de Aduanas y Protección Fronteriza (U.S. Customs and Border Protection - CBP) [1][2].
  • Reporte Consular de Defunción en el Extranjero (Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad - CRDA): Una vez emitida el Acta de Defunción mexicana, presente el acta original y el pasaporte estadounidense de su familiar ante el consulado para la cancelación del pasaporte y la emisión del CRDA (Formulario DS-2060) a favor del familiar más cercano o representante legal (next of kin) [1][2]. El CRDA funciona en todos los estados de los Estados Unidos como comprobante oficial de defunción en inglés ante tribunales sucesorios (probate courts), bancos y aseguradoras; posteriormente pueden solicitarse copias certificadas adicionales al Departamento de Estado mediante el Formulario DS-5542 [2].

steps.title: Coordinar la recepción en los Estados Unidos y las notificaciones ante el Seguro Social (SSA)
steps.html:
Cuando el féretro ingresa por el aeropuerto o puerto fronterizo de entrada en los Estados Unidos, la funeraria receptora estadounidense acredita la documentación ante U.S. Customs and Border Protection, tramita el permiso estatal de tránsito o inhumación (burial-transit permit) conforme a las leyes del estado de destino (por ejemplo, en California, Texas, Illinois o Nueva York) y coordina el servicio funerario local [1][4].

Para las gestiones administrativas iniciales en los Estados Unidos:

  • Notificación a la Administración del Seguro Social y beneficios de sobrevivientes: Comuníquese con la Social Security Administration (teléfono: +1 800 772 1213; TTY: +1 800 325 0778) para reportar el fallecimiento ocurrido en el extranjero [6]. Aunque el consulado suele notificar el deceso al tramitar el CRDA, la familia debe confirmar directamente ante la Social Security Administration la suspensión de pagos mensuales (cualquier pago recibido correspondiente al mes del fallecimiento o posterior debe devolverse) y consultar el derecho al pago único por defunción de $255 y a las pensiones mensuales de sobrevivientes (survivor benefits), los cuales dependen del parentesco con la persona fallecida (por ejemplo, cónyuge sobreviviente, ex cónyuge elegible, hijos menores o con discapacidad, o padres dependientes) [6].
  • Sucesiones, cuentas bancarias y seguros en los Estados Unidos: Utilice el CRDA (y, cuando alguna institución lo solicite, copias apostilladas del Acta de Defunción mexicana) para notificar a bancos, compañías de seguros de vida, administradores de pensiones o cuentas de retiro y al tribunal sucesorio (probate court) del condado donde residía su familiar en los Estados Unidos [1][2].

es.closingQuestion: Para poder indicarle los datos exactos del distrito consular y los requisitos locales aplicables, ¿en qué municipio y estado de México ocurrió el fallecimiento y en qué estado de los Estados Unidos residía su familiar o se realizará la recepción?

title: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Spain and United Kingdom: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a British citizen dies in a hospital in Spain, mortuary sanitary rules and civil registration deadlines move quickly, so the immediate priorities are confirming the medical death certificate, checking insurance coverage, and appointing a coordinating funeral director [1].

steps.title: Confirm the Medical Death Certificate at the hospital and check sanitary deadlines
steps.html:
The hospital physician who attended the deceased person issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción), recording the date, time, and cause of death [1][2]. Provide the hospital with your family member's British passport (as well as their Foreigner Identity Card - Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero or TIE - or NIE number, if they held one) so that their full name, date of birth, and nationality are recorded accurately [1].

  • Natural death versus judicial investigation: If the death is due to natural causes certified at the hospital, the attending doctor signs the Certificado Médico de Defunción directly [1]. If the death was sudden, accidental, or requires investigation, the duty court (Juzgado de Guardia) intervenes, orders a judicial post-mortem examination, and must issue formal authorization before the funeral home can move the body or register the death [1].
  • 24-to-48-hour Mortuary Sanitary Rules window: Under the Mortuary Sanitary Regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria) of Spain's autonomous communities (for example, in Andalusia, the Valencian Community, Catalonia, Madrid, or the Canary Islands), transfer to an authorized mortuary (tanatorio) takes place immediately, and burial, cremation, or embalming/preservation normally must occur between 24 and 48 hours after death [1].

steps.title: Check assistance insurance and appoint a funeral company in Spain or the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Before signing an independent contract at the hospital or mortuary (tanatorio), check whether your family member had travel insurance, private medical insurance, bank account coverage, or a Spanish funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos) [1]. Insurers operate 24-hour assistance lines that directly appoint an international funeral company and cover eligible repatriation or local funeral costs [1].

If no insurance policy applies, you will need to appoint an authorized funeral company in Spain for transfer to the tanatorio, civil registration, and sanitary permits, and, if you choose to repatriate the body to the United Kingdom, a receiving funeral director in the destination UK nation [1]:

  • Funeral company in Spain: You can consult the consular lists of English-speaking funeral directors published by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (phone from Spain: +34 91 714 6300; phone from the United Kingdom: +44 20 7008 5000) [1][3] or contact the Spanish national funeral sector association, the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (National Association of Funeral Services - PANASEF, phone: +34 91 576 31 55; email: info@panasef.com) [4].
  • Receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom: To coordinate reception in the United Kingdom, you can locate an accredited provider through the directory of the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) [5]. Clarvia provides directory information for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific funeral providers.

steps.title: Register the death with the Civil Registry and request the Multilingual Certificate
steps.html:
The death must be registered with the municipal Civil Registry (Registro Civil) where the hospital is located, normally within 24 hours of the death and always before a burial, cremation, or transit license can be issued [1][2]. In practice, the Spanish funeral company submits the Certificado Médico de Defunción and your family member's British passport to the Registro Civil on the family's behalf [1].

Request two types of official certificates through the funeral company or the civil registry service under the Ministerio de Justicia (Ministry of Justice of Spain, phone: +34 91 837 22 95) [1][2]:

  • Full Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción): Request several official copies for all legal, banking, tax, and inheritance procedures in Spain [1][2].
  • Multilingual Death Certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción - Vienna Convention Form C): This international extract includes headings in English and is generally accepted directly by UK authorities and institutions without requiring an additional sworn translation [1]. Because Spanish Registro Civil certificates do not state the medical cause of death, also ask the hospital or funeral company for a copy of the medical certificate or hospital report, as UK coroners and insurers frequently require it [1].

steps.title: Coordinate with the British Consulate and arrange repatriation or a local funeral
steps.html:
You may notify the British Consulate in Spain or the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office to receive consular guidance and lists of lawyers and sworn translators (traductores jurados), although the consulate cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [1][3]. It is not mandatory to re-register a death that occurred in Spain with the UK General Register Office in order for the Spanish certificate to be valid in the United Kingdom [1].

The funeral director will coordinate the permits according to the option chosen by the family:

  • Repatriation of the body to the United Kingdom: The Spanish funeral company performs embalming, provides a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, and obtains the sanitary transit authorization, the certificate of absence of communicable disease, and the international mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio) for air transport [1]. Upon arrival in the United Kingdom, procedures vary by UK nation: in England and Wales, the British funeral director must notify the local coroner to authorize burial or cremation (particularly if cremation in the UK is requested); in Scotland, authorization rests with the procurator fiscal (with an application to the Scottish Government when cremating remains brought from abroad); and in Northern Ireland, the Coroners Service for Northern Ireland handles authorization [1][5].
  • Local cremation or burial in Spain: If cremation in Spain is chosen, the crematorium issues an official cremation certificate and provides a sealed urn so a family member can carry the ashes by air to the United Kingdom in accordance with airline security and cabin baggage rules [1].

steps.title: Complete post-death procedures in Spain and in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once the funeral service or repatriation is underway, follow-up administrative procedures depend on the deceased person's habitual residence and assets:

  • Registry of Last Wills and inheritance tax in Spain (if resident or holding assets in Spain): After 15 working days from the date of death, apply to the General Registry of Last Wills (Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad) of the Ministerio de Justicia using Form 790 (Modelo 790, code 006) for the Certificate of Last Wills (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Life Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento) [2]. This confirms whether your family member executed a notarized will in Spain [2]. If they held real estate, bank accounts, or rights in Spain, note that Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within 6 months of the date of death (an extension may be requested within the first 5 months).
  • Pension, government, and probate notifications in the United Kingdom:
    • If your family member ordinarily resided in England, Scotland, or Wales and died during a temporary stay in Spain, you can use the UK Tell Us Once service by calling the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) with the death certificate details to notify HM Revenue & Customs, HM Passport Office, local councils, and pension services at the same time [6].
    • If your family member resided permanently in Spain, Tell Us Once is not available [6]; instead, contact the International Pension Centre directly (phone: +44 191 218 7777) to stop the UK State Pension and check eligibility for survivor benefits depending on family relationship (such as a surviving spouse or civil partner), cancel the British passport with HM Passport Office, and use the Certificado Plurilingüe for UK banking and probate (or confirmation in Scotland) [1][6][7].

closingQuestion: To provide the exact guidance for your situation, in which municipality and autonomous community of Spain did the death occur, and did your family member reside in Spain or were they visiting from a UK nation (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland)?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando un ciudadano británico fallece en España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Pasos oficiales para el Certificado Médico de Defunción en España, inscripción en el Registro Civil en 24 horas (Certificado Plurilingüe), asistencia consular británica (FCDO), repatriación al Reino Unido o funeral local, y trámites de últimas voluntades y pensiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona de nacionalidad británica fallece en un hospital en España, los plazos sanitarios y de inscripción civil avanzan con rapidez, por lo que las prioridades inmediatas son confirmar el certificado médico, verificar la cobertura de seguro y designar una empresa funeraria coordinadora [1].

steps.title: Confirmar el Certificado Médico de Defunción en el hospital y los plazos sanitarios
steps.html:
El médico que atendió a la persona fallecida en el hospital expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial, haciendo constar la fecha, la hora y la causa del fallecimiento [1][2]. Entregue en el hospital el pasaporte británico de su familiar (así como su Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero - TIE - o número de NIE, si disponía de ellos) para que su nombre completo, fecha de nacimiento y nacionalidad queden registrados sin errores [1].

  • Fallecimiento natural frente a intervención judicial: Si el fallecimiento se debe a causas naturales certificadas en el hospital, el facultativo firma directamente el Certificado Médico de Defunción [1]. Si la muerte ha sido súbita, accidental o requiere investigación, interviene el Juzgado de Guardia competente, que debe ordenar la práctica de la autopsia judicial y emitir la autorización antes de que la funeraria pueda trasladar el cuerpo o inscribir el deceso [1].
  • Plazo de 24 a 48 horas de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Conforme a la normativa de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria de las comunidades autónomas españolas (por ejemplo, en Andalucía, la Comunidad Valenciana, Cataluña, Madrid o Canarias), el traslado a un tanatorio autorizado es inmediato y la inhumación, cremación o conservación/embalsamamiento suele realizarse entre las 24 y las 48 horas siguientes al fallecimiento [1].

steps.title: Verificar seguros de asistencia y contratar una empresa funeraria en España o el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Antes de firmar un contrato independiente en el hospital o en el tanatorio, compruebe si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, seguro médico privado, cobertura vinculada a una cuenta bancaria o una póliza española de seguro de decesos [1]. Las aseguradoras disponen de centrales de asistencia de 24 horas que designan directamente a la funeraria internacional y asumen los gastos cubiertos de repatriación o funeral local [1].

Si no existe seguro aplicable, deberá designar una empresa funeraria autorizada en España para el traslado al tanatorio, el registro civil y los permisos sanitarios y, si opta por repatriar el cuerpo al Reino Unido, un director funerario receptor en la nación británica de destino [1]:

  • Empresa funeraria en España: Puede consultar las listas consulares de funerarias que atienden en inglés publicadas por el Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (teléfono desde España: +34 91 714 6300; teléfono desde el Reino Unido: +44 20 7008 5000) [1][3] o acudir a la patronal española del sector, la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (teléfono: +34 91 576 31 55; correo electrónico: info@panasef.com) [4].
  • Director funerario receptor en el Reino Unido: Para coordinar la recepción en el Reino Unido, puede localizar un proveedor acreditado a través del directorio de la National Association of Funeral Directors (teléfono: +44 121 711 1343; correo electrónico: info@nafd.org.uk) [5]. Clarvia facilita información de directorios únicamente a título orientativo y no avala, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores funerarios concretos.

steps.title: Inscribir el fallecimiento en el Registro Civil y solicitar el Certificado Plurilingüe
steps.html:
El fallecimiento debe inscribirse en el Registro Civil del municipio español donde se ubica el hospital, habitualmente dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al deceso y siempre antes de que se expida la licencia de enterramiento, incineración o traslado [1][2]. En la práctica, la empresa funeraria española presenta ante el Registro Civil el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el pasaporte británico de su familiar en nombre de la familia [1].

Solicite a través de la funeraria o ante el servicio de registros civiles dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia (teléfono: +34 91 837 22 95) dos modalidades de certificación [1][2]:

  • Certificado Literal de Defunción: Solicite varios ejemplares oficiales para todas las gestiones legales, bancarias, fiscales y sucesorias en España [1][2].
  • Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C del Convenio de Viena): Este extracto internacional incluye encabezados en inglés y suele ser aceptado directamente por las autoridades y entidades del Reino Unido sin necesidad de traducción jurada adicional [1]. Dado que las actas del Registro Civil español no reflejan la causa médica de la muerte, pida también al hospital o a la funeraria copia del certificado médico o informe hospitalario, ya que las autoridades forenses y aseguradoras británicas suelen requerirlo [1].

steps.title: Coordinar con el Consulado Británico y gestionar la repatriación o el funeral local
steps.html:
Puede notificar el fallecimiento al Consulado Británico en España o al Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office para recibir orientación consular y listados de abogados y traductores jurados, si bien el consulado no puede sufragar gastos funerarios ni de repatriación [1][3]. No es obligatorio volver a inscribir en el Registro General del Reino Unido (General Register Office) una defunción ocurrida en España para que el certificado español tenga validez en territorio británico [1].

La funeraria coordinará los permisos según la opción elegida por la familia:

  • Repatriación del cuerpo al Reino Unido: La funeraria española realiza el embalsamamiento, dispone un féretro hermético con revestimiento de zinc y tramita la autorización sanitaria de traslado, el certificado de ausencia de enfermedades infectocontagiosas y el salvoconducto mortuorio internacional (laissez-passer) para el transporte aéreo [1]. A la llegada al Reino Unido, el procedimiento varía según la nación británica de destino: en Inglaterra y Gales, el director funerario británico debe notificar obligatoriamente al coroner local para que autorice el entierro o la cremación (sobre todo si se desea cremar en el Reino Unido); en Escocia, la autorización corresponde al procurator fiscal (con solicitud al Scottish Government en caso de cremación de restos procedentes del extranjero), y en Irlanda del Norte interviene el Coroners Service for Northern Ireland [1][5].
  • Cremación o inhumación local en España: Si se opta por la cremación en España, el crematorio emite el certificado oficial de cremación y entrega una urna sellada para que un familiar pueda trasladar las cenizas por vía aérea al Reino Unido, cumpliendo los requisitos de seguridad y equipaje de mano de la aerolínea [1].

steps.title: Realizar los trámites posteriores en España y en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Una vez encaminado el servicio funerario o la repatriación, las gestiones administrativas dependen del lugar de residencia habitual y de los bienes de la persona fallecida:

  • Registro de Últimas Voluntades e impuestos en España (si tenía residencia o bienes en España): Transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la fecha del fallecimiento, solicite ante el Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad del Ministerio de Justicia, mediante el Modelo 790 (código 006), el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [2]. Este documento acredita si su familiar otorgó testamento ante notario en España [2]. Si poseía inmuebles, cuentas bancarias o derechos en España, tenga en cuenta que el Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones debe presentarse en el plazo de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (pudiendo solicitarse una prórroga dentro de los primeros 5 meses).
  • Notificaciones de pensiones, administración pública y sucesión en el Reino Unido:
    • Si su familiar residía habitualmente en Inglaterra, Escocia o Gales y falleció durante una estancia temporal en España, puede utilizar el servicio británico Tell Us Once llamando al Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (teléfono: 0800 151 2012) con los datos del certificado de defunción para notificar simultáneamente a HM Revenue & Customs, HM Passport Office, autoridades locales y servicios de pensiones [6].
    • Si su familiar residía de forma permanente en España, el servicio Tell Us Once no está disponible [6]; en ese caso, comuníquese directamente con el International Pension Centre (teléfono: +44 191 218 7777) para dar de baja la pensión estatal británica (UK State Pension) y consultar posibles prestaciones de supervivencia según el vínculo familiar (por ejemplo, para cónyuge o pareja civil sobreviviente), cancele el pasaporte ante HM Passport Office y utilice el Certificado Plurilingüe para los trámites bancarios y de sucesión (probate o confirmation) en el Reino Unido [1][6][7].

es.closingQuestion: Para ofrecerle las indicaciones específicas aplicables a su caso, ¿en qué municipio y comunidad autónoma de España ocurrió el fallecimiento, y su familiar residía en España o se encontraba de visita desde alguna nación del Reino Unido (Inglaterra, Gales, Escocia o Irlanda del Norte)?

title: What to Do When a German Citizen or Resident Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a German Citizen or Resident Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Turkey and Germany: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences on the passing of your family member. When a German citizen residing in Germany dies in a hospital in Turkey, medical death reporting and civil registration begin in Turkey, while coffin repatriation to Germany (Sargüberführung) or local burial in Turkey is coordinated between Turkish and German authorities through an authorized funeral director [1][3].

steps.title: Issuance of the Medical Death Certificate via the Turkish Ministry of Health Death Notification System (ÖBS)
steps.html:
Because the death occurred in a hospital in Turkey, the attending hospital physician records the death electronically through the Death Notification System (Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi - ÖBS) operated by the T.C. Sağlık Bakanlığı (Ministry of Health of the Republic of Turkey, information line Alo 184) [1]. This generates the official medical Death Certificate (Ölüm Belgesi, which also serves as the burial permit / Gömme İzin Belgesi) and transmits the record electronically to the civil registry system [1][2].

  • Documents to submit to the hospital: To ensure identity details match without error, provide the hospital administration with the deceased person's German passport (Reisepass) or national ID card (Personalausweis) and, if applicable under dual citizenship or former Turkish nationality, their Turkish Identification Number (T.C. Kimlik Numarası) or Blue Card (Mavi Kart) [2][3].
  • Natural death versus judicial investigation: When the hospital certifies a death from natural causes, the Ölüm Belgesi is issued directly [1]. If the death resulted from an accident, sudden unexplained event, or suspicious circumstances, the body cannot be released until the Public Prosecutor's Office (Cumhuriyet Savcılığı) and the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tıp Kurumu) complete their investigation and issue a prosecutor's burial or transit permit [3].

steps.title: Coordinate with a Funeral Assistance Fund, Travel Insurance, or International Funeral Director (Bestatter)
steps.html:
Rather than attempting to manage airport cargo, customs, or mortuary procedures individually, check whether existing coverage applies before signing an independent contract:

  • Funeral assistance funds (Cenaze Fonu): If the deceased person was a member of a community funeral assistance fund operating in Germany (such as DITIB ZSU, IGMG UKBA, or ATIB, cited as publicly known examples for information only; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank these organizations), contact that fund first. These funds manage either local burial in Turkey or coffin repatriation to Germany end-to-end through their contracted units.
  • Travel health and assistance insurance: If the deceased person held international travel health insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung) or credit card assistance coverage, call the insurer's 24/7 emergency assistance hotline so their assistance unit can appoint an international repatriation company directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral director (Bestatter): If no fund or insurance policy applies, you can appoint an authorized international funeral company in Germany or Turkey. To find a funeral director (Bestatter) in Germany experienced in international repatriation, you can use the directory of the Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Federal Association of German Undertakers, main phone: +49 211 16008-10; 24/7 emergency support line: +49 211 16008-86; email: info@bestatter.de) [4]. Lists of local funeral companies in Turkey are published by the Deutsche Auslandsvertretungen in der Türkei (German Diplomatic Missions in Turkey) [3]. Clarvia provides directory information for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific funeral providers. The appointed firm obtains a written power of attorney (Vollmacht) from the family and the deceased person's ID/passport documents to handle all technical permits in Turkey and Germany [3][4].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Provincial or District Civil Registry and Obtain the Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C)
steps.html:
Under Article 31 of the Population Services Law No. 5490, deaths occurring in Turkey must be recorded within 10 days at the Provincial or District Directorate of Civil Registration (İl veya İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü) under the Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü (General Directorate of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs, domestic call center Alo 199; international phone: +90 312 591 21 00) responsible for the place of death [2].

  • Importance of the international Formül C certificate: A local Ölüm Belgesi issued solely in Turkish is not sufficient on its own for official authorities in Germany [3]. Once the hospital's ÖBS notification appears in the Civil Registry system, your authorized funeral company or a family member must apply to the relevant District Directorate of Civil Registration (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü) to request the multilingual extract of the death record (Formül C / Çok Dilli Ölüm Kayıt Örneği) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [2][3].
  • Direct validity in Germany: Because both Turkey and Germany are parties to the Vienna Convention on Multilingual Extracts, the Formül C certificate (which includes German headings) is accepted directly by German civil registry offices (Standesamt), courts, banks, and pension institutions without requiring an Apostille or sworn translation [3]. Requesting at least 3 to 5 wet-signed and stamped Formül C originals is advisable for administrative procedures in Germany.

steps.title: Obtain the Consular Corpse Transit Permit (Leichenpass), Municipal Cemetery Permits, and Arrange Burial or Repatriation
steps.html:
Depending on the family's decision, the deceased may be buried locally in Turkey or repatriated by coffin to Germany (Sargüberführung) [3][4]:

  • Coffin repatriation to Germany and municipal permits: For international air transport, the funeral company in Turkey coordinates with the municipal Department of Cemeteries (Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü, reachable nationwide via the ALO 188 Funeral Services line, for example the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality or Antalya Metropolitan Municipality Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü) and municipal health units to complete mandatory embalming (Einbalsamierung / tahnit), hermetic zinc/soldered coffin sealing, issuance of the Road Transit Permit (Yol İzin Belgesi / Cenaze Nakil İzin Belgesi), and airport customs clearance [2][3].
  • Consular processing and Leichenpass: Bringing the body into Germany requires a consular corpse transit permit (Leichenpass) alongside the Formül C death certificate, medical death report, and embalming/sealing certificate [3]. The appointed funeral company contacts the competent mission of the Deutsche Auslandsvertretungen in der Türkei for the place of death (German Embassy Ankara: +90 312 455 51 00; Consulate General Istanbul: +90 212 334 61 00; Consulate General Izmir: +90 232 488 88 88; Consulate Antalya: +90 242 314 11 01; after-hours nationwide emergency duty phone: +90 532 111 91 05) to obtain the Leichenpass and cancel the German passport [3][5]. German diplomatic missions provide consular assistance and document certification, but they do not pay repatriation expenses or act as an operational funeral company [3].
  • Local burial option in Turkey: If your family member also held Turkish citizenship or Mavi Kart rights, or if the family requests burial in Turkey, local grave allocation and burial procedures can be carried out directly through the relevant municipality's Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü (ALO 188) using the ÖBS burial permit [2].

steps.title: Notify the German Civil Registry (Standesamt) and Pension Authorities (Deutsche Rentenversicherung)
steps.html:
Once the multilingual Formül C death certificate has been obtained, administrative and financial notifications in Germany can begin:

  • German statutory pension notifications (Deutsche Rentenversicherung): If the deceased person received a German statutory pension, report the death immediately to the Renten Service der Deutschen Post (phone from abroad: +49 221 5692-777; fax: +49 221 5692-778) or directly to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (toll-free helpline within Germany: 0800 1000 4800) to prevent overpayments [6][7]. Submit the deceased person's pension insurance number (Versicherungsnummer or Zahlungskennzeichen) together with a copy of the Formül C certificate [6]. The pension is paid through the end of the month of death; keeping the bank account open initially is advisable for settlement adjustments [6]. If the deceased leaves behind a surviving spouse, registered partner, or eligible children, they can apply for a widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Witwen-/Witwerrente or Waisenrente), and a surviving spouse may request the three-month transition advance (Sterbevierteljahr) through the Renten Service within 30 days of death [6][7].
  • German civil registry (Standesamt) subsequent registration: A death occurring in Turkey is not automatically forwarded to civil registry or pension authorities in Germany [3]. While the Formül C certificate is accepted directly by German health insurers (Krankenkasse), banks, and probate courts (Nachlassgericht), eligible relatives (spouse, children, or parents) may apply to the Standesamt at the deceased person's last German place of residence (or to Standesamt I in Berlin if they never resided in Germany) for subsequent registration of a death abroad (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland under § 36 PStG) and issuance of a German death certificate (deutsche Sterbeurkunde) [3].

closingQuestion: So that we can tailor the next steps to your situation, in which province of Turkey did your family member pass away (and do you plan repatriation to Germany or burial in Turkey), and in which German federal state (Bundesland) or city was their place of residence?
caseDependentItems: Whether the deceased held German citizenship, dual citizenship, or Mavi Kart (Blue Card), which determines consular and local registry procedures
Coordination with an existing funeral assistance fund (Cenaze Fonu) vs. travel insurance or independent German Bestatter
Municipal cemetery department (Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü) transit permit, embalming, and airport customs clearance in Turkey and Germany
German Standesamt registration (Nachbeurkundung) and Deutsche Rentenversicherung survivor pension (Witwen-/Waisenrente) rules by family relationship

contacts.note: German Diplomatic Missions in Turkey (Embassy in Ankara, Consulates General in Istanbul and Izmir, and Consulate in Antalya) providing consular assistance, Leichenpass issuance, and lists of local funeral companies.

contacts.note: Federal Association of German Undertakers offering a directory to locate licensed funeral directors (Bestatter) for international repatriation and funeral services in Germany.

tr.title: Almanya Vatandaşı veya Mukimi Bir Kişi Türkiye'de Vefat Ettiğinde Yapılması Gerekenler: 5 Adımlı Resmi Rehber
tr.cardSummary: Türkiye'de Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) raporu, Nüfus Müdürlüğü'nden Formül C çok dilli ölüm belgesi, Alman Dış Temsilcilikleri (Leichenpass), cenaze nakli veya yerel defin ve Almanya Standesamt ile emeklilik (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) işlemleri.
tr.introHtml: Aile yakınınızın vefatı nedeniyle başsağlığı dileriz. Almanya'da ikamet eden bir Almanya vatandaşının Türkiye'de hastanede vefat etmesi halinde, tıbbi ölüm bildirimi ve nüfus tescili Türkiye'de başlatılır; cenazenin Almanya'ya nakli (Sargüberführung) veya Türkiye'de yerel defin işlemleri ise yetkilendirilen cenaze nakil sorumlusu aracılığıyla Türkiye ve Almanya makamları arasında yürütülür.

steps.title: T.C. Sağlık Bakanlığı Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) Üzerinden Tıbbi Ölüm Belgesinin Düzenlenmesi
steps.html:
Vefat Türkiye'de bir hastanede gerçekleştiği için, ilgili hastane hekimi ölüm kaydını elektronik ortamda T.C. Sağlık Bakanlığı (danışma hattı Alo 184) tarafından yürütülen Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) üzerinden düzenler [1]. Bu işlem sonucunda resmi tıbbi Ölüm Belgesi (defin ruhsatı / Gömme İzin Belgesi) oluşturulur ve bilgiler elektronik olarak nüfus kayıt sistemine aktarılır [1][2].

  • Hastaneye ibraz edilecek belgeler: Kimlik bilgilerinin eksiksiz eşleşmesi için vefat eden kişinin Alman pasaportunu (Reisepass) veya kimlik kartını (Personalausweis) ve varsa çifte vatandaşlık kapsamındaki T.C. Kimlik Numarasını ya da Mavi Kart belgesini hastane idaresine teslim edin [2][3].
  • Doğal ölüm ve adli inceleme ayrımı: Hastane ölümü doğal nedenli olarak belgelendirdiğinde Ölüm Belgesi doğrudan düzenlenir. Ölümün kaza, ani vefat veya şüpheli bir durum sonucu gerçekleşmesi halinde ise Cumhuriyet Savcılığı ve Adli Tıp Kurumu incelemesi tamamlanıp savcılık defin/nakil izni verilene kadar cenaze teslim edilmez [3].

steps.title: Cenaze Yardımlaşma Fonu, Seyahat Sigortası veya Uluslararası Cenaze Nakil Firması (Bestatter) ile Koordinasyon
steps.html:
Havalimanı kargo, gümrük veya morg işlemlerini bireysel olarak yürütmeye çalışmak yerine, bağımsız bir sözleşme imzalamadan önce mevcut bir güvencenin bulunup bulunmadığını kontrol edin:

  • Cenaze yardımlaşma fonları (Cenaze Fonu): Vefat eden kişinin Almanya'da faaliyet gösteren bir cenaze yardımlaşma fonuna (örneğin DITIB ZSU, IGMG UKBA veya ATIB gibi kamuya açık bilgi amaçlı örnekler; Clarvia bu kuruluşları onaylamaz, önermez veya sıralamaz) üyeliği varsa ilk olarak ilgili fonla iletişime geçin. Bu fonlar hem Türkiye'de yerel defin hem de Almanya'ya cenaze nakli süreçlerini anlaşmalı birimler aracılığıyla uçtan uca üstlenir.
  • Seyahat sağlık ve asistans sigortası: Vefat eden kişinin yurt dışı seyahat sağlık sigortası (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung) veya kredi kartına bağlı asistans güvencesi bulunuyorsa, sigorta şirketinin 7/24 acil yardım hattını arayın; sigorta asistans birimi uluslararası nakil firmasını doğrudan görevlendirir.
  • Yetkili cenaze firması (Bestatter) görevlendirilmesi: Herhangi bir fon veya sigorta kapsamı yoksa, Almanya'da veya Türkiye'de yetkili bir uluslararası cenaze firması görevlendirebilirsiniz. Almanya genelinde uluslararası nakil tecrübesi olan bir Bestatter bulmak için Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Almanya Federal Cenaze Levazımatçıları Birliği, merkez telefon +49 211 16008-10, 7/24 acil destek hattı +49 211 16008-86, e-posta info@bestatter.de) rehberini kullanabilirsiniz [4]. Türkiye'deki yerel cenaze firmaları listesine ise Deutsche Auslandsvertretungen in der Türkei (Türkiye'deki Alman Dış Temsilcilikleri) üzerinden ulaşılabilir [3]. Görevlendirilen firma aileden yazılı vekaletname (Vollmacht) ve vefat eden kişinin kimlik/pasaport belgelerini alarak Türkiye ve Almanya'daki tüm teknik izinleri takip eder [3][4].

steps.title: İl veya İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü'nde Ölüm Kaydı ve Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi (Formül C) Alınması
steps.html:
5490 sayılı Nüfus Hizmetleri Kanunu'nun 31. maddesi uyarınca, Türkiye'de meydana gelen ölüm olayları en geç 10 gün içinde Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü (yurt içi çağrı merkezi Alo 199, yurt dışı telefon +90 312 591 21 00) bünyesindeki vefat yerinin bağlı olduğu İl veya İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü kayıtlarına işlenir [2].

  • Uluslararası Formül C belgesinin önemi: Yalnızca Türkçe düzenlenen yerel Ölüm Belgesi, Almanya'daki resmi makamlar nezdinde tek başına yeterli değildir [3]. Hastanenin ÖBS bildirimi Nüfus Müdürlüğü sistemine düştükten sonra, yetkilendirdiğiniz cenaze firması veya aile yakını ilgili İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü'ne başvurarak 1976 Viyana CIEC Sözleşmesi kapsamındaki çok dilli ölüm kayıt örneğini (Formül C / Çok Dilli Ölüm Kayıt Örneği) talep etmelidir [2][3].
  • Almanya'da doğrudan geçerlilik: Türkiye ve Almanya Viyana Çok Dilli Belge Sözleşmesi'ne taraf olduğundan, Almanca başlıklar içeren Formül C belgesi Almanya'daki nüfus müdürlükleri (Standesamt), mahkemeler, bankalar ve emeklilik kurumlarında Apostil şerhi veya yeminli tercüme aranmaksızın doğrudan kabul edilir [3]. Almanya'daki işlemler için en az 3 ila 5 adet ıslak imzalı ve mühürlü Formül C nüshası alınması yararlıdır.

steps.title: Alman Dış Temsilcilikleri (Leichenpass), Belediye Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü İzinleri ve Defin veya Nakil Süreci
steps.html:
Ailenin tercihine göre cenaze Türkiye'de defnedilebilir veya tabutla Almanya'ya nakledilebilir (Sargüberführung) [3][4]:

  • Almanya'ya cenaze nakli ve belediye izinleri: Uluslararası hava yolu nakli için Türkiye'deki cenaze firması, vefatın gerçekleştiği il veya ilçedeki belediye Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü (Türkiye genelinde ALO 188 Cenaze Hizmetleri hattı; örneğin İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi veya Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü) ve belediye sağlık birimleriyle koordinasyon sağlayarak zorunlu tahnit (Einbalsamierung / ilaçlama) işlemini, çinko/lehimli sızdırmaz tabut mühürlemesini, Yol İzin Belgesi (Cenaze Nakil İzin Belgesi) düzenlenmesini ve havalimanı gümrük işlemlerini tamamlar [2][3].
  • Konsolosluk işlemleri ve Leichenpass: Cenazenin Almanya'ya girişi için Formül C ölüm belgesi, tıbbi ölüm raporu ve tahnit/sızdırmazlık tutanağının yanı sıra cenaze geçiş belgesi (Leichenpass) düzenlenmesi gerekir [3]. Görevlendirilen cenaze firması, vefat yerinin bağlı olduğu görev bölgesine göre Deutsche Auslandsvertretungen in der Türkei (Ankara Alman Büyükelçiliği: +90 312 455 51 00; İstanbul Başkonsolosluğu: +90 212 334 61 00; İzmir Başkonsolosluğu: +90 232 488 88 88; Antalya Konsolosluğu: +90 242 314 11 01; mesai saatleri dışında Türkiye geneli ortak nöbetçi acil durum hattı: +90 532 111 91 05) ile iletişime geçerek Leichenpass ve pasaport iptal işlemlerini tamamlar [3][5]. Alman dış temsilcilikleri konsolosluk desteği ve belge onayı sağlar; ancak nakil masraflarını karşılamaz ve operasyonel cenaze firması yerine geçmez [3].
  • Türkiye'de yerel defin seçeneği: Aile yakınınızın aynı zamanda Türk vatandaşlığı veya Mavi Kart hakkı bulunuyorsa ya da aile Türkiye'de defin talep ediyorsa, ÖBS defin ruhsatı ile doğrudan ilgili belediyenin Mezarlıklar Müdürlüğü (ALO 188) üzerinden yerel mezar yeri tahsisi ve defin işlemleri yürütülebilir [2].

steps.title: Almanya'da Standesamt (Nachbeurkundung) ve Emeklilik Kurumlarına (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) Bildirim
steps.html:
Çok dilli Formül C ölüm belgesi alındıktan sonra Almanya'daki idari ve mali bildirimler başlatılır:

  • Alman yasal emeklilik bildirimleri (Deutsche Rentenversicherung): Vefat eden kişi Almanya'dan emekli aylığı alıyorsa, fazla ödemeleri önlemek için vefat durumu derhal Renten Service der Deutschen Post birimine (yurt dışından telefon +49 221 5692-777, faks +49 221 5692-778) veya doğrudan Deutsche Rentenversicherung kurumuna (Almanya içi ücretsiz hizmet hattı 0800 1000 4800) bildirilmelidir [6][7]. Bildirimde vefat eden kişinin sigorta numarası (Versicherungsnummer veya Zahlungskennzeichen) ile Formül C belgesinin bir örneği sunulur [6]. Emekli aylığı vefat ayının sonuna kadar ödenir; olası mahsuplaşmalar için banka hesabının hemen kapatılmaması önerilir [6]. Vefat eden kişinin geride kalan eşi, kayıtlı hayat arkadaşı veya hak sahibi çocukları bulunuyorsa, bu kişiler dul veya yetim aylığı (Witwen-/Witwerrente veya Waisenrente) başvurusu yapabilir ve eşler vefattan itibaren 30 gün içinde Renten Service üzerinden üç aylık geçiş avansı (Sterbevierteljahr) talep edebilir [6][7].
  • Alman nüfus müdürlüğü (Standesamt) tescili: Türkiye'de gerçekleşen bir vefat, Almanya'daki nüfus veya emeklilik makamlarına otomatik olarak iletilmez. Formül C belgesi Almanya'daki sağlık sigortası (Krankenkasse), bankalar ve miras mahkemesi (Nachlassgericht) işlemlerinde doğrudan geçerli olmakla birlikte, başvuru hakkına sahip yakınlar (eş, çocuklar veya ebeveynler) vefat eden kişinin Almanya'daki son ikamet yerindeki Standesamt birimine (Almanya'da hiç ikameti olmamışsa Berlin Standesamt I'e) başvurarak yurt dışındaki ölümün Alman nüfus kütüğüne sonradan tescilini (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland - § 36 PStG) ve Alman ölüm belgesi (deutsche Sterbeurkunde) düzenlenmesini isteyebilir [3].

tr.closingQuestion: Süreci durumunuza göre netleştirebilmemiz için, aile yakınınız Türkiye'nin hangi ilinde vefat etti (Almanya'ya nakil mi yoksa Türkiye'de defin mi planlıyorsunuz) ve Almanya'daki ikamet yeri hangi eyalet (Bundesland) veya şehirde bulunuyor?

title: What to Do When an Indian National Dies in the UAE: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When an Indian National Dies in the UAE: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official steps for UAE hospital notification and police clearance, Ministry of Health/DHA/DOH death certificate, Indian Embassy/Consulate registration and NOC, air cargo repatriation to India (eCARe) or local rites, and employer/gratuity settlement.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When an Indian national working in the United Arab Emirates dies in a hospital, the medical notification and police clearance in the relevant emirate unlock both the official UAE death certificate and the Indian consular clearances required to repatriate the mortal remains to India (or arrange local rites in the UAE).

steps.title: Obtain the UAE Hospital Medical Notification of Death
steps.html:
When a death occurs in a hospital anywhere in the UAE, the attending physician records the cause of death electronically and issues the official Medical Notification of Death, after which the deceased is transferred to a designated government mortuary [1][2].

  • Identity documents to provide: The family or local representative must present the deceased's original Indian passport, UAE residence visa details, and Emirates ID to the hospital administration so the medical notification matches official civil and immigration records [1][2].
  • Emirate health systems and forensic clearance: In Dubai, hospital notifications connect with the Dubai Health Authority (toll-free 800 342 or +971 4 219 8888) [2]; in Abu Dhabi, hospitals record the notification on the Department of Health (DOH) system (linked to the Sanadkom bereavement service on the TAMM portal) [1]; and in the Northern Emirates (Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah), notifications run through the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) / Emirates Health Services (EHS) [1]. If the death was natural, the notification is released once hospital formalities are cleared. If the death was sudden, accidental, work-related, or under investigation, the case is referred to the emirate police and forensic medicine department for clearance before the body can be released [1][2].

steps.title: Coordinate with the UAE Employer/Sponsor, Community Repatriation Volunteers, or ICWF Support
steps.html:
Before paying a commercial repatriation agency, confirm who is legally responsible and authorized to handle the local filings in the UAE:

  • Employer/sponsor statutory obligation: Under Article 15 of UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 (UAE Labour Law), regulated across the UAE by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (call center 600 590000 inside the UAE, +971 6 803 4000 from abroad, labour advisory line 800 84, email ask@mohre.gov.ae), the UAE employer is legally required to bear the full costs of preparing and repatriating the deceased worker's mortal remains to their home country when requested by the family [3]. In practice, the employer's Public Relations Officer (PRO) normally coordinates the local clearances.
  • Authorizing a local representative: If no immediate family member is present in the UAE, the next of kin in India must sign a written authorization letter (Power of Attorney / No Objection letter) naming a representative in the UAE - such as a relative, colleague, employer representative, or accredited community social worker - to collect certificates, complete police and consular steps, and dispatch or accompany the coffin [4][5].
  • ICWF assistance and avoiding unaccredited middlemen: If the employer is absent or defaulting, or if the family faces financial distress, contact the Indian mission immediately via the 24x7 Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra (PBSK) toll-free helpline (800 46342, WhatsApp +971 54 3090571), the Consulate General of India in Dubai 24x7 death helpline (+971 50 7347676), or the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi death emergency number (+971 56 4038863) [4][5]. Through the Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF), the Indian missions provide means-tested financial assistance (covering embalming, coffin box, local ambulance, and air cargo/airfare to India) and connect families with empanelled community volunteers who handle all local UAE formalities at zero service charge [4][5]. Indian missions explicitly warn families to avoid unauthorized private middlemen charging excessive fees [4][5].

steps.title: Secure UAE Police Clearance (NOC), the Official Health Authority Death Certificate, and Visa Cancellation
steps.html:
With the hospital's Medical Notification of Death and the next-of-kin/employer authorization letter, the appointed representative completes the local emirate clearances [1][2]:

  • Police clearance and NOCs: The representative submits the hospital notification, original Indian passport, Emirates ID, and authorization letters to the competent emirate police headquarters - for example, Dubai Police in Dubai (emergency 999, non-emergency inquiries 901, email mail@dubaipolice.gov.ae) or Abu Dhabi Police / the relevant Northern Emirate police directorate [1][6]. The police verify the circumstances of death and issue the official Police Clearance / No Objection Certificates (NOCs) authorizing release of the body from the mortuary, embalming, and export of the mortal remains outside the UAE (or local burial/cremation) [1][6].
  • Official UAE Death Certificate: Using the hospital notification and police NOC, the representative obtains the official UAE Death Certificate from the competent health authority - via the Dubai Health Authority in Dubai [2], the DOH / Sanadkom service in Abu Dhabi [1], or MOHAP / EHS in the Northern Emirates [1]. Request the certificate in both Arabic and English (or with an official English translation) along with several certified copies [1][4].
  • UAE residency visa cancellation: The employer or representative submits the death certificate and passport through the federal immigration authority (ICP, or GDRFA in Dubai) to cancel the deceased's UAE residence visa and work permit, which is required before airport cargo clearance [1].

steps.title: Register the Death, Cancel the Indian Passport, and Obtain the Consular NOC
steps.html:
Consular jurisdiction in the UAE depends on the emirate of death and residence [4][5]:

  • Which Indian mission to contact: For deaths in Dubai and the five Northern Emirates (Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah), contact the Consulate General of India in Dubai (24x7 death registration mobile/WhatsApp +971 50 7347676, PBSK toll-free 800 46342, email deathregistration.dubai@mea.gov.in) [4]. For deaths in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi (including Al Ain and Al Dhafra), contact the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi (24x7 death case mobile/WhatsApp +971 56 4038863, PBSK toll-free 800 46342, email cons.abudhabi@mea.gov.in) [5].
  • Documents required by the Indian mission: The authorized representative presents the original UAE Death Certificate and hospital medical notification (with copies), the deceased's original Indian passport, the UAE Police NOC, the employer's letter on company letterhead detailing service status and a "dues and drawn" statement, the next-of-kin authorization letter, flight cargo booking details, and the passport/ID copies of the representative and any attendant accompanying the remains [4][5].
  • Certificates issued: The mission registers the death of the Indian citizen abroad, issues an Indian Consular Death Certificate, cancels the deceased's Indian passport (returning it stamped as cancelled for travel with the coffin), and issues the Consular No Objection Certificate (NOC) required by UAE airport authorities, airlines, and Indian health and customs officials [4][5]. Both missions process death cases on priority, including outside office hours and on public holidays [4][5].

steps.title: Complete Mortuary Embalming, Air Cargo and Indian eCARe Clearance (or Local Rites), and MOHRE Gratuity Settlement
steps.html:
Once the police, health, and consular certificates are issued, the representative completes the transport (or local funeral) and financial settlement steps:

  • Mortuary embalming and UAE air cargo (or local rites): For repatriation to India, mandatory embalming and hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin preparation (boxing) are completed at the authorized government mortuary - for example, the Muhaisnah medical fitness and mortuary facility coordinated with Dubai Municipality (24/7 call center 800 900 or +971 4 2215555, email info@dm.gov.ae) in Dubai, or the municipal central mortuary in Abu Dhabi or Sharjah [1][7]. The mortuary issues the official Embalming Certificate, Coffin Sealing Certificate, and Certificate of Non-Infectious Disease [1][8]. The representative books the sealed coffin as air cargo (such as through DNATA Cargo at Dubai International Airport or Etihad Cargo at Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi) [1][4]. (If the family instead chooses local cremation or burial in the UAE, the police NOC, death certificate, and Indian mission NOC are presented to the municipal cemetery or cremation facility, such as the Jebel Ali cremation facility in Dubai or the Abu Dhabi non-Muslim cemetery [1][4].)
  • Indian Airport Health Organisation (APHO) clearance via eCARe: Under the rules of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in India, public health clearance for bringing mortal remains into India is processed through the online eCARe portal (preferably submitted 48 hours before arrival, with emergency expedition available) by uploading four mandatory documents: the official Death Certificate showing cause of death, the Embalming Certificate, the Indian Embassy/Consulate NOC, and the cancelled Indian passport [8]. At the receiving international airport in India, the designated family member presents valid ID to the APHO and cargo terminal to receive the coffin and register the burial or cremation locally [8].
  • UAE end-of-service gratuity and bank accounts: Under Article 15 of the UAE Labour Law, the employer must disburse all unpaid wages, accrued leave, and the full end-of-service gratuity to the worker's designated family beneficiary or legal heirs within 10 days of the death [3]. Request a formal "dues and drawn" statement from the employer [5]. If the employer delays or fails to pay, file a labour claim with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (600 590000 or 800 84) or seek assistance from the Indian mission's labour/welfare wing [3][4][5]. Note that UAE bank accounts held in the deceased's name are frozen upon notification of death and require a legal heirship/succession certificate attested by the Indian mission and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs for release through the local emirate court [1].

closingQuestion: To help us provide exact local details, in which emirate did your family member pass away (and is the employer cooperating with the arrangements), and which airport and state in India will receive the mortal remains?
