title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in the United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in the United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide to terminal illness preparation in the US: Medicare hospice & palliative care, Advance Directives (Health Care Proxy, Living Will, POLST), Durable Financial Power of Attorney, Social Security Compassionate Allowances / FMLA, and account organization.
introHtml: We are very sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. Taking care and legal steps now, while your family member still has full decision-making capacity, keeps them in control of their medical care, establishes clear legal authority for their chosen representatives, and avoids court guardianship or probate delays later. Below are the five main practical and administrative steps to take in order across the United States.

steps.title: Arrange Palliative Care or Elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit
steps.html:
Start by asking your family member's treating specialist or primary care physician for a referral to palliative care or hospice, depending on their current treatment goals [1][2]:

  • Palliative care: Provides symptom management, pain relief, and care coordination at any stage of a serious illness, and can be provided alongside curative or life-prolonging treatments [2].
  • Hospice care (Medicare Part A Hospice Benefit): Focuses on comfort and quality of life at home or in an inpatient facility once curative treatment for the terminal illness stops [1][2]. Under federal Medicare Part A rules, both the person's regular physician (if they have one) and the hospice medical director must certify a terminal prognosis with a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the illness runs its normal course, and the patient (or their authorized healthcare representative) must sign an election statement choosing hospice care instead of curative treatment for the terminal condition [1]. Coverage provides two initial 90-day benefit periods followed by unlimited 60-day periods as long as a hospice physician recertifies eligibility [1].
  • If your family member is covered by employer or private insurance, state Medicaid, or Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health care, ask the clinical care coordinator to confirm in-network hospice agencies and home-care coverage. For federal Medicare coverage questions or to compare Medicare-approved hospice providers, contact Medicare at 1-800-633-4227 (1-800-MEDICARE; TTY 1-877-486-2048) [1].

steps.title: Complete State-Recognized Advance Directives, POLST, and a HIPAA Release
steps.html:
Because legal execution rules (such as required witnesses, disqualified witnesses, or notarization) are governed by individual U.S. state statutes, complete the statutory forms for the state where your family member resides and receives care while they can clearly express and sign their wishes [2][3]:

  • Health Care Proxy (Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care): Names a trusted healthcare agent (and at least one alternate agent) to make medical decisions if the person loses decision-making capacity [2]. Depending on the state, this document may be called a Health Care Proxy (for example, in New York or Massachusetts), a Medical Power of Attorney (for example, in Texas), or an Advance Health Care Directive (for example, in California) [3].
  • Living Will: Documents the person's specific instructions regarding life-sustaining interventions - including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition and hydration, and comfort care [2].
  • HIPAA Release (Authorization): A signed authorization under the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act lets clinicians, hospitals, and health plans share protected health information and billing details with designated family members immediately, even while the patient still has capacity and before a Health Care Proxy takes effect [4].
  • POLST or MOLST (Physician or Medical Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment): Unlike a Living Will, a state POLST or MOLST form (such as POLST in California or Oregon, or MOLST in New York) is an actionable medical order signed by a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant that Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and hospitals must follow immediately during an emergency [2]. Ask the treating clinician to complete this order with your family member and keep a copy visible at home.

You can request free federal advance care planning guides from the National Institute on Aging at 1-800-222-2225 or niaic@nia.nih.gov [2], and download free state-specific advance directive forms from CaringInfo at 1-800-658-8898 [3]. Provide signed copies to the medical team, the named healthcare agent, and local hospital electronic health record portals [2].

steps.title: Execute a Durable Financial Power of Attorney
steps.html:
A medical proxy does not grant legal authority to manage bank accounts, real estate, tax filings, insurance claims, or government benefits [2][5]. While your family member has legal capacity:

  • Sign a state-compliant Durable Financial Power of Attorney: Ensure the document is explicitly "durable" under state law (many states follow the Uniform Power of Attorney Act, while states such as New York have specific statutory short forms) so the financial agent's authority remains valid if the principal becomes incapacitated [5]. Decide whether the power of attorney should take effect immediately upon signing (allowing the agent to help pay bills and manage paperwork right away) or only upon a physician's written certification of incapacity.
  • Verify bank and brokerage requirements in advance: Contact the person's primary banks, mortgage servicer, and investment firms now. Many financial institutions require their own internal power of attorney forms or advance legal department review before honoring a state statutory form.
  • For plain-language fiduciary guides on acting as a financial agent, contact the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at 1-855-411-2372 [5]. To connect with local Area Agencies on Aging, caregiver support, and state elder law resources, contact the Eldercare Locator at 1-800-677-1116 [6].

steps.title: Claim Expedited Social Security Disability and Protect Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Social Security Compassionate Allowances and TERI: If your family member is under full retirement age and can no longer work, apply immediately for federal Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) [7]. Explicitly state the terminal diagnosis and any hospice enrollment on the application so the Social Security Administration flags the claim under its Terminal Illness (TERI) procedure and screens it against the Compassionate Allowances list, which fast-tracks medical determinations for qualifying life-limiting conditions to weeks rather than months [7]. Call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (TTY 1-800-325-0778) to file or expedite a pending claim [7].
  • Federal FMLA and State Paid Family Leave: Under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), an eligible employee of a covered employer (generally 50 or more employees within 75 miles, or a public agency) may take up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period to care for a covered immediate family member (a spouse, child, or parent) with a serious health condition, supported by medical certification form WH-380-F [8]. For questions on federal leave eligibility, contact the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division at 1-866-487-9243 [8]. In addition, check whether the caregiver works in a state with a statutory Paid Family Leave insurance program (such as California, New York, New Jersey, Washington, Massachusetts, or Oregon), which may provide partial wage replacement and sometimes covers a broader range of family relationships.

steps.title: Organize Wills, POD/TOD Beneficiary Designations, and Vital Documents
steps.html:
• Review Payable-on-Death (POD) and Transfer-on-Death (TOD) designations: Check primary and contingent beneficiary designations on all life insurance policies, 401(k) and 403(b) plans, IRAs, and pensions, as these contractual designations generally override instructions in a will (note that federal ERISA rules and community-property state laws often require written spousal consent if someone other than a current spouse is named). Where appropriate, add Payable-on-Death (POD) designations to bank accounts and Transfer-on-Death (TOD) registrations to brokerage accounts (and TOD real estate deeds or vehicle titles in states that recognize them) so those assets transfer directly outside probate.
  • Update or execute a Last Will and Testament: Confirm that your family member's will (and any revocable living trust) is signed, witnessed, and notarized according to their state's statutory formalities (including a self-proving affidavit where available) so the named executor or personal representative can administer remaining estate assets smoothly.
  • Assemble a central vital documents folder: Gather original or certified copies of birth and marriage or divorce certificates, Social Security cards, military discharge records (DD-214 if applicable), property deeds, vehicle titles, insurance policies, recent tax returns, and a secure written inventory of digital accounts, passwords, and recurring household bills [2].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in the United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in the United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide to terminal illness preparation in the UK: NHS palliative care & NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track, SR1 form & fast-track Special Rules benefits (PIP/AA/UC), Lasting Power of Attorney (OPG), Advance Decision (ADRT) / ReSPECT, and will preparation.
introHtml: We are very sorry to hear about your family member's diagnosis. Putting care coordination, fast-track benefits, and legal authority in place now in the United Kingdom, while the person still has mental capacity, ensures their wishes are legally protected and urgent support is ready when needed. Below are the five main practical and administrative steps to take in order across the UK (highlighting standard procedures in England and Wales alongside key differences in Scotland and Northern Ireland).

steps.title: Coordinate NHS Palliative Care, Hospice Support, and NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track
steps.html:
Ask your family member's GP, hospital consultant, or clinical nurse specialist to coordinate community palliative care and hospice support right away [1][2]:

  • Community palliative care and GP register: The GP or hospital specialist team can refer the person to community district nurses, specialist palliative care teams, and local hospice services (including outpatient therapy, symptom control, and Hospice at Home) [1][2]. Ask the GP practice to add the person to its palliative care register so out-of-hours doctors and ambulance services have immediate access to their coordinated care summary (such as the Key Information Summary in Scotland) [1].
  • NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC) Fast Track funding: In England and Wales, if the person's condition is deteriorating rapidly and may be entering a terminal phase requiring an urgent package of care at home or in a nursing home or hospice, a doctor or registered nurse can complete the NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool and submit it directly to the local NHS Integrated Care Board (ICB) in England (or Local Health Board in Wales) [3]. Unlike local council social care, NHS Continuing Healthcare is 100% funded by the NHS and is free regardless of income or savings [3]. The local ICB must accept a properly completed Fast Track referral without a lengthy multi-disciplinary assessment and aims to put funded care in place rapidly (normally within 48 hours) [3]. (In Scotland, hospital-based complex clinical care and free personal and nursing care apply via the local NHS board and council; in Northern Ireland, urgent palliative care packages are arranged through the local Health and Social Care Trust.)
  • For free clinical and practical guidance on terminal illness care across the UK, you can call the Marie Curie Support Line at 0800 090 2309 [4] or locate local hospices through Hospice UK at 020 7520 8200 or info@hospiceuk.org [2].

steps.title: Request an SR1 Medical Form and Claim Fast-Track Special Rules Benefits
steps.html:
Because clinicians expect your family member may have 12 months or less to live, they can claim disability and income benefits under the Special Rules for End of Life (SREL), which fast-tracks decisions to a matter of days, pays the highest rate automatically, and waives face-to-face assessments and qualifying waiting periods [5]:

  • Ask a clinician for form SR1 (or BASRiS in Scotland): In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, ask the person's GP, hospital consultant, hospice doctor, or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical evidence form confirming the diagnosis and treatment [5]. There is no charge for the SR1, and the clinician will either send it directly to the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) (or Department for Communities in Northern Ireland) or give you a copy to submit [5]. In Scotland, clinicians complete a BASRiS (Benefits Assessment under Special Rules in Scotland) form instead of an SR1 for benefits administered by Social Security Scotland, where no fixed 12-month time limit applies [5].
  • Submit the benefit claim (which a family member or representative can also initiate on the person's behalf):
    • If the person has reached State Pension age: In England and Wales, claim Attendance Allowance by calling the Attendance Allowance Helpline at 0800 731 0122 (or applying online via GOV.UK) [5][6]; claims under the Special Rules automatically receive the higher weekly rate [6]. (In Scotland, check whether the area uses Attendance Allowance or Social Security Scotland's Pension Age Disability Payment.)
    • If the person is under State Pension age: In England and Wales, claim Personal Independence Payment (PIP) by calling the Personal Independence Payment New Claims Line at 0800 917 2222 (which automatically awards the enhanced daily living component under Special Rules), and check entitlement to Universal Credit or New Style Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) [5]. (In Scotland, claim Adult Disability Payment through Social Security Scotland.)

steps.title: Register Lasting Powers of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian
steps.html:
While your family member has mental capacity, prepare and register formal powers of attorney so their chosen attorneys can act legally if they lose capacity [7]:

  • England and Wales (Lasting Powers of Attorney): Set up both types of Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) [7]:
    • Property and Financial Affairs LPA: Authorizes attorneys to manage bank accounts, pay household bills, claim benefits, and handle property. With the donor's consent, this LPA can be used as soon as it is registered, even while they still have capacity [7].
    • Health and Welfare LPA: Authorizes attorneys to make decisions about medical care, daily care routines, care placement, and (if the donor ticks the specific option on the form) life-sustaining treatment. It can only be used once the donor lacks mental capacity to make the specific decision [7].
  • Registration and statutory waiting period: Complete the LPA forms online on GOV.UK, ensure they are signed and witnessed in the strict statutory order (the donor first, then the independent certificate provider confirming capacity, then the attorneys), and submit them for registration to the Office of the Public Guardian at 0300 456 0300 or customerservices@publicguardian.gov.uk [7]. Registration in England and Wales costs £92 per LPA (the statutory fee set from 17 November 2025, subject to periodic Ministry of Justice review, with a 50% remission or full exemption available for qualifying low income or means-tested benefits) and includes a mandatory 4-week statutory notice period before the registered LPA can be issued, so apply promptly [7].
  • Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the person executes a Continuing Power of Attorney (financial) and/or Welfare Power of Attorney certified by a solicitor or medical practitioner and registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland). In Northern Ireland, financial authority is granted through an Enduring Power of Attorney.

steps.title: Record Care Preferences, an Advance Decision (ADRT), and a ReSPECT Plan
steps.html:
• Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT / living will): If your family member wishes to refuse specific medical treatments in defined future circumstances should they lose capacity, they can complete a written ADRT (legally binding in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, and treated as strong evidence of wishes in Scotland as an Advance Directive) [8]. In England and Wales, if an ADRT refuses life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or clinically assisted nutrition and hydration), it must be in writing, explicitly state that it applies even if life is at risk, and be signed by the person and a witness in each other's presence [8]. Take care with sequencing in England and Wales: signing a Health and Welfare LPA after an ADRT overrides the ADRT if the LPA gives attorneys authority over life-sustaining treatment, whereas an ADRT signed after the LPA takes precedence over the attorneys on that treatment [8].
  • Advance Statement and ReSPECT plan: The person can also write a non-binding Advance Statement setting out their general values and preferred place of care [1], and ask their GP or palliative care clinician to complete a ReSPECT emergency care summary plan overseen by the Resuscitation Council UK [9]. The ReSPECT plan records personalized clinical guidance for emergency care and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (including any DNACPR decision) and stays with the patient so paramedics and hospital staff can follow it immediately [9].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Pension Expression-of-Wish Forms, and Practical Documents
steps.html:
• Verify or execute the will: Under the law of England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, a valid will must be made voluntarily while the person has testamentary capacity, and must be signed by the person in the simultaneous physical presence of two independent adult witnesses (neither of whom can be a beneficiary or the spouse/civil partner of a beneficiary), who then sign in the person's presence (Scotland has slightly different witnessing rules under Scottish succession law) [10]. Where a person is seriously ill, instructing a solicitor to draft the will and asking a medical practitioner to witness it or record capacity helps prevent future challenges [10]. You can find a regulated private client solicitor in England and Wales through The Law Society at 020 7320 5650 [11], or ask a local hospice about charity will schemes.
  • Update pension expression-of-wish nominations: Workplace and personal pension lump-sum death benefits and life insurance policies written in trust normally pass outside the will according to nomination or expression-of-wish forms held by the pension scheme administrator. Ask your family member to review and update their nominated beneficiaries directly with each pension provider.
  • Assemble essential documents: Gather birth and marriage or civil partnership certificates, the person's National Insurance number, bank and savings account statements, property deeds or tenancy agreements, utility and council tax accounts, and any written funeral wishes in one accessible folder [1][10].

title: What to Do When a German Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a German Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Italy and Germany: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a German citizen dies in Italy, medical certification, civil registration, and the issuance of the mortuary passport (Passaporto Mortuario) must first be completed in the Italian municipality (Comune) where the death occurred before repatriation to Germany or local burial can take place [1][2].

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certification of Death and Necroscopic Certificate in Italy (Hospital or Non-Hospital)
steps.html:
The first mandatory step under the Italian Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria, Presidential Decree D.P.R. 285/1990) depends on where the death occurred [2][3]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The hospital medical management (direzione sanitaria) directly handles the clinical pronouncement of death, completes the ISTAT cause-of-death statistical form (scheda ISTAT), performs the internal necroscopic examination, transfers the body to the hospital mortuary, and sends the notice of death to the municipal Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) [2][3]. Provide the deceased person's German passport or national identity card (Personalausweis) immediately so that personal details are recorded accurately [1].
  • Death outside a hospital (private residence, hotel, holiday accommodation, or public place): Call the single European emergency number 112 (or 118 for medical emergencies) or a physician immediately so that a doctor can issue the initial pronouncement of death (constatazione di decesso) and the cause-of-death report [2]. Next, the public health medical examiner (medico necroscopo) of the local health authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) must conduct the necroscopic examination between 15 and 30 hours after death to issue the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico), which is required before the coffin can be closed and burial or transport authorised [2][3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or public-place death involving the judicial authorities: If the death occurred without medical attendance, suddenly, in an accident, or under suspicious circumstances, law enforcement intervenes and the body is placed under the authority of the Public Prosecutor's Office (Procura della Repubblica) [1][2]. In such cases, removal, cremation, or repatriation can proceed only after the duty prosecutor issues formal judicial clearance (nulla osta) for burial or transport [1][2].

steps.title: Check Travel Insurance Coverage and Appoint a Funeral Director in Italy and Germany
steps.html:
Before signing private contracts, check whether your family member held travel health insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung), credit card coverage, or automobile club / assistance membership covering repatriation of remains (Rücktransport im Todesfall) [1]. When coverage is active, the insurer's emergency assistance centre appoints the international funeral provider directly and covers eligible policy costs [1].

If no insurance policy applies, the family appoints an authorised funeral director in Italy (impresa funebre) to handle municipal and public health formalities and coordinate with a receiving funeral director (Bestatter) in the destination municipality in Germany [1]:

  • Finding a funeral director in Italy: You can consult the guidance lists of funeral directors published by the German diplomatic missions in Italy - referring for Central and Southern Italy to the Ambasciata di Germania a Roma (German Embassy in Rome, phone: +39 06 492131) and for Northern Italy to the Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano (German Consulate General in Milan, phone: +39 02 62311010) [1] - or contact the Italian national funeral federation, Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (FENIOF, phone: +39 051 6650285) [4].
  • Finding a receiving funeral director in Germany: To receive the coffin or urn and arrange the funeral ceremony in Germany, you can locate a qualified funeral director through the directory of the Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter (Federal Association of German Undertakers, phone: +49 211 1600810; emergency number: +49 211 1600886) [5]. Clarvia provides professional directory references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific funeral operators.

steps.title: Register the Death with the Italian Civil Status Office Within 24 Hours and Request the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
The declaration of death (dichiarazione di morte) must be filed within 24 hours of the death at the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian municipality (Comune) where the death occurred (for example, at the civil registry offices of Roma Capitale or the Comune di Milano) [2][3]. In standard practice, the Italian funeral director authorised by the family (or the hospital medical management) submits the death declaration together with the necroscopic certificate and the ISTAT form [2][3].

Through the funeral director or directly at the municipal Civil Status Office, request:

  • Full copies or certificates of the Italian death record (copie integrali / certificati dell'atto di morte): required for municipal transport, cremation, or burial permits in Italy [2][3].
  • Multilingual death certificate extract (estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue - Form C / Modello C under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976): This standardised international document is accepted directly by civil registry offices (Standesamt), courts, and pension authorities in Germany without an Apostille or certified translation [1][2].

steps.title: Obtain the Municipal Mortuary Passport and Coordinate Repatriation to Germany or Local Burial
steps.html:
Because both Italy and Germany are parties to the Berlin International Convention of 10 February 1937 on the Transport of Corpses, cross-border transfer follows a unified procedure handled by the funeral director [1][2][3]:

  • Repatriation of the coffin to Germany (Passaporto Mortuario / Leichenpass): The Italian funeral director applies for the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) directly from the Civil Status Office of the Italian municipality of death (such as the Comune di Milano or Roma Capitale), which issues it in multilingual format without requiring separate German consular clearance [1][2][3]. For international coffin transport, the competent local health authority (ASL) certifies the preservative anti-putrefactive treatment and the double coffin (hermetically soldered inner zinc liner and outer wooden casket) in accordance with D.P.R. 285/1990 and the Berlin Convention [2][3].
  • Cremation in Italy and transport of ashes or local burial: If cremation in Italy is chosen, the Civil Status Officer (Ufficiale di Stato Civile) issues the cremation permit after verifying the deceased person's expressed wishes or a declaration by the surviving spouse or closest next of kin (and after judicial nulla osta from the Public Prosecutor if the death was under investigation) [2][3]. The sealed cinerary urn travels with the municipal foreign transport permit and the cremation certificate for placement in a German cemetery (note that compulsory cemetery interment, Friedhofszwang, applies across Germany under the burial laws, Bestattungsgesetz, of the relevant Bundesland) [1][5].
  • Role of the German consular missions: The Ambasciata di Germania a Roma and the Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano provide procedural guidance to families and assist if relatives in Germany need to authenticate authorisations, but they do not pay for repatriation or funeral expenses [1].

steps.title: Complete Administrative Steps in Germany with the Standesamt, Deutsche Rentenversicherung, and Nachlassgericht
steps.html:
Once you have the multilingual death certificate extract (Form C / Modello C), family members or beneficiaries in Germany can complete domestic administrative notifications:

  • Subsequent registration at the German civil registry (Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls at the Standesamt): Although the Italian multilingual Form C extract is already directly valid across Germany, eligible family members (spouse, registered partner, parents, or children) may apply for optional subsequent registration of the death in the German death register (Sterberegister) at the Standesamt of the deceased person's last German residence in order to obtain German death certificates (deutsche Sterbeurkunden) [1][6].
  • Pensions and survivor benefits (Deutsche Rentenversicherung): Notify the Renten Service of Deutsche Post and the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (toll-free within Germany: 0800 1000 4800; from abroad: +49 800 1000 4800) promptly, enclosing the multilingual death extract [6]. Depending on their relationship to the deceased, a surviving spouse or registered partner can apply for a survivor's pension (Witwenrente or Witwerrente) and the three-month bereavement pension payment (Sterbevierteljahr, under which the deceased's full pension rate is paid for the three calendar months following the month of death), while eligible children may claim an orphan's pension (Waisenrente) [6].
  • Probate, banks, and insurance (Nachlassgericht): Use the multilingual extract (Form C) to notify the German health insurance fund (Krankenkasse), German banks, and life insurers, and contact the probate court (Nachlassgericht at the Amtsgericht of the deceased's last habitual residence in Germany) if a will must be deposited or a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) is required [1][6].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide specific details for the relevant municipal and regional authorities, in which Italian municipality (Comune) did the death occur (in a hospital or outside a hospital), and in which city or Bundesland in Germany did your family member reside?
caseDependentItems: Italian municipal (Comune) civil status office and ASL medico necroscopo clearance (or Procura nulla osta if sudden/outside hospital)
Passaporto Mortuario under the 1937 Berlin Convention for road or air transport between Italy and Germany
Competent German Embassy or Consulate General in Italy (Rome, Milan) and receiving German Bundesland burial laws (Bestattungsgesetz)
German Standesamt registration (Nachbeurkundung), Deutsche Rentenversicherung survivor pension (Witwen-/Waisenrente), and Erbschein rules

contacts.note: Diplomatic mission and consular section of the Federal Republic of Germany in Rome providing assistance following the death of German citizens in Central, Southern, and Insular Italy.

contacts.note: Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in Milan responsible for consular assistance following the death of German citizens in Northern Italy.

contacts.note: Italian national funeral industry federation (FENIOF) for locating authorised funeral directors in Italy for domestic and international funeral transport.

contacts.note: Federal Association of German Undertakers providing a public directory to locate a receiving funeral director (Bestatter) in Germany.

contacts.note: German statutory pension insurance authority for reporting the death of an insured person or pensioner and applying for survivor pensions (Hinterbliebenenrente) and the three-month transition payment (Sterbevierteljahr).

it.title: Cosa fare quando un cittadino tedesco muore in Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Passaggi ufficiali per la constatazione di decesso e il certificato necroscopico in Italia (in ospedale o fuori), registrazione allo Stato Civile (Modello C plurilingue), Passaporto Mortuario, assistenza consolare tedesca e pratiche Standesamt e pensionistiche in Germania.
it.introHtml: Esprimiamo le nostre più sincere condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona di cittadinanza tedesca decede in Italia, gli accertamenti sanitari, la registrazione dello stato civile e il rilascio del passaporto mortuario devono essere completati nel Comune italiano del decesso prima di procedere al rimpatrio verso la Germania o alla sepoltura locale [1][2].

steps.title: Ottenere la constatazione di decesso e il certificato necroscopico in ospedale o fuori dall'ospedale
steps.html:
Il primo passaggio obbligatorio ai sensi del Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria italiano (D.P.R. 285/1990) varia in base al luogo in cui si è verificato il decesso [2][3]:

  • Decesso in ospedale o struttura sanitaria: La direzione sanitaria ospedaliera provvede direttamente alla constatazione clinica della morte, alla compilazione della scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte e all'accertamento necroscopico interno, trasferendo la salma nella camera mortuaria dell'ospedale e trasmettendo l'avviso di morte all'Ufficio di Stato Civile [2][3]. È fondamentale consegnare subito il passaporto o la carta d'identità tedesca (Personalausweis) della persona deceduta affinché i dati anagrafici siano riportati senza errori [1].
  • Decesso fuori dall'ospedale (abitazione privata, albergo, struttura ricettiva o luogo pubblico): Occorre chiamare immediatamente il numero unico di emergenza 112 (o il 118) o un medico affinché rediga il certificato di constatazione di decesso e la denuncia della causa di morte [2]. Successivamente deve intervenire il medico necroscopo della Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) competente per territorio, che effettua la visita necroscopica tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso per rilasciare il certificato necroscopico indispensabile alla chiusura del feretro e alla sepoltura o al trasporto [2][3].
  • Decesso improvviso, accidentale o in luogo pubblico con intervento dell'Autorità Giudiziaria: Se la morte avviene senza assistenza medica, in circostanze improvvise, per incidente o con sospetto di reato, intervengono le forze dell'ordine e la salma viene posta a disposizione della Procura della Repubblica [1][2]. In tal caso, il trasferimento, la cremazione o il rimpatrio possono avvenire solo dopo che il magistrato di turno ha rilasciato il formale nulla osta al seppellimento o al trasporto [1][2].

steps.title: Verificare l'assicurazione di viaggio e incaricare un'impresa funebre in Italia e in Germania
steps.html:
Prima di sottoscrivere contratti autonomi, verificate se il vostro familiare disponeva di un'assicurazione sanitaria di viaggio (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung), di una copertura tramite carta di credito o di un'associazione automobilistica o di assistenza che includa il rimpatrio della salma (Rücktransport im Todesfall) [1]. Quando la copertura è attiva, la centrale operativa dell'assicurazione incarica direttamente l'agenzia funebre internazionale e sostiene i costi previsti dalla polizza [1].

In assenza di copertura assicurativa, la famiglia conferisce mandato a un'impresa funebre autorizzata in Italia affinché gestisca le pratiche comunali e sanitarie e si coordini con un'impresa funebre (Bestatter) nel Comune di destinazione in Germania [1]:

  • Individuazione dell'impresa funebre in Italia: Potete consultare gli elenchi di orientamento delle imprese funebri pubblicati dalle rappresentanze tedesche in Italia, facendo riferimento per il Centro-Sud all'Ambasciata di Germania a Roma (telefono: +39 06 492131) e per il Nord Italia al Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano (telefono: +39 02 62311010) [1], oppure rivolgervi alla Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (telefono: +39 051 6650285) [4].
  • Individuazione dell'impresa funebre ricevente in Germania: Per l'accoglienza del feretro o dell'urna e la cerimonia in Germania, potete individuare un operatore qualificato tramite il registro del Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter (telefono: +49 211 1600810; numero per emergenze: +49 211 1600886) [5]. Clarvia fornisce i riferimenti degli elenchi professionali esclusivamente a scopo orientativo e non raccomanda, non approva e non classifica specifici operatori funebri.

steps.title: Dichiarare il decesso allo Stato Civile entro 24 ore e richiedere l'estratto plurilingue (Modello C)
steps.html:
La dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano in cui è avvenuta la morte (ad esempio presso gli uffici di Stato Civile di Roma Capitale o del Comune di Milano) [2][3]. Nella prassi ordinaria, l'impresa funebre italiana incaricata dalla famiglia (o la direzione sanitaria ospedaliera) presenta la denuncia di morte allegando il certificato del medico necroscopico e la scheda ISTAT [2][3].

Richiedete tramite l'impresa funebre o direttamente allo Stato Civile comunale:

  • Copie integrali o certificati dell'atto di morte italiano: necessari per il rilascio delle autorizzazioni al trasporto e alla cremazione o inumazione [2][3].
  • Estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue (Modello C - Convenzione di Vienna dell'8 settembre 1976): Questo documento internazionale standardizzato è accettato direttamente dagli uffici di stato civile (Standesamt), dai tribunali e dagli enti previdenziali in Germania senza necessità di apostille né di traduzione giurata [1][2].

steps.title: Ottenere il Passaporto Mortuario comunale e coordinare il rimpatrio in Germania o la sepoltura locale
steps.html:
Poiché sia l'Italia sia la Germania aderiscono alla Convenzione internazionale di Berlino del 10 febbraio 1937 sul trasporto dei cadaveri, il trasferimento oltreconfine segue una procedura unificata gestita dall'impresa funebre [1][2][3]:

  • Rimpatrio della salma in Germania (Passaporto Mortuario / Leichenpass): L'impresa funebre italiana richiede il Passaporto Mortuario direttamente all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano del decesso (ad esempio il Comune di Milano o Roma Capitale), che lo rilascia in formato plurilingue senza bisogno di un ulteriore nulla osta consolare tedesco [1][2][3]. Per il trasporto internazionale del feretro, la ASL competente certifica il trattamento antiputrefattivo/conservativo e la doppia cassa (interna in zinco saldata ermeticamente ed esterna in legno) secondo le prescrizioni del D.P.R. 285/1990 e della Convenzione di Berlino [2][3].
  • Cremazione in Italia e trasporto delle ceneri o sepoltura locale: Se si sceglie la cremazione in Italia, l'Ufficiale di Stato Civile rilascia l'autorizzazione previa verifica della volontà espressa in vita dalla persona deceduta o mediante dichiarazione del coniuge o dei parenti più prossimi aventi diritto (e previo nulla osta della Procura se il decesso era sottoposto a indagine giudiziaria) [2][3]. L'urna cineraria sigillata viene accompagnata dall'autorizzazione comunale al trasporto all'estero e dal verbale di cremazione per l'ingresso nel cimitero tedesco (in Germania vige l'obbligo cimiteriale, Friedhofszwang, regolato dalle leggi funerarie del singolo Bundesland) [1][5].
  • Ruolo consolare tedesco: L'Ambasciata di Germania a Roma e il Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano forniscono assistenza informativa ai familiari e intervengono qualora i parenti in Germania abbiano necessità di autenticare deleghe, ma non sostengono le spese di rimpatrio o sepoltura [1].

steps.title: Completare gli adempimenti in Germania presso Standesamt, Deutsche Rentenversicherung e Nachlassgericht
steps.html:
Una volta ottenuto l'estratto di morte plurilingue (Modello C), i familiari o gli aventi diritto in Germania procedono con le comunicazioni amministrative nazionali:

  • Trascrizione presso lo Standesamt (Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls): Sebbene l'estratto plurilingue italiano su Modello C sia già valido in Germania, i familiari (coniuge, partner registrato, genitori o figli) possono richiedere la trascrizione facoltativa del decesso nel registro di stato civile tedesco (Sterberegister) presso lo Standesamt dell'ultimo domicilio tedesco della persona deceduta per ottenere certificati di morte tedeschi (deutsche Sterbeurkunden) [1][6].
  • Pensione e prestazioni ai superstiti (Deutsche Rentenversicherung): Comunicate tempestivamente il decesso al Renten Service di Deutsche Post e alla Deutsche Rentenversicherung (telefono gratuito dalla Germania: 0800 1000 4800; dall'estero: +49 800 1000 4800) allegando l'estratto di morte plurilingue [6]. In base al rapporto di parentela con la persona deceduta, il coniuge o partner registrato superstite può presentare domanda per la pensione di reversibilità (Witwenrente o Witwerrente) e per il trimestre di lutto (Sterbevierteljahr, che prevede per i primi tre mesi successivi al mese del decesso l'erogazione dell'importo pieno della pensione del defunto), mentre i figli aventi diritto possono richiedere la pensione per orfani (Waisenrente) [6].
  • Successione, banche e assicurazioni (Nachlassgericht): Utilizzate l'estratto plurilingue (Modello C) per notificare il decesso alla cassa malati (Krankenkasse), alle banche tedesche e alle assicurazioni sulla vita, e rivolgetevi al tribunale delle successioni (Nachlassgericht presso l'Amtsgericht dell'ultima residenza abituale in Germania) qualora sia necessario depositare un testamento o richiedere il certificato di eredità (Erbschein) [1][6].

title: What to Do When a Brazilian Citizen Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Brazilian Citizen Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Portugal and Brazil: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a Brazilian citizen dies in Portugal, electronic medical certification, Portuguese civil registration, and Brazilian consular registration follow a strict sequence before the body or ashes can be repatriated to Brazil or buried locally in Portugal [1][3].

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death via SICO (in a Hospital or Outside a Hospital)
steps.html:
In Portugal, medical verification of death is recorded electronically in the Death Certificate Information System (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito - SICO), managed by the Shared Services of the Ministry of Health (SPMS) and the Directorate-General of Health (Direção-Geral da Saúde - DGS), which transmits the record directly to the civil registry [3][4]. The initial procedure depends on the place and circumstances of death:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending hospital physician verifies the death, issues the Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Óbito) directly in the SICO platform, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary [3][4]. Provide the deceased person's Brazilian passport (along with their Portuguese Residence Permit, Título de Residência, or Cartão de Cidadão, if held) so that personal and parentage details are recorded without discrepancies [1][4].
  • Death outside a hospital (private residence, hotel, holiday accommodation, or public place): Call the European emergency number 112 immediately (or the local police authority, PSP or GNR) [1][4]. If the death resulted from a known natural cause and an attending physician or local health officer (delegado de saúde) can certify the cause of death, that physician issues the Medical Certificate of Death in SICO [3][4].
  • Sudden, violent, or unexplained death (Public Prosecutor and INMLCF intervention): If the death occurred without prior medical attendance, suddenly, or under suspicious circumstances, the police report the matter to the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público), which orders the removal of the body to the medico-legal office of the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses - INMLCF) for an autopsy or forensic examination [3][4]. Only after release by the Ministério Público and registration in SICO by the forensic pathologist can the funeral agency take charge of the body [3][4].

steps.title: Check Assistance Insurance, Appoint a Funeral Agency, and Grant Power of Attorney if the Family Is in Brazil
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international health insurance, credit card assistance coverage, or life insurance covering funeral repatriation [1]. When an active policy exists, the insurer's assistance centre appoints the international funeral provider directly and covers eligible expenses [1]. Note that the Brazilian State and the Brazilian Consulates General do not have public funds to pay for funerals, cremations, or the repatriation of human remains or ashes [1].

If no insurance coverage applies, the family must appoint a licensed funeral agency in Portugal (registered with the Directorate-General for Economic Activities, Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) to handle civil registration, preparation, and international transport or local burial [1][2]:

  • Selecting a funeral agency in Portugal: You can consult the consular guidance published by the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa (Consulate General of Brazil in Lisbon, emergency consular duty phone: +351 962 520 581) [1] or contact the Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, National Association of Funeral Enterprises, phone: +351 218 687 978) to identify licensed funeral agencies [2]. Clarvia provides public and trade association references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific funeral providers.
  • Authorising procedures when the family is in Brazil: If no family member can travel to Portugal, the closest next of kin in Brazil can execute a power of attorney (procuração, either a public deed at a Brazilian notary office, cartório de notas, or a private instrument with notarised signature, apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention) authorising the contracted Portuguese funeral agency or a local representative in Portugal to claim the body, declare the death, apply for consular registration, and authorise cremation or international repatriation [1].

steps.title: Declare the Death at the Civil Registry Office Within 48 Hours
steps.html:
A death occurring in Portugal must be declared within the statutory 48-hour deadline following the death or following forensic release by the INMLCF [4]:

  • Filing the declaration at the Conservatória do Registo Civil: In practice, the appointed funeral agency files the declaration at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil, overseen by the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado - IRN, Registry Helpline: +351 211 950 500) using the electronic Medical Certificate of Death recorded in SICO and the deceased person's identification documents [3][4].
  • Obtaining the Portuguese death record and medical cause-of-death certificate: The Conservatória do Registo Civil registers the death entry (Assento de Óbito) free of charge and issues the Portuguese death certificate (Certidão de Óbito), which is required for the burial, cremation, or international transit permit (alvará de trasladação) [4]. For Brazilian consular registration and repatriation to Brazil, also ask the funeral agency to obtain the supplementary medical declaration expressly stating the medical cause of death (causa mortis, extracted from SICO/DGS), because the standard Portuguese civil death certificate does not list the cause of death and Brazilian authorities require it [1][5].

steps.title: Complete Brazilian Consular Death Registration and Arrange Repatriation to Brazil or Local Cremation
steps.html:
For the death to have legal effect in Brazil and to allow the entry of human remains or ashes into Brazilian territory, the death must be registered with the Brazilian consular mission holding jurisdiction over the place of death in Portugal (the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa for Lisbon, Central Portugal, and the Islands; the Consulate General of Brazil in Porto for Northern and parts of Central Portugal; or the Consulate General of Brazil in Faro for the Algarve and Alentejo) [1]:

  • Issuance of the Brazilian Consular Death Certificate (Certidão Consular de Óbito): The application is submitted via the electronic e-Consular platform by the declaring family member or the duly authorised funeral agency representative, presenting the Portuguese Assento de Óbito, the medical document stating the causa mortis, the deceased's Brazilian passport or identity card, and their Brazilian birth or marriage certificate [1].
  • International repatriation of the body to Brazil: Repatriation of a body requires embalming (tanatopraxia / formalin preservation), placement in an impermeable coffin with a hermetically sealed inner zinc liner, an international mortuary transit permit (alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário) issued in Portugal, a sanitary certificate confirming the absence of contagious disease, and the Certidão Consular de Óbito [1][5]. At the arrival airport in Brazil, health clearance follows the regulations of the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA, Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency, phone in Brazil: 0800 642 9782), and a receiving Brazilian funeral home must clear the coffin at the air cargo terminal [5].
  • Cremation in Portugal and transporting ashes: If the family chooses cremation in Portugal (subject to authorisation by the entitled next of kin and medical/judicial clearance), the ashes are placed in a sealed urn accompanied by the cremation certificate and the Certidão Consular de Óbito, and may be transported by air to Brazil in accordance with airline rules and the requirements of the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária [1][5].

steps.title: Transcribe the Death Record in Brazil and Notify Segurança Social and INSS
steps.html:
Once consular registration and the funeral or repatriation are complete, civil registry and social security records should be updated in both countries:

  • Transcription of the Consular Death Certificate in Brazil: The Certidão Consular de Óbito issued by the Consulate General in Portugal must be transcribed (trasladada) at the 1st Civil Registry Office (Cartório do 1.º Ofício de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais) of the deceased's last domicile in Brazil (or at the Cartório do 1.º Ofício of the Federal District if the deceased had no prior domicile in Brazil) so that it produces full civil, banking, and probate (inventário) effects in Brazil [1].
  • Portuguese death benefits (Segurança Social): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension in Portugal, report the death to the Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, phone: +351 210 545 400 or 300 502 502) to check entitlement to the death grant (subsídio por morte), funeral expense reimbursement, and survivor's pension (pensão de sobrevivência) for an eligible spouse, civil partner (unido de facto), or descendants [6].
  • Brazilian survivor's pension (INSS) and the Brazil-Portugal Social Security Agreement: If the deceased was insured or retired under the Brazilian social security system, report the death to the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, National Institute of Social Security, phone in Brazil: 135; Meu INSS portal) to apply for the survivor's pension (pensão por morte) for eligible dependants based on family relationship (spouse, domestic partner, or minor/disabled children) [7]. Under the Bilateral Social Security Agreement between Brazil and Portugal (Acordo Previdenciário Brasil-Portugal), contribution periods completed in both countries can be totalised to establish entitlement to survivor benefits [6][7].

pt.title: O que fazer quando um cidadão brasileiro falece em Portugal: guia oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Passos oficiais após o óbito de um cidadão brasileiro em Portugal: certificado médico de óbito (SICO), agência funerária e seguro, Conservatória do Registo Civil, registo consular no Consulado-Geral do Brasil (Lisboa, Porto ou Faro), traslado para o Brasil (ANVISA) ou sepultamento local, e Segurança Social / INSS.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos os nossos mais sinceros sentimentos pelo falecimento do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa de nacionalidade brasileira falece em Portugal, a certificação médica eletrónica, o registo civil português e o registo consular brasileiro seguem uma sequência específica antes do traslado do corpo ou das cinzas para o Brasil ou do funeral local [1][3].

steps.title: Obter o Certificado Médico de Óbito através do SICO (no hospital ou fora do hospital)
steps.html:
Em Portugal, a verificação médica do óbito é registada eletronicamente no Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito (SICO), gerido pelos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde e pela Direção-Geral da Saúde, que envia os dados diretamente para o registo civil [3][4]. O procedimento inicial depende do local e das circunstâncias do falecimento:

  • Óbito em hospital ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente da unidade hospitalar verifica o óbito, emite o Certificado Médico de Óbito diretamente na plataforma SICO e transfere o corpo para a casa mortuária do hospital [3][4]. Entregue o passaporte brasileiro (e o Título de Residência ou Cartão de Cidadão, caso a pessoa falecida o possuísse) para que a identificação e a filiação fiquem registadas sem divergências [1][4].
  • Óbito fora do hospital (domicílio, hotel, alojamento ou via pública): Deve contactar-se de imediato o número europeu de emergência 112 (ou a autoridade policial local, PSP ou GNR) [1][4]. Se a morte tiver causa natural conhecida e houver médico assistente ou delegado de saúde (autoridade de saúde) que possa atestar a causa da morte, este emite o Certificado Médico de Óbito no SICO [3][4].
  • Morte súbita, violenta ou de causa desconhecida (intervenção do Ministério Público e INMLCF): Se o óbito ocorrer sem assistência médica prévia, de forma súbita ou suspeita, a autoridade policial comunica o facto ao Ministério Público, que determina a remoção do corpo para o gabinete médico-legal do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) para autópsia ou exame pericial [3][4]. Só após a liberação pelo Ministério Público e o registo no SICO pelo médico legista é que a agência funerária pode assumir o serviço [3][4].

steps.title: Verificar seguros de assistência, contratar uma agência funerária e outorgar procuração se a família estiver no Brasil
steps.html:
Antes de contratar diretamente o serviço funerário, verifique se o seu familiar possuía seguro de viagem, seguro de saúde internacional, plano de assistência associado a cartão de crédito ou seguro de vida com cobertura de repatriação funerária [1]. Quando há apólice ativa, a seguradora aciona diretamente a funerária internacional e assume as despesas cobertas [1]. Note que o Estado brasileiro e os Consulados-Gerais não dispõem de verba para custear funerais, cremações ou traslado de restos mortais ou cinzas [1].

Caso não exista seguro aplicável, a família deve contratar uma agência funerária habilitada em Portugal (registada junto à Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) para tratar do registo civil, preparação e transporte internacional ou funeral local [1][2]:

  • Escolha da agência funerária em Portugal: Pode consultar as informações de orientação consular do Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa (plantão consular para emergências: +351 962 520 581) [1] ou contactar a Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (telefone: +351 218 687 978) para identificar agências funerárias habilitadas [2]. A Clarvia fornece referências associativas e públicas apenas para orientação e não recomenda, não endossa nem classifica prestadores funerários específicos.
  • Como autorizar os procedimentos quando a família está no Brasil: Se nenhum familiar puder deslocar-se a Portugal, o familiar mais próximo no Brasil pode outorgar uma procuração (pública em cartório de notas no Brasil ou particular com firma reconhecida, apostilada nos termos da Convenção da Apostila da Haia) conferindo poderes à agência funerária portuguesa contratada ou a um representante em Portugal para retirar o corpo, declarar o óbito, requerer o registo consular e autorizar a cremação ou o traslado internacional [1].

steps.title: Declarar o óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil no prazo de 48 horas
steps.html:
O óbito ocorrido em território português tem de ser declarado no prazo legal de 48 horas após o falecimento ou após a liberação médico-legal pelo INMLCF [4]. Na prática, a agência funerária contratada realiza a declaração em qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil (supervisionada pelo Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado - Linha Registos: +351 211 950 500) com base no Certificado Médico de Óbito eletrónico já inserido no SICO e nos documentos de identificação da pessoa falecida [3][4].

A Conservatória do Registo Civil lavra gratuitamente o Assento de Óbito e emite a Certidão de Óbito portuguesa, necessária para o alvará de sepultamento, cremação ou trasladação internacional [4]. Para fins consulares e de traslado para o Brasil, solicite também à agência funerária a declaração médica complementar com a indicação expressa da causa mortis (extraída do SICO/DGS), uma vez que o assento civil português padrão não especifica a causa médica da morte e as autoridades brasileiras a exigem [1][5].

steps.title: Efetuar o Registo Consular de Óbito e organizar o traslado para o Brasil ou a cremação local
steps.html:
Para que o falecimento produza efeitos jurídicos no Brasil e permita a entrada dos restos mortais ou cinzas em território brasileiro, o óbito deve ser registado na repartição consular brasileira com jurisdição sobre o local do falecimento em Portugal (o Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa para Lisboa, Centro e Ilhas; o Consulado-Geral do Brasil no Porto para o Norte e parte do Centro; ou o Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Faro para o Algarve e Alentejo) [1]:

  • Emissão da Certidão Consular de Óbito: O pedido é submetido na plataforma eletrónica e-Consular pelo familiar declarante ou pelo representante da agência funerária devidamente autorizado, apresentando o Assento de Óbito português, o documento médico com a causa mortis, o passaporte ou documento de identidade brasileiro e a certidão de nascimento ou casamento da pessoa falecida [1].
  • Traslado internacional de corpo para o Brasil: Exige o embalsamamento (tanatopraxia/formolização), acondicionamento em urna funerária impermeável com revestimento interno de zinco hermeticamente fechado, alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário emitido em Portugal, atestado sanitário de inexistência de doença infectocontagiosa e a Certidão Consular de Óbito [1][5]. No aeroporto de chegada no Brasil, a liberação sanitária segue as normas da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (telefone no Brasil: 0800 642 9782), devendo uma funerária receptora brasileira receber a urna no terminal de cargas [5].
  • Cremação em Portugal e transporte de cinzas: Caso a família opte pela cremação em Portugal (mediante autorização do familiar legitimado e confirmação médica/judicial), as cinzas são entregues numa urna lacrada acompanhada do certificado de cremação e da Certidão Consular de Óbito, podendo ser transportadas por via aérea para o Brasil conforme as regras da companhia aérea e da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária [1][5].

steps.title: Transcrever o óbito em Cartório no Brasil e comunicar à Segurança Social e ao INSS
steps.html:
Concluídos o registo consular e o funeral ou traslado, devem ser regularizados os registos civis e previdenciários nos dois países:

  • Transcrição da Certidão Consular de Óbito no Brasil: A Certidão Consular de Óbito emitida pelo Consulado-Geral em Portugal deve ser trasladada (transcrita) no Cartório do 1.º Ofício de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais do último domicílio da pessoa falecida no Brasil (ou no Cartório do 1.º Ofício do Distrito Federal, se não houver domicílio anterior no Brasil) para que passe a produzir plenos efeitos civis, bancários e sucessórios (inventário) no Brasil [1].
  • Prestações por morte em Portugal e no Brasil (Acordo Previdenciário Brasil-Portugal):
    • Em Portugal: Se a pessoa falecida contribuía ou era pensionista em Portugal, comunique o óbito à Segurança Social (telefone: +351 210 545 400 ou 300 502 502) para verificar o direito ao subsídio por morte, ao reembolso de despesas de funeral e à pensão de sobrevivência para o cônjuge, unido de facto ou descendentes elegíveis [6].
    • No Brasil: Se a pessoa falecida era segurada ou aposentada pelo regime brasileiro, comunique o óbito ao Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (telefone no Brasil: 135; portal Meu INSS) para requerer a pensão por morte para os dependentes habilitados conforme o vínculo familiar (cônjuge, companheiro ou filhos menores ou inválidos) [7]. Ao abrigo do Acordo de Segurança Social entre o Brasil e Portugal, os períodos de contribuição cumpridos em ambos os países podem ser totalizados para abertura do direito às prestações de sobrevivência [6][7].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos detalhar a jurisdição consular e os procedimentos específicos aplicáveis, em qual município de Portugal ocorreu o falecimento (num hospital ou fora do hospital) e os familiares encontram-se atualmente em Portugal ou no Brasil?

title: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between France and United Kingdom: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a British citizen dies in France, medical verification and civil registration take place first in the French municipality (commune) where the death occurred, while a licensed funeral director coordinates prefectural, consular, and UK authorities for repatriation or local funeral arrangements.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Verification of Death and French Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
The mandatory first step is to have a physician verify the death and issue the French medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, on paper form Cerfa or electronically via the CertDc application), which is required to register the death at the town hall (mairie) and authorise any funeral transport or procedure [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or care home (EHPAD): The attending hospital or facility doctor issues the certificat médical de décès directly [1][2]. The deceased person's body can remain in the facility's mortuary suite (chambre mortuaire) pending funeral arrangements.
  • Death outside a healthcare facility (private home, hotel, holiday home, or public place): Call the French emergency medical service (SAMU) on 15 (or the European emergency number 112) immediately so that a doctor attends to certify the death and complete the certificate [1]. Once the medical certificate is signed and provided there is no judicial hold, a licensed funeral operator can transfer the body to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) within 48 hours of death [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or suspicious death (obstacle médico-légal): If the cause of death is unknown, violent, or suspicious, the doctor ticks the medico-legal hold box (obstacle médico-légal) on the medical certificate [1][3]. Law enforcement (National Police or Gendarmerie) and the Public Prosecutor (procureur de la République) then take charge of the investigation (which may include transfer to a forensic institute for an autopsy), and burial, cremation, or repatriation cannot proceed until the prosecutor issues formal judicial burial/removal clearance (permis d'inhumer) [1][3].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage and Appoint a Funeral Director in France and the UK
steps.html:
Do not attempt to handle prefectural permits or international air freight formalities without a licensed funeral operator. Before signing an estimate (devis) with a funeral company, verify any existing assistance coverage [3]:

  • Travel insurance, medical assistance, or bank card coverage: If your family member was visiting France temporarily or held repatriation insurance, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance centre immediately before making any financial commitment [3]. The insurer typically appoints the funeral directors in France and the UK directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral operator: If no insurance applies, the family appoints a licensed funeral company in France (entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée) or a UK funeral director working with a French international partner [1][3]. In France, you can locate a licensed professional through the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] or the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. In the United Kingdom, the official directory of the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD, phone +44 121 711 1343, email info@nafd.org.uk) allows you to appoint a UK funeral director to receive the coffin or urn [6].
  • Role of British consular assistance: Contact the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and the consular services of the British Embassy Paris (24/7 consular assistance on +33 1 44 51 31 00 from within France or +44 20 7008 5000 from the UK) [3]. The British consular network provides a list of English-speaking funeral directors in France, guides the family on local procedures, and cancels the British passport, though it cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [3].

steps.title: Register the Death at the French Town Hall Within 24 Hours and Obtain the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
Under the official rules published on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical certification (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the civil status office (service de l'état civil) of the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred [1][2]:

  • Who files the declaration: If the death occurred in a hospital, the facility may transmit the declaration directly to the mairie; in practice, families usually authorise their appointed French funeral operator to complete this step [1][2]. You must provide the certificat médical de décès together with the deceased person's British passport (and, if available, their birth or marriage certificate) [1][2].
  • Documents to request from the mairie and the doctor: Request several full certified copies of the French death record (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès) as well as multilingual death certificate extracts (extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues - Form C / Formule C under the 1976 Vienna Convention) [1][3]. Because a French civil death record never states the medical cause of death, also ask the hospital doctor or the physician who certified the death for a separate medical certificate (attestation médicale) stating the cause of death, which UK authorities require for repatriation [3].

steps.title: Arrange a Local Funeral in France or Repatriation to the United Kingdom
steps.html:
The person authorised to arrange the funeral (personne ayant qualité pour pourvoir aux funérailles) chooses between a local funeral in France and repatriation to the United Kingdom [1][3]:

  • Option A - Burial or cremation in France: In metropolitan France, burial (inhumation) or cremation (crémation) must take place at least 24 hours and no more than 14 calendar days after death (prefectural extensions may be granted in specific circumstances) [7]. The mayor (maire) of the municipality of death (or cremation) issues the coffin-closing permit (autorisation de fermeture du cercueil) and the burial or cremation permit [7]. If cremation takes place in France followed by transport of the ashes to the UK, the sealed urn travels with the death certificate, the cremation certificate (certificat de crémation), and, where applicable, the prefectural transit permit [3][8].
  • Option B - Repatriating the coffin to the United Kingdom: The French funeral operator applies to the prefecture (préfecture) of the department where the coffin is sealed to obtain the prefectural mortuary transit permit (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) [8]. The body undergoes required preservation treatment (soins de conservation) and is placed in a hermetically sealed coffin (with a sealed metal liner and purifying filter) under official supervision prior to air or cross-Channel transport [8].
  • Arrival formalities in the United Kingdom (England and Wales vs Scotland):
    • In England and Wales: Every body repatriated from abroad falls under the jurisdiction of the local Coroner for the district where the funeral will take place [3]. The UK funeral director submits the French death certificate, the medical cause-of-death certificate, and certified translations to the Coroner to obtain the burial or cremation order (Coroner's Order / Form 104 Out-of-England); if the death was violent, unnatural, or unexplained, the Coroner is legally required to open an inquest [3].
    • In Scotland: There is no coroner system. Instead, the Scottish funeral director submits the foreign death certificate and medical documentation to the Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) of Healthcare Improvement Scotland (phone +44 131 623 4300) to obtain authorisation for burial or cremation in Scotland [9], while sudden or suspicious deaths abroad of Scottish residents may be reported to the Procurator Fiscal at the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (phone +44 300 020 3000) [10].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Administrative Steps in the United Kingdom and France
steps.html:
Once the death certificates have been issued, administrative, pension, and estate procedures are divided between the two countries:

  • In the United Kingdom (pensions, tax, and probate): If the deceased was habitually resident in England, Wales, or Scotland and died during a temporary stay in France, the UK government's Tell Us Once service allows you to notify most UK government departments simultaneously (including HMRC, DWP, DVLA, and HM Passport Office) [11]. Conversely, if your relative lived permanently in France, Tell Us Once is not available: you should contact the International Pension Centre of the Department for Work and Pensions directly (phone +44 191 218 7777) regarding the UK State Pension, as well as HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [11][12]. To administer bank accounts and assets located in the UK, the executor or next of kin applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration in England and Wales) or Confirmation (in Scotland) [11].
  • In France (bank accounts, CPAM, and notarial estate settlement): If your relative lived in France or owned assets there, notify French banks (which freeze individual accounts upon receipt of the death certificate), the local health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM, reachable on 3646 within France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad), and the French tax authorities [1]. Settling an estate that includes real property in France (or where the deceased had their habitual residence in France) requires a French notary (notaire) to draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and property transfer certificate (attestation immobilière), with inheritance tax declarations generally due within 6 months (or 12 months if the death occurred outside metropolitan France); you can consult the official directory of the Notaires de France (phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [13].

closingQuestion: So that we can give you exact local details, in which French département or municipality (commune) did the death occur (and was your relative a resident of France or visiting from the UK), and in which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) will the funeral or estate administration take place?
