fr.title: Que faire lorsqu'un citoyen britannique décède en France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Étapes officielles lors du décès d'un ressortissant britannique en France : certificat médical de décès, déclaration en mairie dans les 24 heures (acte plurilingue Formule C), opérateur funéraire et consulat britannique (FCDO), rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni (laissez-passer préfectoral et coroner) ou obsèques en France, et démarches DWP / succession.
fr.introHtml: Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne de nationalité britannique décède en France, la constatation médicale et la déclaration d'état civil s'effectuent d'abord dans la commune française du décès, tandis qu'un opérateur funéraire habilité coordonne les autorisations préfectorales, consulaires et britanniques pour le rapatriement ou les obsèques.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et établissement du certificat médical de décès en France
steps.html:
La première étape obligatoire consiste à faire constater le décès par un médecin afin d'obtenir le certificat médical de décès (sur support papier Cerfa ou par voie électronique via l'application CertDc), document indispensable pour déclarer le décès en mairie et autoriser toute opération funéraire [1][2].

  • Décès à l'hôpital, en clinique ou en EHPAD : Le médecin du service établit directement le certificat médical de décès [1][2]. Le corps de la personne décédée peut reposer à la chambre mortuaire de l'établissement dans l'attente du transport funéraire.
  • Décès hors établissement de santé (domicile, hôtel, résidence secondaire ou voie publique) : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU au 15 (ou le numéro d'urgence européen 112) afin qu'un médecin se déplace pour constater le décès et rédiger le certificat [1]. Une fois le certificat signé et en l'absence d'opposition judiciaire, un opérateur funéraire peut transférer le corps vers une chambre funéraire dans un délai de 48 heures suivant le décès [1].
  • Cas de décès soudain, accidentel ou suspect (obstacle médico-légal) : Si la cause du décès est inconnue, violente ou suspecte, le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat [1][3]. Les forces de l'ordre (police nationale ou gendarmerie) et le procureur de la République prennent alors en charge le dossier (avec transfert éventuel vers un institut médico-légal pour autopsie), et l'inhumation, la crémation ou le rapatriement ne peuvent avoir lieu qu'après délivrance du permis d'inhumer par le parquet [1][3].

steps.title: Vérification de l'assurance et mandat donné à un opérateur funéraire en France et au Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
Ne tentez pas d'effectuer vous-même les démarches techniques auprès des préfectures ou du fret aérien. Avant de signer un devis avec une entreprise de pompes funèbres, vérifiez les garanties d'assistance existantes [3] :

  • Assurance voyage, assistance médicale ou carte bancaire : Si votre proche séjournait temporairement en France ou disposait d'une assurance rapatriement, contactez immédiatement le plateau d'assistance 24h/24 de l'assureur avant tout engagement financier [3]. L'assureur mandate généralement lui-même les opérateurs funéraires en France et au Royaume-Uni.
  • Mandat à un opérateur funéraire habilité : En l'absence d'assurance, la famille mandate une entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée en France ou un directeur funéraire au Royaume-Uni travaillant avec un correspondant français [1][3]. En France, vous pouvez identifier un professionnel via la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (téléphone +33 1 55 43 30 00, courriel contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] ou la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (téléphone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. Au Royaume-Uni, l'annuaire officiel de la National Association of Funeral Directors (téléphone +44 121 711 1343, courriel info@nafd.org.uk) permet de désigner l'entreprise funéraire chargée de la réception du cercueil ou de l'urne [6].
  • Rôle de l'assistance consulaire britannique : Contactez le Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office et les services consulaires de la British Embassy Paris (assistance consulaire 24h/24 au +33 1 44 51 31 00 depuis la France ou au +44 20 7008 5000 depuis le Royaume-Uni) [3]. Le réseau consulaire britannique fournit une liste d'opérateurs funéraires anglophones en France, oriente la famille sur les procédures locales et procède à l'annulation du passeport britannique, mais il ne prend jamais en charge les frais d'obsèques ou de rapatriement [3].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès en mairie dans les 24 heures et obtention de l'acte plurilingue (Formule C)
steps.html:
Selon les règles officielles présentées sur Service-Public.fr, le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures suivant sa constatation (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès du service de l'état civil de la mairie de la commune où le décès a eu lieu [1][2].

  • Qui effectue la déclaration : Si le décès est survenu à l'hôpital, l'établissement peut transmettre la déclaration directement à la mairie ; dans la pratique, la famille confie le plus souvent cette démarche à l'opérateur funéraire français mandaté [1][2]. Il faut présenter le certificat médical de décès ainsi que le passeport britannique de la personne décédée (et, si possible, son acte de naissance ou de mariage) [1][2].
  • Documents à demander à la mairie et au médecin : Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès français ainsi que des extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues (Formule C issue de la Convention de Vienne de 1976) [1][3]. Comme l'acte de décès français ne mentionne jamais la cause médicale du décès, demandez également au médecin hospitalier ou au médecin ayant constaté le décès une attestation médicale séparée précisant la cause du décès (indispensable pour les autorités britanniques lors d'un rapatriement) [3].

steps.title: Organisation des obsèques en France ou du rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
La personne ayant qualité pour pourvoir aux funérailles choisit entre des obsèques locales en France et le rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni [1][3] :

  • Option A - Inhumation ou crémation en France : En France métropolitaine, l'inhumation ou la crémation doit intervenir au moins 24 heures et au plus 14 jours calendaires après le décès (des dérogations préfectorales pouvant être accordées) [7]. Le maire de la commune du décès (ou du lieu de crémation) délivre l'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil et le permis d'inhumer ou l'autorisation de crémation [7]. En cas de crémation en France suivie du transport des cendres vers le Royaume-Uni, l'urne scellée voyage avec l'acte de décès, le certificat de crémation et, le cas échéant, le laissez-passer préfectoral [3][8].
  • Option B - Rapatriement du cercueil vers le Royaume-Uni : L'opérateur funéraire français accomplit les formalités auprès de la préfecture du département où a lieu la fermeture du cercueil pour obtenir l'arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire [8]. Le corps fait l'objet des soins de conservation requis et est placé dans un cercueil hermétique (enveloppe métallique scellée avec filtre épurateur) sous contrôle officiel avant le transport aérien ou transmanche [8].
  • Formalités à l'arrivée au Royaume-Uni (Angleterre/Pays de Galles vs Écosse) :
    • En Angleterre et au Pays de Galles : Tout corps rapatrié de l'étranger relève du contrôle du Coroner local du lieu des funérailles [3]. Le directeur funéraire britannique transmet au Coroner l'acte de décès français, le certificat médical indiquant la cause du décès et leur traduction afin d'obtenir le certificat autorisant l'inhumation ou la crémation (Coroner's Order / Form 104 Out-of-England) ; si le décès est survenu de manière violente, non naturelle ou inexpliquée, le Coroner a l'obligation légale d'ouvrir une enquête (inquest) [3].
    • En Écosse : Il n'existe pas de Coroner. Le directeur funéraire écossais soumet le certificat de décès étranger et les pièces médicales au Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland (téléphone +44 131 623 4300) pour obtenir l'autorisation d'inhumer ou de crémer en Écosse [9], tandis que les décès soudains ou suspects à l'étranger concernant un résident écossais peuvent relever du Procurator Fiscal au sein du Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (téléphone +44 300 020 3000) [10].

steps.title: Démarches administratives après le décès au Royaume-Uni et en France
steps.html:
Une fois l'acte de décès obtenu, les démarches administratives et successorales se répartissent entre les deux pays :

  • Au Royaume-Uni (pensions, fiscalité et probate) : Si la personne décédée résidait habituellement en Angleterre, au Pays de Galles ou en Écosse et est décédée lors d'un séjour temporaire en France, le service gouvernemental britannique Tell Us Once permet de notifier simultanément la plupart des administrations (HMRC, DWP, DVLA, bureau des passeports) [11]. En revanche, si votre proche résidait de façon permanente en France, Tell Us Once ne s'applique pas : il convient alors de notifier directement l'International Pension Centre du Department for Work and Pensions (téléphone +44 191 218 7777) pour la retraite d'État britannique (UK State Pension) ainsi que HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [11][12]. Pour débloquer les comptes et biens situés au Royaume-Uni, l'exécuteur testamentaire ou les proches demandent le Grant of Probate (en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles) ou la Confirmation (en Écosse) [11].
  • En France (comptes bancaires, CPAM et succession notariale) : Si votre proche résidait en France ou y détenait des biens, informez les banques françaises (qui bloquent les comptes individuels dès réception de l'acte de décès), la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, joignable au 3646 depuis la France ou au +33 1 84 90 36 46 depuis l'étranger) et l'administration fiscale française [1]. Le règlement d'une succession comprenant un bien immobilier en France (ou lorsque la personne décédée avait sa résidence habituelle en France) impose l'intervention d'un notaire français pour établir l'acte de notoriété et l'attestation immobilière dans les 6 mois (ou 12 mois si le décès est hors de France métropolitaine selon le cas) ; vous pouvez consulter l'annuaire officiel des Notaires de France (téléphone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [13].

title: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in the Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in the Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official steps when a U.S. citizen dies in the Philippines: Certificate of Death and Municipal Health Officer / PNP clearance, Local Civil Registrar and PSA registration, Bureau of Quarantine and U.S. Embassy Manila CRDA / Consular Mortuary Certificate, repatriation or local cremation, and SSA / VA survivor claims.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a United States citizen dies in the Philippines, medical certification and civil registration take place first in the Philippine city or municipality of death, while a licensed mortuary coordinates with Philippine health authorities and the U.S. Embassy in Manila (or the U.S. Consular Agency in Cebu) for the Consular Report of Death Abroad and international transport.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death (Municipal Form No. 103) and Health Officer or Police Clearance
steps.html:
Every death in the Philippines must first be documented on the official Certificate of Death (Municipal Form No. 103, prepared in four copies), which records the personal particulars of the deceased and the medical cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: The attending physician completes and signs the medical certification section of Municipal Form No. 103 directly [1]. Once hospital billing and release formalities are completed, a licensed funeral home can transfer the body to its mortuary facility.
  • Death outside a hospital (residence, hotel, or public place): Report the death immediately to local barangay officials and the Philippine National Police (PNP, emergency hotline 911). When a death occurs without medical attendance, the Municipal Health Officer (MHO) or City Health Officer (CHO) of the local government unit (for example, in Manila, Quezon City, or Cebu City) must examine the deceased and certify the cause of death on Municipal Form No. 103 [1][2]. If the death was sudden, accidental, or under unclear circumstances, PNP Scene of the Crime Operatives (SOCO) or the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) conduct a medico-legal investigation before releasing the body [2][3].
  • 48-hour sanitary rule: Under Chapter XXI (Section 91) of Presidential Decree No. 856 (the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines, enforced by the Department of Health and local health officers), an unembalmed body may not remain unburied or undisposed of for more than 48 hours after death unless held in authorized mortuary cold storage or pending a medico-legal investigation [2][4]. Families planning international repatriation or a viewing should therefore instruct a licensed mortuary promptly.

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Philippine and U.S. Funeral Directors, and Authorize a Representative
steps.html:
Do not attempt to navigate airport cargo, quarantine clearances, or embassy mortuary paperwork alone. Before signing an independent contract with a funeral parlor, verify whether existing coverage applies [3]:

  • Travel or medical-assistance insurance: Check whether your family member held travel medical insurance or medical evacuation/repatriation coverage, and call the insurer's 24-hour assistance center before making independent financial commitments.
  • Appointing Philippine and U.S. funeral homes: To handle local preparation, cremation, or international shipment, the legal next of kin appoints a licensed Philippine funeral home alongside a receiving funeral home in the United States [3][5]. The U.S. Embassy in the Philippines publishes an informational list of funeral homes in Metro Manila, Cebu, Pampanga, and other regions (provided as public-source information for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank any provider) [3][6]. In the United States, you can locate a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination state through the National Funeral Directors Association (toll-free 800-228-6332 or +1 262-789-1880) [7].
  • How next of kin in the United States grant authority: If no immediate family member is physically present in the Philippines, the legal next of kin in the United States must execute a notarized Next-of-Kin Affidavit / Letter of Authorization stating the chosen disposition of the remains (repatriation or local cremation/burial) and naming the authorized Philippine funeral home or local representative, and send it to the U.S. Embassy (ACSInfoManila@state.gov) and the appointed mortuary [3][6].

steps.title: Register the Death Within 30 Days with the Local Civil Registrar (LCR) and Request PSA Certificates
steps.html:
Under Philippine civil registration law administered by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA central inquiry line +63 2 8461-0500), the death must be registered at the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) of the city or municipality where the death occurred within 30 calendar days of the date of death [1]:

  • Health Officer review and LCR filing: Before the Local Civil Registrar records the death, the Municipal or City Health Officer reviews and signs the medical certification on Municipal Form No. 103 (forwarded within 48 hours of certification) and issues the local burial, cremation, or transfer permit [1][2]. In practice, the appointed Philippine funeral home files Municipal Form No. 103 with the LCRO on the family's behalf [1][3]. (Deaths reported after the 30-day period are treated as delayed registrations requiring additional affidavits and a 10-day municipal posting period [1].)
  • PSA Security Paper (SECPA) Death Certificate: Ask the funeral home and Local Civil Registrar for both certified local copies of the registered Certificate of Death and expedited electronic transmittal to the Philippine Statistics Authority so you can obtain official PSA Death Certificates printed on Security Paper (SECPA) [1].

steps.title: Report the Death to the U.S. Embassy in Manila (or Cebu Consular Agency) for the CRDA and Export Permits
steps.html:
Report the death of the U.S. citizen as soon as possible to the U.S. Embassy in the Philippines in Manila (American Citizens Services telephone +63 2 5301-2000, email ACSInfoManila@state.gov with the subject line "Death of a U.S. Citizen") or, for deaths in the Visayas, to the U.S. Consular Agency in Cebu (telephone +63 32 231-1261) [3][8]:

  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Provide the certified Philippine Certificate of Death, the deceased's U.S. passport, and proof of the next of kin's identity and relationship [3]. The Embassy cancels the U.S. passport and issues the official electronic Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060), which U.S. banks, insurers, courts, and federal agencies accept as official English-language proof of death [3]. The U.S. government cannot pay funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [3].
  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) human remains to the United States: Your Philippine funeral director obtains the local Health Officer's Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease and Transfer Permit, a Quarantine Permit from the Philippine Bureau of Quarantine (under the Department of Health, telephone +63 2 5318-7500) [4], and the U.S. Embassy's Consular Mortuary Certificate (which includes the Consular Mortuary Certificate, Affidavit of Foreign Funeral Director, and Certificate of Hermetic Sealing) [3][5]. Under the federal rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, telephone 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains placed in a hermetically sealed casket and accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death and the consular mortuary documents may be imported into the United States consigned to a licensed U.S. funeral home without a separate CDC import permit, provided the person did not die of a quarantinable communicable disease [5].
  • Transporting cremated remains (ashes) to the United States: If the family chooses local cremation in the Philippines, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for fully cremated remains [5]. The ashes must be placed in a sealed, non-metallic urn that can pass airport X-ray security screening and be accompanied by the certified Philippine Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, the Bureau of Quarantine clearance, and U.S. Customs declaration upon arrival [3][4][5].

steps.title: Coordinate U.S. State Reception and Notify Social Security (SSA / FBU Manila) and Veterans Affairs (VA)
steps.html:
Once the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and Philippine death certificates are issued, complete the U.S. reception and federal benefit notifications:

  • Reception in the destination U.S. state: For casketed repatriation, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the arrival airport and obtains the state burial-transit permit in the destination U.S. state [5][7].
  • Social Security Administration (SSA) and FBU Manila: Report the death immediately so monthly retirement or disability payments stop (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to claim the one-time lump-sum death payment and monthly survivor benefits if eligible family members (such as a surviving spouse, eligible divorced spouse, minor or disabled child, or dependent parent) survive the deceased [9][10]. Families in the United States can call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 [9]. If the deceased or surviving beneficiaries lived in the Philippines, report the death directly to the U.S. Embassy Manila Federal Benefits Unit (telephone +63 2 5301-6200, email FBU.Manila@ssa.gov with the subject line "Report of Death") [9][10].
  • Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and estate administration: If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, notify the Department of Veterans Affairs (U.S. toll-free 1-800-827-1000, or the VA Regional Benefit Office at the U.S. Embassy in Manila) to check eligibility for burial allowances, a U.S. government headstone or marker, national cemetery interment, or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [11]. Use the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and PSA Death Certificate to administer U.S. bank accounts, life insurance, and probate in the U.S. state of domicile, as well as any local Philippine accounts [1][3].

closingQuestion: To help us provide exact local details, in which city or municipality in the Philippines did your family member pass away (and are you planning casketed repatriation or cremation), and in which U.S. state will the remains or estate be handled?

title: What to Do When a Romanian Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Romanian Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Italy and Romania: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a Romanian citizen dies in Italy, medical verification, civil death registration, and the issuance of the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) for international transport are handled by the Italian authorities (the local health authority, Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL, and the municipality, Comune, where the death occurred), while transcription of the death into the Romanian civil registry and funeral grant claims involve the Romanian consular network and the social security institutions of both countries.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Pronouncement of Death and Necroscopic Certificate (in a Hospital or Outside a Hospital)
steps.html:
The initial medical procedure depends on where the death occurred, in accordance with the Italian National Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento nazionale di polizia mortuaria, Presidential Decree D.P.R. No. 285/1990) [1]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or residential care facility: The facility's medical management (direzione sanitaria) certifies the death, completes the death notice and the ISTAT statistical cause-of-death form (scheda ISTAT), and transmits the paperwork directly to the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the competent municipality [1].
  • Death outside a hospital (private home, temporary accommodation, workplace, or public place): Contact the attending physician or the single European emergency number 112 (or 118) immediately for the initial pronouncement of death (constatazione di decesso) and completion of the cause-of-death report within 24 hours [1]. Subsequently, the public health medical examiner (medico necroscopo) appointed by the territorially competent local health authority (ASL or ATS) performs the mandatory necroscopic examination (normally between 15 and 30 hours after death) and issues the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico) required to seal the coffin and authorise burial or transport [1].
  • Sudden, suspicious, or workplace accident death: If the death occurred at work, in a public place, or from violent or unclear causes, law enforcement intervenes and the body is placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority; in such cases, removal of the body, burial, or repatriation can proceed only after formal judicial clearance (nulla osta della Procura della Repubblica) is issued by the Public Prosecutor's Office [1].

steps.title: Appoint an Authorised Funeral Director and Provide Family Authorisation
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether the deceased person held an insurance policy (travel, accident, or medical repatriation insurance) providing direct assistance through an emergency operations centre. In the absence of insurance coverage, the family may appoint a licensed funeral company in Italy (impresa di onoranze funebri) experienced in international funeral transport between Italy and Romania [2]. To locate qualified operators in Italy, you can consult the national trade federations: FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, tel. +39 051 6650285, email info@feniof.it) [4] and FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, tel. +39 02 33403992, email info@federcofit.it) [5]. Clarvia provides these directory references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific funeral companies.

  • What the funeral director handles: Acting on the family's behalf, the appointed funeral company manages the paperwork with the hospital medical management or the ASL, files the death declaration with the municipality (Comune), prepares the regulation double coffin for international transport, and applies for the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) [1][2].
  • Family members residing in Romania: If the closest next of kin are in Romania and cannot travel to Italy, they can issue a formal written authorisation (delega scritta) to the funeral company (accompanied by a copy of the authorising family member's identity document) or execute a notarised power of attorney (procura notarile) in Romania authorising a representative in Italy or the funeral agency to claim the body and request municipal permits [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Status Office and Obtain the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
The declaration of death (dichiarazione di morte) must be filed within 24 hours of the death at the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian municipality (Comune) where the death occurred (for example, at the Civil Status offices of Roma Capitale, the Comune di Milano, or the Comune di Torino) [1][2]. In standard practice, the declaration is submitted by the funeral company authorised by the family or by the hospital medical management [1].

  • Certificates to request immediately in multiple copies: In addition to the burial permit and the domestic Italian death certificate, ask the municipal Civil Status Office to issue several copies of the multilingual death certificate extract (Form C / Modello C, estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue) under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 [2].
  • Exemption from Apostille and translation: Because both Italy and Romania are parties to the 1976 Vienna Convention, the multilingual death extract (Form C / Modello C) is directly valid in Romania and at Romanian Consulates without legalisation (Prefecture Apostille) or certified translation [2]. Conversely, if a domestic-only Italian death certificate is used, it will require an Apostille from the competent Italian Prefecture (Prefettura) and a certified translation into Romanian [2].

steps.title: Obtain the Municipal Mortuary Passport, Coordinate Repatriation to Romania, and Complete Consular Transcription
steps.html:
For the international transport of the body from Italy to Romania (whether by road in an authorised hearse or by air), the funeral company applies to the Civil Status / Mortuary Police Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile / Polizia Mortuaria) of the Italian municipality of death for the Passaporto Mortuario (Mortuary Passport) under the Berlin International Convention of 10 February 1937 and Article 27 of D.P.R. 285/1990 [1][2]:

  • Requirements for transporting the coffin or ashes: For repatriation of a body, Italian public health regulations require a double coffin (an outer wooden casket and a hermetically soldered inner zinc coffin) accompanied by the official coffin-sealing report (verbale di chiusura del feretro) and the ASL sanitary certificate [1][2]. Under the international agreements applied by Romania, no separate Romanian consular mortuary passport is required for repatriation from Italy: the Passaporto Mortuario issued by the Italian municipality together with the death certificate extract is sufficient [2]. If the deceased is cremated in Italy and the cinerary urn is transported to Romania, the sealed urn travels with the death certificate and the ash transport permit (autorizzazione al trasporto delle ceneri) issued by the Italian municipality [2].
  • Consular assistance and transcription into Romanian civil registers: To report the death or obtain emergency consular assistance, you can contact the territorially competent Romanian consular mission in Italy (for example, the Consolato Generale di Romania a Roma - Consulate General of Romania in Rome, emergency phone for deaths and severe emergencies +39 345 147 3935; or the Consulate General of Romania in Milan on emergency phone +39 366 108 1444, as well as the consulates in Turin, Bologna, Bari, Catania, and Trieste) [2][3]. The Italian death record must be transcribed into the Romanian civil status registers (within the standard 6-month timeframe) to obtain a Romanian death certificate (certificat de deces): the application can be submitted at the competent Romanian Consulate in Italy by appointment via the official consular portal (eConsulat.ro), or directly in Romania at the town hall (Primăria / Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP) of the deceased person's last Romanian domicile, enclosing the multilingual Form C extract, the deceased's Romanian identity documents, and their birth and marriage certificates [2].

steps.title: Claim the Romanian Funeral Grant (CNPP), Handle Italian Social Security (INPS and INAIL), and Settle the Estate
steps.html:
Once the death certificate extracts have been obtained, family members can initiate pension, funeral benefit, insurance, and banking procedures in both countries:

  • Funeral grant in Romania (ajutor de deces): If the deceased person was insured or retired under the Romanian public pension system (or held insured status during the 6 months prior to death), or if a dependent family member of a person insured or retired in Romania has died, the person who proves they paid the funeral expenses can claim the funeral grant (ajutor de deces) from the Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (CNPP, National House of Public Pensions, Bucharest headquarters tel. +40 21 318 88 00, email petitii.sesizari@cnpp.ro, through the competent county pension house, Casa Județeană de Pensii) within the 3-year limitation period from the issuance of the death certificate [6]. The application must include the death certificate, the claimant's identity document, civil status records proving family relationship, and original funeral invoices/receipts; payment is normally made within 3 working days of submitting a complete claim [6].
  • INPS and INAIL procedures in Italy: If your family member worked or received a pension/benefit in Italy, the Italian municipality transmits the death notification electronically to INPS (Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale), but eligible survivors (such as a surviving spouse or dependent children) must submit an online claim (or apply free of charge through a Patronato advice centre) for a survivor's pension (pensione ai superstiti - reversibilità or pensione indiretta) or lump-sum benefit [7]. If the death resulted from a workplace accident or occupational disease (infortunio sul lavoro o malattia professionale) in Italy, the employer must file a report within 24 hours with INAIL (Istituto Nazionale per l'Assicurazione contro gli Infortuni sul Lavoro), and surviving family members are entitled to the INAIL survivor's annuity (rendita ai superstiti) and the INAIL funeral grant (assegno funerario) [8].
  • Banks and succession: Present the multilingual death certificate extract to any banks in Italy or Romania where the deceased held accounts. In Italy, an inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) must be filed with the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) within 12 months of the opening of the succession if the deceased was resident in Italy or owned real estate or taxable assets in Italy.

closingQuestion: So that we can give you more specific guidance on territorial jurisdiction, in which Italian municipality (Comune) did the death occur, and have you already decided whether to repatriate your family member to Romania or arrange burial or cremation in Italy?

it.title: Cosa fare quando un cittadino rumeno muore in Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Passaggi ufficiali dopo il decesso di un cittadino rumeno in Italia: certificato necroscopico (in ospedale o fuori), Stato Civile del Comune (estratto plurilingue Modello C), Passaporto Mortuario per il rimpatrio in Romania, Consolato della Romania e assegno funerario INPS / CNPP.
it.introHtml: Vi esprimiamo le nostre più sincere condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona di cittadinanza rumena muore in Italia, gli accertamenti sanitari, la formazione dell'atto di morte e il rilascio del Passaporto Mortuario per il trasporto internazionale competono alle autorità italiane (Azienda Sanitaria Locale e Comune del luogo di decesso), mentre la trascrizione dell'atto nei registri di stato civile rumeni e le eventuali prestazioni funerarie in Romania coinvolgono la rete consolare rumena e gli enti previdenziali dei due Paesi.

steps.title: Constatazione di decesso e certificato necroscopico (in ospedale o fuori dall'ospedale)
steps.html:
Il primo adempimento sanitario varia in base al luogo in cui è avvenuto il decesso, ai sensi del Regolamento nazionale di polizia mortuaria (D.P.R. n. 285/1990) [1]:

  • Decesso in ospedale, clinica o struttura residenziale: La direzione sanitaria della struttura accerta la morte, redige l'avviso di decesso e la scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte e trasmette la documentazione direttamente all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune competente [1].
  • Decesso fuori dall'ospedale (abitazione privata, alloggio temporaneo, luogo di lavoro o luogo pubblico): È necessario contattare immediatamente il medico curante o il numero unico di emergenza 112 (o 118) per la prima constatazione di decesso e la compilazione della denuncia della causa di morte entro 24 ore [1]. Successivamente, il medico necroscopo nominato dalla ASL (o ATS) territorialmente competente effettua la visita necroscopica obbligatoria (di norma tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso) e rilascia il certificato necroscopico indispensabile per la chiusura del feretro e l'autorizzazione al seppellimento o al trasporto [1].
  • Decesso improvviso, sospetto o per infortunio sul lavoro: Se il decesso avviene sul posto di lavoro, sulla pubblica via o per cause violente o non chiare, intervengono le forze dell'ordine e la salma viene posta a disposizione dell'Autorità Giudiziaria; in questi casi la movimentazione della salma, la sepoltura o il rimpatrio possono procedere solo dopo il rilascio del nulla osta della Procura della Repubblica [1].

steps.title: Incarico a un'impresa funebre autorizzata e delega da parte dei familiari
steps.html:
Prima di sottoscrivere un contratto a titolo privato, verificate se la persona deceduta disponeva di una polizza assicurativa (viaggio, infortuni o rimpatrio sanitario) che preveda l'intervento diretto di una centrale operativa di assistenza. In assenza di copertura assicurativa, i familiari possono conferire mandato a un'impresa di onoranze funebri autorizzata in Italia ed esperta in trasporti funebri internazionali tra Italia e Romania [2]. Per individuare operatori qualificati sul territorio nazionale è possibile consultare le federazioni nazionali di categoria: FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, tel. +39 051 6650285, email info@feniof.it) [4] e FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, tel. +39 02 33403992, email info@federcofit.it) [5]. Clarvia fornisce questi riferimenti a solo scopo orientativo e non raccomanda, approva né classifica specifiche imprese funebri.

  • Cosa gestisce l'impresa funebre: L'impresa incaricata si occupa in nome e per conto della famiglia del disbrigo delle pratiche presso la direzione sanitaria o la ASL, della dichiarazione di morte presso il Comune, della preparazione regolamentare del feretro per il trasporto internazionale e della richiesta del Passaporto Mortuario [1][2].
  • Familiari residenti in Romania: Se i congiunti più prossimi si trovano in Romania e non possono recarsi in Italia, possono conferire formale delega scritta all'impresa funebre (corredata da copia del documento d'identità del familiare delegante) oppure sottoscrivere una procura notarile in Romania per autorizzare un rappresentante in Italia o l'agenzia funebre a ritirare la salma e richiedere i permessi comunali [1][2].

steps.title: Dichiarazione di morte all'Ufficio di Stato Civile e rilascio dell'estratto plurilingue (Modello C)
steps.html:
La dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano in cui è avvenuta la morte (ad esempio presso gli uffici di Stato Civile di Roma Capitale, del Comune di Milano o del Comune di Torino) [1][2]. Nella prassi ordinaria la dichiarazione viene trasmessa dall'impresa funebre delegata dalla famiglia o dalla direzione sanitaria dell'ospedale [1].

  • Certificati da richiedere subito in più copie: Oltre al permesso di seppellimento e al certificato di morte italiano, chiedete all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune il rilascio di più esemplari dell'estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue (Modello C) previsto dalla Convenzione di Vienna dell'8 settembre 1976 [2].
  • Esenzione da apostille e traduzione: Poiché sia l'Italia sia la Romania aderiscono alla Convenzione di Vienna del 1976, l'estratto di morte plurilingue (Modello C) è valido direttamente in Romania e presso i Consolati rumeni senza necessità di legalizzazione (Apostille della Prefettura) né di traduzione giurata [2]. Se invece viene utilizzato un certificato di morte italiano in formato solo nazionale, occorrerà l'Apostille della Prefettura competente e la traduzione in lingua rumena [2].

steps.title: Passaporto Mortuario comunale, rimpatrio in Romania e trascrizione consolare
steps.html:
Per il trasporto internazionale della salma dall'Italia alla Romania (sia su strada tramite autofunebre autorizzata sia per via aerea), l'impresa funebre richiede all'Ufficio di Stato Civile / Polizia Mortuaria del Comune italiano di decesso il Passaporto Mortuario ai sensi della Convenzione internazionale di Berlino del 10 febbraio 1937 e dell'art. 27 del D.P.R. 285/1990 [1][2]:

  • Requisiti per il trasporto del feretro o delle ceneri: Per il rimpatrio della salma, la normativa sanitaria richiede la doppia cassa (cofano in legno con cassa interna di zinco ermeticamente saldata) accompagnata dal verbale di chiusura del feretro e dalla certificazione igienico-sanitaria della ASL [1][2]. Grazie agli accordi internazionali applicati dalla Romania, per il rimpatrio dall'Italia non è richiesto un ulteriore passaporto mortuario consolare rumeno: è sufficiente il Passaporto Mortuario rilasciato dal Comune italiano insieme all'estratto di morte [2]. In caso di cremazione in Italia e trasporto dell'urna cineraria in Romania, l'urna sigillata viaggia con il certificato di morte e l'autorizzazione al trasporto delle ceneri rilasciata dal Comune italiano [2].
  • Assistenza consolare e trascrizione nei registri rumeni: Per segnalare il decesso o ricevere assistenza consolare d'urgenza è possibile contattare l'ufficio consolare rumeno competente per territorio (ad esempio il Consolato Generale di Romania a Roma, telefono di emergenza per decessi e casi gravi +39 345 147 3935; oppure il Consolato Generale di Romania a Milano al numero di emergenza +39 366 108 1444, oltre alle sedi di Torino, Bologna, Bari, Catania e Trieste) [2][3]. L'atto di morte italiano deve essere trascritto nei registri di stato civile rumeni (entro il termine ordinario di 6 mesi) per ottenere il certificato di morte rumeno (certificat de deces): la domanda può essere presentata presso il Consolato rumeno in Italia previa prenotazione sul portale consolare ufficiale, oppure direttamente in Romania presso il Comune (Primăria / Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP) dell'ultimo domicilio della persona deceduta, allegando l'estratto plurilingue Modello C, i documenti d'identità rumeni e i certificati di nascita e matrimonio della persona deceduta [2].

steps.title: Assegno funerario rumeno (CNPP), pratiche previdenziali in Italia (INPS e INAIL) e successione
steps.html:
Una volta ottenuti gli estratti di morte, i familiari possono avviare le pratiche previdenziali, assicurative e bancarie nei due Paesi:

  • Assegno funerario in Romania (ajutor de deces): Se la persona deceduta era assicurata o pensionata nel sistema pubblico rumeno (o ha avuto qualità di assicurato negli ultimi 6 mesi precedenti il decesso), oppure se è deceduto un familiare a carico di un assicurato/pensionato in Romania, la persona che dimostra di aver sostenuto le spese funebri può richiedere l'ajutor de deces alla Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (CNPP, sede centrale a Bucarest tel. +40 21 318 88 00, email petitii.sesizari@cnpp.ro, tramite la Casa Județeană de Pensii competente) entro il termine di prescrizione di 3 anni dall'emissione del certificato di morte [6]. Alla domanda vanno allegati il certificato di morte, il documento d'identità del richiedente, gli atti di stato civile che attestano il grado di parentela e le fatture/ricevute originali delle spese funebri; il pagamento avviene di norma entro 3 giorni lavorativi dalla presentazione della domanda completa [6].
  • Adempimenti INPS e INAIL in Italia: Se il vostro familiare lavorava o percepiva una prestazione previdenziale in Italia, il Comune italiano trasmette telematicamente la comunicazione di decesso all'INPS, ma i superstiti aventi diritto (come il coniuge o i figli a carico) devono presentare domanda telematica (o tramite un Patronato gratuito) per l'eventuale pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o pensione indiretta) o indennità una tantum [7]. Qualora il decesso sia avvenuto per infortunio sul lavoro o malattia professionale in Italia, il datore di lavoro ha l'obbligo di inviare la denuncia entro 24 ore all'INAIL e i familiari superstiti hanno diritto alla rendita ai superstiti e all'assegno funerario INAIL [8].
  • Banche e successione: Presentate l'estratto dell'atto di morte agli istituti bancari in Italia o in Romania presso cui la persona deceduta deteneva conti correnti. In Italia, la dichiarazione di successione va presentata all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione qualora la persona deceduta fosse residente in Italia o possedesse beni immobili o attivi soggetti all'imposta sulle successioni in Italia.

title: What to Do When a Dutch Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Dutch Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Spain and Netherlands: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a Dutch citizen dies in Spain, medical certification, registration in the municipal Civil Registry (Registro Civil), and public health transit permits are governed by Spanish law, while insurance coordination, reception of the coffin or ashes, and updates to civil, tax, and pension records are handled through institutions in the Netherlands.

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death in Spain (in a hospital or outside a hospital)
steps.html:
The first requirement is for a licensed physician in Spain to issue the official Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción), which is essential for registering the death and authorizing any transfer or funeral service [1][5]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: The medical team at the healthcare facility directly issues the Certificado Médico de Defunción for natural causes and coordinates moving the deceased to the mortuary (tanatorio) [1][5].
  • Death outside a hospital (private residence, hotel, holiday apartment, or public place): Call the emergency number 112 immediately. If a primary care or emergency physician has access to the deceased person's medical history and can certify natural causes, they will issue the medical certificate. However, if the death is sudden, accidental, without a medical record in Spain, or occurs in a public place, the police and the duty court (Juzgado de Guardia) will intervene, ordering a transfer to the Institute of Legal Medicine (Instituto de Medicina Legal) for a judicial autopsy before issuing judicial clearance for registration and transport [5].
  • Mortuary health regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria): Under Spain's regional mortuary health regulations, burial or cremation generally cannot take place until at least 24 hours after death, and final disposition or embalming/preservation for international repatriation must typically be arranged within 48 hours of death.

steps.title: Notifying the emergency assistance center (*alarmcentrale*) and appointing funeral directors in Spain and the Netherlands
steps.html:
Before hiring a local funeral home independently, check immediately whether the deceased held Dutch travel insurance (reisverzekering) or funeral insurance (uitvaartverzekering) [5].

  • Coordination through the alarmcentrale: If an insurance policy is in place, contact the Dutch insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance center (alarmcentrale) first, as it directly appoints a partner funeral home in Spain and a receiving funeral director in the Netherlands, managing technical logistics and covered costs [5].
  • Direct appointment of licensed funeral directors: If no insurance coverage applies, the family may appoint an authorized funeral company in Spain through the directory of PANASEF (Spanish National Association of Funeral Services, tel. +34 910 800 895, email secretaria@panasef.com) [3], which will coordinate with a certified funeral director in the Netherlands belonging to the Verbond van Uitvaartzorg (the Dutch Funeral Care Association formed by the merger of the Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen - BGNU and Nardus, tel. +31 70 364 75 00, email info@verbondvanuitvaartzorg.nl) [4]. Clarvia provides these professional directories for orientation only and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Registration in the Spanish Civil Registry and requesting the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
The death must be registered with the municipal Civil Registry (Registro Civil) where the death occurred (under the Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, the Spanish Ministry of Justice), usually within 24 hours of death and always before burial, cremation, or repatriation [1].

  • Who submits the registration: In standard Spanish practice, the authorized funeral company submits the Certificado Médico de Defunción and the deceased's Dutch passport or identity card electronically or in person on behalf of the family [1].
  • Certificates to request: In addition to the full Spanish death certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) and the burial or cremation permit, request several copies of the Multilingual Death Certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción, Form C / Fórmula C) issued under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 [1][6]. Because both Spain and the Netherlands are party to this convention, the multilingual extract is accepted directly by Dutch municipalities (gemeenten) and authorities without a Hague Apostille or sworn translation [6].

steps.title: International repatriation of the body or ashes to the Netherlands or local funeral in Spain
steps.html:
The appointed funeral company obtains the required public health and transit permits according to the family's chosen arrangements [5]:

  • Repatriation of the body to the Netherlands: For air or road transport of a coffin, the Spanish funeral director arranges sanitary preparation (embalming or temporary preservation and a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner), foreign health clearance (Sanidad Exterior), and the international mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio) [5]. For consular guidance or urgent assistance, the official Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal NederlandWereldwijd and the Embassy of the Netherlands in Madrid operate a 24-hour contact center at +31 247 247 247 (or via WhatsApp at +31 857 737 400 and the Madrid Embassy number +34 913 53 75 00) [5]. Upon arrival in the Netherlands, the Dutch funeral director presents the death certificate and laissez-passer to the destination Dutch municipality to obtain the statutory permit for burial or cremation (verlof tot begraven of cremeren) under the Dutch Corpse Disposal Act (Wet op de lijkbezorging) [5].
  • Cremation in Spain and transport of ashes: If cremation takes place in Spain, transporting a sealed funerary urn to the Netherlands does not require a coffin laissez-passer; it is sufficient to carry the sealed urn accompanied by the cremation certificate and the Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (after checking the airline's cabin baggage rules in advance) [5].

steps.title: Post-death formalities in the Netherlands (BRP, Gemeente Den Haag, SVB, and Belastingdienst) and in Spain
steps.html:
Using the Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción and the Spanish Certificado Literal de Defunción, next of kin must complete administrative steps in both countries:

  • Municipal registration in the Netherlands (BRP vs. Municipality of The Hague): If the deceased lived and was registered as a resident in the Netherlands, family members must present the Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción to the deceased's municipality of residence (woongemeente) to update the Personal Records Database (Basisregistratie Personen - BRP), which automatically notifies Dutch public agencies [6]. If the deceased lived outside the Netherlands (not registered as a resident in the BRP), optional transcription of the foreign death certificate into the Dutch civil registers is handled by the National Tasks Department of the Municipality of The Hague (Gemeente Den Haag, Afdeling Landelijke Taken) [6].
  • Dutch pensions (SVB) and taxes (Belastingdienst): If the deceased lived outside the Netherlands or died abroad while receiving a Dutch state pension (AOW) or survivor benefit (Anw), the death must be reported to the Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB, Social Insurance Bank) within 4 to 6 weeks via Mijn SVB or through the SVB office at the Embassy in Madrid (tel. +34 913 537 500, option 2) [7]. For questions regarding Dutch inheritance tax (erfbelasting) or final income tax settlement, the Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax and Customs Administration) provides a dedicated bereavement helpline (BelastingTelefoon voor nabestaanden: 0800 235 83 54 within the Netherlands or +31 555 385 385 from abroad) [8].
  • Succession and assets in Spain: If the deceased was a resident of Spain or held bank accounts or real estate in Spanish territory, after 15 working days from the date of death you must apply to the Spanish Ministry of Justice (using Modelo 790) for the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Death Insurance Contracts to verify whether a Spanish will was executed and to settle inheritance and succession taxes within the standard 6-month deadline [2].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more tailored guidance, in which municipality or autonomous community in Spain did the death occur, and was your family member registered as a resident in a Dutch municipality (BRP) or habitually resident in Spain?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando un ciudadano neerlandés fallece en España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Pasos oficiales cuando un ciudadano de los Países Bajos fallece en España: Certificado Médico de Defunción (en hospital o fuera de él), central de asistencia (alarmcentrale) y funeraria, Registro Civil (Certificado Plurilingüe), repatriación a los Países Bajos o funeral local, y trámites ante la gemeente, SVB y Belastingdienst.
es.introHtml: Le expresamos nuestras más sinceras condolencias por el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona de nacionalidad neerlandesa fallece en España, la certificación médica, la inscripción en el Registro Civil municipal y los permisos sanitarios de salida se rigen por la normativa española, mientras que la coordinación del seguro, la recepción del féretro o de las cenizas y la actualización de los registros civiles, fiscales y de pensiones se realizan ante las instituciones de los Países Bajos.

steps.title: Obtención del Certificado Médico de Defunción en España (en hospital o fuera de él)
steps.html:
El primer paso consiste en que un médico colegiado en España expida el Certificado Médico de Defunción, requisito indispensable para inscribir el fallecimiento y autorizar cualquier traslado o servicio funerario [1][5]:

  • Fallecimiento en un hospital o clínica: El equipo médico del centro sanitario emite directamente el Certificado Médico de Defunción por causas naturales y coordina el traslado del cuerpo al tanatorio [1][5].
  • Fallecimiento fuera de un hospital (domicilio, hotel, apartamento turístico o vía pública): Debe llamarse de inmediato al teléfono de emergencias 112. Si un médico de atención primaria o de urgencias conoce el historial clínico de la persona fallecida y puede certificar causas naturales, expedirá el certificado médico. En cambio, si el fallecimiento es repentino, accidental, sin historial médico en España o en la vía pública, interviene la policía y el Juzgado de Guardia, ordenando el traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal para la práctica de la autopsia judicial antes de emitir la autorización judicial para la inscripción y el traslado [5].
  • Plazos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Según la normativa sanitaria autonómica en España, por regla general no puede practicarse la inhumación ni la cremación antes de las 24 horas desde el fallecimiento, y el destino final o la conservación/embalsamamiento para traslado internacional debe gestionarse habitualmente dentro de las 48 horas posteriores al óbito.

steps.title: Notificación a la central de asistencia (alarmcentrale) y designación de funeraria en España y los Países Bajos
steps.html:
Antes de contratar por cuenta propia a una empresa funeraria local, compruebe de inmediato si la persona fallecida disponía de un seguro de viaje neerlandés (reisverzekering) o de un seguro de decesos (uitvaartverzekering) [5].

  • Coordinación a través de la alarmcentrale: Si existe póliza de seguro, contacte primero con la central de asistencia 24 horas (alarmcentrale) de la aseguradora neerlandesa, ya que esta designa directamente una funeraria colaboradora en España y una empresa funeraria receptora en los Países Bajos, asumiendo la gestión técnica y los costes cubiertos [5].
  • Contratación directa de empresas funerarias autorizadas: Si no existe seguro aplicable, la familia puede designar una empresa funeraria autorizada en España a través del directorio de PANASEF (Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios, tel. +34 910 800 895, correo electrónico secretaria@panasef.com) [3], la cual trabajará en coordinación con una empresa funeraria certificada en los Países Bajos perteneciente al Verbond van Uitvaartzorg (organización resultante de la unión de la Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen - BGNU y Nardus, tel. +31 70 364 75 00, correo electrónico info@verbondvanuitvaartzorg.nl) [4]. Clarvia facilita estos directorios profesionales únicamente a título orientativo y no recomienda, avala ni clasifica a proveedores concretos.

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil español y solicitud del Certificado Plurilingüe (Fórmula C)
steps.html:
La defunción debe inscribirse obligatoriamente en el Registro Civil del municipio español donde ocurrió el fallecimiento (dependiente del Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes), habitualmente dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al óbito y siempre antes de la inhumación, cremación o repatriación [1].

  • Quién realiza el trámite: En la práctica habitual en España, la empresa funeraria autorizada presenta de forma telemática o presencial el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el pasaporte o documento de identidad neerlandés de la persona fallecida en representación de la familia [1].
  • Certificados que deben solicitarse: Además del Certificado Literal de Defunción español y de la licencia de enterramiento o incineración, solicite varios ejemplares del Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C) conforme al Convenio de Viena de 8 de septiembre de 1976 [1][6]. Dado que tanto España como los Países Bajos son Estados parte en dicho convenio, el extracto plurilingüe es aceptado directamente por los municipios (gemeenten) y organismos neerlandeses sin necesidad de Apostilla de La Haya ni de traducción jurada [6].

steps.title: Traslado internacional del cuerpo o de las cenizas a los Países Bajos o funeral local en España
steps.html:
La empresa funeraria designada gestiona los permisos sanitarios y de transporte según la opción elegida por la familia [5]:

  • Repatriación del cuerpo a los Países Bajos: Para el transporte aéreo o terrestre del féretro, la funeraria española tramita el acondicionamiento sanitario (embalsamamiento o conservación transitoria y féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada), la autorización de Sanidad Exterior y el salvoconducto mortuorio (laissez-passer) internacional [5]. Para consultas consulares o apoyo en situaciones de urgencia, el portal oficial del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores neerlandés NederlandWereldwijd y la Embajada de los Países Bajos en Madrid atienden las 24 horas en el teléfono +31 247 247 247 (o por WhatsApp en el +31 857 737 400 y en el teléfono local de la Embajada en Madrid +34 913 53 75 00) [5]. Al llegar a los Países Bajos, la funeraria neerlandesa presenta el certificado de defunción y el laissez-passer ante el municipio neerlandés de destino para obtener el permiso legal de inhumación o cremación (verlof tot begraven of cremeren) conforme a la ley funeraria neerlandesa (Wet op de lijkbezorging) [5].
  • Cremación en España y traslado de cenizas: Si la cremación se realiza en España, el transporte de la urna funeraria cerrada hacia los Países Bajos no requiere salvoconducto mortuorio de féretro; basta con portar la urna sellada acompañada del certificado de cremación y del Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (verificando previamente las normas de equipaje de mano de la aerolínea) [5].

steps.title: Trámites posteriores en los Países Bajos (BRP, Gemeente Den Haag, SVB y Belastingdienst) y en España
steps.html:
Con el Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción y el Certificado Literal español, los familiares deben completar las gestiones administrativas en ambos países:

  • Registro municipal en los Países Bajos (BRP vs. Municipio de La Haya): Si la persona fallecida residía y estaba empadronada en los Países Bajos, los familiares deben presentar el Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción en su propio municipio de residencia (woongemeente) para actualizar el registro de población (Basisregistratie Personen - BRP), el cual notifica automáticamente a las administraciones neerlandesas [6]. Si la persona fallecida residía fuera de los Países Bajos (no inscrita como residente en la BRP), la inscripción opcional del acta extranjera en los registros civiles neerlandeses se tramita ante el departamento de tareas nacionales del Municipio de La Haya (Gemeente Den Haag, Afdeling Landelijke Taken) [6].
  • Pensiones neerlandesas (SVB) e impuestos (Belastingdienst): Si la persona fallecida residía fuera de los Países Bajos o falleció en el extranjero percibiendo pensión estatal (AOW) o prestaciones de supervivencia (Anw), el fallecimiento debe comunicarse a la Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) en un plazo de 4 a 6 semanas a través de Mijn SVB o de la oficina de la SVB en la Embajada en Madrid (tel. +34 913 537 500, opción 2) [7]. Para cuestiones sobre el impuesto de sucesiones neerlandés (erfbelasting) o el cierre fiscal, la Belastingdienst dispone del teléfono de atención a familiares (BelastingTelefoon voor nabestaanden: 0800 235 83 54 desde los Países Bajos o +31 555 385 385 desde el extranjero) [8].
  • Sucesión y bienes en España: Si la persona fallecida era residente en España o poseía cuentas bancarias o bienes inmuebles en territorio español, transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde el fallecimiento debe solicitarse el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento ante el Ministerio de Justicia (Modelo 790) para verificar si otorgó testamento en España y tramitar la herencia e impuestos sucesorios dentro del plazo general de 6 meses [2].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Germany & Turkey
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Germany & Turkey
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border terminal illness checklist between Germany and Turkey: palliative care coordination, separate Advance Directives, separate financial and medical Powers of Attorney, caregiver leave and benefits, and cross-border estate and repatriation planning.
introHtml: A diagnosis of an incurable, advanced illness places heavy medical and organizational demands on your family. Where personal, legal, or financial ties exist with both Germany and Turkey, it is especially important to arrange care pathways, powers of attorney, and succession matters while the ill person still has full mental and legal capacity, because German and Turkish authorities and banks often require separate legal instruments. Below are the five primary official steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Clarify palliative and hospice care in Germany as well as health insurance coverage if relocating to Turkey
steps.html:
First, contact the treating medical team or hospital social service (Krankenhaussozialdienst) in Germany to establish seamless symptom and pain management [1][2]:

  • Care in Germany (SAPV, hospice care, and fast-track care level assessment): In cases of complex symptoms, the general practitioner or hospital can prescribe Specialized Outpatient Palliative Care (Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung - SAPV under § 37b SGB V), which provides 24-hour home care by a multi-professional palliative team covered by statutory health insurance [1]. Alternatively or additionally, outpatient hospice services and inpatient hospices offer support; nationwide contacts are provided by the umbrella organization Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband (German Hospice and Palliative Association) at 030 82 00 758-0 or via email at info@dhpv.de [2]. In parallel, submit an initial or upgrade application for a care level (Pflegegrad) to the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse), explicitly noting the palliative situation in writing: under § 18(3) sentence 3 SGB XI (in conjunction with § 18a SGB XI), the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) must complete the assessment within one week if the ill person is receiving outpatient palliative care or is in a hospice [3].
  • If planning continued care or return to Turkey (Form T/A 11 and fitness to fly): If your family member wishes to spend the final stage of life in Turkey, insurance coverage must be clarified prior to departure with the German statutory health insurance fund (gesetzliche Krankenkasse - GKV) and using the guidance sheets of the liaison body Deutsche Verbindungsstelle Krankenversicherung - Ausland (DVKA, German Liaison Office for Health Insurance - Abroad) [4]. For a temporary stay, the health insurance fund issues the entitlement certificate T/A 11 (also referred to as A/T 11) under the German-Turkish Social Security Agreement [4][5]. In Turkey, this form must be submitted to a local branch of the state social security institution (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK) to obtain a YUPASS number for medical treatment at contracted Turkish hospitals [4][5]. Note that this covers only benefits available under Turkish statutory health rules, medical repatriation back to Germany is not included, entitlement to German care allowance (Pflegegeld) generally ceases upon permanent relocation to Turkey, and a medical fitness-to-fly certificate (Fit-to-fly) must be obtained in advance [4][5].

steps.title: Draft a written advance healthcare directive and treatment plan for Germany and Turkey
steps.html:
While the ill person has capacity to give informed consent, they should record their medical preferences in writing [6]:

  • Advance directive (Patientenverfügung) under § 1827 BGB: In Germany, a written, personally signed Patientenverfügung bindingly specifies which end-of-life medical interventions (such as mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, or cardiopulmonary resuscitation) are consented to or refused [6]. The Bundesministerium der Justiz (Federal Ministry of Justice) provides legally vetted text modules and drafting guides free of charge [6].
  • Emergency palliative sheet and cross-border documentation: Ask the SAPV team or general practitioner to draw up a palliative emergency sheet (Notfallbogen) for emergency medical services [1][6]. If a stay in Turkey is planned, current medical reports, the medication schedule (particularly for strong opioid analgesics), and documented treatment preferences should be carried along with a certified Turkish translation so that Turkish medical teams are informed of the therapeutic goal and designated trusted representatives [5][6].

steps.title: Execute legally valid powers of attorney separately for Germany and Turkey
steps.html:
Because a privately signed German power of attorney is not accepted by Turkish banks and authorities, two separate powers of attorney should be executed while the person retains full legal capacity [6][7]:

  • For Germany (Vorsorgevollmacht and Betreuungsverfügung): With a German durable power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht, supplemented by an advance care directive for court-appointed guardianship, Betreuungsverfügung), the ill person authorizes one or more trusted individuals to handle healthcare, residence decisions, official administrative matters, and financial affairs [6]. Real estate transactions in Germany require notarization (notarielle Beurkundung) or public certification (öffentliche Beglaubigung); for German bank accounts, a separate bank power of attorney valid beyond death (transmortale Vollmacht) should also be lodged directly with the bank [6]. Register the Vorsorgevollmacht with the Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer (Central Register of Advance Directives of the Federal Chamber of Notaries) via the toll-free number 0800 3550500 so that guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) and attending physicians can access it immediately in an emergency [8].
  • For Turkey (Düzenleme Şeklinde Vekâletname): For bank accounts, pension matters (SGK), land registry transactions (Tapu), and administrative procedures in Turkey, the representative requires a notarized power of attorney drawn up in formal deed form under Turkish notarial law (Düzenleme Şeklinde Vekâletname) [7]. After completing an online application and booking an appointment, this can be executed in person at the locally competent Türkisches Generalkonsulat (Turkish Consulate General) in Germany (the Consular Call Center for Germany is available 24/7 at +49 30 30 80 70 90, or internationally at +90 312 292 29 29) [7]. Required items include valid identification (T.C. Kimlik Kartı, Mavi Kart, or passport), biometric passport photos, and the personal details of the appointed representative; in cases of serious illness or advanced age, Turkish consulates routinely require a same-day specialist medical certificate confirming full mental capacity (Akıl Sağlığı Raporu) [7].

steps.title: Use statutory caregiver leave and care support allowance in Germany
steps.html:
Employed family caregivers in Germany can claim statutory leave and wage-replacement benefits, on which the Pflegetelefon des Bundesministeriums für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (Care Helpline of the Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth) provides advice at 030 20 17 91 31 or by email at info@wege-zur-pflege.de [9]:

  • Short-term inability to work (Kurzzeitige Arbeitsverhinderung, up to 10 working days): To organize care in an acute care situation, employees may take up to 10 working days off work and apply to the ill person's Pflegekasse for Care Support Allowance (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) as a wage-replacement benefit [9].
  • End-of-life care leave (Pflegezeit in der letzten Lebensphase) and Family Care Leave (Familienpflegezeit): Under the German Care Leave Act (Pflegezeitgesetz), employees (in businesses with 16 or more employees) are entitled to full or partial leave of up to three months to accompany a close relative during the final phase of life - even if care is provided in an inpatient hospice [9]. For home care, employees may also claim up to 6 months of Pflegezeit or up to 24 months of Familienpflegezeit (in businesses with 26 or more employees), supplemented by the option of an interest-free loan from the Federal Office of Family Affairs and Civil Society Functions (Bundesamt für Familie und zivilgesellschaftliche Aufgaben) [9].

steps.title: Organize cross-border succession, bank accounts, and funeral wishes between Germany and Turkey
steps.html:
Put asset and estate documents in order early, as special conflict-of-laws rules apply between Germany and Turkey [10][11]:

  • Account for the split estate (Nachlassspaltung) regarding real property: Under the bilateral German-Turkish Agreement on Succession of 1929 (Annex to Article 20 of the Consular Treaty), which remains in force, as well as Turkish private international law (MÖHUK Art. 20), immovable property is mandatorily governed by the law of the state in which the real estate is situated (lex rei sitae), as explained by the Deutsche Vertretungen in der Türkei (German Missions in Turkey) [10]. Real estate in Turkey is therefore always inherited under Turkish succession law regardless of nationality (including Turkish compulsory share rules and a Turkish certificate of inheritance, Veraset İlamı), whereas movable assets (such as bank accounts) are governed by nationality or a choice of law under the EU Succession Regulation [10]. Because certain German forms of wills (such as a joint Berliner Testament) can create legal complications in Turkey, seeking notarial advice in Germany is advisable, along with official custody of the will and registration in the Zentrales Testamentsregister der Bundesnotarkammer (Central Register of Wills of the Federal Chamber of Notaries) at 0800 3550700 [10][11].
  • Funeral wishes and repatriation burial funds (Cenaze Fonu): Discuss with your family member whether burial in Germany or repatriation to Turkey is preferred, and check whether they hold membership in a mutual funeral assistance fund (Cenaze Fonu, for example through DITIB or IGMG) or funeral expense insurance (Sterbegeldversicherung), which coordinates official formalities and international transport in the event of death [7][10].
