title: What to Do When a German Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a German Citizen Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Spain and Germany: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a German citizen dies in Spain, Spanish medical, public health, and civil registry formalities must be coordinated with the consular, funeral, pension, and succession rules of Germany [1][2].

Because the death took place in Spain and the deceased held German nationality, medical certification, the burial or cremation permit, and immediate civil registration are governed by Spanish law, whereas the reception of the coffin or ashes, termination of pensions, and inheritance certificates depend on the German legal framework [1][2][3]. The exact procedure depends on three main factors: whether the death occurred in a hospital or outside a healthcare facility (such as a private residence, hotel, or public place), whether the family chooses local burial or cremation in Spain or repatriation of the coffin or ashes to Germany, and whether your family member was habitually resident in Germany or permanently resident in Spain [1][2][3].

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death and sanitary timeframes in Spain
steps.html:
The first mandatory step in Spain is obtaining the official Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción, issued on the form of the Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos), which is required to register the death in the Civil Registry and move the body [1][3]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: If your family member died in a hospital from diagnosed natural causes, the attending physician directly issues the Certificado Médico de Defunción [1][3]. It is important to provide the hospital with the deceased's German passport or identity card (Personalausweis or Reisepass) and, if resident in Spain, their EU Citizen Registration Certificate or NIE number, so that personal details match their German documents exactly [1][3].
  • Death in a private residence, hotel, or public place: If the death occurs outside a hospital, call the emergency number 112 immediately [1][2]. If the emergency doctor can certify a natural cause supported by Spanish medical records, they will sign the medical certificate; however, if the death is sudden, accidental, without a medical history in Spain, or of undetermined cause, the police and the competent duty court (Juzgado de Guardia) will intervene, ordering removal of the body to the Institute of Legal Medicine (Instituto de Medicina Legal) for a judicial autopsy before authorizing registration in the Civil Registry and release to the funeral home [1][2].
  • Mortuary health regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria): Under the regional mortuary health regulations of Spain's autonomous communities (such as the Balearic Islands, Canary Islands, Andalusia, Valencian Community, Catalonia, or Madrid), transfer to an authorized mortuary (tanatorio) takes place immediately, and burial, cremation, or embalming is generally carried out between 24 and 48 hours after death [1][4].

steps.title: Verifying insurance, appointing funeral directors, and German consular assistance
steps.html:
Before entering into a private contract with a funeral provider, check existing insurance policies and contact accredited operators in both countries [1][2]:

  • Travel or assistance insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung): Check whether the deceased held German travel health insurance covering repatriation in the event of death (Rücktransport im Todesfall), coverage through an automobile club or bank card, or a Spanish funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos) [1][2]. If coverage exists, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance center before signing private funeral contracts, as the insurer typically appoints the international funeral director directly and covers authorized costs [1][2].
  • Appointing a funeral director in Spain and in Germany: If no insurance applies, you will need to hire an authorized funeral company in Spain, which can be located through the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF, Spanish National Association of Funeral Services, tel. +34 91 576 31 55; email: info@panasef.com) [4]. If you wish to repatriate the body or ashes to Germany, the Spanish funeral company must coordinate with a receiving funeral director in Germany (Bestatter) belonging to the Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter (Federal Association of German Funeral Directors, BDB, tel. +49 211 1600810; emergency number: +49 211 1600886; email: info@bestatter.de) [5]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific funeral providers.
  • Guidance from the German Missions in Spain: You can request consular guidance and lists of funeral homes, lawyers, and translators from the Embajada de la República Federal de Alemania en Madrid (Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in Madrid, Calle de Fortuny, 8, 28010 Madrid; switchboard: +34 91 557 9000; consular emergency phone for Peninsular Spain and the Canary Islands: +34 661 611 104; consular emergency phone for the Balearic Islands: +34 659 011 017) or from the German consulates in Barcelona, Málaga, Palma de Mallorca, or Las Palmas de Gran Canaria [1][2].

steps.title: Registration in the Spanish Civil Registry and obtaining the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
The death must be registered in the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the Spanish municipality where the death occurred, usually within 24 hours and always before the burial, cremation, or international transit permit is issued [1][3]. As a rule, the Spanish funeral company completes this step by presenting the Certificado Médico de Defunción and your family member's German identity card or passport [1][3].

Through the funeral home or the civil registry services of the Ministerio de Justicia (Spanish Ministry of Justice, citizen helpline: +34 91 837 22 95), request two essential certificates [3]:

  • Full Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción): Required for the funeral permit and for any banking, notarial, tax, or inheritance procedures in Spain [3].
  • Multilingual Death Certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción, Vienna Convention Form C): Because both Spain and Germany are contracting states to CIEC Convention No. 16 of Vienna (1976), the multilingual extract of death (Fórmula C / Internationale Sterbeurkunde) is recognized directly by civil registry offices (Standesämter), courts, and pension authorities in Germany without an apostille or sworn translation [1][2][3]. Furthermore, under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191, civil status public documents issued in Spain are exempt from the apostille requirement in Germany [2][3].

steps.title: Local burial or cremation in Spain vs. repatriation of the coffin or ashes to Germany
steps.html:
Public health and transport documentation depends on the arrangement chosen by the family [1][2][4][5]:

  • Repatriation of the body in a coffin to Germany: The Spanish funeral company arranges statutory embalming or sanitary preparation (tanatopraxia), placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner, foreign health clearance (Sanidad Exterior), and issuance of the international mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio / Leichenpass) under the 1937 Berlin Agreement and the Strasbourg Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses [1][2][4]. The receiving German funeral director (Bestatter) collects the coffin at the destination airport in Germany and arranges burial or cremation with the German municipality [5].
  • Cremation in Spain and transfer of ashes to Germany (Urnenüberführung): If cremation takes place in Spain, it is essential to observe the statutory cemetery interment requirement (Friedhofszwang) in force across German federal states [1][2][5]. Unlike in some other countries, private individuals in Germany are not permitted to keep a funerary urn at home or carry it freely in their luggage for home storage: to ship or transfer an urn to Germany, authorities and crematoria require a written confirmation of acceptance (Übernahmebescheinigung) from a German cemetery administration (Friedhofsverwaltung) or an authorized German funeral director (Bestatter), to whom the sealed urn is consigned together with the cremation certificate and the Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción [1][2][5].
  • Final burial or cremation in Spain: If burial or placement of the ashes takes place entirely in a Spanish cemetery or columbarium, only Spanish municipal permits and fees apply [3][4].

steps.title: Subsequent civil registry, pension, and succession formalities in Germany and in Spain
steps.html:
Once the funeral service or repatriation has been arranged, administrative and estate notifications must be completed in both countries [2][3][6][7]:

  • Civil Registry in Germany (Standesamt): Using the Spanish Multilingual Death Certificate (Fórmula C), you can notify the Standesamt of the deceased's last place of residence in Germany to update the municipal population register (Melderegister); you may also optionally apply for subsequent registration in the German death register (Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls im Ausland under § 36 of the Personenstandsgesetz) at the local German Standesamt or at Standesamt I in Berlin if the deceased never had a residence in Germany [2].
  • German pensions (Renten Service and Deutsche Rentenversicherung): If your family member received a German statutory pension, immediately notify Deutsche Post AG Niederlassung Renten Service (13496 Berlin; tel. +49 221 5692-777), enclosing a copy of the Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción to prevent overpayments (Sterbemonat) [6][7]. Also contact the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German Statutory Pension Insurance, toll-free within Germany: 0800 1000 4800) to apply - where there is an eligible surviving spouse, registered partner, or child - for the three-month death quarter advance (Sterbevierteljahr, within 30 days of death) and the survivor's or orphan's pension (Witwenrente, Witwerrente, or Waisenrente) [6][7].
  • Succession in Germany (Nachlassgericht) and in Spain (Últimas Voluntades and taxes): To access bank accounts or real estate located in Germany where no transmortal power of attorney or sufficient notarized German will exists, apply for a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession (Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis) from the competent German probate court (Nachlassgericht / Amtsgericht) [2]. If the deceased lived in Spain or owned assets in Spain, wait 15 working days after the death and apply to the Ministerio de Justicia using Modelo 790 (code 006) for the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Death Insurance Contracts to verify whether a will was made in Spain; note that Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be self-assessed within 6 months of death (with the option to request an extension within the first 5 months) [3].

es.title: Qué hacer cuando un ciudadano alemán fallece en España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Pasos oficiales tras el fallecimiento de un ciudadano alemán en España: Certificado Médico de Defunción (hospital o 112/Juzgado de Guardia), seguro y funeraria (PANASEF / Bestatter en Alemania), Registro Civil (Certificado Plurilingüe Fórmula C), traslado a Alemania (salvoconducto / Leichenpass) o entierro local, y Standesamt / Deutsche Rentenversicherung.
es.introHtml:
Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona de nacionalidad alemana fallece en España, es necesario coordinar los trámites médicos, sanitarios y registrales españoles con las normas consulares, funerarias, de pensiones y sucesorias de Alemania [1][2].

Dado que el deceso ha tenido lugar en España y la persona fallecida ostentaba la nacionalidad alemana, la certificación médica, la licencia de enterramiento o cremación y la inscripción civil inmediata se rigen por la legislación española, mientras que la recepción de los restos o cenizas, la baja de pensiones y el certificado sucesorio dependen del marco jurídico alemán [1][2][3]. El recorrido concreto varía según tres factores principales: si el fallecimiento ocurrió en un hospital o fuera de un centro sanitario (como un domicilio, hotel o vía pública), si la familia opta por la inhumación o cremación local en España o por la repatriación del féretro o de las cenizas a Alemania, y si su familiar tenía su residencia habitual en Alemania o residía de forma permanente en España [1][2][3].

steps.title: Obtención del Certificado Médico de Defunción y plazos sanitarios en España
steps.html:
El primer paso obligatorio en España es obtener el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial (impreso del Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos), indispensable para inscribir la muerte en el Registro Civil y movilizar el cuerpo [1][3]:

  • Fallecimiento en un hospital o clínica: Si su familiar falleció en un centro hospitalario por causas naturales diagnosticadas, el médico responsable expide directamente el Certificado Médico de Defunción [1][3]. Es importante entregar en el hospital el pasaporte o documento de identidad alemán (Personalausweis o Reisepass) y, si residía en España, el Certificado de Registro de Ciudadano de la Unión o número de NIE, para que los datos personales coincidan exactamente con la documentación alemana [1][3].
  • Fallecimiento en un domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Si el fallecimiento se produce fuera de un hospital, llame inmediatamente al teléfono de emergencias 112 [1][2]. Si el médico de urgencias puede certificar una causa natural acreditada mediante el historial clínico español, firmará el certificado médico; en cambio, si se trata de una muerte súbita, accidental, sin historial médico en España o de causa indeterminada, intervendrán las fuerzas policiales y el Juzgado de Guardia competente, que ordenará el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal para la práctica de la autopsia judicial antes de autorizar la inscripción en el Registro Civil y la entrega a la funeraria [1][2].
  • Plazos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Conforme a los reglamentos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria de las comunidades autónomas españolas (como Baleares, Canarias, Andalucía, Comunidad Valenciana, Cataluña o Madrid), el traslado a un tanatorio autorizado es inmediato y la inhumación, cremación o embalsamamiento suele efectuarse entre las 24 y las 48 horas posteriores al fallecimiento [1][4].

steps.title: Verificación de seguros, contratación de empresas funerarias y asistencia consular alemana
steps.html:
Antes de contratar por cuenta propia un servicio funerario, conviene verificar las pólizas de seguro y contactar con operadores acreditados en ambos países [1][2]:

  • Seguro de viaje o asistencia (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung): Compruebe si la persona fallecida disponía de un seguro médico de viaje alemán con cobertura de repatriación (Rücktransport im Todesfall), protección a través de clubes automovilísticos o tarjetas bancarias, o una póliza española de seguro de decesos [1][2]. Si existe cobertura, comuníquese con la central de emergencias 24 horas de la aseguradora antes de firmar compromisos particulares, ya que la compañía suele designar directamente a la funeraria internacional y cubrir los gastos autorizados [1][2].
  • Contratación de empresa funeraria en España y en Alemania: Si no hay seguro aplicable, deberá contratar una empresa funeraria autorizada en España, que puede localizar a través de la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (teléfono: +34 91 576 31 55; correo electrónico: info@panasef.com) [4]. Si desea trasladar el cuerpo o las cenizas a Alemania, la funeraria española deberá coordinarse con una funeraria receptora en Alemania (Bestatter) perteneciente al Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter (teléfono: +49 211 1600810; teléfono de emergencias: +49 211 1600886; correo electrónico: info@bestatter.de) [5]. Clarvia facilita información de directorios únicamente a título orientativo y no avala, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores funerarios concretos.
  • Orientación de las Representaciones Alemanas en España: Puede solicitar orientación consular y listados de funerarias, abogados y traductores ante la Embajada de la República Federal de Alemania en Madrid (Calle de Fortuny, 8, 28010 Madrid; teléfono de centralita: +34 91 557 9000; teléfono de emergencias consulares para la Península y Canarias: +34 661 611 104; teléfono de emergencias consulares para las Islas Baleares: +34 659 011 017) o ante los consulados alemanes en Barcelona, Málaga, Palma de Mallorca o Las Palmas de Gran Canaria [1][2].

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil español y obtención del Certificado Plurilingüe (Fórmula C)
steps.html:
El fallecimiento debe inscribirse en el Registro Civil del municipio español donde ocurrió el deceso, habitualmente dentro de las 24 horas siguientes y siempre antes de que se expida la licencia de enterramiento, incineración o traslado internacional [1][3]. Por regla general, la empresa funeraria española realiza este trámite presentando el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el documento de identidad o pasaporte alemán de su familiar [1][3].

Solicite a través de la funeraria o ante los servicios de registro civil del Ministerio de Justicia (teléfono de atención ciudadana: +34 91 837 22 95) dos certificaciones esenciales [3]:

  • Certificado Literal de Defunción: Necesario para la licencia funeraria y para cualquier gestión bancaria, notarial, fiscal o sucesoria en España [3].
  • Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C del Convenio de Viena de 1976): Tanto España como Alemania son Estados parte del Convenio de la CIEC n.º 16 de Viena, por lo que el extracto plurilingüe de defunción (Fórmula C / Internationale Sterbeurkunde) es reconocido directamente por los registros civiles (Standesämter), tribunales y cajas de pensiones en Alemania sin necesidad de apostilla ni traducción jurada [1][2][3]. Asimismo, en virtud del Reglamento (UE) 2016/1191, los documentos públicos de estado civil expedidos en España están exentos de apostilla en Alemania [2][3].

steps.title: Inhumación o cremación local en España frente a repatriación del féretro o de las cenizas a Alemania
steps.html:
La documentación sanitaria y de transporte varía según la modalidad elegida por la familia [1][2][4][5]:

  • Repatriación del cuerpo en féretro a Alemania: La empresa funeraria española gestiona el embalsamamiento o tanatopraxia reglamentaria, el acondicionamiento en un féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada, la autorización de Sanidad Exterior y la expedición del salvoconducto mortuorio internacional (Leichenpass), emitido conforme al Acuerdo de Berlín de 1937 y al Acuerdo de Estrasburgo sobre traslado de cadáveres [1][2][4]. La funeraria alemana receptora (Bestatter) recoge el féretro en el aeropuerto de destino en Alemania y tramita la inhumación o cremación ante el municipio alemán [5].
  • Cremación en España y traslado de las cenizas a Alemania (Urnenüberführung): Si se opta por la incineración en España, es fundamental tener en cuenta la obligación legal de cementerio vigente en la práctica totalidad de los estados federados alemanes (Friedhofszwang) [1][2][5]. A diferencia de otros países, en Alemania los particulares no están autorizados a conservar la urna funeraria en su domicilio ni a transportarla libremente en su equipaje para guardarla en casa: para enviar o trasladar la urna a Alemania, las autoridades y crematorios exigen presentar una confirmación de admisión (Übernahmebescheinigung) de un cementerio alemán (Friedhofsverwaltung) o de una empresa funeraria autorizada en Alemania (Bestatter), a quien se remite la urna sellada junto con el certificado de cremación y el Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción [1][2][5].
  • Inhumación o cremación definitiva en España: Si el entierro o el depósito de las cenizas se realiza íntegramente en un cementerio o columbario español, se aplican únicamente las tasas y licencias municipales españolas [3][4].

steps.title: Trámites posteriores de registro, pensiones y sucesiones en Alemania y en España
steps.html:
Una vez gestionado el servicio funerario o el traslado, deberán completarse las notificaciones administrativas y patrimoniales en ambos países [2][3][6][7]:

  • Registro Civil en Alemania (Standesamt): Con el Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción español (Fórmula C) puede notificar el fallecimiento al Standesamt del último domicilio en Alemania para actualizar el padrón municipal (Melderegister); también existe la posibilidad opcional de solicitar la inscripción posterior en el registro alemán de defunciones (Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls im Ausland, art. 36 de la Personenstandsgesetz) ante el Standesamt del domicilio en Alemania o ante el Standesamt I in Berlin si la persona fallecida nunca tuvo domicilio en Alemania [2].
  • Pensiones alemanas (Renten Service y Deutsche Rentenversicherung): Si su familiar percibía una pensión pública alemana, comunique inmediatamente el deceso a Deutsche Post AG Niederlassung Renten Service (13496 Berlin; teléfono: +49 221 5692-777) adjuntando copia del Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción para evitar cobros indebidos (Sterbemonat) [6][7]. Asimismo, contacte con la Deutsche Rentenversicherung (teléfono gratuito en Alemania: 0800 1000 4800) para tramitar, cuando exista cónyuge o pareja registrada sobreviviente o hijos con derecho, el anticipo del trimestre de defunción (Sterbevierteljahr, dentro de los 30 días siguientes al deceso) y la pensión de viudedad o de orfandad (Witwenrente, Witwerrente o Waisenrente) [6][7].
  • Sucesión en Alemania (Nachlassgericht) y en España (Últimas Voluntades e impuestos):
    • En Alemania: Para disponer de cuentas bancarias o inmuebles situados en Alemania cuando no exista un poder trans-mortem ni testamento notarial alemán suficiente, solicite el certificado sucesorio alemán (Erbschein) o el Certificado Sucesorio Europeo (Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis) ante el tribunal sucesorio competente (Nachlassgericht / Amtsgericht) [2].
    • En España (si la persona fallecida residía o poseía bienes en España): Transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la defunción, solicite ante el Ministerio de Justicia mediante el Modelo 790 (código 006) el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento para comprobar si otorgó testamento en España [3]. Tenga presente que el Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones en España debe autoliquidarse en el plazo de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (con posibilidad de solicitar una prórroga durante los primeros 5 meses) [3].

es.closingQuestion: Para orientarle con mayor precisión según su situación concreta, ¿en qué municipio y comunidad autónoma de España ocurrió el fallecimiento, tuvo lugar en un hospital o fuera de él, y su familiar residía habitualmente en Alemania o de forma permanente en España?

title: What to Do When a Portuguese Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Portuguese Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between France and Portugal: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a Portuguese national dies in France, the procedures involve both the local French authorities at the place of death and the Portuguese consular and civil registration authorities, whether the family chooses a funeral in France or the repatriation of the body or ashes to Portugal.

Here are the five essential steps to follow in chronological order:

steps.title: Medical certification of death in France (immediately)
steps.html:
The first step is to have a physician officially certify the death and issue the French medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, on the Cerfa paper form or electronically via CertDc), which is required for all funeral and administrative procedures [1]:

  • Death in a healthcare or medico-social facility (hospital, clinic, or EHPAD nursing home): The attending physician on the ward issues the medical certificate of death directly [1]. The facility keeps the deceased in its mortuary chamber and guides the family through the initial formalities.
  • Death at home, at a workplace, or in a public place: Immediately call the emergency medical service SAMU (15), the European emergency number (112), or an on-call doctor so a physician can attend in person to certify the death and complete the medical certificate [1]. If the body is to be transferred to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) before being placed in a coffin, the funeral director must file a prior declaration with the town hall (mairie) of the place of death, and the transfer must take place within 48 hours of death [5].
  • Medico-legal obstacle (obstacle médico-légal) or suspicious death: In the event of a sudden death, a workplace accident, or an unknown cause, the physician ticks the medico-legal obstacle box on the certificate. The police (police nationale) or gendarmerie and the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) then take over, and the body cannot be buried, cremated, or repatriated until judicial clearance is issued by the prosecutor's office (parquet) [1].

steps.title: Check insurance coverage and appoint a licensed funeral director
steps.html:
Before signing an estimate, check whether the deceased held funeral insurance, travel insurance, a Portuguese or French mutual health policy (mutuelle), or bank card assistance coverage that arranges and pays for international repatriation:

  • Appointing a funeral operator: International transport of a deceased person and prefectural permits must be handled by a licensed funeral company (entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée) in France, which will coordinate reception with a funeral agency legally registered in Portugal [5][6].
  • Official directories and professional bodies: Clarvia does not recommend, endorse, or rank commercial providers. To find a licensed funeral operator in France, you can consult the official register of licensed operators at the town hall (mairie) or prefecture of the place of death via Service-Public.fr [1], or contact the national trade federations: the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (French National Funeral Federation, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [10] and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (French Federation of Funeral Directors, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [11]. In Portugal, funeral providers are regulated by the Directorate-General for Economic Activities (Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) through the official gov.pt portal [6].

steps.title: Declare the death at the French town hall (*mairie*) within 24 hours
steps.html:
Under official rules published on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical certification (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the civil status office (service d'état civil) of the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred [1]:

  • Who declares the death: Any relative or the funeral company authorised by the family may make the declaration [1].
  • Documents to present: The medical certificate of death, proof of identity of the informant, and the civil status documents of the deceased (Portuguese citizen card Cartão de Cidadão or passport, birth or marriage certificate, and family record book livret de famille) [1].
  • Certificates to request: Request several full copies of the French death certificate (acte de décès intégral) as well as several multilingual death certificate extracts on Form C (extrait d'acte de décès plurilingue - Formule C) issued under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [1][2]. Because both France and Portugal are parties to this convention and subject to Regulation (EU) 2016/1191, the multilingual extract is directly recognised by Portuguese authorities without an Apostille or certified translation [2].

steps.title: Choose between a funeral in France and repatriation to Portugal, and register the death with Portuguese authorities
steps.html:
Depending on the wishes of the deceased and the family's decision, two main pathways apply:

  • Option A - Burial or cremation in France: Burial or cremation in France must take place no earlier than 24 hours after death and no later than 14 calendar days starting the day after death (prefectural extensions remain possible in special circumstances) [4]. The authorisation to close the coffin (autorisation de fermeture du cercueil) and the burial or cremation permit are issued by the mayor of the municipality of death [1][4].
  • Option B - Repatriation of the body or ashes to Portugal:
    • Prefectural mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire): To transport the body out of metropolitan France, the funeral operator applies for a mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) from the prefect (préfet) of the department where the coffin is sealed [5]. Because both France and Portugal are signatories to the Strasbourg Agreement of 26 October 1973 on the Transfer of Corpses, this international mortuary transit permit authorises entry of the body into Portugal. The body must be placed in a compliant hermetically sealed coffin (with a sealed metal liner and embalming care depending on air or road transport) in the presence of a public official [5].
    • Repatriation of a cinerary urn: If cremation takes place in France prior to departure, international transport of the ashes in a sealed urn also requires a prefectural ash transport permit accompanied by the death certificate and cremation certificate [5].
    • Registration and transcription of the death with Portuguese authorities: The death of a Portuguese citizen in France must be registered in the Portuguese civil registry (registo de óbito) [2]. This registration is free of charge and can be completed at the territorially competent Portuguese consulate in France (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux, or Strasbourg) or directly in Portugal at any civil registry office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) under the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary Services, phone +351 211 950 500) [2][7]. For the Paris consular district and consular emergencies, you can contact the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Paris (Consulate General of Portugal in Paris, phone +33 1 73 01 16 80, weekend and holiday consular emergency line +33 6 95 83 57 11, email cgparis@mne.pt) as well as the Centro de Atendimento Consular (Consular Assistance Centre, phone +33 1 73 01 16 80) [2][3][12].

steps.title: Administrative, social security, banking, and estate formalities in both countries
steps.html:
Once the French death certificate and its Portuguese transcription have been obtained, several institutions must be notified in France and Portugal:

  • Portuguese social security benefits and bereavement grants: If the deceased was covered by the Portuguese social security system, family members can apply to Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, phone +351 210 545 400 or +351 300 502 502) [8][9]:
    • Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (reimbursement of funeral expenses to the person who proves payment), which must be claimed within 90 consecutive days of the date of death when there is no beneficiary entitled to the subsídio por morte [9].
    • Subsídio por Morte (lump-sum death grant paid to an eligible spouse, de facto partner, or descendants), which must be claimed within 180 days from the registration of the death, along with a survivor's pension (pensão de sobrevivência) [8].
  • French health insurance and pension funds: If the deceased worked, resided, or received a pension in France, notify the local health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM, for any statutory lump-sum death benefit capital décès and reimbursement of final medical expenses), the basic pension fund Assurance Retraite (phone +33 9 71 10 39 60 or 3960 within France), and supplementary pension schemes (Agirc-Arrco) [1][13].
  • Banks, taxation, and cross-border succession (EU Regulation No 650/2012): Notify French and Portuguese banks (presenting the death certificate freezes sole accounts pending estate settlement, while in France funeral expenses up to the statutory cap may be paid directly from the deceased's account upon presentation of the invoice) [1]. In Portugal, the death must be reported to the tax authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira) before the end of the third month following the death, and heirs formalise the declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) via an Espaço Óbito or Balcão das Heranças desk of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [7]. If the deceased owned real estate or resided in France, you can instruct a French notary office through Notaires de France (Chamber of French Notaries, phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [14].

fr.title: Que faire lorsqu'un citoyen portugais décède en France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Étapes officielles lors du décès d'un ressortissant portugais en France : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire en France et agence funéraire au Portugal, déclaration en mairie dans les 24 heures (acte plurilingue Formule C), laissez-passer préfectoral et consulat du Portugal pour le rapatriement ou les obsèques, et démarches Segurança Social / retraite.
fr.introHtml:
Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne de nationalité portugaise décède en France, les démarches s'articulent entre les autorités locales françaises du lieu du décès et les autorités consulaires et civiles portugaises, que la famille opte pour des obsèques en France ou pour un rapatriement du corps ou des cendres vers le Portugal.

Voici les étapes essentielles à suivre par ordre chronologique :

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et certificat médical en France (immédiatement)
steps.html:
La première démarche consiste à faire constater officiellement le décès par un médecin afin d'établir le certificat médical de décès (modèle Cerfa ou voie électronique CertDc), document indispensable pour toute opération funéraire et administrative [1] :

  • Décès dans un établissement de santé ou médico-social (hôpital, clinique, EHPAD) : Le médecin du service établit directement le certificat médical de décès [1]. L'établissement assure la conservation du corps en chambre mortuaire et vous accompagne pour les premières formalités.
  • Décès à domicile, sur le lieu de travail ou sur la voie publique : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU (15), le numéro d'urgence européen (112) ou un médecin de garde afin qu'un praticien se déplace pour constater le décès et rédiger le certificat [1]. Si le corps doit être transféré vers une chambre funéraire avant la mise en bière, l'opérateur funéraire doit effectuer une déclaration préalable auprès de la mairie du lieu de décès, et ce transfert doit intervenir dans un délai de 48 heures suivant le décès [5].
  • Obstacle médico-légal ou mort suspecte : En cas de décès soudain, d'accident du travail ou de cause inconnue, le médecin coche la case relative à l'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat. La police ou la gendarmerie ainsi que le procureur de la République prennent alors le relais, et le corps ne peut être inhumé, incinéré ni rapatrié avant la délivrance d'une autorisation judiciaire du parquet [1].

steps.title: Vérification des assurances et choix d'un opérateur funéraire habilité
steps.html:
Avant de signer un devis, vérifiez si la personne décédée disposait d'une assurance obsèques, d'une assurance voyage, d'une mutuelle portugaise ou française ou d'une garantie d'assistance liée à une carte bancaire prenant en charge l'organisation et les frais de rapatriement international :

  • Mandater un opérateur funéraire : Le transport international d'un défunt et les formalités préfectorales doivent obligatoirement être confiés à une entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée en France, qui coordonnera l'arrivée avec une agence funéraire légalement enregistrée au Portugal [5][6].
  • Organismes professionnels de référence : Clarvia ne recommande, ne cautionne ni ne classe aucun prestataire commercial. Pour identifier une entreprise habilitée en France, vous pouvez consulter la liste officielle des opérateurs funéraires auprès de la mairie ou de la préfecture du lieu de décès via Service-Public.fr [1], ou contacter les fédérations professionnelles du secteur : la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (téléphone +33 1 55 43 30 00, courriel contact@federation-fnf.fr) [10] et la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (téléphone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [11]. Au Portugal, l'exercice de l'activité funéraire est encadré par la Direction générale des activités économiques (Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) via le portail officiel gov.pt [6].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès à la mairie en France (dans les 24 heures)
steps.html:
Selon les règles officielles publiées sur Service-Public.fr, le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures suivant sa constatation (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès du service d'état civil de la mairie de la commune où le décès a eu lieu [1] :

  • Qui déclare le décès : Tout proche ou l'entreprise de pompes funèbres mandatée par la famille peut effectuer cette déclaration [1].
  • Pièces à présenter : Le certificat médical de décès, une pièce d'identité du déclarant et les documents d'état civil de la personne décédée (Cartão de Cidadão ou passeport portugais, acte de naissance ou de mariage, livret de famille) [1].
  • Actes à demander : Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès français ainsi que plusieurs extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues (Formule C) délivrés en application de la Convention de Vienne de 1976 [1][2]. La France et le Portugal étant tous deux parties à cette convention ainsi qu'au Règlement (UE) 2016/1191, l'extrait plurilingue est directement reconnu par les autorités portugaises sans apostille ni traduction assermentée [2].

steps.title: Choix entre obsèques en France et rapatriement vers le Portugal, et enregistrement consulaire
steps.html:
Selon les volontés de la personne décédée et le choix de la famille, deux parcours s'offrent à vous :

  • Option A - Inhumation ou crémation en France : L'inhumation ou la crémation en France doit avoir lieu au plus tôt 24 heures après le décès et au plus tard dans un délai de 14 jours calendaires suivant le lendemain du décès (des dérogations préfectorales restent possibles en cas de circonstances particulières) [4]. L'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil et le permis d'inhumer ou l'autorisation de crémation sont délivrés par le maire de la commune du décès [1][4].
  • Option B - Rapatriement du corps ou des cendres vers le Portugal :
    • Laissez-passer mortuaire préfectoral : Pour le transport du corps hors de France métropolitaine, l'entreprise funéraire sollicite un laissez-passer mortuaire auprès du préfet du département où a lieu la fermeture du cercueil [5]. La France et le Portugal étant tous deux signataires de l'Accord de Strasbourg du 26 octobre 1973 sur le transfert des corps des personnes décédées, ce laissez-passer mortuaire international permet l'entrée du corps au Portugal. Le corps doit être placé dans un cercueil hermétique réglementaire (avec enveloppe métallique scellée et soins de conservation selon le mode de transport aérien ou routier) en présence d'un représentant de l'autorité publique [5].
    • Rapatriement d'une urne cinéraire : Si la crémation a lieu en France avant le départ, le transport international des cendres dans une urne scellée requiert également une autorisation préfectorale de transport de cendres accompagnée de l'acte de décès et du certificat de crémation [5].
    • Déclaration et transcription de l'acte de décès auprès des autorités portugaises : Le décès d'un citoyen portugais survenu en France doit obligatoirement être enregistré à l'état civil portugais (registo de óbito) [2]. Cette démarche est gratuite et peut être effectuée auprès du consulat portugais territorialement compétent en France (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux ou Strasbourg) ou directement au Portugal auprès de n'importe quel bureau d'état civil (Conservatória do Registo Civil) relevant de l'Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (téléphone +351 211 950 500) [2][7]. Pour la circonscription de Paris et les urgences consulaires, vous pouvez contacter le Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Paris (téléphone +33 1 73 01 16 80, urgence consulaire week-ends et jours fériés +33 6 95 83 57 11, courriel cgparis@mne.pt) ainsi que le Centro de Atendimento Consular (téléphone +33 1 73 01 16 80) [2][3][12].

steps.title: Démarches administratives, sociales, bancaires et successorales dans les deux pays
steps.html:
Une fois l'acte de décès français et sa transcription portugaise obtenus, plusieurs organismes doivent être informés en France et au Portugal :

  • Prestations sociales et aides au décès au Portugal : Si la personne décédée relevait du régime portugais de protection sociale, les proches peuvent solliciter auprès de la Segurança Social (téléphone +351 210 545 400 ou +351 300 502 502) [8][9] :
    • Le Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (remboursement des frais d'obsèques à la personne qui justifie les avoir payés), à demander dans un délai de 90 jours consécutifs à compter du décès lorsqu'il n'y a pas de bénéficiaire du subsídio por morte [9].
    • Le Subsídio por Morte (allocation de décès versée au conjoint, partenaire de fait ou descendants éligibles), à demander dans un délai de 180 jours à compter de l'enregistrement du décès, ainsi que la pension de survie (pensão de sobrevivência) [8].
  • Protection sociale et retraites en France : Si la personne décédée travaillait, résidait ou percevait une pension en France, informez la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, pour le versement d'un éventuel capital décès et le remboursement des derniers frais de santé), la caisse de retraite de base Assurance Retraite (téléphone +33 9 71 10 39 60 ou le 3960 depuis la France) et les caisses complémentaires (Agirc-Arrco) [1][13].
  • Banques, fiscalité et succession (Règlement UE n° 650/2012) : Informez les établissements bancaires français et portugais (la présentation de l'acte de décès entraîne le blocage des comptes individuels jusqu'au règlement de la succession, tout en permettant le prélèvement des frais d'obsèques sur justificatif dans la limite réglementaire en France) [1]. Au Portugal, le décès doit être déclaré à l'administration fiscale (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira) avant la fin du 3e mois suivant le décès, et les héritiers procèdent à l'habilitação de herdeiros via un guichet Espaço Óbito ou Balcão das Heranças de l'Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [7]. Si la personne décédée possédait des biens immobiliers ou résidait en France, vous pouvez solliciter un office notarial via le réseau des Notaires de France (téléphone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [14].

title: What to Do When a Polish Citizen Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Polish Citizen Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Germany and Poland: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a Polish citizen dies in Germany, the German regulations of the place of death interact with Polish consular and civil registration rules. This applies both when arranging a burial or cremation in Germany and when repatriating the body or urn to Poland.

Below are the five essential steps in chronological order:

steps.title: Medical examination of the body and death certificate in Germany (immediately)
steps.html:
First, a physician must officially examine the deceased (ärztliche Leichenschau) and issue the German medical certificate of death (Todesbescheinigung or Totenschein, comprising a confidential medical section and a non-confidential section) [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, nursing home, or hospice: The facility arranges the medical examination and issuance of the death certificate on site and provides initial care in its mortuary cooling room [1][2].
  • Death in a private home, at work, or in a public place: Immediately contact the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst, nationwide number 116 117), emergency services (112), or the family doctor so the examination can be performed [2]. A funeral director may only collect the deceased and transfer them to a mortuary once the medical certificate of death has been issued.
  • Unexplained or non-natural cause of death: If the physician records an unexplained or non-natural manner of death (such as a sudden death or a workplace or traffic accident), the police and public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) are notified. In such cases, cremation, burial, or international repatriation cannot proceed until the public prosecutor's office issues a written release [1][4].

steps.title: Check insurance coverage and appoint a licensed funeral director
steps.html:
Before signing contracts, check whether the deceased held travel health insurance, accident or repatriation insurance, a Polish or German funeral insurance policy, or breakdown/assistance cover that pays for international repatriation costs:

  • Coordination between Germany and Poland: For international repatriation to Poland, you can instruct either a licensed funeral director in Germany or a Polish funeral company (zakład pogrzebowy) specialising in international repatriations, which will handle the formalities with the German authorities, the Polish consulate, and the Polish county administration [2][4].
  • Neutral professional directories: Clarvia does not recommend, endorse, or rank commercial providers. You can locate a qualified funeral director in Germany through the German funeral association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Federal Association of German Undertakers, phone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour helpline +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de) [2]. In Poland, you can search for a licensed funeral company through the Polish funeral industry chamber Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej (Polish Chamber of the Funeral Industry, phone +48 798 198 997, email biuro@polskaizbabranzypogrzebowej.com) [3].

steps.title: Register the death at the German civil registry office (*Standesamt*) within 3 working days
steps.html:
Under Section 28 of the German Civil Status Act (Personenstandsgesetz - PStG), a death in Germany must be reported to the civil registry office (Standesamt) of the place of death no later than the third working day following the death [1]:

  • Who reports the death: When a death occurs in a hospital or nursing home, the facility usually submits the written notification; otherwise, the funeral director appointed by the family registers the death with the Standesamt [1][2].
  • Required documents: You must present the medical certificate of death, the deceased's Polish national identity card (dowód osobisty) or passport, and civil status records (birth certificate and, where applicable, marriage certificate or proof of dissolution of marriage) [1].
  • Multilingual death certificate (Form C): In addition to several German death certificates (Sterbeurkunden), be sure to request multilingual extracts from the death register on Form C (mehrsprachiger Auszug auf Formblatt C) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [4][6]. Because both Germany and Poland are contracting states to this convention and EU Regulation 2016/1191 also applies, the international death certificate (Form C) is directly recognised in Poland without an Apostille or certified translation [4][6].

steps.title: Choose between burial/cremation in Germany and repatriation to Poland
steps.html:
Depending on the wishes of the deceased and the family, there are two main options:

  • Option A - Burial or cremation in Germany: If the funeral takes place in Germany, the minimum waiting period (typically 48 hours after death) and the statutory burial deadline are governed by the burial act (Bestattungsgesetz) of the relevant German federal state (Bundesland) [2]. For cremation in Germany, almost all federal states require a second medical examination (zweite Leichenschau) at the crematorium [2].
  • Option B - Repatriation of the body or urn to Poland: Repatriating human remains or ashes to Poland requires a multi-stage permit procedure between Polish and German authorities [4]:
    • Permit from the Polish County Governor or City President (pozwolenie starosty lub prezydenta miasta): First, an application must be submitted to the County Governor (Starosta) or City President (Prezydent miasta) competent for the intended burial place in Poland to authorise the import and burial of the body or ashes (this is usually handled by the instructed funeral company on the family's behalf) [4].
    • Polish Consular Certificate (zaświadczenie konsula): Once the permit from the Polish Starosta or Prezydent miasta and the German death certificate (or an interim certificate of deferred registration from the Standesamt) have been obtained, the consular repatriation certificate is issued by the Consular Section of the Botschaft der Republik Polen in Berlin (Embassy of the Republic of Poland in Berlin, phone +49 30 22 313 0, email berlin.konsul@msz.gov.pl) or by the territorially competent Polish Consulate General in Hamburg, Cologne, or Munich [4][5]. Due to urgency, no prior appointment in the e-Konsulat system is required for death repatriation matters; the consular fee is 50 EUR [4].
    • German corpse transit permit (Leichenpass) or urn certificate: For cross-border transport of a body, the competent German authority at the place of death (public order office Ordnungsamt, Standesamt, or health authority Gesundheitsamt) issues a multilingual Leichenpass on the basis of the medical death certificate and civil death certificate; the body must be placed in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin in accordance with regulations [2][4]. If cremation takes place in Germany followed by transport of the urn to Poland, you will need the death certificate, the cremation certificate from the German crematorium (Urnenbescheinigung), the permit from the Polish Starosta, and the Polish consular certificate [4].

steps.title: Civil registry transcription, Polish funeral grant (*zasiłek pogrzebowy*), pensions, and estate
steps.html:
Once the initial repatriation or funeral arrangements are underway, the following administrative steps apply in Poland and Germany:

  • Transcription of the death certificate in Poland (transkrypcja aktu zgonu): Prior transcription is not mandatory simply to obtain the consular repatriation permit [4][6]. However, for subsequent inheritance, banking, and administrative proceedings in Poland, the German death certificate must be transcribed into the Polish civil status register [6]. The application can be filed at any civil registry office (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego - USC) in Poland (administrative fee of 50 PLN) or through a Polish consulate in Germany [6].
  • Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy) and survivor's pension (renta rodzinna): If funeral and repatriation costs were paid by family members or other parties and the deceased (or an applying family member) was covered by Polish pension or social insurance, you can apply to the Polish Social Insurance Institution, Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (Customer Contact Centre CKK at phone +48 22 560 16 00, email cot@zus.pl), for the Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy, form Z-12) [7][8]. The application deadline is 12 months from the date of death (or from the date of burial if identification or repatriation was delayed) [7]. Eligible survivors can also apply there for a Polish family survivor's pension (renta rodzinna) [9].
  • Notification of German pension authorities, health insurance, banks, and estate settlement: If the deceased worked, lived, or received a statutory pension in Germany, report the death with the death certificate to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German Statutory Pension Insurance, toll-free within Germany 0800 1000 4800 or +49 30 865 0 from abroad) [10] or through the Renten Service der Deutschen Post (Pension Service of Deutsche Post, phone +49 221 569 2777) to stop ongoing payments and, where applicable, apply for the three-month survivor transition payment (Sterbevierteljahr) or a widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension [10][11]. Also notify health insurers and banks in Germany and Poland; the transcribed death certificate is required to settle the estate (poświadczenie dziedziczenia before a Polish notary or a judicial certificate of inheritance under EU Succession Regulation No 650/2012) [6].

closingQuestion: To tailor this guidance to your situation: in which German federal state (Bundesland) did the death occur, and are you planning a coffin repatriation or an urn transport to Poland?

de.title: Was tun, wenn ein polnischer Staatsangehöriger in Deutschland stirbt: Offizielle Checkliste in 5 Schritten
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Anleitung nach dem Tod eines polnischen Staatsangehörigen in Deutschland: ärztliche Leichenschau & Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Polen, Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) beim Standesamt, Leichenpass & Genehmigung des polnischen Starosta / Konsulats für die Überführung nach Polen sowie ZUS (zasiłek pogrzebowy) und Deutsche Rentenversicherung.
de.introHtml:
Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit polnischer Staatsangehörigkeit in Deutschland verstirbt, greifen die deutschen Vorschriften des Sterbeortes und die polnischen konsularischen sowie personenstandsrechtlichen Bestimmungen ineinander. Dies gilt sowohl bei einer Bestattung in Deutschland als auch bei einer Überführung des Leichnams oder der Urne nach Polen.

Nachfolgend finden Sie die wesentlichen Schritte in chronologischer Reihenfolge:

steps.title: Ärztliche Leichenschau und Todesbescheinigung in Deutschland (unmittelbar)
steps.html:
Der Tod muss zunächst durch eine Ärztin oder einen Arzt im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Leichenschau festgestellt werden, damit die amtliche Todesbescheinigung (Totenschein mit vertraulichem und nicht-vertraulichem Teil) ausgestellt wird [1][2]:

  • Sterbefall im Krankenhaus, Pflegeheim oder Hospiz: Die Einrichtung veranlasst die ärztliche Leichenschau sowie die Ausstellung der Todesbescheinigung direkt vor Ort und übernimmt die erste Versorgung in der hauseigenen Kühlkammer [1][2].
  • Sterbefall in einer Privatwohnung, am Arbeitsplatz oder in der Öffentlichkeit: Verständigen Sie umgehend den ärztlichen Bereitschaftsdienst (bundesweite Rufnummer 116 117), den Rettungsdienst (Notruf 112) oder die Hausärztin bzw. den Hausarzt, um die Leichenschau durchzuführen [2]. Erst nach Vorliegen der ärztlichen Todesbescheinigung darf ein Bestattungsunternehmen die verstorbene Person abholen und in eine Leichenhalle überführen.
  • Ungeklärte oder nicht-natürliche Todesursache: Bescheinigt der Arzt eine ungeklärte oder nicht-natürliche Todesart (etwa bei einem plötzlichen Todesfall oder einem Arbeits- bzw. Verkehrsunfall), werden Polizei und Staatsanwaltschaft eingeschaltet. In diesem Fall dürfen weder eine Einäscherung noch eine Bestattung oder Auslandsüberführung stattfinden, bevor die schriftliche staatsanwaltschaftliche Freigabe vorliegt [1][4].

steps.title: Prüfung von Versicherungen und Beauftragung eines Bestattungsunternehmens
steps.html:
Bevor Sie Aufträge erteilen, prüfen Sie, ob für die verstorbene Person eine Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung, eine Unfall- oder Rückholversicherung, eine polnische oder deutsche Sterbegeldversicherung oder ein Schutzbrief bestand, der die Überführungskosten übernimmt:

  • Koordination zwischen Deutschland und Polen: Für eine internationale Überführung nach Polen können Sie entweder ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland oder direkt ein auf internationale Überführungen spezialisiertes polnisches Bestattungsunternehmen (zakład pogrzebowy) beauftragen, das die Formalitäten bei den deutschen Behörden, dem polnischen Konsulat und der polnischen Kreisverwaltung erledigt [2][4].
  • Neutrale Berufsverbände: Clarvia spricht keine Empfehlungen für kommerzielle Anbieter aus und nimmt keine Bewertungen oder Rankings vor. Ein qualifiziertes Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland finden Sie über den deutschen Berufsverband Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Telefon +49 211 16008-10, 24-Stunden-Notfallnummer +49 211 16008-86, E-Mail info@bestatter.de) [2]. In Polen können Sie sich zur Suche nach einem zugelassenen Bestattungsunternehmen an den polnischen Branchenverband Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej (Telefon +48 798 198 997, E-Mail biuro@polskaizbabranzypogrzebowej.com) wenden [3].

steps.title: Anzeige des Sterbefalls beim deutschen Standesamt (spätestens am dritten Werktag)
steps.html:
Nach § 28 des deutschen Personenstandsgesetzes (PStG) muss der Sterbefall spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag beim Standesamt des deutschen Sterbeortes angezeigt werden [1]:

  • Anzeigepflichtige Stellen: Bei einem Tod im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim erfolgt die schriftliche Anzeige in der Regel durch die Einrichtung; andernfalls übernimmt das von der Familie beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen die Meldung beim Standesamt [1][2].
  • Erforderliche Unterlagen: Vorzulegen sind die ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, der polnische Personalausweis (dowód osobisty) oder Reisepass der verstorbenen Person sowie Personenstandsurkunden (Geburtsurkunde, gegebenenfalls Heiratsurkunde oder Nachweis über die Auflösung einer Ehe) [1].
  • Mehrsprachige Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C): Beantragen Sie beim deutschen Standesamt neben mehreren deutschen Sterbeurkunden unbedingt auch mehrsprachige Auszüge aus dem Sterbeeintrag auf Formblatt C gemäß dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen vom 8. September 1976 [4][6]. Da sowohl Deutschland als auch Polen Vertragsstaaten dieses Übereinkommens sind und zudem die EU-Verordnung 2016/1191 gilt, wird die internationale Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) in Polen direkt ohne Apostille und ohne vereidigte Übersetzung anerkannt [4][6].

steps.title: Wahl zwischen Bestattung in Deutschland und Überführung nach Polen
steps.html:
Je nach Wunsch der Familie und den Verfügungen der verstorbenen Person bestehen zwei Wege:

  • Option A - Erdbestattung oder Feuerbestattung in Deutschland: Erfolgt die Bestattung in Deutschland, richten sich die Wartefrist (in der Regel frühestens 48 Stunden nach Eintritt des Todes) und die Bestattungsfrist nach dem jeweiligen Landesbestattungsgesetz des deutschen Bundeslandes [2]. Für eine Feuerbestattung in Deutschland ist in fast allen Bundesländern eine zweite ärztliche Leichenschau im Krematorium vorgeschrieben [2].
  • Option B - Überführung des Leichnams oder der Urne nach Polen: Für die Rückführung nach Polen ist ein mehrstufiges Genehmigungsverfahren zwischen den polnischen und deutschen Behörden vorgeschrieben [4]:

1. Genehmigung des polnischen Landrats oder Stadtpräsidenten (pozwolenie starosty lub prezydenta miasta): Zunächst muss bei dem für den geplanten Bestattungsort in Polen zuständigen Landrat (Starosta) oder Stadtpräsidenten (Prezydent miasta) die Genehmigung zur Bestattung und Einfuhr des Leichnams bzw. der Asche beantragt werden (dies erledigt meist das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen im Namen der Angehörigen) [4]. 2. Konsularische Bescheinigung (zaświadczenie konsula): Mit der Genehmigung des polnischen Landrats bzw. Stadtpräsidenten und der deutschen Sterbeurkunde (oder einer vorläufigen Bescheinigung des Standesamtes über die Zurückstellung der Sterbeurkunde) wird die konsularische Überführungsbescheinigung durch die Konsularabteilung der Botschaft der Republik Polen in Berlin (Telefon +49 30 22 313 0, E-Mail berlin.konsul@msz.gov.pl) oder durch das territorial zuständige polnische Generalkonsulat in Hamburg, Köln oder München ausgestellt [4][5]. Aufgrund der Eilbedürftigkeit ist für Sterbefallangelegenheiten keine Terminbuchung im System e-Konsulat erforderlich; die Konsulargebühr beträgt 50 EUR [4]. 3. Deutscher Leichenpass bzw. Urnenbescheinigung: Für den grenzüberschreitenden Leichentransport stellt die zuständige deutsche Behörde des Sterbeortes (Ordnungsamt, Standesamt oder Gesundheitsamt) auf Grundlage der Todesbescheinigung und der Sterbeurkunde einen mehrsprachigen Leichenpass aus; der Leichnam muss hierfür vorschriftsgemäß in einem verlöteten Zinksarg (bzw. Sarg mit Metalleinsatz) eingesargt werden [2][4]. Bei einer Einäscherung in Deutschland und anschließender Überführung der Urne nach Polen werden die Sterbeurkunde, die Einäscherungsbescheinigung des deutschen Krematoriums (Urnenbescheinigung), die Genehmigung des polnischen Landrats und die konsularische Bescheinigung benötigt [4].

steps.title: Standesamtliche Transkription, Bestattungsgeld (*zasiłek pogrzebowy*), Renten und Nachlass
steps.html:
Nach Abschluss der ersten Überführungs- oder Bestattungsschritte stehen in Polen und Deutschland folgende behördliche Meldungen an:

  • Transkription der Sterbeurkunde in Polen (transkrypcja aktu zgonu): Für die konsularische Überführungsgenehmigung ist die vorherige Transkription noch nicht zwingend erforderlich [4][6]. Für spätere Nachlass-, Bank- und Behördenverfahren in Polen muss die deutsche Sterbeurkunde jedoch in das polnische Personenstandsregister übertragen werden [6]. Der Antrag kann bei jedem beliebigen Standesamt (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego - USC) in Polen (Verwaltungsgebühr 50 PLN) oder über das polnische Konsulat in Deutschland eingereicht werden [6].
  • Polnisches Bestattungsgeld (zasiłek pogrzebowy) und Hinterbliebenenrente (renta rodzinna): Wurden die Bestattungs- und Überführungskosten von Familienangehörigen oder Dritten getragen und war die verstorbene Person (oder ein antragstellender Angehöriger) in Polen renten- oder sozialversichert, kann bei der polnischen Sozialversicherungsanstalt (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych, Kundenkontaktzentrum CKK unter Telefon +48 22 560 16 00, E-Mail cot@zus.pl) das Bestattungsgeld (zasiłek pogrzebowy auf Formular Z-12) beantragt werden [7][8]. Die Antragsfrist beträgt 12 Monate ab dem Todestag (bzw. ab dem Tag der Bestattung, falls sich die Identifizierung oder Überführung verzögert hat) [7]. Ebenso prüfen Hinterbliebene dort Ansprüche auf eine polnische Hinterbliebenenrente (renta rodzinna) [9].
  • Meldung an deutsche Rentenstellen, Krankenkasse, Banken und Nachlassregelung: Falls die verstorbene Person in Deutschland gearbeitet, gelebt oder eine deutsche Rente bezogen hat, melden Sie den Sterbefall unter Vorlage der Sterbeurkunde an die Deutsche Rentenversicherung (kostenfreie Servicenummer 0800 1000 4800 aus Deutschland bzw. +49 30 865 0 aus dem Ausland) [10] oder über den Renten Service der Deutschen Post (Telefon +49 221 569 2777) zur Einstellung der Zahlungen und eventuellen Beantragung des Sterbevierteljahres bzw. einer Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente [10][11]. Informieren Sie zudem die Krankenversicherung sowie Banken in Deutschland und Polen; für die Regelung der Erbfolge (poświadczenie dziedziczenia beim polnischen Notar oder gerichtlicher Erbschein nach der EU-Erbrechtsverordnung Nr. 650/2012) ist die transkribierte Sterbeurkunde maßgeblich [6].

title: What to Do When an Indian Citizen Dies in Saudi Arabia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When an Indian Citizen Dies in Saudi Arabia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official steps when an Indian national dies in Saudi Arabia: Ministry of Health death report & police/forensic clearance, family Power of Attorney & Indian Community Welfare Wing assistance (Riyadh/Jeddah), Ahwal Madaniyah civil death certificate & exit clearance, Embassy/Consulate NOC for repatriation to India or local burial, and eMigrate / PBBY / EPFO claims.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When an Indian national passes away in Saudi Arabia, procedures require coordination between the employer or sponsor (Kafeel), Saudi medical and civil authorities, and the Indian diplomatic mission. Below is the official 5-step checklist to guide you and your family through the required formalities.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Death Notification and Saudi Police Report
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital: When your family member dies of natural causes in a Saudi hospital, the attending physician issues the electronic Medical Death Notification (Tabligh Wafat) directly through the Ministry of Health system linked to the Civil Status Agency (Ahwal Madaniyah), and the body is placed in the hospital mortuary [1][3][5].
  • Death outside a hospital, at a workplace, or in a road accident: Call the Saudi Unified Emergency Operations Number (911 in Riyadh, Makkah, and the Eastern Province, or 999 in other regions) immediately. Saudi Police will attend the scene, open a mandatory investigation, and transfer the deceased to a government forensic medical facility for post-mortem examination if the death was accidental, work-related, or sudden [2][3][5].
  • Police clearance: In all non-hospital, traffic accident, or unnatural death cases, the investigating police station (Shurta) must issue an official Police Report and forensic clearance explicitly permitting either local burial in Saudi Arabia or repatriation of the mortal remains to India before any civil or consular registration can proceed [2][3][5].

steps.title: Issue a Family Power of Attorney (Wakala) and Notify the Indian Mission
steps.html:
• Execute a Power of Attorney (Wakala) from India: If the next of kin resides in India, Saudi regulations require the legal heirs to issue a notarized Power of Attorney (Consent Letter or Wakala) naming a representative in Saudi Arabia (typically the employer/sponsor Kafeel, a relative, or an authorized community welfare volunteer) to complete local formalities and stating clearly whether the family requests air repatriation to India or local burial in Saudi Arabia [3][5].
  • Attestation and submission: Have the Power of Attorney notarized in India and email a clear scanned copy (along with copies of the deceased's Indian passport, Saudi residency permit Iqama, and next-of-kin identification) to the relevant Indian diplomatic mission so it can issue an introductory facilitation letter to Saudi authorities [3][5].
  • Contact the competent Indian diplomatic mission by region:
    • Central, Eastern, and Northern Saudi Arabia: Contact the Embassy of India, Riyadh (Death Registration email: dr.riyad@mea.gov.in, Community Welfare email: cw.riyadh@mea.gov.in, telephone: +966 11 488 4144 ext. 119 / 110 / 325, 24x7 Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra helpline: +966 11 488 4697, toll-free within Saudi Arabia: 800 247 1234, WhatsApp: +966 542126748) [3][4].
    • Western and Southern Saudi Arabia (including Jeddah, Makkah, Madinah, Taif, Tabuk, Abha, Jazan, and Najran): Contact the Consulate General of India, Jeddah (Community Welfare email: conscw.jeddah@mea.gov.in or vccw.jeddah@mea.gov.in, telephone: +966 12 284 6130, 24x7 emergency mobile and WhatsApp: +966 556122301, toll-free: 800 244 0003) [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with Saudi Civil Affairs (Ahwal Madaniyah) and Obtain Jawazat Clearance
steps.html:
• Saudi Civil Death Certificate: Using the hospital death notification, police clearance (if applicable), the original Indian passport, the original Saudi residency permit (Iqama), and the attested Power of Attorney, the authorized representative books an appointment via the Absher platform with the Saudi Civil Affairs Directorate (Ahwal Madaniyah) to obtain the official Saudi Death Certificate and its attested English translation [1][3][5].
  • Employer end-of-service clearance: Under Saudi Labor Law, the employer or sponsor (Kafeel) is responsible for settling the deceased worker's unpaid wages, accrued leave, and statutory End-of-Service Benefit (ESB), and for bearing the cost of preparing and transporting the mortal remains to the worker's home country [3][5].
  • Iqama cancellation and exit clearance: The authorized representative and sponsor submit the Saudi Death Certificate and settlement letter to the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) to cancel the deceased's Iqama and obtain the final exit and mortuary release clearance [2][3][5].

steps.title: Complete Indian Consular Registration and Arrange Repatriation to India or Local Burial
steps.html:
• Indian Consular Death Certificate and NOC: Present the original Saudi Death Certificate (with English translation), police and medical reports, the deceased's original Indian passport, and the Power of Attorney to the Embassy of India, Riyadh or the Consulate General of India, Jeddah. The Mission cancels the Indian passport and issues the official Indian Consular Death Certificate and No Objection Certificate (NOC) free of charge [3][5].
  • Option A - Air repatriation of mortal remains to India:
    • Obtain a hospital Embalming Certificate and Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease, have the body placed in a hermetically sealed coffin at the designated mortuary, and book air cargo transport (through Saudia Cargo, Air India, or another carrier) [2][3][5].
    • Email the flight airway bill, Indian Consular Death Certificate, Embalming Certificate, Non-Contagious Certificate, and cancelled passport copy at least 48 hours before departure to the Airport Health Organization (APHO) at the destination airport in India for public health clearance [3][5].
    • If the deceased's sponsor or family is genuinely destitute and unable to pay for air transport, the Indian Mission can fund repatriation through the Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) administered by the Ministry of External Affairs [3][5][6].
  • Option B - Local burial in Saudi Arabia:
    • If the family opts for burial in Saudi Arabia, the authorized representative submits the family's notarized consent letter (Wakala), the Indian Mission's NOC, and the Saudi medical/police permit via the municipal Balady (Ikram) portal to obtain a municipal burial permit and cemetery plot allocation at no municipal fee [1][2][5].

steps.title: Claim Legal Dues, Saudi GOSI Compensation, PBBY Insurance, and Indian EPFO Benefits
steps.html:
• Unpaid salary, End-of-Service Benefit, and Blood Money (Diyah): If unpaid wages, End-of-Service Benefits, or court-awarded traffic/accident compensation (Diyah) remain pending, the legal heirs must submit a Succession Certificate (Legal Heirship Certificate) issued by the competent district collector or civil court in India, attested by the Ministry of External Affairs in New Delhi and the Indian Mission in Saudi Arabia, so the Mission's Death Claims Cell can collect and remit the funds to India [3][5].
  • Saudi occupational hazard benefits (GOSI): If your family member died due to a work injury or occupational hazard in Saudi Arabia, file an occupational death compensation claim with the Saudi General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI, customer service 199044, email gosi@gosi.gov.sa), which covers repatriation expenses and statutory survivor benefits [7].
  • Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) insurance: If the deceased held an Emigration Check Required (ECR) passport or was insured under the mandatory Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana scheme overseen by the Ministry of External Affairs, the legal heirs can claim up to INR 10 lakhs for accidental death plus one economy-class return air ticket for an accompanying attendant [8].
  • Indian Provident Fund, Pension, and EDLI insurance: If your family member had prior or active contributions in India with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), the surviving spouse or legal heirs should file the Composite Claim Form in Death Cases (Form 20 for Provident Fund settlement, Form 10-D for Employees' Pension Scheme monthly survivor pension, and Form 5-IF for Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance up to INR 7 lakhs) online via the EPFO Unified Portal or at the regional EPFO office [9].

closingQuestion: To help us provide any region-specific details, in which city or province in Saudi Arabia did the death occur, and does the family intend to repatriate the mortal remains to India or arrange local burial in Saudi Arabia?
