title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Romania: medical death certification, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and burial/cremation permits, survivor pensions and funeral grants, and estate succession, banks, and tax filings.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for your loss. When a family member dies in Romania, national law sets out clear steps and strict deadlines for medical certification, civil registration, funeral arrangements, and social security and inheritance procedures. Below is the official 5-step checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the medical certificate of cause of death (at the hospital or at home)
steps.html:
• Death in a healthcare facility (hospital): If the deceased was admitted to a hospital in Romania, the attending physician or on-call doctor completes and issues the medical certificate of cause of death (Certificatul medical constatator al decesului, an official form on which the cause of death is entered in block capitals without abbreviations or erasures), typically after the statutory observation period following confirmation of signs of death [1][2].
  • Death at home from natural causes: Contact the deceased's family doctor (medic de familie) or, outside their working hours (overnight or on non-working days), the ambulance service via the single emergency number 112. The physician who examines the body at home and rules out any suspicion of violent death issues the Certificatul medical constatator al decesului [1][2].
  • Death from violent, accidental, or suspicious causes: Call 112 immediately. The police and public prosecutor order a medico-legal autopsy at the Institute or County Medico-Legal Service (Institutul de Medicină Legală - IML), and in addition to the medical certificate issued by the forensic pathologist, you must obtain the official clearance issued by the police or prosecutor's office (dovada eliberată de poliție sau de parchet) confirming that the authorities have been notified and authorise burial or cremation [1].
  • Mortuary transport and care: Collection, embalming (tanatopraxie), and transport of the body may be carried out solely by funeral service providers holding a public health permit issued by the county public health directorates or the Bucharest Public Health Directorate (for example, in the capital, Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București, phone +40 21 252 79 78, email dspb@dspb.ro), in accordance with Government Decision (HG) No 741/2016 [2].

steps.title: Register the death with the Civil Registry within 3 days (or 48 hours)
steps.html:
• Competent authority: The death declaration is made in person at the local community public service for personal records (Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP) or before the civil registrar (ofițerul de stare civilă) at the town hall (primăria) of the administrative-territorial unit where the death occurred, which are methodologically coordinated nationwide by Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor (Directorate-General for Personal Records, phone +40 21 413 54 42, email dgep@mai.gov.ro), under Law No 119/1996 on Civil Status Documents [1].
  • Mandatory statutory deadlines:
    • Within 3 days of the date of death for deaths resulting from natural causes [1].
    • Within 48 hours from the time the medical certificate of death or the police/prosecutor clearance was issued when the death resulted from suicide, an accident, or other violent causes, or when the body was found; missing these deadlines requires prior approval from the prosecutor's office (parchet) for late registration [1].
  • Documents required at the civil registry desk:
    • The original medical certificate of cause of death (Certificatul medical constatator al decesului) and, where applicable, the clearance issued by the police or prosecutor's office [1].
    • The original identity document (carte de identitate or buletin de identitate), birth certificate, and, where applicable, marriage certificate of the deceased [1].
    • The military record book (livret militar) or recruitment certificate of the deceased (if under age 60 with military obligations) [1].
    • The identity document of the informant (family member or other entitled person) [1].
  • Documents issued on the spot and free of charge: The civil registrar draws up the death entry and issues the original death certificate (Certificatul de deces) and a single original burial or cremation permit (Adeverința de înhumare sau de incinerare) [1].

steps.title: Arrange burial or cremation and apply for the statutory funeral grant
steps.html:
• Presenting the burial or cremation permit: Burial or cremation of your family member can take place only on the basis of the original burial or cremation permit (Adeverința de înhumare sau de incinerare), which is handed over to the cemetery administration, parish, or human crematorium [1][2]. If burial or cremation takes place in a different municipality from where the death occurred, the coffin must be transported in licensed funeral vehicles compliant with HG No 741/2016 [2].
  • Eligibility for the statutory funeral grant (ajutor de deces): Upon the death of an insured person in the public pension system, a pensioner, or a dependent family member who had no independent social insurance entitlement, the funeral grant (ajutor de deces) is paid to a single person (surviving spouse, child, parent, or any natural or legal person) who provides documentary proof of having borne the funeral expenses [4].
  • Where and when the funeral grant is paid: The standard application is submitted to the territorial pension house (casa teritorială de pensii) for the deceased's place of residence, operating under Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (National House of Public Pensions, central phone +40 21 316 28 30, email petitii.sesizari@cnpp.ro), together with the death certificate (original and copy), the applicant's ID, civil status documents proving family relationship, and proof of funeral expenses (invoice and receipt). The funeral grant is paid within 3 working days of submitting a complete file and may be claimed within the general limitation period of 3 years from the date the death certificate was issued [3][4].

steps.title: Settle pensions, health insurance, bank accounts, and utilities
steps.html:
• Stopping ongoing pension payments and claiming unpaid amounts: The territorial pension house stops pension payments starting the month following the death; any unpaid pension amounts for the month of death (or accrued arrears) may be claimed by the surviving spouse, children, parents, or, in their absence, other legal or testamentary heirs [4].
  • Survivor's pension (pensia de urmaș): The surviving spouse and the deceased's children (up to age 16, up to age 26 if enrolled in legally accredited education, or for the entire duration of disability arising during those periods) can apply for a survivor's pension (pensia de urmaș) at the territorial pension house within the network coordinated by Casa Națională de Pensii Publice, provided the deceased was a pensioner or met the eligibility conditions for a pension [3][4].
  • Banks, private insurance, and utility providers: Notify the banks where the deceased held accounts, deposits, or loans (presenting the death certificate to block unauthorised transactions and check for any credit life insurance policies) as well as electricity, gas, water, telecommunications providers, and the local municipal tax office (direcția de taxe și impozite locale) [1][4].

steps.title: Open the notarial succession procedure and observe the 2-year tax exemption window
steps.html:
• Opening the succession procedure before a public notary: To settle the estate and obtain the Certificate of Heir (Certificatul de moștenitor), heirs apply to a notary office within the jurisdiction of the district court (judecătorie) where the deceased had their last domicile, through a public notary registered with Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (National Union of Public Notaries of Romania, phone +40 21 313 99 20, email secretariat@unnpr.ro) [5].
  • Documents required for the notarial succession:
    • The original death certificate of the deceased and the civil status documents of the heirs proving their right to inherit (birth certificates, marriage certificate, ID documents), plus the will if one exists [5].
    • Ownership deeds for movable and immovable assets (sale-purchase contracts, property titles, land register extracts extrase de carte funciară, vehicle registration certificates, bank statements, or securities) [5].
    • A municipal tax clearance certificate (Certificatul de atestare fiscală showing no outstanding local tax arrears on estate assets) and the presence of at least two witnesses who knew the deceased and the composition of the family [5].
  • Right of succession option (1 year) and tax regime (2 years):
    • Under the Romanian Civil Code, the deadline for exercising the right of succession option (accepting the inheritance or expressly renouncing it by notarised declaration) is 1 year from the date the succession opens (the date of death) [5].
    • For tax purposes, rules are administered by Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală (National Agency for Fiscal Administration - ANAF, Call Center +40 31 403 91 60): under Article 111 of the Fiscal Code, if the succession procedure is completed within at most 2 years from the date of death, heirs are exempt from the real estate transfer tax on inherited personal property; if the succession is not finalised within the 2-year window, heirs owe a 1% tax on the value of the inherited real estate [6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this information to your situation, in which municipality or county in Romania did the death occur, and would you like further details on civil registration or opening the notarial succession procedure?

Documents required to claim the statutory funeral grant (ajutor de deces) and survivor pension (pensie de urmaș) from the territorial Casa de Pensii (CNPP)

ro.title: Ce trebuie să faceți când cineva decedează în România: ghid oficial în 5 pași
ro.cardSummary: Ghid oficial în 5 pași după un deces în România: certificatul medical constatator al decesului (în spital sau acasă/112/IML), firmă de servicii funerare autorizată DSP, înregistrarea decesului la Stare Civilă (SPCLEP / Primărie) în 3 zile, ajutorul de deces și pensia de urmaș la Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (CNPP), și succesiunea notarială (UNNPR).
ro.introHtml: Ne pare foarte rău pentru pierderea suferită. Atunci când membrul familiei dumneavoastră decedează în România, legislația națională stabilește pași clari și termene stricte pentru constatarea medicală, înregistrarea stării civile, organizarea serviciilor funerare și reglementarea drepturilor de asigurări sociale și succesorale. Mai jos găsiți lista oficială în 5 pași.

steps.title: Obțineți certificatul medical constatator al decesului (la spital sau la domiciliu)
steps.html:
• Deces survenit într-o unitate sanitară (spital): Dacă persoana decedată s-a aflat internată într-un spital din România, medicul curant sau medicul de gardă întocmește și eliberează Certificatul medical constatator al decesului (formular oficial în care cauza decesului este înscrisă cu majuscule, fără prescurtări sau ștersături), de regulă după împlinirea termenului legal de observație de la constatarea semnelor morții [1][2].
  • Deces survenit la domiciliu din cauze naturale: Apelați medicul de familie al persoanei decedate sau, în afara programului acestuia (noaptea ori în zilele nelucrătoare), serviciul de ambulanță prin numărul unic de urgență 112. Medicul care examinează corpul neînsuflețit la domiciliu și exclude suspiciunile de moarte violentă eliberează Certificatul medical constatator al decesului [1][2].
  • Deces din cauze violente, accidentale sau suspecte: Apelați imediat 112. Poliția și procurorul dispun efectuarea necropsiei medico-legale la Institutul sau Serviciul Județean de Medicină Legală, iar pe lângă certificatul medical constatator eliberat de medicul legist este obligatorie și dovada eliberată de poliție sau de parchet din care să rezulte că aceste autorități au fost sesizate și își dau acordul pentru înhumare sau incinerare [1].
  • Transportul și îngrijirile mortuare: Preluarea, îmbălsămarea (tanatopraxia) și transportul corpului neînsuflețit pot fi efectuate exclusiv de prestatori de servicii funerare care dețin autorizație sanitară emisă de direcțiile de sănătate publică județene sau a municipiului București (de exemplu, la nivelul capitalei, instituția Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București, telefon +40 21 252 79 78, e-mail dspb@dspb.ro), în conformitate cu normele din HG nr. 741/2016 [2].

steps.title: Înregistrați decesul la Starea Civilă în termen de 3 zile (sau 48 de ore)
steps.html:
• Autoritatea competentă: Declarația de deces se face verbal la serviciul public comunitar local de evidență a persoanelor sau la ofițerul de stare civilă din cadrul primăriei unității administrativ-teritoriale în a cărei rază s-a produs decesul, structuri coordonate metodologic la nivel național de instituția Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor (telefon +40 21 413 54 42, e-mail dgep@mai.gov.ro), conform Legii nr. 119/1996 cu privire la actele de stare civilă [1].
  • Termene legale obligatorii:
    • În termen de 3 zile de la data încetării din viață pentru decesul datorat unor cauze naturale [1].
    • În termen de 48 de ore calculat din momentul în care s-a întocmit certificatul medical constatator sau s-a eliberat dovada poliției ori a parchetului, atunci când decesul se datorează unei sinucideri, unui accident, altor cauze violente sau când cadavrul a fost găsit; depășirea acestor termene necesită aprobarea parchetului pentru înregistrarea tardivă [1].
  • Documente necesare la ghișeul de stare civilă:
    • Certificatul medical constatator al decesului (în original) și, dacă este cazul, dovada eliberată de poliție sau de parchet [1].
    • Actul de identitate (cartea sau buletinul de identitate), certificatul de naștere și, după caz, certificatul de căsătorie ale persoanei decedate, în original [1].
    • Livretul militar sau adeverința de recrutare a persoanei decedate (dacă aceasta avea sub 60 de ani și obligații militare) [1].
    • Actul de identitate al declarantului (membru al familiei sau altă persoană îndreptățită) [1].
  • Documente eliberate pe loc și gratuit: Ofițerul de stare civilă întocmește actul de deces și eliberează declarantului Certificatul de deces (în original) și Adeverința de înhumare sau de incinerare (într-un singur exemplar original) [1].

steps.title: Organizați înhumarea sau incinerarea și solicitați ajutorul de deces
steps.html:
• Predarea adeverinței de înhumare sau de incinerare: Înhumarea sau incinerarea membrului familiei dumneavoastră se poate face numai pe baza Adeverinței de înhumare sau de incinerare în original, care se predă administrației cimitirului, parohiei sau crematoriului uman [1][2]. Dacă înhumarea sau incinerarea are loc în altă localitate decât cea în care s-a produs decesul, transportul sicriului se realizează cu autospeciale funerare autorizate conform HG nr. 741/2016 [2].
  • Solicitarea ajutorului de deces: În cazul decesului unui asigurat în sistemul public de pensii, al unui pensionar sau al unui membru de familie aflat în întreținerea acestuia care nu avea un drept propriu de asigurări sociale, ajutorul de deces se acordă unei singure persoane (soț supraviețuitor, copil, părinte sau oricărei persoane fizice ori juridice) care face dovada cu documente că a suportat cheltuielile ocazionate de deces [4].
  • Unde și când se plătește ajutorul de deces: Cererea-tip se depune la casa teritorială de pensii din raza de domiciliu a persoanei decedate, structură aflată în subordinea instituției Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (telefon centrală +40 21 316 28 30, e-mail petitii.sesizari@cnpp.ro), împreună cu certificatul de deces (original și copie), actul de identitate al solicitantului, actele de stare civilă care atestă gradul de rudenie și dovezile cheltuielilor funerare (factură și chitanță). Ajutorul de deces se achită în termen de 3 zile lucrătoare de la depunerea dosarului complet și poate fi solicitat în cadrul termenului general de prescripție de 3 ani de la data emiterii certificatului de deces [3][4].

steps.title: Reglementați pensia, asigurarea de sănătate, conturile bancare și utilitățile
steps.html:
• Sistarea pensiei în plată și sumele neîncasate: Casa teritorială de pensii oprește plata pensiei începând cu luna următoare celei în care a survenit decesul; sumele rămase neîncasate pe luna în curs (sau drepturile restante) pot fi solicitate de soțul supraviețuitor, copii, părinți sau, în lipsa acestora, de ceilalți moștenitori legali ori testamentari [4].
  • Pensia de urmaș: Soțul supraviețuitor și copiii persoanei decedate (până la vârsta de 16 ani, până la 26 de ani dacă își continuă studiile într-o formă de învățământ organizată potrivit legii, sau pe toată durata invalidității ivite în aceste perioade) pot solicita acordarea pensiei de urmaș la casa teritorială de pensii din rețeaua coordonată de instituția Casa Națională de Pensii Publice, dacă persoana decedată era pensionară sau îndeplinea condițiile pentru obținerea unei pensii [3][4].
  • Bănci, asigurări private și furnizori de servicii: Notificați băncile la care persoana decedată deținea conturi, depozite sau credite (prezentând certificatul de deces pentru blocarea rulajelor neautorizate și verificarea eventualelor asigurări de viață atașate creditelor), precum și furnizorii de energie, gaze, apă, telecomunicații și direcția locală de taxe și impozite a primăriei.

steps.title: Deschideți procedura succesorală notarială și respectați termenul fiscal de 2 ani
steps.html:
• Deschiderea procedurii succesorale la notarul public: Pentru dezbaterea moștenirii și eliberarea Certificatului de moștenitor, moștenitorii se adresează unui birou individual sau unei societăți profesionale notariale din circumscripția judecătoriei în care persoana decedată a avut ultimul domiciliu, notarul fiind membru al organizației Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (telefon +40 21 313 99 20, e-mail secretariat@unnpr.ro) [5].
  • Acte necesare pentru dezbaterea succesiunii:
    • Certificatul de deces al defunctului (în original) și actele de stare civilă ale moștenitorilor care dovedesc calitatea succesorală (certificate de naștere, certificat de căsătorie, acte de identitate), plus testamentul (dacă există) [5].
    • Actele de proprietate asupra bunurilor mobile și imobile (contracte de vânzare-cumpărare, titluri de proprietate, extrase de carte funciară, certificate de înmatriculare auto, extrase de cont bancar sau titluri de valoare) [5].
    • Certificatul de atestare fiscală (fără datorii restante la bugetul local pentru bunurile din masa succesorală) și prezența a 2 martori care l-au cunoscut pe defunct și cunosc componența familiei [5].
  • Dreptul de opțiune succesorală (1 an) și regimul fiscal (2 ani):
    • Conform Codului civil, termenul de opțiune succesorală (pentru acceptarea moștenirii sau renunțarea expresă la succesiune prin declarație autentică notarială) este de 1 an de la data deschiderii moștenirii (data decesului) [5].
    • Din punct de vedere fiscal, regulile sunt administrate de instituția Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală (Call Center +40 31 403 91 60): potrivit art. 111 din Codul fiscal, dacă procedura succesorală este dezbătută și finalizată în termen de cel mult 2 ani de la data decesului, moștenitorii sunt scutiți de impozitul pe transferul proprietăților imobiliare din patrimoniul personal; în cazul nefinalizării succesiunii în termenul de 2 ani, moștenitorii datorează un impozit de 1% calculat la valoarea masei succesorale imobiliare [6].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: UK & Spain
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: UK & Spain
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border terminal illness checklist between Spain and United Kingdom: palliative care coordination, separate Advance Directives, separate financial and medical Powers of Attorney, caregiver leave and benefits, and cross-border estate and repatriation planning.
introHtml: Supporting a family member diagnosed with a serious or terminal illness when family life, healthcare, and assets span Spain and the United Kingdom carries a heavy emotional and administrative burden. To prevent medical, banking, or probate delays across both jurisdictions while focusing on your family member's comfort, it is helpful to organise the practical arrangements into five priority steps.

steps.title: Coordinate palliative care in Spain and cross-border healthcare coverage with the UK
steps.html:
• Public palliative care in Spain (SNS and ESAD): In Spain, palliative care is provided free of charge within the National Health System (Sistema Nacional de Salud - SNS) through hospital palliative care units and Home Care Support Teams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD), activated by referral from the primary care doctor or hospital specialist in the relevant autonomous community. The Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos (Spanish Society for Palliative Care, phone +34 659 694 706, email info@secpal.org) maintains an updated directory of palliative care units and support teams across every province [1].
  • UK-Spain healthcare coordination (S1, GHIC, S2, and Fit-to-fly): If your family member is a UK state pensioner residing in Spain who has registered form S1 with the Spanish National Institute of Social Security (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social - INSS), they are entitled to Spanish public healthcare on the same basis as a local insured resident while also retaining the right to receive NHS care during temporary visits to the United Kingdom [2]. Temporary visitors in Spain use the UK GHIC or UK EHIC card, whereas planned specialist treatment requires prior authorisation via form S2 arranged through NHS Overseas Healthcare Services (phone +44 191 218 1999) [2][3]. If a transfer to an NHS hospital or hospice in the UK is being considered, it is essential to obtain advance Fit-to-fly medical clearance or arrange air ambulance transport and carry a translated clinical summary detailing pain relief and symptom control regimens [2][3].

steps.title: Execute a Spanish Advance Directive (*Instrucciones Previas*) and a UK Living Will
steps.html:
• Spanish Advance Directive (Documento de Instrucciones Previas / Testamento Vital): So that decisions regarding life-sustaining treatment, palliative sedation, and end-of-life care are legally binding on medical teams in Spain, the ill person - while retaining full legal capacity - should execute a Documento de Instrucciones Previas (also called Voluntades Anticipadas or Testamento Vital depending on the autonomous community) under Law 41/2002 [4]. Depending on regional rules, it can be signed before a notary, before an official at the regional registry, or before three adult witnesses (at least two of whom must have no family relationship within the second degree or financial link to the grantor), and registered in the regional registry so it is synchronised with the National Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) of the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health), accessible from any SNS hospital [4].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative and UK Advance Decision (ADRT): In the Spanish directive, it is advisable to expressly appoint a healthcare proxy (representante sanitario) to act as interlocutor with the medical team if the patient loses capacity to express their wishes [4]. If there is any possibility of receiving medical care in the United Kingdom, it is wise to sign in parallel an Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT or Living Will) under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 in England and Wales (or an Advance Directive in Scotland), together with an emergency care plan (ReSPECT), providing copies to the GP and close relatives.

steps.title: Put in place a Spanish Preventive Power of Attorney and a UK Lasting Power of Attorney
steps.html:
• Why separate powers are required in both countries: A power of attorney granted in the UK cannot be used automatically before Spanish banks, notaries, or public authorities without a Hague Apostille, sworn translation (traducción jurada), and verification of legal equivalence - and the reverse is equally true. It is therefore essential to execute separate instruments in each jurisdiction while the ill person retains full cognitive capacity [5][6].
  • Spanish Poder Preventivo and UK Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): In Spain, you should contact a notary office through the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of the Spanish Notariat) to execute a public deed of Preventive Power of Attorney (Poder Preventivo or Poder General con cláusula de subsistencia en caso de incapacidad), authorising the attorney-in-fact to manage Spanish bank accounts, pensions, utilities, tax filings, and real estate without requiring court support proceedings [5]. If the ill person cannot travel for medical reasons, the Spanish notary can attend their home or hospital bed to authorise the deed [5]. In the United Kingdom, you should prepare and register with the Office of the Public Guardian (phone +44 203 518 9639, email customerservices@publicguardian.gov.uk) a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) in both forms - Property and Financial Affairs for UK bank accounts and assets, and Health and Welfare for health and care decisions in England and Wales (or a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian in Scotland) [6].

steps.title: Request an urgent Spanish dependency assessment and UK Special Rules terminal illness benefits
steps.html:
• Urgent dependency assessment in Spain (SAAD / Ley 39/2006): To activate public home-help hours, telecare, day care, or financial allowances for family caregivers in Spain, submit an application for dependency grading under the System for Autonomy and Care for Dependency (Sistema para la Autonomía y Atención a la Dependencia - SAAD, Law 39/2006), coordinated nationally by the Instituto de Mayores y Servicios Sociales (Institute for Older Persons and Social Services - IMSERSO, phone +34 912 667 713) and administered by the regional or municipal social services [7]. By attaching a palliative medical report confirming a serious prognosis or rapid functional decline, health-centre or hospital social workers can request the fast-track emergency procedure available in that autonomous community [7].
  • UK Special Rules for End of Life (form SR1): In parallel, if your family member has UK social security links and an estimated medical prognosis of 12 months or less, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) applies fast-track processing under the Special Rules for End of Life using clinical form SR1 [8]. UK pensioners or insured residents in Spain covered by social security coordination rules can check eligibility and claim exportable disability benefits such as Attendance Allowance or the daily living component of Personal Independence Payment (PIP) through the International Pension Centre and the DWP Exportability Team (phone +44 191 218 7777) [8][9].

steps.title: Coordinate Spanish and UK wills under the EU Succession Regulation and record funeral wishes
steps.html:
• Coordinating a Spanish notarial will and a UK Will: When assets are held in both Spain and the United Kingdom, it is generally advisable to execute a Spanish open notarial will (Testamento Abierto Notarial) limited to assets located in Spain alongside a separate British Will covering UK assets, ensuring that neither document inadvertently revokes the other [5][10]. A will signed before a Spanish notary is automatically recorded in the Central Registry of Last Wills (Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad) of the Ministerio de Justicia (Spanish Ministry of Justice), avoiding the lengthy delay and expense of legalising and translating a UK Grant of Probate to release Spanish bank accounts or transfer property [10].
  • Choice of UK national law (professio iuris) and final wishes: For British nationals residing in Spain, EU Regulation No 650/2012 applies the law of habitual residence by default unless the testator expressly includes a choice-of-law clause (professio iuris) in their will electing the law of their UK nationality (English and Welsh, Scottish, or Northern Irish law), preserving UK testamentary freedom instead of Spain's forced heirship rules (legítimas) [5]. Finally, record clear preferences regarding local burial or cremation in Spain versus repatriation to the UK, and gather any funeral insurance (seguro de decesos) or life insurance policies in both countries [10].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación anticipada entre España y el Reino Unido: guía oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos ante una enfermedad terminal con vínculos entre España y el Reino Unido: cuidados paliativos en el SNS (SECPAL) y cobertura sanitaria S1/GHIC (INSS y NHS), Documento de Instrucciones Previas (Testamento Vital) y Advance Decision en Reino Unido, Poder Preventivo notarial y Lasting Power of Attorney (OPG), prestaciones DWP (SR1) y dependencia, y testamentos en ambos países.
es.introHtml: Acompañar a un familiar con una enfermedad grave o terminal cuando la vida, el patrimonio y la familia están repartidos entre España y el Reino Unido supone una enorme carga emocional y administrativa. Para evitar bloqueos médicos, bancarios o sucesorios entre ambas jurisdicciones y centrarse en el bienestar de su familiar, conviene organizar las gestiones en cinco pasos prioritarios.

steps.title: Coordinar los cuidados paliativos en España y la cobertura sanitaria con el Reino Unido
steps.html:
En España, la atención paliativa se presta gratuitamente dentro del Sistema Nacional de Salud a través de las unidades hospitalarias de cuidados paliativos y de los Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria (ESAD), activados mediante derivación del médico de atención primaria o del especialista hospitalario de su comunidad autónoma. La Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos (teléfono +34 659 694 706, correo info@secpal.org) mantiene el directorio actualizado de unidades y recursos paliativos disponibles en cada provincia [1].

Si su familiar es pensionista británico residente en España y tiene registrado el formulario S1 ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS), recibe asistencia sanitaria pública española en las mismas condiciones que un asegurado local y conserva además el derecho a recibir atención del NHS en visitas temporales al Reino Unido [2]. Para estancias temporales en España se utiliza la tarjeta sanitaria UK GHIC o UK EHIC, mientras que los tratamientos programados específicos requieren autorización previa mediante el formulario S2 gestionado ante NHS Overseas Healthcare Services (teléfono +44 191 218 1999) [2][3]. Si se valora un traslado hacia un hospice o centro del NHS en el Reino Unido, es indispensable solicitar con antelación el alta para volar (Fit-to-fly) o coordinar transporte sanitario medicalizado y transferir el historial clínico traducido con las pautas de analgesia y control de síntomas [2][3].

steps.title: Formalizar el documento de instrucciones previas en España y la directiva médica en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Para que las decisiones sobre tratamientos de soporte vital, sedación paliativa y cuidados al final de la vida sean jurídicamente vinculantes para los equipos médicos en España, la persona enferma - mientras conserve plena capacidad de obrar - debe otorgar el Documento de Instrucciones Previas (denominado Voluntades Anticipadas o Testamento Vital según la comunidad autónoma) conforme a la Ley 41/2002 [4]. Según la normativa autonómica aplicable, puede formalizarse ante notario, ante personal funcionario del registro autonómico o ante tres testigos mayores de edad (dos de ellos sin relación de parentesco hasta segundo grado ni vínculo patrimonial), y debe inscribirse en el registro autonómico correspondiente para su incorporación al Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas (RNIP) del Ministerio de Sanidad, accesible desde cualquier hospital del Sistema Nacional de Salud [4].

En este documento conviene designar expresamente a una persona representante (representante sanitario) que actúe como interlocutora ante el equipo médico si el paciente pierde la capacidad de expresar su voluntad [4]. Si existe la posibilidad de recibir asistencia médica en el Reino Unido, conviene suscribir en paralelo una Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT o Living Will) conforme a la Mental Capacity Act 2005 en Inglaterra y Gales (o una Advance Directive en Escocia), así como un plan clínico de recomendaciones de emergencia (ReSPECT), entregando copias al médico de cabecera (GP) y a los familiares directos.

steps.title: Otorgar poderes preventivos en España y el Lasting Power of Attorney en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Un poder otorgado en el Reino Unido no permite operar de forma automática ante bancos, notarías o administraciones españolas sin trámites de apostilla de La Haya, traducción jurada y verificación de equivalencia funcional, y lo mismo ocurre a la inversa. Por ello, es fundamental otorgar instrumentos separados en cada país mientras la persona enferma conserve su capacidad cognitiva [5][6].

En España, debe acudirse a una notaría a través del Consejo General del Notariado para firmar en escritura pública un Poder Preventivo (o un Poder General con cláusula de subsistencia en caso de incapacidad), facultando a la persona apoderada para administrar cuentas bancarias, pensiones, suministros, trámites tributarios y bienes inmuebles en territorio español sin necesidad de acudir a un procedimiento judicial de provisión de medidas de apoyo [5]. Si la persona enferma no puede desplazarse por motivos médicos, el notario puede acudir al domicilio o al centro hospitalario para autorizar la escritura [5]. En el Reino Unido, debe tramitarse y registrarse ante la Office of the Public Guardian (teléfono +44 203 518 9639, correo customerservices@publicguardian.gov.uk) un Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) en sus dos modalidades - Property and Financial Affairs para cuentas y bienes británicos, y Health and Welfare para decisiones sociosanitarias en Inglaterra y Gales - (o un Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney ante la Office of the Public Guardian en Escocia) [6].

steps.title: Solicitar la valoración urgente de dependencia y las prestaciones británicas por enfermedad terminal
steps.html:
Para activar ayudas de cuidado domiciliario, teleasistencia, centro de día o prestación económica para cuidados en el entorno familiar en España, debe presentarse la solicitud de reconocimiento de grado de dependencia en el marco del Sistema para la Autonomía y Atención a la Dependencia (SAAD, Ley 39/2006), coordinado por el Instituto de Mayores y Servicios Sociales (teléfono +34 912 667 713) y gestionado por los servicios sociales de la comunidad autónoma o del ayuntamiento de residencia [7]. Aportando un informe médico paliativo que acredite el pronóstico grave o el deterioro funcional acelerado, los trabajadores sociales del centro de salud o del hospital pueden instar el trámite de urgencia o emergencia social disponible en la comunidad autónoma [7].

En paralelo, si su familiar tiene vínculos de seguridad social con el Reino Unido y el pronóstico médico estimado es de 12 meses o menos, el Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) aplica el procedimiento acelerado Special Rules for End of Life mediante el formulario clínico SR1 [8]. Los pensionistas o asegurados británicos residentes en España amparados por las normas de coordinación de seguridad social pueden consultar y tramitar la exportación de prestaciones como Attendance Allowance o el componente de vida diaria de Personal Independence Payment (PIP) ante el International Pension Centre y el equipo de exportación del DWP (teléfono +44 191 218 7777) [8][9].

steps.title: Ordenar los testamentos bajo el Reglamento Europeo de Sucesiones y las disposiciones finales
steps.html:
Cuando existen bienes en España y en el Reino Unido, resulta aconsejable otorgar un Testamento Abierto Notarial en España limitado al patrimonio situado en territorio español y coordinado con un Will británico para los bienes situados en el Reino Unido, cuidando que ninguno de los dos documentos revoque de forma involuntaria al otro [5][10]. El testamento otorgado ante notario español queda inscrito de oficio en el Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad del Ministerio de Justicia, lo que evita el largo proceso y coste de legalizar y traducir un Grant of Probate británico para adjudicar inmuebles o desbloquear cuentas en España [10].

Para ciudadanos británicos residentes en España, el Reglamento (UE) n.º 650/2012 aplica por defecto la ley del país de residencia habitual a la sucesión, salvo que el testador realice expresamente en su testamento una elección de ley nacional (professio iuris) a favor del derecho inglés, galés, escocés o norirlandés, lo que permite conservar la libertad de testar propia del derecho británico frente al sistema español de legítimas forzosas [5]. Finalmente, conviene dejar por escrito las preferencias sobre inhumación o cremación en España o eventual repatriación al Reino Unido y reunir las pólizas de seguro de decesos o de vida en ambos países [10].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: US & Mexico
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: US & Mexico
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border terminal illness checklist between Mexico and United States: palliative care coordination, separate Advance Directives, separate financial and medical Powers of Attorney, caregiver leave and benefits, and cross-border estate and repatriation planning.
introHtml: Supporting a family member diagnosed with a serious or terminal illness when family ties, healthcare, and assets span the United States and Mexico requires coordinating procedures across two very different legal and healthcare systems. To prevent frozen bank accounts, medical transport delays, or duplicate probate proceedings while prioritising your family member's comfort, it is best to organise the arrangements into five essential steps.

steps.title: Coordinate palliative care in Mexico and the Medicare Hospice Benefit in the United States
steps.html:
• Palliative care and pain management in Mexico: In Mexico, the right to multidisciplinary palliative care and pain control for terminal illness is guaranteed under Title Eight Bis of the General Health Law (Ley General de Salud) [1][2]. Insured members (derechohabientes) of the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (Mexican Social Security Institute - IMSS, helpline 800 623 2323) access Pain Clinics (Clínicas del Dolor) and Palliative Care Services at secondary and tertiary hospitals - as well as home-care programmes - by referral from their Family Medicine Unit (Unidad de Medicina Familiar) or attending specialist [1]. Patients treated through federal health institutes or state health services have access to specialised departments such as the Palliative Care Service of the Instituto Nacional de Cancerología (National Cancer Institute - INCan, phone +52 55 5628 0400) [2].
  • US Medicare Hospice Benefit and cross-border transport limits: In the United States, if the ill person is enrolled in Medicare (Part A) and both the attending physician and the hospice medical director certify a life expectancy of six months or less if the illness runs its normal course, the Medicare Hospice Benefit (phone 1-800-633-4227) can be activated to cover home or inpatient hospice care, medical equipment, and symptom-relief medications [3]. Keep in mind that Medicare generally does not cover hospice services or medical care inside Mexico; before any cross-border transfer, families must coordinate a bilingual medical file, special prescriptions for controlled opioid analgesics, and ground or air ambulance handover at the border [1][3].

steps.title: Execute a Mexican Advance Directive (*Voluntad Anticipada*) and a US Advance Directive
steps.html:
• Mexican Advance Directive (Documento o Formato de Voluntad Anticipada): For end-of-life medical wishes to be legally binding in Mexico, the ill person - while retaining full legal capacity - may sign an Advance Directive Deed (Documento de Voluntad Anticipada) before a Mexican public notary or complete the official clinical form (Formato de Voluntad Anticipada) before authorised healthcare personnel at a public or private hospital, in accordance with the Advance Directive Law of Mexico City, equivalent state laws across Mexican federal entities, and the guidelines of the Comisión Nacional de Bioética (National Bioethics Commission - CONBIOÉTICA) [4]. This instrument allows the patient to refuse disproportionate medical measures that artificially prolong life (obstinación terapéutica), guarantees that palliative care and pain relief are never withdrawn, and appoints a representative to ensure their wishes are respected [4].
  • US State Advance Directive and portable medical orders (POLST/MOLST): If medical care is taking place or may be transferred to the United States, it is essential to sign in parallel a state-specific Advance Directive (comprising a Living Will and a Medical Power of Attorney or Health Care Proxy), supplemented by portable physician orders for emergency medical services (POLST or MOLST) signed by the attending physician [5]. The National Institute on Aging Information Center (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) provides free official guides on advance care planning across the United States [5].

steps.title: Grant separate powers of attorney for Mexico and the United States
steps.html:
• Why separate powers of attorney are necessary: A Durable Power of Attorney executed under US state law cannot be used directly before Mexican banks, notary offices, or property registries without a Hague Apostille, translation by a court-certified translator (perito traductor), and formal protocolisation before a Mexican notary. While your family member retains full cognitive capacity, it is therefore crucial to execute separate instruments for each country [6][7].
  • Mexican Poder Notarial (in Mexico or at a Mexican Consulate) and US Durable POA: To manage bank accounts, pensions, or real estate located in Mexico, an ill person who is in Mexico can contact a notary office through the Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano (National College of Mexican Notaries, phone +52 55 5514 6058, email colegionacional@notariadomexicano.org.mx) to grant a general notarial power of attorney (Poder Notarial for litigation and collections, administration, and, if needed, ownership acts) [6]. If the ill person is in the United States, they can execute a Mexican Poder Notarial directly before any Consulate of Mexico operated by the Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (Mexican Ministry of Foreign Affairs - SRE, booking a Fe Pública appointment via MiConsulado at 1-424-309-0009); the consular deed (testimonio) has immediate legal effect throughout Mexico without an Apostille or translation [7]. For US bank accounts, pensions, and real estate, a state-compliant financial Durable Power of Attorney should be executed, with local legal aid referrals available through the Eldercare Locator (phone 1-800-677-1116, email eldercarelocator@usaging.org) [8].

steps.title: Activate caregiver family leave and expedited terminal illness disability benefits
steps.html:
• US Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Paid Family Leave: In the United States, employed family members who meet employer-size and service-hour requirements are entitled under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), enforced by the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division (phone 1-866-487-9243), to up to 12 weeks of job-protected leave to care for a spouse, child, or parent with a serious health condition - even when the family member's medical care takes place in Mexico - in addition to state Paid Family Leave programmes where applicable [9].
  • Expedited Social Security (TERI) and Mexican IMSS/ISSSTE benefits: When the ill person has an eligible US work record or residence status, the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) applies fast-track processing for disability claims (SSDI and SSI) under its Terminal Illness (TERI) and Compassionate Allowances protocols [10]. In Mexico, workers and pensioners insured with the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (phone 800 623 2323) or ISSSTE can apply for temporary disability certificates, invalidity rulings, and social security support benefits [1].

steps.title: Coordinate a Mexican Open Public Will (*Testamento Público Abierto*), a US Will, and account beneficiaries
steps.html:
• Coordinating Mexican and US wills without cross-revocation: To avoid intestate court proceedings (juicio sucesorio intestamentario) in Mexico or costly delays recognising foreign probate orders, it is advisable to execute a Mexican Open Public Will (Testamento Público Abierto) limited to assets located in Mexico alongside a US Last Will and Testament (or Revocable Living Trust) for assets in the United States, ensuring each document's revocation clause is strictly limited to its own jurisdiction [6][11]. A Testamento Público Abierto can be signed before a notary in Mexico or at any Mexican Consulate in the United States and is logged in the National Registry of Will Notices (Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento - RENAT) coordinated by the Secretaría de Gobernación (Mexican Ministry of the Interior - SEGOB) [6][11].
  • Payable-on-Death designations and funeral/repatriation planning: In parallel, verify that Mexican bank accounts have formally designated beneficiaries (beneficiarios) recorded in the account contract, and that US bank accounts, retirement plans (401(k), IRA), and life insurance policies have updated Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations. Finally, document preferences regarding burial or cremation and review consular mortuary transit requirements in case international repatriation across the US-Mexico border is envisaged [7][11].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación anticipada entre México y EE. UU.: guía oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos ante una enfermedad terminal con vínculos entre México y Estados Unidos: cuidados paliativos en México (Secretaría de Salud / IMSS / ISSSTE) y reglas de Medicare Hospice en EE. UU., Voluntad Anticipada en México y Advance Directive/POLST en EE. UU., poderes notariales en México/Consulado y Durable POA estatal en EE. UU., licencias laborales (FMLA) y testamentos.
es.introHtml: Acompañar a un familiar con una enfermedad grave o en etapa terminal cuando la familia, la atención médica y el patrimonio se dividen entre Estados Unidos y México exige coordinar trámites en dos sistemas jurídicos y sanitarios muy distintos. Para evitar bloqueos bancarios, retrasos médicos o juicios sucesorios duplicados mientras se prioriza el bienestar de su familiar, conviene organizar las gestiones en cinco pasos esenciales.

steps.title: Coordinar los cuidados paliativos en México y el beneficio de hospicio de Medicare en Estados Unidos
steps.html:
En México, el derecho a recibir cuidados paliativos multidisciplinarios y control del dolor en enfermedades en situación terminal está garantizado por el Título Octavo Bis de la Ley General de Salud [1][2]. Las personas derechohabientes del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (orientación telefónica en el 800 623 2323) acceden a las Clínicas del Dolor y Servicios de Cuidados Paliativos en hospitales de segundo y tercer nivel - así como a esquemas de atención domiciliaria - mediante referencia de su Unidad de Medicina Familiar o del especialista tratante [1]. Quienes reciben atención en institutos federales o servicios estatales de salud cuentan con unidades especializadas como el Servicio de Cuidados Paliativos del Instituto Nacional de Cancerología (teléfono +52 55 5628 0400) [2].

En Estados Unidos, si la persona enferma está afiliada a Medicare (Parte A) y el médico tratante junto con el director médico del programa certifican un pronóstico de vida de seis meses o menos si la enfermedad sigue su curso normal, puede activarse el beneficio de hospicio (Medicare Hospice Benefit, teléfono 1-800-633-4227) para cubrir atención paliativa domiciliaria o institucional, equipo médico y medicamentos para el control de síntomas [3]. Es fundamental considerar que Medicare por regla general no cubre servicios de hospicio ni atención médica en territorio mexicano, por lo que antes de cualquier traslado transfronterizo deben coordinarse el expediente clínico bilingüe, las recetas especiales para analgésicos opioides controlados y las condiciones de transporte médico terrestre o aéreo [1][3].

steps.title: Formalizar el Documento de Voluntad Anticipada en México y el Advance Directive en Estados Unidos
steps.html:
Para que las decisiones sobre el final de la vida sean respetadas legalmente en México, la persona enferma - mientras conserve plena capacidad de ejercicio - puede otorgar un Documento de Voluntad Anticipada ante notario público o suscribir el Formato de Voluntad Anticipada ante el personal de salud autorizado de la institución médica pública o privada, conforme a la legislación aplicable en la Ciudad de México y en la mayoría de las entidades federativas y a las directrices de la Comisión Nacional de Bioética [4]. Este instrumento permite rechazar medios o procedimientos médicos desproporcionados que prolonguen artificialmente la vida (obstinación terapéutica), garantizando que nunca se suspendan los cuidados paliativos ni el alivio del dolor, y designa a un representante para vigilar el cumplimiento de su voluntad [4].

Si la atención médica tiene lugar o puede trasladarse a Estados Unidos, es indispensable suscribir en paralelo una directiva médica estatal (Advance Directive que incluya un Living Will y un Medical Power of Attorney o Health Care Proxy), complementada con órdenes médicas portátiles para servicios de emergencia (POLST o MOLST) firmadas por el médico tratante [5]. El National Institute on Aging Information Center (teléfono 1-800-222-2225, correo niaic@nia.nih.gov) ofrece guías oficiales gratuitas sobre planificación anticipada de cuidados médicos en Estados Unidos [5].

steps.title: Otorgar poderes notariales separados para México y Estados Unidos
steps.html:
Un poder otorgado conforme a las leyes estatales de Estados Unidos (Durable Power of Attorney) no permite operar de forma directa ante bancos, notarías o registros públicos de la propiedad en México sin trámites de apostilla, traducción por perito oficial y protocolización ante notario mexicano. Por ello, mientras su familiar conserve plena capacidad cognitiva, conviene formalizar instrumentos separados para cada país [6][7].

Para administrar cuentas bancarias, pensiones o inmuebles situados en México, si la persona enferma se encuentra en territorio mexicano puede acudir a una notaría a través del Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano (teléfono +52 55 5514 6058, correo colegionacional@notariadomexicano.org.mx) para otorgar un Poder Notarial general para pleitos y cobranzas, actos de administración y, en su caso, actos de dominio [6]. Si la persona enferma se encuentra en Estados Unidos, puede tramitar dicho poder directamente en funciones de Notaría Pública ante cualquier Consulado de México de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (programando cita de Fe Pública a través de MiConsulado en el teléfono 1-424-309-0009); el testimonio expedido por el consulado mexicano tiene validez directa e inmediata en todo México sin necesidad de apostilla ni traducción [7]. Para las cuentas, pensiones e inmuebles en Estados Unidos, debe otorgarse un Durable Power of Attorney financiero conforme a la ley del estado respectivo, apoyándose en caso necesario en los servicios de orientación jurídica para adultos mayores del Eldercare Locator (teléfono 1-800-677-1116, correo eldercarelocator@usaging.org) [8].

steps.title: Activar licencias laborales para cuidadores y prestaciones aceleradas por enfermedad terminal
steps.html:
En Estados Unidos, los familiares trabajadores que cumplan los criterios de horas trabajadas y tamaño del empleador tienen derecho, bajo la Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) supervisada por la U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division (teléfono 1-866-487-9243), a un máximo de 12 semanas de licencia laboral con protección del puesto de trabajo para cuidar a un cónyuge, hijo, hija o progenitor con una condición de salud grave, incluso cuando la atención médica del familiar se preste fuera de Estados Unidos, además de los programas de licencia familiar pagada (Paid Family Leave) vigentes en diversos estados [9].

Asimismo, cuando la persona enferma tiene historial laboral o residencia elegible en Estados Unidos, la Social Security Administration (teléfono 1-800-772-1213) aplica procedimientos de resolución urgente para solicitudes de incapacidad (SSDI y SSI) bajo los protocolos de casos terminales (TERI) y Compassionate Allowances [10]. En México, las personas aseguradas ante el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (teléfono 800 623 2323) o el ISSSTE pueden tramitar los certificados de incapacidad temporal, dictámenes de invalidez y apoyos previstos en la legislación de seguridad social [1].

steps.title: Coordinar el Testamento Público Abierto en México, el testamento en Estados Unidos y los beneficiarios
steps.html:
Para evitar la apertura de juicios intestamentarios o demoras en el reconocimiento de resoluciones extranjeras (Probate), resulta conveniente otorgar un Testamento Público Abierto específico para los bienes situados en México y coordinarlo con un Last Will and Testament (o Revocable Living Trust) para el patrimonio ubicado en Estados Unidos, cuidando que las cláusulas de revocación de cada instrumento se limiten expresamente a los bienes de su respectiva jurisdicción [6][11]. El Testamento Público Abierto puede otorgarse ante notario en México o ante cualquier Consulado de México en Estados Unidos y queda registrado a través del sistema vinculado al Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento (RENAT) de la Secretaría de Gobernación [6][11].

De forma complementaria, conviene verificar que las cuentas bancarias en México tengan designados formalmente a sus beneficiarios en el contrato bancario, y que en Estados Unidos estén actualizadas las cláusulas de transferencia directa por fallecimiento (Payable-on-Death - POD y Transfer-on-Death - TOD) en cuentas bancarias, planes de retiro (401(k), IRA) y seguros de vida. Finalmente, es importante dejar asentadas las preferencias sobre inhumación o cremación y conocer los requisitos consulares de tránsito funerario en caso de contemplarse una repatriación entre ambos países [7][11].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in France: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives, enduring powers of attorney, caregiver leave and fast-track benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: We are sincerely sorry to hear about your family member's diagnosis. In France, organizing medical support, legal representation, and estate arrangements while the ill person still retains full legal capacity ensures that their care wishes are respected, secures administrative procedures for the family, and activates financial and practical assistance without delay. Below are the five official and practical steps to follow in order.

steps.title: Set Up Palliative Care, 100% ALD Coverage, and Home Support
steps.html:
Start by coordinating with the attending general practitioner (médecin traitant) and the hospital specialist team (such as oncology) to put the palliative care pathway and financial coverage in place [3][4][8]:

  • Organizing palliative care at home or in a facility: Depending on medical needs and your relative's wishes, the attending or hospital physician can prescribe Hospitalization at Home (Hospitalisation à domicile - HAD), call upon a Mobile Palliative Care Team (équipe mobile de soins palliatifs - EMSP), contact the departmental Care Coordination Support Service (dispositif d'appui à la coordination - DAC) to organize home care, or request admission to an inpatient Palliative Care Unit (unité de soins palliatifs - USP) or designated palliative care beds [3][4]. You can obtain official guidance on patient rights and care services from the Centre national des soins palliatifs et de la fin de vie (National Center for Palliative and End-of-Life Care) at 01 53 72 33 04 [3], as well as through the directory and helpline of the Société Française d'Accompagnement et de Soins Palliatifs (French Society for Support and Palliative Care - SFAP) at 01 53 72 33 00 [4].
  • 100% long-term illness coverage (ALD) and health insurance grants: Verify that the attending physician has established an exempting Long-Term Illness (Affection de Longue Durée - ALD) care protocol so that medical care, medications, and transport related to the condition are reimbursed at 100% of the statutory Social Security rate by Assurance Maladie (French National Health Insurance, reachable at 36 46) [8]. When palliative care is provided at home, the social service department of the local health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM) can also draw on its health and social action fund to help finance home-care assistant hours or non-reimbursable medical supplies [8].
  • Emergency Personalized Autonomy Allowance (APA): If the ill person is aged 60 or older and experiencing a rapid loss of independence (GIR 1 to 4), submit an application for home-based Allocation personnalisée d'autonomie (APA) to the departmental council (conseil départemental); in the event of a certified medical or social emergency, the president of the departmental council can grant a provisional flat-rate emergency APA (APA d'urgence) as soon as the application is filed [5].

steps.title: Draft Advance Directives and Designate a Healthcare Proxy in Writing
steps.html:
Under France's Claeys-Leonetti Act, two distinct legal instruments ensure that the ill person's medical wishes are respected if they become unable to express themselves [1][2][3]:

  • Advance directives (directives anticipées): Any adult may write their directives anticipées at any time (either on dated and signed plain paper stating their full name, date, and place of birth, or using the official template issued by the Ministry of Health and the Haute Autorité de Santé) [1][3]. These directives specify the person's wishes regarding the continuation, limitation, withdrawal, or refusal of end-of-life treatments or medical procedures, and are binding on the physician (except in a life-threatening emergency while the situation is being assessed, or if they appear manifestly inappropriate) [1][3]. If the person is physically unable to write, two witnesses (including the designated healthcare proxy) may attest in writing that the document expresses their free and informed wishes [1].
  • The healthcare proxy (personne de confiance): The ill person may designate a personne de confiance (a trusted relative, family member, or their attending physician) in writing via a document co-signed by both parties [2]. This person may accompany them to medical consultations and will be consulted first by the healthcare team to attest to the patient's wishes if the patient can no longer express them; their testimony takes precedence over any other non-medical opinion, subject only to written advance directives [1][2].
  • Storage and accessibility: Upload both documents to the shared medical record on Mon espace santé, provide copies to the attending physician and the hospital or HAD team, and keep the originals at home with the personne de confiance [1][2].

steps.title: Secure Everyday Powers of Attorney and Legal Representation
steps.html:
Designating a personne de confiance for medical matters grants no authority to manage bank accounts, housing, or property [2][6]. While your family member retains full legal capacity:

  • Bank and postal powers of attorney: Set up powers of attorney (procurations bancaires) directly with each bank for current and savings accounts, as well as a postal power of attorney (procuration postale) with La Poste, so that a designated family member can pay routine bills, manage direct debits, and collect registered mail [6]. Note that all bank powers of attorney automatically terminate on the date of death [6].
  • Future protection mandate or notarial power of attorney: To prepare for a potential decline in capacity that would prevent the person from managing their own affairs (and thus avoid court-ordered guardianship proceedings such as habilitation familiale, curatelle, or tutelle), they may execute a Future Protection Mandate (mandat de protection future) with one or more representatives [6]. This mandate can be drawn up under private signature (Form Cerfa n° 1359204, limited to routine administrative acts) or by notarial deed (acte notarié) through Notaires de France (which allows acts of disposition over the estate, including selling real property) [6]. The mandate only takes effect once a medical certificate issued by a court-approved physician confirms incapacity and is certified by the registry of the judicial court (tribunal judiciaire) [6]. In parallel, an immediately effective general notarial power of attorney (procuration générale notariée*) can be signed if the person wishes to delegate administrative or property management tasks right away [6].

steps.title: Activate Family Solidarity Leave and the Daily Caregiver Allowance (AJAP)
steps.html:
Relatives who suspend or reduce their professional activity to care for a loved one at the end of life are entitled to specific statutory leave and financial support [7][8]:

  • Family solidarity leave (congé de solidarité familiale): Any private-sector employee or public servant (ascendant, descendant, sibling, person sharing the same household, or designated personne de confiance) has the right to request congé de solidarité familiale from their employer as soon as a medical certificate attests that the relative suffers from a life-threatening condition or is in the advanced or terminal phase of a serious and incurable illness [7]. Granted for a maximum of 3 months, renewable once (up to 6 months in total), it may be taken continuously, in blocks, or on a part-time basis with the employer's agreement, and the employer can neither refuse nor postpone it [7].
  • Daily End-of-Life Caregiving Allowance (AJAP): When the ill person is cared for at home (or in an EHPAD care home), Assurance Maladie (or the MSA agricultural fund, depending on affiliation) pays the Allocation journalière d'accompagnement d'une personne en fin de vie (AJAP) to recipients of family solidarity leave (as well as to self-employed workers or benefit-receiving jobseekers who suspend their activity) for up to 21 days (or 42 half-days for part-time leave), which can be shared among several family caregivers [8]. For full administrative rules and forms covering statutory leave and social rights, consult the official portal Service-Public.fr (or call 39 39 Allô Service Public) [7].
  • Alternative prior to the terminal phase: If loss of independence requires regular support before the strictly terminal stage, a caregiver may apply for Caregiver Leave (congé de proche aidant) compensated by the Daily Caregiver Allowance (Allocation journalière du proche aidant - AJPA) through the Family Allowance Fund (Caisse d'allocations familiales - CAF) [7].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Life Insurance Beneficiary Clauses, and Funeral Wishes
steps.html:
• Drafting and registering the will (FCDDV): The person may draw up a holographic will (testament olographe, entirely handwritten, dated, and signed by them) or dictate an authentic will (testament authentique) before a notary [9]. Even for a handwritten holographic will, it is strongly advisable to deposit it with a notary's office through the Notaires de France network so that it is kept safely and recorded in the Central Register of Last Wills (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), ensuring it will be located when the estate is settled [9].
  • Life insurance policies and Social Security death grant: Ask your relative to review the exact wording of the beneficiary clauses (clauses bénéficiaires) in their life insurance (assurance-vie) and retirement savings contracts (which pass outside the civil estate) and gather the insurers' contact details. Also check eligibility requirements for the Social Security lump-sum death grant (capital décès) with Assurance Maladie if the person was recently employed, receiving benefits from France Travail, or drawing an invalidity pension or permanent disability annuity [8].
  • Funeral wishes and administrative file: Encourage your relative to record their funeral preferences in writing (choice between burial and cremation, civil or religious ceremony, organ or body donation to science, and details of any prepaid funeral contract - contrat obsèques) and assemble the family record book (livret de famille), birth certificate, property deeds, bank statements, and digital credentials in a single folder [3][9].

closingQuestion: In which French department (département) does your family member reside, and is care currently organized at home (for example through HAD) or in a hospital facility?

Setting up bank powers of attorney and, if real estate or complex assets exist, a notarial procuration or mandat de protection future (Notaires de France)
Claiming the congé de solidarité familiale and the daily AJAP allowance from the CPAM/MSA vs. emergency departmental APA support (age 60+)

fr.title: Maladie grave et démarches de fin de vie en France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Liste officielle en 5 étapes pour organiser l'accompagnement médical, juridique et administratif d'une fin de vie en France : soins palliatifs (HAD, USP, SFAP / CNSPFV) et prise en charge ALD 100 %, directives anticipées et personne de confiance (loi Claeys-Leonetti), procurations et mandat de protection future, congé de solidarité familiale et allocation AJAP (CPAM), et dispositions testamentaires (Notaires de France).
fr.introHtml: Nous sommes sincèrement désolés d'apprendre le diagnostic qui touche votre proche. En France, organiser l'accompagnement médical, la représentation juridique et les dispositions patrimoniales tant que la personne malade conserve sa pleine capacité juridique permet de faire respecter ses choix de soins, de sécuriser les démarches de la famille et d'activer rapidement les aides financières et humaines. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles et pratiques à suivre dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Mettre en place les soins palliatifs, la prise en charge ALD à 100 % et les aides à domicile
steps.html:
Prenez d'abord appui sur le médecin traitant et l'équipe hospitalière (oncologie ou spécialité concernée) pour coordonner le parcours de soins palliatifs et les prises en charge financières [3][4][8] :

  • Organisation des soins palliatifs à domicile ou en établissement : Selon les besoins médicaux et le souhait de votre proche, le médecin traitant ou hospitalier peut prescrire une Hospitalisation à domicile (HAD), solliciter l'intervention d'une équipe mobile de soins palliatifs (EMSP), saisir le dispositif d'appui à la coordination (DAC) départemental pour organiser le maintien à domicile, ou demander une admission en unité de soins palliatifs (USP) ou sur des lits identifiés de soins palliatifs [3][4]. Vous pouvez obtenir des informations sur les droits et l'offre de soins auprès du Centre national des soins palliatifs et de la fin de vie au 01 53 72 33 04 [3] ainsi que via l'annuaire et la ligne d'écoute de la Société Française d'Accompagnement et de Soins Palliatifs au 01 53 72 33 00 [4].
  • Prise en charge à 100 % (ALD) et aides de l'Assurance Maladie : Vérifiez que le médecin traitant a établi le protocole de soins en Affection de Longue Durée (ALD) exonérante afin que les soins, médicaments et transports liés à la pathologie soient remboursés à 100 % du tarif de la Sécurité sociale par l'Assurance Maladie (joignable au 36 46) [8]. En cas de soins palliatifs à domicile, le service social de la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM) peut également mobiliser le fonds d'action sanitaire et sociale pour financer des heures de garde-malade ou des fournitures non remboursables [8].
  • Allocation personnalisée d'autonomie (APA) en urgence : Si la personne malade est âgée de 60 ans ou plus et subit une perte d'autonomie rapide (GIR 1 à 4), déposez une demande d'APA à domicile auprès du conseil départemental ; en cas d'urgence médicale ou sociale attestée, le président du conseil départemental peut attribuer une APA d'urgence forfaitaire à titre provisoire dès le dépôt du dossier [5].

steps.title: Rédiger les directives anticipées et désigner par écrit la personne de confiance
steps.html:
Dans le cadre de la loi Claeys-Leonetti, deux documents distincts permettent de garantir le respect des volontés médicales de la personne malade si elle n'est plus en mesure de s'exprimer [1][2][3] :

  • Les directives anticipées : Toute personne majeure peut rédiger à tout moment ses directives anticipées (sur papier libre daté et signé avec mention des nom, prénoms, date et lieu de naissance, ou à l'aide du modèle officiel du ministère chargé de la Santé et de la Haute Autorité de Santé) [1][3]. Elles précisent les volontés de la personne quant à la poursuite, la limitation, l'arrêt ou le refus de traitements ou d'actes médicaux en fin de vie, et s'imposent au médecin (hors urgence vitale le temps d'évaluer la situation ou caractère manifestement inapproprié) [1][3]. Si la personne est physiquement dans l'impossibilité d'écrire, deux témoins (dont la personne de confiance) peuvent attester par écrit que le document exprime sa volonté libre et éclairée [1].
  • La personne de confiance : La personne malade peut désigner par écrit (document cosigné par les deux parties) une personne de confiance (un proche, un parent ou le médecin traitant) [2]. Celle-ci peut l'accompagner aux consultations médicales et sera consultée en priorité par l'équipe soignante pour témoigner de la volonté de la personne malade si cette dernière ne peut plus s'exprimer ; son témoignage prévaut sur tout autre avis non médical, à l'exception des directives anticipées [1][2].
  • Conservation et accessibilité : Déposez ces deux documents dans le dossier médical partagé sur Mon espace santé, remettez-en une copie au médecin traitant et à l'équipe hospitalière ou d'HAD, et conservez l'original à domicile avec la personne de confiance [1][2].

steps.title: Sécuriser les procurations courantes et la représentation juridique
steps.html:
La désignation d'une personne de confiance ne confère aucun pouvoir pour gérer les comptes bancaires, le logement ou le patrimoine [2][6]. Tant que votre proche dispose de sa pleine capacité juridique :

  • Procurations bancaires et postales : Établissez des procurations directement auprès de chaque banque (sur les comptes courants et livrets) ainsi qu'une procuration postale auprès de La Poste afin qu'un proche désigné puisse régler les factures courantes, gérer les prélèvements et retirer les courriers recommandés. Sachez que toute procuration bancaire prend automatiquement fin au jour du décès.
  • Mandat de protection future ou procuration notariée : Pour anticiper une éventuelle altération des facultés empêchant la personne de pourvoir seule à ses intérêts (et éviter ainsi une ouverture judiciaire d'habilitation familiale, de curatelle ou de tutelle), elle peut conclure un mandat de protection future avec un ou plusieurs mandataires [6]. Ce mandat peut être établi sous signature privée (formulaire Cerfa n° 13592*04, limité aux actes d'administration courante) ou par acte notarié auprès de l'instance Notaires de France (ce qui permet d'inclure les actes de disposition sur le patrimoine ou la vente d'un bien immobilier) [6]. Le mandat ne prend effet que lorsqu'un certificat médical émanant d'un médecin inscrit sur la liste du procureur de la République constate l'inaptitude et est visé par le greffe du tribunal judiciaire [6]. En parallèle, une procuration générale notariée à effet immédiat peut être signée si la personne souhaite déléguer dès maintenant certaines démarches administratives ou patrimoniales [6].

steps.title: Mobiliser le congé de solidarité familiale et l'allocation journalière (AJAP)
steps.html:
Les proches qui suspendent ou réduisent leur activité professionnelle pour accompagner la personne en fin de vie disposent de droits spécifiques [7][8] :

  • Le congé de solidarité familiale : Tout salarié ou agent public (ascendant, descendant, frère, sœur, personne partageant le même domicile ou désignée comme personne de confiance) a le droit de demander un congé de solidarité familiale à son employeur dès lors qu'un certificat médical atteste que le proche souffre d'une pathologie mettant en jeu le pronostic vital ou est en phase avancée ou terminale d'une affection grave et incurable [7]. D'une durée maximale de 3 mois renouvelable une fois (soit jusqu'à 6 mois au total), il peut être pris de manière continue, fractionnée ou transformé en temps partiel avec l'accord de l'employeur, qui ne peut ni le refuser ni le reporter [7].
  • L'Allocation journalière d'accompagnement d'une personne en fin de vie (AJAP) : Lorsque la personne accompagnée est suivie à domicile (ou en EHPAD), l'Assurance Maladie (ou la MSA selon le régime) verse l'AJAP aux bénéficiaires du congé de solidarité familiale (ainsi qu'aux travailleurs indépendants ou demandeurs d'emploi indemnisés suspendant leur activité) pendant un maximum de 21 jours (ou 42 demi-journées en cas de temps partiel), partageables entre plusieurs proches aidants [8]. Pour connaître toutes les démarches administratives liées au congé et aux droits sociaux, vous pouvez consulter le portail Service-Public.fr (ou appeler le 39 39 Allô Service Public) [7].
  • Alternative en amont de la phase terminale : Si la perte d'autonomie nécessite une aide régulière avant la phase terminale proprement dite, l'aidant peut solliciter un congé de proche aidant indemnisé par l'Allocation journalière du proche aidant (AJPA) auprès de la Caisse d'allocations familiales (CAF) [7].

steps.title: Organiser le testament, les clauses d'assurance-vie et les volontés funéraires
steps.html:
• Rédaction et enregistrement du testament (FCDDV) : La personne peut rédiger un testament olographe (entièrement écrit, daté et signé de sa main) ou dicter un testament authentique à un notaire [9]. Même pour un testament olographe, il est vivement conseillé de le confier à un office notarial via le réseau Notaires de France afin qu'il soit conservé en sécurité et inscrit au Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés (FCDDV), ce qui garantit qu'il sera retrouvé lors du règlement de la succession [9].
  • Contrats d'assurance-vie et capital décès : Demandez à votre proche de vérifier la rédaction exacte des clauses bénéficiaires de ses contrats d'assurance-vie et d'épargne retraite (qui se transmettent hors succession civile) et de rassembler les coordonnées des assureurs. Vérifiez également les conditions d'ouverture du droit au capital décès de la Sécurité sociale auprès de l'Assurance Maladie si la personne était récemment salariée, indemnisée par France Travail ou titulaire d'une pension d'invalidité ou d'une rente d'incapacité permanente [8].
  • Volontés funéraires et dossier administratif : Encouragez votre proche à consigner par écrit ses souhaits concernant ses obsèques (choix entre inhumation et crémation, cérémonie civile ou religieuse, don d'organes ou du corps à la science, et coordonnées d'un éventuel contrat obsèques) et regroupez dans un dossier unique le livret de famille, l'acte de naissance, les titres de propriété, les relevés bancaires et les identifiants numériques [3][9].
