title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Germany: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for your loss. When a family member dies in Germany, federal rules governing civil status, social security, and inheritance law work alongside the burial laws of the respective federal state (Landesbestattungsgesetze). The five official steps below guide you through the required procedures in order.

steps.title: Medical Examination of the Body and Issuance of the Death Certificate
steps.html:
Before any transfer or funeral arrangement can take place, a physician must officially pronounce the death, perform the external post-mortem examination (Leichenschau), and issue an official medical death certificate (Todesbescheinigung or Totenschein) [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, hospice, or care home: The attending or on-duty physician at the facility performs the post-mortem examination on site, issues the Todesbescheinigung (both the confidential and non-confidential sections), and arranges temporary care of the body in the facility's mortuary [1][2].
  • Natural death at home: Immediately notify the deceased person's general practitioner (Hausarztpraxis) or, outside office hours, the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) via the nationwide number 116 117 (or emergency services at 112) so a doctor can perform the examination and issue the Todesbescheinigung [2]. Keep the deceased person's identity card (Personalausweis) ready.
  • Unexplained or non-natural cause of death, or death in a public place: If the examining physician records an unexplained or non-natural manner of death (for example following an accident or sudden unexpected death), the police (emergency number 110 or 112) are called automatically. The public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) investigates the death and must issue written clearance (Bestattungsfreigabe) before burial or cremation can proceed [2].

steps.title: Check Funeral Pre-Arrangements and Appoint a Funeral Director
steps.html:
First check the deceased person's personal papers to see whether a prepaid funeral contract (Bestattungsvorsorgevertrag), funeral expense insurance (Sterbegeldversicherung), or written funeral directive (Bestattungsverfügung) exists:

  • Appointing a funeral director (Bestattungsinstitut): You can find a qualified funeral company through the national professional association (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., telephone +49 211 16008-10) [2]. The appointed funeral director handles collection and transfer to the mortuary (under state burial laws often required within 24 to 36 hours of death), organizes earth burial, cremation, or burial at sea in compliance with Germany's mandatory cemetery requirement (Friedhofszwang), and can complete civil registry formalities on your behalf [2].
  • State burial deadlines (Landesbestattungsgesetze): Statutory timelines for burial depend on the federal state (Bundesland) where the death occurred (generally no earlier than 48 hours after death, and for earth burials usually within 4 to 10 days; prior to cremation, a mandatory second official medical examination is carried out at the crematorium) [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Office and Obtain Death Certificates
steps.html:
Under Section 28 of the Civil Status Act (§ 28 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG), a death must be reported to the competent civil registry office (Standesamt) of the place of death no later than the third working day following the death (with Saturday counting as a working day for deadline purposes) [1]:

  • Who reports the death: When a death occurs in a hospital or care home, the facility operator is legally required to submit the written notification to the Standesamt; when a death occurs at home, the funeral director you appoint almost always handles timely registration on your behalf [1][2].
  • Required documents and certificates issued: The Standesamt requires the medical death certificate (Todesbescheinigung), identity card, birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde), and - depending on marital status - the marriage or civil partnership certificate (plus any final divorce decree or a predeceased spouse's death certificate) [1][2]. The Standesamt issues the official civil death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), the burial permit (Bestattungsschein) for the cemetery administration, free copies for statutory social insurance funds, and, where cross-border matters are involved, a multilingual extract on Form C (Formblatt C) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [1][2]. While the Standesamt automatically notifies the population registry (Meldeamt), tax office (Finanzamt), and probate court (Nachlassgericht), it does not cancel private contracts or bank accounts.

steps.title: Claim the Quarter-Year Pension Advance, Survivor Pensions, and Health Insurance
steps.html:
Statutory pension and health insurance entitlements are not paid automatically; they must be claimed using the civil death certificates issued by the Standesamt:

  • Three-month transition advance (Sterbevierteljahr within 30 days): If the deceased person was already receiving a statutory old-age or reduced-earning-capacity pension, the surviving spouse or registered civil partner can apply within 30 days of the date of death - through the pension payment office (Renten Service der Deutschen Post) or via the funeral director - for an advance payment equal to three times the deceased's last monthly pension covering the Sterbevierteljahr (quarter-year following death) [3][4][5].
  • Survivor pensions (Witwen-, Witwer- und Waisenrente): Eligible survivors submit the formal application for a small or large widow/widower's pension (Form R0500) or orphan's pension directly to the statutory pension insurance authority (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, toll-free service number 0800 1000 4800), ideally within 12 calendar months, as survivor pensions are paid retroactively for a maximum of one year [3][4].
  • Statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung - GKV): Notify the deceased person's health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) and submit a copy of the Sterbeurkunde to terminate membership and, where applicable, transition surviving family members covered under family insurance (Familienversicherung) [2].

steps.title: Probate Court, Certificate of Inheritance, Banks, and Tax Office
steps.html:
To settle the estate, manage bank accounts, and fulfill tax obligations in Germany, observe the following rules:

  • Will submission and probate court (Nachlassgericht): Anyone in possession of a handwritten will (Testament) of the deceased is legally obligated under Section 2259 of the German Civil Code (§ 2259 BGB) to deliver the original document without delay to the competent Nachlassgericht (a division of the local court, Amtsgericht, at the deceased's last habitual residence) [6]. Notarial wills or wills held in official custody are located automatically by the Federal Chamber of Notaries' electronic registry (Zentrales Testamentsregister, toll-free hotline 0800 35 50 100, email info@testamentsregister.de) upon notification from the Standesamt, which alerts the Nachlassgericht to open the will [6].
  • Certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) and renunciation deadline: If there is no notarial will or inheritance contract (Erbvertrag) with an official opening record and no post-mortem bank power of attorney (transmortale Bankvollmacht), banks and the land registry (Grundbuchamt) generally require a judicial Certificate of Inheritance (Erbschein), requested via the Nachlassgericht or a notary [6]. If the estate is over-indebted, the statutory deadline to renounce the inheritance (Erbausschlagung) before the Nachlassgericht or a notary is six weeks from learning of the inheritance (or six months if residing abroad) [6].
  • Banks, insurers, and tax office (Finanzamt): Notify banks, private life or accident insurers (accidental deaths must often be reported to insurers within 48 hours), and the landlord [2]. Heirs must also file the deceased person's final income tax return for the year of death and, if statutory allowances are exceeded, an inheritance tax return (Erbschaftsteuererklärung) with the Finanzamt.

de.title: Was tun im Todesfall in Deutschland: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste nach einem Todesfall in Deutschland: ärztliche Totenbeschau, Beauftragung eines Bestatters, Beurkundung beim Standesamt, Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlassverfahren.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zu Ihrem Verlust. Wenn ein Familienangehöriger in Deutschland verstirbt, greifen bundesrechtliche Vorgaben zum Personenstands-, Sozial- und Erbrecht sowie die jeweiligen Landesbestattungsgesetze ineinander. Die folgenden fünf offiziellen Schritte führen Sie geordnet durch die anstehenden Aufgaben.

steps.title: Ärztliche Leichenschau und Ausstellung der Todesbescheinigung
steps.html:
Vor jeder Überführung oder Bestattung muss der Tod ärztlich festgestellt und durch die äußere Leichenschau eine amtliche Todesbescheinigung (Totenschein) ausgestellt werden [1][2]:

  • Tod im Krankenhaus, Hospiz oder Pflegeheim: Die behandelnde Ärztin oder der diensthabende Arzt der Einrichtung führt die Leichenschau vor Ort durch, stellt die Todesbescheinigung (vertraulicher und nicht-vertraulicher Teil) aus und veranlasst die vorübergehende Versorgung im hauseigenen Kühlraum [1][2].
  • Natürlicher Tod zu Hause: Verständigen Sie umgehend die Hausarztpraxis der verstorbenen Person oder außerhalb der Sprechzeiten den ärztlichen Bereitschaftsdienst unter der bundesweiten Rufnummer 116 117 (bzw. den Rettungsdienst unter 112), damit eine Ärztin oder ein Arzt die Leichenschau vornimmt und die Todesbescheinigung ausstellt [2]. Halten Sie den Personalausweis der verstorbenen Person bereit.
  • Ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesursache bzw. Tod im öffentlichen Raum: Bescheinigt die Ärztin oder der Arzt eine ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesart (etwa nach einem Unfall oder plötzlichen Tod), wird automatisch die Polizei (Notruf 110 oder 112) hinzugezogen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft prüft den Todesfall und muss den Leichnam erst schriftlich zur Bestattung (insbesondere vor einer Feuerbestattung) freigeben [2].

steps.title: Bestattungsvorsorge prüfen und ein Bestattungsunternehmen beauftragen
steps.html:
Prüfen Sie zunächst in den Unterlagen der verstorbenen Person, ob bereits ein Bestattungsvorsorgevertrag, eine Sterbegeldversicherung oder eine schriftliche Bestattungsverfügung vorliegt:

  • Beauftragung eines Bestattungsinstituts: Ein qualifiziertes Bestattungsunternehmen finden Sie über den Berufsverband (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., Telefon +49 211 16008-10) [2]. Das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen übernimmt die Abholung und Überführung in die Leichenhalle (je nach Landesbestattungsgesetz oft innerhalb von 24 bis 36 Stunden nach Eintritt des Todes), die Organisation der Erd-, Feuer- oder Seebestattung unter Beachtung des gesetzlichen Friedhofszwangs sowie auf Wunsch die Behördengänge [2].
  • Bestattungsfristen der Bundesländer: Die Fristen für die Beisetzung richten sich nach dem jeweiligen Landesbestattungsgesetz des Sterbeortes (in der Regel frühestens 48 Stunden nach dem Tod und bei einer Erdbestattung meist innerhalb von 4 bis 10 Tagen; vor einer Kremation findet im Krematorium eine gesetzlich vorgeschriebene zweite Amtsarztleichenschau statt) [2].

steps.title: Sterbefall beim Standesamt anzeigen und Sterbeurkunden beantragen
steps.html:
Nach § 28 des Personenstandsgesetzes (PStG) muss ein Sterbefall spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag (wobei der Samstag fristenrechtlich als Werktag zählt) beim zuständigen Standesamt des Sterbeortes angezeigt werden [1]:

  • Wer die Anzeige erstattet: Bei einem Tod im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim ist der Träger der Einrichtung gesetzlich zur schriftlichen Anzeige beim Standesamt verpflichtet; bei einem Sterbefall zu Hause übernimmt in der Praxis fast immer das von Ihnen beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen die fristgerechte Meldung [1][2].
  • Erforderliche Unterlagen und Urkunden: Dem Standesamt sind die ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, der Personalausweis, die Geburtsurkunde sowie je nach Familienstand die Eheurkunde oder Lebenspartnerschaftsurkunde (und gegebenenfalls ein rechtskräftiges Scheidungsurteil oder die Sterbeurkunde eines vorverstorbenen Ehepartners) vorzulegen [1][2]. Das Standesamt stellt die Sterbeurkunde, den Bestattungsschein für die Friedhofsverwaltung, kostenfreie Ausfertigungen für Sozialversicherungsträger sowie bei Auslandsbezug einen mehrsprachigen Auszug auf Formblatt C (nach dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen von 1976) aus [1][2]. Das Standesamt informiert automatisch das Meldeamt, das Finanzamt und das Nachlassgericht, kündigt jedoch keine privaten Verträge oder Bankkonten.

steps.title: Sterbevierteljahr, Hinterbliebenenrenten und Krankenversicherung regeln
steps.html:
Gesetzliche Renten- und Krankenversicherungsansprüche werden nicht automatisch ausgezahlt, sondern müssen mit den standesamtlichen Sterbeurkunden beantragt werden:

  • Vorschuss für das Sterbevierteljahr (innerhalb von 30 Tagen): Bezog die verstorbene Person bereits eine gesetzliche Alters- oder Erwerbsminderungsrente, kann der überlebende Ehegatte oder eingetragene Lebenspartner innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Todestag über die Zahlstelle (Renten Service der Deutschen Post) oder das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen einen Vorschuss in Höhe des Dreifachen der letzten Monatsrente für das sogenannte Sterbevierteljahr beantragen [3][4][5].
  • Hinterbliebenenrente (Witwen-, Witwer- und Waisenrente): Den regulären Antrag auf kleine oder große Witwen-/Witwerrente (Formular R0500) oder Waisenrente stellen Berechtigte direkt beim zuständigen Rentenversicherungsträger (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, kostenfreie Servicenummer 0800 1000 4800), idealerweise innerhalb von 12 Kalendermonaten, da die Rente maximal ein Jahr rückwirkend gezahlt wird [3][4].
  • Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung (GKV): Informieren Sie die Krankenkasse der verstorbenen Person unter Vorlage der Sterbeurkunde, um die Mitgliedschaft zu beenden und gegebenenfalls die Weiterführung einer bestehenden Familienversicherung für Hinterbliebene zu klären [2].

steps.title: Nachlassgericht, Erbschein, Banken und Finanzamt
steps.html:
Für die Abwicklung des Nachlasses, der Bankkonten und der Steuererklärungen gelten folgende Zuständigkeiten:

  • Testamentsablieferung und Nachlassgericht: Wer ein handschriftliches Testament der verstorbenen Person auffindet, ist gesetzlich verpflichtet (§ 2259 BGB), dieses unverzüglich im Original beim zuständigen Nachlassgericht (Abteilung des Amtsgerichts am letzten gewöhnlichen Aufenthaltsort der verstorbenen Person) abzuliefern [6]. Notarielle oder amtlich verwahrte Verfügungen ermittelt das elektronische Register der Bundesnotarkammer (Zentrales Testamentsregister, kostenfreie Hotline 0800 35 50 100, E-Mail info@testamentsregister.de) automatisch nach der Sterbefallmeldung des Standesamts und benachrichtigt das Nachlassgericht zur Testamentseröffnung [6].
  • Erbschein oder notarielles Testament (und Ausschlagungsfrist): Liegt kein notarielles Testament oder Erbvertrag mit Eröffnungsprotokoll und keine transmortale Bankvollmacht vor, verlangen Banken und das Grundbuchamt regelmäßig einen gerichtlichen Erbschein, der beim Nachlassgericht oder über ein Notariat beantragt wird [6]. Falls der Nachlass überschuldet ist, beträgt die gesetzliche Frist zur Erbausschlagung sechs Wochen ab Kenntnis des Erbfalls (bzw. sechs Monate bei Auslandsaufenthalt) gegenüber dem Nachlassgericht oder einem Notariat.
  • Banken, Versicherungen und Finanzamt: Benachrichtigen Sie Kreditinstitute, private Lebens- oder Unfallversicherungen (Unfalltod ist der Versicherung oft binnen 48 Stunden zu melden) sowie den Vermieter. Die Erben müssen zudem für das Todesjahr die abschließende Einkommensteuererklärung der verstorbenen Person sowie bei Überschreiten der Freibeträge eine Erbschaftsteuererklärung beim Finanzamt einreichen.

de.closingQuestion: Um Ihnen noch gezielter weiterhelfen zu können: In welchem Bundesland (bzw. welcher Gemeinde) ist der Sterbefall eingetreten, und liegt ein Testament oder eine über den Tod hinaus geltende Bankvollmacht vor?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in France: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences. When a family member dies in France, medical certification, funeral arrangements, civil registration, and estate administration follow a strict statutory timetable. Below are the five official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and Issuance of the Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
Every funeral or civil registry procedure in France must begin with a physician verifying the death and issuing the official medical death certificate (certificat médical de décès, either on a paper Cerfa form or electronically via the CertDc application), which comprises an administrative section and a confidential medical section [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or care home (EHPAD): The attending or facility physician verifies the death and issues the certificat médical de décès directly [1][2]. The facility cares for the body in its mortuary (chambre mortuaire) while funeral arrangements are organized [2].
  • Natural death at home: Call the deceased person's attending physician (médecin traitant), SOS Médecins, or the SAMU (15) emergency medical service (or the European emergency number 112) so a doctor can come to the home to pronounce the death and complete the medical death certificate [1][2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or public-space death (obstacle médico-légal): In the event of a violent, sudden, or suspicious death, contact emergency services immediately (15, 17, or 112). Law enforcement (police or gendarmerie) draws up an official report and the physician checks the medico-legal hold box (obstacle médico-légal) on the certificate; the body is then transferred to a forensic institute (institut médico-légal), and burial or cremation cannot take place without formal authorization from the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) [1][2].

steps.title: Check Funeral Wishes and Appoint a Licensed Funeral Director
steps.html:
Before signing an estimate, check whether your relative held a funeral insurance policy (contrat d'assurance obsèques) or left written instructions regarding their funeral (choice between burial and cremation, place of interment) [2]:

  • Appointing a licensed funeral operator (opérateur funéraire habilité): You must use a funeral company holding official prefectoral accreditation (habilitation préfectorale); you can consult the official list of licensed operators displayed at the town hall (mairie) or hospital mortuary, or find a provider through national trade federations such as the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) or the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF) [2]. The appointed funeral operator coordinates transport of the body (to a funeral home, chambre funéraire, within 48 hours of death if transfer before coffining is requested), placement in the coffin (mise en bière), and municipal authorizations for closing the coffin and for burial (permis d'inhumer) or cremation (autorisation de crémation) [2].
  • Statutory burial or cremation deadlines: In mainland France, burial or cremation must take place no earlier than 24 hours after death and no later than 14 calendar days following the day after death (unless a prefectoral exemption is granted) [2]. Funeral expenses may be paid directly from the deceased person's bank account up to 5,910 EUR (a statutory ceiling indexed annually) upon presentation of the funeral director's invoice [2][6].

steps.title: Register the Death at the Town Hall Within 24 Hours
steps.html:
Registering the death (déclaration de décès) is mandatory and must be completed at the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred within 24 hours of medical verification (excluding weekends and public holidays) [1][2]:

  • Who registers the death and required documents: When a death occurs in a hospital or EHPAD, the facility may submit the declaration directly; otherwise, a family member or the appointed funeral director attends the civil status office (service d'état civil) of the mairie with their own ID, the medical death certificate (certificat médical de décès), and civil status documents for the deceased (such as the livret de famille, identity card, passport, or birth certificate) [1][2].
  • Official death certificates and inter-agency notifications: The mairie draws up the official death record and issues several full copies of the death certificate (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès), as well as a multilingual extract on Form C (Formule C) under the 1976 Vienna Convention if cross-border procedures are anticipated [1]. You can consult all official rules and forms on the French administration portal Service-Public.fr (telephone 3939) [1][2]. The mairie automatically forwards the death notice to the national statistics institute (INSEE), which notifies the tax authorities and French pension funds to suspend ongoing payments, though claiming survivor benefits and closing private accounts remain the family's responsibility [4][5][7].

steps.title: Claim the Social Security Death Grant and Survivor Pensions
steps.html:
Depending on the deceased person's employment or retirement status, eligible survivors may claim lump-sum grants and survivor pensions:

  • Social Security lump-sum death grant (capital décès): If the deceased was employed, receiving unemployment benefits, or drawing an invalidity pension during the three months preceding death, priority beneficiaries (dependents who were wholly and permanently supported by the deceased at the time of death, who have one month to assert their priority) or, failing that, the surviving spouse, civil partner (partenaire de PACS), children, or ascendants can apply for the lump-sum capital décès (Form S3180) from the local health insurance fund (CPAM) via Ameli.fr (telephone 3646) within two years of the death [3].
  • Basic and supplementary survivor pensions (pensions de réversion): Although the death is reported via civil registry channels, you should notify the basic state pension fund L'Assurance Retraite (CNAV / CARSAT, telephone 3960) [4] as well as the private-sector supplementary pension scheme Agirc-Arrco (telephone 0 970 660 660) [5]. A surviving spouse or divorced ex-spouse (note that PACS civil partnerships and unmarried cohabitation do not confer entitlement to a survivor pension under these schemes) can submit a single online application for a survivor pension (pension de réversion) covering all French retirement schemes [4][5].

steps.title: Notify Banks and Tax Authorities and Settle the Estate Through a Notary
steps.html:
To close accounts, fulfill tax obligations, and settle the estate (succession) in France:

  • Engaging a notary and opening the succession: Appointing a notary (notaire) is mandatory whenever the estate includes real estate, a will (testament), or a gift between spouses (donation entre époux), or when gross estate assets reach or exceed 5,000 EUR (in order to draw up the certificate of heirship, acte de notoriété) [1][6]. You can consult the official directory on Notaires de France to instruct a notary's office, which will search the Central Register of Last Wills (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV) and draw up the inventory of the estate [1][6]. For small estates under 5,000 EUR with no real property or will, a signed heirship declaration (attestation signée par l'ensemble des héritiers) may suffice to release bank funds [2][6].
  • Banks and insurance companies: Send a copy of the acte de décès to all banks as soon as possible (which freezes the deceased's individual accounts, apart from direct payment of funeral bills, while joint accounts remain usable by the surviving co-holder unless heirs object) and submit a search request to AGIRA if you believe your relative held a life insurance policy (assurance-vie) [2][6].
  • Tax filings (Impots.gouv.fr): The notary or the heirs must file the inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) with the registration office of the Public Finance Directorate (DGFiP) via Impots.gouv.fr (telephone 0 809 401 401) within 6 months of the date of death if the death occurred in mainland France (12 months if the death occurred outside mainland France), and report the income received by the deceased up to the date of death during the annual income tax filing campaign [6][7].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation, in which French municipality (commune) did the death occur, and does the estate include real property or a known will?

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès en France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès en France : certificat médical de décès, choix des pompes funèbres, déclaration à l'état civil, capital décès et pensions de réversion, et règlement de la succession.
fr.introHtml: Nous vous présentons nos sincères condoléances. Lorsqu'un proche décède en France, les démarches médicales, funéraires, d'état civil et successorales obéissent à un calendrier réglementaire précis. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles pour organiser la suite dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et établissement du certificat de décès
steps.html:
Toute démarche funéraire ou d'état civil commence obligatoirement par la constatation médicale du décès et la délivrance du certificat médical de décès (formulaire Cerfa ou certificat électronique via l'application CertDc), composé d'un volet administratif et d'un volet médical confidentiel [1][2] :

  • Décès à l'hôpital, en clinique ou en EHPAD : Le médecin du service ou de l'établissement constate le décès et établit directement le certificat médical de décès [1][2]. L'établissement assure la conservation du corps en chambre mortuaire dans l'attente de l'organisation des obsèques [2].
  • Décès naturel à domicile : Appelez le médecin traitant de la personne décédée, SOS Médecins ou le SAMU (15) (ou le numéro d'urgence européen 112) afin qu'un médecin se déplace au domicile pour constater le décès et rédiger le certificat médical de décès [1][2].
  • Décès soudain, accidentel ou sur la voie publique (obstacle médico-légal) : En cas de mort violente, soudaine ou suspecte, contactez immédiatement les secours (15, 17 ou 112). Les forces de l'ordre (police ou gendarmerie) dressent un procès-verbal et le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat ; le corps est alors transféré vers un institut médico-légal et l'inhumation ou la crémation ne peut avoir lieu qu'après l'autorisation formelle du procureur de la République [1][2].

steps.title: Vérification des volontés funéraires et mandat d'un opérateur funéraire habilité
steps.html:
Avant de signer un devis, vérifiez si votre proche avait souscrit un contrat d'assurance obsèques ou exprimé ses volontés par écrit (choix entre inhumation et crémation, lieu de sépulture) [2] :

  • Choix d'une entreprise de pompes funèbres : Vous devez faire appel à un opérateur funéraire disposant d'une habilitation préfectorale (vous pouvez consulter la liste officielle des entreprises habilitées affichée en mairie ou en chambre mortuaire, ou vous orienter via les fédérations professionnelles telles que la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire ou la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres) [2]. L'opérateur mandaté coordonne le transport du corps (en chambre funéraire dans les 48 heures suivant le décès si un transfert avant mise en bière est demandé), la mise en bière, ainsi que les demandes d'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil et de permis d'inhumer ou d'autorisation de crémation auprès de la mairie [2].
  • Délais légaux d'inhumation ou de crémation : En France métropolitaine, l'inhumation ou la crémation doit intervenir au plus tôt 24 heures après le décès et au plus tard dans un délai maximal de 14 jours calendaires suivant le lendemain du décès (sauf dérogation préfectorale) [2]. Les frais d'obsèques peuvent être prélevés directement sur le compte bancaire de la personne décédée à hauteur de 5 910 EUR (plafond revalorisé annuellement) sur présentation de la facture de l'opérateur funéraire [2][6].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès à la mairie dans les 24 heures
steps.html:
La déclaration de décès est obligatoire et doit être effectuée à la mairie du lieu de décès dans les 24 heures suivant la constatation du décès (hors week-ends et jours fériés) [1][2] :

  • Qui effectue la déclaration et avec quelles pièces : En cas de décès dans un établissement de santé ou un EHPAD, l'établissement peut se charger de la déclaration ; dans les autres cas, la famille ou l'entreprise de pompes funèbres mandatée se présente au service d'état civil de la mairie avec sa propre pièce d'identité, le certificat médical de décès et un justificatif d'état civil de la personne décédée (livret de famille, carte d'identité, passeport ou acte de naissance) [1][2].
  • Acte de décès et transmission aux organismes : La mairie dresse l'acte de décès et vous remet plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès (ainsi qu'un extrait plurilingue sur Formule C de la Convention de Vienne de 1976 si des démarches à l'étranger sont prévues) [1]. Vous pouvez retrouver l'ensemble des règles et formulaires sur le portail officiel Service-Public.fr (téléphone 3939) [1][2]. La mairie transmet automatiquement l'avis de décès à l'INSEE, qui informe notamment l'administration fiscale et les caisses de retraite françaises pour suspendre les versements, mais les demandes de prestations et la clôture des comptes privés restent à l'initiative des proches [4][5][7].

steps.title: Demande du capital décès et des pensions de réversion
steps.html:
Selon le statut professionnel ou de retraité de la personne décédée, les ayants droit peuvent solliciter des aides financières et pensions de survivant :

  • Capital décès de la Sécurité sociale : Si la personne décédée était salariée, au chômage indemnisé ou titulaire d'une pension d'invalidité dans les trois mois précédant le décès, les bénéficiaires prioritaires (personnes à la charge effective, totale et permanente au jour du décès, qui disposent d'un mois pour faire valoir leur priorité) ou, à défaut, le conjoint survivant, le partenaire de PACS, les enfants ou les ascendants peuvent demander le versement forfaitaire du capital décès (formulaire S3180) auprès de la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie via le portail Ameli.fr (téléphone 3646) dans un délai maximal de deux ans [3].
  • Retraite de base et complémentaire (réversion) : Bien que le décès soit signalé via l'état civil, il est conseillé d'en informer le régime de base L'Assurance Retraite (CNAV / CARSAT, téléphone 3960) [4] ainsi que le régime complémentaire des salariés du secteur privé Agirc-Arrco (téléphone 0 970 660 660) [5]. Le conjoint ou ex-conjoint survivant (le PACS et le concubinage n'ouvrent pas droit à la réversion dans ces régimes) peut déposer une demande unique en ligne de pension de réversion couvrant l'ensemble des régimes de retraite [4][5].

steps.title: Information des banques, des impôts et règlement de la succession par un notaire
steps.html:
Pour clôturer les comptes, accomplir les obligations fiscales et régler la succession en France :

  • Recours à un notaire et ouverture de la succession : L'intervention d'un notaire est obligatoire dès lors que la succession comprend un bien immobilier, qu'il existe un testament ou une donation entre époux, ou que l'actif successoral atteint ou dépasse 5 000 EUR (afin d'établir l'acte de notoriété prouvant la qualité d'héritier) [1][6]. Vous pouvez consulter l'annuaire officiel sur le portail Notaires de France pour mandater une étude notariale, qui interrogera le Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés (FCDDV) et dressera le bilan patrimonial [1][6]. Pour les petites successions sans bien immobilier ni testament inférieures à 5 000 EUR, une attestation signée par l'ensemble des héritiers peut suffire auprès de la banque [2][6].
  • Banques et compagnies d'assurance : Transmettez une copie de l'acte de décès aux banques dès que possible (ce qui bloque les comptes individuels de la personne décédée, hors prélèvement des frais d'obsèques, tandis que les comptes joints restent utilisables par le cotitulaire sauf opposition des héritiers) et interrogez l'AGIRA si vous pensez que votre proche détenait un contrat d'assurance-vie [2][6].
  • Obligations fiscales (Impots.gouv.fr) : Le notaire ou les héritiers doivent déposer la déclaration de succession auprès du service de l'enregistrement de la Direction générale des finances publiques via Impots.gouv.fr (téléphone 0 809 401 401) dans un délai de 6 mois à compter du décès lorsque celui-ci a eu lieu en France métropolitaine (12 mois en cas de décès hors métropole), et déclarer les revenus perçus par la personne décédée jusqu'à la date du décès lors de la campagne annuelle d'impôt sur le revenu [6][7].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Spain: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When someone dies in Spain, urgent medical and civil registration formalities are coordinated primarily through a licensed funeral company and the Civil Registry (Registro Civil), followed by social security claims and inheritance procedures. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Verification and Official Certification of Death
steps.html:
The essential first step is obtaining the official Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción), which is required to register the death and authorize transfer or burial [1][5]:

  • Death in a hospital or care home: The facility's medical team verifies the death and issues the official Certificado Médico de Defunción directly [1][5].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs outside a healthcare facility from known natural causes, call emergency services (112) or the local primary healthcare center (centro de salud) so a physician can attend and certify the death [5]. In the event of a sudden, violent, or unexplained death, emergency services and law enforcement notify the Duty Court (Juzgado de Guardia), which orders the removal of the body and its transfer to the competent Institute of Legal Medicine (Instituto de Medicina Legal) for an autopsy before authorizing civil registration and burial [1][5].
  • Sanitary timelines (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria): Regional mortuary health regulations across Spain's autonomous communities generally stipulate that burial or cremation cannot take place until at least 24 hours have elapsed since death (unless expressly authorized by judicial or health authorities) and is typically carried out within 48 hours once registry formalities are complete [5].

steps.title: Funeral Insurance and Appointing a Licensed Funeral Provider
steps.html:
Before contracting funeral services independently, check whether the deceased person held a funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos - very common in Spain) or life/bank card coverage [5]:

  • Activating funeral insurance (seguro de decesos): If a funeral insurance policy exists, call the insurer's 24-hour assistance helpline immediately so they can coordinate the entire funeral service from the outset [5].
  • Appointing a licensed funeral company (empresa funeraria habilitada): If there is no policy in place, the family must directly appoint an authorized funeral company, which can be located through the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (National Association of Funeral Services - PANASEF) or municipal and regional registries [5]. The funeral provider collects the Certificado Médico de Defunción, transfers the body to the funeral home (tanatorio), arranges the burial or cremation permit (licencia de enterramiento o incineración), and manages the statutory mortuary health timelines of the relevant autonomous community [5]. Always request an itemized quote before signing the contract [5].

steps.title: Registration with the Civil Registry and Obtaining Official Certificates
steps.html:
The death must be registered with the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred - operating under the Ministerio de Justicia (Ministry of Justice) - generally within 24 hours of death and always before burial or cremation takes place [1].

In standard practice, the funeral company submits the declaration and the Certificado Médico de Defunción (or files them electronically from the hospital or tanatorio) with the Registro Civil, presenting the deceased person's national identity card (DNI) or foreigner identity number (NIE) [1][5]. Once registered, the Registro Civil issues:

  • The burial or cremation permit (licencia de enterramiento o incineración): Mandatory for the cemetery or crematorium to proceed [1].
  • The Full Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción): Request several certified copies for banks, insurers, and public authorities [1].
  • The Multilingual Death Certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción - Fórmula C): If assets, pensions, or legal procedures exist in another European country, also request Form C under the 1976 Vienna Convention, which is exempt from translation and apostille across signatory states [1].

steps.title: Claiming the Funeral Grant and Survivor Pensions
steps.html:
Using the Certificado Literal de Defunción, eligible family members can apply for Death and Survivor Benefits (Prestaciones por Muerte y Supervivencia) from the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (National Institute of Social Security - INSS), either online via the Social Security Electronic Headquarters (Sede Electrónica de la Seguridad Social) or in person at a Social Security Information and Service Center (CAISS) [3][4]:

  • Funeral grant (auxilio por defunción): A one-time grant payable to the person who bore the funeral expenses (surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, children, or cohabiting relatives) upon presentation of the funeral invoice [3][4].
  • Widow/widower's and orphan's pensions (pensión de viudedad y pensión de orfandad): Periodic pensions payable to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner (pareja de hecho) and to minor or disabled children (or older children within statutory age and study limits) [3][4]. Where the deceased was a pensioner or an active social security contributor, the application may be submitted at any time, although retroactive economic effects are generally capped at three months prior to the application date [4].

steps.title: Last Wills Registry, Notary, Banks, and Inheritance Tax
steps.html:
To settle the estate, unlock bank accounts, and comply with Spanish tax deadlines, follow this official sequence:

  • Certificates of last wills and life/accident insurance: Once 15 working days (15 días hábiles) have passed since the date of death, apply to the Ministerio de Justicia using Form 790 (Modelo 790, Código 006) for the Certificate from the General Registry of Last Wills (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad, which shows whether the deceased made a will and before which notary) and the Certificate of Insurance Contracts Providing Death Coverage (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento) [1][2].
  • Notarial inheritance deed: Taking these certificates and the Certificado Literal de Defunción, contact a notary's office - which you can locate through the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of the Notariat) - to obtain an authorized copy (copia autorizada) of the last will and execute the deed of acceptance and division of inheritance (escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia), or, if there is no will, to process the intestate declaration of heirs (acta de declaración de herederos abintestato) [6].
  • Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones): Heirs and life insurance beneficiaries have a statutory deadline of 6 months from the date of death to file the self-assessment or tax return with the competent regional tax authority of the autonomous community or, where applicable due to non-residency or state rules, with the Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency) [7]. You may request a 6-month extension provided the application is submitted within the first 5 months following the death [7].
  • Bank accounts: Notify banks of the death by submitting the Certificado Literal de Defunción. Banks will place a precautionary freeze on the deceased's funds (except for authorized debits covering funeral expenses) until heirship and payment or exemption of Inheritance Tax are documented [6][7].

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en España: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona fallece en España, las gestiones urgentes se coordinan principalmente a través de la empresa funeraria autorizada y el Registro Civil, seguidas de las solicitudes de prestaciones y los trámites sucesorios. A continuación se detallan los cinco pasos oficiales en orden.

steps.title: Verificación médica y certificación oficial de la defunción
steps.html:
El primer paso indispensable es la emisión del Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial, necesario para inscribir el fallecimiento y autorizar el traslado o sepelio [1][5]:

  • Fallecimiento en hospital o centro residencial: El equipo médico del centro sanitario verifica el fallecimiento y expide directamente el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial [1][5].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Si el deceso ocurre fuera de un centro sanitario por causas naturales conocidas, debe avisarse a los servicios de emergencias (112) o al centro de salud de atención primaria para que un facultativo acuda a certificar la muerte [5]. Si se trata de una muerte súbita, violenta o con causas no esclarecidas, los servicios de emergencia y las fuerzas de seguridad dan aviso al Juzgado de Guardia, que ordena el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal correspondiente para practicar la autopsia antes de autorizar la inscripción y el entierro [1][5].
  • Plazos sanitarios: Los reglamentos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria establecen con carácter general que la inhumación o cremación no puede realizarse antes de las 24 horas desde el fallecimiento (salvo autorización judicial o sanitaria expresa) y suele efectuarse dentro de las 48 horas siguientes, una vez cumplidos los trámites registrales [5].

steps.title: Seguro de decesos y designación de una empresa funeraria habilitada
steps.html:
Antes de contratar servicios por cuenta propia, compruebe si la persona fallecida disponía de una póliza de seguro de decesos, seguro de vida o cobertura vinculada a tarjetas bancarias. Si existe seguro de decesos, llame inmediatamente al teléfono de asistencia 24 horas de la aseguradora para que coordine el servicio funerario desde el inicio [5].

Si no hay póliza contratada, la familia debe designar directamente una empresa funeraria habilitada, que puede localizarse a través de la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) o de los registros municipales y autonómicos [5]. La funeraria se encarga de recoger el Certificado Médico de Defunción, trasladar el cuerpo al tanatorio, tramitar la licencia de enterramiento o incineración y gestionar los tiempos exigidos por la normativa de sanidad mortuoria de la comunidad autónoma correspondiente [5]. Solicite siempre un presupuesto desglosado antes de firmar el contrato.

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil y obtención de certificados oficiales
steps.html:
El fallecimiento debe inscribirse en el Registro Civil del municipio donde se produjo el deceso, dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia, con carácter general dentro de las 24 horas siguientes a la defunción y siempre antes de proceder a la inhumación o cremación [1].

En la práctica habitual, la empresa funeraria presenta la declaración y el Certificado Médico de Defunción (o los remite telemáticamente desde el centro sanitario o tanatorio) ante el Registro Civil, entregando el DNI o NIE de la persona fallecida [1][5]. Una vez practicada la inscripción, el Registro Civil expide:

  • La licencia de enterramiento o incineración, imprescindible para el cementerio o crematorio [1].
  • El Certificado Literal de Defunción, del que conviene solicitar varias copias para bancos, aseguradoras y administraciones [1].
  • Si existen bienes, pensiones o trámites en otro país europeo, solicite también el Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C) conforme al Convenio de Viena de 1976, que exime de traducción y apostilla en los Estados parte [1].

steps.title: Solicitud de auxilio por defunción y pensiones de supervivencia
steps.html:
Con el Certificado Literal de Defunción, los familiares con derecho pueden solicitar las Prestaciones por Muerte y Supervivencia ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS), ya sea a través de la Sede Electrónica de la Seguridad Social o en un Centro de Atención e Información de la Seguridad Social (CAISS) [3][4]:

  • Auxilio por defunción: Ayuda única destinada a quien haya sufragado los gastos del sepelio (cónyuge, pareja de hecho, hijos o familiares convivientes), presentando la factura funeraria [3][4].
  • Pensión de viudedad y pensión de orfandad: Prestaciones económicas periódicas destinadas al cónyuge o pareja de hecho registrada superviviente y a los hijos menores o incapacitados (o mayores dentro de los límites legales de edad y estudios) [3][4]. Si la persona fallecida era pensionista o cotizante en alta, la solicitud puede presentarse en cualquier momento, aunque los efectos económicos retroactivos generales alcanzan un máximo de tres meses previos a la solicitud [4].

steps.title: Últimas voluntades, notaría, bancos e Impuesto sobre Sucesiones
steps.html:
Para tramitar la herencia, desbloquear cuentas bancarias y cumplir las obligaciones fiscales, siga esta secuencia oficial:

  • Certificados de actos de última voluntad y de seguros: Transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la fecha del fallecimiento, solicite ante el Ministerio de Justicia mediante el Modelo 790 (Código 006) el Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (que indica si existe testamento y ante qué notario se otorgó) y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento [1][2].
  • Tramitación notarial: Con dichos certificados y el Certificado Literal de Defunción, acuda a una notaría - localizable mediante el Consejo General del Notariado - para solicitar copia autorizada del último testamento y otorgar la escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia, o bien, si no existe testamento, tramitar el acta de declaración de herederos abintestato [6].
  • Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones: Los herederos y beneficiarios de seguros de vida disponen de un plazo legal de 6 meses desde la fecha del fallecimiento para presentar la autoliquidación o declaración ante la administración tributaria autonómica competente o, cuando corresponda por residencia o normativa estatal, ante la Agencia Tributaria [7]. Es posible solicitar una prórroga de otros 6 meses siempre que se pida dentro de los primeros 5 meses desde el fallecimiento [7].
  • Entidades bancarias: Notifique el fallecimiento a los bancos presentando el Certificado Literal de Defunción. Las entidades bloquearán cautelarmente la disposición de fondos (salvo cargos autorizados de gastos de sepelio) hasta que se acredite la condición de heredero y la liquidación o exención del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones [6][7].

es.closingQuestion: Para poder ofrecerle indicaciones más precisas si las necesita: 1. ¿En qué municipio y comunidad autónoma ha tenido lugar el fallecimiento y dónde tenía su residencia habitual la persona fallecida? 2. ¿El fallecimiento se ha producido en un hospital o requiere intervención judicial en domicilio?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Italy: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. In Italy, initial medico-legal and civil status formalities are usually coordinated by the appointed funeral company together with the healthcare facility or municipal offices, while social security and inheritance filings take place over the following days and months. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and the Necroscopic Certificate
steps.html:
The first requirement is the medical verification of death and the official examination by the necroscopic physician (medico necroscopo) under Italy's Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento di polizia mortuaria, Presidential Decree D.P.R. No. 285/1990) [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or care facility (struttura sanitaria / RSA): The hospital's medical management (direzione sanitaria) handles the verification of death, completes the necroscopic certification, and transmits the formal notice of death (avviso di morte) to the Civil Status Officer (Ufficiale dello Stato Civile) of the municipality [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs in a private residence from known natural causes, contact the attending general practitioner (medico curante) or out-of-hours medical service (guardia medica, or emergency numbers 112 / 118) to issue the initial certificate of verification of death (certificato di constatazione del decesso) and the ISTAT cause-of-death statistical form (scheda ISTAT) [1][2]. Subsequently, the medico necroscopo appointed by the Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) performs the official post-mortem examination - normally between 15 and 30 hours after death - and issues the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico) [2]. In the event of a sudden death in a public place, or a suspicious or violent death, emergency services (112/118) and law enforcement notify the Public Prosecutor's Office (Procura della Repubblica); the body remains at the disposal of the Judicial Authority until a formal burial clearance (nulla osta alla sepoltura) is issued [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage and Appoint an Authorized Funeral Provider
steps.html:
Before entering into financial commitments, check whether the deceased person held a funeral expense insurance policy or a prepaid funeral contract (contratto di previdenza funeraria) [2][3]:

  • Selecting a licensed funeral company (impresa funebre autorizzata): The family grants a mandate to an authorized funeral operator, which can be identified through municipal registries or the main national trade associations such as the Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (National Federation of Funeral Directors - FENIOF) or the Federazione del Comparto Funerario Italiano (Federcofit) [2][3].
  • Statutory observation period and funeral coordination: As a rule, the coffin cannot be sealed and burial or cremation cannot take place until at least 24 hours have elapsed since death (48 hours in cases of sudden death, unless early instrumental verification is performed or the Judicial Authority directs otherwise) [1][2]. The funeral company coordinates preparation of the body, transport, and filing of the medical documents with the municipality (Comune) to obtain the required permits [1][2].

steps.title: Registering the Death with the Civil Status Office and Obtaining Certificates
steps.html:
Under Presidential Decree D.P.R. No. 396/2000, the formal declaration of death (dichiarazione di morte) must be filed within 24 hours of death with the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the municipality (Comune) where the death occurred, under the institutional oversight of the Ministero dell'Interno (Ministry of the Interior) [1].

In standard practice, the declaration is submitted either by the hospital medical management (for hospital deaths) or by the funeral company expressly delegated by the family, enclosing the certificato necroscopico and the scheda ISTAT [1]. The Civil Status Officer draws up the death record (atto di morte) and issues:

  • The burial permit (permesso di seppellimento): Together with, where requested and authorized on the basis of the deceased's expressed wishes or family attestation, the cremation authorization (autorizzazione alla cremazione) [1].
  • The death certificate (certificato di morte) and summary extract (estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte): Including, where cross-border procedures are required in other signatory states, the multilingual extract on Form C (Modello C) under the 1976 Vienna Convention, which is exempt from translation and apostille [1].

Recording the death in Italy's National Resident Population Register (Anagrafe Nazionale della Popolazione Residente - ANPR) automatically updates municipal population records and notifies connected public agencies such as INPS and the Revenue Agency [1][4].

steps.title: Claiming Survivor Pensions and Social Security Benefits
steps.html:
Even though the municipality transmits the death notification electronically, eligible family members must submit a formal claim to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Institute for Social Security - INPS) to receive survivor benefits [4]:

  • Survivor's pension (pensione ai superstiti - reversibilità or indiretta): Payable to the surviving spouse or civil union partner, minor children, dependent student or disabled children, and - under specific dependency conditions - grandchildren, parents, or siblings [4]. It is termed a pensione di reversibilità if the deceased was already drawing a pension, or a pensione indiretta if the deceased was an insured worker who met statutory contribution requirements [4].
  • Accrued and unpaid pension installments (ratei maturati e non riscossi): Any pension installments or thirteenth-month bonus (tredicesima) accrued by the deceased prior to death but not yet paid out [4].

Applications are filed online via the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale portal using digital credentials (SPID, CIE, or CNS) or free of charge through an accredited Patronato assistance office [4].

steps.title: Will Search, Bank Notifications, and the Inheritance Tax Return
steps.html:
To administer the estate, handle bank accounts, and fulfill Italian tax obligations, complete the following steps:

  • Searching for a will (Registro Generale dei Testamenti): You can verify the existence of public, secret, or officially deposited holographic wills by requesting a certificate from the General Register of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) under the Ministero della Giustizia (Ministry of Justice - Central Office of Notarial Archives, Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili) or by consulting a notary through the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Notaries) [6][7].
  • Notifying banks and insurers: Inform banks and post offices (Poste Italiane) of the death by submitting the certificato di morte. Accounts held by the deceased are temporarily frozen pending hereditary documentation (an affidavit of heirship, atto di notorietà, or statutory substitute declaration, dichiarazione sostitutiva dell'atto di notorietà, identifying the heirs, together with proof that the inheritance tax return has been filed where required) [5][7].
  • Filing the inheritance tax return (dichiarazione di successione): Heirs, persons called to the estate, or legatees must file the electronic inheritance tax return (dichiarazione di successione telematica) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months of the date the succession opens (the date of death) [5]. Only the surviving spouse and direct-line relatives (children, parents) are exempt from filing if the gross estate contains no real property or real property rights and its total value does not exceed 100,000 EUR [5].

it.title: Cosa fare quando muore un familiare in Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso in Italia: certificazione medica e visita necroscopica, scelta dell'impresa funebre, denuncia di morte allo Stato Civile, pensione ai superstiti e dichiarazione di successione.
it.introHtml: Esprimiamo la nostra vicinanza per la perdita del vostro familiare. In Italia le prime formalità medico-legali e anagrafiche sono solitamente coordinate dall'impresa funebre incaricata insieme alla struttura sanitaria o ai servizi comunali, mentre le pratiche previdenziali e successorie vengono avviate nei giorni e mesi successivi. Di seguito trovate i cinque passaggi ufficiali in ordine.

steps.title: Constatazione medica e certificato necroscopico
steps.html:
Il primo adempimento riguarda l'accertamento medico della morte e la visita del medico necroscopo secondo il Regolamento di polizia mortuaria (D.P.R. n. 285/1990) [1][2]:

  • Decesso in ospedale o struttura sanitaria/RSA: La direzione sanitaria della struttura provvede alla constatazione del decesso, all'accertamento necroscopico e alla trasmissione dell'avviso di morte all'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile del Comune [1].
  • Decesso a domicilio, in albergo o in luogo pubblico: Se la morte avviene in abitazione per cause naturali note, occorre contattare il medico curante o la guardia medica (oppure il numero di emergenza 112 / 118) per il certificato di constatazione del decesso e la scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte [1][2]. Successivamente, il medico necroscopo incaricato dall'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) effettua la visita necroscopica, di norma tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso, rilasciando il certificato necroscopico [2]. In caso di morte improvvisa in luogo pubblico, sospetta o violenta, intervengono il 112/118 e le forze dell'ordine, che informano la Procura della Repubblica; la salma resta a disposizione dell'Autorità Giudiziaria fino al rilascio del nulla osta alla sepoltura [1].

steps.title: Verifica di coperture assicurative e incarico a un'impresa funebre autorizzata
steps.html:
Prima di assumere impegni economici, verificate se la persona deceduta aveva sottoscritto una polizza assicurativa per spese funebri o un contratto di previdenza funeraria. Successivamente, la famiglia conferisce mandato a un'impresa funebre autorizzata, individuabile tramite i registri comunali o le principali associazioni nazionali di categoria come la Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (FENIOF) o la Federazione del Comparto Funerario Italiano (Federcofit) [2][3].

Di norma non è possibile procedere alla chiusura del feretro o alla sepoltura prima che siano trascorse 24 ore dal decesso (48 ore nei casi di morte improvvisa, salvo accertamento strumentale precoce o disposizione dell'Autorità Giudiziaria) [1][2]. L'impresa funebre coordina la vestizione, il trasporto e la presentazione dei documenti sanitari al Comune per ottenere i permessi necessari [1][2].

steps.title: Dichiarazione di morte allo Stato Civile e rilascio dei certificati
steps.html:
Ai sensi del D.P.R. n. 396/2000, la dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune in cui è avvenuto il decesso, sotto la vigilanza istituzionale del Ministero dell'Interno [1].

Nella prassi ordinaria la dichiarazione viene effettuata dalla direzione sanitaria (per i decessi in ospedale) oppure dall'impresa funebre espressamente delegata dai familiari, allegando il certificato necroscopico e la scheda ISTAT [1]. L'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile forma l'atto di morte e rilascia:

  • Il permesso di seppellimento (e, se richiesta e autorizzata in base alla volontà espressa in vita o attestata dai familiari aventi titolo, l'autorizzazione alla cremazione) [1].
  • Il certificato di morte e l'estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte, inclusa la versione plurilingue sul Modello C ai sensi della Convenzione di Vienna del 1976 qualora il documento debba essere utilizzato in altri Stati aderenti senza necessità di traduzione o apostille [1].

La registrazione del decesso nell'Anagrafe Nazionale della Popolazione Residente (ANPR) aggiorna automaticamente l'anagrafe comunale e comunica il decesso agli enti pubblici collegati, come l'INPS e l'Agenzia delle Entrate [1][4].

steps.title: Richiesta della pensione ai superstiti e prestazioni previdenziali
steps.html:
Anche se il Comune trasmette telematicamente la comunicazione di decesso, i familiari aventi diritto devono presentare una domanda specifica all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS) per ottenere le prestazioni economiche spettanti [4]:

  • Pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o indiretta): Spetta al coniuge o parte dell'unione civile superstite, ai figli minori, studenti a carico o inabili e, in determinati casi, a nipoti, genitori o fratelli/sorelle a carico [4]. Si chiama pensione di reversibilità se la persona deceduta era già pensionata, oppure pensione indiretta se era un lavoratore assicurato con i requisiti contributivi di legge [4].
  • Ratei maturati e non riscossi: Eventuali quote di pensione o tredicesima maturate dalla persona deceduta e non ancora incassate [4].

La domanda si presenta online sul portale dell'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale tramite SPID, CIE o CNS, oppure gratuitamente attraverso un Patronato riconosciuto [4].

steps.title: Ricerca testamentaria, banche e dichiarazione di successione
steps.html:
Per gestire il patrimonio ereditario, i conti bancari e gli adempimenti fiscali, occorre seguire questi passaggi:

  • Verifica del testamento: È possibile verificare l'esistenza di testamenti pubblici, segreti o olografi depositati consultando il Registro Generale dei Testamenti presso il Ministero della Giustizia (Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili) o rivolgendosi a un notaio tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [6][7].
  • Notifica a banche e assicurazioni: Comunicate il decesso agli istituti bancari e postali consegnando il certificato di morte. I conti intestati alla persona deceduta vengono temporaneamente bloccati in attesa della documentazione ereditaria (atto di notorietà o dichiarazione sostitutiva dell'atto di notorietà attestante gli eredi e, ove dovuta, prova della presentazione della dichiarazione di successione) [5][7].
  • Dichiarazione di successione: Gli eredi, i chiamati all'eredità o i legatari devono presentare la dichiarazione di successione telematica all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione (data del decesso) [5]. Sono esonerati dalla presentazione solo il coniuge e i parenti in linea retta qualora l'attivo ereditario non comprenda beni immobili o diritti reali immobiliari e abbia un valore complessivo non superiore a 100.000 euro [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Belgium: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Belgium: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Belgium: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. In Belgium, the initial medical and municipal formalities are usually coordinated with the assistance of an accredited funeral director, while survivor pension claims, bank account unblocking, and inheritance tax filings follow strict statutory deadlines. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Verification and Official Certification of Death
steps.html:
Every death occurring in Belgium must first be officially verified by a physician, who completes the medical death certificate (attestation médicale de décès, Form Modèle IIIC for a person aged one year or older, or Form Modèle IIID for an infant under one year of age) [1]:

  • Death in a hospital or care home: The facility's attending physician verifies the death and directly issues the medical death certificate (Modèle IIIC or Modèle IIID) required for civil registry formalities [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs at home from a known natural cause, call the attending general practitioner or the on-call doctor (médecin de garde, or 112 in an emergency) to examine the body and complete the medical certificate [1]. If the death is unexpected, suspicious, or violent, the physician notes a medico-legal objection (obstacle médico-légal) and notifies the police and the Public Prosecutor's Office (parquet du procureur du Roi). A forensic medical examiner (médecin légiste) then investigates, and burial or cremation cannot take place until the Public Prosecutor (procureur du Roi) issues formal clearance [1].
  • Pacemaker or battery-powered implant: The examining physician must also check for and certify the removal of any cardiac pacemaker (stimulateur cardiaque) or battery-operated implant before the coffin is sealed or cremation takes place [1].

steps.title: Checking Funeral Pre-Arrangements and Appointing an Accredited Funeral Director
steps.html:
Before signing a service contract, check whether the deceased person held a funeral insurance policy (assurance obsèques) or left formal pre-arranged funeral instructions (convention préalable de funérailles) filed with the municipality. Next, the family appoints an accredited funeral director (entreprise de pompes funèbres agréée), which can be located through the Fédération Royale du Secteur Funéraire Belge (Royal Federation of the Belgian Funeral Sector - FUNEBRA) [3]:

  • Transport and regional timelines: In practice, the funeral director arranges the transfer of the deceased to the funeral home (funérarium), ensures compliance with the statutory preservation, burial, and cremation timelines applicable in the relevant Region (Wallonia, Brussels-Capital Region, or Flanders), and handles day-to-day coordination with the municipal authorities [1][3].
  • Written cost estimate: Always request a detailed written itemized quote (devis écrit) covering both funeral services and municipal burial or cremation taxes before signing an agreement [3].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration at the Municipality and Obtaining Certificates and Permits
steps.html:
The death must be declared as soon as possible to the civil registry office (service de l'état civil) of the municipal administration (administration communale) in the municipality where the death occurred, following the procedures published on the federal portal Belgium.be [1].

In most cases, the funeral director submits this declaration on behalf of the family by presenting the medical death certificate (Modèle IIIC), the deceased person's identity card and driving licence, the marriage record book (livret de mariage) if applicable, and the formal application for cremation authorization if cremation is chosen [1]. The civil registrar records the death in the Database of Civil Status Records (Banque de données des actes de l'état civil - BAEC) and issues:

  • Burial or cremation permit: The official burial permit (permis d'inhumer) or cremation authorization (autorisation de crémation) [1].
  • Official death certificates: Certified copies and extracts of the death certificate (acte de décès), as well as a multilingual extract on Form C (extrait plurilingue Formule C) issued under the 1976 Vienna Convention if administrative steps must be completed in another signatory state [1].

Recording the death in the National Register (Registre national) automatically notifies several Belgian public bodies (such as pension authorities and health insurance funds if the deceased resided in Belgium), whereas banks, private insurers, and landlords must be notified directly by the family [1][4].

steps.title: Claiming Survivor Pensions and Health Insurance Notifications
steps.html:
Once the death is registered, surviving relatives should review their statutory pension and social security entitlements:

  • Survivor pension or transition allowance: The Service fédéral des Pensions (Federal Pensions Service - SFP, accessible via MyPension.be or the toll-free number 1765) assesses the entitlements of the surviving spouse [4]. If the deceased already received a Belgian retirement pension, the survivor pension (pension de survie) or transition allowance (allocation de transition) is often examined automatically following municipal registration; if the deceased was still employed or had insurance periods abroad, submit an application directly to the Service fédéral des Pensions [4]. A specific statutory funeral grant (indemnité de funérailles) also applies upon the death of a retired civil servant [5].
  • Health insurance fund (mutuelle): Although the general lump-sum funeral grant under the employee healthcare scheme was abolished by the National Institute for Health and Disability Insurance (Institut national d'assurance maladie-invalidité - INAMI), you must still contact the deceased's health insurance fund (mutuelle) to claim reimbursement for final medical invoices, close the file, and check whether supplementary insurance covers funeral expenses [6].

steps.title: Unblocking Bank Accounts, Certificate of Inheritance, and Succession Tax Return
steps.html:
Administering the estate and fulfilling tax obligations in Belgium follows strict legal rules:

  • Freezing and unblocking bank accounts: As soon as a bank is notified of the death, it freezes the bank accounts and safe deposit boxes of both the deceased and the surviving spouse [2][7]. However, the surviving spouse or legal cohabitant (cohabitant légal) is entitled to a statutory advance (up to half of the available balances, capped at EUR 5,000) and may have funeral expenses and urgent final household bills paid directly from the estate accounts upon presentation of invoices [2]. To unblock the accounts permanently, heirs must present either a certificate of inheritance (certificat d'hérédité, issued free of charge by the Legal Certainty Office of SPF Finances via MyMinfin for straightforward estates without a will or marriage contract) or a notarial deed of inheritance (acte d'hérédité) drawn up by a notary via the Fédération Royale du Notariat Belge (Royal Federation of Belgian Notaries - Notaire.be) [2][7].
  • Will search and succession options: The notary checks the Central Register of Wills (Registre central des testaments - CRT) and advises heirs on choosing between unconditional acceptance (acceptation pure et simple), acceptance under benefit of inventory (acceptation sous bénéfice d'inventaire), or renunciation (renonciation) [2].
  • Inheritance tax return within 4 months: When a death occurs in Belgium, the heirs must file the inheritance declaration (déclaration de succession) within 4 months of the date of death [2][8]. This declaration is filed with the Federal Public Service Finance (SPF Finances) if the deceased's last tax domicile was in Wallonia or the Brussels-Capital Region, or with the Flemish Tax Administration (Vlaamse Belastingdienst - VLABEL) if the last tax domicile was in Flanders [8].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your situation, in which municipality and Region (Brussels-Capital, Wallonia, or Flanders) did the deceased have their last tax domicile, and does the estate include real estate in Belgium, a will, or a marriage contract?
