title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Turkey: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml:
Please accept our condolences on the death of your family member. When a death occurs in Turkey, issuing the medical death certificate, registering the death in the civil registry, arranging the funeral, and completing inheritance procedures are coordinated through specific official authorities [1][2].

Below are the five main official and practical steps to follow in order:

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and Issuance of the Death Certificate (Burial Permit)
steps.html:
Before the deceased person can be transported or buried, an official Death Certificate (Ölüm Belgesi, which also serves as the Burial Permit / Gömme İzin Belgesi or Defin Ruhsatı) must be issued electronically through the Ministry of Health Death Notification System (Sağlık Bakanlığı Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi - ÖBS) [1]:

  • Death in a hospital or care facility: If the death occurred in a healthcare facility, the attending physician verifies the death and issues and approves the Ölüm Belgesi electronically via the ÖBS system [1].
  • Natural death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurred outside a healthcare facility, call the 112 Emergency Call Center (112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi) or the ALO 188 Funeral Services Line (ALO 188 Cenaze Hizmetleri) to request a municipal physician (belediye tabibi) or a community/family health center physician (toplum sağlığı merkezi / aile sağlığı merkezi hekimi). After examining the body on site and confirming that death resulted from natural causes, the physician records the Ölüm Belgesi in the ÖBS system [1].
  • Suspicious, accidental, or forensic death: If the death appears unnatural or suspicious, notify the Police (Polis - 155) or Gendarmerie (Jandarma - 156) through the 112 Emergency Call Center. The body must not be moved; the burial permit is issued by the judicial authorities after the Public Prosecutor's Office (Cumhuriyet Savcılığı) and the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tıp Kurumu) complete the forensic examination or autopsy [1].

steps.title: Checking Funeral Funds and Appointing Municipal or Authorized Funeral Services
steps.html:
Once the Ölüm Belgesi has been issued, check whether the deceased person belonged to a funeral mutual aid foundation (such as Diyanet funeral funds or cross-border funeral assistance funds) or held private funeral insurance, and confirm any burial wishes [1][7]:

  • Municipal funeral services (ALO 188): Across Turkey, municipal funeral departments (belediye cenaze hizmetleri, reachable 24/7 via ALO 188) provide mortuary transport, washing, shrouding or coffining, grave plot allocation, and local city transport free of charge upon presentation of the Ölüm Belgesi [1].
  • Intercity or international repatriation: If the burial will take place in another province or country, a Road Transit Permit (Yol İzin Belgesi) must be obtained from the relevant municipal physician or community health center. For international repatriation, an authorized international funeral transport provider must be appointed to handle embalming (tahnit), hermetically sealed coffining, and consular formalities in accordance with the procedures of T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Turkey) [7]. Clarvia provides these details for orientation only and does not endorse or rank commercial providers.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration and Multilingual Death Certificate (Formula C)
steps.html:
Official registration of deaths in Turkey's central civil registry system (MERNİS) is carried out by the central civil registration authority, Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs), and its local District Civil Registry Offices (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlükleri) [1]:

  • 10-day statutory notification deadline: Death certificates issued electronically via ÖBS by healthcare institutions or municipal physicians are transmitted electronically to the relevant District Civil Registry Office (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü) within 10 days of the event, and the civil registry record is closed automatically [1]. The deceased person's Turkish Republic identity card (T.C. kimlik kartı) is surrendered to the civil registry office [1].
  • Death Registration Extract and Formula C: Official Civil Registry Extracts (Nüfus Kayıt Örneği) and Death Registration Extracts (Ölüm Kayıt Örneği) needed for inheritance, insurance, and banking matters can be obtained from District Civil Registry Offices or online via the official government portal, e-Devlet Kapısı [1][3]. If documents are needed for foreign authorities, banks, or pension institutions abroad, request a Multilingual Extract of the Death Record (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) from the District Civil Registry Office, which is valid without an apostille in signatory states under the 1976 Vienna Convention [1][7]. For consular questions involving foreign jurisdictions, guidance is available from the Consular Call Center of T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı (+90 312 292 29 29) [7].

steps.title: Claiming the SGK Funeral Grant and Survivor Pensions (Widow and Orphan Pensions)
steps.html:
After the death has been recorded in the civil registry, applications for social security death benefits should be submitted to the national social security authority, Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (Social Security Institution - SGK) [2][3]:

  • Funeral grant (Cenaze ödeneği): Provided the deceased insured person had at least 360 days of reported disability, old-age, and survivors insurance contributions or was receiving a retirement pension, a one-off funeral grant is paid in order of priority to the surviving spouse, children, parents, or siblings [2]. Applications can be submitted after consulting the ALO 170 helpline either at Provincial/Local Social Security Directorates (Sosyal Güvenlik İl/Merkez Müdürlükleri) or directly online via e-Devlet Kapısı under the application screen Gelir, Aylık, Ödenek Talep Belgesinin Verilmesi (Submission of Income, Pension, and Allowance Claim Form); the right to claim is subject to a 5-year limitation period from the date of death [2][3].
  • Survivor pension (Ölüm aylığı / dul ve yetim aylığı): Where the deceased person met the required contribution conditions, the surviving spouse, children, and under certain conditions parents can apply for a survivor pension online through e-Devlet Kapısı or by written petition to Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu offices [2][3].

steps.title: Certificate of Inheritance (Probate), Inheritance Tax Filing, and Bank Procedures
steps.html:
To manage or transfer the deceased person's bank accounts, real estate (tapu), vehicles, and other estate assets, the statutory succession and tax steps must be completed [4][5][6]:

  • Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı): Where there is no discrepancy in the civil registry records, the official Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı) identifying the legal heirs and their respective shares can be obtained from any notary public under Türkiye Noterler Birliği (Union of Turkish Bar Notaries) or queried via e-Devlet Kapısı [4][5]. If there is a will (vasiyetname), if any heir holds foreign citizenship, or if parentage is disputed, the petition must be filed with the Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [5]. If renunciation of inheritance (reddi miras) is being considered, the statutory deadline is 3 months from learning of the death.
  • Inheritance and Transfer Tax Return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi - 4-month deadline): When the death occurred in Turkey and the heirs are in Turkey, the Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi must be filed within 4 months following the date of death with a local tax office under the central tax authority, Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (Turkish Revenue Administration), or online via the Interactive/Digital Tax Office (İnteraktif/Dijital Vergi Dairesi) [6].
  • Banks and Land Registry (Tapu) transfers: Using the tax clearance letter (ilişiksizlik / temiz yazısı) issued by the tax office together with the Mirasçılık Belgesi, heirs can release frozen bank funds in proportion to their inheritance shares, collect private insurance payouts, and complete property title transfers at Land Registry Directorates (Tapu Müdürlükleri) [5][6].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide more specific information, in which province or district of Turkey did the death occur, and did the deceased person hold any assets, pension rights, or foreign citizenship abroad?

tr.title: Türkiye'de Bir Yakınınız Vefat Ettiğinde Yapılması Gerekenler: 5 Adımlı Resmi Rehber
tr.cardSummary: Türkiye'de vefat sonrası 5 adımlı resmi rehber: Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) ve defin ruhsatı, belediye cenaze hizmetleri, Nüfus Müdürlüğü kaydı, SGK cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı ile veraset ilamı ve vergi işlemleri.
tr.introHtml:
Aile yakınınızın vefatı dolayısıyla başsağlığı dileriz. Türkiye'de bir vefat gerçekleştiğinde tıbbi ölüm belgesinin düzenlenmesi, nüfus tescili, defin işlemleri ve miras süreçleri belirli resmi makamların koordinasyonuyla yürütülür [1][2].

İzlenmesi gereken beş temel resmi ve pratik adım sırasıyla aşağıdadır:

steps.title: Tıbbi Ölüm Tespiti ve Ölüm Belgesinin (Defin Ruhsatı) Düzenlenmesi
steps.html:
Cenazenin nakledilebilmesi veya defnedilebilmesi için öncelikle Sağlık Bakanlığı'nın elektronik Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) üzerinden resmi Ölüm Belgesi (aynı zamanda Gömme İzin Belgesi / Defin Ruhsatı yerine geçer) düzenlenmelidir [1]:

  • Hastanede veya bakım kurumunda vefat: Vefat bir sağlık kuruluşunda gerçekleşmişse, ilgili hekim ölüm tespitini yapar ve Ölüm Belgesini ÖBS üzerinden elektronik olarak düzenleyip onaylar [1].
  • Evde, otelde veya kamusal alanda doğal vefat: Vefat sağlık kuruluşu dışında meydana gelmişse, 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi veya ALO 188 Cenaze Hizmetleri hattı aranarak belediye tabibi ya da toplum sağlığı merkezi / aile sağlığı merkezi hekimi çağrılır. Hekim yerinde muayene yaparak ölümün doğal nedenlerle gerçekleştiğini tespit ederse Ölüm Belgesini ÖBS sistemine kaydeder [1].
  • Şüpheli, kaza sonucu veya adli vefat: Ölümün doğal olmayan veya şüpheli bir nedene dayanması halinde 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi üzerinden Polis (155) veya Jandarma (156) birimlerine haber verilmelidir. Bu durumda cenazeye dokunulmamalıdır; Cumhuriyet Savcılığı ve Adli Tıp Kurumu incelemesi veya otopsi işlemi tamamlandıktan sonra adli makamlarca defin ruhsatı verilir [1].

steps.title: Cenaze Fonu Kontrolü ve Belediye veya Yetkili Cenaze Hizmetlerinin Görevlendirilmesi
steps.html:
Ölüm Belgesi düzenlendikten sonra, vefat eden kişinin herhangi bir cenaze yardımlaşma vakfına (örneğin Diyanet vakıfları veya yurt dışı bağlantılı cenaze fonları) ya da özel sigortaya üyeliği olup olmadığını kontrol edin ve vasiyet edilen defin tercihini teyit edin [1][7].

  • Belediye cenaze hizmetleri (ALO 188): Türkiye genelinde belediyelerin cenaze hizmetleri birimleri (ALO 188 üzerinden 7/24 ulaşılabilir), Ölüm Belgesi ibraz edildiğinde cenazenin morga alınması, yıkanması, kefenlenmesi/tabutlanması, mezar yeri tahsisi ve şehir içi nakil işlemlerini ücretsiz olarak yürütür [1].
  • Şehirler arası veya uluslararası nakil: Cenaze başka bir ilde veya ülkede defnedilecekse, ilgili belediye tabibliğinden veya toplum sağlığı merkezinden Yol İzin Belgesi alınır. Uluslararası nakillerde ise tahnit (ilaçlama), sızdırmaz tabutlama ve konsolosluk işlemleri için yetkili bir uluslararası cenaze nakil firması görevlendirilir ve dışişleri makamları (T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı) süreçlerine uyulur [7]. Clarvia bu bilgileri yönlendirme amacıyla sunar; herhangi bir ticari firmayı önermez veya sıralamaz.

steps.title: Nüfus Müdürlüğüne Ölüm Bildirimi ve Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi (Formül C)
steps.html:
Türkiye'de vefat olaylarının resmi nüfus kütüklerine (MERNİS) tescili, merkezi nüfus idaresi (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü) ve bağlı İlçe Nüfus Müdürlükleri tarafından gerçekleştirilir [1]:

  • 10 günlük yasal bildirim süresi: Sağlık kuruluşları veya belediye tabipleri tarafından ÖBS üzerinden düzenlenen ölüm tutanakları, olayın gerçekleştiği tarihten itibaren 10 gün içinde elektronik ortamda ilgili İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğüne iletilir ve nüfus kaydı otomatik olarak kapatılır [1]. Vefat eden kişinin T.C. kimlik kartı nüfus müdürlüğüne teslim edilir [1].
  • Ölüm Kayıt Örneği ve Formül C: Miras, sigorta ve banka işlemleri için resmi Nüfus Kayıt Örneği ve Ölüm Kayıt Örneği, İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüklerinden veya resmi devlet portalı (e-Devlet Kapısı) üzerinden temin edilebilir [1][3]. Yurt dışındaki resmi makamlar, bankalar veya emeklilik kurumları için belge gerekiyorsa, İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğünden 1976 Viyana Sözleşmesi uyarınca apostil şerhine gerek kalmadan geçerli olan Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi (Formül C) talep edilmelidir [1][7]. Yurt dışı bağlantılı konsolosluk sorularınız için T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi (+90 312 292 29 29) üzerinden bilgi alınabilir [7].

steps.title: SGK Cenaze Ödeneği ve Ölüm Aylığı (Dul ve Yetim Aylığı) Başvurusu
steps.html:
Nüfus kütüğüne ölüm tescili işlendikten sonra, vefat eden kişinin sosyal güvenlik hakları için ulusal kurum olan Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu nezdinde başvuru yapılmalıdır [2][3]:

  • Cenaze ödeneği: Vefat eden sigortalının (en az 360 gün malullük, yaşlılık ve ölüm sigortası primi bildirilmiş olması veya emekli aylığı alıyor olması şartıyla) sırasıyla eşine, çocuklarına, anne-babasına veya kardeşlerine bir defaya mahsus cenaze ödeneği ödenir [2]. Başvurular ALO 170 hattı üzerinden bilgi alınarak Sosyal Güvenlik İl/Merkez Müdürlüklerine veya doğrudan resmi devlet portalı (e-Devlet Kapısı) üzerindeki Gelir, Aylık, Ödenek Talep Belgesinin Verilmesi ekranından yapılabilir; hak sahipleri için talep hakkı ölüm tarihinden itibaren 5 yıllık zamanaşımına tabidir [2][3].
  • Ölüm aylığı (dul ve yetim aylığı): Vefat eden kişinin gerekli prim gün şartlarını sağlaması halinde geride kalan eşine, çocuklarına ve belirli şartlarda anne-babasına bağlanacak ölüm aylığı için yine e-Devlet Kapısı üzerinden veya yazılı dilekçeyle Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu birimlerine başvurulur [2][3].

steps.title: Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı), Vergi Beyannamesi ve Banka İşlemleri
steps.html:
Vefat eden kişinin banka hesapları, taşınmazları (tapu), araçları ve diğer malvarlığı unsurları üzerinde işlem yapabilmek için miras hukuku ve vergi adımlarının tamamlanması gerekir [4][5][6]:

  • Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı): Yasal mirasçıları ve miras paylarını gösteren Mirasçılık Belgesi, nüfus kayıtlarında engel bulunmayan hallerde herhangi bir noterlikten (meslek kuruluşu: Türkiye Noterler Birliği) veya resmi devlet portalı (e-Devlet Kapısı) üzerinden sorgulanıp alınabilir [4][5]. Vasiyetname bulunması, mirasçılardan birinin yabancı uyruklu olması veya soybağı uyuşmazlığı gibi durumlarda ise başvuru Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesine yapılmalıdır [5]. Mirasın reddi (reddi miras) düşünülüyorsa, yasal süre ölümün öğrenilmesinden itibaren 3 aydır.
  • Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi (4 ay sınırı): Ölüm Türkiye'de gerçekleşmiş ve mirasçılar Türkiye'de bulunuyorsa, ölüm tarihini takip eden 4 ay içinde merkezi vergi idaresi (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı) bünyesindeki vergi dairesine veya İnteraktif/Dijital Vergi Dairesi üzerinden Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi verilmelidir [6].
  • Bankalar ve Tapu devirleri: Vergi dairesinden alınan ilişiksizlik (temiz) yazısı ve Mirasçılık Belgesi ile bankalardaki bloke hesapların miras payları oranında çözülmesi, özel sigorta tazminatlarının tahsili ve Tapu Müdürlüklerinde intikal işlemleri tamamlanır [5][6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in United Arab Emirates: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml:
We are sorry for the loss of your family member. When a death occurs in the United Arab Emirates, medical certification, police clearance, civil registration, and estate succession follow strict federal and emirate-level procedures on the Official UAE Government Portal (u.ae) [1][2].

Here are the five essential official steps in sequence:

steps.title: Medical Notification of Death and Police Forensic Clearance
steps.html:
Every death in the UAE must first be medically certified and cleared by the police before burial, cremation, or repatriation permits can be issued [1][2].

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending physician certifies the death, issues the official electronic Medical Notification of Death (death declaration), and arranges the transfer of the deceased to a government-approved hospital or municipal morgue [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, at a workplace, or in a public place: Call the Police immediately on 999 and the National Ambulance on 998 [1]. Do not move the deceased. The police and forensic medical team (such as Dubai Police Forensic Medicine or Abu Dhabi Police Forensic Evidence) examine the scene and transfer the deceased to the government morgue to establish the cause of death [1][2].
  • Police No-Objection Certificate (NOC): Whether the death occurred in a hospital or outside, you or your authorized representative must submit the Medical Notification of Death, along with the deceased person's original passport and Emirates ID, through the local police portal or smart app (Dubai Police, Abu Dhabi Police, or the Ministry of Interior in the Northern Emirates). Once any Public Prosecution or forensic investigation is cleared, the police issue the official No-Objection Certificate (NOC) for local burial, cremation, or international repatriation [1][4].

steps.title: Checking Employer/Insurance Coverage and Appointing an Authorized Mortuary Coordinator
steps.html:
Check whether the deceased held private life or repatriation insurance, and if the person was employed in the UAE, notify the employer or sponsor immediately [1]. Under UAE Labour Law, the employer is legally responsible for covering the costs of preparing and repatriating a deceased employee's remains to their home country (or place of recruitment) if requested by the family [1].

Next, coordinate with the municipal mortuary and funeral unit or appoint an authorized funeral and repatriation cargo provider in the emirate where the death occurred [1][2][4]:

  • Local burial or cremation: For Muslim burials, municipal cemetery services (such as Dubai Municipality or the Abu Dhabi municipal mortuary service via the TAMM platform) coordinate ritual washing (ghusl), shrouding (kafan), funeral prayers, and burial at designated public cemeteries, normally within 24 hours once permits are issued [1][2]. For non-Muslim burials or cremations, municipal authorities issue permits for designated non-Muslim cemeteries or licensed crematoria in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, or other emirates [1][2].
  • International repatriation: If the remains are being transferred abroad, an authorized funeral coordinator or cargo agent arranges official embalming through the preventative medicine unit of the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DOH), Dubai Municipality / Dubai Health Authority, or Emirates Health Services (EHS) (formerly under the Ministry of Health and Prevention - MOHAP), sealed zinc-lined coffin preparation, and air cargo booking [1][3][4]. Clarvia provides public-source information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Registering the Death and Obtaining the Official Bilingual Death Certificate
steps.html:
With the hospital's Medical Notification of Death and the Police NOC, register the death with the competent health authority in the emirate of death to obtain the official bilingual (Arabic and English) Death Certificate [1][2][4]:

  • Abu Dhabi: Submit the application digitally through the Abu Dhabi Government Services Portal (TAMM) under the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DOH) using UAE PASS [2][3].
  • Dubai: Apply through the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) or the integrated bereavement service channels in Dubai [1].
  • Sharjah and the Northern Emirates: Apply online or at a customer happiness centre of Emirates Health Services (EHS), which operates the federal preventative medicine centres across Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah [1][4].

To complete registration, you must surrender the deceased person's original passport and Emirates ID so that the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) (or GDRFA in Dubai) cancels the residency visa and identity record [1][2]. If the Death Certificate will be used outside the UAE, have it attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) and registered with the deceased's embassy or consulate [1][2].

steps.title: Claiming End-of-Service Gratuity, Workplace Insurance, and Survivor Pensions
steps.html:
Financial entitlements depend on whether the deceased was a UAE national or an expatriate resident, as well as their employment sector [1]:

  • Private-sector and free-zone employees: Notify the employer and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) (or the relevant free-zone authority such as DIFC or ADGM) [1]. Under UAE Labour Law, the employer must settle all unpaid wages, accrued leave, and statutory end-of-service gratuity within 10 days of the date of death, paying them to the family member designated in writing by the employee or into the competent court's treasury for distribution to legal heirs [1]. Also check for any group life or workman's compensation insurance policy held by the employer [1].
  • UAE nationals and GCC public/private insured workers: Surviving family members of insured UAE citizens can apply for a monthly survivor pension and lump-sum death grant through the General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA) or the Abu Dhabi Pension Fund, depending on the employer's registration [1].

steps.title: Bank Account Freeze Clearance and UAE Court Estate Succession / Probate
steps.html:
In the UAE, banks are legally required to freeze both individual and joint bank accounts, safe deposit boxes, and local investment accounts as soon as they are notified of an account holder's death, pending an official succession or probate order from a competent UAE court [1][5][6]:

  • Registered Non-Muslim Wills (DIFC or ADJD): If the deceased was a non-Muslim who registered a will with the DIFC Courts Wills Service (covering Dubai and UAE-wide assets) or the Non-Muslim Wills Registry at the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (ADJD), the named executor applies directly to that court for a Grant of Probate and estate distribution orders [5][6].
  • Civil Personal Status and Inheritance Courts: If no registered local will exists, legal heirs must apply for an official Legal Heirs / Succession Certificate (Hasr Irth) and estate distribution order through the Personal Status Court (such as the Abu Dhabi Civil Family Court under the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (ADJD) or Dubai Courts) [1][6]. For non-Muslim expatriates without a registered will, Federal Decree-Law No. 41 of 2022 on Civil Personal Status generally provides default civil intestacy rules (typically allocating 50% to the surviving spouse and 50% equally among children, or to parents/siblings if there are no children), unless an heir successfully petitions to apply the law of the deceased's nationality or a valid home-country will [6]. For Muslim estates, Sharia inheritance principles (Faraid) apply unless otherwise governed by specific statutory provisions [1][6].
  • Tax and Liabilities: The UAE does not levy personal income tax or inheritance/estate tax on individuals, though court filing fees, translation costs, and outstanding UAE debts (such as mortgages, credit cards, or personal loans not covered by credit life insurance) must be settled from the estate before remaining funds and real estate are released to the heirs [1][5][6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance: In which emirate did the death occur, and what was the nationality and religion of your family member?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Brazil: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. In Brazil, medical certification of death, civil death registration, social security benefit claims, and estate inventory proceedings follow well-defined statutory steps and deadlines [1][2][3].

Below are the five essential official steps in order:

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and Issuance of the Medical Death Declaration (DO)
steps.html:
Before any removal of the body, burial, or civil registry filing can take place, a physician must issue the official Medical Death Declaration (Declaração de Óbito - DO), a three-copy medical form standardized by the Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde) [1]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending or on-duty physician verifies the death and completes the Declaração de Óbito (DO) directly [1].
  • Natural death at home: If the deceased person was under regular medical care, contact the attending physician to issue the DO. If there was no recent medical supervision, call the Mobile Emergency Care Service (Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência - SAMU) on 192; after initial verification, the body is referred to the municipal or state Death Verification Service (Serviço de Verificação de Óbito - SVO), or assessed by a public health physician where no SVO exists, to issue the DO [1].
  • Death in a public place or violent, accidental, or suspicious death: Call the Military Police (Polícia Militar) immediately on 190 (and SAMU on 192 if needed) and do not disturb the scene. A Police Report (Boletim de Ocorrência - BO) must be filed at the Civil Police Station (Delegacia de Polícia Civil), which orders removal and autopsy by the Forensic Medical Institute (Instituto Médico Legal - IML), the sole authority authorized to issue the DO in such cases [1].

steps.title: Checking Funeral Plans and Appointing a Licensed Funeral Service
steps.html:
Before contracting services independently, review any existing funeral coverage and confirm burial or cremation requirements [1]:

  • Funeral insurance or pre-need plans: Check whether the deceased person held life insurance with funeral assistance or a pre-arranged funeral plan (plano funerário), confirming coverage for transport, coffin, and burial with the insurer or employer [1].
  • Municipal or licensed funeral provider and cremation rules: Contact the municipal funeral service (serviço funerário municipal) of the local city hall (prefeitura) or appoint a licensed funeral company (represented at industry level by bodies such as the Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF) [1]. In Brazil, burial typically takes place between 24 and 36 hours after death. If cremation is chosen, the law requires the Declaração de Óbito to be signed by two physicians (or one forensic pathologist) and, in cases of violent death handled by the IML, express judicial authorization is required [1]. Clarvia provides public references for orientation only and does not endorse or rank commercial providers.

steps.title: Civil Registration at the Cartório and Issuance of the Death Certificate
steps.html:
With the signed medical Declaração de Óbito (DO) in hand, a close relative or authorized representative (often assisted by the funeral service) must appear before the Civil Registry Office of Natural Persons (Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais) for the district where the death occurred or where the deceased person resided, whose services are integrated nationwide through the Portal Oficial do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) (Official Civil Registry Portal) [1]:

  • Statutory deadlines and free issuance: Under the Public Registries Law (Lei de Registros Públicos, Law No. 6.015/1973), death registration must be completed prior to burial, within the ordinary deadline of 24 hours after death or, where impossible, within up to 15 days (extended to up to 3 months in locations more than 30 km from the registry office) [1]. Both the death registration and the first copy of the Civil Death Certificate (Certidão de Óbito), as well as the Burial Permit (Guia de Sepultamento), are free of charge by law for all citizens [1].
  • Required documents: Original Declaração de Óbito (DO) signed by the physician, official identity card (RG/CIN), taxpayer registry number (CPF), Birth or Marriage Certificate, voter registration card (título de eleitor), and INSS/PIS/PASEP registration number or Employment Record Card (Carteira de Trabalho) of the deceased person, together with the declarant's identification document [1].
  • Automatic notifications and use abroad: The Cartório de Registro Civil electronically notifies the Federal Revenue Service (Receita Federal, updating the CPF status to Titular Falecido / Deceased Holder), the INSS, and the Electoral Justice (Justiça Eleitoral) [1][2]. If the Certidão de Óbito must take legal effect outside Brazil, request a Hague Apostille (Apostila da Haia) at an authorized notary/registry office regulated by the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) (National Council of Justice), or consular registration with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministério das Relações Exteriores - Itamaraty) where a consular post is involved [4][5].

steps.title: Claiming the INSS Survivor Pension, Funeral Allowance, and FGTS/PIS Withdrawals
steps.html:
Once the Certidão de Óbito has been issued, surviving dependents and family members should review social security and labor entitlements [2]:

  • Survivor Pension (Pensão por Morte - INSS): Legal dependents of a person insured under the General Social Security Regime (spouse or domestic partner in a stable union, children under age 21 or with a qualifying disability, or parents and siblings who prove financial dependence) can apply for the Pensão por Morte through the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) (National Institute of Social Security) directly via the Meu INSS digital platform (on the gov.br portal) or by calling 135 [2]. The pension is payable retroactively from the date of death if claimed within 90 days of death (or within 180 days for children under age 16); after that deadline, payments run from the application date [2].
  • FGTS, PIS/PASEP, and municipal funeral assistance: Using the Certidão de Óbito and the certificate of eligible survivor pension dependents issued by the INSS (or a judicial warrant / extrajudicial inventory deed), survivors can request withdrawal of FGTS severance fund balances and PIS/PASEP quotas at Caixa Econômica Federal or Banco do Brasil, as well as municipal funeral assistance (auxílio-funeral via CRAS) for low-income families [2][3].

steps.title: Estate Inventory (Extrajudicial or Judicial), 2-Month Deadline (ITCMD), Banks, and Income Tax
steps.html:
Transferring legal title to estate assets, bank accounts, vehicles, and real property requires completing the formal estate inventory and partition process (inventário e partilha) [3][4]:

  • 2-month (60-day) deadline and state inheritance tax (ITCMD): Under Article 611 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Código de Processo Civil), inventory proceedings must be opened within 2 months (60 days) from the date of death; late filing subjects heirs to a tax penalty on the state Inheritance and Gift Tax (Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação - ITCMD), whose rate and tax return follow the rules of the relevant State Secretariat of Finance (Secretaria da Fazenda) [3].
  • Extrajudicial Inventory at a Notary Office vs. Judicial Probate: Where all heirs are in agreement and assisted by a mandatory lawyer (advogado) or public defender (defensor público), the inventory can be completed rapidly by public deed (escritura pública) at any Notary Office (Cartório de Notas) or online via the e-Notariado platform, following the guidelines of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil (CNB) (Notarial College of Brazil) and updated rules of the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) (which now allow extrajudicial inventory even where there is a will or minor heirs, provided forced heirship shares are respected and the Public Prosecutor's Office issues a favorable opinion) [3][4]. If there is a dispute among the heirs, the inventory must proceed through the state courts (Poder Judiciário) [3].
  • Banks, insurers, and Federal Revenue Service (Receita Federal): Notify banks of the death (individual account withdrawals are frozen until the notarial inventory deed, court partition order, or judicial warrant is presented) and submit any life insurance claims within the statutory limitation period [3]. Finally, the estate administrator (inventariante) must file the Final Estate Income Tax Return (Declaração Final de Espólio de Imposto de Renda) with the Receita Federal once the partition is completed [3].

closingQuestion: So that we can guide you more precisely, in which Brazilian state and municipality did the death occur, and did the deceased person leave a will or assets to be partitioned?

pt.title: O que fazer quando alguém falece em Brasil: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um óbito em Brasil: certificado médico de óbito, contratação de agência funerária, registo civil, subsídio por morte e pensão de sobrevivência, e habilitação de herdeiros ou inventário.
pt.introHtml:
Apresentamos os nossos sentidos pêsames pelo falecimento do seu familiar. No Brasil, os procedimentos médicos, o registo civil do óbito, o requerimento de benefícios previdenciários e a abertura do inventário seguem etapas e prazos legais bem definidos [1][2][3].

Abaixo estão os cinco passos oficiais essenciais por ordem:

steps.title: Verificação Médica do Óbito e Emissão da Declaração de Óbito (DO)
steps.html:
Antes de qualquer remoção, sepultamento ou registo em cartório, é obrigatória a emissão da Declaração de Óbito (DO), documento médico oficial padronizado pelo Ministério da Saúde em três vias [1]:

  • Óbito em hospital ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente ou plantonista constata o falecimento e preenche diretamente a Declaração de Óbito (DO) [1].
  • Óbito em residência de causa natural: Se a pessoa falecida recebia acompanhamento médico regular, contacte o médico assistente para emitir a DO. Caso não houvesse assistência médica recente, acione o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU) pelo telefone 192; após a constatação inicial, o corpo é encaminhado ao Serviço de Verificação de Óbito (SVO) do município ou estado (ou avaliado pelo médico da rede pública local onde não houver SVO) para emissão da DO [1].
  • Óbito em via pública ou morte violenta, acidental ou suspeita: Ligue imediatamente para a Polícia Militar pelo 190 (e SAMU 192, se necessário) e não altere o local. Deve ser registado um Boletim de Ocorrência (BO) na Delegacia de Polícia Civil, que requisita a remoção e necropsia pelo Instituto Médico Legal (IML), único órgão habilitado a emitir a DO nesses casos [1].

steps.title: Verificação de Plano Funerário e Contratação de Serviço Funerário Habilitado
steps.html:
Verifique se a pessoa falecida possuía seguro de vida com assistência funeral ou plano funerário contratado (auferindo junto à seguradora ou empregador a cobertura para remoção, urna e sepultamento) [1].

Em seguida, acione o serviço funerário municipal da prefeitura local ou contrate uma empresa funerária devidamente habilitada (representada setorialmente por entidades como a Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF) [1]. No Brasil, o sepultamento ocorre habitualmente entre 24 e 36 horas após o óbito. Caso a opção seja a cremação, a lei exige que a Declaração de Óbito seja assinada por dois médicos (ou por um médico legista) e, em casos de morte violenta (IML), depende de autorização judicial expressa [1]. A Clarvia disponibiliza referências públicas apenas para orientação e não recomenda nem classifica prestadores.

steps.title: Registo em Cartório de Registro Civil e Emissão da Certidão de Óbito
steps.html:
Com a Declaração de Óbito (DO) médica em mãos, um familiar próximo ou representante autorizado (muitas vezes com o apoio do serviço funerário) deve comparecer ao Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais da circunscrição do local do óbito ou da residência da pessoa falecida, cujos serviços são integrados pelo Portal Oficial do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) [1]:

  • Prazos legais e gratuidade: Pela Lei de Registros Públicos (Lei n.º 6.015/1973), o registo deve ser feito antes do sepultamento, no prazo ordinário de 24 horas após o falecimento ou, na impossibilidade, em até 15 dias (ampliado para até 3 meses em locais distantes mais de 30 km da sede do cartório) [1]. O registo do óbito e a primeira via da Certidão de Óbito (bem como a Guia de Sepultamento) são gratuitos por lei para todos os cidadãos [1].
  • Documentos necessários: Declaração de Óbito (DO) original assinada pelo médico, documento de identidade oficial (RG/CIN), CPF, Certidão de Nascimento ou de Casamento, título de eleitor e número de inscrição no INSS/PIS/PASEP ou Carteira de Trabalho da pessoa falecida, além do documento de identificação do declarante [1].
  • Comunicações automáticas e uso no exterior: O Cartório de Registro Civil comunica eletronicamente o óbito à Receita Federal (atualizando a situação do CPF para "Titular Falecido"), ao INSS e à Justiça Eleitoral [1][2]. Se a Certidão de Óbito precisar de produzir efeitos fora do Brasil, solicite num cartório autorizado a aposição da Apostila da Haia, regulamentada pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ), ou o registo consular junto ao Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) se o falecimento envolver repartição consular [4][5].

steps.title: Requerimento de Pensão por Morte no INSS, Auxílio-Funeral e Saque de FGTS/PIS
steps.html:
Obtida a Certidão de Óbito, os dependentes e familiares devem verificar os direitos previdenciários e trabalhistas [2]:

  • Pensão por Morte (INSS): Os dependentes legais de segurado do Regime Geral de Previdência Social (cônjuge ou companheiro em união estável, filhos menores de 21 anos ou inválidos/com deficiência, ou pais e irmãos que comprovem dependência económica) podem solicitar a Pensão por Morte junto ao Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) diretamente pela plataforma digital Meu INSS (no portal gov.br) ou pela central telefónica 135 [2]. O benefício é devido desde a data do óbito se for requerido em até 90 dias após o falecimento (ou em até 180 dias para filhos menores de 16 anos); após esse prazo, o pagamento conta a partir da data do requerimento [2].
  • FGTS, PIS/PASEP e auxílio-funeral: Com a Certidão de Óbito e a certidão de dependentes habilitados à pensão por morte emitida pelo INSS (ou alvará judicial/escritura de inventário), é possível solicitar o saque de saldos de FGTS e quotas de PIS/PASEP na Caixa Econômica Federal ou no Banco do Brasil, além de eventual auxílio-funeral municipal (via CRAS) para famílias de baixa renda [2][3].

steps.title: Inventário (Extrajudicial ou Judicial), Prazo de 2 Meses (ITCMD), Bancos e Imposto de Renda
steps.html:
A transferência legal de bens, contas bancárias, veículos e imóveis exige a realização do procedimento de inventário e partilha [3][4]:

  • Prazo de 2 meses (60 dias) e imposto estadual (ITCMD): Pelo Código de Processo Civil (art. 611), o inventário deve ser instaurado no prazo de 2 meses (60 dias) a contar da data do óbito; o atraso sujeita os herdeiros a multa fiscal sobre o Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação (ITCMD), cuja alíquota e declaração seguem as regras da Secretaria da Fazenda do respetivo estado [3].
  • Inventário Extrajudicial em Cartório de Notas vs. Judicial: Havendo consenso entre todos os herdeiros e acompanhamento obrigatório de um advogado ou defensor público, o inventário pode ser lavrado de forma rápida por escritura pública em qualquer Cartório de Notas (ou online pela plataforma e-Notariado), conforme as diretrizes do Colégio Notarial do Brasil (CNB) e das normas atualizadas do CNJ (que hoje admitem a via extrajudicial mesmo com testamento ou herdeiros menores, desde que garantida a parte legítima e haja manifestação favorável do Ministério Público) [3][4]. Caso haja litígio entre os herdeiros, o inventário deve tramitar perante o Poder Judiciário estadual [3].
  • Bancos, seguradoras e Receita Federal: Comunique o falecimento aos bancos (que bloqueiam a movimentação individual da conta até à apresentação da escritura pública de inventário ou formal de partilha/alvará judicial) e acione eventuais apólices de seguro de vida no prazo prescricional [3]. Por fim, o inventariante deve entregar à Receita Federal a Declaração Final de Espólio de Imposto de Renda após a conclusão da partilha [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist in Mexico: medical death certification and coroner/police clearance, appointing a licensed funeral director, civil death registration and statutory deadlines, pension and survivor benefit claims, and estate probate, tax filings, and bank notifications.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences on the death of your family member in Mexico. Below are the five main official steps in order to manage medical certification of death, funeral arrangements, civil registration, social security survivor benefits, and estate succession.

steps.title: Medical Verification and Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
The first mandatory document is the Medical Death Certificate (Certificado de Defunción), regulated by the Secretaría de Salud (Ministry of Health), which certifies the medical causes and circumstances of death and is required to obtain the civil death record and any sanitary permit [1][2].

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: If the death occurred in a public or private medical facility, the attending licensed physician (médico tratante con cédula profesional) issues the Certificado de Defunción directly and free of charge after verifying the identity of the deceased person [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the deceased person was under medical supervision for a known chronic illness and died at home of natural causes, the attending physician can attend to certify the death [1]. If death occurred suddenly without an attending physician, in a hotel, in a public place, or from accidental or forensic causes, do not move the body: report the death immediately to the 911 emergency line so that the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público or state Fiscalía General de Justicia) and the Forensic Medical Service (Servicio Médico Forense - SEMEFO) can perform the statutory autopsy and issue the corresponding certificate [1].
  • Sanitary timeline: Under Mexican health regulations overseen by the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (Federal Commission for the Protection against Sanitary Risks - COFEPRIS), burial or cremation must generally take place between 12 and 48 hours after death, unless otherwise ordered by the health authority or the Public Prosecutor's Office [2].

steps.title: Funeral Insurance and Appointing an Authorized Funeral Home
steps.html:
Before contracting funeral services independently, check whether the deceased person held a funeral expense insurance policy, a pre-need funeral plan, or institutional funeral hall coverage (velatorios) through the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (Mexican Social Security Institute - IMSS) or the Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado (Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers - ISSSTE) [3][5].

  • Appointing a licensed funeral home: Select a legally established funeral agency (agencia funeraria) that holds an operating notice and sanitary authorization from the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios or the state health authority (COEPRIS) and whose service contracts are registered with the Federal Consumer Protection Agency (Procuraduría Federal del Consumidor - PROFECO) under the applicable official standard [2].
  • Operational coordination: Provide the funeral agency with the Certificado de Defunción and the deceased person's official identification so that its staff can transport the body, prepare the remains, and obtain the local sanitary permits for burial, cremation, or transport within the statutory 12-to-48-hour window [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Registry Registration, Civil Death Certificate, and Sanitary Permits
steps.html:
With the original Certificado de Defunción, the family or the authorized funeral representative must appear before the local Civil Registry Office (Oficialía o Juzgado del Registro Civil) of the relevant municipality or borough (alcaldía) to record the death officially [1].

  • Issuance of the Acta de Defunción and permits: The Civil Registry retains the medical certificate and issues the official Civil Death Certificate (Acta de Defunción) together with the official burial, cremation, or transit permit (boleta o permiso de inhumación, cremación o traslado) [1][2]. Request several certified copies of the Acta de Defunción, as they will be required for banks, insurers, pension funds, and notarial proceedings; certified digital copies can also be downloaded subsequently via the official Government of Mexico portal [1].
  • International cases or documents for use abroad: If the Acta de Defunción must take legal effect outside Mexico, you must obtain a Hague Apostille (Apostilla) from the State Ministry of Government (Secretaría de Gobierno de la entidad federativa) where the certificate was issued, or contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores - SRE) where consular representation is involved [1].

steps.title: Funeral Expense Grants, Survivor Pensions, and AFORE Retirement Account Withdrawal
steps.html:
Once you have obtained the Acta de Defunción and the original tax invoice (factura fiscal) for the funeral expenses, eligible beneficiaries or the person who paid for the funeral can claim social security death benefits:

  • IMSS insured persons and pensioners: The person who paid the funeral bill (holding an original invoice in their name) has up to one year to claim the funeral expense grant (ayuda para gastos de funeral, equal to twice the monthly value of the UMA) at the Family Medicine Unit (Unidad de Medicina Familiar) of the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (helpline 800 623 23 23), provided the deceased insured person had at least 12 contributed weeks in the preceding nine months or was a current pensioner [3]. In addition, the surviving spouse or domestic partner (concubina o concubinario) and children under age 16 (or up to age 25 if studying) can apply for a widowhood or orphanhood pension (pensión de viudez o de orfandad) [3][4].
  • ISSSTE insured persons and pensioners: If the deceased person was a pensioner or retiree of the Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado, the person who paid the funeral expenses can claim the funeral grant (pago de marcha, equal to 120 days of pension) by presenting the death certificate and original invoice to the relevant pensions department, in addition to applying for survivor pensions for eligible family members [5][6].
  • Individual AFORE retirement account: Legal or substitute beneficiaries can apply to the relevant pension fund administrator (AFORE), regulated by the Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (National Commission for the Retirement Savings System - CONSAR), to withdraw retirement funds following death by submitting the Acta de Defunción, official identification, a bank statement showing a CLABE account number, and the pension grant (or denial) resolution issued by the social security institution [6].

steps.title: Estate Succession, Will Search, Banks, and Tax Deregistration with the SAT
steps.html:
To administer the deceased person's estate, bank accounts, and tax obligations, complete the following steps in order:

  • Will search and succession proceedings: Consult a notary public through the directory or state associations affiliated with the National College of Mexican Notaries (Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano) or a family court judge with the Acta de Defunción so that they can request an official search of the National Registry of Will Notices (Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento - RENAT), coordinated by the Secretaría de Gobernación (Ministry of the Interior - SEGOB) [7]. The RENAT is not open to direct public lookup; only a notary or judge can verify whether a will exists and which testamentary instrument was the last executed [7]. If there is a valid will and agreement among adult heirs, testamentary succession can be completed before a notary public; if there is no will or a dispute exists, intestate probate proceedings (juicio sucesorio intestamentario) must be opened to appoint an estate executor (albacea).
  • Banks and insurance companies: Notify banks and insurers by presenting a certified copy of the Acta de Defunción to block unauthorized charges, claim life insurance payouts as a named beneficiary, or release account balances through the appointed executor (albacea).
  • Taxpayer registry (RFC) cancellation notice: The executor or any family member must file the notice of cancellation in the Federal Taxpayer Registry due to death (Aviso de cancelación en el RFC por defunción - Form RX) with the Servicio de Administración Tributaria (Tax Administration Service - SAT) within one month following the death, presenting a certified copy of the Acta de Defunción and official identification by prior appointment [8].

closingQuestion: To give you specific guidance on the local offices, in which state and municipality of Mexico did the death occur, and with which social security institution (IMSS, ISSSTE, or neither) was your family member affiliated?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en México: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en México: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos el fallecimiento de su familiar en México. A continuación se explican los cinco pasos oficiales principales en orden para gestionar la certificación médica, el servicio funerario, el registro civil, las prestaciones de seguridad social y la sucesión patrimonial.

steps.title: Verificación médica y Certificado de Defunción
steps.html:
El primer documento obligatorio es el Certificado de Defunción, regulado por la Secretaría de Salud, el cual acredita las causas médicas y circunstancias del fallecimiento y es indispensable para tramitar el acta civil y cualquier permiso sanitario [1][2].

  • Fallecimiento en hospital o clínica: Si el deceso ocurrió en una unidad médica pública o privada, el personal médico tratante con cédula profesional emite directamente el Certificado de Defunción sin costo tras verificar la identidad de la persona fallecida [1].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Si la persona fallecida contaba con seguimiento médico por una enfermedad crónica conocida y muere en casa por causas naturales, el médico tratante puede acudir a certificar el deceso [1]. Si la muerte ocurre de forma súbita sin médico tratante, en un hotel, en la vía pública o por causas accidentales o sujetas a investigación, no mueva el cuerpo: reporte de inmediato al número de emergencias 911 para que intervenga el Ministerio Público o la Fiscalía General de Justicia de la entidad federativa y el Servicio Médico Forense (SEMEFO) practique la necropsia de ley y expida el certificado correspondiente [1].
  • Plazo sanitario: Conforme a la normativa sanitaria mexicana vigilada por la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios, la inhumación o cremación debe realizarse por regla general entre las 12 y las 48 horas siguientes al fallecimiento, salvo orden específica de la autoridad sanitaria o del Ministerio Público [2].

steps.title: Seguro funerario y contratación de una agencia funeraria autorizada
steps.html:
Antes de contratar servicios por cuenta propia, revise si la persona fallecida contaba con una póliza de seguro de gastos funerarios, un plan de previsión funeraria o cobertura institucional a través de los velatorios del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social o del Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado [3][5].

  • Designación de funeraria: Seleccione una agencia funeraria legalmente establecida que cuente con aviso de funcionamiento y autorización sanitaria ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios o la autoridad sanitaria estatal (COEPRIS) y cuyos contratos estén registrados ante la Procuraduría Federal del Consumidor conforme a la norma oficial aplicable [2].
  • Coordinación operativa: Entregue a la agencia funeraria el Certificado de Defunción y la identificación oficial de la persona fallecida para que su personal traslade el cuerpo, prepare los restos y gestione ante las autoridades locales las órdenes sanitarias de inhumación, cremación o traslado dentro del plazo legal de 12 a 48 horas [1][2].

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil, Acta de Defunción y permisos sanitarios
steps.html:
Con el Certificado de Defunción original, la familia o el gestor autorizado de la funeraria debe acudir ante la Oficialía o Juzgado del Registro Civil del municipio o alcaldía correspondiente para levantar el registro oficial [1].

  • Emisión del Acta de Defunción y permisos: El Registro Civil retiene el certificado médico y expide el Acta de Defunción junto con la boleta o permiso oficial de inhumación, cremación o traslado [1][2]. Solicite varias copias certificadas del Acta de Defunción, ya que las necesitará para bancos, aseguradoras, pensiones y trámites notariales; posteriormente también puede descargar copias certificadas digitales en el portal oficial del Gobierno de México [1].
  • Casos internacionales o documentos para el extranjero: Si se requiere que el Acta de Defunción surta efectos fuera de México, deberá tramitar la Apostilla ante la Secretaría de Gobierno de la entidad federativa donde se emitió el acta, o acudir a la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores si interviene representación consular [1].

steps.title: Ayuda para gastos de funeral, pensiones de sobrevivencia y retiro de AFORE
steps.html:
Una vez obtenida el Acta de Defunción y la factura fiscal original de los gastos funerarios, las personas beneficiarias o quien haya pagado el funeral pueden solicitar las prestaciones económicas de seguridad social:

  • Derechohabientes del IMSS: Quien haya cubierto el servicio funerario (con factura original a su nombre) tiene un plazo de hasta un año para reclamar la ayuda para gastos de funeral (equivalente a dos veces el valor mensual de la UMA) en la Unidad de Medicina Familiar del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (teléfono de atención 800 623 23 23), siempre que la persona asegurada contara con al menos 12 semanas cotizadas en los nueve meses previos o fuera pensionada vigente [3]. Adicionalmente, el cónyuge, concubina o concubinario y los hijos menores de 16 años (o hasta 25 años si estudian) pueden tramitar la pensión de viudez o de orfandad [3][4].
  • Derechohabientes del ISSSTE: Si la persona fallecida era pensionada o jubilada del Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado, la persona que pagó el funeral puede reclamar el pago de marcha (equivalente a 120 días de pensión) presentando el certificado o acta de defunción y la factura original ante el departamento de pensiones correspondiente, además de gestionar las pensiones por causa de muerte para familiares derechohabientes [5][6].
  • Cuenta individual de AFORE: Los beneficiarios legales o sustitutos pueden acudir a la administradora correspondiente, regulada por la Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro, para solicitar el retiro de recursos por fallecimiento presentando el Acta de Defunción, identificación oficial, estado de cuenta bancario con CLABE y la resolución de pensión (o negativa) emitida por la institución de seguridad social [6].

steps.title: Sucesión patrimonial, búsqueda de testamento, bancos y baja fiscal ante el SAT
steps.html:
Para administrar los bienes, cuentas bancarias y obligaciones fiscales de la persona fallecida, siga este orden:

  • Búsqueda de testamento y trámite sucesorio: Acuda con un notario público a través del directorio o colegios vinculados al Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano o ante un juez familiar con el Acta de Defunción para que soliciten la búsqueda oficial en el Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento, coordinado por la Secretaría de Gobernación [7]. El Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento no es de consulta pública directa; únicamente el notario o el juez puede verificar si existe un testamento y cuál fue el último otorgado [7]. Si hay testamento válido y acuerdo entre herederos mayores de edad, la sucesión testamentaria puede tramitarse ante notario público; si no hay testamento o existe controversia, se tramita un juicio sucesorio intestamentario para designar albacea.
  • Bancos y aseguradoras: Notifique a las instituciones bancarias y aseguradoras presentando el Acta de Defunción certificada para bloquear cargos indebidos, reclamar seguros de vida como beneficiario designado o liberar saldos mediante el nombramiento de albacea.
  • Aviso de cancelación en el RFC: El albacea o cualquier familiar debe presentar el aviso de cancelación en el Registro Federal de Contribuyentes por defunción (Forma RX) ante el Servicio de Administración Tributaria dentro del mes siguiente al fallecimiento, adjuntando copia certificada del Acta de Defunción e identificación oficial previa cita [8].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Canada: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Canada is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key medical, legal, and administrative steps while the person still has full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and simplifies future administration. Because healthcare delivery and powers of attorney are governed provincially and territorially alongside federal benefits, here are the five main steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinating specialist palliative care, home care, and hospice services
steps.html:
Begin by asking the person's primary physician, nurse practitioner, or hospital specialist for a referral to the provincial or territorial home and community palliative care program [1].

  • Home and hospice care: Provincial health authorities coordinate multidisciplinary palliative teams (nurses, pain specialists, occupational therapists, and personal support workers) for home care, outpatient clinics, or residential hospice placement [1]. You can also locate regional hospices and support resources through the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association [2].
  • Palliative drug and equipment benefits: Ask the care coordinator to register the person in the applicable provincial palliative care drug plan (such as Ontario's Palliative Care Facilitated Access program, BC Palliative Care Benefits Plan B, or Alberta's Palliative Coverage program) so prescribed symptom-management medications and medical supplies at home are covered.

steps.title: Preparing and registering a written Advance Directive and emergency care plan
steps.html:
While the person has capacity to express their treatment goals, document their healthcare preferences in writing so clinicians and family members have clear instructions [1][3].

  • Written Advance Care Plan or Directive: Depending on the province or territory, this document is known as an Advance Healthcare Directive, Personal Directive, Representation Agreement, or Living Will [2][3]. Resources and province-specific workbooks from Advance Care Planning Canada help structure preferences regarding pain relief, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and preferred place of care [3].
  • Clinical emergency orders: Have the treating physician or nurse practitioner translate these wishes into an active clinical order kept at home for paramedics and emergency staff (such as a Goals of Care Designation in Alberta, a Medical Order for Scope of Treatment in British Columbia, or a Do Not Resuscitate Confirmation Form in Ontario) [1][3].

steps.title: Executing financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney and bank mandates
steps.html:
A person can only sign a Power of Attorney while they retain the legal mental capacity to understand the nature and effect of the appointment [1][2].

  • Healthcare and Personal Care Substitute Decision-Maker: Execute the legally witnessed provincial instrument appointing a substitute decision-maker for medical and personal care decisions (for example, a Power of Attorney for Personal Care in Ontario, a Representation Agreement in British Columbia, a Personal Directive in Alberta, or a Protection Mandate / Mandat de protection in Quebec) [2][3].
  • Financial and Property Power of Attorney: Execute a Continuing or Enduring Power of Attorney for Property (or Protection Mandate in Quebec) so the chosen representative can pay bills, manage real estate, and deal with government agencies if capacity declines [1][2].
  • Bank mandates: Provide certified copies of the Continuing or Enduring Power of Attorney directly to the person's financial institutions early, as banks often verify the document through their internal legal teams before granting account access.

steps.title: Accessing statutory caregiver leave and Employment Insurance caregiving benefits
steps.html:
Family members or close friends ("like family") who reduce their work hours to provide care or support can apply for federal income support and provincial job-protected leave [4].

  • EI Compassionate Care Benefits: Administered by Service Canada, Employment Insurance (EI) Compassionate Care Benefits provide up to 26 weeks of income support (at 55% of average insurable weekly earnings up to the statutory maximum) to care for a person who has a significant risk of death within 26 weeks [2][4]. The Weeks can be shared among eligible caregivers within a 52-week window [4].
  • EI Family Caregiver Benefits: If the person is critically ill or injured without an immediate 26-week terminal prognosis, Service Canada also administers Family Caregiver Benefits for Adults (up to 15 weeks) [4].
  • How to apply: Ask the treating medical doctor or nurse practitioner to sign the official Medical Certificate for Employment Insurance Compassionate Care Benefits, request a Record of Employment from the employer, and submit the application online via Service Canada as soon as work earnings decrease by more than 40% [4]. Remember to notify the employer in writing to claim matching unpaid job-protected compassionate care leave under provincial or federal labour standards.

steps.title: Organizing the will, beneficiary nominations, vital documents, and future estate steps
steps.html:
Reviewing estate and benefit records in advance prevents delays and protects the executor and surviving family members later:

  • Will and beneficiary designations: Verify that the person has a valid, properly witnessed Will naming an executor (liquidator in Quebec), and confirm that designated beneficiaries on life insurance policies, RRSPs, RRIFs, TFSAs, and occupational pensions are current.
  • Vital documents and pension records: Gather birth and marriage certificates, Social Insurance Number (SIN) details, property deeds, and account statements. Note whether the person contributed to the Canada Pension Plan (administered by Service Canada, which provides the one-time CPP Death Benefit and monthly Survivor's Pension) or the Quebec Pension Plan (administered by Retraite Québec) [5].
  • Future tax and probate requirements: Ensure the named executor knows that after a death, they will need to apply for provincial Probate (Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee) where required, file the Final T1 Return and any T3 Trust returns with the Canada Revenue Agency, and request an official Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) from the Canada Revenue Agency after Notices of Assessment are issued and before distributing estate assets [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Australia: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Australia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and administrative steps while the person still has full decision-making capacity ensures their wishes are respected and reduces later burden on the family. Because powers of attorney and advance care directives are regulated at the state and territory level alongside federal support systems, here are the five main steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinating specialist palliative care, home care, and hospice services
steps.html:
Ask the person's general practitioner (GP) or treating specialist for a referral to state or territory specialist palliative care services for symptom management, community nursing at home, or inpatient hospice admission [1][2].

  • Locating specialist services: Use the national service directory maintained by Palliative Care Australia to find public and community palliative care teams, inpatient hospices, and equipment support in the person's state or territory [1].
  • Home support and aged care assessments: If the person requires domestic assistance, nursing, or home modifications (particularly if aged 65 or over, or 50 or over for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people), contact My Aged Care on 1800 200 422 to request an urgent palliative or high-priority assessment for Commonwealth Home Support or a Home Care Package [3].

steps.title: Preparing and registering a written Advance Care Directive and emergency plan
steps.html:
While the person has decision-making capacity, record their medical treatment preferences and goals of care in a written document recognized in their state or territory [2][4].

  • State and territory Advance Care Directive forms: Download the official state or territory form through Advance Care Planning Australia (such as an Advance Care Directive in New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, or Tasmania; an Advance Health Directive in Queensland or Western Australia; or a Health Direction in the Australian Capital Territory) [2][4]. Clearly specify preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, life-sustaining interventions, pain relief, and preferred place of care [1][2].
  • Uploading to My Health Record: Once signed and witnessed according to state rules, upload the completed Advance Care Directive to the person's My Health Record via myGov so ambulance paramedics, emergency departments, and hospital clinicians nationwide can view it immediately [2].

steps.title: Executing financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney and bank mandates
steps.html:
Legal appointment of substitute decision-makers can only take place while the person has full legal mental capacity to understand the nature and effect of the documents [2][4].

  • Financial and legal authority: Execute a state or territory Enduring Power of Attorney so a trusted attorney can manage bank accounts, bills, property, and legal affairs if capacity declines [2][4]. Ensure it is witnessed by an authorized witness (such as a lawyer, registrar, or qualified Justice of the Peace, depending on the state).
  • Medical and personal care decision-maker: Appoint a substitute decision-maker for health and personal care using the applicable state instrument (such as an Enduring Guardian in New South Wales, Tasmania, or Western Australia; a Medical Treatment Decision Maker in Victoria; or an Enduring Power of Attorney covering personal/health matters in Queensland or the ACT) [2][4].
  • Bank and land registry registration: Register the Enduring Power of Attorney with the person's banks early, and register it with the state land titles office if real property transactions may be required (or with the Tasmania Land Titles Office, where registration is mandatory for all Enduring Powers of Attorney).

steps.title: Accessing statutory caregiver leave, Carer Payment, and early superannuation release
steps.html:
Both the person with a terminal diagnosis and family carers can access federal financial support and workplace leave:

  • Carer Payment and Carer Allowance: Family members providing constant daily care can apply online via myGov to Services Australia for the means-tested Carer Payment and the non-means-tested fortnightly Carer Allowance, supported by a medical report from the treating doctor confirming the terminal condition [5].
  • Workplace leave: Under the National Employment Standards (Fair Work framework), employees can use paid personal/carer's leave to care for an immediate family or household member with a serious illness, as well as compassionate leave when a life-threatening illness occurs.
  • Terminal illness early release of superannuation: Under rules regulated by the Australian Taxation Office, a person diagnosed with a terminal medical condition can apply directly to their superannuation fund for a tax-free lump-sum withdrawal of their super balance if two registered medical practitioners (including at least one specialist in the relevant field) certify that the illness is likely to result in death within 24 months [6]. Separately, a family member can apply to the Australian Taxation Office via myGov for early release of their own super on compassionate grounds to pay for palliative care expenses [6].

steps.title: Reviewing the will, superannuation death benefit nominations, and future estate steps
steps.html:
Organizing legal and financial records in advance prevents delays and protects the executor and beneficiaries later:

  • Will and Binding Death Benefit Nominations: Confirm that the person has a valid, witnessed Will naming an executor. Because superannuation does not automatically form part of the estate under a Will, ask the person's superannuation fund to verify or update a Binding Death Benefit Nomination (and check whether any life or total and permanent disability insurance is held inside the super fund).
  • Centralized documents and post-death notifications: Assemble birth and marriage certificates, Medicare and Centrelink details, super fund statements, and property records. When a death later occurs and is registered with the state Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, the family or executor can notify Services Australia, use the free Australian Death Notification Service to alert participating banks, utilities, and My Aged Care in one step [3][7], apply to the relevant State or Territory Supreme Court for a Grant of Probate where required, and lodge the Official Notification of a Deceased Person and final Date of Death tax return with the Australian Taxation Office [8].
