title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Ireland: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Ireland is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and financial planning steps while the person still has full decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and simplifies later administration. Under Ireland's Assisted Decision-Making (Capacity) Act 2015 and public healthcare framework, here are the five main steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinating specialist palliative care, home care, and hospice services
steps.html:
Ask the person's general practitioner (GP) or hospital consultant for a referral to the local Specialist Palliative Care team operated by the Health Service Executive [1].

  • Community home care and inpatient hospice: Specialist Palliative Care teams from the Health Service Executive coordinate community palliative nursing at home, day care, outpatient symptom management, and admission to an inpatient hospice unit [1].
  • Additional support and night nursing: The Irish Hospice Foundation works alongside public services to provide planning tools (such as the Think Ahead planning pack) and supports nightly nursing care at home in partnership with the Irish Cancer Society and local hospice groups [2]. Ask the GP or public health nurse early about applying for a Medical Card under emergency/end-of-life guidelines, which removes means testing for people with a terminal diagnosis.

steps.title: Preparing a written Advance Healthcare Directive and emergency care plan
steps.html:
While the person has decision-making capacity, they can make a legally recognized Advance Healthcare Directive under the Assisted Decision-Making (Capacity) Act 2015 [3][4].

  • Advance Healthcare Directive (AHD): In an Advance Healthcare Directive, an adult (aged 18 or over with capacity) sets out their preferences for medical treatment and any specific treatments they legally refuse (including life-sustaining treatment, provided they state clearly whether the refusal applies even if their life is at risk) [3][4]. Unlike a power of attorney for property, making an Advance Healthcare Directive does not require a solicitor, though it must be signed in the presence of two witnesses [2][4].
  • Designated Healthcare Representative: Within the Advance Healthcare Directive, the person can appoint a trusted Designated Healthcare Representative (who must also sign the document) to interpret their wishes and consent to or refuse treatment in line with the directive if capacity is lost [3][4]. Templates and statutory guidance are provided by the Decision Support Service, and copies should be given to the GP, hospital team, and family [3].

steps.title: Executing an Enduring Power of Attorney and bank mandates while capacity exists
steps.html:
In Ireland, an Enduring Power of Attorney covers property, finances, and personal welfare (such as accommodation and daily care), whereas medical treatment decisions are governed by an Advance Healthcare Directive [2][4].

  • Enduring Power of Attorney (EPA) registration: Under the reformed Assisted Decision-Making (Capacity) Act 2015 framework, an Enduring Power of Attorney must be created and registered through the online portal of the Decision Support Service while the donor still has capacity [2][3]. The process requires a legal statement from a practising solicitor, a capacity statement from a doctor or qualified healthcare professional, and formal notice to specified family members before registration with the Decision Support Service [2][3].
  • Later activation and bank mandates: If the person later loses capacity, the appointed attorney must apply to the Decision Support Service to notify and bring the Enduring Power of Attorney into effect before exercising full powers [3]. For immediate day-to-day bill paying while capacity remains intact, check with the person's bank about setting up a third-party mandate.

steps.title: Accessing statutory Carer's Leave and Department of Social Protection carer supports
steps.html:
Family members who provide full-time care and attention can apply for income support and statutory job protection:

  • Carer's Benefit and Carer's Allowance: The Department of Social Protection administers Carer's Benefit (for insured employees who leave work or reduce hours to care for someone, based on PRSI contributions) and Carer's Allowance (a means-tested weekly payment for full-time carers on lower incomes) [5][6]. Applications can be submitted online using a verified MyGovID account on MyWelfare or by post [5].
  • Carer's Support Grant and Carer's Leave: Qualifying full-time carers also receive the annual tax-free Carer's Support Grant from the Department of Social Protection, and employees can apply to their employer for up to 104 weeks of statutory unpaid job-protected Carer's Leave [5][6].

steps.title: Reviewing the will, beneficiary nominations, tax records, and probate readiness
steps.html:
Organizing legal, pension, and tax documentation in advance prevents delays for the executor and surviving family members:

  • Will and pension/insurance nominations: Ensure the person has a valid Will executed with a solicitor naming an executor, and verify beneficiary nominations on occupational pensions, PRSAs, and life assurance policies.
  • Social welfare bereavement supports: Note that Ireland's historic once-off Bereavement Grant was discontinued, but the Department of Social Protection provides the weekly Bereaved Partner's Pension (Contributory or Non-Contributory, formerly the Widow's, Widower's or Surviving Civil Partner's Pension and extended to eligible cohabiting partners), the once-off Bereaved Parent Grant (where there are dependent children), and a 6- to 12-week post-death payment continuation for qualifying Carer's Allowance or State Pension recipients [5][6].
  • Tax and Probate administration: Centralize PPS numbers, birth and marriage certificates, property deeds, and account details. After a death, the executor or family notifies the Revenue Commissioners (via myAccount or ROS) to adjust tax credits and file the Statement of Affairs (Probate) Form SA.2, which generates the Notice of Acknowledgement required to apply to the Probate Office of the High Court (part of the Courts Service) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, alongside any Capital Acquisitions Tax (Form IT38) filings [7].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in New Zealand: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in New Zealand (Aotearoa) is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and financial planning steps while the person still has full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and makes later administration much clearer for family and whānau. Here are the five main steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinating specialist palliative care, home care, and hospice services
steps.html:
Ask the person's general practitioner (GP) or hospital specialist for a referral to regional specialist palliative care services funded through Health New Zealand (Te Whatu Ora) and local community hospices [1][2].

  • Hospice and community palliative care: Regional hospices represented by Hospice New Zealand provide free specialist palliative nursing, symptom and pain management, equipment loan, inpatient beds, and family/whānau support at home or in a hospice unit [1].
  • Needs Assessment and Service Coordination (NASC): Ask the GP or hospice nurse to refer the person to the local Needs Assessment and Service Coordination agency through Health New Zealand (Te Whatu Ora) to arrange publicly funded personal care at home, domestic support, and Carer Support relief days.

steps.title: Preparing and sharing a written Advance Care Plan and Advance Directive
steps.html:
While the person has decision-making capacity, document their values, care goals, and specific medical treatment choices in writing [2].

  • Advance Care Plan (ACP): Use the official templates and guides from New Zealand Advance Care Planning (Tō Tātou Reo) to write down what matters most to the person, their preferred place of care, cultural or spiritual practices, and everyday care preferences [2].
  • Advance Directive under the Code of Rights: Under Right 7(5) of the Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers' Rights, a competent person can include a legally recognized Advance Directive inside their Advance Care Plan (or as a standalone signed document) refusing specific future medical treatments, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation or mechanical ventilation, if they later lose capacity [2][3]. Ask the GP to review and upload the completed Advance Care Plan and Advance Directive into the person's shared electronic health record so ambulance and hospital teams can see it immediately [2].

steps.title: Executing Enduring Powers of Attorney and bank mandates while capacity exists
steps.html:
Under the Protection of Personal and Property Rights Act 1988, an Enduring Power of Attorney can only be signed while the donor has mental capacity to understand the nature and effect of the appointment [3].

  • Two types of Enduring Power of Attorney (EPA):
    • EPA for Personal Care and Welfare: Appoints one individual attorney (not joint attorneys) to make decisions about healthcare, medical treatment, and living arrangements; by law, it only takes effect if a medical practitioner certifies (or the Family Court determines) that the donor has lost mental capacity in relation to the matter [3].
    • EPA for Property: Appoints one or more attorneys (or a trustee corporation) to manage bank accounts, bills, and property; the donor can choose whether it takes effect immediately while they still have capacity or only upon loss of capacity [3].
  • Mandatory legal witnessing: In New Zealand, the donor's signature on an Enduring Power of Attorney must be witnessed by an independent lawyer, qualified legal executive, or authorized officer of a trustee corporation, who must certify that they explained the effects and implications of the EPA to the donor [3]. Provide certified copies of the Property EPA to the person's bank early so account access is ready when needed.

steps.title: Accessing carer financial support, KiwiSaver serious illness withdrawal, and leave
steps.html:
Both the person with a terminal illness and family carers can apply for financial support:

  • Work and Income carer and health payments: A person providing full-time care at home to someone (other than their spouse or partner) who would otherwise require hospital-level or rest-home care can apply to Work and Income (part of the Ministry of Social Development) for the Supported Living Payment (Carer), alongside supplementary help such as the Disability Allowance [4]. The person diagnosed with a terminal illness (particularly where life expectancy is under two years) may also qualify directly for the Supported Living Payment on health grounds [4].
  • KiwiSaver early withdrawal for serious or terminal illness: Under rules overseen by Inland Revenue and KiwiSaver scheme providers, a member experiencing a serious illness (an injury, illness, or disability that is permanent or likely to result in death) can apply directly to their KiwiSaver provider with medical certification for an early lump-sum withdrawal of their entire KiwiSaver balance [5]. Separately, early withdrawal under significant financial hardship can cover palliative care expenses for a member or dependent [5].
  • Workplace leave: Employees can use statutory sick leave (which covers caring for a dependent family or household member who is sick or injured) and negotiate flexible working arrangements with their employer.

steps.title: Organizing the will, beneficiary nominations, vital documents, and probate planning
steps.html:
Reviewing estate and end-of-life records now prevents administrative delays for the executor and whānau later:

  • Will, funeral wishes, and Te Hokinga ā-Wairua: Ensure the person has a valid, witnessed Will naming an executor, and record funeral, burial, cremation, or tangihanga wishes using the government's Te Hokinga ā-Wairua End of Life Service planning portal [6].
  • Vital documents and future notifications: Gather birth, marriage, or civil union certificates, IRD number, KiwiSaver provider details, bank statements, and insurance policies. Note that after a death, the funeral director or family registers the death with Births, Deaths and Marriages, and the executor or family notifies Work and Income (Regarding NZ Superannuation and any means-tested Survivor's Grant or Funeral Grant, or ACC if the death resulted from a covered injury) and Inland Revenue (to finalize tax up to the date of death) [4][5][6].
  • High Court Probate: If the estate holds a single asset (such as a bank account, KiwiSaver balance, or shares) exceeding the statutory small-estate threshold (NZD 15,000, rising to NZD 40,000 under updated administration thresholds) or real property held in the deceased's sole name, the executor will need to apply to the High Court of New Zealand (through the Ministry of Justice) for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no Will) [7].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in South Africa: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in South Africa is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key medical, legal, and financial steps while the person still holds full decision-making capacity prevents court delays and protects the household's wishes. Below is the 5-step official administrative pathway in South Africa.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Care, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
Ask the treating specialist or hospital team for a clinical referral to an interdisciplinary palliative care team or an accredited community hospice registered with the Association of Palliative Care Centres (formerly the Hospice Palliative Care Association of South Africa, HPCA) [1]. Member hospices across South Africa (such as St Luke's Combined Hospices in Cape Town, HospiceWits in Johannesburg, or Highway Hospice in Durban, listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank them) provide home-based nursing, pain and symptom control, and inpatient care [1].

If your family member belongs to a private medical scheme regulated by the Council for Medical Schemes, ask the treating doctor to submit a motivation under the Prescribed Minimum Benefits (PMB) framework of the Medical Schemes Act 131 of 1998 [2][3]. Qualifying PMB diagnoses (including oncology, HIV/AIDS palliative pain management, and listed Diagnosis and Treatment Pairs) must be covered in full when using the scheme's Designated Service Providers, and many schemes also activate dedicated compassionate or advanced illness home-nursing benefits once a palliative care plan is registered [2][3]. Patients using public healthcare can request referral through their provincial Department of Health tertiary hospital palliative care clinic or community health centre [1].

steps.title: Prepare a Written Advance Directive (Living Will) and Emergency Care Plan
steps.html:
While your family member has full mental capacity, document clear instructions regarding future medical care in a written Advance Healthcare Directive (Living Will) [4]. Under the ethical guidelines of the Health Professions Council of South Africa (Booklet 7: Guidelines for the Withholding and Withdrawing of Treatment, and Booklet 4: Seeking Patients' Informed Consent), a clear written refusal of futile or artificial life-prolonging interventions (such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or artificial nutrition and hydration) made while competent must be respected by clinicians [4].

Under the updated Health Professions Council of South Africa guidelines, the person may also designate a written patient representative (healthcare proxy) to deliberate with clinicians if the person loses capacity [4]. Sign and date the Living Will in the presence of two independent witnesses, lodge copies in the hospital file and with the primary general practitioner and palliative care team, and keep a copy accessible at home so emergency personnel have immediate sight of agreed comfort-focused care plans [4].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Plan for Incapacity Under South African Law
steps.html:
While your family member still has full legal capacity, they can sign a General Power of Attorney or bank-specific mandate (with supporting FICA identity and proof-of-address documents) so a trusted representative can manage day-to-day bank accounts, municipal billing, and administrative tasks [5].

Crucially, under South African common law, an ordinary Power of Attorney or bank mandate automatically lapses the moment the principal loses mental capacity; South Africa does not currently recognise a statutory enduring power of attorney [5][6]. Acting through a lapsed Power of Attorney after mental incapacity is unlawful. To ensure continuity if capacity declines later, consult an attorney or fiduciary specialist while the person is still competent to evaluate setting up an inter vivos (living) trust, or prepare for the two statutory/court mechanisms supervised by the Master of the High Court [5][6]:

  • Section 60 Administrator (Mental Health Care Act 17 of 2002): An administrative application lodged directly with the Master of the High Court to appoint an Administrator to manage property and financial affairs where incapacity arises from a diagnosed mental illness or severe intellectual disability [6].
  • Rule 57 Curatorship (Uniform Rules of Court): A High Court application to appoint a Curator Bonis (for finances and property) and/or a Curator Personae (for personal and medical welfare) where physical or cognitive incapacity prevents the person from managing their affairs [5][6].

steps.title: Access Caregiver Leave, UIF Illness Benefits, and SASSA Disability Support
steps.html:
If your family member is an employed contributor to the Unemployment Insurance Fund (administered by the Department of Employment and Labour) and is unable to work due to illness for more than 14 consecutive days while receiving reduced or zero pay, they (or an authorised proxy if too ill to attend in person) can claim UIF Illness Benefits within 6 months via the uFiling portal or a local Labour Centre [7]. Prepare the 13-digit barcoded ID or smart ID card, Form UI-2.2 (completed with the attending medical practitioner), Form UI-19 and Form UI-2.7 (completed by the employer), and Form UI-2.8 (bank-stamped account verification) [7].

Employed family caregivers are entitled under Section 27 of the Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA) to at least 3 days of paid Family Responsibility Leave per annual cycle when an immediate family member (spouse, life partner, parent, adoptive parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, or sibling) is ill, and can negotiate extended unpaid or flexible care leave with their employer. For lower-income households where the person is aged 18 to 59 and meets the means test, apply through the South African Social Security Agency (toll-free helpline 0800 60 10 11, email GrantEnquiries@sassa.gov.za) for a SASSA Disability Grant using a medical assessment report less than 3 months old, plus a supplemental SASSA Grant-in-Aid if the person requires full-time home care from another person [8].

steps.title: Organise the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, Vital Documents, and Estate Reporting File
steps.html:
While your family member has full testamentary capacity, review and update their written Will under the Wills Act 7 of 1953: it must be signed at the end by the testator (and initialled on each preceding page) in the simultaneous presence of two competent witnesses aged 14 or older who are not beneficiaries, executors, or spouses of beneficiaries. Separate from the Will, review beneficiary nominations on retirement funds (governed by Section 37C of the Pension Funds Act, where trustees allocate benefits among dependants and nominees), life insurance policies, and medical aid files.

Assemble a master file containing original certified copies of the person's green barcoded ID or smart ID card, birth and marriage certificates (or customary marriage registration and antenuptial contract), property title deeds, bank and policy schedules, tax reference number, and written funeral or cremation wishes. This preparation directly streamlines post-death reporting:

  • Master of the High Court: An estate must be reported within 14 days of death to the Master of the High Court (or designated Magistrate's Office) using Form J294 (Death Notice), alongside the Department of Home Affairs Death Certificate, original Will, and asset inventory, to obtain Letters of Executorship (Form J238) or, for estates valued at ZAR 250,000 or less under Section 18(3) of the Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, Letters of Authority (Form J170) [9].
  • South African Revenue Service: The executor or representative must notify the South African Revenue Service to code the deceased estate and complete pre-date-of-death and post-date-of-death tax assessments before final distribution [10].
  • UIF Death Benefits: Surviving spouses or life partners can claim Dependants' Benefits from the Unemployment Insurance Fund within 18 months of death using Form UI-2.5 (or Form UI-2.6 for dependent children or nominees), Form UI-19, Form UI-2.8, and the official Death Certificate [11].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in India: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in India is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key medical, legal, and financial steps while the person still holds full decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and prevents later administrative delays. Below is the 5-step official pathway in India.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Care, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
Ask the treating specialist or oncology/internal medicine team for a referral to a dedicated pain and palliative medicine unit. Under the National Programme for Palliative Care overseen by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (implemented through the National Health Mission and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs / district hospitals), public district and tertiary hospitals provide outpatient and home-based palliative support and essential pain medications [1][2].

To locate accredited specialist centres, inpatient hospices, and home-care teams across Indian states, consult the national directory maintained by the Indian Association of Palliative Care [3]. Established nonprofit and hospital services (such as Pallium India in Thiruvananthapuram, Karunashraya in Bengaluru, Cipla Palliative Care and Training Centre in Pune, or CanSupport in Delhi NCR, listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank them) coordinate home nursing, symptom management, and family caregiver training [3][4].

steps.title: Prepare and Attest a Written Advance Medical Directive (Living Will)
steps.html:
While your family member is of sound mind and retains full decision-making capacity, they can execute a written Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) under the Supreme Court of India judgment in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018), as simplified by the Supreme Court's Constitution Bench order of 24 January 2023 (MA 1699 of 2019) [5]. The directive sets out when artificial life-sustaining treatment (such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or artificial nutrition) should be withheld or withdrawn in the event of an irreversible terminal condition, and names a guardian or close relative to be consulted by clinicians [5].

Under the 2023 Supreme Court rules, countersignature by a Judicial Magistrate First Class is no longer required [5]. Instead:

  • The person signs the Advance Medical Directive voluntarily in the presence of two independent witnesses [5].
  • The document is attested before a Notary Public or a Gazetted Officer [5].
  • Give copies to the appointed guardian/surrogate, the family physician, the treating hospital (to be incorporated into the medical record), and the competent local government officer (municipal corporation, municipality, or panchayat custodian) [5]. If the person later loses capacity in a terminal phase, withdrawal of life support is reviewed by the hospital's Primary Medical Board and corroborated by a Secondary Medical Board including a nominee of the Chief Medical Officer [5].

steps.title: Execute a Registered Power of Attorney and Record Bank and Demat Nominations
steps.html:
While your family member has full legal capacity, execute a General Power of Attorney or Special Power of Attorney on the required state non-judicial stamp paper and register it before the jurisdictional Sub-Registrar of Assurances (under the Registration Act, 1908) so an authorised representative can manage property, tax filings, and banking affairs [10]. If the person or the appointed representative resides outside India, a Power of Attorney executed abroad must be attested by the Indian Embassy or Consulate (or apostilled under the guidelines of the Ministry of External Affairs) and adjudicated/stamped in India within 3 months of receipt [10].

Note that under Section 201 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an ordinary Power of Attorney is subject to termination if the principal becomes of unsound mind, and expires immediately upon death. Therefore, alongside a Power of Attorney, ensure your family member registers statutory nominations while competent across all financial accounts: Form DA-1 for bank accounts and fixed deposits (under the Banking Regulation Act), Form SH-13 for company shares, and NSDL/CDSL nominations for demat and mutual fund holdings, so funds can be released directly to nominees without waiting for lengthy court probate.

steps.title: Access Medical Advances, ESIC Sickness Benefits, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's employment and insurance coverage, activate immediate financial and medical support:

  • EPFO Medical Advance: Salaried members covered by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation can apply online via the Unified Member Portal using the Composite Claim Form (Form 31 under Paragraph 68-J of the EPF Scheme) to withdraw a non-refundable advance for treatment of severe or terminal illness; a self-declaration suffices without requiring hospital proformas [6].
  • ESIC Sickness and Extended Sickness Benefits: Workers insured under the Employees' State Insurance Corporation can claim cash Sickness Benefit (Form 9, up to 91 days) and Extended Sickness Benefit (for specified malignant or long-term diseases, up to 308 days at an enhanced daily rate) through their local branch office and dispensary [7].
  • Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and Private Insurance: Eligible families under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana administered by the National Health Authority can access cashless secondary and tertiary hospital care (including oncology and palliative packages) up to INR 5 lakh per family per year at empanelled hospitals [8]. Central and state government employees can combine Earned Leave, Half Pay Leave, and Commuted Leave for caregiving or medical treatment.

steps.title: Organise the Will, EPFO/ESIC/PBBY Nominations, Vital Documents, and Estate Records
steps.html:
While your family member has testamentary capacity, review or execute a written Will under the Indian Succession Act, 1925: it must be signed by the testator in the presence of at least two attesting witnesses (optional registration before the Sub-Registrar of Assurances helps prevent later authenticity disputes). Assemble a master folder containing the person's Aadhaar card, PAN card, passport, marriage certificate, property title deeds, and written funeral or cremation preferences.

Verify and update survivor nominations across statutory schemes to prevent post-death bottlenecks:

  • EPFO Survivor Claims: Ensure e-Nomination is completed on the UAN portal so survivors can file the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation Composite Claim Form in Death Cases (integrating Form 20 for PF final settlement, Form 10-D for Employees' Pension Scheme monthly survivor pension, and Form 5-IF for Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance lump-sum payout) [6].
  • ESIC Funeral and Dependants' Benefits: Ensure family particulars are updated with the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (Form 22 for funeral expenses and Form 15/Form 24 for Dependants' Benefit where applicable) [7].
  • Overseas Indian Workers (PBBY): If your family member is an Indian emigrant worker covered under the Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana managed by the Ministry of External Affairs on the eMigrate portal, keep policy and employment records ready for medical, repatriation, or survivor claims [9].
  • Post-Death Estate Certificates: Clarify whether the state and asset types will require a Legal Heir Certificate (from the Tehsildar/Talukdar for service benefits), a Succession Certificate from the Civil Court for movable debts and securities where no valid nomination exists, or High Court/District Court Probate (mandatory under Sections 57 and 213 of the Indian Succession Act for applicable Wills in Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai) alongside registration of the death within 21 days under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.

closingQuestion: To help tailor this guidance, which state and city in India is your family member located in, and are they covered under EPFO/ESIC, a public scheme such as Ayushman Bharat, or private medical insurance?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Philippines: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in the Philippines is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and benefit steps while the person still holds full decision-making capacity protects their care preferences and prevents financial or estate delays. Below is the 5-step official administrative pathway in the Philippines.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Care, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
Ask the attending specialist or hospital oncology/internal medicine department for a referral to an accredited pain and palliative medicine service. Under the National Integrated Cancer Control Act (Republic Act No. 11215) and the National Policy on Palliative and Hospice Care overseen by the Department of Health, tertiary government hospitals (such as the Philippine General Hospital in Manila, Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center in Cebu, or Southern Philippines Medical Center in Davao) operate multidisciplinary palliative care units and pain clinics [1].

For financial risk protection against catastrophic illnesses, verify package eligibility with the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth), which administers PhilHealth Z-Benefits and case-rate packages at accredited contracted hospitals [2]. To locate board-certified palliative specialists and community or home-based hospice teams nationwide, consult the Philippine Society of Hospice and Palliative Medicine and the National Hospice and Palliative Care Council of the Philippines (Hospice Philippines) [3][4].

steps.title: Prepare a Written Advance Healthcare Directive and Emergency Care Plan
steps.html:
While your family member has full decision-making capacity, document their treatment goals and end-of-life preferences in a written Advance Healthcare Directive and Advance Care Plan [3]. Although the Philippines does not have a single standalone Living Will registration statute, patient autonomy and the right to refuse extraordinary or futile life-prolonging interventions are recognised under Department of Health palliative care policies and hospital bioethics standards [1][3].

Have your family member sign the written Advance Healthcare Directive in the presence of two competent witnesses, designate a primary healthcare proxy (health care representative) from among immediate family members, and discuss specific orders (such as a Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) or Allow Natural Death (AND) order, artificial ventilation limits, and comfort-focused symptom control) with the attending physician and the hospital ethics or palliative care committee so the signed directive is placed directly into the official medical chart [3].

steps.title: Execute a Notarized Special Power of Attorney (SPA) and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
While your family member retains full legal capacity, execute a written Special Power of Attorney (SPA) under the Civil Code of the Philippines (Articles 1874 and 1878) authorising a trusted representative to manage bank accounts, sign hospital and insurance paperwork, process government benefit claims, and administer real or personal property [10]. The SPA must be signed personally before a commissioned Philippine Notary Public with valid government-issued identification (or, if executed outside the Philippines, acknowledged before a Philippine Embassy or Consulate or apostilled in the host country) [10].

Keep two critical legal rules in mind under Philippine law:

  • Most Philippine commercial banks require their own bank-specific SPA form or joint-account mandate in addition to a general notarized SPA; verify the exact template with each branch while the account holder can sign personally.
  • Under Article 1919 of the Civil Code of the Philippines, an agency (including an SPA) is extinguished by civil interdiction, insanity, or death of the principal. Because a Philippine SPA does not survive permanent mental incapacity or death, organize survivor benefit nominations and estate documents simultaneously while capacity is intact.

steps.title: Access SSS Sickness and Disability Benefits, PhilHealth, and PCSO / Malasakit Assistance
steps.html:
Activate statutory income replacement and medical cost assistance early:

  • SSS Sickness and Disability Benefits: Private-sector and voluntary members of the Social Security System who have exhausted company paid sick leave and are confined at home or in hospital for at least 4 days can claim a daily cash Sickness Benefit (up to 120 days per calendar year), or apply for permanent partial or total Disability Benefits (monthly pension for members with at least 36 monthly contributions, or lump sum otherwise) via the My.SSS online portal [5][6]. Public-sector employees apply through the Government Service Insurance System [7].
  • PCSO Medical Assistance and Malasakit Centers: For chemotherapy, radiation, dialysis, confinement bills, or high-cost palliative medications, request a Guarantee Letter (GL) under the Medical Assistance Program of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office [8]. If your family member is admitted to or treated at a Department of Health hospital or the Philippine General Hospital, submit the clinical abstract, Statement of Account or quotation, and valid IDs at the hospital's Malasakit Center (established under Republic Act No. 11463), which brings together PhilHealth, Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office assistance at a single desk [8].

steps.title: Organise the Will, SSS/GSIS/Pag-IBIG/OWWA Beneficiaries, and BIR Estate Tax Records
steps.html:
While your family member has full testamentary capacity, review or execute a Will strictly observing the formalities of the Civil Code of the Philippines: either a Notarial Will (subscribed by the testator and attested by three or more credible instrumental witnesses, numbered correlatively in letters on the upper part of each page, signed on the left margin of each page, and acknowledged before a Notary Public) or a Holographic Will (entirely written, dated, and signed by the hand of the testator, which requires no witnesses). Compile a master folder of Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) birth and marriage certificates (or CENOMAR if unmarried), Transfer Certificates of Title, Tax Declarations, and written funeral or cremation instructions.

Ensure beneficiary records are updated across all statutory agencies to streamline post-death claims:

  • SSS or GSIS Death and Funeral Benefits: Update primary beneficiaries (legal spouse and dependent children) with the Social Security System (for online Funeral and Death Benefit claims via My.SSS) or the Government Service Insurance System (which provides a Funeral Benefit and survivorship pension) [5][7].
  • Pag-IBIG Fund and OWWA: Verify Member's Data Form beneficiaries with Pag-IBIG Fund (for Provident Benefits and Death Benefit claims via the Application for Provident Benefits form) and, for Overseas Filipino Workers, keep active membership records ready for Overseas Workers Welfare Administration death and burial benefits.
  • Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Estate Tax: Under the National Internal Revenue Code (as amended by the TRAIN Law), the executor, administrator, or legal heirs must file the Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801) with the Bureau of Internal Revenue within 1 year from the date of death (assessing a 6% flat estate tax rate on the net estate after the standard PHP 5,000,000 deduction and family home deduction up to PHP 10,000,000) to obtain the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) [9]. Where the decedent left no Will and no outstanding debts and all heirs are of legal age (or duly represented), heirs may execute a notarized Deed of Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate under Rule 74, Section 1 of the Rules of Court (published once a week for 3 consecutive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation) instead of full court probate [9].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Singapore: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Singapore: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Singapore: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Singapore is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key healthcare, legal, and financial steps while the person still retains mental capacity ensures their care preferences are recorded in national systems and avoids court delays. Below is the 5-step official administrative pathway in Singapore.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Care, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
Ask the treating hospital specialist, polyclinic doctor, or general practitioner to submit a referral for home palliative care, day hospice care, or the Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS) coordinated through the Agency for Integrated Care (hotline 1800-650-6060) [1][2]. You can review accredited charitable and community providers across Singapore (such as HCA Hospice, Assisi Hospice, Dover Park Hospice, or St Luke's Hospital, listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank them) through the Singapore Hospice Council [3].

For Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, the Ministry of Health provides means-tested government subsidies alongside MediShield Life coverage for inpatient palliative care [2]. In addition, when a patient is certified as terminally ill and receives approved home palliative or day hospice care (or inpatient hospice care), there is no withdrawal limit when paying bills from the patient's own MediSave account, while standard daily or lifetime limits apply if family members use their own MediSave accounts for a dependant [4][5].

steps.title: Complete Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Register an Advance Medical Directive (AMD)
steps.html:
While your family member has full mental capacity, Singapore provides two complementary frameworks to record end-of-life care wishes [3][6]:

  • Advance Care Planning (ACP): Through the myACP digital service on MyLegacy@LifeSG (using Singpass) or with a certified ACP facilitator at a hospital or polyclinic, your family member can record their personal care values, preferred place of care and death, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation preferences, and appoint up to two Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons [6]. Completed ACP records are uploaded directly to the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR), making them immediately visible to public hospital and emergency teams [6].
  • Advance Medical Directive (AMD): Under the Advance Medical Directive Act administered by the Ministry of Health, any person aged 21 or older with mental capacity can sign an official AMD instructing doctors not to use extraordinary life-sustaining treatment if they are terminally ill, unconscious, and facing imminent death [7]. The AMD form must be signed in the presence of two witnesses (one of whom must be the patient's medical practitioner) and returned to the Registrar of Advance Medical Directives at the Ministry of Health [7].

steps.title: Register a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) with the Office of the Public Guardian
steps.html:
Because ordinary bank mandates and powers of attorney cease to operate if the donor loses mental capacity, your family member (the Donor, aged 21 or above) should execute a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) under the Mental Capacity Act while capacity is intact, appointing one or more trusted Donees to act on their behalf for Personal Welfare and/or Property and Affairs [8].

Most individuals use standard LPA Form 1 (granting general powers with basic restrictions), while LPA Form 2 is drafted by a lawyer for customised clauses [8]. The process is completed digitally through the Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) portal managed by the Office of the Public Guardian (under the Ministry of Social and Family Development) [8]: 1. The Donor logs into OPGO via Singpass to draft the LPA and appoint Donees (specifying whether multiple Donees act jointly or jointly and severally) [8]. 2. The Donees log into OPGO via Singpass to accept the appointment [8]. 3. Your family member attends in person before an accredited Certificate Issuer (an accredited medical practitioner, practicing lawyer, or registered psychiatrist), who certifies that the Donor understands the LPA and submits it digitally to the Office of the Public Guardian for registration [8].

steps.title: Access the Home Caregiving Grant, MediSave Care, and CPF Reduced Life Expectancy Withdrawals
steps.html:
Activate statutory financial and caregiving support through the Agency for Integrated Care and the Central Provident Fund Board:

  • Home Caregiving Grant (HCG): If your family member permanently requires assistance with at least 3 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), resides at home (not in a residential long-term care institution), and meets the household means test, apply via the Agency for Integrated Care eFASS portal with a Functional Assessment Report (FAR) for monthly cash payouts of SGD 200 to SGD 600 to defray caregiving or domestic helper costs [9]. Severely disabled individuals aged 30 and above can also apply for MediSave Care cash withdrawals [5].
  • CPF Withdrawal on Medical Grounds (Reduced Life Expectancy): If an accredited doctor certifies that your family member has a severely reduced life expectancy or is permanently unfit for work, they (or their registered LPA Donee if capacity is later lost) can apply online to the Central Provident Fund Board under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme to withdraw CPF savings early in a lump sum, with the Medical Assessment Report submitted within 90 days of application [10][11].

steps.title: Organise the Will, CPF Nomination, Public Trustee Thresholds, and Probate Records
steps.html:
While your family member has full testamentary capacity, review or execute a written Will under the Wills Act (signed at the foot by the testator in the simultaneous presence of two or more independent witnesses who are not beneficiaries or spouses of beneficiaries) and optionally log its storage location (without uploading the confidential contents) in the Wills Registry via MyLegacy@LifeSG [6]. Assemble NRIC records, marriage and birth certificates, insurance policies, bank statements, and funeral wishes.

Keep three critical Singapore estate rules in view:

  • CPF Nomination (Separate from a Will): Central Provident Fund savings (Ordinary, Special, MediSave, and Retirement Accounts) are excluded from the estate covered by a Will [12]. Your family member should review or submit a digital CPF Nomination via Singpass with two witnesses through the Central Provident Fund Board so CPF monies are paid directly to named nominees after death; un-nominated CPF funds are transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution under intestacy rules (Intestate Succession Act for non-Muslims, or Administration of Muslim Law Act for Muslims), which carries an administrative fee [12][13].
  • Small Estates (Up to SGD 50,000): If the deceased's non-CPF estate does not exceed SGD 50,000 and meets statutory conditions, the Public Trustee's Office (under the Ministry of Law) can administer and distribute the estate without requiring a court grant [13].
  • Estates Exceeding SGD 50,000 and Tax Clearance: For estates over SGD 50,000, the executor named in the Will applies to the Family Justice Courts for a Grant of Probate (or next of kin apply for Letters of Administration if there is no Will) [14], and the legal representative settles any final income tax obligations up to the date of death with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS; Singapore has no estate duty for deaths on or after 15 February 2008).

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Spain: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When your family member in Spain is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing the medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full legal capacity (capacidad de obrar) ensures that their care wishes are respected and prevents subsequent judicial or financial freezes. Below are the 5 official steps to follow in order in Spain.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Care, and Inpatient Units
steps.html:
Activate specialist palliative care resources through the public health service of your autonomous community:

  • Referral to public palliative care units and home support teams: Ask the specialist medical team or the primary care physician at the local health center (centro de salud) for a referral to the palliative care resources of your autonomous community within the National Health System (Sistema Nacional de Salud), coordinated at state level by the Ministerio de Sanidad (Ministry of Health) [1]. Depending on the autonomous community, care is delivered through hospital Palliative Care Units (Unidades de Cuidados Paliativos) and Home Care Support Teams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD, or PADES in Catalonia, PALCA in the Basque Country, and equivalent units under SERMAS in Madrid or SAS in Andalusia) for pain management, psychosocial support, and home monitoring [1].
  • Directory of specialist units and Advance Care Planning: To locate hospital units, home support teams, and residential care centers in each province, consult the Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos (Spanish Society for Palliative Care - SECPAL), which also provides guidance on Advance Care Planning (Planificación Anticipada de Cuidados - PAC) together with the clinical and social work team [2].

steps.title: Execute and Register an Advance Directive (Living Will)
steps.html:
While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, they can execute a written Advance Directive (Documento de Instrucciones Previas, also called Voluntades Anticipadas or Testamento Vital depending on the autonomous community), regulated nationwide by Article 11 of Law 41/2002 on patient autonomy and Royal Decree 124/2007 [1][3]:

  • Scope of medical instructions and healthcare proxy: In this document, the ill person sets out binding instructions on the medical care and treatments they wish to accept or refuse (such as limitation of therapeutic effort, mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or palliative sedation), appoints a representative (representante) as interlocutor with the medical team, and may record wishes regarding organ donation or disposition of the body [1][3].
  • Formal execution and national registration: Depending on the applicable regional law, the document is executed through one of three channels: before a notary (without the need for witnesses), before registry officials at the Autonomous Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Autonómico de Instrucciones Previas) or designated healthcare facility units, or before three adult witnesses with full legal capacity (at least two of whom must not be related within the second degree or share a financial relationship with the declarant) [1][3]. Once registered in the relevant regional registry, it is synchronized electronically with the National Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) of the Ministerio de Sanidad so that it can be accessed via the electronic health record in any hospital across Spain [1][3].

steps.title: Execute a Public Deed of Preventive Power of Attorney Before a Notary
steps.html:
Because ordinary bank authorizations and standard powers of attorney become invalid or frozen if a loss of legal capacity occurs, it is essential that your family member visit a notary office (notaría) while retaining full discernment to execute a Preventive Power of Attorney (Poder Preventivo) by public deed (escritura pública), following the guidelines of the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of Notaries) and the Civil Code reform introduced by Law 8/2021 [4][5].

There are two main forms that the notary tailors to each situation:

  • General power of attorney with a subsistence clause (Poder general con cláusula de subsistencia): Takes effect immediately upon signing and remains valid even if the grantor subsequently requires support in exercising legal capacity [4][5].
  • Strict preventive power of attorney (Poder preventivo en sentido estricto): Takes effect only at a future point when loss of capacity is certified in accordance with the medical or notarial criteria specified in the deed itself [4][5].
  • Scope and Civil Registry notification: A preventive power of attorney can cover both financial and banking administration (managing accounts, collecting pensions, paying care expenses, or disposing of assets) and personal and healthcare matters, and the notary notifies the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) ex officio to avoid the need for judicial support proceedings (curatela) [4][5].

steps.title: Apply for Urgent Dependency Assessment, Caregiver Leave, and Disability Benefits
steps.html:
Apply early for the social and employment entitlements available to the ill person and family caregivers:

  • Fast-track Dependency Assessment (Valoración de Dependencia por vía de urgencia - Law 39/2006): Through municipal or regional social services integrated into the System for Autonomy and Care for Dependency (Sistema para la Autonomía y Atención a la Dependencia - SAAD), coordinated by the Instituto de Mayores y Servicios Sociales (Institute for Older Persons and Social Services - IMSERSO), submit an application for recognition of the degree of dependency (Grade I, II, or III), attaching the medical report confirming the advanced stage of the illness to request priority or social-emergency processing [6][7]. The Individual Care Program (Programa Individual de Atención - PIA) grants access to home help services, day centers, telecare, or a financial allowance for family care [6][7].
  • Social Security disability benefits and statutory caregiver leave: If the ill person is employed, they can apply for temporary incapacity leave (incapacidad temporal) or a permanent disability pension (incapacidad permanente absoluta or gran invalidez, which includes a supplement to remunerate a caregiver) through the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (National Institute of Social Security - INSS) [8]. Employed family caregivers are entitled under Articles 37.3.b, 37.6, and 46.3 of the Workers' Statute (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) to 5 days of paid leave for serious illness or hospitalization of relatives up to the second degree, as well as to request working-time adaptation or reduction (between one-eighth and one-half of working hours) or unpaid caregiver leave (excedencia) to care for a relative up to the second degree [8].

steps.title: Review the Will, Insurance Policies, and Documentation for Succession Procedures
steps.html:
While your family member retains full testamentary capacity, it is advisable to review or execute an open notarial will (testamento abierto notarial) before a notary of the Consejo General del Notariado, which simplifies future estate administration and avoids a costly intestate declaration of heirs (declaración de herederos abintestato) [4]. Gather in an accessible folder the valid DNI or NIE, literal birth and marriage certificates (or domestic partnership registration), property deeds, bank contracts, life or funeral insurance policies (seguros de vida o de decesos), and written burial or cremation preferences.

Keeping these documents organized streamlines the mandatory post-death procedures:

  • Social Security survivor benefits (Muerte y Supervivencia): Apply to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (via its electronic portal or at a CAISS office) for the death grant (Auxilio por defunción, 5-year claim window) and widowhood, orphanhood, or family survivor pensions [8][9].
  • Certificates of Last Will and Life Insurance (Modelo 790): Once at least 15 working days (días hábiles) have elapsed after the date of death, apply to the Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes (Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Courts) using Form 790 (Modelo 790, code 006) and the literal death certificate for both the Certificate of Acts of Last Will (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Death-Coverage Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento) [10].
  • Inheritance Tax and Municipal Capital Gains Tax: Settle Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) with the tax agency of the relevant autonomous community (or the state tax agency AEAT where non-resident state rules apply) and the municipal urban land value tax (plusvalía municipal / IIVTNU) within the statutory 6-month deadline from death, bearing in mind that a 6-month extension can be requested within the first 5 months of that period [4][10].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en España: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml: Cuando a su familiar en España se le diagnostica una enfermedad avanzada, limitante para la vida o en fase terminal, realizar las gestiones médicas, jurídicas y administrativas mientras la persona enferma conserva plenamente su capacidad de obrar garantiza el respeto a sus deseos asistenciales y evita bloqueos judiciales o patrimoniales posteriores. A continuación se detallan los 5 pasos oficiales que conviene seguir en orden en España.

steps.title: Coordinar los cuidados paliativos especializados, la atención domiciliaria y las unidades hospitalarias
steps.html:
Solicite al equipo médico especialista o al médico de atención primaria del centro de salud la derivación a los recursos específicos de cuidados paliativos de su comunidad autónoma dentro del Sistema Nacional de Salud, coordinado a nivel estatal por el Ministerio de Sanidad [1]. Dependiendo de la comunidad autónoma, la atención se presta mediante Unidades de Cuidados Paliativos hospitalarias y Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria (ESAD, o PADES en Cataluña, PALCA en el País Vasco, y unidades equivalentes del SERMAS en Madrid o del SAS en Andalucía) para el control del dolor, el apoyo psicosocial y el seguimiento en el domicilio.

Para consultar el directorio actualizado de unidades hospitalarias, equipos domiciliarios y centros sociosanitarios en cada provincia, puede acudir a la Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos, que además orienta sobre la Planificación Anticipada de Cuidados (PAC) junto con el equipo clínico y de trabajo social [2].

steps.title: Formalizar e inscribir el Documento de Instrucciones Previas (Testamento Vital)
steps.html:
Mientras su familiar mantenga plena capacidad de decisión, puede otorgar por escrito su Documento de Instrucciones Previas (denominado también Voluntades Anticipadas o Testamento Vital según la comunidad autónoma), regulado a nivel estatal por el artículo 11 de la Ley 41/2002, de autonomía del paciente, y el Real Decreto 124/2007 [1][3]. En este documento la persona enferma expresa sus instrucciones sobre los cuidados y tratamientos médicos que desea recibir o rechazar (como la limitación del esfuerzo terapéutico, la ventilación mecánica, la reanimación cardiopulmonar o la sedación paliativa), designa a una persona representante como interlocutora ante el equipo médico y puede dejar constancia de sus decisiones sobre donación de órganos o destino del cuerpo [1][3].

Dependiendo de la legislación autonómica aplicable, el documento se formaliza por una de estas tres vías: ante notario (sin necesidad de testigos), ante el personal funcionario encargado del Registro Autonómico de Instrucciones Previas o en las unidades habilitadas del centro sanitario, o bien ante tres testigos mayores de edad con plena capacidad de obrar (de los cuales al menos dos no tengan relación de parentesco hasta el segundo grado ni vínculo patrimonial con el otorgante). Una vez inscrito en el registro autonómico correspondiente, se sincroniza telemáticamente con el Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas del Ministerio de Sanidad para que sea consultable desde la historia clínica electrónica en cualquier hospital de España [1][3].

steps.title: Otorgar escritura pública de Poder Preventivo ante notario
steps.html:
Dado que las autorizaciones bancarias ordinarias y los poderes comunes pueden quedar bloqueados si sobreviene una pérdida de capacidad, es fundamental que su familiar acuda a una notaría mientras conserva plena capacidad de discernimiento para otorgar un Poder Preventivo en escritura pública, siguiendo las pautas del Consejo General del Notariado y la reforma del Código Civil introducida por la Ley 8/2021 [4][5].

Existen dos modalidades principales que el notario adapta a cada caso:

  • Poder general con cláusula de subsistencia: Despliega efectos desde el momento de la firma y continúa vigente aunque la persona otorgante precise apoyo en el ejercicio de su capacidad más adelante [4][5].
  • Poder preventivo en sentido estricto: Solo entra en vigor en el momento futuro en que se acredite la pérdida de capacidad conforme a las pautas médicas o notariales fijadas en la propia escritura [4][5].

El poder preventivo puede abarcar tanto la administración patrimonial y bancaria (gestión de cuentas, cobro de pensiones, pago de gastos asistenciales o disposición de bienes) como facultades de esfera personal y de salud, y el notario lo comunica de oficio al Registro Civil para evitar tener que acudir a un procedimiento judicial de provisión de apoyos (curatela) [4][5].

steps.title: Solicitar la valoración urgente de dependencia, permisos laborales e incapacidad
steps.html:
Tramite de forma temprana las prestaciones sociales y laborales disponibles para la persona enferma y quienes la cuidan:

  • Valoración de Dependencia por vía de urgencia (Ley 39/2006): A través de los servicios sociales municipales o autonómicos integrados en el Sistema para la Autonomía y Atención a la Dependencia (SAAD), coordinado por el Instituto de Mayores y Servicios Sociales, presente la solicitud de reconocimiento de grado de dependencia (Grado I, II o III) adjuntando el informe médico que acredite la evolución avanzada de la enfermedad para solicitar su tramitación prioritaria o de urgencia social [6][7]. El Programa Individual de Atención (PIA) permite acceder a servicio de ayuda a domicilio, centro de día, teleasistencia o prestación económica para cuidados en el entorno familiar [6][7].
  • Prestaciones de la Seguridad Social y permisos laborales: Si la persona enferma se encuentra en activo, puede tramitar la baja por incapacidad temporal o solicitar la pensión de incapacidad permanente (absoluta o gran invalidez, que incluye complemento para remunerar a la persona que la atienda) ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social [8]. Por su parte, las personas trabajadoras que cuidan a su familiar tienen derecho, conforme al artículo 37.3.b y al artículo 37.6 y 46.3 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, a un permiso retribuido de 5 días por enfermedad grave u hospitalización de parientes hasta el segundo grado, así como a solicitar la adaptación o reducción de la jornada laboral (entre un octavo y la mitad de la jornada) o una excedencia por cuidado de un familiar hasta el segundo grado.

steps.title: Revisar el testamento, los seguros y la documentación para los trámites sucesorios
steps.html:
Mientras su familiar conserve plena capacidad para testar, conviene revisar u otorgar testamento abierto notarial ante un notario del Consejo General del Notariado, lo que simplifica la futura adjudicación hereditaria y evita el acta de declaración de herederos abintestato [4]. Reúna en una carpeta accesible el DNI o NIE en vigor, certificados literales de nacimiento y matrimonio (o inscripción de pareja de hecho), escrituras de propiedad, contratos bancarios, pólizas de seguro de vida o de decesos y las preferencias escritas sobre inhumación o incineración.

Dejar esta documentación organizada facilita los trámites obligatorios posteriores al fallecimiento:

  • Seguridad Social (Muerte y Supervivencia): Solicitar ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (a través de la Sede Electrónica o en un centro CAISS) el Auxilio por defunción (plazo de 5 años) y las pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o prestaciones en favor de familiares [8][9].
  • Certificados de Últimas Voluntades y de Seguros (Modelo 790): Transcurridos al menos 15 días hábiles desde la fecha de la defunción, solicitar ante el Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes mediante el Modelo 790 (código 006) y el certificado literal de defunción tanto el Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad como el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [10].
  • Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Plusvalía Municipal: Liquidar el Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones ante la agencia tributaria de la comunidad autónoma correspondiente (o ante la AEAT si aplica normativa estatal a no residentes) y la plusvalía municipal (IIVTNU) en el plazo legal de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento, teniendo presente que puede solicitarse una prórroga de otros 6 meses dentro de los primeros 5 meses del plazo.

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Italy: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: Facing an incurable or advanced illness requires timely coordination of healthcare services and legal instruments while your family member still retains full mental and legal capacity (capacità di intendere e di volere). Below are the five official steps to follow in order in Italy.

steps.title: Activate Home Palliative Care and Hospice Care
steps.html:
In Italy, Law No. 38/2010 (Legge n. 38/2010) guarantees citizens free access to palliative care and pain therapy within the National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale - SSN), as overseen by the Ministero della Salute (Ministry of Health) [1]. Care is delivered through Local Palliative Care Networks (Reti Locali di Cure Palliative) across two main settings:

  • Home palliative care (Cure palliative domiciliari - UCP-DOM): Delivered at the ill person's home by multi-professional Palliative Care Units (palliative care physicians, nurses, psychologists, physiotherapists, and healthcare assistants) in coordination with the General Practitioner (Medico di Medicina Generale - MMG), based on an Integrated Care Plan (Piano Assistenziale Integrato - PAI) that includes medication and medical equipment [1][2].
  • Hospice (inpatient residential facilities): Intended for patients requiring complex symptom management or temporary respite stays for the family when home care is no longer feasible [1][2].

To activate care, the family member or the ill person should contact the General Practitioner (or the hospital ward during protected discharge planning / dimissioni protette), who submits the referral (impegnativa) to the Single Point of Access (Punto Unico di Accesso - PUA) or the Palliative Care Unit of the Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) [1][2]. For guidance on regional networks and accredited facilities, you can consult the scientific society Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (Italian Society of Palliative Care - SICP) [2] and the Federazione Cure Palliative (Palliative Care Federation - FCP) [1].

steps.title: Draft and Deposit Advance Healthcare Directives (DAT / Living Will)
steps.html:
As long as the ill person is an adult and retains full decision-making capacity, they can execute Advance Healthcare Directives (Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento - DAT, also known as a living will or biotestamento under Law No. 219/2017) to express consent to or refusal of diagnostic tests, therapeutic choices, and specific medical treatments, including artificial nutrition and hydration [3][4]. In the DAT, the declarant (disponente) may appoint an adult healthcare proxy (fiduciario) who accepts the role (by co-signing the DAT or by subsequent written instrument) and represents the patient in dealings with physicians and healthcare facilities in the event of future incapacity [3][4].

The DAT must be executed in one of the statutory forms provided by law:

  • Private written instrument delivered in person (scrittura privata consegnata personalmente) by the declarant to the Civil Status Office (Ufficio dello Stato Civile) of their municipality of residence (Comune) [3][4].
  • Public deed or authenticated private instrument (atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata) executed before a notary [3][4].
  • Submission at healthcare facilities in Regions that have implemented electronic collection through the Electronic Health Record (Fascicolo Sanitario Elettronico) [3].

Upon deposit, the civil registrar or notary transmits a copy of the DAT (with the declarant's consent) to the National DAT Database (Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT) established at the Ministero della Salute, which can be accessed by the declarant, the fiduciario, and the attending physician using digital identity credentials (SPID, CIE, or CNS) [3].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney, Bank Mandates, and Consider Support Administration
steps.html:
In Italy, ordinary bank authorizations (deleghe bancarie) and informal mandates may be insufficient for extraordinary financial administration or may be challenged if cognitive incapacity arises. While the ill person retains full legal capacity (capacità di agire), it is important to formalize financial management through a notary via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Notaries) [4]:

  • General or special notarial power of attorney (Procura generale o speciale notarile): Grants a trusted person authority to carry out administrative, banking, tax, or real estate acts in the name and on behalf of the principal [4]. At the same time, verify specific account operating mandate forms directly with the relevant banks.
  • Support Administration (Amministrazione di Sostegno - Law No. 6/2004): Where the illness reduces, even partially or temporarily, a person's ability to manage daily affairs, the beneficiary, spouse, domestic partner (convivente), or relatives within the fourth degree may file a petition (ricorso) with the Guardianship Judge (Giudice Tutelare) at the Court (Tribunale) of the place of residence or domicile, following the official guidance of the Ministero della Giustizia (Ministry of Justice) [5]. While still capable, the ill person may also designate their future support administrator (amministratore di sostegno) in advance by public deed or authenticated private instrument before a notary [4][5]. Filing a petition for Amministrazione di Sostegno does not necessarily require a lawyer and is exempt from unified court fees (contributo unificato) and stamp duty [5].

steps.title: Apply for Caregiver Leave, Paid Time Off, and Disability Benefits
steps.html:
To support family caregivers and activate financial benefits for non-self-sufficiency, initiate the medical assessment for civil disability (invalidità civile) and severe disability status (handicap grave under Law No. 104/1992) through the national social security agency, the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Institute for Social Security - INPS, reachable at 803 164 from landlines), or through an accredited Ente di Patronato [6][7]:

  • Fast-track assessment for oncological or severe illnesses: The General Practitioner or hospital specialist submits the introductory medical certificate (certificato medico introduttivo) electronically; for patients with oncological pathologies, the assessment of civil disability and Legge 104 status is carried out under an accelerated statutory procedure within 15 days of the application [6].
  • Paid monthly caregiver leave under Law 104/1992 (Permessi retribuiti Legge 104/1992, Art. 33): Once severe disability status (disabilità in situazione di gravità, Art. 3, para. 3) is recognized, employed family members are entitled to 3 days of paid leave per month (which may also be split into hours) covered by notional pension contributions; multiple family caregivers may alternate taking leave to assist the same person [6][7].
  • Paid extraordinary caregiver leave (Congedo straordinario retribuito, Art. 42, para. 5, Legislative Decree 151/2001): Co-residing family members (in statutory order of priority: spouse, civil union partner, or cohabiting partner, parents, children, brothers, or sisters) may apply for up to a combined maximum of 2 years of paid extraordinary leave over their working life, which can be taken in days or months [8].
  • Attendance allowance (Indennità di accompagnamento): If the medical commission certifies an inability to walk without permanent assistance or an inability to perform everyday activities independently, a monthly tax-free cash benefit is payable regardless of personal income [6].

steps.title: Review the Will, Pension Beneficiaries, and Estate Succession Requirements
steps.html:
Organizing estate and pension documentation in advance substantially reduces future administrative burdens for the family:

  • Wills and forced heirship protection (quote di legittima): Under the official guides of the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, the ill person may dispose of their estate by holographic will (testamento olografo, handwritten, dated, and signed entirely by the testator) or by public notarial will (testamento pubblico) executed before a notary in the presence of two witnesses, while respecting the statutory reserved shares (quote di legittima) protected by law for the spouse, children, or ascendants [9][10]. Public wills and holographic wills formally deposited with a notary are registered in the General Registry of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) [10].
  • Pension records and insurance policies: Gather contribution statements to streamline the future online application for a survivor pension (pensione ai superstiti: pensione di reversibilità if the deceased was already a pensioner, or pensione indiretta for an insured worker) through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale [6], and review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies and supplementary pension funds.
  • Declaration of succession and releasing bank accounts: After death, heirs or estate beneficiaries (chiamati all'eredità) must file the electronic declaration of succession (dichiarazione di successione) within 12 months of the opening of the succession with the national tax authority, Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency, toll-free number 800 90 96 96), a procedure that includes automatic cadastral title updates (voltura catastale) for real estate and issues the official receipt required by banks to release frozen accounts and financial assets [11][12].
