it.title: Malattia terminale e adempimenti legali in Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la pianificazione medica e amministrativa in caso di malattia terminale in Italia: cure palliative e hospice, Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT), procure e amministrazione di sostegno, congedi e testamento.
it.introHtml: Affrontare una malattia inguaribile o in fase avanzata richiede di coordinare tempestivamente l'assistenza sanitaria e gli atti giuridici finché il vostro familiare conserva la piena capacità di intendere e di volere. Di seguito trovate i cinque passaggi ufficiali da seguire in ordine in Italia.

steps.title: Attivare le cure palliative domiciliari e l'assistenza in hospice
steps.html:
In Italia, la Legge n. 38/2010 garantisce al cittadino il diritto all'accesso gratuito alle cure palliative e alla terapia del dolore nell'ambito del Servizio Sanitario Nazionale, come monitorato dal Ministero della Salute [1]. Il percorso si articola nelle Reti Locali di Cure Palliative attraverso due livelli principali:

  • Cure palliative domiciliari (UCP-DOM): erogate al domicilio della persona malata da Unità di Cure Palliative multiprofessionali (medici palliativisti, infermieri, psicologi, fisioterapisti e operatori sociosanitari) in raccordo con il Medico di Medicina Generale (MMG), sulla base di un Piano Assistenziale Integrato (PAI) con fornitura di farmaci e presidi sanitari [1][2].
  • Hospice (strutture residenziali): destinati ai pazienti che necessitano di controllo complesso dei sintomi o di ricoveri temporanei di sollievo per la famiglia quando la gestione a domicilio non è praticabile [1][2].

Per attivare la presa in carico, il familiare o la persona malata deve rivolgersi al Medico di Medicina Generale (o al reparto ospedaliero in sede di dimissioni protette), che invia l'impegnativa e la segnalazione al Punto Unico di Accesso (PUA) o all'Unità di Cure Palliative della propria Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) [1][2]. Per orientarsi sulle reti territoriali e sulle strutture accreditate, è possibile consultare la società scientifica Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [2] e la Federazione Cure Palliative [1].

steps.title: Redigere e depositare le Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT)
steps.html:
Finché la persona malata è maggiorenne e pienamente capace di autodeterminarsi, può redigere le Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT) (cosiddetto biotestamento, disciplinato dalla Legge n. 219/2017) per esprimere il consenso o il rifiuto su accertamenti diagnostici, scelte terapeutiche e singoli trattamenti sanitari, comprese la nutrizione e l'idratazione artificiali [3][4]. Nelle DAT il disponente può nominare un fiduciario maggiorenne che accetti l'incarico (tramite sottoscrizione delle DAT o atto successivo) e lo rappresenti nelle relazioni con il medico e le strutture sanitarie in caso di futura incapacità [3][4].

Le DAT devono essere redatte in una delle seguenti forme previste dalla legge:

  • Scrittura privata consegnata personalmente dal disponente presso l'Ufficio dello Stato Civile del proprio Comune di residenza [3][4].
  • Atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata redatti da un notaio [3][4].
  • Consegna presso le strutture sanitarie nelle Regioni che hanno regolamentato la raccolta tramite il Fascicolo Sanitario Elettronico [3].

Al momento del deposito, l'ufficiale di stato civile o il notaio trasmette copia delle DAT (previo consenso dell'interessato) alla Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT istituita presso il Ministero della Salute, consultabile dal disponente, dal fiduciario e dal medico curante mediante identità digitale (SPID, CIE o CNS) [3].

steps.title: Sottoscrivere procure notarili, deleghe bancarie e valutare l'Amministrazione di Sostegno
steps.html:
In Italia le deleghe bancarie ordinarie e i mandati informali possono risultare insufficienti per gli atti di straordinaria amministrazione o venire contestati al sopravvenire di un'incapacità cognitiva. Finché la persona malata mantiene piena capacità di agire, è importante formalizzare la gestione patrimoniale rivolgendosi a un notaio tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [4]:

  • Procura generale o speciale notarile: conferisce a una persona di fiducia il potere di compiere atti amministrativi, bancari, fiscali o immobiliari in nome e per conto del rappresentato [4]. È opportuno verificare contemporaneamente con gli istituti di credito i moduli specifici di delega a operare sui conti correnti.
  • Amministrazione di Sostegno (Legge n. 6/2004): qualora la malattia riduca, anche parzialmente o temporaneamente, l'autonomia nell'espletamento delle funzioni della vita quotidiana, il beneficiario stesso, il coniuge, il convivente o i parenti entro il quarto grado possono depositare un ricorso al Giudice Tutelare presso il Tribunale del luogo di residenza o domicilio, secondo le indicazioni fornite dal Ministero della Giustizia [5]. La persona malata può anche designare preventivamente il proprio futuro amministratore di sostegno mediante atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata [4][5]. Il ricorso per l'Amministrazione di Sostegno non richiede necessariamente il patrocinio di un avvocato ed è esente dal contributo unificato e dall'imposta di bollo [5].

steps.title: Richiedere permessi lavorativi, congedi per i caregiver e prestazioni di invalidità
steps.html:
Per sostenere chi assiste la persona malata e attivare i benefici economici connessi alla non autosufficienza, occorre avviare l'accertamento sanitario dell'invalidità civile e dell'handicap grave (Legge n. 104/1992) tramite l'ente previdenziale Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (contattabile al numero 803 164 da rete fissa) o un Ente di Patronato [6][7]:

  • Procedura accelerata per patologie oncologiche o gravi: il Medico di Medicina Generale o lo specialista ospedaliero trasmette telematicamente il certificato medico introduttivo; per i pazienti con patologie oncologiche l'accertamento dell'invalidità civile e dell'handicap viene effettuato con iter accelerato (entro 15 giorni dalla domanda) [6].
  • Permessi retribuiti Legge 104/1992 (Art. 33): una volta riconosciuto lo stato di disabilità in situazione di gravità (art. 3, comma 3), i familiari lavoratori dipendenti hanno diritto a 3 giorni di permesso mensile retribuito (frazionabili anche in ore) coperti da contribuzione figurativa; più familiari possono alternarsi nella fruizione per assistere la stessa persona [6][7].
  • Congedo straordinario retribuito (Art. 42, co. 5, D.Lgs. 151/2001): i familiari conviventi (secondo l'ordine di priorità legale: coniuge o parte di unione civile o convivente di fatto, genitori, figli, fratelli o sorelle) possono richiedere fino a un massimo complessivo di 2 anni di congedo retribuito nell'arco della vita lavorativa, frazionabile in giorni o mesi [8].
  • Indennità di accompagnamento: se viene accertata l'impossibilità di deambulare senza l'aiuto permanente di un accompagnatore o l'incapacità di compiere gli atti quotidiani della vita, spetta una prestazione economica mensile erogata a prescindere dal reddito.

steps.title: Verificare testamento, beneficiari previdenziali e adempimenti successori
steps.html:
Organizzare in anticipo la documentazione patrimoniale e previdenziale riduce notevolmente gli oneri burocratici futuri per la famiglia:

  • Testamento e tutela dei legittimari: secondo le guide ufficiali del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, la persona malata può disporre dei propri beni tramite testamento olografo (scritto interamente a mano, datato e sottoscritto dal testatore) o testamento pubblico ricevuto dal notaio in presenza di due testimoni, nel rispetto delle quote di legittima riservate per legge a coniuge, figli o ascendenti [9][10]. I testamenti pubblici e quelli olografi depositati formalmente presso un notaio sono iscritti nel Registro Generale dei Testamenti [10].
  • Posizione previdenziale e polizze: è utile raccogliere gli estratti contributivi per agevolare la futura domanda telematica di pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità se il dante causa è già pensionato, o pensione indiretta) presso l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale [6], nonché verificare le designazioni dei beneficiari sulle polizze vita e sui fondi pensione.
  • Dichiarazione di successione e sblocco dei conti: dopo il decesso, gli eredi o i chiamati all'eredità devono presentare la dichiarazione di successione telematica entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione all'amministrazione fiscale Agenzia delle Entrate (numero verde 800 90 96 96), procedura che integra la voltura catastale automatica degli immobili e rilascia l'attestazione necessaria alle banche per lo sblocco dei rapporti finanziari [11][12].

it.closingQuestion: Per fornirvi indicazioni ancora più mirate: 1. In quale Regione e Comune si trova la persona malata, ed è già seguita da un reparto ospedaliero o dal Medico di Medicina Generale? 2. È già stata presentata la domanda di invalidità civile e Legge 104/1992 o occorre ancora inviare il certificato medico introduttivo?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Netherlands: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in the Netherlands is diagnosed with an incurable, life-limiting illness, arranging medical preferences, powers of attorney, and care provisions in advance brings clarity and peace of mind. Below are the five main official and practical steps to complete in order while your family member still has full decision-making capacity (wilsbekwaam).

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Home Care, District Nursing, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
In the Netherlands, the general practitioner (huisarts) - or the treating hospital medical specialist in coordination with the hospital transfer nurse (transferverpleegkundige) - plays the central role in initiating palliative and terminal care [1][2]. You can use the national platform Overpalliatievezorg.nl (supported by the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport) and the knowledge platform Palliaweb to find an overview of care options and regional facilities [1][2]:

  • Palliative care at home and district nursing (wijkverpleging): if the ill relative remains at home or moves into a volunteer-run hospice (bijna-thuis-huis) and does not yet hold a Long-Term Care Act (Wet langdurige zorg - Wlz) assessment, nursing and personal care are generally funded under the Healthcare Insurance Act (Zorgverzekeringswet - Zvw) based on a care assessment carried out by the district nurse (wijkverpleegkundige) of the home care provider [2]. Trained palliative care volunteers (Vrijwilligers Palliatieve Terminale Zorg - VPTZ) can also provide support at home [1].
  • Hospice care: when care at home is no longer feasible (often when life expectancy is assessed at three months or less), admission can be arranged to a bijna-thuis-huis or a high-care hospice with 24-hour specialist nursing care [2].
  • Long-Term Care Act (Wet langdurige zorg - Wlz) and the CIZ: if your family member already holds a Wlz care assessment from the Centrum Indicatiestelling Zorg (Care Assessment Centre - CIZ) [3], no new assessment is required for palliative terminal care; the physician or care provider can apply directly to the regional care office (zorgkantoor) for additional funding for intensive palliative care [2][3]. A new application to the Centrum Indicatiestelling Zorg is only needed when there is a permanent, long-term need for 24-hour care outside regular Zvw district nursing [2][3].

steps.title: Record a Written Advance Directive and Treatment Limits with the General Practitioner
steps.html:
While the ill relative has full decision-making capacity, they can draw up a written advance directive (schriftelijke wilsverklaring) specifying which medical treatments they do or do not wish to receive if they later become unable to make decisions themselves [1][4]. Under the guidelines of the Rijksoverheid (Government of the Netherlands), an advance directive can be written in the patient's own words, provided the document is clear and bears their full name, date, and signature [4][5]:

  • Refusal of treatment (behandelverbod) and do-not-resuscitate order (niet-reanimeerverklaring): this sets out specific medical interventions that the patient refuses (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, intensive care admission, or hospitalisation). Physicians are legally required in principle to honour a clear refusal of treatment [4].
  • Written healthcare proxy (schriftelijk vertegenwoordiger / medical power of attorney): the patient can authorise a trusted relative or close contact in writing to speak with doctors and make medical decisions on their behalf once incapacity occurs [4].
  • Registration in the medical file: discuss the advance directive during an advance care planning consultation (behandelwensengesprek) with the general practitioner (huisarts) and any treating specialists so that it is recorded in the medical file (including for the out-of-hours GP service and ambulance service) [1][5].

steps.title: Execute a Notarial Living Will, Powers of Attorney, and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
Standard bank mandates (bankmachtigingen) are often limited to everyday payments and may be rejected by financial institutions or public authorities for complex legal acts (such as selling a home or handling tax affairs) once a person loses mental capacity. To avoid having to petition the subdistrict court (kantonrechter) later for protective administration (beschermingsbewind) or mentorship (mentorschap), your family member can have a notarial living will and enduring power of attorney (notarieel levenstestament) drawn up while still fully capable by a civil-law notary affiliated with the Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie (Royal Dutch Association of Civil-Law Notaries - KNB) [6][7]:

  • Financial and medical powers of attorney: in the levenstestament, the grantor appoints one or more trusted representatives (gevolmachtigden or levensexecuteurs) to manage bank accounts, assets, and real estate as well as personal and medical affairs [6][7].
  • Capacity verification and registration in the CLTR: the civil-law notary verifies legal capacity when executing the deed and registers the levenstestament in the Central Register of Living Wills (Centraal Levenstestamentenregister - CLTR), enabling banks, doctors, and care institutions to verify the representative's authority [7].
  • Note when powers of attorney expire: both a levenstestament and an ordinary bank mandate terminate automatically by law at the moment of death; after death, statutory inheritance law or the deceased's regular will governs the estate [6].

steps.title: Access Statutory Caregiver Leave and Informal Care Support
steps.html:
Family members and close relatives providing care can use statutory leave schemes under the Work and Care Act (Wet arbeid en zorg - Wazo) alongside municipal support services [8][9]:

  • Short-term care leave (kortdurend zorgverlof): employees are entitled to a maximum of twice their weekly working hours per 12-month period to provide necessary temporary care for an ill relative, during which the employer continues to pay at least 70% of wages (and at least the statutory minimum wage) [8].
  • Long-term care leave (langdurend zorgverlof): to care for a relative with a life-threatening illness or a prolonged need for care, an employee is entitled to up to six times their weekly working hours per 12-month period [8][9]. By law this leave is unpaid unless an applicable collective labour agreement (cao) or employment contract provides for continued pay [8][9].
  • Municipal support (Wmo) and caregiver guidance: medical aids, home adaptations, or respite care (respijtzorg) can be requested through the municipal Social Support Act desk (Wmo-loket) [9]. In addition, the national association MantelzorgNL provides guidance and support on combining paid work with informal caregiving during the palliative phase [9][10].

steps.title: Prepare the Will, Pensions, Certificate of Inheritance, and Tax Returns
steps.html:
Organising financial and legal documents in advance ensures that surviving relatives know exactly which steps are required before and after death:

  • Will (testament) and executor (executeur): check whether a will has been drawn up and registered in the Central Register of Wills (Centraal Testamentenregister - CTR) via the Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie [6], and whether an executor (executeur) has been appointed to administer the estate after death [6]. Also document funeral wishes and details of any funeral insurance policy (uitvaartverzekering).
  • State pension (AOW), survivor benefit (Anw), and pension funds: once a death is registered with the municipal civil registry (burgerlijke stand), the municipality automatically notifies the Sociale Verzekeringsbank (Social Insurance Bank - SVB) of deaths occurring in the Netherlands [11]. The AOW state pension stops the day after death, a surviving partner automatically receives a lump-sum death benefit (overlijdensuitkering), and a surviving partner who has not yet reached AOW pension age (and who, for example, cares for a child under 18 or is at least 45% incapacitated for work) can apply to the Sociale Verzekeringsbank for a survivor benefit (Anw-nabestaandenuitkering) [11][12]. If the death occurs outside the Netherlands, it must be reported directly to the Sociale Verzekeringsbank within 4 weeks [11].
  • Certificate of inheritance (verklaring van erfrecht) and estate election: accessing frozen bank accounts after death frequently requires a notarial certificate of inheritance (verklaring van erfrecht) [6]. Heirs have three legal choices: unconditional acceptance (zuiver aanvaarden), acceptance under benefit of inventory (beneficiair aanvaarden, which protects heirs from personal liability for estate debts beyond the estate's assets), or renunciation (verwerpen) [13][14]. For acceptance under benefit of inventory or renunciation, a formal declaration must be filed with the district court (rechtbank) of the deceased's last place of residence via de Rechtspraak (the Dutch Judiciary), and heirs must refrain from selling or withdrawing estate assets beforehand to avoid tacit unconditional acceptance [13][14].
  • Final income tax return (F-biljet) and inheritance tax (erfbelasting): the Belastingdienst (Tax and Customs Administration; Bereaved Relatives Tax Helpline BelastingTelefoon voor Nabestaanden: 0800 - 235 83 54, free of charge within the Netherlands) sends instructions regarding the final income tax return for the year of death (F-form / F-biljet or online via survivor authorisation) and the inheritance tax return (aangifte erfbelasting); for deaths on or after 1 January 2026, the filing deadline for inheritance tax is 20 months after the date of death [15][16].

Have a notarial living will (levenstestament) and a regular will (testament) already been drawn up?

nl.title: Ongeneeslijke ziekte en praktische regelingen in Nederland: officiële checklist in 5 stappen
nl.cardSummary: Officiële checklist in 5 stappen bij een ongeneeslijke ziekte in Nederland: palliatieve zorg en hospice, schriftelijke wilsverklaringen, levenstestament en volmachten, zorgverlof en nalatenschap.
nl.introHtml: Wanneer een familielid in Nederland te horen krijgt dat een ziekte niet meer te genezen is, geeft het tijdig regelen van medische wensen, volmachten en zorgvoorzieningen rust en overzicht. Hieronder vindt u de vijf belangrijkste officiële en praktische stappen op volgorde zolang uw familielid nog volledig wilsbekwaam is.

steps.title: Palliatieve zorg thuis, wijkverpleging en hospicezorg coördineren
steps.html:
In Nederland staat de huisarts (of de behandelend medisch specialist in overleg met de transferverpleegkundige van het ziekenhuis) centraal bij het opstarten van palliatieve en terminale zorg [1][2]. U kunt via het landelijke platform Overpalliatievezorg.nl (ondersteund door het Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport) en kennisplatform Palliaweb een overzicht vinden van zorgmogelijkheden en voorzieningen in de regio [1][2]:

  • Palliatieve zorg thuis en wijkverpleging: als de zieke naaste thuis verblijft of naar een bijna-thuis-huis gaat en nog geen indicatie voor de Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz) heeft, loopt de bekostiging van verpleging en verzorging doorgaans via de Zorgverzekeringswet (Zvw) op basis van een indicatie door de wijkverpleegkundige van de thuiszorgorganisatie [2]. Daarnaast kunnen getrainde vrijwilligers (VPTZ) ondersteuning bieden in de thuissituatie [1].
  • Hospicezorg: wanneer zorg thuis niet langer passend is (vaak bij een vastgestelde levensverwachting van drie maanden of korter), kan opname in een bijna-thuis-huis of een high-care hospice met 24-uurs verpleegkundige zorg worden geregeld [2].
  • Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz) en het CIZ: heeft uw familielid al een Wlz-indicatie van het Centrum Indicatiestelling Zorg [3], dan is voor palliatief terminale zorg geen herindicatie nodig; de arts of zorgaanbieder kan rechtstreeks bij het regionale zorgkantoor extra budget voor intensieve palliatieve zorg aanvragen [2][3]. Een nieuwe aanvraag bij het Centrum Indicatiestelling Zorg is alleen aan de orde wanneer er sprake is van blijvende, langdurige 24-uurszorgbehoefte buiten de reguliere Zvw-wijkverpleging [2][3].

steps.title: Schriftelijke wilsverklaring en behandelgrenzen vastleggen bij de huisarts
steps.html:
Zolang de zieke naaste wilsbekwaam is, kan in een schriftelijke wilsverklaring worden vastgelegd welke medische behandelingen wel of niet gewenst zijn voor het geval uw familielid later niet meer zelf kan beslissen [1][4]. Volgens de richtlijnen van de Rijksoverheid kan een wilsverklaring in eigen woorden worden opgesteld, mits het document duidelijk is en voorzien is van de volledige naam, dagtekening en handtekening [4][5]:

  • Behandelverbod en niet-reanimeerverklaring: hierin legt de patiënt vast welke ingrepen worden geweigerd (zoals reanimatie, kunstmatige beademing, opname op de intensive care of ziekenhuisopname). Artsen zijn in beginsel wettelijk verplicht een duidelijk behandelverbod te volgen [4].
  • Schriftelijk vertegenwoordiger (medische volmacht): de patiënt kan een naaste schriftelijk machtigen om met artsen te spreken en medische beslissingen te nemen zodra wilsonbekwaamheid intreedt [4].
  • Vastlegging in het medisch dossier: bespreek de wilsverklaring tijdens een behandelwensengesprek met de huisarts en eventuele behandelend specialisten, zodat de verklaring in het medisch dossier (en voor de huisartsenpost en ambulancedienst) wordt geregistreerd [1][5].

steps.title: Notarieel levenstestament, volmachten en bankmachtigingen regelen
steps.html:
Gewone bankmachtigingen zijn vaak beperkt tot dagelijkse betalingen en kunnen door financiële instellingen of instanties worden geweigerd bij complexe rechtshandelingen (zoals de verkoop van een woning of belastingzaken) zodra iemand wilsonbekwaam wordt. Om te voorkomen dat later via de kantonrechter beschermingsbewind of mentorschap moet worden aangevraagd, kan uw familielid bij volledige wilsbekwaamheid een notarieel levenstestament laten opstellen via een notaris aangesloten bij de Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie [6][7]:

  • Financiële en medische volmacht: in het levenstestament wijst de volmachtgever een of meer vertrouwenspersonen (gevolmachtigden of levensexecuteurs) aan voor zowel het beheer van bankrekeningen, vermogen en onroerend goed als voor persoonlijke en medische belangen [6][7].
  • Controle en registratie in het CLTR: de notaris toetst de wilsbekwaamheid bij het passeren van de akte en schrijft het levenstestament in bij het Centraal Levenstestamentenregister (CLTR), zodat banken, artsen en zorginstellingen de bevoegdheid kunnen verifiëren [7].
  • Let op het einde van de volmacht: een levenstestament en een gewone bankvolmacht eindigen van rechtswege op het moment van overlijden; daarna geldt het reguliere erfrecht of het testament [6].

steps.title: Wettelijk zorgverlof en ondersteuning voor mantelzorgers aanvragen
steps.html:
Familieleden en naasten die de zorg op zich nemen, kunnen gebruikmaken van wettelijke verlofregelingen onder de Wet arbeid en zorg (Wazo) en lokale voorzieningen [8][9]:

  • Kortdurend zorgverlof: werknemers hebben per 12 maanden recht op maximaal tweemaal de wekelijkse arbeidsduur voor noodzakelijke tijdelijke verzorging van een zieke naaste, waarbij de werkgever ten minste 70% van het loon (minimaal het wettelijk minimumloon) doorbetaalt [8].
  • Langdurend zorgverlof: voor de verzorging van een naaste met een levensbedreigende ziekte of langdurige hulpbehoefte heeft een werknemer per 12 maanden recht op maximaal zesmaal de wekelijkse arbeidsduur [8][9]. Dit verlof is wettelijk onbetaald, tenzij de toepasselijke cao of arbeidsovereenkomst loondoorbetaling voorschrijft [8][9].
  • Gemeentelijke ondersteuning (Wmo) en mantelzorgadvies: via het Wmo-loket van de gemeente kunnen hulpmiddelen, woningaanpassingen of respijtzorg worden aangevraagd [9]. Daarnaast biedt de landelijke vereniging MantelzorgNL informatie en advies over het combineren van werk en mantelzorg in de palliatieve fase [9][10].

steps.title: Testament, pensioenen, verklaring van erfrecht en fiscale aangiften voorbereiden
steps.html:
Door alvast financiële en juridische documenten te ordenen, weten de nabestaanden precies welke stappen vóór en na het overlijden nodig zijn:

  • Testament en executeur: controleer of er een testament is opgesteld en ingeschreven in het Centraal Testamentenregister (CTR) via de Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie [6], en of daarin een executeur is benoemd die na het overlijden de nalatenschap mag beheren [6]. Leg daarnaast uitvaartwensen en gegevens van een eventuele uitvaartverzekering vast.
  • AOW, Anw en pensioenfondsen: na de aangifte van overlijden bij de burgerlijke stand van de gemeente geeft de gemeente het overlijden in Nederland automatisch door aan de Sociale Verzekeringsbank [11]. De AOW-uitkering stopt op de dag na het overlijden, een achterblijvende partner ontvangt automatisch een overlijdensuitkering, en een partner die nog geen AOW-leeftijd heeft (en bijvoorbeeld zorgt voor een kind onder 18 jaar of ten minste 45% arbeidsongeschikt is) kan bij de Sociale Verzekeringsbank een Anw-nabestaandenuitkering aanvragen [11][12]. Vindt het overlijden buiten Nederland plaats, dan moet dit binnen 4 weken rechtstreeks worden gemeld bij de Sociale Verzekeringsbank [11].
  • Verklaring van erfrecht en keuze over de erfenis: om na het overlijden toegang te krijgen tot geblokkeerde bankrekeningen is vaak een notariële verklaring van erfrecht nodig [6]. Erfgenamen hebben drie keuzes: zuiver aanvaarden, beneficiair aanvaarden (aanvaarden onder voorrecht van boedelbeschrijving, zodat erfgenamen niet met privévermogen aansprakelijk zijn voor schulden) of verwerpen [13][14]. Voor beneficiaire aanvaarding of verwerping moet een verklaring worden afgelegd bij de rechtbank van de laatste woonplaats van de overledene via de Rechtspraak, en erfgenamen moeten vooraf geen goederen verkopen of onttrekken om stilzwijgende zuivere aanvaarding te voorkomen [13][14].
  • Inkomstenbelasting (F-biljet) en erfbelasting: de Belastingdienst (BelastingTelefoon voor Nabestaanden: 0800 - 235 83 54, gratis) stuurt informatie over de slot-inkomstenbelastingaangifte over het overlijdensjaar (F-biljet of online via nabestaandenmachtiging) en de aangifte erfbelasting; voor overlijdens vanaf 1 januari 2026 geldt een aangiftetermijn voor de erfbelasting van 20 maanden na het overlijden [15][16].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Belgium: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Belgium: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Belgium: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a relative in Belgium is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness, arranging palliative care, advance directives, and powers of attorney early makes it possible to honour their wishes while their decision-making capacity remains intact. Below are the five main official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support Teams, and the Palliative Lump-Sum Allowance
steps.html:
In Belgium, setting up palliative support at home or in a specialist unit is coordinated with the general practitioner (médecin généraliste / huisarts) - or the hospital specialist in liaison with the hospital social service - and the patient's health insurance fund (mutualité / ziekenfonds), within the framework of the Institut national d'assurance maladie-invalidité (National Institute for Health and Disability Insurance - INAMI / RIZIV) [1][2]:

  • Palliative status and home palliative allowance (forfait palliatif / palliatief forfait): when the ill person is cared for at home and meets the medical criteria for palliative status, the attending physician completes the official notification form for the advising physician (médecin-conseil / adviserend arts) of the health insurance fund [1][2]. This status grants entitlement to the palliative lump-sum allowance (awarded for a 30-day period and renewable once, to cover medication, care supplies, and medical equipment) as well as the abolition of patient co-payments (ticket modérateur / remgeld) for GP home visits, home nursing care, and certain physiotherapy sessions [1][2].
  • Home support teams and inpatient palliative units: multidisciplinary second-line support teams assist the GP and home nurses at the patient's home, while residential palliative care units (unités de soins palliatifs) admit patients when care at home is no longer possible [2][3]. Depending on the region, you can locate the appropriate network or mobile team through the Fédération Wallonne des Soins Palliatifs in Wallonia [2][3], the Fédération bruxelloise pluraliste de soins palliatifs et continus in Brussels [4], or Palliatieve Zorg Vlaanderen in Flanders [5].

steps.title: Draft and Register Written Advance Directives and the Care Plan
steps.html:
As long as the ill relative is an adult and capable of expressing their wishes, they can formalise their medical preferences in writing as part of Advance Care Planning (which is reimbursed during a consultation with the general practitioner) [1][6]:

  • Negative advance directive on healthcare (déclaration anticipée négative de soins / negatieve wilsverklaring under the Patients' Rights Act): the patient can record in writing specific medical examinations or treatments that they refuse (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition) in case they become unable to express their wishes, and appoint a healthcare proxy (mandataire) or trusted support person (personne de confiance) to uphold their rights with healthcare providers [6]. This directive is legally binding on practitioners and should be given to the GP for inclusion in the medical file.
  • Advance directive on euthanasia (déclaration anticipée relative à l'euthanasie): drafted according to the statutory template in the presence of two adult witnesses (at least one of whom has no material interest in the patient's death), this applies solely if a patient suffering from a serious and incurable condition falls into a state of irreversible unconsciousness (such as an irreversible coma) [6][7]. Following the April 2020 reform, advance directives drawn up or renewed after that date have unlimited validity and can be registered free of charge with the municipal administration (administration communale / gemeentebestuur) in the national database of the SPF Santé publique (Federal Public Service Health, Food Chain Safety and Environment) [6][7].

steps.title: Execute an Extrajudicial Protection Mandate and Review Bank Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
An ordinary bank power of attorney may prove insufficient for major asset management transactions or may be challenged if mental incapacity occurs. While your relative retains full legal capacity, they can draw up an extrajudicial protection mandate (mandat de protection extrajudiciaire / zorgvolmacht) with the assistance of a notary via the Fédération Royale du Notariat Belge (Royal Federation of Belgian Notaries - Fednot) [8][9]:

  • Financial and personal scope: the grantor (mandant) appoints one or more trusted representatives (mandataires) to manage bank accounts, income, and movable or immovable property and, if desired, to make personal welfare decisions (such as choosing a care residence or exercising patient rights) without having to apply immediately for judicial administration before the justice of the peace (juge de paix / vrederechter) [8][9].
  • Mandatory registration: to remain effective after the grantor loses decision-making capacity, the mandate must be registered in the Central Register of Mandate Contracts (Registre central des contrats de mandats) via a notary or the registry of the justice of the peace [8][9].

steps.title: Access Statutory Palliative Care Leave and Informal Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Employed relatives or civil servants caring for the ill person can apply for a full suspension or a reduction of working hours with a replacement allowance from the Office national de l'Emploi (National Employment Office - ONEM / RVA) [10][11]:

  • Palliative care leave (congé pour soins palliatifs, Info Sheet T20): any employee may take a complete career break or reduce their working hours (by half or by one-fifth) for 1 month, which can be extended twice by 1 month (up to 3 months in total per patient) [10][11]. The employee provides their employer with a certificate issued by the patient's attending physician and submits an allowance application to the Office national de l'Emploi [10][11].
  • Informal caregiver leave (congé pour aidants proches, Info Sheet T164): after obtaining official recognition as an informal caregiver (reconnaissance de la qualité d'aidant proche with social rights) from their health insurance fund (mutualité), an employee can apply for thematic caregiver leave compensated by the Office national de l'Emploi [10][12].

steps.title: Organise the Will, Pensions, Unblocking of Bank Accounts, and Inheritance Tax Declaration
steps.html:
Gathering essential documents ahead of time simplifies the legal and administrative steps that follow a death:

  • Will and funeral preferences: a will (holographic or notarial) can be registered in the Central Register of Wills (Registre central des testaments) through a notary of the Fédération Royale du Notariat Belge [8][13], and the ill relative can also register their last wishes regarding burial or cremation (dernières volontés) with their municipality.
  • Survivor's pension (pension de survie) and health insurance fund: for employees and civil servants, the Service fédéral des Pensions (Federal Pensions Service - SFP, reachable via the Pension Line at 1765 or on MyPension.be) automatically examines entitlement to a survivor's pension (or transitional allowance, allocation de transition) if the deceased was already receiving a pension; if the deceased was still working, an application should preferably be submitted within 12 months of death [14]. Beneficiary clauses on life insurance and group insurance policies should also be reviewed.
  • Freezing and unblocking of bank accounts: as soon as a bank is notified of a death, the deceased's accounts and safe-deposit boxes are frozen [15]. Unblocking them requires either a free certificate of inheritance (certificat d'hérédité) issued by a Legal Certainty office (bureau Sécurité juridique) of the SPF Finances (available only for straightforward estates with no will, no marriage contract, and no legally incapacitated heir) or a notarial deed of inheritance (acte d'hérédité) drawn up by a notary [8][15]. Before full unblocking, the bank can release funds to pay funeral expenses as well as a capped statutory advance for the surviving spouse or legal cohabitant [15].
  • Inheritance tax declaration (déclaration de succession / aangifte van nalatenschap): when a death occurs in Belgium, heirs have a statutory deadline of 4 months from the date of death to file the inheritance tax declaration with the SPF Finances (for Wallonia and the Brussels-Capital Region) or the Flemish Tax Administration VLABEL (for Flanders) [16].

fr.title: Maladie en phase terminale et démarches en Belgique : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes pour les démarches médicales et juridiques en fin de vie en Belgique : soins palliatifs, directives anticipées, procurations et mandats, congés d'aidant familial et organisation patrimoniale.
fr.introHtml: Lorsqu'un proche en Belgique reçoit le diagnostic d'une maladie grave, évolutive ou en phase terminale, l'organisation précoce des soins, des déclarations anticipées et des mandats de protection permet de respecter ses volontés tant que sa capacité de discernement est intacte. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles à accomplir dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Coordonner les soins palliatifs, les équipes à domicile et le forfait palliatif
steps.html:
En Belgique, la mise en place d'un accompagnement palliatif à domicile ou en unité spécialisée s'organise avec le médecin généraliste (ou le médecin spécialiste hospitalier en lien avec le service social de l'hôpital) et la mutualité de la personne malade, dans le cadre de l'Institut national d'assurance maladie-invalidité [1][2] :

  • Statut palliatif et forfait palliatif à domicile : lorsque la personne malade est soignée à domicile et répond aux critères médicaux du statut palliatif, le médecin traitant complète le formulaire officiel de notification destiné au médecin-conseil de la mutualité [1][2]. Ce statut ouvre le droit au forfait palliatif (octroyé pour une période de 30 jours, renouvelable une seule fois, afin de couvrir les médicaments, le matériel de soins et les dispositifs médicaux) ainsi qu'à la suppression du ticket modérateur pour les visites du médecin généraliste, les soins infirmiers à domicile et certaines séances de kinésithérapie [1][2].
  • Équipes de soutien à domicile et unités hospitalières : des équipes pluridisciplinaires de seconde ligne interviennent à domicile en appui du médecin traitant et des infirmiers, et des unités résidentielles de soins palliatifs accueillent les patients lorsque le maintien à domicile n'est plus possible [2][3]. Selon la région, vous pouvez identifier l'équipe ou le réseau compétent via la Fédération Wallonne des Soins Palliatifs en Wallonie [2][3], la Fédération bruxelloise pluraliste de soins palliatifs et continus à Bruxelles [4] ou Palliatieve Zorg Vlaanderen en Flandre [5].

steps.title: Rédiger et enregistrer les déclarations anticipées de soins et le plan de soins
steps.html:
Tant que la personne malade est majeure et capable d'exprimer sa volonté, elle peut formaliser par écrit ses choix médicaux dans le cadre de la planification anticipée des soins (Advance Care Planning, remboursée lors de la consultation avec le médecin généraliste) [1][6] :

  • Déclaration anticipée négative de soins (loi relative aux droits du patient) : la personne malade peut consigner par écrit les examens ou traitements médicaux précis qu'elle refuse (tels que la réanimation cardiopulmonaire, la ventilation mécanique ou l'alimentation artificielle) pour le cas où elle ne serait plus en mesure de s'exprimer, et désigner un mandataire ou une personne de confiance pour faire valoir ses droits auprès des soignants [6]. Cette déclaration s'impose aux praticiens et doit être remise au médecin généraliste pour intégration au dossier médical.
  • Déclaration anticipée relative à l'euthanasie : rédigée selon le modèle légal en présence de deux témoins majeurs (dont au moins un n'a aucun intérêt matériel au décès), elle s'applique uniquement si le patient, atteint d'une affection grave et incurable, tombe dans un état d'inconscience irréversible [6][7]. Depuis la réforme d'avril 2020, les déclarations établies ou renouvelées ont une durée de validité illimitée et peuvent être enregistrées gratuitement auprès de l'administration communale dans la base de données nationale du SPF Santé publique [6][7].

steps.title: Établir un mandat extrajudiciaire de protection et vérifier les procurations bancaires
steps.html:
Une simple procuration bancaire peut être jugée insuffisante pour des actes de gestion patrimoniale importants ou remise en cause si l'incapacité survient. Tant que votre proche dispose de sa pleine capacité juridique, il est possible d'établir un mandat de protection extrajudiciaire (souvent appelé zorgvolmacht) avec l'appui d'un notaire via la Fédération Royale du Notariat Belge [8][9] :

  • Portée financière et personnelle : le mandant désigne une ou plusieurs personnes de confiance (les mandataires) pour gérer ses comptes bancaires, ses revenus, ses biens mobiliers ou immobiliers et, s'il le souhaite, prendre des décisions relatives à sa personne (choix du lieu de séjour, exercice des droits du patient) sans devoir recourir d'emblée à une mesure d'administration judiciaire devant le juge de paix [8][9].
  • Enregistrement obligatoire : pour continuer à produire ses effets après la perte de capacité du mandant, le mandat doit obligatoirement être enregistré au Registre central des contrats de mandats (via le notaire ou le greffe de la justice de paix) [8][9].

steps.title: Mobiliser le congé pour soins palliatifs et le congé d'aidant proche
steps.html:
Les proches salariés ou agents qui accompagnent la personne malade peuvent demander une suspension complète ou une réduction de leurs prestations de travail avec allocation auprès de l'Office national de l'Emploi [10][11] :

  • Congé pour soins palliatifs (Feuille info T20) : tout travailleur peut interrompre totalement sa carrière ou réduire ses prestations (à mi-temps ou d'un cinquième) pendant 1 mois, prolongeable 2 fois d'un mois (soit jusqu'à 3 mois au total par patient) [10][11]. Le travailleur remet à son employeur une attestation délivrée par le médecin traitant de la personne malade et introduit sa demande d'allocations auprès de l'Office national de l'Emploi [10][11].
  • Congé pour aidants proches (Feuille info T164) : après avoir obtenu la reconnaissance officielle de la qualité d'aidant proche avec ouverture de droits sociaux auprès de sa mutualité, le travailleur peut solliciter un congé thématique d'aidant proche indemnisé par l'Office national de l'Emploi [10][12].

steps.title: Organiser le testament, les pensions, le déblocage des comptes et la succession
steps.html:
Rassembler les documents essentiels à l'avance facilite les démarches qui suivront le décès :

  • Testament et volontés funéraires : un testament (olographe ou notarié) peut être inscrit au Registre central des testaments par l'intermédiaire d'un notaire de la Fédération Royale du Notariat Belge [8][13], et la personne malade peut également faire enregistrer ses dernières volontés quant au mode de sépulture auprès de sa commune.
  • Pension de survie et mutualité : pour les salariés et fonctionnaires, le Service fédéral des Pensions (joignable via la Ligne Pension au 1765 ou sur le portail MyPension.be) examine automatiquement le droit à la pension de survie (ou à l'allocation de transition) si la personne décédée était déjà pensionnée ; si elle était encore en activité, une demande doit être introduite de préférence dans les 12 mois suivant le décès [14]. Il convient aussi de vérifier les bénéficiaires des assurances-vie ou assurances-groupe.
  • Blocage et déblocage des comptes bancaires : dès la notification du décès, les comptes et coffres bancaires sont bloqués [15]. Leur déblocage nécessite soit un certificat d'hérédité gratuit délivré par un bureau Sécurité juridique du SPF Finances (uniquement pour les successions simples sans testament, sans contrat de mariage et sans héritier incapable), soit un acte d'hérédité établi par un notaire [8][15]. Avant le déblocage complet, la banque peut libérer les fonds nécessaires au paiement des frais funéraires et une avance légale plafonnée pour le conjoint ou cohabitant légal survivant [15].
  • Déclaration de succession : lorsque le décès survient en Belgique, les héritiers disposent d'un délai légal de 4 mois à compter du décès pour déposer la déclaration de succession auprès du SPF Finances (pour la Wallonie et la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale) ou de l'administration fiscale flamande VLABEL (pour la Flandre) [16].

Votre proche souhaite-t-il mettre en place un mandat extrajudiciaire notarié ou un congé pour soins palliatifs est-il envisagé par un membre de l'entourage ?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Portugal: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Portugal is diagnosed with an advanced, progressive, or terminal illness, arranging clinical support, advance healthcare directives, and legal instruments early makes it possible to honour their wishes while they still have full decision-making capacity. Below are the five main official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Home Palliative Care and Inpatient Services
steps.html:
In Portugal, free access to palliative care within the Serviço Nacional de Saúde (National Health Service - SNS, SNS 24 helpline: 808 24 24 24) is organised through the National Palliative Care Network (Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos - RNCP) upon referral by the family doctor at the primary healthcare unit or by the hospital medical team [1][2]:

  • Community Palliative Care Support Teams (Equipas Comunitárias de Suporte em Cuidados Paliativos - ECSCP): multidisciplinary teams (physicians, nurses, psychologists, and social workers) that provide specialist palliative care directly at the patient's home and support informal caregivers, working in coordination with the local health centre and the National Network for Integrated Continuous Care (Rede Nacional de Cuidados Continuados Integrados - RNCCI) [2][3].
  • In-Hospital Palliative Support Teams (EIHSCP) and Palliative Care Units (Unidades de Cuidados Paliativos - UCP): provide specialist consultation during a hospital stay or inpatient admission to a dedicated residential unit when complex symptom management can no longer be maintained at home [2][3].
  • Guidance and regional directories: alongside the channels of the Serviço Nacional de Saúde [1][2], the Associação Portuguesa de Cuidados Paliativos (Portuguese Association for Palliative Care - APCP) publishes information and national directories of palliative care teams and services across Portugal [3].

steps.title: Prepare and Register an Advance Healthcare Directive (Living Will)
steps.html:
As long as the ill relative is an adult with full mental capacity and autonomy, they can execute an Advance Directive of Will (Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade - DAV), commonly known as a Living Will (Testamento Vital, governed by Law no. 25/2012), stating the medical care they wish to receive or refuse should they later become incapable of expressing their autonomous will [1][4]:

  • Clinical preferences and Healthcare Proxy (Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde): on the official DAV form, the patient can refuse artificial life support, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or disproportionate treatments, guarantee access to palliative care, and appoint a Healthcare Proxy (Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde, primary and alternate) to make healthcare decisions on their behalf with the medical team [1][4].
  • Registration in RENTEV: the official form is available via the SNS 24 portal or the public services portal gov.pt (ePortugal) and must either be submitted in person at a RENTEV desk (Balcão RENTEV at Local Health Units or health centre groups, where it is signed before the certifying officer) or sent by registered post with a notarised signature [1][4]. The directive is recorded in the National Living Will Register (Registo Nacional do Testamento Vital - RENTEV), managed by the Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde (Shared Services of the Ministry of Health - SPMS), and remains valid for 5 years (renewable or revocable at any time) [1][4].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney, Bank Mandates, and a Mandate for Accompanied Adult Status
steps.html:
Simple bank authorisations may be insufficient for extraordinary asset administration or may lapse if mental incapacity supervenes. While your relative retains full civil capacity, representation instruments should be formalised through a notary office via the Ordem dos Notários (Order of Notaries) or the registry offices of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary - IRN, Justice portal) [5][6]:

  • Notarial power of attorney (procuração notarial) or authenticated private document: grants specific or general powers to a trusted person to operate bank accounts, represent the ill person before public and tax authorities, or administer movable and immovable property, and can be registered on the Procurações Online service of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [5][6].
  • Mandate with a view to accompaniment (mandato com vista a acompanhamento, Article 156 of the Civil Code): to prepare for a potential future loss of autonomy requiring the legal regime of the Accompanied Adult (Maior Acompanhado, Law no. 49/2018), the ill person may execute a preventive mandate designating who should serve as their accompanying representative (acompanhante) and defining the scope of personal and patrimonial management, which guides any subsequent court decision [7][8].

steps.title: Apply for Dependency Benefits, Informal Caregiver Status, and Family Care Leave
steps.html:
To provide financial support for a dependent ill relative and employment protection for family caregivers, several statutory benefits and workplace rights are administered through the Instituto da Segurança Social (Institute of Social Security - ISS) [9][10]:

  • Dependency Supplement (Complemento por Dependência): a monthly cash benefit paid by Social Security (at 1st or 2nd degree dependency, subject to assessment by the Disability Verification System, Sistema de Verificação de Incapacidades) to pensioners or beneficiaries of the special disability protection scheme who require permanent third-party assistance with basic activities of daily living [9].
  • Informal Caregiver Status (Estatuto do Cuidador Informal) and care leave: a family member providing regular or permanent care can apply for recognition of Informal Caregiver Status (non-primary or primary caregiver, the latter giving access to a means-tested support allowance, subsídio de apoio) via Segurança Social Direta [10][11]. In addition, the Portuguese Labour Code (Código do Trabalho) provides for justified absences and leave to provide urgent and essential assistance to household members or relatives suffering from a serious or chronic illness.

steps.title: Organise the Will, Death Benefits, Qualification of Heirs, and Tax Obligations
steps.html:
Gathering civil, property, and social security documentation in advance simplifies the formalities that follow a death:

  • Will and funeral preferences: the ill relative may execute a public will (testamento público) or sealed will (testamento cerrado) at a notary office (via the Ordem dos Notários) or notary registry, respecting the statutory forced heirship share (quota legítima) reserved for forced heirs (spouse, descendants, and ascendants) [5], and record their funeral arrangements.
  • Social Security death benefits: after death, eligible family members can claim from the Instituto da Segurança Social the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days of the date of death), Reimbursement of Funeral Expenses (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days for the person who paid for the funeral where no entitlement to the Death Grant exists), and the monthly Survivor's Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [12][13].
  • One-stop death desk (Espaço Óbito), Inheritance Desk (Balcão das Heranças), and Stamp Duty (Imposto do Selo): after death, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) can use an Espaço Óbito or the Balcão das Heranças of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado to complete the qualification of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros, the official deed needed to unblock bank accounts and re-register assets) and any estate division [14][15]. Where the estate includes assets, the cabeça-de-casal is legally required to report the death and file the inventory of assets (Stamp Duty Form Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) with the Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Tax and Customs Authority, via Portal das Finanças / ePortugal) by the end of the 3rd month following the month in which the death occurred, even when the heirs (spouse or unido de facto, descendants, and ascendants) are exempt from paying Stamp Duty [15][16].

pt.title: Doença terminal e administração em fim de vida em Portugal: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos para o planeamento médico e jurídico em situação de doença terminal em Portugal: cuidados paliativos, diretivas antecipadas de vontade, procurações, apoios ao cuidador e organização sucessória.
pt.introHtml: Quando um familiar em Portugal recebe o diagnóstico de uma doença avançada, progressiva ou em fase terminal, organizar atempadamente o acompanhamento clínico, as diretivas médicas e os instrumentos jurídicos permite respeitar a sua vontade enquanto mantém plena capacidade de decisão. Apresentam-se de seguida os cinco principais passos oficiais por ordem.

steps.title: Coordenar os cuidados paliativos domiciliários e o internamento especializado
steps.html:
Em Portugal, o acesso gratuito a cuidados paliativos no Serviço Nacional de Saúde (linha SNS 24: 808 24 24 24) processa-se através da Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (RNCP), mediante referenciação pelo médico de família na unidade de cuidados de saúde primários ou pela equipa médica hospitalar [1][2]:

  • Equipas Comunitárias de Suporte em Cuidados Paliativos (ECSCP): são equipas multidisciplinares (médicos, enfermeiros, psicólogos e assistentes sociais) que prestam cuidados paliativos especializados diretamente no domicílio da pessoa doente e apoiam os cuidadores informais, articulando-se com o centro de saúde e com a Rede Nacional de Cuidados Continuados Integrados (RNCCI) [2][3].
  • Equipas Intra-Hospitalares (EIHSCP) e Unidades de Cuidados Paliativos (UCP): asseguram consultoria especializada durante um internamento hospitalar ou o internamento em unidade residencial dedicada quando o controlo de sintomas complexos não pode ser mantido em casa [2][3].
  • Orientação e diretórios regionais: além dos canais do Serviço Nacional de Saúde [1][2], a Associação Portuguesa de Cuidados Paliativos disponibiliza informação e diretórios sobre as equipas e recursos paliativos existentes em território nacional [3].

steps.title: Preparar e registar a Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade (Testamento Vital)
steps.html:
Enquanto a pessoa doente for maior de idade, capaz e autónoma, pode formalizar uma Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade (DAV), conhecida como Testamento Vital (regulada pela Lei n.º 25/2012), para expressar os cuidados médicos que deseja receber ou recusar caso fique incapaz de manifestar a sua vontade de forma autónoma [1][4]:

  • Decisões clínicas e Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde: no formulário oficial da DAV, o utente pode recusar suporte artificial das funções vitais, reanimação cardiorrespiratória ou tratamentos desproporcionados, garantir o acesso a cuidados paliativos e nomear um Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde (efetivo e suplente) para decidir em seu nome perante a equipa médica [1][4].
  • Registo no RENTEV: o formulário pode ser obtido através do portal SNS 24 ou do portal público ePortugal (gov.pt) e deve ser entregue presencialmente num Balcão RENTEV (nas Unidades Locais de Saúde ou agrupamentos de centros de saúde, sendo assinado perante o funcionário) ou enviado por correio registado com assinatura reconhecida por notário [1][4]. O documento fica registado no Registo Nacional do Testamento Vital (RENTEV), plataforma gerida pelos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde, e tem validade de 5 anos (renovável ou revogável a qualquer momento) [1][4].

steps.title: Outorgar procurações notariais, mandatos bancários e mandato com vista a acompanhamento
steps.html:
As autorizações bancárias simples podem ser insuficientes para atos de administração extraordinária ou perder eficácia se sobrevier incapacidade. Enquanto o seu familiar conserva plena capacidade civil, importa formalizar instrumentos de representação recorrendo a um cartório notarial através da Ordem dos Notários ou aos serviços do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (portal da Justiça) [5][6]:

  • Procuração notarial ou documento particular autenticado: confere poderes específicos ou gerais a uma pessoa de confiança para movimentar contas bancárias, representar a pessoa doente perante serviços públicos e fiscais ou administrar bens móveis e imóveis, podendo ser registada no serviço Procurações Online do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [5][6].
  • Mandato com vista a acompanhamento (Artigo 156.º do Código Civil): em prevenção de uma eventual perda futura de autonomia que exija o regime jurídico do Maior Acompanhado (Lei n.º 49/2018), a pessoa doente pode celebrar preventivamente um mandato que define quem deverá exercer as funções de acompanhante e o âmbito da gestão patrimonial e pessoal, vinculando a apreciação futura do tribunal [7][8].

steps.title: Solicitar apoios por dependência, Estatuto do Cuidador Informal e faltas para assistência
steps.html:
Para apoiar financeiramente a pessoa doente em situação de dependência e proteger laboralmente os familiares cuidadores, existem prestações e direitos geridos pelo Instituto da Segurança Social [9][10]:

  • Complemento por Dependência: prestação pecuniária mensal atribuída pela Segurança Social (no 1.º ou 2.º grau, mediante avaliação pelo Sistema de Verificação de Incapacidades) a pensionistas ou beneficiários do regime especial de proteção na invalidez que necessitem da assistência permanente de terceira pessoa para as atividades básicas da vida diária [9].
  • Estatuto do Cuidador Informal e faltas ao trabalho: o familiar que presta cuidados regulares ou permanentes pode requerer o reconhecimento do Estatuto do Cuidador Informal (não principal ou principal, este último com acesso a subsídio de apoio sujeito a condição de recursos) através da Segurança Social Direta [10][11]. Adicionalmente, o Código do Trabalho prevê o direito a faltas justificadas e licenças para assistência inadiável e imprescindível a membros do agregado familiar ou familiares com doença grave ou crónica.

steps.title: Organizar o testamento, prestações por morte, habilitação de herdeiros e obrigações fiscais
steps.html:
Reunir antecipadamente a documentação civil, patrimonial e previdenciária facilita os procedimentos posteriores ao falecimento:

  • Testamento e desejos fúnebres: a pessoa doente pode outorgar um testamento público ou testamento cerrado num cartório notarial (através da Ordem dos Notários) ou conservatória, respeitando a quota legítima reservada aos herdeiros legitimários (cônjuge, descendentes e ascendentes) [5], bem como deixar registadas as suas preferências para o funeral.
  • Prestações por morte na Segurança Social: após o óbito, os familiares elegíveis podem requerer junto do Instituto da Segurança Social o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do falecimento), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias para quem comprovadamente pagou o funeral, quando não haja direito ao subsídio por morte) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência mensal [12][13].
  • Espaço Óbito, Balcão das Heranças e Imposto do Selo: após o falecimento, o cabeça-de-casal pode recorrer ao Espaço Óbito ou ao Balcão das Heranças do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado para realizar a habilitação de herdeiros (documento indispensável para desbloquear contas bancárias e registar bens) e eventual partilha [14][15]. Havendo bens na herança, o cabeça-de-casal é obrigado a participar o óbito e a relação de bens (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) à Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portal das Finanças / ePortugal) até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao mês em que ocorreu o óbito, mesmo quando os herdeiros (cônjuge ou unido de facto, descendentes e ascendentes) beneficiem de isenção de Imposto do Selo [15][16].

O seu familiar pretende registar o Testamento Vital no RENTEV ou formalizar uma procuração notarial a curto prazo?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Poland: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Poland is diagnosed with an advanced or incurable life-limiting illness, organising medical care, authorisations, and financial affairs early ensures that their wishes are respected while they still retain full legal capacity and decision-making ability. Below are the five main official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Hospice, or Inpatient Hospice Services
steps.html:
In Poland, publicly funded palliative and hospice care is financed by the Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia (National Health Fund - NFZ; 24/7 toll-free Patient Telephone Information helpline Telefoniczna Informacja Pacjenta: 800 190 590) on the basis of a medical referral (skierowanie) issued by any health insurance physician (such as a primary care doctor or a hospital specialist upon discharge) together with the patient's written consent [1][2]:

  • Home hospice (hospicjum domowe): a multidisciplinary team (physicians, nurses, psychologists, and physiotherapists) provides care in the patient's home, including pain management, 24/7 access to medical consultations (doctor visits at least twice a month and nursing visits at least twice a week), and free loan of medical and rehabilitation equipment (such as an oxygen concentrator or hospital bed) [1][2].
  • Inpatient hospice (hospicjum stacjonarne), palliative medicine ward (oddział medycyny paliatywnej), and outpatient clinic: intended for patients requiring 24-hour inpatient care, temporary respite care (opieka wyręczająca) to relieve family caregivers, or outpatient consultations; there is no geographic catchment restriction (rejonizacja) in palliative care [1][2].
  • Protection of patient rights: if problems arise regarding access to care or the right to effective pain relief, assistance is available from the Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta (Patient Ombudsman, which operates the joint helpline at 800 190 590 with the NFZ) [3].

steps.title: Prepare Patient Declarations and Medical Authorisations (Including via IKP)
steps.html:
While the ill relative is conscious and able to express informed consent, they should formalise medical authorisations under the Act on Patient Rights and the Patient Ombudsman (ustawa o prawach pacjenta i Rzeczniku Praw Pacjenta) [3][4]:

  • Authorising a close person for medical information and records (upoważnienie osoby bliskiej): the patient may designate by name a trusted person authorised to receive information about their health status and planned procedures and to inspect and obtain copies of medical records both during the patient's lifetime and after death [3][4].
  • Digital authorisation on the government portal: through the Internetowe Konto Pacjenta (Online Patient Account - IKP) or the mojeIKP mobile app, the patient can go to the Authorisations (Upoważnienia) tab to grant a close relative access to their e-prescriptions (e-recepty), e-referrals (e-skierowania), and treatment history [4][5].
  • Written statement of treatment preferences (oświadczenie woli): although Polish statutory law does not regulate a standalone 'living will' (testament życia) in a separate act, a written patient statement setting out consent or refusal regarding specific medical procedures in the event of loss of consciousness should be placed in the medical records held by the attending physician and hospice team [1][3].

steps.title: Execute a Notarial Power of Attorney and Bank Directives
steps.html:
An ordinary written power of attorney is often insufficient for major legal and property transactions, and banks or public offices may refuse to honour it if the grantor loses consciousness or capacity. While your family member retains full legal capacity, it is advisable to arrange a deed with a civil-law notary (who can be located through the Krajowa Rada Notarialna, the National Council of Notaries) [6]:

  • Power of attorney in the form of a notarial deed (pełnomocnictwo w formie aktu notarialnego) or with a notarised signature: enables a trusted representative to act on the ill person's behalf before administrative authorities, courts, and financial institutions, or to manage real estate [6]. If the patient's health prevents travel to a notary's office, the notary may perform the act outside the office (at the patient's home or in hospital) [6].
  • Bank account power of attorney and instructions on bank deposits in the event of death (dyspozycja wkładem na wypadek śmierci): verify the scope of any bank account mandate (which expires automatically upon the account holder's death) and consider filing a bank deposit instruction in the event of death (dyspozycja wkładem na wypadek śmierci, Article 56 of the Banking Law) in favour of immediate family members (spouse, descendants, ascendants, or siblings), which allows a specified statutory sum to be paid out after death outside probate proceedings.

steps.title: Access the Care Allowance, Caregiver Leave, and the Supporting Benefit
steps.html:
Family caregivers and the ill relative can draw on statutory employment and financial support administered by the Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (Social Insurance Institution - ZUS) [7][8]:

  • ZUS care allowance (zasiłek opiekuńczy): an employee or other person covered by sickness insurance who is released from work to personally care for an ill family member (such as a spouse, parent, or adult child sharing the same household during the period of care) is entitled to a care allowance for up to 14 days per calendar year paid at 80% of the assessment basis (on the basis of an electronic medical certificate e-ZLA and application form Z-15B) [7][8].
  • Caregiver leave (urlop opiekuńczy under the Labour Code): an employee working under an employment contract is entitled to 5 days of unpaid caregiver leave per calendar year to provide personal care or support to a family member (son, daughter, mother, father, or spouse) or a person living in the same household for serious medical reasons (applied for at least 1 day in advance).
  • Supporting benefit (świadczenie wspierające): an adult with a disability who obtains a decision from the Voivodeship Disability Assessment Team (WZON) setting their level of support need at between 70 and 100 points may submit an electronic application for the non-means-tested supporting benefit (świadczenie wspierające), paid by the Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych [9].

steps.title: Organise the Will, Survivor Benefits, and Inheritance and Tax Formalities
steps.html:
Gathering civil status certificates and policy and account details in advance simplifies post-death procedures:

  • Will and Inheritance Register: the ill person may draw up a holographic will (testament własnoręczny, written entirely by hand, signed, and dated) or a notarial will, which the notary can register free of charge in the Notarial Register of Wills (Notarialny Rejestr Testamentów - NORT) maintained by the Krajowa Rada Notarialna [6]. Beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, open pension funds (OFE), individual retirement accounts (IKE/IKZE), and employee capital plans (PPK) should also be reviewed.
  • Funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy) and survivor's pension (renta rodzinna): after the death of an insured person or pension/disability beneficiary, an application for the funeral grant (form Z-12 in ZUS or SR-26 in KRUS) must be filed within 12 months of the date of death with the Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych [10][11] or the agricultural social insurance fund Kasa Rolniczego Ubezpieczenia Społecznego (KRUS) [12][13]. Eligible family members may also apply for a survivor's pension (renta rodzinna) (or combined benefits under the widow's pension rules, renta wdowia) [11][14].
  • Confirmation of inheritance rights and tax form SD-Z2: heirs have 6 months from the date they learn of their entitlement to make a declaration before a notary or court accepting the estate (with benefit of inventory, z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza, or unconditionally) or renouncing it; title to the estate is confirmed either by a notarial Deed of Certification of Inheritance (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia, entered in the Inheritance Register, Rejestr Spadkowy) or by a final court order confirming acquisition of the estate (stwierdzenie nabycia spadku) [6][15]. For immediate family members (the 'zero tax group': spouse, descendants, ascendants, stepchildren, siblings, stepfather, and stepmother) to qualify for full exemption from inheritance and gift tax, they must submit form SD-Z2 to the competent tax office within a strict deadline of 6 months from the date the Deed of Certification of Inheritance is registered or the court order becomes final (electronically via e-Urząd Skarbowy, operated by the Ministerstwo Finansów, the Ministry of Finance) [16].

pl.title: Choroba terminalna i sprawy formalno-prawne w kraju Polska: oficjalna lista w 5 krokach
pl.cardSummary: Oficjalna lista kontrolna w 5 krokach przy chorobie terminalnej w kraju Polska: opieka paliatywna i hospicyjna (NFZ), upoważnienia medyczne, pełnomocnictwa notarialne, zasiłek opiekuńczy i testament.
pl.introHtml: Gdy członek rodziny w Polsce otrzymuje diagnozę zaawansowanej lub nieuleczalnej choroby ograniczającej życie, wczesne uporządkowanie opieki medycznej, upoważnień oraz spraw majątkowych pozwala uszanować wolę tej osoby, dopóki zachowuje ona pełną zdolność do czynności prawnych i świadomego podejmowania decyzji. Poniżej przedstawiono pięć głównych oficjalnych kroków w kolejności.

steps.title: Zorganizowanie specjalistycznej opieki paliatywnej, hospicjum domowego lub stacjonarnego
steps.html:
W Polsce bezpłatne świadczenia z zakresu opieki paliatywnej i hospicyjnej finansuje instytucja publiczna (Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia, całodobowa bezpłatna Telefoniczna Informacja Pacjenta: 800 190 590) na podstawie skierowania wystawionego przez dowolnego lekarza ubezpieczenia zdrowotnego (np. lekarza podstawowej opieki zdrowotnej lub lekarza specjalistę przy wypisie ze szpitala) oraz pisemnej zgody pacjenta [1][2]:

  • Hospicjum domowe: wielodyscyplinarny zespół (lekarze, pielęgniarki, psycholodzy i fizjoterapeuci) sprawuje opiekę w miejscu zamieszkania, zapewniając leczenie bólu, całodobowy dostęp do konsultacji medycznych (wizyty lekarskie co najmniej 2 razy w miesiącu i pielęgniarskie co najmniej 2 razy w tygodniu) oraz bezpłatne wypożyczenie sprzętu medycznego i rehabilitacyjnego (np. koncentratora tlenu lub łóżka rehabilitacyjnego) [1][2].
  • Hospicjum stacjonarne, oddział medycyny paliatywnej i poradnia: przeznaczone dla pacjentów wymagających całodobowej opieki stacjonarnej, czasowej opieki wyręczającej dla odciążenia opiekunów lub konsultacji ambulatoryjnych; w opiece paliatywnej nie obowiązuje rejonizacja [1][2].
  • Ochrona praw pacjenta: w razie problemów z dostępem do świadczeń lub poszanowaniem praw do łagodzenia bólu wsparcia udziela organ państwowy (Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta, prowadzący wspólnie z NFZ infolinię pod numerem 800 190 590) [3].

steps.title: Sporządzenie oświadczeń pacjenta i upoważnień medycznych (w tym przez IKP)
steps.html:
Dopóki osoba chora jest przytomna i zdolna do świadomego wyrażenia woli, powinna sformalizować upoważnienia medyczne zgodnie z ustawą o prawach pacjenta i Rzeczniku Praw Pacjenta [3][4]:

  • Upoważnienie osoby bliskiej do informacji i dokumentacji medycznej: pacjent może wskazać z imienia i nazwiska osobę upoważnioną do uzyskiwania informacji o jego stanie zdrowia i planowanych zabiegach oraz do wglądu i pobierania kopii dokumentacji medycznej zarówno za życia, jak i po śmierci pacjenta [3][4].
  • Upoważnienie cyfrowe w serwisie rządowym: za pośrednictwem portalu pacjenta (Internetowe Konto Pacjenta) lub aplikacji mojeIKP osoba chora może w zakładce Upoważnienia nadać bliskiej osobie dostęp do swoich e-recept, e-skierowań oraz historii leczenia [4][5].
  • Pisemne oświadczenie o woli dotyczącej leczenia: choć polskie prawo nie reguluje odrębnej instytucji tzw. testamentu życia w osobnej ustawie, pisemne oświadczenie pacjenta dotyczące zgody lub sprzeciwu wobec określonych procedur medycznych na wypadek utraty przytomności warto dołączyć do dokumentacji medycznej prowadzonej przez lekarza prowadzącego i hospicjum [1][3].

steps.title: Udzielenie pełnomocnictwa notarialnego oraz dyspozycji bankowych
steps.html:
Zwykłe pełnomocnictwo pisemne bywa niewystarczające do poważniejszych czynności prawnych i majątkowych, a w razie utraty świadomości przez osobę chorą banki oraz urzędy mogą odmówić jego honorowania. Dopóki członek rodziny zachowuje pełną zdolność do czynności prawnych, warto udać się do notariusza (którego można wyszukać poprzez samorząd notarialny: Krajowa Rada Notarialna) [6]:

  • Pełnomocnictwo w formie aktu notarialnego (lub z podpisem notarialnie poświadczonym): umożliwia osobie zaufanej reprezentowanie osoby chorej przed urzędami, sądami, instytucjami finansowymi czy przy zarządzie nieruchomościami [6]. Jeżeli stan zdrowia uniemożliwia dotarcie do kancelarii, notariusz może dokonać czynności poza kancelarią (w domu lub w szpitalu) [6].
  • Pełnomocnictwo do rachunku bankowego i dyspozycja wkładem na wypadek śmierci: w banku należy sprawdzić zakres pełnomocnictwa do rachunku (które wygasa z chwilą śmierci posiadacza) oraz rozważyć złożenie dyspozycji wkładem na wypadek śmierci (art. 56 Prawa bankowego) na rzecz najbliższych członków rodziny (małżonka, zstępnych, wstępnych lub rodzeństwa), co pozwala na wypłatę określonej kwoty po śmierci z pominięciem postępowania spadkowego.

steps.title: Skorzystanie z zasiłku opiekuńczego, urlopu opiekuńczego i świadczenia wspierającego
steps.html:
Opiekunowie oraz sama osoba chora mogą skorzystać z ustawowych form wsparcia pracowniczego i finansowego, które obsługuje organ rentowy (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych) [7][8]:

  • Zasiłek opiekuńczy z ZUS: pracownikowi lub innej osobie objętej ubezpieczeniem chorobowym, zwolnionej od pracy z powodu konieczności osobistego sprawowania opieki nad chorym członkiem rodziny (np. małżonkiem, rodzicem lub dorosłym dzieckiem pozostającym we wspólnym gospodarstwie domowym w czasie sprawowania opieki), przysługuje zasiłek opiekuńczy przez okres do 14 dni w roku kalendarzowym w wysokości 80% podstawy wymiaru (na podstawie zaświadczenia lekarskiego e-ZLA i wniosku Z-15B) [7][8].
  • Urlop opiekuńczy (Kodeks pracy): pracownik zatrudniony na podstawie umowy o pracę ma prawo do 5 dni bezpłatnego urlopu opiekuńczego w roku kalendarzowym w celu zapewnienia osobistej opieki członkowi rodziny (synowi, córce, matce, ojcu lub małżonkowi) albo osobie zamieszkującej w tym samym gospodarstwie domowym z poważnych względów medycznych (wniosek składa się co najmniej 1 dzień wcześniej).
  • Świadczenie wspierające: pełnoletnia osoba z niepełnosprawnością, która uzyska decyzję wojewódzkiego zespołu ds. orzekania o niepełnosprawności (WZON) ustalającą poziom potrzeby wsparcia na poziomie od 70 do 100 punktów, może złożyć elektroniczny wniosek o świadczenie wspierające (bez kryterium dochodowego), które wypłaca Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych [9].

steps.title: Uporządkowanie testamentu, świadczeń pośmiertnych i formalności spadkowo-podatkowych
steps.html:
Wcześniejsze zebranie odpisów aktów stanu cywilnego oraz informacji o polisach i rachunkach ułatwia późniejsze formalności po śmierci:

  • Testament i Rejestr Spadkowy: osoba chora może sporządzić testament własnoręczny (w całości napisany ręcznie, podpisany i opatrzony datą) lub testament w formie aktu notarialnego, który notariusz może bezpłatnie zarejestrować w Notarialnym Rejestrze Testamentów (NORT) prowadzonym przez samorząd notarialny (Krajowa Rada Notarialna) [6]. Warto również sprawdzić osoby uposażone w polisach na życie, OFE, IKE/IKZE oraz PPK.
  • Zasiłek pogrzebowy i renta rodzinna: po śmierci osoby ubezpieczonej lub pobierającej świadczenie emerytalno-rentowe wniosek o zasiłek pogrzebowy (druk Z-12 w ZUS lub SR-26 w KRUS) należy złożyć w terminie 12 miesięcy od dnia śmierci do właściwej instytucji, którą jest Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych [10][11] albo jednostka rolnicza (Kasa Rolniczego Ubezpieczenia Społecznego) [12][13]. Uprawnieni członkowie rodziny mogą również ubiegać się o rentę rodzinną (lub zbieg świadczeń w ramach tzw. renty wdowiej) [11][14].
  • Potwierdzenie praw do spadku i zgłoszenie SD-Z2: spadkobiercy mają 6 miesięcy od dnia dowiedzenia się o tytule swego powołania na złożenie przed notariuszem lub sądem oświadczenia o przyjęciu spadku (z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza lub wprost) albo o jego odrzuceniu; potwierdzenie praw do spadku następuje poprzez notarialny Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia (wpisywany do Rejestru Spadkowego) lub prawomocne postanowienie sądu o stwierdzeniu nabycia spadku [6][15]. Aby najbliższa rodzina (tzw. grupa zerowa: małżonek, zstępni, wstępni, pasierb, rodzeństwo, ojczym i macocha) skorzystała z całkowitego zwolnienia z podatku od spadków i darowizn, musi w nieprzekraczalnym terminie 6 miesięcy od dnia zarejestrowania Aktu Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia lub uprawomocnienia się postanowienia sądu złożyć formularz SD-Z2 do właściwego urzędu skarbowego (elektronicznie przez e-Urząd Skarbowy, który prowadzi resort finansów: Ministerstwo Finansów) [16].
