title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Romania: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Romania is diagnosed with a serious or advanced life-limiting illness, organising medical care and legal documents early - while the ill person still retains full legal capacity (capacitate deplină de exercițiu) - ensures that their wishes are respected and simplifies subsequent procedures for the family. Below are the five main official and practical steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care at Home and in Inpatient Units
steps.html:
In Romania, initiating specialist medical and palliative care begins with a medical recommendation issued by the treating oncologist, hospital specialist, or family doctor (medic de familie) [1]:

  • Publicly reimbursed palliative care via CNAS: inpatient palliative care (hospital wards or palliative care beds), outpatient care, and home care (îngrijiri paliative la domiciliu) are reimbursed through the Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate (National Health Insurance House - CNAS) and the county or Bucharest health insurance houses (casele de asigurări de sănătate județene sau a Municipiului București), within statutory service packages and funding ceilings [1]. For home care, the physician issues a standardised referral form submitted to the territorial health insurance house to approve the reimbursement decision, after which the family selects an accredited provider under contract with the insurance house [1].
  • Charitable and NGO palliative networks: alongside the public network, patients can access specialist services run by accredited non-governmental organisations. As an illustrative example from public sources, the foundation HOSPICE Casa Speranței provides free specialist palliative care services (inpatient units, mobile home care teams, and outpatient clinics) for adult patients with incurable diagnoses in Bucharest, Brașov, and surrounding areas [2]. Clarvia provides these details solely for informational orientation and does not endorse, approve, or rank the providers mentioned.

steps.title: Record Written Informed Consent and Designate the Patient's Legal Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
Romania does not operate a separate national registry for a standardised living will (testament biologic), but the ill person's right to make decisions regarding treatment and end-of-life care is governed by the Patients' Rights Law no. 46/2003 (Legea drepturilor pacientului nr. 46/2003), overseen by the Ministerul Sănătății (Ministry of Health) [3]:

  • Recording treatment preferences and refusals: while your family member has mental capacity (discernământ), they may ask the medical team to record their therapeutic preferences in their clinical observation chart (foaia de observație clinică), including acceptance or refusal of specific medical interventions or the cessation of an intervention, confirming their decision in writing after receiving full medical information [3].
  • Written designation of a healthcare representative (reprezentant legal): under Law no. 46/2003, the patient should designate in writing a trusted person (legal representative for medical matters) to receive information regarding diagnosis and prognosis and to give or withhold consent for medical interventions if the patient subsequently loses the capacity to express their wishes [3]. Keep a copy of this signed declaration in the hospital medical file and at home for the palliative care team.

steps.title: Execute Authentic Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Full Capacity Exists
steps.html:
For a family member to legally manage bank accounts, pension collection, bill payments, dealings with public authorities, or property administration, a special or general authentic power of attorney (procură autentică) must be executed while the ill person retains full mental capacity (discernământ deplin) [4]:

  • Notarial power of attorney and RNNEPR registration: within Romania, a power of attorney is authenticated by any public notary belonging to the Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (National Union of Public Notaries of Romania - UNNPR), and all powers of attorney are recorded in the National Notarial Register of Powers of Attorney and their Revocation (Registrul Național Notarial de Evidență a Procurilor și a Revocării acestora - RNNEPR) [4]. If the patient cannot travel for medical reasons, you can request a mobile visit by the public notary to the patient's home or healthcare facility within that territorial district [4].
  • Commercial bank mandates and consular authentication: many commercial banks in Romania require either specific clauses in the notarial power of attorney (explicitly listing IBAN account numbers and permitted transactions) or the signing of the bank's own account mandate form (împuternicire pe cont). If the grantor or representative is abroad, notarial powers of attorney and declarations can be authenticated at Romanian diplomatic missions or consular offices by prior appointment through the consular portal (eConsulat.ro) of the Ministerul Afacerilor Externe (Ministry of Foreign Affairs - MAE) [5].

steps.title: Access Oncology Caregiver Leave and Statutory Carer Rights
steps.html:
Employed family members who are insured in the public health system and meet the minimum contribution requirement (6 months within the last 12 months) can access statutory leave and financial support [1]:

  • Leave and allowance for caring for an oncology patient (concediu și indemnizație pentru îngrijirea pacientului cu afecțiuni oncologice): insured employees may claim up to 45 calendar days per year per patient to care for and accompany an oncology patient aged over 18 to surgical interventions and treatments prescribed by a specialist physician, with the patient's written consent for one accompanying person per treatment [1]. The medical leave certificate is issued by the attending specialist based on a certificate of used days from the health insurance house (under Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate rules), and the gross allowance equals 85% of the calculation basis [1].
  • Statutory carer's leave (concediu de îngrijitor) and disability assessment: under the Labour Code (Codul muncii), any employee is entitled upon request to up to 5 working days of carer's leave per calendar year to provide personal care or support to a relative or household member suffering from a serious medical condition. Additionally, where the illness causes severe loss of autonomy, the specialist physician can issue the medical report (referat medical) needed for severe disability classification (including entitlement to a personal assistant or companion allowance, indemnizație de însoțitor) through the county or Bucharest sector General Directorate of Social Assistance and Child Protection (DGASPC).

steps.title: Organise the Will, Pension Rights, Civil Status Documents, and Succession Procedure
steps.html:
While the ill person retains full legal capacity, they can organise their estate and prepare key documents to streamline post-death formalities for the family [4]:

  • Authentic notarial will and vital documents: the patient may execute a notarial will (testament autentic) before a public notary - registered in the National Notarial Register of Liberalities (RNNEL) administered by the Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România - respecting the statutory reserved share (rezerva succesorală) of forced heirs [4]. Gather original civil status documents (identity card, birth and marriage certificates), the pension decision, property deeds, bank contracts, and life insurance policies, and note funeral or cremation wishes.
  • Death grant (ajutor de deces) and survivor's pension (pensie de urmaș): after a death, applications for the death grant and survivor's pension are submitted through the Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (National House of Public Pensions - CNPP, via the local territorial pension house) [6]. The death grant is paid to a single person who presents the original death certificate and proof of bearing the funeral expenses, while the surviving spouse and eligible children may claim a survivor's pension under Law no. 360/2023 [6].
  • Notarial succession procedure and 2-year tax exemption: where heirs agree on their shares and assets, the estate is settled through the notarial succession procedure (procedura succesorală notarială) before a public notary in the judicial district of the deceased's last domicile [4]. Under the Fiscal Code administered by the Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală (National Agency for Fiscal Administration - ANAF), heirs are exempt from real estate transfer tax if the succession is completed within 2 years of the date of death; after the 2-year deadline, a 1% tax on the value of inherited real estate applies and is withheld by the notary upon issuing the certificate of heir (certificat de moștenitor) [7].

ro.title: Boală în stadiu terminal și demersuri legale în România: listă oficială în 5 pași
ro.cardSummary: Ghid oficial în 5 pași pentru planificarea medicală și juridică în caz de boală gravă în România: îngrijiri paliative, desemnarea reprezentantului medical, procuri notariale, concediu pentru îngrijirea pacientului și testament.
ro.introHtml: Când membrul familiei dumneavoastră din România primește diagnosticul unei afecțiuni grave sau în stadiu avansat, organizarea din timp a îngrijirilor medicale și a documentelor juridice cât timp persoana bolnavă are deplină capacitate de exercițiu permite respectarea dorințelor sale și simplifică procedurile ulterioare pentru familie. Mai jos găsiți cei cinci pași oficiali și practici în ordinea priorității.

steps.title: Coordonarea îngrijirilor paliative specializate, la domiciliu și în unități cu paturi
steps.html:
Primul pas este obținerea unei recomandări medicale de la medicul specialist oncolog, medicul curant din spital sau medicul de familie pentru servicii de îngrijiri medicale și paliative. În sistemul public, îngrijirile paliative în regim de spitalizare continuă (secții sau compartimente cu paturi), în ambulatoriu sau la domiciliu sunt decontate prin instituția Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate și casele de asigurări de sănătate județene sau a Municipiului București, în limita pachetelor de servicii și a plafoanelor legale [1]. Pentru îngrijiri la domiciliu, medicul eliberează o recomandare tipizată care se depune la casa de asigurări de sănătate teritorială pentru aprobarea deciziei de decontare, după care familia alege un furnizor acreditat aflat în contract cu casa de asigurări [1].

În paralel cu rețeaua publică, persoana bolnavă poate accesa servicii specializate oferite de organizații neguvernamentale acreditate. Ca exemplu orientativ din surse publice, fundația HOSPICE Casa Speranței oferă gratuit servicii de îngrijire paliativă (unități cu paturi, echipe mobile la domiciliu și ambulatoriu) pentru pacienții adulți cu diagnostice incurabile în București, Brașov și zonele limitrofe [2]. Clarvia oferă aceste informații exclusiv pentru orientare și nu recomandă, nu aprobă și nu clasifică furnizorii menționați.

steps.title: Exprimarea în scris a consimțământului informat și desemnarea reprezentantului legal al pacientului
steps.html:
În România nu există o procedură separată de înregistrare a unui testament biologic standardizat într-un registru național unic, însă dreptul persoanei bolnave de a decide asupra tratamentelor și îngrijirilor terminale este reglementat prin Legea drepturilor pacientului nr. 46/2003, aplicată sub coordonarea autorității Ministerul Sănătății [3]. Cât timp membrul familiei dumneavoastră are discernământ, poate solicita echipei medicale consemnarea în foaia de observație clinică a preferințelor sale terapeutice, inclusiv acceptarea sau refuzul anumitor intervenții medicale ori oprirea unei intervenții, asumându-și în scris decizia după informarea medicală completă [3].

Tot în baza Legii nr. 46/2003, persoana bolnavă ar trebui să desemneze în scris o persoană de încredere (reprezentant legal pentru situații medicale) care să fie informată cu privire la diagnostic și prognostic și care să își poată exprima consimțământul pentru intervenții medicale în cazul în care pacientul își pierde ulterior capacitatea de a-și exprima voința [3]. Păstrați o copie a acestei declarații la dosarul medical și la domiciliu, la îndemâna echipei de îngrijire paliativă.

steps.title: Întocmirea procurilor notariale autentice și a mandatelor bancare cât timp există capacitate deplină
steps.html:
Pentru ca un membru al familiei să poată gestiona legal conturile bancare, încasarea pensiei, plata facturilor, relația cu instituțiile publice sau administrarea bunurilor, este esențială întocmirea unei procuri speciale sau generale în formă autentică cât timp persoana bolnavă are discernământ deplin. În țară, procura se autentifică la orice notar public membru în organizația profesională Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România, iar toate procurile sunt înscrise în Registrul Național Notarial de Evidență a Procurilor și a Revocării acestora (RNNEPR) [4]. Dacă persoana bolnavă nu se poate deplasa din motive medicale, puteți solicita deplasarea notarului public la domiciliu sau la unitatea sanitară din circumscripția teritorială respectivă [4].

În plus, multe bănci comerciale din România solicită fie clauze specifice în procura notarială (indicarea expresă a conturilor IBAN și a operațiunilor permise), fie semnarea unui formular propriu de împuternicire pe cont direct la bancă. Dacă persoana care acordă sau primește o împuternicire se află în străinătate, actele notariale (procuri și declarații) pot fi autentificate la misiunile diplomatice sau oficiile consulare ale României cu programare prealabilă prin portalul consular al instituției Ministerul Afacerilor Externe [5].

steps.title: Accesarea concediului pentru îngrijirea pacientului oncologic și a drepturilor pentru aparținători
steps.html:
Membrii familiei care sunt salariați asigurați în sistemul public de sănătate și îndeplinesc stagiul minim de cotizare (6 luni în ultimele 12 luni) pot solicita concediu și indemnizație pentru îngrijirea pacientului cu afecțiuni oncologice în vârstă de peste 18 ani [1]. Acest concediu este de maximum 45 de zile calendaristice pe an pentru un pacient și se acordă pentru însoțirea persoanei bolnave la intervenții chirurgicale și tratamente prescrise de medicul specialist, cu acordul scris al pacientului pentru o singură persoană însoțitoare la fiecare tratament [1]. Certificatul de concediu medical este eliberat de medicul specialist curant pe baza adeverinței emise de casa de asigurări de sănătate privind zilele utilizate, iar indemnizația brută este de 85% din baza de calcul [1].

Suplimentar, orice salariat are dreptul, conform Codului muncii, la un concediu de îngrijitor de până la 5 zile lucrătoare într-un an calendaristic, acordat la cerere pentru a oferi îngrijire sau sprijin personal unei rude sau unei persoane care locuiește în aceeași gospodărie și suferă de o problemă medicală gravă. De asemenea, dacă boala determină o limitare severă a autonomiei, medicul specialist poate elibera referatul medical necesar evaluării pentru încadrarea în grad de handicap (inclusiv cu asistent personal sau indemnizație de însoțitor) prin Direcția Generală de Asistență Socială și Protecția Copilului (DGASPC) din județul sau sectorul de domiciliu.

steps.title: Organizarea testamentului, a drepturilor de pensie, a actelor de stare civilă și a procedurii succesorale
steps.html:
Cât timp persoana bolnavă are capacitate deplină de exercițiu, poate întocmi un testament autentic la notarul public (înregistrat în Registrul Național Notarial de Evidență a Liberalităților - RNNEL, administrat de Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România) pentru a-și exprima voința privind împărțirea bunurilor, cu respectarea rezervei succesorale legale a moștenitorilor rezervatari [4]. Este recomandat să centralizați într-un dosar accesibil actele de stare civilă în original (carte de identitate, certificate de naștere și de căsătorie), decizia de pensionare, titlurile de proprietate, contractele bancare și polițele de asigurare de viață, precum și preferințele persoanei privind organizarea înmormântării sau incinerării.

Pentru etapa ulterioară unui deces, este util să cunoașteți din timp regulile și termenele oficiale:

  • Ajutorul de deces și pensia de urmaș se solicită prin instituția Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (la casa teritorială de pensii din raza de domiciliu). Ajutorul de deces se acordă unei singure persoane care prezintă certificatul de deces în original și dovada suportării cheltuielilor funerare, iar soțul supraviețuitor și copiii îndreptățiți pot solicita pensia de urmaș în condițiile Legii nr. 360/2023 [6].
  • Dezbaterea moștenirii se realizează prin procedura succesorală notarială la un notar public din circumscripția judecătoriei ultimului domiciliu al persoanei decedate, dacă moștenitorii se înțeleg asupra cotelor și bunurilor [4].
  • Conform Codului fiscal aplicat de autoritatea fiscală Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală, moștenitorii sunt scutiți de impozitul pe transferul proprietății imobiliare dacă succesiunea este dezbătută și finalizată în termen de 2 ani de la data decesului; după depășirea termenului de 2 ani, se datorează un impozit de 1% din valoarea masei succesorale imobiliare, reținut de notar la eliberarea certificatului de moștenitor [7].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Austria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Austria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Austria: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Austria has been diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or incurable illness, organizing medical care as well as legal and financial arrangements early helps safeguard the ill person's wishes while full decision-making capacity still exists. Below are the five main official and practical steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Home Nursing, Hospice Services, and Care Allowance
steps.html:
The first step is taken through the treating medical team at the hospital or the general practitioner (Hausärztin or Hausarzt) to assess pain and symptom management needs and arrange a referral to specialist care:

  • Specialist palliative and hospice care: Because hospice and palliative care in Austria is organized by federal province (Bundesland), the national umbrella organization Dachverband HOSPIZ Österreich (Austrian Hospice Association) provides an official directory of all regional associations, mobile palliative teams (mobile Palliativteams), hospital palliative wards (Palliativstationen), and inpatient hospices (stationäre Hospize) [1].
  • Care allowance (Pflegegeld) application: At the same time, submit an immediate application for Pflegegeld (care allowance, or an upgrade of an existing care level) to the competent pension insurance institution, in most cases the Pensionsversicherungsanstalt (PVA, Pension Insurance Institution) [2]. Pflegegeld is divided into seven levels to help cover care-related expenses; for serious illness, attach current medical reports and the hospital discharge summary directly to accelerate the assessment [2].
  • Continuation of proceedings after death: If the ill person has already submitted an application before death or if Pflegegeld was due, caregiving relatives may continue the procedure within six months after the death [2].

steps.title: Prepare a Written Advance Directive under the Advance Directives Act and an Emergency Plan
steps.html:
While the ill person has full decision-making capacity, they can execute a written advance directive (Patientenverfügung) under the Advance Directives Act (Patientenverfügungs-Gesetz, PatVG) to specify in advance which medical measures (such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or artificial nutrition) they refuse in a terminal condition if they can no longer express their wishes later [3]. Austrian law distinguishes between two forms, as explained on the official government portal oesterreich.gv.at [3]:

  • Binding advance directive (Verbindliche Patientenverfügung): Legally binding on physicians. It requires comprehensive medical counseling (including documentation of why the ill person accurately assesses the consequences of refusing treatment) followed by personal execution with the date before a notary (Notarin or Notar), an attorney (Rechtsanwältin or Rechtsanwalt), a patient advocacy office (Patientenanwaltschaft of the respective province), or an adult protection association (Erwachsenenschutzverein) [3]. It is generally valid for eight years (five years under older rules) and remains binding indefinitely if the person loses decision-making capacity in the meantime [3].
  • Non-binding (noteworthy) advance directive (Nicht verbindliche / beachtliche Patientenverfügung): If the document does not meet all formal requirements for a binding directive, the medical team must still consider it when determining the patient's presumed wishes [3].
  • Registration and emergency access: Once executed, the Patientenverfügung can be registered in the Advance Directives Register (Patientenverfügungsregister) of the Austrian notariat or bar association as well as in the Electronic Health Record (Elektronische Gesundheitsakte, ELGA) so emergency services and hospitals can access it immediately [3].

steps.title: Execute a Legally Valid Enduring Power of Attorney in the ÖZVV and Bank Mandates While Capacity Exists
steps.html:
Whereas an advance directive refuses specific medical treatments, an enduring power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht) allows your family member to appoint one or more trusted representatives to make decisions on their behalf in medical matters, choice of residence and care facility, dealings with authorities, and financial and asset management if decision-making capacity is later lost [4]:

  • Formal execution requirements: A Vorsorgevollmacht must be drawn up in writing and in person before a notary, an attorney, or (provided no real estate, businesses, or complex assets are involved) an adult protection association (Erwachsenenschutzverein) [4].
  • Registration and activation in the ÖZVV: Upon execution, the Vorsorgevollmacht is registered in the Austrian Central Representation Register (Österreichisches Zentrales Vertretungsverzeichnis, ÖZVV), maintained by the Österreichische Notariatskammer (Austrian Chamber of Civil-Law Notaries) [4][5]. In practice, the Vorsorgevollmacht only takes effect once the contingency event (Vorsorgefall - the actual loss of decision-making capacity) is also recorded in the ÖZVV on the basis of a medical certificate [4][5].
  • Dedicated bank mandates: So that relatives can already handle everyday transfers or pay bills while the ill person still has decision-making capacity, a separate bank and account power of attorney (Bank- und Kontovollmacht, optionally valid beyond death) should also be signed directly at the person's bank using the bank's own forms.

steps.title: Apply for Family Hospice Leave, Care Leave, and Care Leave Allowance for Relatives
steps.html:
Employed close relatives have statutory rights to take leave or reduce working hours to care for a dying relative and receive financial support during that period [6]:

  • Family hospice leave (Familienhospizkarenz): Under Section 14a of the Employment Contract Law Adaptation Act (Arbeitsvertragsrechts-Anpassungsgesetz, AVRAG), close relatives have a legal entitlement to full leave (Familienhospizkarenz) or part-time hours (Familienhospizteilzeit) to accompany a dying close relative [6]. It can initially be taken for up to three months and extended if needed to a total of up to six months per case; the employer must be notified in writing at least five working days before the start (and ten working days before an extension) [6]. Special protection against dismissal as well as health and pension insurance coverage apply during this leave [6].
  • Care leave allowance (Pflegekarenzgeld): To bridge the loss of income during Familienhospizkarenz or agreed care leave (Pflegekarenz), caregivers have a legal entitlement to Pflegekarenzgeld, which is applied for through the federal authority Sozialministeriumservice (Ministry of Social Affairs Service, regional office of the respective province) [6]. The amount is based on the basic unemployment benefit rate (55 percent of daily net income plus any child supplements), and in cases of financial hardship an additional grant from the Family Hospice Leave Hardship Fund (Familienhospizkarenz-Härteausgleichsfonds) can be requested via the Sozialministeriumservice [6].

steps.title: Prepare the Will, Beneficiary Designations, Vital Documents, and Future Probate Proceedings
steps.html:
While full testamentary capacity exists, your family member should review their estate arrangements and organize essential personal records for the statutory procedures that follow a death in Austria:

  • Will and essential documents: Check whether a valid will (Testament - either handwritten and signed throughout, or signed before three simultaneous witnesses, or executed before a notary) exists and whether it is registered in the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister) of the Österreichische Notariatskammer [5]. Gather original vital documents (birth certificate, proof of citizenship, marriage or registered partnership certificate, life or funeral insurance policies, and written burial or cremation wishes).
  • Automatic probate proceedings (Verlassenschaftsverfahren): After a death is registered, the civil registry office (Standesamt) automatically forwards the death notice to the competent district court (Bezirksgericht) of the last place of residence, whereupon the assigned notary acting as court commissioner (Gerichtskommissär) initiates the estate inquiry (Todesfallaufnahme) ex officio and contacts the relatives [7]. Powers of attorney expire upon death, and sole bank accounts of the deceased generally become part of the frozen estate until the court issues the decree of distribution (Einantwortung) [5][7].
  • Survivor pensions and health insurance: A widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenpension) is not paid automatically and must be actively claimed from the competent pension insurer such as the Pensionsversicherungsanstalt; if filed within six months of the date of death, the pension is paid retroactively from the day after death [8]. Deregistration from statutory health insurance (such as the Austrian Health Insurance Fund, Österreichische Gesundheitskasse) generally takes place automatically via the umbrella association of social insurance institutions once the death certificate is issued.

de.title: Vorsorge & Administration bei schwerer Erkrankung in Österreich: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensverkürzender Erkrankung in Österreich: Palliativ- und Hospizversorgung, Patientenverfügung, Vorsorgevollmacht, Pflegezeit und Nachlassordnung.
de.introHtml: Wenn bei Ihrem Familienangehörigen in Österreich eine fortgeschrittene, lebensverkürzende oder unheilbare Erkrankung diagnostiziert wurde, hilft eine frühzeitige Organisation der medizinischen Betreuung sowie der rechtlichen und finanziellen Vorsorge dabei, den Willen der erkrankten Person zu sichern, solange volle Entscheidungsfähigkeit besteht. Nachfolgend finden Sie die fünf zentralen offiziellen und praktischen Schritte in der empfohlenen Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Spezialisierte Palliativversorgung, Hauskrankenpflege, Hospizangebote und Pflegegeld koordinieren
steps.html:
Der erste Schritt erfolgt über das behandelnde Ärzteteam im Krankenhaus oder die Hausärztin beziehungsweise den Hausarzt: Lassen Sie den Bedarf an spezialisierter Schmerz- und Symptomlinderung abklären und eine Zuweisung an ein mobiles Palliativteam, einen mobilen Pflegedienst, eine Palliativstation oder ein stationäres Hospiz veranlassen. Da die Hospiz- und Palliativversorgung in Österreich nach Bundesländern organisiert ist, bietet die bundesweite Koordinationsstelle Dachverband HOSPIZ Österreich ein Verzeichnis aller regionalen Landesverbände, mobilen Palliativteams, Palliativstationen und stationären Hospize [1].

Parallel dazu sollte umgehend ein Antrag auf Pflegegeld (oder auf Erhöhung einer bestehenden Pflegegeldstufe) beim zuständigen Pensionsversicherungsträger, in den meisten Fällen bei der Anstalt Pensionsversicherungsanstalt (PVA), gestellt werden [2]. Das Pflegegeld ist in sieben Stufen unterteilt und dient der pauschalen Abgeltung pflegebedingter Mehraufwendungen; bei schwerer Erkrankung sollten aktuelle ärztliche Befunde und der Entlassungsbericht des Krankenhauses direkt beigelegt werden, um die Begutachtung zu beschleunigen [2]. Falls die erkrankte Person vor dem Tod bereits einen Antrag gestellt hat oder Pflegegeld fällig war, können pflegende Angehörige das Verfahren innerhalb von sechs Monaten nach dem Tod fortführen [2].

steps.title: Schriftliche Patientenverfügung nach dem Patientenverfügungs-Gesetz und Notfallplan erstellen
steps.html:
Solange die erkrankte Person voll entscheidungsfähig ist, kann sie in einer schriftlichen Patientenverfügung nach dem Patientenverfügungs-Gesetz (PatVG) im Voraus festlegen, welche konkreten medizinischen Maßnahmen (etwa künstliche Beatmung, Reanimation oder künstliche Ernährung) sie in einer aussichtslosen Krankheitssituation ablehnt, falls sie sich später nicht mehr selbst äußern kann [3]. Das österreichische Recht unterscheidet dabei zwei Formen, wie auf dem Amtsportal oesterreich.gv.at erläutert wird [3]:

  • Verbindliche Patientenverfügung: Sie ist für Ärztinnen und Ärzte rechtlich unmittelbar bindend. Voraussetzung ist eine umfassende ärztliche Aufklärung (inklusive Dokumentation, warum die erkrankte Person die Folgen zutreffend einschätzt) sowie die anschließende persönliche Errichtung unter Angabe des Datums vor einer Notarin oder einem Notar, einer Rechtsanwältin oder einem Rechtsanwalt, einer Patientenvertretung (Patientenanwaltschaft des jeweiligen Bundeslandes) oder einem Erwachsenenschutzverein [3]. Sie gilt grundsätzlich für acht Jahre (bzw. nach älterer Rechtslage fünf Jahre) und bleibt darüber hinaus verbindlich, wenn die betroffene Person zwischenzeitlich ihre Entscheidungsfähigkeit verliert [3].
  • Nicht verbindliche (beachtliche) Patientenverfügung: Erfüllt das Dokument nicht sämtliche Formvorschriften, muss es vom Behandlungsteam dennoch zur Ermittlung des mutmaßlichen Patientenwillens herangezogen werden [3].

Nach der Errichtung kann die Patientenverfügung im Patientenverfügungsregister des österreichischen Notariats oder der Rechtsanwälte sowie in der Elektronischen Gesundheitsakte (ELGA) hinterlegt werden, damit Rettungsdienste und Krankenanstalten im Notfall sofort darauf zugreifen können [3].

steps.title: Rechtsgültige Vorsorgevollmacht im ÖZVV und Bankvollmachten bei voller Entscheidungsfähigkeit errichten
steps.html:
Während eine Patientenverfügung bestimmte Behandlungen ablehnt, bestimmt Ihr Familienangehöriger mit einer Vorsorgevollmacht eine oder mehrere Vertrauenspersonen, die bei einem späteren Verlust der Entscheidungsfähigkeit stellvertretend in medizinischen Fragen, bei der Wahl des Wohn- und Pflegeortes, gegenüber Behörden sowie in Finanz- und Vermögensangelegenheiten entscheiden dürfen [4]. Eine Vorsorgevollmacht muss schriftlich und höchstpersönlich vor einer Notarin oder einem Notar, einer Rechtsanwältin oder einem Rechtsanwalt oder (sofern keine Immobilien, Unternehmen oder komplexen Vermögenswerte betroffen sind) vor einem Erwachsenenschutzverein errichtet werden [4].

Die Vorsorgevollmacht wird bei der Errichtung im Österreichischen Zentralen Vertretungsverzeichnis (ÖZVV) registriert, das von der Standesvertretung Österreichische Notariatskammer geführt wird [4][5]. Wichtig für die Praxis: Die Vorsorgevollmacht tritt erst in Kraft, wenn der sogenannte Vorsorgefall (der tatsächliche Verlust der Entscheidungsfähigkeit) aufgrund eines ärztlichen Zeugnisses ebenfalls im ÖZVV eingetragen wird [4][5]. Damit Angehörige bereits jetzt im Alltag Überweisungen tätigen oder Rechnungen begleichen können, während die erkrankte Person noch entscheidungsfähig ist, sollte zusätzlich direkt bei der Hausbank eine gesonderte Bank- und Kontovollmacht (auf Wunsch als über den Tod hinaus geltende Vollmacht) auf den Formularen des Kreditinstituts unterzeichnet werden.

steps.title: Familienhospizkarenz, Pflegekarenz und Pflegekarenzgeld für Angehörige beantragen
steps.html:
Berufstätige nahe Angehörige haben nach § 14a des Arbeitsvertragsrechts-Anpassungsgesetzes (AVRAG) einen Rechtsanspruch auf Familienhospizkarenz (gänzliche Dienstfreistellung) oder Familienhospizteilzeit (Herabsetzung oder Änderung der Arbeitszeit) zur Sterbebegleitung eines nahen Angehörigen [6]. Diese Maßnahme kann zunächst für bis zu drei Monate in Anspruch genommen und bei Bedarf auf insgesamt bis zu sechs Monate pro Anlassfall verlängert werden; sie ist dem Arbeitgeber schriftlich mindestens fünf Arbeitstage vor Beginn (bei Verlängerung zehn Arbeitstage vorher) bekanntzugeben [6]. Während der Familienhospizkarenz besteht ein besonderer Kündigungs- und Entlassungsschutz sowie eine kranken- und pensionsversicherungsrechtliche Absicherung [6].

Zur finanziellen Überbrückung des Einkommensentfalls besteht während der Familienhospizkarenz oder einer vereinbarten Pflegekarenz ein Rechtsanspruch auf Pflegekarenzgeld, das bei der Bundesbehörde Sozialministeriumservice (Landesstelle des jeweiligen Bundeslandes) beantragt wird [6]. Die Höhe des Pflegekarenzgeldes orientiert sich am Grundbetrag des Arbeitslosengeldes (55 Prozent des täglichen Nettoeinkommens zuzüglich allfälliger Kinderzuschläge), und bei finanzieller Notlage kann über das Sozialministeriumservice zusätzlich ein Zuschuss aus dem Familienhospizkarenz-Härteausgleichsfonds beantragt werden [6].

steps.title: Testament, Bezugsberechtigungen, Personenstandsdokumente und das spätere Verlassenschaftsverfahren vorbereiten
steps.html:
Solange volle Testierfähigkeit besteht, sollte Ihr Familienangehöriger prüfen, ob ein formgültiges Testament (eigenhändig geschrieben und unterschrieben oder fremdhändig vor drei gleichzeitigen Zeugen bzw. notariell errichtet) vorliegt und ob dieses im Zentralen Testamentsregister der Einrichtung Österreichische Notariatskammer registriert ist [5]. Stellen Sie außerdem die wichtigsten Originaldokumente (Geburtsurkunde, Staatsbürgerschaftsnachweis, Heirats- oder Partnerschaftsurkunde, Polizzen von Lebens- oder Sterbeversicherungen sowie schriftliche Bestattungswünsche zur Erd- oder Feuerbestattung) geordnet zusammen.

Für die spätere Abwicklung nach einem Todesfall gelten in Österreich folgende gesetzliche Abläufe:

  • Automatisches Verlassenschaftsverfahren: Nach der Beurkundung des Sterbefalls übermittelt das Standesamt die Sterbemeldung automatisch an das zuständige Bezirksgericht des letzten Wohnsitzes, woraufhin die zuständige Notarin oder der zuständige Notar als Gerichtskommissär von Amts wegen die Todesfallaufnahme einleitet und die Angehörigen kontaktiert [7]. Vorsorgevollmachten erlöschen mit dem Tod, und Bankkonten der verstorbenen Person werden bis zur gerichtlichen Einantwortung grundsätzlich Teil der Verlassenschaft [5][7].
  • Hinterbliebenenpensionen und Krankenversicherung: Eine Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenpension wird nicht automatisch ausgezahlt, sondern muss aktiv beim zuständigen Pensionsversicherungsträger wie der Anstalt Pensionsversicherungsanstalt beantragt werden; erfolgt der Antrag innerhalb von sechs Monaten ab dem Todestag, gebührt die Pension rückwirkend ab dem Tag nach dem Tod [8]. Die Abmeldung bei der gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung (etwa bei der Österreichischen Gesundheitskasse) erfolgt nach der standesamtlichen Sterbebeurkundung im Regelfall automatisch über den Dachverband der Sozialversicherungsträger.

de.closingQuestion: Um diese Hinweise auf Ihre Situation abzustimmen: In welchem österreichischen Bundesland wird die erkrankte Person betreut, und besteht bereits eine Pflegegeldstufe oder eine Vorsorgevollmacht?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Switzerland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Switzerland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Switzerland: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Switzerland has been diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or incurable illness, early planning of medical care as well as legal and administrative arrangements ensures that the ill person's wishes are respected while full capacity of judgment (Urteilsfähigkeit) still exists. Below are the five main official and practical steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care, Spitex Home Nursing, and Hospice Services
steps.html:
The first step is taken through the treating medical team at the hospital (Spital) or the general practitioner (Hausärztin or Hausarzt) to assess palliative pain and symptom management needs and issue a medical nursing prescription (Pflegeverordnung):

  • Home and inpatient palliative networks: For care at home, local Spitex (home care nursing) services work alongside specialized mobile palliative services (Brückendienste) to provide nursing and support. Because healthcare structures in Switzerland are organized by canton, the regional sections of the specialist association palliative.ch (Swiss Association for Palliative Medicine, Care and Support) help families locate mobile palliative teams, hospital palliative units, and inpatient hospices in the respective canton [1].
  • Mandatory health insurance coverage: Under a physician's prescription, compulsory basic health insurance (Obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung, OKP) reimburses medical and nursing palliative care services provided at home (by Spitex), in hospital, or in a nursing home in accordance with the Healthcare Benefits Ordinance (Krankenpflege-Leistungsverordnung, KLV), as explained by the federal authority Bundesamt für Gesundheit (Federal Office of Public Health) [2]. Clarify early with the care team and health insurer (Krankenkasse) which basic care costs and any cantonal residual financing or hospice daily rates are covered in the canton of residence [2].

steps.title: Prepare a Written Advance Directive under Art. 370 et seq. ZGB and an Emergency Plan
steps.html:
While the ill person retains capacity of judgment, they can establish a binding written advance directive (Patientenverfügung) under Articles 370 et seq. of the Swiss Civil Code (Schweizerisches Zivilgesetzbuch, ZGB) specifying which medical measures (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition) they consent to or refuse if they later become incapable of judgment [3]:

  • Appointing a therapeutic representative: The directive should also designate at least one trusted representative (plus an alternate) to inform the medical team of the patient's presumed wishes and make healthcare decisions on their behalf in an emergency [3].
  • Formal validity and official templates: To be valid under Swiss law, the Patientenverfügung must be in writing, dated, and personally signed by the ill person; it does not need to be handwritten in its entirety, meaning recognized standard forms can be used [3][4]. Proven short and comprehensive templates with guidance are provided by the medical association Verbindung der Schweizer Ärztinnen und Ärzte FMH (Swiss Medical Association) and the humanitarian organization Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz (Swiss Red Cross) [3][4].
  • Distribution and emergency access: Provide copies of the signed Patientenverfügung and a medical emergency plan (covering symptom management at home) to the general practitioner, Spitex, and the representative, and record a note on the health insurance card (Versichertenkarte) or in the electronic patient record (elektronisches Patientendossier, EPD) [3].

steps.title: Execute a Legally Valid Advance Care Mandate under Art. 360 et seq. ZGB and Bank Mandates While Capacity Exists
steps.html:
Whereas an advance directive covers purely medical treatments, an advance care mandate (Vorsorgeauftrag) under Articles 360 et seq. ZGB governs personal care (everyday living and housing arrangements), financial affairs (income, assets, payment transactions), and legal representation before authorities, banks, and insurers in the event of future incapacity of judgment [4][5]. Without a Vorsorgeauftrag (and where the statutory representation rights of spouses or registered partners do not suffice for extraordinary asset management), the competent Child and Adult Protection Authority (Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde, KESB) will examine appointing an official deputyship (Beistandschaft) if incapacity occurs [4][5]. Under Article 361 ZGB, strict formal requirements apply [4][5]:

  • Holographic execution (Eigenhändige Errichtung): The entire text must be handwritten from beginning to end, include the place and date, and be personally signed [4][5].
  • Public authentication (Öffentliche Beurkundung): If the ill person can no longer write the entire text by hand due to illness, the Vorsorgeauftrag must be publicly notarized by an authenticating official (Urkundsperson / notary) [4][5].
  • KESB validation and bank powers of attorney: The Vorsorgeauftrag takes formal legal effect only once incapacity of judgment actually occurs and the competent KESB examines and validates the document [4]. The storage location of the Vorsorgeauftrag can be registered with the civil registry office (Zivilstandsamt) in the civil status register [4][5]. So that relatives can handle banking and bill payments while the person still has capacity of judgment, a separate bank power of attorney (Bank- und Kontovollmacht) should also be signed directly with the Swiss banks on their own forms.

steps.title: Use Paid Caregiver Leave under the Code of Obligations, Helplessness Allowance, and Respite Services
steps.html:
Employed relatives in Switzerland can draw on statutory leave provisions, disability/care allowances, and cantonal respite support [6][7]:

  • Paid caregiver leave (Betreuungsurlaub): Under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 329g OR), employed relatives are entitled to paid leave to care for a family member or life partner with a health impairment, as outlined by the federal authority Bundesamt für Sozialversicherungen (Federal Social Insurance Office) [6]. This short-term caregiver leave covers up to three working days per event and at most ten working days per service year (in addition, parents caring for a severely ill minor child are entitled under Art. 329h OR to 14 weeks of caregiver leave compensated via the income compensation scheme, Erwerbsersatzordnung) [6].
  • Helplessness allowance (Hilflosenentschädigung): If the ill person permanently requires third-party assistance or personal supervision for everyday activities (such as dressing, personal hygiene, eating, or mobility), check eligibility for a Hilflosenentschädigung under Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AHV) or Disability Insurance (IV) with the cantonal compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) or IV office; official fact sheets and forms are provided by the Informationsstelle AHV/IV (AHV/IV Information Center) [7]. The allowance is independent of income and wealth but subject to statutory waiting periods (generally six months of uninterrupted helplessness under AHV, or one year under IV) [7].
  • Immediate home respite: For immediate relief at home, cantonal sections of the Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz, the Cancer League (Krebsliga), and municipal relief services offer hourly care and visiting services [4].

steps.title: Prepare the Will, Pension Beneficiary Nominations (1st and 2nd Pillars), Vital Documents, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
While full capacity of judgment exists, the ill person can establish their estate plan by executing a last will (Testament under Art. 498 et seq. ZGB - either handwritten, dated, and signed in full, or publicly notarized) or a notarized inheritance contract (Erbvertrag) while respecting statutory forced heirship shares (Pflichtteile), and prepare for key Swiss pension and probate rules:

  • Vital documents and 1st Pillar (AHV): Gather key documents (family record book or certificate, Familienbüchlein / Familienausweis, AHV insurance card, occupational pension statement, Pillar 3a/3b policies, and written funeral wishes kept separate from the will). After a death, claims for survivors' pensions (Hinterlassenenrenten - widow's, widower's, and orphan's pensions) must be filed with the competent compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) where the deceased last paid AHV contributions or drew a pension, as documented by the Informationsstelle AHV/IV [8].
  • 2nd Pillar (Occupational Pension / Pensionskasse) and Pillar 3a: Review the pension fund regulations (Vorsorgereglement) as well as vested benefits and Pillar 3a foundations during the person's lifetime. Many pension funds require a written beneficiary declaration (Begünstigungserklärung / support agreement) for unmarried partners that must be submitted to the Pensionskasse while the insured person is still alive.
  • Certificate of inheritance and 3-month disclaimer deadline: Following a death, the competent cantonal court or inheritance office (Erbschaftsamt) at the last place of residence issues the certificate of inheritance (Erbenbescheinigung / Erbschein) upon application so heirs can jointly access estate accounts, as described on the official Swiss authorities portal ch.ch [9]. If the estate is over-indebted, the statutory deadline to disclaim the inheritance (Ausschlagung der Erbschaft under Art. 567 ZGB) is strictly three months from learning of the death; anyone considering disclaiming must not order an Erbenbescheinigung or interfere in estate affairs beforehand, and may instead request a public inventory (öffentliches Inventar) or an information-only certificate to inspect assets and liabilities [9].

de.title: Vorsorge & Administration bei schwerer Erkrankung in Schweiz: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensverkürzender Erkrankung in Schweiz: Palliativ- und Hospizversorgung, Patientenverfügung, Vorsorgevollmacht, Pflegezeit und Nachlassordnung.
de.introHtml: Wenn bei Ihrem Familienangehörigen in der Schweiz eine fortgeschrittene, lebensverkürzende oder unheilbare Krankheit diagnostiziert wurde, ermöglicht eine frühzeitige Planung der medizinischen Betreuung sowie der rechtlichen und administrativen Vorsorge, dass die Wünsche der erkrankten Person gewahrt bleiben, solange volle Urteilsfähigkeit besteht. Nachfolgend finden Sie die fünf wichtigsten offiziellen und praktischen Schritte in der empfohlenen Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Spezialisierte Palliative Care, Spitex-Pflege zu Hause und Hospizangebote koordinieren
steps.html:
Der erste Schritt führt über das behandelnde Ärzteteam im Spital oder die Hausärztin beziehungsweise den Hausarzt: Lassen Sie den Bedarf an palliativer Schmerz- und Symptomlinderung abklären und eine ärztliche Pflegeverordnung ausstellen. Für die Betreuung zu Hause übernimmt die lokale Spitex in Zusammenarbeit mit spezialisierten mobilen Palliativdiensten (Brückendiensten) die Pflege und Begleitung. Da die Versorgungsstrukturen in der Schweiz kantonal organisiert sind, helfen die regionalen Sektionen der Fachgesellschaft palliative.ch (Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Palliative Medizin, Pflege und Begleitung) dabei, mobile Palliativteams, Palliativstationen in Spitälern und stationäre Hospize im jeweiligen Kanton zu finden [1].

Die obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung (OKP, Grundversicherung) vergütet auf ärztliche Anordnung hin die medizinischen und pflegerischen Leistungen der Palliative Care zu Hause (durch die Spitex), im Spital oder im Pflegeheim gemäss der Krankenpflege-Leistungsverordnung (KLV), wie die Bundesbehörde Bundesamt für Gesundheit erläutert [2]. Klären Sie mit dem Pflegeteam und der Krankenkasse frühzeitig ab, welche Kosten der Grundpflege und allfälliger kantonaler Restfinanzierungen oder Hospiz-Tagessätze im Wohnkanton übernommen werden [2].

steps.title: Schriftliche Patientenverfügung nach Art. 370 ff. ZGB und Notfallplan erstellen
steps.html:
Solange die erkrankte Person urteilsfähig ist, kann sie in einer schriftlichen Patientenverfügung nach Art. 370 ff. des Schweizerischen Zivilgesetzbuches (ZGB) verbindlich festlegen, welchen medizinischen Massnahmen (beispielsweise Reanimation, künstliche Beatmung oder künstliche Ernährung) sie zustimmt oder welche sie ablehnt, falls sie später urteilsunfähig wird [3]. Zudem sollte darin mindestens eine Vertrauensperson (sowie eine Ersatzperson) bezeichnet werden, die das Behandlungsteam über den mutmasslichen Willen informiert und im Ernstfall stellvertretend entscheidet [3].

Damit die Patientenverfügung nach Schweizer Recht gültig ist, muss sie schriftlich verfasst, datiert und von der erkrankten Person eigenhändig unterschrieben werden; eine komplette Handschriftlichkeit ist für die Patientenverfügung nicht erforderlich, sodass anerkannte Formularvorlagen genutzt werden können [3][4]. Bewährte Kurz- und Ausführlich-Vorlagen inklusive Wegleitung stellen unter anderem der Berufsverband Verbindung der Schweizer Ärztinnen und Ärzte FMH sowie das Hilfswerk Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz zur Verfügung [3][4]. Übergeben Sie Kopien der unterschriebenen Patientenverfügung und eines ärztlichen Notfallplans (etwa zur Symptombehandlung zu Hause) an die Hausärztin oder den Hausarzt, die Spitex und die Vertretungsperson und hinterlegen Sie einen Hinweis auf der Versichertenkarte oder im elektronischen Patientendossier (EPD) [3].

steps.title: Rechtsgültigen Vorsorgeauftrag nach Art. 360 ff. ZGB und Bankvollmachten bei voller Urteilsfähigkeit errichten
steps.html:
Während die Patientenverfügung rein medizinische Behandlungen betrifft, regelt der Vorsorgeauftrag nach Art. 360 ff. ZGB die Personensorge (Alltags- und Wohnangelegenheiten), die Vermögenssorge (Einkommen, Vermögen, Zahlungsverkehr) und die Vertretung im Rechtsverkehr gegenüber Behörden, Banken und Versicherungen für den Fall einer künftigen Urteilsunfähigkeit [4][5]. Ohne Vorsorgeauftrag (und soweit das gesetzliche Vertretungsrecht von Ehegatten oder eingetragenen Partnern für ausserordentliche Vermögensverwaltung nicht ausreicht) prüft die zuständige Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde (KESB) bei Urteilsunfähigkeit die Errichtung einer behördlichen Beistandschaft [4][5].

Für den Vorsorgeauftrag gelten nach Art. 361 ZGB strenge gesetzliche Formvorschriften [4][5]:

  • Eigenhändige Errichtung: Der gesamte Text muss von Anfang bis Ende vollständig von Hand geschrieben, mit Ort und Datum versehen und eigenhändig unterschrieben werden [4][5].
  • Öffentliche Beurkundung: Wenn die erkrankte Person den Text krankheitsbedingt nicht mehr vollständig selbst von Hand schreiben kann, muss der Vorsorgeauftrag zwingend durch eine Urkundsperson (Notariat) öffentlich beurkundet werden [4][5].

Der Vorsorgeauftrag entfaltet seine formelle Wirkung erst, wenn tatsächlich Urteilsunfähigkeit eintritt und die zuständige Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde (KESB) das Dokument prüft und validiert (in Kraft setzt) [4]. Der Aufbewahrungsort des Vorsorgeauftrags kann beim Zivilstandsamt im Personenstandsregister eingetragen werden [4][5]. Damit Angehörige bereits während bestehender Urteilsfähigkeit Bankgeschäfte und Zahlungen erledigen können, sollte zusätzlich direkt bei den Schweizer Banken eine Bank- und Kontovollmacht auf den bankeigenen Formularen erteilt werden.

steps.title: Bezahlten Betreuungsurlaub nach Obligationenrecht, Hilflosenentschädigung und Entlastungsangebote nutzen
steps.html:
Erwerbstätige Angehörige haben nach dem Schweizer Obligationenrecht (Art. 329g OR) Anspruch auf bezahlten Betreuungsurlaub für die notwendige Betreuung eines Familienmitglieds oder der Lebenspartnerin beziehungsweise des Lebenspartners mit gesundheitlicher Beeinträchtigung, wie die Fachbehörde Bundesamt für Sozialversicherungen darlegt [6]. Dieser kurzzeitige Betreuungsurlaub umfasst bis zu drei Arbeitstage pro Ereignis und höchstens zehn Arbeitstage pro Dienstjahr (bei der Betreuung schwer kranker minderjähriger Kinder durch die Eltern besteht darüber hinaus nach Art. 329h OR ein über die Erwerbsersatzordnung entschädigter 14-wöchiger Betreuungsurlaub) [6].

Ist die erkrankte Person bei alltäglichen Lebensverrichtungen (wie Ankleiden, Körperpflege, Essen oder Fortbewegung) dauerhaft auf Hilfe Dritter oder persönliche Überwachung angewiesen, sollte bei der kantonalen Ausgleichskasse oder IV-Stelle eine Hilflosenentschädigung der AHV oder IV geprüft werden, zu der die offizielle Stelle Informationsstelle AHV/IV Merkblätter und Anmeldeformulare bereitstellt [7]. Die Hilflosenentschädigung ist einkommens- und vermögensunabhängig, setzt jedoch im AHV- und IV-Bereich gesetzliche Wartefristen voraus (in der AHV in der Regel sechs Monate ununterbrochene Hilflosigkeit, in der IV ein Jahr) [7]. Für die sofortige Entlastung zu Hause bieten kantonale Sektionen des Schweizerischen Roten Kreuzes, die Krebsliga und kommunale Entlastungsdienste stundenweise Betreuung und Besuchsdienste an [4].

steps.title: Testament, Vorsorgebegünstigungen (1. und 2. Säule), Dokumente und Nachlassregelung vorbereiten
steps.html:
Solange volle Urteilsfähigkeit besteht, kann die erkrankte Person ihre Nachlassregelung durch eine letztwillige Verfügung (Testament nach Art. 498 ff. ZGB, entweder vollständig von Hand geschrieben, datiert und unterschrieben oder öffentlich beurkundet) oder einen öffentlich beurkundeten Erbvertrag unter Beachtung der gesetzlichen Pflichtteile festhalten. Stellen Sie zudem sämtliche wichtigen Dokumente (Familienbüchlein bzw. Familienausweis, Versicherungsausweis der AHV, Vorsorgeausweis der Pensionskasse, Policen der gebundenen oder freien Vorsorge der Säule 3a/3b sowie schriftliche Bestattungswünsche außerhalb des Testaments) geordnet zusammen.

Für die administrativen Schritte bei den Vorsorgeeinrichtungen und Nachlassbehörden gelten in der Schweiz folgende zentrale Regeln:

  • 1. Säule (AHV): Nach einem Todesfall sind Ansprüche auf Hinterlassenenrenten (Witwen-, Witwer- und Waisenrenten) bei der zuständigen Ausgleichskasse anzumelden, bei der die verstorbene Person zuletzt AHV-Beiträge geleistet oder eine Rente bezogen hat; die Voraussetzungen sind bei der Stelle Informationsstelle AHV/IV dokumentiert [8].
  • 2. Säule (Berufliche Vorsorge / Pensionskasse) und Säule 3a: Prüfen Sie bereits zu Lebzeiten das Vorsorgereglement der Pensionskasse sowie von Freizügigkeits- und Säule-3a-Stiftungen. Viele Pensionskassen verlangen für unverheiratete Lebenspartnerinnen und Lebenspartner eine schriftliche Begünstigungserklärung (Unterstützungsvertrag), die zwingend noch zu Lebzeiten der versicherten Person bei der Pensionskasse eingereicht werden muss.
  • Erbenbescheinigung und 3-monatige Ausschlagungsfrist: Nach einem Todesfall stellt das zuständige kantonale Gericht oder Erbschaftsamt am letzten Wohnsitz auf Antrag die Erbenbescheinigung (Erbschein) aus, mit der Erben gemeinsam über Nachlasskonten verfügen können, wie auf dem Schweizer Behördenportal ch.ch beschrieben wird [9]. Sollte der Nachlass überschuldet sein, beträgt die gesetzliche Frist zur Ausschlagung der Erbschaft nach Art. 567 ZGB strikt 3 Monate ab Kenntnis des Todesfalls; wer das Erbe ausschlagen will, darf zuvor keine Erbenbescheinigung bestellen und sich nicht in die Nachlassangelegenheiten einmischen, sondern kann zur Prüfung der Aktiven und Passiven zunächst ein öffentliches Inventar oder eine reine Auskunftsbescheinigung verlangen [9].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Turkey: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When a family member in Turkey has been diagnosed with an advanced or life-threatening illness, completing medical care arrangements, legal representation, and administrative preparations in sequence while the ill person still has full mental capacity (ayırt etme gücü / fiil ehliyeti) both safeguards their personal wishes and simplifies the official procedures your family will face later. Below are the five main official and practical steps to follow in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care Centers and Home Health Services
steps.html:
The first step is to consult the treating specialist physician or family physician (aile hekimi) to establish a palliative care plan covering pain management, symptom control, and nutritional support:

  • Inpatient Palliative Care Centers (Palyatif Bakım Merkezleri): Operating within public training and research hospitals, state hospitals, and university hospitals under the coordination of the Sağlık Bakanlığı (Ministry of Health), palliative care wards handle inpatient admissions arranged through the relevant hospital's palliative care unit or attending physician [1]. For patients covered by social security, treatment costs in public hospital palliative care wards are covered under general health insurance (Genel Sağlık Sigortası) [1].
  • Home Health Services (Evde Sağlık Hizmetleri): If your family member's treatment and follow-up need to continue at home, you can apply by calling 444 38 33, the national call line of the Sağlık Bakanlığı Home Health Services Communication Center (Evde Sağlık Hizmetleri İletişim Merkezi) [1]. Following the application, the provincial home health coordination center and the family physician evaluate the patient and schedule regular home visits, wound dressings, catheter care, pain therapy, and renewal of medical device or medication reports (for acute medical emergencies, call the 112 Emergency Call Center directly) [1].

steps.title: Document Written Medical Consent and Treatment Preferences under the Patient Rights Regulation
steps.html:
Although Turkish law does not have a standalone living will statute with a separate central registry, the Patient Rights Regulation (Hasta Hakları Yönetmeliği, Articles 24 and 25) provides a clear legal basis for documenting treatment choices while capacity exists [2]:

  • Informed consent and refusal of treatment: Under the Hasta Hakları Yönetmeliği, the patient's informed consent (aydınlatılmış rıza) is required for every medical intervention, and a patient with decision-making capacity has the right to refuse planned or ongoing treatment or request its discontinuation by submitting a written declaration [2]. While conscious and able to make decisions, your family member can consult their attending physician to record in writing in the medical file which invasive procedures or intensive care interventions they accept or decline, as well as their palliative care preferences [1][2].
  • Designated family contacts: Clearly listing on hospital admission and palliative care medical records which family members the patient wishes to be kept informed and who should be contacted in emergencies ensures uninterrupted communication with the healthcare team [2].

steps.title: Execute a Notarial or Consular Power of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Full Capacity Exists
steps.html:
Under Turkish law, powers of attorney (vekâletname) require the principal to possess full legal capacity (fiil ehliyeti / ayırt etme gücü) at the time of execution; once a person permanently loses decision-making capacity, a notary cannot issue a power of attorney and a court-appointed guardian (vasi) must be sought through the Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [3]:

  • Notarial power of attorney in form of a deed (Düzenleme Şeklinde Vekâletname): While your family member is lucid and retains full capacity, arrange a Düzenleme Şeklinde Vekâletname at a notary public in Turkey (registered in the system of the Türkiye Noterler Birliği, Union of Turkish Public Notaries) granting specific authority for banking transactions, land registry (tapu) actions, official agency applications, and managing healthcare/care documentation [3]. In cases of advanced age or severe illness, the notary may request a same-day mental capacity report (akıl sağlığı raporu) from a state hospital or forensic medicine office so future legal validity cannot be challenged; if the patient cannot travel to the notary office, a home or hospital visit can be requested from the competent or on-duty notary [3].
  • Banking specifications and consular execution abroad: Turkish banks require a notarial power of attorney to explicitly list each permitted banking operation (such as cash withdrawals, EFT/wire transfers, and time-deposit management). If the person executing the document is abroad, powers of attorney executed by appointment via konsolosluk.gov.tr at Turkish Consulates General under the Dışişleri Bakanlığı (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) are integrated directly with notary offices in Turkey through the Union of Turkish Public Notaries Information System (TNBBS) [4].

steps.title: Apply for Inpatient Companion Rights, Incapacity Benefits, and Home Care Financial Assistance
steps.html:
Both employed caregivers and insured patients can access statutory social security benefits and social assistance programs in Turkey [5][6]:

  • Companion rights and SGK incapacity benefits: When an attending physician or medical board certifies that an inpatient companion (refakatçi) is medically necessary during hospitalization, employed family members can use companion leave entitlements under labor and civil service rules, and the Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, Social Security Institution, helpline ALO 170) covers medically necessary companion bed and meal expenses under the Healthcare Implementation Communiqué (Sağlık Uygulama Tebliği) [5]. An insured patient's own applications for temporary incapacity benefit (geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği) or disability pension (malullük aylığı) are also processed through SGK provincial directorates or the e-Devlet portal [5].
  • Home Care Assistance (Evde Bakım Yardımı): For adult patients who cannot perform daily living activities (nutrition, dressing, personal hygiene, mobility) without assistance, an application for Evde Bakım Yardımı can be submitted to Provincial Directorates or Social Service Centers of the Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı (Ministry of Family and Social Services, call center ALO 183), provided an Adult Disability Medical Board Report (Erişkinler İçin Engellilik Sağlık Kurulu Raporu) from an authorized public hospital includes the designation "Fully Dependent" (Tam Bağımlı) and household income per capita is below two-thirds of the net minimum wage [6].

steps.title: Prepare the Will, Pension/Insurance Beneficiaries, Certificate of Inheritance, and Inheritance Tax Filing
steps.html:
While possessing full mental capacity, your family member can secure their estate wishes and organize key documents for the legal steps that follow a death in Turkey:

  • Official will and document file: Under the Turkish Civil Code, an official will (resmi vasiyetname) can be executed before a notary in the presence of two witnesses; notarized wills are stored confidentially in the records of the Türkiye Noterler Birliği and notified to the civil registry (nüfus müdürlüğü) [3]. Gather private life insurance and individual pension (Bireysel Emeklilik Sistemi, BES) beneficiary records, title deeds (tapu), bank contracts, and burial or religious ceremony preferences in one accessible folder.
  • Funeral allowance and survivor pensions: Following the death of an insured person, applications for the one-time funeral allowance (cenaze ödeneği) and survivor pensions (ölüm aylığı / widow's and orphan's pensions for eligible spouses and children) are submitted to Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, ALO 170) offices or via e-Devlet [5].
  • Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı): Required after death to unfreeze bank accounts and transfer title deeds, the Mirasçılık Belgesi can be obtained from any notary public (via the Türkiye Noterler Birliği) if there is no civil registry obstacle, will, or foreign element, or otherwise from the Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [3]. Powers of attorney granted during lifetime generally terminate upon death, and bank accounts remain blocked until the Mirasçılık Belgesi and tax clearance certificate (vergi ilişiksiz yazısı) are presented.
  • Inheritance and Transfer Tax Return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi): If the death occurs in Turkey and the heirs are in Turkey, filing a Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi with the Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (Revenue Administration, via the tax office or Digital Tax Office, Dijital Vergi Dairesi) within four months from the date of death is mandatory by law (extended to six or eight months if the death or heirs are abroad) [7].

tr.title: Türkiye'de İleri Evre Hastalık ve Hukuki/İdari Hazırlık: 5 Adımlı Resmi Rehber
tr.cardSummary: Türkiye'de ağır veya ileri evre hastalık sürecinde 5 adımlı resmi rehber: palyatif bakım ve evde sağlık hizmetleri, tıbbi irade beyanı, noter vekaletnameleri, bakım destekleri ve vasiyetname planlaması.
tr.introHtml: Türkiye'de bulunan aile yakınınıza ileri evre veya yaşamı tehdit eden ciddi bir hastalık teşhisi konulduğunda, hasta yakınınızın ayırt etme gücü (fiil ehliyeti) tam iken tıbbi bakım, hukuki temsil ve idari hazırlıkları sırasıyla tamamlamak hem kendisinin tercihlerini güvence altına alır hem de ailenizin sonraki süreçlerde karşılaşacağı işlemleri kolaylaştırır. Aşağıda sırasıyla izlenmesi gereken beş ana resmi ve pratik adım yer almaktadır.

steps.title: Uzman palyatif bakım merkezleri ve evde sağlık hizmetlerinin koordine edilmesi
steps.html:
İlk adım, tedaviyi yürüten uzman hekim veya aile hekimi ile görüşerek ağrı yönetimi, semptom kontrolü ve beslenme desteği için palyatif bakım planlaması yapmaktır. Türkiye'de kamu eğitim ve araştırma hastaneleri, devlet hastaneleri ve üniversite hastaneleri bünyesinde faaliyet gösteren Palyatif Bakım Merkezleri (servisleri), Sağlık Bakanlığı koordinasyonunda hizmet verir ve yatış işlemleri ilgili hastanenin palyatif bakım birimi veya müdavi hekimi tarafından düzenlenir [1]. Sosyal güvencesi bulunan hastaların kamu hastanelerindeki palyatif bakım servislerinde gördükleri tedavi giderleri genel sağlık sigortası kapsamında karşılanır [1].

Hasta yakınınızın tedavisinin ve takibinin ev ortamında sürdürülmesi gerekiyorsa, Sağlık Bakanlığı Evde Sağlık Hizmetleri İletişim Merkezi'nin ulusal çağrı hattı olan 444 38 33 numarası aranarak başvuru yapılabilir [1]. Başvuru sonrasında il evde sağlık koordinasyon merkezi ve aile hekimi hastayı değerlendirerek düzenli ev ziyaretlerini, pansuman, kateter bakımı, ağrı tedavisi ve tıbbi cihaz/ilaç raporlarının yenilenmesi süreçlerini planlar (acil tıbbi durumlarda ise doğrudan 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi aranmalıdır) [1].

steps.title: Hasta Hakları Yönetmeliği kapsamında yazılı tıbbi onam ve tedavi tercihlerinin belgelenmesi
steps.html:
Türk hukukunda ayrı bir merkezi sicile kaydedilen bağımsız bir tıbbi vasiyet (yaşam vasiyeti) kanunu bulunmamakla birlikte, Hasta Hakları Yönetmeliği (Madde 24 ve Madde 25) uyarınca her tıbbi müdahalede hastanın aydınlatılmış rızası şarttır ve ayırt etme gücüne sahip hasta kendisine uygulanması planlanan veya uygulanmakta olan tedaviyi yazılı belge vererek reddetme ya da durdurulmasını isteme hakkına sahiptir [2]. Hasta yakınınız, bilinci ve karar verme yetisi açıkken müdavi hekimiyle görüşerek hangi girişimsel işlemleri veya yoğun bakım müdahalelerini kabul edip etmediğini ve palyatif dönemdeki bakım tercihlerini hasta dosyasına yazılı olarak kaydettirebilir [1][2].

Ayrıca hastane yatışlarında ve palyatif bakım sürecinde, hasta yakınınızın bilgilendirilmesini istediği aile bireylerini ve acil durumlarda ulaşılacak kişileri tıbbi kayıt formlarında açıkça belirtmesi, sağlık ekibiyle iletişimin kesintisiz yürütülmesini sağlar [2].

steps.title: Ayırt etme gücü tam iken noterlik veya başkonsoloslukta vekâletname ve banka yetkilerinin düzenlenmesi
steps.html:
Türk hukukunda vekâletnameler, vekâlet verenin işlem anında fiil ehliyetine (ayırt etme gücüne) sahip olmasını gerektirir; kişi karar verme yetisini tamamen kaybettikten sonra noterden vekâletname düzenlenemez ve Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi kararıyla vasi atanması (vesayet süreci) gerekir. Bu nedenle hasta yakınınızın bilinci ve ayırt etme gücü yerinde iken, Türkiye genelindeki noterliklerde (Türkiye Noterler Birliği sistemine kayıtlı olarak) banka işlemleri, tapu işlemleri, resmi kurum başvuruları ve sağlık/bakım evraklarının takibi için özel yetkiler içeren Düzenleme Şeklinde Vekâletname çıkarılması kritik önem taşır [3]. İleri yaş veya ağır hastalık durumlarında noter, ileride hukuki geçerlilik tartışması yaşanmaması için işlem gününde devlet hastanesinden veya adli tabiplikten aynı gün tarihli akıl sağlığı (fiil ehliyeti) raporu talep edebilir; hastanın sağlık durumu noterliğe gitmeye elverişli değilse ilgili nöbetçi veya yetkili noterlikten ev ya da hastane ziyareti talep edilebilir [3].

Banka hesaplarının yönetimi için Türkiye'deki bankalar, noter vekâletnamesinde hangi bankacılık işlemlerinin (para çekme, EFT/havale, vadeli hesap işlemleri) yapılacağının açıkça yazılmasını şart koşar. İşlem yapacak kişi yurt dışında bulunuyorsa, Dışişleri Bakanlığı bünyesindeki Türk Başkonsolosluklarından konsolosluk.gov.tr üzerinden randevu alınarak düzenlenen vekâletnameler Türkiye Noterler Birliği Bilişim Sistemi (TNBBS) üzerinden doğrudan Türkiye'deki noterliklerle entegre edilir [4].

steps.title: Refakatçi izinleri, iş göremezlik hakları ve evde bakım yardımına başvurulması
steps.html:
Hasta yakınınızın yatarak tedavisi sırasında sağlık kurulu veya hekim raporuyla refakatçi bulunmasının tıbben zorunlu görülmesi halinde, refakatçi olarak kalan çalışan aile bireyleri iş mevzuatı ve memur mevzuatı kapsamındaki refakatçi izni haklarından yararlanabilir; ayrıca Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, danışma hattı ALO 170) Sağlık Uygulama Tebliği çerçevesinde hastanede yatarak tedavilerde tıbben gerekli görülen refakatçi yatak ve yemek giderlerini karşılar [5]. Sigortalı bir hastanın kendi geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği veya malullük aylığı başvuruları da SGK il müdürlükleri ya da e-Devlet üzerinden yürütülür [5].

Hastalık nedeniyle günlük yaşam aktivitelerini (beslenme, giyinme, kişisel bakım, hareket) başkasının yardımı olmadan sürdüremeyen yetişkin hastalar için, yetkili kamu hastanelerinden alınan Erişkinler İçin Engellilik Sağlık Kurulu Raporunda Tam Bağımlı ibaresi yer alması ve hane içi kişi başına düşen gelirin net asgari ücretin üçte ikisinden az olması şartıyla Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı (çağrı merkezi ALO 183) İl Müdürlükleri veya Sosyal Hizmet Merkezlerine Evde Bakım Yardımı başvurusu yapılabilir [6].

steps.title: Vasiyetname, emeklilik/sigorta hak sahipliği, mirasçılık belgesi ve veraset vergisi hazırlığı
steps.html:
Hasta yakınınız ayırt etme gücüne sahipken malvarlığına ilişkin tasarruflarını Türk Medeni Kanunu uyarınca noterlikte iki tanık huzurunda düzenlenen resmi vasiyetname ile güvenceye alabilir; düzenlenen vasiyetnameler Türkiye Noterler Birliği kayıtlarında gizlilik kuralları çerçevesinde saklanır ve nüfus müdürlüğüne bildirilir [3]. Özel hayat sigortası ve bireysel emeklilik (BES) sözleşmelerindeki lehdar (hak sahibi) kayıtlarını, tapu senetlerini, banka sözleşmelerini ve kişinin cenaze/defin tercihlerini (defin yeri, dini merasim tercihleri) tek bir dosyada düzenli şekilde bir araya getirin.

Vefat sonrasında aile yakınlarının tamamlaması gereken başlıca resmi işlemler ve yasal süreler şunlardır:

  • Cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı: Vefat eden sigortalının hak sahiplerine (sırasıyla eş, çocuklar, anne-baba veya kardeşler) bir defaya mahsus cenaze ödeneği ile şartları sağlayan eş ve çocuklara ölüm aylığı (dul ve yetim aylığı) bağlanması için Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, ALO 170) birimlerine veya e-Devlet kapısı üzerinden başvuru yapılır [5].
  • Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı): Vefat sonrasında banka hesapları ve tapu devirleri için yasal mirasçıları gösteren Mirasçılık Belgesi, nüfus kayıtlarında engel veya vasiyetname/yabancılık unsuru yoksa herhangi bir noterlikten (Türkiye Noterler Birliği üzerinden), aksi halde Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesinden alınır [3]. Vefatla birlikte kişinin sağlığında verdiği vekâletnameler kural olarak sona erer ve banka hesapları mirasçılık belgesi ile vergi ilişiksiz yazısı ibraz edilene kadar bloke edilir.
  • Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi: Ölüm Türkiye'de gerçekleşmiş ve mirasçılar Türkiye'de bulunuyorsa, vefat tarihini takip eden 4 ay içinde Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (vergi dairesi veya Dijital Vergi Dairesi) nezdinde Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi verilmesi yasal zorunluluktur (mirasçılar veya ölüm yeri yurt dışında ise süre 6 veya 8 aya uzar) [7].
