title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in United Arab Emirates: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml: When your family member in the United Arab Emirates is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key medical, legal, and financial steps while the person still has full decision-making capacity helps protect their wishes and prevents administrative blocks across the Emirates. Below are the five main official and practical steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate specialist palliative care, home healthcare, and hospital oncology units
steps.html:
Begin with the treating oncology or specialist medical team at the hospital to arrange an integrated symptom-management and palliative care plan. In the UAE, specialist palliative and home healthcare services are regulated at the emirate and federal levels:

  • In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DOH) regulates inpatient hospice and palliative medicine as well as licensed home healthcare providers that deliver multidisciplinary pain and symptom management at home, integrated through the Malaffi health information exchange [1].
  • In Dubai, the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) licenses hospital oncology centres and certified home healthcare facilities authorized to provide home-based palliative nursing, physician visits, controlled analgesic protocols, and home medical equipment [2].
  • In the Northern Emirates, tertiary hospitals under the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) coordinate oncology and supportive inpatient care.

Ask the hospital case manager or treating specialist to submit a prior-authorization request to the person's health insurer (such as Thiqa or Daman in Abu Dhabi, or a DHA-compliant insurer in Dubai) to confirm coverage limits for inpatient palliative beds, home nursing visits, and specialist medical equipment [1][2].

steps.title: Document the care plan, informed consent, and federal medical liability rules
steps.html:
The UAE does not operate a standalone statutory living-will registry for broad advance refusals of life-sustaining treatment in the same manner as some Western jurisdictions. Instead, clinical care and resuscitation rules are governed by UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability (and its Executive Regulations under Cabinet Resolution No. 40 of 2019, as amended), published on the official UAE Legislation portal [3]. Under this federal framework, every medical intervention requires the informed consent of the patient (or their legal representative if capacity is lost), and physicians must document the treatment plan and explain expected outcomes and risks in the medical record [3].

Under UAE medical liability rules, cardiopulmonary resuscitation and life-sustaining measures remain the clinical default unless the specific statutory criteria for withholding or withdrawing resuscitation (such as confirmed brain death or terminal, irreversible cessation of vital functions certified by at least three specialist physicians including the treating consultant) are met in accordance with federal health regulations [3]. While your family member has full capacity, they should meet with their treating consultant to record their symptom-management preferences, designate the primary family spokesperson in the hospital file, and obtain a written clinical summary and emergency care plan to keep at home for ambulance or emergency staff [1][2][3].

steps.title: Execute notarized Powers of Attorney and bank mandates while full capacity exists
steps.html:
To allow a trusted representative to manage property, residency or visa administration, utility contracts, and financial affairs in the UAE, your family member must execute a formal Power of Attorney (POA) while they retain full mental capacity. In the UAE, a Power of Attorney must be drafted in Arabic (or bilingual Arabic-English) and notarized before an official UAE Notary Public, such as through the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (ADJD) e-Notary portal or Dubai Courts Notary Public [4]. Verification and signing can be completed online via video conference using UAE PASS, or in person [4].

Keep two practical rules in mind when preparing Powers of Attorney in the UAE:

  • UAE retail banks rarely accept a generic Power of Attorney unless it contains explicit banking clauses naming the account powers, and many banks require the account holder to sign the bank's own internal mandate form in person while capacity is intact.
  • If a Power of Attorney is executed outside the UAE for use within the country, it must be notarized and legalized in the country of origin, attested by the UAE Embassy abroad, attested in the UAE by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), and translated into Arabic by a Ministry of Justice certified legal translator [4][5].

steps.title: Access statutory leave provisions and health insurance catastrophic coverage
steps.html:
Under the UAE Federal Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), documented on The Official Portal of the UAE Government, private-sector employees who have completed their probation period are entitled to up to 90 days of sick leave per year of service (the first 15 days at full pay, the next 30 days at half pay, and the remaining 45 days unpaid), supported by an official medical report [6]. While the private-sector labour law does not create a separate long-term paid caregiver leave for looking after an ill adult relative, employees can request paid annual leave or mutually agreed unpaid leave from their employer, and statutory paid bereavement (compassionate) leave of 5 days for the death of a spouse or 3 days for the death of a parent, child, sibling, grandparent, or grandchild applies following a death [6].

Public-sector employees and UAE nationals working for federal or emirate government entities may have access to additional escort or patient-accompaniment leave under local human-resources laws when accompanying a family member for approved hospital treatment. At the same time, review the person's health insurance policy and any group life or critical-illness policy held through their employer to check whether a terminal-illness or permanent-disability benefit can be claimed early.

steps.title: Organize wills, workplace end-of-service benefits, bank account rules, and estate courts
steps.html:
In the UAE, individual and joint bank accounts, real estate, and local assets are frozen immediately once a bank or authority is notified of an account holder's death, and any lifetime Power of Attorney automatically expires upon death. Preparing the succession route while your family member has full capacity is therefore critical:

  • Registering a Will: Without a registered will, estate distribution and guardianship of minor children in the UAE may be subject to default statutory or Sharia-based inheritance procedures. Non-Muslim residents and asset holders can register a civil or common-law will in advance through the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department Civil Family Court (which registers civil wills for non-Muslims covering assets across the UAE) or through the DIFC Courts Wills Service in Dubai (which registers common-law English-language wills and handles probate for non-Muslims) [7][8]. Muslim residents may register wills in accordance with UAE personal status law before the Personal Status Court in their emirate.
  • Employment end-of-service gratuity and workplace insurance: Under UAE labour rules explained on The Official Portal of the UAE Government, an expatriate employee with at least one year of continuous service accrues statutory end-of-service gratuity (21 days' basic wage per year for the first five years and 30 days' basic wage per year thereafter), which the employer must settle within 14 days of contract termination or to the designated beneficiaries/heirs upon death [6]. Check whether the person has updated their beneficiary nomination form with their employer, free-zone authority, or workplace savings scheme (such as DEWS in DIFC).
  • Vital documents and funeral wishes: Gather the person's original passport, Emirates ID, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates (all attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs where issued abroad), property title deeds, and insurance policies, and record whether the family will arrange local burial or cremation in the UAE or international repatriation to a home country [5].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance, could you share which emirate your family member resides in and whether they are a UAE national or an expatriate resident (Muslim or non-Muslim)?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Brazil: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry for the difficult time your family is going through. When a person is diagnosed with an advanced or terminal illness in Brazil, organizing clinical care together with legal and social security arrangements while the ill person still retains full civil decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and reduces the administrative burden on the family.

Below are the five main official steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care and Home Care Services
steps.html:
The first step should be coordinated with the attending medical team or the hospital where the ill person receives treatment:

  • Public healthcare network (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS): Within the SUS, the National Palliative Care Policy (Política Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos) of the Ministério da Saúde (Ministry of Health) integrates pain control, relief of physical symptoms, and psychosocial support across the public network [1]. When the ill person has mobility limitations and needs frequent clinical follow-up at home, the primary care team (Unidade Básica de Saúde, UBS) or the hospital team (at discharge) can refer them to the Melhor em Casa program (Home Care Service, Serviço de Atenção Domiciliar), run by multidisciplinary teams providing free clinical care at home [1].
  • Private health insurance (saúde suplementar): If care is provided through a private health plan or private hospital network, the family should request an individualized palliative care or home care (internação domiciliar) plan from the medical team, and may consult technical standards published by the National Academy of Palliative Care (Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos, ANCP) [1].

steps.title: Formalize Advance Directives of Will (Living Will)
steps.html:
While the ill person is lucid and has full civil capacity, they can record in writing their Advance Directives of Will (Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade, commonly known as a Living Will or Testamento Vital), regulated by Resolution CFM No. 1,995/2012 (Resolução CFM n.º 1.995/2012) of the Conselho Federal de Medicina (Federal Council of Medicine) [2]:

  • Medical record registration (prontuário médico): This document states the medical treatments and procedures the ill person accepts or refuses (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive mechanical ventilation, or artificial feeding) should they become unable to express their wishes autonomously [2]. The ill person can ask their attending physician directly to record these directives in the medical chart (where they are binding on the clinical team) and designate a trusted representative to communicate with healthcare professionals [2].
  • Public deed at a Civil Law Notary (Cartório de Notas): For greater legal certainty and easier access by hospitals and relatives, the ill person can also execute a Public Deed of Advance Directives of Will (Escritura Pública de Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade) at a Cartório de Notas or 100% digitally via videoconference through the e-Notariado platform, administered by the Colégio Notarial do Brasil (Notarial College of Brazil) [3].

steps.title: Execute a Public Power of Attorney for Financial, Property, and Healthcare Management
steps.html:
To prevent day-to-day financial and administrative management from becoming blocked if the illness progresses to an inability to communicate or travel, the ill person should grant a Public Power of Attorney (Procuração Pública) while retaining full civil capacity [3]:

  • In-person or digital execution: The deed is drawn up in person at any Cartório de Notas or electronically via the e-Notariado portal of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil (or at a Brazilian Consulate abroad if the person resides outside Brazil) [3].
  • Specific powers and bank registration: In the public deed, specify express powers to operate bank accounts, manage investments, pay medical expenses, represent the principal before public bodies (such as the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social and the Receita Federal), and administer real estate [3]. Because many Brazilian banks require periodic updates of powers of attorney or prior branch registration, the appointed attorney-in-fact (procurador) should present the Procuração Pública directly to the bank immediately after issuance to validate operational access.

steps.title: Apply for Incapacity Benefits, Income Tax Exemption, and FGTS Withdrawal
steps.html:
Several statutory social security, tax, and labor fund entitlements apply when a serious or terminal illness prevents work or requires ongoing care [4][5][6]:

  • INSS incapacity benefits and 25% care supplement: When the illness prevents working, the ill person (or their legal representative) should apply for temporary incapacity benefit (auxílio por incapacidade temporária) or permanent incapacity retirement (aposentadoria por incapacidade permanente) with the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, National Social Security Institute) via the Meu INSS portal/app or by calling 135 [4]. For listed severe illnesses (such as malignant neoplasm, severe heart or liver disease, Parkinson's disease, or irreversible paralysis), the 12-contribution waiting period (carência) is waived [4]. If a retiree receiving permanent incapacity retirement requires permanent assistance from another person for daily activities, the law provides a 25% supplement (acréscimo de 25%) to the benefit subject to medical examination [4].
  • Income Tax exemption (isenção de Imposto de Renda): Retirees and pensioners diagnosed with a qualifying severe illness under Law No. 7,713/1988 are entitled to exemption from Individual Income Tax (Imposto de Renda) on their pension income, requested through the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social and regulated by the Receita Federal (Federal Revenue Service of Brazil) upon submission of a medical report containing the ICD (CID) code and physician's stamp [5].
  • Full FGTS withdrawal: Finally, an account holder (or their dependent) in a terminal stage of life or with a qualifying severe illness can request full withdrawal of the Severance Indemnity Fund (Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço, FGTS) directly in the FGTS app of the Caixa Econômica Federal, attaching the Medical Report of Severe Illness (Relatório Médico de Doenças Graves) signed by the attending physician [6].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Social Security Dependents, Vital Documents, and Funeral Directives
steps.html:
While still living and capable, it is advisable to organize estate documents, beneficiary designations, and funeral instructions to prepare for post-death procedures in Brazil:

  • Will, beneficiaries, and INSS dependents: Verify whether a public will (testamento público) exists (or execute one at a Cartório de Notas if the person wishes to dispose of the available portion of their estate), update beneficiary designations on life insurance and private pension plans (VGBL/PGBL), and gather updated birth or marriage certificates, ID documents (RG and CPF), insurance policies, and bank statements in an accessible place [3][4]. Also confirm the registration of legal dependents in Meu INSS to facilitate future survivor's pension (Pensão por Morte) claims with the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social [4].
  • Funeral wishes and 2-month estate inventory deadline: Recording preferences regarding burial or cremation (which in Brazil requires an express lifetime declaration witnessed by two witnesses under local rules, plus a death certificate signed by two physicians in cases of natural death) helps the family coordinate municipal or private funeral services smoothly. After death, the heirs have a statutory deadline of two months (60 days) from the date of death to open judicial or extrajudicial estate inventory proceedings (inventário judicial ou extrajudicial) at a Cartório de Notas, avoiding state penalties on the Estate and Gift Tax (Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação, ITCMD) [3].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide more specific information for your family member's situation, in which Brazilian state and municipality does the ill person reside and receive medical care, and are they covered under the general social security regime (INSS), a civil service pension scheme, or a private health plan?

pt.title: Doença terminal e administração em fim de vida em Brasil: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos para o planeamento médico e jurídico em situação de doença terminal em Brasil: cuidados paliativos, diretivas antecipadas de vontade, procurações, apoios ao cuidador e organização sucessória.
pt.introHtml:
Lamentamos o momento difícil que a sua família está a atravessar. Quando uma pessoa recebe o diagnóstico de uma doença avançada ou terminal no Brasil, organizar os cuidados clínicos e as providências jurídicas e previdenciárias enquanto a pessoa doente mantém plena capacidade civil de decisão protege a sua autonomia e reduz a sobrecarga administrativa sobre a família.

Abaixo encontram-se os 5 principais passos oficiais por ordem de prioridade.

steps.title: Coordenar cuidados paliativos especializados e atenção domiciliar
steps.html:
O primeiro passo deve ser articulado com a equipa médica assistente ou o hospital onde a pessoa doente realiza o tratamento. No âmbito do Sistema Único de Saúde, a Política Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos do Ministério da Saúde integra o controlo da dor, o alívio de sintomas físicos e o apoio psicossocial em toda a rede pública [1]. Quando a pessoa doente apresenta limitações de locomoção e necessita de acompanhamento frequente em residência, a equipa da Unidade Básica de Saúde ou a equipa hospitalar (no momento da alta) pode encaminhá-la para o programa Melhor em Casa (Serviço de Atenção Domiciliar), operado por equipas multiprofissionais que prestam assistência clínica gratuita no domicílio [1].

Se o acompanhamento ocorrer pela saúde suplementar (plano de saúde) ou rede privada, a família deve solicitar à equipa médica um plano individualizado de cuidados paliativos ou internação domiciliar (home care), podendo consultar referenciais técnicos junto da Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos [1].

steps.title: Formalizar Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade (Testamento Vital)
steps.html:
Enquanto a pessoa doente estiver lúcida e com plena capacidade civil, pode registar por escrito as suas Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade (conhecidas como Testamento Vital), regulamentadas pela Resolução CFM n.º 1.995/2012 do Conselho Federal de Medicina [2]. Este documento expressa os tratamentos e procedimentos médicos que a pessoa doente aceita ou recusa (como reanimação cardiorrespiratória, ventilação mecânica invasiva ou alimentação artificial) caso venha a ficar incapaz de manifestar a sua vontade de forma autónoma [2].

A pessoa doente pode solicitar diretamente ao médico assistente que registe essas diretivas no prontuário médico (onde têm força vinculante para a equipa clínica) e designar um representante de confiança para dialogar com os profissionais de saúde [2]. Para maior segurança jurídica e facilidade de localização por hospitais e familiares, a pessoa doente também pode lavrar uma Escritura Pública de Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade num Cartório de Notas ou de forma 100% digital por videoconferência através da plataforma e-Notariado, administrada pelo Colégio Notarial do Brasil [3].

steps.title: Outorgar Procuração Pública para gestão financeira, patrimonial e de saúde
steps.html:
Para evitar o bloqueio da gestão quotidiana caso a doença evolua para uma incapacidade de comunicação ou locomoção, a pessoa doente deve outorgar uma Procuração Pública enquanto conserva a sua capacidade civil plena [3]. O ato é lavrado presencialmente em qualquer Cartório de Notas ou eletronicamente pelo portal e-Notariado (ou ainda num Consulado do Brasil no exterior, caso a pessoa resida fora do país) [3].

Na escritura pública, convém especificar poderes claros para movimentar contas bancárias, gerir aplicações, pagar despesas médicas, representar o titular perante órgãos públicos (como o Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social e a Receita Federal) e administrar bens imóveis [3]. Como diversas instituições financeiras brasileiras exigem atualização periódica de procurações ou cadastramento prévio na agência, o procurador nomeado deve apresentar a Procuração Pública diretamente ao banco logo após a emissão para validar o mandato operacional.

steps.title: Solicitar benefícios por incapacidade, isenção de Imposto de Renda e saque do FGTS
steps.html:
Quando a doença impede o exercício do trabalho, a pessoa doente (ou o seu representante legal) deve requerer o auxílio por incapacidade temporária ou a aposentadoria por incapacidade permanente junto do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social, através do portal ou aplicação Meu INSS ou pela central telefónica 135 [4]. Para doenças graves previstas em portaria interministerial (como neoplasia maligna, cardiopatia grave, hepatopatia grave, doença de Parkinson ou paralisia irreversível), há dispensa do prazo de carência de 12 contribuições [4]. Caso o segurado aposentado por incapacidade permanente necessite de assistência permanente de outra pessoa para as atividades diárias, a legislação prevê um acréscimo de 25% no valor do benefício mediante avaliação pericial [4].

Adicionalmente, aposentados e pensionistas com diagnóstico de moléstia grave enquadrada na Lei n.º 7.713/1988 têm direito à isenção do Imposto de Renda sobre os rendimentos previdenciários, solicitada junto do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social e regulada pela Receita Federal mediante apresentação de laudo médico com CID e carimbo profissional [5]. Por fim, o trabalhador titular ou o seu dependente em estágio terminal de vida ou com doença grave pode solicitar o saque integral do Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço diretamente na aplicação FGTS da Caixa Econômica Federal, anexando o Relatório Médico de Doenças Graves assinado pelo médico assistente [6].

steps.title: Organizar testamento, dependentes previdenciários, documentos vitais e diretrizes funerárias
steps.html:
Ainda em vida, é recomendável verificar se existe testamento público (ou lavrar um em Cartório de Notas caso a pessoa deseje dispor da parte disponível do património), atualizar a designação de beneficiários em seguros de vida e planos de previdência complementar (VGBL/PGBL), e reunir em local acessível as certidões de nascimento ou casamento atualizadas, documentos de identidade (RG e CPF), apólices e extratos bancários [3][4]. Deve também confirmar no Meu INSS os vínculos dos dependentes legais para facilitar a futura concessão de Pensão por Morte pelo Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social [4].

Deixar registadas as preferências sobre funeral, sepultamento ou cremação (que no Brasil exige manifestação expressa em vida ou declaração com duas testemunhas conforme as normas locais e certidão de óbito assinada por dois médicos em caso de morte natural) ajuda a família a coordenar o serviço funerário municipal ou privado sem dúvidas. Após o falecimento, os herdeiros terão o prazo legal de 2 meses (60 dias) a contar do óbito para instaurar o inventário judicial ou extrajudicial em Cartório de Notas, evitando multas estaduais sobre o Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação (ITCMD) [3].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos indicar informações mais específicas para a situação do seu familiar: 1. Em que estado e município do Brasil a pessoa doente reside e recebe acompanhamento médico? 2. A pessoa doente é segurada ou aposentada pelo regime geral (INSS), servidor público com regime próprio, ou possui plano de saúde privado?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Administration in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step checklist for terminal illness and advance care administration in Mexico: specialist palliative and hospice care, written advance directives and living wills, enduring powers of attorney and bank mandates, caregiver leave and fast-track disability benefits, and wills, beneficiaries, and funeral planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry for the situation your family is going through. When a person is diagnosed with an advanced or terminal illness in Mexico, organizing medical care together with legal and estate procedures while the ill person retains full legal decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents subsequent administrative blocks.

Below are the five main official steps in order of priority.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Palliative Care and Pain Clinics
steps.html:
The first step is to ask the treating physician or referral hospital to establish an integrated palliative care and pain management plan:

  • Statutory right to palliative care: Under Title Eighth Bis (Título Octavo Bis) of the General Health Law (Ley General de Salud), all institutions within Mexico's National Health System are legally required to provide multidisciplinary palliative care (including home care when clinically feasible, pharmacological pain control, and psychosocial support) to patients in a terminal condition [1][2].
  • Referral through public health institutions: The family should arrange a medical referral to the pain clinic (clínica del dolor) or palliative care service of the institution where the ill person is affiliated - whether the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS, Mexican Social Security Institute, phone 800 623 23 23), the Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers (Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado, ISSSTE), state health services under the Secretaría de Salud (Ministry of Health), or national specialty institutes such as the Instituto Nacional de Cancerología (INCan, National Cancer Institute) [1][5].

steps.title: Execute and Register the Advance Directive Document or Form
steps.html:
While the ill person has full mental capacity, they can sign an Advance Directive (Voluntad Anticipada) to accept or refuse medical means, treatments, or procedures that artificially prolong life (obstinación terapéutica), while guaranteeing pain relief and comfort palliative care at all times [1][2]. Specific rules depend on the state (such as the Advance Directive Law of Mexico City, Ley de Voluntad Anticipada de la Ciudad de México, and analogous statutes in more than fifteen Mexican states, under the bioethical guidelines of the National Bioethics Commission, Comisión Nacional de Bioética, CONBIOÉTICA) [2]. There are two official pathways to formalize it in states where legislation is in force:

  • Advance Directive Document before a Notary Public (Documento de Voluntad Anticipada ante Notario Público): Any adult with legal capacity can appear before a notary affiliated with the Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano (National College of Mexican Notaries), appoint a representative (and an alternate), and sign before witnesses [2][3].
  • Advance Directive Form at a healthcare institution (Formato de Voluntad Anticipada en institución de salud): When a medical diagnosis of terminal illness already exists, the ill person may sign the official form free of charge directly before authorized medical staff at the public or private institution providing care, in the presence of two witnesses, so that it is immediately incorporated into their clinical file (expediente clínico) [2].

steps.title: Execute a Notarial Power of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Full Legal Capacity Exists
steps.html:
To prevent bank accounts, pension collection, or property administration from becoming frozen if the illness prevents the person from traveling or communicating, it is essential to execute a Notarial Power of Attorney (Poder Notarial) in a public deed (escritura pública) while full legal capacity remains intact [3][4]:

  • Notarial or consular execution: This procedure is carried out before a Notary Public (Notario Público) in Mexico (searchable via the directory of the Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano) or, if the principal is outside the country, before a Mexican Consulate abroad under the Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (SRE, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) [3][4].
  • Scope of powers and bank validation: Depending on anticipated needs, the person may grant a general power of attorney for litigation, collections, and acts of administration (poder general para pleitos y cobranzas y actos de administración), or a special power of attorney (poder especial) detailing powers for medical procedures, benefit collection, and banking management [3][4]. Because banks in Mexico generally require internal legal validation of notarial powers of attorney and registration of authorized signatures or co-holders, visit the bank branch immediately after obtaining the notarial deed (testimonio notarial) to confirm operational acceptance and update beneficiary designations on each bank contract.

steps.title: Manage Work Incapacity Certificates, Caregiver Leave, and Medical Benefits
steps.html:
Active insured workers and caregiving relatives should coordinate statutory social security certificates and leave provisions early [5]:

  • Incapacity certificates and disability assessment: If the ill person is an actively employed insured worker, they should obtain temporary work incapacity certificates (certificados de incapacidad temporal para el trabajo) through their treating physician or initiate a disability assessment (dictamen de invalidez) before the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (or the ISSSTE for state employees), enabling access to wage subsidies or a disability pension (pensión por invalidez) [5].
  • Caregiver leave rules: Regarding paid leave for family caregivers, current federal law (Article 140 Bis of the Social Security Law and Article 37 Bis of the ISSSTE Law) provides medical care leave (licencia por cuidados médicos) specifically for insured working mothers or fathers whose children under age 16 suffer from cancer during critical hospitalization or treatment periods [5]. For caring for adult relatives with terminal illnesses, employed relatives should review paid or unpaid family leave clauses in their collective bargaining agreement (contrato colectivo de trabajo) or general working conditions.

steps.title: Organize the Will, Pension and AFORE Beneficiaries, and Funeral Wishes
steps.html:
Using the period of full legal capacity to organize testamentary and social security records avoids lengthy intestate succession proceedings and secures survivor entitlements:

  • Open Public Will and beneficiary updates: Executing or reviewing an Open Public Will (Testamento Público Abierto) before a Notary Public avoids costly intestate probate; the notary files an official notice for registration in the National Register of Will Notices (Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento, RENAT), coordinated by the Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB, Ministry of the Interior) [3][6]. In addition, verify and update designated beneficiaries on the individual retirement savings account (AFORE) supervised by the Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (CONSAR, National Commission for the Retirement Savings System), as well as on life insurance policies and bank accounts [7].
  • Vital documents and IMSS survivor benefits: Gather in an accessible folder the birth certificate, marriage certificate or proof of cohabitation (constancia de concubinato), CURP, Social Security Number (Número de Seguridad Social, NSS), AFORE statements, and property deeds [5][7]. Recording burial or cremation preferences in writing and checking contracted funeral plans or institutional funeral homes (velatorios) simplifies later arrangements; after death, survivors or the person who pays the funeral expenses can apply for the Funeral Expense Grant (Ayuda para Gastos de Funeral) and process widowhood, orphanhood, or ascendant pensions at the Family Medicine Unit (Unidad de Medicina Familiar) of the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social by presenting the original funeral invoice and death certificate [5].

closingQuestion: To guide you more precisely on the procedures applicable to your family member, in which Mexican state or municipality does the ill person reside and receive medical care, and with which social security institution are they affiliated (IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar, or private health insurance)?

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en México: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en México: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml:
Lamentamos la situación por la que atraviesa su familia. Cuando una persona recibe el diagnóstico de una enfermedad avanzada o en fase terminal en México, organizar la atención médica y los trámites legales y patrimoniales mientras la persona enferma conserva plena capacidad jurídica de decisión permite proteger su voluntad y evitar bloqueos administrativos posteriores.

A continuación se detallan los 5 pasos oficiales principales en orden de prioridad.

steps.title: Coordinar los cuidados paliativos especializados y clínicas del dolor
steps.html:
El primer paso consiste en solicitar al médico tratante o al hospital de referencia la integración de un plan de cuidados paliativos y control del dolor. Bajo el Título Octavo Bis de la Ley General de Salud, todas las instituciones del Sistema Nacional de Salud tienen la obligación de ofrecer cuidados paliativos multidisciplinarios (incluyendo atención domiciliaria cuando sea clínicamente viable, control farmacológico del dolor y apoyo psicosocial) a pacientes en situación terminal [1][2].

La familia debe gestionar la referencia médica a la clínica del dolor o al servicio de cuidados paliativos de la institución donde la persona enferma esté afiliada, ya sea el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (teléfono 800 623 23 23), el Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado, los servicios estatales de la Secretaría de Salud o institutos nacionales de alta especialidad como el Instituto Nacional de Cancerología [1][5].

steps.title: Otorgar y registrar el Documento o Formato de Voluntad Anticipada
steps.html:
Mientras la persona enferma se encuentre en pleno uso de sus facultades mentales, puede suscribir su declaración de Voluntad Anticipada para aceptar o rechazar medios, tratamientos o procedimientos médicos que prolonguen artificialmente la vida (obstinación terapéutica), garantizando en todo momento el alivio del dolor y los cuidados paliativos de confort [1][2]. La regulación específica depende de la entidad federativa (como la Ley de Voluntad Anticipada de la Ciudad de México y las leyes homólogas en más de quince estados del país, bajo los lineamientos bioéticos de la Comisión Nacional de Bioética) [2].

Existen dos vías oficiales para formalizarla en las entidades donde está legislada:

  • Documento de Voluntad Anticipada ante Notario Público: Cualquier persona mayor de edad con capacidad de ejercicio puede acudir ante un fedatario afiliado al Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano, designar un representante (y un sustituto) y firmar ante testigos [2][3].
  • Formato de Voluntad Anticipada en institución de salud: Cuando ya existe un diagnóstico médico de enfermedad en etapa terminal, la persona enferma puede suscribir gratuitamente el formato oficial directamente ante el personal médico autorizado de la institución pública o privada donde recibe atención, en presencia de dos testigos, para que se integre de inmediato a su expediente clínico [2].

steps.title: Otorgar Poder Notarial y mandatos bancarios con plena capacidad jurídica
steps.html:
Para evitar que las cuentas bancarias, el cobro de pensiones o la administración de bienes queden bloqueados si la enfermedad impide a la persona desplazarse o comunicarse, es fundamental otorgar un Poder Notarial en escritura pública mientras conserve plena capacidad legal [3][4]. Este trámite se realiza ante un Notario Público en México (localizable a través del directorio del Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano) o, si el otorgante se encuentra fuera del país, ante un Consulado de México en el exterior dependiente de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores [3][4].

Según las necesidades previstas, puede otorgarse un poder general para pleitos y cobranzas y actos de administración, o bien un poder especial detallando facultades para trámites médicos, cobro de prestaciones y gestión bancaria [3][4]. Dado que los bancos en México suelen requerir validación interna de los poderes notariales y el registro de firmas autorizadas o cotitulares, conviene acudir a la sucursal bancaria inmediatamente después de obtener el testimonio notarial para verificar su aceptación operativa y actualizar la designación de beneficiarios en cada contrato bancario.

steps.title: Gestionar incapacidades, licencias de cuidados y prestaciones médicas
steps.html:
Si la persona enferma es trabajadora asegurada en activo, debe tramitar a través de su médico tratante los certificados de incapacidad temporal para el trabajo o iniciar el dictamen de invalidez ante el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (o ante el ISSSTE en caso de trabajadores al servicio del Estado), lo que permite acceder a subsidios salariales o a una pensión por invalidez [5].

En cuanto a las licencias laborales remuneradas para cuidadores familiares, la legislación federal vigente (artículo 140 Bis de la Ley del Seguro Social y artículo 37 Bis de la Ley del ISSSTE) contempla la licencia por cuidados médicos específicamente para madres o padres trabajadores asegurados cuyos hijos menores de 16 años padezcan cáncer durante periodos críticos de hospitalización o tratamiento [5]. Para el cuidado de familiares adultos con enfermedades terminales, los familiares trabajadores deben revisar las cláusulas de permisos con o sin goce de sueldo en su contrato colectivo de trabajo o condiciones generales de trabajo.

steps.title: Organizar el testamento, beneficiarios de pensiones y AFORE, y deseos funerarios
steps.html:
Aprovechar el periodo de plena capacidad jurídica para revisar u otorgar un Testamento Público Abierto ante Notario Público evita juicios sucesorios intestamentarios largos y costosos; el notario da aviso oficial para su inscripción en el Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento, coordinado por la Secretaría de Gobernación [3][6]. Asimismo, se recomienda verificar y actualizar los beneficiarios designados en la cuenta individual de ahorro para el retiro supervisada por la Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (AFORE), en seguros de vida y en cuentas bancarias [7].

Conviene reunir en una carpeta accesible el acta de nacimiento, acta de matrimonio o constancia de concubinato, CURP, Número de Seguridad Social (NSS), estados de cuenta de la AFORE y escrituras de propiedad [5][7]. Dejar por escrito las preferencias sobre inhumación o cremación y verificar los servicios funerarios contratados o los velatorios institucionales facilita la gestión posterior; tras el fallecimiento, los deudos o la persona que cubra los costos del sepelio podrán solicitar la Ayuda para Gastos de Funeral y tramitar las pensiones de viudez, orfandad o ascendencia ante la Unidad de Medicina Familiar del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social presentando la factura original del servicio funerario y el acta de defunción [5].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Ireland
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Ireland
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Ireland: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United Kingdom and Ireland, completing clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in both jurisdictions while the person still has full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate specialist palliative care, hospice services, and cross-border coverage
steps.html:
Start with the treating hospital consultant or general practitioner (GP) to establish a coordinated palliative care plan where your family member currently receives care. In the United Kingdom, the National Health Service provides community palliative nursing, symptom management, and referrals to inpatient or home hospice services (supported alongside charities such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie) [1][2]. If the person has rapidly deteriorating health needs and is approaching the end of life, ask a clinician or specialist nurse to submit a Fast Track Pathway Assessment for NHS Continuing Healthcare so that a fully funded care package (at home, in a care home, or in a hospice) can be arranged urgently without means testing [2].

In Ireland, a GP or hospital team can refer the person to Health Service Executive (HSE) Specialist Palliative Care teams, which provide free community home care nurses and inpatient hospice beds across each health region, alongside planning resources from the Irish Hospice Foundation [6]. Under the Common Travel Area arrangements between the United Kingdom and Ireland, British and Irish citizens residing in either jurisdiction generally have access to public healthcare, though planned cross-border relocation during advanced illness requires advance coordination between the discharging and receiving clinical teams to ensure continuity of controlled pain medications, medical equipment, and community nursing.

steps.title: Execute written Advance Directives in both the United Kingdom and Ireland
steps.html:
Because clinical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where medical treatment is delivered, a person who spends time in or may relocate between the United Kingdom and Ireland should prepare written directives in both systems while full mental capacity remains [1][6].

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales (under the Mental Capacity Act 2005), the person can prepare a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, often called a Living Will) specifying treatments they refuse if capacity is lost [1]. Any refusal of life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition) must be in writing, signed, witnessed, and include the explicit statement that the refusal applies even if life is at risk [1]. Clinicians can also record a ReSPECT emergency care summary plan in the medical file.
  • Ireland: Under the Assisted Decision-Making (Capacity) Act 2015, the person can make an Advance Healthcare Directive (AHD) setting out legally binding refusals of treatment and care preferences [6][7]. The AHD must be in writing, signed by the directive-maker in the presence of two witnesses, and can appoint a Designated Healthcare Representative (who also signs the document) to interpret and uphold those wishes; templates and guidance are issued by the Decision Support Service [7].

steps.title: Establish separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
A Power of Attorney registered in the United Kingdom is not automatically operable for Irish banks, property, or healthcare providers without complex recognition steps, and vice versa. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate mandates in each country where assets, pensions, or care are located [3][7]:

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, complete and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian: a Lasting Power of Attorney for Health and Welfare and a Lasting Power of Attorney for Property and Financial Affairs (in Scotland, a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registered with the Office of the Public Guardian in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, an Enduring Power of Attorney) [3]. Registration with the Office of the Public Guardian takes roughly 8 to 10 weeks and is mandatory before the document can be used [3].
  • Ireland: Create and register an Enduring Power of Attorney (EPOA) for property and personal welfare through the online portal of the Decision Support Service (phone +353 1 211 9750) [7]. Under the 2015 Act framework, an Irish EPOA requires capacity verification by a legal practitioner and a healthcare professional, witness signatures, and formal registration with the Decision Support Service while the donor has capacity [7].

steps.title: Claim fast-track terminal illness benefits and statutory caregiver support
steps.html:
Both countries offer expedited disability support and caregiver entitlements that should be initiated early:

  • United Kingdom: If a clinician judges that the person may have 12 months or less to live, claims can be fast-tracked under the Special Rules for End of Life administered by the Department for Work and Pensions [4]. Ask the GP, consultant, or specialist nurse to provide an SR1 medical form so that Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit is processed rapidly at the enhanced rate without a face-to-face assessment [4]. Family caregivers in the UK may also qualify for Carer's Allowance and one week of unpaid statutory Carer's Leave per year from employment.
  • Ireland: Caregivers providing full-time care can apply to the Department of Social Protection (via MyWelfare.ie using a verified MyGovID account) for PRSI-based Carer's Benefit or means-tested Carer's Allowance, as well as the annual Carer's Support Grant [8]. Employees in Ireland can also request statutory Carer's Leave (up to 104 weeks of job-protected unpaid leave) certified by the attending doctor [8].

steps.title: Align cross-border wills, beneficiary nominations, vital documents, and funeral wishes
steps.html:
While capacity is intact, review whether the person has separate, coordinated wills for UK and Irish assets (or a single will carefully drafted by a cross-border solicitor so that one neither inadvertently revokes the other nor delays probate), and update pension and life-insurance beneficiary nominations in both countries [5]. Gather civil certificates, National Insurance and PPS numbers, bank details, and property deeds in a secure file, and record whether the person wishes to be buried or cremated in the United Kingdom or repatriated to Ireland.

When a death occurs in the United Kingdom, the informant registers the death with the local Register Office and receives a unique reference for the Tell Us Once service, which notifies the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) in one step, while the executor applies to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Confirmation in Scotland) [5]. In Ireland, survivors notify the Department of Social Protection to claim a Widow's, Widower's or Surviving Civil Partner's Pension, file tax returns with the Revenue Commissioners, and apply to the High Court Probate Office for an Irish Grant of Probate where Irish estate assets require it [8].

Where is your family member currently living and receiving medical care (and if in the UK, is it in England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland)? 2. Does your family member hold bank accounts, property, or pensions in both the United Kingdom and Ireland?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & United Kingdom
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & United Kingdom
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and United Kingdom: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and the United Kingdom, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate specialist palliative care, hospice services, and cross-border coverage
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams can provide symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) once a hospice physician and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for pain and symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and advance care guides are also available through CaringInfo (an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization) [1].
  • United Kingdom: In the UK, the National Health Service coordinates community palliative nursing, GP home visits, and referrals to hospice care (alongside charitable providers such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie) [4][5]. If the person is in the UK and experiencing rapidly deteriorating needs, ask a clinician to submit a Fast Track Pathway Assessment for NHS Continuing Healthcare so a fully funded care package can be arranged urgently without means testing [5]. Because Medicare does not generally cover healthcare outside the United States and NHS eligibility is based on ordinary residence in the UK, any planned relocation for end-of-life care requires advance verification of health coverage, private medical transport insurance, and direct clinical handover.

steps.title: Execute written Advance Directives in both the United States and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so a person with ties to both countries should execute written directives in each jurisdiction while full mental capacity remains [1][4]:

  • United States: Execute a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state [1]. For a person with an advanced illness, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to complete actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST, or MOLST in certain states), which translate treatment boundaries into standing medical orders recognized by emergency medical personnel.
  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales (under the Mental Capacity Act 2005), prepare a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT / Living Will) [4]. To validly refuse life-sustaining treatment in England and Wales, the ADRT must be in writing, signed, witnessed, and contain an explicit statement that the refusal applies even if life is at risk; clinicians can also record a ReSPECT emergency care summary plan in the medical record [4].

steps.title: Establish separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
Financial institutions and healthcare providers in the United Kingdom rarely accept a US state Power of Attorney directly, and US banks normally require state-compliant mandates. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country [3][6]:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy / Medical POA) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements. In addition, ask US banks and brokerage firms to register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations on accounts so funds remain accessible after death without waiting for court probate.
  • United Kingdom: Complete and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian in England and Wales: a Lasting Power of Attorney for Health and Welfare and a Lasting Power of Attorney for Property and Financial Affairs (or a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian in Scotland) [6]. Registration with the Office of the Public Guardian takes roughly 8 to 10 weeks and is required before the attorney can act [6].

steps.title: Claim fast-track terminal illness benefits and statutory caregiver leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions provide fast-track disability pathways and statutory caregiver protections:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for expedited disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which fast-track Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for qualifying life-limiting diagnoses [2]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can request up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act administered by the U.S. Department of Labor, alongside paid family leave programs available in several US states [3].
  • United Kingdom: Where a clinician judges that the person may have 12 months or less to live, benefit claims can be expedited under the Special Rules for End of Life administered by the Department for Work and Pensions [7]. Ask the GP, consultant, or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical form to fast-track Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment; UK caregivers may also claim Carer's Allowance and statutory Carer's Leave [7].

steps.title: Align cross-border wills, beneficiary designations, tax filings, and funeral wishes
steps.html:
While capacity is intact, coordinate wills covering US and UK assets with cross-border legal professionals so that one will does not accidentally revoke the other, review pension and life-insurance beneficiary designations on both sides of the Atlantic, and gather civil certificates, Social Security and National Insurance numbers, property deeds, and account records [2][8]. Record clear wishes regarding burial, cremation, or international repatriation of remains or ashes.

Following a death, US administration involves notifying the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the US Embassy in London), contacting the Department of Veterans Affairs (if the person served in the US military), filing the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service, and opening estate administration with the local state Probate Court where required [2]. In the United Kingdom, registering the death unlocks the Tell Us Once service to notify the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), while the executor applies to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate in England and Wales (or Confirmation in Scotland) [8].

Where is your family member currently residing and receiving medical treatment?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & India
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & India
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and India: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and India, completing medical, legal, and financial steps in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate specialist palliative care, hospice services, and cross-border coverage
steps.html:
Start with the treating oncology or specialist team where your family member currently receives care to establish pain management and home or inpatient palliative support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide symptom relief alongside active treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) once a hospice physician and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing care, medical equipment, symptom-control medications, respite care, and family bereavement support; directories and planning guides are also provided through CaringInfo (an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization) [1].
  • India: If care takes place in India or the person plans to relocate there, specialist services are coordinated through public hospital palliative care units under the National Programme for Palliative Care (implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare) as well as accredited centers listed by the Indian Association of Palliative Care [4][5]. Because US Medicare does not cover treatment in India and domestic Indian schemes (such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY or private Indian health policies) apply domestic network rules, any international medical transfer requires advance clinical coordination, fit-to-fly medical clearance, and continuity plans for opioid pain medications.

steps.title: Execute written Advance Directives in both the United States and India
steps.html:
Advance care documents are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where medical care is delivered, so separate written directives should be executed while the person has full mental capacity [1][5]:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state [1]. Ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST or MOLST), which convert those preferences into standing medical orders for emergency personnel.
  • India: Under the Supreme Court of India judgment in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018, as streamlined by the January 2023 modification order), a competent adult can execute an Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) specifying when life-sustaining treatment should be withheld or withdrawn in an irreversible terminal condition [5]. Under the updated 2023 rules, the directive is signed by the executor in the presence of two attesting witnesses and attested before a Notary Public or a Gazetted Officer (without requiring countersignature by a Judicial Magistrate), with copies provided to the appointed healthcare surrogate, the family physician, and the local municipal authority or panchayat; explanatory guides are published by the Indian Association of Palliative Care [5].

steps.title: Establish separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
Indian banks, property registries, and hospitals generally do not operate on a standard US domestic Power of Attorney without specific Indian attestation and stamping, and US institutions require state-specific documents. Execute separate mandates while full legal capacity remains [3][6]:

  • United States: Execute a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney, and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiaries on US bank and brokerage accounts so funds remain accessible without court probate.
  • India: For property, banking, and administrative representation in India, execute a General or Special Power of Attorney [6]. If the person is in India, it is registered before the local Sub-Registrar of Assurances. If the person is in the United States, the Power of Attorney must be signed before two witnesses, notarized, and attested through the Embassy of India or the regional Consulate General of India (processed via VFS Global), then sent to India for adjudication/stamping within the statutory period (typically 3 months of receipt in India) [6]. Simultaneously, verify that statutory nominations (Form DA-1 for bank accounts and demat account nominations) are recorded with Indian financial institutions.

steps.title: Claim fast-track terminal illness benefits and statutory caregiver leave
steps.html:
Both countries offer financial and workplace entitlements during serious illness:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for expedited processing of Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs [2]. Eligible family caregivers employed in the US can request up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act administered by the U.S. Department of Labor, alongside paid family leave benefits in participating US states [3].
  • India: If the person is an insured worker in India, they can claim cash Sickness Benefit (and Extended Sickness Benefit for specified long-term conditions) through the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), or apply for non-refundable medical advances for life-threatening illness from their provident fund account via the Unified Portal of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation using the Composite Claim Form [7].

steps.title: Align cross-border wills, beneficiary nominations, vital documents, and funeral wishes
steps.html:
While capacity is intact, review or execute separate wills tailored to US assets and Indian assets (ensuring neither will inadvertently revokes the other), verify beneficiary nominations on US retirement accounts (401(k)/IRA) and Indian provident fund or insurance accounts, and assemble civil certificates, passports, OCI card, Social Security Number, Aadhaar, and PAN card in a single accessible folder [2][7]. Discuss whether the person wishes to be buried or cremated locally or whether remains or ashes should be transported between the United States and India (which requires Consular No Objection Certificates through the Consulate General of India) [6].

For post-death administration in the United States, survivors notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 or via the Federal Benefits Unit abroad), contact the Department of Veterans Affairs if applicable, file the final federal tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service, and complete state Probate Court filings where required [2]. In India, survivors submit the death certificate and Composite Claim Form to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (for Provident Fund settlement, Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance, and EPS survivor pension), notify ESIC or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) insurers where applicable, and obtain a Legal Heir Certificate (from the local Tehsildar/revenue office) or a court Succession Certificate if required to release un-nominated Indian assets [7].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Philippines
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Philippines
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Philippines: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is facing a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness with residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both the United States and the Philippines, early coordination while the person still has full decision-making capacity prevents legal and financial delays across both jurisdictions. Below are the five priority steps and the responsible authorities in each country.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coverage
steps.html:
In the United States, ask your family member's attending physician or hospital discharge team for a palliative care consultation, or request an evaluation for the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and explained via Medicare.gov at 1-800-633-4227) [1]. Hospice coverage applies when a hospice physician and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of six months or less if the illness runs its normal course and the person elects comfort-focused care rather than curative treatment [1]. It covers home or inpatient nursing, physician services, medical equipment, medications for pain and symptom control, and family respite care [1]. You can locate accredited providers and planning guides through CaringInfo, a program of the National Alliance for Care at Home (formerly the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization, NHPCO) [2].

If care takes place in the Philippines or the family is considering relocating the person there, check coverage early because U.S. Medicare generally does not pay for healthcare outside the United States [1]. In the Philippines, hospital palliative care units operate under the Department of Health National Integrated Cancer Control Act (NICCA) framework alongside organizations such as Hospice Philippines and the Philippine Society of Hospice and Palliative Medicine, while the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) provides Z-Benefits packages for qualifying catastrophic illnesses at contracted facilities (requiring pre-authorization through the hospital's PhilHealth liaison) [3]. Before any air travel, obtain formal fit-to-fly medical clearance and verify whether private medical evacuation insurance is required.

steps.title: Executing Written Advance Directives in Both Countries While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Medical directives should be executed separately in each jurisdiction while your family member retains full decision-making capacity:

  • United States: Execute a state-specific Advance Directive combining a Living Will (stating preferences on life-sustaining treatment, artificial nutrition, and pain management) and a medical decision-making designation [2]. Free state-specific forms matching each state's witness or notarization rules are available from CaringInfo [2]. For someone with an advanced life-limiting condition, ask the treating physician or palliative team to complete a state-recognized Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST or MOLST) form so emergency medical personnel have actionable medical orders [2].
  • Philippines: Put a written Advance Healthcare Directive and any Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) or comfort-care instructions on file directly with the attending physician and the hospital ethics or palliative care committee in the Philippines, ensuring that informed consent and treatment limits are recorded in the patient's clinical chart.

steps.title: Establishing Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
A power of attorney drafted only for one country often faces delays or rejection by banks and land registries in the other. Establish separate instruments while your family member has full legal capacity:

  • United States: Execute a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney so the appointed agent can manage medical decisions, property, and financial institutions if capacity is lost [2]. For U.S. bank and brokerage accounts, setting up Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) designations directly with each financial institution allows funds to transfer outside state probate.
  • Philippines: Philippine banks, the Land Registration Authority, and government agencies normally require a specific, notarized Special Power of Attorney (SPA) naming the exact transactions authorized [4]. If signed in the Philippines, execute the SPA before a commissioned Philippine Notary Public. If signed in the United States, your family member can either appear in person to have the SPA consularized/notarized at the Embassy of the Philippines in Washington, D.C. (or the nearest Philippine Consulate General, inquiries via consular@phembassy-us.org) or sign before a local U.S. Notary Public and obtain a U.S. State Apostille from the relevant Secretary of State, which makes the document directly valid in the Philippines without consular legalization [4].

steps.title: Claiming Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer financial support and job-protected leave during serious illness:

  • United States: Eligible employees caring for a spouse, parent, or child with a serious health condition can request up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), administered by the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division (using medical certification Form WH-380-F), alongside applicable state Paid Family Leave programs [5]. For disability benefits, the Social Security Administration (SSA, reachable at 1-800-772-1213) operates the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs to fast-track Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) medical reviews within weeks for qualifying diagnoses [6].
  • Philippines: If your family member has qualifying contributions to the Social Security System (SSS, hotline 1455, email usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph), file for the SSS Sickness Benefit (up to 120 days per calendar year) or Permanent Total/Partial Disability Benefit via the My.SSS portal or an SSS branch [7]. Combine this with PhilHealth catastrophic Z-Benefits [3] and medical assistance programs through the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) or the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Beneficiary Designations, and Post-Death Estate Procedures
steps.html:
Reviewing wills, beneficiary records, and post-death filing deadlines across both countries prevents conflicting estate proceedings:

  • United States: Ensure any U.S. will complies with state execution rules for probate before the state Probate Court, verify life insurance and retirement beneficiaries, and review veterans benefits with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if applicable. When a death occurs, report it promptly to the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 or via the U.S. Embassy Federal Benefits Unit if residing in the Philippines) [6], and note that the estate representative must file a final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service.
  • Philippines: Verify that beneficiary records are current with the Social Security System (which pays a separate SSS Funeral Benefit of PHP 12,000 to PHP 60,000 to whoever paid burial expenses, plus a monthly or lump-sum SSS Death Benefit to primary/secondary beneficiaries) [7], or with the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), PhilHealth [3], the Pag-IBIG Fund, and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) for eligible overseas workers. For property in the Philippines, note that the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) requires filing the Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801, taxed at a flat 6% rate on the net taxable estate) within one year from the date of death to obtain the electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) needed to transfer titles, whether through probate or a notarized Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate [8].
