title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Canada & India
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Canada & India
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Canada and India: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Canada and India, putting care coordination, capacity documents, and cross-border powers of attorney in place early while the person has full legal capacity prevents administrative delays in both jurisdictions.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care in Canada and India
steps.html:
In Canada, publicly funded palliative and end-of-life care is administered at the provincial and territorial level through home care programs, hospital specialist teams, and community residential hospices [1]. Ask the treating physician, oncologist, or nurse practitioner for a referral to the provincial home and community care service (for example, Ontario Health atHome, regional health authorities in British Columbia, or Alberta Health Services) and to enroll the person in provincial palliative drug coverage so symptom-management medications and home nursing supplies are covered [1]. You can also locate local hospice and palliative support resources nationwide through the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association [2].

If the person is considering travelling between Canada and India for family support or care, confirm medical fitness to fly and check health coverage before travel, as Canadian provincial health insurance plans restrict out-of-country coverage and standard travel insurance typically excludes pre-existing terminal conditions. In India, public palliative care services operate under the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC) within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare across government medical colleges and district hospitals [5], alongside specialist hospital and home-care centers listed by the Indian Association of Palliative Care [6].

steps.title: Executing Written Advance Directives and Living Wills While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Because healthcare providers follow the legal rules of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, execute separate written advance care documents for Canada and India while your family member retains full decision-making capacity.

  • Canada: Each province and territory governs its own advance care directive and clinical order formats (such as an Advance Care Plan, a Representation Agreement in British Columbia, a Personal Directive in Alberta or Nova Scotia, or a medical Goals of Care designation signed with the treating team) [1][2]. National workbooks and provincial guides are available through the Advance Care Planning Canada initiative led by the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association [2].
  • India: Under the Supreme Court of India's Common Cause judgment (2018, as simplified by the Supreme Court's 2023 modifications), an adult of sound mind and full capacity can execute a written Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) specifying when life-sustaining treatment may be withheld or withdrawn in a terminal condition [5][6]. Under the 2023 rules, the directive must be signed by the executor in the presence of two attesting witnesses and notarized by a Notary Public or attested by a Gazetted Officer, with copies lodged with the local municipal or panchayat custodian and added to the hospital's medical records [6].

steps.title: Establishing Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Canada and India
steps.html:
A Canadian Power of Attorney is not directly accepted by Indian banks or property registries without formal Indian legal formalities, and an Indian Power of Attorney does not satisfy provincial statutory rules in Canada.

  • Canada: Execute two separate provincial instruments while the person has full capacity: a Continuing or Enduring Power of Attorney for Property (covering banking, tax, and real estate) and a Power of Attorney for Personal Care, Representation Agreement, Health Care Directive, or Mandat de protection in Quebec (appointing a substitute decision-maker for medical and personal care decisions) [1][2].
  • India: For financial, banking, and real estate matters in India, execute a specific or general Power of Attorney naming a trusted representative in India [7]. If your family member is currently in Canada, the Power of Attorney must be signed before two witnesses and either attested via the High Commission of India in Ottawa (or the jurisdictional Consulate General of India in Toronto or Vancouver through BLS International) or notarized in Canada and issued a Hague Apostille by Global Affairs Canada or the competent provincial authority [7]. Once received in India, the instrument must be adjudicated/stamped and registered where required before the local Sub-Registrar of Assurances within the statutory period, and the person should also verify that formal nominations are recorded directly on all Indian bank accounts, fixed deposits, and demat accounts [7].

steps.title: Claiming Caregiver Leave and Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions provide financial and employment protections during a serious or terminal illness:

  • Canada: Eligible caregivers who take time away from work to care for or support a gravely ill person at significant risk of death within 26 weeks can apply to Service Canada for Employment Insurance (EI) Compassionate Care Benefits, which provide up to 26 weeks of financial support that can be shared among family members, alongside the EI Family Caregiver Benefit for Adults (up to 15 weeks for a critically ill adult) [3]. Caregivers are also protected by unpaid job-protected compassionate care leave under federal and provincial employment standards, and a person with a severe and prolonged terminal condition can request priority processing for the Canada Pension Plan (CPP) Disability benefit [3].
  • India: If the person is covered under Indian social security or health schemes, check eligibility for Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) sickness and extended sickness benefits, non-refundable medical advances from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) for life-threatening illness hospitalization, and inpatient coverage under Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) or private health insurance policies.

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Beneficiary Designations, Tax, and Post-Death Procedures Across Borders
steps.html:
Coordinating estate documents and beneficiary designations in advance simplifies later administration across Canada and India:

  • Wills and Probate: Ensure wills clearly address assets in Canada and India (often by executing separate, coordinated wills for Canadian and Indian assets so each can go through local probate or succession independently without revoking the other). In Canada, review beneficiary designations on RRSPs, RRIFs, TFSAs, and life insurance so those funds pass outside the estate where intended.
  • Canada post-death administration: After a death, the executor or family notifies Service Canada to cancel Old Age Security and Canada Pension Plan payments and to claim the CPP Death Benefit and any Survivor's Pension (or contacts Retraite Québec for the Quebec Pension Plan) [3][4]. The legal representative must also notify the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) on 1-800-959-8281 or via Form RC4111, file the Final T1 Income Tax and Benefit Return, apply for provincial Probate (Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee) where required, and obtain a CRA Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) before distributing estate assets [4].
  • India post-death administration: In India, nominees or legal heirs submit the Composite Claim Form in Death Cases to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to claim Provident Fund accumulations, Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI), and the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension, or claim ESIC Dependants' Benefit or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) repatriation/insurance cover where applicable. Where no valid bank nomination or probated will applies, heirs obtain a Legal Heir Certificate from the local Tehsildar/revenue authority or a court Succession Certificate to transfer Indian movable assets and property.

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps, which Canadian province or territory and which Indian state are involved, and is your family member currently receiving care in Canada or in India?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Canada & Philippines
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Canada & Philippines
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Canada and Philippines: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Canada and the Philippines, organizing palliative care, advance directives, and separate powers of attorney while the person retains full decision-making capacity avoids cross-border legal and banking bottlenecks.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care in Canada and the Philippines
steps.html:
In Canada, publicly funded palliative and end-of-life care is delivered through provincial and territorial home care services, hospital palliative care consultations, and community residential hospices [1]. Ask the treating physician or nurse practitioner for a referral to the provincial home and community care team and provincial palliative drug benefit plan so symptom-management medications and home nursing visits are covered [1]. You can also search national and provincial hospice resources through the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association [2].

If your family member is considering relocating between Canada and the Philippines for care, check medical fitness to fly and health coverage before booking travel, as Canadian provincial health plans severely limit out-of-country coverage. In the Philippines, palliative and supportive cancer and serious-illness care is provided through Department of Health (DOH) specialty centers under the National Integrated Cancer Control Act (NICCA), hospital palliative care teams linked with Hospice Philippines and the Philippine Society of Hospice and Palliative Medicine, and catastrophic illness packages administered by PhilHealth (Z-Benefits) at contracted tertiary hospitals [5].

steps.title: Executing Written Advance Directives and Living Wills While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Complete separate written advance care documents for Canada and the Philippines while your family member has full capacity so local clinical teams have clear, recognizable instructions.

  • Canada: Each province and territory has specific statutory forms and clinical medical order frameworks (such as an Advance Care Plan, a Representation Agreement in British Columbia, a Personal Directive in Alberta or Nova Scotia, or a clinical Goals of Care designation completed with the attending physician) [1][2]. National guides and provincial links are provided through Advance Care Planning Canada led by the Canadian Hospice Palliative Care Association [2].
  • Philippines: While the Philippines does not have a single national statute governing standalone living wills, patients with full decision-making capacity can execute a written Advance Healthcare Directive, Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) order, and informed refusal or goals-of-care documentation directly with their attending physician and the hospital ethics or palliative care committee, reinforced by a notarized Special Power of Attorney naming a trusted health care proxy [5].

steps.title: Establishing Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
A Canadian Power of Attorney is not automatically usable at Philippine banks or land registries unless executed or authenticated according to Philippine legal standards, and a Philippine instrument does not satisfy Canadian provincial requirements.

  • Canada: Execute two separate provincial instruments while the person retains full mental capacity: a Continuing or Enduring Power of Attorney for Property (for banking, tax, and real estate) and a Power of Attorney for Personal Care, Representation Agreement, Health Care Directive, or Mandat de protection in Quebec (for medical and personal care decisions) [1][2].
  • Philippines: To authorize a representative in the Philippines to manage bank accounts, real property, or benefit filings (such as with PhilHealth or the Social Security System), execute a written Special Power of Attorney (SPA) that specifically enumerates each authorized act [5][6]. If signed in the Philippines, the SPA must be notarized before a Philippine Notary Public. If your family member is in Canada, the SPA can either be acknowledged directly before the Philippine Embassy in Ottawa (or the Philippine Consulate General in Toronto, Vancouver, or Calgary) or notarized before a Canadian Notary Public and issued a Hague Apostille by Global Affairs Canada or the designated provincial authority.

steps.title: Claiming Caregiver Leave and Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits
steps.html:
Both countries offer financial and workplace support during a serious or terminal illness:

  • Canada: Caregivers who take time off work to care for or support a gravely ill person at significant risk of death within 26 weeks can apply to Service Canada for Employment Insurance (EI) Compassionate Care Benefits (providing up to 26 weeks of shareable benefits), or the EI Family Caregiver Benefit for Adults (up to 15 weeks for a critically ill adult), alongside job-protected compassionate care leave under federal and provincial labour standards [3]. Terminal patients can also request fast-track processing for Canada Pension Plan (CPP) Disability benefits through Service Canada [3].
  • Philippines: Eligible members can claim the Social Security System (SSS) Sickness Benefit (a daily cash allowance for up to 120 days per calendar year during hospital or home confinement) and Permanent Partial or Total Disability Benefits through the My.SSS portal [6], alongside inpatient coverage and Z-Benefit catastrophic packages from PhilHealth [5] and medical assistance for indigent or financially strained patients through the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) Medical Assistance Program.

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Beneficiary Designations, Tax, and Post-Death Administration
steps.html:
Aligning estate plans and beneficiary records now avoids freezes and conflicting procedures across Canada and the Philippines:

  • Wills and Beneficiary Designations: Review wills covering Canadian and Philippine assets (taking account of mandatory compulsory heirship/legitime rules under the Civil Code of the Philippines) and confirm beneficiary designations on Canadian RRSPs, RRIFs, TFSAs, and insurance policies as well as member beneficiary records with Philippine agencies.
  • Canada post-death administration: Following a death, the family or executor notifies Service Canada to stop Old Age Security and Canada Pension Plan payments and to apply for the CPP Death Benefit and Survivor's Pension (or contacts Retraite Québec for QPP) [3][4]. The legal representative notifies the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) on 1-800-959-8281 or via Form RC4111, files the Final T1 Income Tax and Benefit Return, applies for provincial Probate where needed, and requests a CRA Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) prior to final estate distribution [4].
  • Philippines post-death administration: Surviving family members or claimants file for the Social Security System (SSS) Funeral Benefit (a cash grant of PHP 12,000 to PHP 60,000 paid to the person who shouldered burial expenses) and SSS Death Benefit (monthly survivor pension or lump sum) [7][8] - or GSIS survivorship benefits for government employees - alongside Pag-IBIG Fund provident claims and Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) death and burial benefits for active OFW members. For Philippine bank accounts and real property, the executor or heirs must file the Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801, taxed at a flat 6% rate on the net estate) with the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) within one year from the date of death to obtain the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR), using either judicial settlement or a notarized Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate where there is no will and no outstanding debt [9].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Poland
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Poland
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Poland: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both the United Kingdom and Poland, coordinating care pathways, capacity documents, and cross-border powers of attorney while the person retains full decision-making capacity avoids court delays and banking freezes in both jurisdictions.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care in the United Kingdom and Poland
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, ask the GP, hospital consultant, or specialist nurse for a referral to NHS community palliative care teams and local charitable hospices (supported nationally through networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie) [2]. If your family member has a rapidly deteriorating condition that may be entering a terminal phase, ask the clinician or social worker to submit a Fast-Track Pathway Tool for NHS Continuing Healthcare so a fully funded package of home nursing or hospice care can be arranged urgently [2].

If the person is considering relocating from the United Kingdom to Poland for care, verify health insurance entitlement and medical fitness to travel in advance, as UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) cover only applies to temporary stays and planned treatment abroad requires prior S2 funding authorization or active Polish health insurance. In Poland, publicly funded palliative and hospice care (including home hospice care, hospicjum domowe, inpatient palliative medicine wards, oddział medycyny paliatywnej, and outpatient palliative clinics) is financed by Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia (NFZ, with 24-hour patient information via Telefoniczna Informacja Pacjenta on 800 190 590) on the basis of an e-referral (e-skierowanie) issued by a health insurance physician [5], alongside patient rights support through Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta [6].

steps.title: Executing Written Advance Directives and Patient Authorizations While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Complete separate written care directives and medical record authorizations in the United Kingdom and Poland while your family member has full mental capacity.

  • United Kingdom: A person aged 18 or over with mental capacity can make a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, or Living Will) to legally refuse specific future medical treatments, as well as a non-binding Advance Statement of preferences and a clinician-signed ReSPECT emergency care summary [1][2]. If an ADRT refuses life-sustaining treatment, it must be in writing, signed by the person, and signed in their presence by a witness, with copies provided to the GP and hospital team [1].
  • Poland: Under the Act on Patient Rights and the Patient Ombudsman (ustawa o prawach pacjenta i Rzeczniku Praw Pacjenta), a patient should sign written authorizations (upoważnienie osoby bliskiej) naming trusted individuals to receive medical information (informacja o stanie zdrowia) and access medical records (dokumentacja medyczna), and can also grant access directly through the online patient portal Internetowe Konto Pacjenta (IKP at pacjent.gov.pl) [5][6]. Any written statement regarding future medical treatment should be lodged in the person's medical records and discussed with the Polish treating team [6].

steps.title: Establishing Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
A UK Lasting Power of Attorney is not automatically recognized for property or banking transactions in Poland, and a Polish notarial power of attorney cannot replace a registered UK Lasting Power of Attorney.

  • United Kingdom: While the person has mental capacity, prepare and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG in England and Wales; or a Continuing Power of Attorney and Welfare Power of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian in Scotland; or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland): a Lasting Power of Attorney for Health and Welfare and a Lasting Power of Attorney for Property and Financial Affairs [1][2]. Note that if an LPA for Health and Welfare is made after an ADRT and gives the attorney authority over the same treatment decisions, the LPA overrides the earlier ADRT [1].
  • Poland: For property, inheritance, or administrative acts in Poland, execute a power of attorney in the form of a notarial deed (pełnomocnictwo w formie aktu notarialnego) before a Polish civil-law notary (notariusz, searchable via Krajowa Rada Notarialna) or have a notarized power of attorney executed in the United Kingdom and legalized with a Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) Hague Apostille accompanied by a sworn Polish translation (tłumacz przysięgły) [9]. Because Polish banks frequently require bank-specific forms, also set up a direct bank account power of attorney (pełnomocnictwo do rachunku bankowego) and a payment-on-death instruction (dyspozycja wkładem na wypadek śmierci) under Polish Banking Law while the account holder has capacity.

steps.title: Claiming Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits and Statutory Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer fast-track financial support and caregiver leave rights:

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, a person whose clinician estimates they may have 12 months or less to live can ask their doctor or specialist nurse to provide an SR1 medical form for fast-track, top-rate assessment of Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, Disability Living Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment [3]. Qualifying caregivers providing at least 35 hours of care a week can claim Carer's Allowance, and UK employees have a statutory right to one week of unpaid Carer's Leave per year.
  • Poland: If the caregiver is insured under the Polish social insurance system, Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (ZUS) pays care allowance (zasiłek opiekuńczy, claimed on unified form Z-15 with a medical certificate e-ZLA) for up to 14 days per calendar year when caring for an ill adult family member [7]. Polish employees are also entitled to up to 5 days of unpaid caregiver leave (urlop opiekuńczy) per calendar year under the Polish Labour Code, and adults with disabilities residing in Poland may qualify for the state supportive benefit (świadczenie wspierające) administered by ZUS following a provincial assessment (WZON) [7].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Pensions, Probate, and Post-Death Administration Across the UK and Poland
steps.html:
Reviewing wills, pension nominations, and succession rules in advance prevents conflicts between UK and Polish estate administration:

  • Wills and Succession: Ensure wills clearly address assets in the United Kingdom and Poland without accidentally revoking one another, and check expression-of-wish nominations on UK workplace and private pensions.
  • United Kingdom post-death administration: When a death is registered in England, Wales, or Scotland, the registrar issues a reference number for the Tell Us Once service on GOV.UK, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP Bereavement Service and the International Pension Centre), the Passport Office, and local councils in one step [4]. All UK Lasting Powers of Attorney end automatically upon death, and the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation in Scotland.
  • Poland post-death administration: For individuals insured or receiving pensions in Poland, family members can claim the funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy, PLN 7,000 from 2026) on form Z-12 within 12 months of death and survivor's pension (renta rodzinna) on form ERR through Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (ZUS, or KRUS for agricultural social insurance) [7][8]. To confirm heirship over Polish assets, heirs obtain either a notarial Deed of Certification of Inheritance (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia, recorded in the Rejestr Spadkowy maintained by Krajowa Rada Notarialna) or a court inheritance order (sądowe stwierdzenie nabycia spadku) [9]. Remember two strict Polish deadlines: heirs have 6 months from learning of their title to the estate to make a declaration accepting or rejecting the inheritance, and immediate family members (zero tax group) have 6 months from the registration of the Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia or finality of the court order to file form SD-Z2 with the Polish tax office (Urząd Skarbowy) for full inheritance tax exemption [9].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & India
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & India
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and India: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both the United Kingdom and India, coordinating care pathways, capacity documents, and cross-border powers of attorney while the person retains full decision-making capacity avoids court delays and banking freezes in both jurisdictions.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care in the United Kingdom and India
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, ask the GP, hospital consultant, or specialist nurse for a referral to NHS community palliative care teams and local charitable hospices (supported nationally through networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie) [2]. If your family member has a rapidly deteriorating condition that may be entering a terminal stage, ask the clinician or social worker to submit a Fast-Track Pathway Tool for NHS Continuing Healthcare so a fully funded care package at home, in a care home, or in a hospice can be arranged urgently [2].

If the person is considering relocating between the United Kingdom and India for family support or care, confirm medical fitness to fly and health coverage before booking travel, as ordinary NHS entitlement is residence-based and standard travel insurance typically excludes terminal pre-existing conditions. In India, publicly funded palliative care operates under the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC) within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare across government medical colleges and district hospitals [5], alongside specialist hospital, hospice, and home-care centers listed by the Indian Association of Palliative Care [6].

steps.title: Executing Written Advance Directives and Living Wills While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Complete separate written advance care documents for the United Kingdom and India while your family member retains full mental capacity.

  • United Kingdom: An adult aged 18 or over with mental capacity can execute a legally binding Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, or Living Will) stating which specific medical treatments they refuse in future circumstances if they lose capacity, alongside a non-binding Advance Statement of preferences and values and a clinician-signed ReSPECT emergency care summary [1][2]. Any ADRT that refuses life-sustaining treatment must be in writing, signed by the person, and signed in their presence by a witness, and copies should be lodged with the GP and hospital team [1].
  • India: Under the Supreme Court of India's Common Cause judgment (2018, as simplified by the Supreme Court's 2023 modifications), an adult of sound mind and full capacity can execute a written Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) specifying when life-sustaining treatment may be withheld or withdrawn in a terminal condition [5][6]. Under the 2023 rules, the directive must be signed in the presence of two attesting witnesses and notarized by a Notary Public or attested by a Gazetted Officer, with copies provided to the designated local municipal or panchayat custodian and the treating hospital [6].

steps.title: Establishing Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
A UK Lasting Power of Attorney is not directly accepted by Indian banks or property registries without formal Indian execution or attestation, and an Indian Power of Attorney cannot replace a registered UK Lasting Power of Attorney.

  • United Kingdom: While the person has mental capacity, prepare and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG in England and Wales; or a Continuing Power of Attorney and Welfare Power of Attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian in Scotland; or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland): a Lasting Power of Attorney for Health and Welfare and a Lasting Power of Attorney for Property and Financial Affairs [1][2]. Note that if an LPA for Health and Welfare is made after an ADRT and gives the attorney authority over the same treatment decisions, the LPA overrides the earlier ADRT [1].
  • India: For banking, financial, and property administration in India, execute a specific or general Power of Attorney naming a trusted representative in India [7]. If your family member is in the United Kingdom, the Power of Attorney must be signed by the executant and at least two witnesses (with matching passport and address proofs) and attested through the High Commission of India in London (or the Consulate General of India in Birmingham or Edinburgh via VFS Global), or notarized and apostilled through the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) where applicable [7]. Once sent to India, the Power of Attorney must be stamped/adjudicated and registered where required before the local Sub-Registrar of Assurances, and the person should also verify that formal nominations are recorded on all Indian bank accounts, fixed deposits, and demat accounts [7].

steps.title: Claiming Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits and Statutory Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer financial support and employment protections during a terminal illness:

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, a person whose clinician estimates they may have 12 months or less to live can ask their doctor or specialist nurse for an SR1 medical form to fast-track claims for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, Disability Living Allowance, or Universal Credit at the highest rate without a face-to-face assessment [3]. Qualifying caregivers providing at least 35 hours of care per week can apply for Carer's Allowance, and UK employees have a statutory right to one week of unpaid Carer's Leave per year.
  • India: If the person is covered under Indian social security or health schemes, check eligibility for Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) sickness and extended sickness benefits, non-refundable medical advances from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) for life-threatening illness hospitalization, and inpatient coverage under Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) or private health insurance.

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Pensions, Probate, and Post-Death Administration Across the UK and India
steps.html:
Coordinating wills, beneficiary nominations, and estate procedures in advance avoids delays across the United Kingdom and India:

  • Wills and Beneficiary Designations: Ensure wills clearly address assets in the United Kingdom and India (often by executing separate, coordinated wills for UK and Indian assets so each can go through local probate or succession independently without revoking the other), and check expression-of-wish nominations on UK workplace and private pensions.
  • United Kingdom post-death administration: When a death is registered in England, Wales, or Scotland, the registrar issues a reference number for the Tell Us Once service on GOV.UK, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP Bereavement Service and the International Pension Centre), the Passport Office, and local councils in one step [4]. All UK Lasting Powers of Attorney end automatically upon death, and the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation in Scotland.
  • India post-death administration: In India, nominees or legal heirs submit the Composite Claim Form in Death Cases to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to claim Provident Fund balances, Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI), and the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension, or claim ESIC Dependants' Benefit or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY / eMigrate) insurance cover where applicable. Where no valid bank nomination or probated will applies, heirs obtain a Legal Heir Certificate from the local Tehsildar/revenue authority or a court Succession Certificate to transfer Indian movable assets and property.

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Australia
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Australia
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Australia: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and holds ties across the United Kingdom and Australia, coordinating care, capacity documents, benefits, and estate administration early across both countries prevents legal and financial delays later. Because healthcare entitlements, powers of attorney, and probate rules operate separately in each jurisdiction (and vary across UK nations and Australian states and territories), key documents must be executed while the person still has full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, the primary route for symptom control and community support is through the person's GP or hospital specialist, who can refer the person to local National Health Service (NHS) specialist palliative care teams and charitable hospices supported by networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie [1]. If your family member has rapidly deteriorating needs and may be entering a terminal phase, ask an appropriate clinician (such as a hospital consultant, GP, or community nurse) to submit the NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool so an urgent, fully NHS-funded care package at home, in a care home, or in a hospice can be arranged without means testing [1].

In Australia, specialist palliative care is coordinated through state and territory public health networks, general practitioners, and community palliative teams, which can be located through the national directory maintained by Palliative Care Australia [2]. For older adults requiring home-based practical support alongside palliative treatment, referrals can also be arranged through My Aged Care and the Commonwealth Home Support Programme [2][3]. If the family is considering relocating between the UK and Australia for care, confirm coverage and fitness-to-fly rules before booking travel: the UK-Australia Reciprocal Health Care Agreement covers only medically necessary treatment for temporary visitors and does not fund planned cross-border palliative relocation, non-emergency medical repatriation, or long-term residential care.

steps.title: Written Advance Directives and Emergency Care Plans in Both Countries
steps.html:
While your family member has full mental capacity, separate written advance care documents should be completed for each country where care may take place, as clinical forms are not automatically recognized across borders.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person can make a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, often called a Living Will) under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 [1]. To refuse life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition and hydration), the ADRT must be in writing, signed and witnessed, and contain an explicit statement that the refusal applies even if life is at risk [1]. Alongside an ADRT, ask the clinical team to complete a ReSPECT emergency care and treatment summary plan and an Advance Statement of general care preferences so ambulance crews and out-of-hours doctors have immediate clinical guidance [1].
  • Australia: Advance Care Directives are governed by state and territory legislation (for example, in New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, or Western Australia), with official state-specific forms and guidance provided through Advance Care Planning Australia (national advisory line 1300 208 582) [3]. Once completed, signed, and witnessed according to the relevant state or territory rules, upload a copy of the Advance Care Directive directly to the person's My Health Record via myGov and share copies with the treating GP and hospital team [3].

steps.title: Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
A power of attorney registered in the UK is generally not accepted directly by Australian banks, land registries, or hospitals, and vice versa. Separate instruments should be executed in both jurisdictions while your family member retains full legal capacity.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person should make and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs) with the Office of the Public Guardian (phone 0300 456 0300): one LPA for Health and Welfare (which takes effect only when mental capacity is lost) and one LPA for Property and Financial Affairs (which can be used as soon as registered, with the person's consent) [4]. If the person lives or holds property in Scotland, prepare a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland), or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland [4].
  • Australia: The person should execute a state or territory Enduring Power of Attorney covering financial and legal affairs (for banks, real estate, and superannuation communication) as well as a separate medical authority (called an Enduring Guardian in New South Wales and Tasmania, a Medical Treatment Decision Maker in Victoria, or included within an Advance Health Directive in Queensland and Western Australia) following the statutory witnessing rules of that state or territory [3].

steps.title: Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Superannuation, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both countries offer expedited financial pathways and workplace protections when a terminal diagnosis is confirmed.

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, if a clinician expects death within 12 months, ask the doctor or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical form [5]. This fast-tracks claims for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment and at enhanced rates [5]. Family caregivers providing at least 35 hours of care per week can claim Carer's Allowance, and employees in Great Britain have a statutory right to up to one week of unpaid Carer's Leave per year to provide or arrange care for a dependant with a long-term care need [6].
  • Australia: Family carers residing in Australia can apply to Services Australia (Centrelink carer line 132 717) for the means-tested Carer Payment and the supplementary Carer Allowance [7]. Under the Fair Work system, employees are entitled to paid personal/carer's leave and compassionate leave when an immediate family or household member has a life-threatening illness. In addition, under rules administered by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO), if two registered medical practitioners (including at least one specialist in the relevant field) certify that the illness is likely to result in death within 24 months, your family member can apply to their superannuation fund (or via the ATO for ATO-held super) for early, tax-free lump-sum release of superannuation under the terminal medical condition condition of release [8].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Superannuation Nominations, and Post-Death Administration
steps.html:
Reviewing estate and notification arrangements in advance avoids conflicting probate filings and tax traps across the two jurisdictions.

  • Wills and Superannuation Alignment: Ask a cross-border solicitor or estate lawyer to ensure that separate UK and Australian wills cover assets in each respective jurisdiction without inadvertently revoking one another through a global revocation clause. In Australia, superannuation does not automatically form part of the estate under a will; check that a valid Binding Death Benefit Nomination is on file with the super fund and note that withdrawing super tax-free during the person's lifetime under a terminal medical condition can differ significantly in tax treatment from a post-death superannuation death benefit paid to non-tax-dependant adult beneficiaries [8].
  • United Kingdom Post-Death Steps: After a death in the UK, once the death is registered, use the Tell Us Once service to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre), passport offices, and local councils in a single step [9]. An executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales (or Confirmation in Scotland) to administer UK bank accounts and property [10].
  • Australia Post-Death Steps: Notify Services Australia (Centrelink and Medicare on 132 300) within 28 days of a death; eligible carers receiving Carer Payment may continue receiving support for up to 14 weeks after the death [7]. Families can use the Australian Death Notification Service (ADNS) to notify multiple banks, utilities, and super funds online, while the executor or legal personal representative applies to the relevant State or Territory Supreme Court for a Grant of Probate (or resealing of a UK grant) and submits a final Date of Death tax return and any deceased estate trust return to the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) [8].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Portugal
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Portugal
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Portugal: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across the United Kingdom and Portugal, early coordination across both countries protects the person's care preferences and avoids complex legal or financial bottlenecks. Because medical directives, powers of attorney, and succession procedures operate under separate national frameworks (common law in UK jurisdictions and civil law in Portugal), key documents should be prepared while your family member still has full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, the primary route for symptom management and specialist end-of-life support is through the person's GP or hospital specialist, who can refer the person to local National Health Service (NHS) specialist palliative care teams and community hospices supported by networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie [1]. When a person has rapidly deteriorating health needs entering a terminal phase, an appropriate clinician (hospital consultant, GP, or community nurse) can submit the NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool to arrange an urgent, fully NHS-funded care package at home, in a care home, or in a hospice without means testing [1].

In Portugal, public palliative support is organised through the Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (RNCP) within the Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS), accessible via the family doctor at the local health centre (centro de saúde), hospital palliative care teams (EIHSCP), or community support teams (ECSCP), with 24-hour clinical triage available through SNS 24 (phone 808 24 24 24) and professional directories maintained by the Associação Portuguesa de Cuidados Paliativos (APCP) [2][3]. If the family is considering relocating between the UK and Portugal for care, check UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or S1 healthcare coordination rules in advance: temporary cover applies only to medically necessary care during a stay, whereas planned cross-border treatment or medical transport requires prior insurer or health authority authorisation.

steps.title: Written Advance Directives and Living Wills in Both Countries
steps.html:
Because clinical advance care forms are not automatically transferable between the UK and Portugal, separate written directives should be executed in each jurisdiction while your family member retains full mental capacity.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person can execute a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, or Living Will) under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 [1]. If the ADRT refuses life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition and hydration), it must be in writing, signed, witnessed, and state explicitly that the refusal applies even if life is at risk [1]. Ask the treating clinical team to record an emergency care summary using the ReSPECT emergency care and treatment summary process so ambulance crews and out-of-hours clinicians have immediate access to agreed care goals [1].
  • Portugal: The person can execute a formal Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade (DAV, commonly known as a Testamento Vital) and appoint a healthcare proxy (Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde) under Law no. 25/2012 [2]. To make the directive immediately accessible to doctors across the Portuguese health system, file the official form with the Registo Nacional do Testamento Vital (RENTEV), managed by the Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde (SPMS) via SNS 24, either in person at a local RENTEV desk (health centre or grouping) or by post with a notarised signature [2].

steps.title: Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
Banks, property registries, and healthcare providers in Portugal generally do not accept a UK Lasting Power of Attorney directly without complex legalisation, and UK institutions require domestic statutory instruments. Separate powers of attorney should be put in place in both countries while full legal capacity remains.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person should execute and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs) with the Office of the Public Guardian (phone 0300 456 0300): one LPA for Health and Welfare (effective only if mental capacity is lost) and one LPA for Property and Financial Affairs (which can be used once registered, with the person's consent) [4]. If the person resides or owns assets in Scotland, execute a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland), or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland [4].
  • Portugal: For banking, tax administration, and property management in Portugal, the person should execute a formal notarial power of attorney (procuração) before a Portuguese notary (Cartório Notarial through the Ordem dos Notários), a registry office of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN), or a Portuguese consulate in the UK [5]. To protect personal and financial decision-making in the event of future incapacity under Portuguese civil law, the person can also execute an advance mandate for accompaniment (mandato com vista a acompanhamento) so a Portuguese court respects their chosen representative if a formal regime do maior acompanhado is ever required.

steps.title: Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions provide expedited financial benefits and statutory employment protections for family caregivers.

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, when a clinician expects death within 12 months, ask the doctor or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical report [6]. This fast-tracks claims for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment and at enhanced rates [6]. Unpaid carers providing at least 35 hours a week of care can apply for Carer's Allowance, and employees in Great Britain are entitled to up to one week of statutory unpaid Carer's Leave per year [7].
  • Portugal: Through the Instituto da Segurança Social, a person requiring third-party assistance for daily living activities can claim the Complemento por Dependência (assessed in 1st or 2nd degree by the disability verification system, including under the special invalidity protection regime for severe progressive illnesses) [8]. Family members providing regular or permanent care in Portugal can apply for recognition under the Estatuto do Cuidador Informal (via Segurança Social Direta) to access support measures and respite services, while employees under the Portuguese Labour Code (Código do Trabalho) are entitled to statutory family-assistance absences and caregiver leave [3].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Estate Administration, and Post-Death Deadlines
steps.html:
Reviewing wills, tax obligations, and post-death registration rules in advance prevents conflicts between UK freedom of testamentary disposition and Portuguese forced-heirship rules (legítima).

  • Cross-Border Wills Alignment: Coordinate with a cross-border legal adviser or notary so UK and Portuguese wills are aligned without accidentally revoking one another, and check whether an election of national law under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) is relevant to Portuguese assets.
  • United Kingdom Post-Death Steps: Following a death in the UK, use the Tell Us Once service after civil registration to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre), passport offices, and local councils at once [9]. The executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales (or Confirmation in Scotland) to administer UK estates [10].
  • Portugal Post-Death Steps: In Portugal, surviving family members or payers of funeral costs can claim survivor and bereavement benefits from Segurança Social: the lump-sum Subsídio por Morte must generally be claimed within 180 days of the death, the funeral expense reimbursement (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral) within 90 days, alongside any ongoing Pensão de Sobrevivência [11]. The head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) can use the Espaço Óbito and the Balcão das Heranças (administered by the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN) via the Portal da Justiça) to complete the formal identification of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and property partition, and must report the death and estate assets to the Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (AT) for Stamp Duty (Imposto do Selo) by the end of the third month following the month of death [5].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Italy
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Italy
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Italy: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and holds residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across the United Kingdom and Italy, early planning across both jurisdictions helps protect the person's medical wishes and prevents administrative delays. Because health systems, powers of attorney, and succession rules operate independently under UK common law (or Scots law) and Italian civil law, key legal instruments must be completed while your family member retains full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, the primary route for symptom management and specialist end-of-life care is a referral from the person's GP or hospital specialist to local National Health Service (NHS) palliative care teams and community hospices supported by networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie [1]. If your family member has rapidly deteriorating health needs entering a terminal phase, ask an appropriate clinician (hospital consultant, GP, or community nurse) to complete the NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool so an urgent, fully NHS-funded care package at home, in a care home, or in a hospice can be put in place without means testing [1].

In Italy, access to specialist palliative care and pain therapy is guaranteed nationwide under Law no. 38/2010 through the Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore, overseen by the Ministero della Salute [2]. Care is activated via the family doctor (medico di medicina generale) or hospital specialist through the local health authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale, or ASL), which coordinates home palliative care units (UCP-DOM) and residential Hospice facilities, with directory support also available through the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (SICP) [2]. If relocating between the UK and Italy for care, verify UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC), S1 pensioner healthcare registration, or prior planned-treatment authorisation before travel, as routine visitor cover does not fund planned cross-border care relocation or non-emergency medical transport.

steps.title: Written Advance Directives and Living Wills in Both Countries
steps.html:
Because clinical advance directives made in one country are not automatically integrated into the other country's medical registries, separate written directives should be prepared in both jurisdictions while your family member has full capacity.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person can make a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, or Living Will) under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 [1]. To refuse life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition and hydration), the ADRT must be written, signed, witnessed, and explicitly state that the refusal applies even if life is at risk [1]. Alongside an ADRT, ask the clinical team to complete a ReSPECT emergency care and treatment summary plan and an Advance Statement of care preferences so ambulance crews and out-of-hours doctors have immediate guidance [1].
  • Italy: Under Law no. 219/2017, an adult with full mental capacity can execute Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT, commonly called a Biotestamento) to express consent or refusal regarding future diagnostic tests and medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and to appoint a trusted healthcare representative (fiduciario) [3]. The DAT is filed in person at the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the person's Italian municipality of residence (Comune), executed as a notarial deed before an Italian notary, or lodged at an Italian consulate abroad, and is transmitted to the Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT maintained by the Ministero della Salute [3].

steps.title: Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
Italian banks, land registries, and notaries do not accept a UK Lasting Power of Attorney directly for property or banking transactions without formal Italian legal recognition, and UK institutions require domestic statutory instruments. Separate powers should be established in both jurisdictions while full legal capacity remains.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person should execute and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs) with the Office of the Public Guardian (phone 0300 456 0300): one LPA for Health and Welfare (which takes effect only when capacity is lost) and one LPA for Property and Financial Affairs (usable once registered, with the person's consent) [4]. If the person lives or holds property in Scotland, prepare a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland), or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland [4].
  • Italy: For managing bank accounts, property, or tax filings in Italy, the person can sign a general or special notarial power of attorney (procura generale o speciale) before an Italian notary (regulated through the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or at an Italian consular office in the UK. Because an ordinary Italian mandate can be affected by supervening incapacity, where vulnerability or declining capacity arises, Italian law provides for the court-supervised appointment of a support administrator (Amministrazione di Sostegno under Law no. 6/2004) by petitioning the guardianship judge (Giudice Tutelare) at the competent Italian court (Tribunale), and the person can designate their chosen support administrator in advance by public deed or authenticated private writing.

steps.title: Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both the UK and Italy provide expedited disability assessments, financial allowances, and statutory workplace leave for family caregivers.

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, if a clinician expects death within 12 months, ask the doctor or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical form [5]. This fast-tracks claims for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment and at enhanced rates [5]. Unpaid caregivers providing at least 35 hours of care per week can claim Carer's Allowance, and employees in Great Britain have a statutory right to up to one week of unpaid Carer's Leave per year [6].
  • Italy: Through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS), a person with a severe, rapidly progressing or oncological illness can request an accelerated disability and severe-handicap assessment (often completed within 15 days under fast-track oncology rules) [7]. Recognition of severe disability under Law no. 104/1992 (art. 3, comma 3) entitles working family caregivers in Italy to 3 days of paid monthly leave (permessi retribuiti Legge 104) and up to 2 years of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) via INPS [7]. Where the person is assessed as 100% invalid and unable to walk independently or perform daily living acts without continuous assistance, INPS also pays the non-means-tested attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento, often referred to as assegno di accompagnamento) [8].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Estate Administration, and Post-Death Deadlines
steps.html:
Aligning wills and beneficiary arrangements in advance prevents conflicts between UK testamentary freedom and Italian forced-heirship rules (quota di legittima).

  • Cross-Border Wills Alignment: Consult a cross-border solicitor or Italian notary (via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, which oversees the Registro Generale dei Testamenti) so that UK and Italian wills complement each other without accidentally revoking earlier wills, and verify whether an explicit choice of national law under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) applies to Italian assets.
  • United Kingdom Post-Death Steps: After a death in the UK is registered, use the Tell Us Once service to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre), passport services, and local councils in one step [9]. The executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales (or Confirmation in Scotland) to release UK bank accounts and property [10].
  • Italy Post-Death Steps: In Italy, surviving spouses and eligible family members apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS) for survivor or reversionary pensions (pensione ai superstiti / pensione di reversibilità) [7]. Heirs and legatees must file the mandatory Italian inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) electronically with the Agenzia delle Entrate within 12 months of the date of death, which also triggers cadastral property transfers (voltura catastale) for any real estate in Italy [11].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & Germany
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & Germany
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Spain and Germany: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Spain and Germany, planning medical, legal, and estate steps in advance across both countries prevents administrative freezes and ensures their wishes are respected. Because healthcare registries, powers of attorney, and succession procedures operate independently in each state, key documents should be formalized while the patient retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
• Spain: Palliative care is arranged through the primary care physician or hospital specialist within the National Health System (Sistema Nacional de Salud - SNS), who refers the patient to hospital palliative care units or home palliative support teams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD) in the relevant autonomous community, supported by the care directory of the Spanish Society for Palliative Care (Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos - SECPAL) and clinical frameworks coordinated by the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health) [1].
  • Germany: Patients with advanced, incurable illnesses have a statutory right to general outpatient palliative care (Allgemeine Ambulante Palliativversorgung - AAPV) and, where complex symptoms arise, specialized outpatient palliative care (Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung - SAPV under § 37b SGB V), prescribed by the attending physician and funded by statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung), as well as inpatient hospice care (stationäre Hospize) coordinated alongside networks such as the German Hospice and Palliative Association (Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. - DHPV) and overseen by the Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (German Federal Ministry of Health) [2][3]. In palliative situations in Germany, the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse) can also be asked for an expedited care-level assessment (verkürzte Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung under § 18a SGB XI), which must be issued within one week for hospital or hospice patients [2]. If your family member plans to relocate between Spain and Germany for care, verify coverage beforehand via the European Health Insurance Card (temporary stays), portable document S1 (resident pensioners), or prior authorization S2 for scheduled treatment.

steps.title: Executing Advance Directives and Living Wills in Both Countries
steps.html:
While the patient retains full decision-making capacity, separate advance directive documents should be executed for each jurisdiction, as clinical registries are not automatically interconnected across borders.

  • Spain: The patient can execute an Advance Directive Document (Documento de Instrucciones Previas or Voluntades Anticipadas, commonly known as a Living Will or Testamento Vital, governed by Law 41/2002) before a notary, before staff of the regional registry, or before three witnesses depending on the rules of their autonomous community [1]. Once registered in the relevant regional registry (Registro Autonómico), the document is synchronized with the National Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) of the Ministerio de Sanidad so that any medical team in Spain can consult it in the patient's clinical record [1].
  • Germany: A written and signed advance medical directive (schriftliche Patientenverfügung under § 1827 of the German Civil Code, BGB) should be drawn up, for instance using the official text modules (Textbausteine) published by the Federal Ministry of Justice (Bundesministerium der Justiz) and provided on the Wege zur Pflege portal [4]. It is advisable to supplement the Patientenverfügung with a palliative emergency sheet (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen) signed together with the general practitioner or SAPV team to guide emergency medical services at home [2][4].

steps.title: Preventive Powers of Attorney, Healthcare Proxy, and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
A power of attorney executed in Spain is rarely accepted immediately by German banks or registries without additional apostille and sworn translation formalities (or bank-specific forms), and vice versa. Separate instruments should therefore be formalized in both countries while your family member retains full legal capacity.

  • Spain: It is advisable to execute a public deed before a notary (via the General Council of Notaries, Consejo General del Notariado) granting a Preventive Power of Attorney (Poder Preventivo, or a general power of attorney with an express subsistence clause in the event of future incapacity or support needs), authorizing the representative to manage bank accounts, real estate, tax filings, and personal decisions without having to wait for judicial support proceedings [1].
  • Germany: The patient should execute a precautionary power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht covering financial and healthcare matters) and, as a fallback, a care directive (Betreuungsverfügung), registering both documents with the Central Register of Precautionary Mandates (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister of the Federal Chamber of Notaries, Bundesnotarkammer) so that guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) can locate them immediately [2][4]. To operate accounts at German financial institutions both before and after death, it is particularly useful to sign a transmortal or postmortal bank power of attorney (transmortale Bankvollmacht) directly with the German bank on its own forms [4].

steps.title: Fast-Track Dependency Benefits and Statutory Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both legal systems provide financial support and statutory employment leave when a family member requires end-of-life care.

  • Spain: An urgent dependency assessment (valoración urgente de la situación de dependencia under Law 39/2006, coordinated by IMSERSO and the regional social services) can be requested to access home help services, day centers, or financial allowances for family care. In employment law, the Workers' Statute (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) grants paid leave for serious illness or hospitalization of relatives, as well as the right to reduced working hours (reducción de jornada) or unpaid caregiver leave (excedencia) to care for a dependent relative [5].
  • Germany: Under the Caregiver Time Act (Pflegezeitgesetz), employed relatives in Germany can take short-term absence from work of up to 10 working days with entitlement to the care support allowance (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) paid by the Pflegekasse, as well as full or partial release from work for up to 3 months to accompany a close relative in the final phase of life (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase) [4][6]. The official Wege zur Pflege portal and the Care Helpline (Pflegetelefon at 030 20179131) of the Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth (Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend) provide free guidance on these entitlements and on statutory pension contributions for family caregivers under the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German Statutory Pension Insurance) [4][6].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Survivor Pensions, and Post-Death Formalities
steps.html:
Reviewing wills, life insurance policies, and bank accounts in Spain and Germany in advance streamlines estate administration under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012).

  • Testamentary coordination: Where assets exist in both countries, verify with a notary in Spain (Consejo General del Notariado) and in Germany that testamentary dispositions are aligned, assessing whether to include an express choice of national law (professio iuris) and ensuring a later will does not inadvertently revoke provisions intended for the other country [1].
  • Post-death procedures in Spain: Following death, applications are submitted to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) (Spanish National Institute of Social Security) for the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and survivor or orphan pensions (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) [5][7]. Once 15 working days have elapsed since the death, the Certificate of the General Registry of Last Wills (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad, using Ministry of Justice Modelo 790) is obtained to execute the deed of acceptance and division of inheritance before a notary, and the Inheritance and Gift Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within the general 6-month deadline from death (extendable by a further 6 months if requested within the first 5 months) [5][7].
  • Post-death procedures in Germany: In Germany, the death must be reported to the statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) and survivor or orphan pensions (Witwen-/Witwerrente or Waisenrente) claimed from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung [6]. The surviving spouse can apply through the Renten Service der Deutschen Post for the three-month death quarter advance (Sterbevierteljahr, during which the deceased's full pension rate is paid) within 30 days of the death [6]. To prove heirship before German banks or land registries where a notarized will with opening protocol is insufficient, a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or European Certificate of Succession is obtained from the probate court (Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht), which automatically consults the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister).
