title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Italy & Romania
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Italy & Romania
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Italy and Romania: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Italy and Romania, it is important to coordinate healthcare, legal, and social security arrangements in both countries without delay. Below are the five official and practical steps to follow in order while your ill relative still retains full legal and mental capacity.

steps.title: Organizing palliative care, hospice care, and cross-border health coverage between Italy and Romania
steps.html:
The first step is to activate the palliative care team in the country where care is being provided and to verify European health insurance coverage rules if a transfer between Italy and Romania is being considered.

  • Palliative care network and hospices in Italy: Under Law 38/2010 (Legge 38/2010), the general practitioner (medico di medicina generale) or hospital specialist activates the Local Palliative Care Network (Rete Locale di Cure Palliative) of the Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL, for example ASL Roma 1 or ATS della Città Metropolitana di Milano) for specialized home palliative care (UCP-DOM) or admission to dedicated residential facilities (Hospice), covered in full by the National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale - SSN), as set out by the Ministero della Salute (Italian Ministry of Health) [1]. Information on regional networks and specialist centers is also available through the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (Italian Society of Palliative Care - SICP) [2].
  • Palliative care (îngrijiri paliative) and healthcare coordination in Romania: In Romania, home palliative care (îngrijiri paliative la domiciliu) and inpatient admission to dedicated palliative wards are reimbursed by the public health insurance system through the Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate (National Health Insurance House - CNAS) and the county health insurance houses (Casele Județene de Asigurări de Sănătate, for example in Bucharest or Cluj), based on a specialist medical referral [3]. Accredited non-profit specialist networks also operate across the country, including HOSPICE Casa Speranței and the National Palliative Care Association (Asociația Națională de Îngrijiri Paliative - ANIP) [4]. If you plan to transfer the ill person between Italy and Romania to continue care, verify in advance with the ASL or CNAS the issuance of European forms S1 (for residents insured in the other Member State) or S2 (for planned cross-border medical treatment).

steps.title: Executing Advance Healthcare Directives and informed consent designations in Italy and Romania
steps.html:
Written medical directives are governed by the law of the state where care is delivered; it is therefore advisable to formalize them separately in both countries while your family member has full capacity.

  • Advance Healthcare Directives (Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento - DAT / Biotestamento) in Italy: Under Law 219/2017 (Legge 219/2017), the ill person can express their wishes regarding diagnostic tests, therapeutic choices, and specific medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and appoint a healthcare proxy (fiduciario) to represent them before doctors [5]. DATs are executed by notarial public deed, authenticated private deed, or private document delivered in person to the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the municipality of residence (for example in the Municipality of Milan, Rome, or Turin), which transmits them to the National DAT Database (Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT) managed by the Ministero della Salute [5][6].
  • Informed consent and representative designation in Romania: In Romania, the Patients' Rights Law (Legea drepturilor pacientului nr. 46/2003, under the purview of the Ministry of Health, Ministerul Sănătății) protects the patient's right to accept or refuse medical treatments and to designate in writing a legal or family representative authorized to receive clinical information and express consent if the patient becomes unable to decide independently [3]. It is advisable to file this written designation directly in the medical record at the Romanian healthcare facility.

steps.title: Establishing separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
Banks, public offices, and notaries in Italy and Romania require instruments of representation that comply with their respective domestic laws.

  • Notarial power of attorney and Support Administration (Amministrazione di Sostegno) in Italy: While the ill person retains full legal capacity, they can grant a general or special power of attorney (procura generale o speciale) by public deed or authenticated private agreement through a notary belonging to the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Notaries) to manage bank accounts, real estate, and administrative matters in Italy [7]. If a partial or total limitation of autonomy later arises, family members can apply for Support Administration (Amministrazione di Sostegno) by filing a petition with the Tutelary Judge (Giudice Tutelare) at the court (Tribunale) of the place of residence or domicile.
  • Authentic notarial or consular power of attorney (procură autentică notarială) for Romania: To manage bank accounts, pensions, or real estate located in Romania, an authentic special or general power of attorney (procură autentică notarială) drawn up by a Romanian public notary belonging to the Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (National Union of Public Notaries of Romania - UNNPR) is required [8]. If your family member is in Italy and cannot travel to Romania, a power of attorney that is directly valid under Romanian law - without requiring an apostille or translation - can be signed at a Romanian diplomatic or consular mission in Italy (for example in Rome, Milan, Turin, Bologna, or at the Consolato Generale di Romania a Trieste), by booking an appointment on the official consular services portal (eConsulat.ro) [9].

steps.title: Claiming caregiver leave, work permits, and disability benefits
steps.html:
Both countries provide employment protections for relatives caring for a seriously ill family member as well as financial support benefits.

  • Law 104/1992 (Legge 104/1992), extraordinary leave, and attendance allowance in Italy: By requesting an urgent assessment (fast-tracked within 15 days for oncology patients) for civil invalidity with attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento) and severe disability status (handicap in situazione di gravità under Law 104/1992, Art. 3(3)), employed family caregivers in Italy can claim 3 days of paid monthly leave [10] and up to 2 years in total of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Social Security Institute - INPS, toll-free number 803 164 from landlines or 06 164 164 from mobile phones) [11].
  • Medical leave for caring for an oncology patient in Romania: In Romania, workers insured under the public system are entitled to paid medical leave and an allowance for caring for and accompanying an adult oncology patient (concediu și indemnizație pentru îngrijirea pacientului cu afecțiuni oncologice) for up to 45 calendar days per year, paid through the Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate [3]. In addition, the Romanian Labor Code (Codul muncii) grants employees 5 working days per year of caregiver leave (concediul de îngrijitor) to assist a relative with serious medical problems.

steps.title: Aligning wills, bank accounts, funeral wishes, and succession procedures
steps.html:
Coordinating testamentary dispositions and civil status records in advance between Italy and Romania simplifies social security, banking, and tax formalities following a death.

  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Italy: With the assistance of a notary from the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, your family member can draft or review a will in accordance with EU Regulation No 650/2012 (which allows a Romanian citizen residing in Italy to choose Romanian national law or retain the law of habitual residence) and heirs can later search the General Register of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) [7]. After death, the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale processes survivor pension claims (pensione ai superstiti, either reversibilità or indiretta) [12], while the inheritance tax return (dichiarazione di successione) must be submitted electronically to the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months of the opening of the succession [13].
  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Romania: In Romania, the Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (National House of Public Pensions - CNPP, via its territorial pension offices, Case Teritoriale de Pensii) pays the statutory funeral grant (ajutorul de deces) - which by law is disbursed within 3 working days of submitting a complete application with the death certificate and proof of funeral expenses - as well as the survivor pension (pensia de urmaș) [14]. The notarial succession procedure (procedura succesorală notarială) takes place before a Romanian public notary in the district of the deceased's last domicile or where the main assets are located [8][15]; if the succession is completed within 2 years of the date of death, heirs are exempt from the 1% inheritance tax on the value of the estate (which applies after 2 years and is payable to the National Agency for Fiscal Administration, Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală - ANAF) [16]. Finally, it is advisable to leave written instructions regarding preferences between local burial and international repatriation of remains or ashes.

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your specific case, is your family member currently receiving care in Italy or in Romania, and in which Italian region and Romanian county (județ) are their residence, bank accounts, or real estate located?

it.title: Malattia terminale e pianificazione tra Italia e Romania: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la gestione medica e legale di una malattia grave tra Italia e Romania: cure palliative, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento (DAT), procure nei due Paesi, congedi per familiari e successione.
it.introHtml: Quando il vostro familiare riceve una diagnosi di malattia grave, ingravescente o terminale e presenta legami di residenza, cittadinanza, famiglia o patrimonio tra l'Italia e la Romania, è importante coordinare tempestivamente gli aspetti sanitari, legali e previdenziali in entrambi gli Stati. Di seguito trovate i cinque passaggi ufficiali e pratici da seguire in ordine, agendo finché la persona malata conserva la piena capacità di intendere e di volere.

steps.title: Organizzazione delle cure palliative, dell'hospice e della copertura sanitaria tra Italia e Romania
steps.html:
Il primo passo consiste nell'attivare l'équipe di cure palliative nel Paese in cui si svolge l'assistenza e nel verificare le regole di copertura sanitaria europea qualora si valuti un trasferimento tra Italia e Romania.

  • Rete di cure palliative e hospice in Italia: Ai sensi della Legge 38/2010, il medico di medicina generale o lo specialista ospedaliero attiva la Rete Locale di Cure Palliative della Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL, ad esempio l'ASL Roma 1 o l'ATS della Città Metropolitana di Milano) per l'assistenza domiciliare specialistica (UCP-DOM) o per il ricovero in strutture residenziali dedicate (Hospice), interamente a carico del Servizio Sanitario Nazionale, come indicato dal Ministero della Salute [1]. Informazioni sulle reti regionali e sui centri specialistici sono disponibili anche tramite la Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [2].
  • Îngrijiri paliative e coordinamento sanitario in Romania: In Romania le cure palliative a domicilio (îngrijiri paliative la domiciliu) e il ricovero in reparti con posti letto dedicati sono rimborsati dal sistema sanitario pubblico tramite la Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate (CNAS) e le casse distrettuali (Casele Județene de Asigurări de Sănătate, ad esempio a Bucarest o Cluj), sulla base di una raccomandazione medica specialistica [3]. Sul territorio operano inoltre reti specializzate no-profit accreditate come HOSPICE Casa Speranței e l'Associazione Nazionale di Cure Palliative (Asociația Națională de Îngrijiri Paliative - ANIP) [4]. Se si pianifica il trasferimento della persona malata tra Italia e Romania per proseguire le cure, verificate preventivamente con la ASL o con la CNAS il rilascio dei moduli europei S1 (per residenti assicurati nell'altro Stato) o S2 (per cure programmate).

steps.title: Redazione delle disposizioni anticipate di trattamento e consenso informato in Italia e Romania
steps.html:
Le volontà mediche scritte seguono la normativa dello Stato in cui vengono prestate le cure; è quindi opportuno formalizzarle separatamente mentre il vostro familiare ha piena capacità.

  • Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT / Biotestamento) in Italia: In base alla Legge 219/2017, la persona malata può esprimere le proprie volontà in merito ad accertamenti diagnostici, scelte terapeutiche e singoli trattamenti sanitari (inclusi nutrizione e idratazione artificiali) e nominare un fiduciario che la rappresenti davanti ai medici [5]. Le DAT si redigono per atto pubblico notarile, scrittura privata autenticata o scrittura privata consegnata personalmente presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune di residenza (ad esempio presso il Comune di Milano, Roma o Torino), che provvede a trasmetterle alla Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT gestita dal Ministero della Salute [5][6].
  • Consenso informato e designazione del rappresentante in Romania: In Romania la Legge sui diritti del paziente (Legea drepturilor pacientului nr. 46/2003, nell'ambito di competenza del Ministerul Sănătății) tutela il diritto del paziente di accettare o rifiutare trattamenti medici e di designare per iscritto un rappresentante legale o familiare autorizzato a ricevere le informazioni cliniche e a esprimere il consenso qualora la persona non sia più in grado di decidere autonomamente [3]. È consigliabile depositare tale designazione scritta direttamente nella cartella clinica presso la struttura sanitaria rumena.

steps.title: Costituzione di procure finanziarie e sanitarie separate nei due ordinamenti
steps.html:
Banche, uffici pubblici e notai in Italia e in Romania richiedono atti di rappresentanza conformi alle rispettive leggi nazionali.

  • Procura notarile e Amministrazione di Sostegno in Italia: Finché la persona malata conserva piena capacità d'agire, può conferire una procura generale o speciale per atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata tramite un notaio del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato per la gestione di conti bancari, immobili e pratiche amministrative in Italia [7]. Qualora sopraggiunga una limitazione dell'autonomia, è possibile ricorrere all'istituto dell'Amministrazione di Sostegno presentando ricorso al Giudice Tutelare presso il Tribunale del luogo di residenza o domicilio.
  • Procură autentică notarială o consolare per la Romania: Per gestire conti correnti, pensioni o beni immobili situati in Romania, è necessaria una procura speciale o generale in forma autentica (procură autentică notarială) redatta da un notaio pubblico rumeno appartenente all'Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (UNNPR) [8]. Se il vostro familiare si trova in Italia e non può viaggiare in Romania, la procura valida direttamente nell'ordinamento rumeno senza necessità di apostille né traduzione può essere sottoscritta presso una rappresentanza consolare della Romania in Italia (ad esempio a Roma, Milano, Torino, Bologna o presso il Consolato Generale di Romania a Trieste), previa prenotazione sul portale ufficiale dei servizi consolari (eConsulat.ro) [9].

steps.title: Richiesta di congedi per caregiver, permessi lavorativi e prestazioni di invalidità
steps.html:
Entrambi i Paesi prevedono tutele lavorative per i familiari che assistono una persona gravemente malata e prestazioni economiche di supporto.

  • Legge 104/1992, congedo straordinario e indennità in Italia: Richiedendo con procedura d'urgenza (particolarmente accelerata per i pazienti oncologici con iter entro 15 giorni) l'accertamento dell'invalidità civile con indennità di accompagnamento e dello stato di handicap in situazione di gravità (Legge 104/1992, art. 3 comma 3), i familiari lavoratori dipendenti in Italia possono fruire di 3 giorni di permesso mensile retribuito [10] e fino a 2 anni complessivi di congedo straordinario retribuito tramite l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, numero verde 803 164 da fisso o 06 164 164 da cellulare) [11].
  • Concediu per assistenza a paziente oncologico in Romania: In Romania i lavoratori assicurati nel sistema pubblico hanno diritto al congedo medico e alla relativa indennità per l'assistenza e l'accompagnamento del paziente con patologie oncologiche maggiorenne (concediu și indemnizație pentru îngrijirea pacientului cu afecțiuni oncologice), fino a 45 giorni di calendario all'anno, erogati tramite la Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate [3]. Inoltre, il Codice del lavoro rumeno (Codul muncii) riconosce ai lavoratori dipendenti il congedo per caregiver (concediul de îngrijitor) di 5 giorni lavorativi all'anno per assistere un familiare con gravi problemi medici.

steps.title: Allineamento di testamenti, conti bancari, volontà funerarie e pratiche di successione
steps.html:
Coordinare in anticipo le disposizioni testamentarie e la documentazione anagrafica tra Italia e Romania semplifica gli adempimenti previdenziali, bancari e fiscali successivi a un eventuale decesso.

  • Pianificazione e adempimenti successori in Italia: Con l'assistenza di un notaio del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato è possibile redigere o verificare un testamento conforme al Regolamento UE n. 650/2012 (che consente al cittadino rumeno residente in Italia di scegliere la legge nazionale rumena o di mantenere quella della residenza abituale) e interrogare in seguito il Registro Generale dei Testamenti [7]. Dopo il decesso, l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale gestisce le domande di pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o pensione indiretta) [12], mentre la dichiarazione di successione deve essere presentata telematicamente all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione [13].
  • Pianificazione e adempimenti successori in Romania: In Romania la Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (CNPP, tramite le Case Teritoriale de Pensii) eroga l'assegno funerario (ajutorul de deces), che per legge viene pagato entro 3 giorni lavorativi dalla presentazione della domanda completa del certificato di decesso e delle prove di spesa, oltre alla pensione ai superstiti (pensia de urmaș) [14]. La procedura successorale notarile (procedura succesorală notarială) si svolge davanti a un notaio pubblico rumeno nella circoscrizione dell'ultimo domicilio o dove si trovano i beni principali [8][15]; se la successione viene conclusa entro 2 anni dalla data del decesso, gli eredi sono esenti dall'imposta di successione dell'1% sul valore della massa ereditaria (applicata oltre i 2 anni a favore dell'Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală - ANAF) [16]. Si raccomanda infine di lasciare istruzioni scritte sulle preferenze tra sepoltura locale e rimpatrio internazionale della salma o delle ceneri.

it.closingQuestion: Per adattare queste indicazioni al vostro caso specifico: 1. Il vostro familiare si trova attualmente in cura in Italia o in Romania, e in quale dei due Paesi sono assicurati i familiari che prestano assistenza lavorativa? 2. In quale Regione italiana e in quale distretto (județ) della Romania si trovano la residenza e gli eventuali beni immobili o conti bancari?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Italy & Switzerland
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Italy & Switzerland
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Italy and Switzerland: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is facing a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Italy and Switzerland, it is essential to coordinate the healthcare, legal, and social security instruments of both jurisdictions in advance. Because Switzerland is not an EU Member State and applies its own statutory rules on advance directives, advance care mandates, and international succession law, below are the five official steps in chronological order to initiate while your ill relative retains full capacity of judgment.

steps.title: Organizing palliative care, hospice care, and cross-border health coverage between Italy and Switzerland
steps.html:
The first step is to activate the palliative care team in the country of care and verify cross-border reimbursement rules between the Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale) and the Swiss health insurer (Krankenkasse / cassa malati).

  • Palliative care network and hospices in Italy: Under Law 38/2010 (Legge 38/2010), the general practitioner (medico di medicina generale) or hospital specialist activates the Local Palliative Care Network (Rete Locale di Cure Palliative) of the Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL, for example ASL Città di Torino, ATS Insubria, or ASL Roma 1) for specialist home palliative care (UCP-DOM) or inpatient admission to a Hospice, fully covered by the National Health Service in accordance with guidance from the Ministero della Salute (Italian Ministry of Health) [1]. Additional information on regional networks is provided by the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (Italian Society of Palliative Care - SICP) [2].
  • Spitex palliative care, cantonal networks, and KLV coverage in Switzerland: In Switzerland, home and inpatient palliative care are coordinated through home care nursing services (Spitex-Palliativpflege) and the cantonal networks affiliated with the national association palliative.ch (Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Palliative Medizin, Pflege und Begleitung, such as palliative ti in Ticino or palliative zh+sh in Zurich) [3]. Medical and nursing palliative care benefits are covered under compulsory basic health insurance in accordance with the Healthcare Benefits Ordinance (Krankenpflege-Leistungsverordnung - KLV / OPre). In the event of a transfer or cross-border care between Italy and Switzerland, verify in advance with the ASL or the Swiss health insurer (Krankenkasse) the issuance of Form S1 or prior authorization Form S2 under the bilateral social security coordination agreements.

steps.title: Executing Advance Healthcare Directives and patient directives in Italy and Switzerland
steps.html:
To ensure that end-of-life clinical decisions are immediately recognized by physicians in both Italy and Switzerland, it is advisable to execute both documents while your family member has full capacity.

  • Advance Healthcare Directives (Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento - DAT / Biotestamento) in Italy: Under Law 219/2017 (Legge 219/2017), the ill person can state their wishes regarding medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and appoint a healthcare proxy (fiduciario) to liaise with the medical team [4]. DATs are executed by notarial deed or by private document delivered in person to the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the municipality of residence (for example in the Municipality of Milan, Como, or Rome), which transmits them to the National DAT Database (Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT) at the Ministero della Salute [4][5].
  • Patient directive (Patientenverfügung) in Switzerland: Under Swiss law, patient directives (schriftliche Patientenverfügung / direttive del paziente) are governed by Articles 370 et seq. of the Swiss Civil Code (ZGB / CC) and must be drawn up in writing, dated, and signed by hand by a person who has capacity of judgment, as explained on the official Swiss portal ch.ch [6]. The patient may designate an individual to represent them in medical decisions and use the official templates prepared by the Federazione dei medici svizzeri - FMH (Verbindung der Schweizer Ärztinnen und Ärzte, Swiss Medical Association) or the Swiss Red Cross (Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz - SRK) [3][7].

steps.title: Establishing separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
Swiss and Italian banks and public authorities require separate instruments of representation that meet their respective formal rules in order to prevent frozen accounts or administrative paralysis if incapacity occurs.

  • Notarial power of attorney and Support Administration (Amministrazione di Sostegno) in Italy: While the ill person retains legal capacity, they can grant a general or special power of attorney (procura generale o speciale) by public deed or authenticated private instrument before a notary of the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Notaries) to manage bank accounts, real estate, and tax matters in Italy [8]. If a partial or total loss of autonomy occurs without an adequate power of attorney, family members can petition the Tutelary Judge (Giudice Tutelare) of the competent court (Tribunale) for the appointment of a Support Administrator (Amministratore di Sostegno).
  • Advance care mandate (Vorsorgeauftrag) and bank powers of attorney in Switzerland: In Switzerland, under Articles 360 et seq. ZGB, an advance care mandate (Vorsorgeauftrag / mandato precauzionale) allows a person to appoint a natural or legal person to handle personal care (Personensorge), financial affairs (Vermögenssorge), and legal representation in the event of incapacity of judgment [6][9]. To be valid, it must either be written, dated, and signed entirely by hand by the principal (eigenhändig) or executed as an authentic notarial deed (öffentlich beurkundet); once incapacity occurs, it is validated by the Child and Adult Protection Authority (Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde - KESB / APMA) [6][9]. Because many Swiss banks also require their own internal authorization forms, it is advisable to sign dedicated bank powers of attorney (Bankvollmachten) directly with the Swiss financial institutions at the same time.

steps.title: Claiming caregiver leave, work permits, and disability benefits
steps.html:
Both Italy and Switzerland provide paid leave for employed family caregivers as well as allowances for continuous care needs.

  • Law 104/1992 (Legge 104/1992), extraordinary leave, and attendance allowance in Italy: By activating the fast-track procedure for recognition of civil invalidity with attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento) and severe disability status (handicap in situazione di gravità under Law 104/1992, Art. 3(3)), employees in Italy are entitled to 3 days of paid monthly leave [10] and up to 2 years of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Social Security Institute - INPS, toll-free number 803 164 from landlines or 06 164 164 from mobile phones) [11].
  • Caregiver leave and helplessness allowance (Hilflosenentschädigung) in Switzerland: In Switzerland, the Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht - Art. 329g OR / CO) entitles employees to paid leave to care for family members with health problems (up to 3 days per event and up to 10 days per year, in addition to up to 14 weeks of care leave for parents of severely ill children financed through the EO/APG loss-of-earnings scheme), as confirmed by the Ufficio federale delle assicurazioni sociali (Federal Social Insurance Office - UFAS / BSV) [12]. For an insured person who regularly requires assistance with everyday activities, a helplessness allowance (Hilflosenentschädigung / assegno per grandi invalidi) under AHV/IV (AVS/AI) can be claimed through the competent compensation fund or IV/AI office, alongside cantonal relief services for family caregivers [13].

steps.title: Aligning wills, bank accounts, funeral wishes, and succession procedures
steps.html:
Because Italy applies EU Regulation No 650/2012 and Switzerland applies the Federal Act on Private International Law (IPRG / LDIP), aligning wills with notarial guidance is essential to avoid conflicts of jurisdiction between the two countries.

  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Italy: Through a notary of the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, your family member can review their testamentary dispositions, and heirs can subsequently search the General Register of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) [8]. Following death, the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale handles applications for survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti, either reversibilità or indiretta) [14], while heirs must file the inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months of the date of death [15].
  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Switzerland: In Switzerland, the AHV compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse der AHV), coordinated by the Centro d'informazione AVS/AI (AHV/IV Information Center), pays 1st-pillar survivor pensions (Hinterlassenenrenten: widow's, widower's, and orphan's pensions) [13], while the occupational pension fund (Pensionskasse / 2nd pillar) disburses occupational survivor benefits under its scheme rules. To access bank accounts and transfer assets in Switzerland, heirs apply for a certificate of inheritance (Erbenbescheinigung / certificat d'héritier / certificato ereditario) from the competent cantonal authority (Erbschaftsamt, Bezirksgericht, or Pretura, for example in Zurich, Bern, or Lugano); if the estate is over-indebted, renunciation of the inheritance (Ausschlagung) must be declared within the strict statutory deadline of 3 months from learning of the death under the Swiss Civil Code, as explained on ch.ch [16]. Finally, it is advisable to document wishes regarding local burial or international repatriation of remains or ashes in writing.

closingQuestion: To help us provide more targeted guidance, is your family member currently receiving medical care in Italy or in Switzerland, and in which Swiss canton and Italian region are their habitual residence, bank accounts, or real estate located?

it.title: Malattia terminale e pianificazione tra Italia e Svizzera: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la gestione medica e legale di una malattia grave tra Italia e Svizzera: cure palliative, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento (DAT), procure nei due Paesi, congedi per familiari e successione.
it.introHtml: Quando il vostro familiare affronta una malattia grave, ingravescente o terminale e possiede legami di residenza, cittadinanza, famiglia o patrimonio tra l'Italia e la Svizzera, è fondamentale coordinare in anticipo gli strumenti sanitari, legali e previdenziali di entrambi gli ordinamenti. Poiché la Svizzera non fa parte dell'Unione Europea e applica regole proprie su direttive anticipate, mandato precauzionale e diritto successorio, vi illustriamo di seguito i cinque passaggi ufficiali in ordine cronologico, da avviare finché la persona malata conserva la piena capacità di discernimento.

steps.title: Organizzazione delle cure palliative, dell'hospice e della copertura sanitaria tra Italia e Svizzera
steps.html:
Il primo passo consiste nell'attivare il team di cure palliative nel Paese di cura e nel verificare le condizioni di rimborso transfrontaliero tra il Servizio Sanitario Nazionale italiano e la cassa malati svizzera.

  • Rete di cure palliative e hospice in Italia: Ai sensi della Legge 38/2010, il medico di medicina generale o lo specialista ospedaliero attiva la Rete Locale di Cure Palliative della Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL, ad esempio l'ASL Città di Torino, l'ATS Insubria o l'ASL Roma 1) per l'assistenza domiciliare specialistica (UCP-DOM) o per il ricovero in Hospice, interamente coperti dal Servizio Sanitario Nazionale secondo le indicazioni del Ministero della Salute [1]. Ulteriori riferimenti sulle reti regionali sono messi a disposizione dalla Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [2].
  • Cure palliative Spitex, reti cantonali e copertura KLV in Svizzera: In Svizzera le cure palliative domiciliari e stazionarie sono coordinate tramite i servizi di assistenza e cura a domicilio (Spitex-Palliativpflege) e le reti cantonali aderenti all'associazione nazionale palliative.ch (Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Palliative Medizin, Pflege und Begleitung, come palliative ti in Ticino o palliative zh+sh a Zurigo) [3]. Le prestazioni mediche e infermieristiche di cure palliative rientrano nell'assicurazione obbligatoria delle cure medico-sanitarie secondo l'Ordinanza sulle prestazioni (Krankenpflege-Leistungsverordnung - KLV / OPre). In caso di trasferimento o cure tra Italia e Svizzera, verificate preventivamente con la ASL o con l'assicuratore malattia svizzero (Krankenkasse) il rilascio del modulo S1 o dell'autorizzazione preventiva S2 in base agli accordi bilaterali sul coordinamento della sicurezza sociale.

steps.title: Redazione delle disposizioni anticipate di trattamento e delle direttive del paziente in Italia e Svizzera
steps.html:
Per garantire che le decisioni cliniche di fine vita siano immediatamente riconosciute dai medici sia in Italia sia in Svizzera, è consigliabile predisporre entrambi i documenti finché il vostro familiare ha piena capacità.

  • Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT / Biotestamento) in Italia: In base alla Legge 219/2017, la persona malata può esprimere le proprie volontà sui trattamenti sanitari (inclusi nutrizione e idratazione artificiali) e nominare un fiduciario per i rapporti con l'équipe sanitaria [4]. Le DAT vengono redatte per atto notarile o mediante scrittura privata consegnata personalmente presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune di residenza (ad esempio presso il Comune di Milano, Como o Roma), che le trasmette alla Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT presso il Ministero della Salute [4][5].
  • Direttive del paziente (Patientenverfügung) in Svizzera: Nel diritto svizzero, le direttive del paziente (schriftliche Patientenverfügung) sono disciplinate dagli articoli 370 e seguenti del Codice civile svizzero (ZGB / CC) e devono essere redatte per iscritto, datate e firmate di proprio pugno dalla persona capace di discernimento, come illustrato dal portale ufficiale ch.ch [6]. È possibile designare una persona fisica che rappresenti il paziente nelle decisioni mediche e utilizzare i modelli ufficiali predisposti dalla Federazione dei medici svizzeri - FMH (Verbindung der Schweizer Ärztinnen und Ärzte) o dalla Croce Rossa Svizzera (Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz - SRK) [3][7].

steps.title: Costituzione di procure finanziarie e sanitarie separate nei due ordinamenti
steps.html:
Le banche e le autorità svizzere e italiane richiedono strumenti di rappresentanza distinti e conformi alle rispettive norme formali per evitare il blocco dell'operatività in caso di incapacità.

  • Procura notarile e Amministrazione di Sostegno in Italia: Mentre la persona malata conserva la capacità di agire, può conferire una procura generale o speciale per atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata presso un notaio del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato per gestire conti correnti, immobili e adempimenti fiscali in Italia [8]. Qualora subentri una perdita parziale o totale di autonomia senza procura adeguata, i familiari possono rivolgersi al Giudice Tutelare del Tribunale competente per la nomina di un Amministratore di Sostegno.
  • Mandato precauzionale (Vorsorgeauftrag) e procure bancarie in Svizzera: In Svizzera, ai sensi degli articoli 360 e seguenti ZGB, il mandato precauzionale (Vorsorgeauftrag) consente di incaricare una persona fisica o giuridica della cura della persona (Personensorge), della cura del patrimonio (Vermögenssorge) e della rappresentanza nelle relazioni giuridiche in caso di incapacità di discernimento [6][9]. Per essere valido, deve essere interamente scritto a mano, datato e firmato dall'interessato (eigenhändig) oppure rogato per atto pubblico notarile (öffentlich beurkundet); al verificarsi dell'incapacità, viene validato dall'Autorità di protezione dei minori e degli adulti (Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde - KESB / APMA) [6][9]. Poiché molte banche svizzere richiedono anche moduli interni specifici, è opportuno sottoscrivere contestualmente apposite procure bancarie (Bankvollmachten) presso gli istituti di credito elvetici.

steps.title: Richiesta di congedi per caregiver, permessi lavorativi e prestazioni di invalidità
steps.html:
Sia l'Italia sia la Svizzera prevedono permessi retribuiti per i familiari lavoratori e assegni per il bisogno di assistenza continuativa.

  • Legge 104/1992, congedo straordinario e accompagnamento in Italia: Attivando la procedura d'urgenza per il riconoscimento dell'invalidità civile con indennità di accompagnamento e dell'handicap in situazione di gravità (Legge 104/1992, art. 3 comma 3), i lavoratori dipendenti in Italia hanno diritto a 3 giorni di permesso mensile retribuito [10] e fino a 2 anni di congedo straordinario retribuito tramite l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, numero verde 803 164 da fisso o 06 164 164 da cellulare) [11].
  • Congedo di assistenza e assegno per grandi invalidi in Svizzera: In Svizzera il Codice delle obbligazioni (Obligationenrecht - Art. 329g OR / CO) garantisce ai lavoratori dipendenti un congedo pagato per l'assistenza ai familiari con problemi di salute (fino a 3 giorni per evento e massimo 10 giorni all'anno, oltre al congedo di assistenza fino a 14 settimane per genitori di figli gravemente malati finanziato tramite le IPG), come confermato dall'Ufficio federale delle assicurazioni sociali (UFAS / BSV) [12]. Per la persona assicurata che necessita di aiuto regolare per gli atti ordinari della vita, è possibile richiedere l'assegno per grandi invalidi (Hilflosenentschädigung) dell'AVS/AI tramite la cassa di compensazione o l'ufficio AI competente, affiancato dai servizi cantonali di sgravio per familiari curanti [13].

steps.title: Allineamento di testamenti, conti bancari, volontà funerarie e pratiche di successione
steps.html:
Poiché l'Italia applica il Regolamento UE n. 650/2012 e la Svizzera applica la Legge federale sul diritto internazionale privato (LDIP / IPRG), è essenziale allineare i testamenti con l'assistenza notarile per evitare conflitti di competenza tra i due Paesi.

  • Pianificazione e adempimenti successori in Italia: Tramite un notaio del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato è possibile verificare le disposizioni testamentarie e successivamente consultare il Registro Generale dei Testamenti [8]. Dopo il decesso, l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale gestisce le domande di pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o pensione indiretta) [14], mentre gli eredi devono presentare la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data del decesso [15].
  • Pianificazione e adempimenti successori in Svizzera: In Svizzera la cassa di compensazione dell'AVS (Ausgleichskasse der AHV), coordinata dal Centro d'informazione AVS/AI, eroga le rendite per superstiti (Hinterlassenenrenten: rendita vedovile e per orfani del 1° pilastro) [13], mentre la cassa pensioni (Pensionskasse / 2° pilastro) liquida le prestazioni della previdenza professionale secondo il proprio regolamento. Per accedere ai conti e trasferire i beni in Svizzera, gli eredi richiedono il certificato ereditario (Erbenbescheinigung / certificat d'héritier) presso l'autorità cantonale competente (Erbschaftsamt, Bezirksgericht o Pretura, ad esempio a Zurigo, Berna o Lugano); qualora l'eredità sia gravata da debiti, la rinuncia all'eredità (Ausschlagung) deve essere dichiarata entro il termine perentorio di 3 mesi dalla conoscenza del decesso secondo il Codice civile svizzero, come indicato da ch.ch [16]. Si consiglia infine di documentare per iscritto le volontà su sepoltura locale o rimpatrio internazionale della salma o delle ceneri.

it.closingQuestion: Per fornirvi indicazioni ancora più mirate: 1. Il vostro familiare riceve attualmente le cure mediche in Italia o in Svizzera, e presso quale dei due Paesi è iscritto al servizio sanitario o alla cassa malati? 2. In quale Cantone svizzero e in quale Regione italiana si trovano la residenza abituale, i conti bancari o gli immobili?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Portugal & Brazil
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Portugal & Brazil
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Portugal and Brazil: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Portugal and Brazil, it is essential to coordinate clinical, notarial, and social security instruments in both countries without delay. Below are the five official and practical steps in order of priority, which should be initiated while your ill relative retains full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Organizing palliative care and coordinating health coverage between Portugal and Brazil
steps.html:
The first step is to activate the palliative care team in the country where care is taking place and verify bilateral healthcare protection rules if travel or relocation between Portugal and Brazil is being considered.

  • National Palliative Care Network in Portugal: Within the Serviço Nacional de Saúde (Portuguese National Health Service - SNS), referrals to community palliative care support teams (home care) or inpatient palliative care units of the National Palliative Care Network (Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos - RNCP, integrated into Local Health Units, Unidades Locais de Saúde, such as in Lisbon or Porto) are made by the family doctor or hospital team, with guidance also available via the SNS 24 helpline (808 24 24 24) [1]. Additional resources and directories of specialized teams are provided by the Portuguese Association for Palliative Care (Associação Portuguesa de Cuidados Paliativos - APCP).
  • Palliative care under SUS and coordination with Brazil: In Brazil, the National Palliative Care Policy (Política Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos) within the Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde - SUS, coordinated by the Ministério da Saúde) integrates palliative support across primary, hospital, and home care through the Melhor em Casa program [2], supported by technical mapping from the Conselho Federal de Medicina (Federal Council of Medicine - CFM) [3] and the Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (National Academy of Palliative Care - ANCP) [4]. For travel or relocation between Portugal and Brazil, verify in advance the issuance of the Certificate of Entitlement to Medical Assistance (Certificado de Direito à Assistência Médica - CDAM / PB4) under the bilateral Portugal-Brazil social security agreement, as well as medical air transport coverage with the insurer.

steps.title: Executing Advance Healthcare Directives (Living Wills) in Portugal and Brazil
steps.html:
Written advance medical directives follow the formal requirements of each jurisdiction; it is therefore advisable to register them separately in Portugal and Brazil while your family member has full capacity.

  • Advance Directive (Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade - DAV) and RENTEV in Portugal: In Portugal, the ill person can formalize an Advance Healthcare Directive (Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade / Testamento Vital) and appoint a Healthcare Proxy (Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde) to make decisions on medical treatments (such as artificial life support or futile treatments) if they become unable to express their wishes autonomously [5]. The official form is registered in the National Living Will Registry (Registo Nacional do Testamento Vital - RENTEV, managed by the Shared Services of the Ministry of Health, Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde - SPMS) either in person at a RENTEV desk or with a digital signature via the SNS 24 portal, making it accessible to doctors in the electronic health record for a renewable 5-year period [5].
  • Advance Directives (Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade) in Brazil: In Brazil, the Living Will (Testamento Vital / Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade) is regulated by CFM Resolution No. 1,995/2012 (Resolução CFM n.º 1.995/2012) of the Conselho Federal de Medicina, which directs physicians to respect the instructions previously expressed by the patient regarding care and treatment in the terminal phase [3][4]. To ensure legal certainty and easy access, the document should be recorded directly in the patient's medical chart (prontuário médico) with the treating team and may also be executed as a public deed at a Notary Office (Cartório de Notas) in Brazil (or via the e-Notariado platform) [4].

steps.title: Granting separate financial and healthcare Powers of Attorney in both jurisdictions
steps.html:
Banks, registry offices, notary offices, and public agencies in Portugal and Brazil require instruments of representation issued in accordance with their respective national rules.

  • Notarial power of attorney and mandate for accompanied adulthood in Portugal: While retaining full mental capacity, the ill person can grant a power of attorney (procuração) at a Notary Office (Cartório Notarial, overseen by the Order of Notaries, Ordem dos Notários) or at a Registry Office (Conservatória) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary - IRN) for banking transactions, property management, and tax representation in Portugal [6]. To prepare for potential future incapacity, Portuguese law also allows the execution of a mandate with a view to accompaniment (mandato com vista a acompanhamento), which guides the court if the accompanied adult legal regime (regime jurídico do maior acompanhado) later becomes necessary.
  • Public and social security Powers of Attorney for Brazil: To manage bank accounts, real estate, and benefits in Brazil, a Public Power of Attorney (Procuração Pública) drawn up at a Notary Office (Cartório de Notas, for example in São Paulo or Rio de Janeiro, or electronically via the e-Notariado platform of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil - CNB for holders of a notarized digital certificate) is required. If your family member resides in Portugal and holds Brazilian citizenship, they can execute a Public Power of Attorney directly at a Consulate-General of Brazil (in Lisbon, Porto, or Faro) with immediate validity in Brazil, in addition to registering a specific power of attorney for representation before the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (National Institute of Social Security - INSS, helpline 135) [7].

steps.title: Claiming serious illness support, disability benefits, and caregiver leave
steps.html:
Both countries provide fast-track social benefits for severe dependency and labor protections for family caregivers.

  • Dependency Supplement, Informal Caregiver Status, and caregiver leave in Portugal: In Portugal, Segurança Social (Social Security) grants the Dependency Supplement (Complemento por Dependência) to pensioners who require permanent third-party assistance and recognizes Informal Caregiver Status (Estatuto do Cuidador Informal, which includes a means-tested Main Informal Caregiver Support Allowance, Subsídio de Apoio ao Cuidador Informal Principal) [8][9]. Under the Portuguese Labor Code (Código do Trabalho), employees in Portugal are also entitled to statutory absences and leave to provide urgent and indispensable care to a family member with a serious or chronic illness.
  • 25% INSS supplement, Income Tax exemption, and FGTS withdrawal in Brazil: In Brazil, a person insured with the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) is entitled to temporary incapacity benefit (auxílio por incapacidade temporária) or permanent incapacity retirement (aposentadoria por incapacidade permanente), increased by a 25% supplement (acréscimo de 25%) when permanent assistance from another person is required [7]. Retirees and pensioners diagnosed with a qualifying serious illness under Law No. 7,713/1988 (Lei n.º 7.713/1988, such as malignant neoplasia, severe heart disease, or irreversible paralysis) can apply for an Income Tax exemption (isenção de Imposto de Renda) through the INSS and the Receita Federal (Federal Revenue Service of Brazil) [10][11], and a worker (or account holder with a dependent suffering from a serious illness or in the terminal stage of life) may withdraw their full FGTS balance through the Caixa Econômica Federal (including via the FGTS app) [12].

steps.title: Aligning wills, bank access, funeral wishes, and estate settlement between Portugal and Brazil
steps.html:
Planning estate succession and post-death formalities in advance prevents conflicts between the EU Succession Regulation (applicable in Portugal) and Brazilian law (which reserves the probate and partitioning of assets located in Brazil exclusively to Brazilian courts and notary offices).

  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Portugal: Following a death in Portugal, family members can apply to Segurança Social for the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days), Reimbursement of Funeral Expenses (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days), and the Survivor Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [13]. Confirmation of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and estate partitioning are handled through the Inheritance Desk (Balcão das Heranças) and the Death Desk (Espaço Óbito) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [6][14], and the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must file the free property transfer declaration (Stamp Duty Form 1, Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) with the Tax and Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira) via the Finance Portal on Gov.pt by the end of the third month following the month of death [15].
  • Succession planning and post-death formalities in Brazil: In Brazil, dependents apply for the Survivor Pension (Pensão por Morte) from the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, via the Meu INSS portal or app or by calling 135) [16] and request the release of remaining FGTS and PIS/PASEP balances at the Caixa Econômica Federal [12]. If there are assets located in Brazil, opening judicial or extrajudicial probate (inventário judicial ou extrajudicial, the latter at a Cartório de Notas of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil when all heirs are of legal age, capable, and in agreement) is mandatory within the statutory deadline of 2 months (60 days) from the date of death to avoid state penalties on the Estate and Gift Tax (Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação - ITCMD). It is also advisable to record preferences between a local funeral and international repatriation in writing.

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your family's specific situation, is your family member currently receiving medical care in Portugal or in Brazil, and in which Portuguese municipality (concelho) and Brazilian state are their residence, bank accounts, or real estate located?

pt.title: Doença terminal e planeamento legal entre Portugal e Brasil: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos perante doença grave ou terminal com ligações entre Portugal e Brasil: cuidados paliativos, diretivas antecipadas de vontade, procurações nos dois países, apoios ao cuidador e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Quando o seu familiar recebe o diagnóstico de uma doença grave, progressiva ou terminal e possui vínculos de residência, nacionalidade, família ou património entre Portugal e o Brasil, é essencial articular atempadamente os instrumentos clínicos, notariais e previdenciários de ambos os países. Abaixo apresentamos os cinco passos oficiais e práticos por ordem de prioridade, que devem ser iniciados enquanto a pessoa doente mantém plena capacidade de decisão.

steps.title: Organização de cuidados paliativos e coordenação de cobertura de saúde entre Portugal e o Brasil
steps.html:
O primeiro passo consiste em acionar a equipa de cuidados paliativos no país onde decorre a assistência e verificar as regras bilaterais de proteção na saúde caso se pondere uma deslocação entre Portugal e o Brasil.

  • Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos em Portugal: No Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS), a referenciação para equipas comunitárias de suporte em cuidados paliativos (domiciliárias) ou unidades de internamento da Rede Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (RNCP, integradas nas Unidades Locais de Saúde, como em Lisboa ou no Porto) é feita pelo médico de família ou pela equipa hospitalar, podendo obter orientação através da linha SNS 24 (808 24 24 24) [1]. Recursos adicionais e diretórios de equipas especializadas são disponibilizados pela Associação Portuguesa de Cuidados Paliativos (APCP).
  • Cuidados paliativos no SUS e coordenação com o Brasil: No Brasil, a Política Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos no âmbito do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS, coordenada pelo Ministério da Saúde) integra o acompanhamento paliativo na atenção primária, hospitalar e na atenção domiciliar através do programa Melhor em Casa [2], contando ainda com o mapeamento técnico do Conselho Federal de Medicina [3] e da Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos [4]. Para deslocações entre Portugal e o Brasil, verifique previamente a emissão do Certificado de Direito à Assistência Médica (CDAM / PB4) ao abrigo do acordo bilateral luso-brasileiro, bem como as condições de transporte aéreo médico junto da seguradora.

steps.title: Formalização de diretivas antecipadas de vontade (Testamento Vital) em Portugal e no Brasil
steps.html:
As declarações antecipadas de vontade médica seguem as regras formais de cada jurisdição; por isso, convém registá-las separadamente em Portugal e no Brasil enquanto o seu familiar tem plena capacidade.

  • Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade (DAV) e RENTEV em Portugal: Em Portugal, a pessoa doente pode formalizar a sua Diretiva Antecipada de Vontade (Testamento Vital) e nomear um Procurador de Cuidados de Saúde para decidir sobre tratamentos médicos (como suporte artificial das funções vitais ou tratamentos fúteis) caso fique incapaz de expressar a sua vontade autonomamente [5]. O formulário oficial é registado no Registo Nacional do Testamento Vital (RENTEV, gerido pelos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde - SPMS) presencialmente num balcão RENTEV ou com assinatura digital através do portal do SNS 24, ficando acessível aos médicos no processo clínico eletrónico por um período renovável de 5 anos [5].
  • Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade no Brasil: No Brasil, o Testamento Vital (Diretivas Antecipadas de Vontade) é regulamentado pela Resolução CFM n.º 1.995/2012 do Conselho Federal de Medicina, que determina que os médicos respeitem as instruções previamente expressas pelo paciente sobre cuidados e tratamentos em fase terminal [3][4]. Para garantir segurança jurídica e fácil acesso, o documento deve ser registado diretamente no prontuário médico junto da equipa assistente e pode ser lavrado por escritura pública num Cartório de Notas no Brasil (ou via plataforma e-Notariado) [4].

steps.title: Outorga de procurações financeiras e de cuidados de saúde separadas nas duas jurisdições
steps.html:
Instituições bancárias, conservatórias, cartórios e serviços públicos em Portugal e no Brasil exigem instrumentos de representação emitidos segundo as respetivas normas nacionais.

  • Procuração notarial e mandato com vista a acompanhamento em Portugal: Enquanto mantém plena capacidade, a pessoa doente pode outorgar uma procuração num Cartório Notarial (Ordem dos Notários) ou numa Conservatória do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN) para movimentação bancária, administração de imóveis e representação fiscal em Portugal [6]. Para prevenir uma futura incapacidade, a lei portuguesa permite também celebrar um mandato com vista a acompanhamento, que orienta o tribunal caso venha a ser necessário o regime jurídico do maior acompanhado.
  • Procuração pública e previdenciária para o Brasil: Para gerir contas bancárias, imóveis e benefícios no Brasil, é exigida uma Procuração Pública lavrada em Cartório de Notas (por exemplo, em São Paulo ou no Rio de Janeiro, ou de forma eletrónica através da plataforma e-Notariado do Colégio Notarial do Brasil - CNB para quem possua certificado digital notarizado). Se o seu familiar residir em Portugal e tiver nacionalidade brasileira, pode lavrar a Procuração Pública diretamente no Consulado-Geral do Brasil (em Lisboa, no Porto ou em Faro) com validade imediata no Brasil, além de poder cadastrar procuração específica para representação perante o Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, telefone 135) [7].

steps.title: Requerimento de apoios por doença grave, benefícios por incapacidade e licenças para cuidadores
steps.html:
Ambos os países disponibilizam prestações sociais céleres para situações de dependência grave e proteção laboral para familiares cuidadores.

  • Complemento por Dependência, Cuidador Informal e faltas em Portugal: Em Portugal, a Segurança Social atribui o Complemento por Dependência a pensionistas que necessitem da assistência permanente de terceira pessoa e reconhece o Estatuto do Cuidador Informal (com Subsídio de Apoio ao Cuidador Informal Principal mediante condição de recursos) [8][9]. Ao abrigo do Código do Trabalho, os trabalhadores em Portugal têm ainda direito a faltas e licenças para assistência inadiável e imprescindível a familiar com doença grave ou crónica.
  • Acréscimo de 25% no INSS, isenção de Imposto de Renda e saque do FGTS no Brasil: No Brasil, o segurado do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) tem direito ao auxílio por incapacidade temporária ou à aposentadoria por incapacidade permanente, acrescida de um adicional de 25% quando necessitar da assistência permanente de outra pessoa [7]. Aposentados e pensionistas com moléstia grave prevista na Lei n.º 7.713/1988 (como neoplasia maligna, cardiopatia grave ou paralisia irreversível) podem solicitar a isenção de Imposto de Renda junto do INSS e da Receita Federal [10][11], e o trabalhador (ou titular com dependente acometido por doença grave ou estágio terminal de vida) pode efetuar o saque integral do saldo do FGTS junto da Caixa Econômica Federal (inclusive pela aplicação FGTS) [12].

steps.title: Alinhamento de testamentos, acesso bancário, desejos funerários e sucessões entre Portugal e o Brasil
steps.html:
Planear antecipadamente a sucessão patrimonial e as formalidades pós-óbito evita conflitos entre o Regulamento Europeu das Sucessões (aplicável em Portugal) e a lei brasileira (que reserva aos tribunais e cartórios brasileiros a partilha de bens situados no Brasil).

  • Planeamento e formalidades sucessórias em Portugal: Após um falecimento em Portugal, os familiares podem requerer na Segurança Social o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [13]. A habilitação de herdeiros e a partilha tratam-se de forma integrada no Balcão das Heranças e no Espaço Óbito do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [6][14], devendo o cabeça-de-casal apresentar a participação de transmissões gratuitas (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) à Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira através do Portal das Finanças (Gov.pt) até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao mês do óbito [15].
  • Planeamento e formalidades sucessórias no Brasil: No Brasil, os dependentes requerem a Pensão por Morte junto do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, pelo portal ou aplicação Meu INSS ou pelo telefone 135) [16] e a liberação de saldos remanescentes de FGTS e PIS/PASEP na Caixa Econômica Federal [12]. Caso existam bens situados no Brasil, é obrigatória a abertura de inventário judicial ou extrajudicial (em Cartório de Notas do Colégio Notarial do Brasil, quando todos os herdeiros forem capazes e estiverem de acordo) no prazo legal de 2 meses (60 dias) a contar do óbito, para evitar multas estaduais sobre o Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação (ITCMD). Recomendamos também deixar registadas por escrito as preferências entre funeral local ou transladação internacional.

pt.closingQuestion: Para ajustarmos estas orientações à situação concreta da família: 1. O seu familiar encontra-se atualmente em acompanhamento médico em Portugal ou no Brasil, e possui dupla nacionalidade ou residência fiscal num só país? 2. Em que concelho português e em que estado brasileiro se localizam a residência, as contas bancárias ou os imóveis?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Poland & Ukraine
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Poland & Ukraine
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Poland and Ukraine: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
When a family member with residential, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Poland and Ukraine is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness, medical care, advance directives, and powers of attorney should be organized early in both legal systems while the ill person still retains full legal and decision-making capacity.

Below are the 5 main official steps in order.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coordination (Poland and Ukraine)
steps.html:
The first step is to establish a symptom-management plan and care arrangement with the attending physician in the country where the ill person is currently staying:

  • Poland: On the basis of a medical referral (with an ICD-10 diagnosis code confirming eligibility), the National Health Fund (Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia - NFZ, 24/7 toll-free Patient Telephone Information at 800 190 590) funds home hospice care (hospicjum domowe, including medical, nursing, and psychological visits and free loan of medical equipment), outpatient palliative medicine clinics (poradnia medycyny paliatywnej), and inpatient palliative medicine wards (oddział medycyny paliatywnej) or inpatient hospices [1]. Information and support regarding patient rights are also provided by the Patient Rights Ombudsman (Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta, toll-free helpline 800 190 590) [2].
  • Ukraine: If care is organized in Ukraine or a return to Ukraine is planned, under the state Program of Medical Guarantees (Програма медичних гарантій) funded by the National Health Service of Ukraine (Національна служба здоров'я України - NSZU, contact center 16-77), patients are entitled to free inpatient palliative care (стаціонарна паліативна медична допомога) and mobile home palliative care (мобільна паліативна медична допомога) [5]. Admission requires an electronic referral (е-направлення) issued by a family doctor or attending specialist in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України) [5][6]. Before any medical transport between Poland and Ukraine, consult the medical team regarding fitness to travel, pain-medication supply for the journey, and continuity of medical records.

steps.title: Executing Written Medical Declarations and Authorizations While Maintaining Full Capacity
steps.html:
Because medical authorizations and healthcare proxies are governed by the law of the state where treatment is provided, separate declarations should be prepared in Poland and in Ukraine while the ill person has full capacity:

  • Poland: Under the Act on Patient Rights and the Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta (Patient Rights Ombudsman), the patient should file in the medical records of the hospital and clinic a written authorization designating a close person to receive information on their state of health and medical services provided (upoważnienie osoby bliskiej do uzyskiwania informacji o stanie zdrowia) as well as access to medical records (dokumentacja medyczna, both during life and after death) [2]. This authorization should also be registered electronically via the Online Patient Account (Internetowe Konto Pacjenta - IKP) on pacjent.gov.pl, accompanied by a written statement of the patient's wishes regarding consent to or refusal of specific medical procedures [2].
  • Ukraine: Under the Fundamentals of Legislation of Ukraine on Healthcare (Основи законодавства України про охорону здоров'я) overseen by the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України), an adult with legal capacity provides written informed consent (письмова інформована згода пацієнта) to medical interventions or a written refusal of specific procedures, and explicitly designates in the medical record the trusted persons authorized to receive health information and inspect the medical file [6].

steps.title: Establishing Separate Notarial and Banking Powers of Attorney in Poland and in Ukraine
steps.html:
Simple written authorizations or powers of attorney executed in one country without the required statutory form are frequently rejected by banks and public registries in the other country. While your family member retains full legal capacity, separate instruments should be executed:

  • Poland: For acts exceeding ordinary management, real estate transactions, and representation before Polish authorities and courts, execute a power of attorney in the form of a notarial deed (pełnomocnictwo w formie aktu notarialnego) before a Polish notary belonging to the Polish National Council of Notaries (Krajowa Rada Notarialna; in cases of serious illness, a notary may perform the act outside the notarial office, at the patient's home or hospital) [3]. Separately from the notarial deed, file a dedicated bank account power of attorney (pełnomocnictwo do rachunków bankowych) directly with each Polish bank on its own form, as well as a banking disposition in the event of death (dyspozycja wkładem na wypadek śmierci under Article 56 of the Polish Banking Law), which allows designated close relatives to withdraw funds up to the statutory limit outside probate proceedings.
  • Ukraine: Managing assets, bank accounts, or real estate in Ukraine requires a notarized power of attorney (нотаріальна довіреність) registered in the Unified Register of Powers of Attorney (Єдиний реєстр довіреностей), executed either before a notary in Ukraine (organized under the Notary Chamber of Ukraine, Нотаріальна палата України) [7] or certified abroad by a Ukrainian consul - for example at the Consular Section of the Embassy of Ukraine in Warsaw (Wydział Konsularny Ambasady Ukrainy w Warszawie, ul. Antoniego Malczewskiego 17, general tel. +48 22 621 39 79, emergency tel. +48 698 608 837, email consul_pl@mfa.gov.ua) [8]. A power of attorney executed before a Polish notary requires a sworn translation into Ukrainian before it can be used in Ukraine.

steps.title: Caregiver Leave, Care Allowances, and Disability Support Benefits
steps.html:
Both the Polish and Ukrainian social security systems provide statutory leave and financial support for family caregivers and seriously ill persons:

  • Poland: An employee covered by sickness insurance may apply to the Social Insurance Institution (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych - ZUS, Customer Contact Center tel. +48 22 560 16 00, email cot@zus.pl) for a care allowance (zasiłek opiekuńczy) for personally caring for an ill family member for up to 14 days per calendar year (based on an electronic medical certificate e-ZLA and form Z-15B) [4]. In addition, the Polish Labor Code entitles employees to 5 days of unpaid caregiver leave (urlop opiekuńczy) per calendar year to provide personal care or support to a family member. For an ill person holding a decision from the Provincial Disability Assessment Team (WZON) determining their level of support need, an electronic application can be submitted to Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych for the payment of a supporting benefit (świadczenie wspierające) [4].
  • Ukraine: Within the Ukrainian electronic healthcare system, the attending physician issues an electronic medical conclusion of temporary incapacity for work to care for a sick family member (медичний висновок про тимчасову непрацездатність по догляду за хворим членом сім'ї), which generates an electronic sick leave certificate (е-лікарняний) paid through the Pension Fund of Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України) [9]. Furthermore, in cases of severe limitation of independence, state social care assistance (державна соціальна допомога на догляд) and disability pensions are administered via the Пенсійний фонд України [9].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Survivor Benefits, and Succession Procedures Across Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Coordinating testamentary dispositions early and gathering official civil status certificates helps prevent conflicts of succession law between Poland and Ukraine:

  • Poland: A will executed as a notarial deed can be registered free of charge in the Notarial Register of Wills (Notarialny Rejestr Testamentów - NORT) maintained by the Krajowa Rada Notarialna [3]. Following the death of an insured person or family member, the person covering the funeral expenses has 12 months from the date of death to file form Z-12 for the funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy, set at PLN 7,000 for deaths from 1 January 2026 onward) as well as an application for a survivor pension (renta rodzinna) with Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (or KRUS) [4]. Proof of inheritance rights in Poland is obtained either through a notarial Deed of Certification of Inheritance (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia, entered into the Inheritance Register, Rejestr Spadkowy, operated by the Krajowa Rada Notarialna) [3] or through a court order confirming acquisition of inheritance; heirs have 6 months from learning of their entitlement to file a declaration accepting or renouncing the estate, and 6 months from the registration of the Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia or finality of the court order to submit form SD-Z2 to the competent Tax Office (Urząd Skarbowy) to claim the close-family inheritance tax exemption.
  • Ukraine: Following the death of a pensioner or insured person in Ukraine, applications for the funeral grant (допомога на поховання) and survivor pension for loss of a breadwinner (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) are submitted at any service center or via the electronic portal of the Пенсійний фонд України (detailed instructions are available on the state portal Портал Дія) [9]. Succession proceedings in Ukraine are opened before a Ukrainian notary (member of the Нотаріальна палата України, with registration in the Inheritance Register of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine, Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України): heirs must within a strict deadline of 6 months from the date of death personally file a declaration of acceptance of inheritance (заява про прийняття спадщини) or send it by post with a signature certified by a notary or a Ukrainian consulate (such as the Wydział Konsularny Ambasady Ukrainy w Warszawie) [7][8].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance more closely to your situation, in which country (Poland or Ukraine) is your ill family member currently staying and receiving medical treatment, and in which country are their bank accounts, real estate, or pension entitlements located?
