pl.title: Choroba terminalna i formalności między krajem Polska a Ukraina: oficjalna lista w 5 krokach
pl.cardSummary: Oficjalna lista w 5 krokach w przypadku ciężkiej choroby z powiązaniami między Polska a Ukraina: opieka paliatywna, oświadczenia woli, pełnomocnictwa notarialne w obu krajach, świadczenia opiekuńcze i sprawy spadkowe.
pl.introHtml:
Diagnoza poważnej, nieuleczalnej choroby u członka rodziny posiadającego powiązania życiowe, obywatelskie lub majątkowe między Polską a Ukrainą wymaga wczesnego uporządkowania opieki medycznej, dokumentów woli oraz pełnomocnictw w obu porządkach prawnych, dopóki osoba chora zachowuje pełną zdolność do czynności prawnych i świadomego podejmowania decyzji.

Poniżej przedstawiamy 5 głównych oficjalnych kroków w kolejności.

steps.title: Organizacja opieki paliatywnej i hospicyjnej oraz koordynacja transgraniczna (Polska i Ukraina)
steps.html:
Pierwszym krokiem jest ustalenie z lekarzem prowadzącym planu leczenia objawowego oraz formy opieki w kraju, w którym aktualnie przebywa osoba chora:

  • Polska: Na podstawie skierowania lekarskiego (z kodem rozpoznania ICD-10 potwierdzającym kwalifikację) fundusz Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia (całodobowa, bezpłatna Telefoniczna Informacja Pacjenta pod numerem 800 190 590) finansuje opiekę w warunkach domowych (hospicjum domowe z wizytami lekarskimi, pielęgniarskimi, psychologicznymi i bezpłatnym wypożyczeniem sprzętu medycznego), poradnię medycyny paliatywnej oraz stacjonarny oddział medycyny paliatywnej lub hospicjum stacjonarne [1]. Wsparcie informacyjne w zakresie praw pacjenta zapewnia także urząd Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta (bezpłatna infolinia 800 190 590) [2].
  • Ukraina: Jeżeli opieka jest organizowana na Ukrainie lub planowany jest powrót osoby chorej do tego kraju, w ramach państwowego programu gwarancji medycznych (Програма медичних гарантій), który finansuje ukraińska służba zdrowia (Національна служба здоров'я України, infolinia 16-77), pacjentom przysługuje bezpłatna stacjonarna opieka paliatywna (стаціонарна паліативна медична допомога) oraz mobilna opieka paliatywna w domu (мобільна паліативна медична допомога) [5]. Podstawą przyjęcia jest elektroniczne skierowanie (е-направлення) wystawione przez lekarza rodzinnego lub lekarza specjalistę zgodnie z wytycznymi resortu zdrowia (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України) [5][6]. Przed ewentualnym transportem medycznym między Polską a Ukrainą należy uzgodnić z zespołem medycznym zdolność pacjenta do podróży, zapas leków przeciwbólowych oraz ciągłość dokumentacji medycznej.

steps.title: Sporządzenie pisemnych oświadczeń medycznych i upoważnień przy zachowaniu pełnej świadomości
steps.html:
Ponieważ upoważnienia medyczne podlegają przepisom państwa, w którym udzielane są świadczenia zdrowotne, dokumenty te należy przygotować osobno w Polsce i na Ukrainie, dopóki osoba chora jest w pełni świadoma:

  • Polska: Zgodnie z ustawą o prawach pacjenta i urzędzie Rzecznik Praw Pacjenta, pacjent powinien złożyć w dokumentacji medycznej szpitala i przychodni pisemne upoważnienie osoby bliskiej do uzyskiwania informacji o stanie zdrowia i udzielanych świadczeniach oraz do uzyskiwania dokumentacji medycznej (za życia oraz po śmierci) [2]. Upoważnienie to warto jednocześnie zarejestrować elektronicznie poprzez Internetowe Konto Pacjenta (IKP) na portalu pacjent.gov.pl oraz dołączyć pisemne oświadczenie woli pacjenta dotyczące zgody lub sprzeciwu wobec określonych zabiegów medycznych [2].
  • Ukraina: Zgodnie z ukraińskimi Podstawami ustawodawstwa o ochronie zdrowia (Основи законодавства України про охорону здоров'я), które nadzoruje Міністерство охорони здоров'я України, osoba pełnoletnia i zdolna do czynności prawnych wyraża pisemną świadomą zgodę (письмова інформована згода пацієнта) na interwencje medyczne lub pisemną odmowę określonych procedur, a także wskazuje w dokumentacji medycznej osoby upoważnione do otrzymywania informacji o stanie zdrowia i wglądu w historię choroby [6].

steps.title: Ustanowienie odrębnych pełnomocnictw notarialnych i bankowych w Polsce oraz na Ukrainie
steps.html:
Zwykłe pełnomocnictwa pisemne lub pełnomocnictwa sporządzone w jednym kraju bez odpowiedniej formy często nie są honorowane przez banki i rejestry w drugim państwie. Dopóki członek rodziny zachowuje pełną zdolność do czynności prawnych, należy ustanowić osobne umocowania:

  • Polska: Dla czynności przekraczających zwykły zarząd, obrotu nieruchomościami oraz reprezentacji przed urzędami i sądami w Polsce należy sporządzić pełnomocnictwo w formie aktu notarialnego przed polskim notariuszem (zrzeszonym w samorządzie Krajowa Rada Notarialna; w razie ciężkiej choroby notariusz może dokonać czynności poza kancelarią, w domu lub w szpitalu) [3]. Niezależnie od aktu notarialnego należy złożyć bezpośrednio w każdym polskim banku pełnomocnictwo do rachunków bankowych na formularzu bankowym oraz dyspozycję wkładem na wypadek śmierci (art. 56 Prawa bankowego), która pozwala wskazanym członkom najbliższej rodziny pobrać środki do ustawowego limitu z pominięciem postępowania spadkowego.
  • Ukraina: Do zarządzania majątkiem, rachunkami bankowymi lub nieruchomościami na Ukrainie wymagane jest pełnomocnictwo notarialne (нотаріальна довіреність) z wpisem do Jednolitego Rejestru Pełnomocnictw (Єдиний реєстр довіреностей), sporządzone przed notariuszem na Ukrainie (organizacja zawodowa Нотаріальна палата України) [7] albo poświadczone poza granicami Ukrainy przez ukraińskiego konsula - na przykład przez urząd Wydział Konsularny Ambasady Ukrainy w Warszawie (ul. Antoniego Malczewskiego 17, tel. ogólny +48 22 621 39 79, tel. alarmowy +48 698 608 837, e-mail consul_pl@mfa.gov.ua) [8]. Pełnomocnictwo sporządzone u polskiego notariusza wymaga do użycia na Ukrainie tłumaczenia przysięgłego na język ukraiński.

steps.title: Urlopy dla opiekunów, zasiłki opiekuńcze oraz wsparcie z tytułu niepełnosprawności
steps.html:
Zarówno polski, jak i ukraiński system zabezpieczenia społecznego przewiduje uprawnienia dla opiekunów oraz wsparcie dla osób ciężko chorych:

  • Polska: Pracownik objęty ubezpieczeniem chorobowym może wystąpić do instytucji Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (Centrum Kontaktu Klientów ZUS tel. +48 22 560 16 00, e-mail cot@zus.pl) o zasiłek opiekuńczy z tytułu osobistego sprawowania opieki nad chorym członkiem rodziny w wymiarze do 14 dni w roku kalendarzowym (na podstawie elektronicznego zwolnienia lekarskiego e-ZLA oraz wniosku Z-15B) [4]. Dodatkowo polski Kodeks pracy uprawnia pracownika do 5 dni bezpłatnego urlopu opiekuńczego w roku kalendarzowym w celu zapewnienia osobistej opieki lub wsparcia osobie będącej członkiem rodziny. Dla osoby chorej posiadającej decyzję Wojewódzkiego Zespołu ds. Orzekania o Niepełnosprawności (WZON) ustalającą poziom potrzeby wsparcia można złożyć wniosek elektroniczny do instytucji Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych o wypłatę świadczenia wspierającego [4].
  • Ukraina: W ukraińskim systemie elektronicznej ochrony zdrowia lekarz wystawia elektroniczne orzeczenie o czasowej niezdolności do pracy z tytułu opieki nad chorym członkiem rodziny (медичний висновок про тимчасову непрацездатність по догляду за хворим членом сім'ї), na podstawie którego generowany jest e-szpitalny (е-лікарняний) opłacany przez instytucję Пенсійний фонд України [9]. Ponadto w razie znacznego ograniczenia samodzielności przysługuje państwowa pomoc społeczna na opiekę (державна соціальна допомога на догляд) oraz renta inwalidzka przyznawana przez Пенсійний фонд України [9].

steps.title: Uporządkowanie testamentów, świadczeń pośmiertnych oraz spraw spadkowych w obu jurysdykcjach
steps.html:
Wczesne uzgodnienie rozrządzeń testamentowych oraz zebranie odpisów aktów stanu cywilnego pozwala uniknąć kolizji przepisów spadkowych między Polską a Ukrainą:

  • Polska: Testament sporządzony w formie aktu notarialnego można bezpłatnie zarejestrować w Notarialnym Rejestrze Testamentów (NORT), który prowadzi Krajowa Rada Notarialna [3]. Po śmierci osoby ubezpieczonej lub członka jej rodziny osoba pokrywająca koszty pochówku może w terminie 12 miesięcy od dnia śmierci złożyć wniosek Z-12 o zasiłek pogrzebowy (w wysokości 7 000 zł dla zgonów od 1 stycznia 2026 r.) oraz wniosek o rentę rodzinną do instytucji Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (lub do KRUS) [4]. Potwierdzenie praw do spadku w Polsce następuje poprzez notarialny Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia (wpisywany do bazy Rejestr Spadkowy, którą prowadzi Krajowa Rada Notarialna) [3] albo poprzez sądowe stwierdzenie nabycia spadku; spadkobiercy mają 6 miesięcy od dowiedzenia się o powołaniu do spadku na złożenie oświadczenia o przyjęciu lub odrzuceniu spadku oraz 6 miesięcy od zarejestrowania Aktu Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia lub uprawomocnienia się postanowienia sądu na zgłoszenie formularza SD-Z2 we właściwym Urzędzie Skarbowym w celu skorzystania ze zwolnienia z podatku dla najbliższej rodziny.
  • Ukraina: Po śmierci emeryta lub osoby ubezpieczonej na Ukrainie wniosek o zasiłek pogrzebowy (допомога на поховання) oraz o rentę z tytułu utraty żywiciela (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) składa się w dowolnym centrum obsługi lub przez portal elektroniczny, który prowadzi Пенсійний фонд України (szczegółowe instrukcje udostępnia państwowy serwis Портал Дія) [9]. Sprawę spadkową na Ukrainie otwiera się przed ukraińskim notariuszem (zrzeszonym w organizacji Нотаріальна палата України, z rejestracją w bazie Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України): spadkobiercy muszą w nieprzekraczalnym terminie 6 miesięcy od dnia otwarcia spadku (dnia śmierci) osobiście złożyć oświadczenie o przyjęciu spadku (заява про прийняття спадщини) lub przesłać je pocztą z podpisem poświadczonym notarialnie albo w ukraińskim konsulacie (np. poprzez Wydział Konsularny Ambasady Ukrainy w Warszawie) [7][8].

pl.closingQuestion: Abyśmy mogli dokładniej dopasować wskazówki do Państwa sytuacji: 1. W którym kraju (w Polsce czy na Ukrainie) przebywa obecnie chory członek rodziny i gdzie prowadzone jest jego leczenie? 2. W którym państwie znajdują się rachunki bankowe, nieruchomości lub świadczenia emerytalno-rentowe osoby chorej?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Germany & Ukraine
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Germany & Ukraine
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Germany and Ukraine: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member with residential, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Germany and Ukraine is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness, medical, legal, and financial advance care measures should be coordinated early in both legal systems while the ill person still retains full legal and decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coordination (Germany and Ukraine)
steps.html:
Begin with the attending medical team in the country where the ill person is currently staying to set up pain management, symptom control, and outpatient or inpatient support:

  • Germany: In the case of an incurable, progressive illness with complex symptoms, the patient is entitled to Specialized Outpatient Palliative Care (Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung - SAPV under Section 37b SGB V), prescribed by a physician and covered by statutory health insurance [1]. Where palliative or hospice care is needed, a shortened fast-track care level assessment deadline of one week (Eilbegutachtungsfrist, Section 18a SGB XI) applies for classification by the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) [1]. Regional SAPV teams, outpatient hospice services, palliative wards, and inpatient hospices can be located through the national umbrella association, Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. (German Hospice and Palliative Association) [1].
  • Ukraine: If care takes place in Ukraine or a return there is planned, under the state Program of Medical Guarantees (Програма медичних гарантій) the National Health Service of Ukraine (Національна служба здоров'я України, telephone contact center 16-77) covers the costs of inpatient palliative care (стаціонарна паліативна медична допомога) as well as mobile home palliative teams (мобільна паліативна медична допомога) [6]. Admission requires an electronic referral (е-направлення) issued by a family physician or attending specialist in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України) [6][7]. Before any patient transfer between Germany and Ukraine, fitness to travel, pain-medication continuity, and health insurance coverage should be coordinated in advance with the attending physicians.

steps.title: Written Advance Directives and Medical Proxies While Maintaining Full Capacity
steps.html:
Because living wills and medical information rights vis-à-vis physicians are governed by the law of the respective country of treatment, separate declarations should be drawn up for both countries while the ill person retains capacity:

  • Germany: Prepare a written, personally signed living will (Patientenverfügung under Section 1827 BGB) documenting specific decisions on life-sustaining measures, supplemented by a palliative emergency sheet (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen / Krisenbogen) for emergency medical services [2]. Official, free text modules and drafting guides are provided by the Federal Ministry of Justice (Bundesministerium der Justiz) [2].
  • Ukraine: Under the Fundamentals of Legislation of Ukraine on Healthcare (Основи законодавства України про охорону здоров'я), which fall under the remit of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України), an adult with decision-making capacity submits a written informed consent to or refusal of medical interventions (письмова інформована згода пацієнта) and explicitly designates a trusted person (довірена особа) in the medical file who is authorized to receive information about their health status and inspect medical documentation [7].

steps.title: Separate Healthcare, Financial, and Banking Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Powers of attorney for real estate, bank accounts, and public authorities should be executed according to each country's local formal requirements to avoid rejection in German-Ukrainian legal transactions:

  • Germany: Combine a written healthcare and financial power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht) with a care directive (Betreuungsverfügung) [2] and register them with the Central Register of Advance Directives of the Federal Chamber of Notaries (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer) so that guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) and attending physicians have immediate access in an emergency [3]. If real estate transactions or commercial register matters in Germany are covered, notarial recording (Beurkundung) or certification (Beglaubigung) is required; additionally, a separate post-mortem bank power of attorney (transmortale Kontovollmacht, valid beyond death) should be lodged directly with German banks.
  • Ukraine: For banking transactions, asset administration, dealings with authorities, and real estate matters in Ukraine, a notarized power of attorney (нотаріальна довіреність) entered into the Unified Register of Powers of Attorney (Єдиний реєстр довіреностей) is required [8]. This can be executed either in Ukraine before a state or private notary (organized within the Notary Chamber of Ukraine, Нотаріальна палата України) [8] or outside Ukraine directly at a Ukrainian consular mission in Germany - such as the Embassy of Ukraine in Germany (Botschaft der Ukraine in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Berlin or the Consulates General in Munich, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, or Düsseldorf) - which eliminates the need for a separate Apostille [9].

steps.title: Short-Term Care Absence, Caregiver Leave, and Support Benefits for Relatives
steps.html:
Both countries provide statutory leave entitlements and financial support for family caregivers and seriously ill individuals:

  • Germany: In an acute care situation, employees may take up to 10 working days off work and apply to the ill person's long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse) for the care support allowance (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) as a wage-replacement benefit [4]. For end-of-life accompaniment (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase), the Caregiver Leave Act (Pflegezeitgesetz) allows full or partial leave from work for up to 3 months (including when care is provided in a hospice) [4]. Free, confidential advice is available from the Care Helpline (Pflegetelefon) of the Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth (Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend, reachable at 030 20 17 91 31 or by email at info@wege-zur-pflege.de) [4].
  • Ukraine: In Ukraine, the attending medical team issues an electronic medical conclusion of temporary incapacity for work to care for a sick family member (медичний висновок про тимчасову непрацездатність по догляду за хворим членом сім'ї), on the basis of which sickness benefit is paid through the Pension Fund of Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України) [10]. In addition, where long-term care is required, entitlements exist for state social care assistance (державна соціальна допомога на догляд) and disability pensions administered by the Пенсійний фонд України [10].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Survivor Benefits, and Succession Procedures
steps.html:
Early coordination of estate planning prevents subsequent conflicts between German and Ukrainian authorities:

  • Germany: With specialist notarial advice, review any choice-of-law clause in the will and place testamentary dispositions into official custody (amtliche Verwahrung) with the probate court (Nachlassgericht at the Amtsgericht), registered in the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister). Upon death, notify the statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) and apply for widow's, widower's, or orphan's pensions with the German statutory pension insurance body (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) [5]. If the deceased person was already receiving a German pension, an advance payment for the three-month transition period (Sterbevierteljahr, three months at the full insured pension rate) can be claimed within 30 days of death through the Renten Service der Deutschen Post; to access estate assets without a post-mortem power of attorney, the Nachlassgericht at the Amtsgericht issues a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) [5].
  • Ukraine: Following a death, the Ukrainian funeral grant (допомога на поховання, generally equal to two months of pension) and survivor pension for loss of a breadwinner (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) are claimed from the Пенсійний фонд України (or online via the PFU electronic services web portal, as detailed on the state portal Портал Дія) [10]. To open succession proceedings in Ukraine (відкриття спадкової справи, registered in the Inheritance Register of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine, Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України), a strict statutory deadline of 6 months from the date of death applies, within which heirs must submit their personal declaration of acceptance of inheritance (заява про прийняття спадщини) before a Ukrainian notary (member of the Нотаріальна палата України) or file it with a signature certified by a notary or a Ukrainian consulate (such as the Botschaft der Ukraine in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland) [8][9].

closingQuestion: To tailor this guidance specifically to your situation, is the ill person currently receiving medical treatment in Germany or in Ukraine, and in which of the two countries are their habitual residence as well as any bank accounts, pension entitlements, or real estate located?

de.title: Schwere Erkrankung & Vorsorge zwischen Deutschland und Ukraine: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensbedrohlicher Erkrankung mit Bezug zu Deutschland und Ukraine: Palliativversorgung, Patientenverfügungen in beiden Ländern, Vorsorgevollmachten, Pflegezeit sowie Nachlass- und Rückführungsplanung.
de.introHtml: Wenn bei einem Familienangehörigen eine schwere, lebensverkürzende oder unheilbare Erkrankung diagnostiziert wurde und Verbindungen durch Wohnsitz, Staatsangehörigkeit, Familie oder Vermögen sowohl nach Deutschland als auch in die Ukraine bestehen, sollten medizinische, rechtliche und finanzielle Vorsorgeschritte frühzeitig in beiden Rechtsordnungen abgestimmt werden, solange die erkrankte Person noch voll geschäfts- und einwilligungsfähig ist.

steps.title: Palliativ- und Hospizversorgung sowie grenzüberschreitende Koordination (Deutschland und Ukraine)
steps.html:
Beginnen Sie mit dem behandelnden Ärzteteam in dem Land, in dem sich die erkrankte Person derzeit aufhält, um Schmerztherapie, Symptomkontrolle und ambulante oder stationäre Unterstützung einzurichten:

  • Deutschland: Bei einer nicht heilbaren, fortschreitenden Erkrankung mit komplexem Symptomgeschehen besteht Anspruch auf Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung (SAPV nach § 37b SGB V), die ärztlich verordnet und von der gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung getragen wird [1]. Bei einem Palliativ- oder Hospizbedarf gilt für die Einstufung in einen Pflegegrad durch den Medizinischen Dienst eine verkürzte Eilbegutachtungsfrist von einer Woche (§ 18a SGB XI) [1]. Regionale SAPV-Teams, ambulante Hospizdienste, Palliativstationen und stationäre Hospize finden Sie über den Dachverband (Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V.) [1].
  • Ukraine: Findet die Versorgung in der Ukraine statt oder ist eine Rückkehr dorthin geplant, übernimmt im Rahmen des staatlichen Programms der medizinischen Garantien (Програма медичних гарантій) die Behörde des ukrainischen Nationalen Gesundheitsdienstes (Національна служба здоров'я України, telefonisches Kontaktzentrum 16-77) die Kosten für die stationäre Palliativversorgung (стаціонарна паліативна медична допомога) sowie für mobile Palliativteams zu Hause (мобільна паліативна медична допомога) [6]. Voraussetzung ist eine elektronische Überweisung (е-направлення) durch die Hausärztin, den Hausarzt oder die behandelnde Fachärztin bzw. den Facharzt gemäß den Richtlinien des ukrainischen Gesundheitsministeriums (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України) [6][7]. Vor einer Verlegung zwischen Deutschland und der Ukraine sollten Transportfähigkeit, Schmerzmittelversorgung und Krankenversicherungsschutz vorab mit den behandelnden Ärztinnen und Ärzten abgestimmt werden.

steps.title: Schriftliche Patientenverfügungen und medizinische Vollmachten bei voller Einwilligungsfähigkeit
steps.html:
Da Patientenverfügungen und Auskunftsrechte gegenüber Ärztinnen und Ärzten dem Recht des jeweiligen Behandlungsstaates unterliegen, sollten für beide Länder getrennte Erklärungen verfasst werden, solange die erkrankte Person einwilligungsfähig ist:

  • Deutschland: Erstellen Sie eine schriftliche, eigenhändig unterschriebene Patientenverfügung nach § 1827 BGB, in der konkrete Entscheidungen zu lebenserhaltenden Maßnahmen dokumentiert werden, ergänzt durch einen palliativmedizinischen Notfallbogen (z. B. Krisenbogen) für den Rettungsdienst [2]. Offizielle und kostenfreie Textbausteine sowie Formulierungshilfen stellt das Justizministerium (Bundesministerium der Justiz) bereit [2].
  • Ukraine: Nach den Grundlagen der Gesetzgebung der Ukraine über das Gesundheitswesen (Основи законодавства України про охорону здоров'я), die im Zuständigkeitsbereich des ukrainischen Gesundheitsministeriums (Міністерство охорони здоров'я України) liegen, gibt die volljährige und einwilligungsfähige Person eine schriftliche informierte Einwilligung oder Ablehnung medizinischer Eingriffe (письмова інформована згода пацієнта) ab und benennt in der Patientenakte ausdrücklich eine Vertrauensperson (довірена особа), die Auskünfte über den Gesundheitszustand und Einsicht in die medizinische Dokumentation erhalten darf [7].

steps.title: Getrennte Vorsorge-, Vermögens- und Bankvollmachten in beiden Rechtsordnungen
steps.html:
Vollmachten für Immobilien, Bankkonten und Behörden sollten jeweils nach den lokalen Formvorschriften errichtet werden, um Zurückweisungen im deutsch-ukrainischen Rechtsverkehr zu vermeiden:

  • Deutschland: Kombinieren Sie eine schriftliche Vorsorgevollmacht und eine Betreuungsverfügung [2] und lassen Sie diese im staatlichen Register (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer) registrieren, damit Betreuungsgerichte sowie behandelnde Ärztinnen und Ärzte im Notfall umgehend Zugriff auf die Angaben haben [3]. Wenn Grundstücksgeschäfte oder Handelsregisterangelegenheiten in Deutschland umfasst sind, ist eine notarielle Beurkundung oder Beglaubigung erforderlich; zudem sollte bei deutschen Kreditinstituten direkt eine gesonderte transmortale Kontovollmacht (Vollmacht über den Tod hinaus) hinterlegt werden.
  • Ukraine: Für Bankgeschäfte, Vermögensverwaltung, Behördengänge und Grundstücksangelegenheiten in der Ukraine ist eine notariell beurkundete Vollmacht (нотаріальна довіреність) mit Eintragung in das Einheitliche Vollmachtsregister (Єдиний реєстр довіреностей) erforderlich [8]. Diese kann entweder in der Ukraine vor einem staatlichen oder privaten Notar (organisiert in der Ukrainischen Notarkammer Нотаріальна палата України) [8] oder außerhalb der Ukraine direkt bei einer ukrainischen konsularischen Vertretung in Deutschland - beispielsweise bei der Auslandsvertretung (Botschaft der Ukraine in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Berlin bzw. den Generalkonsulaten in München, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg oder Düsseldorf) - errichtet werden, wodurch eine zusätzliche Apostille entfällt [9].

steps.title: Kurzzeitige Freistellung, Pflegezeit und Unterstützungsleistungen für Angehörige
steps.html:
Beide Staaten sehen gesetzliche Freistellungsansprüche und finanzielle Hilfen für pflegende Angehörige und schwer erkrankte Personen vor:

  • Deutschland: Beschäftigte können bei einer akut auftretenden Pflegesituation bis zu 10 Arbeitstage der Arbeit fernbleiben und bei der Pflegekasse der erkrankten Person Pflegeunterstützungsgeld als Lohnersatzleistung beantragen [4]. Für die Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase ermöglicht das Pflegezeitgesetz eine vollständige oder teilweise Freistellung von bis zu 3 Monaten (auch bei einer Versorgung im Hospiz) [4]. Kostenfreie, vertrauliche Beratung bietet das Pflegetelefon des Familienministeriums (Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend, erreichbar unter 030 20 17 91 31 oder per E-Mail an info@wege-zur-pflege.de) [4].
  • Ukraine: In der Ukraine stellt das behandelnde Ärzteteam im elektronischen Gesundheitssystem einen medizinischen Befund über die vorübergehende Arbeitsunfähigkeit zur Pflege eines erkrankten Familienmitglieds (медичний висновок про тимчасову непрацездатність по догляду за хворим членом сім'ї) aus, auf dessen Grundlage über die Behörde des Pensionsfonds der Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України) Krankengeld gezahlt wird [10]. Zudem bestehen bei dauerhafter Pflegebedürftigkeit Ansprüche auf staatliche Sozialhilfe für die Pflege (державна соціальна допомога на догляд) sowie auf Invaliditätsrenten über die Behörde (Пенсійний фонд України) [10].

steps.title: Abstimmung von Testamenten, Hinterbliebenenleistungen und Nachlassverfahren
steps.html:
Eine frühzeitige Abstimmung der Nachlassplanung verhindert spätere Konflikte zwischen deutschen und ukrainischen Behörden:

  • Deutschland: Prüfen Sie mit fachkundiger notarieller Beratung die Rechtswahl im Testament und hinterlegen Sie letztwillige Verfügungen in der amtlichen Verwahrung beim Nachlassgericht (Amtsgericht) mit Registrierung im Zentralen Testamentsregister. Im Todesfall sind die Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung zu informieren sowie Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrenten beim Rentenversicherungsträger (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) zu beantragen [5]. Hat die verstorbene Person bereits eine deutsche Rente bezogen, kann innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod beim Renten Service der Deutschen Post der Vorschuss für das Sterbevierteljahr (drei Monate volle Versichertenrente) beantragt werden; für den Zugriff auf Nachlassvermögen ohne transmortale Vollmacht stellt das Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht einen Erbschein aus [5].
  • Ukraine: Nach einem Todesfall werden das ukrainische Bestattungsgeld (допомога на поховання, in der Regel in Höhe einer zweimonatigen Rente) sowie die Hinterbliebenenrente wegen Verlusts des Ernährers (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) bei der Behörde (Пенсійний фонд України bzw. online über das Webportal der elektronischen Dienste des ПФУ, erläutert im staatlichen Portal Дія) beantragt [10]. Für die Eröffnung des Nachlassverfahrens in der Ukraine (відкриття спадкової справи mit Eintragung in das Erbschaftsregister Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України) gilt eine gesetzliche Frist von 6 Monaten ab dem Todestag, innerhalb derer Erbinnen und Erben ihre persönliche Annahmeerklärung (заява про прийняття спадщини) vor einem ukrainischen Notar (Kammer Нотаріальна палата України) abgeben oder mit konsularisch bzw. notariell beglaubigter Unterschrift (etwa über die Vertretung Botschaft der Ukraine in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland) einreichen müssen [8][9].

de.closingQuestion: Um die Hinweise gezielt auf Ihre Situation abzustimmen: 1. Befindet sich die erkrankte Person derzeit zur medizinischen Behandlung in Deutschland oder in der Ukraine? 2. In welchem der beiden Länder befinden sich der gewöhnliche Aufenthalt sowie etwaige Bankkonten, Rentenansprüche oder Immobilien?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Germany
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Germany
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Germany: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Germany, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Germany)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and planning guides are also available through CaringInfo (phone 1-800-658-8898, an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Germany: If care takes place in Germany or a relocation is planned, patients with an incurable, progressive condition and complex symptoms are entitled to Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung (SAPV nach § 37b SGB V), prescribed by a physician and funded by statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) [6]. For patients receiving palliative or hospice care, statutory long-term care insurance applies a fast-track assessment deadline of one week for care-level classification (Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung nach § 18a SGB XI) [6]. Regional SAPV teams, inpatient palliative wards, and hospices can be located through Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. [6]. Because US Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States and German statutory health insurance requires prior coordination for cross-border treatment, verify insurance coverage and medical transport fitness before any international transfer.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Germany
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Germany while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in California, New York, or Texas), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Germany: Prepare a written, personally signed Patientenverfügung nach § 1827 BGB specifying consent or refusal for medical measures in defined end-of-life situations, supplemented by an emergency palliative instruction sheet (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen) for emergency services [7]. Official German templates and drafting modules (Textbausteine) are published free of charge by the Bundesministerium der Justiz [7].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
German banks, land registries, and authorities rarely accept a US state Power of Attorney directly, and US financial institutions require state-compliant mandates. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Germany: Execute a written Vorsorgevollmacht and Betreuungsverfügung [7] and register them with the Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer so German guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) and attending physicians can verify the representative's authority immediately [8]. If the mandate covers German real estate or commercial register transactions, it must be notarized or publicly certified (before a German notary or a German embassy or consulate in the US); additionally, set up an explicit post-mortem bank mandate (transmortale Bankvollmacht) directly with each German bank.

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer expedited disability processing and statutory leave for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [9].
  • Germany: Employees insured in Germany can take up to 10 working days off work in an acute care crisis and claim wage-replacement benefits (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) from the patient's long-term care fund (Pflegekasse) [10]. Under the Pflegezeitgesetz, caregivers are also entitled to full or partial release from work for up to 3 months to accompany a close relative in the final phase of life (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase), whether at home or in a hospice [10]. Free advice is available via the Pflegetelefon of the Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (phone 030 20 17 91 31, email info@wege-zur-pflege.de) [10].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and German assets with cross-border estate professionals so that a new will in one country does not inadvertently revoke the other, and consider whether an explicit choice of law is appropriate under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012). Gather civil certificates, Social Security and German pension insurance numbers, property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Consulate General in Frankfurt for residents in Germany) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Italy
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Italy
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Italy: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Italy, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Italy)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and planning guides are also available through CaringInfo (phone 1-800-658-8898, an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Italy: If care takes place in Italy or a relocation is planned, Legge 38/2010 guarantees access to the national palliative care and pain therapy network (Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore) within the Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale), overseen by the Ministero della Salute [6][7]. Through a referral from the general practitioner (Medico di Medicina Generale) or hospital team to the local health authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL), patients can access home palliative care units (cure palliative domiciliari UCP-DOM) or residential Hospice facilities; regional network information is published by the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [6]. Because US Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States and SSN enrollment in Italy depends on residence or reciprocal coverage, verify health coverage and medical transport arrangements before any cross-border transfer.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Italy
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Italy while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in New York, California, or New Jersey), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Italy: Under Legge 219/2017, an adult with full mental capacity can execute written Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT / Biotestamento) expressing consent or refusal regarding diagnostic tests, therapeutic choices, and specific medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and appointing a trusted healthcare representative (fiduciario) [7][8]. In Italy, DAT are executed as a public deed or authenticated private writing before a notary (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or delivered in person to the municipal civil registry (Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune of residence) - or via an Italian consulate abroad for Italian citizens residing outside Italy - and transmitted to the Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT maintained by the Ministero della Salute [7][8].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Italian banks, notaries, and land registries generally require a notarized Italian power of attorney rather than a US state mandate, while US institutions require state-compliant forms. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Italy: For banking, property, tax, and administrative representation in Italy, execute a notarized general or special power of attorney (procura generale o speciale notarile) before an Italian notary (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or before the consular office of an Italian Embassy or Consulate in the United States (or before a US notary with an Apostille and certified Italian translation) [8]. If the illness later impairs the person's autonomy in Italy without sufficient mandates in place, family members or the beneficiary can petition the guardianship judge (Giudice Tutelare del Tribunale) for the appointment of a support administrator under the Amministrazione di Sostegno procedure (Law 6/2004), as detailed by the Ministero della Giustizia [9].

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer expedited disability processing and statutory leave for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [10].
  • Italy: Through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, toll-free 803 164 from Italian landlines), patients with oncological or severe life-limiting conditions qualify for an accelerated medical assessment (within 15 days) for severe disability recognition (riconoscimento urgente dell'handicap grave under Legge 104/1992) and the non-means-tested attendance allowance (assegno / indennità di accompagnamento) [11]. Employed family caregivers in Italy are entitled under Legge 104/1992 to 3 days of paid monthly leave and up to 2 years of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) administered by the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale [11].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and Italian assets with cross-border legal professionals so that one will does not inadvertently revoke the other, taking into account Italian forced-heirship rules (quote di legittima) and choice-of-law rules under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) [8]. Gather civil certificates, Social Security and Italian tax codes (codice fiscale), property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Mission in Italy) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.
  • Italy: Apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale for Italian survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti / reversibilità) [11]. If the estate includes Italian real estate or assets, heirs must file the electronic inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (toll-free 800 90 96 96 in Italy) within 12 months of the date of death to calculate inheritance/cadastral taxes and unlock Italian bank accounts [12]. Public and formally deposited wills in Italy can be searched through the Registro Generale dei Testamenti via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato and the Ministero della Giustizia [8][9].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Colombia
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Colombia
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Colombia: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Colombia, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Colombia)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1].   • Colombia: If care takes place in Colombia or a return to Colombia is planned, Ley 1733 de 2014 (Ley Consuelo Devis Saavedra) guarantees the right of patients with terminal, chronic, degenerative, and irreversible illnesses to receive comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, and home-based palliative care (cuidados paliativos) and pain management [6][7]. Services are coordinated and funded through the person's health promotion entity (Entidad Promotora de Salud - EPS) within the Sistema General de Seguridad Social en Salud, under standards issued by the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social [6][7]. Because US Medicare does not cover healthcare in Colombia and Colombian EPS coverage requires active affiliation, confirm insurance status, opioid medication prescriptions, and medical fit-to-fly clearance before any international relocation.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Colombia
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Colombia while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in Florida, New York, Texas, or California), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Colombia: Under Ley 1733 de 2014 and Resolución 2665 de 2018 of the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, any adult with full mental capacity can sign a written Documento de Voluntad Anticipada (DVA) expressing treatment preferences, refusal of disproportionate interventions, and palliative care wishes [6][7]. Under Resolution 2665 of 2018, a DVA can be formalized through any of three official methods: before the attending physician (médico tratante), in writing before two witnesses (dos testigos), or before a Notary (ante notario), and a copy must be incorporated into the patient's clinical history (historia clínica) [6].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Colombian banks, notaries, and land registries do not accept a domestic US state Power of Attorney unless Colombian formalities are met, and US financial institutions require state-compliant mandates. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Colombia: For broad property, banking, and legal representation in Colombia, execute a Poder General por escritura pública (General Power of Attorney by public deed) before a Notary in Colombia (Notaría en Colombia) or before a Colombian Consulate in the United States (Consulado de Colombia en el exterior under the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores), or execute a targeted Poder Especial with authenticated signature (reconocimiento de firma) [8][9]. Notarial deeds and property registrations in Colombia are supervised by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro [9]. If a power of attorney is signed before a US notary public rather than a Colombian consul, it must carry a Hague Apostille and an official Spanish translation.

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions provide disability pathways and workplace protections for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [10].
  • Colombia: Under Colombian labor law, employees may request paid workplace leave for serious domestic calamity (licencia por calamidad doméstica) when a close family member suffers a grave health crisis, while medical incapacity benefits are processed through the person's EPS [6]. If the illness results in a certified loss of working capacity of 50% or more (pérdida de capacidad laboral), the insured person can apply for a disability pension (pensión de invalidez) through the public pension administrator Colpensiones (or their private pension fund, AFP) [11].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and Colombian assets with cross-border legal professionals so that one will does not accidentally revoke the other, taking into account Colombian forced-heirship rules (asignaciones forzosas / legítimas rigurosas). Gather civil certificates, Social Security numbers, Colombian citizenship ID cards (cédula de ciudadanía), property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Bogotá) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.
  • Colombia: Apply to Colpensiones (or the relevant private pension fund) for the statutory funeral grant (auxilio funerario, paid to the person who covered funeral expenses, equivalent to between 5 and 10 monthly legal minimum wages - SMLMV) and the survivor pension (pensión de sobrevivientes) for eligible family beneficiaries [11]. To transfer Colombian bank accounts and real estate, heirs may complete a notarial succession procedure (trámite de sucesión ante notaría, when all heirs are in agreement, before a Colombian notary overseen by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro and the Unión Colegiada del Notariado Colombiano) or a judicial succession (sucesión ante juzgado) [9].

cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Arab Emirates and India: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and holds residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both the United Arab Emirates and India, early coordination is essential. Because medical decision-making frameworks, powers of attorney, workplace entitlements, and succession laws operate separately in each country, key legal and financial documents must be executed in the appropriate format for each jurisdiction while your family member retains full mental and legal capacity [1][4][5].

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Medical Coverage Between the United Arab Emirates and India
steps.html:
Begin by asking your family member's treating oncology or specialist team to establish a multidisciplinary palliative care and symptom-management plan, and clarify with the health insurer whether care will remain in the United Arab Emirates or involve medical relocation to India [1][2].

  • Palliative and home care in the United Arab Emirates: Under the federal Patient Rights and Responsibilities Charter on the Official Portal of the UAE Government and emirate-level clinical standards issued by the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (phone: +971 2 449 3333), the Dubai Health Authority (DHA, phone: 800 342), and the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP, phone: 800 11111), patients with life-limiting illnesses are entitled to multidisciplinary pain management and palliative care across licensed tertiary hospitals (such as Tawam Hospital in Abu Dhabi or Dubai Hospital) and licensed home-healthcare providers [1][2]. Before initiating inpatient or home palliative care, have the hospital case manager submit a prior-authorization request to the mandatory health insurer (such as Thiqa or Daman in Abu Dhabi, or an ISAHD-compliant insurer in Dubai) to confirm coverage limits for home nursing and controlled pain medications [1][2].
  • Palliative care networks and care relocation to India: In India, public tertiary hospitals, Regional Cancer Centres, and district hospitals provide pain relief and supportive care under the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare), while accredited inpatient hospices and home-care teams across Indian states can be located through the directory of the Indian Association of Palliative Care [3]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers. If your family member plans to travel to India for ongoing care, request a complete English medical summary, pathology reports, and a fit-to-fly certificate (MEDIF clearance for commercial airlines or air ambulance arrangements) from the UAE treating physician, and verify rules for carrying prescribed narcotic analgesics with both UAE authorities and Indian customs in advance [1][3].

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives and End-of-Life Care Plans in Both Jurisdictions While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Advance care preferences and resuscitation rules differ substantially between the United Arab Emirates and India, so written care preferences should be documented separately for whichever country provides clinical care [1][2].

  • Care plans and resuscitation rules in the United Arab Emirates: Under the federal Patient Rights Charter on the Official Portal of the UAE Government, a patient with decision-making capacity has the right to be fully informed of their diagnosis and prognosis and to refuse or discontinue specific medical treatments after being informed of the medical consequences [1]. Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability (and its updated federal medical liability framework), Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) orders in cases of incurable terminal illness are strictly regulated clinical orders that must be evaluated and signed by at least three treating consultant/specialist physicians in accordance with Department of Health - Abu Dhabi, DHA, or MOHAP protocols, rather than relying solely on a foreign living will [1][2]. Ask the treating specialist team in the UAE to record your family member's goals of care and designated family spokesperson directly in the hospital electronic medical record (such as Malaffi in Abu Dhabi or Nabidh in Dubai) [1][2].
  • Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) in India: Under the Supreme Court of India's constitutional guidelines (Common Cause v. Union of India, 2018, as simplified by the Supreme Court in January 2023), an adult of sound mind and full capacity can execute a written Advance Medical Directive specifying the withdrawal or withholding of life-sustaining treatment in a terminal or irreversible condition and naming a healthcare proxy/guardian [3]. Under the 2023 guidelines, the directive must be signed by the declarant in the presence of two independent attesting witnesses and attested before a Notary Public or a Gazetted Officer, with copies provided to the appointed guardian, the family physician, and the local municipal or district custodian for inclusion in health records [3].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in the United Arab Emirates and India
steps.html:
A Power of Attorney (POA) executed in one country is not automatically accepted by banks, land registries, or hospitals in the other without specific notarization, legalization, and local registration [4][5]. Arrange separate instruments while your family member can still appear in person or via video notarization [4][5]:

  • Notarized Power of Attorney in the United Arab Emirates: To manage UAE bank accounts, property, vehicles, residency visa matters, or medical representation, your family member must execute a notarized Power of Attorney (in Arabic or bilingual Arabic-English) before a UAE Notary Public, such as through the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (phone: +971 2 651 2222) e-Notary portal or the Dubai Courts Notary Public [4]. UAE banks strictly scrutinize general POAs and frequently require explicit clauses authorizing banking transactions or their own internal mandate forms; remember that under UAE civil law, any Power of Attorney automatically expires upon the principal's death [4][6].
  • Power of Attorney and account nominations for India: If your family member is currently in the UAE and needs to appoint an attorney-in-fact for property, banking, or legal matters in India, they can sign a General or Special Power of Attorney before the Consulate General of India, Dubai (phone: +971 4 397 1222; emergency helpline: +971 50 734 7676; email: cons1.dubai@mea.gov.in) or the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi [5]. Once attested by the Indian mission and sent to India, the POA must be adjudicated and stamped before the local Collector of Stamps or Sub-Registrar of Assurances in the relevant Indian state within 3 months of receipt in India to be legally valid for property or banking transactions [5]. Simultaneously, ensure your family member registers or updates statutory nominations (Form DA-1 for bank accounts, demat account nominations, and mutual fund nominations) with all Indian financial institutions [5][9].

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Medical Advances, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Check employment contracts, mandatory health insurance policies, and statutory social security schemes in both countries before taking extended leave or paying major out-of-pocket medical bills [1][9]:

  • Sick leave, compassionate leave, and critical illness insurance in the United Arab Emirates: Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 (UAE Labour Law), private-sector employees who have completed probation are entitled to up to 90 days of sick leave per year (the first 15 days at full pay, the next 30 days at half pay, and 45 days unpaid) upon submitting an approved medical report [1][6]. If a family member employed in the UAE is caring for the patient, they should check their employer's HR policy for flexible working arrangements or unpaid compassionate leave, as statutory paid bereavement leave in the UAE private sector (5 days for a spouse; 3 days for a parent, child, sibling, grandchild, or grandparent) applies only after a death occurs [6]. Also review any employer-sponsored group life or critical illness insurance policy, which may pay a lump-sum terminal illness benefit upon diagnosis [1].
  • Medical advances and social security support in India: If your family member has an active or prior account with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (toll-free helpline: 1800 118 005; email: employeefeedback@epfindia.gov.in), they can apply online via the Unified Member Portal for a non-refundable medical advance under Paragraph 68J of the EPF Scheme for hospitalization or treatment of a life-threatening illness (such as cancer or major organ failure) without requiring a minimum service period [9]. Workers covered under the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC, toll-free: 1800 11 2526) may claim Extended Sickness Benefit (up to 2 years at 80% of wages for specified malignant and long-term diseases), while eligible families in India can verify inpatient coverage under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY or private health insurance policies [3][9].

steps.title: Align Wills, Beneficiary Designations, Bank Access, and Repatriation or Funeral Wishes Across Both Countries
steps.html:
Because UAE bank accounts (including joint accounts) are routinely frozen immediately upon the account holder's death until a UAE court succession order is issued, aligning wills and beneficiary records in advance prevents severe financial disruption [6][7][8]:

  • Non-Muslim wills, bank accounts, and workplace entitlements in the United Arab Emirates: Under UAE personal status legislation for non-Muslims (Federal Decree-Law No. 41 of 2022 and Abu Dhabi Law No. 14 of 2021), expatriates can register a formal Will covering UAE bank accounts, real estate, and guardianship so that UAE assets are distributed directly according to their stated wishes [6][7]. Depending on where assets are held, your family member can register a Will with the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department Civil Family Court, the Dubai Courts Notary Public, or the DIFC Courts Wills Service (phone: +971 4 427 3333; email: info@difcwills.ae) [4][6][7]. In addition, an employee in the UAE should confirm in writing with their employer (under MOHRE or the relevant free-zone authority) the designated beneficiary to receive unpaid wages and end-of-service gratuity (which the employer must disburse within 10 days in the event of an employee's death, alongside covering repatriation costs of mortal remains if requested) [6][8].
  • Provident fund, pension nominations, wills, and consular repatriation procedures for India: In India, verify that digital e-Nomination is completed with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation so eligible family members can seamlessly claim the EPF balance, the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) lump-sum assurance benefit, and the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension via the online Composite Claim Form [9]. For separate assets in India (real estate, bank accounts, NRE/NRO deposits, and investments), executing a clean Indian Will witnessed by two witnesses (and optionally registered before the local Sub-Registrar in India) avoids lengthy interstate succession disputes or the need for a court Succession Certificate [5][9]. Finally, discuss and record your family member's wishes regarding local burial/cremation in the UAE versus repatriation to India, noting that the Consulate General of India, Dubai (or the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi) issues the mandatory No Objection Certificate (NOC) and passport cancellation for transporting mortal remains or ashes to India [8].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation, which emirate in the United Arab Emirates and which state in India are involved, and is your family member currently receiving care in the UAE or planning to relocate to India?
