title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Spain: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Spain, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Spain.
introHtml: We are sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residential ties dies in Spain, the administrative steps must be coordinated between the health and civil registry authorities of the Spanish municipality where the death occurred, the U.S. consular mission in Spain, and the federal and state agencies in the destination U.S. state. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic or Judicial Clearance in Spain
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: If the death occurs from natural causes under medical care in a hospital (for example, in Madrid, Barcelona, or Málaga), the attending medical staff issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción), which is required to register the death and authorize the transfer of the body [1].
  • Death at a private residence, hotel, or public place: If the deceased person is outside a healthcare facility, call the emergency number 112 immediately so that emergency medical services can attend and confirm the death [1].
  • Judicial intervention and mortuary health timelines: When a death is sudden, accidental, or lacks a documented clinical cause, the police and the duty court (Juzgado de Guardia) intervene and order the transfer of the body to the competent Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses) for an autopsy before authorizing civil registration and burial or repatriation [1][3]. Under Spanish regional mortuary health regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria), burial or cremation of an unembalmed body generally takes place between 24 and 48 hours after death, whereas temporary preservation or embalming allows this window to be extended (up to 96 hours or longer for international repatriation) [3].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Spain and the United States, and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance policies: Before signing private contracts on your own, verify whether your family member had travel, medical assistance, or funeral insurance covering international repatriation. If a policy exists, contact the insurer's assistance center first so they can appoint the funeral operators and cover the technical arrangements and costs [4].
  • Appointing a funeral provider in Spain and a receiving funeral home in the United States: If no insurance policy applies, appoint a licensed Spanish funeral company (empresa funeraria habilitada, represented at the national industry level by the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios - PANASEF) to coordinate the mortuary facility (tanatorio), embalming, and customs clearance [4]. For reception in the United States, coordinate the transfer with a state-licensed funeral home located through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA) [5]. Clarvia provides directory links solely for orientation and does not endorse specific commercial providers. Under the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes are required to provide an itemized General Price List over the phone or in person and to charge only for the specific receiving and burial or cremation services you select [6].
  • U.S. consular notification: Report the death as soon as possible to the U.S. Embassy and Consulate in Spain and Andorra (Embajada y Consulado de los Estados Unidos en España y Andorra, in Madrid or the Consulate General in Barcelona, emergency telephone +34 91 587 2200) [2][3]. The consular service guides family members on local formalities, safeguards personal effects if the deceased person was traveling alone, and issues the U.S. consular death certificate, although the U.S. Government has no funds to pay for funeral or repatriation expenses [2][3].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Spain, Apostille or Form C, and U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Registration with the Spanish Civil Registry: The death declaration is filed with the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred, ordinarily within 24 hours - a step usually handled directly by the Spanish funeral director using the Certificado Médico de Defunción and the deceased person's passport [1]. Request several copies of the full literal death certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción, issued free of charge via the electronic portal of the Spanish Ministry of Justice, Ministerio de Justicia) [1]. Although Spain issues the multilingual extract Fórmula C (under the 1976 Vienna Convention), the United States is not a party to that convention; therefore, if a U.S. state authority requires the Spanish certificate in addition to the consular report, request a Hague Apostille (Apostilla de La Haya) from the Ministerio de Justicia (Territorial Offices or High Court of Justice) together with a sworn English translation [1].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Submit the Spanish Certificado Literal de Defunción and your family member's U.S. passport to the Embajada y Consulado de los Estados Unidos en España y Andorra to obtain the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060, issued electronically as an e-CRODA) [2][3]. This official English-language document serves as the equivalent of a domestic death certificate before probate courts, banks, insurers, and state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics agencies in the United States [2][3].

steps.title: International Repatriation of the Body or Ashes to the United States vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Spain
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body from Spain to the United States: For the international transfer of uncremated remains, the Spanish funeral company obtains authorization from External Health (Sanidad Exterior) and a mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio) in accordance with health and international regulations (and consular procedures coordinated with the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación, where applicable), carrying out mandatory embalming and sealing the body in an airtight coffin with a soldered inner zinc liner [3][7]. For entry into the United States under federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) regulations (42 CFR 71.55), the remains must be shipped in a leak-proof container consigned directly to a licensed U.S. funeral home or cemetery, accompanied by the official death certificate and a statement confirming the absence of any quarantinable communicable disease [7]. Upon arrival at the U.S. airport, U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment and the receiving funeral home obtains the state burial-transit permit.
  • Transporting cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in Spain (which requires express written authorization signed by the next of kin), cremated remains are exempt from CDC public health import permits under 42 CFR 71.55 [3][7]. They may be transported to the United States in a sealed, X-ray-scannable urn accompanied by the death certificate and the cremation certificate (certificado de cremación) [3][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in Spain: If the family chooses final burial or cremation in Spain without repatriation, the Registro Civil issues the burial license (licencia de sepultura) once the death has been registered [1][3].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Probate in the United States and in Spain
steps.html:
• Social Security, veterans' benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States: Report the death to the federal Social Security Administration (SSA) by calling 1-800-772-1213 (from within the United States) or by contacting the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Madrid (fbu.madrid@ssa.gov) to stop monthly payments (any payment received for the month of death must be returned) and to apply for the USD 255 lump-sum death payment or monthly survivor benefits [3][11]. If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regarding burial allowances (Form VA 21P-530EZ) or interment in a national cemetery [12]. The personal representative or surviving relative must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040 marked "DECEASED") with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) covering income earned up to the date of death by the regular April filing deadline of the following year [13], and open estate administration (probate) before the competent Probate Court in the U.S. county where the deceased held residence or property.
  • Benefits and succession procedures in Spain: If the deceased person contributed to social security or resided in Spain, check with the Spanish National Institute of Social Security (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social - INSS) regarding the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and widow's/widower's or orphan's pensions (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) [8]. If they left property or bank accounts in Spain, once 15 working days have passed since the death, apply to the Ministerio de Justicia (using Modelo 790) for the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Life Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento) [9]. With those certificates, consult a Spanish notary through the General Council of Notaries (Consejo General del Notariado) to obtain an authorized copy of the will or execute a declaration of heirs, and settle Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) within the statutory deadline of 6 months from the date of death (extendable by an additional 6 months if requested within the first 5 months) [10].

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre España y Estados Unidos: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre España y Estados Unidos: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía o vínculos de residencia en los Estados Unidos fallece en España, los trámites deben coordinarse entre las autoridades sanitarias y registrales del municipio español donde ocurrió el deceso, la representación consular estadounidense en España y los organismos federales y estatales del estado de destino en los Estados Unidos. A continuación se detallan los cinco pasos oficiales en orden.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción e intervención forense o judicial en España
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento en centro hospitalario o sociosanitario: Si el deceso ocurre por causas naturales bajo asistencia médica en un hospital (por ejemplo, en Madrid, Barcelona o Málaga), el personal facultativo expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial, requisito indispensable para inscribir el fallecimiento y autorizar el traslado del cuerpo [1].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Si la persona fallecida se encuentra fuera de un centro sanitario, llame de inmediato al teléfono de emergencias 112 para que los servicios médicos de urgencia confirmen la defunción [1].
  • Intervención judicial y plazos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Cuando la muerte es súbita, accidental o sin causa clínica documentada, intervienen las fuerzas policiales y el Juzgado de Guardia, que ordena el traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses correspondiente para practicar la autopsia antes de autorizar la inscripción y el sepelio [1][3]. Conforme a los reglamentos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria, en España la inhumación o cremación de un cuerpo no embalsamado suele realizarse entre las 24 y las 48 horas posteriores al fallecimiento, mientras que la conservación o el embalsamamiento permite ampliar el plazo (hasta 96 horas o más para la repatriación internacional) [3].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriación, servicios funerarios en España y en los Estados Unidos y asistencia consular estadounidense
steps.html:
• Verificación de pólizas de viaje o repatriación: Antes de contratar servicios por cuenta propia, compruebe si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, de asistencia médica o de decesos con cobertura internacional. Si existe póliza, contacte primero con la central de asistencia de la aseguradora para que designe a los operadores funerarios y asuma la gestión técnica y los costes [4].
  • Designación de empresa funeraria en España y funeraria receptora en los Estados Unidos: Si no interviene una aseguradora, encargue la gestión en España a una empresa funeraria habilitada (representada sectorialmente por la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios) para que coordine el tanatorio, el embalsamamiento y la salida aduanera [4]. Para la recepción en los Estados Unidos, coordine el traslado con una funeraria con licencia estatal localizable a través del directorio de la asociación National Funeral Directors Association [5]. En virtud de la normativa de protección al consumidor Funeral Rule de la Federal Trade Commission, las funerarias estadounidenses están obligadas a entregarle un listado desglosado de precios (General Price List) por teléfono o en persona y a cobrar únicamente por los servicios de recepción e inhumación o cremación que usted seleccione [6].
  • Notificación consular estadounidense: Comunique el fallecimiento lo antes posible a la Embajada y Consulado de los Estados Unidos en España y Andorra (en Madrid o el Consulado General en Barcelona, teléfono de urgencias +34 91 587 2200) [2][3]. El servicio consular orienta a los familiares sobre las formalidades locales, custodia los efectos personales si la persona fallecida viajaba sola y tramita el certificado consular estadounidense de defunción, si bien el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos no dispone de fondos para sufragar gastos funerarios ni de repatriación [2][3].

steps.title: Inscripción de la defunción en el Registro Civil en España, apostilla o Fórmula C y reporte consular estadounidense (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Inscripción en el Registro Civil español: La declaración de fallecimiento se presenta ante el Registro Civil del municipio donde ocurrió el deceso, habitualmente dentro de las 24 horas siguientes, trámite que suele realizar directamente la funeraria española con el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el pasaporte de la persona fallecida [1]. Solicite varios ejemplares del Certificado Literal de Defunción (trámite gratuito en la Sede Electrónica del Ministerio de Justicia) [1]. Aunque España emite el extracto plurilingüe Fórmula C (Convenio de Viena de 1976), los Estados Unidos no son parte de dicho convenio; por ello, si una autoridad estatal estadounidense exige el certificado español además del documento consular, solicite la Apostilla de La Haya en el Ministerio de Justicia (Gerencias Territoriales o Tribunal Superior de Justicia) junto con traducción jurada al inglés [1].
  • Reporte Consular de Defunción en el Extranjero (CRDA): Remita el Certificado Literal de Defunción español y el pasaporte estadounidense de su familiar a la Embajada y Consulado de los Estados Unidos en España y Andorra para obtener el Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Formulario DS-2060, emitido en formato electrónico e-CRODA) [2][3]. Este documento oficial en inglés equivale a un acta de defunción ante tribunales de sucesiones, bancos, aseguradoras y agencias estatales o del condado (Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) en los Estados Unidos [2][3].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional del cuerpo o de las cenizas a los Estados Unidos frente a inhumación o cremación local en España
steps.html:
• Repatriación del cuerpo desde España a los Estados Unidos: Para el traslado internacional de restos no incinerados, la funeraria española tramita la autorización de Sanidad Exterior y el acta o salvoconducto mortuorio conforme a la normativa sanitaria e internacional (y a las gestiones consulares supervisadas con el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación cuando procede), realizando el embalsamamiento obligatorio y el acondicionamiento en féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada [3][7]. Para la entrada en los Estados Unidos bajo la regulación federal de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55), el cuerpo debe enviarse en contenedor estanco a prueba de fugas, consignado directamente a una funeraria o cementerio con licencia estadounidense, acompañado del certificado oficial de defunción y de la declaración de que no concurre enfermedad cuarentenable [7]. A la llegada al aeropuerto estadounidense, U.S. Customs and Border Protection autoriza el despacho aduanero y la funeraria receptora obtiene el permiso estatal de tránsito e inhumación (burial-transit permit).
  • Traslado de cenizas: Si se opta por la cremación en España (que requiere autorización expresa firmada por el familiar legitimado), las cenizas están exentas de permiso sanitario de importación según la norma 42 CFR 71.55 de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [3][7]. Pueden transportarse a los Estados Unidos en una urna sellada apta para escáner de rayos X acompañada del certificado de defunción y del certificado de cremación [3][7].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en España: Si la familia decide realizar el entierro o la cremación definitiva en España sin repatriación, el Registro Civil expide la licencia de sepultura una vez inscrita la defunción [1][3].

steps.title: Notificaciones posteriores, pensiones de supervivencia, impuestos y sucesión en los Estados Unidos y en España
steps.html:
• Seguridad Social, veteranos, impuestos y sucesión (probate) en los Estados Unidos: Notifique la defunción a la agencia federal Social Security Administration llamando al 1-800-772-1213 (desde los Estados Unidos) o contactando con la Unidad de Beneficios Federales (Federal Benefits Unit) en la Embajada en Madrid (fbu.madrid@ssa.gov) para detener pagos mensuales indebidos (cualquier abono correspondiente al mes del fallecimiento debe devolverse) y solicitar el pago único de 255 USD o pensiones mensuales de supervivencia [3][11]. Si su familiar sirvió en las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses, consulte al Department of Veterans Affairs sobre subsidios de entierro (Formulario VA 21P-530EZ) o sepultura en cementerios nacionales [12]. El representante personal o familiar superviviente debe presentar ante el Internal Revenue Service la declaración final del impuesto federal sobre la renta (Formulario 1040 marcado como "DECEASED") por los ingresos obtenidos hasta la fecha del fallecimiento antes del plazo ordinario de abril del año siguiente [13], así como abrir el procedimiento sucesorio (probate) ante el tribunal competente (Probate Court) del condado estadounidense donde radicaran sus bienes o domicilio.
  • Prestaciones y trámites sucesorios en España: Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o residía en España, consulte al Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social sobre el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad u orfandad [8]. Si dejó bienes o cuentas bancarias en España, transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde el deceso solicite al Ministerio de Justicia (mediante el Modelo 790) el Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento [9]. Con dichos certificados, acuda a una notaría a través del Consejo General del Notariado para obtener copia autorizada del testamento o tramitar la declaración de herederos y liquidar el Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones dentro del plazo legal de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (prorrogable por otros 6 meses si se solicita dentro de los primeros 5 meses) [10].

es.closingQuestion: Para ofrecerle indicaciones más específicas: 1. ¿En qué municipio y comunidad autónoma de España ocurrió el fallecimiento y a qué estado o ciudad de los Estados Unidos se dirigirían los restos o los trámites sucesorios? 2. ¿Desean organizar la repatriación del cuerpo, la cremación en España con traslado de las cenizas a los Estados Unidos, o la inhumación/cremación local en España?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Italy: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Italy, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Italy.
introHtml: We extend our condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residential ties dies in Italy, the process requires coordination among Italian health and municipal authorities, the U.S. consular mission in Italy, and federal and state agencies in the United States. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Pronouncement of Death, Necroscopic Examination, and Judicial Clearance in Italy
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: If the death occurs in a hospital or clinic (for example, in Rome, Milan, Florence, or Naples), the hospital medical management handles the clinical pronouncement of death (constatazione di decesso), completes the ISTAT cause-of-death statistical form (scheda ISTAT), and performs the necroscopic certification under the Italian Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento di polizia mortuaria, D.P.R. 285/1990) [1].
  • Death at a private residence, hotel, or public place: Call the single emergency number 112 (or 118) immediately so a physician can attend and issue the constatazione di decesso. Subsequently, the forensic/necroscopic physician (medico necroscopo) appointed by the competent Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) conducts the official necroscopic examination (visita necroscopica), which by law must take place no earlier than 15 hours and no later than 30 hours after death in order to issue the certificato necroscopico [1].
  • Sudden, violent, or unattended death: If the death occurs without medical attendance or under sudden or suspicious circumstances, law enforcement intervenes and reports the case to the Public Prosecutor's Office (Procura della Repubblica / Autorità Giudiziaria). In such cases, the body remains at the disposal of the magistrate for forensic examination or autopsy, and neither sealing the coffin nor cremation or international repatriation may proceed until the Prosecutor issues the formal burial/release authorization (nulla osta alla sepoltura) [1].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Italy and the United States, and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Verifying insurance coverage: Before signing private funeral contracts on your own, check whether your family member held travel, medical, or international assistance insurance covering repatriation of remains. If so, contact the insurer's operations center immediately so that it can appoint the funeral providers directly and cover the expenses [3].
  • Appointing a licensed funeral director in Italy and the United States: If no insurance company is involved, appoint a licensed funeral home in Italy (impresa funebre autorizzata, belonging to national industry federations such as FENIOF or Federcofit, or listed on the directories provided by U.S. consular offices) to handle sanitary preparation of the body as well as municipal and customs formalities [1][3]. For reception in the United States, select a state-licensed funeral home in the destination state through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA) [5]. Clarvia provides directory links solely for orientation and does not endorse specific commercial providers. Under the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized General Price List (including over the phone) and allow you to select only the services needed for receiving the remains and burial or cremation [6].
  • U.S. consular assistance: Report the death promptly to the U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy (Ambasciata e Consolati degli Stati Uniti in Italia - Rome and Florence: +39 06 46741; Milan: +39 02 290351; Naples: +39 081 583 8111) [2][3]. The consular office assists relatives in communicating with Italian authorities, safeguards personal effects if the deceased person was traveling alone, and issues the consular report of death, while noting that the U.S. Government cannot pay funeral or transportation costs [2][3].

steps.title: Registration with the Municipal Civil Status Office in Italy, Apostille or Form C, and U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Death declaration with the Italian municipality: Within 24 hours of the death, the appointed funeral company (a family member, or the hospital management) files the declaration of death with the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian municipality (Comune) where the death occurred in order to draw up the death record (atto di morte) and obtain the burial permit (permesso di seppellimento) [1]. Request multiple copies of the death certificate and summary extract (estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte) [1]. Although the Italian municipality can issue a multilingual death extract on Modello C (under the 1976 Vienna Convention), the United States is not a party to that convention; therefore, if a U.S. court or state authority requires the Italian certificate in addition to the consular report, the Italian death extract must be legalized with a Hague Apostille (Apostille dell'Aja) at the competent territorial Prefecture (Prefettura, under the Italian Ministry of the Interior, Ministero dell'Interno) and accompanied by a certified English translation [1][4].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Submit the Italian atto di morte and the deceased person's U.S. passport to the Ambasciata e Consolati degli Stati Uniti in Italia for the issuance of the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060) [2][3]. The CRDA carries official legal validity in English throughout the United States and is used in place of state Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics certificates for banking, insurance, and probate procedures [2][3].

steps.title: International Repatriation of the Body or Ashes to the United States vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Italy
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body from Italy to the United States: For the international transport of uncremated remains to the United States (which is not a party to the 1937 Berlin Convention), the Italian municipality of the place of death issues the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) upon receiving the ASL certificate confirming anti-putrefactive/embalming treatment and hermetic sealing in a double coffin (a soldered metal liner enclosed in a wooden casket in accordance with D.P.R. 285/1990), in accordance with the rules of the Ministero dell'Interno and the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale - MAECI) [1][4]. For entry into the United States, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) regulations (42 CFR 71.55) require uncremated human remains to travel in a leak-proof container consigned to a licensed U.S. funeral home or cemetery, accompanied by the official death certificate (or certification that the deceased had no quarantinable communicable disease) [7]. Upon arrival at the U.S. airport, U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment and the receiving funeral director obtains the state burial-transit permit.
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation in Italy is chosen (authorized by the Ufficio di Stato Civile based on the expressed wishes of the deceased or entitled next of kin), cremated ashes are exempt from CDC public health import permits under 42 CFR 71.55 [7] and may be transported in a sealed, X-ray-scannable urn accompanied by the death certificate, cremation record (verbale di cremazione), and transport authorization [1][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in Italy: If the family opts for final entombment (tumulazione), earth burial (inumazione), or cremation in Italy, the municipality issues the permesso di seppellimento directly to the Italian funeral company [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Probate in the United States and in Italy
steps.html:
• Social Security, taxes, and probate in the United States: Report the death to the Social Security Administration (SSA) by calling 1-800-772-1213 (from the United States) or by contacting the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Rome or the Consulate General in Naples to stop any undue monthly payments (benefits credited for the month of death must be returned) and to apply for the USD 255 lump-sum death payment or monthly survivor benefits [3][12]. If the deceased was a veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regarding burial allowances (Form VA 21P-530EZ) or burial in a national cemetery [13]. The legal representative or surviving relative must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040 marked "DECEASED") with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for income received up to the date of death by the regular April deadline of the following year [14], and initiate probate or estate administration before the competent county Probate Court in the United States.
  • Pensions, wills, and inheritance tax return in Italy: If your family member received a pension or paid social security contributions in Italy, contact the Italian National Social Security Institute (Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale - INPS) regarding survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti / reversibilità) or payment of accrued pension installments (ratei maturati e non riscossi) [8]. To verify whether a will was registered in Italy, you can request a certificate from the General Register of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) at the Italian Ministry of Justice (Ministero della Giustizia) and consult a notary through the National Council of Notaries (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) [10][11]. If the estate includes real property or assets in Italy, the heirs must electronically file the Italian inheritance return (dichiarazione di successione) with the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) within 12 months from the date of death [9].

closingQuestion: To provide more targeted guidance, in which Italian municipality (Comune) did the death occur, in which U.S. state did your family member reside or are repatriation and probate planned, and do you intend to proceed with repatriation of the body, cremation in Italy with transport of the ashes to the United States, or local burial/cremation in Italy?

it.title: Cosa fare in caso di decesso tra Italia e Stati Uniti: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso tra Italia e Stati Uniti: certificato medico di morte, impresa funebre autorizzata, registrazione allo Stato Civile, pratiche consolari e rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri, e pensione di reversibilità e successione.
it.introHtml: Esprimiamo le nostre condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona con cittadinanza o legami di residenza negli Stati Uniti muore in Italia, la procedura richiede il coordinamento tra le autorità sanitarie e comunali italiane, la rappresentanza consolare statunitense in Italia e gli enti federali e statali negli Stati Uniti. Di seguito sono illustrati in ordine i cinque passaggi ufficiali.

steps.title: Constatazione medica del decesso, visita necroscopica e nulla osta dell'Autorità Giudiziaria in Italia
steps.html:
• Decesso in struttura ospedaliera o sanitaria: Se il decesso avviene in ospedale o clinica (ad esempio a Roma, Milano, Firenze o Napoli), la direzione sanitaria provvede alla constatazione di decesso, alla compilazione della scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte e all'accertamento necroscopico secondo il Regolamento di polizia mortuaria (D.P.R. 285/1990) [1].
  • Decesso a domicilio, in albergo o in luogo pubblico: Chiamate immediatamente il numero unico di emergenza 112 (o il 118) affinché un medico intervenga per la constatazione di decesso. Successivamente, il medico necroscopo nominato dall'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) competente effettua la visita necroscopica, che per legge deve avvenire non prima di 15 ore e non oltre le 30 ore dal decesso per rilasciare il certificato necroscopico [1].
  • Morte improvvisa, violenta o in luogo pubblico: Se il decesso avviene senza assistenza medica o in circostanze improvvise o sospette, intervengono le forze dell'ordine e il caso viene segnalato alla Procura della Repubblica (Autorità Giudiziaria). In tali ipotesi la salma rimane a disposizione del magistrato per eventuali accertamenti medico-legali o autopsia, e né la chiusura del feretro né la cremazione o l'espatrio possono procedere prima del rilascio del formale nulla osta alla sepoltura da parte della Procura [1].

steps.title: Assicurazione per il rimpatrio, imprese funebri in Italia e negli Stati Uniti e assistenza consolare statunitense
steps.html:
• Verifica della copertura assicurativa: Prima di sottoscrivere contratti autonomi, verificate se il vostro familiare disponeva di un'assicurazione di viaggio, sanitaria o di assistenza internazionale comprensiva del rimpatrio della salma. In caso affermativo, contattate subito la centrale operativa dell'assicurazione affinché incarichi direttamente gli operatori funebri e copra le spese [3].
  • Nomina dell'impresa funebre in Italia e negli Stati Uniti: Se non interviene un'assicurazione, incaricate un'impresa funebre autorizzata in Italia (aderente alle federazioni nazionali di categoria come FENIOF o Federcofit, oppure presente negli elenchi messi a disposizione dagli uffici consolari statunitensi) per curare la preparazione sanitaria della salma e le pratiche comunali e doganali [1][3]. Per l'accoglienza negli Stati Uniti, individuate un'impresa funebre autorizzata nello Stato di destinazione tramite il repertorio della National Funeral Directors Association [5]. In base alla Funeral Rule della Federal Trade Commission, le imprese funebri statunitensi devono fornire un listino prezzi dettagliato (General Price List) anche telefonicamente e consentire di selezionare solo le prestazioni necessarie per il ricevimento e la sepoltura o cremazione [6].
  • Assistenza consolare statunitense: Segnalate tempestivamente il decesso all'Ambasciata e Consolati degli Stati Uniti in Italia (Roma e Firenze: +39 06 46741; Milano: +39 02 290351; Napoli: +39 081 583 8111) [2][3]. L'ufficio consolare assiste i familiari nelle comunicazioni con le autorità italiane, tutela gli effetti personali se la persona deceduta viaggiava da sola ed emette il rapporto consolare di morte, fermo restando che il Governo degli Stati Uniti non può sostenere i costi funebri o di trasporto [2][3].

steps.title: Registrazione presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile in Italia, apostille o Modello C e rapporto consolare statunitense (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Dichiarazione di morte nel Comune italiano: Entro 24 ore dal decesso, l'impresa funebre incaricata (un familiare o la direzione ospedaliera) presenta la dichiarazione di morte all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano in cui è avvenuto il decesso per formare l'atto di morte e ottenere il permesso di seppellimento [1]. Richiedete più copie del certificato e dell'estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte [1]. Sebbene il Comune italiano rilasci l'estratto di morte plurilingue su Modello C (Convenzione di Vienna del 1976), gli Stati Uniti non aderiscono a tale convenzione; pertanto, qualora un tribunale o un'autorità statale statunitense richieda l'atto italiano oltre al documento consolare, l'estratto di morte italiano dovrà essere munito di Apostille dell'Aja presso la Prefettura competente e di traduzione certificata in inglese [1][4].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Trasmettete l'atto di morte italiano e il passaporto statunitense della persona deceduta all'Ambasciata e Consolati degli Stati Uniti in Italia per il rilascio del Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Modulo DS-2060) [2][3]. Il CRDA ha valore ufficiale in inglese negli Stati Uniti ed è utilizzato al posto dei certificati statali (Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) per le pratiche bancarie, assicurative e successorie [2][3].

steps.title: Rimpatrio internazionale della salma o delle ceneri negli Stati Uniti rispetto a sepoltura o cremazione locale in Italia
steps.html:
• Rimpatrio internazionale della salma dall'Italia agli Stati Uniti: Per il trasporto internazionale di una salma verso gli Stati Uniti (Paese non aderente alla Convenzione di Berlino del 1937), il Comune italiano del luogo di decesso rilascia il Passaporto Mortuario previa acquisizione del certificato dell'ASL che attesta il trattamento antiputrefattivo/imbalsamazione e la chiusura ermetica in doppia cassa (cofano metallico saldato racchiuso in cassa di legno secondo il D.P.R. 285/1990), in raccordo con le indicazioni del Ministero dell'Interno e del Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale [1][4]. Per l'ingresso negli Stati Uniti, le norme dei Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) richiedono che i resti non cremati viaggino in un contenitore a tenuta stagna indirizzato a un'impresa funebre o cimitero autorizzato negli Stati Uniti, accompagnati dal certificato ufficiale di morte (o attestazione di assenza di malattie infettive sottoposte a quarantena) [7]. All'arrivo in aeroporto negli Stati Uniti, U.S. Customs and Border Protection effettua lo sdoganamento e l'impresa funebre ricevente ottiene il permesso statale di trasporto e sepoltura (burial-transit permit).
  • Rimpatrio delle ceneri: Se si sceglie la cremazione in Italia (autorizzata dall'Ufficio di Stato Civile sulla base della volontà espressa dalla persona deceduta o dai familiari aventi titolo), le ceneri sono esenti dal permesso sanitario di importazione dei Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) [7] e possono essere trasportate in un'urna sigillata ispezionabile ai raggi X accompagnata dal certificato di morte, dal verbale di cremazione e dall'autorizzazione al trasporto [1][7].
  • Sepoltura o cremazione locale in Italia: Se i familiari optano per la tumulazione, inumazione o cremazione definitiva in Italia, il Comune rilascia direttamente il permesso di seppellimento all'impresa funebre italiana [1].

steps.title: Adempimenti post-decesso, pensioni ai superstiti, fisco e successione negli Stati Uniti e in Italia
steps.html:
• Previdenza, fisco e successione (probate) negli Stati Uniti: Comunicate il decesso alla Social Security Administration telefonando al numero 1-800-772-1213 (dagli Stati Uniti) o contattando la Federal Benefits Unit presso l'Ambasciata statunitense a Roma o il Consolato Generale a Napoli per interrompere eventuali pagamenti mensili non dovuti (i ratei accreditati per il mese del decesso devono essere restituiti) e richiedere l'assegno una tantum di 255 USD o la pensione ai superstiti [3][12]. Se la persona deceduta era un veterano delle forze armate statunitensi, rivolgetevi al Department of Veterans Affairs per i contributi sulle spese funebri (Modulo VA 21P-530EZ) o la sepoltura in un cimitero nazionale [13]. Il rappresentante legale o il familiare superstite deve presentare all'Internal Revenue Service la dichiarazione finale dei redditi federali (Modulo 1040 con la dicitura "DECEASED") per i redditi percepiti fino alla data del decesso entro la scadenza ordinaria di aprile dell'anno successivo [14], e avviare la procedura di omologazione testamentaria o amministrazione ereditaria (probate) presso la Probate Court della contea statunitense competente.
  • Previdenza, testamenti e dichiarazione di successione in Italia: Se il vostro familiare percepiva una pensione o aveva contributi in Italia, contattate l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale per la pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o indiretta) o per la liquidazione dei ratei maturati e non riscossi [8]. Per verificare l'esistenza di un testamento in Italia, è possibile richiedere un certificato al Registro Generale dei Testamenti presso il Ministero della Giustizia e consultare un notaio tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [10][11]. Se nella successione rientrano beni immobili o attività in Italia, gli eredi devono presentare telematicamente la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data del decesso [9].

it.closingQuestion: Per fornirvi indicazioni più mirate: 1. In quale Comune italiano è avvenuto il decesso e in quale Stato degli Stati Uniti risiedeva il vostro familiare o sono previsti il rimpatrio e le pratiche ereditarie? 2. Intendete procedere con il rimpatrio della salma, con la cremazione in Italia e il trasporto delle ceneri negli Stati Uniti, oppure con la sepoltura/cremazione locale in Italia?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in France: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in France, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and France.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties dies in France, the official procedures are coordinated among French medical, municipal, and prefectural authorities, the U.S. consular services in France, and federal and state agencies in the United States. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in France
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, clinic, or nursing home (EHPAD): When a death occurs in a healthcare facility (for example in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, or Nice), the attending department physician immediately examines the deceased and issues the official medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, on a Cerfa paper form or via the electronic CertDc system), which is required to register the death and authorize any funeral operations [1][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Call the French emergency medical service (SAMU at 15) or the European emergency number (112) immediately so that a physician can certify the death on site and complete the certificat médical de décès [1]. Transfer of the body to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) prior to placement in a coffin must generally take place within 48 hours of death [4].
  • Medico-legal obstacle (obstacle médico-légal) and judicial investigation: In the event of a sudden, violent, or unexplained death, the physician checks the obstacle médico-légal box on the medical certificate. The police or gendarmerie and the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) take charge, and the body is transferred to a forensic institute (institut médico-légal). No coffin sealing, cremation, or departure from French territory may take place until the prosecutor's office issues the official release order (procès-verbal d'autorisation d'inhumer ou de transporter) [1][4].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in France and the United States, and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance first: Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, medical assistance coverage, or an employer policy covering international repatriation of remains. If coverage applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance center immediately, as it will appoint the funeral providers directly and cover the arrangements [3][5].
  • Appointing licensed funeral directors in France and the United States: If no insurance coverage applies, appoint a prefecture-licensed funeral operator in France (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture, such as a member of the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire - FNF or the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres - FFPF, or a provider on the U.S. consular list) to coordinate the chambre funéraire, embalming (soins de conservation), and prefectural permits [3][4]. For reception in the United States, appoint a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination state through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [6]. Under the federal Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission, U.S. funeral homes are required to provide an itemized General Price List over the phone or in person and to charge only for the specific goods and services you select [7].
  • U.S. consular notification: Report the death promptly to the Ambassade et Consulats des États-Unis en France (U.S. Embassy and Consulates in France, American Citizens Services unit in Paris at +33 1 43 12 22 22 or the Consulate General in Marseille) [2][3]. Consular officers guide the family through French procedures, safeguard personal effects if the deceased was traveling alone, and issue the consular death report, though the U.S. government does not pay for funeral or repatriation expenses [2][3].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration at the French Town Hall, Apostille or Form C, and U.S. Consular Report (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Civil registry declaration at the town hall (mairie) in France: The death must be registered within 24 hours (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred, a step usually completed by the French funeral director upon presenting the certificat médical de décès and the deceased's passport [1]. Request several full certified copies of the death certificate (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès) via Service-Public.fr or in person at the town hall [1]. Although French town halls issue multilingual death extracts on Formule C (under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention), the United States is not a party to that convention; if a U.S. court or agency requires the French certificate in addition to the consular report, obtain a Hague Apostille together with a certified English translation [1][5].
  • U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA): Submit the full French death certificate (copie intégrale de l'acte de décès) and your family member's U.S. passport to the Ambassade et Consulats des États-Unis en France to obtain the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060) [2][3]. This official English-language record serves as proof of death before U.S. Probate Courts, banks, insurance companies, and state Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics offices [2][3].

steps.title: International Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to the United States vs. Local Burial or Cremation in France
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body from France to the United States: For international transport of a body out of France, the French funeral director applies to the prefect (préfet) of the department where the coffin is sealed for a prefectural mortuary transit permit (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire), following embalming (soins de conservation / thanatopraxie) and placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered metal liner in accordance with public health regulations and procedures overseen with the Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs) [4][5]. For entry into the United States under the regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55), the body must be placed in a leak-proof container, consigned directly to a licensed funeral home or cemetery in the United States, and accompanied by the official death certificate and certification that the deceased did not die from a quarantinable communicable disease [8]. Upon arrival at the U.S. airport of entry, U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment and the receiving funeral home obtains the local state burial-transit permit.
  • Transport of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in France (authorized by the mayor of the municipality of death or cremation), transporting a funerary urn to the United States is exempt from a public health import permit under standard 42 CFR 71.55 of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [8]. The sealed urn (made of an X-ray-scannable material for cabin transport) must be accompanied by the death certificate, the cremation certificate (certificat de crémation), and the prefectural permit for the removal of ashes [3][4][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in France: If the family chooses final burial or cremation in France without international repatriation, the burial (inhumation) or cremation must take place between 24 hours and 14 calendar days after death upon authorization by the mayor [4].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in the United States and France
steps.html:
• Social Security, veterans benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States: Report the death to the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 (from within the United States) or by contacting the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy to stop monthly benefits (any payment received for the month of death must be returned) and to claim the USD 255 lump-sum death payment or monthly survivor benefits [3][12]. If your family member was a U.S. military veteran, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial allowances (Form VA 21P-530EZ) or interment in a national cemetery [13]. The estate executor or surviving family member must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040 marked "DECEASED") with the Internal Revenue Service for income received up to the date of death by the standard April filing deadline of the following year [14], and open estate administration (probate) before the appropriate county Probate Court in the United States.
  • Social security bodies, taxation, and estate settlement in France: If the deceased was affiliated with the French social security system or resided in France, notify the local health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM) via the Assurance Maladie portal to claim any applicable lump-sum death benefit (capital décès) and reimbursement of final medical expenses [9], as well as the French pension funds (such as L'Assurance Retraite / CNAV and Agirc-Arrco) for survivor pensions (pensions de réversion) [10]. If the deceased held real estate, bank accounts, or tax residence in France, instruct a notary's office through the Notaires de France network to search the central register of wills (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété), and file the French inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) within 6 months when the death occurred in metropolitan France [11].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation, in which French municipality did the death occur, in which U.S. state did your family member reside (or where do you plan to arrange the funeral and probate), and are you considering coffin repatriation, cremation in France followed by urn transport to the United States, or local burial or cremation in France?

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre France et États-Unis : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre France et États-Unis : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml: Nous vous présentons nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne ayant la nationalité américaine ou des attaches de résidence aux États-Unis décède en France, les démarches s'organisent entre les autorités médicales, municipales et préfectorales françaises, les services consulaires américains en France et les administrations fédérales et d'État aux États-Unis. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et levée d'un éventuel obstacle médico-légal en France
steps.html:
• Décès en établissement de santé ou EHPAD : Lorsqu'un décès survient à l'hôpital ou en clinique (par exemple à Paris, Lyon, Marseille ou Nice), le médecin du service procède immédiatement au constat et établit le certificat médical de décès (formulaire Cerfa ou certificat électronique CertDc), indispensable pour déclarer le décès et autoriser toute opération funéraire [1][4].
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU (15) ou le numéro d'urgence européen (112) afin qu'un médecin constate le décès et rédige le certificat médical de décès [1]. Le transport du corps vers une chambre funéraire avant la mise en bière doit en principe intervenir dans un délai de 48 heures suivant le décès [4].
  • Obstacle médico-légal et enquête judiciaire : En cas de mort soudaine, violente ou d'origine inconnue, le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat. Les services de police ou de gendarmerie et le procureur de la République sont alors saisis, et le corps est transféré vers un institut médico-légal. Aucune fermeture de cercueil, crémation ni sortie du territoire français ne peut avoir lieu avant la délivrance du procès-verbal d'autorisation d'inhumer ou de transporter par le parquet [1][4].

steps.title: Assurance rapatriement, opérateurs funéraires en France et aux États-Unis et assistance consulaire américaine
steps.html:
• Vérification préalable d'un contrat d'assurance : Avant de signer un devis funéraire en propre, vérifiez si votre proche bénéficiait d'une assurance voyage, d'une couverture d'assistance médicale ou d'un contrat d'employeur incluant le rapatriement du corps. Si une garantie s'applique, contactez immédiatement le plateau d'assistance de l'assureur, qui mandate directement les opérateurs funéraires et prend en charge l'organisation [3][5].
  • Choix d'un opérateur funéraire en France et aux États-Unis : En l'absence d'assureur, mandatez un opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture en France (affilié par exemple à la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire - FNF ou à la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres - FFPF, ou figurant sur la liste consulaire américaine) pour coordonner la chambre funéraire, les soins de conservation et les autorisations préfectorales [3][4]. Pour la réception aux États-Unis, désignez un établissement funéraire agréé dans l'État de destination via l'annuaire de la National Funeral Directors Association [6]. En vertu de la règle fédérale Funeral Rule de la Federal Trade Commission, les pompes funèbres américaines ont l'obligation de vous communiquer un barème détaillé des tarifs (General Price List) par téléphone ou sur place et de ne facturer que les prestations choisies [7].
  • Notification consulaire américaine : Signalez rapidement le décès à l'Ambassade et Consulats des États-Unis en France (unité des Services aux citoyens américains à Paris au +33 1 43 12 22 22 ou Consulat général à Marseille) [2][3]. Les services consulaires orientent la famille sur les procédures françaises, assurent la sauvegarde des effets personnels si la personne décédée voyageait seule et établissent le rapport consulaire de décès, étant précisé que le gouvernement américain ne finance pas les frais d'obsèques ni de transport [2][3].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès en mairie en France, apostille ou Formule C et rapport consulaire américain (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Déclaration à l'état civil de la mairie en France : Le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès de la mairie de la commune du lieu de décès, démarche généralement accomplie par l'entreprise de pompes funèbres française sur présentation du certificat médical de décès et du passeport de la personne décédée [1]. Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès sur le portail Service-Public.fr ou en mairie [1]. Bien que les mairies françaises délivrent l'extrait d'acte de décès plurilingue (Formule C issue de la Convention de Vienne de 1976), les États-Unis ne sont pas signataires de cette convention ; si un tribunal ou organisme américain exige l'acte français en complément du document consulaire, faites apposer l'Apostille de La Haye accompagnée d'une traduction assermentée en anglais [1][5].
  • Rapport consulaire américain de décès à l'étranger (CRDA) : Transmettez la copie intégrale de l'acte de décès français et le passeport américain de votre proche à l'Ambassade et Consulats des États-Unis en France afin d'obtenir le Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (formulaire DS-2060) [2][3]. Ce document officiel rédigé en anglais tient lieu d'acte de décès auprès des tribunaux américains (Probate Courts), des banques, des compagnies d'assurance et des bureaux d'état civil des États (Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) [2][3].

steps.title: Rapatriement international du corps ou des cendres vers les États-Unis ou inhumation et crémation en France
steps.html:
• Rapatriement du corps de la France vers les États-Unis : Pour le transport international d'un corps hors de France, l'opérateur funéraire français sollicite auprès du préfet du département de fermeture du cercueil un arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire, après réalisation des soins de conservation (thanatopraxie) et mise en bière dans un cercueil hermétique avec enveloppe métallique scellée conformément aux règles sanitaires et aux procédures suivies avec le Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères [4][5]. Pour l'entrée sur le territoire américain selon la réglementation des Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55), le corps doit être placé dans un contenant étanche, expédié directement à un opérateur funéraire ou cimetière agréé aux États-Unis et accompagné de l'acte de décès officiel ainsi que de l'attestation d'absence de maladie contagieuse soumise à quarantaine [8]. À l'arrivée à l'aéroport américain, U.S. Customs and Border Protection procède au dédouanement et la maison funéraire réceptrice obtient le permis local d'inhumer ou de transport (burial-transit permit).
  • Transport des cendres : Si la crémation a lieu en France (sur autorisation du maire de la commune du décès ou de crémation), le transport d'une urne cinéraire vers les États-Unis est dispensé de permis sanitaire d'importation au titre de la norme 42 CFR 71.55 des Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [8]. L'urne scellée (compatible avec le contrôle par rayons X en cabine) doit être accompagnée de l'acte de décès, du certificat de crémation et de l'autorisation préfectorale de sortie des cendres [3][4][8].
  • Inhumation ou crémation locale en France : Si la famille choisit des obsèques définitives en France sans rapatriement, l'inhumation ou la crémation intervient entre 24 heures et 14 jours calendaires après le décès sur autorisation du maire [4].

steps.title: Démarches après décès, pensions de réversion, fiscalité et succession aux États-Unis et en France
steps.html:
• Sécurité sociale, anciens combattants, impôts et succession (probate) aux États-Unis : Déclarez le décès à la Social Security Administration en appelant le 1-800-772-1213 (depuis les États-Unis) ou en contactant l'unité des prestations fédérales (Federal Benefits Unit) auprès de l'ambassade américaine afin d'interrompre les versements mensuels (tout versement perçu pour le mois du décès devant être restitué) et de demander l'allocation forfaitaire de 255 USD ou une pension de survivant [3][12]. Si votre proche était un ancien combattant américain, contactez le Department of Veterans Affairs pour les indemnités funéraires (formulaire VA 21P-530EZ) ou une sépulture en cimetière national [13]. Le représentant de la succession ou le proche survivant doit déposer auprès de l'Internal Revenue Service la déclaration fédérale finale d'impôt sur le revenu (formulaire 1040 portant la mention « DECEASED ») pour les revenus perçus jusqu'au jour du décès avant l'échéance habituelle d'avril de l'année suivante [14], et ouvrir la procédure d'homologation successorale (probate) devant la Probate Court du comté américain compétent.
  • Organismes sociaux, fiscalité et règlement de la succession en France : Si la personne décédée était affiliée ou résidait en France, informez la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie via le portail de l'Assurance Maladie pour demander, le cas échéant, le versement du capital décès et le remboursement des derniers frais de santé [9], ainsi que les caisses de retraite (telles que L'Assurance Retraite / CNAV et l'Agirc-Arrco) pour les pensions de réversion [10]. En présence de biens immobiliers, de comptes bancaires ou d'une résidence fiscale en France, mandatez un office notarial via le réseau des Notaires de France afin d'interroger le Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés (FCDDV), d'établir l'acte de notoriété et de déposer la déclaration fiscale de succession dans un délai de 6 mois lorsque le décès est survenu en France métropolitaine [11].

fr.closingQuestion: Afin de préciser ces démarches selon votre situation : 1. Dans quelle commune française le décès est-il survenu, et dans quel État américain votre proche résidait-il ou souhaitez-vous organiser les obsèques et la succession ? 2. Envisagez-vous un rapatriement du corps en cercueil, une crémation en France suivie du transport de l'urne vers les États-Unis, ou une inhumation/crémation locale en France ?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Germany: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Germany, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Germany.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties dies in Germany, state-level German burial and civil status laws intersect with U.S. consular and federal/state regulations. The following five official steps explain the required procedures in order.

steps.title: Medical Examination of the Deceased, Death Certificate, and Police or Prosecutor Clearance in Germany
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or nursing home: If the death occurs in a clinic or care facility (for example in Berlin, Frankfurt am Main, or Munich), the medical staff immediately arranges the statutory post-mortem examination (ärztliche Leichenschau) and issues the official medical certificate of death (Todesbescheinigung or Totenschein), comprising a confidential medical section and a non-confidential section [1][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately contact the emergency medical services by dialing 112 or the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) at 116 117 so that a physician can perform the Leichenschau and issue the Totenschein [4].
  • Unexplained or unnatural cause of death: If the examining physician records an unexplained or unnatural manner of death, the police and the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) are notified. The body is temporarily taken into custody and transferred to an institute of forensic medicine (Institut für Rechtsmedizin); registration at the civil registry office, cremation, or international repatriation may only proceed once the Staatsanwaltschaft issues written burial clearance (schriftliche Freigabe zur Bestattung) [1][4].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Germany and the United States, and U.S. Consular Support
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance: Before commissioning a funeral home independently, verify whether the deceased person held travel health insurance, repatriation coverage, or an employer-sponsored policy. If coverage exists, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance center first, as it typically instructs the funeral providers directly and covers repatriation costs [4].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Germany and the United States: If no insurance coverage applies, appoint a licensed funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen) in Germany via the national professional association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Federal Association of German Undertakers) or the consular lists maintained by the U.S. missions [3][4]. Because of German state burial laws (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and mandatory cemetery rules (Friedhofszwang), the German funeral director handles hygienic preparation, administrative permits, and air cargo booking [4]. For reception at the destination in the United States, select a licensed U.S. funeral home through the National Funeral Directors Association [6]. Under the consumer protection Funeral Rule enforced by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, every U.S. funeral provider must give you an itemized General Price List over the phone and in person so that you book only the receiving and burial services actually needed [7].
  • Notification to the U.S. diplomatic mission: Report the death promptly to the US-Botschaft und Konsulate in Deutschland (U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Germany) in Berlin (phone +49 30 8305-0), Frankfurt am Main, or Munich [2][3]. The consulate assists family members with German formalities, safeguards personal effects if no relatives are present locally, and issues the U.S. consular death report; however, the U.S. government does not pay for funeral or repatriation costs [2][3].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration at the German Standesamt, Apostille or Form C, and U.S. Consular Report (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Registration at the civil registry (Standesamt) in Germany: Under Section 28 of the German Civil Status Act (§ 28 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG), the death must be reported to the civil registry office (Standesamt) of the place of death no later than the third working day following the death; for hospital deaths, the hospital administration or the appointed funeral director usually handles this filing [1]. Request several certified copies of the German death certificate (Sterbeurkunde) [1]. Although German registry offices also issue international multilingual extracts on Formblatt C (under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention), the United States is not a signatory to that convention; if a U.S. court or agency requires the German certificate in addition to the consular report, have the funeral director obtain a Hague Apostille (issued depending on the German federal state by the Regierungspräsidium, Bezirksregierung, or Landgericht) together with a certified English translation [5].
  • U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA): Submit the German Sterbeurkunde and the deceased person's U.S. passport to the US-Botschaft und Konsulate in Deutschland to obtain the electronic Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060 / CRODA) [2][3]. This English-language document is recognized across the United States by Probate Courts, banks, insurance companies, and state Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics offices as equivalent to a domestic death certificate [2][3].

steps.title: International Repatriation of the Body or Urn to the United States vs. Local Burial in Germany
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body from Germany to the United States: For international transport of a body, the German funeral director obtains a multilingual corpse transit permit (Leichenpass, under the 1937 International Berlin Agreement and state burial laws) from the local public health or regulatory office (Gesundheitsamt or Ordnungsamt) at the place of death, along with consular transit documents in accordance with guidance from the Auswärtiges Amt (German Federal Foreign Office) [4][5]. The body is embalmed and hermetically sealed inside a soldered zinc liner within a transport coffin [4][8]. For entry into the United States, the regulations of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) require a leak-proof container, direct consignment to a licensed U.S. funeral home or cemetery, and the official death certificate (or certification that no quarantinable communicable disease is present) [8]. At the U.S. arrival airport, U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment and the receiving U.S. funeral home secures the state burial-transit permit.
  • Transport of an urn after cremation in Germany: If cremation (Feuerbestattung) takes place in Germany following a mandatory second medical examination by an official public health physician (Amtsarzt), note the German mandatory cemetery requirement (Friedhofszwang): many German crematoria release the urn only upon presentation of a cemetery acceptance certificate (Übernahmebescheinigung) or proof of international shipment handled by an authorized funeral director [4]. For entry into the United States, cremated human remains are exempt from a CDC import permit under 42 CFR 71.55 and may be transported in a tightly sealed, X-ray-transparent urn accompanied by the death certificate and cremation certificate (Einäscherungsbescheinigung) [3][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in Germany: If the family prefers burial or cremation in Germany without repatriation to the United States, the Standesamt issues the burial permit (Bestattungsschein) for the local cemetery or crematorium [1][4].

steps.title: Deregistrations, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Probate in the United States and Germany
steps.html:
• Social Security, veterans benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States: Report the death to the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 (within the United States) or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Consulate General in Frankfurt am Main to prevent overpayments (benefits paid for the month of death must be returned) and to apply for the USD 255 one-time lump-sum death payment or ongoing survivor benefits [3][12]. If the deceased person served in the U.S. armed forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial allowances (Form VA 21P-530EZ) or interment in a U.S. national cemetery [13]. The estate administrator or surviving relative must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040 marked "DECEASED") with the Internal Revenue Service by the regular April deadline of the following year for income earned up to the date of death [14], and open probate proceedings for U.S. assets before the appropriate County Probate Court in the relevant U.S. state.
  • Pensions, health insurance, and probate court (Nachlassgericht) in Germany: If your family member received a German pension or had German social insurance periods, promptly notify the pension payment service Renten Service der Deutschen Post to stop ongoing payments or apply for the three-month transition payment (Sterbevierteljahr, an advance application due within 30 days of death), and file a claim for a widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Form R0500) with the statutory pension authority Deutsche Rentenversicherung [9][10]. Also notify the German statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung). If assets or real estate were located in Germany, the Standesamt automatically notifies the Zentrales Testamentsregister (Central Register of Wills) of the Federal Chamber of Notaries (Bundesnotarkammer), which forwards any deposited testamentary dispositions to the competent probate court (Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht), where heirs may apply for a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession if needed [11].

closingQuestion: So that we can assist you more specifically, in which German municipality (and federal state) did the death occur, in which U.S. state did your family member reside (or where should the repatriation be sent), and are you planning coffin repatriation to the United States, cremation in Germany followed by urn transport to the United States, or local burial in Germany?
