de.title: Todesfall in Deutschland (Vereinigte Staaten): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Deutschland und Vereinigte Staaten: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit Staatsangehörigkeit oder Wohnsitzbezug zu den Vereinigten Staaten in Deutschland verstirbt, greifen die deutschen landesrechtlichen Bestattungs- und Personenstandsvorschriften sowie die konsularischen und bundesstaatlichen Regelungen der Vereinigten Staaten ineinander. Die folgenden fünf offiziellen Schritte erläutern das Vorgehen in der richtigen Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Ärztliche Leichenschau, Todesbescheinigung und polizeiliche oder staatsanwaltschaftliche Freigabe in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Sterbefall im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim: Tritt der Tod in einer Klinik (beispielsweise in Berlin, Frankfurt am Main oder München) ein, veranlasst das medizinische Personal unverzüglich die ärztliche Leichenschau und stellt die amtliche Todesbescheinigung (Totenschein) mit einem vertraulichen und einem nicht vertraulichen Teil aus [1][4].
  • Sterbefall zu Hause, im Hotel oder an einem öffentlichen Ort: Verständigen Sie sofort den Rettungsdienst über den Notruf 112 oder den ärztlichen Bereitschaftsdienst unter 116 117, damit eine Ärztin oder ein Arzt die Leichenschau durchführt und den Totenschein ausstellt [4].
  • Ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesursache: Bescheinigt die Ärztin oder der Arzt eine ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesart, werden Polizei und Staatsanwaltschaft eingeschaltet. Der Leichnam wird dann zunächst beschlagnahmt und in ein Institut für Rechtsmedizin überführt; eine Beurkundung beim Standesamt, eine Einäscherung oder eine Auslandsüberführung darf erst erfolgen, wenn die Staatsanwaltschaft die schriftliche Freigabe zur Bestattung erteilt hat [1][4].

steps.title: Rückholversicherung, Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und den USA sowie US-konsularische Unterstützung
steps.html:
• Prüfung einer Reise- oder Rückholversicherung: Prüfen Sie vor einer eigenen Auftragsvergabe, ob für die verstorbene Person eine Reisekranken-, Rückhol- oder Arbeitgeberversicherung bestand. Falls ja, kontaktieren Sie zuerst die 24-Stunden-Notrufzentrale der Versicherung, da diese in der Regel die Bestattungsunternehmen direkt beauftragt und die Überführungskosten übernimmt [4].
  • Beauftragung von Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und den USA: Besteht kein Versicherungsschutz, beauftragen Sie in Deutschland ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen über den Berufsverband (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V.) oder über die Konsularlisten der US-Vertretungen [3][4]. Wegen der Landesbestattungsgesetze und des deutschen Friedhofszwangs übernimmt der deutsche Bestatter die hygienische Versorgung, die Behördengänge und die Flugbuchung [4]. Für die Übernahme am Zielort in den Vereinigten Staaten wählen Sie ein lizenziertes US-Bestattungsinstitut über den US-Fachverband (National Funeral Directors Association) [6]. Nach der Verbraucherschutzvorschrift Funeral Rule der US-Behörde Federal Trade Commission muss Ihnen jedes US-Bestattungsunternehmen telefonisch und vor Ort eine aufgeschlüsselte Preisliste (General Price List) aushändigen, sodass Sie nur die tatsächlich benötigten Empfangs- und Beisetzungsleistungen buchen [7].
  • Meldung an die US-Auslandsvertretung: Melden Sie den Todesfall zeitnah an die zuständige diplomatische Vertretung (US-Botschaft und Konsulate in Deutschland) in Berlin (Telefon +49 30 8305-0), Frankfurt am Main oder München [2][3]. Das Konsulat unterstützt Angehörige bei den deutschen Formalitäten, sichert den persönlichen Nachlass, falls keine Angehörigen vor Ort sind, und stellt die US-konsularische Sterbeurkunde aus; die US-Regierung übernimmt jedoch keine Bestattungs- oder Überführungskosten [2][3].

steps.title: Sterbefallanzeige beim deutschen Standesamt, Apostille oder Formblatt C und US-Konsularbericht (CRDA)
steps.html:
• Beurkundung beim Standesamt in Deutschland: Der Sterbefall muss gemäß § 28 Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag beim Standesamt des Sterbeortes angezeigt werden; bei einem Tod im Krankenhaus erledigt dies meist die Klinikverwaltung oder das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen [1]. Beantragen Sie mehrere beglaubigte Abschriften der deutschen Sterbeurkunde [1]. Zwar stellen deutsche Standesämter auch internationale mehrsprachige Auszüge auf Formblatt C (Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen von 1976) aus, jedoch sind die Vereinigten Staaten diesem Abkommen nicht beigetreten; verlangt ein US-Gericht oder eine US-Behörde neben dem Konsularbericht die deutsche Urkunde, lassen Sie durch das Bestattungsunternehmen eine Haager Apostille (je nach Bundesland durch das Regierungspräsidium, die Bezirksregierung oder das Landgericht) sowie eine beglaubigte englische Übersetzung anfertigen [5].
  • US-Konsularbericht über den Tod im Ausland (CRDA): Reichen Sie die deutsche Sterbeurkunde und den US-Reisepass der verstorbenen Person bei der Vertretung (US-Botschaft und Konsulate in Deutschland) ein, um den elektronischen Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Formular DS-2060 / CRODA) zu erhalten [2][3]. Dieses englischsprachige Dokument wird in den Vereinigten Staaten von Nachlassgerichten, Banken, Versicherungen und Standesämtern (Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) wie eine inländische Sterbeurkunde anerkannt [2][3].

steps.title: Internationale Überführung von Leichnam oder Urne in die USA gegenüber lokaler Bestattung in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Überführung des Leichnams aus Deutschland in die USA: Für den internationalen Transport eines Leichnams beantragt das deutsche Bestattungsunternehmen beim zuständigen Gesundheits- oder Ordnungsamt des Sterbeortes einen mehrsprachigen Leichenpass (nach dem Internationalen Berliner Abkommen von 1937 bzw. den Landesbestattungsgesetzen) sowie die konsularischen Begleitpapiere im Einklang mit den Hinweisen der Außenbehörde (Auswärtiges Amt) [4][5]. Der Leichnam wird konserviert (einbalsamiert) und in einem verlöteten Zinksarg innerhalb eines Transportsargs luftdicht verschlossen [4][8]. Für die Einfuhr in die Vereinigten Staaten schreiben die Richtlinien der US-Gesundheitsbehörde Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) einen auslaufsicheren Behälter, die direkte Adressierung an ein lizenziertes US-Bestattungsinstitut oder einen Friedhof sowie die amtliche Sterbeurkunde (bzw. den Nachweis, dass keine quarantänepflichtige Infektionskrankheit vorliegt) vor [8]. Am US-Ankunftsflughafen gibt U.S. Customs and Border Protection die Sendung frei, und das empfangende US-Bestattungsinstitut holt die bundesstaatliche Transport- und Bestattungsgenehmigung (burial-transit permit) ein.
  • Überführung einer Urne nach Einäscherung in Deutschland: Erfolgt die Feuerbestattung nach einer zweiten ärztlichen Amtsarzt-Leichenschau in Deutschland, beachten Sie den deutschen Friedhofszwang: Viele deutsche Krematorien geben die Urne nur gegen eine Übernahmebescheinigung eines Friedhofs oder den Nachweis der Auslandsverbringung durch einen befugten Bestatter frei [4]. Für die Einreise in die USA sind eingeäscherte sterbliche Überreste gemäß 42 CFR 71.55 von einer CDC-Einfuhrgenehmigung befreit und können in einer röntgendurchlässigen, fest verschlossenen Urne zusammen mit der Sterbeurkunde und der Einäscherungsbescheinigung befördert werden [3][8].
  • Lokale Erd- oder Feuerbestattung in Deutschland: Wünscht die Familie eine Beisetzung in Deutschland ohne Überführung in die USA, stellt das Standesamt den Bestattungsschein für den örtlichen Friedhof oder das Krematorium aus [1][4].

steps.title: Abmeldungen, Hinterbliebenenrenten, Steuern und Nachlassverfahren in den USA und in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Sozialversicherung, Veteranenleistungen, Steuern und Probate in den USA: Melden Sie den Todesfall der US-Rentenbehörde (Social Security Administration) telefonisch unter 1-800-772-1213 (innerhalb der USA) oder über die Federal Benefits Unit beim US-Generalkonsulat in Frankfurt am Main, um Überzahlungen zu stoppen (Rentenzahlungen für den Sterbemonat müssen zurückgezahlt werden) und das einmalige Sterbegeld von 255 USD oder laufende Hinterbliebenenrenten zu beantragen [3][12]. War die verstorbene Person Angehörige der US-Streitkräfte, wenden Sie sich bezüglich Bestattungsbeihilfen (Formular VA 21P-530EZ) oder einer Beisetzung auf einem US-Nationalfriedhof an die US-Veteranenbehörde (Department of Veterans Affairs) [13]. Der Nachlassverwalter oder hinterbliebene Angehörige muss bei der US-Steuerbehörde (Internal Revenue Service) bis zur regulären April-Frist des Folgejahres die abschließende Einkommensteuererklärung (Formular 1040 mit dem Vermerk „DECEASED“) für das bis zum Todestag erzielte Einkommen einreichen [14] und für US-Vermögenswerte das Nachlassverfahren (Probate) beim zuständigen County Probate Court im jeweiligen US-Bundesstaat eröffnen.
  • Renten, Krankenversicherung und Nachlassgericht in Deutschland: Bezog Ihr Familienangehöriger eine deutsche Rente oder bestanden deutsche Versicherungszeiten, informieren Sie umgehend die Auszahlungsstelle (Renten Service der Deutschen Post) zur Einstellung der laufenden Zahlung bzw. zur Beantragung des Sterbevierteljahres (Vorschusszahlung innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod) und beantragen Sie beim deutschen Rententräger (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) eine Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente (Formular R0500) [9][10]. Melden Sie den Sterbefall zudem der Gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung. Befanden sich Vermögenswerte oder Immobilien in Deutschland, informiert das Standesamt automatisch das Registerportal (Zentrales Testamentsregister) der Bundesnotarkammer, welches hinterlegte Verfügungen von Todes wegen an das zuständige Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht übermittelt, wo Erben bei Bedarf einen Erbschein oder ein Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis beantragen können [11].

de.closingQuestion: Damit wir Ihnen noch gezielter weiterhelfen können: 1. In welcher deutschen Gemeinde (und welchem Bundesland) ist der Todesfall eingetreten, und in welchem US-Bundesstaat hatte Ihr Familienangehöriger seinen Wohnsitz bzw. wohin soll die Überführung erfolgen? 2. Planen Sie eine Sargüberführung in die USA, eine Einäscherung in Deutschland mit anschließendem Urnentransport in die USA oder eine Bestattung vor Ort in Deutschland?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Philippines Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Philippines Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Philippines dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Philippines and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the Philippines dies in the United States, medical certification and civil death registration are completed first at the U.S. state and county level, followed by consular registration (Report of Death) and a Consular Mortuary Certificate through the Philippine Embassy or Consulate General if the remains or ashes are being repatriated to the Philippines [1][3][5]. Below is the five-step official sequence.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
Before a funeral director can register the death or prepare the body for transport or local disposition, an authorized medical professional or county medico-legal authority must pronounce the death and certify the cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, nursing facility, or under hospice care: The attending physician or authorized medical staff pronounces the death, completes the medical cause-of-death certification in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes release of the deceased to the family's appointed funeral home [1][2]. If the death occurs at home under registered hospice care, contact the hospice nurse on duty rather than emergency services so the hospice team can pronounce the death directly [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital: Call 911 immediately and do not move the body [1]. Local police and emergency medical services respond and refer sudden, unexplained, accidental, or unattended deaths to the county Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City or the County of Los Angeles Department of Medical Examiner) [1][2]. The Coroner or Medical Examiner conducts an investigation or autopsy if required by state law, issues the medical cause-of-death certification, and releases the body to the appointed funeral director [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint U.S. and Philippine Funeral Directors, and Notify the Philippine Embassy or Consulate
steps.html:
Do not attempt to arrange international air cargo, embalming certificates, or airport quarantine clearance independently. First verify whether existing coverage or government migrant worker assistance applies [1][5]:

  • Travel, medical, or OFW repatriation coverage: Check whether your family member had travel medical insurance, international health coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation insurance, and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance center before signing independent contracts. If the deceased was an Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW), contact the Migrant Workers Office (MWO) and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) through the Philippine Embassy or Consulate to coordinate government repatriation and bereavement assistance [3][5].
  • Appointing a U.S. funeral home and a receiving Philippine mortuary: Appoint a state-licensed U.S. funeral home (searchable via the National Funeral Directors Association directory at +1 262-789-1880 or 800-228-6332) to coordinate local preparation and export, paired with a Department of Health (DOH)-licensed receiving funeral establishment and mortuary in the Philippines to handle airport cargo reception and local transport [4][5][7]. Clarvia provides public directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Consumer protections under the FTC Funeral Rule: Under the federal Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (phone +1 877-382-4357), U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized written General Price List (GPL) before you commit to services, quote prices by telephone on request, and allow you to select only the specific services and merchandise required [6].
  • Notifying the Philippine Foreign Service Post: Contact the Embassy of the Philippines in Washington, D.C. (Assistance-to-Nationals desk +1 202-769-8049, emergency duty officer +1 202-368-2767, civil registration email civilregistration@phembassy-us.org) or the Philippine Consulate General holding consular jurisdiction over the U.S. state where the death occurred (such as New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Chicago, Honolulu, or Houston) [3][5]. If next of kin are located in the Philippines, they can execute a notarized Letter of Authorization / Special Power of Attorney empowering a representative in the United States or the appointed funeral home to process the consular and mortuary documents [3][5].

steps.title: Register the Death with U.S. Vital Records and File the Consular Report of Death for the Philippines
steps.html:
The death must be officially recorded in the U.S. state of death and reported to Philippine civil registry authorities so it is recognized in both countries [1][2][3]:

  • U.S. state or county Vital Records registration: The U.S. funeral director gathers the deceased's personal details and files the death certificate with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the statutory state deadline (typically 3 to 5 days after death) [1][2]. Request at least 5 to 10 certified copies of the official U.S. Death Certificate (explicitly showing the cause of death) through the funeral director or via the state Vital Records office listed on USA.gov (+1 844-872-4681) [1][2][3].
  • Philippine Consular Report of Death (ROD) and PSA SECPA Certificate: When a Filipino citizen dies in the United States, the death is registered for the Philippines by filing a Report of Death (ROD) (typically in four typed copies, submitted in person or notarized by mail) with the Embassy of the Philippines in Washington, D.C. or the competent Philippine Consulate General, presenting the original U.S. Death Certificate stating the cause of death, the deceased's Philippine passport (or proof of dual citizenship), and the informant's ID [3]. The Philippine Embassy or Consulate transmits the registered Report of Death through the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA, central inquiry line +63 2 8461-0500) so the family can obtain an official PSA Death Certificate on Security Paper (SECPA) [3]. (Note: the 30-day Local Civil Registry Office filing of Municipal Form No. 103 applies when a death occurs domestically inside a Philippine municipality, whereas U.S. deaths are recorded via the Consular Report of Death; if a U.S. public document is presented directly in the Philippines outside the ROD channel, obtain a Hague Apostille from the U.S. state's Secretary of State [2][3].)

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the Philippines and Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
Your appointed U.S. funeral director and the Philippine Embassy or Consulate coordinate the permits required for international shipment or local disposition [5][7][8]:

  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) human remains to the Philippines: The U.S. funeral home obtains the state or county Burial-Transit Permit, a notarized Mortuary Certificate confirming that the body was properly embalmed and placed in a hermetically sealed casket containing only the deceased, and a Certificate of No Contagious Disease from the local U.S. health department [5]. Submit these documents along with the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the deceased's passport, and the consignee details of the receiving DOH-licensed funeral home in the Philippines to the Embassy of the Philippines in Washington, D.C. (or regional Philippine Consulate General) at least seven (7) working days before the scheduled flight to obtain the Consular Mortuary Certificate (CMC) and Report of Death [5]. The U.S. funeral home arranges air cargo clearance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the airline (incorporating applicable public health rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention at 800-232-4636) [7]. Upon arrival at the Philippine international airport (such as Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila or Mactan-Cebu International Airport), the receiving Philippine funeral provider presents the Consular Mortuary Certificate, U.S. Death Certificate, and embalming/non-contagious certificates to the Department of Health Bureau of Quarantine (BOQ, phone +63 2 5318-7500) for quarantine release and local transfer/burial permits [5][8].
  • Repatriating cremated remains (ashes) to the Philippines: If cremation takes place in the United States, apply to the Philippine Embassy or Consulate for a Consular Mortuary Certificate (or consular clearance for ashes) by submitting the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, a certificate confirming the urn contains only cremated human ashes, and the flight itinerary or passport copy of the person hand-carrying the urn [5]. At the Philippine port of entry, present the documents to the Bureau of Quarantine for release [5][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United States, the U.S. funeral director uses the state burial-transit or cremation permit (subject to any state-mandated 24- to 48-hour waiting period and Coroner/Medical Examiner cremation clearance) to complete local interment or cremation, while the family still files the Consular Report of Death so Philippine civil records are updated [1][2][3].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in the Philippines and the United States
steps.html:
With the certified U.S. Death Certificates and the Philippine Consular Report of Death (and subsequent PSA SECPA Death Certificate), complete notifications in both jurisdictions:

  • In the Philippines (SSS, GSIS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, OWWA, and BIR Estate Tax):
    • Social Security System (SSS) or GSIS: For private-sector or voluntary OFW members, the person who paid the funeral expenses can claim the SSS Funeral Benefit (PHP 20,000 to PHP 60,000) [9], and eligible beneficiaries can claim the SSS Death Benefit (monthly survivorship pension or lump sum) via the My.SSS portal or any branch of the Social Security System (hotline +63 2 81455, email usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph) [10]. For public-sector employees or pensioners, file Funeral and Survivorship Benefit claims with the Government Service Insurance System (hotline +63 2 8847-4747) [11].
    • Pag-IBIG Fund, PhilHealth, and OWWA: Claim the deceased member's Total Accumulated Value (TAV) savings and death benefit from the Pag-IBIG Fund, notify PhilHealth, and, for eligible OFWs, file for death and burial benefits (up to PHP 100,000 for natural death or PHP 200,000 for accidental death, plus PHP 20,000 burial aid for active members) with OWWA.
    • BIR Estate Tax Return within 1 year and Extrajudicial Settlement: If the deceased left property or bank accounts in the Philippines, the heirs, executor, or administrator must file the Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801) with the Bureau of Internal Revenue (phone +63 2 8538-3200) within one (1) year from the date of death (6% flat estate tax on the net estate after the PHP 5,000,000 standard deduction and up to PHP 10,000,000 family home deduction) to obtain the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) [12]. If there is no will and no unpaid debts, the heirs may execute a notarized Deed of Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate (published once a week for three consecutive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation); if there is a will, file for judicial probate in the Philippine Regional Trial Court [12].
  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately to stop monthly payments and apply for survivor benefits or the $255 one-time lump-sum death payment by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or, if surviving beneficiaries live in the Philippines, by contacting the U.S. Embassy Manila Federal Benefits Unit at +63 2 5301-6200 or FBU.Manila@ssa.gov) [13].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs at +1 800-827-1000 (or the VA Regional Benefit Office in Manila at +63 2 8550-3888) regarding burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), headstones, and Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [14].
    • IRS final tax return and State Probate Court: The personal representative must file the deceased's final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (+1 800-829-1040) by April 15 of the year following death (and Form 1041 if estate post-death income reaches $600 or more) [15]. For U.S. bank accounts and property without designated beneficiaries, file the will or petition for administration (or use a state Small Estate Affidavit if below the statutory threshold) in the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) of the U.S. state of domicile [1].

closingQuestion: To help us provide exact contacts and requirements, in which U.S. state and county did your family member pass away (and what is the destination city or province in the Philippines), and are you planning casketed repatriation, shipment of cremated ashes, or a local service in the United States?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in India: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in India, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and India.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in India, medical certification, police clearance (where required), and municipal civil registration must be completed first in India, while an international funeral coordinator works with the U.S. Embassy or Consulate General in India to issue the Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) and arrange repatriation or local disposition [1][2][3]. Below is the five-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4 or Form 4A) and Police Clearance in India
steps.html:
Under India's Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, no burial, cremation, embalming, or civil registration can proceed without an official medical certification of the cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinical facility: The attending hospital physician verifies the death and issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death on Form 4 (for institutional deaths), which allows the hospital mortuary to release or refrigerate the body and initiates the municipal death report [1][2]. Present the deceased's U.S. passport (and Indian visa or Overseas Citizen of India - OCI card, if held) so the name and nationality match official travel documents [3].
  • Natural death at a residence or hotel under medical care: If the deceased was attended by a registered medical practitioner (RMP), that doctor examines the body and issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death on Form 4A (for non-institutional deaths) [1][2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital: Do not move the body. Call India's national emergency number 112 immediately so local police can attend, record a First Information Report (FIR) or inquest report (under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, formerly Section 174 CrPC), and transfer the deceased to an authorized government hospital for a mandatory post-mortem examination [2][3]. Once the post-mortem is completed, the police issue a formal Police No Objection Certificate (NOC) releasing the body for funeral arrangements or international export [2][3].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Indian and U.S. Funeral Providers, and Contact the U.S. Embassy or Consulate
steps.html:
Before making independent payments to a private undertaker, check whether travel or medical-evacuation insurance covers the arrangements [3]:

  • Travel or repatriation insurance: Check whether your family member held travel medical insurance, international health insurance, or credit-card travel protection, and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance coordinator immediately.
  • Appointing Indian and U.S. funeral directors: For international repatriation (or local cremation/burial), engage an experienced international human remains cargo/undertaker service in India alongside a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state [3][6]. The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in India maintain informational lists of local funeral directors and mortuary facilities across New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Kolkata, and in the United States you can locate a state-licensed receiving funeral home through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (phone +1 262-789-1880 or 800-228-6332) [3][4]. Clarvia provides public directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers. In the United States, your receiving funeral home is bound by the Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (+1 877-382-4357), which guarantees your right to an itemized written General Price List (GPL) and to purchase only the services you select [5].
  • Notifying the U.S. Embassy or Consulate General in India: Report the death immediately to American Citizens Services at the U.S. Embassy and Consulates in India covering the state of death - U.S. Embassy New Delhi (+91 11 2419-8000), or the U.S. Consulates General in Mumbai (+91 22 2672-4000), Chennai (+91 44 2857-4000), Hyderabad (+91 40 6932-8000), or Kolkata (+91 33 6827-2400) [3]. If no immediate family member is physically present in India, the legal next of kin in the United States must execute a notarized affidavit or letter of authorization instructing the U.S. Embassy/Consulate and the appointed Indian funeral director on the disposition of remains [3].

steps.title: Register the Death Within 21 Days via the Indian Civil Registration System (CRS) and Obtain the U.S. CRDA
steps.html:
The death must be registered with Indian municipal authorities and documented by the U.S. mission so the record is valid in both jurisdictions [1][2][3]:

  • Indian civil registration within 21 days (CRS portal): Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, every death in India must be registered within 21 days with the local Registrar of Births and Deaths at the competent Municipal Corporation, Municipality, or Gram Panchayat (for example, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi / New Delhi Municipal Council, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation in Mumbai, or the Greater Chennai Corporation) through the national Civil Registration System (CRS) portal [1][2]. For hospital deaths, the hospital transmits Form 4 directly to the local Registrar; for deaths outside a hospital, the informant or authorized funeral representative submits Form 2 and Form 4A (plus the police NOC if applicable) to obtain multiple certified copies of the official Indian Death Certificate [1][2].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Submit the official Indian Death Certificate, the medical cause-of-death certificate (Form 4/4A or post-mortem report), the deceased's U.S. passport, and next-of-kin identification to the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in India (monitored at the federal level by the U.S. Department of State Overseas Citizens Services at +1 888-407-4747 or +1 202-501-4444) [3][7]. The consular officer cancels the U.S. passport and issues the electronic Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060), which is accepted across all U.S. states, courts, banks, and federal agencies as official English-language proof of death [3][7]. (If a standalone Indian civil document is required for court use outside the CRDA, India and the United States are both parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, and Indian public documents can be apostilled through the Ministry of External Affairs e-Sanad system.)

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in India
steps.html:
Your appointed Indian funeral coordinator handles the police, health, and airport cargo clearances required to export casketed remains or ashes, or arranges local rites in India [3][6]:

  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) human remains from India to the United States: The Indian funeral director obtains: (1) the official Indian Death Certificate and Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4/4A), (2) the local Police No Objection Certificate (NOC) for export of mortal remains (and Foreigners Regional Registration Office - FRRO clearance where required), (3) an Embalming Certificate from an authorized hospital/mortuary and a Coffin Sealing / Non-Infectious Disease Certificate confirming the body is placed in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, (4) airport health clearance from the Airport Health Organisation (APHO) under India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (which operates the eCARe portal and airport public health units) [8], and (5) the U.S. Embassy or Consulate's Consular Mortuary Certificate (including the Affidavit of Foreign Funeral Director and Transit Permit) [3][6]. Under U.S. federal public health regulations enforced by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone 800-232-4636), embalmed remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death and the consular mortuary documents do not require a separate CDC import permit unless the person died of a quarantinable communicable disease [6]. At the U.S. arrival airport, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection and obtains the destination state's burial-transit permit [4][6].
  • Transporting cremated remains (ashes) from India to the United States: If the family chooses cremation in India at a municipal electric, gas, or traditional crematorium, the funeral director obtains the official Indian Death Certificate, the municipal Cremation Certificate, the Police NOC (if applicable), and a sealing certificate confirming the urn contains only cremated human ashes [2][3]. Under CDC rules (42 CFR 71.55), cremated remains do not require a CDC import permit when accompanied by the death and cremation certificates in a screenable non-metallic urn [6]. (Note: if the deceased held Indian nationality or OCI ties and mortal remains were instead being moved into India or supported under Indian welfare rules, Indian missions abroad issue an Indian Consular NOC, eCARe APHO advance clearance, and means-tested Indian Community Welfare Fund - ICWF assistance [8].)
  • Local burial or cremation in India: If final burial or cremation takes place in India with no shipment of remains, the local municipal crematorium or burial ground requires Form 4/4A (plus the police NOC in medico-legal cases) and the deceased's passport/ID, and the family still obtains the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060) for U.S. legal and estate use [1][2][3].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in the United States and India
steps.html:
Once you hold the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and certified Indian Death Certificates, complete the benefit, tax, and probate steps in the United States and, if the deceased worked or held assets locally, in India:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death promptly to stop monthly payments and claim survivor pensions or the $255 lump-sum death benefit by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or, if surviving beneficiaries reside in India, by contacting the regional U.S. Federal Benefits Unit at U.S. Embassy Manila at +63 2 5301-6200) [9].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs at +1 800-827-1000 regarding veteran burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), government headstones or markers, national cemetery interment, and Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [10].
    • IRS final tax return and State Probate Court: File the deceased's final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (+1 800-829-1040) by April 15 of the year following death (and Form 1041 if post-death estate income is $600 or more) [11]. Submit the CRDA and original will to the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state of domicile to obtain Letters Testamentary or Letters of Administration (or use a state Small Estate Affidavit where eligible) [7].
  • In India (if the deceased was employed or held bank accounts or property in India):
    • EPFO, ESIC, and PBBY: If the deceased contributed to an Indian provident fund, eligible nominees or legal heirs file the Composite Claim Form in Death Cases (Form 20 for EPF balance, Form 10D for EPS monthly survivor pension, and Form 5IF for EDLI insurance) with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (helpline 14470 or 1800-118-005) [12], or claim ESIC Funeral Expenses (ESIC Form 22) if covered by ESIC [13] (and Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana - PBBY / eMigrate benefits where applicable [14]).
    • Indian banks, Legal Heir / Succession Certificate, and Income Tax: Notify Indian banks and apply to the local Tehsildar/Revenue Officer for a Legal Heir Certificate or to the competent Indian Civil Court for a Succession Certificate (or Probate of Will) under the Indian Succession Act, 1925. If the deceased was an Indian income taxpayer, register as a Representative Assessee on the e-Filing portal of the Income Tax Department (helpline 1800-103-0025) to file the final Indian income tax return [15].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of India dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in India and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of India dies in the United States, medical certification and civil death registration are completed first at the U.S. state and county level, followed by mandatory consular death registration, passport cancellation, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Indian Embassy or Consulate in the United States, and advance public health clearance on India's eCARe portal if the mortal remains or ashes are transported to India [1][3][4]. Below is the five-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
Before a funeral director can register the death or prepare the body for repatriation or cremation, an authorized physician or county medico-legal authority must pronounce the death and certify the cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, nursing home, or under hospice care: The attending hospital physician or authorized medical practitioner pronounces the death, completes the medical cause-of-death certification in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes release of the body to the family's appointed funeral home [1][2]. If the death occurred at home under registered hospice care, contact the hospice nurse on duty rather than 911 so the hospice team can pronounce the death directly [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital: Call 911 immediately and do not move the body [1]. Local police and emergency medical services respond and refer sudden, accidental, unexplained, or unattended deaths to the county Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City or the County of Los Angeles Department of Medical Examiner) [1][2]. The Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, conducts an autopsy if required by state statute, issues the medical certification of death, and releases the body to your funeral director [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint U.S. and Indian Funeral Providers, and Contact the Indian Embassy or Consulate
steps.html:
Do not attempt to arrange international air cargo, embalming certificates, or airport health clearances on your own. First verify whether insurance or consular welfare support applies [1][3][4]:

  • Travel, employer, or student repatriation insurance: Check whether your family member held international travel medical insurance, university student health insurance (which normally includes mandatory medical evacuation and repatriation coverage for F-1/J-1 students), or employer-sponsored life and repatriation coverage, and notify the insurer's 24-hour assistance team before signing independent contracts.
  • Appointing a U.S. funeral home and a receiving coordinator in India: Appoint a state-licensed U.S. funeral home (searchable through the National Funeral Directors Association directory at +1 262-789-1880 or 800-228-6332) experienced in international air cargo repatriation, coordinated with a receiving funeral/undertaker service or municipal mortuary/crematorium at the destination city in India [4][5]. Clarvia provides public directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers. Under the federal Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (phone +1 877-382-4357), every U.S. funeral provider must give you an itemized written General Price List (GPL) at the start of discussions, quote prices over the phone on request, and allow you to choose only the specific goods and services you want [6].
  • Contacting the Indian Embassy or Consulate General in the United States: Contact the Indian diplomatic mission with consular jurisdiction over the U.S. state where the death occurred - the Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., or the competent Consulate General of India in New York, San Francisco, Chicago, Houston, Atlanta, or Seattle (for example, the Consulate General of India in San Francisco or the Consulate General of India in New York) [3][4]. Indian missions maintain emergency death-assistance numbers and, in cases of verified financial distress where no insurance or employer cover exists, can evaluate means-tested support for repatriation or local cremation through the Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) [3][4]. If the legal next of kin are in India and no immediate family member is present in the United States, the next of kin must provide a notarized Letter of Consent / Authorization naming a local representative or the appointed funeral home to complete the consular and shipping formalities [3][4].

steps.title: Register the Death with U.S. Vital Records and Complete Consular Registration and Apostille Formalities
steps.html:
The death must be officially recorded in the U.S. state of death and authenticated for legal recognition in India [1][2][3][4]:

  • U.S. state or county Vital Records registration: Your U.S. funeral director files the death record with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the statutory state deadline (typically 3 to 5 days after death) [1][2]. Order at least 5 to 10 certified copies of the official U.S. Death Certificate (including long-form copies explicitly stating the medical cause of death) through the funeral director or via the state Vital Records office listed on USA.gov (+1 844-872-4681) [1][2][3].
  • Indian consular registration vs. Hague Apostille and local Indian records: If the deceased was an Indian citizen, the death must be registered with the competent Indian Embassy or Consulate in the United States, which issues an Indian Consular Death Certificate and cancels the deceased's Indian passport [3][4]. Because both the United States and India are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Secretary of State of the U.S. state that issued the Death Certificate so the U.S. Death Certificate is legally recognized by Indian banks, courts, and government authorities [2][4]. (Note: India's domestic 21-day registration rule with the local Registrar of Births and Deaths at the Municipal Corporation, Municipality, or Gram Panchayat via the Civil Registration System (CRS) portal under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 applies to deaths occurring inside India, though you will present the consular and U.S. certificates to the local municipal crematorium or burial ground in India if remains are repatriated for final rites [4][8][9].)

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to India and Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
Whether you repatriate casketed mortal remains, carry cremated ashes to India, or hold the funeral in the United States, follow the specific health and consular clearance pathway [3][4][7]:

  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) mortal remains from the United States to India:

1. U.S. mortuary and health permits: The U.S. funeral director prepares and embalms the body, places it in a hermetically sealed casket, and obtains the state or county Burial-Transit Permit, a notarized Embalming Certificate, a Coffin Sealing Certificate, and a Non-Communicable / Non-Contagious Disease Certificate from the local U.S. public health department confirming the absence of quarantinable infectious diseases (in compliance with U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention rules at 42 CFR 71.55, phone 800-232-4636, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection export clearance) [3][4][7]. 2. Indian Embassy or Consulate No Objection Certificate (NOC): Submit the certified U.S. Death Certificate (showing cause of death), the Embalming Certificate, Non-Contagious Disease Certificate, Burial-Transit Permit, the deceased's original Indian passport (or U.S. passport and OCI card) for cancellation, next-of-kin consent, and flight cargo details to the competent Indian Embassy or Consulate in the United States to obtain the Consular No Objection Certificate (NOC) for transporting mortal remains (issued gratis for Indian nationals) [3][4]. 3. Advance clearance via India's eCARe portal (APHO): Under the guidelines of India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, submit an online application on the eCARe (e-Clearance for Afterlife Remains) portal (preferably at least 48 hours before arrival) to the receiving Airport Health Organisation (APHO) in India (such as Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, or Kolkata), uploading four mandatory documents: the Death Certificate showing cause of death, the Embalming Certificate, the Indian Embassy/Consulate NOC, and the cancelled passport [4].

  • Transporting cremated remains (ashes) from the United States to India: If cremation is performed in the United States, obtain the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the official Cremation Certificate, and a crematory certificate confirming the sealed, non-metallic urn contains only cremated human ashes [3][4]. Apply to the Indian Embassy or Consulate for a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to carry ashes to India, and carry the original certificates and NOC in hand luggage for airline security and Indian customs/APHO inspection on arrival [3][4].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses final cremation or burial in the United States, the U.S. funeral home completes the local state burial or cremation permit steps (including county Coroner/Medical Examiner cremation authorization), while the family registers the death with the Indian Embassy/Consulate and obtains apostilled U.S. Death Certificates for administrative use in India [1][3][4].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in India and the United States
steps.html:
With the apostilled U.S. Death Certificates and Indian consular registration documents, complete the benefit, tax, and estate steps in both countries:

  • In India (EPFO, ESIC, PBBY, Banks, Legal Heir / Succession Certificate, and Income Tax):
    • EPFO, ESIC, and PBBY benefits: If the deceased held an Indian Provident Fund account, the registered nominee or legal heirs file the unified Composite Claim Form in Death Cases (Form 20 for final EPF settlement, Form 10D for EPS monthly survivor pension, and Form 5IF for EDLI assurance payout) with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (helpline 14470 or 1800-118-005) [10]. Where applicable, claim ESIC Funeral Expenses (Form 22) [11] or accidental death/repatriation cover under the Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) / eMigrate scheme [12].
    • Indian banks, Legal Heir / Succession Certificate, and Income Tax: Notify Indian banks (including NRE/NRO accounts) and insurers with the apostilled U.S. Death Certificate / Indian Consular Death Certificate. Where an account or property has no registered nominee, apply to the local Tehsildar/Revenue Officer in India for a Legal Heir Certificate or to the competent Indian Civil Court for a Succession Certificate (or Probate of Will) under the Indian Succession Act, 1925. If the deceased had taxable income in India, register as a Representative Assessee on the e-Filing portal of the Income Tax Department (helpline 1800-103-0025) to file the final Indian income tax return [13].
  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): If the deceased worked in the United States and earned Social Security credits, report the death immediately and inquire about monthly survivor benefits (for an eligible surviving spouse, minor/disabled child, or dependent parent) and the $255 lump-sum death benefit by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or, if surviving beneficiaries live in India, by contacting the regional U.S. Federal Benefits Unit at U.S. Embassy Manila at +63 2 5301-6200) [14].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs at +1 800-827-1000 for burial and survivor benefits [15].
    • IRS final tax return and State Probate Court: File the deceased's final U.S. federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040 or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens) with the Internal Revenue Service (+1 800-829-1040) by the applicable filing deadline (and Form 1041 if U.S. estate income after death is $600 or more) [16]. For U.S. bank accounts, brokerage accounts, or real estate without designated payable-on-death beneficiaries, open probate or administration (or use a state Small Estate Affidavit if below the statutory threshold) in the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) of the U.S. state where the deceased resided [1].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Brazil: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Brazil, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Brazil.
introHtml: Please accept our heartfelt condolences on the death of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Brazil, the medical certification of death and civil registration at a Brazilian civil registry office (Cartório) must first be completed in the municipality where the death occurred, while the appointed funeral home coordinates with the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in Brazil to obtain the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) and the public health permits required for international repatriation or a local funeral [1][2][5]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and Release by the SVO or IML in Brazil
steps.html:
In Brazil, no body may be removed for funeral preparation, buried, cremated, or registered at a civil registry office without the prior issuance of the official medical declaration of death (Declaração de Óbito - DO), a three-copy medical form standardized by the Ministry of Health [2]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending or on-duty physician verifies the death and completes the Declaração de Óbito (DO) directly [2]. Present the deceased person's U.S. passport (and Brazilian National Migration Registry Card - CRNM or CPF tax number, if held) so that the spelling of the name and parentage matches the official documents exactly [1][2].
  • Natural death at a residence or hotel: If the deceased was under regular medical care at that location, the attending physician may issue the DO [2]. If the death occurred without prior medical attendance, call the Mobile Emergency Care Service (SAMU, phone 192); the body is referred to the municipal or state Death Verification Service (Serviço de Verificação de Óbito - SVO, such as the SVO in São Paulo or state capitals) to determine the natural cause of death and issue the DO [2].
  • Death in a public place or sudden, accidental, violent, or suspicious death: Call the Military Police (190) immediately and do not disturb the scene [1][2]. A police report (Boletim de Ocorrência - BO) is filed at the Civil Police station (or Tourist Police precinct), which orders a mandatory forensic autopsy at the Forensic Medical Institute (Instituto Médico Legal - IML) of the state Scientific Police, the sole body legally authorized to issue the DO and release the remains in such cases [1][2]. Note that if the family chooses cremation in Brazil, Brazilian law requires the DO to be signed by two physicians or by one forensic pathologist, and in the case of a violent death handled by the IML, express judicial authorization is required [2].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Appointing Funeral Homes in Brazil and the United States, and Consular Contact
steps.html:
Before making private financial commitments for international air transport, check for insurance coverage and establish coordination between funeral providers in both countries [1][6]:

  • Travel or repatriation insurance: Verify whether your family member held international travel insurance, credit card medical assistance, or a corporate policy covering funerary repatriation, and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance center immediately. The United States government has no public funds to pay for funeral, cremation, or international repatriation expenses [1][6].
  • Appointing funeral providers in Brazil and the United States: To carry out international repatriation (or a local funeral), appoint the municipal funeral service of the local city hall or a Brazilian funeral company licensed for international air transport (a sector represented nationally by the Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF), working in direct coordination with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination state in the United States [1][7][8]. The Embaixada e Consulados dos EUA no Brasil (U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Brazil) maintain informational lists of local funeral directors in each consular district [1], and in the United States you can locate licensed funeral homes through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (phone +1 262-789-1880 or 800-228-6332) [7]. Clarvia provides public directory references for informational guidance only and does not endorse or rank commercial providers. In the United States, the receiving funeral home is subject to the consumer protection requirements of the Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (phone +1 877-382-4357), which guarantees the right to receive a written, itemized General Price List and to purchase only the services you select [8].
  • Notifying the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in Brazil: Report the death as soon as possible to the American Citizens Services unit of the Embaixada e Consulados dos EUA no Brasil (Embassy in Brasília at +55 61 3312-7000 or after-hours emergency duty officer at +55 61 3312-7400, or the Consulates General in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Recife, and Porto Alegre) [1]. If the legal next of kin is in the United States and cannot travel to Brazil, they must execute a notarized authorization or power of attorney (with a Hague Apostille if required by the Brazilian registry office) authorizing the Brazilian funeral home or a local representative to register the death, claim the body, and arrange repatriation or cremation [1][4].

steps.title: Registration at the Civil Registry Office in Brazil, Hague Apostille, and Issuance of the CRDA (DS-2060)
steps.html:
The death must be recorded in the Brazilian civil registry prior to burial, cremation, or international shipment, and then documented by the U.S. consular authorities [1][2][6]:

  • Death Certificate (Certidão de Óbito) at the Civil Registry Office (ARPEN Brasil): Using the medical Declaração de Óbito (DO), the deceased's passport, and the declarant's identification (or the funeral home's power of attorney), the death is registered at the Civil Registry Office of Natural Persons (Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais) having jurisdiction over the place of death, integrated nationally through the Portal Oficial do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) [2]. Under the Brazilian Public Registries Law (Law No. 6,015/1973), registration must take place within the ordinary period of 24 hours after death or, where that is not possible, within 15 days (up to 3 months in locations more than 30 km from the registry office), and the first copy of the Certidão de Óbito is free of charge [2]. Request additional full-text certified copies (certidões em inteiro teor) if needed.
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) and Hague Apostille: Submit the original Brazilian Certidão de Óbito, the medical Declaração de Óbito stating the cause of death, and the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. consular office in Brazil (overseen by the U.S. Department of State, phone +1 888-407-4747 in the US/Canada or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) [1][6]. The consulate cancels the passport and electronically issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) in English, an official document accepted by Probate Courts, banks, insurers, and federal agencies across all U.S. states (as well as state Vital Records offices listed on USA.gov) [1][6]. For additional Brazilian certificates needed for direct legal use in the United States, request a Hague Apostille (Apostila da Haia) at an authorized Brazilian notary or registry office regulated by the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) (National Council of Justice, or registration through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Itamaraty where applicable) [4][5].

steps.title: Choosing Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in Brazil
steps.html:
International transport of human remains or cremated ashes between Brazil and the United States requires simultaneous compliance with Brazilian public health rules (ANVISA) and U.S. entry rules (CDC and CBP) [1][9][10]:

  • Repatriation of the body (embalmed in a zinc-lined coffin) from Brazil to the United States:

1. Public health and police requirements in Brazil (ANVISA): Under the sanitary regulations of the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency - ANVISA, phone 0800 642 9782, regulatory framework established under RDC No. 33/2011 and consolidated in RDC No. 662/2022 for ports, airports, and borders), international transport of a body requires: (a) the Certidão de Óbito and Declaração de Óbito stating the cause of death; (b) an Embalming / Preservation Record (Ata de Conservação / Embalsamamento) signed by a physician or licensed technician; (c) a Certificate of Non-Existence of Communicable Disease (Atestado de Inexistência de Doença Infectocontagiosa); (d) placement in an impermeable funerary casket with a hermetically sealed metal (zinc) liner; and (e) a Mortuary Transit Permit (Guia de Livre-Trânsito Mortuário) issued by the competent police/health authority and inspected by ANVISA at the international departure airport (such as Guarulhos in São Paulo or Galeão in Rio de Janeiro) [9]. 2. U.S. Consular Mortuary Certificate and entry (CDC 42 CFR 71.55): The funeral home presents the Brazilian documents (with English translations where required) to the U.S. Embassy or Consulate for issuance of the Consular Mortuary Certificate [1][10]. Under the federal regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death and the consular mortuary documentation may enter the United States without a separate prior CDC permit, provided the death did not result from a quarantinable communicable disease [10]. At the U.S. arrival airport, the receiving U.S. funeral home completes clearance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [7][10].

  • Transport of cremated ashes to the United States: If cremation takes place in Brazil, the ashes are placed in a sealed non-metallic urn (allowing X-ray security screening at airports), accompanied by the Certidão de Óbito, the Cremation Certificate (Certificado de Cremação), the CRDA (DS-2060), and the customs declaration, and are exempt from a CDC import permit [1][9][10].
  • Local burial or cremation in Brazil: If the family opts for final disposition in Brazil, burial normally takes place within 24 to 36 hours after death using the Burial Permit (Guia de Sepultamento) issued by the Civil Registry Office, while still requesting the CRDA (DS-2060) from the U.S. consulate to settle financial and legal matters in the United States [1][2][6].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Probate in the United States and Brazil
steps.html:
With the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and the apostilled Brazilian Certidão de Óbito in hand, complete the social security, tax, and estate procedures in both countries:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately to stop monthly payments (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to claim survivor benefits or the USD 255 lump-sum death payment from the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the Federal Benefits Unit - FBU covering Brazil if beneficiaries reside abroad) [11].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs at +1 800-827-1000 to check eligibility for burial in a national cemetery, a government headstone, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), and Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) survivor benefits [12].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and state Probate Court: The estate representative must file the deceased person's final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by April 15 of the year following death (and Form 1041 if the estate earns gross income of USD 600 or more after death) [13]. For U.S. bank accounts and assets without a direct payable-on-death beneficiary, open probate (or file a Small Estate Affidavit depending on state thresholds) in the Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) of the county of U.S. domicile [6][13].
  • In Brazil (if the deceased held assets, bank accounts, or social security coverage in Brazil):
    • INSS and FGTS/PIS: If the deceased was insured under the Brazilian social security system, eligible dependents may apply for a Survivor Pension (Pensão por Morte) from the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) via the Meu INSS portal (gov.br) or by calling 135 (within 90 days of death to receive benefits retroactive to the date of death, or within 180 days for children under age 16) [3], as well as claim any remaining FGTS or PIS/PASEP balances.
    • Estate inventory within 2 months (ITCMD), Notary Office (Cartório de Notas), and Federal Revenue Service (Receita Federal): If the deceased left real estate, vehicles, or bank accounts in Brazil, estate inventory proceedings (inventário) must be opened within the statutory deadline of 2 months (60 days) from the date of death to avoid state late-filing penalties on inheritance tax (ITCMD) [4]. Where all heirs agree and are assisted by a lawyer, an extrajudicial inventory may be executed by public deed at any Notary Office (Cartório de Notas, or online via the e-Notariado platform of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil - CNB), concluding Brazilian tax obligations with the Final Estate Tax Return (Declaração Final de Espólio) filed with the Receita Federal [4].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide guidance tailored to your local jurisdiction: in which municipality and state in Brazil did the death occur (and in which U.S. state did your family member reside), and does the family plan to repatriate the body, transport the cremated ashes, or arrange burial in Brazil?

pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Brasil e Estados Unidos: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Brasil e Estados Unidos: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos os nossos sentidos pêsames pelo falecimento do seu familiar. Quando um cidadão ou residente dos Estados Unidos falece no Brasil, a certificação médica do óbito e o registo civil em Cartório brasileiro devem ser realizados primeiro no município do falecimento, enquanto a empresa funerária contratada se articula com a Embaixada ou Consulado dos Estados Unidos no Brasil para a emissão do relatório consular de óbito no exterior (Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad - CRDA, Formulário DS-2060) e para as autorizações sanitárias de traslado internacional ou funeral local [1][2][5]. Abaixo estão os cinco passos oficiais por ordem.

steps.title: Verificação Médica do Óbito e Liberação pelo SVO ou IML no Brasil
steps.html:
No Brasil, nenhum corpo pode ser removido para preparação funerária, sepultado, cremado ou registado em cartório sem a prévia emissão da Declaração de Óbito (DO), documento médico oficial padronizado pelo Ministério da Saúde em três vias [2]:

  • Óbito em hospital ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente ou plantonista constata o falecimento e preenche diretamente a Declaração de Óbito (DO) [2]. Apresente o passaporte norte-americano da pessoa falecida (e a Carteira de Registro Nacional Migratório - CRNM ou CPF, se possuir) para que a grafia do nome e a filiação coincidam exatamente com os documentos oficiais [1][2].
  • Óbito natural em residência ou hotel: Se a pessoa falecida recebia acompanhamento médico no local, o médico assistente pode emitir a DO [2]. Caso o óbito ocorra sem assistência médica prévia, acione o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU, telefone 192); o corpo é encaminhado ao Serviço de Verificação de Óbito (SVO) municipal ou estadual (como o SVO em São Paulo ou nas capitais estaduais) para determinação da causa natural da morte e emissão da DO [2].
  • Óbito em via pública ou morte súbita, acidental, violenta ou suspeita: Ligue imediatamente para a Polícia Militar (190) e não altere o local [1][2]. A ocorrência é registada em Boletim de Ocorrência (BO) na Delegacia de Polícia Civil (ou Delegacia de Atendimento ao Turista), que requisita o exame necroscópico obrigatório no Instituto Médico Legal (IML) da Polícia Técnico-Científica estadual, único órgão legalmente competente para emitir a DO e liberar o corpo nesses casos [1][2]. Note que, caso a família opte pela cremação no Brasil, a legislação brasileira exige que a DO seja assinada por dois médicos ou por um médico legista e, tratando-se de morte violenta atendida pelo IML, exige autorização judicial expressa [2].

steps.title: Verificação de Seguro, Contratação de Funerárias no Brasil e nos EUA e Contacto Consular
steps.html:
Antes de assumir compromissos particulares de transporte aéreo internacional, verifique a existência de cobertura securitária e estabeleça a coordenação entre os prestadores funerários dos dois países [1][6]:

  • Seguro de viagem ou repatriação: Verifique se o seu familiar possuía seguro de viagem internacional, assistência médica de cartão de crédito ou apólice corporativa com cobertura de repatriação funerária, acionando imediatamente a central 24 horas da seguradora. O governo dos Estados Unidos não dispõe de fundos públicos para custear despesas de funeral, cremação ou traslado internacional [1][6].
  • Contratação de serviço funerário no Brasil e nos Estados Unidos: Para realizar o traslado internacional (ou o funeral local), contrate o serviço funerário municipal da prefeitura local ou uma empresa funerária brasileira habilitada para transporte aéreo internacional (setor representado institucionalmente pela Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF), em coordenação direta com uma funerária receptora licenciada (licensed funeral home) no estado de destino nos Estados Unidos [1][7][8]. A Embaixada e Consulados dos EUA no Brasil disponibilizam listas informativas de agentes funerários locais em cada jurisdição consular [1], e nos Estados Unidos é possível localizar funerárias licenciadas pelo diretório da National Funeral Directors Association (telefone +1 262-789-1880 ou 800-228-6332) [7]. A Clarvia fornece referências públicas apenas para orientação e não endossa nem classifica prestadores. Nos Estados Unidos, a funerária receptora está sujeita às normas de proteção ao consumidor da Funeral Rule fiscalizada pela Federal Trade Commission (telefone +1 877-382-4357), que garante o direito a receber uma tabela detalhada de preços por escrito (General Price List) e a contratar apenas os serviços selecionados [8].
  • Comunicação à Embaixada ou Consulado dos EUA no Brasil: Comunique o falecimento o quanto antes ao setor de Serviços a Cidadãos Americanos (American Citizens Services) da Embaixada e Consulados dos EUA no Brasil (Embaixada em Brasília pelo telefone +55 61 3312-7000 ou plantão de emergência +55 61 3312-7400, ou Consulados-Gerais em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Recife e Porto Alegre) [1]. Se o familiar mais próximo (legal next of kin) estiver nos Estados Unidos e não puder viajar ao Brasil, deve lavrar uma autorização/procuração notarizada (com Apostila da Haia se exigida pelo cartório brasileiro) autorizando a funerária brasileira ou um representante local a declarar o óbito, retirar o corpo e tratar do traslado ou cremação [1][4].

steps.title: Registo em Cartório de Registro Civil no Brasil, Apostila da Haia e Emissão do CRDA (DS-2060)
steps.html:
O óbito precisa de ser lavrado no registo civil brasileiro antes do sepultamento, cremação ou embarque internacional, e em seguida documentado pelas autoridades consulares norte-americanas [1][2][6]:

  • Certidão de Óbito no Cartório de Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil): Com a Declaração de Óbito (DO) médica, o passaporte da pessoa falecida e o documento do declarante (ou procurador da funerária), o óbito é registado no Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais da circunscrição do local do falecimento, integrado nacionalmente pelo Portal Oficial do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) [2]. Pela Lei de Registros Públicos (Lei n.º 6.015/1973), o registo deve ocorrer no prazo ordinário de 24 horas após o falecimento ou, na impossibilidade, em até 15 dias (até 3 meses em locais distantes mais de 30 km), sendo a primeira via da Certidão de Óbito gratuita [2]. Solicite vias adicionais em inteiro teor se necessário.
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Formulário DS-2060) e Apostila da Haia: Apresente a Certidão de Óbito brasileira original, a Declaração de Óbito médica indicando a causa da morte e o passaporte norte-americano da pessoa falecida à repartição consular dos EUA no Brasil (supervisionada pelo U.S. Department of State, telefone +1 888-407-4747 nos EUA/Canadá ou +1 202-501-4444 no exterior) [1][6]. O consulado cancela o passaporte e emite eletronicamente o Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Formulário DS-2060) em língua inglesa, documento oficial aceito por tribunais de sucessão (Probate Courts), bancos, seguradoras e agências federais em todos os estados dos EUA (bem como pelos serviços estaduais de Vital Records listados em USA.gov) [1][6]. Para certidões brasileiras adicionais que precisem de uso direto nos EUA, solicite num cartório autorizado a aposição da Apostila da Haia, regulamentada no Brasil pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) (ou registo pelo Ministério das Relações Exteriores / Itamaraty quando aplicável) [4][5].

steps.title: Escolha entre Traslado Internacional para os Estados Unidos e Sepultamento ou Cremação Local no Brasil
steps.html:
O transporte internacional de restos mortais ou cinzas entre o Brasil e os Estados Unidos exige o cumprimento simultâneo das normas sanitárias brasileiras (ANVISA) e norte-americanas (CDC e CBP) [1][9][10]:

  • Traslado de corpo (embalsamado em urna zincada) do Brasil para os Estados Unidos:

1. Requisitos sanitários e policiais no Brasil (ANVISA): Conforme as normas sanitárias da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA, telefone 0800 642 9782, histórico normativo da RDC n.º 33/2011 consolidado na RDC n.º 662/2022 para portos, aeroportos e fronteiras), o traslado internacional de corpo exige: (a) Certidão de Óbito e Declaração de Óbito com causa da morte; (b) Ata de Conservação / Embalsamamento assinada por médico ou responsável técnico; (c) Atestado de Inexistência de Doença Infectocontagiosa; (d) acondicionamento em urna funerária impermeável com revestimento metálico (zinco) hermeticamente lacrado; e (e) Guia de Livre-Trânsito Mortuário expedida pela autoridade policial/sanitária competente e fiscalizada pela ANVISA no aeroporto internacional de embarque (como Guarulhos em São Paulo ou Galeão no Rio de Janeiro) [9]. 2. Certificado Mortuário Consular dos EUA e entrada (CDC 42 CFR 71.55): A funerária apresenta os documentos brasileiros (com tradução para o inglês quando exigido) à Embaixada ou Consulado dos EUA para emissão do Consular Mortuary Certificate [1][10]. Pelas regras federais do Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, telefone 800-232-4636), restos mortais humanos embalsamados em urna hermeticamente selada, acompanhados da certidão oficial de óbito indicando a causa da morte e da documentação mortuária consular, ingressam nos Estados Unidos sem necessidade de licença prévia separada do CDC, desde que o óbito não decorra de doença transmissível quarentenável [10]. No aeroporto de chegada nos EUA, a funerária norte-americana receptora realiza o desembaraço junto à U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) e obtém a licença estadual de transporte e sepultamento (state burial-transit permit) [7][10].

  • Transporte de cinzas (restos mortais cremados) para os Estados Unidos: Se a cremação for realizada no Brasil, as cinzas são acondicionadas em urna lacrada não metálica (que permita inspeção por raio-X nos aeroportos), acompanhada da Certidão de Óbito, do Certificado de Cremação, do CRDA (DS-2060) e da declaração alfandegária, sendo isentas de licença de importação do CDC [1][9][10].
  • Sepultamento ou cremação local no Brasil: Caso a família opte pelo funeral definitivo no Brasil, o sepultamento ocorre normalmente entre 24 e 36 horas após o óbito com a Guia de Sepultamento emitida pelo Cartório de Registro Civil, mantendo-se a recomendação de solicitar o CRDA (DS-2060) junto ao consulado norte-americano para encerrar assuntos financeiros nos EUA [1][2][6].

steps.title: Comunicações Pós-Óbito, Pensões, Impostos e Inventário nos Estados Unidos e no Brasil
steps.html:
Com o CRDA (Formulário DS-2060) e a Certidão de Óbito brasileira apostilada em mãos, conclua as obrigações previdenciárias, fiscais e sucessórias nos dois países:

  • Nos Estados Unidos (SSA, VA, IRS e State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Comunique o óbito imediatamente para interromper pagamentos mensais (qualquer benefício pago no mês do óbito ou posteriormente deve ser devolvido) e para requerer pensão de sobrevivência (survivor benefits) ou o auxílio único por morte de US$ 255 junto à Social Security Administration pelo telefone 1-800-772-1213 (ou através da Federal Benefits Unit - FBU responsável pelo Brasil caso os beneficiários residam no exterior) [11].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): Se o seu familiar serviu nas Forças Armadas dos EUA, contacte o U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs pelo telefone +1 800-827-1000 para verificar o direito a sepultamento em cemitério nacional, lápide oficial, auxílio-funeral (VA Form 21P-530EZ) e pensão de sobrevivência (DIC) [12].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) e Probate Court estadual: O representante do espólio deve apresentar a declaração final de imposto de renda federal da pessoa falecida (IRS Form 1040) ao Internal Revenue Service (telefone +1 800-829-1040) até 15 de abril do ano seguinte ao óbito (e o Form 1041 se o espólio auferir renda bruta igual ou superior a US$ 600 após o óbito) [13]. Para contas bancárias e bens nos EUA sem beneficiário direto (payable-on-death), abra o processo de sucessão (probate ou Small Estate Affidavit conforme o limite estadual) no Probate Court (ou Surrogate's Court) do condado de domicílio nos EUA [6][13].
  • No Brasil (caso a pessoa falecida possuísse bens, contas bancárias ou vínculo com o INSS no Brasil):
    • INSS e FGTS/PIS: Se a pessoa falecida era segurada da previdência brasileira, os dependentes legais podem requerer a Pensão por Morte junto ao Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) pelo portal Meu INSS (gov.br) ou pelo telefone 135 (em até 90 dias do óbito para garantir o pagamento desde a data do falecimento; ou 180 dias para filhos menores de 16 anos) [3], bem como o levantamento de eventuais saldos de FGTS ou PIS/PASEP.
    • Inventário em 2 meses (ITCMD), Cartório de Notas e Receita Federal: Existindo imóveis, veículos ou contas bancárias no Brasil, o inventário deve ser aberto no prazo legal de 2 meses (60 dias) a contar do óbito para evitar multa estadual sobre o imposto de transmissão (ITCMD) [4]. Havendo acordo entre os herdeiros e assistência de advogado, o inventário extrajudicial pode ser lavrado por escritura pública em qualquer Cartório de Notas (ou online pelo e-Notariado do Colégio Notarial do Brasil (CNB)), encerrando-se as obrigações fiscais brasileiras com a Declaração Final de Espólio perante a Receita Federal [4].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos orientar com detalhes específicos da jurisdição local: em qual município e estado do Brasil ocorreu o falecimento (e em qual estado norte-americano residia o seu familiar), e a família pretende realizar o traslado do corpo, o transporte das cinzas ou o sepultamento no Brasil?
