title: What to Do When a Citizen of Brazil Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Brazil Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Brazil dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Brazil and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Brazil dies in the United States, medical certification and civil death registration are completed first at the U.S. state and county level, followed by a Hague Apostille from the U.S. state's Secretary of State, consular death registration through the competent Consulate-General of Brazil in the United States, and sanitary clearance from Brazil's Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA) if the body or cremated ashes are repatriated to Brazil [1][3][4][9]. Below is the five-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
Before a funeral director can register the death or prepare the deceased for repatriation or cremation, an authorized physician or county medico-legal authority must pronounce the death and certify the cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, nursing home, or under hospice care: The attending physician or authorized medical staff pronounces the death, completes the medical cause-of-death certification in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes release of the body to the family's appointed funeral home [1][2]. If the death occurs at home under registered hospice care, contact the hospice nurse on duty rather than 911 so the hospice team can pronounce the death directly [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital: Call 911 immediately and do not disturb the scene [1]. Local police and emergency medical services respond and refer sudden, accidental, unexplained, or unattended deaths to the county Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Miami-Dade County Medical Examiner Department, or the County of Los Angeles Department of Medical Examiner) [1][2]. The Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, performs an autopsy if required by state statute, issues the official medical certification of death, and releases the body to your funeral director [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint U.S. and Brazilian Funeral Providers, and Contact the Brazilian Consulate-General
steps.html:
Before committing to private international shipping contracts, check whether insurance coverage applies and establish coordination between funeral providers in both countries [3][4][5]:

  • Travel or repatriation insurance: Check whether your family member held international travel medical insurance, credit-card travel protection, or a life/funeral policy with international repatriation coverage, and notify the insurer's 24-hour assistance center immediately. Note that under Brazilian law, the Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Itamaraty) and Brazilian Consulates have no legal or budgetary authority to pay for funeral, cremation, embalming, or repatriation expenses [3][5].
  • Appointing a U.S. funeral home and a receiving provider in Brazil: Appoint a state-licensed U.S. funeral home (searchable through the National Funeral Directors Association directory at +1 262-789-1880 or 800-228-6332) experienced in international air cargo repatriation, coordinated with a municipal funeral service (serviço funerário municipal) or licensed funeral company in the destination Brazilian municipality (represented sectorally in Brazil by the Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF) to receive the coffin at the arrival airport [3][5][6]. Clarvia provides public directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers. Under the federal Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (phone +1 877-382-4357), every U.S. funeral provider must give you a written itemized General Price List (GPL) at the start of discussions, quote prices by telephone on request, and allow you to purchase only the specific goods and services you select [7].
  • Contacting the Consulate-General of Brazil in the United States: Contact the Brazilian diplomatic or consular post with jurisdiction over the U.S. state where the death occurred - such as the Consulates-General of Brazil in Miami (Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Miami), New York (Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Nova York), Atlanta (Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Atlanta), Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, Orlando, or San Francisco, or the Consular Section of the Embassy of Brazil in Washington, D.C. [3][4][5]. If immediate family members are in Brazil and cannot travel to the United States, they may execute a notarized Power of Attorney (procuração) or written authorization naming a representative in the United States or the appointed funeral director to sign the consular death declaration and arrange shipment or cremation [4][5].

steps.title: Register the Death with U.S. Vital Records, Obtain a Hague Apostille, and Complete Brazilian Consular Registration
steps.html:
The death must be officially recorded in the U.S. state of death and registered for legal validity in Brazil [1][2][4][5]:

  • U.S. state or county Vital Records registration: Your U.S. funeral director files the official death record with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the statutory state deadline (typically 3 to 5 days after death) [1][2]. Order 5 to 10 certified copies of the official U.S. Death Certificate (explicitly stating the medical cause of death) through the funeral director or via the state Vital Records office listed on USA.gov (+1 844-872-4681) [1][2][4].
  • Hague Apostille and Brazilian Consular Registration of Death (Certidão Consular de Óbito):

1. U.S. Secretary of State Apostille: Obtain a Hague Apostille on the certified U.S. Death Certificate (and mortuary/cremation certificates) from the Secretary of State of the U.S. state where the death occurred (for example, the Florida Department of State or the New York Department of State) [3][5]. 2. Brazilian Consular Registration via e-consular: Submit an application through the electronic e-consular portal of the competent Brazilian Consulate-General (for example, the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Nova York or the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Miami) presenting the Death Registration Form, the original U.S. Death Certificate stating the cause of death, the Cremation Certificate (if applicable), the deceased's Brazilian passport or birth/marriage certificate (plus CPF, voter registration, or INSS number if available), and the declarant's photo ID [4][5]. The declarant (family member or authorized funeral representative) attends the scheduled consular appointment to sign the registry term and receive the Certidão Consular de Óbito [4][5]. 3. Transcription (Traslado) at the 1st Civil Registry Office in Brazil: To produce full legal, banking, pension, and inheritance effects inside Brazil, the Certidão Consular de Óbito (or the apostilled U.S. Death Certificate with a sworn translation into Portuguese by a tradutor público juramentado) must be transcribed (trasladada) at the Cartório do 1.º Ofício de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais of the deceased's last domicile in Brazil (or the 1st Office of the Distrito Federal), integrated nationally through the Portal Oficial do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) and regulated by the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) [4][10][12]. (Note: the ordinary 24-hour to 15-day direct registration deadline applies when a death occurs domestically inside Brazil [10].)

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to Brazil and Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
Whether you ship casketed remains to Brazil, carry cremated ashes, or hold a local service in the United States, follow the required U.S. and Brazilian health clearances [3][5][8][9]:

  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) human remains from the United States to Brazil:

1. U.S. mortuary, health, and apostille documents: The U.S. funeral home embalms the body, places it in a hermetically sealed metal/zinc-lined casket inside a shipping container (urna zincada lacrada), and obtains: (a) the certified U.S. Death Certificate showing cause of death; (b) the state or county Burial-Transit Permit (livre-trânsito mortuário); (c) a notarized Embalming Certificate (ata de embalsamamento/conservação); and (d) a Non-Contagious Disease Certificate from the local U.S. health department confirming the absence of communicable diseases [3][5][8]. Have the Death Certificate, Embalming Certificate, and Non-Contagious Disease Certificate apostilled by the U.S. state's Secretary of State, and complete the Brazilian consular registration (in conjunction with U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention export/import rules under 42 CFR 71.55 at 800-232-4636 and U.S. Customs and Border Protection air cargo clearance) [5][8]. 2. Brazilian airport sanitary clearance (ANVISA): Upon arrival at the international airport in Brazil (such as São Paulo/Guarulhos, Rio de Janeiro/Galeão, Campinas/Viracopos, or Belo Horizonte/Confins), sanitary inspection and release are conducted by the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA, phone in Brazil 0800 642 9782, governed by the framework of RDC n.º 33/2011 and updated RDC n.º 662/2022) upon presentation of the airway bill, the Brazilian Consular Death Certificate (or apostilled U.S. Death Certificate), the embalming/conservation certificate, the non-contagious disease certificate, and the transit permit to the receiving Brazilian funeral company [5][9].

  • Transporting cremated remains (ashes) from the United States to Brazil: If the family chooses cremation in the United States, obtain the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the official Cremation Certificate (notarized and apostilled by the U.S. state Secretary of State), and the Brazilian Certidão Consular de Óbito [4][5]. Place the ashes in a sealed, waterproof, X-ray-screenable urn accompanied by the certificates for airline security and ANVISA/customs inspection upon arrival in Brazil [5][8][9].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If final burial or cremation takes place in the United States, the U.S. funeral home completes the state burial or cremation permit steps, while the family still registers the death at the Brazilian Consulate-General and transcribes the Certidão Consular de Óbito in Brazil to update the deceased's CPF, civil status, and estate records [1][4][10].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Brazil and the United States
steps.html:
Once the death is registered in the United States and transcribed at the Brazilian Cartório de 1.º Ofício, complete the pension, tax, and probate steps in both jurisdictions:

  • In Brazil (INSS Pensão por Morte, FGTS/PIS, 2-Month Inventory / ITCMD, and Receita Federal):
    • INSS survivor pension (Pensão por Morte) and FGTS/PIS: If the deceased contributed to or received benefits from Brazil's social security system, eligible dependents (spouse, domestic partner, children under 21 or with a disability, or economically dependent parents/siblings) can apply for Pensão por Morte with the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) via the Meu INSS portal (gov.br) or by calling 135 in Brazil (filing within 90 days of death secures payments retroactive to the date of death, or 180 days for minor children under 16) [11]. Under the U.S.-Brazil Social Security Agreement, coverage periods in both countries can be totalized to qualify for survivor benefits [11][13]. Eligible heirs may also claim remaining FGTS or PIS/PASEP balances at Caixa Econômica Federal.
    • Estate inventory (inventário) within 2 months (ITCMD) and Cartório de Notas: Under Article 611 of the Brazilian Code of Civil Procedure, if the deceased left real estate, vehicles, or bank accounts in Brazil, the estate inventory (inventário) must be opened within 2 months (60 days) of the date of death to avoid state tax penalties on the inheritance tax (ITCMD) [10][12]. If all heirs agree and are assisted by a lawyer, an extrajudicial inventory can be completed quickly by public deed at any Notary Office (Cartório de Notas) in Brazil or online via the e-Notariado platform of the Colégio Notarial do Brasil (CNB); otherwise, file a judicial inventory in the Brazilian state court, followed by the final estate tax declaration (Declaração Final de Espólio) with the Receita Federal [12].
  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately to stop monthly payments and apply for U.S. Social Security survivor benefits or the $255 one-time lump-sum death benefit by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the competent U.S. Embassy Federal Benefits Unit if surviving claimants reside in Brazil) [13].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs at +1 800-827-1000 for veteran burial and survivor benefits [14].
    • IRS final tax return and State Probate Court: File the deceased's final U.S. federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040 or Form 1040-NR) with the Internal Revenue Service (+1 800-829-1040) by April 15 of the year following death (and Form 1041 if post-death U.S. estate income is $600 or more) [15]. For U.S. bank accounts or property without payable-on-death beneficiaries, complete probate or administration (or use a state Small Estate Affidavit if below the statutory threshold) in the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) of the U.S. state of domicile [1].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Colombia: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Colombia, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Colombia.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties dies in Colombia, the medical, civil registry, consular, and funeral formalities must be coordinated between Colombian and U.S. authorities. Below are the five main official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in Colombia
steps.html:
• Death from natural causes in a clinic or hospital: If the death occurs under medical care at a healthcare facility (for example in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali), the attending physician issues the Antecedent Medical Certificate of Death for the Civil Registry (Certificado de Defunción Antecedente para el Registro Civil) through the RUAF-ND system (Single Registry of Affiliates - Births and Deaths of the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and DANE) [2]. This medical certificate is the essential prerequisite for registering the death and obtaining public health burial or transit permits [2][6].
  • Sudden, accidental, or out-of-hospital death: If the deceased dies at a residence, in a hotel, or in a public place, or from violent or undetermined causes, call the single national emergency number 123 immediately so that the National Police (Policía Nacional) and the Technical Investigation Corps (Cuerpo Técnico de Investigación - CTI) of the Attorney General's Office (Fiscalía General de la Nación) respond to the scene [5]. The body is transferred to the Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses (National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences) for a mandatory medico-legal autopsy [5]. Once full identity is verified and the prosecutor's office (Fiscalía) issues the release order, the Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses issues the antecedent death certificate and releases the body to the funeral home authorized by the family [5].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Binational Funeral Coordination, and Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance policies: Before making direct financial commitments, check whether your family member had travel insurance, a repatriation policy, or credit card travel coverage. Where active coverage exists, the insurer's assistance center typically appoints and pays the international funeral providers directly.
  • Appointing licensed funeral directors in Colombia and the United States: The family must appoint a licensed funeral home (funeraria habilitada) in Colombia to claim the body, prepare the sanitary documentation, and apply for the burial, cremation, or transit permit from the municipal or district health authority, such as the Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá (Bogotá District Secretariat of Health) [6]. If the family chooses to repatriate the body to the United States, the Colombian funeral home coordinates directly with a licensed receiving funeral home in the U.S. destination state; you can consult the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association to locate accredited local providers [8]. In the United States, the federal FTC Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission guarantees the family's right to receive an itemized General Price List over the phone or in person and to purchase only the specific goods and services selected [7]. Clarvia provides references to official directories for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers.
  • U.S. consular notification: Report the death as soon as possible to the American Citizens Services unit of the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia (U.S. Embassy in Colombia) in Bogotá (phone +57 (601) 275-2000) or the Consular Agency in Barranquilla [1]. The consulate verifies the deceased's U.S. citizenship, guides the family on local funeral homes, issues the consular mortuary documentation for repatriation, and processes the consular report of death [1][3]. The United States government does not pay for funeral, cremation, or international transport expenses [1].

steps.title: Registration in the Colombian Civil Registry, Apostille, and U.S. Consular Report
steps.html:
• Civil Death Registration (Registro Civil de Defunción) in Colombia: With the antecedent medical or forensic certificate and the deceased's identity document (U.S. passport or Colombian foreign ID card - cédula de extranjería), the death must be registered within the statutory deadline of two (2) business days at an office of the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil (National Civil Registry) or a notary office at the place of death (inquiries or record updates via defuncionesdnrc@registraduria.gov.co) [2]. If that deadline expires, an order from a police inspector or competent authority is required for late registration (inscripción extemporánea). Request several certified copies of the Registro Civil de Defunción [2].
  • Electronic Hague Apostille: For the Colombian Registro Civil de Defunción to have direct legal validity before courts or institutions in the United States, apply for an electronic Hague Apostille online through the official portal of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Cancillería), available 24 hours a day in PDF format [4].
  • Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRODA): Upon presentation of the Colombian Registro Civil de Defunción and the deceased's U.S. passport to the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia, the consulate issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA, Form DS-2060) in English [1][3]. The CRODA functions as an official death certificate in the United States for banking, insurance, pension, and probate proceedings; additional copies can later be requested from the U.S. Department of State (Passport Vital Records Section) [3].

steps.title: International Repatriation of Remains or Ashes vs. Local Disposition in Colombia
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body (coffin) to the United States: If the family decides to transport the uncremated body to the United States, the funeral home in Colombia applies to the territorial health authority (for example, the Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá via its digital portal Agilínea) for the international sanitary transit license, together with the medical certificate of embalming, the certificate of sealing in a hermetic coffin, and the consular mortuary certificate issued by the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia [1][6]. For entry into the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention require under 42 CFR 71.55 that the body travel in a leak-proof hermetic container, accompanied by the official death certificate or certification that there is no risk of a quarantinable communicable disease, and consigned directly to a licensed funeral home, cemetery, or crematory in the United States [9]. Following documentary inspection at the U.S. port of entry, the receiving funeral home obtains the state burial-transit permit.
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes to the United States: If cremation takes place in Colombia (subject to a cremation license from the Secretariat of Health and authorization by the legal next of kin), international transport of ashes is faster and less expensive [6]. Cremated human remains are not subject to quarantine restrictions of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, but they must travel in an X-ray-scannable urn (wood, plastic, or non-metallic material) accompanied by the Registro Civil de Defunción, the cremation certificate (certificado de cremación) and its English translation, or the consular CRODA [1][9].
  • Local burial or cremation in Colombia: If the family chooses final burial or cremation in Colombia, the local funeral home coordinates the sanitary burial or cremation license directly with the Secretariat of Health of the corresponding municipality or district [6].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in the United States and Colombia
steps.html:
• Benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security (SSA): Report the death to the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 (from within the United States) or through the corresponding Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy to stop monthly payments (any payment received for the month of death must be returned) and to check eligibility for survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [10].
    • Veterans (VA): If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial benefits in national cemeteries, memorial headstones, or burial allowances [12].
    • Federal taxes (IRS) and state probate: The personal representative or responsible family member must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death, reporting income received up to the date of death [11]. For bank accounts and real property located in the United States without a designated beneficiary, estate administration (probate) is conducted before the competent Probate Court in the county and state of last domicile.
  • Pensions, funeral grant, and estate settlement in Colombia:
    • Colpensiones or private pension funds: If the deceased contributed to or received a pension in Colombia, the person who proves payment of the funeral expenses with a paid invoice may claim the statutory funeral grant (auxilio funerario) from Colpensiones (under the Public Pay-As-You-Go Scheme - Régimen de Prima Media) or the relevant private pension fund, and statutory beneficiaries may apply for a survivor pension (pensión de sobrevivientes) [13].
    • Estate settlement (sucesión) in Colombia: If your family member left bank accounts, vehicles, or real estate in Colombia, the estate can be settled by mutual agreement through a public deed (escritura pública) before a Colombian notary (with representation by an attorney where the estate exceeds the statutory minimum threshold) or through judicial succession proceedings before a family court (juzgado de familia) if the heirs do not reach an agreement.

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance on the next steps, in which Colombian municipality or city did the death occur (and did it take place inside or outside a medical facility), and does the family prefer to repatriate the body or ashes to a specific U.S. state or arrange burial or cremation in Colombia?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre Colombia y Estados Unidos: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre Colombia y Estados Unidos: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía o vínculos de residencia en los Estados Unidos fallece en Colombia, los trámites médicos, registrales, consulares y funerarios deben coordinarse entre las autoridades colombianas y estadounidenses. A continuación se detallan los cinco pasos oficiales principales en orden práctico.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción y autorización forense en Colombia
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento por causas naturales en clínica u hospital: Si el deceso ocurre bajo atención médica en una institución de salud (por ejemplo, en Bogotá, Medellín o Cali), el profesional médico tratante expide el Certificado de Defunción Antecedente para el Registro Civil a través del sistema RUAF-ND (Registro Único de Afiliados - Nacimientos y Defunciones del Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social y el DANE) [2]. Este documento médico es el requisito indispensable para inscribir la defunción y gestionar las licencias sanitarias [2][6].
  • Fallecimiento súbito, accidental o fuera de un centro médico: Si la persona fallecida muere en un domicilio, hotel o vía pública, o por causas violentas o por establecer, se debe llamar de inmediato a la línea única de emergencias 123 para que acudan la Policía Nacional y el Cuerpo Técnico de Investigación (CTI) de la Fiscalía General de la Nación [5]. El cuerpo es trasladado al Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses para la práctica de la necropsia médico-legal obligatoria [5]. Una vez verificada la identidad plena y emitida la orden de entrega por la Fiscalía, el Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses expide el certificado de defunción antecedente y entrega el cuerpo a la funeraria autorizada por la familia [5].

steps.title: Seguro de viaje, coordinación funeraria binacional y notificación consular
steps.html:
• Verificación de pólizas de seguro o asistencia: Antes de asumir compromisos económicos directos, revise si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, póliza de repatriación o cobertura mediante tarjeta de crédito. Si existe cobertura activa, la central de asistencia de la aseguradora suele designar y cubrir directamente los servicios funerarios internacionales.
  • Designación de funerarias autorizadas en Colombia y Estados Unidos: La familia debe contratar una funeraria habilitada en Colombia para retirar el cuerpo, preparar la documentación sanitaria y tramitar la licencia de inhumación, cremación o traslado ante la autoridad sanitaria municipal o distrital, como la Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá [6]. Si se opta por repatriar el cuerpo a los Estados Unidos, la funeraria colombiana debe coordinarse con una funeraria receptora con licencia en el estado de destino en los Estados Unidos; puede consultar el directorio de la National Funeral Directors Association para ubicar proveedores locales [8]. En los Estados Unidos, la regla federal de funerales (FTC Funeral Rule) de la Federal Trade Commission garantiza el derecho de la familia a recibir una lista general de precios desglosada (General Price List) por teléfono o en persona y a contratar únicamente los bienes y servicios que elija [7]. Clarvia ofrece referencias de directorios oficiales únicamente a título informativo y no respalda, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores comerciales.
  • Notificación consular a los Estados Unidos: Notifique el deceso lo antes posible a la unidad de Servicios a Ciudadanos Estadounidenses (American Citizens Services) de la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia en Bogotá (teléfono +57 (601) 275-2000) o a la Agencia Consular en Barranquilla [1]. El consulado verifica la ciudadanía estadounidense de la persona fallecida, orienta a la familia sobre funerarias locales, expide la documentación mortuoria consular para la repatriación y tramita el reporte consular de defunción [1][3]. El gobierno de los Estados Unidos no sufraga gastos funerarios, de cremación ni de traslado internacional [1].

steps.title: Inscripción en el registro civil colombiano, apostilla y reporte consular estadounidense
steps.html:
• Registro Civil de Defunción en Colombia: Con el certificado médico o forense antecedente y el documento de identidad de la persona fallecida (pasaporte estadounidense o cédula de extranjería), la defunción debe inscribirse dentro del plazo legal de dos (2) días hábiles ante una oficina de la Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil o una notaría del lugar del fallecimiento (solicitudes de actualización o consultas a defuncionesdnrc@registraduria.gov.co) [2]. Si transcurre ese plazo, se requiere orden de inspector de policía o autoridad competente para la inscripción extemporánea. Solicite varias copias auténticas del Registro Civil de Defunción [2].
  • Apostilla electrónica de La Haya: Para que el Registro Civil de Defunción colombiano tenga validez jurídica directa ante tribunales o entidades en los Estados Unidos, debe tramitarse su apostilla en línea a través del portal oficial del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Colombia (Cancillería), disponible las 24 horas en formato PDF [4].
  • Reporte Consular de Defunción en el Exterior (CRODA): Presentando el Registro Civil de Defunción colombiano y el pasaporte estadounidense de la persona fallecida ante la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia, el consulado emite el Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA, formulario DS-2060) en inglés [1][3]. El CRODA equivale funcionalmente a un acta de defunción en los Estados Unidos para trámites bancarios, de seguros, pensiones y sucesiones; copias adicionales posteriores pueden solicitarse al U.S. Department of State (Passport Vital Records Section) [3].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional de restos o cenizas frente a disposición local en Colombia
steps.html:
• Repatriación de cuerpo (féretro) a los Estados Unidos: Si la familia decide trasladar el cuerpo sin cremar hacia los Estados Unidos, la funeraria en Colombia gestiona ante la autoridad de salud territorial (por ejemplo, la Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá a través de su ventanilla digital Agilínea) la licencia sanitaria de traslado internacional, junto con el certificado médico de embalsamamiento, el acta de sellado en féretro hermético y el certificado mortuorio consular emitido por la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en Colombia [1][6]. Para el ingreso a los Estados Unidos, los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention exigen bajo la norma 42 CFR 71.55 que el cuerpo viaje en un contenedor hermético a prueba de fugas, acompañado del acta de defunción oficial o certificación de que no existe riesgo de enfermedad infecciosa cuarentenable, y consignado directamente a una funeraria, cementerio o crematorio autorizado en los Estados Unidos [9]. Tras la inspección documental en el aeropuerto de entrada, la funeraria receptora tramita el permiso estatal de tránsito e inhumación (burial-transit permit).
  • Repatriación de cenizas a los Estados Unidos: Si se realiza la cremación en Colombia (previa licencia de cremación de la Secretaría de Salud y autorización de los familiares legitimados), el traslado internacional de cenizas es más ágil y menos costoso [6]. Las cenizas humanas cremadas no están sujetas a restricciones cuarentenarias de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, pero deben viajar en una urna apta para escaneo por rayos X (madera, plástico o material no metálico) acompañada del Registro Civil de Defunción, el certificado de cremación y su traducción o el CRODA consular [1][9].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en Colombia: Si la familia opta por la sepultura o cremación definitiva en territorio colombiano, la funeraria local coordina directamente la licencia sanitaria de inhumación o cremación ante la Secretaría de Salud del municipio o distrito correspondiente [6].

steps.title: Pensiones de sobrevivientes, impuestos y sucesión en Estados Unidos y Colombia
steps.html:
• Prestaciones y obligaciones fiscales en los Estados Unidos:
    • Seguridad Social (SSA): Notifique el fallecimiento a la Social Security Administration llamando al 1-800-772-1213 (desde los Estados Unidos) o a través de la Unidad de Beneficios Federales (Federal Benefits Unit) correspondiente en la embajada para detener pagos mensuales improcedentes (los pagos del mes del fallecimiento deben devolverse) y consultar el derecho a pensiones de sobrevivientes o al pago único por defunción [10].
    • Veteranos (VA): Si la persona fallecida prestó servicio militar en las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses, consulte al Department of Veterans Affairs sobre beneficios de entierro en cementerios nacionales, lápidas conmemorativas o subsidios funerarios [12].
    • Impuestos federales (IRS) y sucesión estatal (Probate): El representante personal o familiar encargado debe presentar la declaración final del impuesto sobre la renta federal (Form 1040) ante el Internal Revenue Service hasta el 15 de abril del año siguiente al fallecimiento, reportando los ingresos percibidos hasta la fecha del deceso [11]. Para cuentas bancarias e inmuebles ubicados en los Estados Unidos sin beneficiario directo, se tramita el proceso sucesorio (probate) ante el tribunal competente (Probate Court) del condado y estado del último domicilio.
  • Pensiones, auxilio funerario y sucesión en Colombia:
    • Colpensiones o fondos privados: Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o recibía pensión en Colombia, quien demuestre haber sufragado los gastos fúnebres mediante factura cancelada puede solicitar el auxilio funerario ante Colpensiones (Régimen de Prima Media) o el fondo privado correspondiente, y los beneficiarios de ley pueden reclamar la pensión de sobrevivientes [13].
    • Sucesión en Colombia: Si su familiar dejó cuentas bancarias, vehículos o bienes inmuebles en Colombia, la liquidación de la herencia puede tramitarse de mutuo acuerdo mediante escritura pública ante notaría colombiana (con representación de abogado cuando supere la cuantía mínima legal) o mediante proceso de sucesión ante un juzgado de familia si no existe acuerdo entre los herederos.

es.closingQuestion: Para orientarle con mayor precisión sobre los pasos siguientes: 1. ¿En qué municipio o ciudad de Colombia ocurrió el fallecimiento y el deceso tuvo lugar en un centro médico o fuera de él? 2. ¿Prefiere la familia realizar la repatriación del cuerpo o de las cenizas hacia un estado específico de los Estados Unidos, o disponer la sepultura o cremación en Colombia?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Colombia Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Colombia Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Colombia dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Colombia and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Colombia dies in the United States, medical certification, civil registration, consular reporting, and international transport or local disposition must be coordinated between state authorities in the United States and national institutions in Colombia. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, hospice, or care facility: When the death occurs under medical care, the attending physician, nurse practitioner, or hospital medical staff certifies the time and cause of death in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS) and authorizes the release of your family member's body to a licensed funeral home [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a medical facility: If the death occurs at a private residence, workplace, hotel, or public space, call 911 immediately. Local law enforcement and emergency medical services will respond and refer the case to the county or municipal Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Miami-Dade County Medical Examiner Department in Florida, or the Harris County Institute of Forensic Sciences in Texas). The Medical Examiner or Coroner investigates the cause and manner of death, conducts an autopsy if legally required, signs the medical portion of the death certificate, and issues official release clearance before a funeral home can take custody of the deceased.

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel, assistance, or exequial insurance first: Before signing private funeral contracts, verify whether the deceased held travel insurance, international medical-assistance coverage, or a Colombian pre-need funeral plan (plan exequial) with international repatriation coverage. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance desk immediately so its appointed coordinator can manage and fund the process.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral home in the United States and Colombia: In the United States, a licensed funeral director normally handles custody of the body, civil death registration, state burial-transit permits, and airport cargo booking. You can locate licensed providers through the National Funeral Directors Association directory [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized General Price List (GPL) in person or quotes by telephone, cannot require you to buy unwanted bundled packages, and must obtain explicit permission before charging for embalming [2]. If the remains will be repatriated to Colombia, the U.S. funeral home coordinates with an authorized receiving funeral home (funeraria habilitada) in Colombia, which obtains the local sanitary burial, cremation, or transfer license (licencia sanitaria de inhumación, cremación o traslado) from the municipal or district health authority, such as the Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá [8]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the Colombian Consulate in the United States: Report the death to the nearest Consulate of Colombia in the United States (such as the Consulates General in Miami, New York, Houston, Los Angeles, Chicago, Newark, or Washington, D.C.) or contact the citizen assistance center of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Cancillería) at contactenos@cancilleria.gov.co [5][6]. The Colombian consulate guides the family on local procedures, registers the death in the Colombian civil registry, and coordinates consular mortuary documentation [5].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United States, Apostille, and Colombian Registration
steps.html:
• U.S. Death Certificate (Vital Records): The appointed U.S. funeral director completes the personal demographic details with the family and submits the death record to the state or county Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records in the state where the death occurred. You can verify the competent state agency through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) directory [1]. Request multiple certified copies of the long-form U.S. Death Certificate.
  • Colombian Consular Death Registration vs. Apostille: To register the death in Colombia, you have two official routes:
    • Direct consular registration (fastest route): Present the original certified U.S. Death Certificate and the deceased's Colombian identity document (cédula de ciudadanía or passport) at the nearest Consulate of Colombia in the United States [5]. The consulate issues the official Colombian Registro Civil de Defunción directly in Spanish at no consular fee and transmits the record to the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil in Colombia (defuncionesdnrc@registraduria.gov.co) so the deceased's cédula de ciudadanía is cancelled in the national identification archive (ANI) [5][7].
    • Registration in Colombia via Hague Apostille: If the death is registered directly in Colombia before a notary or office of the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil, the U.S. Death Certificate must first receive a Hague Apostille from the Secretary of State of the U.S. state that issued the certificate, followed by an official Spanish translation [7]. Conversely, if Colombian civil registry documents are needed for legal proceedings in the United States, they can be apostilled online 24/7 through the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores portal [9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Colombia vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating the body (casket) from the United States to Colombia: For full-body transport, the U.S. funeral director prepares the remains (embalming and sealing inside a leak-proof, hermetically sealed metal liner or casket in accordance with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention standards under 42 CFR 71.55 and airline cargo rules), obtains the U.S. state burial-transit permit and non-contagious disease certificate, and coordinates consular mortuary documentation with the Consulate of Colombia [4][5]. Upon arrival at the international airport in Colombia (such as El Dorado in Bogotá, José María Córdova in Rionegro/Medellín, or Alfonso Bonilla Aragón in Cali), the receiving Colombian funeral home clears airport health control and obtains the sanitary burial or cremation license from the local health authority, such as the Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá [8]. Please note that the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores does not have a public budget to pay for commercial casket repatriation [6].
  • Repatriating cremated ashes to Colombia: If cremation takes place in the United States (requiring county Medical Examiner/Coroner clearance and next-of-kin authorization), transporting cremated human ashes is significantly simpler. Ashes must travel in a scan-friendly, non-metallic urn accompanied by the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the cremation certificate, and the Colombian consular death registration [4][5]. Under Colombian Law 2171 of 2021 and consular assistance guidelines, when a family lacks financial resources, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores may evaluate requests to repatriate cremated ashes to Colombia via the diplomatic pouch (valija diplomática) [5][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United States, the U.S. funeral director obtains the county/state disposition permit directly, while the family still registers the death with the Colombian consulate so Colombian civil and estate records are updated [5][7].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Colombia and the United States
steps.html:
• Pensions, funeral grants, and succession in Colombia:
    • Colpensiones or Private Pension Funds (AFP): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension in Colombia, the person who paid the funeral expenses (whether in the United States or Colombia) can claim the statutory funeral grant (auxilio funerario) by presenting the Colombian Registro Civil de Defunción and paid original funeral invoices to Colpensiones (public regime) or the relevant private fund (such as Porvenir, Protección, Colfondos, or Skandia) [10]. Eligible surviving dependents can file for a survivor pension (pensión de sobrevivientes) [10].
    • Colombian Banks and Succession (Sucesión): Notify Colombian banks to freeze sole accounts and verify life/debtor insurance (seguro de vida deudores). To transfer Colombian real estate, vehicles, or bank balances, heirs must complete an inheritance succession (trámite de sucesión), either by mutual agreement before a Colombian notary public (notaría, represented by a licensed attorney when the estate exceeds the statutory threshold) or through a Colombian family court (juzgado de familia) if there is a dispute.
  • Benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA) and Veterans Affairs (VA): If the deceased had a U.S. Social Security number or worked in the United States, report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or via a U.S. Federal Benefits Unit if survivors live in Colombia) to stop ongoing monthly payments and inquire about survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [11]. If the deceased served in the U.S. armed forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial allowances or memorial benefits [13].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate: The personal representative or survivor in charge of the deceased's property must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040 or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens with U.S. source income) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [12]. Assets held solely in the deceased's name in the United States without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or owned property.

closingQuestion: To help tailor the exact local steps for your family: 1. In which U.S. state and county did the death occur, and has a U.S. funeral home or Medical Examiner already taken custody of your family member? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to a specific city in Colombia, or arrange burial or cremation in the United States?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Dominican Republic: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Dominican Republic: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Dominican Republic: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Dominican Republic, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Dominican Republic.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties dies in the Dominican Republic, medical or forensic certification, civil registration, consular reporting, and international repatriation or local disposition require coordinating formalities between Dominican and U.S. authorities. Below are the five main official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Examination in the Dominican Republic
steps.html:
• Death from natural causes in a clinic or hospital: If the death occurs under medical care at a healthcare facility (for example in Santo Domingo, Santiago de los Caballeros, Punta Cana, or Puerto Plata), the attending physician issues the Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción / declaración médica de defunción) certifying the cause of death [1][3].
  • Death in a hotel, residence, or public place, or international repatriation of the body: If the deceased dies outside a hospital or in a tourist area, immediately call the National Emergency and Security System 911, the National Police (Policía Nacional), or the Central Directorate of Tourism Police (POLITUR) [1]. Under Dominican law, the body may not be moved or removed without authorization from the Medical Examiner (Médico Legista) and the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público) [1]. Furthermore, Dominican law requires a medico-legal autopsy performed by a forensic pathologist of the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses (National Institute of Forensic Sciences - INACIF) both for unnatural or sudden deaths and in every case where a body is to be repatriated outside the Dominican Republic [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing Licensed Funeral Directors, and Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance: Before taking on independent financial commitments, verify whether your family member had travel insurance, international medical assistance, or credit card coverage. If an active policy exists, contact the insurer's assistance center immediately so it can coordinate and cover the funeral and repatriation expenses.
  • Appointing a funeral home in the Dominican Republic and in the United States: The family must appoint a licensed funeral home (funeraria autorizada) in the Dominican Republic experienced in international repatriations and embalming to claim the body from the hospital or the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, obtain local certificates and sanitary permits, and coordinate air transport [1][2]. If the body will be repatriated to the United States, the Dominican funeral home must coordinate with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state; you can consult the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association to locate accredited providers [7]. In the United States, the federal FTC Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission guarantees families the right to receive an itemized General Price List over the phone or in person and to purchase only the specific goods and services desired [6]. Clarvia provides references to official directories for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers.
  • Notifying the U.S. consular mission: Report the death as soon as possible to the American Citizens Services unit of the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana (U.S. Embassy in the Dominican Republic) in Santo Domingo by calling (809) 567-7775 (dial 0 for the emergency duty officer) or emailing SDOAmericans@state.gov (consular agencies also operate in Punta Cana and Puerto Plata) [1]. The embassy verifies U.S. citizenship, provides guidance on local funeral homes, issues the consular mortuary certificate for shipment, and prepares the consular report of death; however, the U.S. government does not pay for funeral or repatriation expenses [1][5].

steps.title: Dominican Civil Registration, Hague Apostille, and U.S. Consular Report
steps.html:
• Registration with the Junta Central Electoral (JCE): With the Medical Certificate of Death (or forensic certification) and the deceased's passport or identity document, the death declaration must be filed at the Civil Registry Office (Oficialía del Estado Civil) of the Junta Central Electoral (Central Electoral Board) for the district where the death occurred (or at JCE offices located inside healthcare centers) within the 60-day period established by Law 4-23 [3]. Under Resolution 9-2025 of the Junta Central Electoral, civil status certificates are now issued in a single unified standard Death Certificate format (Acta de Defunción, replacing the former distinction between extracto and in extensa) valid for both domestic and international procedures [3].
  • Apostille from the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MIREX): For the Dominican Acta de Defunción to have direct legal effect in the United States (and for the consular file), it must first be validated at the central headquarters of the Junta Central Electoral and then apostilled online through the digital services portal of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Dominican Republic - MIREX) [4].
  • Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRODA): Once the Dominican Acta de Defunción is obtained, the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA, Form DS-2060) in English [1][5]. This official document is required by banks, insurance companies, pension agencies, and Probate Courts in the United States; additional copies can subsequently be ordered from the U.S. Department of State [5].

steps.title: International Repatriation of Remains or Ashes vs. Local Burial or Cremation
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body (coffin) to the United States: To transport the uncremated body to the United States, the Dominican funeral home obtains the sanitary corpse transit permit from the Ministry of Public Health and Social Assistance (Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social - MISPAS), the autopsy report from the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, the embalming certificate, the certificate of sealing inside a hermetic casket, and the consular mortuary documentation from the Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana [1][2]. For entry into U.S. territory, regulation 42 CFR 71.55 of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention requires that human remains travel in a leak-proof container, accompanied by the official death certificate or a statement confirming the absence of quarantinable communicable diseases, and consigned directly to a licensed funeral home, cemetery, or crematory in the United States [8]. Following clearance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the arrival airport, the receiving funeral home secures the state burial-transit permit.
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes to the United States: If the family chooses cremation in the Dominican Republic (with family and forensic authorization), transporting the ashes to the United States is simpler and less costly. The ashes must be carried in a non-metallic urn suitable for X-ray security screening, accompanied by the Acta de Defunción, the cremation certificate (certificado de cremación), and the consular certificate or an English translation [1][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in the Dominican Republic: If the family decides on final burial or cremation in the Dominican Republic, the local funeral home obtains the municipal permits from the corresponding city hall (ayuntamiento) and sanitary authorization from the Ministry of Public Health and Social Assistance [1].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in the United States and the Dominican Republic
steps.html:
• Benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security (SSA): Report the death to the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 (or through the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Santo Domingo) to stop improper monthly payments and apply for survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [9].
    • Veterans (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial rights in national cemeteries, headstones, or funeral allowances [11].
    • Federal taxes (IRS) and state probate: The personal representative or family member handling the estate must file the final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service no later than April 15 of the year following death [10]. Bank accounts and property in the United States without a designated beneficiary are settled through probate before the competent Probate Court in the relevant U.S. state and county.
  • Inheritance tax and pensions in the Dominican Republic:
    • Sworn Inheritance Tax Return (DGII): If the deceased held bank accounts, real estate, or other assets in the Dominican Republic, the heirs or legatees must file the Sworn Inheritance Return (Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones, Form FSD-1) with the Dirección General de Impuestos Internos (Directorate General of Internal Taxes - DGII) within ninety (90) calendar days after the date of death, subject to a general tax rate of 3% on the net estate after deducting documented funeral expenses and debts [12].
    • Pensions (SIPEN / AFP): If your family member contributed to or was a pensioner under the Dominican Social Security System (Law 87-01), the legal beneficiaries must submit the Acta de Defunción to the corresponding Pension Fund Administrator (Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones - AFP), under the supervision of the Superintendencia de Pensiones (Superintendency of Pensions - SIPEN), to claim a survivor pension (pensión de sobrevivencia) or the return of accumulated account balances as applicable [13].

closingQuestion: To provide more specific guidance for your situation, in which province or municipality of the Dominican Republic did the death occur (and did it take place inside or outside a medical center), and does the family wish to repatriate the body or ashes to a specific U.S. state or arrange burial or cremation in the Dominican Republic?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre República Dominicana y Estados Unidos: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre República Dominicana y Estados Unidos: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía o vínculos de residencia en los Estados Unidos fallece en la República Dominicana, la certificación médica o forense, la inscripción civil, el reporte consular y el traslado internacional o disposición local requieren coordinar trámites entre las autoridades dominicanas y estadounidenses. A continuación se explican los cinco pasos oficiales principales en orden práctico.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción e intervención forense en la República Dominicana
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento por causas naturales en clínica u hospital: Si el deceso ocurre bajo asistencia médica en un centro de salud (por ejemplo, en Santo Domingo, Santiago de los Caballeros, Punta Cana o Puerto Plata), el profesional médico tratante expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción (declaración médica de defunción) que acredita la causa del fallecimiento [1][3].
  • Fallecimiento en hotel, residencia o vía pública, o traslado internacional del cuerpo: Si la persona fallecida muere fuera de un centro hospitalario o en una zona turística, se debe llamar de inmediato al Sistema Nacional de Atención a Emergencias y Seguridad 911, a la Policía Nacional o a la Dirección Central de Policía de Turismo (POLITUR) [1]. Por ley dominicana, el cuerpo no puede ser levantado ni trasladado sin la autorización del Médico Legista y del Ministerio Público [1]. Además, la legislación dominicana exige la práctica de una autopsia médico-legal por parte de un médico forense del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses (INACIF) tanto en muertes no naturales o súbitas como en todo caso en que el cuerpo vaya a ser repatriado fuera de la República Dominicana [1][2].

steps.title: Seguro de viaje, designación de funerarias autorizadas y notificación consular
steps.html:
• Verificación de seguro de viaje o repatriación: Antes de contraer compromisos financieros independientes, verifique si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, asistencia médica internacional o cobertura asociada a tarjetas de crédito. Si existe póliza activa, comuníquese de inmediato con la central de asistencia de la aseguradora para que coordine y cubra los gastos funerarios y de repatriación.
  • Contratación de funeraria en la República Dominicana y en los Estados Unidos: La familia debe designar una funeraria autorizada en la República Dominicana con experiencia en traslados internacionales y embalsamamiento para retirar el cuerpo del hospital o del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, tramitar las actas y permisos sanitarios locales y coordinar el transporte aéreo [1][2]. Si el cuerpo será repatriado a los Estados Unidos, la funeraria dominicana debe coordinarse con una funeraria receptora con licencia en el estado estadounidense de destino; puede consultar el directorio de la National Funeral Directors Association para localizar proveedores acreditados [7]. En los Estados Unidos, la norma federal de funerales (FTC Funeral Rule) de la Federal Trade Commission garantiza a las familias el derecho a recibir una lista desglosada de precios (General Price List) por teléfono o en persona y a contratar únicamente los bienes y servicios deseados [6]. Clarvia ofrece referencias de directorios oficiales a título orientativo y no respalda, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores comerciales.
  • Notificación a la representación consular estadounidense: Reporte el fallecimiento lo antes posible a la unidad de Servicios a Ciudadanos Estadounidenses (American Citizens Services) de la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana en Santo Domingo, llamando al (809) 567-7775 (marque 0 para el oficial de guardia en emergencias) o escribiendo a SDOAmericans@state.gov (también existen agencias consulares en Punta Cana y Puerto Plata) [1]. La embajada verifica la ciudadanía estadounidense, orienta sobre funerarias locales, expide el certificado mortuorio consular para el traslado y emite el reporte consular de defunción; sin embargo, el gobierno estadounidense no sufraga gastos funerarios ni de repatriación [1][5].

steps.title: Registro civil dominicano, Apostilla de La Haya y reporte consular estadounidense
steps.html:
• Inscripción en la Junta Central Electoral (JCE): Con el Certificado Médico de Defunción (o certificación forense) y el pasaporte o documento de identidad de la persona fallecida, la declaración de defunción debe realizarse ante la Oficialía del Estado Civil de la Junta Central Electoral correspondiente a la demarcación donde ocurrió el fallecimiento (o en las delegaciones de la Junta Central Electoral en centros de salud) dentro del plazo oportuno de 60 días establecido por la Ley 4-23 [3]. Conforme a la Resolución 9-2025 de la Junta Central Electoral, las actas del estado civil se emiten ahora en un único formato estándar unificado de Acta de Defunción (que sustituye la antigua distinción entre extracto e in extensa) válido para trámites nacionales e internacionales [3].
  • Apostilla ante el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MIREX): Para que el Acta de Defunción dominicana surta efectos legales directos en los Estados Unidos (y para el expediente consular), primero debe ser validada por la sede central de la Junta Central Electoral y posteriormente apostillada en línea a través del portal de servicios digitales del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de la República Dominicana [4].
  • Reporte Consular de Defunción en el Exterior (CRODA): Una vez obtenida el Acta de Defunción dominicana, la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana emite el Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA, formulario DS-2060) en inglés [1][5]. Este documento oficial es exigido por bancos, aseguradoras, agencias de pensiones y tribunales de sucesiones (Probate Courts) en los Estados Unidos; copias adicionales posteriores pueden solicitarse al U.S. Department of State [5].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional de restos o cenizas frente a sepultura o cremación local
steps.html:
• Repatriación de cuerpo (féretro) a los Estados Unidos: Para trasladar el cuerpo sin cremar hacia los Estados Unidos, la funeraria dominicana gestiona el permiso sanitario de traslado de cadáveres ante el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MISPAS), el informe de autopsia del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, el certificado de embalsamamiento, el acta de encajonamiento en féretro hermético sellado y la documentación mortuoria consular de la Embajada de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana [1][2]. Para la entrada a territorio estadounidense, la normativa 42 CFR 71.55 de los Centers for Disease Control and Prevention exige que los restos humanos viajen en un contenedor a prueba de fugas, acompañados del certificado oficial de defunción o declaración sobre ausencia de agentes infecciosos sujetos a cuarentena, y consignados directamente a una funeraria, cementerio o crematorio autorizado en los Estados Unidos [8]. Tras el despacho ante U.S. Customs and Border Protection en el aeropuerto de llegada, la funeraria receptora tramita el permiso estatal de tránsito e inhumación (burial-transit permit).
  • Repatriación de cenizas a los Estados Unidos: Si la familia opta por la cremación en la República Dominicana (previa autorización familiar y forense), el traslado de las cenizas hacia los Estados Unidos es más sencillo y económico. Las cenizas deben transportarse en una urna no metálica apta para inspección por rayos X, acompañadas del Acta de Defunción, el certificado de cremación y el certificado consular o traducción al inglés [1][8].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en la República Dominicana: Si se decide realizar la sepultura o cremación definitiva en territorio dominicano, la funeraria local gestiona los permisos municipales ante el ayuntamiento correspondiente y la autorización sanitaria del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social [1].

steps.title: Pensiones de sobrevivientes, impuestos y sucesión en Estados Unidos y República Dominicana
steps.html:
• Trámites previsionales, fiscales y sucesorios en los Estados Unidos:
    • Seguridad Social (SSA): Notifique el fallecimiento a la Social Security Administration llamando al 1-800-772-1213 (o a través de la Unidad de Beneficios Federales - Federal Benefits Unit en la Embajada en Santo Domingo) para suspender pagos mensuales improcedentes y solicitar prestaciones de sobrevivientes o el pago global por defunción [9].
    • Veteranos (VA): Si su familiar prestó servicio en las fuerzas armadas de los Estados Unidos, consulte al Department of Veterans Affairs sobre derechos de entierro en cementerios nacionales, lápidas o subsidios funerarios [11].
    • Impuestos federales (IRS) y sucesión estatal (Probate): El representante personal o familiar encargado del patrimonio debe presentar la declaración final del impuesto sobre la renta federal (Form 1040) ante el Internal Revenue Service a más tardar el 15 de abril del año siguiente al fallecimiento [10]. Las cuentas bancarias y bienes en los Estados Unidos sin beneficiario designado se liquidan mediante el proceso de sucesión (probate) ante el tribunal competente (Probate Court) del estado y condado estadounidense correspondiente.
  • Impuesto sucesoral y pensiones en la República Dominicana:
    • Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones (DGII): Si la persona fallecida poseía cuentas bancarias, inmuebles o activos en la República Dominicana, los herederos o legatarios deben presentar la Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones (Formulario FSD-1) ante la Dirección General de Impuestos Internos dentro de los noventa (90) días calendario posteriores a la fecha del fallecimiento, sujeta a una tasa general del 3% sobre la masa sucesoral neta tras deducir gastos funerarios y deudas fehacientes [12].
    • Pensiones (SIPEN / AFP): Si su familiar cotizaba o era pensionado en el Sistema Dominicano de Seguridad Social (Ley 87-01), los beneficiarios legales deben presentar el Acta de Defunción ante la Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones (AFP) correspondiente, bajo la supervisión de la Superintendencia de Pensiones, para reclamar la pensión de sobrevivencia o la devolución de saldos acumulados según corresponda [13].

es.closingQuestion: Para brindarle indicaciones más específicas según su situación: 1. ¿En qué provincia o municipio de la República Dominicana ocurrió el fallecimiento y el deceso se produjo en un centro médico o fuera de él? 2. ¿Desea la familia repatriar el cuerpo o las cenizas hacia un estado específico de los Estados Unidos, o realizar la sepultura o cremación en la República Dominicana?
