title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Thailand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Thailand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Thailand.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Thailand, medical certification, Thai civil registration, consular release letters, and international repatriation or local cremation must be coordinated between Thai authorities and United States federal and state institutions. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in Thailand
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinic: When the death occurs under medical supervision in a Thai hospital, the attending physician issues the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1, Bai Rab Rong Kan Tai), which states the cause of death in Thai and serves as the mandatory prerequisite for civil registration [2].
  • Death in a residence, hotel, or public place: For any sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital, call the Royal Thai Police at 191, the Tourist Police at 1155, or emergency medical services at 1669 immediately [1]. Do not move the body before police arrive. Under Thai law, deaths occurring outside a hospital or from unnatural or undetermined causes require a police investigation report and a forensic autopsy, typically performed at the Police General Hospital Institute of Forensic Medicine in Bangkok or a designated provincial forensic hospital (such as in Chiang Mai, Phuket, or Chonburi) [1][2].
  • Mandatory Embassy release letter for foreign nationals: Thai hospitals, police, and forensic morgues will not release the body of a U.S. citizen to a family member or funeral director until the U.S. Embassy and Consulate in Thailand issues an official consular Letter of Release (No-Objection Letter) confirming the identity of the legal next of kin or authorized representative [1][4].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel or medical-assistance insurance first: Before signing independent funeral contracts, check whether the deceased carried travel insurance, international health coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation insurance. If a policy is active, notify the insurer's 24-hour assistance center immediately so its appointed repatriation agent can manage and pay for the arrangements.
  • Contacting the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in Thailand: Report the death as soon as possible to the American Citizens Services (ACS) unit at the U.S. Embassy and Consulate in Thailand in Bangkok (02-205-4000 within Thailand or +66-2-205-4000 from abroad) or the U.S. Consulate General in Chiang Mai [1]. The U.S. Embassy verifies citizenship and next-of-kin priority, issues the mandatory consular Letter of Release so the hospital or forensic institute can release the remains, provides a list of international funeral directors in Thailand, and prepares the Consular Report of Death Abroad [1][5]. The U.S. government cannot pay for hospital bills, local cremation, or international shipping of remains [1].
  • Appointing funeral coordinators in Thailand and the United States: Families generally appoint an experienced international funeral and repatriation director in Thailand (or a local funeral coordinator working with a Buddhist temple, Wat, if choosing local cremation) to handle Thai civil registration, translation, and airport cargo clearance [1]. If repatriating the body to the United States, the Thai provider coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state; you can find licensed U.S. providers through the National Funeral Directors Association directory [7]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) and allow you to select only the specific goods and services you want [6]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Thailand, MFA Legalization, and U.S. Consular Registration
steps.html:
• Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4): Using the hospital's Form Tor.Ror.4/1 (or police/forensic documentation), the deceased's passport, and the U.S. Embassy Letter of Release, the death must be reported within 24 hours of death or discovery to the local District Office (Amphoe in provinces, or Khet in Bangkok) under the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA, citizen hotline 1548) [2]. The District Registrar issues the official Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) [2]. Many District Offices can also issue an official English-language civil registration extract directly [2].
  • Translation and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Legalization: Because Thailand is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, if the Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) is needed for legal or non-CRODA administrative use outside Thailand, it must be translated into English and authenticated by the Legalization Division of the Department of Consular Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand [3].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA): Once the local Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) is issued, submit it along with the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. Embassy and Consulate in Thailand [1]. The Embassy issues the official Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA / CRDA, Form DS-2060) in English, which serves as the primary death record accepted by U.S. courts, banks, insurers, and federal agencies [1][5]. Additional certified copies can later be requested from the U.S. Department of State Passport Vital Records Section [5].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United States vs. Local Cremation or Burial in Thailand
steps.html:
• Repatriating the body (casket) from Thailand to the United States: To ship uncremated remains by air cargo, the international funeral director in Thailand arranges medical embalming, hermetically sealed coffin packaging, and export clearance with the Thai Customs Department (such as at Suvarnabhumi Airport, Customs Service Sub-Division I at +66 2-134-0490 or Sub-Division II at +66 2-134-0641) [4]. The Thai Customs Department does not require a formal Export Declaration Form for human remains, but requires originals and two copies of the hospital/police death confirmation, the deceased's passport, the U.S. Embassy permission letter, the Air Waybill, and the Export Control Document [4]. For entry into the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) requires that the remains be contained in a leak-proof casket, accompanied by the official death certificate or an infectious-disease certification statement, and consigned directly to a licensed U.S. mortuary, cemetery, or crematory [8]. Upon arrival and U.S. Customs and Border Protection clearance, the receiving U.S. funeral home obtains the state burial-transit permit [9].
  • Repatriating cremated ashes to the United States: Many families choose local cremation in Thailand (typically performed at a Buddhist temple, Wat, once the U.S. Embassy Letter of Release and Thai Death Certificate Form Tor.Ror.4 are presented) followed by transporting the cremated ashes to the United States [1][4]. Under Thai Customs Department and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention rules, cremated human ashes may be shipped as air cargo or carried in passenger luggage in a non-metallic, X-ray scan-friendly urn accompanied by the Thai Death Certificate, the temple or crematory cremation certificate, the U.S. Embassy letter/CRODA, and a copy of the deceased's cancelled passport [4][8].
  • Local cremation or burial in Thailand: If final disposition takes place in Thailand, the appointed funeral coordinator and next of kin present the U.S. Embassy Letter of Release and Form Tor.Ror.4 to the selected temple or cemetery [1][2].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in the United States and Thailand
steps.html:
• Benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death to the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 from the United States (or by contacting the regional U.S. Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Manila, which covers Thailand) to halt ongoing monthly benefits (any payment for the month of death must be returned) and apply for eligible survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [10].
    • Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member was a U.S. military veteran, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding eligibility for burial in a VA national cemetery, headstones, memorial flags, or burial allowances [12].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate: The executor, administrator, or survivor in charge of the deceased's assets must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following the death [11]. U.S. bank accounts, brokerage accounts, or real estate held in the deceased's sole name without a beneficiary designation are settled through the county Probate Court in the U.S. state of domicile.
  • Estate and probate administration in Thailand:
    • Thai Court Probate Order: If the deceased held sole-name bank accounts, a vehicle, a long-term lease, or a condominium unit in Thailand, Thai banks and the Land Department generally will not release funds or transfer title solely on a U.S. will or CRODA. Under the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, the family or executor normally must retain a licensed attorney in Thailand to petition the competent Thai Civil or Provincial Court for a formal court order appointing an estate administrator (Phu Chat Kan Moradok).

closingQuestion: To help tailor the next steps for your situation: 1. In which province or city in Thailand did the death occur, and did it take place in a hospital or outside a medical facility? 2. Does the family plan to arrange local cremation in Thailand (with or without bringing the ashes to the United States) or full-body repatriation to a specific U.S. state?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Ireland: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Ireland, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Ireland.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Ireland, medical certification, Irish civil registration, consular reporting, and international repatriation or local burial/cremation must be coordinated between authorities in Ireland and the United States. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner Clearance in Ireland
steps.html:
• Expected death under medical care in a hospital, hospice, or home: If a registered medical practitioner attended the deceased during the final illness and can certify a natural cause of death, the doctor completes and signs Part 1 of the Death Notification Form (DNF), which contains the Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death, and provides it to a qualified informant or relative [2][3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death: If the death occurs unexpectedly outside a hospital, or if the attending doctor cannot certify a natural cause of death, call 999 or 112 immediately. An Garda Síochána (the Irish police) will attend and report the death to the local Coroner (such as the Dublin District Coroner or Cork City Coroner) [2][3]. The Coroner may direct a post-mortem examination or inquest, issues an Interim Certificate of the Fact of Death if needed by the family for urgent financial or administrative steps, and transmits the final Coroner's Certificate directly to the HSE Civil Registration Service to register the death [2][3].
  • Coroner notification for removal outside Ireland: Whenever human remains are to be repatriated out of the Republic of Ireland, the local Coroner must be notified and issue an official Coroner's removal certificate authorizing the body to leave the State [3].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel or repatriation insurance first: Before entering into private funeral contracts, verify whether your family member held travel insurance, international medical-assistance coverage, or credit-card travel protection. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance desk immediately so its appointed repatriation coordinator can arrange and fund the transfer [3][4].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Ireland and the United States: International repatriation requires coordination between a funeral director in Ireland (who collects the deceased, prepares the remains, and arranges Irish customs and airport cargo dispatch, such as through Dublin Airport or Shannon Airport) and a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state [1][3]. You can locate member funeral directors in Ireland through the Irish Association of Funeral Directors [4], and licensed receiving providers in the United States through the National Funeral Directors Association directory [10]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized General Price List (GPL) by phone or in person and allow you to select only the specific goods and services you want [9]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the U.S. Embassy in Ireland: Report the death as soon as possible to the American Citizens Services (ACS) unit at the U.S. Embassy in Ireland in Dublin (phone +353 1 903-6255; if the death occurred in Northern Ireland, contact the U.S. Consulate General in Belfast) [1]. The U.S. Embassy verifies citizenship, guides next of kin on Irish funeral and shipping procedures, issues the Consular Report of Death Abroad, and takes temporary custody of personal effects if no family member or legal representative is present in Ireland [1][8]. The U.S. government cannot pay for funeral, cremation, or international shipping expenses [1].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Ireland, Apostille, and U.S. Consular Registration
steps.html:
• Registering the death with the HSE Civil Registration Service / GRO: Unless referred to the Coroner, a relative or qualified informant must complete Part 2 of the Death Notification Form (DNF) and register the death in person at any HSE Civil Registration Service office in Ireland (under the General Register Office, GRO) as soon as possible and within 3 months of the date of death, bringing the signed DNF and the informant's government photo ID [2]. Registration itself is free, and certified standard Irish Death Certificates cost EUR 20 per copy [2].
  • Hague Apostille via the Department of Foreign Affairs: Although Irish Death Certificates are already issued in English (or bilingual Irish/English), U.S. probate courts or financial institutions that require an authenticated foreign record outside the consular report route may request a Hague Apostille. The Authentication Section of the Department of Foreign Affairs in Dublin (Knockmaun House, Lower Mount Street) or Cork (South Mall) issues physical Hague Apostille stamps on original Irish Death Certificates for EUR 40 per stamp, either in person or by registered post [5].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA): Once the Irish Death Certificate (or Coroner's certificate) is issued, submit it along with the deceased's U.S. passport and the embassy informational questionnaire to the U.S. Embassy in Ireland [1]. The Embassy issues the official Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRODA / CRDA, Form DS-2060), which is accepted across the United States for estate probate, insurance claims, and bank accounts [1][8]. Additional copies can later be requested from the U.S. Department of State Passport Vital Records Section [8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United States vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Ireland
steps.html:
• Repatriating the body (casket) from Ireland to the United States: For full-body transport, the Irish funeral director obtains the certified Irish Death Certificate (or Coroner's certificate), the Coroner's removal-out-of-State authorization, an HSE Environmental Health certificate confirming freedom from infectious disease, a certificate of professional embalming, and a hermetically sealed casket or zinc-lined container certificate, and coordinates consular mortuary clearance with the U.S. Embassy in Ireland [1][3]. For entry into the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55) requires that human remains arrive in a leak-proof container accompanied by the official death certificate (or infectious-disease certification statement) and consigned directly to a licensed U.S. mortuary, cemetery, or crematory [11]. After U.S. Customs and Border Protection clearance at the U.S. port of entry, the receiving U.S. funeral director secures the state burial-transit permit.
  • Repatriating cremated ashes to the United States: If cremation is carried out in Ireland (requiring medical referee and, where applicable, Coroner clearance), cremated human ashes can be transported to the United States by air cargo or as passenger hand luggage in a non-metallic, X-ray scan-friendly urn accompanied by the Irish Death Certificate, the crematorium's Certificate of Cremation, and the CRODA [1][3][11].
  • Local burial or cremation in Ireland: If the family chooses burial or cremation in Ireland, the appointed Irish funeral director coordinates directly with the local authority or private cemetery/crematorium using the Death Notification Form or Coroner's authorization [2][4].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in the United States and Ireland
steps.html:
• Benefits, taxes, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 from the United States, or contact the Federal Benefits Unit (FBU) at the U.S. Embassy in Ireland in Dublin, to stop ongoing monthly benefit payments (any payment received for the month of death must be returned) and apply for eligible U.S. survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [12].
    • Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If the deceased served in the U.S. armed forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial in a VA national cemetery, memorial headstones, burial flags, or burial allowances [14].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate: The executor, administrator, or person in charge of the deceased's property must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [13]. U.S. bank accounts, investments, or real estate held in the deceased's sole name without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court in the relevant U.S. state.
  • Social protection, tax clearance, and probate in Ireland:
    • Department of Social Protection (DSP): If the deceased or surviving partner had Irish social insurance (PRSI) ties or residence in Ireland, notify the Department of Social Protection (accessible via gov.ie and MyGovID) to check eligibility for the Bereaved Partner's (Contributory or Non-Contributory) Pension (which covers eligible surviving legal partners, civil partners, and qualified cohabitants), the once-off Bereaved Parent Grant, or the 6-week continuation of certain social welfare payments [6].
    • Revenue Commissioners and Irish Probate Office: If the deceased held bank accounts, property, or other estate assets in Ireland requiring a formal Grant of Representation (Grant of Probate with a will, or Letters of Administration without a will), the executor or administrator must first submit an online Statement of Affairs (Probate) Form SA.2 to the Revenue Commissioners (via myAccount or ROS) to obtain a Notice of Acknowledgement (Probate) [7]. The application is then filed with the Courts Service of Ireland High Court Probate Office in Dublin or the relevant District Probate Registry (noting that an Irish solicitor is mandatory if the deceased was domiciled outside Ireland and left a foreign-language will or complex cross-border domicile issues) [7].

closingQuestion: To help tailor the next steps to your specific circumstances: 1. In which county or city in Ireland did the death occur, and has the attending doctor issued the Death Notification Form or has the local Coroner been notified? 2. Does the family plan to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to a specific U.S. state, or arrange burial or cremation in Ireland?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Portugal: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Portugal, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Portugal.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties dies in Portugal, electronic medical certification and civil registration take place first in Portugal, followed by consular registration with the United States diplomatic mission to issue the official English-language death report and coordinate international repatriation or local funeral arrangements [1][4][7]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Obtain the Electronic Medical Death Certificate via SICO and Medical or Forensic Clearance in Portugal
steps.html:
In Portugal, the medical certification of death is recorded electronically in the SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito - Death Certificate Information System), under the technical guidance of the Direção-Geral da Saúde (DGS, Directorate-General of Health) and managed by the Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde (SPMS, Shared Services of the Ministry of Health), which transmits the data directly to the civil registry [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility: The attending physician verifies the death, issues the electronic Certificado de Óbito (medical death certificate) directly in SICO, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary [1][2]. Provide the deceased person's U.S. passport (and Portuguese residence card, if held) so that identification details are recorded without discrepancies [1][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call the European emergency number 112 (or contact the local PSP or GNR police) [1][2]. If the death occurred from a known natural cause under medical supervision, the attending physician or local health authority (delegado de saúde) can verify the death and register the certificate in SICO [1][2].
  • Sudden, violent, or unexplained death: When a natural cause cannot be certified immediately, the police notify the Ministério Público (Public Prosecutor's Office), which orders the transfer of the body to a forensic medical office of the Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) (National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences, for example in Lisbon, Porto, or Coimbra) for an autopsy or forensic examination [1][2]. Only after authorization from the Ministério Público and registration in SICO by the forensic pathologist can the funeral director receive the body [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Funeral Directors in Portugal and the United States, and Contact the U.S. Embassy
steps.html:
Before entering into private financial commitments, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international health insurance, or funeral assistance and repatriation coverage linked to a credit card or employment contract [4][7]. The United States Government does not have funds to pay for funeral, cremation, or international repatriation expenses [4][7].

  • Licensed funeral agency in Portugal: The family (or insurance assistance company) must appoint a funeral agency (agência funerária) legally registered with the Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE, Directorate-General for Economic Activities / gov.pt portal), which also regulates funeral services and the statutory Funeral Social (social funeral) [3]. Funeral providers in Portugal are represented by sector associations such as the Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, phone +351 218 687 978) or the Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro (AAFC) [3].
  • Receiving funeral home in the United States and FTC protections: If you choose to repatriate the body to the United States, the Portuguese funeral agency coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which can be located through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, phone +1 262-789-1880) [5]. In the United States, the Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC, phone +1 877-382-4357) guarantees the family's right to receive an itemized General Price List before contracting local funeral services [6]. Clarvia provides official and association references for guidance only and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific providers.
  • Consular assistance and Next-of-Kin authorization from the U.S.: Immediately contact the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal (U.S. Embassy in Lisbon, phone +351 217 273 300, email conslisbon@state.gov, or the U.S. Consulate in Ponta Delgada for the Azores), which provides informational lists of funeral homes and guides families through the documentary requirements [4]. If the next of kin is in the United States and cannot travel to Portugal, they can execute a notarized Next-of-Kin Affidavit authorizing the Portuguese funeral agency to handle civil registration, cremation, or international repatriation [4][7].

steps.title: Register the Death at the Civil Registry (Within 48 Hours), Obtain an Apostille, and Request the CRDA (Form DS-2060)
steps.html:
A death occurring in Portugal must be declared within the statutory period of 48 hours after medical verification of death or after completion or waiver of a forensic autopsy [1]:

  • Portuguese Civil Death Record (Assento de Óbito) and multilingual certificate: In standard practice, the appointed funeral agency files the declaration at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN, Institute of Registries and Notary / Justiça.gov.pt portal, Registries Helpline +351 211 950 500), presenting the SICO electronic death certificate number and the deceased person's identification documents [1]. The initial Assento de Óbito (civil death registration record) is issued free of charge; you may also request a multilingual death certificate under the 1976 Vienna Convention (CIEC Form C) for European use and a Hague Convention Apostille (issued by the Procuradoria-Geral da República / Public Prosecutor's Office) for direct legal recognition in the United States [1][4]. Also ask the funeral agency for the supplementary medical statement showing the cause of death (causa mortis) extracted from SICO, which is required for U.S. consular mortuary certificates and U.S. public health import clearance [4][8].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Based on the Portuguese Assento de Óbito, the medical cause-of-death statement, and the deceased person's U.S. passport, the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal (under the oversight of the U.S. Department of State, phone +1 888-407-4747 in the U.S. or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) [4][7]. The CRDA is the official English-language death record accepted across all U.S. states by banks, insurers, probate courts, and federal agencies in place of a state Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics certificate [7].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in Portugal
steps.html:
The family may choose either international repatriation of the body or cremated remains to the United States or a local burial or cremation in Portugal [1][4][8]:

  • International repatriation of the body in a casket to the United States: The Portuguese funeral agency obtains the international transfer permit (alvará de trasladação) and mortuary transit pass (livre-trânsito mortuário, governed by Portuguese health regulations and international conventions such as the Strasbourg Agreement and Berlin Arrangement, with consular information also published on the Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Centro de Atendimento Consular of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs), performs embalming (tanatopraxia), places the body in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined casket, and obtains the consular mortuary certificate from the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal [1][4][8].
  • U.S. public health and customs entry rules (CDC and CBP): Under federal regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone +1 800-232-4636), human remains that are embalmed or placed in a hermetically sealed casket and accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death do not require a prior special CDC import permit, provided the person did not die of a quarantinable communicable disease [8]. At the U.S. airport of arrival, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [5][8].
  • Local cremation or burial in Portugal: If you choose cremation in Portugal, the ashes are delivered in a sealed urn accompanied by the cremation certificate and the Assento de Óbito [1][4]. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention do not require a public health import permit for cremated ashes [8]; if carrying the urn by air to the United States, use a non-metallic, X-ray scan-friendly container and carry the cremation certificate, the Assento de Óbito, and the CRDA [4][8].

steps.title: Claim Survivor Benefits, Fulfill Tax Obligations, and Administer the Estate in the United States and Portugal
steps.html:
Once the Portuguese Assento de Óbito and the CRDA (Form DS-2060) have been issued, pension notifications, tax filings, and estate administration must be completed in both jurisdictions:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death promptly to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213 in the U.S.) or, if the deceased person or surviving family members reside in Portugal, directly to the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Lisbon (email fbu.lisbon@ssa.gov) to stop monthly payments and apply for monthly survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment for eligible family members [9][10].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone +1 800-827-1000) to check eligibility for burial in a national cemetery, a government headstone, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [11].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and State Probate Court: The personal representative of the estate must file the final federal individual income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by the regular April 15 deadline of the year following death (and Form 1041 if the estate generates income) [12], and open probate proceedings with the Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. county and state where the deceased was domiciled or held property.
  • In Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças, and Tax Authority):
    • Portuguese Social Security benefits: If the deceased contributed to or received a pension in Portugal, apply to Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, phone +351 210 545 400 or 300 502 502) for the Subsídio por Morte (Death Grant, within 180 days of death), the Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (Funeral Expense Reimbursement, within 90 days under the CGA public-sector scheme or up to 6 months under the general scheme for the person who paid the funeral when no beneficiaries qualify for the Death Grant), and the Pensão de Sobrevivência (Survivor's Pension) [13].
    • Registration of heirs (Habilitação de Herdeiros) and Stamp Duty (Imposto do Selo): If the deceased left bank accounts, real estate, or other assets in Portugal, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must report the death and file the inventory of assets (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) with the Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority) by the end of the third month following the month of death, and complete the formal declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) at an Espaço Óbito or Balcão das Heranças desk of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [1][14].

closingQuestion: So that we can provide exact local contact details, in which municipality in Portugal did the death occur, and to which U.S. state do you plan to repatriate the remains or administer the estate (or do you prefer local burial or cremation in Portugal)?

pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Portugal e Estados Unidos: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Portugal e Estados Unidos: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos as nossas sinceras condolências pelo falecimento do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa com cidadania ou residência nos Estados Unidos falece em Portugal, a certificação médica eletrónica e o registo civil decorrem primeiro em território português, seguindo-se o registo consular junto da representação diplomática dos Estados Unidos para emissão do certificado oficial em língua inglesa e a coordenação da trasladação internacional ou do funeral local [1][4][7]. Abaixo descrevem-se os cinco passos oficiais por ordem.

steps.title: Obter o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico através do SICO e a liberação médica ou médico-legal em Portugal
steps.html:
Em Portugal, a certificação médica do falecimento é registada eletronicamente no SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito), sob orientação técnica da Direção-Geral da Saúde (DGS) e gestão dos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde (SPMS), que transmite os dados diretamente para o registo civil [1][2]:

  • Óbito em hospital, clínica ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente verifica o óbito, emite diretamente o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico no SICO e transfere o corpo para a casa mortuária da unidade hospitalar [1][2]. Entregue o passaporte norte-americano (e o título de residência português, caso a pessoa falecida o possuísse) para que a identificação fique registada sem divergências [1][4].
  • Óbito no domicílio, hotel ou via pública: Ligue de imediato para o número europeu de emergência 112 (ou contacte a PSP ou a GNR da área) [1][2]. Se a morte tiver ocorrido por causa natural conhecida sob acompanhamento médico, o médico assistente ou o delegado de saúde (autoridade de saúde local) pode verificar o óbito e registar o certificado no SICO [1][2].
  • Morte súbita, violenta ou de causa desconhecida: Quando não é possível atestar de imediato uma causa natural, a autoridade policial comunica o óbito ao Ministério Público, que determina a remoção do corpo para o gabinete médico-legal do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) (por exemplo, nas delegações de Lisboa, Porto ou Coimbra) para autópsia ou exame pericial [1][2]. Só após a autorização do Ministério Público e o registo no SICO pelo médico legista é que a agência funerária pode receber o corpo [1][2].

steps.title: Verificar seguros, contratar agências funerárias em Portugal e nos Estados Unidos e contactar a Embaixada dos EUA
steps.html:
Antes de assumir compromissos financeiros autónomos, verifique se o seu familiar possuía seguro de viagem, seguro de saúde internacional ou cobertura de assistência e repatriação funerária associada a cartão de crédito ou contrato de trabalho [4][7]. O Governo dos Estados Unidos não dispõe de fundos para pagar despesas de funeral, cremação ou trasladação internacional [4][7].

  • Agência funerária habilitada em Portugal: A família (ou a seguradora) deve mandatar uma agência funerária legalmente habilitada junto da Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE / portal gov.pt), onde estão também definidas as regras legais da atividade funerária e do Funeral Social [3]. As agências funerárias encontram-se representadas em associações do setor como a Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, telefone +351 218 687 978) ou a Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro (AAFC) [3].
  • Casa funerária recetora nos Estados Unidos e proteções da FTC: Caso opte pela trasladação do corpo para os Estados Unidos, a agência funerária portuguesa articula-se com uma casa funerária licenciada no estado norte-americano de destino, que pode ser localizada através do diretório da National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, telefone +1 262-789-1880) [5]. Nos Estados Unidos, a Funeral Rule aplicada pela Federal Trade Commission (FTC, telefone +1 877-382-4357) garante o direito da família a receber uma lista discriminada de preços (General Price List) antes de contratar serviços funerários locais [6]. A Clarvia disponibiliza referências associativas e oficiais apenas para orientação e não recomenda, não endossa nem classifica prestadores específicos.
  • Assistência consular e autorização por familiares nos EUA: Contacte de imediato a U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal (Embaixada dos EUA em Lisboa, telefone +351 217 273 300, e-mail conslisbon@state.gov, ou o Consulado dos EUA em Ponta Delgada para os Açores), que disponibiliza listas informativas de agências funerárias e orienta o processo documental [4]. Se o familiar mais próximo (next of kin) se encontrar nos Estados Unidos e não puder deslocar-se a Portugal, pode outorgar uma declaração/autorização reconhecida notarialmente (Next-of-Kin Affidavit) designando a agência funerária portuguesa para tratar do registo, cremação ou trasladação [4][7].

steps.title: Declarar o óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil (48 horas), Apostila e obter o CRDA (Form DS-2060)
steps.html:
O falecimento ocorrido em território português tem de ser declarado no prazo legal de 48 horas após a verificação do óbito ou após a realização/dispensa de autópsia médico-legal [1]:

  • Assento de Óbito português e certidão plurilingue: Na prática habitual, a agência funerária mandatada efetua a declaração perante qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / portal Justiça.gov.pt, Linha Registos +351 211 950 500), apresentando o número do Certificado de Óbito eletrónico do SICO e os documentos da pessoa falecida [1]. O primeiro Assento de Óbito é gratuito; pode também solicitar uma certidão de óbito em modelo plurilingue da Convenção de Viena de 1976 (Modelo C da CIEC) para uso no espaço europeu e a Apostila da Convenção da Haia (emitida pela Procuradoria-Geral da República / Ministério Público) para reconhecimento direto nos Estados Unidos [1][4]. Solicite igualmente à agência funerária a declaração médica complementar com a indicação da causa mortis extraída do SICO, necessária para os documentos mortuários consulares e de importação sanitária nos EUA [4][8].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Com base no Assento de Óbito português, no documento médico com a causa da morte e no passaporte norte-americano da pessoa falecida, a U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal (sob supervisão do U.S. Department of State, telefone +1 888-407-4747 nos EUA ou +1 202-501-4444 a partir do estrangeiro) emite o Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) [4][7]. O CRDA é o documento oficial em língua inglesa aceite em todos os estados norte-americanos por bancos, seguradoras, tribunais de sucessões e agências federais em substituição de uma certidão estadual de Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics [7].

steps.title: Escolher entre a trasladação internacional para os Estados Unidos e a inumação ou cremação local em Portugal
steps.html:
A família pode optar pela trasladação internacional do corpo ou das cinzas para os Estados Unidos ou pela realização do funeral em Portugal [1][4][8]:

  • Trasladação internacional do corpo em urna para os Estados Unidos: A agência funerária portuguesa obtém o alvará de trasladação internacional e o livre-trânsito mortuário (enquadrado pelas normas sanitárias portuguesas e convenções internacionais como o Acordo de Estrasburgo e a Convenção de Berlim, com informação consular também disponível no Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Centro de Atendimento Consular do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros), procede ao embalsamamento (tanatopraxia), acondiciona o corpo num caixão de zinco hermeticamente selado e obtém o certificado mortuário consular junto da U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Portugal [1][4][8].
  • Regras sanitárias e aduaneiras de entrada nos EUA (CDC e CBP): Ao abrigo das normas federais dos Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, telefone +1 800-232-4636), os restos mortais humanos embalsamados ou encerrados em urna hermeticamente selada e acompanhados da certidão de óbito oficial com a causa da morte não necessitam de licença especial prévia do CDC, desde que a morte não tenha resultado de doença infetocontagiosa sujeita a quarentena [8]. No aeroporto de chegada nos Estados Unidos, a casa funerária norte-americana recetora trata do desalfandegamento junto da U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) e obtém a guia estadual de transporte e sepultamento (burial-transit permit) [5][8].
  • Cremação ou inumação local em Portugal: Se optar pela cremação em Portugal, as cinzas são entregues numa urna selada acompanhada do certificado de cremação e do Assento de Óbito [1][4]. Os Centers for Disease Control and Prevention não exigem licença sanitária de importação para cinzas cremadas [8]; caso sejam transportadas por via aérea para os Estados Unidos, utilize uma urna não metálica que permita o rastreio de raios X de segurança aeroportuária e faça acompanhar a urna do certificado de cremação, do Assento de Óbito e do CRDA [4][8].

steps.title: Requerer prestações de sobrevivência, cumprir obrigações fiscais e tratar da sucessão nos EUA e em Portugal
steps.html:
Após a obtenção do Assento de Óbito português e do CRDA (Form DS-2060), devem ser regularizadas as notificações de pensões, impostos e herança nas jurisdições aplicáveis:

  • Nos Estados Unidos (SSA, VA, IRS e Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Comunique o óbito de imediato à Social Security Administration (telefone 1-800-772-1213 nos EUA) ou, caso a pessoa falecida ou os familiares residam em Portugal, diretamente à Federal Benefits Unit da Embaixada dos EUA em Lisboa (através do e-mail fbu.lisbon@ssa.gov) para cessar pagamentos mensais e requerer prestações de sobrevivência ou o subsídio único por morte de $255 para familiares elegíveis [9][10].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): Se o seu familiar serviu nas Forças Armadas dos EUA, contacte o U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (telefone +1 800-827-1000) para verificar o direito a sepultamento num cemitério nacional de veteranos, lápide oficial, subsídio de funeral (VA Form 21P-530EZ) ou pensão de sobrevivência (DIC) [11].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) e Probate Court estadual: O representante legal da herança deve entregar a declaração final de imposto federal sobre o rendimento (Form 1040) junto do Internal Revenue Service (telefone +1 800-829-1040) até ao prazo normal de 15 de abril do ano seguinte ao falecimento (e o Form 1041 se o património gerar rendimento próprio) [12], bem como abrir o processo sucessório (probate) junto do Probate Court (ou Surrogate's Court) do condado e estado norte-americano onde a pessoa falecida tinha domicílio ou bens.
  • Em Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças e Finanças):
    • Prestações da Segurança Social: Se a pessoa falecida também descontava ou era pensionista em Portugal, requeira junto da Segurança Social (telefone +351 210 545 400 ou 300 502 502) o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do óbito), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias no regime convergente da CGA ou até 6 meses no regime geral para quem pagou o funeral quando não há titulares de subsídio por morte) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [13].
    • Habilitação de herdeiros e Imposto do Selo: Caso a pessoa falecida tenha deixado contas bancárias, imóveis ou outros bens em Portugal, o cabeça-de-casal deve efetuar a participação do óbito e apresentar a relação de bens (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) junto da Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao mês do falecimento e tratar da habilitação de herdeiros no Espaço Óbito ou no Balcão das Heranças do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [1][14].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos detalhar os contactos locais exatos, em que município de Portugal ocorreu o falecimento, para qual estado dos Estados Unidos pretendem trasladar os restos mortais ou tratar da sucessão (ou preferem inumação/cremação local em Portugal)?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Greece: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Greece, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Greece.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Greece, medical certification and civil registration take place first in the Greek municipality where the death occurred, while a licensed funeral home coordinates with Greek health authorities and the U.S. Embassy in Athens (or the U.S. Consulate General in Thessaloniki) for the Consular Report of Death Abroad and international transport [1][2][4]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death and Emergency or Forensic Clearance in Greece
steps.html:
Before civil registration, burial, cremation, or international repatriation can proceed, a licensed physician or forensic medical examiner in Greece must issue the official Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου) [1][2][4]:

  • Death in a Greek hospital or clinic: When a person dies in a public or private hospital (for example, in Athens, Thessaloniki, Heraklion, or Rhodes), the attending hospital physician verifies the death, completes the Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου) stating the exact medical cause of death, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary until an appointed funeral director arrives [1][2][4]. Provide the deceased's U.S. passport (and Greek residence permit or tax/AMKA details, if held) so personal particulars match across Greek and U.S. records [1][4].
  • Death at a hotel, private residence, beach, or public place: Call the National Centre for Emergency Care (EKAB on 166), the European emergency number (112), and the Hellenic Police (100) (or the Hellenic Coast Guard on 108 if the death occurred at sea or on a beach) [1][2].
  • Forensic autopsy (Ιατροδικαστική Υπηρεσία) for sudden or unattended deaths: Under Greek law, whenever a death occurs outside a hospital without prior medical attendance, or is sudden, accidental, or unexplained, the Hellenic Police or Coast Guard orders a mandatory forensic examination and autopsy by the regional Forensic Medical Service (Ιατροδικαστική Υπηρεσία) of the Ministry of Justice (such as the Forensic Medical Service of Athens, Piraeus, Thessaloniki, or Crete) [1][2]. The forensic pathologist issues the Medical Certificate of Death and release order once the examination is complete [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Greek and U.S. Funeral Homes, and Contact the U.S. Embassy
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel medical insurance, international health coverage, or credit-card repatriation protection, and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance team first [1][2]. Note that the U.S. government cannot pay for funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [1][7].

  • Appointing a licensed Greek funeral home (Γραφείο Τελετών): In Greece, a licensed Greek funeral home (Γραφείο Τελετών) handles the collection of the deceased from the hospital or forensic morgue, files the municipal death registration, and arranges embalming, sealed coffin preparation, and air cargo clearance [1][2][4]. The U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Greece publishes an informational Disposition of Remains Report and list of funeral homes experienced in international repatriation across Athens, Thessaloniki, and the Greek islands [1][2].
  • Appointing a receiving U.S. funeral provider and FTC protections: For repatriation to the United States, the Greek funeral director coordinates with a state-licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can locate through the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, phone +1 262-789-1880 or toll-free 800-228-6332) [5]. In the United States, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC, phone +1 877-382-4357) enforces the federal Funeral Rule, requiring U.S. funeral providers to give families an itemized General Price List (GPL) and the right to select only the goods and services they want [6]. Clarvia lists official directories and consular resources for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Notifying the U.S. Embassy in Athens or Consulate General in Thessaloniki: Report the death immediately to the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Greece (U.S. Embassy Athens phone +30 210-721-2951; U.S. Consulate General Thessaloniki phone +30 2310-376-300) [1][2]. If the legal next of kin is in the United States and cannot travel to Greece, they can sign a notarized authorization/affidavit empowering the appointed Greek funeral home to act on their behalf before Greek municipal, health, and airport authorities [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Registry (Ληξιαρχείο) Within 24 Hours and Obtain the CRDA
steps.html:
Under Greek civil registration law (Law 344/1976), a death in Greece must be declared within 24 hours of the death (or within 24 hours of the forensic pathologist's release) [2][4]:

  • Greek Death Certificate (Ληξιαρχική Πράξη Θανάτου): In practice, the appointed Greek funeral director submits the signed Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου), the deceased's U.S. passport, and a family status/birth details declaration to the municipal Civil Registry Office (Ληξιαρχείο / Lixiarcheio) of the municipality where the death occurred (for example, the Municipality of Athens or Municipality of Thessaloniki), or processes the declaration and extracts digitally via the national portal gov.gr [3][4]. The registrar retains the deceased's passport for forwarding to the U.S. Embassy and issues the official Greek Death Certificate (Ληξιαρχική Πράξη Θανάτου) alongside the burial, cremation, or transfer permit [1][2][3][4].
  • Apostille and Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): If you need the Greek Death Certificate for direct legal use in the United States, ask the funeral director to obtain the Hague Apostille from the Decentralized Administration (Αποκεντρωμένη Διοίκηση) in Greece together with an official English translation [1][2]. In addition, submit the Greek Death Certificate and the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Greece (under the U.S. Department of State, Overseas Citizens Services phone +1 888-407-4747 from the U.S. or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) to obtain the electronic Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060) [1][7]. The CRDA serves across all U.S. states as official English-language proof of death equivalent to a certificate from a state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics [1][7].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in Greece
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes and family arrangements, you may choose international repatriation or local disposition in Greece [1][2][8]:

  • Repatriating casketed human remains to the United States: Your Greek funeral home arranges mandatory arterial embalming by an accredited physician/pathologist, places the remains in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin inside a wooden outer casket, and obtains the official mortuary laissez-passer / transfer and non-contagious disease permit from the regional Public Health Directorate (pursuant to the Berlin/Strasbourg international mortuary agreements) plus the Consular Mortuary Certificate from the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Greece [1][2]. Under the federal regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone +1 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death do not require a separate CDC import permit unless the person died of a quarantinable communicable disease [8]. At the U.S. port of entry, the receiving U.S. funeral director clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [5][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in Greece and transporting ashes: Local burials take place in municipal cemeteries across Greece, while cremation is performed at licensed Greek cremation facilities (such as the Ritsona Crematorium near Chalkida, serving Athens and nationwide transfers) upon presentation of the municipal cremation permit [2][4]. If you transport cremated ashes to the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for cremated remains; carry the ashes in a sealed, non-metallic X-ray-scannable urn accompanied by the Greek Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, and the CRDA [1][2][8].

steps.title: Complete Benefit Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Probate in the United States and Greece
steps.html:
Once the Greek Death Certificate (Ληξιαρχική Πράξη Θανάτου) and the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060) are issued, complete the post-death benefit and estate steps in both countries:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately so monthly benefits stop (any payment received for the month of death or later must be returned) and to apply for monthly survivor pensions or the $255 lump-sum death payment for eligible family members [9][10]. Call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 in the United States, or, if the deceased or surviving beneficiaries resided in Greece, contact the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Athens [9][10].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone +1 800-827-1000) to claim national cemetery burial benefits, a government headstone or marker, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [11].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and State Probate Court: The court-appointed executor or administrator files the deceased's final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by the standard April 15 filing deadline (plus Form 1041 if the estate generates $600 or more in annual gross income) [12], and petitions the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state of domicile for Letters Testamentary or Letters of Administration.
  • In Greece (e-EFKA and Greek Inheritance Certificate / Κληρονομητήριο):
    • Greek social security (e-EFKA): If your family member was insured or receiving a pension in Greece, notify the Unified Social Security Fund (e-EFKA via gov.gr, phone 1555 in Greece) so the person who paid the funeral bill can apply electronically for the statutory funeral expenses reimbursement (Έξοδα Κηδείας) and eligible survivors can claim a Greek survivor pension (Σύνταξη λόγω θανάτου) (or totalized benefits under the U.S.-Greece Social Security Totalization Agreement) [13].
    • Greek estate succession, tax declaration (AADE), and Κληρονομητήριο: If the deceased owned real estate, bank accounts, or other assets in Greece, heirs or their appointed Greek lawyer/notary obtain the Certificate of Closest Relatives and Certificate of Non-Publication of a Will via gov.gr, apply to the competent Greek court/notary for a Greek Certificate of Inheritance (Κληρονομητήριο) or execute a notarial acceptance of inheritance, and file the Greek inheritance tax declaration with the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) within the statutory deadline (12 months when the deceased passed away abroad or heirs reside abroad, or 6 months domestically; note that renunciation of a Greek inheritance must be filed within 4 months, or 12 months if the deceased lived abroad or the heir resided abroad when learning of the death) [14].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your situation, in which municipality or island in Greece did the death occur, and are you planning casketed repatriation to a specific U.S. state or cremation/burial in Greece?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Israel: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Israel: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Israel: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Israel, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Israel.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Israel, medical certification, police or forensic clearance, and civil registration take place first through Israeli health and interior authorities, followed by consular registration with the U.S. Embassy in Israel (in Jerusalem or the Embassy Branch Office in Tel Aviv) for the Consular Report of Death Abroad and coordination of international repatriation or local burial [1][3][4]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Death Notification (Hoda'at Ptira) and Police or Forensic Clearance in Israel
steps.html:
Before a burial permit or international transport permit can be issued in Israel, an authorized physician must issue the official Death Notification (Hoda'at Ptira / הודעת פטירה) under the regulations of the Israeli Ministry of Health (Misrad HaBriut) [1][4]:

  • Death in an Israeli hospital or medical center: When a person dies in a hospital (for example, in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, or Haifa), the attending hospital physician pronounces the death, issues the official hospital Death Notification (Hoda'at Ptira) stating the cause of death, and transfers the deceased to the hospital mortuary [1][4]. Provide the deceased's U.S. passport (and Israeli identity card / Te'udat Zehut, if held by a dual citizen or resident) so that personal particulars are recorded accurately [1][3].
  • Death outside a hospital (residence, hotel, or public place): Call Magen David Adom (101) for emergency medical attendance so a paramedic or physician can pronounce the death, and call the Israel Police (100) [1][4].
  • Unnatural, sudden, or unattended deaths (Abu Kabir clearance): Whenever a death occurs outside a hospital or under sudden, accidental, or unclear circumstances, the Israel Police must examine the scene and issue a formal police waiver before the body can be released for burial or embalming [1][4]. If the cause of death requires a medico-legal investigation, the deceased is transferred to the National Center of Forensic Medicine (Abu Kabir) in Tel Aviv-Yafo (operating under the Ministry of Health), which performs the forensic examination or autopsy and issues the medical death notification and release [1][4]. Under Israeli law, unembalmed remains must generally be buried within 48 hours unless held in authorized refrigeration for international shipment or forensic review [1][4].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Israeli and U.S. Funeral Providers, and Contact the U.S. Embassy
steps.html:
Before signing independent funeral or air-cargo contracts, check whether your family member held travel medical insurance, international health coverage, or credit-card repatriation coverage, and notify the insurer's 24-hour assistance team first [1][7]. Note that the U.S. government cannot pay for funeral, burial, or international repatriation expenses [1][7].

  • Appointing a funeral/repatriation service or burial society in Israel:
    • For international repatriation to the United States: Appoint a Ministry of Health-authorized international funeral and repatriation service in Israel (or coordinate through the National Center of Forensic Medicine (Abu Kabir), which performs official arterial embalming required for international air transport) [1][4].
    • For local burial in Israel: Funeral and interment arrangements in Israel are organized through a licensed Chevra Kadisha (Jewish burial society), the relevant Christian or Muslim religious community burial board, or a licensed civil/alternative cemetery operator [1][13].
  • Appointing a receiving U.S. funeral home and FTC protections: If repatriating remains to the United States, the Israeli repatriation coordinator works with a state-licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can locate through the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, phone +1 262-789-1880 or toll-free 800-228-6332) [5]. In the United States, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC, phone +1 877-382-4357) enforces the federal Funeral Rule, giving you the right to receive a written, itemized General Price List (GPL) before selecting goods or services [6]. Clarvia lists official directories and consular information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Contacting the U.S. Embassy in Israel: Report the death immediately to the U.S. Embassy in Israel - either the American Citizen Services unit at the U.S. Embassy in Jerusalem (phone +972 2-630-4000; email JerusalemACS@state.gov) or the U.S. Embassy Branch Office in Tel Aviv (phone +972 3-519-7575; email TelAvivACS@state.gov) [1]. If the legal next of kin is in the United States and cannot travel to Israel, they can execute a notarized authorization/affidavit instructing the U.S. Embassy and the appointed Israeli repatriation provider on the disposition of the remains [1][7].

steps.title: Register the Death with PIBA (Misrad HaPnim) and Obtain the Te'udat Ptira, Apostille, and CRDA
steps.html:
Using the hospital or forensic Death Notification (Hoda'at Ptira) and the Burial Permit (Rishayon Kvura), the death is registered in the Israeli civil registry [1][3][4]:

  • Israeli Death Certificate (Te'udat Ptira) and Apostille: The Population and Immigration Authority (PIBA / Misrad HaPnim via the national portal gov.il, national service center 3450) registers the death and issues the official Israeli Death Certificate (Te'udat Ptira* / תעודת פטירה), which can be requested in a bilingual Hebrew-English format (or downloaded digitally by first-degree relatives holding an Israeli ID) [1][3]. For direct legal recognition in the United States, have the Israeli Death Certificate authenticated with a Hague Apostille by the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Jerusalem [1][3].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Submit the official Israeli Death Certificate (Te'udat Ptira), the hospital Death Notification (Hoda'at Ptira showing cause of death), and the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. Embassy in Israel (operating under the U.S. Department of State, Overseas Citizens Services phone +1 888-407-4747 from the U.S. or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) [1][7]. The Embassy issues the electronic Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA / eCRODA, Form DS-2060), which serves across all U.S. states as official English-language proof of death equivalent to a domestic certificate from a state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics [1][7].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in Israel
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes, religious traditions, and residence ties, you may choose international shipment to the United States or local disposition in Israel [1][4][8][13]:

  • Repatriating casketed human remains to the United States: Your Israeli international funeral coordinator arranges arterial embalming (typically at the National Center of Forensic Medicine (Abu Kabir)), places the body in a hermetically sealed metal/zinc-lined transfer casket inside an outer shipping container, and obtains the official permit for the export/transport of human remains and non-contagious disease certificate from the District Health Office of the Israeli Ministry of Health (Misrad HaBriut) along with the Consular Mortuary Certificate from the U.S. Embassy in Israel [1][4]. Under the federal rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone +1 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death may be imported into the United States without a separate CDC permit unless the person died of a quarantinable communicable disease [8]. At the arrival airport, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [5][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in Israel: If your family member was an Israeli resident (or died in Israel and is buried locally by an authorized burial society), the National Insurance Institute of Israel (Bituach Leumi) directly covers standard local burial costs (Dmei Kvura) so families are not charged for basic burial plot and interment services [13]. Private cremation services also operate in Israel on a civil contractual basis; if cremated ashes are transported to the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for cremated remains, provided they are carried in a sealed, non-metallic X-ray-scannable urn with the official death and cremation certificates [8].

steps.title: Complete Benefit Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Probate in the United States and Israel
steps.html:
Once the Israeli Death Certificate (Te'udat Ptira) and the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060) are issued, complete the survivor benefit, tax, and probate steps in both jurisdictions:

  • In the United States (SSA / FBU Jerusalem, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death promptly so monthly payments stop (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to apply for monthly survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment for eligible family members [2][9]. In the United States, call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 [9]; if the deceased or surviving beneficiaries lived in Israel, the West Bank, or Gaza, report the death directly to the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Jerusalem by emailing FBU.Jerusalem@ssa.gov [2].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone +1 800-827-1000, or via FBU.Jerusalem@ssa.gov when abroad) regarding national cemetery interment, government headstones, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [2][10].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and State Probate Court: The court-appointed personal representative files the deceased's final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by the standard tax deadline (and Form 1041 if the estate earns $600 or more in gross annual income) [11], and petitions the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or held property.
  • In Israel (Bituach Leumi and Registrar for Matters of Inheritance / Rasham HaYerushot):
    • National Insurance Institute of Israel (Bituach Leumi): If the deceased was an insured Israeli resident, surviving eligible family members (such as a surviving spouse/partner and qualifying children) can apply to the National Insurance Institute of Israel (Bituach Leumi, call center 6050) for a monthly Survivors' Pension (Gimlat She'erim) or lump-sum death grant (Ma'anak Ptira), in addition to direct coverage of local burial expenses (Dmei Kvura*) [13][14].
    • Registrar for Matters of Inheritance (Rasham HaYerushot): To release frozen Israeli bank accounts, pension/provident funds (Kupot Gemel), or real estate in Israel, heirs or executors must apply online or through an Israeli attorney to the Registrar for Matters of Inheritance (Rasham LeInyanei Yerusha / Rasham HaYerushot under the Ministry of Justice on gov.il, call center 2416) for a formal Probate Order (Tzav Kiyum Tzava'a) if the deceased left a valid will, or an Inheritance Order (Tzav Yerusha*) if intestate (noting that for non-resident decedents, applications typically include an expert legal opinion on the inheritance law of the deceased's U.S. state of domicile) [12]. Israel does not levy a separate statutory inheritance or estate tax, though capital gains or property tax rules may apply upon future sale of inherited Israeli assets.
