title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in United Arab Emirates: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Arab Emirates, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and United Arab Emirates.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in the United Arab Emirates, medical certification, police clearance, and civil death registration must first be completed through the competent emirate and federal authorities, alongside consular notification to the U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi or the U.S. Consulate General in Dubai for the Consular Report of Death Abroad and international transport or local disposition permits [1][2][3]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Notification of Death and Police Forensic Clearance in the UAE
steps.html:
Every death in the UAE must first be medically certified and cleared by local police before any civil Death Certificate, burial/cremation permit, or repatriation permit can be issued [1][3][4]:

  • Death in a UAE hospital or healthcare facility: The attending physician verifies the death, issues the official electronic Medical Notification of Death (death declaration), and arranges the transfer of the deceased to a government-approved hospital or municipal mortuary [3][4]. Provide the deceased's original U.S. passport and UAE Emirates ID (if resident) [1][3].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, at a workplace, or in a public place: Call the Police immediately on 999 and the National Ambulance on 998, and do not move the deceased [3]. Police and forensic medical examiners (such as Dubai Police Forensic Medicine or Abu Dhabi Police Forensic Evidence) attend the scene and transfer the deceased to the government forensic morgue to establish the cause of death [1][3].
  • Police No-Objection Certificate (NOC) and Public Prosecution clearance: Whether the death occurred in a hospital or outside, the next of kin, employer/sponsor, or authorized representative submits the Medical Notification of Death and original passports through the local police smart app or service center (Dubai Police, Abu Dhabi Police, or the Ministry of Interior in the Northern Emirates) [3][6]. Once any forensic examination or Public Prosecution investigation is cleared, the police issue the official Police NOC authorizing local burial, cremation, or international repatriation [1][3][6].

steps.title: Check Insurance/Employer Coverage, Appoint UAE and U.S. Funeral Providers, and Contact the U.S. Mission
steps.html:
Before paying independent shipping or mortuary fees, check all applicable insurance and statutory employer obligations [1][3]:

  • Travel insurance and UAE employer obligations: Check whether your family member held travel medical or repatriation insurance [1]. If your family member was employed in the UAE, notify their employer or visa sponsor immediately; under UAE Labour Law, the employer is legally responsible for covering the costs of preparing and repatriating a deceased employee's remains to their home country (or place of recruitment) upon the family's request [3]. Note that the U.S. government cannot pay for funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [1][9].
  • Appointing a UAE mortuary/repatriation coordinator and U.S. receiving funeral home: In the UAE, an emirate-licensed mortuary and repatriation cargo agent coordinates with the municipal mortuary and public health embalming unit (such as Dubai Municipality, the preventative medicine unit of the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DOH), or Emirates Health Services (EHS) / Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP)) [1][3][5][6]. For casketed repatriation to the United States, the UAE agent coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can locate through the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, phone +1 262-789-1880 or toll-free 800-228-6332) [7]. In the United States, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC, phone +1 877-382-4357) enforces the federal Funeral Rule, guaranteeing your right to an itemized General Price List (GPL) and to purchase only the goods and services you choose [8]. Clarvia provides official directories and consular lists for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Reporting to the U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi or U.S. Consulate General in Dubai: Report the death immediately to the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in the UAE: for deaths in Abu Dhabi or Al Ain, contact the U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi (phone +971 2 414 2200; email AbuDhabiACS@state.gov with subject code E22); for deaths in Dubai, Sharjah, or the Northern Emirates, contact the U.S. Consulate General in Dubai (phone +971 4 309 4000; email DubaiACS@state.gov with subject code E11) [1][2]. If the legal next of kin is in the United States, they can execute a notarized Letter of Authorization / Next-of-Kin Affidavit naming a local representative or funeral coordinator in the UAE to complete all formalities [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death in the UAE, Cancel UAE Residency, and Obtain the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060)
steps.html:
With the hospital's Medical Notification of Death and the Police NOC, register the death with the competent health authority in the emirate of death to obtain the official bilingual (Arabic and English) UAE Death Certificate [3][4][5][6]:

  • Emirate health authority registration:
    • Abu Dhabi and Al Ain: Apply digitally through the Abu Dhabi Government Services Portal (TAMM) under the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DOH) [4][5].
    • Dubai: Apply through the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) or Dubai's integrated bereavement service channels [2][3].
    • Sharjah and the Northern Emirates: Apply through Emirates Health Services (EHS) / Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) preventative medicine centers [3][6].
  • ICP residency visa/Emirates ID cancellation and MoFA UAE attestation: If the deceased held a UAE residency visa and Emirates ID, present the original passport and Emirates ID to the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP, or GDRFA in Dubai) to cancel the residency visa and obtain the visa cancellation confirmation required for exit clearance [2][3][4]. Have the official UAE Death Certificate attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA UAE) (available digitally via TAMM/MoFA channels) [3][4][5].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Present the attested bilingual UAE Death Certificate, the Medical Notification of Death showing cause of death, and the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in the UAE (under the U.S. Department of State, phone +1 888-407-4747 in the U.S. or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) [1][9]. The consular officer cancels the U.S. passport, issues a Consular No-Objection Certificate (NOC) for local authorities, and issues the electronic Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA / CRODA, Form DS-2060), which serves across all U.S. states as official English-language proof of death equivalent to a state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics certificate [1][9].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in the UAE
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes, you may arrange international shipment to the United States or local burial or cremation in the UAE [1][2][3][10]:

  • Repatriating casketed human remains to the United States: Your UAE mortuary coordinator obtains the official public health Embalming Certificate and Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease from the municipal/health authority mortuary unit, the Police NOC for export of human remains, MoFA UAE attestation, and the Consular Mortuary Certificate & NOC from the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in the UAE, and seals the body in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin for air cargo transport [1][2][3]. Under the federal rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone +1 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death do not require a separate CDC import permit unless the person died of a quarantinable communicable disease [10]. At the U.S. arrival airport, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [7][10].
  • Local burial or cremation in the UAE and transporting ashes: Local Muslim and non-Muslim burials and non-Muslim cremations take place at municipality-designated cemeteries and crematoria in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, and other emirates upon issuance of the Police NOC, Embassy NOC, and municipal permit [1][2][3]. If you transport cremated ashes to the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for cremated remains; carry the ashes in a sealed, non-metallic X-ray-scannable urn accompanied by the UAE Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, Police/Health clearance, and the CRDA [1][2][10].

steps.title: Complete Benefit Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Probate in the United States and the UAE
steps.html:
Once the UAE Death Certificate and the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060) are issued, complete the financial, benefit, and estate procedures in both countries:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately so monthly payments stop (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to apply for monthly survivor pensions or the $255 lump-sum death payment for eligible family members by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the regional Federal Benefits Unit serving the UAE via the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in the UAE) [1][11].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone +1 800-827-1000) regarding national cemetery interment, government headstones, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [12].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and State Probate Court: The court-appointed executor or administrator files the deceased's final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by the applicable filing deadline (plus Form 1041 if the estate earns $600 or more in gross annual income) [13], and petitions the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state of domicile for Letters Testamentary or Letters of Administration.
  • In the United Arab Emirates (MOHRE / Free-Zone Gratuity, Bank Freeze Clearance, and UAE Estate Courts):
    • End-of-service gratuity and workplace insurance: If the deceased was employed in the UAE private sector or a free zone, notify the employer and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) (or the relevant free-zone authority such as DIFC or ADGM) [3]. Under UAE Labour Law, the employer must settle unpaid wages, accrued leave, and statutory end-of-service gratuity within 10 days of death (paid to the employee's designated family beneficiary or into the court treasury), alongside any employer group life or workplace accident insurance [3].
    • Bank account freeze clearance and UAE Wills / Personal Status Courts: UAE banks freeze individual and joint accounts upon learning of an account holder's death until a UAE court order is presented [3][14][15]. If the deceased registered a non-Muslim will with the DIFC Courts Wills Service or the Non-Muslim Wills Registry at the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (ADJD), the named executor applies directly to that court for a Grant of Probate [14][15]. If no local will was registered, legal heirs apply to the Abu Dhabi Civil Family Court (under the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (ADJD)) or the Personal Status & Non-Muslim Estate Court at Dubai Courts for a Succession / Legal Heirs Certificate (Hasr Irth) and estate distribution order (under Federal Decree-Law No. 41 of 2022 on Civil Personal Status for non-Muslims, or by petitioning to apply the law/probate grant of the deceased's U.S. nationality) [3][14][15].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Australia: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Australia, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Australia.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in Australia, medical certification, coroner clearance (if applicable), and civil death registration are governed by the Australian state or territory where the death occurred, while consular reporting and international repatriation or estate administration are coordinated with the U.S. Consulates General in Australia and U.S. federal and state authorities [1][2][3]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) or State/Territory Coroner Clearance in Australia
steps.html:
Before a funeral director can transfer the deceased, register the death, or arrange cremation, burial, or international shipment, a registered medical practitioner in Australia must verify the death and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), or the State or Territory Coroner must authorize release [2][4][5]:

  • Death in an Australian hospital, hospice, or residential aged care facility: The attending doctor or authorized medical officer verifies the death, completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), and arranges care of the deceased in the facility mortuary until your appointed funeral director arrives [4][5]. Provide the deceased's U.S. passport (and Australian visa or Medicare details, if resident) so personal particulars are recorded accurately [1][4].
  • Expected death at home under palliative care: Contact the treating general practitioner (GP) or community palliative care team so a doctor can attend and sign the MCCD without triggering an emergency police investigation [4][5].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained death (at home, in a hotel, or in a public place): Call Triple Zero (000) immediately for police and ambulance attendance, and do not disturb the surroundings [1][4][5]. Where a doctor cannot certify a natural cause of death, or where the death was sudden, accidental, or otherwise reportable under state or territory law, police refer the case to the State or Territory Coroner (such as the NSW State Coroner, the Coroners Court of Victoria, or the Coroners Court of Queensland), who investigates the cause of death and issues the Coroner's certificate and burial, cremation, or repatriation release [2][4][5].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Australian and U.S. Funeral Directors, and Contact the U.S. Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent international funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel medical insurance, international health coverage, or credit-card repatriation protection, and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance team first [1][2]. Note that the U.S. government cannot pay for funeral, cremation, or international repatriation expenses [1][8].

  • Appointing a funeral director in Australia: In Australia, an accredited funeral director coordinates the transfer of the deceased, files the state or territory death registration, and arranges embalming, cremation, or international air cargo shipment [2][4][6]. You can locate accredited funeral directors experienced in international repatriation across all Australian states and territories through the Australian Funeral Directors Association (now operating as Funerals Australia, phone +61 3 9859 9966, email info@afda.org.au) or the consular lists maintained by the U.S. Mission in Australia [1][2][6].
  • Appointing a receiving U.S. funeral provider and FTC protections: For casketed repatriation to the United States, your Australian funeral director coordinates with a state-licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can locate through the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA, phone +1 262-789-1880 or toll-free 800-228-6332) [7]. Under the federal Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC, phone +1 877-382-4357), U.S. funeral providers must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) in writing and allow you to select only the goods and services you want [9]. Clarvia provides official directories and consular information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Reporting to the U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Australia: Report the death immediately to the U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Australia serving the consular district where the death occurred: the U.S. Consulate General in Sydney (phone +61 2 8219-2100, covering NSW, QLD, and ACT), the U.S. Consulate General in Melbourne (phone +61 3 9526-5900, covering VIC, SA, TAS, and NT), or the U.S. Consulate General in Perth (phone +61 8 6144-5100, covering WA) [1][2]. If the legal next of kin is in the United States and cannot travel to Australia, they can execute a notarized authorization/affidavit instructing the U.S. Consulate and the appointed Australian funeral director on the disposition of the remains [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the State or Territory BDM Registry and Obtain the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060)
steps.html:
In Australia, civil death registration is administered by the State or Territory Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) in the jurisdiction where the death occurred (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT, or NT) [3][4][5]:

  • Australian Death Certificate and Apostille: The appointed Australian funeral director submits the official death registration statement (together with the doctor's MCCD or Coroner's certificate) directly to the relevant registry - typically within 7 days at the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages (phone 13 77 88 or +61 2 8894 1555 from overseas) [4] or within 14 days at Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria (phone 1300 369 367 or +61 3 9613 5800 from overseas) [5] and the Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (phone 13 74 68), which then issues the official Australian Death Certificate [4][5]. If an Australian Death Certificate must be presented directly to a U.S. court or state authority outside the consular CRDA process, have it legalized with a Hague Apostille by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT / Australian Passport Office, phone 131 232 within Australia or +61 2 6196 0196) [2][3].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Submit the official Australian BDM Death Certificate (along with the MCCD or Coroner's finding of cause of death) and the deceased's U.S. passport to the U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Australia (under the U.S. Department of State, Overseas Citizens Services phone +1 888-407-4747 in the U.S. or +1 202-501-4444 from abroad) [1][8]. The U.S. Consulate cancels the U.S. passport and issues the electronic Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA / CRODA, Form DS-2060), which is accepted across all U.S. states as official English-language proof of death equivalent to a certificate from a state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics [1][8].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to the United States and Local Burial or Cremation in Australia
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes, you may arrange international repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to the United States, or local burial or cremation in Australia [1][2][10]:

  • Repatriating casketed human remains from Australia to the United States: Your Australian funeral director arranges arterial embalming, places the deceased in a hermetically sealed metal-lined casket or air-tray shipping container, obtains the Australian public health Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease / Embalming Certificate, Coroner or BDM export clearance, and Australian Border Force export clearance, and obtains the Consular Mortuary Certificate from the U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Australia [1][2]. Under the federal rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, phone +1 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains in a hermetically sealed casket accompanied by the official English-language death certificate stating the cause of death do not require a separate CDC import permit unless the person died of a quarantinable communicable disease [10]. At the U.S. arrival airport, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and obtains the state burial-transit permit [7][10]. (Similarly, when human remains are imported into Australia, biosecurity and border clearances are regulated by the Australian Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry and Australian Border Force.)
  • Local burial or cremation in Australia and transporting ashes: If the family chooses cremation in Australia, an independent medical referee must review the MCCD (or the Coroner must issue a cremation permit) before cremation takes place [2][4][5]. To bring or ship cremated ashes to the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for cremated remains; place the ashes in a sealed, non-metallic container that can pass airport X-ray screening and accompany them with the certified Australian BDM Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, and the CRDA for U.S. Customs declaration upon arrival [1][2][10].

steps.title: Complete Benefit Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Probate in the United States and Australia
steps.html:
Once the Australian BDM Death Certificate and the U.S. CRDA (Form DS-2060) are issued, complete the survivor benefit, tax, and estate steps in both countries:

  • In the United States (SSA, VA, IRS, and State Probate Court):
    • Social Security Administration (SSA): Report the death immediately so monthly payments stop (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to apply for monthly survivor pensions or the $255 lump-sum death payment for eligible family members (and totalized pension credits under the U.S.-Australia Social Security Agreement, if applicable) by calling the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 in the U.S. or contacting the regional Federal Benefits Unit serving Australia (FBU Manila via the U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Australia) [1][11].
    • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone +1 800-827-1000) to check eligibility for national cemetery interment, government headstones, burial allowances (VA Form 21P-530EZ), or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [12].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and State Probate Court: The court-appointed personal representative files the deceased's final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (phone +1 800-829-1040) by the applicable deadline (plus Form 1041 if the estate earns $600 or more in gross annual income) [13], and petitions the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state of domicile.
  • In Australia (Services Australia, ADNS, Superannuation, ATO, and State Supreme Court Probate):
    • Services Australia and Australian Death Notification Service (ADNS): If the deceased held Australian residency, Medicare, or Centrelink entitlements, notify Services Australia within 28 days (Centrelink bereavement line 132 300 inside Australia or +61 3 6222 3455 from overseas; Medicare 132 011) [3], and use the government-backed Australian Death Notification Service (operated by the state and territory BDM registries) to notify participating Australian banks, insurers, superannuation funds, and utilities online in one place [14].
    • Superannuation death benefits, ATO Date of Death return, and State Supreme Court Probate: If the deceased held Australian superannuation, contact the super fund trustee directly to claim death benefits (which are governed by a Binding or Non-Binding Death Benefit Nomination and held in trust outside the will unless paid to the estate's Legal Personal Representative) [16]. For Australian real estate or substantial bank/investment assets, the executor applies to the Probate Office of the relevant State or Territory Supreme Court (such as the Supreme Court of NSW, Victoria, or Queensland) for a Grant of Probate (or resealing of a foreign grant), and notifies the Australian Taxation Office (ATO, phone 13 28 61 in Australia or +61 2 6216 1111 from overseas) to lodge a final Australian Date of Death tax return if required [15][16].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your situation, in which Australian state or territory did the death occur, and are you planning casketed repatriation to a specific U.S. state or local cremation/burial in Australia?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in New Zealand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in New Zealand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and New Zealand.
introHtml: We are sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in New Zealand, the practical process involves medical certification and civil registration in New Zealand alongside consular reporting, transport clearances, and estate administration across both countries [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Certification and Coronial Clearance in New Zealand
steps.html:
• Hospital or natural deaths: If your family member died in a hospital, hospice, or under regular medical care (for example, at Auckland City Hospital or Wellington Regional Hospital), an attending doctor or general practitioner (GP) who knows the medical history issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form HP4720), which is required before burial, cremation, or international transfer can proceed [3][4].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 111 so New Zealand Police can attend. When a doctor cannot certify the cause of death or the death was sudden or unnatural, the police refer the case to the Duty Coroner through the Coronial Services of New Zealand and the National Initial Investigation Office (0800 266 800 within New Zealand or +64 4 910 4482 internationally) [3]. The coroner determines whether a post-mortem examination is required and issues the formal order releasing the body to the appointed funeral director [3].

steps.title: Funeral Directors, Insurance, and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Travel and repatriation insurance: Before signing an independent funeral or transport contract, check whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation coverage, as the insurer's assistance coordinator often appoints the local and receiving providers directly [1].
  • Appointing a funeral director in New Zealand: In New Zealand, families normally mandate a local funeral director to manage mortuary care, civil death registration, and export logistics [4]. You can locate a provider through the Funeral Directors Association of New Zealand directory [4].
  • Appointing a receiving funeral home in the United States: If you choose to return the body to the United States, your New Zealand funeral director coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can search via the National Funeral Directors Association directory [5]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral providers must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) before you commit to services [6]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank the listed organisations.
  • Notifying the U.S. Consulate: Report the death to the U.S. Embassy and Consulate in New Zealand (Consulate General in Auckland at +64 9 303 2724 or after-hours duty officer at +64 4 462 6000) [2]. Consular officers verify U.S. citizenship, cancel the U.S. passport, assist with documenting personal effects, and issue the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration, Apostille, and U.S. Consular Documentation
steps.html:
• New Zealand civil death registration: Every death in New Zealand must be registered with Births, Deaths and Marriages (part of the Department of Internal Affairs) within 3 working days after burial or cremation [4][7]. When you appoint a New Zealand funeral director, they normally submit the Notification of Death for Registration (BDM 28) on your behalf and order official New Zealand Death Certificates [4][7].
  • Apostille for cross-border recognition: Both New Zealand and the United States are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply here). If a U.S. bank, court, or state agency requires the New Zealand Death Certificate directly, request an Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs Authentication Unit (0800 872 675 within New Zealand or +64 4 460 2221 internationally) [8].
  • U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA): Once the New Zealand Death Certificate is issued, submit it to the U.S. Consulate General in Auckland so they can issue the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060) [1][2]. State and county Vital Records offices do not register deaths that occurred outside the United States, so the CRDA serves as the primary English-language death record accepted by U.S. courts, insurers, and federal agencies [1].

steps.title: International Repatriation vs. Local Burial or Cremation
steps.html:
• Repatriating human remains to the United States: If you return the body to the United States, the New Zealand funeral director arranges embalming, a hermetically sealed leak-proof shipping container, Public Health Service non-infectious disease clearance, and New Zealand Customs Service export documentation [2][9]. For entry into the United States under Centers for Disease Control and Prevention regulations (42 CFR 71.55), human remains for burial or cremation must be consigned in a leak-proof container to a licensed U.S. mortuary or cemetery and accompanied by the official death certificate or embalming/non-infectious certification, clearing U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the port of arrival (such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, or New York) before the receiving funeral home obtains the state burial-transit permit [1][10].
  • Transporting cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in New Zealand, cremated ashes are exempt from CDC infectious-disease permit rules under 42 CFR 71.55 [10]. Ashes may be carried in passenger hand luggage (in a security-screenable non-metallic urn accompanied by the New Zealand Death Certificate and cremation certificate) or shipped via international air cargo with customs clearance [9][10].
  • Local burial or cremation in New Zealand: If you choose burial or cremation in New Zealand, your local funeral director coordinates directly with the municipal cemetery or crematorium (for example, through Auckland Council or Wellington City Council) once medical or coronial clearance is signed [4][7].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Benefits, Taxes, and Probate in Both Countries
steps.html:
• New Zealand notifications, benefits, and probate: You can use the government Te Hokinga ā-Wairua End of Life Service to check which New Zealand agencies are notified automatically when the death is registered [7]. If the deceased lived or worked in New Zealand, contact Work and Income (0800 559 009) regarding stopping NZ Superannuation or applying for a Funeral Grant, check whether ACC accidental death support or KiwiSaver estate withdrawal applies, and notify Inland Revenue (0800 227 774 or +64 4 978 0779) for final tax assessment [7][11]. If the deceased left New Zealand assets exceeding the small-estate threshold (NZD 15,000 in any single financial institution), the executor or administrator must apply to the High Court of New Zealand (Wellington Registry) for Probate or Letters of Administration [7].
  • United States benefits, taxes, and probate: Report the death to the Social Security Administration (1-800-772-1213 within the U.S., or through the regional Federal Benefits Unit for overseas residents) to stop monthly payments and inquire about survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [12]. If your family member served in the U.S. military, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) regarding burial allowances, memorial items, or survivor compensation [1][12]. The personal representative must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service and open estate administration or ancillary probate in the relevant state or county Probate Court (such as a County Surrogate's Court or Superior Court Probate Division) where U.S. real property or accounts are held [1][12].

Have you decided between international repatriation of the body, cremation in New Zealand with return of ashes, or local burial in New Zealand?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in South Africa: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in South Africa, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and South Africa.
introHtml: We are sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United States dies in South Africa, the process involves medical certification and civil registration in South Africa alongside U.S. consular documentation, mortuary transport clearances, and estate administration across both countries [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Certification and Forensic Clearance in South Africa
steps.html:
• Hospital or natural deaths: If your family member died of natural causes in a hospital, clinic, or under medical care (for example, in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Pretoria, or Durban), the attending medical practitioner completes the medical section of the Notice of Death / Still-Birth (Form BI-1663 / DHA-1663), which is mandatory to register the death and issue a burial order [3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unnatural deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital or from unnatural causes, contact the South African Police Service on 10111 (or emergency services on 112 from a mobile phone) [3]. The police open an inquest docket and transfer the deceased to the provincial Forensic Pathology Service mortuary for a medico-legal post-mortem examination, after which the forensic medical officer completes the unnatural-death section of Form DHA-1663 and releases the remains to the appointed funeral undertaker [3][4].

steps.title: Funeral Undertakers, Insurance, and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Travel and repatriation insurance: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance, as the insurer's assistance service typically appoints the South African and U.S. providers directly [1].
  • Appointing a funeral undertaker in South Africa: Under South African health regulations, human remains must be handled by a designated funeral undertaker whose premises hold a municipal Certificate of Competence (often affiliated with the National Funeral Directors Association of South Africa) [4]. The South African funeral undertaker collects the deceased, submits Form DHA-1663 to register the death, and arranges mortuary preparation [3][4].
  • Appointing a receiving funeral home in the United States: If you repatriate the body to the United States, your South African undertaker coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which you can search through the National Funeral Directors Association directory [5]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized General Price List (GPL) before you commit to services [6]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank the listed organisations.
  • Notifying the U.S. Mission in South Africa: Report the death to the U.S. Embassy and Consulates in South Africa (Consulate General Johannesburg at +27 11 290 3000, Consulate General Cape Town at +27 21 702 7411, or Consulate General Durban at +27 31 310 3300) [2]. Consular officers verify U.S. citizenship, cancel the U.S. passport, assist with personal effects, and issue the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration, Apostille, and U.S. Consular Documentation
steps.html:
• South African civil death registration: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act, the death must be reported to the Department of Home Affairs (typically through your appointed funeral undertaker) using Form BI-1663 / DHA-1663 together with the deceased's passport or identity document [3]. Upon registration, Home Affairs issues a Death Report (Form BI-1680), a Burial Order (Form BI-14, required before any burial, cremation, or export), and an abridged Death Certificate, while you can apply on Form DHA-132 for a full unabridged Death Certificate for international legal use [3].
  • Apostille for cross-border recognition: Both South Africa and the United States are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply). To use a South African unabridged Death Certificate directly before U.S. courts or institutions, request an Apostille Certificate from the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO Legalisation Section in Pretoria, +27 12 351 1726) [7].
  • U.S. Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA): Submit the South African Death Certificate and DHA-1663 cause-of-death documentation to the U.S. Consulate General so they can issue the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060 / eCRODA) [1][2]. Because U.S. state and county Vital Records offices do not register foreign deaths, the CRDA serves as the official English-language death record accepted by U.S. courts, banks, insurers, and federal agencies [1].

steps.title: International Repatriation vs. Local Burial or Cremation
steps.html:
• Repatriating human remains to the United States: If you return the body to the United States, the South African funeral undertaker applies to the National Department of Health Director-General for an export permit for human remains, supported by the Death Certificate, Burial Order (Form BI-14), embalming certificate, non-infectious disease declaration, and hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin certification [4]. For entry into the United States under Centers for Disease Control and Prevention rules (42 CFR 71.55), human remains imported for burial or cremation must be consigned in a leak-proof container to a licensed U.S. mortuary or cemetery accompanied by the death certificate and embalming/non-infectious certification, clearing U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the port of entry (such as New York JFK, Atlanta, or Washington Dulles) before the receiving funeral home secures the state burial-transit permit [1][8].
  • Transporting cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in South Africa, an export permit from the National Department of Health is not required for cremated ashes, and ashes are exempt from CDC infectious-disease permit rules under 42 CFR 71.55 [4][8]. Ashes may be transported in passenger hand luggage (in a security-screenable non-metallic urn accompanied by the Death Certificate, cremation certificate, and Burial Order) or shipped via air cargo [4][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in South Africa: If you choose local burial or cremation in South Africa, your appointed funeral undertaker uses the Burial Order (Form BI-14) to book the municipal cemetery or crematorium directly [3][4].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Benefits, Taxes, and Probate in Both Countries
steps.html:
• South African estate reporting, taxes, and benefits: If the deceased left any property or assets in South Africa, the estate must be reported within 14 days of death to the Master of the High Court (in Pretoria, Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, or the relevant provincial seat) using the Death Notice (Form J294), inventory (Form J243), original will, and Death Certificate [9]. The Master issues Letters of Authority (for estates valued up to R250,000 under Section 18(3)) or Letters of Executorship (for estates exceeding R250,000) [9]. The executor must notify the South African Revenue Service (0800 00 7277) to reconcile pre-death and estate taxes, and eligible dependants of a South African contributor can claim Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) dependant benefits through the Department of Employment and Labour within 18 months of death (or report any social grant termination to SASSA at 0800 60 10 11) [10][11].
  • United States benefits, taxes, and probate: Report the death to the Social Security Administration (1-800-772-1213 within the U.S., or via the servicing Federal Benefits Unit abroad) to stop monthly benefits and apply for survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [12]. If your family member was a U.S. military veteran, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) regarding burial allowances and survivor programs [1][12]. Finally, the personal representative must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service and open estate administration or probate in the appropriate U.S. state or county Probate Court where U.S. assets or real estate are located [1][12].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Netherlands: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Netherlands, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Netherlands.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with United States citizenship or residence ties to the United States dies in the Netherlands, you will follow five sequential steps covering medical certification, civil registration, consular reporting, international repatriation or local funeral arrangements, and estate administration in both countries [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in the Netherlands
steps.html:
• Natural death in a hospital or care facility: If your family member dies in a Dutch hospital (for example in Amsterdam, The Hague, or Rotterdam) or under the care of a general practitioner (huisarts), the attending physician or municipal medical examiner performs the official external examination (lijkschouwing) [3]. In the case of a natural death, the physician completes the medical declaration of death (verklaring van overlijden, consisting of the A-verklaring for the civil registry and the sealed B-verklaring envelope for Statistics Netherlands, CBS), which is required for civil registration and transport [3][4].
  • Unexpected or non-natural death outside a hospital: If the death occurs suddenly outside a hospital or the cause of death is unclear, call the emergency number 112 so that the police and a physician attend the scene [2]. If the attending doctor cannot certify a natural cause of death, they call in the municipal forensic medical examiner (gemeentelijk lijkschouwer, a forensic physician from the GGD), who reports to the public prosecutor (officier van justitie) [3]. Only after the public prosecutor officially releases the body can the municipality grant a permit for burial, cremation, or international transport [3].

steps.title: Insurance, Licensed Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and the U.S. Consulate
steps.html:
• Checking travel and repatriation insurance: Before instructing a funeral director privately, check whether the deceased held travel, health, or repatriation insurance, as the insurer's emergency assistance center typically appoints a specialized international repatriation provider directly [1][2].
  • Funeral director in the Netherlands and statutory timeframe: Under the Dutch Burial and Cremation Act (Wet op de lijkbezorging), burial or cremation in the Netherlands may take place no earlier than 36 hours after death and no later than the sixth working day after death (unless the mayor grants an extension for international transport) [2][3]. You can appoint a certified Dutch funeral director (uitvaartondernemer, for instance affiliated with the Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen - BGNU) to handle the civil registration and transport [2][4].
  • Receiving funeral home in the United States: When repatriating the body to the United States, the Dutch funeral director coordinates with a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which can be found through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [5]. Under the Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission, you have the right in the United States to receive an itemized General Price List before purchasing services [6]. Clarvia provides this information solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank any listed organizations.
  • Reporting the death to the U.S. Consulate: Report the death to the U.S. Consulate General Amsterdam (reachable for emergencies at +31 70 310 2209 or from the U.S. at 1-888-407-4747) [2]. The consulate verifies U.S. citizenship, cancels the U.S. passport, advises on local funeral and repatriation procedures, and prepares the official U.S. report of death abroad [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Registration at the Municipality, Apostille, and U.S. Consular Report
steps.html:
• Registering the death with the Dutch municipality: The death must be registered with the Civil Registry (Burgerlijke Stand) of the Dutch municipality where the death occurred (such as Gemeente Den Haag - Municipality of The Hague - or the respective municipality of death), which in practice is usually handled by the funeral director using the A and B medical forms and the deceased's passport [4]. The municipality draws up the civil death certificate (akte van overlijden), issues the burial or cremation permit (verlof tot begraven of cremeren), and automatically updates the Personal Records Database (Basisregistratie Personen - BRP) if the deceased was registered in the Netherlands (or the Non-Residents Records Database, RNI, via the National Tasks division of Gemeente Den Haag) [4][7].
  • Multilingual extract and Apostille for the United States: You can request a multilingual extract of the death record (meertalig uittreksel, CIEC Form C) from the municipality, but because the United States is not a party to the CIEC Convention and is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, you should have the Dutch extract authenticated with an Apostille at the clerk's office (griffie) of a Dutch district court through de Rechtspraak (the Dutch Judiciary) [8].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Using the Dutch death certificate (akte van overlijden) and the medical cause-of-death statement, apply to the U.S. Consulate General Amsterdam for the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060 / CRODA) [1][2]. Because U.S. state and county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics offices do not register deaths that occur outside the United States, the CRDA serves in the United States as the official English-language proof of death for courts, banks, and government agencies [1][2].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the U.S. or Local Burial or Cremation
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body to the United States: To transport human remains from the Netherlands to a country outside the Benelux, the mayor of the municipality of death issues a mortuary laissez-passer (laissez-passer voor lijken / lijkenpas), under which the body is embalmed and placed in a hermetically sealed zinc or lead inner liner in accordance with international treaty standards and the requirements of the Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken (NederlandWereldwijd) (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and the U.S. Consulate [2][3][9]. Entry into the United States is governed by the regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55): the body must be consigned in a leak-proof casket directly to a licensed U.S. funeral home accompanied by the death certificate and an embalming/non-infectiousness statement, after which U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment at the arrival airport and the receiving funeral home obtains the local state burial-transit permit [2][10].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United States: If cremation takes place in the Netherlands, no municipal mortuary laissez-passer is required to export the ashes from the Netherlands, and cremated remains are exempt from CDC import permits under 42 CFR 71.55 [3][10]. The urn (in an X-ray translucent container accompanied by the death certificate and cremation certificate) may be transported to the United States as carry-on luggage or air cargo [2][10].
  • Local burial or cremation in the Netherlands: If you choose burial or cremation in the Netherlands, the Dutch funeral director uses the municipal burial or cremation permit to arrange the service directly with the local cemetery or crematorium [3][4].

steps.title: Survivor Benefits, Taxes, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
• Dutch pensions, notary, court filings, and taxes: If the deceased had pension or residence ties to the Netherlands, check with the Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB, Social Insurance Bank) whether the death was reported automatically via the BRP or whether you must report it yourself within 4 weeks (if residing outside the Netherlands) for the AOW state pension and any Anw survivor benefit [7]. Through the Central Register of Wills (Centraal Testamentenregister - CTR) and a Dutch civil-law notary affiliated with the Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie (Royal Dutch Association of Civil-Law Notaries / Notaris.nl), you can verify whether a will exists and obtain a certificate of inheritance (verklaring van erfrecht) to access Dutch bank accounts [11][12]. Heirs may accept a Dutch estate unconditionally, or file a declaration with the district court registry (de Rechtspraak) to accept under benefit of inventory (beneficiair aanvaarden) or renounce (verwerpen) the estate [13]. For Dutch tax purposes, survivors file an income tax return for the year of death (F-biljet) and, where applicable, an inheritance tax return (erfbelasting) with the Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax and Customs Administration; Bereavement Tax Helpline: 0800 235 8354 within the Netherlands) [14].
  • U.S. benefits, taxes, and probate: Report the death in the United States to the Social Security Administration (1-800-772-1213 within the U.S., or via the competent Federal Benefits Unit for Europe) to stop ongoing payments and claim survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [15]. If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, you can contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) regarding burial allowances or survivor benefits [1][15]. Finally, the executor or personal representative files the final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and administers the U.S. estate through the competent Probate Court or Surrogate's Court in the U.S. state where assets or real estate are located [1][2].

nl.title: Wat te doen bij een overlijden tussen Nederland en Verenigde Staten: officiële checklist in 5 stappen
nl.cardSummary: Officiële checklist in 5 stappen na een overlijden tussen Nederland en Verenigde Staten: medische verklaring van overlijden, uitvaartondernemer, aangifte bij de burgerlijke stand, consulaire formaliteiten en repatriëring (lijkenpas) of lokale uitvaart, en nabestaandenpensioen en nalatenschap.
nl.introHtml: Gecondoleerd met het verlies van uw familielid. Wanneer iemand met de Amerikaanse nationaliteit of woonplaatsbanden met de Verenigde Staten in Nederland overlijdt, doorloopt u vijf opeenvolgende stappen voor de medische vaststelling, burgerlijke aangifte, consulaire melding, repatriëring of lokale uitvaart en de afwikkeling van de nalatenschap in beide landen [1][2].

steps.title: Medische vaststelling van het overlijden en forensische vrijgave in Nederland
steps.html:
• Natuurlijk overlijden in een ziekenhuis of zorginstelling: Als uw familielid in een Nederlands ziekenhuis (bijvoorbeeld in Amsterdam, Den Haag of Rotterdam) of onder behandeling van een huisarts overlijdt, verricht de behandelend arts of schouwarts de officiële lijkschouwing [3]. Bij een natuurlijk overlijden vult de arts de verklaring van overlijden in (de A-verklaring voor de burgerlijke stand en de gesloten B-envelop voor het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek), die vereist is voor aangifte en vervoer [3][4].
  • Onverwacht of niet-natuurlijk overlijden buiten het ziekenhuis: Als het overlijden plotseling buiten een ziekenhuis plaatsvindt of de doodsoorzaak onduidelijk is, belt u het noodnummer 112 zodat de politie en een arts ter plaatse komen [2]. Wanneer de arts geen verklaring van natuurlijk overlijden kan afgeven, schakelt deze de gemeentelijk lijkschouwer (forensisch arts van de GGD) in, die rapporteert aan de officier van justitie [3]. Pas nadat de officier van justitie het lichaam officieel vrijgeeft, kan de gemeente verlof verlenen voor begraving, crematie of internationaal vervoer [3].

steps.title: Verzekering, uitvaartondernemers in beide landen en Amerikaans consulaat
steps.html:
• Controle van reis- en repatriëringsverzekering: Controleer voordat u zelf opdracht geeft aan een uitvaartondernemer of de overledene een reis-, zorg- of repatriëringsverzekering had, aangezien de alarmcentrale van de verzekeraar doorgaans rechtstreeks een gespecialiseerde repatriëringsondernemer aanwijst [1][2].
  • Uitvaartondernemer in Nederland en wettelijke termijn: Op grond van de Wet op de lijkbezorging vindt begraving of crematie in Nederland niet eerder dan 36 uur na het overlijden en uiterlijk op de zesde werkdag na het overlijden plaats (tenzij de burgemeester uitstel verleent voor internationaal vervoer) [2][3]. U kunt een gecertificeerde Nederlandse uitvaartondernemer inschakelen (bijvoorbeeld aangesloten bij de Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen - BGNU) om de aangifte en het vervoer te verzorgen [2][4].
  • Ontvangende uitvaartonderneming in de Verenigde Staten: Bij overbrenging van het lichaam naar de Verenigde Staten werkt de Nederlandse uitvaartondernemer samen met een erkende ontvangende uitvaartonderneming (licensed funeral home) in de Amerikaanse staat van bestemming, te vinden via het register van de National Funeral Directors Association [5]. Onder de Funeral Rule van de Federal Trade Commission heeft u in de Verenigde Staten recht op een gespecificeerde prijslijst (General Price List) voordat u diensten afneemt [6]. Clarvia verstrekt deze informatie uitsluitend ter oriëntatie en geeft geen aanbeveling, goedkeuring of rangschikking van genoemde organisaties.
  • Melding bij het Amerikaanse consulaat: Meld het overlijden bij het U.S. Consulate General Amsterdam (bereikbaar voor spoedgevallen op +31 70 310 2209 of vanuit de VS op 1-888-407-4747) [2]. Het consulaat bevestigt de Amerikaanse nationaliteit, annuleert het Amerikaanse paspoort, adviseert over lokale uitvaart- en repatriëringsprocedures en stelt het officiële Amerikaanse overlijdensrapport op [1][2].

steps.title: Aangifte bij de Burgerlijke Stand, Apostille en Amerikaans consulair rapport
steps.html:
• Aangifte van overlijden bij de Nederlandse gemeente: Het overlijden moet worden aangegeven bij de Burgerlijke Stand van de Nederlandse gemeente waar het overlijden heeft plaatsgevonden (zoals bij de Gemeente Den Haag of de betreffende gemeente van overlijden), wat in de praktijk meestal door de uitvaartondernemer wordt gedaan met het A- en B-formulier en het paspoort van de overledene [4]. De gemeente maakt de akte van overlijden op, geeft het verlof tot begraven of cremeren af en werkt automatisch de Basisregistratie Personen (BRP) bij als de overledene in Nederland ingeschreven stond (of het Register Niet-Ingezetenen via de afdeling Landelijke Taken van de Gemeente Den Haag) [4][7].
  • Meertalig uittreksel en Apostille voor de Verenigde Staten: U kunt bij de gemeente een meertalig uittreksel van de overlijdensakte (CIEC-model C) aanvragen, maar omdat de Verenigde Staten geen partij zijn bij het CIEC-verdrag en wel bij het Haags Apostilleverdrag, laat u het Nederlandse uittreksel voorzien van een Apostille bij de griffie van een Nederlandse rechtbank via de Rechtspraak [8].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA): Met de Nederlandse akte van overlijden en de medische doodsoorzaakverklaring vraagt u bij het U.S. Consulate General Amsterdam het Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060 / CRODA) aan [1][2]. Omdat Amerikaanse staats- en county-registers (Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) geen sterfgevallen registreren die buiten de VS plaatsvinden, geldt het CRDA in de Verenigde Staten als het officiële Engelstalige overlijdensbewijs voor rechtbanken, banken en overheidsinstanties [1][2].

steps.title: Internationale repatriëring naar de VS of lokale begrafenis of crematie
steps.html:
• Repatriëring van het lichaam naar de Verenigde Staten: Voor vervoer van een stoffelijk overschot vanuit Nederland naar een land buiten de Benelux geeft de burgemeester van de gemeente van overlijden een laissez-passer voor lijken (lijkenpas) af, waarbij het lichaam volgens de internationale verdragsregels en eisen van het Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken (NederlandWereldwijd) en het Amerikaanse consulaat gebalsemd en in een luchtdicht gesloten zinken of loden binnenkist wordt vervoerd [2][3][9]. Voor invoer in de Verenigde Staten gelden de voorschriften van de Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55): het lichaam moet in een lekvrije kist rechtstreeks worden geadresseerd aan een erkende Amerikaanse uitvaartonderneming met de overlijdensakte en balsemings-/niet-infectieverklaring, waarna de U.S. Customs and Border Protection het transport op de luchthaven van aankomst vrijgeeft en de ontvangende uitvaartondernemer de lokale transportvergunning (state burial-transit permit) regelt [2][10].
  • Vervoer van crematie-as naar de Verenigde Staten: Als de crematie in Nederland plaatsvindt, is voor het uitvoeren van de as uit Nederland geen gemeentelijk laissez-passer vereist en geldt onder 42 CFR 71.55 een vrijstelling van CDC-invoervergunningen [3][10]. De urn (in een röntgendoorlaatbare verpakking met overlijdensakte en crematieverklaring) kan als handbagage of per luchtvracht naar de Verenigde Staten worden vervoerd [2][10].
  • Lokale begrafenis of crematie in Nederland: Kiest u voor een begrafenis of crematie in Nederland, dan regelt de Nederlandse uitvaartondernemer met het gemeentelijk verlof tot begraven of cremeren rechtstreeks de reservering bij de lokale begraafplaats of het crematorium [3][4].

steps.title: Nabestaandenuitkeringen, belastingen en afwikkeling van de nalatenschap
steps.html:
• Nederlandse pensioenen, notaris, rechtbank en belastingen: Had de overledene pensioen- of woonbanden met Nederland, controleer dan bij de Sociale Verzekeringsbank of het overlijden via de BRP is doorgegeven of dat u dit (bij woonplaats buiten Nederland) binnen 4 weken zelf moet melden voor de AOW en een eventuele Anw-nabestaandenuitkering [7]. Via het Centraal Testamentenregister (CTR) en een Nederlandse notaris aangesloten bij de Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie (Notaris.nl) laat u nagaan of er een testament is en vraagt u een verklaring van erfrecht aan om toegang te krijgen tot Nederlandse bankrekeningen [11][12]. Erfgenamen kunnen een Nederlandse nalatenschap zuiver aanvaarden, of via een verklaring bij de griffie van de rechtbank (de Rechtspraak) beneficiair aanvaarden of verwerpen [13]. Voor de Nederlandse fiscaliteit dienen nabestaanden een aangifte inkomstenbelasting voor het overlijdensjaar (F-biljet) en, indien van toepassing, aangifte erfbelasting in bij de Belastingdienst (BelastingTelefoon voor nabestaanden: 0800 235 8354 vanuit Nederland) [14].
  • Amerikaanse uitkeringen, belastingen en probate: Meld het overlijden in de Verenigde Staten bij de Social Security Administration (1-800-772-1213 binnen de VS, of via de bevoegde Federal Benefits Unit voor Europa) om lopende uitkeringen stop te zetten en survivor benefits of de eenmalige overlijdensuitkering aan te vragen [15]. Als uw familielid in het Amerikaanse leger heeft gediend, kunt u contact opnemen met het Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) voor begrafenisvergoedingen of nabestaandenvoorzieningen [1][15]. Tot slot dient de executeur of vertegenwoordiger de definitieve federale belastingaangifte (Form 1040) in bij de Internal Revenue Service (IRS) en wordt de Amerikaanse nalatenschap afgewikkeld via de bevoegde Probate Court of Surrogate's Court in de Amerikaanse staat waar vermogen of onroerend goed zich bevindt [1][2].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United States Dies in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United States dies in Poland: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Poland, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United States and Poland.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a United States citizen or a person with residence or estate ties to the United States dies in Poland, the process involves five main official steps across both countries: obtaining the medical death card (karta zgonu), arranging funeral services or transport and notifying the U.S. consulate, registering the death with the civil registry together with an Apostille and the U.S. consular death report, completing international repatriation of remains or ashes (or local burial), and handling survivor benefits, taxes, and succession [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Pronouncement of Death, Karta Zgonu, and Forensic Clearance in Poland
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or from natural causes: If your family member died in a Polish hospital or hospice (for example in Warsaw, Kraków, Gdańsk, or Poznań), the attending ward physician issues the official medical death card (karta zgonu) [3]. Without the karta zgonu, the death cannot be registered with the civil registry and the body cannot be released for burial or international transport [3].
  • Death at home or in a public place and non-natural causes: In the event of a sudden death outside a hospital, call emergency medical services at 112 or 999, or contact a primary care physician (lekarz POZ) or out-of-hours medical service (nocna i świąteczna opieka zdrowotna) to pronounce the death and issue the karta zgonu [2][3]. If there is any suspicion that the death resulted from an accident, third-party involvement, or other non-natural causes, the physician or paramedics notify the Police (Policja) and the public prosecutor (prokurator), who orders the transfer of the body to the Department of Forensic Medicine (Zakład Medycyny Sądowej) for an autopsy; in such cases, both the karta zgonu and written authorization to release the body for cremation or export abroad must be issued by the competent prosecutor [2][3].

steps.title: Insurance, Funeral Directors in Poland and the U.S., and U.S. Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Verifying insurance coverage: Before signing a contract with a funeral home, check whether the deceased held travel, health, or employer insurance covering medical evacuation and repatriation of remains, as the insurer's emergency assistance center typically appoints and pays a specialized international funeral operator directly [1][2].
  • Selecting a funeral home in Poland and the United States: The family may authorize a Polish funeral home (zakład pogrzebowy) affiliated with a national industry association (such as the Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej - Polish Funeral Industry Chamber - or the Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe - Polish Funeral Association) or consult the list of local funeral homes published by the U.S. Embassy [2][4]. When repatriating human remains to the United States, the Polish funeral director coordinates with a licensed funeral home in the destination U.S. state, which can be located through the directory maintained by the National Funeral Directors Association [5]. Under U.S. federal consumer protection regulations (the Funeral Rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission), the U.S. funeral home is required to provide an itemized General Price List before you enter into an agreement [6]. Clarvia provides this information solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank any listed organizations.
  • Contacting the U.S. consular mission in Poland: The death of a U.S. citizen should be reported to the Ambasada i Konsulaty USA w Polsce (U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Poland: U.S. Embassy in Warsaw at +48 22 504 2000, U.S. Consulate General in Kraków at +48 12 424 5100, Consular Agency in Poznań at +48 61 851 8516, or from the U.S. at +1 703 988 7101) [2]. The U.S. consul confirms citizenship, cancels the U.S. passport, assists with safeguarding personal effects, and issues the official U.S. report of death abroad [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration at the USC, Multilingual Extracts, Apostille, and Form DS-2060
steps.html:
• Registering the death at the Polish Civil Registry Office: The death must be reported within 3 days of the issuance of the karta zgonu (or within 24 hours if the death resulted from an infectious disease) to the competent Urząd Stanu Cywilnego (USC, Civil Registry Office for the place of death, such as USC Warsaw or USC Kraków), a step usually completed on the family's behalf by the authorized funeral director [3]. Upon registration, the USC issues one free short-form death certificate (odpis skrócony aktu zgonu), and the family or representative may apply for additional full copies (odpisy zupełne) as well as multilingual short-form extracts on CIEC Form C under the 1976 Vienna Convention [3][7].
  • Apostille and certified translation for U.S. authorities: Because the United States is not a party to the CIEC Vienna Convention on multilingual civil status extracts, but is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Polish death certificates intended for direct legal use before U.S. courts or agencies must be authenticated with an Apostille issued by the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych in Warsaw, Legalization Division) [8].
  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA / CRODA): Based on the Polish civil death certificate (odpis aktu zgonu) and the medical death card (karta zgonu), the U.S. consul in Warsaw or Kraków prepares the official Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (Form DS-2060, also issued electronically as an eCRODA) [1][2]. Because U.S. state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics offices do not register deaths that occur outside U.S. territory, Form DS-2060 serves in the United States as the official English-language death certificate for probate, banking, and insurance proceedings [1][2].

steps.title: International Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to the U.S. vs. Local Burial in Poland
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body (casket) from Poland to the United States: Exporting human remains from Poland requires a permit from the competent county administrator (starosta) or city mayor (prezydent miasta) with county rights - issued after obtaining a sanitary opinion from the State County Sanitary Inspector (Państwowy Powiatowy Inspektor Sanitarny - Sanepid) - as well as embalming and placement of the body in a hermetically sealed casket with a metal liner [2][4]. Entry into the United States is governed by the public health regulations of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55): the hermetically sealed casket must be consigned directly to a licensed U.S. funeral home accompanied by the death certificate, a cause-of-death statement ruling out quarantinable communicable diseases, and an embalming and hermetic-sealing certificate, after which U.S. Customs and Border Protection clears the shipment at the U.S. port of entry (for example in New York, Chicago, or Los Angeles) and the receiving U.S. funeral home obtains the local state burial-transit permit [2][9].
  • Transporting an urn with cremated ashes from Poland: If cremation takes place in Poland, transporting the cremated remains to the United States is significantly simpler and is exempt from the CDC public health permit rules applicable to uncremated remains under 42 CFR 71.55 [2][9]. An urn made of X-ray scan-friendly material (such as wood, plastic, or ceramic), accompanied by the death certificate, cremation certificate, and a certificate confirming that the urn is sealed, may be carried in hand luggage (subject to airline rules) or shipped as air cargo [2][9].
  • Local burial or cremation in Poland: If you choose a traditional casket burial or urn interment at a municipal or religious cemetery in Poland, the Polish funeral home arranges the service directly on the basis of the karta zgonu and the registered Polish death certificate [3][4].

steps.title: Survivor Benefits, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Poland and the U.S.
steps.html:
• ZUS benefits, notarial or judicial succession, and tax filings in Poland: If the deceased was covered by Polish social insurance or received a Polish retirement or disability pension (or if the family paid the funeral expenses of such a person), applications for the Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy, Form Z-12, filed within 12 months of the date of death) and survivor's pension (renta rodzinna) are processed by the Polish Social Insurance Institution (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych - ZUS, or KRUS for agricultural social insurance) [10]. If the deceased left property or real estate in Poland, heirs may obtain a notarial Deed of Certification of Inheritance (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia), registered in the Inheritance Register maintained by the National Council of Notaries (Krajowa Rada Notarialna), or petition the district court (sąd rejonowy) for a judicial declaration of inheritance acquisition (stwierdzenie nabycia spadku), keeping in mind the 6-month deadline to file a declaration accepting the estate with benefit of inventory or renouncing it [11]. To claim the full inheritance tax exemption for immediate family members in Poland, heirs must submit Form SD-Z2 to the competent tax office (urząd skarbowy) overseen by the Polish tax administration (Ministerstwo Finansów (Portal Podatkowy) - Ministry of Finance Tax Portal) within 6 months of the registration of the notarial deed or the finality of the court order [12][13].
  • Benefits, taxes (IRS), and probate in the United States: Report the death to the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the U.S. or through the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Warsaw and ZUS branch offices) to stop ongoing payments and apply for survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [2][14]. If the deceased was a veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces, the family may contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) regarding burial allowances and survivor pensions [1][14]. Finally, the executor or estate administrator must file the deceased's final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and conduct probate proceedings before the competent state Probate Court or Surrogate's Court in the U.S. state where the deceased had their last domicile or held assets [1][2].

closingQuestion: So that we can tailor this guidance to your situation, in which locality in Poland did the death occur, with which U.S. state was your family member connected (for final burial or estate assets), and are you considering casket repatriation to the United States, cremation in Poland with transport of the urn, or local burial in Poland?
