pl.title: Co zrobić w przypadku zgonu między krajem Polska a Stany Zjednoczone: oficjalna lista w 5 krokach
pl.cardSummary: Oficjalna lista kontrolna w 5 krokach po zgonie między krajem Polska a Stany Zjednoczone: karta zgonu, zakład pogrzebowy, rejestracja w Urzędzie Stanu Cywilnego, formalności konsularne i przewóz zwłok lub prochów oraz zasiłek pogrzebowy i sprawy spadkowe.
pl.introHtml: Proszę przyjąć wyrazy współczucia z powodu śmierci członka rodziny. Gdy w Polsce umiera obywatel Stanów Zjednoczonych lub osoba posiadająca powiązania rezydencyjne czy majątkowe z USA, procedura obejmuje pięć głównych kroków w obu państwach: wystawienie karty zgonu, organizację transportu lub pochówku i zgłoszenie konsularne, rejestrację stanu cywilnego wraz z klauzulą Apostille i raportem konsularnym USA, międzynarodowy przewóz zwłok lub prochów albo pochówek lokalny oraz sprawy spadkowe, podatkowe i świadczenia pośmiertne [1][2].

steps.title: Stwierdzenie zgonu, karta zgonu i ewentualne czynności prokuratorskie w Polsce
steps.html:
• Zgon w szpitalu lub z przyczyn naturalnych: Jeżeli członek rodziny zmarł w polskim szpitalu lub hospicjum (na przykład w Warszawie, Krakowie, Gdańsku czy Poznaniu), lekarz prowadzący na oddziale wystawia urzędowy dokument, jakim jest karta zgonu [3]. Bez karty zgonu nie można zarejestrować zgonu ani odebrać ciała w celu pochówku lub transportu międzynarodowego [3].
  • Zgon w domu lub w miejscu publicznym oraz przyczyny nienaturalne: W razie nagłego zgonu poza szpitalem należy wezwać zespół ratownictwa medycznego pod numerem alarmowym 112 lub 999, albo skontaktować się z lekarzem podstawowej opieki zdrowotnej (POZ) lub nocnej i świątecznej opieki zdrowotnej w celu stwierdzenia zgonu i wypisania karty zgonu [2][3]. Jeżeli zachodzi podejrzenie, że zgon nastąpił w wyniku wypadku, udziału osób trzecich lub z innych przyczyn nienaturalnych, lekarz lub ratownicy powiadamiają Policję oraz prokuratora, który zleca przewiezienie ciała do Zakładu Medycyny Sądowej w celu przeprowadzenia sekcji zwłok; w takim przypadku kartę zgonu oraz pisemną zgodę na wydanie ciała i kremację lub wywóz za granicę wydaje właściwy prokurator [2][3].

steps.title: Ubezpieczenie, zakłady pogrzebowe w Polsce i USA oraz pomoc konsularna USA
steps.html:
• Weryfikacja polisy ubezpieczeniowej: Przed podpisaniem umowy z zakładem pogrzebowym warto sprawdzić, czy osoba zmarła posiadała ubezpieczenie podróżne, zdrowotne lub pracownicze obejmujące koszty transportu medycznego i repatriacji zwłok, ponieważ centrum alarmowe ubezpieczyciela zazwyczaj samo wyznacza i opłaca wyspecjalizowanego operatora międzynarodowego [1][2].
  • Wybór zakładu pogrzebowego w Polsce i w Stanach Zjednoczonych: Rodzina może upoważnić do przeprowadzenia procedur w Polsce zakład pogrzebowy zrzeszony w ogólnokrajowej organizacji branżowej (takiej jak Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej lub Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe) albo skorzystać z listy lokalnych firm pogrzebowych publikowanej przez ambasadę USA [2][4]. W przypadku przewozu zwłok do Stanów Zjednoczonych polski dom pogrzebowy współpracuje z licencjonowanym domem pogrzebowym (licensed funeral home) w docelowym stanie USA, który można wyszukać poprzez katalog prowadzony przez amerykańską organizację branżową National Funeral Directors Association [5]. Zgodnie z amerykańskimi przepisami ochrony konsumentów (Funeral Rule, które nadzoruje Federal Trade Commission), amerykański zakład pogrzebowy ma obowiązek przedstawić szczegółowy cennik usług (General Price List) przed zawarciem umowy [6]. Clarvia przekazuje te informacje wyłącznie orientacyjnie i nie prowadzi oceny, klasyfikacji ani wsparcia promocyjnego dla wymienionych podmiotów.
  • Kontakt z placówką konsularną USA w Polsce: Zgon obywatela amerykańskiego należy zgłosić w urzędzie konsularnym, którym jest Ambasada i Konsulaty USA w Polsce (Ambasada USA w Warszawie: +48 22 504 2000, Konsulat Generalny USA w Krakowie: +48 12 424 5100, Agencja Konsularna w Poznaniu: +48 61 851 8516 lub z USA: +1 703 988 7101) [2]. Konsul USA potwierdza obywatelstwo, anuluje amerykański paszport, pomaga w zabezpieczeniu rzeczy osobistych i wystawia amerykański raport o zgonie za granicą [1][2].

steps.title: Rejestracja zgonu w USC, odpisy wielojęzyczne, Apostille i raport DS-2060
steps.html:
• Zgłoszenie zgonu w polskim Urzędzie Stanu Cywilnego: Zgon należy zgłosić w terminie 3 dni od dnia wystawienia karty zgonu (lub w ciągu 24 godzin, jeżeli przyczyną zgonu była choroba zakaźna), a organem właściwym ze względu na miejsce zdarzenia jest Urząd Stanu Cywilnego (np. USC m.st. Warszawy lub USC w Krakowie), co w praktyce najczęściej załatwia upoważniony zakład pogrzebowy [3]. Po rejestracji urząd wydaje bezpłatnie jeden odpis skrócony aktu zgonu, a rodzina lub pełnomocnik może złożyć wniosek o kolejne odpisy zupełne oraz wielojęzyczne odpisy skrócone na formularzu C (zgodnie z Konwencją Wiedeńską CIEC) [3][7].
  • Klauzula Apostille i tłumaczenie dla instytucji w USA: Ponieważ Stany Zjednoczone nie są stroną Konwencji Wiedeńskiej CIEC dotyczącej wielojęzycznych formularzy, lecz należą do Konwencji haskiej z 1961 r., polskie odpisy aktu zgonu przeznaczone do bezpośredniego użycia przed sądami lub urzędami w USA opatruje klauzulą Apostille polski resort dyplomacji (Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych w Warszawie, Dział Legalizacji) [8].
  • Raport konsularny o zgonie obywatela USA za granicą (CRDA / CRODA): Na podstawie polskiego odpisu aktu zgonu oraz karty zgonu konsul amerykański w Warszawie lub Krakowie sporządza oficjalny dokument Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (formularz DS-2060, wydawany również w formie elektronicznej eCRODA) [1][2]. Amerykańskie urzędy stanu cywilnego (state or county Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics) nie rejestrują zgonów, które nastąpiły poza terytorium USA, dlatego w Stanach Zjednoczonych to właśnie raport DS-2060 pełni funkcję oficjalnego anglojęzycznego dokumentu potwierdzającego zgon w postępowaniach spadkowych, bankowych i ubezpieczeniowych [1][2].

steps.title: Międzynarodowy przewóz zwłok lub prochów do USA a pochówek lokalny w Polsce
steps.html:
• Przewóz ciała (trumny) z Polski do Stanów Zjednoczonych: Wywóz zwłok z Polski za granicę wymaga uzyskania pozwolenia właściwego starosty lub prezydenta miasta na prawach powiatu (wydawanego po zasięgnięciu opinii Państwowego Powiatowego Inspektora Sanitarnego - Sanepidu), zabalsamowania ciała i umieszczenia go w szczelnie zalutowanej trumnie z wkładem metalowym [2][4]. Przy wwozie do Stanów Zjednoczonych obowiązują przepisy sanitarne Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (42 CFR 71.55): szczelna trumna musi być zaadresowana bezpośrednio do licencjonowanego amerykańskiego domu pogrzebowego wraz z aktem zgonu, zaświadczeniem o przyczynie zgonu wykluczającym chorobę zakaźną oraz protokołem balsamacji i hermetycznego zamknięcia trumny, po czym odprawę na lotnisku docelowym (np. w Nowym Jorku, Chicago lub Los Angeles) przeprowadza U.S. Customs and Border Protection, a amerykański zakład pogrzebowy uzyskuje lokalne zezwolenie na przewóz i pochówek (state burial-transit permit) [2][9].
  • Przewóz urny z prochami po kremacji w Polsce: Jeżeli kremacja odbywa się w Polsce, przewóz prochów do USA jest znacznie prostszy i nie podlega rygorom pozwoleń sanitarnych CDC dla ciał niespopielonych (42 CFR 71.55) [2][9]. Urnę wykonaną z materiału prześwietlanego przez skanery rentgenowskie (np. drewno, tworzywo lub ceramika) wraz z aktem zgonu, świadectwem kremacji i zaświadczeniem o szczelnym zamknięciu urny można przewieźć w bagażu podręcznym (po uzgodnieniu z linią lotniczą) lub wysłać transportem lotniczym cargo [2][9].
  • Lokalny pochówek lub kremacja w Polsce: W razie decyzji o pochówku tradycyjnym lub urnowym na cmentarzu komunalnym bądź wyznaniowym w Polsce, polski zakład pogrzebowy organizuje ceremonię bezpośrednio na podstawie karty zgonu i zarejestrowanego polskiego aktu zgonu [3][4].

steps.title: Świadczenia pośmiertne, podatki i sprawy spadkowe w Polsce i w USA
steps.html:
• Świadczenia z ZUS, notarialne lub sądowe sprawy spadkowe i podatki w Polsce: Jeżeli osoba zmarła podlegała polskiemu ubezpieczeniu społecznemu lub pobierała polską emeryturę bądź rentę (albo rodzina pokryła koszty pogrzebu takiej osoby), wniosek o zasiłek pogrzebowy (druk Z-12, w terminie 12 miesięcy od dnia śmierci) oraz o rentę rodzinną rozpatruje polska instytucja ubezpieczeniowa (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych lub odpowiednio KRUS) [10]. Jeżeli po osobie zmarłej pozostał majątek lub nieruchomości w Polsce, spadkobiercy mogą uzyskać notarialny Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia, który rejestruje samorząd notarialny (Krajowa Rada Notarialna, prowadzący Rejestr Spadkowy), albo złożyć wniosek do sądu rejonowego o stwierdzenie nabycia spadku (pamiętając o 6-miesięcznym terminie na złożenie oświadczenia o przyjęciu spadku z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza lub odrzuceniu spadku) [11]. Aby skorzystać ze zwolnienia z podatku od spadków w najbliższej rodzinie, w terminie 6 miesięcy od zarejestrowania aktu poświadczenia dziedziczenia lub uprawomocnienia się postanowienia sądu należy złożyć formularz SD-Z2 we właściwym urzędzie skarbowym, który nadzoruje administracja skarbowa (Ministerstwo Finansów (Portal Podatkowy)) [12][13].
  • Świadczenia, podatki (IRS) i postępowanie spadkowe (probate) w Stanach Zjednoczonych: Zgon należy zgłosić do amerykańskiej instytucji ubezpieczeniowej, którą jest Social Security Administration (pod numerem 1-800-772-1213 w USA lub za pośrednictwem Biura Świadczeń Federalnych - Federal Benefits Unit przy Ambasadzie USA w Warszawie oraz oddziałach ZUS), aby wstrzymać bieżące wypłaty i złożyć wniosek o świadczenia rodzinne (survivor benefits) lub jednorazową odprawę pośmiertną [2][14]. Jeżeli osoba zmarła była weteranem sił zbrojnych USA, rodzina może skontaktować się z Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) w sprawie świadczeń pogrzebowych i rentowych [1][14]. Wykonawca testamentu lub zarządca masy spadkowej ma również obowiązek złożyć końcowe zeznanie podatkowe (Form 1040) w amerykańskim urzędzie skarbowym Internal Revenue Service (IRS) oraz przeprowadzić postępowanie spadkowe (probate) przed właściwym sądem stanowym (state Probate Court lub Surrogate's Court) w stanie, w którym znajdowało się ostatnie miejsce zamieszkania lub aktywa w USA [1][2].

pl.closingQuestion: Abyśmy mogli dopasować te informacje do Państwa sytuacji: 1. W jakiej miejscowości w Polsce nastąpił zgon oraz z jakim stanem w USA związana była osoba zmarła (miejsce docelowego pochówku lub położenia majątku)? 2. Czy rozważają Państwo przewóz ciała w trumnie do USA, kremację w Polsce i przewóz urny z prochami, czy pochówek na miejscu w Polsce?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Poland Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Poland Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Poland dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Poland and United States.
introHtml: We are sorry for the loss of your family member. When a Polish citizen or someone with residence or family ties to Poland dies in the United States, the practical sequence involves medical certification and state death registration in the United States alongside Polish consular clearance, cross-border transport or local funeral arrangements, and benefits and estate administration in both countries [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Certification and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Hospital or hospice deaths: If your family member died under medical care in a U.S. hospital, nursing facility, or hospice (for example, in Chicago, New York City, Los Angeles, or Newark), the attending physician or designated medical certifier completes the medical cause-of-death section in the state's electronic death registration system so a funeral home can take custody of the deceased [1].
  • Sudden, unattended, or accidental deaths outside a hospital: If the death occurred suddenly at home or in a public place without a physician in attendance, call 911 immediately. Local police and emergency medical services respond and refer unattended, accidental, or unexplained deaths to the county or city Coroner or Medical Examiner (such as the Cook County Medical Examiner in Illinois or the NYC Office of Chief Medical Examiner) [1]. The Medical Examiner or Coroner determines whether an autopsy is required, certifies the cause of death, and issues the formal release allowing the appointed funeral director to transfer the remains [1][2].

steps.title: Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and Polish Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Checking travel and repatriation insurance: Before signing a private contract with a funeral home, check whether your family member held travel, health, or employer insurance covering international repatriation, as the insurer's assistance service usually appoints and pays the U.S. and Polish funeral operators directly [2].
  • Appointing a U.S. funeral director and a receiving Polish funeral provider: In the United States, a licensed funeral director handles mortuary care, files the death certificate with the local registrar, and obtains the burial-transit permit; you can search for a licensed U.S. provider through the National Funeral Directors Association directory [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) before you select goods or services [4]. If you repatriate the body or ashes to Poland, the U.S. funeral home coordinates with a receiving Polish funeral provider (zakład pogrzebowy, such as a member of the Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej or Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe), which obtains the municipal and sanitary permits in Poland [2][5]. Clarvia supplies information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank the listed organisations.
  • Contacting the Polish Embassy or Consulate in the United States: Report the death and coordinate repatriation documentation with the competent consular district of the Embassy and Consulates of the Republic of Poland in the United States (Washington, D.C., Chicago, New York, Los Angeles, or Houston) [2][6]. The Polish Consul issues the mandatory certificate for transporting remains or ashes into Poland and accepts applications to transcribe the U.S. Death Certificate into the Polish civil registry [2][6].

steps.title: U.S. Civil Death Registration, Hague Apostille, and Polish Civil Registry Transcription
steps.html:
• Obtaining certified U.S. Death Certificates: The appointed U.S. funeral director registers the death with the county or state Vital Records / Office of Vital Statistics (which you can also look up by state through the National Center for Health Statistics directory) [1]. Request multiple certified copies of the long-form U.S. Death Certificate (showing the cause of death), as both U.S. institutions and Polish authorities require original certified copies [1][2].
  • Hague Apostille and sworn Polish translation: Both the United States and Poland are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual European CIEC Form C extracts are not issued by U.S. states, though a Polish USC can issue a Form C extract after transcription) [6][7]. To use a state-issued U.S. Death Certificate in Poland, obtain an Apostille from the Secretary of State of the U.S. state where the death occurred and have the certificate translated into Polish by a sworn translator (tłumacz przysięgły) registered with the Polish Ministry of Justice or certified by the Polish Consul [6].
  • Transcription in the Polish civil registry (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego): To settle inheritance, property, or pension matters in Poland, the apostilled U.S. Death Certificate and its sworn Polish translation must undergo transcription (transkrypcja zagranicznego aktu zgonu) into the Polish civil registry (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego - USC) [6][8]. You can file the transcription application either through the Polish Consulate in the United States or directly (in person or via a representative) at any chosen Urząd Stanu Cywilnego in Poland [6][8]. Note that when a death occurs in Poland, it must be reported to the local USC within 3 days of the medical karta zgonu (or 24 hours for infectious diseases), whereas for a death in the United States you transcribe the issued U.S. certificate (and urgent repatriation permits can be issued by the Polish Consul even before transcription is completed) [2][6][8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Poland vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating the body or cremated ashes from the United States to Poland: To bring human remains or cremated ashes into Poland, your family or the authorized Polish funeral home first obtains a permit (pozwolenie na sprowadzenie zwłok lub szczątków) from the county executive (starosta) or city mayor (prezydent miasta na prawach powiatu) competent for the intended place of burial in Poland, issued after consulting the county sanitary inspector (Państwowy Powiatowy Inspektor Sanitarny - Sanepid) [2][5]. Next, the U.S. funeral director or family submits that Polish permit to the Polish Consulate in the U.S. along with the certified U.S. Death Certificate, an official U.S. health/medical examiner non-infectious disease statement, the U.S. state burial-transit permit, and a notarized funeral director's statement confirming embalming and placement in a hermetically sealed metal casket (or sealed urn with a cremation certificate for ashes) so the Consul can issue the consular transport certificate (zaświadczenie konsula RP na przewóz zwłok lub prochów) [2]. Cross-border shipments also comply with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention containment standards (42 CFR 71.55) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection air-cargo export rules [9].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If you choose burial or cremation in the United States, the licensed U.S. funeral home uses the state burial-transit permit and medical examiner/coroner clearance (where required before cremation) to arrange the service at the local U.S. cemetery or crematory, after which you can still transcribe the U.S. Death Certificate in Poland via the Polish Consulate [1][6].

steps.title: Survivor Benefits, Taxes, and Estate or Probate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• Poland benefits (ZUS / KRUS), inheritance, and tax filings: If the deceased was insured in Poland or if a family member covered the funeral costs of a person insured or receiving a pension under the Polish system, apply to the Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (ZUS, or KRUS for agricultural social insurance) within 12 months of the date of death using Form Z-12 for the Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy) and inquire about survivor pension eligibility (renta rodzinna) [10]. To administer Polish assets or real estate, heirs either obtain a notarial Certificate of Inheritance (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia) registered in the Inheritance Register (Rejestr Spadkowy) maintained by the Krajowa Rada Notarialna or petition the Polish District Court (Sąd Rejonowy) for confirmation of inheritance acquisition (stwierdzenie nabycia spadku), bearing in mind the 6-month deadline from learning of the title to file a declaration accepting the estate with benefit of inventory or rejecting it [11]. Close family members (Zero Tax Group) have 6 months from the registration of the notarial deed or finality of the court order to submit Form SD-Z2 to the competent Polish tax office (Urząd Skarbowy via the Ministry of Finance Tax Portal) to claim complete exemption from Polish inheritance tax [12].
  • United States benefits, taxes, and state probate: Report the death to the Social Security Administration (1-800-772-1213 inside the U.S., or through the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Warsaw / ZUS Foreign Pensions Divisions under the U.S.-Poland Social Security Agreement) to stop ongoing payments and claim survivor benefits or the lump-sum death payment [13]. If the deceased served in the U.S. armed forces, contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (1-800-827-1000) regarding burial benefits or survivor pensions [13]. Finally, the executor or administrator must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and complete estate administration in the county or state Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) where the deceased resided or held U.S. property [1][13].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation: 1. In which U.S. state and city did the death occur, and which city or municipality (powiat) in Poland is the intended place of burial or estate administration? 2. Have you decided between repatriating the body in a casket to Poland, cremation in the U.S. with transport of the urn to Poland, or local burial in the United States?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Ukraine dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Ukraine and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Ukraine dies in the United States, medical certification, civil death registration, Apostille authentication, and international transport or local disposition must be coordinated between state authorities in the United States and consular, civil registry, and notarial institutions in Ukraine. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, hospice, or care facility: When the death occurs under medical supervision in a hospital or licensed care facility, the attending physician or authorized medical practitioner pronounces the death, records the medical cause of death in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes the release of your family member's body to a licensed funeral home [1]. If the person died at home under registered hospice care, contact the hospice nurse on duty first so the hospice team can verify the death without triggering an unnecessary emergency investigation.
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a medical facility: If the death occurs unexpectedly at a private residence, workplace, hotel, or public place, call 911 immediately. Local law enforcement and emergency medical services will respond and refer the death to the county or municipal Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office in Illinois, or the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner in California) [1]. The Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, performs an autopsy if required by state law, completes the medical certification of death, and issues formal release clearance before a funeral provider can transfer the deceased [1].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and Ukrainian Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member had travel insurance, international medical-assistance coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation coverage. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints the funeral coordinator and pays eligible transport costs directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral home in the United States and a receiving funeral service in Ukraine: In the United States, a state-licensed funeral director handles care of the body, civil death registration, state burial-transit permits, and international air cargo booking [1][3]. You can search for a licensed provider through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) in person and quote prices over the telephone, allow you to select only the specific goods and services you want, and obtain explicit permission before charging for embalming [2]. If repatriating remains to Ukraine, the U.S. funeral director coordinates with a receiving municipal or licensed funeral provider in Ukraine (ритуальна служба, such as the municipal enterprise КП Ритуальна служба in Kyiv or Lviv) to handle customs reception and cemetery interment. Clarvia supplies directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate of Ukraine in the United States: Report the death immediately to the Embassy of Ukraine in the United States (consular emergency phone: +1 202-349-2947; email: consul_us@mfa.gov.ua) or the competent Ukrainian Consulate General in New York, Chicago, San Francisco, or Houston (or the 24/7 hotline of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine at +38 044 238-15-88, email: cons_or@mfa.gov.ua) [5][6]. Consular officers guide the family on required repatriation documents, register or verify civil status records, and process the deceased's Ukrainian passport for official cancellation [5][6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United States, Hague Apostille, and Ukrainian Recognition
steps.html:
• Obtaining certified U.S. Death Certificates (Vital Records): Your appointed U.S. funeral director gathers the deceased's personal and demographic information and files the death record with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records in the U.S. state of death [1]. You can verify the competent state Vital Records agency through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) directory [1]. Request multiple certified copies of the long-form U.S. Death Certificate.
  • Hague Apostille and Ukrainian translation vs. Consular registration: Neither the United States nor Ukraine uses the multilingual CIEC Form C, so U.S. civil records must be authenticated for official use in Ukraine:
    • Hague Apostille and certified Ukrainian translation: Because both the United States and Ukraine are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille on the certified U.S. Death Certificate from the Office of the Secretary of State in the U.S. state where the death certificate was issued, followed by a notarized translation into Ukrainian [5][6]. Once apostilled and translated (with the translation notarized in Ukraine or certified by a Ukrainian consulate), the U.S. Death Certificate is legally recognized across Ukraine by civil registry departments (відділ державної реєстрації актів цивільного стану - ДРАЦС of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine), Administrative Service Centers (ЦНАП), notaries, and pension authorities without requiring duplicate civil registration [6][9].
    • Consular registration and domestic deadlines: Where a death of a Ukrainian citizen abroad is registered directly by a Ukrainian diplomatic mission or consulate, the consulate issues a Ukrainian Death Certificate (свідоцтво про смерть) and transmits the record to the State Register of Civil Status Acts ( whereas for deaths occurring inside Ukraine, declaration to the ДРАЦС or via the Дія portal is ordinarily required within 3 days to obtain the death certificate and funeral grant extract) [5][7][9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Ukraine vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating a casket or cremated ashes from the United States to Ukraine:
    • U.S. export and transit preparation: For casket repatriation, the U.S. funeral director embalms the body, seals it inside a hermetically soldered zinc-lined or metal shipping casket, and obtains the state burial-transit permit, a medical/health department certificate confirming the absence of communicable disease, and a mortuary certificate confirming no unauthorized objects are inside the casket [4][5]. (In reverse cross-border cases entering the United States, human remains importation is governed by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention regulations under 42 CFR 71.55 and cleared by U.S. Customs and Border Protection [4]).
    • Ukrainian border and consular requirements: Under Ukrainian border and sanitary rules overseen by the Embassy of Ukraine in the United States and Ukraine's sanitary-epidemiological and customs authorities, importing a casket or an urn with cremated ashes into Ukraine requires: (1) a notarized statement from the next of kin expressing their wishes regarding the place and manner of burial in Ukraine; (2) the U.S. Death Certificate bearing a Hague Apostille and notarized Ukrainian translation; (3) the health/non-infectious disease certificate and the certificate of absence of foreign objects inside the hermetically sealed casket or urn, each bearing an Apostille and notarized Ukrainian translation; and (4) submission of the deceased's Ukrainian passport to the Embassy or Consulate for official processing [5][6]. Because civil aviation into Ukraine is currently suspended, international air cargo shipments typically fly to a neighboring European hub airport (such as Warsaw, Krakow, Rzeszów, or Chisinau) for licensed overland hearse transfer across the Ukrainian state border.
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United States without repatriation, the U.S. funeral director obtains the county/state disposition permit locally, and the family still submits the apostilled U.S. Death Certificate and the deceased's Ukrainian passport to the Embassy of Ukraine in the United States so Ukrainian civil and pension records can be updated [5][6].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Funeral Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Ukraine and the United States
steps.html:
• Funeral grants, survivor pensions, and inheritance in Ukraine:
    • Pension Fund of Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України): If the deceased received a Ukrainian pension, the person who paid for the funeral can apply to any service center of the Pension Fund of Ukraine (or online through the Diia Portal / PFU electronic portal) for the statutory funeral benefit (допомога на поховання, equal to two months' pension for a civilian pensioner or three months' pension for a military pensioner, with no statutory time limit on claiming) as well as any unpaid pension up to the month of death [7]. Eligible dependent family members can also apply for a survivor's pension (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) supported by the Free Legal Aid System of Ukraine (Безоплатна правнича допомога) [8].
    • Opening an inheritance case within 6 months (Нотаріальна палата України): Under the Civil Code of Ukraine, heirs who did not permanently reside with the deceased at the time of death must personally submit an application to accept the inheritance (заява про прийняття спадщини) to a Ukrainian state or private notary within 6 months from the date of death (or, under martial law rules where death registration was delayed by more than one month, within 6 months from the date of civil death registration) [9][10]. The notary registers the case in the Inheritance Register (Спадковий реєстр of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine), and families can check open inheritance files via the Notary Chamber of Ukraine [9][10]. If heirs remain in the United States, they can sign the inheritance acceptance statement before a Ukrainian consular officer (or before a U.S. notary public with a Hague Apostille and certified Ukrainian translation) and mail it to the notary in Ukraine before the 6-month deadline expires [9].
  • Social Security, Veterans benefits, tax filings, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA) and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member had a U.S. Social Security number or worked in the United States, report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the relevant U.S. Federal Benefits Unit if survivors reside abroad) to stop ongoing payments and check eligibility for monthly survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment [11]. If the deceased served in the U.S. armed forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial allowances and memorial benefits [13].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate Court: The personal representative or survivor responsible for the estate must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040, or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens with U.S. source income) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [12]. Any U.S. bank accounts, real property, or other assets held solely in the deceased's name without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or held property.

In which U.S. state and county did the death occur, and has a licensed U.S. funeral home or Medical Examiner already taken custody of your family member? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to a specific city in Ukraine, or arrange burial or cremation in the United States?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in the United States, medical certification, civil registration, consular reporting, and international repatriation or local burial or cremation must be coordinated between state and county authorities in the United States and the relevant constituent nation in the United Kingdom (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland). Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, hospice, or care facility: When the death occurs under medical care in a hospital or licensed care facility, the attending physician or authorized medical practitioner pronounces the death, completes the medical cause-of-death certification in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes the release of your family member's body to a licensed funeral home [1][5]. If the death occurred at home under registered hospice care, contact the hospice nurse on duty first so the hospice team can verify the death without triggering an unnecessary emergency investigation.
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a medical facility: If the death occurs unexpectedly at a private residence, hotel, workplace, or public space, call 911 immediately [5]. Local law enforcement and emergency medical services will respond and refer the death to the county or municipal Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Miami-Dade County Medical Examiner Department in Florida, or the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner in California) [1][5]. For sudden, unexplained, or unattended deaths, the Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, conducts an autopsy (post-mortem) if required by state statute, completes the medical certification of death, and issues official release clearance before a funeral home can take custody of the deceased [5].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and British Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international medical-assistance coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation coverage [5][6]. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints an approved international funeral director and covers eligible repatriation or local disposition costs directly [5][6].
  • Appointing a licensed funeral home in the United States and a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom: In the United States, a state-licensed funeral director handles physical care of the body, civil death registration, state burial-transit permits, and international air cargo booking [1][3][5]. You can locate a licensed U.S. provider through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must provide an itemized General Price List (GPL) in person and quote prices over the telephone, allow you to purchase only the specific goods and services you choose, and obtain explicit permission before charging for embalming [2]. If returning the body or ashes to the United Kingdom, the U.S. funeral home coordinates with a receiving UK funeral director registered with the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (phone: +44 1279 726777; email: info@saif.org.uk) or the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) [7]. Clarvia supplies directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the British Embassy or Consulate in the United States: Report the death to the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (phone: +44 20 7008 5000 in London) or the nearest British Embassy or Consulate General in the United States (such as the British Embassy in Washington, D.C. at +1 202-588-6500, or the British Consulates General in New York, Los Angeles, Miami, Chicago, Houston, Boston, Atlanta, or San Francisco) [5][6]. British consular staff provide guidance on local U.S. procedures, international funeral options, and cancelling the deceased's British passport, though the UK government cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [5][6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United States, Apostille Rules, and UK Recognition
steps.html:
• Obtaining certified U.S. Death Certificates (Vital Records): Your appointed U.S. funeral director gathers the deceased's personal details and files the death record with the local county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the state statutory deadline (typically 3 to 5 days after death) [1][5]. You can verify the competent state Vital Records office through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) directory [1]. Order multiple certified copies of the long-form U.S. Death Certificate (showing the cause of death), as UK authorities, banks, insurers, and probate registries require original certified copies [5][6]. (Note: In reverse cases when a U.S. citizen dies outside the United States, the U.S. Embassy issues a Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad - CRDA Form DS-2060).
  • UK recognition and Hague Apostille: Because U.S. death certificates are issued in English, no translation is required for the United Kingdom, and neither the United States nor the United Kingdom uses the multilingual CIEC Form C [6]. You do not have to register a death that occurred in the United States at a local UK Register Office (where domestic deaths must be registered within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland), though you may optionally apply to the FCDO Overseas Registration Unit for a UK consular death registration if the deceased was a British national [6]. If a UK court, land registry, or financial institution requires formal authentication of the U.S. Death Certificate, the U.S. funeral director can obtain a Hague Apostille from the Office of the Secretary of State in the U.S. state where the certificate was issued.

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating non-cremated human remains from the United States to the United Kingdom:
    • U.S. export preparation: For full-body transport, the U.S. funeral director embalms the body, seals it inside a leak-proof, hermetically sealed metal liner or shipping casket, and obtains the certified U.S. Death Certificate, a county or state burial-transit permit, an embalming certificate, and a public health certificate confirming the absence of communicable disease [4][5]. (Under 42 CFR 71.55 of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and U.S. Customs and Border Protection rules, leak-proof containment and cause-of-death documentation also govern cross-border human remains shipments entering or transiting the United States [4]).
    • Clearance for burial or cremation upon arrival in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland: Your receiving UK funeral director presents the certified U.S. Death Certificate and U.S. export/burial-transit permit to customs at the UK airport of arrival [6]. To bury a body repatriated from abroad in England and Wales, the local Register Office in the district where the burial will take place issues a Certificate of No Liability to Register; however, if the repatriated body is to be cremated in England and Wales, or if the death abroad was sudden, violent, or unnatural, the receiving funeral director must notify the local Coroner (who issues Cremation Form 6 or conducts an investigation if required, and also issues an Out-of-England Order / Form 104 whenever remains are moved out of England and Wales) [6].
    • Clearance for burial or cremation upon arrival in Scotland (DCRS): If your family member's body is repatriated to Scotland, burial or cremation cannot legally proceed until the receiving funeral director obtains formal authorization from the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS, email: his.dcrs@nhs.scot), submitting scans of the U.S. Death Certificate, the deceased's passport, the U.S. removal/transit permit, and Form A1 if cremation is planned (typically reviewed within 5 working days) [8].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United Kingdom or choosing local U.S. burial/cremation: If cremation takes place in the United States (after county Coroner/Medical Examiner clearance), cremated ashes can be transported to the United Kingdom in a security-scannable non-metallic urn accompanied by the certified U.S. Death Certificate and cremation certificate without requiring a UK Coroner permit [5][6]. If the family chooses local burial or cremation in the United States, the U.S. funeral director obtains the county/state disposition permit locally [1][5].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Probate in the United Kingdom and the United States
steps.html:
• Notifications, pensions, and probate in the United Kingdom:
    • Tell Us Once and Department for Work and Pensions (DWP): If your family member normally lived in England, Scotland, or Wales (or received a UK State Pension), you can use the GOV.UK Tell Us Once service by calling the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012 from the UK, or the International Pension Centre at +44 191 218 7777 from abroad) once you have the certified U.S. Death Certificate [6][9]. Tell Us Once notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), DWP, the Passport Office, DVLA, and local councils in one step [9]. Eligible surviving spouses or civil partners under State Pension age may also claim Bereavement Support Payment from the Department for Work and Pensions (apply within 3 months of death to receive the full 18 monthly payments) [10].
    • UK Grant of Probate or Confirmation: If the deceased held UK real property or sole UK bank accounts above small-estate thresholds, the executor or administrator reports the estate to HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) and applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland [11].
  • Social Security, Veterans benefits, tax filings, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA) and U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member had a U.S. Social Security number or worked in the United States, report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in London if survivors live in the UK) to stop ongoing monthly payments and inquire about survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment (note that the US-UK Social Security Totalization Agreement may allow combined credits) [12]. If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (phone: +1 800-827-1000) regarding burial allowances and memorial benefits [14].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate Court: The personal representative or survivor responsible for the estate must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040, or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens with U.S. source income) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [13]. Any U.S. bank accounts or property held solely in the deceased's name without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or owned assets.

closingQuestion: To help tailor the exact local steps for your family: 1. In which U.S. state and county did the death occur, and in which UK constituent nation (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) was your family member resident or will final arrangements take place? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body, arrange cremation in the United States and bring the ashes to the United Kingdom, or hold the burial or cremation in the United States?

cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Germany dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Germany and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Germany dies in the United States, medical certification, civil death registration, Hague Apostille authentication, and international repatriation or local disposition must be coordinated between state and county authorities in the United States and consular, civil registry, and probate authorities in Germany. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, hospice, or care facility: When the death occurs under medical supervision in a hospital or licensed care facility, the attending physician or authorized medical practitioner pronounces the death, records the medical cause of death in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes the release of your family member's body to a licensed funeral home [1]. If the death occurred at home under registered hospice care, call the hospice nurse on duty first so the hospice team can verify the death without triggering an unnecessary emergency investigation.
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a medical facility: If the death occurs unexpectedly at a private residence, hotel, workplace, or public place, call 911 immediately. Local law enforcement and emergency medical services will respond and refer the death to the county or municipal Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Miami-Dade County Medical Examiner Department in Florida, or the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner in California) [1]. For sudden, unexplained, or unattended deaths, the Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, performs an autopsy if required by state statute, signs the medical portion of the death certificate, and issues official release clearance before a funeral home can take custody of the deceased [1].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and German Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member had travel insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung), international medical-assistance coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation coverage. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints the coordinating funeral provider and manages eligible transport costs directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral home in the United States and a receiving funeral provider in Germany: In the United States, a state-licensed funeral director handles physical care of the body, civil death registration, state burial-transit permits, and airport cargo booking [1][3]. You can locate a licensed U.S. provider through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) in person and quote prices over the telephone, allow you to purchase only the specific goods and services you select, and obtain explicit permission before charging for embalming [2]. If returning the body or cremated ashes to Germany, the U.S. funeral home coordinates with a receiving German funeral provider (Bestattungsunternehmen), which you can locate through the professional association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (phone: +49 211 16008-10; email: info@bestatter.de), operating in compliance with the relevant German state burial law (Landesbestattungsgesetz) and mandatory cemetery interment rule (Friedhofszwang) [6][7]. Clarvia supplies directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the German Embassy or Consulate in the United States: Report the death to the German Missions in the United States (the German Embassy in Washington, D.C. at +1 202-298-4000, or the competent German Consulate General in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, or San Francisco, under the Federal Foreign Office / Auswärtiges Amt) [5][6]. German consular officers assist with notifying next of kin in Germany, issuing consular mortuary transport certificates (Leichenpass or Urnenbescheinigung), and accepting applications for German civil death registration, though public funds cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [5][6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United States, Hague Apostille, and German Standesamt Registration
steps.html:
• Obtaining certified U.S. Death Certificates (Vital Records): Your appointed U.S. funeral director gathers the deceased's personal details and files the death record with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the state statutory deadline [1]. You can verify the competent state Vital Records office through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) directory [1]. Order multiple certified copies of the long-form U.S. Death Certificate (including the cause of death, which German consulates require for mortuary transit permits) [1][6]. (Note: In reverse cases when a U.S. citizen dies in Germany, the local German Standesamt registers the death by the third following working day under § 28 of the Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) and issues a German Sterbeurkunde and multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention, while the U.S. mission issues a Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad - CRDA Form DS-2060 [8]).
  • Hague Apostille and German subsequent registration (Nachbeurkundung under § 36 PStG): Because the United States is not a party to the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention, U.S. authorities do not issue multilingual CIEC Form C certificates. To use a U.S. Death Certificate in Germany, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Office of the Secretary of State in the U.S. state where the certificate was issued, along with a certified German translation by a sworn translator (beeidigter Übersetzer) [5][6]. If the deceased was a German citizen, eligible family members (parents, children, spouse, or registered partner) can also apply under § 36 of the Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) for subsequent registration of the foreign death (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland) at the German Standesamt of the deceased's last German residence (or at Standesamt I in Berlin if the deceased never resided in Germany), either directly or through the German Missions in the United States, to obtain a German Sterbeurkunde [5][9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Germany vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating a casket (body) from the United States to Germany (Leichenpass):
    • U.S. preparation and German consular Leichenpass: Under German state burial laws and the 1937 International Berlin Agreement framework, full-body repatriation to Germany must be handled by a licensed funeral home [6][7]. The U.S. funeral director embalms the body, seals it inside an airtight soldered zinc liner (verlöteter Zinksarg) or hermetically sealed metal shipping casket, and obtains the certified U.S. Death Certificate (with cause of death), a county/state burial-transit permit, a medical certificate confirming no contagious disease, and an embalming/sealing affidavit [4][6][7]. The U.S. funeral director submits these documents (and the deceased's German passport) to the competent German Consulate General to obtain the consular corpse transit permit (Leichenpass) required for customs clearance and entry into Germany [5][6]. (Under 42 CFR 71.55 of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and U.S. Customs and Border Protection rules, leak-proof containment and cause-of-death documentation likewise govern human remains shipments entering or transiting the United States [4]).
  • Repatriating cremated ashes to Germany (Friedhofszwang and Urnenbescheinigung):
    • Mandatory cemetery acceptance certificate (Übernahmebescheinigung): Because Germany enforces mandatory cemetery interment (Friedhofszwang) even for cremated remains, private individuals are not permitted to carry or ship an urn with cremated ashes into Germany themselves [5][6]. Instead, the urn must be shipped directly to a German cemetery administration (Friedhofsverwaltung) or a commissioned German funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen) [6]. Before the German Consulate in the United States issues the consular urn certificate (Urnenbescheinigung), you must present the certified U.S. Death Certificate, the cremation certificate, the deceased's passport, and the written acceptance confirmation (Übernahmebescheinigung) from the receiving German cemetery or funeral home [6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United States without repatriation to Germany, the U.S. funeral director obtains the county/state disposition permit locally, and the family uses the apostilled U.S. Death Certificate to notify German authorities and pension bodies [1][5].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Germany and the United States
steps.html:
• Pensions, health insurance, and succession (Erbschein) in Germany:
    • Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days) and Deutsche Rentenversicherung: If the deceased received a German statutory pension, notify the pension payment office (Renten Service der Deutschen Post) immediately and, if there is a surviving spouse or registered partner, apply within 30 days of death for the three-month transition advance (Vorschuss für das Sterbevierteljahr) [10][11]. File the formal application for a survivor's or orphan's pension (Witwen-/Witwerrente or Waisenrente) with the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (free service telephone in Germany: 0800 1000 4800) [10][11]. Also notify the deceased's German statutory health insurer (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung).
    • German Probate Court (Nachlassgericht), Erbschein, and Central Register of Wills: Anyone holding a handwritten will must deliver it to the competent German probate court (Nachlassgericht at the Amtsgericht of the deceased's last German residence), while the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister of the Bundesnotarkammer, phone: 0800 35 50 100; email: info@testamentsregister.de) notifies the court of officially deposited wills [12]. If heirs need a German Certificate of Inheritance (Erbschein) to access German bank accounts or real estate - or wish to disclaim an indebted estate within the statutory deadline (6 weeks, or 6 months if the deceased resided abroad or the heir is abroad when learning of the inheritance) - they can file the declaration before the German Nachlassgericht, a German notary, or a consular officer at the German Missions in the United States [5][12].
  • Social Security, Veterans benefits, tax filings, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA) and U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member had a U.S. Social Security number or worked in the United States, report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the U.S. Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Consulate General in Frankfurt if survivors live in Germany) to stop ongoing monthly payments and check eligibility for survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment (note that the US-German Social Security Totalization Agreement coordinates combined coverage credits) [13]. If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial and memorial benefits [15].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate Court: The personal representative or survivor responsible for the estate must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040, or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens with U.S. source income) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [14]. Any U.S. bank accounts or real estate held solely in the deceased's name without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or owned assets.

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United States: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Italy dies in United States: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United States, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Italy and United States.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Italy dies in the United States, medical certification, civil death registration, Hague Apostille authentication, consular transcription, and international repatriation or local burial or cremation must be coordinated between state and county authorities in the United States and consular, municipal, and tax institutions in Italy. Below are the five official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in the United States
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital, hospice, or care facility: When the death occurs under medical supervision in a hospital or licensed care facility, the attending physician or authorized medical practitioner pronounces the death, completes the medical cause-of-death certification in the state's Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and authorizes the release of your family member's body to a licensed funeral home [1]. If the death occurred at home under registered hospice care, call the hospice nurse on duty first so the hospice team can verify the death without triggering an unnecessary emergency investigation.
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a medical facility: If the death occurs unexpectedly at a private residence, hotel, workplace, or public space, call 911 immediately. Local law enforcement and emergency medical services will respond and refer the death to the county or municipal Coroner or Medical Examiner (for example, the Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York City, the Miami-Dade County Medical Examiner Department in Florida, or the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner in California) [1]. For sudden, unexplained, or unattended deaths, the Coroner or Medical Examiner investigates the cause and manner of death, performs an autopsy if required by state statute, signs the medical portion of the death certificate, and issues official release clearance before a funeral home can take custody of the deceased [1].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Providers in Both Countries, and Italian Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Check travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member had travel insurance, international medical-assistance coverage, or employer-sponsored repatriation coverage. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints the coordinating funeral provider and manages eligible transport costs directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral home in the United States and a receiving funeral provider in Italy: In the United States, a state-licensed funeral director handles physical care of the body, civil death registration, state burial-transit permits, and coordination with the Italian consulate [1][3][5]. You can locate a licensed U.S. provider through the directory of the National Funeral Directors Association [3]. Under the Federal Trade Commission Funeral Rule, U.S. funeral homes must give you an itemized General Price List (GPL) in person and quote prices over the telephone, allow you to purchase only the specific goods and services you select, and obtain explicit permission before charging for embalming [2]. If returning the body or cremated ashes to Italy, the U.S. funeral home coordinates with an authorized receiving Italian funeral provider (impresa funebre autorizzata), identifiable through national trade federations such as the Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (FENIOF) or Federcofit [7]. Clarvia supplies directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank listed organisations.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate of Italy in the United States: Report the death to the Italian Consulate General or Embassy Consular Chancery with jurisdiction over the U.S. state where the death occurred (such as the Embassy of Italy in Washington, D.C., or the Italian Consulates General in New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Miami, Detroit, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, or San Francisco, operating under the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale - MAECI) [5][6]. The Italian consulate requests municipal burial/interment clearance (nulla osta) from the destination Italian municipality (Comune), issues the consular Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario), and transmits the death record to Italy for civil registry transcription [5][6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United States, Hague Apostille, and Italian Municipal Transcription
steps.html:
• Obtaining certified U.S. Death Certificates (Vital Records): Your appointed U.S. funeral director gathers the deceased's personal details and files the death record with the county health department or state Office of Vital Statistics / Vital Records within the state statutory deadline [1]. You can verify the competent state Vital Records office through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) directory [1]. Order multiple certified copies of the long-form (extended) U.S. Death Certificate showing the exact cause of death (and for married women, ensuring the maiden surname is clearly recorded as required by Italian civil status rules) [1][5]. (Note: In reverse cases when a death occurs in Italy, the declaration of death is filed within 24 hours with the Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune under D.P.R. 396/2000 overseen by the Ministero dell'Interno to obtain the atto di morte, burial permit, and multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention, while the U.S. mission issues a Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad - CRDA Form DS-2060 [8]).
  • Hague Apostille and compulsory transcription in Italy (Trascrizione dell'atto di morte): Because the United States is not a party to the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention, U.S. authorities do not issue multilingual Form C extracts. For the U.S. Death Certificate to be valid in Italy, the death of an Italian citizen must be transcribed into the civil status registers (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian Comune of last residence or AIRE registration [5][8]:
    • Obtain a Hague Apostille on the original long-form U.S. Death Certificate from the Office of the Secretary of State in the U.S. state that issued the certificate [5][6].
    • Prepare a complete, certified Italian translation of the apostilled Death Certificate and submit both, together with the consular transcription application form and proof of the deceased's Italian citizenship (Italian passport or birth certificate), to the competent Italian Consulate in the United States for official transmission to the Italian Comune [5][6].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Italy vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United States
steps.html:
• Repatriating a casket (body) or cremated ashes from the United States to Italy (Passaporto Mortuario):
    • Do not book flights before consular authorization: Because the United States is not a party to the 1937 International Berlin Agreement (under which an Italian Comune issues a domestic Passaporto Mortuario for intra-treaty transfers), repatriating a body or cremated ashes from the United States to Italy requires a consular Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) issued by the competent Italian Consulate under the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale and the Italian Mortuary Police Regulation (D.P.R. 285/1990) [5][6]. Flights must only be booked after the consulate confirms receipt of the municipal nulla osta and issues the Passaporto Mortuario [5].
    • Required U.S. and Italian mortuary documents: For a body (salma), the U.S. funeral director must embalm the remains, place them in a double casket with a hermetically soldered zinc or metal inner liner (doppia cassa con cofano metallico saldato) meeting D.P.R. 285/1990 standards, and provide: (1) the long-form U.S. Death Certificate with Hague Apostille and Italian translation; (2) a statement from the County/State Health Department (comparable to the Italian ASL certificate) with Apostille and translation certifying the cause of death and confirming the deceased did not die of a contagious/infectious disease; (3) a notarized Funeral Director affidavit confirming compliance with Italian mortuary packaging rules and absence of unauthorized items; and (4) the county/state burial-transit permit [4][5][6]. (Under 42 CFR 71.55 of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and U.S. Customs and Border Protection rules, leak-proof containment and cause-of-death documentation also govern cross-border human remains shipments entering or transiting the United States [4]).
    • Repatriating cremated ashes (ceneri): If cremation takes place in the United States, the U.S. funeral home or family submits the apostilled and translated long-form U.S. Death Certificate, the official cremation certificate (with Apostille and translation), and the flight/destination details to the Italian Consulate so the consulate can obtain the municipal nulla osta, place consular seals on the urn, and issue the Passaporto Mortuario [5][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United States: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United States without repatriation, the U.S. funeral director obtains the county/state disposition permit locally, and the family still submits the apostilled and translated U.S. Death Certificate to the Italian Consulate to transcribe the death in the Italian Comune [1][5].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Italy and the United States
steps.html:
• Survivor pensions, wills, and succession tax filing (Dichiarazione di successione) in Italy:
    • INPS Survivor Pension (Pensione ai superstiti): If the deceased held an Italian pension or qualifying contribution record, eligible surviving family members (spouse or civil union partner, minor/student/disabled children, or dependent parents/siblings in specific cases) must submit a claim for the survivor pension (pensione di reversibilità or pensione indiretta) and any accrued unpaid pension (ratei maturati e non riscossi) to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS) online or through an accredited Italian Patronato office in the United States or Italy [9].
    • Will search and Dichiarazione di successione within 12 months: Families can verify whether a will was deposited in Italy through the General Register of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti) or with the assistance of an Italian notary via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [11]. Heirs and legatees must file the electronic inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate within 12 months from the date of death (an exemption applies only to a spouse and direct-line relatives if the estate includes no real estate and does not exceed EUR 100,000) [10].
  • Social Security, Veterans benefits, tax filings, and probate in the United States:
    • Social Security Administration (SSA) and U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA): If your family member had a U.S. Social Security number or worked in the United States, report the death to the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 (or through the U.S. Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Consulate General in Naples if survivors live in Italy) to stop ongoing payments and apply for survivor benefits or the $255 lump-sum death payment (note that the US-Italy Social Security Agreement coordinates combined work credits) [12]. If the deceased served in the U.S. Armed Forces, contact the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs regarding burial and memorial benefits [14].
    • Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and U.S. State Probate Court: The personal representative or survivor responsible for the estate must file a final federal income tax return (Form 1040, or Form 1040-NR for non-resident aliens with U.S. source income) with the Internal Revenue Service by April 15 of the year following death [13]. Any U.S. bank accounts or real estate held solely in the deceased's name without a designated beneficiary are administered through the county Probate Court (or Surrogate's Court) in the U.S. state where the deceased was domiciled or owned assets.

closingQuestion: To help tailor the exact local steps for your family: 1. In which U.S. state and county did the death occur, and which Italian municipality (Comune) is the place of AIRE registration or intended burial? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body in a casket, bring cremated ashes to Italy under a consular Passaporto Mortuario, or arrange burial or cremation in the United States?
