title: What to Do When a Citizen of Canada Dies in Dominican Republic: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Canada Dies in Dominican Republic: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Canada dies in Dominican Republic: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Dominican Republic, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Canada and Dominican Republic.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Canadian citizenship or residence ties to Canada dies in the Dominican Republic, medical or forensic certification, civil registration at the Civil Status Office (Oficialía del Estado Civil), the Hague Apostille, and international repatriation or local disposition require coordinating procedures between Dominican authorities and Canadian consular, border, tax, and pension agencies [1][2][3]. Below are the five main official steps in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in the Dominican Republic
steps.html:
• Death from natural causes in a clinic or hospital: If the death occurs under medical care at a healthcare facility (for example in Santo Domingo, Santiago de los Caballeros, Punta Cana, or Puerto Plata), the attending physician issues the Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción / declaración médica de defunción) certifying the cause of death [2][4]. Provide the deceased person's Canadian passport so that identity details are recorded accurately [1][2].
  • Death in a hotel, residence, or public place, or when repatriating the body abroad: If the death occurs outside a hospital or in a resort area, call the 911 National Emergency and Security System (Sistema Nacional de Atención a Emergencias y Seguridad 911), the National Police (Policía Nacional), or the Tourist Police (Dirección Central de Policía de Turismo - POLITUR) immediately [3]. Under Dominican law, the body cannot be moved or removed without authorization from the Medical Examiner (Médico Legista) and the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público) [3]. Furthermore, Dominican regulations require a medico-legal autopsy performed by a forensic pathologist of the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses (INACIF, the National Institute of Forensic Sciences) both for sudden, accidental, or non-hospital deaths and whenever a body is to be repatriated outside the Dominican Republic [3].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing Licensed Funeral Directors, and Canadian Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Verifying travel or repatriation insurance: Before entering into independent financial commitments, check whether your family member had travel insurance, international medical assistance, or coverage linked to Canadian credit cards or employer benefit plans [2]. If an active policy exists, contact the insurer's emergency assistance center immediately so they can directly appoint the funeral providers and cover repatriation expenses [2].
  • Appointing a funeral home in the Dominican Republic and in Canada: The family (or insurer) must appoint an authorized funeral home (funeraria autorizada) in the Dominican Republic experienced in international repatriation and embalming to collect the body from the hospital or the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, obtain local certificates and health permits, and coordinate air transport [2][3]. If the body will be repatriated to Canada, the Dominican funeral home coordinates with a provincially licensed receiving funeral home in Canada, regulated by provincial bodies such as the Bereavement Authority of Ontario (telephone 1-844-493-6356, email info@thebao.ca) in Ontario or Consumer Protection BC in British Columbia, or located through the national Funeral Service Association of Canada [6][7]. Clarvia provides references to official and industry directories for guidance only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers.
  • Canadian consular assistance in the Dominican Republic: Report the death as soon as possible to the Embajada de Canadá en la República Dominicana (Embassy of Canada to the Dominican Republic) in Santo Domingo (Av. Winston Churchill 1099, Citigroup Tower at Acrópolis Center, 18th floor, Santo Domingo, telephone +1 809-262-3100, or the consular offices in Punta Cana and Puerto Plata) or to the 24-hour Emergency Watch and Response Centre of Global Affairs Canada in Ottawa (telephone +1 613-996-8885, email sos@international.gc.ca) [1][2]. Canadian consular officers provide guidance on local funeral homes, assist in communicating with Dominican authorities, and cancel the Canadian passport, while noting that the Government of Canada does not pay for funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Registration with the Central Electoral Board (JCE), Apostille at MIREX, and Recognition in Canada
steps.html:
• Registration at the Civil Status Office of the Junta Central Electoral (JCE): Using the Medical Death Certificate (or INACIF forensic certificate) and the deceased person's passport, the death declaration is filed with the Civil Status Office (Oficialía del Estado Civil) of the Junta Central Electoral (JCE, Central Electoral Board) for the jurisdiction where the death occurred (or at JCE desks inside health centers) within the timely 60-day period established under Law 4-23 [4]. For international use, request the official Death Certificate (Acta de Defunción In Extensa, now issued by the Junta Central Electoral in the unified standard format pursuant to Resolution 9-2025, valid for both domestic and international procedures) [4].
  • Legalization and Hague Apostille at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MIREX): Both the Dominican Republic and Canada are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force for Canada since January 2024). For the Dominican Acta de Defunción to have full legal effect in Canada, it must first be validated at the headquarters of the Junta Central Electoral and then apostilled online through the digital services portal of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MIREX, Ministry of Foreign Affairs), accompanied by a certified translation into English or French [2][5].
  • Provincial civil registries in Canada (Vital Statistics): Canadian provincial and territorial civil registries (such as ServiceOntario in Ontario, BC Vital Statistics in British Columbia, or the Directeur de l'état civil in Quebec) register deaths that occur within their respective province; when a death occurs in the Dominican Republic, the Dominican Acta de Defunción duly apostilled by the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores and translated into English or French (along with documentary guidance from Global Affairs Canada where applicable) serves as the valid official document before banks, insurers, probate courts, and federal or provincial agencies in Canada [2][9][11].

steps.title: International Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to Canada vs. Local Burial or Cremation
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body (casket) to Canada: To transport an uncremated body to Canada, the Dominican funeral home obtains the sanitary permit for international transfer of remains (permiso sanitario de traslado exterior de cadáveres) from the Ministry of Public Health and Social Assistance (Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social - MISPAS), the autopsy report from the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, the certificate of embalming, the certificate of encasement in a hermetically sealed casket (with a soldered inner zinc liner), and consular document verification [2][3]. For importation into Canada, the Canada Border Services Agency (under Memorandum D19-9-3 and the federal Quarantine Act) requires that human remains travel in a leak-proof hermetically sealed casket, accompanied by the official death certificate, a medical or health statement certifying that the deceased did not have a communicable quarantinable disease, and the certificate of embalming and sealing from the dispatching funeral home, translated into English or French [8].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes to Canada: If the family chooses cremation in the Dominican Republic (following authorization by the family, the Public Prosecutor's Office/INACIF, and MISPAS), cremated human remains are not subject to quarantine health restrictions under the Quarantine Act according to Memorandum D19-9-3 of the Canada Border Services Agency [8]. The ashes must be transported in a sealed urn (preferably non-metallic and suitable for airport X-ray screening), accompanied by the Acta de Defunción and the official cremation certificate translated into English or French [2][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in the Dominican Republic: If the family decides on permanent burial or cremation in the Dominican Republic, the local funeral home obtains the municipal cemetery permits from the relevant city council (ayuntamiento) and the sanitary authorization from MISPAS [2][4].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Canada and the Dominican Republic
steps.html:
• Pension, tax, and probate procedures in Canada:
    • Service Canada and Retraite Québec: Notify Service Canada by calling 1-800-277-9914 (from Canada) or +1 613-990-2244 (from abroad) to stop monthly Old Age Security (OAS) and Canada Pension Plan (CPP) payments, update the Social Insurance Number (SIN) record, and apply for the lump-sum CPP Death Benefit (Form ISP-1200, base amount of 2,500 CAD, with an additional top-up of up to 2,500 CAD to reach 5,000 CAD in legally eligible cases) and the CPP Survivor's Pension (Form ISP-1300) [9]. If the deceased contributed in Quebec, apply for Québec Pension Plan (QPP) benefits through Retraite Québec (telephone 1-800-463-5185 or +1 418-643-5185) [10].
    • Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and provincial Probate: The legal representative of the estate (executor, estate trustee in Ontario, or liquidator in Quebec) must notify the Canada Revenue Agency (telephone 1-800-959-8281), file the final income tax return (Final T1 Return) no later than April 30 of the year following death (or within 6 months of death if it occurred between November 1 and December 31), and apply for a Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) before distributing estate assets to avoid personal tax liability [11]. Probate of the will or estate administration (Probate) is completed before the competent provincial court in Canada.
  • Inheritance tax, pensions, and estate administration in the Dominican Republic:
    • Sworn Inheritance Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones - DGII): If your family member held bank accounts, real property, or other assets in the Dominican Republic, the heirs or legatees must file the Sworn Inheritance Return (Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones, Form FSD-1) with the Dirección General de Impuestos Internos (DGII, Directorate General of Internal Taxes) within ninety (90) calendar days of the death, subject to a general rate of 3% on the net estate after deducting funeral expenses and verified debts, together with the formal determination of heirs (determinación de herederos) before a notary or competent local civil court [12].
    • Dominican pensions (SIPEN / AFP): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension under the Dominican Social Security System (Law 87-01), eligible beneficiaries should contact the relevant Pension Fund Administrator (Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones - AFP), supervised by the Superintendency of Pensions (Superintendencia de Pensiones - SIPEN), to claim a survivor pension or return of accumulated pension funds [13].

closingQuestion: To provide more specific guidance for your situation, in which province or municipality of the Dominican Republic did the death occur, in which Canadian province or territory did your family member reside (or where is repatriation planned), and does the family wish to repatriate the body in a casket, cremate in the Dominican Republic and transport the ashes to Canada, or arrange local burial in the Dominican Republic?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre República Dominicana y Canadá: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre República Dominicana y Canadá: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía o vínculos de residencia en Canadá fallece en la República Dominicana, la certificación médica o forense, la inscripción civil en la Oficialía del Estado Civil, la Apostilla de La Haya y el traslado internacional o disposición local requieren coordinar trámites entre las autoridades dominicanas y las entidades consulares, fronterizas y previsionales de Canadá [1][2][3]. A continuación se explican los cinco pasos oficiales principales en orden práctico.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción e intervención forense en la República Dominicana
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento por causas naturales en clínica u hospital: Si el deceso ocurre bajo asistencia médica en un centro de salud (por ejemplo, en Santo Domingo, Santiago de los Caballeros, Punta Cana o Puerto Plata), el profesional médico tratante expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción (declaración médica de defunción) que acredita la causa del fallecimiento [2][4]. Entregue el pasaporte canadiense de la persona fallecida para que sus datos de identidad se consignen sin errores [1][2].
  • Fallecimiento en hotel, residencia o vía pública, o traslado internacional del cuerpo: Si la persona fallecida muere fuera de un centro hospitalario o en una zona turística, se debe llamar de inmediato al Sistema Nacional de Atención a Emergencias y Seguridad 911, a la Policía Nacional o a la Dirección Central de Policía de Turismo (POLITUR) [3]. Por ley dominicana, el cuerpo no puede ser levantado ni trasladado sin la autorización del Médico Legista y del Ministerio Público [3]. Asimismo, la normativa dominicana exige la práctica de una autopsia médico-legal por parte de un médico forense del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses (INACIF) tanto en muertes súbitas, accidentales o fuera de hospital como en los casos en que el cuerpo vaya a ser repatriado fuera de la República Dominicana [3].

steps.title: Seguro de viaje, designación de funerarias autorizadas y asistencia consular canadiense
steps.html:
• Verificación de seguro de viaje o repatriación: Antes de contraer compromisos financieros independientes, verifique si su familiar contaba con un seguro de viaje, asistencia médica internacional o cobertura asociada a tarjetas de crédito o planes laborales canadienses [2]. Si existe póliza activa, comuníquese de inmediato con la central de asistencia de la aseguradora para que designe directamente a los operadores funerarios y cubra los gastos de repatriación [2].
  • Contratación de funeraria en la República Dominicana y en Canadá: La familia (o la aseguradora) debe designar una funeraria autorizada en la República Dominicana con experiencia en traslados internacionales y embalsamamiento para retirar el cuerpo del hospital o del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, tramitar las actas y permisos sanitarios locales y coordinar el transporte aéreo [2][3]. Si el cuerpo será repatriado a Canadá, la funeraria dominicana se coordina con una funeraria receptora con licencia provincial en Canadá, regulada por organismos provinciales como la Bereavement Authority of Ontario (teléfono 1-844-493-6356, correo info@thebao.ca) en Ontario o Consumer Protection BC en la Columbia Británica, o localizada a través de la asociación nacional Funeral Service Association of Canada [6][7]. Clarvia ofrece referencias de directorios oficiales y gremiales a título orientativo y no respalda, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores comerciales.
  • Asistencia consular de Canadá en la República Dominicana: Reporte el fallecimiento lo antes posible a la Embajada de Canadá en la República Dominicana en Santo Domingo (Av. Winston Churchill 1099, Torre Citigroup en Acrópolis Center, piso 18, Santo Domingo, teléfono +1 809-262-3100, o las oficinas consulares en Punta Cana y Puerto Plata) o al Centro de Vigilancia y Respuesta a Emergencias 24 horas de Global Affairs Canada en Ottawa (teléfono +1 613-996-8885, correo sos@international.gc.ca) [1][2]. Los funcionarios consulares canadienses orientan sobre funerarias locales, asisten en la comunicación con las autoridades dominicanas y gestionan la anulación del pasaporte canadiense, teniendo presente que el Gobierno de Canadá no sufraga gastos funerarios, de cremación ni de repatriación [1][2].

steps.title: Registro civil en la Junta Central Electoral (JCE), Apostilla en el MIREX y reconocimiento en Canadá
steps.html:
• Inscripción en la Oficialía del Estado Civil de la Junta Central Electoral (JCE): Con el Certificado Médico de Defunción (o certificación forense del INACIF) y el pasaporte de la persona fallecida, la declaración de defunción se realiza ante la Oficialía del Estado Civil de la Junta Central Electoral correspondiente a la demarcación donde ocurrió el fallecimiento (o en las delegaciones de la Junta Central Electoral en centros de salud) dentro del plazo oportuno de 60 días establecido por la Ley 4-23 [4]. Para efectos internacionales se solicita el Acta de Defunción In Extensa (emitida actualmente por la Junta Central Electoral en el formato estándar unificado conforme a la Resolución 9-2025, válido para trámites nacionales e internacionales) [4].
  • Legalización y Apostilla de La Haya ante el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MIREX): Tanto la República Dominicana como Canadá son partes del Convenio de La Haya sobre la Apostilla (en vigor para Canadá desde enero de 2024). Para que el Acta de Defunción dominicana surta plenos efectos legales en Canadá, primero debe ser validada en la sede central de la Junta Central Electoral y posteriormente apostillada en línea a través del portal de servicios digitales del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MIREX), acompañada de una traducción certificada al inglés o al francés [2][5].
  • Registros civiles provinciales en Canadá (Vital Statistics): Los registros civiles provinciales y territoriales de Canadá (como ServiceOntario en Ontario, BC Vital Statistics en la Columbia Británica o el Directeur de l'état civil en Quebec) inscriben las defunciones ocurridas dentro de su respectiva provincia; cuando el deceso ocurre en la República Dominicana, el Acta de Defunción dominicana debidamente apostillada por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y traducida al inglés o francés (junto con el apoyo documental de Global Affairs Canada cuando corresponda) constituye el documento oficial válido ante bancos, aseguradoras, tribunales de sucesiones y agencias federales o provinciales en Canadá [2][9][11].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional del cuerpo o de las cenizas a Canadá frente a sepultura o cremación local
steps.html:
• Repatriación de cuerpo (féretro) a Canadá: Para trasladar el cuerpo sin cremar hacia Canadá, la funeraria dominicana gestiona el permiso sanitario de traslado exterior de cadáveres ante el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MISPAS), el informe de autopsia del Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Forenses, el certificado de embalsamamiento, el acta de encajonamiento en féretro hermético sellado (con caja metálica interior de zinc soldada) y la verificación documental consular [2][3]. Para la importación a territorio canadiense, la Canada Border Services Agency (conforme al Memorando D19-9-3 y a la ley federal Quarantine Act) exige que los restos humanos viajen en un féretro hermético a prueba de fugas, acompañados del certificado oficial de defunción, una declaración médica o sanitaria que acredite que la persona fallecida no padecía una enfermedad transmisible sujeta a cuarentena y el certificado de embalsamamiento y sellado de la funeraria de origen, con traducción al inglés o francés [8].
  • Repatriación de cenizas cremadas a Canadá: Si la familia opta por la cremación en la República Dominicana (previa autorización familiar, del Ministerio Público/INACIF y del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social), las cenizas humanas cremadas no están sujetas a restricciones sanitarias de cuarentena bajo la Quarantine Act según el Memorando D19-9-3 de la Canada Border Services Agency [8]. Las cenizas deben transportarse en una urna sellada (preferiblemente no metálica apta para inspección por rayos X en aeropuertos), acompañadas del Acta de Defunción y del certificado oficial de cremación traducidos al inglés o francés [2][8].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en la República Dominicana: Si la familia decide realizar la sepultura o cremación definitiva en territorio dominicano, la funeraria local tramita los permisos municipales ante el ayuntamiento correspondiente y la autorización sanitaria del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social [2][4].

steps.title: Pensiones de sobrevivientes, impuestos y sucesión en Canadá y en la República Dominicana
steps.html:
• Trámites previsionales, fiscales y sucesorios en Canadá:
    • Service Canada y Retraite Québec: Notifique el fallecimiento a Service Canada llamando al 1-800-277-9914 (desde Canadá) o al +1 613-990-2244 (desde el exterior) para suspender pagos mensuales de Old Age Security (OAS) y del Canada Pension Plan (CPP), actualizar el registro del Social Insurance Number (SIN) y solicitar el beneficio único por defunción CPP Death Benefit (Formulario ISP-1200, de 2.500 CAD, con un complemento adicional de hasta 2.500 CAD para alcanzar 5.000 CAD en los casos elegibles por ley) y la pensión de sobreviviente CPP Survivor's Pension (Formulario ISP-1300) [9]. Si la persona fallecida cotizó en Quebec, gestione las prestaciones del Québec Pension Plan (QPP) ante Retraite Québec (teléfono 1-800-463-5185 o +1 418-643-5185) [10].
    • Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) y sucesión provincial (Probate): El representante legal del patrimonio (executor, estate trustee en Ontario o liquidator en Quebec) debe notificar el fallecimiento a la Canada Revenue Agency (teléfono 1-800-959-8281), presentar la declaración final de impuestos sobre la renta (Final T1 Return) a más tardar el 30 de abril del año siguiente al fallecimiento (o dentro de los 6 meses posteriores al deceso si ocurrió entre el 1 de noviembre y el 31 de diciembre) y solicitar el Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) antes de distribuir los bienes de la sucesión para evitar responsabilidad fiscal personal [11]. La homologación del testamento o administración sucesoria (Probate) se tramita ante el tribunal provincial competente en Canadá.
  • Impuesto sucesoral, pensiones y sucesión en la República Dominicana:
    • Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones (DGII): Si su familiar poseía cuentas bancarias, inmuebles u otros bienes en la República Dominicana, los herederos o legatarios deben presentar la Declaración Jurada de Sucesiones (Formulario FSD-1) ante la Dirección General de Impuestos Internos dentro de los noventa (90) días calendario posteriores al fallecimiento, sujeta a una tasa general del 3% sobre la masa sucesoral neta tras deducir gastos funerarios y deudas fehacientes, junto con la determinación de herederos ante notaría o el tribunal civil local competente [12].
    • Pensiones (SIPEN / AFP): Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o era pensionada en el Sistema Dominicano de Seguridad Social (Ley 87-01), los beneficiarios legales deben acudir a la Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones (AFP) correspondiente, bajo la supervisión de la Superintendencia de Pensiones, para reclamar la pensión de sobrevivencia o la devolución del saldo acumulado [13].

es.closingQuestion: Para brindarle indicaciones más específicas según su situación: 1. ¿En qué provincia o municipio de la República Dominicana ocurrió el fallecimiento y en qué provincia o territorio de Canadá residía su familiar (o hacia dónde se prevé el traslado)? 2. ¿Desea la familia repatriar el cuerpo en féretro, realizar la cremación en la República Dominicana y trasladar las cenizas a Canadá, o efectuar la sepultura local en la República Dominicana?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Canada Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Canada Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Canada dies in Thailand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Thailand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Canada and Thailand.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Canada dies in Thailand, immediate medical certification, police clearance, and civil death registration are governed by Thai authorities, while consular release, customs clearance upon return, survivor benefits, and estate administration involve Canadian federal and provincial institutions [1][2][9]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Emergency or Forensic Clearance in Thailand
steps.html:
Before a death can be registered with the local Thai civil registrar or the remains released to a funeral director, an official Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1) must be issued in Thailand [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital: If the deceased passed away in a Thai public or private hospital (for example, in Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, or Pattaya), the attending physician issues the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1) once hospital and mortuary charges have been settled [2]. Provide the deceased's Canadian passport so identity details match across all Thai and Canadian records [1][2].
  • Death in a residence, hotel, or public place: If the death occurred outside a hospital or was sudden, unexpected, or accidental, call the Royal Thai Police at 191, the English-speaking Tourist Police at 1155, or Emergency Medical Services (EMS) at 1669 immediately [1][2]. Under Thai law, the police must inspect the scene, prepare an official police report, and transfer the body for a mandatory forensic post-mortem examination (conducted at the Institute of Forensic Medicine at the Police General Hospital in Bangkok or at a designated provincial hospital) [2]. Once the forensic examination is complete, the forensic physician issues the medical certificate of death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1) and the police issue formal release authorization [2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Funeral Providers in Thailand and Canada, and Contact the Embassy of Canada
steps.html:
Before entering into private funeral contracts, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international medical insurance, or credit card/employer coverage that includes repatriation or local cremation expenses [2]. If a policy is active, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance centre immediately so they can appoint and pay an international funeral coordinator directly [2]. The Government of Canada does not pay for funeral, cremation, or repatriation costs [2].

  • Embassy of Canada in Thailand and consular letter of release: Report the death immediately to the Embassy of Canada to Thailand in Bangkok (15th Floor, Abdulrahim Place, 990 Rama IV Road, Bangrak, Bangkok 10500; phone +66 2 646 4300; email bngkk-cs@international.gc.ca; or the Consulate of Canada in Chiang Mai) or to the 24/7 Emergency Watch and Response Centre at Global Affairs Canada in Ottawa (phone +1 613-996-8885; email sos@international.gc.ca) [1][2]. Thai hospitals, forensic mortuaries, and district offices require a mandatory consular letter of release (no-objection letter) from the Embassy of Canada to Thailand confirming next-of-kin authorization before releasing the body of a Canadian citizen to the next of kin or an appointed funeral director [1][2].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Thailand and Canada: Appoint a licensed international funeral and repatriation director in Thailand (the Embassy of Canada to Thailand can provide a non-exhaustive list of local English-speaking funeral homes, or you may coordinate directly with a Buddhist temple, Wat, for local cremation) [1][2]. If repatriating remains to Canada, the Thai funeral director coordinates with a provincially licensed receiving funeral home in Canada, regulated by provincial authorities such as the Bereavement Authority of Ontario (phone 1-844-493-6356; email info@thebao.ca) in Ontario or Consumer Protection BC in British Columbia, or located through the Funeral Service Association of Canada [4][5]. Clarvia provides regulatory and association directories for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific commercial providers.

steps.title: Register the Death at the Thai District Office (Amphoe or Khet) and Legalize Documents for Canada
steps.html:
Under Thai civil registration rules, a death must be reported within 24 hours of death or discovery of the body at the local District Office (Amphoe in the provinces, or Khet in Bangkok, operating under the Department of Provincial Administration - DOPA) for the locality where the death occurred or where the forensic examination was completed [2][3]:

  • Obtaining the Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4): The authorized funeral director or next of kin presents the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1), the police report (if applicable), the deceased's Canadian passport, and the consular release letter from the Embassy of Canada to Thailand to the Amphoe or Khet registrar, who issues the official Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) in the Thai language [1][2].
  • Certified English translation and legalization: Because Form Tor.Ror.4 is issued in Thai and Thailand is not yet issuing Hague Apostilles for cross-border civil status use with Canada, obtain a certified English (or French) translation of the Thai Death Certificate and have both the original certificate and translation legalized by the Department of Consular Affairs at the Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bangkok (123 Chaeng Watthana Road, Laksi, Bangkok 10210; phone +66 2 575 1058 or call centre +66 2 572 8442; email consular04@mfa.go.th), followed by authentication at the Embassy of Canada to Thailand if required by a Canadian probate court or financial institution [1][2][3].
  • Provincial Vital Statistics in Canada: Provincial and territorial Vital Statistics registries in Canada (such as ServiceOntario in Ontario, the BC Vital Statistics Agency in British Columbia, or the Directeur de l'état civil in Quebec) register deaths that occur within their own province; for a death in Thailand, the legalized Thai Death Certificate and certified English or French translation serve as the official proof of death for Canadian pensions, taxes, and estate probate [2][6][7][8].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to Canada and Local Cremation or Burial in Thailand
steps.html:
Once the consular letter of release and the Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) have been issued, the family can proceed with either international repatriation to Canada or local disposition in Thailand [1][2][9]:

  • Repatriation of casketed human remains to Canada: The Thai international funeral director arranges hospital or forensic embalming, places the body in a hermetically sealed metal-lined coffin, obtains the infectious disease clearance certificate, cancels the deceased's Canadian passport at the Embassy of Canada to Thailand, and clears Thai Customs airport cargo formalities [1][2][9]. For entry into Canada, the Canada Border Services Agency (under Memorandum D19-9-3 and the federal Quarantine Act) requires the hermetically sealed coffin to be accompanied by the official Death Certificate, a medical or public health certificate stating the cause of death and confirming the deceased was free of communicable quarantine diseases, and an embalming/sealing certificate (all with English or French translations) [9].
  • Local cremation in Thailand and transporting ashes to Canada: Cremation at a Thai Buddhist temple (Wat) or crematorium is widely practiced and significantly less expensive than full-body air repatriation [2]. Under Canada Border Services Agency Memorandum D19-9-3, cremated human remains do not pose a quarantine risk under the Quarantine Act and may be brought into Canada in hand luggage (in a sealed, non-metallic urn capable of passing airport X-ray screening) or via air cargo, accompanied by the certified Death Certificate and the official Certificate of Cremation [9].
  • Local burial in Thailand: If the family chooses local burial in Thailand, the Thai funeral director coordinates cemetery plots and municipal permits directly using the Amphoe or Khet burial permit [2].

steps.title: Complete Pension, Tax, and Estate Administration in Canada and Thailand
steps.html:
After obtaining the legalized Thai Death Certificate and certified translation, complete the required financial, pension, and probate filings in both jurisdictions:

  • In Canada (Service Canada, Retraite Québec, CRA, and Provincial Probate):
    • Service Canada and Retraite Québec: Notify Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 (within Canada) or +1 613-990-2244 (from abroad) to stop Old Age Security (OAS) and Canada Pension Plan (CPP) monthly payments, update the Social Insurance Number (SIN) register, and apply for the lump-sum CPP Death Benefit (Form ISP-1200, providing a base $2,500 payment plus a $2,500 top-up to $5,000 for eligible deaths where no retirement/disability pension was paid and no survivor pension applies) and the monthly CPP Survivor's Pension (Form ISP-1300) [10]. If the deceased contributed in Quebec, apply to Retraite Québec at 1-800-463-5185 (or +1 418-643-5185) for Québec Pension Plan (QPP) death and survivor benefits [11].
    • Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Provincial Probate: The executor (called the estate trustee in Ontario or liquidator in Quebec) must notify the Canada Revenue Agency at 1-800-959-8281, file the Final T1 Income Tax and Benefit Return by April 30 of the year following death (or within 6 months of death if it occurred between November 1 and December 31), and apply for a CRA Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) before distributing estate assets to avoid personal liability for unpaid taxes [12][13]. Apply to the competent provincial court in Canada for probate (such as a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee in Ontario or a Grant of Probate in British Columbia) to administer Canadian bank accounts and property [6][7].
  • In Thailand (Thai Civil and Commercial Code Estate Administration):
    • If your family member held sole-name Thai bank accounts, a condominium unit, a vehicle, or a long-term lease in Thailand, Thai banks and the Land Department generally will not release assets solely on the basis of a Canadian will or foreign grant of probate; the heirs or executor must retain a Thai lawyer to petition the competent Thai Provincial or Civil Court for an official Thai court probate order appointing an estate administrator under Book VI of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code [1][2].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your situation: 1. In which Thai province or district did the death occur, and in which Canadian province or territory did your family member reside (or where will the remains be sent)? 2. Are you planning full-body repatriation to Canada, local cremation in Thailand followed by transporting the ashes to Canada, or local funeral arrangements in Thailand?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Ukraine dies in Canada: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Canada, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Ukraine and Canada.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Ukraine dies in Canada, medical pronouncement, funeral licensing, and civil death registration take place under Canadian provincial or territorial law, while Apostille authentication, Ukrainian consular clearance for repatriation, and post-death pension and inheritance steps involve both Canadian and Ukrainian authorities [1][7][9]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Medical Examiner Clearance in Canada
steps.html:
Before a funeral provider in Canada can transfer the deceased or register the death, an authorized health professional or coroner/medical examiner must pronounce death and issue the provincial Medical Certificate of Death (in Quebec, the Attestation of Death, form SP-3) [1][2][5]:

  • Death in a hospital, hospice, or long-term care facility: The attending physician, nurse practitioner, or registered nurse in an extended role pronounces death, completes the Medical Certificate of Death, and authorizes release of the remains to your chosen funeral provider [2][4].
  • Expected death at home under palliative care: Contact the palliative care team or attending physician under the established home-care protocol so they can pronounce death and sign the medical certificate [2].
  • Sudden, unexpected, or unattended death: Call 911 immediately and do not move the body [2]. Police and emergency medical services will respond, and the provincial Coroner or Medical Examiner Service (for example, the Office of the Chief Coroner in Ontario, the BC Coroners Service in British Columbia, the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner in Alberta or Manitoba, or the Bureau du coroner in Quebec) will investigate the cause and manner of death and issue the medical certificate (and, if remains are being exported out of the province, any required coroner's out-of-province/international export certificate) before releasing the body [2][4][5].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Funeral Providers in Canada and Ukraine, and Contact the Embassy or Consulate of Ukraine
steps.html:
Check immediately whether your family member had travel insurance, international repatriation insurance, life insurance, or employer coverage before signing independent funeral contracts. If a policy is active, contact the insurer's emergency assistance coordinator first.

  • Appointing a provincially licensed funeral provider in Canada: Appoint a licensed funeral home or transfer service in the Canadian province where the death occurred, regulated by provincial bodies such as the Bereavement Authority of Ontario (phone 1-844-493-6356; email info@thebao.ca) in Ontario or Consumer Protection BC in British Columbia, or located through the national Funeral Service Association of Canada [3][4][6].
  • Coordinating with a receiving funeral service in Ukraine: If repatriating the body or cremated ashes to Ukraine, the Canadian funeral director coordinates transport and arrival logistics with a receiving funeral provider in Ukraine (ритуальна служба - a municipal enterprise, комунальне підприємство, or licensed funeral service, ліцензована похоронна служба, in the Ukrainian municipality of burial) [7]. Clarvia provides regulatory and association directories for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific commercial providers.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate of Ukraine in Canada: Notify the Ukrainian consular mission covering the province of death: the Embassy of Ukraine in Canada in Ottawa (310 Somerset Street West, Ottawa, ON K2P 0J9; phone +1 613-230-2961; emergency line +1 613-617-2335; email consul_ca@mfa.gov.ua), the Consulate General of Ukraine in Toronto (phone +1 416-763-3114; email gc_cat@mfa.gov.ua), or the Consulate General of Ukraine in Edmonton [7][8]. The Ukrainian consular office advises on repatriation documentation, cancels the deceased's Ukrainian passport, and issues consular clearance for transporting remains across the Ukrainian border [7].

steps.title: Register the Death with Provincial Vital Statistics in Canada, Obtain a Canadian Apostille, and Complete Ukrainian Registry Steps
steps.html:
• Provincial or territorial Vital Statistics registration in Canada: Your appointed Canadian funeral director submits the family's statement of death alongside the Medical Certificate of Death to the provincial or territorial civil registry - such as ServiceOntario (Office of the Registrar General) in Ontario [2], the BC Vital Statistics Agency in British Columbia [4], or the Directeur de l'état civil in Quebec [5]. The funeral director issues a Funeral Director's Statement of Death for immediate domestic notifications and obtains the burial or cremation permit, while you order official provincial Death Certificates (including a long-form / certified copy showing cause of death if required for international transport) from Vital Statistics [2][4][5][7].
  • Canadian Apostille and Ukrainian translation: Because the Hague Apostille Convention entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024, Ukrainian embassies and consulates in Canada no longer perform traditional consular legalization of Canadian civil documents [8][9]. Instead, obtain an official Apostille on the Canadian provincial Death Certificate (and related transport certificates) through Global Affairs Canada or the designated provincial Competent Authority (such as the Official Documents Services in Ontario, the Ministry of the Attorney General in British Columbia, or the Ministère de la Justice in Quebec), and have the documents translated into Ukrainian with notarized/certified translation [7][8][9].
  • Civil status recognition in Ukraine (DRACS / MFA): Under Ukrainian law, while domestic deaths in Ukraine are registered within 3 days at a Civil Status Registration Department (відділ державної реєстрації актів цивільного стану - ДРАЦС Міністерства юстиції України, via a ЦНАП administrative service centre or the портал Дія) to obtain a Ukrainian death certificate (свідоцтво про смерть) and an extract for the funeral grant (витяг з Державного реєстру актів цивільного стану громадян про смерть для отримання допомоги на поховання), a Canadian provincial Death Certificate bearing a Canadian Apostille and a certified Ukrainian translation is legally recognized in Ukraine under the Hague Apostille Convention and coordinated through the Department of Consular Service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine (Департамент консульської служби МЗС України) [7][8][11].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to Ukraine and Local Burial or Cremation in Canada
steps.html:
• International repatriation of casketed remains or cremated ashes from Canada to Ukraine: Under Canada Border Services Agency Memorandum D19-9-3 and the Canadian Quarantine Act, exporting human remains from Canada requires a provincial Death Certificate, a provincial burial/transit or export permit (and Coroner/Medical Examiner export clearance where required), and compliance with international air carrier packaging rules [10]. To import a coffin or urn into Ukraine, the Embassy of Ukraine in Canada outlines the mandatory Ukrainian border and sanitary requirements (enforced in Ukraine alongside the State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection, Держпродспоживслужба / sanitary-epidemiological clearance, довідка санітарно-епідеміологічної служби, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, МЗС України) [7]:
    • For a body in a coffin: The official Canadian Death Certificate, a medical or public health certificate confirming the cause of death and the absence of infectious disease, an embalming certificate, a funeral home certificate confirming that the hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin (оцинкована герметична труна) contains no extraneous objects, and Official sealing of the coffin, all bearing an Apostille and Ukrainian translation, plus proof of a reserved burial plot in Ukraine and details of the accompanying person [7][10].
    • For cremated ashes: The official Canadian Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, and a funeral home/crematorium certificate confirming the absence of extraneous items inside the sealed urn or capsule (капсула з прахом), each apostilled and translated into Ukrainian [7][10].
  • Local burial or cremation in Canada: If the family chooses burial or cremation in Canada, the Canadian funeral director arranges the cemetery or crematorium service directly using the provincial burial/cremation permit [2][3].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Pension, Funeral Benefit, Tax, and Estate Administration in Ukraine and Canada
steps.html:
• In Ukraine (Pension Fund of Ukraine and Notarial Inheritance within 6 Months):
    • Pension Fund of Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України - ПФУ): If the deceased received a Ukrainian pension or was insured in Ukraine, eligible family members or the person who arranged the burial can apply to the Pension Fund of Ukraine (in person at a PFU service centre or online via the Diia Portal / PFU web portal) for the Ukrainian funeral assistance benefit (допомога на поховання) and, for eligible dependents, the survivor's pension (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) using the apostilled and translated death documentation [11].
    • Opening an inheritance case within 6 months (Нотаріальна палата України / Ministry of Justice): If the deceased owned real estate, bank accounts, or other assets in Ukraine, heirs must submit an application to accept the inheritance (заява про прийняття спадщини) within the strict statutory deadline of 6 months from the date of death before a Ukrainian state or private notary (registered in the Inheritance Register of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine, Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України, with professional directory guidance available through the Notary Chamber of Ukraine - Нотаріальна палата України) [12]. Heirs residing in Canada can execute a notarized and apostilled inheritance application or power of attorney (or sign it at a Ukrainian Consulate in Canada) to forward to a notary in Ukraine before the 6-month deadline expires [8][12].
  • In Canada (Service Canada, Retraite Québec, CRA, and Provincial Probate):
    • Service Canada and Retraite Québec: Notify Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 to cancel the Social Insurance Number (SIN), Employment Insurance (EI), Old Age Security (OAS), and Canada Pension Plan (CPP) payments, and apply for the lump-sum CPP Death Benefit (Form ISP-1200, $2,500 base benefit or up to $5,000 with the eligible top-up) and CPP Survivor's Pension (Form ISP-1300) if your family member contributed to the CPP [1][13]. If the deceased worked in Quebec, apply to Retraite Québec at 1-800-463-5185 for Québec Pension Plan (QPP) benefits [14].
    • Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Provincial Probate: The legal representative (executor, estate trustee in Ontario, or liquidator in Quebec) must report the death to the Canada Revenue Agency at 1-800-959-8281, file the Final T1 Income Tax and Benefit Return by April 30 of the following year (or within 6 months of death if the death occurred in November or December), obtain a CRA Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) before distributing Canadian assets, and apply for provincial Probate (Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee or Grant of Probate) where required to release Canadian bank accounts or property [2][15][16].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance for your family: 1. In which Canadian province or territory did the death occur, and to which city or oblast in Ukraine are you considering repatriating the remains or ashes (or do you plan local burial/cremation in Canada)? 2. Did your family member hold employment/pension coverage in Canada, pensions or property in Ukraine, or both?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in Canada: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of India dies in Canada: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Canada, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in India and Canada.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of India dies in Canada, provincial and federal procedures in Canada must be coordinated with Indian consular and public health requirements. Because civil registration, funeral licensing, and probate rules in Canada are administered at the provincial or territorial level, the steps below set out the national corridor framework along with flagship provincial examples.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and coroner or medical examiner clearance in Canada
steps.html:
Before civil registration, cremation, burial, or international repatriation can proceed, a physician, nurse practitioner, or coroner/medical examiner in the Canadian province or territory of death must issue the official medical certification [1].

  • Death in a hospital, hospice, or long-term care facility: The attending physician or qualified nurse practitioner completes and signs the provincial Medical Certificate of Death (or equivalent medical certification of cause of death) and releases the body to the appointed funeral service provider [1].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or non-hospital death: Call emergency services (911) immediately [1]. Local police and the provincial Coroner or Medical Examiner service (such as the Office of the Chief Coroner in Ontario or the BC Coroners Service in British Columbia) will attend to investigate sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths [1]. If an investigation or autopsy is required, the Coroner or Medical Examiner issues the medical certification and must grant formal clearance before the deceased can be embalmed, cremated, or transported outside the province or country [1][3].

steps.title: Funeral coordination, insurance verification, and Indian consular notification
steps.html:
You do not need to manage technical mortuary or customs paperwork across two countries on your own. A licensed funeral director in Canada acts as your primary operational coordinator [1][3].

  • Check travel, medical, or repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral or air-cargo contract, verify whether the deceased held travel insurance, international student/worker coverage (including Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana - PBBY), or an employer assistance plan. Insurers often require their designated assistance coordinator to arrange transport directly.
  • Appoint a licensed funeral provider in Canada and a receiving provider in India: Funeral providers in Canada are regulated provincially - for example, by the Bereavement Authority of Ontario in Ontario, Consumer Protection BC in British Columbia, or provincial regulators represented through the Funeral Service Association of Canada [2]. You can verify licensed providers through the public register of the Bereavement Authority of Ontario [2]. Clarvia supplies regulatory and directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank individual providers. Your Canadian funeral director coordinates flight bookings, embalming, and hermitically sealed casket preparation with a receiving funeral provider, municipal mortuary, or crematorium at the destination airport in India [3][8].
  • Notify the Indian diplomatic mission in Canada: Contact the High Commission of India in Ottawa (10 Springfield Road, Ottawa, email cons.ottawa@mea.gov.in) or the jurisdictional Consulate General of India in Toronto or Vancouver depending on the province where the death occurred [3]. Where a family faces severe financial distress, the mission can also advise on eligibility for assistance from the Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) [3].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Canada, apostille, and Indian registration
steps.html:
The death must be registered in the Canadian province or territory where it occurred before official certificates and consular permits can be issued [1][4].

  • Provincial civil registration in Canada: Your appointed funeral director normally completes the Statement of Death with a family informant and files it alongside the Medical Certificate of Death with the provincial or territorial Vital Statistics registry - such as ServiceOntario in Ontario, Vital Statistics Agency in British Columbia, or the Directeur de l'état civil in Quebec [1][4]. Order multiple original Death Certificates and, where needed for foreign pension or estate procedures, a Certified Copy of Death Registration through ServiceOntario or the relevant provincial registry [4].
  • Apostille and consular registration: Both Canada and India are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention. For Canadian death certificates to be recognized directly by courts, banks, or registries in India, have the provincial document authenticated with an Apostille through Global Affairs Canada or the designated provincial competent authority (such as the Official Documents Services office in Ontario) [5]. In parallel, the death of an Indian national is registered with the High Commission of India in Ottawa (or the relevant Consulate General), which cancels the deceased's Indian passport and issues an official consular certificate of death registration [3].
  • Civil Registration System (CRS) rules in India: Under India's Registration of Births and Deaths Act, deaths occurring within India must be reported to the local Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Corporation or Gram Panchayat via the Civil Registration System portal) within 21 days [6]; for deaths occurring abroad, the Indian mission's consular death certificate and the apostilled Canadian Death Certificate serve as the official proof of death for Indian authorities [3][5].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to India and local burial or cremation in Canada
steps.html:
Your family can choose either to repatriate the deceased (as a casketed body or cremated ashes) to India or to hold a local burial or cremation in Canada [1][3].

  • Repatriation of uncremated human remains to India: Under the Quarantine Act and Memorandum D19-9-3 administered by the Canada Border Services Agency, international air transport of uncremated remains requires an original Death Certificate, a certificate of non-communicable disease (or Public Health Agency of Canada permit if a listed communicable disease is involved), professional embalming, and a hermetically sealed leak-proof casket [7]. You or your funeral director must obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) and passport cancellation from the High Commission of India in Ottawa (or regional Consulate) by submitting the Canadian Death Certificate, Statement/Medical Certificate of Death, embalming and casket sealing certificates, non-communicable disease clearance, flight itinerary, and next-of-kin authorization [3]. In addition, advance public health clearance must be submitted at least 48 hours before arrival to the Airport Health Organization (APHO) of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in India (via the eCARe portal), uploading the Death Certificate, Embalming Certificate, Indian mission NOC, and cancelled passport [3][8].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to India: If cremation takes place in Canada first, cremated remains do not pose a quarantine risk under the guidelines of the Canada Border Services Agency, though passengers should carry the official Death Certificate and Cremation Certificate in a screenable urn [7]. The High Commission of India in Ottawa issues a consular certificate for the transport of ashes upon submission of the Canadian Death Certificate, Cremation Certificate, coroner report (if applicable), original Indian passport, and flight details [3].
  • Local burial or cremation in Canada: If the family chooses final disposition in Canada, your licensed funeral director arranges the provincial burial permit or coroner cremation certificate directly with the local cemetery or crematorium [1][2].

steps.title: Post-death notifications, survivor benefits, taxes, and estate administration in Canada and India
steps.html:
Once official death certificates are issued, the executor, estate representative, or eligible family members must complete tax, pension, and succession steps in both jurisdictions [9][10].

  • Pensions, benefits, and taxes in Canada: Notify Service Canada (or Retraite Québec if the deceased contributed in Quebec) to cancel Old Age Security and Canada Pension Plan payments and to apply for the one-time Canada Pension Plan (CPP) Death Benefit (Form ISP1200) and any eligible Survivor's Pension or children's benefits [9]. Notify the Canada Revenue Agency as soon as possible (by calling 1-800-959-8281 or submitting Form RC4111) [10]. The legal representative must file the deceased's Final T1 Return (and any optional or T3 trust returns) and request a Clearance Certificate (Form TX19) from the Canada Revenue Agency before distributing Canadian estate assets, alongside applying for a provincial Grant of Probate (such as a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee in Ontario) where required by Canadian financial institutions [10].
  • Provident fund, insurance, and succession in India: If the deceased held employment or financial accounts in India, eligible nominees or heirs can file the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) Composite Claim Form in Death Cases to claim Provident Fund (PF) balances, Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension, and Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) benefits, as well as any Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) claims. To transfer bank accounts, securities, or real property in India where no valid nomination exists, family members may need to obtain a Legal Heir Certificate from the local Tehsildar/revenue authority or a Succession Certificate / Letters of Administration from the competent Indian civil court using the apostilled Canadian death documents [5].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance further: 1. In which Canadian province or territory did the death occur, and which city or state in India is the intended destination? 2. Have you decided whether to arrange full-body repatriation, cremation in Canada followed by transporting the ashes, or local burial/cremation in Canada?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Portugal: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Portugal, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Portugal.
introHtml: We are deeply sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with United Kingdom citizenship or residence ties dies in Portugal, the medical, civil registry, and funeral procedures in Portugal must be coordinated with British consular, public health/coroner, and estate administration requirements. Below are the 5 official steps applicable to the Portugal-United Kingdom corridor.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic or Police Clearance in Portugal
steps.html:
The first step is the official verification of the death in Portugal so that the electronic Death Certificate (Certificado de Óbito) can be issued through SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito, the Death Certificate Information System), managed jointly by the Directorate-General of Health (Direção-Geral da Saúde) and the Shared Services of the Ministry of Health (Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde - SPMS) [1].

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or care facility: The attending physician verifies the death, issues the electronic Certificado de Óbito in SICO, and automatically transmits the clinical and identification details to the civil registry system [1][5].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs outside a healthcare facility, immediately call the European emergency number (112) or the local police authority (PSP or GNR) [4][5]. Where there is no suspicion of foul play or violent cause, a family physician or local health authority (delegado de saúde) can verify the death; in cases of sudden, violent, or unexplained death, the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público) orders the intervention of the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses - INMLCF) for a medico-legal autopsy before the body is released [1][4].
  • Important precaution before authorizing cremation in Portugal: If the family intends to repatriate the deceased to England or Wales and there is any possibility of an inquest by a UK Coroner, the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office advises against authorizing cremation in Portugal before confirming Coroner requirements, as cremation prevents a post-mortem examination in the United Kingdom [4].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing a Funeral Director, and British Consular Contact
steps.html:
The family does not need to handle sanitary permits or air transport between the two countries on their own; a licensed funeral agency coordinates the entire operational process [4][5].

  • Checking travel or assistance insurance: Before entering into independent financial commitments, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, international health insurance, or coverage linked to bank cards [4]. Insurers typically appoint an international assistance provider directly and cover repatriation or local funeral costs [4].
  • Appointing a funeral director in Portugal and in the United Kingdom: In Portugal, the service must be carried out by a funeral agency (agência funerária) legally registered with the Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE, Directorate-General for Economic Activities) and, for guidance, affiliated with industry associations such as ANEL or AAFC [2][5]. In the United Kingdom, the Portuguese agency coordinates reception with a funeral director registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [3][4]. Clarvia provides references to official and trade directories for guidance only and does not recommend, endorse, or rank commercial providers.
  • British consular support in Portugal: Contact the British Embassy in Lisbon or the Vice-Consulate in Portimão through the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office at +44 20 7008 5000 (available 24 hours) for consular assistance, guidance on lists of local funeral directors and translators, and cancellation of the British passport [4].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Portugal and Document Recognition for the United Kingdom
steps.html:
A death occurring in Portugal must be registered with the Portuguese civil registry before burial, cremation, or international repatriation can take place [4][5].

  • Declaration at the Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) in Portugal: The death must be declared within 48 hours of the death or the issuance of clearance by the authorities, at a Conservatória do Registo Civil of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary, or at an Espaço Óbito desk, such as in Lisbon, Porto, or Faro) [5]. Ordinarily, the appointed funeral agency files this declaration using the SICO certificate [1][5]. The initial death registration (Assento de Óbito) is free of charge [5].
  • Certificates and translation for the United Kingdom: Request from the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado multiple certified copies of the Assento de Óbito, as well as the multilingual death certificate (CIEC Vienna Convention Form C / Modelo C) or a standard certificate accompanied by a certified English translation [4][5][6].
  • Registration rules in the United Kingdom: When a death occurs abroad, there is no legal requirement to re-register the death at a local UK Register Office (whose 5-day deadline in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8-day deadline in Scotland applies only to deaths occurring within the UK); the Portuguese death certificate (with a certified English translation) is accepted by UK institutions, alongside the option to apply for overseas consular death registration through the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [4][6].

steps.title: Choosing Between International Repatriation to the United Kingdom and Local Burial or Cremation in Portugal
steps.html:
The family may choose to repatriate the body in a sealed casket, transport the cremated ashes after cremation in Portugal, or hold the funeral locally in Portugal [4][6].

  • Repatriation of the body from Portugal to the United Kingdom: The funeral agency in Portugal obtains the international transfer permit / mortuary laissez-passer (alvará de trasladação / livre-trânsito mortuário, under the Strasbourg Agreement and Berlin Convention), the medical certificate confirming freedom from communicable infectious disease, and places the remains in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin [2][4][6]. For entry and burial or cremation in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director submits the translated death certificate and Portuguese export permit to the local Coroner to obtain an Out-of-England Order (or Form 104 for cremation); in Scotland, the documentation is submitted for review by the Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) of Healthcare Improvement Scotland [6]. If the deceased also held Portuguese nationality, additional consular information is available via the Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Consular Assistance Center of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United Kingdom: If cremation is carried out in Portugal, the family or funeral agency may transport the urn of ashes to the United Kingdom accompanied by the Death Certificate (Certidão de Óbito), the cremation certificate, and a funeral agency declaration confirming the contents of the urn, in compliance with airline regulations [4][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in Portugal: If the family chooses a local funeral in Portugal, the funeral agency handles the municipal permits directly with the cemetery or crematorium in the relevant municipality (concelho) [2][5].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in the United Kingdom and Portugal
steps.html:
Once the death certificates have been obtained, heirs or legal representatives must settle social security, tax, and estate obligations in both countries [7][10][11].

  • Notifications, pensions, and Probate in the United Kingdom: If the deceased was ordinarily resident in England, Scotland, or Wales and was in Portugal only temporarily, the family can use the UK government's Tell Us Once service to report the death simultaneously to HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, and local councils [4][7]. If the deceased lived permanently abroad, contact the DWP International Pension Centre directly to stop the UK State Pension and inquire about survivor benefits (Bereavement Support Payment), and notify HMRC [7][8]. To administer bank accounts or property in the United Kingdom, the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation in the Scottish courts) through the official probate portal [9].
  • Social Security, tax notifications, and inheritance in Portugal: If the deceased was covered by the Portuguese social security system, eligible family members may apply to the Instituto da Segurança Social (via Segurança Social Direta or in-person service desks) for the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days of registering the death), Reimbursement of Funeral Expenses (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 consecutive days of the death for the person who paid the funeral expenses where no funeral allowance applies), and the Survivor's Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [10]. Where assets exist in Portugal, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must report the death to the Tax and Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira / Finanças) for Stamp Duty (Imposto do Selo) purposes by the end of the 3rd month following the month of death, and may complete the formal declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and division of assets at an Espaço Óbito or the Balcão das Heranças [5][11].
