pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Portugal e Reino Unido: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Portugal e Reino Unido: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Lamentamos profundamente a perda do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa com cidadania ou residência no Reino Unido falece em Portugal, os procedimentos médicos, civis e funerários em Portugal devem ser articulados com as exigências consulares, sanitárias e sucessórias britânicas. Seguem-se os 5 passos oficiais aplicáveis ao corredor entre Portugal e o Reino Unido.

steps.title: Certificação médica do óbito e intervenção forense ou policial em Portugal
steps.html:
O primeiro passo consiste na verificação oficial do óbito em território português para que possa ser emitido o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico através do SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito), gerido em articulação com a Direção-Geral da Saúde e os Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde [1].

  • Óbito em hospital, clínica ou estrutura residencial: O médico assistente verifica o falecimento da pessoa falecida, emite o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico no SICO e transmite automaticamente os dados clínicos e de identificação ao sistema de registo civil [1][5].
  • Óbito no domicílio, unidade hoteleira ou via pública: Se o falecimento ocorrer fora de uma unidade de saúde, deve contactar de imediato o número europeu de emergência (112) ou a autoridade policial local (PSP ou GNR) [4][5]. Caso não haja suspeita de crime ou causa violenta, o médico de família ou a autoridade de saúde (delegado de saúde) pode verificar o óbito; em caso de morte súbita, violenta ou de causa desconhecida, o Ministério Público determina a intervenção do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) para autópsia médico-legal antes da libertação do corpo [1][4].
  • Atenção antes de autorizar a cremação em Portugal: Se a família pretender trasladar a pessoa falecida para Inglaterra ou País de Gales e existir a possibilidade de um inquérito pelo médico-legista britânico (Coroner), o Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office alerta para não autorizar a cremação em Portugal antes de confirmar os requisitos, pois a cremação impede a realização de exame pós-morte no Reino Unido [4].

steps.title: Seguro de viagem, nomeação de agência funerária e contacto consular britânico
steps.html:
Não é necessário que a família trate isoladamente das licenças sanitárias ou do transporte aéreo entre os dois países; uma agência funerária habilitada coordena todo o processo operacional [4][5].

  • Verificação de seguro de viagem ou assistência: Antes de assumir compromissos financeiros autónomos, verifique se a pessoa falecida dispunha de seguro de viagem, seguro de saúde internacional ou cobertura associada a cartões bancários [4]. As seguradoras costumam nomear diretamente uma empresa de assistência internacional e cobrir os custos de repatriamento ou funeral local [4].
  • Nomeação de agência funerária em Portugal e no Reino Unido: Em Portugal, o serviço deve ser assegurado por uma agência funerária legalmente habilitada junto da Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE) e, a título orientativo, associada em entidades representativas do setor como a ANEL ou a AAFC [2][5]. No Reino Unido, a agência portuguesa articula a receção com um agente funerário registado na National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) ou na National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [3][4]. A Clarvia disponibiliza referências de diretórios oficiais e associativos apenas para orientação e não recomenda, avaliza nem classifica prestadores comerciais.
  • Apoio consular britânico em Portugal: Contacte a Embaixada Britânica em Lisboa ou o Vice-Consulado em Portimão através do Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office pelo telefone +44 20 7008 5000 (disponível 24 horas) para assistência consular, orientação sobre listas de agências funerárias e tradutores locais e anulação do passaporte britânico [4].

steps.title: Registo civil do óbito em Portugal e reconhecimento documental para o Reino Unido
steps.html:
O falecimento ocorrido em território português tem de ser obrigatoriamente registado no registo civil português antes da inumação, cremação ou trasladação internacional [4][5].

  • Declaração na Conservatória do Registo Civil em Portugal: O óbito deve ser declarado no prazo máximo de 48 horas após o falecimento ou a emissão da guia pelas autoridades, numa Conservatória do Registo Civil do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (ou num balcão do Espaço Óbito, como em Lisboa, Porto ou Faro) [5]. Habitualmente, a agência funerária contratada efetua esta comunicação com base no certificado SICO [1][5]. O registo inicial (Assento de Óbito) é gratuito [5].
  • Certidões e tradução para o Reino Unido: Solicite ao Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado várias cópias certificadas do Assento de Óbito, bem como a certidão de óbito em modelo plurilingue (Modelo C da Convenção de Viena da CIEC) ou certidão acompanhada de tradução certificada para inglês [4][5][6].
  • Regras de registo no Reino Unido: Quando o óbito ocorre no estrangeiro, não existe obrigação legal de o registar novamente na conservatória local (Register Office, cujo prazo de 5 dias em Inglaterra, País de Gales e Irlanda do Norte ou 8 dias na Escócia se aplica apenas a óbitos ocorridos em solo britânico), sendo a certidão portuguesa (com tradução certificada para inglês) aceite pelas instituições britânicas, sem prejuízo da possibilidade de inscrição no registo consular de óbitos no estrangeiro através do Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [4][6].

steps.title: Opção entre trasladação internacional para o Reino Unido e inumação ou cremação em Portugal
steps.html:
A família pode optar pelo repatriamento do corpo em urna selada, pelo transporte das cinzas após cremação em Portugal ou pela realização do funeral localmente em Portugal [4][6].

  • Trasladação do corpo de Portugal para o Reino Unido: A agência funerária em Portugal obtém o alvará de trasladação / livre-trânsito mortuário internacional (ao abrigo do Acordo de Estrasburgo e da Convenção de Berlim), o certificado médico comprovativo da inexistência de doença infetocontagiosa e procede ao acondicionamento em caixão de zinco hermeticamente selado [2][4][6]. Para a entrada e inumação ou cremação em Inglaterra ou no País de Gales, o agente funerário recetor apresenta a certidão de óbito traduzida e a licença de saída portuguesa ao médico-legista local (Coroner) para emissão da Out-of-England Order (ou Form 104 para cremação); na Escócia, a documentação é submetida à verificação do Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) da Healthcare Improvement Scotland [6]. Caso a pessoa falecida tivesse também nacionalidade portuguesa, informações adicionais sobre apoio consular podem ser consultadas no Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Centro de Atendimento Consular do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros.
  • Transporte de cinzas para o Reino Unido: Se a cremação for realizada em Portugal, a família ou a agência funerária pode transportar a urna de cinzas para o Reino Unido acompanhada da Certidão de Óbito, do certificado de cremação e de declaração da agência funerária sobre o conteúdo da urna, cumprindo as regras da companhia aérea [4][6].
  • Inumação ou cremação local em Portugal: Caso a família opte pelo funeral em Portugal, a agência funerária trata das guias municipais junto do cemitério ou crematório do concelho respetivo [2][5].

steps.title: Notificações pós-óbito, pensões de sobrevivência, impostos e sucessão no Reino Unido e em Portugal
steps.html:
Após a obtenção das certidões de óbito, os herdeiros ou representantes legais devem regularizar as obrigações previdenciais, fiscais e sucessórias nos dois países [7][10][11].

  • Notificações, pensões e sucessão (Probate) no Reino Unido: Se a pessoa falecida residia habitualmente em Inglaterra, Escócia ou País de Gales e se encontrava em Portugal apenas temporariamente, a família pode utilizar o serviço governamental Tell Us Once para comunicar o óbito simultaneamente ao HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), ao Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), ao serviço de passaportes e às autarquias locais [4][7]. Se a pessoa falecida residia permanentemente no estrangeiro, deve contactar diretamente o International Pension Centre do DWP para cessar a pensão estatal britânica e requerer eventuais prestações de viuvez ou luto (Bereavement Support Payment), bem como notificar o HMRC [7][8]. Para movimentar contas bancárias ou património no Reino Unido, o testamenteiro ou administrador solicita o Grant of Probate (ou Letters of Administration em Inglaterra, País de Gales e Irlanda do Norte, ou Confirmation nos tribunais escoceses) através do portal oficial de sucessões [9].
  • Segurança Social, Finanças e herança em Portugal: Se a pessoa falecida era beneficiária do sistema português, os familiares elegíveis podem requerer junto do Instituto da Segurança Social (através da Segurança Social Direta ou nos balcões de atendimento) o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do registo do óbito), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias consecutivos a contar do óbito, para quem pagou o funeral e quando não haja lugar a subsídio de funeral) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [10]. Caso existam bens em Portugal, o cabeça-de-casal deve participar o óbito à Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Finanças) para efeitos de Imposto do Selo até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao do falecimento e pode realizar a habilitação de herdeiros e a partilha no Espaço Óbito ou no Balcão das Heranças [5][11].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos adaptar estas informações à situação específica da sua família: 1. Em que município de Portugal ocorreu o falecimento e para que região do Reino Unido (Inglaterra, País de Gales, Escócia ou Irlanda do Norte) pretendem organizar o funeral ou a administração dos bens? 2. Já decidiram se pretendem a trasladação do corpo, a cremação em Portugal seguida do transporte das cinzas ou o funeral em Portugal?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Italy: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Italy, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Italy.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for your loss. When a person with United Kingdom citizenship or residence ties dies in Italy, Italian medical, civil registry, and mortuary police procedures must be coordinated with British consular, customs, and probate formalities. Below are the 5 official steps applicable to the corridor between Italy and the United Kingdom.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death, Necroscopic Certificate, and Judicial Clearance in Italy
steps.html:
Before proceeding with civil registration, cremation, burial, or international repatriation, the competent medical authorities in Italy must issue the medical certification of death [1][3][4].

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or residential care facility: The hospital medical management (direzione sanitaria) certifies the death of the deceased person, completes the ISTAT cause-of-death statistical form (scheda ISTAT), and arranges the necroscopic examination before transmitting the death notice (avviso di morte) to the competent municipality (Comune) [1][3].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call the emergency number (112 or 118) [1]. The attending physician issues the initial medical confirmation of death (constatazione di decesso); subsequently, the medical examiner (medico necroscopo) of the Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) performs the mandatory necroscopic examination (normally between 15 and 30 hours after death) to issue the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico) and confirm compliance with the statutory observation period [1][4]. In the event of a sudden, violent, accidental, or unattended death, the Judicial Authority (Autorità Giudiziaria / Procura della Repubblica, Public Prosecutor's Office) intervenes and may order transfer to the municipal mortuary and a forensic autopsy before issuing judicial clearance (nulla osta) for burial, cremation, or international transport [1][4].
  • Precaution before authorizing cremation in Italy: If repatriation to the United Kingdom (particularly to England or Wales) is planned and there is any possibility that the British Coroner may require an inquest into the cause of death, the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office advises against cremating the body in Italy before verifying the Coroner's requirements, as cremation would prevent post-mortem examinations in the United Kingdom [1][5].

steps.title: Checking Insurance, Appointing a Funeral Director, and British Consular Assistance
steps.html:
The family does not need to manage health and customs permits between the two countries on their own: a licensed funeral director coordinates the entire operational process [1][4].

  • Checking travel or repatriation insurance: Before signing private funeral contracts, verify whether the deceased person held travel insurance, private health cover, or credit card assistance benefits [1]. Insurance companies normally appoint an international assistance provider that coordinates funeral services directly and covers the costs of repatriation or local burial [1].
  • Appointing a funeral director in Italy and the United Kingdom: In Italy, you can mandate a licensed funeral company (impresa funebre autorizzata, for example a member of national trade federations such as FENIOF or Federcofit, or by consulting consular informational lists) [1][4]. The Italian funeral director works in coordination with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [1][2]. Clarvia provides references to official and trade directories solely for informational guidance and does not recommend, endorse, or rank individual commercial providers.
  • Contacting the UK consular network in Italy: Contact the British Embassy in Rome or the British Consulate General in Milan through the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office on +44 20 7008 5000 (available 24 hours a day) for consular assistance, guidance on lists of funeral directors and sworn translators, and cancellation of the British passport [1].

steps.title: Civil Registration in Italy and Document Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
A death occurring on Italian territory must be registered with the municipality (Comune) where the death took place before burial, cremation, or repatriation permits can be issued [1][3].

  • Death declaration at the Civil Registry Office in Italy: The declaration of death (denuncia di morte) must be submitted within 24 hours of the death to the Civil Registry Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the competent Italian municipality (for example at the Comune di Milano or the Central Registry of Rome, Anagrafe Centrale di Roma Capitale) by a family member, the hospital medical management, or, by family proxy, the appointed funeral company [1][3]. The Civil Registrar (Ufficiale di Stato Civile) draws up the death record (atto di morte), issues the burial permit (permesso di seppellimento), and provides death certificates and extracts, including the multilingual extract on Form C (estratto plurilingue su Modello C, under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention) [3][4].
  • Translation, Apostille, and registration rules in the United Kingdom: Because both Italy (through the Prefettura - Ufficio Territoriale del Governo for administrative and civil status documents) and the United Kingdom are parties to the 1961 Hague Convention, Italian death certificates required by British authorities can be legalized with an Apostille and accompanied by a certified English translation [1][5]. In the United Kingdom, it is not mandatory to re-register a death that occurred abroad at a local Register Office (the 5-day deadline in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or the 8-day deadline in Scotland applies to deaths occurring within the United Kingdom), though relatives may optionally apply for consular death registration through the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [1][5].

steps.title: Choosing Between International Repatriation to the United Kingdom and Local Burial or Cremation in Italy
steps.html:
Family members may choose whether to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to the United Kingdom or proceed with local burial or cremation in Italy [1][4][5].

  • Repatriation of the body from Italy to the United Kingdom: Under the mortuary police regulations outlined by the Ministero dell'Interno (Ministry of the Interior) and the 1937 Berlin International Convention, the funeral company applies to the Italian municipality of death for the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario), supported by the death extract, the ASL health certificate confirming compliance with sanitary standards and the absence of infectious diseases, and the official report confirming sealing of the double coffin with a soldered metal liner [4]. Where the deceased person also held Italian citizenship, foreign consular procedures fall under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale - MAECI). Upon arrival in England or Wales, the British funeral director submits the translated death certificate and the Passaporto Mortuario to the local Coroner to obtain authorization for burial or cremation (Out-of-England Order / Form 104), whereas in Scotland the documentation is reviewed by the Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) of Healthcare Improvement Scotland [5].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United Kingdom: If cremation takes place in Italy (subject to authorization by the Civil Registrar based on the expressed wishes of the deceased person or entitled next of kin), transporting the cinerary urn to the United Kingdom requires the death certificate, the cremation certificate (verbale di cremazione), and the municipal permit for the transport of ashes, in compliance with airline regulations [1][4][5].
  • Local burial or cremation in Italy: If you opt for entombment (tumulazione), ground burial (inumazione), or cremation in Italy, the funeral company manages the burial permit and transport directly with the municipal cemetery services of the competent Italian municipality (such as the Comune di Milano) [3][4].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Probate in the United Kingdom and Italy
steps.html:
Once the death certificates have been obtained, entitled family members or executors must complete social security, tax, and estate administration procedures in both states [6][9][10].

  • Benefits, tax, and probate procedures in the United Kingdom: If the deceased person was habitually resident in England, Scotland, or Wales and was in Italy only temporarily, you can use the UK government's Tell Us Once service to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, and local councils in a single step [1][6]. If the deceased person lived permanently abroad, you must contact the DWP International Pension Centre directly to stop British State Pension payments and check eligibility for survivor benefits (Bereavement Support Payment), as well as notify HMRC directly [6][7]. To administer bank accounts or assets located in the United Kingdom, the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation before the Sheriff Court in Scotland) through the official court service [8].
  • Social security, succession tax return, and will search in Italy: If the deceased person accrued pension contributions or received a pension in Italy, eligible relatives can submit an online claim for a survivor's pension (pensione ai superstiti - pensione di reversibilità or pensione indiretta) to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Social Security Institute - INPS, including via a patronato assistance office) [9]. If your family member owned real estate or financial assets in Italy, the heirs or legatees must electronically file the Italian inheritance tax return (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months from the date of death [10]. To check for the existence of a public, secret, or formally deposited holographic will in Italy or in a state party to the Basel Convention, you can request a certificate from the Registro Generale dei Testamenti (General Register of Wills, managed by the Ministry of Justice - Central Office of Notarial Archives) or consult the National Council of Notaries (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) [11].

it.title: Cosa fare in caso di decesso tra Italia e Regno Unito: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso tra Italia e Regno Unito: certificato medico di morte, impresa funebre autorizzata, registrazione allo Stato Civile, pratiche consolari e rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri, e pensione di reversibilità e successione.
it.introHtml: Vi esprimiamo le nostre più sincere condoglianze per la perdita che vi ha colpito. Quando una persona con cittadinanza o residenza nel Regno Unito decede in Italia, gli adempimenti sanitari, di stato civile e di polizia mortuaria italiani devono essere coordinati con le procedure consolari, doganali e successorie britanniche. Di seguito sono illustrati i 5 passaggi ufficiali applicabili al corridoio tra Italia e Regno Unito.

steps.title: Constatazione medica del decesso, certificato necroscopico e nulla osta dell'Autorità Giudiziaria in Italia
steps.html:
Prima di procedere alla registrazione civile, alla cremazione, alla sepoltura o al rimpatrio internazionale, i sanitari competenti in Italia devono redigere la certificazione medica di morte [1][3][4].

  • Decesso in ospedale, clinica o struttura residenziale: La direzione sanitaria della struttura accerta la morte della persona deceduta, compila la scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte e provvede all'accertamento necroscopico prima di trasmettere l'avviso di morte al Comune competente [1][3].
  • Decesso a domicilio, in albergo o in luogo pubblico: Chiamate immediatamente il numero unico di emergenza (112 o 118) [1]. Il medico intervenuto redige la constatazione di decesso; successivamente, il medico necroscopo dell'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) effettua la visita necroscopica obbligatoria (di norma tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso) per rilasciare il certificato necroscopico e rispettare il periodo legale di osservazione [1][4]. In caso di morte improvvisa, violenta, accidentale o in assenza di assistenza medica, interviene l'Autorità Giudiziaria (Procura della Repubblica), che può disporre il trasferimento all'obitorio comunale e l'autopsia giudiziaria prima di rilasciare il nulla osta alla sepoltura, alla cremazione o al trasporto internazionale [1][4].
  • Avvertenza prima di autorizzare la cremazione in Italia: Se si prevede il trasferimento nel Regno Unito (in particolare in Inghilterra o Galles) e sussiste la possibilità che il Coroner britannico disponga un'indagine sulle cause del decesso, il Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office segnala di non procedere alla cremazione in Italia prima di aver verificato i requisiti del Coroner, poiché la cremazione impedirebbe eventuali accertamenti medico-legali nel Regno Unito [1][5].

steps.title: Verifica dell'assicurazione, incarico all'impresa funebre e assistenza consolare britannica
steps.html:
La famiglia non deve gestire autonomamente i permessi sanitari e doganali tra i due Paesi: un'impresa funebre autorizzata coordina l'intero iter operativo [1][4].

  • Verifica della polizza di viaggio o di rimpatrio: Prima di sottoscrivere contratti autonomi, verificate se la persona deceduta disponeva di un'assicurazione di viaggio, di una copertura sanitaria privata o di servizi di assistenza collegati a carte di credito [1]. Le compagnie assicurative incaricano solitamente una centrale operativa internazionale che coordina direttamente le onoranze funebri e copre le spese di rimpatrio o sepoltura locale [1].
  • Incarico a un'impresa funebre in Italia e nel Regno Unito: In Italia potete conferire mandato a un'impresa funebre autorizzata (ad esempio aderente alle federazioni nazionali di categoria quali FENIOF o Federcofit, oppure consultando gli elenchi informativi consolari) [1][4]. L'impresa italiana opera in raccordo con un'agenzia funebre ricevente nel Regno Unito iscritta alla National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) o alla National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [1][2]. Clarvia fornisce riferimenti a elenchi ufficiali e associativi esclusivamente a scopo orientativo e non raccomanda, approva né classifica singoli operatori commerciali.
  • Contatto con la rete consolare del Regno Unito in Italia: Contattate l'Ambasciata Britannica a Roma o il Consolato Generale Britannico a Milano tramite il Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office al numero +44 20 7008 5000 (attivo 24 ore su 24) per assistenza consolare, indicazioni sugli elenchi di imprese funebri e traduttori giurati e per l'annullamento del passaporte britannico [1].

steps.title: Registrazione presso lo Stato Civile in Italia e riconoscimento dei documenti nel Regno Unito
steps.html:
Il decesso avvenuto sul territorio italiano deve essere registrato presso il Comune in cui si è verificato l'evento prima che possano essere rilasciati i permessi di seppellimento, cremazione o rimpatrio [1][3].

  • Denuncia di morte presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile in Italia: La dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano competente (ad esempio presso il Comune di Milano o l'Anagrafe Centrale di Roma Capitale) da parte di un familiare, della direzione sanitaria ospedaliera o, per delega della famiglia, dall'impresa di onoranze funebri incaricata [1][3]. L'Ufficiale di Stato Civile forma l'atto di morte, rilascia il permesso di seppellimento e fornisce i certificati e gli estratti per riassunto dell'atto di morte, incluso l'estratto plurilingue su Modello C (Convenzione di Vienna del 1976) [3][4].
  • Traduzione, Apostille e regole di registrazione nel Regno Unito: Poiché sia l'Italia (tramite la Prefettura - Ufficio Territoriale del Governo per gli atti amministrativi e di stato civile) sia il Regno Unito aderiscono alla Convenzione dell'Aia del 1961, è possibile munire di Apostille e traduzione certificata in lingua inglese i certificati di morte italiani richiesti dalle autorità britanniche [1][5]. Nel Regno Unito non è obbligatorio registrare nuovamente presso il Register Office locale un decesso avvenuto all'estero (il termine di 5 giorni in Inghilterra, Galles e Irlanda del Nord o di 8 giorni in Scozia vale per i decessi avvenuti nel Regno Unito), ma i familiari possono richiedere facoltativamente la registrazione consolare tramite il Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [1][5].

steps.title: Scelta tra rimpatrio internazionale nel Regno Unito e sepoltura o cremazione in Italia
steps.html:
I familiari possono scegliere se rimpatriare la salma o le ceneri nel Regno Unito oppure procedere alla sepoltura o cremazione in Italia [1][4][5].

  • Rimpatrio della salma dall'Italia al Regno Unito: Secondo la normativa di polizia mortuaria illustrata dal Ministero dell'Interno e dalla Convenzione Internazionale di Berlino del 1937, l'impresa funebre richiede al Comune italiano di decesso il Passaporto Mortuario (corredato dall'estratto di morte, dal certificato dell'ASL che attesta l'osservanza delle prescrizioni igienico-sanitarie e l'assenza di malattie infettivo-diffusive, e dal verbale di chiusura della doppia cassa con cofano metallico saldato a fuoco) [4]. Qualora la persona deceduta avesse anche cittadinanza italiana, le procedure consolari estere fanno capo al Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI). All'arrivo in Inghilterra o Galles, l'agenzia funebre britannica presenta il certificato di morte tradotto e il Passaporto Mortuario al Coroner locale per ottenere l'autorizzazione alla sepoltura o alla cremazione (Out-of-England Order / Form 104), mentre in Scozia la documentazione è sottoposta alla verifica del Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) di Healthcare Improvement Scotland [5].
  • Trasporto delle ceneri nel Regno Unito: Se la cremazione avviene in Italia (previa autorizzazione dell'Ufficiale di Stato Civile sulla base della volontà espressa dalla persona deceduta o dai familiari aventi titolo), il trasporto dell'urna cineraria nel Regno Unito richiede il certificato di morte, il verbale di cremazione e l'autorizzazione comunale al trasporto delle ceneri, nel rispetto delle regole della compagnia aerea [1][4][5].
  • Sepoltura o cremazione locale in Italia: Se si opta per la tumulazione, inumazione o cremazione in Italia, l'impresa funebre gestisce il permesso di seppellimento e il trasporto direttamente con i servizi cimiteriali del Comune italiano competente (come il Comune di Milano) [3][4].

steps.title: Notifiche post-decesso, pensioni ai superstiti, fisco e successione nel Regno Unito e in Italia
steps.html:
Una volta ottenuti i certificati di morte, gli aventi diritto o gli esecutori testamentari devono completare le pratiche previdenziali, fiscali e successorie in entrambi gli Stati [6][9][10].

  • Adempimenti previdenziali, fiscali e Probate nel Regno Unito: Se la persona deceduta risiedeva abitualmente in Inghilterra, Scozia o Galles e si trovava in Italia solo temporaneamente, è possibile utilizzare il servizio governativo Tell Us Once per notificare il decesso in un'unica soluzione a HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), al Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), all'ufficio passaporti e agli enti locali [1][6]. Se invece risiedeva stabilmente all'estero, occorre contattare direttamente l'International Pension Centre del DWP per interrompere l'erogazione della pensione statale britannica e verificare il diritto a prestazioni per i superstiti (Bereavement Support Payment), oltre a informare direttamente HMRC [6][7]. Per amministrare conti bancari o beni situati nel Regno Unito, l'esecutore o amministratore richiede il Grant of Probate (o Letters of Administration in Inghilterra, Galles e Irlanda del Nord, oppure la Confirmation presso la Sheriff Court in Scozia) tramite il servizio ufficiale [8].
  • Previdenza, dichiarazione di successione e ricerca testamentaria in Italia: Se la persona deceduta aveva maturato contributi o percepiva una pensione in Italia, i familiari aventi diritto possono presentare domanda telematica di pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità o pensione indiretta) presso l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (anche tramite un patronato) [9]. Qualora il vostro familiare possedesse immobili o attività finanziarie in Italia, gli eredi o i chiamati all'eredità devono presentare in via telematica la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione (data del decesso) [10]. Per verificare l'esistenza di un testamento pubblico, segreto o olografo depositato formalmente in Italia o in uno Stato aderente alla Convenzione di Basilea, è possibile richiedere una certificazione al Registro Generale dei Testamenti (gestito dal Ministero della Giustizia - Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili) o rivolgersi al Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [11].

it.closingQuestion: Per aiutarci a fornirvi indicazioni ancora più mirate: 1. In quale Comune italiano è avvenuto il decesso e in quale nazione costitutiva del Regno Unito (Inghilterra, Galles, Scozia o Irlanda del Nord) si trovano la residenza o i beni principali? 2. Avete già deciso se procedere con il rimpatrio della salma, con la cremazione in Italia seguita dal trasporto delle ceneri o con la sepoltura in Italia?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Ireland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Ireland: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Ireland, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Ireland.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in Ireland, Irish medical, civil registration, and coroner procedures must be coordinated with United Kingdom consular, repatriation, and estate requirements. Below is the 5-step official corridor guide for Ireland and the United Kingdom.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and police or coroner clearance in Ireland
steps.html:
Before civil death registration, cremation, burial, or repatriation across the Irish Sea or land border to the United Kingdom can take place, the cause of death must be formally certified in Ireland [1][5].

  • Death in a hospital, hospice, or nursing home (expected death): If a registered medical practitioner attended the deceased during the month before death and is certain of the natural cause of death, the doctor completes and signs Part 1 of the Death Notification Form (DNF) (which incorporates the medical certificate of the cause of death) and hands it to a qualified family informant [1][5].
  • Sudden, unexpected, accidental, or non-hospital death: Call emergency services (999 or 112) and An Garda Síochána immediately [1][4]. Where the death was sudden, unexplained, violent, or unnatural, or if no doctor attended the deceased within the preceding month, the death must be reported to the local Coroner (for example, the Dublin District Coroner or Cork City Coroner) [1][5]. In coronial cases, a doctor cannot issue the Death Notification Form; the Coroner may direct a post-mortem examination or inquest and issues an interim Coroner's Certificate to allow funeral and transport arrangements to proceed before sending the final certificate directly to the civil registrar [1][5].
  • Caution before authorizing cremation in Ireland: If the family plans to repatriate the deceased to England or Wales and there is any possibility of a UK coroner's inquest, the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office advises against cremation in Ireland before confirming coronial requirements, as cremation prevents a post-mortem examination in the United Kingdom [4][6].

steps.title: Insurance verification, funeral director appointment, and British consular support
steps.html:
You do not have to coordinate cross-border mortuary transport and customs clearances on your own; licensed funeral directors in Ireland and the United Kingdom handle the operational transfer end-to-end [1][4].

  • Check travel or repatriation insurance first: Before entering into private funeral contracts, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, private medical insurance, or bank/employer bereavement cover, as the insurer's assistance service normally appoints the international funeral coordinator and covers repatriation costs [4].
  • Appoint a funeral director in Ireland and a receiving provider in the United Kingdom: You can appoint an Irish funeral director using the member directory of the Irish Association of Funeral Directors (phone +353 818 935 000, email enquiries@iafd.ie) [2], who will coordinate transport by air or ferry with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [3][4]. Clarvia provides professional directory links for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers.
  • Contact British consular services in Ireland: Contact the British Embassy in Dublin through the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (+44 20 7008 5000, available 24/7) for consular bereavement guidance, local funeral director lists in Ireland, and British passport cancellation [4].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Ireland and document recognition for the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Every death occurring in the Republic of Ireland must be registered with the Irish civil registry [1][5].

  • Registering with the HSE Civil Registration Service / General Register Office (GRO): A qualified informant (usually a relative, or someone present at the death) must bring the completed Death Notification Form (Parts 1 and 2) and valid photo identification to any office of the HSE Civil Registration Service (such as the Dublin Civil Registration Service on Joyce House, Lombard Street East, or local offices in Cork, Galway, or Limerick) within 3 months of the death (accepted up to 12 months before requiring General Register Office approval) [1][5]. Registration is free, and you should order multiple official certified copies of the Irish Death Certificate from the HSE Civil Registration Service or the General Register Office (GRO) [5].
  • Document recognition and UK registration rules: Because Irish Death Certificates are issued in English (or bilingual Irish/English), they do not require translation for use in the United Kingdom, and under Common Travel Area practice and the Hague Apostille Convention (administered by the Department of Foreign Affairs in Dublin and Belfast/Cork offices where formal legalization is ever requested), Irish civil certificates are readily accepted by UK institutions [4][6]. A death that occurred outside the United Kingdom does not need to be re-registered at a UK local Register Office (where the 5-day deadline in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8-day deadline in Scotland applies only to deaths occurring within those jurisdictions), though British nationals may optionally apply for consular death registration via the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [4][6].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to the United Kingdom and local burial or cremation in Ireland
steps.html:
Your family can choose either to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to the United Kingdom or to hold the burial or cremation locally in Ireland [4][6].

  • Repatriation of the body from Ireland to the United Kingdom: To remove uncremated remains outside the State, the Irish funeral director obtains a Coroner's Removal Certificate (certifying that the local Coroner in Ireland has been notified and permits removal out of the jurisdiction), an embalming certificate, a certificate of freedom from infectious disease (coordinated with HSE Environmental Health where required), and prepares a leak-proof or hermetically sealed coffin for ferry or air transfer [1][4][6]. Upon arrival in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director submits the Irish Death Certificate and Coroner's removal documentation to the local Coroner to obtain an Out-of-England Order (or Form 104 for cremation); in Scotland, the documents are reviewed by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) before burial or cremation can proceed [6].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United Kingdom: If cremation takes place in Ireland first, you or your funeral director can transport the cremated ashes to the United Kingdom accompanied by the official Irish Death Certificate and the Cremation Certificate issued by the Irish crematorium, complying with airline or ferry operator screening rules [4][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in Ireland: If the family chooses local burial or cremation in Ireland, the appointed member of the Irish Association of Funeral Directors arranges the cemetery opening or medical referee cremation authorization directly in Ireland [1][2].

steps.title: Post-death notifications, survivor benefits, taxes, and probate in the United Kingdom and Ireland
steps.html:
Once official Death Certificates are obtained, the executor, administrator, or eligible family members must complete social welfare, tax, and estate steps in both jurisdictions [7][9][10][12].

  • Notifications, pensions, tax, and probate in the United Kingdom: If the deceased normally lived in England, Scotland, or Wales and died while temporarily in Ireland, you can use the UK government's Tell Us Once service to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, and local councils in a single step [4][7]. If the deceased lived permanently in Ireland or abroad, contact the DWP's International Pension Centre (or the DWP Bereavement Service) directly to stop UK State Pension payments and check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment, and notify HMRC directly [7][8]. To administer bank accounts, property, or investments in the United Kingdom, the executor or next of kin applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland [9].
  • Social welfare, Revenue, and probate in Ireland: If the deceased worked, lived, or held assets in Ireland, notify the Department of Social Protection (and update MyGovID records) to stop Irish social welfare payments and check eligibility for the Bereaved Partner's (Contributory) Pension (formerly the Widowed or Surviving Civil Partner's Contributory Pension) or the Bereaved Parent Grant (noting that the universal Bereavement Grant has been discontinued, though an Exceptional Needs Payment may assist with funeral costs in cases of financial hardship) [1][10]. For Irish estate assets, the legal representative must submit the online Statement of Affairs (Probate) Form SA.2 to the Revenue Commissioners to obtain a Notice of Acknowledgement (Probate) [11][12], and then apply to the High Court Probate Office (in Dublin or the relevant District Probate Registry) for an Irish Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration [12].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance further: 1. In which county or city in Ireland did the death occur, and which constituent nation of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) is the destination for the funeral or estate administration? 2. Have you decided whether to repatriate the body to the United Kingdom, arrange cremation in Ireland followed by transporting the ashes, or hold the funeral in Ireland?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Ireland Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Ireland Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Ireland dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Ireland and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of Ireland dies in the United Kingdom, medical certification, civil registration, and coroner or procurator fiscal procedures in the relevant UK nation (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) must be coordinated with Irish consular, repatriation, and succession procedures. Below is the 5-step official corridor guide for the United Kingdom and Ireland.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and coroner or procurator fiscal clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Before civil registration, cremation, burial, or international repatriation to Ireland can proceed, an attending doctor or coronial authority in the United Kingdom must certify the cause of death [1][2].

  • Expected death in a hospital, hospice, or care setting: In England and Wales, the attending medical practitioner completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is then scrutinized and countersigned by an independent Medical Examiner (who contacts the family to explain the cause of death and answer questions before sending the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office) [1][2]. In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), subject to random review by the Death Certification Review Service (DCRS); in Northern Ireland, a doctor who treated the deceased within the preceding 28 days transmits the MCCD to the General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI) [1].
  • Sudden, unexpected, accidental, or non-hospital death: Call emergency services (999 or 111) immediately [1]. If the cause of death is unknown, sudden, violent, unnatural, or occurs during surgery or custody, the doctor or police must refer the death to the local Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland) [1][2]. Civil registration and international removal must wait until the Coroner or Procurator Fiscal concludes the initial investigation or post-mortem and issues an interim certificate or release order [1][2].

steps.title: Insurance verification, funeral director appointment, and Irish consular assistance
steps.html:
You do not have to manage cross-border mortuary transport and customs paperwork on your own; licensed funeral directors in the United Kingdom and Ireland coordinate the transfer end-to-end [5][6].

  • Check travel, medical, or repatriation insurance first: Before entering into independent funeral commitments, verify whether the deceased held travel insurance, private health cover, or employer/bank bereavement cover, as the insurer's assistance team usually appoints the funeral coordinator directly [5][6].
  • Appoint a funeral director in the United Kingdom and a receiving provider in Ireland: You can appoint a UK funeral director through the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [3], who will coordinate air or ferry transport with a receiving funeral director in Ireland listed with the Irish Association of Funeral Directors (phone +353 818 935 000, email enquiries@iafd.ie) [4][6]. Clarvia supplies directory references for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers.
  • Contact the Irish Embassy or Consulate in the United Kingdom: For consular assistance, guidance on local procedures, and liaison with authorities, contact the Department of Foreign Affairs (Consular Assistance Unit in Dublin at +353 1 408 2000, the Embassy of Ireland in London, or the Consulates General of Ireland in Edinburgh, Cardiff, or Manchester) [5][6]. While the Department of Foreign Affairs cannot pay funeral or repatriation bills, charitable advice for sudden deaths abroad is also available from voluntary organizations such as the Kevin Bell Repatriation Trust [5][6].

steps.title: Civil death registration in the United Kingdom and document recognition for Ireland
steps.html:
The death must be registered in the constituent nation of the United Kingdom where it occurred before official Death Certificates and repatriation permits can be issued [1][6].

  • Registering at the local Register Office in the United Kingdom: Once the Medical Examiner (in England & Wales), doctor, or Coroner notifies the registrar, a qualified informant registers the death at the local Register Office (for example, Westminster Register Office in London, Birmingham Register Office, or a local registration office in Scotland or Northern Ireland) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (and, where a coronial inquest is pending, the Coroner's Interim Certificate of the Fact of Death) [1][6].
  • Document recognition and civil registration rules in Ireland: Because UK Death Certificates are issued in English, no translation is required for use in Ireland, and under Common Travel Area practice and the Hague Apostille Convention (administered by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office if an Apostille is ever requested), UK civil death certificates are directly accepted for estate, bank, and social welfare purposes in Ireland [6][7]. When a death is officially registered in the United Kingdom where it occurred, it is generally not re-registered in the domestic register of the HSE Civil Registration Service / General Register Office (GRO, where the 3-month registration window applies to deaths occurring within Ireland), unless the death falls under specific statutory provisions for Irish citizens dying abroad or on transit [6][7].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to Ireland and local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your family can choose either to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to Ireland or to arrange local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom [1][6].

  • Repatriation of uncremated human remains from the United Kingdom to Ireland: In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, the UK funeral director must notify the local Coroner (submitting Form 103 alongside the Death Certificate or Coroner's release) to obtain an Out-of-England Order (or removal notice out of the jurisdiction) at least 4 clear days before removal, unless the Coroner grants an earlier clearance [1][6]. In Scotland, clearance to remove remains outside Scotland is coordinated with the local registrar and the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1][6]. The UK funeral director also provides an embalming certificate, a medical certificate confirming freedom from infectious disease, and prepares a sealed coffin meeting airline or ferry and HSE Environmental Health / Irish customs entry requirements [6]. Upon arrival in Ireland, if a post-mortem or inquest is required by the local Irish Coroner before burial or cremation in Ireland, the receiving member of the Irish Association of Funeral Directors coordinates directly with the local Coroner [4][6].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to Ireland: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom first, you do not need an Out-of-England Order from the Coroner to take cremated ashes out of the United Kingdom; carry the official UK Death Certificate and the Cremation Certificate issued by the UK crematorium in a security-screenable urn in accordance with airline or ferry rules [6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the family chooses burial or cremation in the United Kingdom, the registrar (or Coroner via Form 6 / Cremation Form 6) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to your UK funeral director [1][3].

steps.title: Post-death notifications, survivor benefits, taxes, and probate in Ireland and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once official Death Certificates are issued, the executor, administrator, or eligible family members must settle social protection, tax, and probate matters in both countries [8][10][11][13].

  • Social welfare, tax, and probate in Ireland: Notify the Department of Social Protection (and update MyGovID records) to stop any Irish State pension or welfare payments and to claim eligible survivor supports, such as the Bereaved Partner's (Contributory) Pension (formerly the Widowed or Surviving Civil Partner's Contributory Pension) or the Bereaved Parent Grant (noting that the universal Bereavement Grant has been discontinued, though an Exceptional Needs Payment under the Supplementary Welfare Allowance Scheme may help with funeral costs in cases of financial hardship) [11]. For estate assets in Ireland, the executor or administrator must submit the online Statement of Affairs (Probate) Form SA.2 to the Revenue Commissioners to obtain a Notice of Acknowledgement (Probate) [12][13], and then apply to the High Court Probate Office (in Dublin or the local District Probate Registry) for an Irish Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration [13].
  • Notifications, pensions, tax, and probate in the United Kingdom: In England, Scotland, and Wales, the Tell Us Once service (provided by the registrar at the time of death registration) allows you to report the death simultaneously to HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP Bereavement Service), HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local councils [1][8]. If Tell Us Once is not available (such as in Northern Ireland or for certain cross-border residents), contact the DWP Bereavement Service or the International Pension Centre and HMRC directly [8][9]. If the deceased left bank accounts, property, or investments in the United Kingdom, the legal representative applies for a UK Grant of Probate (England, Wales, or Northern Ireland) or Confirmation (Scotland) [10].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance further: 1. In which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) did the death occur, and which county or city in Ireland is the intended destination? 2. Have you decided whether to repatriate the body to Ireland, arrange cremation in the United Kingdom before bringing the ashes to Ireland, or hold the funeral in the United Kingdom?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Poland Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Poland Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Poland dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Poland and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of Poland dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate medical and civil steps follow UK rules (which differ slightly between England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland), while cross-border transport, civil record transcription, and Polish survivor or inheritance procedures involve Polish consular and domestic authorities.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Expected or hospital deaths: In England and Wales, an attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is scrutinized and countersigned by an independent Medical Examiner before being sent electronically to the local Register Office [1]. In Scotland, a doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for review by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) before funeral or repatriation arrangements can be completed [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or accidental deaths: If the death occurs unexpectedly at home or in a public place, call emergency services on 999 (or 111 when a death was expected at home). Unexplained, sudden, or unnatural deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (for example, Inner West London Coroner's Court) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1][2]. When a Coroner or Procurator Fiscal investigates, civil registration and international release wait until the forensic examination is complete and the Coroner issues the relevant release paperwork (such as an interim certificate of the fact of death or burial/cremation order) [1][2].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Polish Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check insurance coverage first: Before signing an independent funeral or international transport contract, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or employer-sponsored repatriation insurance. If a policy applies, the insurer's assistance team usually appoints the funeral coordinators directly and covers eligible repatriation expenses.
  • Appointing a UK and Polish funeral coordinator: If no insurer is managing the transfer, you can appoint a licensed UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors [3] or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [4], coordinated with a receiving funeral home in Poland (zakład pogrzebowy, such as a member of the Polish Funeral Industry Chamber, Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej, or Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe). These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank providers.
  • Polish consular notification and role: Contact the competent Polish consular mission in the United Kingdom, such as the Embassy of the Republic of Poland in London (Consular and Polish Diaspora Section, email london.op@msz.gov.pl) or the Polish Consulates General in Manchester (manchester@msz.gov.pl), Edinburgh (edinburgh@msz.gov.pl), or Belfast (belfast.kg.sekretariat@msz.gov.pl) [5]. The consulate does not pay for or organize the commercial transport itself, but it issues the mandatory consular certificate (zaświadczenie konsula RP) authorizing the cross-border entry of human remains or cremated ashes into Poland [5].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom and Document Recognition for Poland
steps.html:
• UK civil registration: Once the Medical Examiner or Coroner confirms that registration can proceed, register the death at the local Register Office in the district where the person died (for example, Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1]. The registrar issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the "green form" for local disposition) and official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate, which you should purchase in multiple originals for banks, insurers, and Polish authorities [1][2].
  • Legalization (Apostille) and Polish civil registry transcription: For official use in Poland, UK public documents generally require a Hague Apostille issued by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office [6], together with a certified translation into Polish (tłumaczenie przysięgłe) [5]. While domestic deaths in Poland must be reported to the local civil registry (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego - USC) within 3 days of the medical death card (karta zgonu, or 24 hours in cases of infectious disease), a death occurring in the UK is registered first at the UK Register Office and subsequently transcribed (transkrypcja zagranicznego aktu zgonu) at a chosen Urząd Stanu Cywilnego in Poland (for example, Urząd Stanu Cywilnego m.st. Warszawy) or via the Polish consulate to obtain a Polish death certificate (odpis aktu zgonu) and, if needed for cross-border EU matters, a multilingual Vienna Convention Form C extract [5][7]. Note that prior transcription in a Polish USC is not required before the Polish consul issues the repatriation permit [5].

steps.title: Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to Poland vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Option A - Repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to Poland:
    • UK export clearance: Your UK funeral director obtains the Coroner's Out-of-England Order (Form 104 in England and Wales, or the equivalent clearance in Northern Ireland or Healthcare Improvement Scotland DCRS clearance in Scotland), an official embalming certificate, a medical certificate confirming freedom from communicable disease, and a funeral director's certificate confirming that the coffin (with a hermetically sealed metal/zinc liner) or cremation urn is sealed according to international transport standards [5].
    • Polish permit and consular certificate: Before the Polish consulate can issue its certificate, an entitled family member or the authorized Polish funeral home must obtain a permit to bring the remains or ashes into Poland (pozwolenie na sprowadzenie zwłok lub szczątków) from the competent county head or city mayor (starosta or prezydent miasta, such as Prezydent m.st. Warszawy or Prezydent Miasta Krakowa) for the planned burial location, issued within 3 days after consulting the State County Sanitary Inspector (Państwowy Powiatowy Inspektor Sanitarny - Sanepid) [5]. Once that Polish permit, the UK death or coroner's certificate, and the funeral/embalming certificates are submitted to the Embassy of the Republic of Poland in London (or competent Consulate General), the consul issues the cross-border transport certificate (zaświadczenie konsula RP) [5].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom:
    • If the burial or cremation takes place in the UK, the UK funeral director uses the Register Office "green form" (or the Coroner's Order for Burial or Cremation Form 6) to book the local cemetery or crematorium [1][2]. If the deceased is cremated in the UK and the family later transports the urn to Poland for interment, the starosta/mayor permit and Polish consular certificate are still required for the ashes [5].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Poland and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, benefits, and probate:
    • Tell Us Once and UK benefits: At the Register Office appointment, ask the registrar for a unique reference number for the Tell Us Once service, which must be used within 28 days to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local council services in a single step [2]. Eligible surviving partners (below UK State Pension age) can check entitlement to Bereavement Support Payment through the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (ideally claiming within 3 months of the death for the full payment, and up to 21 months maximum), or contact the International Pension Centre if cross-border UK State Pension records apply [8].
    • UK probate: If the deceased held UK property, bank accounts above institutional release thresholds, or investments, the executor or entitled representative applies to HM Courts and Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England and Wales, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland, after completing any required HMRC Inheritance Tax forms [2].
  • Poland funeral grant, survivor pension, succession, and tax:
    • ZUS funeral grant and survivor pension: If the deceased or the person who paid for the funeral was covered by Polish social insurance (or KRUS for agricultural insurance), apply to Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych on Form Z-12 within 12 months of the death for the Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy), enclosing the death certificate and original funeral/repatriation invoices [9][10]. Eligible family members (such as a surviving legal partner or dependent child) can also apply to Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych on Form ERR for a survivor pension (renta rodzinna) [11].
    • Polish inheritance and tax declaration: To administer assets in Poland, heirs have 6 months from learning of their entitlement to declare acceptance (with limitation of liability for debts, z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza) or rejection of the estate before a Polish notary or district court. Formal proof of succession is obtained either via a Notarial Deed of Succession Certification (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia) recorded in the public Inheritance Register (Rejestr Spadkowy) maintained by Krajowa Rada Notarialna [12] or via a court succession order (sądowe stwierdzenie nabycia spadku). Immediate family members (Tax Group 0) must file form SD-Z2 with the competent Polish tax office via Podatki.gov.pl within 6 months of the court order becoming final or the notarial deed being registered to secure full exemption from Polish inheritance tax [13].

closingQuestion: To help tailor the exact local offices and next steps: 1. In which UK nation and city or council district did the death occur, and has a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death already been issued or has the case been referred to the Coroner or Procurator Fiscal? 2. Do you plan to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to a specific municipality in Poland, or arrange burial or cremation in the United Kingdom?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Poland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Poland: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Poland, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Poland.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences on the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in Poland, the initial medical, sanitary, and civil registration steps take place under Polish law, while consular support, repatriation of the body or ashes to the United Kingdom, and pension and probate matters involve both British and Polish authorities.

steps.title: Medical Confirmation of Death, Death Card, and Police or Prosecutor Clearance in Poland
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or from natural causes: If the death occurred in a hospital or medical facility in Poland, the attending physician confirms the death and issues the official medical death card (karta zgonu) [1]. When a death occurs outside a hospital (for example, at home or in a hotel), you must call the emergency medical services on 112 or 999, or contact a primary care physician (lekarz podstawowej opieki zdrowotnej - POZ) or out-of-hours medical care service (nocna i świąteczna opieka zdrowotna) to officially pronounce the death and issue the karta zgonu [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death: If unnatural causes or third-party involvement are suspected, the Police (Policja) and the Public Prosecutor (prokurator) are called to the scene [1][2]. The deceased person's body is then transferred to the competent Department of Forensic Medicine (Zakład Medycyny Sądowej, for example at the Medical University of Warsaw or Jagiellonian University in Kraków) for a forensic autopsy [2]. In such circumstances, civil death registration and release of the body to a funeral director require written authorization from the competent prosecutor [1][2].

steps.title: Checking Insurance, Appointing a Funeral Director in Poland and the UK, and Consular Contact
steps.html:
• Checking insurance coverage: Before signing an independent contract with a funeral company, check whether the deceased person held travel, health, or repatriation insurance [2]. If such a policy was in force, the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance centre normally appoints a partner funeral director directly and covers the costs of international transport [2].
  • Appointing a funeral director in both countries: If there is no insurance cover, the family may authorize a specialized funeral home in Poland (zakład pogrzebowy, for example a member of a Polish industry association such as the Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej or the Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe), which will coordinate transport with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom [2]. To locate a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom, you can use the official directories of trade bodies such as the National Association of Funeral Directors [3] and the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [4]. These directories and trade associations are listed solely for informational guidance from public sources; Clarvia does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific providers.
  • UK consular support in Poland: You should notify the diplomatic mission of the United Kingdom in Warsaw (British Embassy Warsaw, ul. Kawalerii 12, tel. +48 22 311 00 00), which operates under the consular guidance of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) [2][5]. Consular staff provide the family with information on local procedures, sworn translators, and funeral homes, and cancel the deceased person's British passport, but they do not pay for burial or repatriation costs from public funds [2].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Poland and Document Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Registration with the Polish Civil Registry Office: The death must be registered at the Civil Registry Office (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego - USC, for example the Warsaw Civil Registry Office or Kraków Civil Registry Office) competent for the place of death within 3 days from the date the medical death card (karta zgonu) was issued, or within 24 hours if the death resulted from an infectious disease [1]. The declaration may be made by a family member or a funeral home employee authorized in writing [1]. The office registers the death and issues one free abridged copy of the death certificate (skrócony odpis aktu zgonu) as well as (upon application and payment of stamp duty) additional abridged, full, or multilingual abridged copies of the death certificate on Form C (wielojęzyczny odpis skrócony aktu zgonu na formularzu C, under the Vienna CIEC Convention) [1][2].
  • Document recognition in the United Kingdom: Because the death took place in Poland, it is not subject to standard domestic registration at a local UK Register Office (where deaths occurring in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland are registered within 5 days, and in Scotland within 8 days) [2][6]. British institutions accept the Polish death certificate accompanied by a sworn English translation (or the multilingual extract), and if legalization is required for probate purposes, an Apostille can be obtained from the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych RP) [2]. Under FCDO guidance, the family may also optionally apply to register the overseas death of a British national with the Overseas Registration Unit [2].

steps.title: International Repatriation of the Body or Ashes to the UK vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Poland
steps.html:
• Option A - Repatriation of the body or ashes from Poland to the United Kingdom:
    • Permits in Poland: International transport of a body requires a permit to export human remains (pozwolenie na wywóz zwłok lub szczątków) outside the Republic of Poland, issued by the county governor (starosta) or city mayor with county rights (prezydent miasta na prawach powiatu, e.g. the Mayor of Warsaw or Mayor of Gdańsk) competent for the place of death, in consultation with the State County Sanitary Inspector (Państwowy Powiatowy Inspektor Sanitarny - Sanepid), supervised by the Państwowa Inspekcja Sanitarna (State Sanitary Inspection) [2][7]. The funeral director compiles the embalming protocol, the certificate confirming the absence of infectious disease, and confirmation of hermetic sealing of the metal-lined coffin [2][7]. (Conversely, when bringing a body or ashes from the United Kingdom into Poland, in addition to the Polish starosta permit, a certificate from the Polish Consul and a UK Coroner's Out-of-England Order / Form 104 export document would be required) [8].
    • Clearance and burial in the United Kingdom: To bring the body or ashes into the United Kingdom, the consignment must be accompanied by the Polish death certificate (with an English translation) and the embalming certificate or cremation certificate from the Polish crematorium [2]. Upon arrival of a body in England or Wales, the British funeral director notifies the local Coroner for the district of burial to obtain a burial order or cremation certificate, whereas in Scotland verification of the foreign death documentation by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) is required before burial or cremation can take place [2][6].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in Poland:
    • If the family chooses traditional burial or cremation in Poland, the legal basis is the portion of the medical death card (karta zgonu) designated for cemetery administration together with civil registration of the death at the Urząd Stanu Cywilnego [1][2]. Following cremation in Poland, an urn containing the ashes may be transported to the United Kingdom on the basis of the death certificate and the crematorium certificate, subject to advance agreement on carriage requirements with the airline [2].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Taxes, and Probate in the UK and Poland
steps.html:
• Notifications, benefits, and probate in the United Kingdom:
    • Tell Us Once service and DWP benefits: Once the Polish death certificate has been obtained, the family can use the UK government's Tell Us Once service (also available when a UK citizen or resident dies abroad), which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, DVLA, local councils, and the social security authority (Department for Work and Pensions) in a single step [9]. Through the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP Bereavement Service or International Pension Centre), UK State Pension payments are stopped and a surviving spouse or civil partner can apply for Bereavement Support Payment (ideally within 3 months of death, and up to a maximum of 21 months) [10].
    • Probate / Confirmation in the United Kingdom: To close UK bank accounts above bank release thresholds and deal with property in the United Kingdom, the executor or entitled administrator applies for a grant of representation: a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation before the Sheriff Court in Scotland, after filing the appropriate Inheritance Tax forms with HMRC [9].
  • ZUS benefits, inheritance, and tax filings in Poland:
    • Funeral grant and survivor pension: If the deceased person or the family member paying the funeral expenses was covered by Polish social insurance (in ZUS or KRUS), a claim for the Polish funeral grant (zasiłek pogrzebowy) is submitted on form Z-12 within 12 months from the date of death to the Polish social insurance institution (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych), enclosing a copy of the death certificate and original invoices for the funeral or transport [11]. Eligible family members may also apply to the Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych for a Polish survivor's pension (renta rodzinna, form ERR) [12].
    • Succession and inheritance tax in Poland: If the deceased person left assets or real estate in Poland, heirs have 6 months from learning of their entitlement to make a formal declaration accepting the estate (for example with limitation of liability, z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza) or rejecting it [13]. Proof of inheritance rights in Poland is obtained either before a notary through a Notarial Deed of Succession Certification (Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia, registered in the public Inheritance Register, Rejestr Spadkowy, maintained by the Krajowa Rada Notarialna - National Council of Notaries) [13] or by a court order confirming acquisition of inheritance (sądowe stwierdzenie nabycia spadku) before a district court. Close relatives in the so-called zero tax group (zerowa grupa podatkowa) must file form SD-Z2 with the competent Polish tax office (Urząd Skarbowy, including electronically via the Podatki.gov.pl portal) within 6 months of the court order becoming final or the notarial deed being registered in order to retain full exemption from Polish inheritance and gift tax [14].

closingQuestion: To help us identify the exact local authorities and next steps, in which municipality in Poland did the death occur (and has the doctor already issued the karta zgonu or is the case under prosecutor investigation), and do you plan to repatriate the body or ashes to a specific part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) or arrange a local funeral in Poland?
