pl.title: Co zrobić w przypadku zgonu między krajem Polska a Wielka Brytania: oficjalna lista w 5 krokach
pl.cardSummary: Oficjalna lista kontrolna w 5 krokach po zgonie między krajem Polska a Wielka Brytania: karta zgonu, zakład pogrzebowy, rejestracja w Urzędzie Stanu Cywilnego, formalności konsularne i przewóz zwłok lub prochów oraz zasiłek pogrzebowy i sprawy spadkowe.
pl.introHtml: Składamy wyrazy współczucia z powodu straty bliskiej osoby. W przypadku zgonu obywatela lub rezydenta Zjednoczonego Królestwa na terytorium Polski pierwsze czynności medyczne, sanitarne i rejestracyjne odbywają się według przepisów polskich, natomiast wsparcie konsularne, przewóz ciała lub prochów do Wielkiej Brytanii oraz sprawy emerytalne i spadkowe obejmują instytucje brytyjskie i polskie.

steps.title: Stwierdzenie zgonu, karta zgonu oraz czynności Policji i prokuratury w Polsce
steps.html:
• Zgon w szpitalu lub z przyczyn naturalnych: Jeżeli śmierć nastąpiła w szpitalu lub placówce medycznej w Polsce, lekarz prowadzący stwierdza zgon i wystawia oficjalny dokument medyczny (karta zgonu) [1]. Gdy zgon nastąpił poza szpitalem (np. w domu lub w hotelu), należy wezwać zespół ratownictwa medycznego pod numerem alarmowym 112 lub 999 bądź skontaktować się z lekarzem podstawowej opieki zdrowotnej (POZ) albo nocnej i świątecznej opieki zdrowotnej w celu urzędowego stwierdzenia zgonu i wystawienia karty zgonu [1].
  • Zgon nagły, wypadkowy lub o nieustalonej przyczynie: W razie podejrzenia przyczyn nienaturalnych lub udziału osób trzecich na miejsce wzywana jest Policja oraz prokurator [1][2]. Ciało osoby zmarłej zostaje wówczas przewiezione do właściwego Zakładu Medycyny Sądowej (np. przy Warszawskim Uniwersytecie Medycznym lub Uniwersytecie Jagiellońskim w Krakowie) w celu przeprowadzenia sekcji zwłok [2]. W takich okolicznościach rejestracja zgonu i wydanie ciała zakładowi pogrzebowemu wymagają pisemnego zezwolenia właściwego prokuratora [1][2].

steps.title: Weryfikacja ubezpieczenia, wybór zakładu pogrzebowego w Polsce i Wielkiej Brytanii oraz kontakt konsularny
steps.html:
• Weryfikacja polisy ubezpieczeniowej: Przed podpisaniem samodzielnej umowy z firmą pogrzebową należy sprawdzić, czy osoba zmarła posiadała ubezpieczenie podróżne, zdrowotne lub polisę obejmującą koszty repatriacji [2]. Jeśli taka polisa obowiązywała, całodobowe centrum alarmowe ubezpieczyciela zazwyczaj samo wyznacza współpracujący zakład pogrzebowy i pokrywa koszty transportu międzynarodowego.
  • Wyznaczenie zakładu pogrzebowego w obu krajach: W braku ubezpieczenia rodzina może upoważnić wyspecjalizowany zakład pogrzebowy w Polsce (np. zrzeszony w organizacji branżowej, takiej jak Polska Izba Branży Pogrzebowej lub Polskie Stowarzyszenie Pogrzebowe), który skoordynuje transport z zakładem pogrzebowym przyjmującym w Wielkiej Brytanii [2]. Do wyszukania licencjonowanego domu pogrzebowego w Wielkiej Brytanii służą oficjalne rejestry organizacji branżowych, takie jak National Association of Funeral Directors [3] oraz National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors [4]. Wskazane katalogi i organizacje branżowe są podane wyłącznie orientacyjnie na podstawie źródeł publicznych; Clarvia nie rekomenduje, nie promuje ani nie klasyfikuje konkretnych usługodawców.
  • Wsparcie konsularne Wielkiej Brytanii w Polsce: O zgonie obywatela brytyjskiego należy powiadomić placówkę dyplomatyczną Zjednoczonego Królestwa w Warszawie (British Embassy Warsaw, ul. Kawalerii 12, tel. +48 22 311 00 00), która działa zgodnie z wytycznymi konsularnymi Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) [2][5]. Służby konsularne udzielają rodzinie informacji o lokalnych procedurach, tłumaczach i zakładach pogrzebowych oraz unieważniają brytyjski paszport osoby zmarłej, lecz nie pokrywają kosztów pochówku ani repatriacji ze środków publicznych [2].

steps.title: Rejestracja zgonu w Urzędzie Stanu Cywilnego w Polsce oraz uznawalność dokumentów w Wielkiej Brytanii
steps.html:
• Rejestracja w polskim rejestrze stanu cywilnego: Zgon zgłasza się we właściwym dla miejsca śmierci urzędzie stanu cywilnego (Urząd Stanu Cywilnego, np. Urząd Stanu Cywilnego m.st. Warszawy lub Urząd Stanu Cywilnego w Krakowie) w terminie 3 dni od dnia wystawienia karty zgonu, a w przypadku zgonu na skutek choroby zakaźnej w ciągu 24 godzin [1]. Zgłoszenia może dokonać członek rodziny lub upoważniony na piśmie pracownik zakładu pogrzebowego [1]. Urząd rejestruje zgon i wydaje bezpłatny skrócony odpis aktu zgonu oraz (na wniosek, za opłatą skarbową) kolejne odpisy skrócone, zupełne lub wielojęzyczne odpisy skrócone aktu zgonu na formularzu C (zgodnie z Konwencją Wiedeńską CIEC) [1][2].
  • Uznawalność dokumentów w Zjednoczonym Królestwie: Ponieważ zgon nastąpił na terytorium Polski, nie podlega on standardowemu zgłoszeniu w lokalnym brytyjskim urzędzie rejestracyjnym (Register Office, gdzie zgony w Anglii, Walii i Irlandii Północnej rejestruje się w ciągu 5 dni, a w Szkocji w ciągu 8 dni) [2][6]. W instytucjach brytyjskich wykorzystuje się polski odpis aktu zgonu wraz z tłumaczeniem przysięgłym na język angielski (lub odpis wielojęzyczny), a w razie wymogu legalizacji dla celów spadkowych można uzyskać klauzulę Apostille w Ministerstwie Spraw Zagranicznych RP [2]. Zgodnie z wytycznymi FCDO rodzina może również opcjonalnie zarejestrować zagraniczny zgon obywatela brytyjskiego w rejestrze zamorskim (Overseas Registration Unit) [2].

steps.title: Międzynarodowy przewóz zwłok lub prochów do Wielkiej Brytanii a pochówek lub kremacja w Polsce
steps.html:
• Wariant A - Repatriacja ciała lub prochów z Polski do Wielkiej Brytanii:
    • Pozwolenia w Polsce: Międzynarodowy przewóz ciała wymaga uzyskania pozwolenia na wywóz zwłok lub szczątków poza granice RP, które wydaje właściwy dla miejsca zgonu starosta lub prezydent miasta na prawach powiatu (np. Prezydent m.st. Warszawy lub Prezydent Miasta Gdańska) po porozumieniu z właściwym Państwowym Powiatowym Inspektorem Sanitarnym (Sanepid), nad którym nadzór sprawuje Państwowa Inspekcja Sanitarna [2][7]. Zakład pogrzebowy kompletuje protokół zabalsamowania ciała, zaświadczenie o braku choroby zakaźnej oraz potwierdzenie hermetycznego zamknięcia trumny z wkładem metalowym [2][7]. (Natomiast w sytuacji odwrotnej, przy wwozie ciała lub prochów z Wielkiej Brytanii do Polski, oprócz pozwolenia polskiego starosty wymagane byłoby zaświadczenie konsula RP oraz brytyjski dokument wywozowy Coroner's Out-of-England Order / Form 104) [8].
    • Odprawa i pochówek w Wielkiej Brytanii: Aby przewieźć ciało lub prochy do Wielkiej Brytanii, przesyłce musi towarzyszyć polski akt zgonu (z tłumaczeniem na język angielski), zaświadczenie o zabalsamowaniu lub zaświadczenie o kremacji z polskiego krematorium [2]. Po przybyciu ciała do Anglii lub Walii brytyjski zakład pogrzebowy zgłasza przewóz lokalnemu koronerowi właściwemu dla miejsca pochówku w celu uzyskania zezwolenia na pochówek lub kremację, natomiast w Szkocji wymagana jest weryfikacja zagranicznej dokumentacji zgonu przez Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) przed przeprowadzeniem pochówku lub kremacji [2][6].
  • Wariant B - Pochówek lub kremacja w Polsce:
    • Jeżeli rodzina decyduje się na pochówek tradycyjny lub kremację w Polsce, podstawą do ich przeprowadzenia jest część karty zgonu przeznaczona dla administracji cmentarza oraz rejestracja zgonu w USC [1][2]. Po kremacji w Polsce urna z prochami może zostać przewieziona do Wielkiej Brytanii na podstawie aktu zgonu i zaświadczenia z krematorium, przy wcześniejszym uzgodnieniu wymogów przewozowych z linią lotniczą [2].

steps.title: Powiadomienia pośmiertne, świadczenia rodzinne, podatki i sprawy spadkowe w Wielkiej Brytanii oraz w Polsce
steps.html:
• Formalności, świadczenia i postępowanie spadkowe w Wielkiej Brytanii:
    • Usługa Tell Us Once i świadczenia z DWP: Po uzyskaniu polskiego aktu zgonu rodzina może skorzystać z brytyjskiej rządowej usługi Tell Us Once (dostępnej również w przypadku zgonu obywatela lub rezydenta brytyjskiego za granicą), która pozwala jednorazowo powiadomić urząd skarbowy HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, DVLA, władze samorządowe oraz instytucję zabezpieczenia społecznego (Department for Work and Pensions) [9]. Za pośrednictwem Department for Work and Pensions (DWP Bereavement Service lub International Pension Centre) wstrzymuje się wypłatę brytyjskiej emerytury państwowej (State Pension) oraz składa wniosek o świadczenie dla owdowiałego partnera (Bereavement Support Payment, o które należy wystąpić najlepiej w ciągu 3 miesięcy od zgonu, maksymalnie do 21 miesięcy) [10].
    • Spadek w Wielkiej Brytanii (Probate / Confirmation): W celu zamknięcia brytyjskich rachunków bankowych powyżej progów bankowych oraz dysponowania nieruchomościami w Wielkiej Brytanii wykonawca testamentu lub uprawniony spadkobierca występuje o dokument potwierdzający prawa do zarządzania spadkiem: Grant of Probate (lub Letters of Administration przy braku testamentu) w Anglii, Walii i Irlandii Północnej bądź Confirmation przed sądem Sheriff Court w Szkocji, po uprzednim rozliczeniu formularzy podatku spadkowego z HMRC [9].
  • Świadczenia z ZUS, dziedziczenie i podatki w Polsce:
    • Zasiłek pogrzebowy i renta rodzinna: Jeżeli osoba zmarła lub członek rodziny pokrywający koszty pogrzebu podlegał polskiemu ubezpieczeniu społecznemu (w ZUS lub KRUS), wniosek o zasiłek pogrzebowy składa się na formularzu Z-12 w terminie 12 miesięcy od dnia śmierci do polskiego organu rentowego (Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych), dołączając odpis aktu zgonu i oryginały rachunków za pogrzeb lub transport [11]. Uprawnieni członkowie rodziny mogą również wystąpić do instytucji Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych z wnioskiem o rentę rodzinną (formularz ERR) [12].
    • Spadek i podatek w Polsce: Jeżeli osoba zmarła pozostawiła majątek lub nieruchomości w Polsce, spadkobiercy mają 6 miesięcy od dnia dowiedzenia się o tytule powołania do spadku na złożenie oświadczenia o przyjęciu (np. z dobrodziejstwem inwentarza) lub odrzuceniu spadku. Potwierdzenie praw do spadku w Polsce uzyskuje się przed notariuszem poprzez Akt Poświadczenia Dziedziczenia (rejestrowany w publicznym Rejestrze Spadkowym, który prowadzi Krajowa Rada Notarialna) [13] albo w drodze sądowego stwierdzenia nabycia spadku przed sądem rejonowym. Osoby zaliczane do tzw. zerowej grupy podatkowej (najbliższa rodzina) składają zgłoszenie SD-Z2 do właściwego urzędu skarbowego (w tym elektronicznie przez portal Podatki.gov.pl) w terminie 6 miesięcy od uprawomocnienia się postanowienia sądu lub zarejestrowania aktu poświadczenia dziedziczenia, aby zachować pełne zwolnienie z polskiego podatku od spadków i darowizn [14].

pl.closingQuestion: Abyśmy mogli doprecyzować właściwe urzędy i kolejne kroki: 1. W jakiej miejscowości w Polsce nastąpił zgon i czy lekarz wystawił już kartę zgonu, czy sprawa jest prowadzona przez prokuraturę? 2. Czy planują Państwo przewóz ciała lub prochów do konkretnej części Zjednoczonego Królestwa (Anglia, Walia, Szkocja czy Irlandia Północna), czy pochówek na miejscu w Polsce?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of India Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of India dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in India and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of India dies in the United Kingdom, the initial medical certification, coroner clearance (if applicable), and civil death registration follow UK procedures, while consular registration, repatriation clearance (including the Indian High Commission No Objection Certificate and Airport Health Organization eCARe approval), and Indian benefit or succession claims involve Indian authorities.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Expected or hospital deaths: In England and Wales, an attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by a Medical Examiner before being transmitted to the local Register Office [1]. In Scotland, a doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for scrutiny by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or accidental deaths: If the death occurs unexpectedly outside a hospital, call 999 (or 111 if the death was expected at home). Unexplained, sudden, or accidental deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (for example, Inner West London Coroner's Court or Birmingham and Solihull Coroner's Court) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1][2]. When a Coroner or Procurator Fiscal investigates, civil registration and international release wait until the forensic examination concludes and the Coroner issues an interim certificate of the fact of death or release order [1][2].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Indian Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check insurance and welfare coverage first: Before committing to private repatriation contracts, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, employer-sponsored, or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY / eMigrate) insurance covering repatriation of remains. Where a policy applies, the insurer's assistance service typically appoints the funeral coordinators directly.
  • Appointing a UK and Indian funeral coordinator: You can appoint a licensed UK funeral director experienced in international air repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors [3] (or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors, SAIF), coordinated with a receiving funeral provider, authorized international human remains cargo/undertaker service, or municipal mortuary/crematorium at the destination in India (such as in New Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, or Kochi). These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank providers.
  • Indian consular notification and ICWF support: Report the death to the High Commission of India, London (or the competent Consulate General of India in Birmingham, Edinburgh, or Belfast) [4][5]. The Indian mission registers the death of an Indian national, cancels the deceased's Indian passport, and issues the mandatory No Objection Certificate (NOC) for transporting mortal remains or cremated ashes to India (issued gratis for Indian passport holders) [4][5]. In cases of financial hardship where no insurance or family funds are available, the mission can also assess eligibility for means-tested assistance from the Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF) administered by the Ministry of External Affairs [6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom and Consular or Local Registration for India
steps.html:
• UK civil registration: Once the Medical Examiner or Coroner clears the death for registration, book an appointment at the local Register Office in the UK district where the death occurred (for example, Westminster Register Office or Manchester Register Office) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1]. The registrar provides the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the "green form" for local disposition) and official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate [1][2].
  • Legalization (Apostille) and registration for India: To use the UK Death Certificate for banking, pension, or court succession procedures in India, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office [7]. For Indian nationals, also register the death with the High Commission of India, London (or the relevant Indian Consulate General) by submitting the Death Registration Form, Miscellaneous Application Form, the original UK Death Certificate, and the deceased's Indian passport [4][5]. Whereas domestic deaths occurring inside India must be registered within 21 days with the local Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Corporation or Gram Panchayat via the Civil Registration System - CRS portal under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act) [8], a death in the UK is recorded first at the UK Register Office and registered abroad through the Indian diplomatic mission [4][5].

steps.title: Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to India vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Option A - Repatriation of mortal remains or cremated ashes to India:
    • UK export clearances: Your UK funeral director obtains the Coroner's Out-of-England Order (Form 104 in England and Wales, or Healthcare Improvement Scotland DCRS clearance in Scotland for repatriated remains), an official embalming certificate, a medical certificate confirming the body is free from contagious or infectious disease, and an undertaker's certificate confirming that the hermetically sealed coffin meets WHO and international air transport regulations [4][9].
    • Indian High Commission NOC and MoHFW eCARe portal clearance: Submit the UK Death Certificate and medical cause of death, embalming and infection-free certificates, funeral director's packaging letter, flight details, and the deceased's original Indian passport to the High Commission of India, London (or competent Consulate General) to obtain the No Objection Certificate (NOC) and passport cancellation [4][5]. Under the Indian Aircraft (Public Health) Rules, public health clearance from the Airport Health Organization (APHO) is mandatory before human remains can enter India [9]. The consignee, funeral director, or airline must submit an advance application (normally at least 48 hours before arrival) on the eCARe (e-Clearance for Afterlife Remains) portal operated by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, uploading the Death Certificate, Embalming Certificate, Indian High Commission NOC, cancelled passport copy, and WHO packaging certificate [9].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom:
    • If burial or cremation takes place in the UK, the UK funeral director uses the Register Office "green form" (or Coroner's Order for Burial or Cremation Form 6) to arrange the service locally [1][2]. If the family later carries or ships cremated ashes to India, obtain the cremation certificate from the UK crematorium and a consular NOC/certificate for ashes from the High Commission of India, London [4][5].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in India and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, benefits, and probate:
    • Tell Us Once and DWP claims: Use the unique reference number provided by the UK registrar to complete the Tell Us Once service within 28 days, notifying HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local council services in one step [2]. Eligible surviving partners under UK State Pension age can apply to the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service for Bereavement Support Payment (ideally within 3 months of the death, and up to 21 months maximum), or contact the International Pension Centre regarding UK State Pension records [10].
    • UK probate: To release UK real estate or bank accounts above institutional thresholds, the executor or entitled representative applies to HM Courts and Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England and Wales, or Confirmation via the Sheriff Court in Scotland, after completing any required HMRC Inheritance Tax filings [2].
  • India social security claims, banking, and succession:
    • EPFO, ESIC, and insurance claims: If the deceased held an Indian provident fund account, the nominee or legal heir can file a death claim online through the Member Sewa Portal of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (or via the Composite Claim Form, with support available through the official EPFiGMS portal) to claim the Provident Fund (EPF) balance, Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance (EDLI) lump-sum assurance, and Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) monthly survivor pension [11]. Where applicable, check Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) survivor benefits or Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) insurance claims.
    • Legal Heir Certificate, Succession Certificate, and Indian probate: For Indian bank accounts or investments where a valid nominee is registered, banks can release funds directly to the nominee upon presentation of the Apostilled death certificate and identity proof. Where no nominee is registered or to transfer immovable property and disputed/high-value financial assets in India, heirs apply to the local revenue authority (Tehsildar or District Magistrate) for a Legal Heir Certificate, or petition the competent Indian District Court or High Court for a Succession Certificate (for movable assets and debts) or Probate of Will.

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in India: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in India: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in India, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and India.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in India, the initial medical certification, police clearance, and civil death registration follow Indian municipal and public health rules, while consular support, UK coroner or Scottish review clearance upon repatriation, and UK pension or probate steps involve British authorities.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in India
steps.html:
• Hospital or natural deaths: When a death occurs in an Indian hospital or inpatient medical facility, the attending doctor issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death on Form 4 (or Form 4A when a registered medical practitioner certifies a natural death outside a hospital) under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act [1][2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended deaths: If the death occurs unexpectedly at a residence, hotel, or public place, call the national emergency number 112 (or 100 for police). For any sudden, accidental, or unexplained death (and frequently when a foreign national dies outside a hospital), local police register a First Information Report (FIR) or inquest report (Panchnama) and transfer the body to a designated government hospital (for example, AIIMS in New Delhi, KEM Hospital in Mumbai, or Victoria Hospital in Bengaluru) for a post-mortem examination [1]. A Police No Objection Certificate (NOC) is required before the mortuary can release the body for local cremation, burial, or international repatriation [1].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Funeral Providers in India and the United Kingdom, and British Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check travel and repatriation insurance first: Before signing independent contracts with private undertakers, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance [1]. If a policy is active, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance service immediately so they can appoint their approved local agent in India and UK receiving funeral director directly.
  • Appointing funeral coordinators in India and the United Kingdom: If there is no insurance cover, you can appoint an authorized international human remains cargo/undertaker service or municipal mortuary/crematorium coordinator in India to work alongside a licensed receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors [3] (or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors, SAIF) [1]. These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank providers.
  • British consular notification: Report the death as soon as possible to the British High Commission New Delhi (or the nearest British Deputy High Commission in Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, or Chandigarh, or via the 24/7 Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office consular helpline on +44 20 7008 5000) [1]. British consular staff can issue a consular letter where required by Indian police or municipal authorities, provide lists of local English-speaking lawyers and international undertakers, and cancel the deceased's British passport, though they cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [1].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in India and Document Recognition for the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Civil registration in India: Every death in India must be registered within 21 days with the local Registrar of Births and Deaths (the local Municipal Corporation in cities, such as the Municipal Corporation of Delhi or Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, or the Gram Panchayat / Tehsildar in rural areas) via the national Civil Registration System (CRS) portal under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act [1][2]. For hospital deaths, the hospital typically transmits the Form 4 report to the municipal registrar, after which the family or authorized undertaker obtains multiple official copies of the Indian Death Certificate [1][2].
  • Document recognition and UK registration rules: Because the death occurred in India, it does not go through domestic registration at a local UK Register Office (where deaths in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland are registered within 5 days and in Scotland within 8 days) [1][4]. If the Indian Death Certificate is not issued in English, obtain an official certified English translation, and if required for overseas court or estate purposes, request a Hague Apostille from the Consular, Passport and Visa (CPV / e-Sanad) Division of the Ministry of External Affairs in India [1][5]. Following Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) guidance, families can also optionally apply to record the overseas death of a British national with the FCDO Overseas Registration Unit in the UK [1].

steps.title: Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in India
steps.html:
• Option A - Repatriation of mortal remains or cremated ashes from India to the United Kingdom:
    • Indian export and airport health clearances: To repatriate a body by air from India, the appointed Indian funeral director obtains the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4/4A or post-mortem report), the municipal Death Certificate, a Police No Objection Certificate (NOC) for export, an official Embalming Certificate, a Certificate of Packaging confirming that the body is sealed in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in accordance with WHO and international air transport regulations, and consular/immigration clearance (cancellation of the British passport and FRRO exit/visa clearance where applicable) [1][6]. Airport public health oversight at Indian international airports is managed by the Airport Health Organization (APHO) and the eCARe portal of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare [6] (note that when remains are repatriated in the opposite direction into India, an Indian Embassy/Consulate NOC and, for distressed Indian nationals, means-tested Indian Community Welfare Fund - ICWF support via the Ministry of External Affairs apply) [5][7].
    • UK arrival and Coroner or Scottish DCRS clearance: When human remains arrive in England or Wales for burial or cremation, the receiving UK funeral director submits the Indian Death Certificate, medical/post-mortem papers, and embalming certificate to the local Coroner for the burial district so the Coroner can issue a certificate or order allowing burial or cremation (whereas a Coroner's Out-of-England Order / Form 104 is used when exporting remains out of England and Wales) [1][4]. If the body or ashes are repatriated to Scotland, the UK funeral director submits the foreign death documentation to the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) for clearance before the funeral takes place [1][4].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in India:
    • If the family chooses local burial or cremation in India, the local undertaker arranges the service at a municipal or community crematorium/cemetery using the Form 4/4A medical certificate, Police NOC, and British consular letter [1]. If cremated ashes are subsequently taken to the United Kingdom in hand luggage or by air cargo, obtain the official Cremation Certificate, the municipal Death Certificate, and a sealed urn certificate from the crematorium or undertaker [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in the United Kingdom and India
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, survivor benefits, and probate:
    • Tell Us Once, DWP, and HMRC: Once you have the Indian Death Certificate (and the deceased's UK National Insurance number), you can use the UK government Tell Us Once overseas death route to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local council services at the same time [8]. Contact the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service or International Pension Centre) to stop UK State Pension payments and check whether an eligible surviving partner under UK State Pension age qualifies for Bereavement Support Payment (which should ideally be claimed within 3 months of the death, and up to 21 months maximum) [9].
    • UK probate: To administer UK bank accounts above institutional thresholds, investments, or real property, the executor or entitled person applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland, after submitting the required HMRC Inheritance Tax return [8].
  • India provident fund, insurance, banking, and succession:
    • EPFO, ESIC, and Indian accounts: If the deceased worked in India or held an Indian provident fund account (for example, as an expatriate employee or OCI cardholder), eligible nominees or legal heirs can submit the Composite Claim Form (or file an online death claim via the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation Member Sewa / UMANG portal, helpline 1800-118-005) to claim Provident Fund (EPF) balances, Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance (EDLI), and Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension [10], or claim ESIC / Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana (PBBY) benefits where applicable.
    • Legal Heir or Succession Certificate in India: Indian banks generally release balances directly to a registered nominee upon presentation of the Indian Death Certificate and identity documents. Where no nominee was registered or to transfer immovable property and securities in India, heirs apply to the local revenue officer (Tehsildar / District Magistrate) for a Legal Heir Certificate, or petition the competent Indian District Court or High Court for a Succession Certificate or ancillary Probate/Letters of Administration.

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Romania Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Romania Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Romania dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Romania and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of Romania dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate medical certification, coroner clearance (if applicable), and civil death registration follow UK rules, while consular issuance of the mortuary passport (pașaport mortuar), Romanian civil record transcription, and Romanian pension or succession procedures involve Romanian authorities.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Expected or hospital deaths: In England and Wales, an attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is scrutinized and countersigned by an independent Medical Examiner before being sent electronically to the local Register Office [1]. In Scotland, a doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for review by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or accidental deaths: If the death occurs unexpectedly outside a hospital, call 999 (or 111 when a death was expected at home). Unexplained, sudden, or accidental deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (for example, Inner West London Coroner's Court) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1][2]. When a Coroner or Procurator Fiscal investigates, civil registration and international release wait until the post-mortem inquiry is completed and the Coroner issues the relevant release certificate or order [1][2].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Romanian Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check travel and repatriation insurance first: Before signing an independent funeral or international transport contract, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or employer-sponsored repatriation insurance. Where a policy applies, the insurer's assistance service typically appoints the funeral coordinators directly and covers eligible repatriation expenses.
  • Appointing a UK and Romanian funeral coordinator: If no insurer is managing the transfer, you can appoint a licensed UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors [3] (or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors, SAIF), coordinated with a receiving funeral provider in Romania authorized by the county or Bucharest Public Health Directorate (firmă de servicii funerare autorizată sanitar de Direcția de Sănătate Publică - DSP under Government Decision HG nr. 741/2016 issued by the Romanian Ministry of Health, Ministerul Sănătății). These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank providers.
  • Romanian consular notification and role: Contact the competent Romanian consular mission in the United Kingdom, such as the Consulate General of Romania in London (or the Consulates General in Manchester or Edinburgh, operating under Ministerul Afacerilor Externe via the eConsulat.ro portal) [4][5]. The Romanian consular mission issues the mandatory mortuary passport (pașaport mortuar) free of consular fees for repatriating an uncremated body to Romania and processes the transcription of the UK Death Certificate into the Romanian civil registers [4][5][6].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom and Document Recognition for Romania
steps.html:
• UK civil registration: Once the Medical Examiner or Coroner confirms that registration can proceed, register the death at the local Register Office in the UK district where the death occurred (for example, Westminster Register Office or Manchester Register Office) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1]. The registrar provides the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the "green form" for local disposition) and official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate [1][2].
  • Legalization (Apostille) and Romanian civil registration: To be recognized for consular transcription, repatriation, and succession in Romania, the UK Death Certificate (or Coroner's Certificate) must carry a Hague Apostille issued by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office [7], accompanied by an authorized translation into Romanian when submitted for civil status transcription [5][6]. Whereas a domestic death occurring inside Romania must be declared within 3 days (or within 48 hours accompanied by a police or prosecutor certificate for violent or suspicious deaths) at the local civil registry (Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP or Primăria of the place of death, coordinated nationally by Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor - DGEP) to obtain the Romanian Death Certificate (Certificatul de deces), the Burial/Cremation Permit (Adeverința de înhumare/incinerare), and where needed a multilingual CIEC Form C extract (extras multilingv Formular C) [8], a death occurring in the UK is registered first at the UK Register Office and then transcribed into Romanian civil records either at the Consulate General of Romania in London (or Manchester/Edinburgh) or at the SPCLEP / City Hall of the deceased's last domicile in Romania (for example, Primăria Sectorului 1 București or Primăria Municipiului Cluj-Napoca) [6][8].

steps.title: Repatriation of Remains or Ashes to Romania vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Option A - Repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to Romania:
    • UK export clearances: Your UK funeral director obtains the Coroner's Out-of-England Order (Form 104 in England and Wales, or Healthcare Improvement Scotland DCRS clearance in Scotland for repatriated remains), an official Embalming Certificate (Certificat de îmbălsămare), a medical certificate confirming that the deceased did not suffer from a communicable infectious disease (Free from Infection), and confirmation that the body is placed in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin (sicriu de zinc sigilat) conforming to international transport standards [4][5].
    • Romanian mortuary passport (pașaport mortuar) and DSP rules: Under Romanian Law no. 102/2014 and Government Decision HG nr. 741/2016 (under which local Public Health Directorates, Direcția de Sănătate Publică - DSP, regulate sanitary funeral standards and issue mortuary passports for transfers originating in Romania), bringing an uncremated body from the UK into Romania requires a pașaport mortuar issued free of charge by the Consulate General of Romania in London (or Manchester/Edinburgh via Ministerul Afacerilor Externe / eConsulat.ro) [4][5]. The family or authorized funeral director submits the Apostilled UK Death or Coroner's Certificate, the deceased's Romanian identity document or passport, the UK Out-of-England Order, the Embalming Certificate, the non-infectious disease certificate, and the transport route/burial approval [4][5]. If the deceased is cremated in the UK, a pașaport mortuar is not required to transport the sealed cremation urn to Romania, though the Apostilled UK Death Certificate and Cremation Certificate should accompany the urn [4].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom:
    • If the burial or cremation takes place in the UK, the UK funeral director uses the Register Office "green form" (or Coroner's Order for Burial or Cremation Form 6) to arrange the service locally [1][2]. Even when the funeral takes place in the UK, the Apostilled UK Death Certificate should still be transcribed with the Romanian consular mission or local SPCLEP in Romania to update the deceased's Romanian civil status and settle Romanian estate or pension matters [6][8].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Romania and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, survivor benefits, and probate:
    • Tell Us Once and DWP claims: Use the unique reference number supplied by the UK registrar to complete the Tell Us Once service within 28 days, notifying HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local council services in one step [2]. Eligible surviving partners under UK State Pension age can apply to the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service for Bereavement Support Payment (ideally within 3 months of the death, and up to 21 months maximum), or contact the International Pension Centre if cross-border UK State Pension contributions apply [9].
    • UK probate: If the deceased held UK real estate or bank accounts above institutional release thresholds, the executor or entitled representative applies to HM Courts and Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England and Wales, or Confirmation via the Sheriff Court in Scotland, after filing any required HMRC Inheritance Tax forms [2].
  • Romania funeral grant, survivor pension, notarial succession, and tax exemption:
    • CNPP funeral grant (ajutor de deces) and survivor pension (pensie de urmaș): If the deceased was insured or a pensioner in the Romanian public pension system (or an eligible dependent family member of an insured person), the person who paid the funeral expenses can apply to the territorial pension house (Casa Teritorială de Pensii, such as Casa de Pensii a Municipiului București, under the national pension authority Casa Națională de Pensii Publice - CNPP) for the Romanian funeral grant (ajutorul de deces), which is paid within 3 working days of submitting the complete application, the Romanian death certificate, and original invoices [10]. Eligible surviving partners and dependent children can also apply to the territorial pension house for a monthly survivor pension (pensia de urmaș) under Law no. 360/2023 [10][11].
    • Notarial succession and 2-year tax exemption: To transfer property, land, or bank accounts in Romania, heirs open the notarial succession procedure (procedura succesorală notarială) before a public notary in the district of the deceased's last domicile or where the main Romanian assets are situated, coordinated through the national notary union (Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România - UNNPR), to obtain the Certificate of Heir (Certificatul de moștenitor) [12]. Under the Romanian Fiscal Code administered by the National Agency for Fiscal Administration (Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală - ANAF), if the succession procedure is completed within 2 years from the date of death, heirs are completely exempt from the 1% inheritance tax on immovable property (if completed after 2 years, a 1% tax applies to the value of the real estate in the estate).

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Romania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Romania: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Romania, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Romania.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences for your loss. When your family member with citizenship or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in Romania, official procedures involve the medical, civil registry, and public health authorities in Romania, alongside consular, repatriation, pension, and estate administration formalities in the United Kingdom.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in Romania
steps.html:
The first step is obtaining the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Certificatul medical constatator al decesului), without which civil registration or transport of the body cannot take place [1][5]:

  • Death in a hospital: If the death occurred in a healthcare facility in Romania, the attending or on-duty physician draws up the Certificatul medical constatator al decesului, normally 24 hours after the death is pronounced [1]. In Romanian hospitals, an anatomopathological autopsy is routinely performed to confirm the medical cause of death, although the family may submit a written request to hospital management for an autopsy exemption if there are no forensic concerns [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the deceased person died outside a hospital facility, call the single emergency number 112 or the family doctor (medicul de familie) to confirm the death [1][5].
  • Forensic cases (sudden, violent, or suspicious death): If the death occurred under unclear circumstances, following an accident, or without known medical attendance, the Romanian Police (Poliția Română) intervene and the Prosecutor's Office (Parchetul) orders a medico-legal autopsy through the county forensic medicine service or an institution such as the Mina Minovici National Institute of Legal Medicine (Institutul Național de Medicină Legală Mina Minovici in Bucharest) [1][5]. In such cases, both the Certificatul medical constatator al decesului issued by the forensic pathologist and the clearance certificate (dovada) issued by the police or prosecutor are mandatory to register the death and release the body [5].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Appointing a Funeral Director, and Consular Assistance
steps.html:
Before incurring expenses independently, check whether an insurance policy exists and appoint an authorized funeral coordinator [1]:

  • Checking travel or repatriation insurance: If the deceased person held travel, medical, or repatriation insurance, contact the insurer's emergency assistance centre immediately [1]. The insurer usually appoints partner funeral companies directly and covers transport costs and formalities [1].
  • Appointing a funeral director in Romania and the United Kingdom: If there is no insurance, the family can authorize a funeral services company in Romania holding a sanitary license from the county public health directorate (for example, the Bucharest Public Health Directorate, Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București, tel. +40 21 252 7978) in accordance with Government Decision (Hotărârea Guvernului) no. 741/2016 [2][4]. The Romanian provider coordinates with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered in an official professional directory, such as the National Association of Funeral Directors (tel. +44 121 711 1343; the professional trade association SAIF also operates in the United Kingdom) [3]. These professional bodies are listed solely for informational guidance from public sources; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank them.
  • British consular assistance: Contact the diplomatic mission British Embassy Bucharest (tel. +40 21 201 7200) and the consular service of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) [1]. The Embassy provides consular guidance to the family and informational lists of international funeral providers and translators, but does not pay for repatriation or funeral costs [1].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Romania and Document Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
The death must be registered with the local authorities in Romania before burial, cremation, or repatriation can proceed [1][5]:

  • Registration at the SPCLEP / Town Hall in Romania: The death declaration is submitted to the Local Public Community Service for the Registration of Persons (Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP) or to the civil status officer (ofițerul de stare civilă) at the town hall (Primăria) of the administrative-territorial unit where the death occurred, under the coordination of the General Directorate for the Registration of Persons (Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor, tel. +40 21 410 7557) [5]. The statutory deadline is 3 days from the date of death for natural causes, or 3 days from the issuance of the medical certificate of cause of death (accompanied by the clearance certificate issued by the police or prosecutor) in cases of violent or suspicious death [5]. A funeral company authorized by the family can submit the documents (medical certificate of cause of death, British passport, and declarant's identity document) to obtain the Romanian Death Certificate (Certificatul de deces) and the Burial or Cremation Permit (Adeverința de înhumare sau incinerare) [1][5].
  • Multilingual extract and Apostille: Request a Multilingual Extract of the Death Record on Form C (Extras multilingv al actului de deces - Formularul C) from the civil registry, or obtain a Hague Apostille (through the Prefect's Office, Instituția Prefectului) and a certified English translation for the Romanian death certificate so that the document can be used before institutions and banks in the United Kingdom [1][5].
  • Registration status in the United Kingdom: Once the death has been officially registered in Romania, it does not need to be re-registered at a local UK Register Office (where domestic deadlines are 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland) [1][7]; the Romanian death certificate (accompanied by a certified English translation) is recognized in the United Kingdom [1].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Romania
steps.html:
The family may choose either to repatriate the body or funerary urn to the United Kingdom, or to arrange local burial or cremation in Romania [1][2]:

  • Repatriation of the body from Romania: International transport of the body is handled by the licensed funeral company and requires official embalming, placement in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, and obtaining the Mortuary Passport (Pașaport mortuar) issued by the county public health directorate (or by the Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București for deaths in the capital) based on the Certificatul de deces and the Adeverința de înhumare [2][4]. If the deceased person also held Romanian citizenship, additional information on consular documents is also managed through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministerul Afacerilor Externe - MAE) [4].
  • Receiving formalities in the United Kingdom: Upon arrival in England or Wales, the UK funeral director presents the death and transport documents to the local Coroner to obtain authorization for burial or cremation (for example, a Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104 for cremation) [7]. If the destination is in Scotland, verification and authorization of the foreign documents (Form Y and the foreign death certificate) by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (tel. +44 300 123 1898, email his.dcrs@nhs.scot) is mandatory before burial or cremation [6].
  • Repatriation of ashes or local ceremony in Romania: If cremation takes place in Romania on the basis of the Adeverința de incinerare, international transport of the sealed urn containing ashes does not require a mortuary passport, only the Certificatul de deces, the cremation certificate, and compliance with airline regulations [1][4].

steps.title: Funeral Grant, Survivor Pensions, Tax Obligations, and Probate in the UK and Romania
steps.html:
Once the Certificatul de deces has been obtained, the family or executor can initiate social security, tax, and succession procedures in both jurisdictions [7][8][10]:

  • Notifications and pensions in the United Kingdom: If the deceased person lived or received benefits in the United Kingdom, check whether you can use the government's Tell Us Once service or directly notify the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) through the International Pension Centre (tel. +44 191 218 7777) to stop State Pension payments and claim survivor entitlements (such as Bereavement Support Payment), as well as the tax authority HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [7][8]. To administer bank accounts and assets in the United Kingdom, the executor or entitled next of kin applies to the court or probate registry for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation in Scotland [9].
  • Funeral grant and survivor pension in Romania: If the deceased person was insured or a pensioner in the Romanian public pension system (or a qualifying family member of an insured person or pensioner), the person who proves by invoice that they bore the funeral expenses may claim the Romanian funeral grant (ajutorul de deces) and, where applicable, a survivor pension (pensia de urmaș) from the territorial pension house under the National House of Public Pensions (Casa Națională de Pensii Publice - CNPP, for example the Bucharest Pension House, Casa de Pensii a Municipiului București, tel. +40 21 326 0556) [10]. The funeral grant is paid within 3 working days of submitting the application and may be claimed within the 3-year limitation period [10].
  • Notarial succession procedure and tax rules in Romania: If the deceased person held real estate or bank accounts in Romania, estate settlement is carried out through the notarial succession procedure (procedura succesorală notarială) before a public notary who is a member of the National Union of Public Notaries of Romania (Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România - UNNPR, tel. +40 21 313 9920), who verifies the tax status and obtains the tax clearance certificate (certificatul de atestare fiscală) from the National Agency for Fiscal Administration (Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală - ANAF, tel. +40 31 403 9160) [11][12]. Under the Romanian Fiscal Code, if the succession procedure is completed within 2 years from the date of death, the heirs are exempt from the 1% tax on the transfer of real estate from the succession estate [11][12].

closingQuestion: To help us provide further details tailored to your situation, in which locality in Romania did the death occur, in which constituent nation of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) was the deceased person domiciled, and do you plan to repatriate the body to the United Kingdom or arrange burial or cremation in Romania?

ro.title: Ce trebuie făcut în caz de deces între România și Regatul Unit: listă oficială în 5 pași
ro.cardSummary: Ghid oficial în 5 pași după un deces între România și Regatul Unit: certificat medical constatator al decesului, firmă de servicii funerare autorizată, înregistrarea la Starea Civilă, formalități consulare și repatriere (pașaport mortuar) sau înmormântare locală, și pensie de urmaș și succesiune.
ro.introHtml: Vă transmitem condoleanțe pentru pierderea suferită. Atunci când membrul familiei dumneavoastră, cu cetățenie sau reședință în Regatul Unit, decedează în România, procedurile oficiale implică autoritățile medicale, de stare civilă și sanitare din România, în paralel cu formalitățile consulare, de repatriere și de administrare a bunurilor și pensiilor din Regatul Unit.

steps.title: Constatarea medicală a decesului și eliberarea medico-legală în România
steps.html:
Primul pas este obținerea documentului oficial denumit Certificatul medical constatator al decesului, fără de care nu se pot realiza înregistrarea civilă sau transportul corpului neînsuflețit [1][5]:

  • Decesul în spital: Dacă decesul a survenit într-o unitate sanitară din România, medicul curant sau medicul de gardă întocmește Certificatul medical constatator al decesului, de regulă după 24 de ore de la constatarea decesului [1]. În spitalele din România se efectuează în mod obișnuit autopsia anatomo-patologică pentru confirmarea cauzei medicale a decesului, însă familia poate solicita în scris conducerii spitalului scutirea de autopsie dacă nu există suspiciuni medico-legale [1].
  • Decesul la domiciliu, la hotel sau în spațiul public: Dacă persoana decedată se afla în afara unei unități spitalicești, apelați numărul unic de urgență 112 sau medicul de familie pentru constatarea decesului [1][5].
  • Cazuri medico-legale (moarte subită, violentă sau suspectă): Dacă decesul a avut loc în circumstanțe neclare, în urma unui accident sau fără asistență medicală cunoscută, intervine Poliția Română, iar Parchetul dispune efectuarea autopsiei medico-legale prin serviciul județean de medicină legală sau prin instituții precum Institutul Național de Medicină Legală Mina Minovici (în București) [1][5]. În aceste situații, pentru înregistrarea decesului și ridicarea corpului sunt obligatorii atât Certificatul medical constatator al decesului emis de medicul legist, cât și dovada eliberată de poliție sau parchet [5].

steps.title: Asigurarea de repatriere, desemnarea firmei funerare și asistența consulară
steps.html:
Înainte de a angaja cheltuieli pe cont propriu, verificați existența unei polițe de asigurare și desemnați un coordonator funerar autorizat [1]:

  • Verificarea asigurării de călătorie sau repatriere: Dacă persoana decedată deținea o asigurare de călătorie, medicală sau de repatriere, contactați imediat centrala de asistență a asigurătorului [1]. Asigurătorul desemnează de regulă direct firmele funerare partenere și acoperă costurile de transport și formalitățile [1].
  • Desemnarea firmei funerare în România și în Regatul Unit: Dacă nu există asigurare, familia poate mandata o firmă de servicii funerare din România autorizată sanitar de direcția județeană de sănătate publică (de exemplu, autoritatea sanitară Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București, tel. +40 21 252 7978) conform Hotărârii Guvernului nr. 741/2016 [2][4]. Aceasta colaborează cu un operator funerar receptor din Regatul Unit înregistrat într-un director profesional oficial, cum ar fi asociația National Association of Funeral Directors (tel. +44 121 711 1343; în Regatul Unit activează, de asemenea, asociația profesională SAIF) [3]. Aceste organizații profesionale sunt prezentate exclusiv cu titlu informativ din surse publice pentru orientare; Clarvia nu le avizează, nu le recomandă și nu le ierarhizează.
  • Asistența consulară britanică: Contactați misiunea diplomatică British Embassy Bucharest (tel. +40 21 201 7200) și serviciul consular al Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) [1]. Ambasada oferă îndrumare consulară familiei și liste orientative de prestatori funerari internaționali și traducători, însă nu acoperă costurile de repatriere sau înmormântare [1].

steps.title: Înregistrarea decesului la starea civilă în România și recunoașterea actelor în Regatul Unit
steps.html:
Decesul trebuie înregistrat obligatoriu la autoritățile locale din România înainte de înhumare, incinerare sau repatriere [1][5]:

  • Înregistrarea la SPCLEP / Primărie în România: Declarația de deces se face la Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor (SPCLEP) sau la ofițerul de stare civilă din cadrul primăriei unității administrativ-teritoriale unde s-a produs decesul, sub coordonarea instituției Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor (tel. +40 21 410 7557) [5]. Termenul legal este de 3 zile de la data încetării din viață pentru cauze naturale, respectiv de 3 zile de la eliberarea certificatului medical constatator (însoțit de dovada eliberată de poliție sau parchet) în caz de moarte violentă sau suspectă [5]. Firma funerară împuternicită de familie poate depune actele (certificatul medical constatator, pașaportul britanic și actul de identitate al declarantului) pentru a ridica Certificatul de deces românesc și Adeverința de înhumare sau incinerare [1][5].
  • Extrasul multilingv și Apostila: Solicitați la starea civilă eliberarea unui Extras multilingv al actului de deces (Formularul C) sau aplicați Apostila de la Haga (prin Instituția Prefectului) și o traducere autorizată în limba engleză pe certificatul românesc, astfel încât documentul să poată fi utilizat în fața instituțiilor și băncilor din Regatul Unit [1][5].
  • Statutul înregistrării în Regatul Unit: Atunci când decesul a fost înregistrat oficial în România, nu este necesară reînregistrarea la oficiul local de stare civilă (Register Office, unde termenele interne sunt de 5 zile în Anglia, Țara Galilor și Irlanda de Nord sau 8 zile în Scoția) [1][7]; certificatul de deces românesc (însoțit de traducere certificată în limba engleză) este recunoscut în Regatul Unit [1].

steps.title: Repatrierea internațională în Regatul Unit sau înhumarea și incinerarea locală în România
steps.html:
Familia poate opta fie pentru repatrierea corpului neînsuflețit sau a urnei funerare în Regatul Unit, fie pentru înhumarea sau incinerarea locală în România [1][2]:

  • Repatrierea corpului neînsuflețit din România: Transportul internațional al corpului este gestionat de firma funerară autorizată și necesită îmbălsămare oficială, așezarea într-un sicriu metalic (de zinc) închis ermetic și sigilat, precum și obținerea documentului Pașaport mortuar eliberat de direcția județeană de sănătate publică (sau de instituția Direcția de Sănătate Publică a Municipiului București pentru decesele din Capitală) în baza Certificatului de deces și a Adeverinței de înhumare [2][4]. Dacă persoana decedată deținea și cetățenie română, informații suplimentare privind documentele consulare sunt gestionate și prin Ministerul Afacerilor Externe [4].
  • Formalitățile de recepție în Regatul Unit: La sosirea în Anglia sau Țara Galilor, operatorul funerar britanic prezintă actele de deces și de transport medicului legist local (Coroner) pentru eliberarea autorizației de înhumare sau incinerare (de exemplu, Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104 pentru incinerare) [7]. Dacă destinația este în Scoția, înainte de înhumare sau incinerare este obligatorie verificarea și autorizarea documentelor străine (Form Y și actul de deces străin) de către serviciul Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (tel. +44 300 123 1898, e-mail his.dcrs@nhs.scot) [6].
  • Repatrierea cenușii sau ceremonia locală în România: În cazul incinerării în România pe baza Adeverinței de incinerare, transportul internațional al urnei sigilate cu cenușă nu necesită pașaport mortuar, ci doar Certificatul de deces, certificatul de incinerare și respectarea regulilor companiei aeriene [1][4].

steps.title: Ajutorul de deces, pensiile de urmaș, obligațiile fiscale și succesiunea în Regatul Unit și România
steps.html:
După obținerea Certificatului de deces, familia sau executorul testamentar poate iniția demersurile sociale, fiscale și succesorale în ambele jurisdicții [7][8][10]:

  • Notificări și pensii în Regatul Unit: Dacă persoana decedată locuia sau primea beneficii în Regatul Unit, verificați dacă puteți utiliza serviciul guvernamental Tell Us Once sau notificați direct Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) prin serviciul International Pension Centre (tel. +44 191 218 7777) pentru oprirea plății pensiei de stat și solicitarea drepturilor de urmaș (cum ar fi Bereavement Support Payment), precum și autoritatea fiscală HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [7][8]. Pentru administrarea conturilor bancare și a bunurilor din Regatul Unit, executorul sau ruda îndreptățită solicită în instanță Grant of Probate (sau Letters of Administration) în Anglia, Țara Galilor și Irlanda de Nord, respectiv Confirmation în Scoția [9].
  • Ajutorul de deces și pensia de urmaș în România: Dacă persoana decedată era asigurată sau pensionară în sistemul public de pensii din România (sau membru de familie al unui asigurat/pensionar), persoana care dovedește cu factură că a suportat cheltuielile funerare poate solicita ajutorul de deces și, după caz, pensia de urmaș la casa teritorială de pensii din subordinea Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (de exemplu, instituția Casa de Pensii a Municipiului București, tel. +40 21 326 0556) [10]. Ajutorul de deces se achită în termen de 3 zile lucrătoare de la depunerea cererii și poate fi solicitat în termenul de prescripție de 3 ani [10].
  • Procedura succesorală și obligațiile fiscale în România: Dacă persoana decedată deținea bunuri imobile sau conturi în România, dezbaterea moștenirii se realizează prin procedura succesorală notarială la un notar public membru în Uniunea Națională a Notarilor Publici din România (tel. +40 21 313 9920), care verifică regimul fiscal și obține certificatul de atestare fiscală de la instituția Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală (tel. +40 31 403 9160) [11][12]. Conform Codului fiscal din România, dacă procedura succesorală este finalizată în termen de 2 ani de la data decesului, moștenitorii sunt scutiți de impozitul de 1% pe transferul proprietăților imobiliare din patrimoniul succesoral [11][12].

ro.closingQuestion: Pentru a vă oferi detalii suplimentare adaptate situației dumneavoastră, ne puteți preciza: 1. În ce localitate din România a avut loc decesul și în ce națiune constitutivă a Regatului Unit (Anglia, Țara Galilor, Scoția sau Irlanda de Nord) avea domiciliul persoana decedată? 2. Optați pentru repatrierea corpului neînsuflețit în Regatul Unit sau pentru înhumare ori incinerare în România?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Turkey: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Turkey, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Turkey.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for your loss. When your family member with United Kingdom citizenship or residence ties dies in Turkey, the medical death certificate, civil registration, and border health transit permits in Turkey must be coordinated in sequence with consular, funeral reception, pension, and probate procedures in the United Kingdom.

steps.title: Medical Death Certificate and Forensic Investigation Process in Turkey
steps.html:
For official civil registration, local burial, or international repatriation, the first step is the issuance of an electronic Death Certificate (Ölüm Belgesi, which also serves as the Burial Permit, Defin Ruhsatı) by an authorized physician according to where the death occurred [1][3]:

  • Death in a hospital: If the death occurred from natural causes in a healthcare facility, the attending hospital physician issues the electronic Ölüm Belgesi through the Ministry of Health Death Notification System (Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi - ÖBS) [1][3].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: For natural deaths occurring outside a hospital, you must call the 112 Emergency Call Centre (112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi) or apply to the relevant municipal doctor (belediye tabibi) or community health centre physician (toplum sağlığı merkezi hekimi) [1][3]. Once the physician's examination confirms that death resulted from natural causes, the Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) is issued via the ÖBS [3].
  • Suspicious, sudden, or forensic deaths: If the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or involves an accident or suspicious circumstances, the Police (155 / 112) or Gendarmerie (156 / 112) (Jandarma) are notified and the investigation is conducted by the on-duty Public Prosecutor's Office (Cumhuriyet Savcılığı) [1]. Where deemed necessary by the Public Prosecutor, an autopsy is performed by the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tıp Kurumu, usually within 1 to 3 days), and the body is released only with the prosecutor's burial or transport permit [1].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing a Funeral Director, and Consular Support
steps.html:
Before incurring out-of-pocket expenses, verify insurance coverage and appoint a licensed funeral service provider to coordinate between both countries [1]:

  • Checking travel and repatriation insurance: Immediately check whether the deceased person held travel health insurance, private health insurance, or membership in a mutual funeral assistance fund (such as Diyanet or related funeral fund foundations) [1]. If an insurance policy is in place, the insurer directly appoints an international funeral repatriation company and covers the costs under the policy terms [1].
  • Appointing a funeral director in Turkey and the United Kingdom: For local funeral arrangements within Turkey, families can call the ALO 188 municipal funeral services line (belediye cenaze hizmetleri); for international repatriation abroad, a licensed international funeral repatriation company must be appointed [1][5]. This provider works in coordination with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered in the directory of an official trade body such as the National Association of Funeral Directors (tel. +44 121 711 1343; the SAIF trade association also operates in the United Kingdom) [2]. These professional associations are provided solely as public-source examples for informational guidance; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank them.
  • UK consular support: If the deceased person was a British national, contact the UK diplomatic mission in Turkey, British Embassy Ankara (tel. +90 312 455 33 44) or the relevant Consulate General (Istanbul, Izmir, Antalya), as well as the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO, tel. +44 20 7008 5000) [1]. The Consulate provides a list of English-speaking international funeral directors and procedural guidance, but cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [1].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Turkey and Document Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Before the body can be buried or repatriated abroad, the death must be officially recorded in the Turkish civil registry [1][3]:

  • District Civil Registry registration and Form C certificate: The death notification issued via the ÖBS by the physician or prosecutor is transmitted electronically within 10 days to the District Directorate of Civil Registration (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü, under the central authority Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü - Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship, call centre ALO 199) where the death occurred [1][3]. A family member or the authorized funeral company should request the internationally recognized Multilingual Death Certificate on Form C (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C, under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention) from the İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü [3][4]. If additional official authentication or consular advice is needed, information is available through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Call Centre (Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi, tel. +90 312 292 29 29) [4].
  • Registration and document validity in the United Kingdom: Because the death is officially registered by the authorities in Turkey, it is not mandatory to re-register the death at a local UK Register Office (where domestic registration deadlines are 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland) [1][7]. The Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C) obtained in Turkey, or the official Turkish death certificate accompanied by a sworn English translation and, where required, a Hague Apostille, is used directly before institutions and banks in the United Kingdom [1][7].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial Options in Turkey
steps.html:
The family can decide between repatriating the body to the United Kingdom or arranging local burial in Turkey [1][5]:

  • International repatriation from Turkey: The international funeral company arranges official embalming (tahnit), places the body in a soldered zinc liner inside an outer wooden coffin, obtains the Road Transit Permit (Yol İzin Belgesi) from the relevant municipality or provincial/district health directorate, and completes the international Mortuary Laissez-Passer (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer) inspection and approval through the border health inspection unit at the departure airport or border crossing (under the official authority Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - Directorate General of Health for Borders and Coasts, tel. +90 212 293 36 74) [4][5].
  • Receiving the body and burial/cremation clearance in the United Kingdom: Once the body arrives in England or Wales, the local UK funeral director submits the death and transit documents from Turkey to the local Coroner to obtain authorization for burial or cremation (such as a Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104) [7]. If the body is repatriated to Scotland, the foreign death documents (together with Form Y) must be reviewed and approved before burial or cremation by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (tel. +44 300 123 1898, email his.dcrs@nhs.scot) [6].
  • Local burial and cremation availability in Turkey: Local burial in Turkey is carried out through the municipal cemeteries directorates (belediye mezarlıklar müdürlükleri) using the Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) [3][5]. Because there are no active commercial crematoria operating in Turkey, if cremation is desired the body must be repatriated to the United Kingdom [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Probate in the UK and Turkey
steps.html:
Once the official death certificate has been obtained, social security, tax, and probate procedures can be initiated in both countries [7][8][10]:

  • Notifications, pensions, and probate in the United Kingdom: If the deceased person held a UK State Pension or social security entitlements, check whether the Tell Us Once service is available or contact the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) unit International Pension Centre (tel. +44 191 218 7777) and the tax authority HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) directly to stop pension payments and inquire about survivor benefits (Bereavement Support Payment) [7][8]. To administer bank accounts and estate assets in the United Kingdom, an application is made for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or Confirmation in Scotland [9].
  • SGK funeral grant and survivor pension in Turkey: If the deceased person had social insurance or pension coverage in Turkey, eligible beneficiaries who document funeral expenses can apply for a funeral grant (cenaze ödeneği) and, if qualifying conditions are met, a survivor's pension (ölüm aylığı / dul ve yetim aylığı) via the e-Devlet portal or at provincial/local directorates of the Social Security Institution (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK, call centre ALO 170) [10].
  • Certificate of inheritance and inheritance tax in Turkey: If the deceased person held movable or immovable property or bank accounts in Turkey, heirs must obtain a Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) from a notary public affiliated with the Union of Turkish Bar Notaries (Türkiye Noterler Birliği, tel. +90 312 218 80 00) or, where there is a foreign element or a will, from the Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [11]. For assets in Turkey, an Inheritance and Transfer Tax Return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi Beyannamesi) must be filed within 4 months following the date of death (when death occurs in Turkey, subject to statutory extensions if beneficiaries reside abroad) with the tax offices of the Turkish Revenue Administration (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı - GİB, call centre ALO 189) or via the Digital Tax Office (Dijital Vergi Dairesi) [12].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more detailed guidance tailored to your situation, in which province or district of Turkey did the death occur, which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) is the destination or location of the estate assets, and do you prefer repatriation to the United Kingdom or local burial in Turkey?
