title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Netherlands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Netherlands: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Netherlands, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Netherlands.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with British nationality or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in the Netherlands, medical certification of death and registration with the Dutch civil registry must be completed first before international repatriation to the United Kingdom, a local funeral in the Netherlands, and estate administration can be arranged [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Examination, Death Certification, and Forensic Clearance in the Netherlands
steps.html:
• Natural death in a hospital, care facility, or at home: The attending physician or on-call general practitioner (huisarts) performs the official post-mortem examination (lijkschouwing) and, if the cause of death is natural, issues the Declaration of Death (verklaring van overlijden / A-verklaring) together with the sealed Form B (B-verklaring) cause-of-death statistical envelope for Statistics Netherlands (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) [1][3].
  • Unexpected or non-natural death (112, GGD, and Public Prosecutor): If the death is sudden, unexplained, or potentially non-natural, call 112 [1]. The police and the municipal coroner (gemeentelijk lijkschouwer), who is a forensic physician from the Municipal Health Service (GGD), investigate the circumstances and report to the Public Prosecutor (officier van justitie), who must officially release the body before burial, cremation, or transport to the United Kingdom is permitted [1][3].

steps.title: Checking Insurance, Appointing Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and UK Consular Support
steps.html:
• Check travel or repatriation insurance first: Before signing a funeral contract, verify whether the deceased held travel, health, or repatriation insurance, as the insurer's emergency assistance centre typically appoints an international funeral coordinator directly and must pre-approve costs [1][2].
  • Certified funeral directors in the Netherlands and the United Kingdom: In the Netherlands, you can engage a certified funeral director through the Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen (BGNU, the Association of Certified Dutch Funeral Directors), who will ensure compliance with the statutory time limits under the Corpse Disposal Act (Wet op de lijkbezorging) - burial or cremation may take place no earlier than 36 hours and no later than the 6th working day after death, unless the mayor (burgemeester) grants an extension for repatriation [3][4]. For repatriation to the United Kingdom, the Dutch funeral director coordinates with a receiving UK funeral director registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][5]. These trade directories serve as public orientation examples; Clarvia does not recommend, endorse, or rank individual providers.
  • British consular support: Contact the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO, +44 20 7008 5000 in London or via the British Embassy in The Hague / Consulate-General in Amsterdam) to report the death, arrange cancellation of the British passport, and obtain an overview of English-speaking funeral directors and lawyers [1][2]. Consular staff cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the Netherlands and Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Registration with the municipality of death: Using Form A (A-verklaring) and the sealed Form B envelope (B-enveloppe), the funeral director (or next of kin) registers the death with the Civil Registry (Burgerlijke Stand) of the Dutch municipality where the death occurred - such as Gemeente Den Haag (Municipality of The Hague), which also processes non-resident records through its National Tasks Department (afdeling Landelijke Taken) [1][3]. If the deceased was registered in the Dutch Personal Records Database (Basisregistratie Personen - BRP), the municipality automatically notifies Dutch government agencies of the death [6].
  • Death certificate and multilingual CIEC Form C extract: Request both the standard Dutch death certificate (akte van overlijden) and the multilingual international extract on CIEC Form C (internationaal uittreksel op CIEC-model C) issued under the 1976 Vienna Convention, which includes English headings [1][3]. If a UK institution requires an apostille, it can be obtained from the registry (griffie) of any Dutch district court (rechtbank) [1].
  • Recognition in the United Kingdom: Whereas a death occurring inside the United Kingdom must be registered within 5 days at a local Register Office in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or within 8 days in Scotland (via mygov.scot) [7], a death that takes place in the Netherlands does not need to be re-registered with the UK civil registry [1][2]. The multilingual CIEC Form C extract (or a certified English translation of the Dutch certificate) is accepted directly in the United Kingdom; if desired, optional consular death registration is available through the FCDO Overseas Registration Unit [1][2].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the Netherlands
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body (laissez-passer voor lijken): To transport the body from the Netherlands to the United Kingdom, the Dutch funeral director applies to the mayor (burgemeester) of the municipality of death for a corpse transit permit (laissez-passer voor lijken) under the Strasbourg Agreement [8][9]. The funeral director arranges a medical certificate of non-infection, embalming, and placement in a hermetically soldered zinc liner or approved international transport coffin (see also the general guidance on NederlandWereldwijd from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs) [1][9].
  • Clearance upon arrival in the United Kingdom (Coroner or DCRS): Upon arrival in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director submits the death documentation to the local Coroner for an Out-of-England Order or Form 104 (authorisation to cremate remains brought from abroad) [1][2]; in Scotland, review and clearance for burial or cremation of repatriated remains are handled by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [10].
  • Transport of cremated ashes or local funeral in the Netherlands: For a local burial or cremation in the Netherlands, the municipality issues a permit for burial or cremation (verlof tot begraven of cremeren) [3][8]. Bringing an urn containing cremated ashes to the United Kingdom does not require a hermetically lined coffin or a laissez-passer, but the death certificate, the cremation certificate (crematieverklaring) from the Dutch crematorium, and a sealed urn must be presented [1][8].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• Notifications, pensions, and probate in the United Kingdom: If the deceased was ordinarily resident in England, Scotland, or Wales and died while temporarily in the Netherlands, you can use the Tell Us Once service via a local UK Register Office to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, and local councils simultaneously [2][11]. If the deceased lived permanently outside the United Kingdom or in Northern Ireland, contact the DWP Bereavement Service or the International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777, including to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment) and HMRC directly [2][12]. To administer UK bank accounts or assets, the executor or entitled representative applies for a Grant of Probate (in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland) or Confirmation (through the Sheriff Court in Scotland) [2][7].
  • Pensions, notarial succession, and taxes in the Netherlands: If the deceased held Dutch pension entitlements or assets, contact the Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB, Social Insurance Bank) to stop an AOW state pension and check eligibility for a survivor benefit (Algemene nabestaandenwet - Anw) [6][13]. Through the Central Register of Wills (Centraal Testamentenregister - CTR) and a Dutch civil-law notary (see Notaris.nl, operated by the Royal Dutch Association of Civil-Law Notaries, Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie - KNB), verify whether a will exists and obtain a certificate of inheritance (verklaring van erfrecht) [14]. Heirs can file a declaration at the district court registry (de Rechtspraak) for unconditional acceptance (zuiver aanvaarden), acceptance under benefit of inventory (beneficiair aanvaarden), or renunciation (verwerpen) of the estate [15], and must file the final income tax return (F-biljet) and inheritance tax return (aangifte erfbelasting) with the Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax and Customs Administration; Bereavement Tax Helpline BelastingTelefoon voor nabestaanden: 0800 235 83 54) [16].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your exact situation, in which Dutch municipality did the death occur, in which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) did the deceased hold residence or assets, and do you plan to arrange international repatriation to the United Kingdom or a local burial or cremation in the Netherlands?

nl.title: Wat te doen bij een overlijden tussen Nederland en Verenigd Koninkrijk: officiële checklist in 5 stappen
nl.cardSummary: Officiële checklist in 5 stappen na een overlijden tussen Nederland en Verenigd Koninkrijk: medische verklaring van overlijden, uitvaartondernemer, aangifte bij de burgerlijke stand, consulaire formaliteiten en repatriëring (lijkenpas) of lokale uitvaart, en nabestaandenpensioen en nalatenschap.
nl.introHtml: Gecondoleerd met het verlies van uw familielid. Wanneer een persoon met de Britse nationaliteit of banden met het Verenigd Koninkrijk in Nederland overlijdt, moeten eerst de medische lijkschouwing en de aangifte bij de Nederlandse burgerlijke stand plaatsvinden voordat internationale repatriëring naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk, een lokale uitvaart in Nederland en de afwikkeling van de nalatenschap kunnen worden geregeld [1][2].

steps.title: Officiële lijkschouwing, verklaring van overlijden en vrijgave in Nederland
steps.html:
• Natuurlijk overlijden in een ziekenhuis, zorginstelling of thuis: De behandelend arts of dienstdoende huisarts verricht de officiële lijkschouwing en stelt bij een natuurlijke doodsoorzaak de verklaring van overlijden (A-verklaring) én de gesloten B-verklaring (doodsoorzaakformulier voor het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) op [1][3].
  • Onverwacht of niet-natuurlijk overlijden (112, GGD en officier van justitie): Is het overlijden plotseling, onverklaard of mogelijk niet-natuurlijk, bel dan 112 [1]. De politie en de gemeentelijk lijkschouwer (forensisch arts van de GGD) stellen een onderzoek in en rapporteren aan de officier van justitie, die het lichaam eerst officieel moet vrijgeven voordat begraving, crematie of vervoer naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk is toegestaan [1][3].

steps.title: Verzekering controleren, uitvaartondernemers in beide landen en Britse consulaire bijstand
steps.html:
• Reis- of repatriëringsverzekering eerst raadplegen: Controleer vóór het tekenen van een uitvaartopdracht of de overledene een reis-, zorg- of repatriëringsverzekering had, aangezien de alarmcentrale van de verzekeraar doorgaans zelf een internationale uitvaartcoördinator aanwijst en kosten vooraf moet goedkeuren [1][2].
  • Gecertificeerde uitvaartondernemers in Nederland en het Verenigd Koninkrijk: U kunt in Nederland een gecertificeerde uitvaartondernemer inschakelen via de Branchevereniging Gecertificeerde Nederlandse Uitvaartondernemingen (BGNU), die let op de wettelijke termijn van de Wet op de lijkbezorging (begraving of crematie niet eerder dan 36 uur en uiterlijk op de 6e werkdag na het overlijden, tenzij de burgemeester uitstel verleent voor repatriëring) [3][4]. Voor overbrenging naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk werkt het Nederlandse bedrijf samen met een ontvangende Britse uitvaartondernemer, te vinden via de National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) of de National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][5]. Deze brancheregisters dienen als openbare oriëntatievoorbeelden; Clarvia beveelt geen individuele aanbieders aan, keurt deze niet goed en rangschikt deze niet.
  • Britse consulaire ondersteuning: Neem contact op met het Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO, +44 20 7008 5000 in Londen of via de Britse Ambassade in Den Haag / het Consulaat-Generaal in Amsterdam) om het overlijden te melden, het Britse paspoort te laten annuleren en een overzicht van Engelstalige uitvaartondernemers en juristen te ontvangen [1][2]. Consulaire medewerkers kunnen geen uitvaart- of repatriëringskosten vergoeden [1][2].

steps.title: Aangifte van overlijden bij de Burgerlijke Stand in Nederland en erkenning in het Verenigd Koninkrijk
steps.html:
• Aangifte bij de gemeente van overlijden: De uitvaartondernemer (of een nabestaande) doet met het A-formulier en de B-enveloppe aangifte bij de Burgerlijke Stand van de Nederlandse gemeente waar de persoon is overleden (zoals bij Gemeente Den Haag, die via de afdeling Landelijke Taken ook akten voor niet-ingezetenen verwerkt) [1][3]. Stond de overledene ingeschreven in de Nederlandse Basisregistratie Personen (BRP), dan geeft de gemeente het overlijden automatisch door aan Nederlandse overheidsinstanties [6].
  • Akte van overlijden en meertalig CIEC-uittreksel Model C: Vraag bij de Nederlandse gemeente zowel de originele akte van overlijden als het meertalige internationaal uittreksel op CIEC-model C (Overeenkomst van Wenen 1976, voorzien van een Engelse vertaling) aan [1][3]. Indien een Britse instantie een apostille verlangt, kan die bij de griffie van elke Nederlandse rechtbank worden gehaald [1].
  • Erkenning in het Verenigd Koninkrijk: Terwijl een overlijden binnen het Verenigd Koninkrijk binnen 5 dagen in Engeland, Wales en Noord-Ierland bij het lokale Register Office of binnen 8 dagen in Schotland (via mygov.scot) moet worden geregistreerd [7], hoeft een overlijden dat in Nederland plaatsvindt niet verplicht opnieuw bij de Britse burgerlijke stand te worden ingeschreven [1][2]. Het meertalige CIEC-uittreksel (of een beëdigde Engelse vertaling van de Nederlandse akte) wordt in het Verenigd Koninkrijk rechtstreeks geaccepteerd; desgewenst is een optionele consulaire registratie mogelijk via de Overseas Registration Unit van het FCDO [1][2].

steps.title: Internationale repatriëring naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk of begraving/crematie in Nederland
steps.html:
• Repatriëring van het lichaam (laissez-passer voor lijken): Voor het vervoer van het lichaam vanuit Nederland naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk vraagt de Nederlandse uitvaartondernemer bij de burgemeester van de gemeente van overlijden een laissez-passer voor lijken (lijkenpas op grond van de Overeenkomst van Straatsburg) aan [8][9]. Daarbij zorgt de uitvaartondernemer voor een medische verklaring van niet-besmettelijkheid, balseming en plaatsing in een luchtdicht gesoldeerde zinken binnenkist of goedgekeurde transportkist (zie ook de algemene richtlijnen op NederlandWereldwijd van het Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken) [1][9].
  • Vrijgave bij aankomst in het Verenigd Koninkrijk (Coroner of DCRS): Na aankomst in Engeland of Wales legt de ontvangende Britse uitvaartondernemer de overlijdensdocumenten voor aan de lokale Coroner voor een Out-of-England Order dan wel Form 104 (toestemming voor crematie van een vanuit het buitenland overgebracht lichaam) [1][2]; in Schotland verloopt de beoordeling en vrijgave voor begraving of crematie via de Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [10].
  • Vervoer van crematie-as of lokale uitvaart in Nederland: Bij een lokale begraving of crematie in Nederland geeft de gemeente een verlof tot begraven of cremeren af [3][8]. Voor het overbrengen van een urn met crematie-as naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk zijn geen luchtdichte kist of laissez-passer vereist, maar moeten wel de overlijdensakte, de crematieverklaring van het Nederlandse crematorium en een gesloten asbus worden overlegd [1][8].

steps.title: Meldingen na overlijden, nabestaandenpensioen, belastingen en erfrecht in beide landen
steps.html:
• Meldingen, pensioenen en erfrecht in het Verenigd Koninkrijk: Woonde de overledene gewoonlijk in Engeland, Schotland of Wales en verbleef deze tijdelijk in Nederland, dan kunt u via een lokaal Brits Register Office de melddienst Tell Us Once gebruiken om HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), het Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office en lokale gemeenten gelijktijdig te informeren [2][11]. Bij permanente woonplaats buiten het Verenigd Koninkrijk of in Noord-Ierland neemt u rechtstreeks contact op met de DWP Bereavement Service of het International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777, inclusief controle op recht op Bereavement Support Payment) en met HMRC [2][12]. Voor het beheren van Britse bankrekeningen of bezittingen vraagt de executeur of gerechtigde een Grant of Probate (in Engeland, Wales of Noord-Ierland) of Confirmation (bij de Sheriff Court in Schotland) aan [2][7].
  • Pensioenen, notariaat en belastingen in Nederland: Had de overledene Nederlandse pensioenaanspraken of bezittingen, controleer dan bij de Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) de stopzetting van een AOW-pensioen en het eventuele recht op een nabestaandenuitkering (Anw) [6][13]. Via het Centraal Testamentenregister (CTR) en een Nederlandse notaris (zie Notaris.nl van de Koninklijke Notariële Beroepsorganisatie, KNB) laat u controleren of er een testament is en vraagt u een verklaring van erfrecht aan [14]. Erfgenamen kunnen via de griffie van de rechtbank (de Rechtspraak) de erfenis zuiver aanvaarden, beneficiair aanvaarden of verwerpen [15], en dienen bij de Belastingdienst (BelastingTelefoon voor nabestaanden: 0800 235 83 54) de slot-inkomstenbelastingaangifte (F-biljet) en de aangifte erfbelasting in [16].

nl.closingQuestion: Om de stappen precies af te stemmen op uw situatie, kunt u nog aangeven: 1. In welke Nederlandse gemeente is het overlijden ingetreden, en in welk deel van het Verenigd Koninkrijk (Engeland, Wales, Schotland of Noord-Ierland) had de overledene woonplaats of vermogen? 2. Kiest u voor internationale repatriëring van het lichaam of de as naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk, of voor een begrafenis of crematie in Nederland?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in South Africa: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in South Africa: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in South Africa, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and South Africa.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member with citizenship or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in South Africa, medical certification and civil death registration must first be completed with the South African authorities before international repatriation to the United Kingdom, local burial or cremation, and estate administration in both countries can proceed [1][2].

steps.title: Medical Certification, SAPS Notification, and Forensic Pathology Clearance in South Africa
steps.html:
• Natural death in a hospital, clinic, or residence: When a person dies of natural causes in South Africa, an attending medical practitioner examines the remains and completes the Department of Home Affairs Notice of Death / Death Report (Form BI-1663 / DHA-1663), which is required to register the death and obtain a burial order [1][3].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or unnatural death (SAPS and Forensic Pathology Service): If the death is sudden, unnatural, or outside medical care, the South African Police Service (SAPS 10111) must be called to the scene [1]. The deceased is transferred to a provincial Forensic Pathology Service mortuary for a statutory medico-legal post-mortem (autopsy) under the Inquests Act before the forensic pathologist completes Form DHA-1663 and releases the body to your appointed funeral undertaker [1][3].

steps.title: Insurance Check, Licensed Funeral Undertakers in Both Countries, and British Consular Support
steps.html:
• Check travel or repatriation insurance first: Before signing private funeral contracts, verify whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or employer insurance covering international repatriation, as the insurer's assistance service typically appoints the funeral coordinator and must approve costs in advance [1][2].
  • Appointing licensed funeral directors in South Africa and the UK: In South Africa, only a designated funeral undertaker holding a valid Certificate of Competence can remove, prepare, and register remains [3][4]. You can locate an accredited South African provider through the National Funeral Directors Association of South Africa (NFDA) [5] and coordinate with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [2][6]. These professional directories are provided as public-source orientation examples; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank individual providers.
  • British consular notification: Contact the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO, +44 20 7008 5000 in London) or the British High Commission Pretoria (or British Consulate General Cape Town) to report the death, cancel the deceased's British passport, and obtain lists of local English-speaking funeral undertakers and lawyers [1][2]. Consular staff provide procedural guidance and cannot pay funeral, legal, or repatriation costs [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in South Africa and Document Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Registration with the Department of Home Affairs (DHA): Your appointed South African funeral undertaker submits the completed medical Form BI-1663 / DHA-1663, the deceased's passport or ID, and the informant's identification to the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) [1][3]. DHA registers the death and issues the Burial Order (Form BI-14) together with an official abridged Death Certificate (you should also apply for an unabridged Death Certificate where required for cross-border probate or pension claims) [1][3].
  • Document recognition in the United Kingdom: While domestic deaths in the United Kingdom must be registered at a local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or within 8 days in Scotland (via mygov.scot) [7], the UK General Register Office does not re-register overseas deaths that occurred in Commonwealth countries such as South Africa [1][2].
  • Using South African Death Certificates in the UK: Because the official South African DHA Death Certificate is issued in English, UK government departments, banks, and probate registries accept it directly without translation or a multilingual CIEC Form C [1][2]. Where a court or foreign institution requires formal legalisation, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO Legalisation Section in Pretoria) issues a Hague Apostille on the original DHA Death Certificate [8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in South Africa
steps.html:
• South African Department of Health export permit: To repatriate the body from South Africa to the United Kingdom, your South African funeral undertaker must obtain an official Export Permit for Human Remains from the National Department of Health (Director-General of Health, submitted via humanremainspermits@health.gov.za) before the remains reach the airport [4][8]. The application package includes the DHA Death Certificate stating the cause of death, the Burial Order (Form BI-14), an embalming certificate, a medical non-infectious disease certificate, the undertaker's Certificate of Competence, and confirmation that the body is sealed in an airtight zinc-lined or hermetically sealed coffin for Port Health and SARS customs clearance [4][8].
  • UK Coroner or Scottish DCRS clearance on arrival: Once the body arrives in the United Kingdom, the receiving UK funeral director submits the South African Death Certificate and export documents to obtain local disposal authority: in England and Wales, the local Coroner issues an Out-of-England Order (or Coroner Form 104 / Form 6 for cremation of remains brought from abroad) [1][2]; in Scotland, authorisation is obtained through the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [9].
  • Repatriating cremated ashes or choosing local burial/cremation in South Africa: Local burial or cremation in South Africa proceeds once DHA issues the Burial Order (Form BI-14) [1][3]. Cremated human ashes do not require a Department of Health export permit to leave South Africa, but must be transported in a sealed urn accompanied by the certified DHA Death Certificate, the Cremation Certificate, and a copy of the deceased's passport [1][4].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Taxes, and Probate in the UK and South Africa
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate: If the deceased normally lived in England, Scotland, or Wales and died while temporarily in South Africa, contact a local UK Register Office with the South African Death Certificate to access the Tell Us Once service, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, and local councils in one step [2][10]. If the person lived permanently in South Africa or in Northern Ireland, notify the DWP Bereavement Service or the International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777, including checking eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment) and HMRC directly [2][11]. To administer UK property or bank accounts, apply for a UK Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or Confirmation in Scotland [2][7].
  • Reporting a South African estate to the Master of the High Court: If the deceased left property, bank accounts, or estate assets in South Africa, the estate must be reported to the Master of the High Court within 14 days of death using the Death Notice (Form J294), inventory of assets (Form J243), certified DHA Death Certificate, and original will (either in person or via the Department of Justice online portal at dojonline.justice.gov.za, support email DojDEOnlineSupport@justice.gov.za) to obtain Letters of Executorship or Letters of Authority [12][13].
  • South African tax and social security claims (SARS, UIF, and SASSA): Once appointed by the Master, the executor must notify the South African Revenue Service (SARS) to complete pre- and post-death income tax and Estate Duty compliance (to obtain a Deceased Estate Compliance letter) [14]. Where the deceased contributed to South African social security or held local grants, dependants can inquire with the Department of Employment and Labour regarding UIF Death Benefits and notify the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) to stop or adjust any social grant [3][12].

closingQuestion: To help tailor the exact local offices and legal steps, could you confirm: 1. Which South African province and municipality did the death occur in, and which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) held the person's residence or assets? 2. Are you planning international repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to the United Kingdom, or local burial or cremation in South Africa?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Philippines Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Philippines Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Philippines dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Philippines and United Kingdom.
introHtml: When a family member with citizenship or residence ties to the Philippines dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate practical steps depend on which constituent nation of the United Kingdom the death occurred in (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the remains will be repatriated to the Philippines or buried or cremated locally. Below is the official 5-step cross-border sequence.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Expected deaths and hospital deaths: In England and Wales, an attending doctor completes a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which must be independently countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner before being transmitted electronically to the local Register Office [1]. In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11) [2].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained deaths outside hospital: Call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 when no emergency resuscitation applies) so police and medical personnel can attend. In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, sudden or unexplained deaths are referred to the local Coroner, whereas in Scotland they are reported to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service [1][2]. Civil registration and international transfer permits cannot proceed until the Coroner (via a Coroner interim certificate or release) or Procurator Fiscal issues formal clearance [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Philippine Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check insurance and Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW) coverage first: Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance. If the deceased was an active Overseas Filipino Worker, contact the Migrant Workers Office at the embassy, the Department of Migrant Workers (24/7 hotline 1348, email feedback@dmw.gov.ph), and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (email opcenter@owwa.gov.ph) so statutory employer or welfare repatriation support can be activated [6][7].
  • Appointing a coordinating funeral director: You can mandate a UK funeral provider registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) to coordinate the preparation and air transport with a Department of Health (DOH)-licensed receiving funeral establishment and mortuary in the Philippines (for example in Metro Manila, Cebu, or Davao) [3][8]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank individual providers.
  • Consular notification: Notify the Philippine Embassy in London (consular phone +44 20 7451 1780, emergency mobile +44 7802 790695) to obtain current requirements for the consular Report of Death and Consular Mortuary Certificate [4].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom, Apostille, and Philippine Civil Registry Recording
steps.html:
• UK civil registration: Once the Medical Examiner or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal clears the cause of death, register the death at the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or the City of Edinburgh Council Registration Service via National Records of Scotland) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1][2]. Request multiple official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate.
  • Apostille and Philippine registration: Because both the United Kingdom and the Philippines are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille on the UK Death Certificate through the UK Legalisation Office [5]. File a Report of Death with the Philippine Embassy in London (generally within 30 days where possible, or via delayed registration with an affidavit of delay) so the record is forwarded through the Department of Foreign Affairs to the Local Civil Registrar (LCRO) and the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) for issuance of a Security Paper (SECPA) Death Certificate [4][8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the Philippines Versus Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body: Your UK funeral director prepares and embalms the body in a hermetically sealed, zinc-lined casket, obtains a free-from-infection certificate from public health authorities, and secures an Out-of-England Order (Form 104) from the Coroner in England and Wales (or clearance from the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service in Scotland) [1][2]. The funeral coordinator submits these documents with the apostilled UK Death Certificate to the Philippine Embassy in London to obtain the Consular Mortuary Certificate, and coordinates entry clearance at Ninoy Aquino International Airport or another port of entry with the Department of Health Bureau of Quarantine [4][9].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the ashes are placed in a sealed urn accompanied by the UK Death Certificate, Certificate of Cremation, and consular clearance from the Philippine Embassy in London [4][9].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: During civil registration, the registrar issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the Green Form in England and Wales, or Form 14 in Scotland) directly to the funeral director so local interment or cremation can proceed [1][2].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, benefits, and probate: When registering the death, ask the registrar for a Tell Us Once reference number (usable within 28 days) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local councils in one step [10]. Eligible surviving partners in the UK or abroad may claim Bereavement Support Payment or survivor pension entitlements through the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service phone +44 800 151 2012, or via the International Pension Centre) [11][12]. If the deceased held UK bank accounts or property in their sole name, the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland [2][13].
  • Philippines benefits, pensions, and estate settlement: In the Philippines, eligible survivors or the person who paid funeral expenses can claim funeral and death benefits from the Social Security System (or GSIS for government employees), alongside PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG Fund, and Overseas Workers Welfare Administration death and burial benefits for active OFW members [7][14][15]. For Philippine assets, heirs or executors must file an Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801) with the Bureau of Internal Revenue within 1 year from the date of death and complete either an Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate before a Philippine notary (with newspaper publication) or judicial probate [16].

closingQuestion: To help tailor this guidance further: 1. In which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) did the death occur, and has the Medical Examiner or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal issued clearance? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to the Philippines, or arrange a local funeral in the United Kingdom?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Philippines: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Philippines, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Philippines.
introHtml: When a family member with citizenship or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in the Philippines, you will need to coordinate Philippine medical and civil registration rules with UK consular, mortuary, and estate procedures. Below is the official 5-step cross-border checklist.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Emergency or Police Clearance in the Philippines
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital or medical facility in the Philippines, the attending physician completes the medical portion of the Certificate of Death (Municipal Form No. 103) within 48 hours [1][4].
  • Deaths at a residence, hotel, or public place: Report the death immediately to the local Barangay and the Philippine National Police (emergency hotline 911). When there is no attending physician, the local Municipal Health Officer (MHO) or City Health Officer (CHO) (for example at the Manila Health Department or Cebu City Health Department) must examine the deceased, determine whether a medico-legal autopsy is required by the PNP Scene of the Crime Operatives (SOCO) or National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), and certify the cause of death on Municipal Form No. 103 [1][4].
  • 48-hour sanitation rule: Under Presidential Decree No. 856 (Code on Sanitation of the Philippines), human remains must generally be buried, cremated, or embalmed within 48 hours of death unless specific preservation and health permits are obtained [1][5].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and UK Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check travel and medical-assistance insurance first: Before entering into an independent funeral contract, contact the deceased's travel or international health insurer, as policies normally appoint an international assistance coordinator to manage local mortuary care and air repatriation directly [1][3].
  • Appointing licensed funeral providers: If no insurer coordinator is in place, appoint a Department of Health (DOH)-licensed funeral establishment and mortuary in the Philippines to handle embalming or cremation, coordinated with a receiving UK funeral director registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][6]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank individual providers.
  • UK consular support: Notify the British Embassy Manila (phone +63 2 8858 2200) or the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) to obtain the Philippines bereavement pack, local English-speaking funeral provider lists, and consular assistance [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the Philippines, Apostille, and UK Document Recognition
steps.html:
• Local Civil Registrar (LCRO) and PSA SECPA certificate: The local funeral director or next of kin must register the completed Municipal Form No. 103 within 30 days at the Local Civil Registrar (LCRO) of the city or municipality where the death occurred (such as Quezon City, Makati, or Davao City) [1][4]. Because Philippine civil death certificates are issued in English, translation is generally not required for the United Kingdom, though you should request expedited transmission to the Philippine Statistics Authority to obtain official copies on PSA Security Paper (SECPA) [1][4].
  • Apostille and UK recognition: Obtain a Hague Apostille from the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Office of Consular Affairs if UK courts or financial institutions require legalised foreign civil documents [1][7]. A death that occurs outside the United Kingdom is not re-registered at a local Register Office within the 5-day (England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or 8-day (Scotland) domestic registration window, though the Philippine Death Certificate is accepted directly by UK authorities and you may optionally apply for an overseas death record with the General Register Office [3][8][9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom Versus Local Burial or Cremation in the Philippines
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body: Your Philippine funeral director prepares the embalming certificate, non-contagious disease certificate, hermetically sealed casket certificate, local transfer permit from the City or Municipal Health Officer, and export quarantine clearance from the Department of Health Bureau of Quarantine [1][5]. If the deceased also held Overseas Filipino Worker ties, the Department of Migrant Workers (hotline 1348, email feedback@dmw.gov.ph) and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (email opcenter@owwa.gov.ph) provide welfare guidance [14]. Upon arrival in the United Kingdom, your UK funeral director obtains Coroner clearance in England and Wales (where Coroner notification and Form 104 / burial or cremation orders apply) or clearance from the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) via National Records of Scotland in Scotland [3][8][9].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the Philippines, the ashes are placed in a sealed urn accompanied by the official Death Certificate, Certificate of Cremation, and quarantine clearance from the Department of Health Bureau of Quarantine for airline transport to the United Kingdom [1][3][5].
  • Local burial or cremation in the Philippines: Local interment or cremation requires a burial or cremation permit from the local City or Municipal Health Officer; note that public cemetery leases in the Philippines are often fixed-term (commonly 5 years) unless permanent private memorial arrangements are made [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate: If the deceased normally lived in England, Wales, or Scotland, contact your local Register Office or follow GOV.UK overseas bereavement instructions to access the Tell Us Once service (within 28 days of receiving a reference) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office (to cancel the British passport), DVLA, and local councils [1][10]. Eligible surviving partners may claim Bereavement Support Payment or survivor pension entitlements from the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service phone +44 800 151 2012, or via the International Pension Centre for residents abroad) [11][12]. To administer UK bank accounts or property, apply for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland [9][13].
  • Philippines benefits, pensions, and estate tax: If the deceased contributed to Philippine social insurance or held assets in the Philippines, eligible survivors can file funeral and survivor death benefit claims with the Social Security System (or GSIS for public-sector workers), PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG Fund, and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration [14][15]. For any real property, bank accounts, or investments in the Philippines, heirs or executors must file an Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801) with the Bureau of Internal Revenue within 1 year of death and execute an Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate before a Philippine notary or complete judicial probate [16].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Ukraine Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Ukraine dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Ukraine and United Kingdom.
introHtml: When a family member with citizenship or residence ties to Ukraine dies in the United Kingdom, you must coordinate UK medical certification and civil registration with Ukrainian consular legalization, border transport rules, and inheritance procedures. Below is the official 5-step cross-border sequence.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Hospital and expected deaths: In England and Wales, the attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is scrutinized and countersigned by an independent NHS Medical Examiner before being transmitted directly to the local Register Office [1]. In Scotland, the attending physician issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11) [2].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained deaths outside hospital: Call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 for non-emergency medical attendance) so police and medical personnel can attend. Sudden or unexplained deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1][2]. Civil registration and international transfer cannot proceed until the Coroner or Procurator Fiscal issues formal release or an interim certificate of fact of death [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Funeral Directors in Both Countries, and Ukrainian Consular Notification
steps.html:
• Check travel and medical-assistance insurance first: Before entering into an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel, medical, or repatriation insurance, as the insurer's assistance service normally appoints and funds the international repatriation coordinator [3].
  • Appointing licensed funeral providers: If no insurer coordinator applies, appoint a UK funeral director registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) to coordinate preparation and transport with a receiving municipal or licensed funeral service in Ukraine (ритуальна служба - комунальне підприємство або ліцензована похоронна служба, for example in Kyiv, Lviv, or Odesa) [3][5]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation and does not endorse, recommend, or rank individual providers.
  • Notifying Ukrainian consular authorities: Contact the Embassy of Ukraine in the United Kingdom in London (consular phone +44 20 7243 8923, emergency line +44 7553 483 628, email consul_gb@mfa.gov.ua) or the Consulate of Ukraine in Edinburgh for guidance on consular registration and cross-border repatriation requirements [4][5].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom, Apostille, and Ukrainian Civil Registry Recognition
steps.html:
• UK civil death registration: Once medical examiner or coroner/fiscal clearance is issued, register the death at the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or the City of Edinburgh Council Registration Service via National Records of Scotland) within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland [1][2]. Obtain multiple certified copies of the UK Death Certificate.
  • Apostille, translation, and Ukrainian recognition: Because both the United Kingdom and Ukraine are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille on the UK Death Certificate (and any coroner or medical certificates) from the UK Legalisation Office, followed by an official Ukrainian translation certified by a notary or by the Department of Consular Service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine (Департамент консульської служби МЗС України) via the Embassy of Ukraine in the United Kingdom [4][5][6]. For deaths registered in Ukraine or requiring registry updates, the civil registry departments of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine (відділ державної реєстрації актів цивільного стану - ДРАЦС Міністерства юстиції України, accessible via ЦНАП or the Diia portal - портал Дія, where domestic deaths are registered within 3 days) issue the Ukrainian death certificate (свідоцтво про смерть) and registry extract for funeral benefits (витяг для допомоги на поховання) [7].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Ukraine Versus Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body: Your UK funeral director embalms the body, seals it in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin (оцинкована герметична труна), obtains a public health sanitary/non-infectious disease certificate (довідка санітарно-епідеміологічної служби / Держпродспоживслужба equivalent for border sanitary-epidemiological clearance), and secures an Out-of-England Order (Form 104) from the Coroner in England and Wales (or clearance from the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service in Scotland) [1][2][5]. All UK certificates must carry a UK Legalisation Office Apostille and certified Ukrainian translation, and the Embassy of Ukraine in the United Kingdom inspects and seals the transport documentation for entry across the Ukrainian state border [4][5][6].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the cremated remains are placed in a sealed urn/capsule (капсула з прахом) accompanied by the apostilled and translated UK Death Certificate, Certificate of Cremation, and certificate confirming the urn contains only cremated human ashes [5][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: During UK registration, the registrar issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the Green Form in England and Wales, or Form 14 in Scotland) so a local funeral can proceed [1][2].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• United Kingdom notifications, benefits, and probate: When registering the death at the Register Office, request a Tell Us Once reference number (valid for 28 days) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office, DVLA, and local councils in one step [8]. Eligible surviving partners may claim Bereavement Support Payment or survivor pension entitlements through the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service phone +44 800 151 2012, or via the International Pension Centre) [9][10]. To administer UK bank accounts or property held in the deceased's sole name, apply for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland [2][11].
  • Ukraine funeral grant, survivor pension, and inheritance: In Ukraine, the person who arranged the burial or eligible dependents can apply to any service centre or the electronic portal of the Pension Fund of Ukraine (Пенсійний фонд України - ПФУ) for the pensioner funeral grant (допомога на поховання) and survivor pension (пенсія у зв'язку з втратою годувальника) [12][13]. To claim assets or real estate in Ukraine, heirs must submit an application to open an inheritance case (відкриття спадкової справи) with a Ukrainian public or private notary (registered in the Inheritance Register - Спадковий реєстр Міністерства юстиції України and coordinated via the Notary Chamber of Ukraine - Нотаріальна палата України) within 6 months from the date of death; heirs residing in the United Kingdom can sign the inheritance acceptance statement before a consul at the Embassy of Ukraine in the United Kingdom and mail it to a notary in Ukraine [4][13][14].

closingQuestion: To help tailor this guidance further: 1. In which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) did the death occur, and has the Medical Examiner or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal issued clearance? 2. Are you planning to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to Ukraine, or arrange a local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Mexico: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Mexico: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Mexico, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Mexico.
introHtml: When your family member with citizenship or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in Mexico, it is necessary to coordinate Mexican medical certification, civil registration, and sanitary permits with British consular, funeral, and probate procedures. Below are the 5 official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Public Prosecutor Clearance in Mexico
steps.html:
• Death from natural causes in a hospital or clinic: The attending medical staff issues the Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción) free of charge on the official form of the Ministry of Health (Secretaría de Salud) [3].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call the national emergency number 911. If there is no attending physician able to certify a natural cause of death, or if the death is sudden, accidental, or violent, the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público) of the relevant State Attorney General's Office (Fiscalía General de Justicia estatal, for example in Mexico City, Quintana Roo, or Jalisco) and the Forensic Medical Service (Servicio Médico Forense - SEMEFO) must intervene to perform a statutory autopsy (necropsia de ley) before releasing the body and authorising the Medical Certificate of Death [1][3].
  • Statutory sanitary timeframe: Under Mexico's General Health Law (Ley General de Salud), burial, cremation, or embalming must generally take place between 12 and 48 hours following death, unless otherwise ordered by judicial or health authorities [3][6].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Agencies, and British Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance: Before hiring funeral services privately, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, international medical assistance, or bank card coverage, as the insurer typically appoints and funds the coordinating funeral directors in both countries directly [1][2].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Mexico and the United Kingdom: If no insurer is involved, appoint a Mexican funeral agency (agencia funeraria) licensed by the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (COFEPRIS, Federal Commission for the Protection against Sanitary Risk) and state health authorities, coordinated with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom affiliated with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][4][6]. These official directories serve as public orientation examples; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • British consular contact: Notify the British Embassy Mexico City (telephone +52 55 1670 3200) or the 24-hour consular assistance line of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) to receive consular guidance and an informational list of English-speaking local funeral directors [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Mexico, Apostille, and Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Mexican civil death certificate and local permit: With the Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción) - and the release order (oficio de liberación) from the Ministerio Público where applicable - the local funeral agency or next of kin registers the death at the local Civil Registry office (Oficialía or Juzgado del Registro Civil) of the municipality or borough (alcaldía) where the death occurred to obtain the official Death Certificate (Acta de Defunción) and the Burial, Cremation, or Transit Permit (Permiso de Inhumación, Cremación o Traslado) [1][3].
  • Apostille, SRE guidance, and recognition in the United Kingdom: For the Mexican Acta de Defunción to have full legal effect in the United Kingdom, request a Hague Apostille (Apostilla de La Haya) from the State Ministry of Government (Secretaría de Gobierno) of the Mexican federal state where the certificate was issued (while the Federal Ministry of the Interior, Secretaría de Gobernación - SEGOB, apostilles federal documents and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores - SRE, sets consular transit rules) [5][7], accompanied by a certified English translation [1]. A death occurring outside the United Kingdom does not require re-registration within the domestic 5-day deadline at a local Register Office (England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or 8-day deadline at National Records of Scotland, as UK authorities accept the apostilled and translated foreign death certificate in accordance with Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office consular guidance [1][8][9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Mexico
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body to the United Kingdom: The Mexican funeral agency arranges mandatory embalming, placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered metal liner (féretro hermético), a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious disease, and the international sanitary transit permit (permiso sanitario de traslado internacional de cadáveres) from the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (COFEPRIS) or the state health ministry (Secretaría de Salud estatal) [6][7]. Upon arrival in the United Kingdom, the British funeral director obtains burial or cremation clearance through the Coroner in England and Wales (where Coroner oversight and Form 104 / an Out-of-England Order govern cross-border transfers) or through review by the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) via National Records of Scotland in Scotland [1][8][9].
  • International transport of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in Mexico, cremated ashes are treated as inert material and are transported in a sealed urn accompanied by the Acta de Defunción, the official cremation certificate, and their certified English translations [1][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in Mexico: Local burial or cremation is carried out under the permit issued by the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) and municipal health authority; if the Ministerio Público intervened in the death, cremation requires explicit authorisation from the prosecutor's office (fiscalía) [1][3].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• Notifications, pensions, and probate (Probate / Confirmation) in the United Kingdom: If the deceased was ordinarily resident in England, Wales, or Scotland, use the government Tell Us Once service (within 28 days of obtaining the reference number) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office (to cancel the British passport), the DVLA, and the local council simultaneously [1][10]. Eligible survivors can claim Bereavement Support Payment or state pension entitlements from the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service, telephone +44 800 151 2012, or via the International Pension Centre) [11][12]. To administer UK bank accounts, investments, or property, the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or judicial Confirmation in Scotland [9][13].
  • Social security benefits and succession in Mexico: If the deceased contributed to Mexican social security or held assets in Mexico, beneficiaries may claim the funeral expense grant (ayuda para gastos de funeral) and survivor pensions (pensión de viudez/orfandad) from the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS, Mexican Social Security Institute) or ISSSTE, as well as retirement funds held in an AFORE (Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro - SAR) [14]. For assets located in Mexico, heirs or executors initiate testate or intestate succession (sucesión testamentaria o intestamentaria) before a Mexican civil-law notary (notaría pública - with a prior search of the National Register of Notices of Wills, Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento - RENAT, under the Secretaría de Gobernación, and guidance from the Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano) or before the competent family court (juzgado familiar) [5].

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre México y Reino Unido: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre México y Reino Unido: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Cuando su familiar con ciudadanía o vínculos de residencia en el Reino Unido fallece en México, es necesario coordinar la certificación médica, el registro civil y los permisos sanitarios mexicanos con las gestiones consulares, funerarias y sucesorias británicas. A continuación se presentan los 5 pasos oficiales en orden.

steps.title: Certificación Médica de Defunción e Intervención del Ministerio Público en México
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento por causas naturales en hospital o clínica: El personal médico tratante expide sin costo el Certificado Médico de Defunción en el formato oficial de la Secretaría de Salud [3].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Llame de inmediato al número nacional de emergencias 911. Si no existe médico tratante que certifique una causa natural o si el deceso es súbito, accidental o violento, deben intervenir el Ministerio Público de la Fiscalía General de Justicia estatal correspondiente (por ejemplo, en la Ciudad de México, Quintana Roo o Jalisco) y el Servicio Médico Forense (SEMEFO) para practicar la necropsia de ley antes de liberar el cuerpo y autorizar el Certificado Médico de Defunción [1][3].
  • Plazo sanitario legal: Conforme a la Ley General de Salud de México, la inhumación, cremación o embalsamamiento debe realizarse generalmente entre las 12 y las 48 horas siguientes al fallecimiento, salvo orden expresa de las autoridades judiciales o sanitarias [3][6].

steps.title: Seguro de Repatriación, Agencias Funerarias Autorizadas y Asistencia Consular Británica
steps.html:
• Verificación del seguro de viaje o repatriación: Antes de contratar servicios funerarios por cuenta propia, verifique si la persona fallecida contaba con seguro de viaje, asistencia médica internacional o cobertura por tarjeta bancaria, ya que la aseguradora suele designar y financiar directamente a las funerarias coordinadoras en ambos países [1][2].
  • Designación de agencias funerarias en México y en el Reino Unido: Si no interviene una aseguradora, contrate en México una agencia funeraria autorizada ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (COFEPRIS) y las autoridades sanitarias estatales, coordinada con una funeraria receptora en el Reino Unido afiliada a la National Association of Funeral Directors o a la National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][4][6]. Clarvia facilita información de directorios oficiales a título orientativo y no respalda, recomienda ni clasifica a proveedores concretos.
  • Contacto consular británico: Notifique el deceso a la British Embassy Mexico City (teléfono +52 55 1670 3200) o a la línea de asistencia consular de 24 horas del Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office en Londres (+44 20 7008 5000) para recibir orientación consular y el listado informativo de funerarias locales que atienden en inglés [1][2].

steps.title: Inscripción de la Defunción en el Registro Civil en México, Apostilla y Reconocimiento en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
• Acta de Defunción y permiso local en México: Con el Certificado Médico de Defunción (y el oficio de liberación del Ministerio Público cuando proceda), la funeraria local o los familiares tramitan ante la Oficialía o Juzgado del Registro Civil del municipio o alcaldía del lugar del fallecimiento el Acta de Defunción oficial y el Permiso de Inhumación, Cremación o Traslado [1][3].
  • Apostilla, orientación de la SRE y reconocimiento en el Reino Unido: Para que el Acta de Defunción mexicana surta plenos efectos legales en el Reino Unido, solicite la Apostilla de La Haya ante la Secretaría de Gobierno de la entidad federativa mexicana donde se expidió el acta (mientras que la Secretaría de Gobernación apostilla documentos federales y la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores regula las normas consulares de traslado) [5][7], acompañada de una traducción certificada al inglés [1]. Un fallecimiento ocurrido fuera del Reino Unido no exige reinscripción dentro del plazo interno de 5 días ante el Register Office local (Inglaterra, Gales e Irlanda del Norte) ni de 8 días ante National Records of Scotland (Escocia), ya que las autoridades británicas aceptan el Acta de Defunción extranjera apostillada y traducida, conforme a la guía consular del Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [1][8][9].

steps.title: Repatriación Internacional al Reino Unido frente a Inhumación o Cremación Local en México
steps.html:
• Repatriación internacional del cuerpo al Reino Unido: La funeraria mexicana gestiona el embalsamamiento obligatorio, el encajonamiento en féretro hermético con caja metálica sellada, el certificado médico de no padecimiento de enfermedad infectocontagiosa y el permiso sanitario de traslado internacional de cadáveres ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (COFEPRIS) o la autoridad sanitaria estatal [6][7]. A la llegada al Reino Unido, el director funerario británico tramita la autorización de inhumación o cremación con intervención del Coroner en Inglaterra y Gales (donde rige el control del Coroner y el formulario Form 104 / Out-of-England Order para traslados transfronterizos) o la revisión del Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) a través de National Records of Scotland en Escocia [1][8][9].
  • Traslado internacional de cenizas: Si se opta por la cremación en México, las cenizas se consideran material inerte y se transportan en una urna sellada acompañada del Acta de Defunción, el certificado oficial de cremación y sus traducciones al inglés [1][7].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en México: Se realiza mediante el permiso expedido por el Registro Civil y la autoridad sanitaria municipal; en caso de intervención previa del Ministerio Público, la cremación requiere autorización expresa de la fiscalía [1][3].

steps.title: Notificaciones Posteriores, Pensiones de Sobrevivencia, Impuestos y Sucesiones en Ambos Países
steps.html:
• Trámites, pensiones y sucesión (Probate / Confirmation) en el Reino Unido: Si la persona fallecida residía habitualmente en Inglaterra, Gales o Escocia, utilice el servicio gubernamental Tell Us Once (dentro de los 28 días posteriores a la obtención del número de referencia) para notificar simultáneamente a HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), al Department for Work and Pensions, a HM Passport Office (para cancelar el pasaporte británico), a la DVLA y al ayuntamiento local [1][10]. Las personas sobrevivientes con derecho pueden solicitar el Bereavement Support Payment o prestaciones de pensión estatal ante el Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service, teléfono +44 800 151 2012, o a través del International Pension Centre) [11][12]. Para administrar cuentas bancarias, inversiones o inmuebles en el Reino Unido, la persona albacea o administradora solicita el Grant of Probate (o Letters of Administration) en Inglaterra y Gales, o la Confirmation judicial en Escocia [9][13].
  • Prestaciones de seguridad social y sucesión en México: Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o poseía bienes en México, las personas beneficiarias pueden reclamar la ayuda para gastos de funeral y las pensiones de sobrevivencia ante el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) o el ISSSTE, así como la recuperación de recursos de retiro en la AFORE (SAR) [14]. Para bienes ubicados en México, las personas herederas o albaceas inician la sucesión testamentaria o intestamentaria ante una notaría pública (con consulta previa al Registro Nacional de Avisos de Testamento - RENAT de la Secretaría de Gobernación y orientación del Colegio Nacional del Notariado Mexicano) o ante el juzgado familiar competente [5].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Morocco: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Morocco: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Morocco: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Morocco, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Morocco.
introHtml: When your family member with British nationality or residence ties to the United Kingdom dies in Morocco, you will need to coordinate Moroccan medical, municipal, and prefectural formalities with consular, funeral, and probate procedures in the United Kingdom. Below are the 5 official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Judicial or Sanitary Clearance in Morocco
steps.html:
• Death in a clinic or hospital: The attending hospital physician issues the medical certificate of death (certificat médical de constatation de décès), specifying whether the death was due to natural and non-contagious causes [1][5].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately contact the emergency services in Morocco (SAMU 141, Police 19 in urban areas, or Royal Gendarmerie / Gendarmerie Royale 177 outside urban areas). A physician from the Municipal Hygiene Office (Bureau municipal d'hygiène - BMH) of the municipality or district (for example in Casablanca, Marrakesh, Rabat, or Tangier) attends the scene to certify the death and issue the medical certificate [1][5]. In the event of a sudden, suspicious, accidental, or non-natural death, a police or gendarmerie investigation is opened and authorisation from the King's Prosecutor (procureur du Roi) at the competent court (often following a medico-legal autopsy) is required before the body can be released, buried, or repatriated [1].

steps.title: Repatriation Insurance, Licensed Funeral Directors, and British Consular Assistance
steps.html:
• Checking travel or repatriation insurance: Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, international medical assistance, or bank card coverage; the assistance company generally appoints and funds the funeral operators in both countries directly [1][3].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Morocco and the United Kingdom: If no coordinating insurer is involved, appoint a licensed international funeral and mortuary transport company in Morocco (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée), working in coordination with a receiving funeral director in the United Kingdom affiliated with the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][4]. These official directories serve as public orientation examples; Clarvia does not recommend, endorse, or rank individual providers.
  • British consular contact: Notify the British Embassy Rabat (telephone +212 537 63 33 33) or the 24-hour consular assistance centre of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) to obtain the official bereavement information pack for Morocco and a list of English- and French-speaking local funeral directors [1][2].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Morocco, Apostille, and Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
• Registration with the Civil Registry Office in Morocco: Presenting the medical certificate of death (and, where applicable, the permit from the procureur du Roi), the family or funeral company registers the death with the Civil Registry Office (Bureau de l'état civil) of the municipality where the death occurred in Morocco, following the procedures set out on the Portail national de l'État civil (National Civil Registry Portal, alhalalmadania.ma) and the consular portal (consulat.ma), in order to obtain full copies (copies intégrales) and official extracts of the death certificate (acte de décès) [1][5][6].
  • Apostille, translation, and recognition in the United Kingdom: Because the Moroccan death certificate is issued in Arabic or French, obtain a Hague Apostille (Apostille de La Haye) from the competent Moroccan authority (court of first instance or authorised local authority) and arrange a certified English translation [1][7]. A death occurring outside the United Kingdom is not subject to mandatory domestic registration within 5 days at a local Register Office (England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or 8 days at National Records of Scotland; the apostilled Moroccan death certificate accompanied by a certified English translation is recognised by UK authorities in accordance with Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office guidance [1][8][9].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial in Morocco
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body to the United Kingdom: The Moroccan funeral director compiles the death certificate (acte de décès), medical certificate of non-contagion (certificat médical de non-contagion), embalming certificate (certificat de soins de conservation / thanatopraxie), official report of coffining in a hermetically sealed coffin with a zinc-lined metal insert (procès-verbal de mise en bière en cercueil hermétique) supervised by the Municipal Hygiene Office (BMH), and the body transfer authorisation (autorisation de transfert de corps) and mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) issued by the prefectural or provincial authorities and Ministry of Health services [1][6]. Upon arrival in the United Kingdom, the British funeral director completes clearance formalities with the Coroner in England and Wales (where Coroner authorisation and Form 104 / an Out-of-England Order govern cross-border transfers and burial or cremation clearance) or with the Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) via National Records of Scotland in Scotland [1][8][9].
  • Local burial and rules regarding cremation: Local burial in Morocco can be arranged promptly once the municipal burial permit (permis d'inhumer) is issued; however, as Morocco generally does not have an operating crematorium, cremation in practice requires prior repatriation of the body to the United Kingdom or another country with licensed cremation facilities [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
• Administrative notifications, benefits, and probate (Probate / Confirmation) in the United Kingdom: If the deceased was ordinarily resident in England, Wales, or Scotland, use the government Tell Us Once service (within 28 days of obtaining the reference number) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office (to cancel the British passport), the DVLA, and local council services simultaneously [1][10]. Eligible surviving partners can claim Bereavement Support Payment or pension entitlements from the Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service on +44 800 151 2012, or via the International Pension Centre) [11][12]. To unfreeze bank accounts or administer assets located in the United Kingdom, the executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or Confirmation before the Sheriff Court in Scotland [9][13].
  • Social security benefits and estate settlement in Morocco: If the deceased was affiliated with a Moroccan social security scheme or held assets in Morocco, eligible beneficiaries may claim the death grant (allocation au décès) and survivor pension (pension de survivants - which should be filed within 12 months of death to preserve retroactive payment from the date of death) from the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS, National Social Security Fund; call centre 3939 or +212 80 20 30 100) or the Moroccan Pension Fund (Caisse Marocaine des Retraites - CMR) for the public sector [14][15]. Freezing and settling Moroccan bank accounts and administering estate assets located in Morocco are carried out before a Moroccan notary (notaire) or Islamic legal officiants (adoul) according to the applicable succession law [1][5].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these procedures to your situation, in which city or province of Morocco did the death occur, has the medical certificate of death (or authorisation from the procureur du Roi) already been issued, and are you planning international repatriation of the remains to the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) or a local burial in Morocco?
