fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre Maroc et Royaume-Uni : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre Maroc et Royaume-Uni : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml: Lorsque votre proche ayant la nationalité britannique ou des liens de résidence avec le Royaume-Uni décède au Maroc, il convient de coordonner les formalités médicales, communales et préfectorales marocaines avec les démarches consulaires, funéraires et successorales au Royaume-Uni. Voici les 5 grandes étapes officielles dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Constatation Médicale du Décès et Autorisation Judiciaire ou Sanitaire au Maroc
steps.html:
• Décès en clinique ou à l'hôpital : Le médecin traitant de l'établissement hospitalier établit le certificat médical de constatation de décès précisant si la mort est de cause naturelle et non contagieuse [1][5].
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Contactez immédiatement les services d'urgence au Maroc (SAMU 141, Police 19 en zone urbaine ou Gendarmerie Royale 177 hors agglomération). Le médecin du Bureau municipal d'hygiène (BMH) de la commune ou de l'arrondissement (par exemple à Casablanca, Marrakech, Rabat ou Tanger) se déplace pour constater le décès et délivrer le certificat médical [1][5]. En cas de mort subite, suspecte, accidentelle ou non naturelle, une enquête de police ou de gendarmerie est ouverte et l'autorisation du procureur du Roi près le tribunal compétent (souvent après autopsie médico-légale) est indispensable avant toute levée du corps, inhumation ou rapatriement [1].

steps.title: Assurance Rapatriement, Opérateurs Funéraires Agréés et Assistance Consulaire Britannique
steps.html:
• Vérification de l'assurance voyage ou rapatriement : Avant de signer un contrat funéraire à titre individuel, vérifiez si la personne décédée bénéficiait d'une assurance voyage, d'une assistance médicale internationale ou d'une garantie liée à une carte bancaire ; la compagnie d'assistance mandate et finance généralement directement les opérateurs funéraires dans les deux pays [1][3].
  • Mandatement des pompes funèbres au Maroc et au Royaume-Uni : En l'absence d'assureur coordinateur, mandatez une société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc, qui travaillera en coordination avec une entreprise funéraire réceptrice au Royaume-Uni affiliée à la National Association of Funeral Directors ou à la National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [1][4]. Clarvia mentionne ces répertoires officiels à titre purement informatif et ne cautionne, ne conseille ni ne classe aucun prestataire.
  • Contact consulaire britannique : Informez la British Embassy Rabat (téléphone +212 537 63 33 33) ou le centre d'assistance consulaire 24h/24 du Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office à Londres (+44 20 7008 5000) pour obtenir le guide officiel en cas de décès au Maroc ainsi que la liste des entreprises de pompes funèbres locales anglophones et francophones [1][2].

steps.title: Déclaration du Décès à l'État Civil au Maroc, Apostille et Reconnaissance au Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
• Déclaration auprès du Bureau de l'état civil au Maroc : Munie du certificat médical de décès (et, le cas échéant, du permis du procureur du Roi), la famille ou l'entreprise de pompes funèbres déclare le décès auprès du Bureau de l'état civil de la commune du lieu de décès au Maroc, conformément aux procédures centralisées sur le Portail national de l'État civil (alhalalmadania.ma) et le portail consulaire (consulat.ma), afin d'obtenir des copies intégrales et extraits de l'acte de décès [1][5][6].
  • Apostille, traduction et reconnaissance au Royaume-Uni : L'acte de décès marocain étant rédigé en arabe ou en français, faites apposer l'Apostille de La Haye par les autorités marocaines compétentes (tribunal de première instance ou autorité locale habilitée) et faites établir une traduction certifiée en anglais [1][7]. Un décès survenu hors du Royaume-Uni ne fait pas l'objet d'une déclaration obligatoire dans le délai national de 5 jours auprès d'un Register Office local (Angleterre, Pays de Galles et Irlande du Nord) ou de 8 jours auprès de National Records of Scotland (Écosse) ; l'acte de décès marocain apostillé et traduit en anglais est reconnu par les administrations britanniques, selon les directives du Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office [1][8][9].

steps.title: Rapatriement International vers le Royaume-Uni ou Inhumation Locale au Maroc
steps.html:
• Rapatriement international du corps vers le Royaume-Uni : L'entreprise de pompes funèbres marocaine réunit l'acte de décès, le certificat médical de non-contagion, le certificat de soins de conservation (thanatopraxie), le procès-verbal de mise en bière en cercueil hermétique muni d'un caisson métallique zingué établi sous le contrôle du Bureau municipal d'hygiène (BMH), ainsi que l'autorisation de transfert de corps et le laissez-passer mortuaire délivrés par les autorités préfectorales ou provinciales et les services du ministère de la Santé [1][6]. À l'arrivée au Royaume-Uni, l'entreprise funéraire britannique accomplit les formalités auprès du Coroner en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles (où l'autorisation du Coroner et le formulaire Form 104 / Out-of-England Order régissent les mouvements transfrontaliers et l'autorisation de crémation ou d'inhumation) ou auprès du Healthcare Improvement Scotland Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) via National Records of Scotland en Écosse [1][8][9].
  • Inhumation locale et règles relatives à la crémation : Une inhumation locale au Maroc peut être organisée rapidement après délivrance du permis d'inhumer communal ; en revanche, le Maroc ne disposant généralement pas de crématorium en activité, la crémation nécessite en pratique le rapatriement préalable du corps vers le Royaume-Uni ou un autre pays disposant d'installations autorisées [1].

steps.title: Notifications Administratives, Pensions de Survivants, Fiscalité et Règlement de la Succession
steps.html:
• Démarches administratives, prestations et succession (Probate / Confirmation) au Royaume-Uni : Si la personne décédée résidait habituellement en Angleterre, au Pays de Galles ou en Écosse, utilisez le service public Tell Us Once (dans les 28 jours suivant l'obtention du numéro de référence) pour notifier simultanément HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), le Department for Work and Pensions, HM Passport Office (pour annuler le passeport britannique), la DVLA et les services municipaux [1][10]. Les partenaires survivants éligibles peuvent demander le Bereavement Support Payment ou les droits à pension auprès du Department for Work and Pensions (Bereavement Service au +44 800 151 2012, ou via l'International Pension Centre) [11][12]. Pour débloquer les comptes bancaires ou gérer les biens situés au Royaume-Uni, l'exécuteur ou l'administrateur sollicite un Grant of Probate (ou Letters of Administration) en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles, ou une Confirmation auprès du Sheriff Court en Écosse [9][13].
  • Prestations sociales et règlement de la succession au Maroc : Si la personne décédée était affiliée à un régime marocain ou détenait des biens au Maroc, les ayants droit peuvent solliciter l'allocation au décès et la pension de survivants (qu'il est conseillé de déposer dans un délai de 12 mois suivant le décès pour conserver l'effet rétroactif au jour du décès) auprès de la Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (centre d'appel 3939 ou +212 80 20 30 100) ou de la Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR) pour le secteur public [14][15]. Le blocage et le règlement des comptes bancaires ainsi que la dévolution successorale des biens situés au Maroc s'effectuent devant un notaire marocain ou des adoul selon le statut successoral applicable [1][5].

fr.closingQuestion: Pour nous permettre de préciser ces démarches selon votre situation : 1. Dans quelle ville ou province du Maroc le décès est-il survenu, et le certificat médical de décès (ou l'autorisation du procureur du Roi) a-t-il déjà été délivré ? 2. Envisagez-vous un rapatriement de la dépouille vers le Royaume-Uni (Angleterre, Pays de Galles, Écosse ou Irlande du Nord) ou une inhumation locale au Maroc ?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Egypt: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Egypt: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Egypt: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Egypt, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Egypt.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in Egypt, local medical certification, prosecutorial clearance, and civil registration in Egypt must be completed before international repatriation or local burial can proceed, alongside consular and post-death administration across both countries [1][2]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Public Prosecution Clearance in Egypt
steps.html:
Before civil registration, funeral arrangements, or international transport can take place, the cause of death must be certified by Egyptian medical and judicial authorities [1][2].

  • Death in a hospital: When a person dies in an Egyptian public or private hospital (for example, in Cairo, Alexandria, Hurghada, Luxor, or Sharm El-Sheikh), the attending physician issues the initial Arabic Medical Death Notification, recording the time and medical cause of death [1][2]. Provide the hospital with the deceased's British passport so personal details are transcribed accurately [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital: If the death occurs at a hotel, residence, or public place, call the Egyptian Ambulance Service on 123 and the Police on 122 (or Tourist Police on 126) immediately [1]. Do not move the body before authorities arrive. A medical inspector from the local Health Office (Maktab El-Seha, under the Ministry of Health and Population) examines the deceased, and the police refer the case to the Public Prosecution (El-Niyaba El-Amma) [1][2]. For any foreign national who dies in Egypt, the Public Prosecution reviews the circumstances, determines whether a forensic examination is required, and issues a mandatory Public Prosecution No-Objection Permit before the body can be released for burial or repatriation [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Funeral Directors in Egypt and the UK, and Consular Support
steps.html:
Check immediately whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance [1][2]. If covered, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team before signing any independent local contract, as the insurer normally appoints the Egyptian and UK repatriation coordinators directly and pays eligible costs [1][2].

  • Notifying the British Embassy in Egypt: Report the death to the British Embassy Cairo (+20 2 2791 6000) or the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) [1][3]. Consular staff cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses, but they provide the official Egypt bereavement pack, share lists of English-speaking international funeral operators and lawyers in Cairo, Alexandria, Hurghada, and Sharm El-Sheikh, cancel the deceased's British passport, and issue the consular mortuary documentation required by Egyptian authorities [1][2][3].
  • Appointing funeral coordinators in Egypt and the United Kingdom: In Egypt, families or insurers mandate a licensed international mortuary and repatriation operator in the governorate of death to handle Health Office filings, Ministry of Health embalming, and Cairo Airport Cargo Village quarantine formalities [1][2]. To receive the deceased in the United Kingdom, appoint an accredited UK funeral director through the National Association of Funeral Directors (+44 121 711 1343, info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (+44 1279 726777, info@saif.org.uk) [4][5]. These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Egypt and Document Recognition for the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Every death in Egypt must be reported to the local Health Office (Maktab El-Seha) in the district where the death occurred within 24 hours [1][2].

  • Egyptian Death Certificate and Civil Status Organization: Your appointed Egyptian funeral coordinator (or an authorized representative holding Power of Attorney) submits the hospital Medical Death Notification, the Public Prosecution release, and the deceased's passport to the local Health Office, which registers the death and issues the initial Arabic death certificate and burial/transfer permit [1][2]. Once recorded, obtain multiple official computerised copies of the Egyptian Death Certificate from the Civil Status Organization (الأحوال المدنية under the Ministry of Interior) [1][2].
  • Legalization, translation, and UK recognition: Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention or the Vienna CIEC Form C convention [1]. To use the Egyptian Death Certificate for legal and estate procedures in the United Kingdom, have the computerised certificate authenticated by an Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs ratification office (Maktab Tasdiqat), translated into English by a certified translator, and legalized if required by the British Embassy Cairo or the Consulate General of Egypt in London [1][6]. Deaths that occur within the UK must be registered at a local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland, whereas for a death in Egypt the translated Egyptian Death Certificate is accepted directly by UK banks, pension bodies, and probate courts (you may also apply for an optional UK overseas consular death registration via the FCDO if the deceased was a British national) [1][7].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial in Egypt
steps.html:
Your family and funeral coordinators will arrange either international repatriation to the United Kingdom or local burial in Egypt [1][2].

  • Repatriating the body to the United Kingdom: To export human remains from Egypt, the Egyptian repatriation operator obtains five mandatory clearances: (1) the official Egyptian Death Certificate from the Health Office and Civil Status Organization, (2) the Public Prosecution (Niyaba) no-objection permit for repatriation, (3) an official Embalming Certificate and Hermetic Coffin Sealing Certificate from the Ministry of Health and Population confirming the body is placed in a zinc-lined, hermetically sealed casket free of infectious disease, (4) a Consular Mortuary / No-Objection Certificate from the British Embassy Cairo, and (5) final Airport Quarantine clearance at Cairo International Airport (or Hurghada/Sharm El-Sheikh airport) [1][2].
  • Clearance upon arrival in the United Kingdom: When repatriated human remains arrive in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director presents the translated Egyptian Death Certificate and mortuary certificates to HM Customs and notifies the local Coroner, who issues a Coroner's Certificate for burial or cremation (and a Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104 would apply if remains were ever removed out of England and Wales) [1][7]. If the destination is in Scotland, before repatriated remains from abroad can be buried or cremated, the receiving Scottish funeral director must submit the foreign death documents to Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) for statutory verification [8].
  • Local burial or cremation in Egypt: Local burial in Egypt takes place in a designated cemetery according to religious or community plot arrangements once the Health Office and Public Prosecution issue the burial permit [1][2]. Public crematoria are extremely limited in Egypt, so families wishing for cremation normally repatriate the deceased to the United Kingdom [1].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Tax, and Probate in the UK and Egypt
steps.html:
Once you hold the official Death Certificate and certified English translation, complete benefits, tax, and estate administration in both countries.

  • UK notifications, pensions, and Tell Us Once: If your family member normally lived in England, Scotland, or Wales and died while temporarily in Egypt, contact the Tell Us Once service via the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (0800 151 2012) to notify HM Revenue & Customs, HM Passport Office, DVLA, local councils, and state benefit offices in a single step [9]. If your family member lived permanently outside the UK, contact the International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777) to report the death, stop UK State Pension payments, and inquire about Bereavement Support Payment eligibility [10].
  • UK Probate or Confirmation: To administer UK bank accounts, property, or investments above institutional thresholds, the executor or entitled administrator reports the estate value and any Inheritance Tax (Form IHT400) to HM Revenue & Customs (+44 300 123 1072) and applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, or Confirmation through the Sheriff Court in Scotland, via HM Courts & Tribunals Service Probate [11][12].
  • Egyptian social insurance and inheritance administration: If your family member worked, resided, or held bank accounts or real estate in Egypt, notify the National Organization for Social Insurance (الهيئة القومية للتأمين الاجتماعي, hotline 16217) regarding any Egyptian social insurance pension, death grant, or funeral expenses grant [13]. To release Egyptian bank balances or transfer property in Egypt, heirs must apply to the competent Egyptian Family Court (Mahkamat El-Osra) for an official Inheritance Declaration (I'lam El-Waratha / إعلام الوراثة) or have an English Grant of Probate legalized through the FCDO, the Consulate General of Egypt in London, and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular sector for local enforcement [1][6].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation: 1. In which city or governorate in Egypt did the death occur, and which UK nation (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) is the destination or place of residence? 2. Have you decided between repatriating your family member to the United Kingdom or arranging local burial in Egypt, and is there travel insurance in place?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Singapore: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in Singapore: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in Singapore: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Singapore, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and Singapore.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. Singapore operates a digital system for medical death certification, automatic civil death registration, and Port Health export clearances, which must be coordinated with British consular guidance and UK funeral, pension, tax, and probate procedures [1][2][3]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner Clearance in Singapore
steps.html:
Before funeral arrangements, cremation, burial, or international repatriation can proceed, a registered medical practitioner or the State Coroner must digitally certify the cause of death in Singapore [2][3].

  • Death in a hospital or expected natural death at home: When a person dies in a public or private hospital in Singapore (such as Singapore General Hospital, Tan Tock Seng Hospital, or National University Hospital), the attending ward doctor examines the body and digitally issues the Certificate of Cause of Death (CCOD) online [2][3]. If a natural death occurs at a residence or hotel and a regular or house-call doctor can confirm a natural cause of death, the doctor certifies the digital CCOD on site (have the deceased's British passport and Singapore FIN/NRIC card ready) [3].
  • Sudden, unnatural, or unattended death outside a hospital: If the death is sudden, accidental, or the doctor cannot determine the cause of death, call the Singapore Police Force on 999 (or emergency ambulance on 995) [2][3]. The police arrange for the Police Hearse to transfer the deceased to the Health Sciences Authority Forensic Medicine Division (Mortuary@HSA, located at Block 9, Singapore General Hospital, Outram Road, phone +65 6222 1712) [3][4]. The next of kin attend Mortuary@HSA the following morning with the deceased's and their own passports so the State Coroner can review the case, decide whether an autopsy or Coroner's Inquiry is required, and issue the digital CCOD and body release order [2][3][4].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Licensed Funeral Directors, and British Consular Support
steps.html:
Check immediately whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance [1][2]. Contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance centre before signing any independent local contract, as the insurer normally appoints the Singapore and UK funeral coordinators directly and covers eligible repatriation or local funeral costs [1][2].

  • Notifying the British High Commission in Singapore: Report the death to the British High Commission Singapore (+65 6424 4200) or the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) [1][2][5]. Consular staff provide the official Singapore bereavement guidance, supply a list of international funeral directors in Singapore, cancel the deceased's British passport, and liaise with local authorities where required [1][2][5].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Singapore and the United Kingdom: In Singapore, you can locate a licensed funeral director experienced in international repatriation or local wakes through the Association of Funeral Directors Singapore (email: secretariat@afd.org.sg) [6]. For local cremation or burial in Singapore, your funeral director books a cremation slot at Mandai Crematorium or a burial plot at Choa Chu Kang Cemetery via the National Environment Agency (+65 6225 5632) [3]. If repatriating the deceased to the United Kingdom, also appoint a receiving UK funeral director via the National Association of Funeral Directors (+44 121 711 1343, info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [7]. These directories are provided as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Digital Death Registration in Singapore and Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Physical visits to a registration counter are no longer required to register a death in Singapore [3][8].

  • Automatic ICA registration and 30-day download deadline: Once the hospital doctor or Coroner certifies the CCOD digitally, the death is registered automatically within 24 hours with the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority [8][9]. The next of kin (or authorized funeral director) must download the official Digital Death Certificate from the MyLegacy@LifeSG portal within 30 days of certification using the Death Document Number, the deceased's FIN/NRIC or British passport number, and the date of death [8][9]. Save and print multiple copies immediately, as retrieving a Death Extract from ICA after 30 days requires a formal application and fee [8][9].
  • Apostille and recognition in the United Kingdom: Singapore's Digital Death Certificate is issued in English [2][8]. Both Singapore and the United Kingdom are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply in Singapore). Where a UK probate court, bank, or foreign institution requires legalized authentication, apply online for a Hague Apostille through the Singapore Academy of Law legalisation portal [10]. While deaths occurring inside the UK must be registered at a local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland, a death in Singapore does not need to be re-registered at a local UK Register Office for the Singapore Death Certificate to be valid in the UK (though families of British nationals may optionally apply for an overseas consular death registration via the FCDO) [1][2].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Singapore
steps.html:
Your family can choose between repatriating the body or cremated ashes to the United Kingdom or holding a local funeral in Singapore [2][3][11].

  • Repatriating human remains (casket) from Singapore to the UK: To export a body from Singapore, your licensed Singapore funeral director arranges arterial embalming, hermetically seals the deceased in a zinc-lined export coffin, and applies online via the ePortal to the National Environment Agency Port Health Office for a mandatory Coffin (Export) Permit (providing the Digital Death Certificate, CCOD, embalming certificate, coffin sealing certificate, and flight details) [2][11]. Where foreign consular facilitation is involved, the Singapore Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) and the British High Commission Singapore coordinate any required diplomatic or customs clearances [2][11].
  • Clearance upon arrival in the United Kingdom: When repatriated remains arrive in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director clears HM Customs using the Singapore Death Certificate and NEA Coffin Export Permit and notifies the local Coroner to obtain a Coroner's Certificate for burial or cremation (a Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104 is required whenever remains are removed out of England and Wales) [1][2]. In Scotland, before repatriated remains from outside the UK can be buried or cremated, the receiving funeral director submits the Singapore death and export documents to Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) for statutory review [12].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to the United Kingdom: If cremation takes place in Singapore (for example, at Mandai Crematorium), an NEA Coffin Export Permit is not required to take cremated ashes out of Singapore [11]. You may carry the sealed urn in airline hand luggage or ship it via air cargo to the UK accompanied by the official Digital Death Certificate, the Cremation Certificate, and a letter from the crematorium or funeral director [2][11].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Tax, and Probate in the UK and Singapore
steps.html:
Once you hold the Digital Death Certificate, complete benefits, tax, and estate steps in both jurisdictions.

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate: If your family member ordinarily resided in England, Scotland, or Wales and died during a temporary stay in Singapore, call the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (0800 151 2012) to use the Tell Us Once service, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, DVLA, local councils, and UK benefit offices simultaneously, or contact the International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777) if your family member lived permanently abroad [1][13]. For UK estate assets, report the estate and any Inheritance Tax (Form IHT400) to HMRC and apply for a Grant of Probate in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland (or Confirmation via the Sheriff Court in Scotland) [1][13].
  • Singapore CPF, tax clearance, and estate administration: If the deceased held Singapore Permanent Residence, employment passes, bank accounts, or property in Singapore:
    • Central Provident Fund (CPF) and small estates: If the deceased was a CPF member, the Central Provident Fund Board (+65 6227 1188) is notified automatically by ICA and pays nominated CPF savings to beneficiaries, or transfers un-nominated CPF savings to the Public Trustee's Office (1800-225-5529), which can also administer small non-CPF estates in Singapore valued up to SGD 50,000 without a court grant [14].
    • Singapore Courts Probate or Resealing and IRAS tax: For Singapore assets exceeding SGD 50,000, the executor or administrator applies to the Family Justice Courts (+65 6435 5110) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, or applies to the High Court of Singapore to reseal a UK Grant of Probate (as the UK is a Commonwealth jurisdiction eligible for probate resealing in Singapore) [15]. Finally, notify the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (1800-356-8300) to settle final Singapore income tax up to the date of death (Singapore has no estate duty for deaths on or after 15 February 2008) [16].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation: 1. Was your family member visiting Singapore or living and working there as a resident, and which UK nation (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) is their home or destination jurisdiction? 2. Have you decided between repatriating the body to the UK, cremating at Mandai Crematorium in Singapore and bringing the ashes back, or holding a local funeral in Singapore?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of United Kingdom Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of United Kingdom dies in New Zealand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in New Zealand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in United Kingdom and New Zealand.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of the United Kingdom dies in New Zealand, medical certification or coronial release and civil death registration in New Zealand must be completed alongside British consular reporting, international repatriation or local funeral arrangements, and estate administration across both countries [1][2]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coronial Clearance in New Zealand
steps.html:
Before burial, cremation, or international transport from New Zealand can proceed, the cause of death must be certified by a medical practitioner or cleared by the Duty Coroner [2][3][4].

  • Expected or natural death in a hospital, hospice, or under GP care: When a person dies in a hospital (such as Auckland City Hospital, Wellington Regional Hospital, or Christchurch Hospital), hospice, or aged-care facility, or under the regular care of a general practitioner (GP), a doctor or nurse practitioner examines the body and completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form HP4720) via the Ministry of Health Death Documents system [3][4].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death outside a hospital: If the death is sudden, accidental, unexplained, or occurs during travel where no NZ doctor can certify a natural cause of death, call emergency services on 111 immediately [2][3]. New Zealand Police attend and refer the death to the Duty Coroner through Coronial Services of New Zealand and the National Initial Investigation Office (0800 266 800 within New Zealand or +64 4 910 4482 internationally) [3]. When a death is referred to the Coroner, a standard HP4720 is not issued; the Coroner determines whether a post-mortem examination or inquiry is required and signs the formal Coroner's Authorization for Release of the Body so your funeral director can proceed [2][3].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Funeral Directors in New Zealand and the UK, and British Consular Assistance
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance [1][2]. If covered, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team immediately, as they normally appoint the New Zealand and UK funeral coordinators directly and pay eligible repatriation or local funeral costs [1][2].

  • Notifying the British High Commission in New Zealand: Report the death to the British High Commission Wellington (+64 4 924 2888) or the British Consulate General in Auckland, or call the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in London (+44 20 7008 5000) [1][2][5]. Consular staff provide New Zealand bereavement guidance, share lists of local international funeral directors and lawyers, and cancel the deceased's British passport, though they cannot pay funeral or repatriation costs [1][2][5].
  • Appointing funeral directors in New Zealand and the United Kingdom: In New Zealand, families normally mandate a local funeral director to care for the deceased, submit the civil death registration, and manage export permits; you can find an accredited provider through the Funeral Directors Association of New Zealand (+64 4 473 7475, info@funeraldirectors.co.nz) [4][6]. If repatriating your family member to the United Kingdom, coordinate with a receiving UK funeral director registered with the National Association of Funeral Directors (+44 121 711 1343, info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (+44 1279 726777, info@saif.org.uk) [7][8]. These directories are provided as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in New Zealand and Recognition in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Under New Zealand's Births, Deaths, Marriages, and Relationships Registration Act, every death in New Zealand must be registered with Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM, part of the Department of Internal Affairs, phone 0800 22 52 52 from New Zealand or +64 9 339 0852 from overseas) within 3 working days after burial or cremation (or prior to export for international repatriation) [4][9].

  • Official New Zealand Death Certificates: Your appointed New Zealand funeral director collects the family's demographic details and submits the Death Registration (Form BDM 28) online to Births, Deaths and Marriages, ordering multiple official New Zealand Death Certificates (which are issued in English and state the cause of death once coronial findings are complete) [2][4][9]. (Note that MFAT SafeTravel provides consular support when New Zealand citizens die overseas, whereas the Department of Internal Affairs registers all deaths occurring inside New Zealand [9].)
  • Apostille and recognition in the United Kingdom: Both New Zealand and the United Kingdom are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply here). Because New Zealand Death Certificates are issued in English, UK banks, pension bodies, and probate courts generally accept them directly; if a formal legalization stamp is requested for court or overseas property purposes, apply for a Hague Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs Authentication Unit (0800 872 675 or +64 4 460 2221) [10]. While deaths occurring inside the UK must be registered at a local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland or 8 days in Scotland, a death in New Zealand does not need to be re-registered at a local UK Register Office to be valid in the UK (though families of British citizens may optionally apply for an overseas consular death registration via the FCDO) [1][2].

steps.title: International Repatriation to the United Kingdom vs. Local Burial or Cremation in New Zealand
steps.html:
Your family can choose to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to the United Kingdom or arrange a local funeral in New Zealand [2][4].

  • Repatriating human remains (casket) from New Zealand to the UK: Your New Zealand funeral director arranges arterial embalming, places the deceased in a hermetically sealed, zinc-lined export casket, obtains a Public Health Service / Ministry of Health non-infectious disease and embalmment clearance, and completes New Zealand Customs Service export documentation at the departure airport (such as Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch) [2][11].
  • Clearance upon arrival in the United Kingdom: When repatriated human remains arrive in England or Wales, the receiving UK funeral director clears HM Customs with the New Zealand Death Certificate, embalming certificate, and freedom-from-infection certificate, and notifies the local Coroner to obtain a Coroner's Certificate for burial or cremation (a Coroner Out-of-England Order / Form 104 is required whenever remains are removed out of England and Wales) [1][2]. If the destination is in Scotland, before repatriated remains from outside the UK can be buried or cremated, the receiving Scottish funeral director must submit the New Zealand death and mortuary documents to Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) for statutory verification [12].
  • Transporting cremated ashes or holding a local funeral in New Zealand: If cremation takes place in New Zealand (requiring Medical Referee permission on Form B), you may carry the cremated ashes to the United Kingdom in airline hand luggage or ship them via air cargo accompanied by the official New Zealand Death Certificate and Certificate of Cremation, without requiring UK Coroner clearance unless the ashes are scattered or interred under specific local cemetery rules [2][11].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Tax, and Probate in the UK and New Zealand
steps.html:
Once the official Death Certificates are issued, complete benefits, tax, and estate steps across both countries.

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate: If your family member ordinarily lived in England, Scotland, or Wales and died while visiting New Zealand, contact the Tell Us Once service via the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (0800 151 2012) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, DVLA, local councils, and UK benefit offices in one step [13]. If your family member resided permanently in New Zealand, contact the International Pension Centre (+44 191 218 7777) to stop UK State Pension payments and inquire about Bereavement Support Payment [14]. To administer UK estate assets, report the estate and any Inheritance Tax (Form IHT400) to HMRC and apply for a Grant of Probate in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland (or Confirmation in Scotland) via HM Courts & Tribunals Service Probate (or reseal a New Zealand grant of probate in the UK under the Colonial Probates Act) [15].
  • New Zealand notifications, ACC / Work and Income benefits, tax, and probate:
    • Te Hokinga ā-Wairua, Work and Income, and ACC: Use the Te Hokinga ā-Wairua End of Life Service on govt.nz to coordinate New Zealand agency notifications [4]. If the deceased died as a result of an accident in New Zealand (including visitors in many accidental death scenarios), contact the Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC, 0800 101 996) regarding the non-means-tested ACC Funeral Grant and Survivor's Grant; if the deceased was a New Zealand resident or superannuitant, also notify Work and Income (0800 559 009) regarding NZ Superannuation and the means-tested Funeral Grant [4][16].
    • KiwiSaver, Inland Revenue (IRD), and High Court Probate: If the deceased held New Zealand bank accounts, KiwiSaver, or property, notify Inland Revenue (0800 227 774 or +64 4 978 0779) to finalize NZ tax obligations [4]. For sole assets exceeding NZD 15,000 in any single NZ institution or NZ real estate, apply to the High Court of New Zealand (Wellington Probate Registry) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, or apply to reseal a UK Grant of Probate in the High Court of New Zealand [4][9].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation: 1. Did your family member die from natural causes or an accident in New Zealand (which may qualify for ACC accidental death support), and which UK nation is their home or destination jurisdiction? 2. Have you decided between repatriating the body to the UK, cremating in New Zealand and transporting the ashes, or holding a local burial in New Zealand?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of New Zealand Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of New Zealand Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of New Zealand dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in New Zealand and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of New Zealand dies in the United Kingdom, you must complete medical certification, civil registration, and coroner or Scottish review clearance in the UK alongside New Zealand consular reporting, customs and biosecurity clearance, and estate administration across both countries [1][2][3]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Before civil registration, funeral arrangements, or international repatriation can proceed, the cause of death must be certified under the rules of the UK constituent nation where the death occurred [1][2].

  • Expected death in a hospital, hospice, or care setting: In England and Wales, an attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently scrutinized and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner before being sent electronically to the local Register Office [1][2]. In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for review by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS), and in Northern Ireland the doctor issues the MCCD reviewed by the Medical Examiner Service [1][4].
  • Sudden, unexpected, or unexplained death outside a hospital: Call emergency services on 999 or NHS 111 immediately so police and medical personnel can attend and verify the death [1]. If the cause of death is sudden, accidental, unnatural, or unknown, the death is referred to the Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal within the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (in Scotland), who decides whether a post-mortem examination or inquest is required before releasing the body for registration and funeral arrangements [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Funeral Directors in the UK and New Zealand, and Consular Support
steps.html:
Check immediately whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, or employer repatriation insurance [3]. Contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance team before signing any independent funeral contract, as the insurer normally appoints the UK and New Zealand funeral coordinators directly and covers eligible repatriation or local funeral costs [3].

  • Notifying the New Zealand High Commission in London: Report the death to the New Zealand High Commission in London (+44 20 7930 8422, LON-Enquiries@mfat.govt.nz, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade 24/7 SafeTravel consular emergency line at +64 9 920 20 20) [3][5]. Consular staff can advise on local UK procedures and tikanga considerations, provide lists of international funeral directors, notify next of kin in New Zealand, and cancel the deceased's New Zealand passport, though the New Zealand Government cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [3][5].
  • Appointing funeral directors in the United Kingdom and New Zealand: Appoint a UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (+44 121 711 1343, info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (+44 1279 726777, info@saif.org.uk) [6][7]. If returning your family member to New Zealand, coordinate with a receiving New Zealand funeral director registered with the Funeral Directors Association of New Zealand (+64 4 473 7475, info@funeraldirectors.co.nz) [8]. These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom and Document Recognition for New Zealand
steps.html:
Once the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or coroner's certificate) reaches the registrar, the death must be registered at the local Register Office in the UK district where the death occurred (for example, Westminster Register Office in London, Manchester Registration Service, or the City of Edinburgh Council Registration Service) [1][2].

  • Statutory UK registration deadlines: Register the death within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland, and purchase multiple certified copies of the official UK Death Certificate (entry in the register of deaths) [1][2]. (Note that Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office consular death registration applies when British nationals die outside the UK [1].)
  • Apostille and recognition in New Zealand: Both the United Kingdom and New Zealand are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply in either country). Because UK Death Certificates are issued in English, New Zealand banks, KiwiSaver schemes, and government agencies generally accept certified UK Death Certificates directly; where formal authentication is required for High Court probate or property transfers, apply for a Hague Apostille through the UK Legalisation Office [9]. In New Zealand, Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM, Department of Internal Affairs - DIA, which registers domestic NZ deaths within 3 working days after burial or cremation) does not register deaths that occurred outside New Zealand unless the deceased was aboard a New Zealand-registered ship or aircraft, so the UK Death Certificate serves as the permanent legal proof of death in New Zealand [3][10].

steps.title: International Repatriation to New Zealand vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your family can choose to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to New Zealand or arrange local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom [1][3].

  • Repatriating human remains (casket) from the UK to New Zealand:
    • UK exit clearances: In England and Wales, before a body can be removed outside England or Wales, the UK funeral director must give notice (Form 103) to the local Coroner, who issues an Out-of-England Order (Form 104) once satisfied no further inquiries are required [1]. In Scotland, exporting human remains abroad requires clearance from Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) (and Procurator Fiscal permission where applicable) [4]. Your UK funeral director also arranges arterial embalming, a hermetically sealed zinc-lined export coffin, and a Freedom from Infection Certificate.
    • New Zealand customs and biosecurity clearance: Upon arrival in New Zealand (for example, at Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch International Airport), the receiving New Zealand funeral director clears the casket through the New Zealand Customs Service and Ministry for Primary Industries / Public Health Service biosecurity using the official UK Death Certificate, the embalming certificate, the hermetically sealed coffin certificate, and the Public Health non-infectious disease certificate [10][11].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to New Zealand: If cremation takes place in the UK, an Out-of-England Order is not required to take cremated ashes abroad [1]. You may carry the sealed urn in airline hand luggage or ship it via air cargo; upon arrival in New Zealand, declare the ashes and wooden or natural-material urn to the New Zealand Customs Service and biosecurity officers, presenting the UK Death Certificate and Certificate of Cremation [11].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Tax, and Probate in New Zealand and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
With the official UK Death Certificates, complete notifications, survivor benefit claims, tax filings, and probate in both jurisdictions.

  • New Zealand notifications, pensions, tax, and High Court Probate:
    • Te Hokinga ā-Wairua and Work and Income (MSD / ACC): Consult the Te Hokinga ā-Wairua End of Life Service on govt.nz for New Zealand post-death checklists [10]. Contact Work and Income (0800 559 009 from New Zealand or +64 4 916 3404 from overseas) to report the death if your family member received New Zealand Superannuation or a Veteran's Pension, and to check eligibility for a means-tested Funeral Grant or survivor assistance (or contact ACC if the death resulted from a covered accident while temporarily abroad) [10][12].
    • KiwiSaver, Inland Revenue (IRD), and High Court Probate: Notify Inland Revenue (0800 227 774 or +64 4 978 0779) to finalize New Zealand tax obligations up to the date of death and file any estate tax return (Form IR6) [13]. Contact the deceased's KiwiSaver provider and New Zealand banks; if any single financial institution or KiwiSaver balance in New Zealand exceeds NZD 15,000 or the deceased owned New Zealand real property, apply to the High Court of New Zealand (Wellington Probate Registry) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, or apply to reseal a UK Grant of Probate in the High Court of New Zealand [10].
  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, tax, and Probate: When registering the death in England, Scotland, or Wales, obtain a reference number from the registrar to use the Tell Us Once service (or call the DWP Bereavement Service on 0800 151 2012 / International Pension Centre on +44 191 218 7777), which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, DVLA, and local councils in one step [14][15]. If your family member held UK bank accounts, property, or investments requiring court authority, report the estate and any Inheritance Tax (Form IHT400) to HMRC and apply for a Grant of Probate in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland (or Confirmation in Scotland) via HM Courts & Tribunals Service Probate (or reseal a New Zealand grant in the UK under the Colonial Probates Act) [16].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation: 1. In which UK nation (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland) and city did the death occur, and which city or region in New Zealand is the destination or place of residence? 2. Have you decided whether to repatriate the body to New Zealand, cremate in the United Kingdom and return the ashes, or hold a local burial in the UK?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of South Africa Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist

When a citizen or resident of South Africa dies in the United Kingdom, you must complete medical certification, civil registration, and coroner or Scottish review clearance in the UK alongside South African consular death registration, Department of Health import mortuary permits, and estate reporting to the Master of the High Court and UK probate authorities [1][2][3]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Before civil registration, funeral arrangements, or international repatriation can proceed, the cause of death must be certified under the rules of the UK constituent nation where the death occurred [1][2].

In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be reviewed by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS), and in Northern Ireland the attending doctor issues the MCCD reviewed by the Medical Examiner Service [1][4].
  • Sudden, unexpected, or unexplained death outside a hospital: Call emergency services on 999 or NHS 111 immediately so police and paramedics can attend and verify the death [1]. If the cause of death is sudden, accidental, unnatural, or unknown, the case is referred to the Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal within the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (in Scotland), who decides whether a post-mortem examination or inquest is required before releasing the body for registration and funeral arrangements [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Funeral Directors in the UK and South Africa, and Consular Support
steps.html:
Check immediately whether your family member held travel, medical-assistance, South African funeral cover, or employer repatriation insurance [3]. Contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance team before signing any independent funeral contract, as the insurer normally appoints the UK and South African funeral coordinators directly and covers eligible repatriation costs [3].

  • Notifying the South African High Commission in London: Report the death to the South African High Commission in London (15 Whitehall, London SW1A 2DD, email milnet@dirco.gov.za) or the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO Consular Section in Pretoria, +27 12 351 1000) [3][5]. Consular officials guide families on registering the death in the South African National Population Register and coordinating import permits, though the South African Government cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [3][5].
  • Appointing funeral providers in the United Kingdom and South Africa: Appoint a UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (+44 121 711 1343, info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (+44 1279 726777, info@saif.org.uk) [6][7]. If returning your family member to South Africa, coordinate with a receiving South African funeral undertaker holding a municipal Certificate of Competence and Department of Home Affairs designation, searchable via the National Funeral Directors Association of South Africa (email: info@nfda.org.za) [8][9]. These directories are listed as public-source examples for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in the United Kingdom, Apostille, and South African DHA Registration
steps.html:
Once the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or coroner's certificate) reaches the registrar, the death must be registered at the local Register Office in the UK district where the death occurred (for example, Westminster Register Office in London, Birmingham Register Office, or the City of Edinburgh Council Registration Service) [1][2].

  • Statutory UK registration deadlines: Register the death within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days in Scotland, and order multiple certified copies of the official UK Death Certificate (entry in the register of deaths) [1][2]. (Note that Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office consular death registration applies when British nationals die abroad [1].)
  • UK Apostille and South African consular death registration: Both the United Kingdom and South Africa are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (multilingual CIEC Form C extracts do not apply). To register the death of a South African citizen in South Africa's National Population Register and use the UK Death Certificate before the Master of the High Court or South African insurers, first have the original UK Death Certificate legalized with a Hague Apostille by the UK Legalisation Office (part of the FCDO) [5][10]. Then book an in-person appointment with the South African High Commission in London (milnet@dirco.gov.za) or submit the apostilled UK Death Certificate and the deceased's South African ID book/card or passport to the Department of Home Affairs (Contact Centre 0800 60 11 90) so the death is recorded on the National Population Register and a South African Death Certificate (Form DHA-132) or Burial Order (Form BI-14) can be issued [5][8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to South Africa vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your family can choose to repatriate the body or cremated ashes to South Africa or arrange local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom [1][3][9].

  • Repatriating human remains (casket) from the UK to South Africa:
    • UK exit clearances: In England and Wales, before a body can be removed outside England or Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner (Form 103) to obtain an Out-of-England Order (Form 104) [1]. In Scotland, exporting human remains abroad requires clearance from Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [4]. Your UK funeral director also completes arterial embalming, places the body in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined export coffin, and obtains a Freedom from Infection / Non-Infectious Disease Certificate.
    • South African Department of Health Import Permit: Before human remains can enter South Africa (for example, via O.R. Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg or Cape Town International Airport), the receiving South African funeral undertaker or DIRCO submits the apostilled UK Death Certificate, cause of death, embalming certificate, non-infectious disease certificate, coffin sealing certificate, and flight details to the National Department of Health Director-General to obtain a mandatory Import Permit for Human Remains, after which the receiving undertaker secures the local Burial Order (Form BI-14) [3][8][9].
  • Transporting cremated ashes to South Africa: If cremation takes place in the UK, neither a UK Out-of-England Order nor a South African Department of Health human remains import permit is required for cremated ashes [1][9]. Ashes may be carried in passenger hand luggage (in a security-screenable non-metallic urn) or shipped by air cargo accompanied by the certified UK Death Certificate and Certificate of Cremation [9].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Tax, and Estate Administration in South Africa and the UK
steps.html:
With the official Death Certificates, complete estate reporting, benefit claims, and tax filings in both jurisdictions.

  • South African Master of the High Court (14-day rule), SARS, UIF, and SASSA:
    • Reporting the estate to the Master of the High Court: Under South Africa's Administration of Estates Act, if the deceased left any property or assets in South Africa (or was ordinarily resident in South Africa), the estate must be reported within 14 days of death to the Master of the High Court (in Pretoria, Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, or the relevant provincial seat) using the Death Notice (Form J294), inventory (Form J243), original will, and apostilled Death Certificate [11]. The Master issues Letters of Authority (for estates valued up to R250,000 under Section 18(3)) or Letters of Executorship (for estates exceeding R250,000, or by signing and sealing a UK grant of probate) [11].
    • SARS tax clearance, UIF Death Benefits, and SASSA: Notify the South African Revenue Service (0800 00 7277) to register the deceased estate, file final pre-death and estate income tax returns, settle any Estate Duty (Form REV267), and obtain the SARS Deceased Estate Compliance (DEC) letter [12]. If the deceased contributed to the South African Unemployment Insurance Fund, eligible surviving spouses, life partners, or dependent children can claim UIF Dependant's / Death Benefits within 18 months through the Department of Employment and Labour (0800 030 007), and any SASSA social grant or Government Employees Pension Fund (GEPF) benefit should be notified promptly [8][13].
  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, tax, and Probate: When registering the death in England, Scotland, or Wales, obtain a reference code from the registrar to use the Tell Us Once service (or call the DWP Bereavement Service on 0800 151 2012 / International Pension Centre on +44 191 218 7777), which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions, DVLA, and local councils in one step [14][15]. If the deceased held UK assets requiring court authority, report the estate and any Inheritance Tax (Form IHT400) to HMRC and apply for a Grant of Probate in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland (or Confirmation in Scotland) via HM Courts & Tribunals Service Probate (South Africa is also a designated country under the UK Colonial Probates Act for resealing a South African grant in the UK) [16].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with French citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, procedures depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to France or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral arrangements cannot proceed until the cause of death is officially certified or cleared by the competent medical or forensic authority in the United Kingdom [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner system): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which must be independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. The Medical Examiner's office contacts the family or next of kin to explain the cause of death and transmits the countersigned MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (for example, Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), after which the 5-day registration window begins [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for review by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) before registration completes [1]. In Northern Ireland, the doctor issues the MCCD for submission to the district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If your family member died suddenly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so the police can attend [1]. Unexplained, violent, or perioperative deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1]. If a post-mortem examination or inquest is required, the Coroner or Procurator Fiscal issues interim certificates or direct burial/cremation and transfer authorisations once forensic inquiries conclude [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage, Appoint Funeral Coordinators in the United Kingdom and France, and Notify the French Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, bank-card assistance coverage, employer coverage, or a French pre-need funeral or repatriation policy (contrat d'assurance obsèques or assistance rapatriement) [6][7]. If coverage applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints and pays the international funeral operators directly [6].

If no insurance policy applies, the family can appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom alongside a receiving funeral operator in France to manage the cross-border transfer end-to-end [6][10]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can locate an accredited UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [10].
  • Receiving funeral operator in France: In France, funeral transport and burial/cremation must be carried out by a prefecturally licensed funeral operator (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture), searchable via municipal directories or national federations such as the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF) [7]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • French consular notification: Notify the Consulat général de France à Londres (phone: +44 20 7073 1200) or the French Consular Section in Edinburgh (if the death occurred in Scotland), operating under the Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (France Diplomatie) [6]. Consular staff provide procedural guidance, verify documents for mortuary transit into France, and transcribe the UK death record into the French civil registry, though the French state cannot pay funeral or repatriation costs [6].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Transcribe the Death Record for France
steps.html:
The death must first be registered with the civil registry in the UK district where the death occurred before it can be recorded in the French civil registry [1][6]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Once the Register Office confirms receipt of the MCCD or Coroner's notification, register the death within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days at any Registration Office in Scotland (such as Edinburgh City Chambers or Glasgow Registration Office) [1]. Request multiple official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), as banks, insurers, and French consular authorities require original certificates [1][6].
  • French Consular Transcription vs. Domestic Declaration: Unlike a death occurring inside metropolitan France - which must be declared at the local town hall (mairie du lieu de décès) within 24 hours excluding weekends and public holidays to obtain a French acte de décès intégral or a multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention [7] - a death in the United Kingdom is registered locally first and then submitted to the Consulat général de France à Londres for transcription de l'acte de décès [6]. You can apply by post using the consular transcription form, an original UK Death Certificate, proof of the deceased's French nationality (such as a French passport, national identity card, or French birth certificate), and the livret de famille [6].
  • UK Apostille (when required): While the Consulat général de France à Londres accepts original UK Death Certificates directly for consular transcription [6], French notaries or financial institutions handling estate assets prior to transcription may require a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) [3].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to France or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and French funeral directors handle the technical health, coroner, and border clearances depending on whether you select repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body to France: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director submits notice to the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104), which authorises removal of the body outside England and Wales [1][6]. In Scotland, clearance to move human remains outside Scotland is issued through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. For entry into France under international mortuary transit rules (the Berlin Agreement of 1937 and the Strasbourg Agreement of 1973), the UK funeral director arranges preservation care (soins de conservation / embalming) if required, a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious infection, and a hermetically sealed coffin with a zinc liner (cercueil hermétique), and obtains the consular mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) via the Consulat général de France à Londres (or prefectural authorisation in France) before air or Eurotunnel transport to the receiving French municipality (such as Paris, Lyon, or Marseille) [6][7].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the crematorium issues an official Certificate of Cremation [6]. Ashes placed in a sealed urn can be transported to France accompanied by the UK Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, and consular or municipal clearance; under French law, cremated ashes may be placed in a cemetery columbarium, sealed onto a family grave monument, or scattered in a designated space after declaration to the local mairie (keeping ashes permanently in a private residence is not permitted in France) [6][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the "Green Form" in England and Wales, or Form 14 in Scotland) directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
After the funeral or repatriation is underway, administrative and estate steps frequently span both jurisdictions [2][4][7]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased lived in England, Scotland, or Wales, the registrar provides a unique reference number for the government's Tell Us Once service, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, local councils, and state pension services in one step [2]. You can also contact the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to report the death and check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment or Funeral Expenses Payment [2].
    • If the deceased lived in France but received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) directly [5].
    • If the deceased left property, bank accounts, or investments in the United Kingdom above institution thresholds, the executor or entitled representative must apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England and Wales, or apply to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland, after submitting any required Inheritance Tax forms to HMRC [4].
  • French social security, survivor pensions, taxes, and succession:
    • Lump-sum death grant (capital décès): If the deceased was employed or insured under the French general social security system shortly before death, eligible priority dependents can claim the capital décès from the Caisse Primaire d'Assurance Maladie (CPAM via Ameli.fr) within 2 years of the date of death [7][8].
    • Survivor pensions (pension de réversion): An eligible surviving married or formerly married partner can apply for a survivor pension under the French basic scheme through L'Assurance Retraite (phone from abroad: +33 9 71 10 39 60) and for supplementary employee survivor benefits via Agirc-Arrco (using the unified online portal on info-retraite.fr or lassuranceretraite.fr) [7][9].
    • French notary and inheritance tax (déclaration de succession): If the deceased was domiciled in France, held real estate in France, or had French estate assets above the statutory threshold, instruct a notary via Notaires de France (Conseil supérieur du notariat) or the Paris Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires de Paris) [7][11]. The notary checks the central wills registry (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), drafts the certificate of heirship (acte de notoriété), and prepares the French inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) for the French tax authorities (Direction générale des Finances publiques - impôts) [7][11]. When a death occurs outside metropolitan France (including in the United Kingdom), the statutory deadline to file the déclaration de succession with the French tax office is 12 months from the date of death (compared to 6 months when the death occurs inside metropolitan France) [7][11].
