title: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Spain dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Spain and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Spanish citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate steps depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to Spain or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral or repatriation arrangements in the United Kingdom begin once the medical cause of death is certified and cleared by the appropriate medical or forensic authority [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner review): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. Once approved, the Medical Examiner's office discusses the cause of death with the next of kin and sends the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), unlocking the 5-day civil registration window [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, an attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), subject to potential review by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1]. In Northern Ireland, the attending doctor issues the MCCD for registration at the local district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred suddenly outside a hospital, call 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so police and emergency medical services can attend [1]. Unexplained, accidental, or unnatural deaths are referred to the Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland), who authorises any required post-mortem examination and issues clearance for burial, cremation, or international transfer once forensic inquiries conclude [1].

steps.title: Check Decesos or Travel Insurance, Appoint Funeral Directors in the United Kingdom and Spain, and Contact the Spanish Consulate
steps.html:
Before entering into an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held a Spanish funeral and repatriation insurance policy (seguro de decesos), travel insurance, or bank-card assistance coverage [7]. Spanish seguro de decesos policies commonly include a 24-hour international assistance unit that appoints and pays both the UK and Spanish funeral providers directly [7].

If no insurance policy covers the transfer, the family should appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom coordinated with an authorised receiving funeral company in Spain [7][10][11]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can find an accredited UK funeral provider experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Receiving funeral provider in Spain: For reception, airport clearance, and cemetery or crematorium services in Spain (such as in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Seville, or Bilbao), you can locate a licensed Spanish funeral company (empresa funeraria habilitada) via the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (phone: +34 91 576 31 55; email: info@panasef.com) [10]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Spanish consular assistance: Notify the Consulado General de España en Londres (phone: +44 20 7589 8989; consular emergency phone: +44 7712 764 151; email: cog.londres@maec.es; Civil Registry email: cog.londres.rgc@maec.es), or the Spanish Consulates General in Manchester or Edinburgh depending on the UK region where the death occurred, operating under the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (MAEC) [6][7]. The Consulate guides families on consular civil registration and mortuary transit rules, although Spanish state authorities cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [7].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Complete Spanish Consular Registration and Legalisation
steps.html:
A death occurring in the United Kingdom must first be registered with the local UK civil registry before being recorded in the Spanish civil registry [1][6]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Register the death at the local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (once notified by the Medical Examiner or Coroner) or within 8 days at a Registration Office in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple original certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), as original certificates are required for consular registration, legalisation, and estate administration [1][6].
  • Spanish Consular Civil Registry vs. Domestic Spanish Registration: Whereas a death occurring inside Spain is registered within 24 hours at the municipal Registro Civil under the Ministerio de Justicia to obtain the Certificado Literal de Defunción and the multilingual CIEC Form C extract (1976 Vienna Convention) [8], a death of a Spanish citizen in the United Kingdom must be registered at the Consular Civil Registry (Registro Civil Consular) of the Consulado General de España en Londres (or Manchester/Edinburgh) [6]. Submitting the signed declaration sheet, the original UK Death Certificate, the deceased's Spanish DNI or passport, and a Spanish literal birth certificate allows the Consulate to issue the official Spanish Certificado Literal de Defunción and report the death to the Central Civil Registry in Spain [6].
  • UK Apostille (when presenting UK documents directly in Spain): If you need to present the UK Death Certificate or UK probate documents directly to a Spanish notary, bank, or court before Spanish consular registration is completed, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) alongside a sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) [3][7].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Spain or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and Spanish funeral directors coordinate the health, forensic, and border permits according to whether you choose repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][7]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Spain: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104) authorising removal of the body from England and Wales [1]. In Scotland, clearance to remove remains outside Scotland is issued through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. For transfer to Spain under international mortuary transit agreements (the Strasbourg Agreement of 1973 and Berlin Agreement of 1937) and Spanish Sanidad Exterior regulations, the UK funeral director completes preservation/embalming, provides a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious diseases, seals the remains in a zinc-lined hermetic coffin (féretro de zinc sellado), and coordinates with the Consulado General de España en Londres and Spanish external border health authorities (Sanidad Exterior) for the mortuary transit permit (salvoconducto mortuorio) [7].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the crematorium issues an official Certificate of Cremation [7]. Cremated ashes can be transported to Spain in a sealed urn accompanied by the UK Death Certificate and the Certificate of Cremation (subject to airline cabin-baggage rules and local Spanish municipal cemetery rules) [7].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Wills Registry Checks, and Probate in Spain and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are in place, administrative and succession procedures typically involve authorities in both countries [2][4][8][9]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased resided in England, Scotland, or Wales, use the Tell Us Once reference provided by the registrar or call the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), council services, and state benefit offices, and to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • If the deceased resided in Spain and received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • If the deceased held UK real estate, bank accounts, or investments requiring formal administration, apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland [4].
  • Spanish social security, Last Wills Registry, notary, and inheritance tax:
    • Death grant and survivor pensions (INSS): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension from the Spanish social security system, eligible beneficiaries can apply to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (phone: +34 91 542 11 76) for the funeral expense grant (auxilio por defunción) and survivor benefits (prestaciones de muerte y supervivencia, including pensión de viudedad, pensión de orfandad, or prestaciones en favor de familiares) via the Seguridad Social electronic portal [9].
    • Spanish Registry of Last Wills and Life Insurance (Últimas Voluntades): Once 15 working days (15 días hábiles) have elapsed since the date of death, apply to the Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad of the Ministerio de Justicia (phone: +34 91 837 22 95) using Modelo 790 (code 006) and the death certificate to obtain the Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad (confirming whether the deceased executed a Spanish will before a notary) and the Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [8].
    • Notarial inheritance deed and 6-month tax deadline: If the deceased left assets or habitual residence in Spain, a Spanish notary (Consejo General del Notariado) prepares the deed of acceptance and partition of inheritance (escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia) or declaration of heirs (declaración de herederos abintestato) [8]. Spanish Inheritance Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within 6 months from the date of death (before the AEAT for non-residents via the Oficina Nacional de Gestión Tributaria, or the competent Autonomous Community tax agency), with the option to request a 6-month extension within the first 5 months [8].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Italy dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Italy and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Italian citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate administrative steps depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to Italy or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral or repatriation arrangements in the United Kingdom require official medical certification or forensic clearance of the cause of death [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner system): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. Once approved, the Medical Examiner's office contacts the next of kin to explain the cause of death and transmits the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), starting the 5-day civil registration window [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be reviewed by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1]. In Northern Ireland, the doctor issues the MCCD for registration at the local district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so police and medical personnel can attend [1]. Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths are referred to the local Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland), who conducts any required post-mortem examination or inquest and issues clearance for burial, cremation, or international transfer [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage, Appoint Funeral Directors in the United Kingdom and Italy, and Contact the Italian Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, bank-card assistance coverage, or private repatriation insurance [6]. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance centre immediately so it can appoint and fund the international funeral providers directly.

If no insurance policy applies, the family can appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom coordinated with an authorised receiving funeral company in Italy [6][11]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can locate an accredited UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Receiving funeral company in Italy: For airport clearance, municipal transport, and burial or entombment in Italy (for example in Rome, Milan, Naples, or Turin), coordinate with a licensed Italian funeral operator (impresa funebre autorizzata), such as a member of the national sector federations FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri) or Federcofit [6]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Italian consular assistance: Notify the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (phone: +44 20 7936 5900; Welfare and Repatriation Office email: sociale.londra@esteri.it), or the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Edimburgo (for Scotland and Northern Ireland) or Consolato d'Italia a Manchester, operating under the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) [6][7]. Consular staff process the Italian death transcription and coordinate with the destination Italian municipality (Comune) to issue the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario), though Italian authorities do not pay funeral or repatriation expenses unless specific statutory indigence rules apply [6].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Complete Italian Consular Transcription and Legalisation
steps.html:
The death must first be registered with the civil registry in the UK district where the death occurred before it can be transcribed into the Italian civil registry [1][7]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Register the death at the local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (once notified by the Medical Examiner or Coroner) or within 8 days at a Registration Office in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple original certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death) [1][7].
  • UK Apostille and Italian Translation: For an Italian citizen who died in the United Kingdom, the original UK Death Certificate must be legalised with a paper Hague Apostille issued directly by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) - apostilles issued by a Notary Public or solicitor are not accepted for civil registry transcription - and accompanied by a typed translation into Italian [3][7].
  • Italian Consular Transcription vs. Domestic Registration: Whereas a death occurring inside Italy is declared within 24 hours at the Ufficio di Stato Civile of the Italian Comune of death to issue the atto di morte, burial permit (permesso di seppellimento), and multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention, a death in the United Kingdom is transcribed into the Italian Comune of AIRE registration or last residence by posting the application (Modulo N.5, original apostilled UK Death Certificate, Italian translation, copy of the deceased's passport, and prepaid Special Delivery return envelope) to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (Ufficio Stato Civile, 83/86 Farringdon Street, London EC4A 4BL) [7].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Italy (Passaporto Mortuario) or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and Italian funeral directors handle the technical permits depending on whether you choose repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Italy: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104) authorising removal of the remains outside England and Wales [1][6]. In Scotland, clearance to remove human remains outside Scotland is obtained through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. Under the 1937 Berlin Convention and Italian mortuary police rules, the UK funeral director submits the repatriation dossier by email to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (sociale.londra@esteri.it), specifying the receiving Italian Comune, the exact cemetery and grave/niche details, and the entry border/airport in Italy, together with: (1) the original UK Death Certificate legalised with an FCDO Apostille, (2) the Embalming Certificate (certificato di imbalsamazione), (3) the medical certificate confirming the absence of infectious or contagious diseases (corresponding to local health authority / ASL sanitary certification), (4) the Coroner's Out-of-England certificate, and (5) the funeral director's declaration confirming a double coffin with a hermetically soldered zinc/metal inner casket (doppia cassa con cofano metallico saldato) [6]. The Consulate requests entry authorisation (nulla osta) from the Italian Comune and, once granted, issues the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) and seals the coffin for transport [6].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the funeral director or family submits the apostilled UK Death Certificate, the official Certificate of Cremation, and destination cemetery/Comune details to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra to obtain the consular mortuary permit for transporting the sealed urn to Italy [6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Italy and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are underway, estate and pension formalities frequently apply in both jurisdictions [2][4][8][9][10]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased lived in England, Scotland, or Wales, use the Tell Us Once reference provided by the registrar or contact the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to report the death across HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), passport, and council records and to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • If the deceased resided in Italy and received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • If the deceased held UK real estate, bank accounts, or investments requiring formal authority, apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland [4].
  • Italian survivor pensions, inheritance tax, and wills check:
    • Survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti - INPS): Eligible surviving family members (such as a surviving married/civil partner or eligible dependent children) can apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (phone from Italy: 803 164; from abroad or mobile: +39 06 164 164) for the pensione di reversibilità (if the deceased was already a pensioner) or pensione indiretta (if the deceased was an insured worker), as well as any accrued unpaid pension instalments (ratei maturati e non riscossi), online via SPID/CIE or through a Patronato office [8].
    • Italian inheritance tax declaration (dichiarazione di successione within 12 months): Heirs and legatees must file the dichiarazione di successione telematically with the Agenzia delle Entrate (phone from Italy: 800 90 96 96; from abroad: +39 06 97617689) within 12 months from the date of death (unless the estate devolves solely to the surviving partner and straight-line relatives, has a gross value not exceeding EUR 100,000, and includes no real estate or real property rights) [9].
    • Italian wills search and notarial procedures: To verify whether the deceased left a formal or deposited will in Italy, you can request a search of the General Registry of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti, managed by the Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili of the Ministero della Giustizia) or the voluntary holographic wills registry via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, and instruct an Italian notary to publish any Italian will and update cadastral land records (voltura catastale) [10].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Portugal dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Portugal and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Portuguese citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate steps depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to Portugal or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral or repatriation arrangements in the United Kingdom begin once the cause of death is certified and cleared by the competent medical or forensic authority [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner review): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. Once approved, the Medical Examiner's office contacts the next of kin to explain the cause of death and transmits the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), starting the 5-day civil registration window [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be reviewed by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1]. In Northern Ireland, the doctor issues the MCCD for registration at the local district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so police and medical personnel can attend [1]. Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths are referred to the local Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland), who conducts any required post-mortem examination or inquest and issues clearance for burial, cremation, or international transfer [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage, Appoint Funeral Directors in the United Kingdom and Portugal, and Contact the Portuguese Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, bank-card coverage, or a repatriation insurance policy [7]. If coverage applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance desk immediately so the insurer can appoint and pay the UK and Portuguese funeral providers directly.

If no insurance policy covers the arrangements, the family should appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom coordinated with a licensed receiving funeral agency in Portugal [6][11]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can find an accredited UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Receiving funeral agency in Portugal: In Portugal, funeral transport and burial or cremation services (for example in Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Coimbra, or Funchal) must be carried out by a funeral agency registered with the Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (agência funerária habilitada na DGAE via gov.pt), searchable through Portuguese sector associations such as the Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL) or the Associação de Agentes Funerários de Portugal (AAFC / AAFP) [6][7]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Portuguese consular assistance: Notify the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Londres (repatriation email: consulado.londres@mne.pt; Centro de Atendimento Consular UK phone: +44 20 3433 3624; 24-hour Gabinete de Emergência Consular phone: +351 217 929 714) or the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Manchester (depending on the UK jurisdiction where the death occurred), operating under the Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas of the Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros (MNE) [6].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Complete Mandatory Portuguese Consular Registration
steps.html:
A death occurring in the United Kingdom must first be registered with the local UK civil registry before being recorded in the Portuguese civil registry [1][6]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Register the death at the local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (once notified by the Medical Examiner or Coroner) or within 8 days at a Registration Office in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple original certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death) [1][6].
  • Portuguese Consular Death Registration (Registo de Óbito): Whereas a death occurring inside Portugal must be declared within 48 hours at any Conservatória do Registo Civil under the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / Justiça.gov.pt) to issue the free Portuguese death record (Assento de Óbito gratuito) and, where needed, a multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention [7][9], a death of a Portuguese citizen in the United Kingdom is registered at the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Londres (or Manchester) by appointment or by post [6]. Under the rules of the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Londres, original UK Death Certificates issued in the United Kingdom do not require legalisation or translation into Portuguese for consular registration, provided the deceased's prior marital status changes (such as marriage or divorce) are already updated in the Portuguese civil registry [6].
  • UK Apostille (when presenting UK documents directly in Portugal): If you need to use a UK Death Certificate or a UK Grant of Probate directly before a court, bank, or notary in Portugal without going through the Consulate, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) [3].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Portugal (Alvará de Trasladação) or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and Portuguese funeral agencies coordinate the technical health, coroner, and consular permits depending on whether you select repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Portugal: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104) authorising removal of the body outside England and Wales [1]. In Scotland, clearance to remove human remains outside Scotland is issued through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. Under Portuguese consular rules and international mortuary transit conventions (the Strasbourg Agreement of 1973 and Berlin Convention of 1937), Portuguese death registration (registo de óbito) is mandatory before human remains can be repatriated to Portugal [6]. The UK and Portuguese funeral agencies coordinate directly by email with the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Londres (consulado.londres@mne.pt, without requiring a regular online appointment) to obtain the Mortuary Transit Permit (Alvará de Trasladação / livre-trânsito mortuário), presenting the medical infection-free certificate, embalming certificate, Out-of-England Order, and confirmation of a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin (caixão de zinco selado) [6].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, ashes carried in a plastic or cardboard urn require the cremation certificate issued by the UK crematorium or funeral director [6]. If a wooden urn is used and the airline requires a consular alvará de trasladação de cinzas, the urn must meet consular sealing requirements (including an opening in the base for the official consular seal), arranged in advance by email with the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em Londres [6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Portugal and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are in place, social security, tax, and estate steps frequently apply in both countries [2][4][7][8][9][10]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased resided in England, Scotland, or Wales, use the Tell Us Once reference provided by the registrar or call the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), passport, and council services and to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • If the deceased resided in Portugal and received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • If the deceased held UK real estate, bank accounts, or investments requiring formal administration, apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland [4].
  • Portuguese social security, Balcão das Heranças, and Stamp Duty (Imposto do Selo):
    • Death grant, funeral reimbursement, and survivor pension (Segurança Social): If the deceased was covered by the Portuguese social security system, eligible family members can apply to Segurança Social (phone from Portugal: 210 545 400 or 300 502 502; online via Segurança Social Direta) for the lump-sum Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, which must be claimed within 180 consecutive days of the death) and the monthly Survivor Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [7][8]. If there are no family members entitled to the Subsídio por Morte, the person who paid the funeral invoice can claim Funeral Expense Reimbursement (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral) within 90 days of the death [7][8].
    • Espaço Óbito and Balcão das Heranças (Habilitação de Herdeiros): The head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) can use the one-stop Espaço Óbito or Balcão das Heranças desks operated by the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / Justiça.gov.pt) to execute the formal declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros), partition estate assets, and update property registrations [9][10].
    • Tax notification (Participação do Imposto do Selo by the end of the 3rd month): Where the deceased left assets in Portugal, the cabeça-de-casal must report the death and declare the estate assets using Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo to the Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (via Portal das Finanças, a local Serviço de Finanças, or the Balcão das Heranças) by the end of the third month following the month in which the death occurred (even when close legitimate heirs qualify for exemption from the 10% Stamp Duty rate) [10].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in Indonesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in Indonesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Australia dies in Indonesia: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Indonesia, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Australia and Indonesia.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Australian citizenship or residence ties dies in Indonesia, the immediate priorities are obtaining the Indonesian medical and police clearances, checking travel or repatriation insurance, notifying Australian consular authorities, and appointing coordinated funeral directors in Indonesia and Australia [1][2].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in Indonesia
steps.html:
Civil death registration, embalming, and international transport permits in Indonesia cannot proceed until the medical cause of death is certified and any required police investigation is completed [1][2]:

  • Hospital deaths (Surat Keterangan Kematian): When a death occurs in an Indonesian hospital (for example, at RSUP Prof. Ngoerah / Sanglah Hospital in Denpasar, Bali, or a hospital in Jakarta), the attending physician issues the hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Surat Keterangan Kematian / Surat Pemeriksaan Kematian) [1][2]. Provide the deceased's Australian passport (and Indonesian KITAS/KITAP residence permit, if held) so personal details match official records [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or hotel/villa deaths (Polri clearance): If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital - such as in a hotel, villa, traffic accident, or water incident - call Indonesia's emergency number 112, ambulance service 118/119, or the Indonesian National Police (Kepolisian Negara Republik Indonesia - Polri) on 110 immediately [1][2]. Police attendance and a forensic examination (visum et repertum) at a designated government forensic hospital (such as RSUP Prof. Ngoerah in Bali) are mandatory for unnatural or unattended deaths, and the police must issue an official police report (Surat Keterangan Kepolisian) before the body can be embalmed, cremated, or released for repatriation [1][2].

steps.title: Check Travel Insurance, Appoint Funeral Directors in Indonesia and Australia, and Contact the Australian Embassy or Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent contract with a local mortuary operator, verify whether your family member had travel insurance, credit-card travel protection, or employer medical-evacuation coverage [1][2]. If insured, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team immediately, as the insurer typically appoints the international repatriation specialists and pays covered costs directly [1].

If there is no applicable insurance policy, the family should appoint a licensed international funeral and cargo repatriation specialist in Indonesia alongside a receiving funeral director in Australia [1][3]:

  • Funeral and repatriation specialist in Indonesia: Engage an established Indonesian international funeral provider (in Bali, Jakarta, or Surabaya) experienced in air-cargo mortuary clearances; the Australian Embassy in Jakarta and the Australian Consulate-General in Bali provide lists of local English-speaking funeral directors and translators [1][2].
  • Receiving funeral director in Australia: To handle customs clearance at the arrival airport and burial or cremation in the destination Australian state or territory, you can locate an accredited funeral director through the Australian Funeral Directors Association (operating as Funerals Australia, phone: +61 3 9859 9966; email: info@funeralsaustralia.org.au) [3]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Australian consular assistance: Contact the 24-hour Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Consular Emergency Centre (phone within Australia: 1300 555 135; phone from overseas: +61 2 6261 3305) or the nearest mission in Indonesia, such as the Australian Consulate-General in Bali (phone: +62 361 2000 100; email: consular.bali@dfat.gov.au, covering Bali, West Nusa Tenggara, and East Nusa Tenggara) or the Australian Embassy in Jakarta [1][2]. Consular officers explain local procedures, notify the local funeral director of Australian biosecurity standards, and assist with consular formalities, though the Australian Government cannot pay funeral, cremation, or repatriation costs [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Indonesian Civil Registry (Disdukcapil) and Obtain a Kemenkumham Apostille for Australia
steps.html:
To manage legal, banking, superannuation, and probate matters in Australia, you must obtain the official Indonesian civil death record along with an Apostille and certified English translation [1][4]:

  • Indonesian Civil Registry (Disdukcapil - Akta Kematian): Using the hospital Surat Keterangan Kematian, police clearance (if applicable), and the deceased's passport, your appointed Indonesian funeral director registers the death with the local Regency or Municipal Civil Registry Office (Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil - Disdukcapil, such as Disdukcapil Kota Denpasar or Kabupaten Badung in Bali, or Disdukcapil DKI Jakarta) to obtain the official Indonesian civil Death Certificate (Akta Kematian or Official Statement of Death for a Foreign National) [1][4].
  • Indonesian Apostille (Kemenkumham Ditjen AHU) and translation: Because both Indonesia and Australia are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, have the Indonesian Akta Kematian legalised with an Apostille issued by the Indonesian Ministry of Law (Kementerian Hukum / Kemenkumham) through the Direktorat Jenderal Administrasi Hukum Umum (Ditjen AHU online portal) [4]. Also obtain a certified English translation of the Indonesian death documents (for Australian court and superannuation purposes, institutions frequently require a translation by a NAATI-certified translator) [1][10].
  • Recognition in Australian States and Territories: Australian State and Territory Registries of Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM in New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania, the Australian Capital Territory, and the Northern Territory) generally cannot register a death that occurred overseas unless it occurred on an Australian-registered aircraft or vessel [1][10]. Instead, the original Indonesian Akta Kematian accompanied by the Kemenkumham Apostille and a NAATI-certified English translation serves as the official evidence of death across Australia [1][4][10].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Australia or Local Cremation/Burial in Indonesia
steps.html:
Your Indonesian and Australian funeral directors coordinate the export and import clearances depending on whether you choose repatriation of the body, local cremation in Indonesia and transport of ashes, or local burial [1][5][6][7]:

  • Repatriation of uncremated human remains to Australia: In Indonesia, the international funeral director obtains the hospital formalin embalming certificate (Surat Keterangan Pengawetan Jenazah), medical certificate confirming the absence of infectious diseases, coffin-sealing certificate (using a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin inside a transport container), the Indonesian National Police (Polri) mortuary transport permit (Surat Izin Angkut Jenazah), the Airport Health Quarantine (Balai Besar Kekarantinaan Kesehatan - BBKK, such as at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport in Bali or Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta) export permit, and Australian consular mortuary clearance [1][2]. For entry into Australia (for example at Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, or Adelaide), the receiving Australian funeral director coordinates with the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (phone: 1800 900 090; notified at least 48 hours prior to arrival under BICON biosecurity conditions), the Australian Government Department of Health human biosecurity officers (email: human.remains@health.gov.au), and the Australian Border Force (phone: 131 881), presenting the official death certificate, embalming certificate, and non-infectious disease statement so the remains can be released for burial or cremation under state or territory health regulations [5][6][7].
  • Local cremation in Indonesia and bringing ashes to Australia: If cremation takes place in Indonesia (such as at a licensed crematorium in Bali or Jakarta), obtain the official Cremation Certificate (Surat Keterangan Kremasi) and ensure the ashes are sealed in a clean container free of soil, wood bark, or organic matter [1][5][6]. Under Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry and Australian Border Force rules, clean cremated human ashes do not require an Australian import permit, death certificate, or cremation certificate for biosecurity clearance, though you should declare any wooden urn on your Incoming Passenger Card for inspection and carry the death and cremation certificates for airline security screening [5][6].
  • Local burial in Indonesia: If local burial is chosen in Indonesia, the Indonesian funeral provider coordinates the municipal cemetery permit with Disdukcapil and local religious or community authorities [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Superannuation Claims, Tax Returns, and Probate in Australia and Indonesia
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are underway, financial, pension, tax, and estate steps must be completed [8][9][10]:

  • Services Australia and multi-agency notifications: Contact Services Australia (Bereavement Line phone: 132 300; from overseas: +61 3 6222 3455) to report the death for Medicare, Centrelink pensions or payments, and Child Support, and to check eligibility for any bereavement payment or surviving partner allowance [8]. You can also use the official Australian Death Notification Service to notify participating banks, utilities, and superannuation funds [8][10].
  • Australian Superannuation death benefits: Contact the deceased's Australian superannuation fund(s) directly [8]. Superannuation death benefits (including any life insurance held inside super) generally do not form part of the estate automatically and are paid by the fund trustee according to a valid Binding Death Benefit Nomination or superannuation dependency rules.
  • Australian Taxation Office (ATO): Notify the Australian Taxation Office (phone within Australia: 13 28 61; from overseas: +61 2 6216 1111) of the death using the official notification of a deceased person form, and have the executor or legal personal representative lodge a final "Date of Death" individual tax return (plus any deceased estate trust tax returns if the estate earns income before distribution) [9].
  • State or Territory Supreme Court Grant of Probate: If the deceased held real estate, substantial bank balances, or shareholdings in Australia, the executor (or next-of-kin administrator if there is no will) applies to the Supreme Court Probate Registry of the relevant Australian State or Territory (such as NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT, or NT) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, submitting the apostilled Indonesian Akta Kematian and NAATI-certified translation [9][10]. If the deceased also held Indonesian residency (KITAS/KITAP), Indonesian bank accounts, property rights, or BPJS Ketenagakerjaan coverage, coordinate local closure and benefit claims with an Indonesian lawyer or notary (Notaris/PPAT) [1][2].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Australia dies in Thailand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Thailand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Australia and Thailand.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of Australia dies in Thailand, the immediate priorities are securing medical and police clearance in Thailand, registering the death with the local Thai district office within 24 hours, and coordinating consular release and funeral logistics between Thailand and Australia.

steps.title: Medical Certification and Police or Forensic Clearance in Thailand
steps.html:
Every civil registration and transfer permit in Thailand begins with official medical confirmation of death and, where applicable, police and forensic clearance [1]:

  • Death in a hospital: The attending physician in Thailand issues the official Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1), which states the cause of death and is required to register the death at the local district office [1].
  • Death outside a hospital (residence, hotel, or public place) or sudden/unnatural death: Do not move the body before authorities arrive. Call the Royal Thai Police on 191, the Tourist Police on 1155, or Thai Emergency Medical Services on 1669 [1]. Police officers must inspect the scene and prepare an official police report before authorizing transport of the deceased [1].
  • Forensic examination: For sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths, Thai police normally transfer the deceased for a forensic post-mortem examination (for example, to the Institute of Forensic Medicine at Police General Hospital in Bangkok or a designated provincial regional hospital) before issuing the medical cause-of-death documentation [1].

steps.title: Insurance Verification, Funeral Directors, and Consular Notification
steps.html:
Before entering into private financial commitments, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance [2]. If a policy is active, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team immediately, as the insurer normally appoints and funds the international repatriation agency directly [2].

  • Consular notification and release: Notify the Australian Embassy in Thailand in Bangkok (+66 2 344 6300) or the Australian Consulate-General in Phuket, or call the 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade on 1300 555 135 within Australia or +61 2 6261 3305 from overseas [1][2]. Consular officers cancel the deceased's Australian passport, provide a list of English-speaking funeral directors and lawyers in Thailand, and issue the mandatory Embassy letter of release (no-objection letter) authorizing the hospital or morgue to release the remains to the next of kin or appointed funeral representative [1][2].
  • Appointing funeral coordinators: You can appoint an international funeral and repatriation director in Thailand (or a local Buddhist temple (Wat) cremation coordinator if arranging a local cremation) to handle Thai hospital release, civil registration, and export formalities [1]. If returning the body or ashes to Australia, pair the Thai provider with a receiving funeral director in the relevant Australian state or territory, whom you can locate through the official directory of Funerals Australia (formerly the Australian Funeral Directors Association) [4].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Thailand and Document Legalization for Australia
steps.html:
Under Thai civil registration rules, a death must be reported within 24 hours of the time of death (or within 24 hours of discovery) to the local District Office (Amphoe in provinces, or Khet in Bangkok, operating under the Department of Provincial Administration - DOPA) where the death occurred or where the body was found [1][3]:

  • Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4): In practice, the family or the appointed Thai funeral director (acting under a written authorization from the next of kin) submits the hospital Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1), the police report (if applicable), and the deceased's Australian passport to the District Office (Amphoe or Khet) [1]. The registrar issues only one original Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) in the Thai language [1].
  • Certified translation and legalization: Because the original Form Tor.Ror.4 is issued in Thai and Thailand is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, have the Thai Death Certificate translated into English and submit both the original certificate and the translation for official legalization by the Department of Consular Affairs at the Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (+66 2 572 8442) in Bangkok or its regional legalization offices (such as Chiang Mai, Phuket, Songkhla, or Pattaya) [1][3]. Order several legalized copies and certified translations, as Australian banks, superannuation funds, and courts require them.
  • Recognition in Australia: Australian state and territory Registries of Births, Deaths and Marriages (such as the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages in Sydney or Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria in Melbourne) generally only register deaths that occur within their own state or territory (with narrow exceptions where a person died on an aircraft or vessel bound for Australia) [2][7]. For an Australian citizen who dies in Thailand, the legalized Thai Death Certificate and certified English translation serve as the primary legal proof of death in Australia [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation to Australia Versus Local Burial or Cremation in Thailand
steps.html:
The next of kin must decide whether to arrange local cremation or burial in Thailand or repatriate the body or cremated ashes to Australia [1][2]:

  • Repatriation of human remains (body) to Australia: Your appointed international funeral director in Thailand coordinates clinical embalming, sealing in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, a non-infectious disease certificate, and export cargo clearance with Thai Customs at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket International Airport, using the release letter from the Australian Embassy in Thailand [1]. Upon arrival in Australia, human remains are cleared through the Australian Border Force and biosecurity authorities under the Department of Health and Aged Care; a body accompanied by an official death certificate (with English translation) and free of biosecurity contaminants does not require an advance human biosecurity import permit, and your receiving Australian funeral director manages customs and mortuary transfer to the destination city [5].
  • Returning cremated ashes to Australia: Local cremation at a Thai Buddhist temple (Wat) followed by returning the ashes is a common option [1]. To clear Australian border biosecurity without delay, ashes must be sealed in a clean, non-wooden container (such as metal, ceramic, or plastic) free of soil or plant matter, and accompanied by the legalized Thai Death Certificate, English translation, and cremation certificate [1][5]. Wooden urns must be declared on arrival for biosecurity inspection [5].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Superannuation, Tax, and Probate in Australia and Thailand
steps.html:
Once you hold the legalized Thai Death Certificate and certified English translation, complete the financial and estate administration in both countries:

  • Government notifications and survivor support in Australia: Notify Services Australia within 28 days by calling the Bereavement Line on 132 300 (or +61 3 6222 3455 from overseas) to update Centrelink, Medicare, and Age Pension or Carer Payment records and to check eligibility for a lump-sum bereavement payment or continuations [6]. Note that the Australian Death Notification Service requires an Australian state or territory death certificate to verify a death online, so for a death registered in Thailand you should contact Australian banks, insurers, and utility providers directly using the legalized Thai Death Certificate and English translation [7].
  • Superannuation, tax, and probate in Australia: Contact the deceased's Australian superannuation fund directly to claim superannuation death benefits and any attached life insurance (which are generally paid according to a binding death benefit nomination or trustee discretion outside the will). Notify the Australian Taxation Office on 13 28 61 (or +61 2 6216 1111 from overseas) to lodge an official Notification of a Deceased Person, file a final "Date of Death" individual tax return covering 1 July up to the date of death, and file trust tax returns if the estate earns post-death income [8]. If the deceased held substantial sole-name Australian assets or real estate, the executor or next of kin applies for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration from the Supreme Court of the relevant Australian state or territory (for example, the Supreme Court of New South Wales or the Supreme Court of Victoria).
  • Estate administration in Thailand: If the deceased held sole-name Thai bank accounts, vehicles, or condominium property in Thailand, Thai banks and land offices will not release assets solely on an Australian will or Australian probate grant [1]. Unless a separate Thai will exists and is admitted locally, the family or executor normally engages a Thai lawyer to petition the competent Thai Provincial Court or Civil Court in Bangkok for an official court order appointing an estate administrator under the Thai Civil and Commercial Code [1].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance further, could you let us know: 1. Which province or municipality in Thailand the death occurred in, and which Australian state or territory the deceased lived in or held assets in? 2. Whether you are planning to repatriate the body, cremate locally in Thailand and bring the ashes to Australia, or hold the funeral and burial/cremation entirely in Thailand?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Australia Dies in New Zealand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Australia dies in New Zealand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in New Zealand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Australia and New Zealand.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of Australia dies in New Zealand, the immediate priorities are obtaining medical or coronial clearance in New Zealand, appointing funeral directors to coordinate trans-Tasman repatriation or a local service, registering the death with New Zealand Births, Deaths and Marriages, and completing survivor benefit, tax, and estate steps across Australia and New Zealand.

steps.title: Medical Certification and Police or Coroner Clearance in New Zealand
steps.html:
All civil registration and burial, cremation, or repatriation permits in New Zealand begin with official medical certification or coronial authorization [1][2]:

  • Expected death in a hospital, hospice, or aged-care facility: A registered doctor or nurse practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form HP4720, or an equivalent electronic Death Documents certification) so a funeral director can take the deceased into care [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death outside a hospital: Call 111 immediately for New Zealand Police and ambulance services [1][2]. When a death is unexpected, unnatural, or has an unknown cause, police report the death to the Duty Coroner under Coronial Services of New Zealand (National Initial Investigation Office: 0800 266 800) [2]. The Duty Coroner determines whether a post-mortem examination is required and issues the coronial authorization to release the body before burial, cremation, or international transfer can proceed [2].

steps.title: Insurance Verification, Funeral Directors, and Consular Support
steps.html:
Before entering into private funeral or freight contracts, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance [5]. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team first, as the insurer normally appoints the funeral coordinators and covers repatriation costs directly [5].

  • Appointing funeral directors in New Zealand and Australia: Appoint a funeral director in New Zealand (for example, in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch, or Queenstown) via the directory of the Funeral Directors Association of New Zealand to handle local care, death registration, embalming, and export documentation [3]. If repatriating the body to Australia, pair the New Zealand funeral home with a receiving funeral director in the destination Australian state or territory via Funerals Australia (formerly the Australian Funeral Directors Association) [4].
  • Australian consular assistance: Contact the Australian High Commission in Wellington (+64 4 473 6411), the Australian Consulate-General in Auckland (+64 9 921 8800), or the 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade on 1300 555 135 within Australia or +61 2 6261 3305 from overseas [5]. Consular officers can cancel the deceased's Australian passport and provide guidance on local administrative procedures, though the Australian Government cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [5].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in New Zealand and Document Recognition in Australia
steps.html:
Every death that occurs in New Zealand must be registered with Births, Deaths and Marriages (part of the Department of Internal Affairs, Freephone 0800 22 52 52 within New Zealand or +64 9 339 0852 from overseas) within 3 working days after the burial, cremation, or removal of the body from New Zealand [1]:

  • How registration is filed: When you engage a New Zealand funeral director, the funeral director normally submits the Notification of Death for Registration (Form BDM 28) along with the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (HP4720) or Coroner's authorization on your behalf and orders several official New Zealand Death Certificates [1].
  • Recognition in Australia and Apostille rules: An official New Zealand Death Certificate is issued in English and is widely accepted directly by Australian banks, superannuation funds, and government agencies [5][8]. Where an Australian Supreme Court probate registry requires formal authentication, the Department of Internal Affairs Authentication Unit in New Zealand can issue a Hague Apostille. Australian state and territory Registries of Births, Deaths and Marriages (such as the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages in Sydney or Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria in Melbourne) generally only register deaths that occur within their own state or territory, so the New Zealand Death Certificate serves as the primary legal proof of death in Australia [5][8].

steps.title: Repatriation to Australia Versus Local Burial or Cremation in New Zealand
steps.html:
The next of kin or executor chooses between repatriating the body or cremated ashes across the Tasman to Australia or holding a burial or cremation in New Zealand [1][5]:

  • Repatriation of human remains (body) to Australia: Your New Zealand funeral director arranges sanitary embalming, a sealed casket meeting international air transport standards, a Public Health Service non-infectious disease clearance, and air cargo clearance with the New Zealand Customs Service (0800 428 786) [6]. Upon arrival at the destination airport in Australia (such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, or Perth), the Australian Border Force and biosecurity officers under the Department of Health and Aged Care inspect the documentation; human remains accompanied by an official New Zealand Death Certificate and free of biosecurity contaminants do not require an advance human biosecurity import permit, and your receiving Australian funeral director manages customs clearance and transfer [7].
  • Bringing cremated ashes to Australia: If cremation takes place in New Zealand, cremated ashes can be carried in hand luggage (in a screening-compliant container per airline rules) or sent via international freight accompanied by the official New Zealand Death Certificate and cremation certificate [6][7]. Under Australian border biosecurity rules, clean human ashes do not require an import permit, provided the urn is free of soil or plant material; wooden urns must be declared on the Incoming Passenger Card for biosecurity inspection [7].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, Superannuation, Tax, and Probate in Australia and New Zealand
steps.html:
Once you receive the official New Zealand Death Certificate, complete the benefit, tax, and estate steps in Australia and, if the deceased lived or worked in New Zealand, with New Zealand agencies:

  • Australian notifications, pensions, tax, and probate: Notify Services Australia within 28 days on the Bereavement Line (132 300 within Australia or +61 3 6222 3455 from overseas) to update Centrelink, Medicare, and Age Pension records (including any bilateral social security agreement pension with New Zealand) and check eligibility for bereavement payments [8]. Because the Australian Death Notification Service requires an Australian state or territory death certificate for online verification, notify Australian banks, insurers, and superannuation funds directly using the New Zealand Death Certificate to claim superannuation death benefits and attached life insurance [8]. Notify the Australian Taxation Office on 13 28 61 (or +61 2 6216 1111 from overseas) to lodge a Notification of a Deceased Person, file a final "Date of Death" tax return (covering 1 July to the date of death), and file estate trust returns if the estate earns post-death income [9]. For sole-name Australian real estate or substantial bank assets, apply for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration from the relevant Australian State or Territory Supreme Court (or reseal a New Zealand High Court probate grant under Australian state probate resealing laws).
  • New Zealand benefits, ACC, KiwiSaver, tax, and probate: You can use the New Zealand Government's Te Hokinga a-Wairua End of Life Service guide to coordinate local notifications [1]. If the deceased received New Zealand Superannuation or benefits, notify Work and Income (Ministry of Social Development, 0800 559 009) and check eligibility for a means-tested Funeral Grant; if the death resulted from an accident in New Zealand, check with the Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) regarding an accidental death funeral grant and survivor support [10]. Notify Inland Revenue (0800 227 774 or +64 4 978 0779 from overseas) to finalize New Zealand tax affairs up to the date of death, contact the deceased's KiwiSaver provider to release KiwiSaver funds to the estate, and apply to the High Court of New Zealand (in Wellington) if a New Zealand Grant of Probate or resealing of an Australian probate grant is needed for New Zealand assets exceeding the statutory small-estate threshold [11].

Which city or region in New Zealand the death occurred in, and which Australian state or territory the deceased lived in or held assets in? 2. title: What to Do When a Citizen of New Zealand Dies in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of New Zealand Dies in Australia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of New Zealand dies in Australia: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Australia, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in New Zealand and Australia.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When a citizen or resident of New Zealand dies in Australia, the immediate priorities are securing medical or coronial clearance in the Australian state or territory of death, appointing funeral directors to coordinate trans-Tasman repatriation or a local funeral, registering the death with the relevant Australian state or territory Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, and completing pension, tax, and estate steps across New Zealand and Australia.

steps.title: Medical Certification and Police or Coroner Clearance in Australia
steps.html:
Every burial, cremation, and international transfer permit in Australia requires either a doctor's medical certificate or a state/territory coroner's release [1][7]:

  • Expected death in a hospital, hospice, or aged-care facility: An attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) within 48 hours, allowing an appointed funeral director to transfer the deceased into mortuary care [1][7].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexpected death outside a hospital: Call Triple Zero (000) immediately for state or territory police and ambulance services [7]. When a death is unexpected, unnatural, violent, or lacks a known medical cause, police refer the case to the relevant State or Territory Coroner (for example, the Coroners Court of New South Wales in Sydney or the Coroners Court of Victoria in Melbourne) [1]. The Coroner determines whether a forensic post-mortem examination is required and issues the coronial release and cause-of-death documentation once the examination concludes [1].

steps.title: Insurance Verification, Funeral Directors, and New Zealand Consular Support
steps.html:
Before entering into private funeral or air-cargo commitments, check whether the deceased held travel, medical-assistance, or repatriation insurance [3]. If a policy is active, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance team first, as the insurer normally appoints the funeral coordinators and funds repatriation directly [3].

  • Appointing funeral directors in Australia and New Zealand: Appoint an accredited funeral director in the Australian state or territory of death via Funerals Australia (formerly the Australian Funeral Directors Association) to handle mortuary transfer, state death registration, embalming, and export clearance [4]. If repatriating the body to New Zealand, coordinate with a receiving funeral director in New Zealand (such as in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch) via the Funeral Directors Association of New Zealand [5].
  • New Zealand consular assistance: Contact the New Zealand High Commission in Canberra (+61 2 6270 4211, email CBAReception@mfat.govt.nz), the New Zealand Consulate-General in Sydney (+61 2 9270 5900, email sydney.reception@mfat.govt.nz), or the 24-hour consular emergency line of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (SafeTravel) on +64 4 439 8000 (or 0800 30 10 30 within New Zealand) [2][3]. Consular staff provide guidance on cross-border procedures and local funeral providers, though the New Zealand Government cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [3].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration in Australia and Document Recognition in New Zealand
steps.html:
Under Australian law, every death occurring in Australia must be registered with the Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) in the state or territory where the death took place (for example, the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages on 13 77 88 in New South Wales, Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria in Melbourne, or the Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages in Brisbane) [1][7]:

  • How registration is filed: In Australia, your appointed funeral director normally submits the death registration statement and the doctor's Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) or Coroner's certificate to the state or territory BDM (within 7 days of burial or cremation in New South Wales, or the applicable state statutory window) and orders official Australian Death Certificates on your behalf [1].
  • Recognition in New Zealand: Official Australian state or territory Death Certificates are issued in English and are accepted directly by New Zealand banks, KiwiSaver providers, Work and Income, and the High Court of New Zealand without translation [8][9]. If a formal authentication is ever requested for legal proceedings, the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) Passport Office can issue a Hague Apostille. Note that New Zealand Births, Deaths and Marriages (Department of Internal Affairs) only registers deaths occurring in New Zealand (or on a New Zealand-registered aircraft or ship), so the Australian state or territory Death Certificate serves as the permanent legal proof of death in New Zealand.

steps.title: Repatriation to New Zealand Versus Local Burial or Cremation in Australia
steps.html:
The next of kin or executor chooses between repatriating the body or cremated ashes across the Tasman to New Zealand or holding a burial or cremation in Australia [3][6]:

  • Repatriation of human remains (body) to New Zealand: Your Australian funeral director arranges sanitary embalming, sealing in an airline-approved hermetically lined casket, a non-infectious disease health certificate, and export clearance with the Australian Border Force [4][6]. Upon arrival at the New Zealand entry airport, your receiving New Zealand funeral director clears the shipment through the New Zealand Customs Service (0800 428 786) and Public Health Service / Ministry for Primary Industries biosecurity officers using the air waybill, the importer's identification, the Australian Death Certificate, and the embalming/health certificates [6].
  • Bringing cremated ashes to New Zealand: If cremation is carried out in Australia, cremated ashes can be carried in hand luggage on a flight to New Zealand or shipped via international freight [6]. When travelling with human ashes in accompanied baggage, no formal New Zealand Customs clearance is required on arrival, though you should carry the official Australian Death Certificate and cremation certificate for airline security and declare the urn to biosecurity officers if the container is made of wood or organic material [6].

steps.title: Post-Death Notifications, Pensions, KiwiSaver, Superannuation, Tax, and Probate in New Zealand and Australia
steps.html:
Once you receive the official Australian state or territory Death Certificate, complete the benefit, tax, and estate steps in both countries:

  • New Zealand notifications, benefits, KiwiSaver, tax, and probate: You can consult the New Zealand Government's Te Hokinga a-Wairua End of Life Service guide for a cross-agency overview. Notify Work and Income (Ministry of Social Development, 0800 559 009) to stop or adjust New Zealand Superannuation or benefits and check eligibility for a means-tested Funeral Grant or Survivor's Grant (and check with ACC if the death was accidental and covered under New Zealand accident compensation rules) [8]. Notify Inland Revenue (0800 227 774 within New Zealand or +64 4 978 0779 from overseas) to file a final individual income tax return up to the date of death and obtain an estate IRD number if the estate continues to earn income [9]. Contact the deceased's KiwiSaver scheme provider directly with the Australian Death Certificate and proof of estate authority to release KiwiSaver balances, and apply to the High Court of New Zealand in Wellington for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration (or reseal an Australian Supreme Court grant) if New Zealand estate assets exceed the statutory small-estate threshold.
  • Australian notifications, superannuation, tax, and probate: Because the death is registered with an Australian state or territory BDM, you can use the free Australian Death Notification Service online to notify participating Australian banks, insurers, and utilities in a single step once the state Death Certificate is issued [10]. If the deceased held Australian Medicare, Centrelink benefits, or an Australian Age Pension, notify Services Australia within 28 days on 132 300 (or +61 3 6222 3455 from overseas) [7]. Contact any Australian superannuation fund directly to claim superannuation death benefits and attached life insurance, notify the Australian Taxation Office on 13 28 61 (or +61 2 6216 1111 from overseas) to lodge a Notification of a Deceased Person and final "Date of Death" tax return [11], and apply to the relevant Australian State or Territory Supreme Court for a Grant of Probate (or resealing of a New Zealand High Court probate grant) if the deceased held Australian real estate or substantial Australian bank balances.
