title: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Germany dies in Greece: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Greece, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Germany and Greece.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Germany dies in Greece, medical certification and civil registration take place first in the Greek municipality where the death occurred, while a licensed funeral director coordinates with Greek health authorities, the German diplomatic missions in Greece, and a receiving funeral provider in Germany for international repatriation or local disposition [1][2][3]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death and Emergency or Forensic Clearance in Greece
steps.html:
Before civil registration, burial, cremation, or international repatriation can proceed, a licensed physician or forensic medical examiner in Greece must issue the official Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου) [1][2][3]:

  • Death in a Greek hospital or clinic: When a person dies in a public or private hospital in Greece (for example, in Athens, Thessaloniki, Heraklion, or Rhodes), the attending hospital physician verifies the death, completes the Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου) stating the exact medical cause of death, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary until an appointed funeral director arrives [2][3]. Provide the deceased's German passport (Reisepass) or national identity card (Personalausweis) so personal details match across Greek and German records [1][2].
  • Death at a hotel, private residence, beach, or public place: Call the National Centre for Emergency Care (EKAB on 166), the European emergency number (112), and the Hellenic Police (100) (or the Hellenic Coast Guard on 108 if the death occurred at sea or on a beach) [1][2].
  • Forensic autopsy (Ιατροδικαστική Υπηρεσία) for sudden, unattended, or foreign-national deaths: Under Greek law, whenever a death occurs outside a hospital without prior medical attendance, is sudden or unexplained, or involves a foreign national where Greek authorities require post-mortem clearance, the police or coast guard orders a mandatory forensic examination and autopsy by the regional Forensic Medical Service (Ιατροδικαστική Υπηρεσία) of the Ministry of Justice (such as the Forensic Medical Service in Athens, Piraeus, Thessaloniki, or Crete) [1]. The forensic pathologist issues the Medical Certificate of Death and release order once the examination is complete [1][2].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Funeral Directors in Greece and Germany, and Contact the German Missions
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel medical insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung with Rücktransport im Todesfall), credit-card repatriation cover, or an automobile club protection policy (Schutzbrief), and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance team first [1]. Note that German diplomatic missions cannot pay or advance funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [1].

  • Appointing a licensed Greek funeral home (Γραφείο Τελετών): In Greece, a licensed Greek funeral home (Γραφείο Τελετών) collects the deceased from the hospital or forensic morgue, files the municipal death registration, and arranges embalming, a hermetically sealed coffin, and air or road transport permits [1][2][3].
  • Coordinating with a receiving funeral provider in Germany (Bestattungsunternehmen): For repatriation to Germany, the family can instruct a receiving German funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen) in the destination municipality, which coordinates directly with a Greek partner funeral home in compliance with the funeral laws of the relevant German federal state (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and mandatory cemetery interment rules (Friedhofszwang) [1][4]. You can locate a qualified German funeral provider through the federal professional association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (phone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour emergency line +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de) [4]. Clarvia lists official directories and consular resources for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Contacting the German Embassy in Athens or Consulate General in Thessaloniki: Contact the German Embassy Athens (Botschaft der Bundesrepublik Deutschland Athen, Karaoli & Dimitriou 3, 106 75 Athens; phone +30 210 7285 111, emergency consular duty line +30 210 7285 264) or, for northern Greece, the German Consulate General in Thessaloniki (phone +30 2310 251 120) [1]. The German missions provide informational lists of local funeral homes experienced in international repatriation and assist with next-of-kin authorizations if family members remain in Germany [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry in Greece Within 24 Hours and Obtain Multilingual Extracts for Germany
steps.html:
Under Greek civil registration law (Law 344/1976), a death in Greece must be declared within 24 hours of occurrence (or within 24 hours of the forensic pathologist's release) [2][3]:

  • Greek Death Certificate (Ληξιαρχική Πράξη Θανάτου): In practice, the appointed Greek funeral director submits the signed Medical Certificate of Death (Ιατρικό Πιστοποιητικό Θανάτου), the deceased's German passport or identity card, and family status details in person to the municipal Civil Registry Office (Ληξιαρχείο / Lixiarcheio) of the municipality of death (for example, the Municipality of Athens or Municipality of Thessaloniki) to obtain the official Greek Death Certificate (Ληξιαρχική Πράξη Θανάτου) and burial or transfer permit; once registered, digital extracts can also be accessed via the national portal gov.gr [2][3].
  • Multilingual CIEC Form C extract and recognition in Germany: Request several copies of the Greek Death Certificate together with a multilingual extract on Form C (Formblatt C) issued under the Vienna CIEC Convention of 8 September 1976 [1][6]. Because both Greece and Germany are contracting states to the 1976 Vienna Convention and EU Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 applies between EU Member States, the multilingual Form C death extract is accepted directly in Germany without a Hague Apostille or sworn translation [1][6].
  • German Standesamt rules (§ 28 and § 36 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG): Whereas a domestic death inside Germany must be reported to the local Standesamt no later than the third following working day under § 28 Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) [5], a death occurring in Greece is registered first at the Greek Lixiarcheio [1][3]. With the Greek Death Certificate (or multilingual Form C), surviving relatives (spouse, registered partner, parents, or children) may subsequently apply to the German Standesamt of the deceased's last German residence (or Standesamt I in Berlin if the deceased had no German residence) for optional subsequent registration in the German death register (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland under § 36 PStG) to obtain a domestic German Sterbeurkunde and Form C extracts [1][6].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to Germany and Local Burial or Cremation in Greece
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes and family arrangements, you may choose international repatriation to Germany or local burial or cremation in Greece [1][4]:

  • Repatriating casketed remains to Germany (Leichenpass / Mortuary Laissez-Passer): Both Greece and Germany apply international mortuary transfer standards (the 1937 International Berlin Agreement / Internationales Berliner Abkommen and the Strasbourg Agreement) [1]. The Greek funeral home arranges mandatory arterial embalming, places the body in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin (verlöteter Zinksarg) inside a wooden outer casket, and obtains the non-contagious disease certificate and multilingual mortuary laissez-passer (Leichenpass) from the competent Greek Public Health Directorate, coordinated where required with the German Embassy Athens or Consulate General in Thessaloniki [1]. Because forensic and administrative formalities in Greece typically take 3 to 10 days, the German missions advise confirming a binding funeral date in Germany only after flight and transfer dates are finalized [1].
  • Cremation in Greece and transporting the urn to Germany (Urnenüberführung and Friedhofszwang): If the family chooses cremation in Greece (for example, at the licensed Ritsona Crematorium near Chalkida) followed by transferring the cremated ashes to Germany, note that all German federal states enforce mandatory cemetery interment (Friedhofszwang under the respective Landesbestattungsgesetze) [1][4]. Ashes cannot be kept privately at home in Germany; to ship or carry a sealed urn to Germany, you must obtain an official acceptance certificate (Übernahmebescheinigung) from the receiving German cemetery administration (Friedhofsverwaltung) or a licensed German funeral provider (Bestattungsunternehmen), accompanied by the Greek Death Certificate (Form C) and the official cremation certificate [1][4].
  • Local burial or cremation in Greece: If interment or ash placement takes place entirely in a municipal cemetery in Greece, the Greek funeral home arranges the municipal burial or cremation permit directly with the local municipality [2][3].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Pension, Benefit, Tax, and Probate Steps in Germany and Greece
steps.html:
Once the Greek Death Certificate and multilingual Form C extract are issued, complete the post-death benefit and estate administration steps in both countries:

  • In Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, Health Insurance, and Nachlassgericht):
    • Pensions and Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days): Notify Renten Service der Deutschen Post (phone +49 221 569 2777) and Deutsche Rentenversicherung (toll-free 0800 1000 4800 within Germany, or +49 30 865 0 from abroad) immediately so old-age pension overpayments stop [7][8]. A surviving spouse or registered civil partner can apply through Renten Service der Deutschen Post within 30 days of the death for the three-month bereavement advance payment (Sterbevierteljahr, paid at the full rate of the deceased's pension for the three calendar months following the month of death) [8], and apply to Deutsche Rentenversicherung for a survivor pension (Witwenrente or Witwerrente) or orphan's pension (Waisenrente) [7].
    • Statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung): Submit the Death Certificate to the deceased's German health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) to terminate membership and update any family co-insurance (Familienversicherung) [7].
    • Probate and Certificate of Inheritance (Nachlassgericht / Erbschein): Any person holding a handwritten will must deliver it promptly to the German probate court (Nachlassgericht at the local Amtsgericht of the deceased's last German habitual residence, which also receives automatic electronic notification from the Central Register of Wills / Zentrales Testamentsregister) [1]. To access German bank accounts or real estate where no trans-mortem power of attorney or notarized will suffices, heirs apply to the Nachlassgericht for a German Certificate of Inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession (Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis under EU Regulation No 650/2012) [1]. Note that under German law (§ 1944 BGB), the deadline to renounce an inheritance (Erbausschlagung) is 6 weeks, extended to 6 months if the deceased had their last habitual residence only abroad or if the heir was abroad when learning of the inheritance [1].
  • In Greece (e-EFKA, AADE Inheritance Tax, and Κληρονομητήριο):
    • Greek social security (e-EFKA): If your family member was insured or receiving a pension in Greece, notify the Unified Social Security Fund (e-EFKA via gov.gr, phone 1555 in Greece) to claim the statutory reimbursement of funeral expenses (Έξοδα Κηδείας) and any Greek survivor pension (Σύνταξη λόγω θανάτου), coordinated with Germany under EU social security regulations [9].
    • Greek estate administration (Κληρονομητήριο and AADE): If the deceased held bank accounts, property, or other assets in Greece, heirs or an appointed Greek lawyer/notary obtain the Certificate of Closest Relatives and Certificate of Non-Publication of a Will via gov.gr, apply to the competent Greek court or notary for a Greek Certificate of Inheritance (Κληρονομητήριο) (or present a European Certificate of Succession), and file the Greek inheritance tax declaration with the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) within 12 months if the deceased passed away abroad or the heirs reside abroad (or 6 months domestically; renunciation of a Greek inheritance must be filed within 4 months, or 12 months when the deceased lived abroad or the heir resided abroad) [10].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your situation, in which municipality or island in Greece did the death occur, and are you planning repatriation to a specific German city or federal state (Bundesland) or local burial/cremation in Greece?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Germany dies in Portugal: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Portugal, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Germany and Portugal.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member. When a person with German citizenship or residence ties to Germany dies in Portugal, electronic medical certification and civil death registration take place first in Portugal, while the funeral agency coordinates the international sanitary transport permits with the German diplomatic mission in Lisbon and a receiving funeral provider in Germany [1][4][6]. Below are the five official steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain the electronic death certificate via SICO and medical or forensic clearance in Portugal
steps.html:
In Portugal, medical certification of death is registered electronically in the SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito, Death Certificate Information System) of the Directorate-General of Health (Direção-Geral da Saúde - DGS), managed by the Shared Services of the Ministry of Health (Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde - SPMS), which transmits the data directly to the civil registry [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility: The attending physician verifies the death, issues the electronic Death Certificate (Certificado de Óbito) directly in SICO, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary (for instance in Lisbon, Porto, Coimbra, or Faro) [1][2]. Provide the deceased person's German passport (Reisepass) or German identity card (Personalausweis) (as well as their EU citizen registration certificate or Portuguese tax identification number, NIF, if held) so that personal details match across the Portuguese and German registries [1][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Call the European emergency number 112 immediately (or contact the local PSP or GNR police) [1][2]. If death resulted from a known natural cause under medical care, the attending physician or local health authority officer (delegado de saúde) can verify the death and register the certificate in SICO [1][2].
  • Sudden, violent, or unexplained death: When a death occurs without prior medical attendance or a natural cause cannot be certified immediately, the police notify the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público), which orders the removal of the body to the forensic medical office of the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses - INMLCF) for autopsy or forensic examination [1][2]. Only after authorization from the Ministério Público and registration in SICO by the forensic physician can the funeral agency take custody of the body [1][2].

steps.title: Check insurance coverage, appoint funeral directors in Portugal and Germany, and contact the German Embassy
steps.html:
Before entering into independent financial commitments, check whether your family member held travel health insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung covering repatriation upon death, Rücktransport im Todesfall), credit card protection, or automobile club coverage (Schutzbrief), and contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance hotline first [4][5]. German diplomatic missions do not have public funds to pay for or advance funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [4][5].

  • Licensed funeral agency in Portugal: The family (or the insurer) must appoint a funeral agency (agência funerária) legally registered with the Directorate-General for Economic Activities (Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE / gov.pt portal), which also regulates funeral service standards and the basic social funeral (Funeral Social) [3]. Funeral providers in Portugal are also represented by sector associations such as the National Association of Funeral Companies (Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas - ANEL, telephone +351 218 687 978) or the Central Region Funeral Agents Association (Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro - AAFC) [3].
  • Receiving funeral director in Germany (Bestattungsunternehmen): To repatriate the body or urn to Germany, the Portuguese funeral agency coordinates with a funeral provider in Germany (Bestattungsunternehmen), which can be located through the federal association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (Federal Association of German Funeral Directors, telephone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour emergency line +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de), complying with the funeral laws of the relevant German federal state (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and the statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) [6]. Clarvia provides association and official references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific providers.
  • Contact the German Embassy in Portugal: Contact the Deutsche Botschaft Lissabon (Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in Lisbon, Campo dos Mártires da Pátria 38, 1169-043 Lisbon; general telephone +351 21 881 0210, after-hours duty telephone for consular emergencies +351 96 580 8092) [4][5]. The Embassy provides informational lists of local funeral agencies and guides relatives on powers of attorney or consular certifications if the family remains in Germany [4][5].

steps.title: Register the death with the Civil Registry (within 48 hours) and obtain the multilingual CIEC Form C for Germany
steps.html:
A death occurring in Portugal must be declared within the statutory deadline of 48 hours after medical verification of death or forensic release by the INMLCF [1]:

  • Free death registration (Assento de Óbito) and Vienna Convention multilingual certificate: In standard practice, the appointed funeral agency files the declaration at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) of the Institute of Registries and Notary (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado - IRN / Justiça.gov.pt portal, Registries Helpline +351 211 950 500), using the electronic SICO Death Certificate and the deceased person's German identification document [1]. The initial death entry (Assento de Óbito) is free of charge [1]. Immediately request several copies of the multilingual death certificate extract (certidão de óbito em modelo plurilingue, Form C / Formblatt C) under the CIEC Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 [1][8]. Because both Portugal and Germany are contracting states to the 1976 Vienna Convention and Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 applies, the multilingual Form C extract is recognized directly in Germany without a Hague Apostille or sworn translation [1][8].
  • Rules of the Standesamt in Germany (§ 28 and § 36 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG): Whereas a death occurring on German territory must be reported to the local Standesamt by the third following working day under Section 28 of the Civil Status Act (§ 28 PStG) to obtain the Sterbeurkunde and the multilingual extract on Formblatt C [7], a death in Portugal is registered first with the Portuguese Conservatória [1]. Using the Portuguese multilingual certificate (Form C), surviving family members (spouse, registered partner, parents, or children) may optionally apply for subsequent registration of the foreign death in the German civil register (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland, § 36 PStG) at the Standesamt of the deceased's last German residence (or Standesamt I in Berlin if the deceased never had a residence in Germany), thereby obtaining German death certificates (deutsche Sterbeurkunden) [4][8].

steps.title: Choose between international repatriation to Germany and local burial or cremation in Portugal
steps.html:
The family may choose either international repatriation of the body or ashes to Germany or a local funeral in Portugal [1][4][6]:

  • International repatriation of the body in a coffin to Germany (Livre-Trânsito Mortuário / Leichenpass): Portugal and Germany apply the international conventions on the transport of corpses (the 1937 International Berlin Agreement / Internationales Berliner Abkommen and the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement) [4][6]. The Portuguese funeral agency performs thanatological preparation (embalming), places the body in a hermetically sealed zinc coffin (caixão de zinco selado / verlöteter Zinksarg) inside a wooden outer coffin, and obtains the international mortuary transit permit (alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário / Leichenpass) from the competent health and police authorities in Portugal, in coordination with the Deutsche Botschaft Lissabon (or German honorary consulates in Porto, Lagos/Algarve, or Funchal, as well as consular information from the Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Consular Support Center of the Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs where applicable) [1][4][5].
  • Cremation in Portugal and transport of the urn to Germany (Friedhofszwang): If the family chooses cremation in Portugal followed by shipping or carrying the urn of ashes (Urnenüberführung) to Germany, please note that all German federal states enforce a statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) under their respective state funeral laws (Landesbestattungsgesetze) [6]. In Germany, it is not permitted to keep an urn at home or hand it freely to private individuals; to authorize shipment or entry of the urn into Germany, you must present the cremation certificate, the multilingual death certificate (Form C), and a certificate of acceptance (Übernahmebescheinigung) issued by a German cemetery administration (Friedhofsverwaltung) or a German funeral director (Bestattungsunternehmen) [4][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in Portugal: If burial or placement of the ashes takes place entirely at a municipal cemetery or crematorium in Portugal, only the local Portuguese municipal permits arranged by the local funeral agency are required [1][3].

steps.title: Handle survivor pensions, social benefits, taxes, and probate in Germany and Portugal
steps.html:
With the Portuguese Assento de Óbito and the multilingual certificate (Form C), complete the administrative and probate filings in both countries:

  • In Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, health insurance, and Nachlassgericht):
    • German pensions and Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days): Report the death immediately to the Renten Service der Deutschen Post (German Post Pension Service, telephone +49 221 569 2777) and to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German Statutory Pension Insurance, toll-free in Germany 0800 1000 4800 or from abroad +49 30 865 0) to stop old-age pension payments [9][10]. The surviving spouse or registered partner can apply through the Renten Service der Deutschen Post within 30 days of the death for the advance payment covering the three-month bereavement quarter (Sterbevierteljahr, paid at the full rate of the deceased's pension for the three months following the month of death) [10], and apply to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung for a widow's or widower's pension (Witwenrente or Witwerrente) or orphan's pension (Waisenrente) [9].
    • Statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung): Notify the German health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) by submitting the death certificate to close the membership and update any family coverage (Familienversicherung) [9].
    • Probate court (Nachlassgericht / Erbschein): Any will held in private possession must be delivered to the German probate court (Nachlassgericht at the local court, Amtsgericht, of the last habitual residence in Germany, which also consults the Central Register of Wills, Zentrales Testamentsregister) [4]. To access bank accounts or real estate in Germany where no post-mortem power of attorney or notarized will suffices, heirs apply to the Nachlassgericht for a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession (Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis, Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) [4]. The statutory deadline in Germany to renounce an inheritance (Erbausschlagung, Section 1944 BGB) is 6 weeks, extended to 6 months if the deceased resided exclusively abroad or if the heir was abroad when learning of the inheritance [4].
  • In Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças, and Tax Authority):
    • Social Security benefits: If your family member contributed to or received a pension in Portugal, report the death to Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, telephone +351 210 545 400 or 300 502 502) to claim the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days of the death), Funeral Expense Reimbursement (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days under the convergent CGA scheme or up to 6 months under the general scheme for the person who paid the funeral expenses when there are no relatives entitled to the Death Grant), and the Survivor's Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [11].
    • Declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and Stamp Duty filing (by the end of the 3rd month): If the deceased held bank accounts, real estate, or other assets in Portugal, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must arrange the declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) at an Espaço Óbito or Balcão das Heranças desk of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado and file the death notification and schedule of assets for Stamp Duty purposes (Imposto do Selo, Modelo 1) with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira - AT / Finanças) by the end of the third month following the month in which the death occurred [1][12].

closingQuestion: So that we can tailor this information to your specific situation, in which municipality in Portugal did the death occur, to which city or federal state (Bundesland) in Germany do you plan to repatriate the deceased or handle probate, or are you choosing local burial or cremation in Portugal?

pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Portugal e Alemanha: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Portugal e Alemanha: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos as nossas sinceras condolências pelo falecimento do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa com cidadania ou residência na Alemanha falece em Portugal, a certificação médica eletrónica e o registo civil decorrem primeiro em território português, enquanto a agência funerária articula as licenças sanitárias de transporte internacional com a representação diplomática alemã em Lisboa e uma funerária recetora na Alemanha [1][4][6]. Abaixo descrevem-se os cinco passos oficiais por ordem.

steps.title: Obter o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico através do SICO e a liberação médica ou médico-legal em Portugal
steps.html:
Em Portugal, a certificação médica do falecimento é registada eletronicamente no SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito) da Direção-Geral da Saúde (DGS), gerido pelos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde (SPMS), que transmite os dados diretamente para o registo civil [1][2]:

  • Óbito em hospital, clínica ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente verifica o óbito, emite diretamente o Certificado de Óbito eletrónico no SICO e transfere o corpo para a casa mortuária da unidade hospitalar (por exemplo, em Lisboa, Porto, Coimbra ou Faro) [1][2]. Entregue o passaporte alemão (Reisepass) ou o bilhete de identidade alemão (Personalausweis) da pessoa falecida (e o certificado de registo de cidadão da União Europeia ou número de contribuinte português, caso o possuísse) para que os dados pessoais coincidam nos registos de Portugal e da Alemanha [1][4].
  • Óbito no domicílio, hotel ou via pública: Ligue de imediato para o número europeu de emergência 112 (ou contacte a PSP ou a GNR da área) [1][2]. Se a morte tiver ocorrido por causa natural conhecida sob acompanhamento médico, o médico assistente ou o delegado de saúde (autoridade de saúde local) pode verificar o óbito e registar o certificado no SICO [1][2].
  • Morte súbita, violenta ou de causa desconhecida: Quando o falecimento ocorre sem assistência médica prévia ou não é possível atestar de imediato uma causa natural, a autoridade policial comunica o facto ao Ministério Público, que determina a remoção do corpo para o gabinete médico-legal do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) para autópsia ou exame pericial [1][2]. Só após a autorização do Ministério Público e o registo no SICO pelo médico legista é que a agência funerária pode receber o corpo [1][2].

steps.title: Verificar seguros, contratar agências funerárias em Portugal e na Alemanha e contactar a Embaixada da Alemanha
steps.html:
Antes de assumir compromissos financeiros autónomos, verifique se o seu familiar possuía seguro de saúde de viagem (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung com cobertura de Rücktransport im Todesfall), proteção de cartão de crédito ou cobertura de clube automóvel (Schutzbrief), contactando primeiro a linha de assistência 24 horas da seguradora [4][5]. As representações diplomáticas alemãs não dispõem de verba para custear ou adiantar despesas de funeral, cremação ou trasladação [4][5].

  • Agência funerária habilitada em Portugal: A família (ou a seguradora) deve mandatar uma agência funerária legalmente habilitada na Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE / portal gov.pt), onde estão também reguladas as normas da atividade funerária e do Funeral Social [3]. As empresas do setor encontram-se igualmente agrupadas em associações como a Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, telefone +351 218 687 978) ou a Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro (AAFC) [3].
  • Agência funerária recetora na Alemanha (Bestattungsunternehmen): Para a trasladação do corpo ou da urna para a Alemanha, a funerária portuguesa coordena o serviço com uma empresa funerária na Alemanha (Bestattungsunternehmen), que pode ser localizada através da associação federal Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (telefone +49 211 16008-10, linha de emergência 24 horas +49 211 16008-86, e-mail info@bestatter.de), respeitando as leis funerárias do respetivo estado federado alemão (Landesbestattungsgesetze) e a obrigatoriedade legal de cemitério (Friedhofszwang) [6]. A Clarvia disponibiliza referências associativas e oficiais apenas para orientação e não recomenda, não endossa nem classifica prestadores específicos.
  • Contactar a Embaixada da Alemanha em Portugal: Contacte a Deutsche Botschaft Lissabon (Embaixada da República Federal da Alemanha em Lisboa, Campo dos Mártires da Pátria 38, 1169-043 Lisboa; telefone geral +351 21 881 0210, telefone de plantão para emergências consulares fora do horário de expediente +351 96 580 8092) [4][5]. A Embaixada disponibiliza listas informativas de agências funerárias locais e orienta os familiares sobre procurações ou reconhecimentos consulares caso a família permaneça na Alemanha [4][5].

steps.title: Declarar o óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil (48 horas) e obter a certidão plurilingue (Modelo C) para a Alemanha
steps.html:
O falecimento ocorrido em Portugal tem de ser declarado no prazo legal de 48 horas após a verificação médica do óbito ou após a liberação pelo INMLCF [1]:

  • Assento de Óbito gratuito e certidão plurilingue da Convenção de Viena: Na prática habitual, a agência funerária contratada efetua a declaração perante qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / portal Justiça.gov.pt, Linha Registos +351 211 950 500), com base no Certificado de Óbito eletrónico do SICO e no documento de identificação alemão da pessoa falecida [1]. O registo inicial (Assento de Óbito) é gratuito [1]. Solicite imediatamente várias cópias da certidão de óbito em modelo plurilingue (Fórmula C / Formblatt C) ao abrigo da Convenção de Viena da CIEC de 8 de setembro de 1976 [1][8]. Como Portugal e a Alemanha são Estados contratantes da Convenção de Viena de 1976 e se aplica o Regulamento (UE) 2016/1191, a certidão plurilingue (Modelo C) é reconhecida diretamente na Alemanha sem necessidade de Apostila da Haia nem de tradução ajuramentada [1][8].
  • Regras do Standesamt na Alemanha (§ 28 e § 36 da Personenstandsgesetz - PStG): Enquanto um óbito ocorrido em território alemão tem de ser comunicado ao Standesamt do local do falecimento até ao terceiro dia útil seguinte nos termos do § 28 da Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) para emissão da Sterbeurkunde e do extrato plurilingue no Formblatt C [7], um óbito ocorrido em Portugal é registado primeiro na Conservatória portuguesa [1]. Com a certidão plurilingue portuguesa (Modelo C), os familiares sobrevivos (cônjuge, parceiro registado, pais ou filhos) podem requerer opcionalmente a transcrição posterior do óbito no registo civil alemão (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland, § 36 PStG) junto ao Standesamt do último domicílio na Alemanha (ou ao Standesamt I in Berlin se nunca houve domicílio na Alemanha), obtendo assim certidões de óbito alemãs (deutsche Sterbeurkunden) [4][8].

steps.title: Escolher entre a trasladação internacional para a Alemanha e o sepultamento ou cremação local em Portugal
steps.html:
A família pode optar pela trasladação internacional do corpo ou das cinzas para a Alemanha ou pela realização do funeral em Portugal [1][4][6]:

  • Trasladação internacional do corpo em caixão para a Alemanha (Livre-Trânsito Mortuário / Leichenpass): Portugal e a Alemanha aplicam as convenções internacionais sobre transporte de cadáveres (Convenção Internacional de Berlim de 1937 / Internationales Berliner Abkommen e Acordo de Estrasburgo de 1973) [4][6]. A agência funerária portuguesa trata da preparação tanatológica (embalsamamento), acondiciona o corpo num caixão de zinco hermeticamente selado (verlöteter Zinksarg) dentro de uma urna exterior de madeira e obtém o alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário (Leichenpass) junto da autoridade sanitária e policial competente em Portugal, em articulação com a Deutsche Botschaft Lissabon (ou consulados honorários alemães no Porto, Lagos/Algarve ou Funchal, bem como informação consular do Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas / Centro de Atendimento Consular do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros quando aplicável) [1][4][5].
  • Cremação em Portugal e transporte da urna de cinzas para a Alemanha (Friedhofszwang): Caso a família opte pela cremação em Portugal seguida do envio ou transporte da urna de cinzas (Urnenüberführung) para a Alemanha, tenha em atenção que todos os estados federados alemães impõem a obrigatoriedade legal de cemitério (Friedhofszwang) nas respetivas Landesbestattungsgesetze [6]. Na Alemanha não é permitido guardar a urna em casa nem entregá-la livremente a particulares; para autorizar a expedição ou entrada da urna na Alemanha, é necessário apresentar o certificado de cremação, a certidão de óbito plurilingue (Modelo C) e uma declaração de aceitação (Übernahmebescheinigung) emitida pela administração de um cemitério alemão (Friedhofsverwaltung) ou por uma agência funerária alemã (Bestattungsunternehmen) [4][6].
  • Sepultamento ou cremação local em Portugal: Se a inumação ou a deposição das cinzas ocorrer integralmente num cemitério municipal ou crematório em Portugal, aplicam-se apenas as licenças municipais portuguesas tratadas pela agência funerária local [1][3].

steps.title: Tratar das pensões de sobrevivência, prestações sociais, impostos e sucessão na Alemanha e em Portugal
steps.html:
Com o Assento de Óbito português e a certidão plurilingue (Modelo C), cumpra as comunicações administrativas e sucessórias nos dois países:

  • Na Alemanha (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, seguro de saúde e Nachlassgericht):
    • Pensões alemãs e Sterbevierteljahr (no prazo de 30 dias): Comunique de imediato o falecimento ao Renten Service der Deutschen Post (telefone +49 221 569 2777) e à Deutsche Rentenversicherung (telefone gratuito na Alemanha 0800 1000 4800 ou a partir do estrangeiro +49 30 865 0) para suspender o pagamento da pensão de reforma [9][10]. O cônjuge ou parceiro registado sobrevivo pode requerer através do Renten Service der Deutschen Post, no prazo de 30 dias após o óbito, o adiantamento correspondente ao trimestre de luto (Sterbevierteljahr, pago pelo valor integral da pensão da pessoa falecida durante os três meses seguintes ao mês do óbito) [10], bem como requerer junto da Deutsche Rentenversicherung a pensão de viuvez (Witwenrente ou Witwerrente) ou pensão de orfandade (Waisenrente) [9].
    • Seguro público de saúde (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung): Notifique a caixa de seguro de saúde alemã (Krankenkasse) enviando a certidão de óbito para encerramento da inscrição e atualização de eventual seguro familiar (Familienversicherung) [9].
    • Tribunal de sucessões (Nachlassgericht / Erbschein): Qualquer testamento em posse de particulares deve ser entregue ao tribunal de sucessões (Nachlassgericht junto do Amtsgericht da última residência habitual na Alemanha, que consulta também o Registo Central de Testamentos / Zentrales Testamentsregister) [4]. Para movimentar contas bancárias ou imóveis na Alemanha quando não exista procuração pós-morte ou testamento notarial suficiente, os herdeiros requerem ao Nachlassgericht o certificado sucessório alemão (Erbschein) ou o Certificado Sucessório Europeu (Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis, Regulamento (UE) n.º 650/2012) [4]. O prazo legal na Alemanha para renunciar a uma herança (Erbausschlagung, § 1944 do BGB) é de 6 semanas, alargado para 6 meses se a pessoa falecida residia apenas no estrangeiro ou se o herdeiro se encontrava no estrangeiro quando tomou conhecimento da abertura da sucessão [4].
  • Em Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças e Autoridade Tributária):
    • Prestações da Segurança Social: Se o seu familiar descontava ou recebia pensão em Portugal, comunique o óbito à Segurança Social (telefone +351 210 545 400 ou 300 502 502) para requerer o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do falecimento), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias no regime convergente da CGA ou até 6 meses no regime geral para quem custeou o funeral quando não existam familiares com direito a subsídio por morte) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [11].
    • Habilitação de herdeiros e participação do Imposto do Selo (até ao final do 3.º mês): Caso a pessoa falecida possuísse contas bancárias, imóveis ou outros bens em Portugal, o cabeça-de-casal deve tratar da habilitação de herdeiros num Espaço Óbito ou no Balcão das Heranças do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado e apresentar à Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (AT / Finanças) a participação do óbito e a relação de bens para efeitos de Imposto do Selo (Modelo 1) até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao mês em que ocorreu o falecimento [1][12].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos adaptar estas informações ao seu caso concreto, em que município de Portugal ocorreu o falecimento, para qual cidade ou estado federado (Bundesland) da Alemanha pretendem realizar a trasladação ou tratar da sucessão, ou optam por sepultamento ou cremação local em Portugal?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Germany Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Germany dies in Thailand: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Thailand, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Germany and Thailand.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a citizen or resident of Germany dies in Thailand, medical certification, Thai civil registration, consular release letters, and international repatriation or local cremation must be coordinated between Thai authorities, the German Embassy in Bangkok, and receiving funeral and administrative institutions in Germany [1][2][3]. Below is the 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Emergency or Forensic Clearance in Thailand
steps.html:
Before civil registration, cremation, or international repatriation can proceed, Thai medical or forensic authorities must issue the official medical confirmation of death [1][2][3]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: When a person dies under medical care in a Thai public or private hospital, the attending hospital physician issues the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1) (Bai Rab Rong Kan Tai), which states the medical cause of death in Thai and is required for civil registration [2][3].
  • Death in a residence, hotel, or public place: For any sudden, accidental, or unattended death outside a hospital, call the Royal Thai Police (191), the Tourist Police (1155), or emergency medical services (EMS on 1669) immediately [1][2]. Under Thai law, deaths occurring outside a hospital or from unnatural or undetermined causes require a police investigation report and a mandatory forensic autopsy performed at the Police General Hospital Institute of Forensic Medicine in Bangkok or a designated provincial forensic hospital (such as in Chiang Mai, Phuket, or Chonburi) [1][2][3].
  • Mandatory Embassy release letter for foreign nationals: Thai hospitals, police, and forensic morgues will not release the body of a German citizen to next of kin or an appointed funeral director until the German Embassy Bangkok issues an official consular letter of release (no-objection letter) confirming who is authorized to collect the remains and register the death [1][2][5].

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Licensed Funeral Directors in Thailand and Germany, and Contact the German Embassy
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel medical insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung with repatriation cover / Rücktransport im Todesfall), credit-card coverage, or a death benefit policy (Sterbegeldversicherung), and contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance center first [1][2]. Note that the German Embassy cannot pay or advance hospital, funeral, cremation, or repatriation costs [1][2].

  • Contacting the German Embassy in Thailand: Report the death immediately to the German Embassy Bangkok (Botschaft der Bundesrepublik Deutschland Bangkok, 9 South Sathorn Road, Bangkok 10120; phone +66 2 287 9000) or the German Honorary Consuls in Chiang Mai, Pattaya, or Phuket [1][2]. Upon receiving the deceased's German passport, the hospital/police death notification, and next-of-kin authorization, the Embassy issues the mandatory consular release letter and provides an informational list of international funeral directors in Thailand [1][2].
  • Appointing a licensed funeral director in Thailand and a receiving provider in Germany: Families may appoint a licensed international funeral and repatriation director in Thailand (or a local Buddhist temple / Wat cremation coordinator if choosing local cremation) to handle Thai civil registration, translation, and airport cargo clearance [1][2]. For repatriation to Germany, the Thai provider coordinates with a receiving German funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen) observing German state funeral laws (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and mandatory cemetery interment (Friedhofszwang) [1][2][6]. You can locate a qualified German funeral provider through the federal professional association Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V. (phone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour emergency line +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de) [6]. Clarvia supplies directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.

steps.title: Register the Death at the Thai District Office Within 24 Hours and Complete Legalization for Germany
steps.html:
Under Thai civil registration law, a death must be reported within 24 hours of death or discovery to the local District Office (Amphoe in the provinces, or Khet in Bangkok) operating under the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA, citizen hotline 1548) [2][3]:

  • Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4): Presenting the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1), the police/forensic report, the deceased's German passport, and the consular release letter from the German Embassy Bangkok, the next of kin or authorized funeral director obtains the official Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) (alongside an English civil registration extract where available) [1][2][3].
  • Translation, MFA legalization, and German Embassy legalization: Because Thailand is not a contracting state to the Hague Apostille Convention or the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention, the Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) must be translated into English or German, authenticated by the Legalization Division of the Department of Consular Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand in Bangkok [4], and then legalized (Legalisation) or certified by the German Embassy Bangkok for official recognition in Germany [1][2].
  • German Standesamt rules (§ 28 and § 36 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG): Whereas a domestic death inside Germany must be reported to the local Standesamt of the place of death no later than the third following working day under § 28 Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) (to issue the German Sterbeurkunde and multilingual extract on CIEC Formblatt C under the 1976 Vienna Convention) [7], a death in Thailand is registered first at the Thai Amphoe or Khet [2][3]. Using the legalized Thai Death Certificate, surviving relatives (spouse, registered partner, parents, or children) can apply through the German Embassy Bangkok or directly to the German Standesamt of the deceased's last German residence (or Standesamt I in Berlin if the deceased had no German residence) for subsequent registration in the German death register (Nachbeurkundung eines Sterbefalls im Ausland under § 36 PStG) to obtain domestic German Death Certificates (Sterbeurkunden) and multilingual Formblatt C extracts [1][2][8].

steps.title: Choose Between International Repatriation to Germany and Local Cremation or Burial in Thailand
steps.html:
Depending on your family member's wishes and family arrangements, you may choose international repatriation of casketed remains or cremated ashes to Germany or local disposition in Thailand [1][2][5]:

  • Repatriating casketed human remains to Germany: The international funeral director in Thailand arranges medical embalming, places the body in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin (verlöteter Zinksarg) inside a wooden outer casket, obtains the consular mortuary passport (Leichenpass) and customs certificates from the German Embassy Bangkok (aligned with Germany's Internationales Berliner Abkommen von 1937 / state funeral laws), and completes airport export clearance with the Thai Customs Department (for example, at Suvarnabhumi Airport, Customs Service Sub-Division I at +66 2-134-0490) [1][2][5]. Air repatriation from Thailand to Germany typically takes 1 to 3 weeks, so binding funeral dates in Germany should only be scheduled once flight details are confirmed [1][2].
  • Local cremation in Thailand and transporting the urn to Germany (Friedhofszwang): Cremation at a Thai Buddhist temple (Wat) or crematorium is the most common local procedure in Thailand [1][2]. If the cremated ashes are subsequently flown or shipped in a sealed urn (Urnenüberführung) to Germany, note that all German federal states enforce mandatory cemetery interment (Friedhofszwang under the Landesbestattungsgesetze): families cannot keep an urn privately at home in Germany [2][6]. To clear the urn into Germany and obtain the consular urn certificate from the German Embassy Bangkok, you must provide an official acceptance certificate (Übernahmebescheinigung) issued by a receiving German cemetery (Friedhofsverwaltung) or licensed German funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen), alongside the Thai Death Certificate, the cremation certificate, and the cancelled German passport [1][2][5][6].

steps.title: Complete Survivor Pension, Benefit, Tax, and Probate Steps in Germany and Thailand
steps.html:
Once the legalized Thai Death Certificate (or German Sterbeurkunde) is available, complete the post-death notifications and estate procedures in both jurisdictions:

  • In Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, Health Insurance, and Nachlassgericht):
    • Pensions and Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days): Notify Renten Service der Deutschen Post (phone +49 221 569 2777) and Deutsche Rentenversicherung (toll-free 0800 1000 4800 within Germany, or +49 30 865 0 from abroad) immediately so ongoing pension payments stop [9][10]. A surviving spouse or registered civil partner can apply through Renten Service der Deutschen Post within 30 days of death for the three-month bereavement advance (Sterbevierteljahr, paid at the full rate of the deceased's pension for the three calendar months following the month of death) [10], and file a claim with Deutsche Rentenversicherung for a survivor pension (Witwenrente or Witwerrente) or orphan's pension (Waisenrente) [9].
    • Statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung): Inform the deceased's German health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) and submit the death certificate to end coverage and adjust any family insurance [9].
    • German probate court (Nachlassgericht / Erbschein): Deliver any original will in your possession to the German probate court (Nachlassgericht at the local Amtsgericht of the deceased's last German habitual residence, which also checks the Central Register of Wills / Zentrales Testamentsregister) and apply for a German Certificate of Inheritance (Erbschein) if required for German bank accounts or real estate [1][2]. Under German law (§ 1944 BGB), the deadline to renounce an inheritance (Erbausschlagung) is 6 weeks, extended to 6 months if the deceased resided only abroad or if the heir was abroad when learning of the inheritance [1].
  • In Thailand (Thai Civil and Commercial Code Probate Order):
    • Releasing Thai bank accounts or property: If your family member held sole-name Thai bank accounts, a vehicle, a long-term land lease, or a condominium unit in Thailand, Thai banks and the Land Department generally require a formal probate order from a Thai court - even if a German Erbschein or will exists [2]. Under the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, heirs or the executor normally instruct a lawyer in Thailand to petition the competent Thai Civil or Provincial Court for an order appointing an official estate administrator (Phu Chat Kan Moradok) [2].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your situation, in which province or city in Thailand did the death occur (and was it in a hospital or elsewhere), and are you planning casketed repatriation to a specific German federal state (Bundesland) or local cremation in Thailand?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Spain dies in Germany: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Germany, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Spain and Germany.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Spanish citizenship or residence ties to Spain dies in Germany, the German state-level funeral and civil registration laws interact with the Spanish consular, social security, and inheritance regulations [1][2][4]. The following five official steps explain the procedure in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical examination of the body, death certificate, and police or prosecutor clearance in Germany
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or nursing home: When a death occurs in a hospital or care facility (for instance in Berlin, Frankfurt am Main, Munich, or Düsseldorf), the medical staff immediately arranges the medical post-mortem examination (ärztliche Leichenschau) and issues the official medical certificate of death (Todesbescheinigung / Totenschein) comprising a confidential and a non-confidential part [1][4]. Have the deceased person's Spanish national identity card (DNI) or passport (pasaporte) ready so that their personal details are recorded accurately [2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately contact the emergency services via the emergency number 112 or the on-call medical service at 116 117 (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) so that a physician can perform the external examination on site and issue the Totenschein [4].
  • Unexplained or non-natural cause of death: If the physician records an unexplained or non-natural manner of death, the police and the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) are called in [1][4]. The body is then initially taken into custody for forensic examination; civil registration at the Standesamt, cremation, or international repatriation to Spain may only proceed once the public prosecutor's office has issued written clearance for burial [1][4].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, funeral directors in Germany and Spain, and the Spanish consular mission
steps.html:
• Checking travel, repatriation, or funeral insurance: Before commissioning a funeral provider yourself, check whether your family member held a Spanish funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos), travel health or repatriation insurance, or an breakdown/assistance policy (Schutzbrief) [4][6]. If a policy exists, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance center first, as it normally appoints the funeral providers in Germany and Spain directly and covers the repatriation costs [4][6].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Germany and Spain: If there is no insurance coverage, appoint a licensed funeral provider in Germany (Bestattungsunternehmen) via the German professional association (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., Federal Association of German Funeral Directors, telephone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour emergency number +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de) in compliance with the relevant state funeral laws (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and the German statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) [4]. For reception and burial at the destination in Spain, the German funeral director coordinates with a licensed Spanish funeral provider (empresa funeraria habilitada), which you can locate through the Spanish national funeral industry association (Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios - PANASEF, telephone +34 91 576 31 55, email info@panasef.com) [6]. Clarvia lists professional associations and directories solely for orientation and does not recommend, rate, or rank individual providers.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate General of Spain in Germany: Notify the Spanish diplomatic or consular mission competent for the German place of death (under the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación - MAEC), such as the Consular Section of the Embassy of Spain (Embajada de España en Berlín, Lichtensteinallee 1, 10787 Berlin, telephone +49 30 254 007 0, email emb.berlin.sc@maec.es) or the competent Spanish Consulate General in Düsseldorf, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Munich, or Stuttgart [2][3]. The consular mission assists with consular death registration and transit documents, but does not pay funeral or repatriation expenses [2][3].

steps.title: Death notification at the German Standesamt (Form C) and civil registration for Spain
steps.html:
• Notification at the German Standesamt by the third following working day (§ 28 PStG): Under Section 28 of the German Civil Status Act (§ 28 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG), the death must be reported to the civil registry office (Standesamt des Sterbeortes) in Germany no later than the third working day following the death; for a death in a hospital, the hospital administration or the appointed funeral director usually handles this filing [1][4]. In addition to the German death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), be sure to request several multilingual extracts on Form C (Formblatt C / Fórmula C) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [1][2]. Because both Germany and Spain are contracting states to the Vienna CIEC Convention and Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 also applies, the multilingual Form C is recognized directly in Spain without a Hague Apostille or sworn translation [2][7].
  • Registration in the Spanish Civil Registry (Registro Civil / Registro Civil Consular): Whereas a death occurring within Spain must be reported within 24 hours to the local Registro Civil of the municipality of death (under the supervision of the Spanish Ministry of Justice, Ministerio de Justicia) to obtain the Certificado Literal de Defunción and the multilingual Certificado Plurilingüe Fórmula C [7], the death of a Spanish citizen occurring in Germany must additionally be registered in the Spanish Consular Civil Registry (Registro Civil Consular) at the Embassy (Embajada de España en Berlín) or the competent Spanish Consulate General [2]. To do so, submit the completed data declaration sheet (Hoja declaratoria de datos), the international death certificate on Form C (internationale Sterbeurkunde), and copies of the deceased's last Spanish DNI or passport and the informant's ID (by post or via the consular section) to obtain the Spanish Certificado Literal de Defunción required for probate and pension procedures in Spain [2][7].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to Spain and local burial or cremation in Germany
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body in a coffin to Spain: For transport from Germany to Spain, the German funeral director applies to the competent authority at the German place of death (public health office or public order office) for the multilingual mortuary passport (Leichenpass / salvoconducto mortuorio) under the 1937 International Berlin Agreement (or the Strasbourg Agreement) in accordance with the guidance of the German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt) [4][5]. The body is hygienically prepared and hermetically sealed in a soldered zinc coffin (verlöteter Zinksarg / féretro de zinc sellado) inside a wooden transport coffin [4][5]. In coordination with the Spanish consular mission (Embajada de España en Berlín or MAEC Consulate General) and the Spanish border health authority (Sanidad Exterior), the receiving Spanish funeral company takes custody of the coffin at the destination airport in Spain [2][6].
  • Cremation in Germany and urn transfer to Spain (Friedhofszwang): If cremation takes place in Germany first (following the mandatory second medical post-mortem examination at the crematorium), note the statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) applicable across all German federal states: German crematoria release the urn only against a certificate of acceptance (Übernahmebescheinigung) from a cemetery or proof of cross-border transfer handled by an authorized funeral provider [4]. For transporting the sealed urn to Spain (traslado de urna), the international death certificate (Form C) and the cremation certificate (certificado de cremación) from the German crematorium must accompany the urn [4][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in Germany: If interment is to take place at a German cemetery, the Standesamt of the place of death issues the burial permit (Bestattungsschein); the burial deadlines and cemetery obligation are governed by the respective German state funeral law (Landesbestattungsgesetz) [1][4].

steps.title: Survivor pensions, register of wills, taxes, and probate in Spain and Germany
steps.html:
• In Spain (INSS, Últimas Voluntades, Notary, and Impuesto sobre Sucesiones):
    • Spanish Social Security (INSS): If your family member was insured under Spanish social security or received a Spanish pension, report the death to the National Institute of Social Security (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social - INSS) to apply for the one-off funeral grant (auxilio por defunción, claimable for up to 5 years) as well as ongoing survivor pensions (pensión de viudedad or pensión de orfandad; where insurance periods were completed in both Germany and Spain, they are aggregated under the EU social security coordination regulations) [8].
    • Central Register of Last Wills (Modelo 790), notary, and inheritance tax (6 months): Once 15 working days (15 días hábiles) have elapsed since the date of death, apply to the Spanish Ministry of Justice (Ministerio de Justicia) using official Form Modelo 790 (Code 006) for the Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (certificate of wills executed in Spain) together with the certificate of life and bereavement insurance contracts [9]. With these certificates and the death certificate, contact a Spanish notary's office (notaría) through the General Council of Notaries (Consejo General del Notariado) to open the will or execute the notarial declaration of heirs and acceptance of inheritance [10]. Please note that Spanish inheritance tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be declared within 6 months from the date of death (a 6-month extension can be requested within the first 5 months) [10].
  • In Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, health insurance, and Nachlassgericht):
    • Pensions and Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days): If the deceased received a German pension or had German insurance periods, immediately notify the pension payment service (Renten Service der Deutschen Post, telephone +49 221 569 2777) to prevent overpayments and, for surviving spouses or registered partners, to apply within 30 days of the death for the advance payment of the three-month bereavement quarter (Sterbevierteljahr) [12]. Submit applications for a German widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente) to the German Statutory Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, toll-free service number 0800 1000 4800 in Germany or +49 30 865 0 from abroad) [11].
    • Statutory health insurance and German probate court: Report the death by submitting the death certificate to the German statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung / Krankenkasse) [11]. Where assets or real estate are located in Germany, the Standesamt electronically notifies the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister) of the Federal Chamber of Notaries, which forwards information on wills in official custody to the competent probate court (Nachlassgericht at the local court, Amtsgericht); heirs can apply there if needed for a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession [13].

closingQuestion: So that we can assist you more specifically, in which German municipality (and federal state) did the death occur, to which Spanish municipality or autonomous community will any transfer take place or where was the last habitual residence, and are you planning a coffin repatriation to Spain, cremation in Germany with urn transport to Spain, or burial in Germany?

de.title: Todesfall in Deutschland (Spanien): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Deutschland und Spanien: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit Staatsangehörigkeit oder Wohnsitzbezug zu Spanien in Deutschland verstirbt, greifen die deutschen landesrechtlichen Bestattungs- und Personenstandsvorschriften sowie die spanischen konsularischen, sozialversicherungs- und erbrechtlichen Regelungen ineinander [1][2][4]. Die folgenden fünf offiziellen Schritte erläutern das Vorgehen in chronologischer Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Ärztliche Leichenschau, Todesbescheinigung und polizeiliche oder staatsanwaltschaftliche Freigabe in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Sterbefall im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim: Tritt der Tod in einer Klinik oder Pflegeeinrichtung (beispielsweise in Berlin, Frankfurt am Main, München oder Düsseldorf) ein, veranlasst das medizinische Personal unverzüglich die ärztliche Leichenschau und stellt die amtliche Todesbescheinigung (Totenschein) mit vertraulichem und nicht vertraulichem Teil aus [1][4]. Halten Sie den spanischen Personalausweis (DNI) oder Reisepass (pasaporte) der verstorbenen Person bereit, damit die Personalien fehlerfrei erfasst werden [2].
  • Sterbefall zu Hause, im Hotel oder an einem öffentlichen Ort: Verständigen Sie sofort den Rettungsdienst über den Notruf 112 oder den ärztlichen Bereitschaftsdienst unter 116 117, damit eine Ärztin oder ein Arzt die Leichenschau vor Ort durchführt und den Totenschein ausstellt [4].
  • Ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesursache: Bescheinigt die Ärztin oder der Arzt eine ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesart, werden Polizei und Staatsanwaltschaft eingeschaltet [1][4]. Der Leichnam wird dann zunächst für rechtsmedizinische Untersuchungen beschlagnahmt; eine Beurkundung beim Standesamt, eine Feuerbestattung oder eine Auslandsüberführung nach Spanien darf erst erfolgen, sobald die Staatsanwaltschaft die schriftliche Freigabe zur Bestattung erteilt hat [1][4].

steps.title: Rückholversicherung, Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Spanien sowie spanische Konsularvertretung
steps.html:
• Prüfung von Reise-, Rückhol- oder Sterbegeldversicherungen: Prüfen Sie vor einer eigenen Auftragsvergabe, ob Ihr Familienangehöriger über eine spanische Sterbegeldversicherung (seguro de decesos), eine Reisekranken- oder Rückholversicherung oder einen Schutzbrief verfügte [4][6]. Ist eine Police vorhanden, kontaktieren Sie zuerst die 24-Stunden-Notrufzentrale der Versicherung, da diese in der Regel die Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Spanien direkt beauftragt und die Überführungskosten übernimmt [4][6].
  • Beauftragung von Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Spanien: Besteht kein Versicherungsschutz, beauftragen Sie in Deutschland ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen über den Berufsverband (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., Telefon +49 211 16008-10, 24-Stunden-Notfallnummer +49 211 16008-86, E-Mail info@bestatter.de) unter Beachtung der jeweiligen Landesbestattungsgesetze und des deutschen Friedhofszwangs [4]. Für die Übernahme und Beisetzung am Zielort in Spanien koordiniert sich der deutsche Bestatter mit einem zugelassenen spanischen Bestattungsunternehmen (empresa funeraria habilitada), das Sie über den spanischen Branchenverband (Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios - PANASEF, Telefon +34 91 576 31 55, E-Mail info@panasef.com) finden können [6]. Clarvia nennt Berufsverbände und Verzeichnisse ausschließlich zur Orientierung und gibt keine Empfehlungen, Bewertungen oder Rankings für einzelne Anbieter ab.
  • Kontakt zur Botschaft oder zum Generalkonsulat von Spanien in Deutschland: Informieren Sie die für den deutschen Sterbeort zuständige spanische Auslandsvertretung (unter dem spanischen Außenministerium, Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea und Cooperación - MAEC), etwa die Konsularabteilung der spanischen Botschaft (Embajada de España en Berlín (Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación), Lichtensteinallee 1, 10787 Berlin, Telefon +49 30 254 007 0, E-Mail emb.berlin.sc@maec.es) oder das zuständige spanische Generalkonsulat in Düsseldorf, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, München oder Stuttgart [2][3]. Die Konsularvertretung unterstützt bei der konsularischen Sterbefallregistrierung und den Überführungsdokumenten, übernimmt jedoch keine Bestattungs- oder Überführungskosten [2][3].

steps.title: Sterbefallanzeige beim deutschen Standesamt (Formblatt C) und Registrierung für Spanien
steps.html:
• Anzeige beim deutschen Standesamt spätestens am dritten folgenden Werktag (§ 28 PStG): Gemäß § 28 Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) muss der Sterbefall spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag beim Standesamt des Sterbeortes in Deutschland angezeigt werden; bei einem Tod im Krankenhaus übernimmt dies meist die Klinikverwaltung oder das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen [1][4]. Beantragen Sie neben der deutschen Sterbeurkunde unbedingt mehrere mehrsprachige Auszüge auf Formblatt C (Fórmula C) nach dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen vom 8. September 1976 [1][2]. Da sowohl Deutschland als auch Spanien Vertragsstaaten des Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommens sind und zudem die EU-Verordnung (EU) 2016/1191 gilt, wird das mehrsprachige Formblatt C in Spanien direkt ohne Haager Apostille und ohne vereidigte Übersetzung anerkannt [2][7].
  • Eintragung im spanischen Personenstandsregister (Registro Civil / Registro Civil Consular): Während ein im Inland in Spanien eingetretener Todesfall innerhalb von 24 Stunden beim örtlichen Registro Civil des Sterbemunizips (unter Aufsicht der spanischen Justizbehörde Ministerio de Justicia) gemeldet wird, um das Certificado Literal de Defunción und das Certificado Plurilingüe Fórmula C zu erhalten [7], muss der in Deutschland eingetretene Tod eines spanischen Staatsangehörigen zusätzlich im spanischen Konsularregister (Registro Civil Consular) bei der Botschaft (Embajada de España en Berlín) oder dem zuständigen spanischen Generalkonsulat eingetragen werden [2]. Reichen Sie hierzu das ausgefüllte Datenblatt (Hoja declaratoria de datos), die internationale Sterbeurkunde auf Formblatt C (internationale Sterbeurkunde) sowie Kopien des letzten spanischen DNI oder Reisepasses der verstorbenen Person und des Ausweises der anzeigenden Person ein (per Post oder über die Konsularabteilung), um das spanische Certificado Literal de Defunción für Nachlass- und Rentenverfahren in Spanien zu erhalten [2][7].

steps.title: Wahl zwischen internationaler Überführung nach Spanien und lokaler Bestattung in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Internationale Überführung des Leichnams im Sarg nach Spanien: Für die Überführung von Deutschland nach Spanien beantragt das deutsche Bestattungsunternehmen bei der zuständigen Behörde des deutschen Sterbeortes (Gesundheits- oder Ordnungsamt) den mehrsprachigen Leichenpass (salvoconducto mortuorio) nach dem Internationalen Berliner Abkommen von 1937 (bzw. dem Straßburger Übereinkommen) im Einklang mit den Hinweisen der deutschen Außenbehörde (Auswärtiges Amt) [4][5]. Der Leichnam wird hygienisch versorgt und in einem verlöteten Zinksarg (féretro de zinc sellado) innerhalb eines Holztransportsargs luftdicht verschlossen [4][5]. In Abstimmung mit der spanischen Konsularvertretung (Embajada de España en Berlín bzw. Generalkonsulat des MAEC) und der spanischen grenzsanitären Behörde (Sanidad Exterior) übernimmt das empfangende spanische Bestattungsunternehmen den Sarg am Zielflughafen in Spanien [2][6].
  • Einäscherung in Deutschland und Urnenüberführung nach Spanien (Friedhofszwang): Erfolgt zunächst eine Feuerbestattung in Deutschland (nach der gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen zweiten ärztlichen Leichenschau im Krematorium), beachten Sie den in allen deutschen Bundesländern geltenden Friedhofszwang: Deutsche Krematorien händigen die Urne nur gegen eine Übernahmebescheinigung eines Friedhofs oder den Nachweis der grenzüberschreitenden Überführung durch ein befugtes Bestattungsunternehmen aus [4]. Für den Transport der versiegelten Urne nach Spanien (traslado de urna) sind die internationale Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) und die Einäscherungsbescheinigung (certificado de cremación) des deutschen Krematoriums beizufügen [4][6].
  • Lokale Erd- oder Feuerbestattung in Deutschland: Soll die Beisetzung auf einem deutschen Friedhof stattfinden, stellt das Standesamt des Sterbeortes den Bestattungsschein aus; die Bestattungsfristen und der Friedhofszwang richten sich nach dem jeweiligen deutschen Landesbestattungsgesetz [1][4].

steps.title: Hinterbliebenenrenten, Testamentsregister, Steuern und Nachlass in Spanien und Deutschland
steps.html:
• In Spanien (INSS, Últimas Voluntades, Notariat und Impuesto sobre Sucesiones):
    • Spanische Sozialversicherung (INSS): War Ihr Familienangehöriger in Spanien sozialversichert oder Rentenbezieher, melden Sie den Sterbefall beim spanischen Sozialversicherungsträger (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social - INSS), um die einmalige Bestattungsbeihilfe (auxilio por defunción, Antragsfrist bis zu 5 Jahre) sowie laufende Hinterbliebenenrenten (pensión de viudedad oder pensión de orfandad) zu beantragen (bei Versicherungszeiten in Deutschland und Spanien werden diese nach den EU-Koordinierungsverordnungen zusammengerechnet) [8].
    • Zentrales Testamentsregister (Modelo 790), Notar und Erbschaftsteuer (6 Monate): Sobald 15 Werktage (15 días hábiles) seit dem Todestag verstrichen sind, beantragen Sie bei der spanischen Justizbehörde (Ministerio de Justicia) über das offizielle Formular Modelo 790 (Code 006) das Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (Nachweis über in Spanien errichtete Testamente) sowie das Zertifikat über Lebens- und Sterbeversicherungen [9]. Mit diesen Bescheinigungen und der Sterbeurkunde wenden Sie sich an ein spanisches Notariat (notaría) über die spanische Notarkammer (Consejo General del Notariado), um das Testament zu eröffnen bzw. die notarielle Erbenerklärung und Erbschaftsannahme zu beurkunden [10]. Beachten Sie, dass die spanische Erbschaftsteuer (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) innerhalb von 6 Monaten ab dem Todestag erklärt werden muss (eine Fristverlängerung um weitere 6 Monate kann innerhalb der ersten 5 Monate beantragt werden) [10].
  • In Deutschland (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, Krankenversicherung und Nachlassgericht):
    • Renten und Sterbevierteljahr (innerhalb von 30 Tagen): Bezog die verstorbene Person eine deutsche Rente oder bestanden deutsche Versicherungszeiten, informieren Sie unverzüglich die Auszahlungsstelle (Renten Service der Deutschen Post, Telefon +49 221 569 2777), um Überzahlungen zu vermeiden und für überlebende Ehegatten oder eingetragene Lebenspartner innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod die Vorschusszahlung für das Sterbevierteljahr zu beantragen [12]. Anträge auf deutsche Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente stellen Sie beim Rententräger (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, kostenfreie Servicenummer 0800 1000 4800 in Deutschland bzw. +49 30 865 0 aus dem Ausland) [11].
    • Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung und deutsches Nachlassgericht: Melden Sie den Tod unter Vorlage der Sterbeurkunde der deutschen Gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung (Krankenkasse) [11]. Bei Vermögen oder Immobilien in Deutschland benachrichtigt das Standesamt elektronisch das Registerportal (Zentrales Testamentsregister) der Bundesnotarkammer, welches verwahrte Verfügungen von Todes wegen an das zuständige Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht übermittelt; dort können Erben bei Bedarf einen deutschen Erbschein oder ein Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis beantragen [13].

de.closingQuestion: Damit wir Ihnen noch gezielter weiterhelfen können: 1. In welcher deutschen Gemeinde (und welchem Bundesland) ist der Sterbefall eingetreten, und in welche spanische Gemeinde oder autonome Gemeinschaft soll die Überführung erfolgen bzw. wo befand sich der letzte Wohnsitz? 2. Planen Sie eine Sargüberführung nach Spanien, eine Einäscherung in Deutschland mit Urnentransport nach Spanien oder eine Bestattung in Deutschland?
