title: What to Do When a Citizen of Luxembourg Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Luxembourg Dies in Germany: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Luxembourg dies in Germany: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Germany, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Luxembourg and Germany.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Luxembourg citizenship or residence ties to Luxembourg dies in Germany, the German state-level funeral and civil registration laws interact with Luxembourg's municipal, social security, and inheritance regulations [1][2][5]. The following five official steps explain the procedure in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical examination of the body, death certificate, and police or prosecutor clearance in Germany
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or nursing home: When a death occurs in a hospital or care facility in Germany (for instance in Trier, Saarbrücken, Bitburg, Frankfurt am Main, or Berlin), the medical staff immediately arranges the medical post-mortem examination (ärztliche Leichenschau) and issues the official medical certificate of death (Todesbescheinigung / Totenschein) with a confidential and a non-confidential part [1][3]. Have the deceased person's Luxembourg identity card (carte d'identité) or passport (passeport) ready so that their personal details are recorded accurately [2][5].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately contact the emergency services via the emergency number 112 or the on-call medical service at 116 117 (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) so that a physician can perform the external examination on site and issue the Totenschein [3].
  • Unexplained or non-natural cause of death: If the physician records an unexplained or non-natural manner of death, the police and the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) are called in [1][3]. The body is then initially taken into custody for forensic examination; civil registration at the Standesamt, cremation, or repatriation to Luxembourg may only proceed once the public prosecutor's office has issued written clearance for burial [1][3].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, funeral directors in Germany and Luxembourg, and the Embassy of Luxembourg
steps.html:
• Checking travel, repatriation, or health insurance coverage: Before commissioning a funeral provider yourself, check whether the deceased held private repatriation or travel health insurance, membership in a Luxembourg rescue or assistance organization, or inpatient treatment abroad pre-authorized by the Luxembourg National Health Fund (Caisse nationale de santé - CNS; in the latter case, the CNS also contributes to repatriation costs within the statutory lump-sum allowance) [3][6].
  • Appointing funeral directors in Germany and Luxembourg: For collection and administrative formalities at the German place of death, appoint a licensed funeral provider (Bestattungsunternehmen) via the German professional association (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., Federal Association of German Funeral Directors, telephone +49 211 16008-10, 24-hour emergency number +49 211 16008-86, email info@bestatter.de) in compliance with the respective state funeral laws (Landesbestattungsgesetze) and the German statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) [3]. The German provider coordinates the transfer seamlessly with an authorized receiving funeral director in Luxembourg (entreprise de pompes funèbres autorisée au Luxembourg), which can also handle all municipal cemetery and civil registry formalities in the Grand Duchy [5]. Clarvia lists professional associations and public portals solely for orientation and does not recommend, rate, or rank individual providers.
  • Contacting the Embassy of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg in Germany: If consular assistance is needed, you can contact the Embassy of Luxembourg in Germany (Ambassade du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg à Berlin, Klingelhöferstraße 7, 10785 Berlin, telephone +49 30 26 39 57 0, email berlin.amb@mae.etat.lu) as well as Luxembourg's honorary consulates in the German federal states, or in urgent out-of-hours emergencies the central switchboard of the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes in Luxembourg at +352 247-82300) [2].

steps.title: Death notification at the German Standesamt (Form C) and registration for Luxembourg
steps.html:
• Notification at the German Standesamt by the third following working day (§ 28 PStG): Under Section 28 of the German Civil Status Act (§ 28 Personenstandsgesetz - PStG), the death must be reported to the civil registry office (Standesamt des Sterbeortes) in Germany no later than the third working day following the death; for a death in a hospital, the hospital administration or the appointed funeral director usually handles this filing [1][3]. In addition to the German death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), request several multilingual extracts on Form C (Formblatt C / extrait plurilingue Formule C) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention [1][5]. Because both Germany and Luxembourg are contracting states to the Vienna CIEC Convention and Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 also applies, the multilingual Form C is recognized directly in Luxembourg without a Hague Apostille or sworn translation [4][5].
  • Civil registry notification and transcription in Luxembourg (Guichet.lu): Whereas a death occurring within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg must be declared within 24 hours to the civil registrar of the municipality of death (officier de l'état civil de la commune du lieu de décès dans les 24 heures, explained in detail on the official government citizen portal Guichet.lu) to obtain the Luxembourg death certificate (acte de décès) and multilingual extract (Formule C) [5], when a death occurs in Germany the relatives or the appointed Luxembourg funeral director present the German death certificate (Form C) to the civil registry office (bureau de l'état civil) of the Luxembourg municipality of residence or municipality of burial [5]. This records the death in the Luxembourg civil status register and the National Registry of Natural Persons (Registre national des personnes physiques - RNPP) and secures the municipal burial and transport permit [5].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to Luxembourg and local burial or cremation in Germany
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body in a coffin to Luxembourg: For cross-border transport from Germany to Luxembourg, the German funeral director applies to the competent authority at the German place of death (public health office or public order office) for the multilingual mortuary passport (Leichenpass) under the 1937 International Berlin Agreement or the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses, in accordance with the guidance of the German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt) [3][4]. The body is placed in accordance with regulations in a hermetically soldered zinc coffin (verlöteter Zinksarg) inside a wooden coffin [3][4]. For entry and onward transport into Luxembourg, the international transit papers (laissez-passer mortuaire) operate in conjunction with the requirements of the Luxembourg Ministry of Health / Health Directorate (Direction de la santé / Inspection sanitaire of the ministère de la Santé et de la Sécurité sociale), the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes), and the civil registry office of the Luxembourg municipality of burial [2][5][7].
  • Cremation in Germany and urn transfer to Luxembourg (Friedhofszwang): If cremation takes place in Germany (following the mandatory second medical post-mortem examination at the crematorium), note the statutory cemetery obligation (Friedhofszwang) applicable across all German federal states: German crematoria release the urn only against an urn requisition / certificate of acceptance (Urnenanforderung / Übernahmebescheinigung) from a cemetery or proof of cross-border transfer to a Luxembourg cemetery or authorized funeral provider, accompanied by the death certificate (Form C) and the cremation certificate [3][5].
  • Local burial or cremation in Germany: If interment takes place locally in Germany, the German Standesamt issues the burial permit (Bestattungsschein), and the deadlines and cemetery obligation of the respective German state funeral law (Landesbestattungsgesetz) apply [1][3].

steps.title: Funeral grant, survivor pensions, taxes, and probate in Luxembourg and Germany
steps.html:
• In Luxembourg (CNS, CNAP, AED, and Chambre des Notaires):
    • Flat-rate funeral grant (indemnité funéraire from the CNS): If your family member was covered by Luxembourg health insurance (as a resident or cross-border commuter / frontalier), the National Health Fund (Caisse nationale de santé - CNS, telephone +352 27 57-1) pays the flat-rate funeral grant (indemnité funéraire) upon presentation of the death certificate (acte de décès or Form C) and the receipted funeral director's invoices (factures acquittées) to the person or institution that advanced the funeral costs [6][7].
    • Luxembourg survivor's pension (pension de survie from the CNAP): Because survivor pensions in Luxembourg are not granted automatically, surviving spouses, registered partners (PACS), or orphans must formally apply to the National Pension Insurance Fund (Caisse nationale d'assurance pension - CNAP, telephone +352 22 41 41-1) for the survivor's pension (pension de survie or pension d'orphelin), enclosing the death certificate [8][9]. If the deceased completed insurance periods in both Luxembourg and Germany, these are coordinated under EU Regulations (EC) No 883/2004 and No 987/2009 [8][9].
    • Inheritance declaration (AED) and notary in Luxembourg: With the Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AED, procedure explained on Guichet.lu), the heirs must file a written inheritance declaration (déclaration de succession) at the inheritance tax office of the deceased's last tax domicile in Luxembourg (or a declaration of transfer upon death, déclaration de mutation par décès, if the deceased was not domiciled in Luxembourg but owned real estate there) [10]. The statutory filing deadline is 6 months for a death in Luxembourg and 8 months when the death occurred in another European country such as Germany [10]. To obtain a notarial certificate of heirship (acte de notoriété), open a will, and settle the estate in Luxembourg, heirs can consult a notary through the Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) [10].
  • In Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, health insurance, and Nachlassgericht):
    • German pensions and Sterbevierteljahr (within 30 days): If the deceased drew a German pension or had German insurance periods, report the death immediately to the pension payment service (Renten Service der Deutschen Post, telephone +49 221 569 2777) to stop overpayments and, for surviving spouses or registered partners, to apply within 30 days of the death for the advance payment of the three-month bereavement quarter (Sterbevierteljahr) [12]. Submit applications for a German widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente) to the German Statutory Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, toll-free number 0800 1000 4800 in Germany or +49 30 865 0 from abroad) [11].
    • Statutory health insurance and German probate court: Where applicable, notify the German statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung / Krankenkasse) [11]. If bank accounts or real estate were held in Germany, the German Standesamt automatically notifies the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister) of the Federal Chamber of Notaries, which forwards testamentary dispositions held in official custody to the competent probate court (Nachlassgericht at the local court, Amtsgericht); heirs can apply there if needed for a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or a European Certificate of Succession [13].

closingQuestion: So that we can assist you more specifically, in which German municipality (and federal state) did the death occur, in which Luxembourg municipality did your family member reside or where should the transfer take place, and are you planning a coffin repatriation to Luxembourg, cremation in Germany with urn transport to Luxembourg, or burial in Germany?

de.title: Todesfall in Deutschland (Luxemburg): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Deutschland und Luxemburg: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit Staatsangehörigkeit oder Wohnsitzbezug zu Luxemburg in Deutschland verstirbt, greifen die deutschen landesrechtlichen Bestattungs- und Personenstandsvorschriften sowie die luxemburgischen kommunalen, sozialversicherungs- und erbrechtlichen Bestimmungen ineinander [1][2][5]. Die folgenden fünf offiziellen Schritte erläutern das Vorgehen in chronologischer Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Ärztliche Leichenschau, Todesbescheinigung und polizeiliche oder staatsanwaltschaftliche Freigabe in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Sterbefall im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim: Tritt der Tod in einer Klinik oder Pflegeeinrichtung in Deutschland (beispielsweise in Trier, Saarbrücken, Bitburg, Frankfurt am Main oder Berlin) ein, veranlasst das medizinische Personal unverzüglich die ärztliche Leichenschau und stellt die amtliche Todesbescheinigung (Totenschein) mit vertraulichem und nicht vertraulichem Teil aus [1][3]. Halten Sie den luxemburgischen Personalausweis (carte d'identité) oder Reisepass (passeport) der verstorbenen Person bereit, damit die Personalien fehlerfrei aufgenommen werden [2][5].
  • Sterbefall zu Hause, im Hotel oder an einem öffentlichen Ort: Verständigen Sie sofort den Rettungsdienst über den Notruf 112 oder den ärztlichen Bereitschaftsdienst unter 116 117, damit eine Ärztin oder ein Arzt die Leichenschau vor Ort durchführt und den Totenschein ausstellt [3].
  • Ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesursache: Bescheinigt die Ärztin oder der Arzt eine ungeklärte oder nicht natürliche Todesart, werden Polizei und Staatsanwaltschaft eingeschaltet [1][3]. Der Leichnam wird dann zunächst für rechtsmedizinische Untersuchungen beschlagnahmt; eine Beurkundung beim Standesamt, eine Feuerbestattung oder eine Überführung nach Luxemburg darf erst erfolgen, sobald die Staatsanwaltschaft die schriftliche Freigabe zur Bestattung erteilt hat [1][3].

steps.title: Rückholversicherung, Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Luxemburg sowie luxemburgische Botschaft
steps.html:
• Prüfung von Reise-, Rückhol- oder Krankenversicherungsschutz: Prüfen Sie vor einer eigenen Auftragsvergabe, ob für die verstorbene Person eine private Rückhol- oder Reisekrankenversicherung, eine Mitgliedschaft bei einer luxemburgischen Rettungs- oder Beistandsorganisation oder eine vorab von der luxemburgischen Gesundheitskasse (Caisse nationale de santé - CNS) genehmigte stationäre Auslandsbehandlung bestand (in letzterem Fall beteiligt sich die CNS im Rahmen des Pauschalbetrags auch an den Überführungskosten) [3][6].
  • Beauftragung von Bestattungsunternehmen in Deutschland und Luxemburg: Beauftragen Sie für die Abholung und Behördengänge am deutschen Sterbeort ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen über den Berufsverband (Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter e.V., Telefon +49 211 16008-10, 24-Stunden-Notfallnummer +49 211 16008-86, E-Mail info@bestatter.de) unter Beachtung der jeweiligen Landesbestattungsgesetze und des deutschen Friedhofszwangs [3]. Dieses koordiniert die Überführung nahtlos mit einem zugelassenen empfangenden Bestattungsunternehmen in Luxemburg (entreprise de pompes funèbres autorisée au Luxembourg), das im Großherzogtum auch sämtliche kommunalen Friedhofs- und Standesamtswege übernehmen kann [5]. Clarvia nennt Berufsverbände und öffentliche Portale ausschließlich zur Orientierung und gibt keine Empfehlungen, Bewertungen oder Rankings für einzelne Anbieter ab.
  • Kontakt zur Botschaft des Großherzogtums Luxemburg in Deutschland: Bei Bedarf an konsularischer Unterstützung erreichen Sie die luxemburgische Botschaft in Deutschland (Ambassade du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg à Berlin, Klingelhöferstraße 7, 10785 Berlin, Telefon +49 30 26 39 57 0, E-Mail berlin.amb@mae.etat.lu) sowie die luxemburgischen Honorarkonsulate in den deutschen Bundesländern oder in dringenden Notfällen außerhalb der Bürozeiten die Zentrale des luxemburgischen Außenministeriums (ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes in Luxemburg unter +352 247-82300) [2].

steps.title: Sterbefallanzeige beim deutschen Standesamt (Formblatt C) und Registrierung für Luxemburg
steps.html:
• Anzeige beim deutschen Standesamt spätestens am dritten folgenden Werktag (§ 28 PStG): Gemäß § 28 Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) muss der Sterbefall spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag beim Standesamt des Sterbeortes in Deutschland angezeigt werden; bei einem Tod im Krankenhaus erledigt dies meist die Klinikverwaltung oder das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen [1][3]. Beantragen Sie neben der deutschen Sterbeurkunde mehrere mehrsprachige Auszüge auf Formblatt C (extrait plurilingue Formule C) gemäß dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen vom 8. September 1976 [1][5]. Da sowohl Deutschland als auch Luxemburg Vertragsstaaten des Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommens sind und zudem die EU-Verordnung (EU) 2016/1191 gilt, wird das mehrsprachige Formblatt C in Luxemburg direkt ohne Haager Apostille und ohne vereidigte Übersetzung anerkannt [4][5].
  • Standesamtliche Meldung und Übertragung in Luxemburg (Guichet.lu): Während ein im Großherzogtum Luxemburg eingetretener Todesfall innerhalb von 24 Stunden beim Standesbeamten der Sterbegemeinde (officier de l'état civil de la commune du lieu de décès dans les 24 heures, ausführlich erläutert auf dem staatlichen Bürgerportal Guichet.lu) gemeldet wird, um die luxemburgische Sterbeurkunde (acte de décès) und den mehrsprachigen Auszug (Formule C) zu erhalten [5], legen die Angehörigen oder das beauftragte luxemburgische Bestattungsunternehmen bei einem Tod in Deutschland die deutsche Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) dem Standesamt (bureau de l'état civil) der luxemburgischen Wohnsitzgemeinde bzw. der Bestattungsgemeinde vor [5]. Dadurch wird der Sterbefall im luxemburgischen Personenstandsregister und im nationalen Personenregister (Registre national des personnes physiques - RNPP) vermerkt sowie die kommunale Bestattungs- und Transportgenehmigung erteilt [5].

steps.title: Wahl zwischen internationaler Überführung nach Luxemburg und lokaler Bestattung in Deutschland
steps.html:
• Internationale Überführung des Leichnams im Sarg nach Luxemburg: Für den grenzüberschreitenden Transport von Deutschland nach Luxemburg beantragt das deutsche Bestattungsunternehmen bei der zuständigen Behörde des deutschen Sterbeortes (Gesundheits- oder Ordnungsamt) den mehrsprachigen Leichenpass nach dem Internationalen Berliner Abkommen von 1937 bzw. dem Straßburger Übereinkommen von 1973 über die Leichenbeförderung im Einklang mit den Hinweisen der deutschen Außenbehörde (Auswärtiges Amt) [3][4]. Der Leichnam wird vorschriftsgemäß in einem luftdicht verlöteten Zinksarg innerhalb eines Holzsargs eingesargt [3][4]. Für die Einfuhr und Weiterbeförderung nach Luxemburg wirken die internationalen Überführungspapiere (laissez-passer mortuaire) mit den Vorgaben des luxemburgischen Gesundheitsministeriums bzw. der Gesundheitsdirektion (Direction de la santé / Inspection sanitaire des ministère de la Santé et de la Sécurité sociale), des Außenministeriums (ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes) und des Standesamts der luxemburgischen Bestattungsgemeinde zusammen [2][5][7].
  • Einäscherung in Deutschland und Urnenüberführung nach Luxemburg (Friedhofszwang): Erfolgt die Feuerbestattung in Deutschland (nach der gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen zweiten ärztlichen Leichenschau im Krematorium), beachten Sie den in allen deutschen Bundesländern geltenden Friedhofszwang: Deutsche Krematorien geben die Urne nur gegen eine Urnenanforderung (Übernahmebescheinigung) eines Friedhofs oder den Nachweis der grenzüberschreitenden Überführung an einen luxemburgischen Friedhof bzw. ein befugtes Bestattungsunternehmen frei, begleitet von der Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) und der Einäscherungsbescheinigung [3][5].
  • Lokale Erd- oder Feuerbestattung in Deutschland: Findet die Beisetzung vor Ort in Deutschland statt, stellt das deutsche Standesamt den Bestattungsschein aus, und es gelten die Fristen sowie der Friedhofszwang des jeweiligen deutschen Landesbestattungsgesetzes [1][3].

steps.title: Bestattungskostenpauschale, Hinterbliebenenrenten, Steuern und Nachlass in Luxemburg und Deutschland
steps.html:
• In Luxemburg (CNS, CNAP, AED und Chambre des Notaires):
    • Bestattungskostenpauschale (indemnité funéraire der CNS): War Ihr Familienangehöriger in Luxemburg krankenversichert (als Einwohner oder als Grenzgänger / frontalier), zahlt die Nationale Gesundheitskasse (Caisse nationale de santé - CNS, Telefon +352 27 57-1) gegen Vorlage der Sterbeurkunde (acte de décès bzw. Formblatt C) und der quittierten Rechnungen des Bestattungsunternehmens (factures acquittées) die pauschale Bestattungsbeihilfe (indemnité funéraire) an die Person oder Stelle aus, welche die Bestattungskosten vorgestreckt hat [6][7].
    • Luxemburgische Hinterbliebenenrente (pension de survie der CNAP): Da Hinterbliebenenrenten in Luxemburg nicht automatisch gewährt werden, müssen überlebende Ehegatten, eingetragene Lebenspartner (PACS) oder Waisen bei der Nationalen Rentenversicherungskasse (Caisse nationale d'assurance pension - CNAP, Telefon +352 22 41 41-1) formell die Hinterbliebenenrente (pension de survie bzw. pension d'orphelin) unter Beifügung der Sterbeurkunde beantragen [8][9]. Hatte die verstorbene Person Versicherungszeiten in Luxemburg und Deutschland, werden diese nach den EU-Verordnungen (EG) Nr. 883/2004 und 987/2009 koordiniert [8][9].
    • Erbschaftserklärung (AED) und Notariat in Luxemburg: Bei der Einregistrierungs-, Domänen- und Mehrwertsteuerverwaltung (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AED, Verfahren erläutert auf Guichet.lu) müssen die Erben beim Erbschaftsteueramt des letzten steuerlichen Wohnsitzes in Luxemburg eine schriftliche Erbschaftserklärung (déclaration de succession) einreichen (bzw. eine déclaration de mutation par décès, falls die verstorbene Person keinen Wohnsitz in Luxemburg hatte, dort aber Immobilien besaß) [10]. Die gesetzliche Einreichungsfrist beträgt 6 Monate bei einem Tod in Luxemburg und 8 Monate, wenn der Tod in einem anderen europäischen Land wie Deutschland eingetreten ist [10]. Für die Ausstellung einer notariellen Erbenbekundung (acte de notoriété), die Testamentseröffnung und die Nachlassabwicklung in Luxemburg empfiehlt sich die Einschaltung eines Notars über die Notarkammer (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) [10].
  • In Deutschland (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, Renten Service, Krankenversicherung und Nachlassgericht):
    • Deutsche Renten und Sterbevierteljahr (innerhalb von 30 Tagen): Bestand ein deutscher Rentenbezug oder lagen deutsche Versicherungszeiten vor, melden Sie den Tod unverzüglich der Auszahlungsstelle (Renten Service der Deutschen Post, Telefon +49 221 569 2777), um Überzahlungen zu stoppen und für überlebende Ehegatten oder eingetragene Lebenspartner innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod die Vorschusszahlung für das Sterbevierteljahr zu beantragen [12]. Anträge auf deutsche Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrente stellen Sie beim Rententräger (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, kostenfreie Rufnummer 0800 1000 4800 in Deutschland bzw. +49 30 865 0 aus dem Ausland) [11].
    • Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung und deutsches Nachlassgericht: Informieren Sie gegebenenfalls die deutsche Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung (Krankenkasse) [11]. Befanden sich Bankkonten oder Immobilien in Deutschland, informiert das deutsche Standesamt automatisch das Registerportal (Zentrales Testamentsregister) der Bundesnotarkammer, welches verwahrte Verfügungen von Todes wegen an das zuständige Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht übermittelt; dort können Erben bei Bedarf einen deutschen Erbschein oder ein Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis beantragen [13].

de.closingQuestion: Damit wir Ihnen noch gezielter weiterhelfen können: 1. In welcher deutschen Gemeinde (und welchem Bundesland) ist der Sterbefall eingetreten, und in welcher luxemburgischen Gemeinde hatte Ihr Familienangehöriger seinen Wohnsitz bzw. wohin soll die Überführung erfolgen? 2. Planen Sie eine Sargüberführung nach Luxemburg, eine Einäscherung in Deutschland mit Urnentransport nach Luxemburg oder eine Bestattung in Deutschland?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in Spain: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Spain, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and Spain.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences for the loss of your family member. When a person with French nationality or residence ties in France dies in Spain, the procedures are coordinated between the Spanish health and civil registry authorities and the French consular services and social welfare bodies. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and forensic clearance in Spain
steps.html:
• Death in a healthcare facility: If the death occurs in a hospital or clinic in Spain, the attending medical team issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción), an essential requirement for registering the death and authorizing any transfer or funeral service [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs outside a hospital or is sudden, accidental, or without an immediately certifiable medical cause, you must call the emergency number 112. In the event of a judicial or suspicious death, the Duty Court (Juzgado de Guardia) intervenes and the body is transferred to the corresponding Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses, for example in Madrid or Barcelona) for an autopsy before the judge issues the burial or transfer authorization [1][2].
  • Sanitary timeframes: Regional mortuary health regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria) and state regulations supervised by the Ministerio de Sanidad (Ministry of Health) govern preservation conditions, embalming, and general timeframes (typically between 24 and 48 hours after death, unless judicial intervention or special preservation techniques apply) [2].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, licensed funeral directors, and French consular assistance
steps.html:
• Checking insurance and assistance coverage: Before hiring services independently, check whether the deceased person held travel insurance, roadside assistance, a bank card with international coverage, or a funeral/repatriation policy, as the insurance company usually appoints and directly funds the funeral operators [3].
  • Appointing funeral directors: The family or the insurer must entrust the arrangements to a licensed funeral company in Spain, a sector represented by the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF), which coordinates with a prefecture-licensed funeral operator in France, grouped under bodies such as the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) [4][5]. These operators handle the technical, sanitary, and logistical formalities between both countries without the family having to visit technical offices in person.
  • Consular assistance: Contact the Consulat général de France à Madrid (Consulate General of France in Madrid, phone +34 91 700 78 00) or the competent French consulate for the district where the death occurred (such as the Consulate General in Barcelona), in accordance with the guidelines of France Diplomatie [3][6]. Consular services guide the family, provide reference lists of funeral companies (purely for informational purposes), and issue the necessary consular documentation, although the French State does not cover funeral or repatriation expenses [3].

steps.title: Registration in the Spanish Civil Registry and transcription or recognition in France
steps.html:
• Local registration in Spain: The death must generally be registered within 24 hours of the event at the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the Spanish municipality where the death occurred, a formality usually carried out by the appointed funeral home with the Ministerio de Justicia (Ministry of Justice) [1]. Request several copies of the full literal death certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción, in Spanish) and the multilingual death certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de defunción, Form C of the 1976 Vienna Convention), which is exempt from an apostille and translation between Spain and France [1][6].
  • Transcription in the French civil registry: With the original Certificado Literal de Defunción issued in Spain, the deceased person's French national identity card or passport, their birth certificate, and the French family record book (livret de famille), you can request the transcription of the death into the French consular registers through the Consulat général de France à Madrid [6]. Once transcribed, the record takes full legal effect before any town hall (mairie) and public administration in France, in accordance with the rules on Service-Public.fr [6][7].

steps.title: International repatriation to France vs. local burial or cremation in Spain
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body or ashes to France: For the international transfer of a body from Spain to France, the Spanish funeral home processes the sanitary authorization and the mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio / laissez-passer mortuaire) under the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin Arrangement, via the electronic Foreign Health (Sanidad Exterior) system of the Ministerio de Sanidad and the French consular authorization [2][3]. Certified embalming or preservation care (soins de conservation) and a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner are required [2][3]. If you choose cremation in Spain and transport the cinerary urn to France, the sanitary requirements are simpler, requiring the cremation certificate, the death certificate, and a sealed urn with the corresponding consular authorization [2][3].
  • Local burial or cremation in Spain: If the family decides to hold the burial or cremation directly in the Spanish municipality, the funeral operator obtains the burial or cremation permit following registration at the local Civil Registry, observing the regional mortuary health timeframes [1][2].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, pensions, taxes, and estate administration in France and Spain
steps.html:
• Social security and pensions in France: Notify the French bodies with which the deceased person was affiliated [7]. With the Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (via the Ameli.fr portal), eligible beneficiaries can claim the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès using form Cerfa S3180), which has a 1-month priority period for direct dependents and a general time limit of up to 2 years [8]. If the deceased person paid contributions or received a pension in France, report the death and check entitlement to a survivor's pension (pension de réversion) with L'Assurance Retraite (phone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and supplementary schemes such as Agirc-Arrco, under the European coordination rules explained by Cleiss [9][10].
  • Succession and taxes in France: To settle bank accounts, property, and taxes in France, families usually instruct a notary through Notaires de France, who prepares the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and the inheritance tax return (the general filing deadline is 6 months if the death occurs in metropolitan France and 12 months when the death occurs abroad) [11].
  • Benefits and succession in Spain: If the deceased person resided, worked, or owned assets in Spain, you can apply for the funeral grant (auxilio por defunción) and widowhood or orphanhood pensions (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) from the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) [12]. Once 15 working days have passed since the death, request the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad, Form 790 / Modelo 790) from the Ministerio de Justicia to verify whether a will exists in Spain and to manage the inheritance and the Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones, general deadline of 6 months from the date of death, extendable within the first 5 months) [1][13].

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre España y Francia: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre España y Francia: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con nacionalidad o vínculos de residencia en Francia fallece en España, las gestiones se coordinan entre las autoridades sanitarias y registrales españolas y los servicios consulares y organismos sociales franceses. A continuación se detallan los cinco pasos oficiales principales en orden.

steps.title: Certificación médica del fallecimiento y autorización forense en España
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento en centro sanitario: Si el deceso ocurre en un hospital o clínica en España, el equipo médico tratante expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial, requisito indispensable para inscribir la defunción y autorizar cualquier traslado o servicio funerario [1].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Si el fallecimiento se produce fuera de un hospital o de forma súbita, accidental o sin causa médica certificable inmediata, se debe llamar al teléfono de emergencias 112. En caso de muerte judicial o sospechosa, interviene el Juzgado de Guardia y el cuerpo se traslada al Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses correspondiente (por ejemplo, en Madrid o Barcelona) para la práctica de la autopsia antes de que el juez emita la autorización de enterramiento o traslado [1][2].
  • Plazos sanitarios: Los reglamentos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria y la normativa estatal supervisada por el Ministerio de Sanidad regulan las condiciones de conservación, embalsamamiento y los plazos generales (habitualmente entre las 24 y las 48 horas desde el fallecimiento, salvo intervención judicial o técnicas de conservación especiales) [2].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriación, empresas funerarias habilitadas y asistencia consular de Francia
steps.html:
• Verificación de seguros y asistencia: Antes de contratar servicios por cuenta propia, compruebe si la persona fallecida disponía de un seguro de viaje, asistencia en carretera, tarjeta bancaria con cobertura internacional o póliza de decesos/repatriación, ya que la compañía aseguradora suele designar y financiar directamente a los operadores funerarios [3].
  • Designación de empresas funerarias: La familia o la aseguradora debe encargar la gestión a una empresa funeraria habilitada en España, sector representado por la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios, que se coordina con un operador funerario habilitado en prefectura en Francia, agrupado en entidades como la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire [4][5]. Estos operadores se encargan de los trámites técnicos, sanitarios y logísticos entre ambos países, sin que la familia tenga que acudir personalmente a las oficinas técnicas.
  • Asistencia consular: Contacte con el Consulat général de France à Madrid (teléfono +34 91 700 78 00) o el consulado francés competente según la demarcación del lugar de fallecimiento (como el Consulado General en Barcelona), conforme a las directrices de France Diplomatie [3][6]. Los servicios consulares orientan a la familia, facilitan listados de empresas funerarias de referencia (sin que ello implique respaldo ni clasificación comercial) y expiden la documentación consular necesaria, aunque el Estado francés no sufraga los gastos funerarios ni de repatriación [3].

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil español y transcripción o reconocimiento en Francia
steps.html:
• Inscripción local en España: El fallecimiento debe inscribirse, por lo general dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al deceso, en el Registro Civil del municipio español donde ocurrió el fallecimiento, trámite que habitualmente realiza la funeraria designada ante el Ministerio de Justicia [1]. Solicite varios ejemplares del Certificado Literal de Defunción (en español) y del Certificado Plurilingüe de defunción (Fórmula C del Convenio de Viena de 1976), que está exento de apostilla y traducción entre España y Francia [1][6].
  • Transcripción en el registro civil francés: Con el Certificado Literal de Defunción original expedido en España, el documento de identidad o pasaporte francés de la persona fallecida, su acta de nacimiento y el libro de familia francés, puede solicitar la transcripción del fallecimiento en los registros consulares franceses a través del Consulat général de France à Madrid [6]. Una vez transcrito, el acto surte plenos efectos ante cualquier alcaldía (mairie) y administración en Francia, conforme a las normas de Service-Public.fr [6][7].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional a Francia frente a inhumación o cremación local en España
steps.html:
• Repatriación del cuerpo o de las cenizas a Francia: Para el traslado internacional de un cuerpo desde España hacia Francia, la funeraria española tramita la autorización sanitaria y el salvoconducto mortuorio (laissez-passer mortuaire) al amparo del Acuerdo de Estrasburgo de 1973 y del Acuerdo de Berlín de 1937, mediante el sistema electrónico de Sanidad Exterior del Ministerio de Sanidad y la autorización consular francesa [2][3]. Se exige embalsamamiento o cuidados de conservación certificados y un féretro hermético con revestimiento de zinc sellado [2][3]. Si se opta por cremar en España y trasladar la urna cineraria a Francia, los requisitos sanitarios son más sencillos, requiriéndose el certificado de cremación, el certificado de defunción y una urna sellada con la autorización consular correspondiente [2][3].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en España: Si la familia decide realizar el entierro o la cremación directamente en el municipio español, el operador funerario gestiona la licencia de enterramiento o incineración tras la inscripción en el Registro Civil local, respetando los plazos sanitarios autonómicos [1][2].

steps.title: Prestaciones de supervivencia, pensiones, impuestos y sucesión en Francia y España
steps.html:
• Seguridad social y pensiones en Francia: Notifique el fallecimiento a los organismos franceses a los que estuviera afiliada la persona fallecida [7]. Ante la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (portal Ameli.fr), los derechohabientes pueden solicitar el capital décès (mediante el formulario Cerfa S3180), con un plazo de prioridad de 1 mes para dependientes directos y hasta 2 años en general [8]. Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o percibía pensión en Francia, comunique el deceso y consulte el derecho a la pensión de viudedad (pension de réversion) ante L'Assurance Retraite (teléfono 3960 o +33 9 71 10 39 60 desde el extranjero) y los regímenes complementarios como Agirc-Arrco, bajo la coordinación europea explicada por el Cleiss [9][10].
  • Sucesión e impuestos en Francia: Para el ajuste de cuentas bancarias, bienes e impuestos en Francia, las familias suelen acudir a un notario a través de Notaires de France, quien tramita el acte de notoriété y la declaración fiscal de sucesión (cuyo plazo general es de 6 meses si el fallecimiento ocurre en Francia metropolitana y de 12 meses cuando el fallecimiento se produce en el extranjero) [11].
  • Prestaciones y sucesión en España: Si la persona fallecida residía, trabajaba o tenía bienes en España, se puede solicitar el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad u orfandad ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social [12]. Transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la defunción, se solicita el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad (Modelo 790) ante el Ministerio de Justicia para verificar si existe testamento en España y gestionar la herencia y el Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones (plazo general de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento, prorrogable dentro de los primeros 5 meses) [1][13].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Spain dies in France: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in France, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Spain and France.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences for the loss of your family member. When a person with Spanish nationality or residence ties in Spain dies in France, the procedures are coordinated between the French medical and municipal authorities and the Spanish consular, social security, and judicial services. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and forensic clearance in France
steps.html:
• Death in a healthcare facility or nursing home (EHPAD): The physician in the hospital department or care facility certifies the death and issues the official medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, on a Cerfa form or electronically via CertDc), which is essential for declaring the death and authorizing any funeral operation [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call SAMU on 15 or the European emergency number 112 so that a doctor can certify the death [1]. In the event of a sudden, accidental, or suspicious death, the doctor ticks the forensic hold box (obstacle médico-légal): the police or gendarmerie and the Public Prosecutor (procureur de la République) then intervene to order a transfer to a forensic medicine institute (institut médico-légal, for example in Paris, Lyon, or Marseille) before issuing the burial permit or authorization to seal the coffin [1].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, licensed funeral operators, and Spanish consular assistance
steps.html:
• Checking insurance policies: Before making any independent financial commitment, check whether the deceased person held a Spanish funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos), travel or repatriation insurance, or coverage linked to a bank card, as the assistance company generally appoints and directly pays the funeral operators [2].
  • Appointing funeral operators: The family or insurer appoints a prefecture-licensed funeral operator in France (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture), represented nationally by the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF), which coordinates with a licensed funeral company in Spain, a sector grouped within the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) [3][4]. These professionals manage all technical and sanitary formalities between France and Spain without the family having to visit technical administrative offices in person.
  • Spanish consular contact: Contact the Consulado General de España en París (Consulate General of Spain in Paris, email cog.paris@maec.es and cog.paris.rgc@maec.es for the civil registry) or the Spanish consulate general territorially competent for the place of death in France (such as Lyon, Marseille, Toulouse, or Bordeaux) [2][5]. The consulate guides the family on transfer and civil registry procedures, although the Spanish State does not cover funeral expenses or repatriation costs [2].

steps.title: Declaration of death at the town hall in France and transcription in the Spanish civil registry
steps.html:
• Declaration at the town hall in France: The death must be declared within 24 hours (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred, following the official procedure set out on Service-Public.fr [1]. In practice, the hospital facility or the appointed funeral home often completes this step on behalf of the family [1]. Request several full copies of the death certificate (copie intégrale de l'acte de décès) as well as multilingual death certificate extracts (Form C of the 1976 Vienna Convention), which are accepted directly in Spain without an apostille or translation [1][5].
  • Consular registration and recording in Spain: For the death to take full legal effect in Spain, it must be registered in the consular civil registry at the Consulado General de España en París (or the competent Spanish consulate) upon presentation of the full copy of the French death certificate, the deceased person's Spanish identity card or passport, and the declaration form [5]. You will then be able to obtain the Spanish full death certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) through the Ministerio de Justicia (Ministry of Justice) [5][6].

steps.title: International repatriation to Spain vs. local burial or cremation in France
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body or ashes to Spain: The international transfer of a body from France to Spain is governed by the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin Arrangement [2][7]. The French funeral operator applies for the prefectural mortuary laissez-passer order (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) from the prefecture of the relevant department, arranges preservation care (soins de conservation) and placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner, and coordinates the entry sanitary inspection with the Foreign Health (Sanidad Exterior) service of the Ministerio de Sanidad (Ministry of Health) in Spain [2][7]. In the case of cremation in France followed by transport of the cinerary urn to Spain, the procedure is simplified and requires the death certificate, the cremation certificate, and a sealed urn [2][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in France: If the funeral takes place in France, the funeral operator obtains the burial or cremation authorization from the mayor of the municipality of death or coffin closure (generally between 24 hours and 6 working days after death) [1].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, pensions, taxes, and estate settlement in Spain and France
steps.html:
• Social security, pensions, and succession in Spain: Through the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS), eligible beneficiaries can apply for the funeral expenses grant (auxilio por defunción) as well as survivor pensions (pensión de viudedad or orfandad), with aggregation of contribution periods completed in Europe under the coordinated rules explained by Cleiss [8][9]. After a waiting period of 15 working days following the death, request the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad, Form 790 / Modelo 790) from the Ministerio de Justicia to check whether a will exists in Spain, settle the estate before a notary, and file the Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) within the statutory 6-month deadline [10].
  • Benefits, pensions, and succession in France: If the deceased person worked, paid contributions, or held assets in France, report the death to the Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (via the Ameli.fr portal) to claim, where applicable, the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès, form Cerfa S3180, with a 1-month priority period for dependents and a maximum time limit of 2 years) [11]. Also notify L'Assurance Retraite (on 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) as well as the supplementary pension fund Agirc-Arrco for any survivor's pension claim (pension de réversion) [12]. Finally, if the estate includes real property or requires a deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) in France, instruct a notarial office through Notaires de France; the inheritance tax declaration in France must be filed within 6 months when the death occurs in metropolitan France [13].

fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre France et Espagne : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml: Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne ayant la nationalité espagnole ou des liens de résidence en Espagne décède en France, les démarches s'articulent entre les autorités médicales et communales françaises et les services consulaires, sociaux et judiciaires espagnols. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et autorisation médico-légale en France
steps.html:
• Décès en établissement de santé ou EHPAD : Le médecin du service hospitalier ou de l'établissement constate le décès et établit le certificat médical de décès officiel (formulaire Cerfa ou par voie électronique CertDc), indispensable pour déclarer le décès et autoriser toute opération funéraire [1].
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU au 15 ou le numéro d'urgence européen 112 pour faire constater le décès par un médecin [1]. En cas de décès soudain, accidentel ou suspect, le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal : les forces de police ou de gendarmerie et le procureur de la République interviennent alors pour ordonner le transfert vers un institut médico-légal (par exemple à Paris, Lyon ou Marseille) avant de délivrer le permis d'inhumer ou l'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil [1].

steps.title: Assurance rapatriement, opérateurs funéraires habilités et assistance consulaire d'Espagne
steps.html:
• Vérification des contrats d'assurance : Avant tout engagement financier indépendant, vérifiez si la personne décédée bénéficiait d'une assurance décès espagnole (seguro de decesos), d'une assurance voyage ou rapatriement ou d'une garantie liée à sa carte bancaire, car l'assisteur mandate et règle généralement directement les opérateurs funéraires [2].
  • Mandatement des opérateurs funéraires : La famille ou l'assureur mandate un opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture en France, représenté au niveau national par la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire, qui se coordonne avec une entreprise funéraire habilitée en Espagne, secteur regroupé au sein de l'Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios [3][4]. Ces professionnels gèrent l'ensemble des formalités techniques et sanitaires entre la France et l'Espagne sans que la famille ait à se déplacer dans les services administratifs techniques.
  • Contact consulaire espagnol : Prenez contact avec le Consulado General de España en París (courriel cog.paris@maec.es et cog.paris.rgc@maec.es pour l'état civil) ou le consulat général d'Espagne territorialement compétent selon le lieu du décès en France (comme Lyon, Marseille, Toulouse ou Bordeaux) [2][5]. Le consulat oriente la famille sur les démarches de transfert et d'état civil, mais l'État espagnol ne prend pas en charge les frais funéraires ni les coûts de rapatriement [2].

steps.title: Déclaration de décès en mairie en France et transcription à l'état civil espagnol
steps.html:
• Déclaration à la mairie en France : Le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès de la mairie de la commune du lieu de décès, selon la procédure officielle décrite sur Service-Public.fr [1]. En pratique, l'établissement hospitalier ou l'entreprise de pompes funèbres mandatée effectue souvent cette démarche pour la famille [1]. Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès (copie intégrale de l'acte de décès) ainsi que des extraits plurilingues d'acte de décès (Formule C de la Convention de Vienne de 1976), acceptés directement en Espagne sans apostille ni traduction [1][5].
  • Inscription consulaire et enregistrement en Espagne : Pour que le décès produise tous ses effets juridiques en Espagne, il doit être inscrit au registre civil consulaire auprès du Consulado General de España en París (ou du consulat espagnol compétent) sur présentation de la copie intégrale de l'acte de décès français, de la pièce d'identité ou du passeport espagnol de la personne décédée et du formulaire de déclaration [5]. Vous pourrez ensuite obtenir le Certificado Literal de Defunción espagnol via le Ministerio de Justicia [5][6].

steps.title: Rapatriement international vers l'Espagne ou inhumation et crémation en France
steps.html:
• Rapatriement du corps ou des cendres vers l'Espagne : Le transfert international d'un corps de la France vers l'Espagne relève de l'Accord de Strasbourg de 1973 et de l'Arrangement de Berlin de 1937 [2][7]. L'opérateur funéraire français sollicite l'arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire auprès de la préfecture du département concerné, organise les soins de conservation et la mise en bière dans un cercueil hermétique muni d'un caisson en zinc scellé, puis coordonne le contrôle sanitaire d'entrée avec le service de Sanidad Exterior du Ministerio de Sanidad en Espagne [2][7]. En cas de crémation en France suivie du transport de l'urne cinéraire vers l'Espagne, la procédure est simplifiée et requiert l'acte de décès, le certificat de crémation et une urne scellée [2][7].
  • Inhumation ou crémation locale en France : Si les obsèques ont lieu en France, l'opérateur funéraire obtient l'autorisation d'inhumation ou de crémation auprès du maire de la commune du décès ou du lieu de mise en bière (généralement entre 24 heures et 6 jours ouvrables après le décès) [1].

steps.title: Prestations de survie, retraites, fiscalité et règlement de la succession en Espagne et en France
steps.html:
• Sécurité sociale, pensions et succession en Espagne : Auprès de l'Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social, les ayants droit peuvent solliciter l'allocation pour frais funéraires (auxilio por defunción) ainsi que les pensions de survie (pensión de viudedad ou orfandad), avec totalisation des périodes cotisées en Europe selon les règles coordonnées présentées par le Cleiss [8][9]. Après un délai de 15 jours ouvrables suivant le décès, demandez le Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad (modèle 790) auprès du Ministerio de Justicia pour vérifier l'existence d'un testament en Espagne, régler la succession devant notaire et déposer l'Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones dans le délai légal de 6 mois [10].
  • Prestations, retraites et succession en France : Si la personne décédée travaillait, cotisait ou détenait des biens en France, signalez le décès à la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (portail Ameli.fr) pour demander, le cas échéant, le capital décès (formulaire Cerfa S3180, priorité d'un mois pour les personnes à charge et délai maximal de 2 ans) [11]. Informez également L'Assurance Retraite (au 3960 ou +33 9 71 10 39 60 depuis l'étranger) ainsi que la retraite complémentaire Agirc-Arrco pour toute demande de pension de réversion [12]. Enfin, si la succession comprend un bien immobilier ou nécessite un acte de notoriété en France, mandatez un office notarial via Notaires de France ; la déclaration fiscale de succession en France doit être déposée dans les 6 mois lorsque le décès survient en France métropolitaine [13].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in Portugal: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Portugal, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and Portugal.
introHtml: Please accept our condolences for the loss of your family member. When a person with French nationality or residence ties in France dies in Portugal, the procedures are coordinated between the Portuguese health and civil registry authorities and the French consular services and social welfare bodies. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and forensic clearance in Portugal
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital facility: If the death occurs in a hospital or clinic in Portugal, the physician verifies the death and electronically issues the Death Certificate (Certificado de Óbito) and Transport Permit (Guia de Transporte) through SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito), the national platform managed by the Serviço Nacional de Saúde (National Health Service) in coordination with the Directorate-General of Health (Direção-Geral da Saúde), automatically transmitting the data to the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary) [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: If the death occurs outside a hospital or is sudden, accidental, or without an immediately verifiable natural cause, you must call the European emergency number 112. The police authority (PSP or GNR) and the public health officer (delegado de saúde) intervene; in the event of a violent death or death of unknown cause, the doctor sends the Clinical and Circumstantial Information Bulletin (Boletim de Informação Clínica e Circunstancial) to the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público) via SICO, and the body may be taken to a branch of the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses, for example in Lisbon, Porto, or Coimbra) for an autopsy before release for the funeral or transfer [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, licensed funeral agencies, and French consular support
steps.html:
• Checking insurance and assistance coverage: Before entering into independent financial commitments, check whether the deceased person held travel insurance, bank card assistance, motor insurance, or a funeral/repatriation policy, as the insurer usually appoints and pays the funeral operators directly [3].
  • Appointing funeral operators: The family or insurer appoints a licensed funeral agency in Portugal (agência funerária habilitada, registered with the Directorate-General for Economic Activities / Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas, as detailed on the gov.pt portal, and represented by sector associations such as ANEL or AAFC), which coordinates the process with a prefecture-licensed funeral operator in France, represented by the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) [4][5]. These professionals handle all technical and sanitary permits between the two countries without the family having to visit technical offices in person.
  • French consular contact: Contact the Ambassade de France au Portugal (Consular Section of the Embassy of France in Lisbon, phone +351 210 608 311), following the general guidelines of France Diplomatie [3][6]. Consular services support the family with administrative formalities and the issuance of consular documents, although the French State does not cover funeral expenses or repatriation costs [3][6].

steps.title: Registration of the death at the Civil Registry Office in Portugal and transcription for France
steps.html:
• Declaration of death in Portugal: A death occurring in Portuguese territory must be declared within 48 hours at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil, or at an Espaço Óbito desk in the hospital) under the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado, a step that in practice is almost always carried out by the appointed funeral agency [2][7]. Registration of the death record (Assento de Óbito) is free of charge [2]. Also request multilingual death certificates (Form C of the 1976 Vienna Convention), which are exempt from an apostille and translation between Portugal and France [2][6].
  • Transcription in the French civil registry: With the original Portuguese death certificate, the deceased person's French national identity card or passport, their French birth certificate, and the French family record book (livret de famille), you can request the consular transcription or declaration of the death at the Ambassade de France au Portugal [6]. Once transcribed, the civil status record is updated before French town halls (mairies) and public services, as detailed on Service-Public.fr [6][8].

steps.title: International repatriation to France vs. local burial or cremation in Portugal
steps.html:
• Repatriation of the body or ashes to France: The international transport of mortal remains between Portugal and France is governed by the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin Arrangement, whose official procedures are set out on the gov.pt portal [4]. The Portuguese funeral agency obtains the transfer permit (alvará de trasladação) and the mortuary laissez-passer (livre-trânsito mortuário / laissez-passer mortuaire) from the health, police, and consular authorities, ensuring thanatological preparation and placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner [3][4]. In the event of cremation in Portugal and transport of the urn of ashes to France, the procedure is simplified, requiring the cremation certificate, the death certificate, and a sealed urn accompanied by consular authorization [3][4].
  • Local burial or cremation in Portugal: If the family chooses burial or cremation in Portugal, the funeral agency handles the municipal and cemetery authorizations immediately after the death entry (assento de óbito) is recorded in the civil registry [2][4].

steps.title: Death benefits, pensions, taxes, and heir qualification in France and Portugal
steps.html:
• Social security and pensions in France: Report the death to the relevant French agencies [8]. With the Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (via the Ameli.fr portal), eligible relatives can apply for the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès, form Cerfa S3180), which offers a 1-month priority period for dependents and a general deadline of 2 years [9]. If the deceased person paid contributions or received a retirement pension in France, report the death and check entitlement to a survivor's pension (pension de réversion) with L'Assurance Retraite (phone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and the supplementary pension scheme Agirc-Arrco, benefiting from the European coordination rules explained by Cleiss [10][11].
  • Succession and taxes in France: To unblock bank accounts, manage property, and fulfill tax obligations in France, heirs usually instruct a notary via Notaires de France to draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and submit the inheritance tax declaration (the statutory deadline in France is 6 months for deaths occurring in metropolitan France and 12 months when the death occurs abroad) [12].
  • Social benefits, inheritance, and taxes in Portugal: If the deceased person had a contribution record or residence in Portugal, family members can apply to Segurança Social (Social Security) for the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days of the death), Reimbursement of Funeral Expenses (Reembolso das Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days for the person who paid for the funeral, not cumulative with the death grant), and the Survivor's Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [13]. To deal with the estate and assets left in Portugal, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) can use the Espaço Óbito and the Inheritance Desk (Balcão das Heranças) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado to complete the qualification of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and division of the estate, and must report the gratuitous transfer of assets (Stamp Duty Form 1 / Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) to the Tax and Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira) by the end of the third month following the month of death [7][14].

pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Portugal e França: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Portugal e França: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Lamentamos o falecimento do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa com nacionalidade ou laços de residência em França falece em Portugal, os procedimentos articulam-se entre as autoridades de saúde e de registo civil portuguesas e os serviços consulares e organismos sociais franceses. Apresentam-se de seguida os cinco principais passos oficiais por ordem.

steps.title: Certificação médica do óbito e autorização médico-legal em Portugal
steps.html:
• Óbito em unidade hospitalar: Se o falecimento ocorrer num hospital ou clínica em Portugal, o médico verifica o óbito e emite eletronicamente o Certificado de Óbito e a Guia de Transporte através do SICO (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito), plataforma nacional gerida pelo Serviço Nacional de Saúde em articulação com a Direção-Geral da Saúde, comunicando automaticamente os dados ao Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [1][2].
  • Óbito no domicílio, hotel ou via pública: Caso o óbito ocorra fora de um hospital ou de forma súbita, acidental ou sem causa natural imediatamente comprovável, deve ligar para o número europeu de emergência 112. Intervêm a autoridade policial (PSP ou GNR) e o delegado de saúde; em caso de morte violenta ou de causa ignorada, o médico envia o Boletim de Informação Clínica e Circunstancial ao Ministério Público através do SICO, podendo o corpo ser encaminhado para uma delegação do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (por exemplo, em Lisboa, no Porto ou em Coimbra) para autópsia antes da libertação para funeral ou trasladação [1][2].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriamento, agências funerárias habilitadas e apoio consular de França
steps.html:
• Verificação de seguros e assistência: Antes de assumir compromissos financeiros autónomos, confirme se a pessoa falecida dispunha de seguro de viagem, assistência de cartão bancário, seguro automóvel ou contrato de previdência/repatriamento, pois a seguradora habitualmente nomeia e paga diretamente aos operadores funerários [3].
  • Nomeação de operadores funerários: A família ou a seguradora mandata uma agência funerária habilitada em Portugal (registada junto da Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas, conforme orientado no portal gov.pt, e representada por associações do setor como a ANEL ou a AAFC), que coordena o processo com um operador funerário habilitado em prefeitura em França, representado pela Fédération Nationale du Funéraire [4][5]. Estes profissionais tratam de todas as licenças técnicas e sanitárias entre os dois países sem que a família tenha de se deslocar a serviços técnicos.
  • Contacto consular francês: Contacte a Ambassade de France au Portugal (Secção Consular em Lisboa, telefone +351 210 608 311), seguindo também as orientações gerais da France Diplomatie [3][6]. Os serviços consulares apoiam a família nas formalidades administrativas e na emissão de documentos consulares, embora o Estado francês não assuma as despesas funerárias nem os custos de repatriamento [3][6].

steps.title: Registo do óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil em Portugal e transcrição para França
steps.html:
• Declaração de óbito em Portugal: O óbito ocorrido em território português deve ser declarado no prazo de 48 horas em qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil (ou num balcão do Espaço Óbito no hospital) junto do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado, diligência que na prática é quase sempre efetuada pela agência funerária mandatada [2][7]. O registo do Assento de Óbito é gratuito [2]. Solicite também certidões de óbito em modelo plurilingue (Fórmula C da Convenção de Viena de 1976), que dispensam apostila e tradução entre Portugal e França [2][6].
  • Transcrição no registo civil francês: Com a certidão de óbito portuguesa original, o bilhete de identidade ou passaporte francês da pessoa falecida, a sua certidão de nascimento francesa e o livret de famille, pode requerer a transcrição ou declaração consular do óbito junto da Ambassade de France au Portugal [6]. Após a transcrição, o registo fica atualizado perante as câmaras municipais (mairies) e serviços públicos franceses, conforme detalhado em Service-Public.fr [6][8].

steps.title: Repatriamento internacional para França ou inumação e cremação local em Portugal
steps.html:
• Repatriamento do corpo ou das cinzas para França: O transporte internacional de restos mortais entre Portugal e França rege-se pelo Acordo de Estrasburgo de 1973 e pelo Acordo de Berlim de 1937, cujos procedimentos oficiais constam do portal gov.pt [4]. A agência funerária portuguesa obtém o alvará de trasladação e o livre-trânsito mortuário (laissez-passer mortuaire) junto das autoridades sanitárias, policiais e consulares, assegurando a preparação tanatológica e o acondicionamento em caixão hermético com caixa de zinco selada [3][4]. Em caso de cremação em Portugal e transporte da urna de cinzas para França, o procedimento é simplificado, exigindo o certificado de cremação, a certidão de óbito e uma urna selada acompanhada da autorização consular [3][4].
  • Inumação ou cremação local em Portugal: Se a família optar pelo funeral ou cremação em Portugal, a agência funerária trata das autorizações municipais e cemiteriais logo após a lavratura do assento de óbito no registo civil [2][4].

steps.title: Prestações por morte, pensões, impostos e habilitação de herdeiros em França e em Portugal
steps.html:
• Segurança social e pensões em França: Comunique o falecimento aos organismos franceses relevantes [8]. Junto da Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (portal Ameli.fr), os familiares elegíveis podem requerer o capital décès (formulário Cerfa S3180), dispondo de 1 mês de prioridade para pessoas a cargo e de um prazo geral de 2 anos [9]. Se a pessoa falecida descontava ou recebia reforma em França, participe o óbito e verifique o direito à pensão de sobrevivência (pension de réversion) junto da L'Assurance Retraite (telefone 3960 ou +33 9 71 10 39 60 a partir do estrangeiro) e do regime complementar Agirc-Arrco, beneficiando das regras de coordenação europeia explicadas pelo Cleiss [10][11].
  • Sucessão e impostos em França: Para desbloquear contas bancárias, gerir património e cumprir obrigações fiscais em França, os herdeiros recorrem habitualmente a um notário através dos Notaires de France para lavrar o acte de notoriété e submeter a declaração fiscal de sucessão (cujo prazo legal em França é de 6 meses para óbitos ocorridos em França metropolitana e de 12 meses quando o óbito ocorre no estrangeiro) [12].
  • Apoios sociais, herança e impostos em Portugal: Caso a pessoa falecida tivesse carreira contributiva ou residência em Portugal, os familiares podem requerer junto da Segurança Social o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do óbito), o Reembolso das Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias para quem pagou o funeral, não acumulável com o subsídio por morte) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [13]. Para tratar da herança e dos bens deixados em Portugal, o cabeça-de-casal pode recorrer ao Espaço Óbito e ao Balcão das Heranças do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado para realizar a habilitação de herdeiros e a partilha, devendo participar a transmissão gratuita de bens (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) à Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira até ao final do 3.º mês seguinte ao do falecimento [7][14].
