it.title: Cosa fare in caso di decesso tra Italia e Francia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso tra Italia e Francia: certificato medico di morte, impresa funebre autorizzata, registrazione allo Stato Civile, pratiche consolari e rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri, e pensione di reversibilità e successione.
it.introHtml:
Vi esprimiamo le nostre più sincere condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona con cittadinanza francese o legami di residenza in Francia muore in Italia, gli accertamenti medici iniziali, la dichiarazione di morte presso il Comune e il rilascio del Passaporto Mortuario seguono la normativa italiana del luogo di decesso, mentre la trascrizione consolare dell'atto di morte, l'accoglienza del feretro o dell'urna in Francia e le pratiche previdenziali e successorie coinvolgono le autorità francesi e italiane.

Ecco i cinque passaggi ufficiali da seguire in ordine cronologico:

steps.title: Constatazione di decesso, certificato necroscopico e nulla osta giudiziario in Italia (immediatamente)
steps.html:
Il primo adempimento sanitario in Italia dipende dal luogo e dalle circostanze del decesso, in conformità al Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria (D.P.R. n. 285/1990) [1]:

  • Decesso in ospedale, clinica o struttura socio-sanitaria: La direzione sanitaria della struttura accerta il decesso, compila l'avviso di morte e la scheda ISTAT delle cause di morte e trasmette la documentazione all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano competente [1].
  • Decesso a domicilio, in hotel o in luogo pubblico: Contattate immediatamente un medico o il numero unico di emergenza 112 (o 118) per la prima constatazione di decesso e la denuncia delle cause di morte entro 24 ore [1]. Successivamente, il medico necroscopo incaricato dall'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL o ATS) effettua la visita necroscopica obbligatoria - di norma tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso - e rilascia il certificato necroscopico indispensabile per l'autorizzazione alla sepoltura, alla cremazione o al trasporto internazionale [1].
  • Morte improvvisa, violenta o sospetta (Autorità Giudiziaria): Se il decesso avviene senza assistenza medica, in luogo pubblico o per cause violente o da accertare, intervengono le forze dell'ordine e la salma è posta a disposizione della Procura della Repubblica. Nessuna chiusura del feretro, cremazione, inumazione o rimpatrio verso la Francia può avvenire prima del rilascio del formale nulla osta alla sepoltura da parte del magistrato [1][2].

steps.title: Verifica delle assicurazioni, incarico alle imprese funebri e contatto con il Consolato di Francia in Italia
steps.html:
Prima di firmare un contratto funebre a titolo privato, verificate subito se la persona deceduta disponeva di un'assicurazione di viaggio o rimpatrio sanitario, di una copertura legata a una carta bancaria o mutua francese (mutuelle), oppure di un contratto di previdenza funeraria (contrat d'assurance obsèques) che organizzi e copra direttamente il trasferimento [2]:

  • Coordinamento tra un'impresa funebre in Italia e un operatore abilitato in Francia: Per il disbrigo delle pratiche comunali e sanitarie in Italia e l'eventuale trasporto transfrontaliero, la famiglia conferisce mandato a un'impresa funebre autorizzata in Italia, che si coordina con un operatore funebre abilitato in prefettura in Francia (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) per l'accoglienza e la sepoltura o cremazione nel comune francese di destinazione [1][2][7].
  • Federazioni nazionali di categoria (riferimenti neutri): Clarvia fornisce questi recapiti a solo scopo informativo e non raccomanda, approva né classifica specifici operatori commerciali. In Italia potete individuare un'impresa qualificata tramite FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, telefono +39 051 6650285, email info@feniof.it) [4] o FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, telefono +39 02 33403992, email info@federcofit.it) [5]. In Francia potete verificare gli operatori abilitati tramite il portale ufficiale Service-Public.fr (telefono 3939 dalla Francia o +33 1 73 60 39 39 dall'estero) [6] oppure contattare la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, telefono +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [8] e la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, telefono +33 1 46 60 24 24) [9].
  • Assistenza consolare di Francia in Italia: Segnalate il decesso alla rete consolare francese competente per territorio: l'Ambasciata di Francia a Roma (Servizio di Stato Civile per il Centro e Sud Italia, telefono +39 06 96 74 80 49, servizio France Consulaire +39 02 38 59 40 17, email etat-civil.rome-amba@diplomatie.gouv.fr) oppure il Consolato Generale di Francia a Milano (per il Nord Italia, telefono +39 02 38 59 40 17) [2][3]. Gli uffici consolari francesi assistono i familiari nelle procedure amministrative, rilasciano le autorizzazioni consolari eventualmente richieste e curano lo stato civile francese [2][3].

steps.title: Dichiarazione di morte in Italia (entro 24 ore), estratto Modello C e trascrizione per la Francia
steps.html:
La dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano in cui è avvenuta la morte (ad esempio presso il Comune di Milano, Roma Capitale o altro Comune competente) [1]:

  • Atti rilasciati dal Comune italiano: L'impresa funebre incaricata o la direzione sanitaria trasmette la dichiarazione all'Ufficiale di Stato Civile, che registra l'atto di morte e rilascia il permesso di seppellimento [1]. Richiedete subito al Comune italiano più esemplari della copia integrale dell'atto di morte (estratto per copia integrale dell'atto di morte) e più estratti di morte plurilingue su Modello C (Convenzione CIEC di Vienna dell'8 settembre 1976) [1][2][3].
  • Esenzione da apostille e riconoscimento in Francia: Poiché sia l'Italia sia la Francia aderiscono alla Convenzione di Vienna del 1976 e applicano il Regolamento (UE) 2016/1191, l'estratto plurilingue su Modello C è direttamente valido in Francia presso mairies, banche, notai ed enti previdenziali senza necessità di Apostille né di traduzione giurata [2][6].
  • Trascrizione nei registri di stato civile francesi: Mentre un decesso avvenuto sul territorio francese viene dichiarato in mairie entro 24 ore (esclusi fine settimana e festivi) secondo Service-Public.fr [6], per il decesso di un cittadino francese avvenuto in Italia è opportuno richiedere la trascrizione dell'atto di morte italiano nei registri dello stato civile consolare francese (presso l'Ambasciata di Francia a Roma o il Consolato Generale a Milano) [2][3]. Per la trascrizione consolare per corrispondenza è richiesto l'originale della copia integrale dell'atto di morte rilasciata dal Comune italiano (il semplice estratto plurilingue non basta per la trascrizione consolare), insieme alla prova della cittadinanza francese della persona deceduta (carta d'identità o passaporto francese), all'atto di nascita e al livret de famille per l'aggiornamento e l'annotazione a margine dell'atto di nascita in Francia [2][3].

steps.title: Scelta tra rimpatrio internazionale verso la Francia e sepoltura o cremazione locale in Italia
steps.html:
L'impresa funebre coordina i permessi sanitari e amministrativi in base alla scelta dei familiari:

  • Opzione A - Rimpatrio internazionale della salma o delle ceneri dall'Italia alla Francia:
    • Passaporto Mortuario comunale e requisiti sanitari: L'Italia e la Francia sono entrambe parti della Convenzione internazionale di Berlino del 10 febbraio 1937 sul trasporto dei cadaveri (mentre la Francia applica anche l'Accordo di Strasburgo del 1973 e il regime dell'arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire per le partenze dal territorio francese) [1][7]. Per il rimpatrio dall'Italia alla Francia, l'impresa funebre richiede all'Ufficio di Stato Civile / Polizia Mortuaria del Comune italiano di decesso il Passaporto Mortuario [1]. La normativa sanitaria prevede il certificato dell'ASL attestante l'assenza di malattie infettivo-diffusive e l'osservanza delle prescrizioni igieniche (trattamento antiputrefattivo / cure conservative ove prescritte) nonché la chiusura in doppia cassa (cofano esterno in legno e cassa interna metallica di zinco ermeticamente saldata) [1][7].
    • Ingresso in Francia senza doppio lasciapassare: In virtù della Convenzione di Berlino seguita dal Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) e dal Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (MEAE / France Diplomatie), il Passaporto Mortuario rilasciato dal Comune italiano consente il transito della frontiera e l'ingresso in Francia verso il comune francese di inumazione o cremazione [1][2][7].
    • Rimpatrio delle ceneri: Se la cremazione avviene in Italia (previa autorizzazione dell'Ufficiale di Stato Civile italiano sulla base della volontà espressa dalla persona deceduta o dai congiunti), il trasporto dell'urna cineraria sigillata verso la Francia è accompagnato dall'autorizzazione comunale al trasporto delle ceneri e, ove richiesto, dall'autorizzazione consolare francese [1][2][7].
  • Opzione B - Sepoltura o cremazione locale in Italia: Se le esequie si svolgono in Italia, l'inumazione, la tumulazione o la cremazione avvengono nel cimitero comunale italiano in base al permesso di seppellimento rilasciato dall'Ufficio di Stato Civile dopo la visita del medico necroscopo [1].

steps.title: Previdenza, capitale decesso, fisco e successione in Francia e in Italia
steps.html:
Con gli estratti di morte su Modello C e l'atto trascritto, avviate gli adempimenti previdenziali, fiscali e successori nei due Paesi:

  • Pratiche in Francia:
    • Assurance Maladie e casse pensioni francesi: Informate l'Assurance Maladie (CPAM / ameli.fr, telefono 3646 dalla Francia o +33 1 84 90 36 46 dall'estero) per la chiusura della posizione sanitaria e l'eventuale richiesta del capital décès (se la persona deceduta era assicurata come lavoratore o in situazione assimilata in Francia) [10]. Comunicate il decesso all'Assurance Retraite (CNAV, telefono 3960 o +33 9 71 10 39 60 dall'estero) e al regime complementare Agirc-Arrco per la richiesta della pensione di reversibilità (pension de réversion) [11].
    • Notaio e dichiarazione di successione in Francia: Se la persona deceduta aveva il domicilio fiscale o possedeva immobili o conti bancari in Francia, rivolgetevi a un notaio francese tramite la rete ufficiale Notaires de France (telefono +33 1 44 90 30 00) per redigere l'acte de notoriété, interrogare il registro francese delle ultime volontà (FCDDV) e presentare la dichiarazione di successione all'amministrazione fiscale francese (entro 6 mesi per un decesso in Francia metropolitana, termine portato a 12 mesi quando il decesso avviene fuori dalla Francia, come in Italia) [12][13].
  • Pratiche in Italia (se la persona risiedeva, lavorava o possedeva beni in Italia):
    • INPS e prestazioni ai superstiti: Se il vostro familiare percepiva una pensione italiana o aveva versato contributi all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS), verificate il diritto alla pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità o pensione indiretta) presentando domanda telematica all'INPS (o tramite un Patronato) [14].
    • Agenzia delle Entrate e Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato: Se la persona deceduta era residente in Italia o possedeva immobili o attivi in Italia, gli eredi devono presentare la dichiarazione di successione per via telematica all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data del decesso (salvo esonero per eredità devoluta a coniuge e parenti in linea retta di valore non superiore a 100.000 euro senza beni immobili) [15]. Per verificare l'esistenza di testamenti ricevuti o depositati in Italia o all'estero e curare la pubblicazione di eventuali testamenti olografi, potete rivolgervi a un notaio italiano e consultare le guide del Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (nonché il Registro Generale dei Testamenti presso il Ministero della Giustizia) [16].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Italy dies in France: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in France, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Italy and France.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with Italian nationality or habitual residence in Italy dies in France, the medical certification of death, initial civil registration, and prefectural authorization to transport the body out of the country are handled by the French authorities at the place of death, while transcription of the death record into the Italian civil status registers, reception of the coffin or urn in Italy, and survivor pension and succession formalities follow Italian and French rules.

Below are the five official steps to follow in chronological order:

steps.title: Medical certification of death and medical certificate in France (immediately)
steps.html:
Every death occurring in France must first be officially certified by a doctor (constatation médicale du décès), who issues the medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, either on the paper Cerfa form or electronically via the CertDc application), which is required to declare the death at the town hall (mairie) and initiate funeral operations [1]:

  • Death in a healthcare or medico-social facility (hospital, clinic, EHPAD nursing home): The ward physician certifies the death and issues the medical death certificate directly [1]. The facility keeps the body in its mortuary chamber (chambre mortuaire) and guides the family through the initial formalities.
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call the emergency medical service (SAMU on 15), the European emergency number (112), or an on-call doctor so that a practitioner can attend on site to certify the death and draw up the medical certificate [1]. If transport before coffining (transport avant mise en bière) to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) is desired, the funeral operator files the prior declaration with the town hall and the transfer must take place within 48 hours of death [3].
  • Forensic hold (obstacle médico-légal for sudden or suspicious death): When the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or suspicious, the doctor ticks the obstacle médico-légal box on the certificate. The police or gendarmerie and the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) take over: no coffining, cremation, burial, or repatriation to Italy may take place before judicial clearance is granted by the public prosecutor's office (parquet) [1].

steps.title: Checking insurance coverage, appointing funeral directors, and contacting the Italian consulate
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral contract, immediately check whether the deceased person held travel or repatriation insurance, assistance coverage linked to a bank card, or a pre-need funeral insurance policy (contrat de prévoyance obsèques) capable of organizing and funding the transfer [7]:

  • Coordination between a licensed funeral operator in France and a funeral provider in Italy: Funeral operations and international transport must be entrusted to a funeral operator licensed by the French prefecture (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture), which coordinates with an authorized funeral company in Italy (impresa funebre autorizzata) for receiving the coffin or urn and arranging burial in the Italian destination municipality [3][7][8].
  • Neutral professional federations: Clarvia provides these contact details for informational orientation only and does not recommend, endorse, or rank any commercial provider. In France, you can consult the official portal Service-Public.fr (phone 3939 from France or +33 1 73 60 39 39 from abroad) [1], or identify a licensed operator via the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. In Italy, you can locate an authorized funeral provider through the national federations FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, phone +39 051 6650285, email info@feniof.it) [8] and FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, phone +39 02 33403992, email info@federcofit.it) [9].
  • Consular assistance from Italy in France: Notify the Italian consular network competent for the place of death in France, operating under the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI, Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation), specifically the Consulat général d'Italie à Paris (Consulate General of Italy in Paris - civil status / death department: email statocivile.parigi@esteri.it) or the Italian Consulates General in Lyon, Marseille, Nice, and Metz [6][7].

steps.title: Registering the death at the French town hall (within 24 hours) and transcription for Italy
steps.html:
In accordance with French regulations detailed on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical certification (excluding weekends and public holidays) before the civil registrar (officier d'état civil) at the town hall (mairie) of the French municipality where the death occurred [1]:

  • Declarant and supporting documents in France: The declaration is made by a relative or, most often in practice, by the appointed funeral operator, upon presentation of the medical death certificate, the declarant's identity document, and the deceased person's documents (Italian identity card / carta d'identità or passport, birth or marriage certificate, family record book / livret de famille) [1].
  • Full death certificate (acte de décès intégral) and multilingual extract (Formule C): Request several full copies of the death certificate (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès) as well as several multilingual death certificate extracts on CIEC Form C (extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues sur Formule C, issued under the Vienna CIEC Convention of 8 September 1976) from the French town hall [1][6]. Because both France and Italy are parties to the 1976 Vienna Convention and apply Regulation (EU) 2016/1191, the multilingual Form C extract is directly recognized by Italian authorities without an apostille or sworn translation [6].
  • Transcription at the Italian Civil Registry (Ufficio di Stato Civile): Whereas a death occurring in Italy is declared within 24 hours to the Ufficio di Stato Civile of the Italian municipality (which issues the death certificate and burial permit), the death of an Italian citizen occurring in France must be transcribed into the civil status registers of the Italian municipality of residence or AIRE registration [6]. To do this, send by post to the Consulat général d'Italie à Paris (or the territorially competent Italian consulate) the original multilingual death certificate extract (Form C / Formule C) issued by the French town hall, accompanied by the transcription request form and a copy of an identity document of the deceased [6].

steps.title: Choosing between repatriation to Italy and local burial or cremation in France
steps.html:
The appointed funeral operator coordinates the administrative and sanitary permits according to the family's choice:

  • Option A - International repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to Italy:
    • Prefectural mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) and 1937 Berlin Agreement: Both France and Italy are parties to the International Berlin Agreement of 10 February 1937 on the Conveyance of Corpses (while France also applies the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement within the framework overseen by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs - Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie) [3][7]. To repatriate a body from France to Italy, the French funeral operator applies for a prefectural order for a mortuary transit permit (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) from the prefecture of the French department where the coffin is closed, upon presentation of the death certificate, the medical certificate of non-contagion, and the coffining report (procès-verbal de mise en bière) [3].
    • Hermetic coffin, embalming care, and reception by the Italian municipality: The body is placed in a regulation hermetic coffin (double coffin with a sealed zinc metal liner and embalming care / soins de conservation in accordance with applicable regulations) [3][7]. Under the rules set out by the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI), transport to Italy relies on the mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire / passaporto mortuario), the public-health certificate of non-contagion, and the reception and burial authorization issued by the Italian destination municipality (for example via the municipal funeral services such as the Comune di Milano or any other Italian municipality) [3][7][10].
    • Repatriation of a cinerary urn: If cremation takes place in France, international transport of the ashes requires a prefectural urn transport authorization issued upon presentation of the death certificate and the cremation certificate (certificat de crémation), coordinated with the authorization for entry into the Italian destination cemetery [3][7].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in France: If the funeral takes place in France, burial (inhumation) or cremation must take place at the earliest 24 hours after death and at the latest within 14 calendar days following the day after death (unless a prefectural waiver is granted), with authorization from the mayor of the municipality of death [2].

steps.title: Survivor pensions, health insurance, taxes, and succession in Italy and France
steps.html:
Using the multilingual death certificate extract (Form C), initiate the social security, tax, and estate settlement formalities in both countries:

  • Procedures in Italy:
    • Survivor pensions with INPS: If the deceased received an Italian pension or paid contributions to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, Italian National Social Security Institute), report the death and submit an online application (or apply free of charge through a Patronato assistance office) for the survivor pension (pensione ai superstiti) (pensione di reversibilità for a retiree or pensione indiretta for an active insured worker) [11].
    • Inheritance tax return in Italy (Agenzia delle Entrate) and Italian notaries: If the deceased resided in Italy or owned real estate or taxable assets there, the heirs must file the Italian inheritance tax return (dichiarazione di successione) electronically with the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months from the date of death (unless exempt where the estate passes to the spouse and direct-line relatives, has a value not exceeding EUR 100,000, and includes no real estate) [12]. To search for a will registered in Italy or abroad (Registro Generale dei Testamenti), publish a holographic will, or unblock Italian bank assets, consult an Italian notary through the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Italian Notaries) [13].
  • Procedures in France (if the deceased resided, worked, or held assets in France):
    • French health insurance and pension funds: Notify Assurance Maladie (CPAM / ameli.fr, phone 3646 from France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad) to close the insured person's file and claim a potential lump-sum death grant (capital décès) [14], as well as Assurance Retraite (CNAV, phone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and the supplementary pension scheme Agirc-Arrco for a survivor pension (pension de réversion) [15].
    • French notary and inheritance tax filing: If the deceased had their tax domicile in France or held real estate or bank accounts there, engage a notary via the Notaires de France network (phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) to draw up the proof of heirship (acte de notoriété), consult the Central Register of Last Wills (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), and file the inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) with the French tax administration within 6 months (for a death occurring in metropolitan France) [1][16].

closingQuestion: To allow us to guide you more precisely: in which French municipality did the death occur (and where was your family member's habitual residence), and are you considering repatriation to a specific Italian municipality or a local funeral in France?

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre France et Italie : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre France et Italie : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml:
Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne ayant la nationalité italienne ou sa résidence habituelle en Italie décède en France, la constatation médicale, l'enregistrement initial à l'état civil et l'autorisation préfectorale de départ du corps relèvent des autorités françaises du lieu du décès, tandis que la transcription de l'acte dans les registres italiens, l'accueil du cercueil ou de l'urne en Italie ainsi que les démarches de retraite et de succession suivent les règles italiennes et françaises.

Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles à suivre dans l'ordre chronologique :

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et certificat médical en France (immédiatement)
steps.html:
Tout décès survenu en France doit d'abord être constaté officiellement par un médecin, qui établit le certificat médical de décès (sur formulaire papier Cerfa ou par voie électronique via l'application CertDc), document indispensable pour déclarer le décès en mairie et engager les opérations funéraires [1] :

  • Décès en établissement de santé ou médico-social (hôpital, clinique, EHPAD) : Le médecin du service constate le décès et rédige directement le certificat médical de décès [1]. L'établissement assure le maintien du corps en chambre mortuaire et oriente la famille pour les premières formalités.
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU (15), le numéro d'urgence européen (112) ou un médecin de garde afin qu'un praticien se déplace pour constater le décès et établir le certificat médical [1]. Si un transfert avant mise en bière vers une chambre funéraire est souhaité, l'opérateur funéraire effectue la déclaration préalable auprès de la mairie et le transport doit intervenir dans les 48 heures suivant le décès [3].
  • Obstacle médico-légal (décès soudain ou suspect) : Lorsque la cause du décès est inconnue, soudaine ou suspecte, le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat. Les services de police ou de gendarmerie ainsi que le procureur de la République sont saisis : aucune mise en bière, crémation, inhumation ni aucun rapatriement vers l'Italie ne peut avoir lieu avant la délivrance de l'autorisation judiciaire du parquet [1].

steps.title: Vérification des assurances, choix des opérateurs funéraires et contact consulaire italien
steps.html:
Avant de signer un contrat funéraire à titre privé, vérifiez immédiatement si la personne décédée bénéficiait d'une assurance voyage ou rapatriement, d'une garantie d'assistance liée à une carte bancaire ou d'un contrat de prévoyance obsèques susceptible d'organiser et de financer le transfert [7] :

  • Coordination entre un opérateur funéraire en France et une entreprise en Italie : Les opérations funéraires et le transport international doivent être confiés à un opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture en France, qui se coordonne avec une entreprise de pompes funèbres autorisée en Italie (impresa funebre autorizzata) pour la réception du feretro ou de l'urne et la sépulture dans la commune italienne de destination [3][7][8].
  • Fédérations professionnelles neutres : Clarvia fournit ces coordonnées à titre d'orientation et ne recommande, ne cautionne ni ne classe aucun prestataire commercial. En France, vous pouvez consulter le portail officiel Service-Public.fr (téléphone 3939 depuis la France ou +33 1 73 60 39 39 depuis l'étranger) [1], ou identifier une entreprise habilitée via la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, téléphone +33 1 55 43 30 00, courriel contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] et la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, téléphone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. En Italie, vous pouvez trouver une entreprise autorisée via les fédérations nationales FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, téléphone +39 051 6650285, courriel info@feniof.it) [8] et FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, téléphone +39 02 33403992, courriel info@federcofit.it) [9].
  • Assistance consulaire d'Italie en France : Informez le réseau consulaire italien compétent pour le lieu du décès en France, placé sous l'autorité du Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI), notamment le Consulat général d'Italie à Paris (service de l'état civil / décès : courriel statocivile.parigi@esteri.it) ou les consulats généraux d'Italie à Lyon, Marseille, Nice et Metz [6][7].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès à la mairie en France (dans les 24 heures) et transcription pour l'Italie
steps.html:
Conformément à la réglementation française détaillée sur Service-Public.fr, le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures suivant sa constatation (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès de l'officier d'état civil de la mairie de la commune française où le décès s'est produit [1] :

  • Déclarant et pièces justificatives en France : La déclaration est effectuée par un proche ou, en pratique le plus souvent, par l'opérateur funéraire mandaté, sur présentation du certificat médical de décès, d'une pièce d'identité du déclarant et des documents de la personne décédée (carte d'identité italienne carta d'identità ou passeport, acte de naissance ou de mariage, livret de famille) [1].
  • Acte de décès intégral et extrait plurilingue (Formule C) : Demandez à la mairie française plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès ainsi que plusieurs extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues sur Formule C (établi selon la Convention CIEC de Vienne du 8 septembre 1976) [1][6]. La France et l'Italie étant toutes deux parties à la Convention de Vienne de 1976 et soumises au Règlement (UE) 2016/1191, l'extrait plurilingue Formule C est directement reconnu par les autorités italiennes sans apostille ni traduction assermentée [6].
  • Transcription à l'état civil italien (Ufficio di Stato Civile) : Alors qu'un décès survenu en Italie est déclaré dans les 24 heures à l'Ufficio di Stato Civile de la commune italienne (qui délivre l'acte de décès et le permis d'inhumer), le décès d'un citoyen italien survenu en France doit être transcrit dans les registres de l'état civil de la commune italienne de résidence ou d'inscription AIRE [6]. Pour cela, adressez par courrier au Consulat général d'Italie à Paris (ou au consulat italien territorialement compétent) l'original de l'extrait d'acte de décès sur formulaire plurilingue (Formule C) délivré par la mairie française, accompagné du formulaire de demande de transcription et de la copie d'une pièce d'identité de la personne décédée [6].

steps.title: Choix entre le rapatriement vers l'Italie et les obsèques locales en France
steps.html:
L'opérateur funéraire mandaté coordonne les autorisations administratives et sanitaires selon le choix de la famille :

  • Option A - Rapatriement international du corps ou des cendres vers l'Italie :
    • Laissez-passer mortuaire préfectoral et Convention de Berlin de 1937 : La France et l'Italie sont toutes deux parties à l'Arrangement international de Berlin du 10 février 1937 sur le transport des corps (tandis que la France applique également l'Accord de Strasbourg de 1973 dans le cadre suivi par le Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie) [3][7]. Pour rapatrier un corps de France vers l'Italie, l'opérateur funéraire français sollicite un arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire auprès de la préfecture du département français où a lieu la fermeture du cercueil, sur présentation de l'acte de décès, du certificat médical de non-contagion et du procès-verbal de mise en bière [3].
    • Cercueil hermétique, soins de conservation et accueil par la commune italienne : Le corps est placé dans un cercueil hermétique réglementaire (double cercueil avec enveloppe métallique en zinc scellée et soins de conservation selon la réglementation applicable) [3][7]. Conformément aux règles rappelées par le Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI), le transport vers l'Italie s'appuie sur le laissez-passer mortuaire (passaporto mortuario), le certificat sanitaire de non-contagion et l'autorisation d'accueil et de sépulture délivrée par la commune italienne de destination (par exemple via les services funéraires de la commune comme le Comune di Milano ou de toute autre municipalité italienne) [3][7][10].
    • Rapatriement d'une urne cinéraire : Si la crémation a lieu en France, le transport international des cendres est soumis à une autorisation préfectorale de transport d'urne délivrée sur présentation de l'acte de décès et du certificat de crémation, coordonnée avec l'autorisation d'introduction dans le cimetière italien de destination [3][7].
  • Option B - Inhumation ou crémation en France : Si les obsèques se déroulent en France, l'inhumation ou la crémation doit intervenir au plus tôt 24 heures après le décès et au plus tard dans un délai de 14 jours calendaires suivant le lendemain du décès (sauf dérogation préfectorale), sur autorisation du maire de la commune du décès [2].

steps.title: Retraites, assurance maladie, fiscalité et règlement de la succession en Italie et en France
steps.html:
Muni de l'extrait plurilingue de l'acte de décès (Formule C), engagez les démarches sociales, fiscales et successorales dans les deux pays :

  • Démarches en Italie :
    • Pensions de survivants auprès de l'INPS : Si la personne décédée percevait une pension italienne ou avait cotisé auprès de l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS), déclarez le décès et déposez une demande en ligne (ou via un Patronato gratuit) pour la pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità pour un retraité ou pensione indiretta pour un assuré actif) [11].
    • Déclaration de succession en Italie (Agenzia delle Entrate) et notariat italien : Si la personne décédée résidait en Italie ou y possédait des biens immobiliers ou des actifs imposables, les héritiers doivent déposer la déclaration de succession (dichiarazione di successione) par voie télématique auprès de l'Agenzia delle Entrate dans un délai de 12 mois à compter de la date du décès (sauf exonération lorsque l'héritage est dévolu au conjoint et aux parents en ligne directe pour une valeur inférieure ou égale à 100 000 euros sans bien immobilier) [12]. Pour rechercher un testament enregistré en Italie ou à l'étranger (Registro Generale dei Testamenti), faire publier un testament olographe ou débloquer des avoirs bancaires italiens, consultez un notaire italien via le Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [13].
  • Démarches en France (si la personne résidait, travaillait ou possédait des biens en France) :
    • Protection sociale et retraites françaises : Informez l'Assurance Maladie (CPAM / ameli.fr, téléphone 3646 depuis la France ou +33 1 84 90 36 46 depuis l'étranger) pour clôturer le dossier d'assuré et demander un éventuel capital décès [14], ainsi que l'Assurance Retraite (CNAV, téléphone 3960 ou +33 9 71 10 39 60 depuis l'étranger) et le régime complémentaire Agirc-Arrco pour la pension de réversion [15].
    • Notaire et fiscalité française : Si la personne décédée avait son domicile fiscal en France ou y détenait des biens immobiliers ou des comptes bancaires, sollicitez un notaire via le réseau des Notaires de France (téléphone +33 1 44 90 30 00) pour établir l'acte de notoriété, consulter le Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés (FCDDV) et déposer la déclaration de succession auprès de l'administration fiscale française dans un délai de 6 mois (pour un décès survenu en France métropolitaine) [1][16].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Switzerland: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Switzerland: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in Switzerland: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Switzerland, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and Switzerland.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with French nationality or residence ties to France dies in Switzerland, the medical certification of death, registration at the civil registry office of the place of death, and issuance of the mortuary passport (Leichenpass) are governed by Swiss federal and cantonal law, whereas transcription into the French civil status register, repatriation to France, and survivor pension and estate procedures involve the French and Swiss authorities.

Below are the five official steps to follow in chronological order:

steps.title: Medical certification of death and medical death certificate in Switzerland (immediately)
steps.html:
Every death in Switzerland must first be certified by a physician so that the medical death certificate (Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung) can be issued for the subsequent civil registry notification [1]:

  • Death in a hospital, nursing home, or hospice: The facility's medical staff performs the medical verification of death, issues the Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, and frequently forwards the death notification directly to the competent civil registry office (Zivilstandsamt) [1].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: In the event of a natural death at home, contact the family doctor (Hausarzt) or the on-call medical service or emergency medical dispatch (Sanität 144) to issue the Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung [1]. If the death occurs in a public place or without a clear medical history, immediately call the Police (117) as well as Emergency Medical Services / Sanität (144) [1].
  • Extraordinary death (aussergewöhnlicher Todesfall - official medical examiner and public prosecutor): In the case of a sudden, unexplained, violent, or accident-related death, it is classified as an aussergewöhnlicher Todesfall. Emergency responders call in the police, the official medical officer (Amtsarzt / forensic medicine), and the cantonal Public Prosecutor's Office (Staatsanwaltschaft); coffining, cremation, burial, or international repatriation to France may only proceed after written clearance from the public prosecutor [1].

steps.title: Checking insurance coverage, appointing funeral directors, and contacting the French consulate
steps.html:
Before placing individual private orders, immediately check whether the deceased person had travel or repatriation insurance, assistance coverage through a French supplementary health insurer (mutuelle) or bank card, or a funeral pre-need insurance policy (contrat d'assurance obsèques) that covers the organization and cost of repatriation:

  • Coordination between a funeral service in Switzerland and a funeral operator in France: For collection, coffining, and administrative formalities in Switzerland, contact the municipal funeral office (Bestattungsamt) of the Swiss municipality or appoint a licensed funeral director in Switzerland, which coordinates any repatriation with a funeral operator licensed by the prefecture in France (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) [1][3][7].
  • Neutral professional associations for orientation: Clarvia provides these directories strictly for neutral orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank commercial providers. In Switzerland, you can find certified funeral directors through the Swiss professional association Schweizerischer Verband der Bestattungsdienste (SVB, Swiss Association of Funeral Services) [3]. In France, you can consult official guidance via the administrative portal Service-Public.fr (phone 3939 from France or +33 1 73 60 39 39 from abroad) [6] or locate a licensed funeral operator through the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [8] and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [9].
  • Consular assistance from France in Switzerland: Notify the competent French consular representation in Switzerland: the French Consulate General in Geneva (Consulat général de France à Genève, covering Western Switzerland, Service France Consulaire at phone +41 22 567 95 59, email ecrire.geneve-cslt@diplomatie.gouv.fr) or the French Consulate General in Zurich (Consulat général de France à Zurich, covering German-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, phone +41 43 547 80 41, email contact.zurich-cslt@diplomatie.gouv.fr) [4][5]. The Consulates General advise relatives on repatriation and, in particular, issue the consular authorization required for transporting a cinerary urn to France [4][5].

steps.title: Registering the death with the Swiss civil registry (within 2 days) and transcription for France
steps.html:
According to the official Swiss authorities portal ch.ch, a death in Switzerland must be reported within 2 days to the civil registry office of the place of death (Zivilstandsamt) (or, depending on the municipality, to the municipal funeral office / Bestattungsamt) [1]:

  • Registration and certificates in Switzerland: Reporting the death - whether by next of kin, the hospital, or the appointed funeral director - requires the medical death certificate (Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung), the deceased person's French passport or national identity card (carte nationale d'identité), any Swiss residence permit, and civil status documents [1]. The Swiss civil registry office records the death in the Swiss civil status register (Infostar) and issues the domestic Swiss death certificate (Todesschein) as well as the multilingual international CIEC extract from the death register on Form C (Formular C) under the 1976 Vienna Convention [1][4].
  • Recognition without an Apostille in France: Because both Switzerland and France are contracting states to the Vienna CIEC Convention of 8 September 1976, the Swiss extract on Form C (Formular C) is recognized directly in France by town halls (mairies), banks, notaries, and social security bodies without an Apostille or certified translation [4][6].
  • Transcription in the French civil status register (Nantes): Whereas a death occurring inside France is declared within 24 hours (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the mairie of the place of death [6], the post-registration (transcription de l'acte de décès) of a French national who died in Switzerland is handled centrally by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs in Nantes: Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - Service central d'état civil (SCEC), Département Transcription - Secteur Europe, 11, rue de la Maison Blanche, 44941 Nantes CEDEX 9, France [4]. The application is sent by post to Nantes together with the original Swiss death certificate (acte de décès / Todesschein), proof of French nationality, the birth certificate, and the livret de famille [4].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation to France and local burial or cremation in Switzerland
steps.html:
The appointed funeral director coordinates the required transport and burial permits depending on the family's decision:

  • Option A - International repatriation of the body or urn from Switzerland to France:
    • Mortuary passport (Leichenpass) for coffin repatriation (Strasbourg and Berlin Agreements): Both Switzerland and France apply the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses as well as the 1937 International Berlin Agreement (under which departures from France use a prefectural arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire and departures from Switzerland use the cantonal mortuary passport (Leichenpass) within the framework overseen by the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs - Eidgenössisches Departement für auswärtige Angelegenheiten - EDA) [4][7]. To transport a body from Switzerland to France, the Swiss funeral director applies to the competent cantonal authority at the place of death for the international Leichenpass [4]. The body is transported in a regulation hermetically sealed coffin (cercueil hermétique with a metal liner and, where required by the mode of transport, embalming care / soins de conservation); under the Strasbourg Agreement, the Swiss Leichenpass suffices to cross the border into France without a separate French consular transit permit, while the receiving French funeral operator obtains the burial or cremation authorization from the French destination municipality [4][7].
    • Repatriation of a cinerary urn (cremated ashes) to France: If cremation takes place in Switzerland, importing the sealed urn into France requires a consular transport authorization issued by the French Consulate General (Consulat général de France à Genève or Consulat général de France à Zurich) upon presentation of the Swiss death certificate, the cremation certificate (certificat d'incinération), and confirmation of the place of interment in France [4][7].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in Switzerland: If the funeral takes place in Switzerland, the family arranges earth burial or cremation through the funeral office (Bestattungsamt) of the Swiss municipality of residence or place of death in accordance with cantonal and municipal cemetery regulations (normally after the cantonal waiting period of typically 48 hours) [1][3].

steps.title: Survivor pensions, health insurance, taxes, and succession in France and Switzerland
steps.html:
With the multilingual CIEC death extract (Form C), initiate the social security, tax, and inheritance procedures in both countries:

  • Procedures in France:
    • Health insurance (CPAM) and French pension funds: Report the death to the French health insurance fund (Assurance Maladie / CPAM, accessible via ameli.fr or by phone at 3646 from France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad) to close the insured person's account and, if eligibility conditions are met, claim the lump-sum death grant (capital décès) [10]. Also notify the statutory French pension insurance scheme (Assurance Retraite / CNAV, phone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and the supplementary pension fund Agirc-Arrco to apply for a survivor pension (pension de réversion) [11].
    • French notary and inheritance tax return: If the deceased had their tax domicile in France or owned real estate or bank accounts there, engage a notary through the official French Chamber of Notaries (Notaires de France, phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) to draw up the proof of heirship (acte de notoriété), query the French Central Register of Last Wills (FCDDV), and file the inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) [12][13]. While the filing deadline is 6 months for a death occurring in France, a statutory filing period of 12 months from the date of death applies when the death occurred outside France - including in Switzerland [12][13].
  • Procedures in Switzerland (if the deceased resided, worked as a resident or cross-border commuter, or held assets in Switzerland):
    • AHV/AVS survivor pensions and occupational pension (2. Säule / 2nd pillar): If the deceased paid contributions to the Swiss Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung - AHV / AVS, for example as a Swiss resident or a French cross-border commuter / frontalier), claims for widow's, widower's, or orphan's pensions under Information Sheet 3.03 must be submitted using official form 318.371 to the competent AHV compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) or, for beneficiaries residing abroad, to the federal compensation authority Zentrale Ausgleichsstelle (Central Compensation Office / Swiss Compensation Office SAK / CSC in Geneva) [14][15]. Also report the death to any Swiss occupational pension fund (Pensionskasse / 2nd pillar), accident insurer (UVG / LAA), and Swiss health insurer [1][14].
    • Cantonal probate authority, certificate of inheritance (Erbenbescheinigung), and 3-month disclaimer deadline: If the deceased had their last domicile or estate assets in Switzerland, any wills must be submitted without delay to the competent cantonal court, notary, or probate office (Erbschaftsamt, e.g., the District Court / Bezirksgericht in the Canton of Zurich or the Justice de paix in Western Switzerland), where heirs also apply for the certificate of inheritance (Erbenbescheinigung / Erbschein) [1][2]. Where the Swiss Civil Code (Zivilgesetzbuch - ZGB) applies, pay strict attention to the statutory 3-month disclaimer deadline (Ausschlagungsfrist) from awareness of the death if the estate may be over-indebted [1][2].

de.title: Todesfall in Schweiz (Frankreich): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Schweiz und Frankreich: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml:
Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit französischer Staatsangehörigkeit oder Wohnsitzbindung an Frankreich in der Schweiz verstirbt, richten sich die ärztliche Todesfeststellung, die Meldung beim Zivilstandsamt des Sterbeortes und die Ausstellung des Leichenpasses nach schweizerischem und kantonalem Recht, während die Nachbeurkundung für das französische Personenstandsregister, die Überführung nach Frankreich sowie die Hinterbliebenen- und Nachlassverfahren die französischen und schweizerischen Behörden betreffen.

Nachfolgend finden Sie die fünf offiziellen Schritte in chronologischer Reihenfolge:

steps.title: Ärztliche Todesfeststellung und Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung in der Schweiz (unmittelbar)
steps.html:
Jeder Todesfall in der Schweiz muss zunächst durch eine Ärztin oder einen Arzt festgestellt werden, damit die Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung für die anschließende zivilstandsamtliche Meldung ausgestellt wird [1]:

  • Todesfall im Spital, Pflegeheim oder Hospiz: Das medizinische Personal der Einrichtung nimmt die ärztliche Todesfeststellung vor, stellt die Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung aus und leitet die Todesmeldung häufig direkt an das zuständige Zivilstandsamt weiter [1].
  • Todesfall zu Hause, im Hotel oder im öffentlichen Raum: Verständigen Sie bei einem natürlichen Todesfall zu Hause die Hausärztin, den Hausarzt oder den ärztlichen Notfalldienst bzw. den medizinischen Notruf (Sanität 144) zur Ausstellung der Ärztlichen Todesbescheinigung [1]. Ereignet sich der Todesfall im öffentlichen Raum oder ohne klare medizinische Vorgeschichte, rufen Sie umgehend die Polizei (117) sowie die Sanität (144) [1].
  • Aussergewöhnlicher Todesfall (Amtsarzt und Staatsanwaltschaft): Bei einem plötzlichen, unklaren, gewaltsamen oder durch einen Unfall verursachten Tod liegt ein sogenannter aussergewöhnlicher Todesfall vor. In diesem Fall ziehen die Einsatzkräfte die Polizei, die Amtsärztin oder den Amtsarzt (bzw. die Rechtsmedizin) sowie die kantonale Staatsanwaltschaft bei; eine Einsargung, Kremation, Erdbestattung oder Auslandsüberführung nach Frankreich darf erst nach der schriftlichen Freigabe der Staatsanwaltschaft erfolgen [1].

steps.title: Versicherungen prüfen, Bestattungsunternehmen beauftragen und französische Vertretung kontaktieren
steps.html:
Prüfen Sie vor der Erteilung privater Einzelaufträge umgehend, ob für die verstorbene Person eine Reise- oder Rückführungsversicherung, eine Beistandsleistung über eine französische Zusatzkrankenversicherung (mutuelle) oder Bankkarte bzw. eine Vorsorgeversicherung (contrat d'assurance obsèques) bestand, welche die Organisation und Kosten der Überführung übernimmt:

  • Koordination zwischen Bestattungsdienst in der Schweiz und Bestattungsunternehmen in Frankreich: Für die Abholung, Einsargung und die behördlichen Schritte in der Schweiz wenden Sie sich an das Bestattungsamt der Schweizer Gemeinde oder beauftragen ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen in der Schweiz, das sich für eine Rückführung mit einem in Frankreich von der Präfektur zugelassenen Bestattungsunternehmen (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) abstimmt [1][3][7].
  • Neutrale Berufsverbände zur Orientierung: Clarvia gibt diese Verzeichnisse ausschließlich zur neutralen Orientierung an und spricht keine Empfehlungen, Bewertungen oder Rankings für kommerzielle Anbieter aus. In der Schweiz finden Sie zertifizierte Bestattungsunternehmen über den schweizerischen Branchenverband (Schweizerischer Verband der Bestattungsdienste) [3]. In Frankreich können Sie die amtlichen Informationen über das offizielle Verwaltungsportal (Service-Public.fr, Telefon 3939 aus Frankreich oder +33 1 73 60 39 39 aus dem Ausland) [6] abrufen oder einen zugelassenen Bestatter über den Fachverband Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, Telefon +33 1 55 43 30 00, E-Mail contact@federation-fnf.fr) [8] sowie den Verband Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, Telefon +33 1 46 60 24 24) [9] suchen.
  • Konsularische Unterstützung Frankreichs in der Schweiz: Informieren Sie die zuständige französische konsularische Vertretung in der Schweiz: das französische Generalkonsulat in Genf (Consulat général de France à Genève, für die Westschweiz, Service France Consulaire unter Telefon +41 22 567 95 59, E-Mail ecrire.geneve-cslt@diplomatie.gouv.fr) oder das französische Generalkonsulat in Zürich (Consulat général de France à Zurich, für die Deutschschweiz und das Tessin, Telefon +41 43 547 80 41, E-Mail contact.zurich-cslt@diplomatie.gouv.fr) [4][5]. Die Generalkonsulate beraten Angehörige bei Rückführungen und stellen insbesondere die konsularische Genehmigung für den Urnentransport nach Frankreich aus [4][5].

steps.title: Meldung beim Zivilstandsamt in der Schweiz (innert 2 Tagen) und Nachbeurkundung für Frankreich
steps.html:
Gemäß den Vorgaben auf dem offiziellen Schweizer Behördenportal (ch.ch) muss ein Todesfall in der Schweiz innert 2 Tagen beim Zivilstandsamt des Sterbeortes (bzw. je nach Gemeinde beim Bestattungsamt) gemeldet werden [1]:

  • Meldung und Urkunden in der Schweiz: Zur Meldung durch die Angehörigen, das Spital oder das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen werden die Ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, der französische Reisepass oder Personalausweis (carte nationale d'identité), eine allfällige Schweizer Aufenthaltsbewilligung sowie Zivilstandsdokumente der verstorbenen Person benötigt [1]. Das Schweizer Zivilstandsamt beurkundet den Tod im Schweizer Personenstandsregister (Infostar) und stellt den schweizerischen Todesschein sowie den mehrsprachigen internationalen CIEC-Auszug aus dem Todesregister auf Formular C (Wiener Übereinkommen von 1976) aus [1][4].
  • Anerkennung ohne Apostille in Frankreich: Da sowohl die Schweiz als auch Frankreich Vertragsstaaten des Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommens vom 8. September 1976 sind, wird der Schweizer Auszug auf Formular C in Frankreich von Gemeinden (mairies), Banken, Notaren und Sozialversicherungsträgern direkt ohne Apostille und ohne beglaubigte Übersetzung anerkannt [4][6].
  • Transkription im französischen Personenstandsregister (Nantes): Während ein Todesfall innerhalb Frankreichs innerhalb von 24 Stunden (ohne Wochenenden und Feiertage) bei der mairie des Sterbeortes gemeldet wird [6], ist für die Nachbeurkundung (transcription de l'acte de décès) eines in der Schweiz verstorbenen französischen Staatsangehörigen zentral das Außenministerium in Nantes zuständig: Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - Service central d'état civil (SCEC), Département Transcription - Secteur Europe, 11, rue de la Maison Blanche, 44941 Nantes CEDEX 9, Frankreich [4]. Der Antrag wird per Post zusammen mit dem Schweizer Original-Todesschein (acte de décès bzw. Todesschein), dem Nachweis der französischen Staatsangehörigkeit, der Geburtsurkunde und dem livret de famille nach Nantes gesandt [4].

steps.title: Wahl zwischen internationaler Überführung nach Frankreich und Bestattung in der Schweiz
steps.html:
Das beauftragte Bestattungsunternehmen koordiniert die erforderlichen Transport- und Bestattungsgenehmigungen je nach Entscheidung der Familie:

  • Option A - Internationale Überführung des Leichnams oder der Urne aus der Schweiz nach Frankreich:
    • Leichenpass für die Überführung eines Sarges (Straßburger und Berliner Abkommen): Sowohl die Schweiz als auch Frankreich wenden das Straßburger Übereinkommen von 1973 über die Leichenbeförderung sowie das Internationale Berliner Abkommen von 1937 an (wobei bei Überführungen aus Frankreich ein arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire der französischen Präfektur und in der Schweiz der kantonale Leichenpass im Rahmen der Vorgaben des Eidgenössischen Departements für auswärtige Angelegenheiten - EDA zum Einsatz kommt) [4][7]. Für den Transport eines Leichnams aus der Schweiz nach Frankreich beantragt das Schweizer Bestattungsunternehmen bei der zuständigen kantonalen Behörde des Sterbeortes den internationalen Leichenpass [4]. Der Leichnam wird in einem vorschriftsgemäßen luftdicht verschlossenen Sarg (cercueil hermétique mit Metalleinsatz und gegebenenfalls Konservierungsbehandlung soins de conservation je nach Transportweg) überführt; dank des Straßburger Abkommens genügt der Schweizer Leichenpass für den Grenzübertritt nach Frankreich ohne separates französisches Konsulardokument, während das empfangende französische Bestattungsunternehmen die Beisetzungs- oder Kremationsgenehmigung der französischen Zielgemeinde einholt [4][7].
    • Überführung einer Urne (Kremationsasche) nach Frankreich: Erfolgt die Kremation in der Schweiz, wird für die Einfuhr der versiegelten Urne nach Frankreich eine konsularische Transportgenehmigung durch das französische Generalkonsulat (Consulat général de France à Genève oder Consulat général de France à Zurich) auf Vorlage des Schweizer Todesscheins, der Kremationsbescheinigung (certificat d'incinération) und der Bestätigung des Bestattungsortes in Frankreich ausgestellt [4][7].
  • Option B - Lokale Erdbestattung oder Kremation in der Schweiz: Findet die Beisetzung in der Schweiz statt, organisiert die Familie diese über das Bestattungsamt der Schweizer Wohngemeinde bzw. des Sterbeortes gemäß den kantonalen und kommunalen Friedhofsreglementen (in der Regel nach Ablauf der kantonalen Wartefrist von meist 48 Stunden) [1][3].

steps.title: Hinterbliebenenrenten, Krankenversicherung, Steuern und Nachlass in Frankreich und in der Schweiz
steps.html:
Mit dem mehrsprachigen CIEC-Todesauszug (Formular C) leiten Sie die sozialversicherungs-, steuer- und erbrechtlichen Schritte in beiden Ländern ein:

  • Verfahren in Frankreich:
    • Krankenversicherung (CPAM) und französische Rentenkassen: Melden Sie den Todesfall an die französische Krankenversicherung (Assurance Maladie / CPAM, erreichbar über ameli.fr oder Telefon 3646 aus Frankreich bzw. +33 1 84 90 36 46 aus dem Ausland), um das Versichertenkonto zu schließen und bei Erfüllung der Voraussetzungen das Sterbegeld (capital décès) zu beantragen [10]. Informieren Sie zudem die gesetzliche französische Rentenversicherung (Assurance Retraite / CNAV, Telefon 3960 oder +33 9 71 10 39 60 aus dem Ausland) sowie die Zusatzrentenkasse Agirc-Arrco zur Beantragung einer Hinterbliebenenrente (pension de réversion) [11].
    • Französisches Notariat und Erbschaftsteuererklärung: Hatte die verstorbene Person ihren steuerlichen Wohnsitz in Frankreich oder besaß sie dort Immobilien oder Bankkonten, ziehen Sie über die offizielle französische Notariatskammer (Notaires de France, Telefon +33 1 44 90 30 00) ein Notariat bei, um den Erbnachweis (acte de notoriété) zu errichten, das zentrale französische Testamentsregister (FCDDV) abzufragen und die Erbschaftsteuererklärung (déclaration de succession) einzureichen [12][13]. Während die Frist bei einem Todesfall in Frankreich 6 Monate beträgt, gilt bei einem Todesfall außerhalb Frankreichs - also auch bei einem Sterbefall in der Schweiz - eine gesetzliche Einreichungsfrist von 12 Monaten ab dem Todestag [12][13].
  • Verfahren in der Schweiz (bei Wohnsitz, Erwerbstätigkeit/Grenzgängerstatus oder Vermögen in der Schweiz):
    • AHV-Hinterlassenenrenten und berufliche Vorsorge (2. Säule): Hat die verstorbene Person Beiträge an die schweizerische Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung (AHV) geleistet (etwa als Einwohner oder französischer Grenzgänger frontalier), sind Ansprüche auf Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenrenten gemäß Merkblatt 3.03 mit dem amtlichen Formular 318.371 bei der zuständigen AHV-Ausgleichskasse bzw. für im Ausland wohnhafte Berechtigte bei der zuständigen Bundesstelle (Zentrale Ausgleichsstelle / Schweizerische Ausgleichskasse SAK in Genf) anzumelden [14][15]. Melden Sie den Tod ebenso einer allfälligen Schweizer Pensionskasse (berufliche Vorsorge / 2. Säule), der Unfallversicherung (UVG) und der Schweizer Krankenkasse [1][14].
    • Kantonales Erbschaftsamt, Erbenbescheinigung und 3-monatige Ausschlagungsfrist: Hatte die verstorbene Person ihren letzten Wohnsitz oder Nachlasswerte in der Schweiz, müssen vorhandene Testamente unverzüglich beim zuständigen kantonalen Gericht, Notariat oder Erbschaftsamt (z. B. beim Bezirksgericht im Kanton Zürich oder der Justice de paix in der Westschweiz) eingereicht werden, wo auch die Erbenbescheinigung (Erbschein) beantragt wird [1][2]. Beachten Sie bei Anwendung des schweizerischen Zivilgesetzbuches (ZGB) zwingend die gesetzliche Ausschlagungsfrist von 3 Monaten ab Kenntnis des Todesfalls, falls der Nachlass überschuldet sein könnte [1][2].

de.closingQuestion: Damit wir Sie noch gezielter unterstützen können: In welchem Schweizer Kanton bzw. welcher Gemeinde ist der Todesfall eingetreten (und wo hatte die verstorbene Person ihren Hauptwohnsitz), und planen Sie eine Überführung nach Frankreich oder eine Bestattung in der Schweiz?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Switzerland Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Switzerland Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Switzerland dies in France: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in France, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Switzerland and France.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with Swiss nationality or habitual residence in Switzerland dies in France, the medical certification of death, initial civil status registration, and prefectural authorization to transport the body out of the country are handled by the French authorities at the place of death, whereas the consular notification for transcription into the Swiss civil status register (Infostar), reception of the coffin or urn in Switzerland, and AVS/AHV, 2nd-pillar, and estate procedures follow Swiss and French rules.

Below are the five official steps to follow in chronological order:

steps.title: Medical certification of death and medical certificate in France (immediately)
steps.html:
Every death occurring in France must first be officially certified by a doctor (constatation médicale du décès), who draws up the medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, either on the paper Cerfa form or electronically via the CertDc application), which is required to declare the death at the town hall (mairie) and initiate funeral arrangements [1]:

  • Death in a healthcare or medico-social facility (hospital, clinic, EHPAD nursing home): The ward physician certifies the death and completes the medical death certificate directly [1]. The facility keeps the body in its mortuary chamber (chambre mortuaire) and guides the family through the initial formalities.
  • Death at home, at temporary accommodation, or in a public place: Immediately call the emergency medical service (SAMU on 15), the European emergency number (112), or an on-call doctor so that a practitioner can attend on site to certify the death and issue the medical certificate [1]. If transport before coffining (transport avant mise en bière) to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) is desired, the funeral operator files the prior declaration with the town hall and the transfer must occur within 48 hours of death [3].
  • Forensic hold (obstacle médico-légal for sudden or suspicious death): When the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or suspicious, the doctor ticks the obstacle médico-légal box on the certificate. The police or gendarmerie and the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) take over: no coffining, cremation, burial, or repatriation to Switzerland may take place until judicial authorization is issued by the public prosecutor's office (parquet) [1].

steps.title: Checking insurance coverage, appointing funeral directors, and contacting the Swiss consulate
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral quote, immediately check whether the deceased person held travel or repatriation insurance (for example via supplementary Swiss health insurance coverage, a rescue membership pass, or a bank card) or a pre-need funeral contract (contrat de prévoyance obsèques) capable of organizing and funding the transfer:

  • Coordination between a licensed funeral operator in France and a funeral service in Switzerland: Funeral operations and cross-border transport must be entrusted to a funeral operator licensed by the French prefecture (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture), which coordinates with the municipal funeral office (Bestattungsamt) of the Swiss destination municipality or a licensed funeral provider in Switzerland [3][7][8].
  • Neutral professional federations: Clarvia provides these contact details for informational orientation only and does not recommend, endorse, or rank any commercial provider. In France, you can consult official guidance via Service-Public.fr (phone 3939 from France or +33 1 73 60 39 39 from abroad) [1], or locate a licensed operator through the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. In Switzerland, you can find a certified funeral company through the directory of the professional association Schweizerischer Verband der Bestattungsdienste (SVB / Swiss Association of Funeral Services) [7].
  • Consular assistance from Switzerland in France: Because French authorities do not automatically forward death certificates to Switzerland, the death must be reported to the competent Swiss representation under the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (Département fédéral des affaires étrangères - DFAE / EDA), specifically the Ambassade de Suisse en France (Embassy of Switzerland in France, in Paris, phone +33 1 49 55 67 00, email paris.chancellerie@eda.admin.ch) or the Consulates General of Switzerland in Lyon (phone +33 4 72 75 79 10, email lyon@eda.admin.ch), Marseille, and Strasbourg depending on the consular district of the place of death [6].

steps.title: Registering the death at the French town hall (within 24 hours) and recording it for Switzerland
steps.html:
Under French regulations detailed on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical certification (excluding weekends and public holidays) before the civil registrar (officier d'état civil) at the town hall (mairie) of the French municipality where the death occurred [1]:

  • Declarant and supporting documents in France: The declaration is made by a relative or, most commonly in practice, by the appointed funeral operator, upon presentation of the medical death certificate, the declarant's identity document, and the deceased person's documents (Swiss passport or identity card, birth or marriage certificate, Swiss family certificate / certificat de famille) [1].
  • Full death certificate (acte de décès intégral) and multilingual extract (Formule C): Request from the French town hall several full copies of the death certificate (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès, bearing the original town hall seal) as well as several multilingual death certificate extracts on CIEC Form C (extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues sur Formule C, issued under the Vienna CIEC Convention of 8 September 1976) [1][6]. Because both France and Switzerland are parties to the 1976 Vienna Convention, the multilingual Form C extract and the French death certificate are directly recognized in Switzerland without an apostille or legalization [6].
  • Transcription in the Swiss civil status register (Infostar): Whereas a death occurring in Switzerland must be reported within 2 days to the civil registry office of the place of death (Zivilstandsamt) according to the official portal ch.ch [8], the death of a Swiss national in France is transcribed free of charge through the Ambassade de Suisse en France or the competent Swiss Consulate General [6]. For this formality, submit to the Swiss representation: 1) the original of a full copy of the French death certificate (copie intégrale de l'acte de décès) (bearing the original seal of the mairie and issued within the last 6 months, which will not be returned), 2) the deceased person's Swiss identity documents (passport and identity card) for cancellation (which can be returned as a keepsake upon prior request), and 3) the contact details of a surviving relative [6].

steps.title: Choosing between repatriation to Switzerland and local burial or cremation in France
steps.html:
The appointed funeral operator coordinates the administrative and public-health authorizations according to the option chosen by the family:

  • Option A - International repatriation of the body or cremated ashes to Switzerland:
    • Prefectural mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire / Leichenpass): Both France and Switzerland apply the Strasbourg Agreement of 26 October 1973 on the Transfer of Corpses as well as the 1937 International Berlin Arrangement (overseen in France by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs - Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie and in Switzerland by the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs - DFAE / EDA and the cantonal authorities) [3]. To repatriate a body from France to Switzerland, the French funeral operator obtains a prefectural order for a mortuary transit permit (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) from the prefecture of the French department where the coffin is closed [3].
    • Hermetic coffin, embalming care, and entry into Switzerland: The body must be placed in a regulation hermetic coffin (cercueil hermétique fitted with a sealed metal liner and, depending on the mode of transport and applicable regulations, after embalming care / soins de conservation) [3]. Under the Strasbourg Agreement and the Berlin Arrangement, the French prefectural mortuary transit permit generally suffices to cross the border and transport the coffin to the cemetery or crematorium of the Swiss destination municipality without requiring an additional Swiss consular mortuary pass (Leichenpass) [3][8].
    • Repatriation of a cinerary urn: If cremation takes place in France, international transport of the ashes is covered by a prefectural authorization issued upon presentation of the death certificate and the cremation certificate (certificat de crémation) [3].
  • Option B - Local burial or cremation in France: If the funeral takes place in France, burial (inhumation) or cremation must take place at the earliest 24 hours after death and at the latest within 14 calendar days following the day after death (unless a prefectural waiver is granted), with authorization from the mayor of the municipality of death [2].

steps.title: Survivor pensions (AVS/AHV and 2nd pillar), taxes, and estate settlement in Switzerland and France
steps.html:
Once the death certificate has been obtained, initiate the social security, banking, and succession procedures in both states:

  • Procedures in Switzerland:
    • AVS/AHV survivor pensions and occupational pension (2nd pillar): Claims for AVS/AHV survivor pensions (widow's, widower's, or orphan's pensions under AVS Information Sheet 3.03, Ausgleichskasse der AHV) must be submitted using official form 318.371 to the compensation fund where the deceased last paid contributions - or, for insured persons residing abroad, to the Central Compensation Office (Zentrale Ausgleichsstelle / Swiss Compensation Office CSC / SAK in Geneva) [10][11]. Also report the death to the Swiss occupational pension institution (pension fund / 2nd pillar), accident insurer (LAA / UVG), and Swiss health insurance fund (caisse-maladie) [8][10].
    • Certificate of inheritance (certificat d'héritier / Erbenbescheinigung) and 3-month disclaimer deadline (ZGB / CC): Any will or inheritance contract must be delivered without delay to the competent cantonal authority of the last Swiss domicile (justice of the peace / justice de paix, district court / Bezirksgericht, probate office / Erbschaftsamt, or notary depending on the canton), where the heirs also apply for the certificate of inheritance (certificat d'héritier / Erbenbescheinigung / Erbschein) required to access bank accounts and real estate in Switzerland [8][9]. If the estate is governed by the Swiss Civil Code (CC / ZGB) and carries a risk of over-indebtedness, pay strict attention to the statutory 3-month deadline from awareness of the death to declare any renunciation / disclaimer of the inheritance (répudiation / Ausschlagung) [8][9].
  • Procedures in France (if the deceased resided, worked, or held assets in France):
    • French health insurance and pension funds: If your family member was insured in France, notify Assurance Maladie (CPAM / ameli.fr, phone 3646 from France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad) to close the file and claim a potential lump-sum death grant (capital décès) [12], as well as Assurance Retraite (CNAV, phone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and the supplementary pension scheme Agirc-Arrco for a survivor pension (pension de réversion) [13].
    • French notary and inheritance tax filing: If the deceased had their tax domicile in France or held real estate or bank accounts there, contact a notary through the Notaires de France network (phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) to draw up the proof of heirship (acte de notoriété), query the Central Register of Last Wills (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), and file the inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) with the French tax administration within 6 months (for a death occurring in metropolitan France) [1][14].

closingQuestion: To help us guide you more precisely according to your situation: in which French municipality did the death occur (and in which Swiss canton or in France was your family member's last domicile), and are you planning repatriation to Switzerland or a local funeral in France?
