title: What to Do When a Citizen of Egypt Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Egypt Dies in United Arab Emirates: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Egypt dies in United Arab Emirates: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Arab Emirates, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Egypt and United Arab Emirates.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When an Egyptian citizen or resident with ties to Egypt dies in the United Arab Emirates, the medical certification, police clearance, and civil registration must first be completed with the authorities in the UAE, followed by Egyptian consular registration, international repatriation or local burial, and pension and succession procedures in Egypt and the UAE.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in the United Arab Emirates
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital: When your family member dies in a hospital in the United Arab Emirates, the attending physician issues an electronic Medical Notification of Death and arranges transfer of the deceased to a government mortuary [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or at a workplace: Immediately call the police on 999 and the ambulance service on 998 [1]. The local police command (such as Dubai Police, Abu Dhabi Police, or the police force of the relevant emirate) attends the scene, transfers the deceased to a forensic medicine department, and coordinates with the Public Prosecution if an investigation or forensic examination is required [1].
  • Police No Objection Certificate (NOC): Before the government mortuary can release the body for embalming, local burial, or repatriation, the police issue a stamped declaration and Police NOC (along with a Public Prosecution clearance for non-natural, sudden, or workplace deaths) [1][3].

steps.title: Repatriation Coverage, Funeral Coordination, and Egyptian Consular Support
steps.html:
• Employer and insurance coverage: Check whether the deceased held travel or medical insurance with a repatriation clause or was employed in the UAE. Under UAE federal labour rules enforced by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (phone: 600590000), the employer is responsible for covering the cost of repatriating the remains of a deceased employee to the home country or point of recruitment when requested by the family [1][6].
  • Appointing funeral and repatriation coordinators: In the UAE, an authorised family representative, employer sponsor, or licensed repatriation coordinator arranges mortuary preparation through the government embalming unit (such as Dubai Health in Dubai, the Department of Health via TAMM Abu Dhabi, or Emirates Health Services in the Northern Emirates) and books air cargo transport [2][3][4]. In Egypt, coordinate with a licensed international mortuary and funeral operator in Cairo, Alexandria, Hurghada, or Sharm El-Sheikh to handle airport customs and quarantine reception and transport to the family cemetery [9].
  • Egyptian diplomatic mission: Contact the Consular Section of the Embassy of Egypt in Abu Dhabi (for deaths in Abu Dhabi or Al Ain) or the Consulate General of Egypt in Dubai (for Dubai and the Northern Emirates), operating under the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to obtain the Egyptian consular NOC and register the death [9][10].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration, Visa Cancellation, and Egyptian Recognition
steps.html:
• Official UAE Death Certificate: Using the hospital notification, Police NOC, and the deceased's passport and Emirates ID, the family's representative or employer obtains the official bilingual (Arabic and English) Death Certificate from the health authority of the emirate where the death occurred: TAMM Abu Dhabi (Department of Health - Abu Dhabi) [3], Dubai Health / Dubai Health Authority (DHA) [2], or Emirates Health Services (EHS / MOHAP) in Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain, and Fujairah [4]. Request multiple copies in Arabic and English [1][3].
  • Residency visa and Emirates ID cancellation: Cancel the deceased's UAE residency visa and Emirates ID through the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) or the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) in Dubai as part of the official exit and registration process [1][3].
  • Attestation and Egyptian Civil Status registration: Have the UAE Death Certificate attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) [1][5]. Submit the attested UAE Death Certificate and the deceased's Egyptian passport and National ID card to the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate, which issues an Egyptian consular death record, cancels the passport, and forwards the registration to the Civil Status Organization (الأحوال المدنية) under the Ministry of Interior in Egypt so the family can obtain the computerised Egyptian Death Certificate [8][9][10]. (Where a death or direct burial registration is processed locally in Egypt, it is reported to the local Health Office / Maktab El-Seha within 24 hours and recorded by the Civil Status Organization, with foreign documents legalized by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs [8][9].)

steps.title: International Repatriation to Egypt vs. Local Burial or Cremation in the UAE
steps.html:
• International repatriation of human remains to Egypt: Repatriating a body from the UAE to Egypt requires government mortuary embalming, an Embalming Certificate, a Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease (Freedom from Infection), hermetic sealing in a zinc-lined coffin, a Police NOC for export of human remains, and UAE MoFA attestation [1][2][3][5]. The Egyptian Embassy or Consulate then issues a Consular Mortuary Certificate and No Objection Permit for shipment [9][10]. Upon arrival at Cairo International Airport or a regional Egyptian airport, the Preventive Medicine / Airport Quarantine authority (under the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population) verifies the embalming, sealing, and consular certificates before releasing the coffin for burial (with Public Prosecution / Niyaba clearance required if the death involved unnatural circumstances or a foreign national inquiry) [9][10]. If next of kin are in Egypt without a relative in the UAE, they execute an attested Power of Attorney (Tawkil) authorising the employer or representative in the UAE to complete the export formalities [3][9].
  • Local burial or disposition in the UAE: Families who choose local burial in the UAE can obtain a municipal burial permit once the Police NOC and health authority death registration are completed; Muslim burials are arranged through municipal cemetery administrations in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, or the Northern Emirates, while non-Muslim cemeteries and municipality-licensed crematoria are available for non-Muslim residents [1][3].

steps.title: Post-Death Benefits, End-of-Service Settlements, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• UAE end-of-service gratuity, insurance, and estates: Under UAE labour law, the employer must pay all unpaid salary, accrued leave, and statutory end-of-service gratuity (for workers with at least one year of continuous service), along with any applicable workplace death insurance, overseen by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation or the relevant free-zone authority [6]. Because UAE bank accounts are frozen upon notification of death, releasing local bank balances or assets requires a formal succession decree or probate order from the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (including the Abu Dhabi Civil Family Court), Dubai Courts (Personal Status Court or Non-Muslim Estate Court), or the DIFC Wills Service Centre if a registered will applies [7].
  • Egyptian survivor pension and funeral grant: Once the computerised Egyptian Death Certificate is issued, eligible dependents can claim the statutory funeral expenses grant and monthly survivor pension from the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) by submitting the death certificate, family registry extract (Qayd A'aely), and beneficiary civil status documents [11]. The Consular Sector of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs also assists families in following up on overseas employment dues and insurance settlements transmitted through diplomatic channels [9].
  • Egyptian inheritance declaration: To transfer bank accounts, real estate, or estate funds in Egypt, the heirs apply to the competent Egyptian Family Court (Mahkamat Al-Usra) for an official Inheritance Declaration (I'lam Al-Waratha / إعلام الوراثة) determining the legal heirs and their statutory shares [8][9].

Do you plan to repatriate the remains to a specific governorate or airport in Egypt, or arrange a local burial in the UAE?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Egypt Dies in Saudi Arabia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Egypt Dies in Saudi Arabia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Egypt dies in Saudi Arabia: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Saudi Arabia, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
introHtml: We are sorry for your loss. When an Egyptian citizen or resident with ties to Egypt dies in Saudi Arabia, the initial medical certification, police clearance, and civil registration are completed through Saudi government platforms, followed by Egyptian consular registration, international repatriation or local burial, and survivor benefit and succession procedures in both countries.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in Saudi Arabia
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital: When your family member dies in a public or private hospital in Saudi Arabia, the attending physician logs an electronic Medical Notification of Death in real time through the Saudi Ministry of Health (phone: 937; email: 937@moh.gov.sa / Sehhaty system) and transfers the deceased to an authorised hospital mortuary [1][2].
  • Death outside a hospital: If the death occurs at home, at a workplace, or in a public place, immediately call 911 (in Riyadh, Makkah, and Eastern Province) or 999 (Saudi Police in other regions) and 997 (Saudi Red Crescent Authority) [1][2]. The police secure the scene, open an official Police Report, and arrange transfer to a Forensic Medicine centre if the death was sudden, accidental, or under investigation, coordinating with the Public Prosecution before issuing a forensic release and police clearance [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation Coverage, Funeral Coordination, and Egyptian Consular Support
steps.html:
• Employer and insurance obligations: Check whether your family member had medical or travel insurance covering repatriation or worked for a Saudi employer. Under Saudi Labour Law administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (phone: 19911), the employer is responsible for preparing and transporting the remains of a deceased expatriate worker back to the home country or point of contracting unless the family agrees to local burial in Saudi Arabia [5].
  • Appointing funeral and repatriation coordinators: In Saudi Arabia, local burial permits and municipal mortuary services are managed through the Balady / Ikram platform of the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing, while international air cargo shipments are coordinated through authorised hospital mortuaries and IATA-accredited cargo agents in Riyadh, Jeddah, or Dammam [3]. In Egypt, appoint a licensed international mortuary and funeral operator in Cairo, Alexandria, Hurghada, or Sharm El-Sheikh to clear airport quarantine and transport the coffin to the cemetery [8][9].
  • Egyptian diplomatic mission: Contact the Embassy of Egypt in Riyadh (for central, eastern, and northern regions) or the Consulate General of Egypt in Jeddah (for western and southern regions), operating under the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to register the death and obtain the consular No Objection Certificate (NOC) [8][9].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration, Visa Cancellation, and Egyptian Recognition
steps.html:
• Saudi Death Certificate and Iqama cancellation: Once the hospital records the electronic death notification and any required police clearance is issued, a family member, employer sponsor (Kafeel), or authorised representative requests the official Saudi Death Certificate digitally through the Saudi Civil Affairs Directorate (Ahwal Madaniyah) via Absher on the Unified National Platform [1][2]. As part of closing the residency record, the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) cancels the deceased's residency permit (Iqama) or visa [1].
  • Legalization and Egyptian Civil Status registration: Have the Saudi Death Certificate attested by the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and presented with the deceased's Egyptian passport and National ID card to the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in Riyadh or Jeddah [8][9]. The mission cancels the passport, issues an Egyptian consular death record, and transmits the registration to the Civil Status Organization (الأحوال المدنية) under the Ministry of Interior in Egypt so the family can obtain the computerised Egyptian Death Certificate [7][8][9]. (When a death or burial registration is filed directly inside Egypt, it is reported to the local Health Office / Maktab El-Seha within 24 hours and recorded by the Civil Status Organization, with foreign certificates legalized by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs [7][8].)

steps.title: International Repatriation to Egypt vs. Local Burial in Saudi Arabia
steps.html:
• Family Power of Attorney (Wakala): If the next of kin reside in Egypt, they must execute a formal Power of Attorney (Wakala / Tawkil) naming the employer sponsor or a designated representative in Saudi Arabia, stating whether they request international repatriation to Egypt or local burial in Saudi Arabia, and have it legalized by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Saudi Embassy or Consulate in Egypt [8][9].
  • International repatriation of human remains: Repatriating the body from Saudi Arabia to Egypt requires the attested family Wakala, Police and provincial Emirate (Imarah) export clearance, an authorised hospital Embalming Certificate, a Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease and hermetic coffin sealing, Saudi MOFA attestation, and the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate Mortuary Certificate and NOC [1][8][9]. Upon arrival at Cairo International Airport or a regional Egyptian airport, the Preventive Medicine / Quarantine office (under the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population) inspects the embalming, sealing, and consular documents before releasing the coffin (with Public Prosecution / Niyaba clearance required where unnatural circumstances or foreign-inquiry rules apply) [8][9].
  • Local burial in Saudi Arabia: With the family's written consent and Police clearance, the authorised recipient can obtain a free electronic burial permit and print the Burial Certificate via the Balady / Ikram service of the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing for burial in a designated municipal cemetery in Saudi Arabia (including in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, Jeddah, or Dammam) [3].

steps.title: Post-Death Benefits, End-of-Service Settlements, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
• Saudi end-of-service award, GOSI benefits, and succession: Under Saudi Labour Law (Article 74), the employment contract ends upon death and the employer must settle unpaid wages, accrued leave, and the full statutory end-of-service award overseen by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development [5]. If the deceased was registered with the General Organization for Social Insurance (phone: 8001243344), eligible heirs can claim survivor pension or occupational work-injury death benefits online [6]. To collect Saudi bank balances or employer dues, the family obtains an official Determination of Heirs deed (Sakk Hasr Al-Waratha) through the Ministry of Justice (Najiz platform) or presents an Egyptian inheritance deed duly legalized for use in Saudi Arabia [4][5].
  • Egyptian survivor pension, consular follow-up, and inheritance: In Egypt, eligible dependents use the computerised Egyptian Death Certificate and family registry extract (Qayd A'aely) to claim funeral expenses grants and monthly survivor pensions from the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) [10]. The Consular Sector of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs also assists heirs in tracking and receiving overseas employment entitlements and blood-money (Diyya) or insurance settlements remitted from Saudi Arabia [8]. For Egyptian bank accounts and real property, heirs petition the Egyptian Family Court for an official Inheritance Declaration (I'lam Al-Waratha / إعلام الوراثة) [7][8].

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in Saudi Arabia
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital: When your family member dies in a public or private hospital in Saudi Arabia, the attending physician records an electronic Medical Notification of Death in real time through the Saudi Ministry of Health (phone: 937; email: 937@moh.gov.sa / Sehhaty system) and transfers the deceased to an authorised hospital mortuary [1][2].
  • Death outside a hospital: If the death occurs at home, in employer accommodation, at a workplace, or in a public area, immediately call 911 (in Riyadh, Makkah, and Eastern Province) or 999 (Saudi Police in other provinces) and 997 (Saudi Red Crescent Authority) [1][2]. The police secure the scene, prepare an official Police Report, and transfer the deceased to a Forensic Medicine centre if the cause of death is unnatural, sudden, or under investigation, coordinating with the Public Prosecution before issuing the forensic clearance and police release [1][2].

steps.title: Repatriation Coverage, Funeral Coordination, and Philippine Consular Support
steps.html:
• Employer, agency, and insurance coverage: Check whether your family member was employed in Saudi Arabia or covered by travel or employment insurance. Under Saudi Labour Law administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (phone: 19911), the employer is obligated to bear the costs of preparing and repatriating the remains of a deceased expatriate worker to the home country or point of recruitment unless the family agrees to local burial [5]. For Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), Philippine recruitment agencies and compulsory migrant worker insurance also share statutory repatriation responsibilities overseen by the Department of Migrant Workers [8].
  • Appointing funeral and cargo coordinators: In Saudi Arabia, municipal burial permits and mortuary services operate through the Balady / Ikram platform under the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing, while international air cargo shipments are arranged through authorised hospital mortuaries and IATA-certified cargo agents in Riyadh, Jeddah, or Dammam [3]. In the Philippines, appoint a Department of Health-licensed funeral establishment in the destination city or province to receive the coffin at the arrival airport (such as Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila, Mactan-Cebu, or Clark) and manage local transport and burial or cremation [7][8].
  • Philippine diplomatic mission: Notify the Embassy of the Philippines in Riyadh (phone: +966 11 482 3559) for deaths in Riyadh, Eastern Province, or northern and central regions, or the Philippine Consulate General in Jeddah for western and southern regions, together with the attached Migrant Workers Office (MWO) and Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) welfare officer [8].

steps.title: Civil Death Registration, Visa Cancellation, and Philippine Recognition
steps.html:
• Saudi Death Certificate and Iqama cancellation: Once the hospital records the electronic death notification and police clearance is issued, a family representative, employer sponsor (Kafeel), or authorised coordinator requests the official Saudi Death Certificate digitally through the Saudi Civil Affairs Directorate (Ahwal Madaniyah) via Absher on the Unified National Platform [1][2]. Simultaneously, the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) cancels the deceased's residency permit (Iqama) and issues the final exit/death record [1].
  • Legalization and Philippine Report of Death: Have the Saudi Death Certificate translated into English (if issued only in Arabic) and attested by the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) [8][9]. Submit the attested certificate, the deceased's original Philippine passport for cancellation, and the accomplished forms to the Philippine Embassy in Riyadh or Consulate General in Jeddah to file the official Report of Death (ROD) [8][9]. The foreign mission transmits the Report of Death through the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) so the family can obtain the official PSA Security Paper (SECPA) Death Certificate via PSA Serbilis [9]. (By contrast, when a death occurs inside the Philippines, it must be registered within 30 days at the Local Civil Registrar Office of the city or municipality of death before transmission to the PSA [9].)

steps.title: International Repatriation to the Philippines vs. Local Burial in Saudi Arabia
steps.html:
• Family Power of Attorney (Wakala / SPA): Because next of kin are usually in the Philippines, the surviving family executes a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) / Wakala authorising the employer sponsor, a relative in Saudi Arabia, or the Philippine Embassy/MWO representative to process local clearances and choose either repatriation to the Philippines or local burial in Saudi Arabia, authenticated through the DFA and the Saudi diplomatic mission [8].
  • International repatriation of human remains: Exporting the body from Saudi Arabia to the Philippines requires the authenticated family Wakala/SPA, Police and provincial Emirate (Imarah) export clearance, an authorised hospital Embalming Certificate, a Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease and hermetic coffin sealing, Saudi MOFA attestation, and the Philippine Embassy or Consulate Report of Death, Consular Mortuary Certificate, and No Objection Certificate (NOC) [1][8][9]. Upon arrival in the Philippines, the receiving funeral provider secures transfer and quarantine clearance from the Department of Health Bureau of Quarantine (BOQ), while OWWA and the Department of Migrant Workers provide airport reception and domestic transport assistance for eligible OFWs [8].
  • Local burial in Saudi Arabia: If the family authorises local burial in Saudi Arabia, the sponsor or representative uses the Police clearance and hospital notification to obtain a free electronic burial permit and print the Burial Certificate via the Balady / Ikram platform of the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing for interment in a designated municipal cemetery (including non-Muslim cemetery sections in cities such as Riyadh, Jeddah, or Dammam, or Muslim cemeteries as applicable) [3][8].

steps.title: Post-Death Benefits, End-of-Service Settlements, Tax, and Probate in Both Countries
steps.html:
• Saudi end-of-service award, GOSI benefits, and succession: Under Saudi Labour Law (Article 74), the employment contract terminates upon death and the employer must pay all unpaid wages, accrued leave, and the full statutory end-of-service award regulated by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development [5]. If the deceased was covered by the General Organization for Social Insurance (phone: 8001243344), eligible family members can claim occupational work-injury death compensation or survivor pensions online [6]. Releasing frozen Saudi bank accounts, blood-money (Diyya) awards, or estate funds requires an official Determination of Heirs deed (Sakk Hasr Al-Waratha) through the Ministry of Justice (Najiz platform) or legalized Philippine heirship documents coordinated through the Philippine Embassy [4][5][8].
  • Philippine statutory benefits: Using the Report of Death or PSA Death Certificate, eligible beneficiaries in the Philippines can claim funeral and survivor death benefits from the Social Security System (SSS) for private-sector and voluntary OFW members (or GSIS for government workers), inpatient reimbursements from PhilHealth, provident savings and death benefits from the Pag-IBIG Fund, and burial and livelihood grants from OWWA and the Department of Migrant Workers AKSYON Fund [7][8].
  • Philippine estate tax and settlement: Under rules administered by the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), the Estate Tax Return (BIR Form 1801) must be filed within one year from the date of death (at a flat 6% estate tax rate on the net taxable estate after statutory deductions; statutory SSS, GSIS, and OWWA death benefits are exempt) to obtain the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) required to transfer Philippine bank accounts or real estate via an Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate or court probate [10].

closingQuestion: To help tailor this guidance to your situation, please let us know: 1. In which city or province of Saudi Arabia did the death occur, and was your family member employed as an OFW at the time? 2. Do you plan to repatriate the remains to a specific city in the Philippines or arrange local burial in Saudi Arabia?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in Brazil: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Portugal dies in Brazil: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Brazil, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Portugal and Brazil.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person with Portuguese citizenship or residence ties to Portugal dies in Brazil, the initial medical certification, civil registration, and public health clearance procedures follow Brazilian law, and are then coordinated with Portuguese consular services and the civil registry, social security, and tax authorities in both Portugal and Brazil.

Below are the five main official steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Forensic Clearance in Brazil
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital: If the death occurs in a hospital or healthcare facility in Brazil, the attending physician issues the official Medical Death Declaration (Declaração de Óbito - DO) free of charge on the standard form issued by the Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde), which is mandatory for civil registration and any funeral procedure [1].
  • Death at home or in a public place: If the death occurs outside a hospital facility, immediately call the Mobile Emergency Care Service (SAMU) at 192 or the Military Police (Polícia Militar) at 190 [1]. In the case of a natural death without medical attendance, the body is referred to the municipal or state Death Verification Service (Serviço de Verificação de Óbito - SVO, for example in São Paulo or Rio de Janeiro) so that the Declaração de Óbito can be issued [1]. Where an external cause, accident, or violent death is suspected, the incident is recorded at the Civil Police station (Delegacia de Polícia Civil) and the body is examined by the Forensic Medical Institute (Instituto Médico Legal - IML), which issues the Declaração de Óbito and the forensic release order (termo de liberação) [1].

steps.title: Insurance, Funeral Coordination in Brazil and Portugal, and Consular Support
steps.html:
• Checking travel or assistance insurance: Before making direct financial commitments, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, life insurance, or bank card assistance covering international repatriation, as the insurer normally appoints the company coordinating international transport [3][5].
  • Appointing funeral providers in both countries: In Brazil, engage the municipal funeral service or a licensed funeral company authorised for international air transport (you can consult the sector represented by the Brazilian Association of Funeral Sector Companies and Directors, Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF) to handle embalming (somatoconservação) and air cargo dispatch [1][3]. In Portugal, coordinate reception at the arrival airport (such as Lisbon, Porto, or Faro) with a funeral agency legally registered with the Directorate-General for Economic Activities, Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE / gov.pt), and represented by sector associations such as ANEL or AAFC [6][7]. Clarvia lists these organisations from public sources solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank individual providers.
  • Contacting the Portuguese consular network: Report the death to the Portuguese consular post with jurisdiction over the place of death, such as the Consulate General of Portugal in São Paulo (Consulado-Geral de Portugal em São Paulo), the Consulate General of Portugal in Rio de Janeiro (Consulado-Geral de Portugal no Rio de Janeiro), or the Consular Section of the Embassy of Portugal in Brasília, which form part of the network of the Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros - MNE / Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas) [4][5].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Brazil, Hague Apostille, and Transcription in Portugal
steps.html:
• Brazilian Death Certificate and Hague Apostille: Using the medical Declaração de Óbito and the deceased's identification documents (passport, National Migration Registry Card CRNM / RNE, or Brazilian CPF tax number), the death must be registered at the Civil Registry Office of Natural Persons (Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais) for the district where the death occurred within the ordinary deadline of 24 hours (or up to 15 days in the cases provided for by the Brazilian Public Records Law); the first certificate is free of charge and duplicate copies can be requested via the Civil Registry Portal (ARPEN Brasil) [1]. For the certificate to take legal effect in Portugal and support international repatriation, request an unabridged full-text Death Certificate (Certidão de Óbito em inteiro teor) and obtain a Hague Apostille (Apostila da Haia) at an authorised registry office under the supervision of the National Council of Justice, Conselho Nacional de Justiça [2][5].
  • Mandatory registration in Portugal: The death of a Portuguese citizen occurring abroad must be registered in the Portuguese legal order [4][5]. Free transcription of the Portuguese death record (Assento de Óbito) can be requested in person or by post through the Consulado-Geral de Portugal em São Paulo, the Consulado-Geral de Portugal no Rio de Janeiro, or the Embassy of Portugal in Brasília, or directly at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) of the Institute of Registries and Notary, Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / Justiça.gov.pt, where deaths occurring inside Portugal are declared within 48 hours and where a Vienna Convention multilingual CIEC Form C extract can also be issued) [4][5][8].

steps.title: International Repatriation to Portugal vs. Local Burial or Cremation in Brazil
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body to Portugal: Air transport of a body from Brazil to Portugal requires prior registration of the death at the Portuguese consulate and free issuance of the consular Repatriation Permit (Alvará de Trasladação, aligned with the international mortuary transit rules of the Strasbourg Agreement and the Berlin Convention) [4][5][9]. To obtain it, the Brazilian funeral company compiles the apostilled unabridged Death Certificate (Certidão de Óbito em inteiro teor), the embalming or thanatopraxy certificate (ata de embalsamamento ou tanatopraxia), a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious disease with a notarised signature and Hague Apostille, the certificate confirming placement in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin (urna zincada lacrada), the police/municipal mortuary transit permit (guia de livre-trânsito mortuário), and the airport sanitary authorisation issued by the Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária - ANVISA, under Resolution RDC No. 33/2011) [2][3][5].
  • Repatriation of ashes or local funeral in Brazil: If the family chooses cremation in Brazil (which requires, for a natural death, a Declaração de Óbito signed by two physicians or one forensic pathologist, or judicial authorisation in the event of a violent death), transporting the urn of ashes to Portugal likewise requires the consular Alvará de Trasladação supported by the apostilled Death Certificate, the Cremation Certificate (Certificado de Cremação), and a copy of the flight ticket [1][5]. If the family opts for local burial at a municipal or private cemetery in Brazil, interment takes place directly using the Brazilian Certidão de Óbito and the burial permit (guia de sepultamento) issued by the Cartório de Registro Civil [1].

steps.title: Social Security Benefits, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Portugal and Brazil
steps.html:
• Benefits and succession in Portugal: Once the death is registered, eligible family members may apply to the Portuguese social security authority, Segurança Social (via Segurança Social Direta or in person), for the Death Grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 days of the death), Reimbursement of Funeral Expenses (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days by the person who proves payment of the funeral), and the Survivor's Pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [10][11]. To handle the formal qualification of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros), bank account procedures, and division of estate assets in Portugal, the family can use the Espaço Óbito one-stop desk and the Inheritance Desk (Balcão das Heranças) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [8][13]. The head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must also file the declaration of gratuitous transfers (Form 1 of Stamp Duty, Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira / Portal das Finanças) by the end of the third month following the month of death, even when close heirs qualify for tax exemption [12].
  • Social security and probate inventory in Brazil: If the deceased was insured under the Brazilian social security system, dependants may apply for the Brazilian Survivor's Pension (Pensão por Morte) from the National Institute of Social Security, Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (via the Meu INSS platform or by calling 135), as well as claim any remaining FGTS severance fund or PIS/PASEP balances at Caixa Econômica Federal [1][14]. Where property, real estate, or bank accounts exist in Brazil, heirs must open a judicial probate inventory (inventário judicial) or, where all heirs are adults in agreement and there is no will, an extrajudicial inventory by public deed at a Brazilian Notary Office (Cartório de Notas, represented by the Notarial College of Brazil, Colégio Notarial do Brasil - CNB), observing the statutory deadline of 2 months (60 days) from the date of death to avoid state penalties on the Brazilian inheritance tax (Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação - ITCMD) [1].

pt.title: O que fazer quando ocorre um óbito entre Brasil e Portugal: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um falecimento entre Brasil e Portugal: certificado médico de óbito, agência funerária autorizada, registo civil do óbito, formalidades consulares e trasladação internacional ou funeral local, e pensões de sobrevivência e sucessão.
pt.introHtml: Lamentamos a perda do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa com nacionalidade ou vínculos de residência em Portugal falece no Brasil, os procedimentos iniciais de certificação médica, registo civil e controlo sanitário decorrem segundo a legislação brasileira, articulando-se em seguida com os serviços consulares portugueses e as entidades de registo civil, segurança social e administração fiscal em Portugal e no Brasil.

steps.title: Certificação Médica do Óbito e Liberação Pericial no Brasil
steps.html:
• Óbito em hospital: Se o falecimento ocorrer num hospital ou unidade de saúde no Brasil, o médico assistente emite gratuitamente a Declaração de Óbito (DO), no formulário oficial padronizado pelo Ministério da Saúde, indispensável para o registo civil e para qualquer procedimento funerário [1].
  • Óbito em residência ou na via pública: Caso o óbito ocorra fora de unidade hospitalar, ligue de imediato para o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU) através do número 192 ou para a Polícia Militar pelo número 190 [1]. Tratando-se de morte natural sem assistência médica, o corpo é encaminhado para o Serviço de Verificação de Óbito (SVO) do município ou estado (por exemplo, em São Paulo ou no Rio de Janeiro) para emissão da Declaração de Óbito [1]. Se houver suspeita de causa externa, acidente ou morte violenta, a ocorrência é registada na Delegacia de Polícia Civil e o corpo é periciado pelo Instituto Médico Legal (IML), que emite a Declaração de Óbito e o termo de liberação [1].

steps.title: Seguro, Coordenação Funerária no Brasil e em Portugal, e Apoio Consular
steps.html:
• Verificação de seguro de viagem ou assistência: Antes de assumir compromissos financeiros diretos, verifique se a pessoa falecida dispunha de seguro de viagem, seguro de vida ou assistência associada a cartão bancário que cubra o repatriamento, uma vez que a seguradora costuma designar a empresa coordenadora do transporte internacional [3][5].
  • Nomeação de agências funerárias nos dois países: No Brasil, contrate o serviço funerário municipal ou uma empresa funerária habilitada para transporte aéreo internacional (podendo consultar o setor representado pela Associação Brasileira de Empresas e Diretores do Setor Funerário - ABREDIF) para tratar da somatoconservação e do embarque de carga aérea [1][3]. Em Portugal, articule a receção no aeroporto de chegada (como Lisboa, Porto ou Faro) com uma agência funerária legalmente habilitada junto da Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE / gov.pt) e representada por associações do setor como a ANEL ou a AAFC [6][7].
  • Contacto com a rede consular portuguesa: Comunique o falecimento ao posto consular português com jurisdição sobre o local do óbito, como o Consulado-Geral de Portugal em São Paulo, o Consulado-Geral de Portugal no Rio de Janeiro ou a Secção Consular da Embaixada de Portugal em Brasília, que integram a rede do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros (MNE / Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas) [4][5].

steps.title: Registo Civil do Óbito no Brasil, Apostila da Haia e Transcrição em Portugal
steps.html:
• Certidão de Óbito no Brasil e Apostila da Haia: Com a Declaração de Óbito médica e os documentos de identificação da pessoa falecida (passaporte, Carteira de Registro Nacional Migratório / RNE ou CPF), o óbito deve ser registado no Cartório de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais da circunscrição onde ocorreu o falecimento, no prazo ordinário de 24 horas (ou até 15 dias nos casos previstos na Lei dos Registros Públicos), sendo a primeira via gratuita e as segundas vias acessíveis através do Portal do Registro Civil (ARPEN Brasil) [1]. Para produzir efeitos em Portugal e instruir a trasladação, solicite a Certidão de Óbito em inteiro teor e providencie a respetiva Apostila da Haia num cartório autorizado sob supervisão do Conselho Nacional de Justiça [2][5].
  • Registo obrigatório em Portugal: O óbito de cidadão português ocorrido no estrangeiro é de registo obrigatório na ordem jurídica portuguesa [4][5]. A transcrição gratuita do Assento de Óbito pode ser requerida presencialmente ou por via postal junto do Consulado-Geral de Portugal em São Paulo, do Consulado-Geral de Portugal no Rio de Janeiro ou da Embaixada de Portugal em Brasília, ou diretamente em qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / Justiça.gov.pt, onde os óbitos ocorridos em território nacional são declarados no prazo de 48 horas e onde também pode ser emitida a certidão plurilingue da Convenção de Viena / CIEC Fórmula C) [4][5][8].

steps.title: Trasladação Internacional para Portugal vs. Inumação ou Cremação Local no Brasil
steps.html:
• Trasladação internacional de corpo para Portugal: O transporte aéreo de cadáver do Brasil para Portugal exige o prévio registo do óbito no consulado português e a emissão gratuita do Alvará de Trasladação consular (em articulação com as regras de livre-trânsito mortuário do Acordo de Estrasburgo e da Convenção de Berlim) [4][5][9]. Para o efeito, a agência funerária brasileira reúne a Certidão de Óbito em inteiro teor apostilada, a ata de embalsamamento ou tanatopraxia, o atestado médico comprovativo da inexistência de doença infetocontagiosa com assinatura reconhecida e Apostila da Haia, o termo de acondicionamento em urna zincada hermeticamente selada, a guia de livre-trânsito mortuário policial/municipal e a autorização sanitária da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA, nos termos da RDC n.º 33/2011 nos postos aeroportuários) [2][3][5].
  • Trasladação de cinzas ou funeral local no Brasil: Caso a família opte pela cremação no Brasil (que exige, em morte natural, Declaração de Óbito assinada por dois médicos ou um médico legista, ou autorização judicial em caso de morte violenta), o transporte da urna de cinzas para Portugal requer igualmente o Alvará de Trasladação consular instruído com a Certidão de Óbito apostilada, o Certificado de Cremação e a cópia do bilhete de passagem aérea [1][5]. Se a família optar pela inumação local num cemitério municipal ou particular no Brasil, o sepultamento realiza-se diretamente com a Certidão de Óbito e a guia de sepultamento emitida pelo Cartório de Registro Civil [1].

steps.title: Prestações Sociais, Impostos e Sucessão em Portugal e no Brasil
steps.html:
• Prestações e sucessão em Portugal: Após o registo do óbito, os familiares elegíveis podem requerer junto da Segurança Social (através da Segurança Social Direta ou atendimento presencial) o Subsídio por Morte (no prazo de 180 dias a contar do falecimento), o Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral (no prazo de 90 dias por quem comprovadamente pagou o funeral) e a Pensão de Sobrevivência [10][11]. Para tratar da habilitação de herdeiros, bloqueio ou movimentação de contas bancárias e partilha de bens em Portugal, a família pode recorrer ao Espaço Óbito e ao Balcão das Heranças do Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado [8][13]. O cabeça-de-casal deve ainda entregar a participação de transmissões gratuitas (Modelo 1 do Imposto do Selo) junto da Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portal das Finanças) até ao final do terceiro mês seguinte ao do falecimento, mesmo quando os herdeiros legitimários beneficiem de isenção [12].
  • Previdência e inventário no Brasil: Se a pessoa falecida era segurada do regime previdenciário brasileiro, os dependentes podem requerer a Pensão por Morte junto do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (através da plataforma Meu INSS ou pelo telefone 135), bem como o levantamento de eventuais saldos de FGTS e PIS/PASEP na Caixa Econômica Federal [1][14]. Existindo bens, imóveis ou contas bancárias no Brasil, os herdeiros devem requerer a abertura de inventário judicial ou, havendo consenso e ausência de testamento ou incapazes, de inventário extrajudicial por escritura pública em Cartório de Notas (Colégio Notarial do Brasil - CNB), observando o prazo legal de 2 meses (60 dias) a contar do óbito para evitar multas estaduais sobre o imposto de transmissão causa mortis (ITCMD) [1].

pt.closingQuestion: Para adaptar estas orientações ao seu caso concreto, por favor indique: 1. Em que cidade e estado do Brasil ocorreu o falecimento, e o óbito teve lugar num hospital ou fora dele? 2. Pretendem realizar a trasladação do corpo ou das cinzas para um município específico em Portugal, ou proceder à inumação ou cremação no Brasil?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Colombia Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Colombia Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Colombia dies in Spain: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Spain, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Colombia and Spain.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member in Spain. Below are the five official steps in order to manage the medical and civil registry formalities in Spain, funeral and consular coordination with Colombia, international repatriation or local burial, and subsequent pension and probate procedures in both countries.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and forensic or judicial clearance in Spain
steps.html:
The legal and public health process in Spain begins with the issuance of the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción) from the General Council of Official Medical Associations (Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos), which is required to register the death and authorize any transport or final disposition [1][2].

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending medical team at the hospital (for example, within the public hospital network in Madrid or Catalonia) issues the Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción) once natural causes of death are confirmed, allowing the licensed funeral provider to transfer the body to the mortuary (tanatorio) [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Call the single European emergency number 112 immediately. If an emergency physician confirms documented natural causes, they may sign the certificate; if the death is sudden, violent, or lacks a clear clinical cause, the police and the Duty Court (Juzgado de Guardia) intervene, ordering the removal of the body and its transfer to the competent Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses, such as the Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses de Madrid or the Institut de Medicina Legal i Ciències Forenses de Catalunya) for a judicial autopsy before authorizing release of the body and civil registration [1][2].
  • Regional Mortuary Health Regulations timeframes: Under Spanish health regulations and regional mortuary health rules (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria), burial, cremation, or final sealing of the coffin generally cannot take place before 24 hours have elapsed since the death, and final disposition or special preservation (embalming or refrigeration) must normally be carried out within 48 hours [2][3].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, appointing funeral directors in Spain and Colombia, and consular assistance
steps.html:
Before entering into direct financial commitments, check whether the deceased held a funeral insurance policy (póliza de decesos), travel insurance, or bank card assistance coverage, as the insurer typically appoints and pays the funeral operators in both countries directly [2].

  • Funeral coordination in Spain and Colombia: If no insurer is involved, the family may appoint a licensed funeral company in Spain (empresa funeraria habilitada) through the industry directory of the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) (National Association of Funeral Services) to handle collection, mortuary care, civil registry formalities, and sanitary preparation [4]. In the event of repatriation, the Spanish provider coordinates with a licensed funeral home (funeraria habilitada) in the destination city in Colombia (such as Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali), which arranges airport reception and the local health permit for burial, cremation, or domestic transport (licencia sanitaria de inhumación, cremación o traslado) from the municipal or district health authority, such as the Bogotá District Secretariat of Health (Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá) [5]. Clarvia provides these institutional references solely for informational and guidance purposes and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific providers.
  • Colombian consular assistance in Spain: Notify the competent Colombian consulate according to the place of death, such as the Consulado General de Colombia en Madrid (Consulate General of Colombia in Madrid, email cmadrid@cancilleria.gov.co, phone +34 917 452 590) or the consulates in Barcelona, Valencia, Seville, Bilbao, Palma de Mallorca, or Las Palmas [6]. The consulate guides the family, performs the consular registration of the death, and verifies the documentation required to transport human remains or ashes to Colombia, although it does not generally pay commercial funeral expenses [6][7].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Spain and document validity in Colombia
steps.html:
Official registration of the death in Spain is a prerequisite for obtaining the burial or cremation permit and the official certificates needed for legal procedures in Colombia [1].

  • Civil Registry in Spain (24-hour timeframe): The death declaration is usually submitted by the funeral company to the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred (under the Ministerio de Justicia, the Spanish Ministry of Justice) within 24 hours of the death [1]. Once registered, the registry issues the burial permit (licencia de sepultura) and the Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción, as well as the multilingual CIEC Form C certificate under the 1976 Vienna Convention when required for European signatory states) [1].
  • Hague Apostille and Colombian Civil Death Registration: Because Colombia is not a party to the Vienna Convention on multilingual extracts, for the Spanish Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) to have full legal effect before Colombian authorities, it must bear the Hague Apostille (Apostilla de La Haya) issued by the justice authorities in Spain [1][8]. With the apostilled Spanish certificate and the deceased person's Colombian identity document (cédula de ciudadanía or passport), family members can request free registration in the Colombian Civil Death Registry (Registro Civil de Defunción) directly before the Consulado General de Colombia en Madrid (or another Colombian consular office in Spain via the online system linked with the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil, the National Civil Registry of Colombia) [6][7][9]. If registration is completed directly in Colombia (where the standard statutory period for local deaths is two business days), it can be processed at any office of the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil or an authorized notary public (notaría) by presenting the duly apostilled foreign certificate [8][9].

steps.title: International repatriation of the body or ashes vs. local burial or cremation in Spain
steps.html:
The family must choose between international repatriation to Colombia or completing the full funeral service in Spain [2][3].

  • Repatriation of the body in a coffin to Colombia: The Spanish funeral director applies to the Foreign Health department (Sanidad Exterior) of the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health, via the SISAEX system) for the international mortuary transport health authorization (autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional de cadáveres) and the mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio), complying with mortuary health regulations and applicable international agreements [3]. This requires authorized embalming or preservation, a medical certificate confirming the absence of quarantinable infectious diseases, and placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc inner liner [3]. For entry into Colombia, the coordinating funeral provider presents the apostilled Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción), the health and embalming certificates verified with consular support, and obtains the health permit for transport and burial (permiso sanitario de traslado e inhumación) from the port/airport health authorities and the municipal or district health secretariats under the guidelines of the Colombian Ministry of Health and Social Protection (Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social) [5][6].
  • International transport of ashes after cremation in Spain: If cremation takes place in Spain, transporting the funerary urn is administratively and financially simpler [2][3]. The sealed and labeled urn must be accompanied by the apostilled Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) and the official cremation certificate issued by the Spanish crematorium, complying with airline rules and health entry controls in Colombia [1][3][5].
  • Local burial or cremation in Spain: If the remains stay in Spain, the service is governed by the municipal cemetery or crematorium bylaws (for example, in Madrid or Barcelona) once the Civil Registry issues the burial permit [1][2].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, funeral grants, taxes, and probate in Colombia and Spain
steps.html:
Once the death is registered in both civil registries, family members or beneficiaries can initiate pension, banking, and estate procedures in each jurisdiction:

  • Pensions, funeral grant, and estate succession in Colombia: If the deceased contributed to or received a pension under the public scheme administered by the Administradora Colombiana de Pensiones - Colpensiones (Colombian Pension Administrator, or a private pension fund such as Porvenir, Protección, Colfondos, or Skandia), the person who paid the funeral expenses (even if paid in Spain, by submitting paid and apostilled invoices) may claim the funeral grant (auxilio funerario) before the one-year limitation period expires, and statutory beneficiaries may apply for the survivor pension or pension substitution (pensión de sobrevivientes o sustitución pensional) [10][11]. For assets and bank accounts in Colombia, if all heirs agree, estate settlement (liquidación de herencia) may be completed before a notary public through a licensed attorney (overseen by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro), granting a special power of attorney from Spain before the Colombian consulate or before a Spanish notary with a Hague Apostille; if there is a dispute, probate is handled through a succession proceeding (proceso de sucesión) before a family court [8][12].
  • Social Security benefits and probate in Spain: If the deceased worked or received a pension in Spain, eligible survivors may claim the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and widowhood, orphan, or family member pensions (pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares) from the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) (National Institute of Social Security), applying where appropriate the bilateral Social Security Agreement between Spain and Colombia to totalize contribution periods [13][14]. To administer an estate with assets in Spain, once 15 business days have passed since the death, heirs must apply to the Ministerio de Justicia (using Modelo 790) for the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Life Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento) [15]. With these certificates, heirs appear before a notary public through the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of Notaries) to obtain an authorized copy of the will or execute an intestate declaration of heirs (acta de declaración de herederos abintestato) and deed of inheritance adjudication [16]. Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) and municipal capital gains tax (plusvalía municipal) must be self-assessed within 6 months of the death (extendable by another 6 months if requested within the first 5 months) [15][16].

closingQuestion: To help tailor the next steps to your specific situation: 1. In which municipality in Spain did the death occur, and to which city or department in Colombia do you wish to transport the body or ashes (or do you prefer local burial or cremation in Spain)? 2. Did your family member have active funeral or repatriation insurance, or leave assets or pension contributions in both Spain and Colombia?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre España y Colombia: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre España y Colombia: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar en España. A continuación le explicamos los cinco pasos oficiales en orden para gestionar las formalidades médicas y registrales en España, la coordinación funeraria y consular con Colombia, el traslado internacional o la sepultura local, y los trámites posteriores de pensiones y sucesión en ambos países.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción y autorización forense o judicial en España
steps.html:
El proceso legal y sanitario en España se inicia con la expedición del Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial del Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos, indispensable para inscribir el fallecimiento y autorizar cualquier traslado o destino final [1][2].

  • Fallecimiento en hospital o centro sanitario: El equipo médico tratante en el hospital (por ejemplo, en centros de la red pública de Madrid o Cataluña) emite el Certificado Médico de Defunción una vez comprobadas las causas naturales del deceso, permitiendo que la empresa funeraria retire el cuerpo hacia el tanatorio [1][2].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Debe llamarse de inmediato al teléfono único de emergencias 112. Si un facultativo de urgencias confirma causas naturales documentadas, puede firmar el certificado; si la muerte es súbita, violenta o sin causa clínica clara, intervienen las fuerzas policiales y el Juzgado de Guardia, que ordena el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses correspondiente (como el Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses de Madrid o el Institut de Medicina Legal i Ciències Forenses de Catalunya) para la práctica de la autopsia judicial antes de autorizar la entrega del cuerpo e inscripción registral [1][2].
  • Plazos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Conforme a la normativa sanitaria española y los reglamentos autonómicos de sanidad mortuoria, con carácter general no puede practicarse la inhumación, cremación ni el cierre definitivo de féretro antes de las 24 horas desde el fallecimiento, y el destino final o la conservación especial (embalsamamiento o refrigeración) debe efectuarse habitualmente antes de las 48 horas [2][3].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriación, designación de funeraria en España y Colombia, y asistencia consular
steps.html:
Antes de asumir compromisos económicos directos, conviene verificar si la persona fallecida contaba con una póliza de decesos, seguro de viaje o cobertura de asistencia vinculada a tarjetas bancarias, ya que la aseguradora suele designar y cubrir directamente a los operadores funerarios en ambos países [2].

  • Coordinación funeraria en España y Colombia: Si no interviene una aseguradora, la familia puede designar una empresa funeraria habilitada en España a través del directorio sectorial de la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) para que gestione la recogida, el tanatorio, los trámites ante el registro civil y la preparación sanitaria [4]. En caso de repatriación, dicha empresa se coordina con una funeraria habilitada en la ciudad de destino en Colombia (por ejemplo, en Bogotá, Medellín o Cali), la cual tramita la recepción aeroportuaria y la licencia sanitaria local de inhumación, cremación o traslado interno ante la autoridad de salud municipal o distrital, como la Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá [5]. Clarvia proporciona estas referencias institucionales únicamente a título informativo y de orientación, y no recomienda, respalda ni clasifica a proveedores concretos.
  • Asistencia consular colombiana en España: Debe notificarse el deceso a la representación consular competente según el lugar del fallecimiento, como el Consulado General de Colombia en Madrid (correo cmadrid@cancilleria.gov.co, teléfono +34 917 452 590) o los consulados en Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla, Bilbao, Palma de Mallorca o Las Palmas [6]. El consulado orienta a la familia, realiza la inscripción consular de la defunción y verifica la documentación exigida para el traslado de restos o cenizas a Colombia, aunque no asume por regla general los costes funerarios comerciales [6][7].

steps.title: Inscripción de la defunción en el Registro Civil en España y validez documental en Colombia
steps.html:
La inscripción oficial del fallecimiento en España es el requisito previo para obtener la licencia de enterramiento o incineración y los certificados necesarios para los trámites en Colombia [1].

  • Registro Civil en España (plazo de 24 horas): La declaración de la defunción se presenta habitualmente por conducto de la empresa funeraria ante el Registro Civil del municipio donde ocurrió el fallecimiento (dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia) dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al deceso [1]. Una vez practicada la inscripción, se expide la licencia de sepultura y el Certificado Literal de Defunción (y, cuando se requiera para países europeos del Convenio de Viena de 1976, el certificado plurilingüe Fórmula C) [1].
  • Apostilla de La Haya e inscripción del Registro Civil de Defunción para Colombia: Como Colombia no es parte del Convenio de Viena sobre certificaciones plurilingües, para que el Certificado Literal de Defunción español surta plenos efectos ante entidades colombianas debe contar con la Apostilla de La Haya expedida por las autoridades de justicia en España [1][8]. Con ese certificado español apostillado y el documento de identidad de la persona fallecida (cédula de ciudadanía o pasaporte), los familiares pueden solicitar de forma gratuita la inscripción en el Registro Civil de Defunción colombiano directamente ante el Consulado General de Colombia en Madrid (u otra oficina consular en España mediante el sistema en línea con la Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil) [6][7][9]. Si la inscripción se realiza directamente en territorio colombiano (donde el plazo ordinario para defunciones locales es de dos días hábiles), se tramita ante cualquier oficina de la Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil o notaría autorizada presentando el certificado extranjero debidamente apostillado [8][9].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional de cuerpo o cenizas frente a inhumación o cremación local en España
steps.html:
La familia debe decidir entre el traslado internacional hacia Colombia o la realización del servicio funerario completo en España [2][3].

  • Repatriación del cuerpo en féretro hacia Colombia: La funeraria española gestiona ante el área de Sanidad Exterior del Ministerio de Sanidad (mediante el sistema SISAEX) la autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional de cadáveres y el salvoconducto mortuorio, cumpliendo las normas técnicas de policía sanitaria mortuoria y convenios internacionales aplicables [3]. Esto exige el embalsamamiento o conservación autorizada, certificado médico de no padecer enfermedades infectocontagiosas de cuarentena y el acondicionamiento en féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada [3]. Para el ingreso en Colombia, la funeraria coordinadora presenta el Certificado Literal de Defunción apostillado, los certificados sanitarios y de embalsamamiento visados o verificados con apoyo del consulado y gestiona el permiso sanitario de traslado e inhumación ante las autoridades portuarias/aeroportuarias de sanidad y las secretarías de salud municipales o distritales bajo los lineamientos del Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social [5][6].
  • Traslado internacional de cenizas tras cremación en España: Si se opta por la incineración en España, el transporte de la urna funeraria resulta administrativa y económicamente más sencillo [2][3]. Se requiere que la urna vaya cerrada e identificada junto con el Certificado Literal de Defunción apostillado y el certificado oficial de cremación expedido por el crematorio español, cumpliendo las normas de la aerolínea y los controles de ingreso sanitario en Colombia [1][3][5].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en España: Si los restos permanecen en España, el servicio se rige por las ordenanzas del cementerio o crematorio municipal correspondiente (por ejemplo, en Madrid o Barcelona) una vez emitida la licencia del Registro Civil [1][2].

steps.title: Prestaciones de supervivencia, auxilio funerario, impuestos y sucesión en Colombia y España
steps.html:
Una vez inscrito el fallecimiento en ambos registros civiles, los familiares o derechohabientes pueden iniciar las gestiones patrimoniales y previsionales en cada jurisdicción:

  • Pensiones, auxilio funerario y sucesión en Colombia: Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o era pensionada en el régimen público administrado por la Administradora Colombiana de Pensiones - Colpensiones (o en un fondo privado de pensiones como Porvenir, Protección, Colfondos o Skandia), quien haya sufragado los gastos exequiales (incluso si se pagaron en España, aportando las facturas canceladas y apostilladas) puede reclamar el auxilio funerario antes de que prescriba al año del fallecimiento, y los beneficiarios legales pueden solicitar la pensión de sobrevivientes o sustitución pensional [10][11]. Para los bienes y cuentas bancarias en Colombia, si existe acuerdo entre todos los herederos, el trámite de liquidación de herencia puede realizarse por vía notarial mediante apoderado abogado (supervisado por la Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro), otorgando poder especial desde España ante el consulado colombiano o ante notario español con Apostilla de La Haya; si hay controversia, se tramita mediante proceso de sucesión ante juzgado de familia [8][12].
  • Prestaciones de la Seguridad Social y herencia en España: Si la persona fallecida trabajaba o percibía pensión en España, los derechohabientes pueden solicitar el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS), aplicándose cuando proceda el Convenio bilateral de Seguridad Social entre España y Colombia para totalizar periodos cotizados [13][14]. Para tramitar la herencia de bienes situados en España, transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde el fallecimiento se debe solicitar al Ministerio de Justicia (mediante el Modelo 790) el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [15]. Con dichos certificados se acude a una notaría a través del Consejo General del Notariado para obtener copia autorizada del testamento o tramitar el acta de declaración de herederos abintestato y la adjudicación de herencia [16]. El Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones y la plusvalía municipal en España deben autoliquidarse dentro de los 6 meses siguientes al fallecimiento (prorrogables por otros 6 meses si la prórroga se solicita dentro de los primeros 5 meses) [15][16].
