title: What to Do When a Citizen of Morocco Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Morocco Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Morocco dies in Spain: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Spain, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Morocco and Spain.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member in Spain. Below are the five official steps in order to manage medical and civil registration formalities in Spain, funeral and consular coordination with the Kingdom of Morocco, international repatriation or local burial, and subsequent social security and probate procedures in both countries.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and forensic or judicial clearance in Spain
steps.html:
All civil registration and mortuary health formalities in Spain begin with the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción) issued by the General Council of Official Medical Associations (Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos), which is essential to register the death and obtain the burial or transport permit [1][2].

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: When death occurs from natural causes under medical care (for example, in public or private hospitals in Madrid, Catalonia, or Andalusia), the attending physician issues the Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción), enabling the funeral company to transfer the body to the mortuary (tanatorio) [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Call the single emergency number 112 immediately. If the emergency physician confirms a documented natural death, they may sign the certificate; if the death is sudden, violent, or without an established clinical cause, the police and the Duty Court (Juzgado de Guardia) intervene, ordering the removal of the body and its transfer to the competent Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses) for a judicial autopsy before authorizing release of the body and registration in the Civil Registry [1][2].
  • Regional Mortuary Health Regulations timeframes: Under Spanish health regulations and regional mortuary health rules (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria), burial, cremation, or final sealing of the coffin generally cannot take place until 24 hours have elapsed since the death, and final disposition or preservation/embalming procedures must normally be carried out within 48 hours [2][3].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, appointing funeral directors in Spain and Morocco, and consular assistance
steps.html:
Before hiring funeral services independently, check whether the deceased held a Spanish funeral policy (póliza de decesos) or Moroccan bank repatriation insurance (such as assistance contracts subscribed through Moroccan or Spanish banks), as the insurer appoints and covers the funeral providers in both countries directly [2][4].

  • Funeral coordination in Spain and Morocco: If no insurer is involved, the family may appoint a licensed funeral company in Spain (empresa funeraria habilitada) through the directory of the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) (National Association of Funeral Services) to manage the mortuary, sanitary preparation, and civil registry formalities [5]. In the case of repatriation to Morocco, the Spanish provider coordinates with an authorized funeral and international mortuary transport company in Morocco (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc), which handles reception at the Moroccan airport or port (for example, in Casablanca, Tangier, Nador, or Marrakesh) and transfer to the municipality (commune) of burial [4]. Clarvia provides these institutional references solely for informational and guidance purposes and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific operators.
  • Moroccan consular assistance in Spain: Notify the competent Consulate General of the Kingdom of Morocco according to the consular district in Spain (Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Algeciras, Almería, Bilbao, Valencia, Palma de Mallorca, Tarragona, Girona, Murcia, or Las Palmas) through the official consular portal Consulat.ma [6][7]. The consulate registers the death in the Moroccan civil registry, processes the authorization to transport the body to Morocco, and - for Moroccan residents abroad in documented situations of indigence or vulnerability without insurance coverage - assesses eligibility for the state support program for the repatriation of mortal remains managed by the Ministry in charge of Moroccans Residing Abroad (Ministère délégué chargé des Marocains Résidant à l'Étranger) [4][6].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Spain and document validity in Morocco
steps.html:
Registration in the Spanish Civil Registry is mandatory to obtain the burial or transport permit and the official certificates required by Moroccan authorities [1].

  • Civil Registry in Spain (24-hour timeframe): The death declaration is usually submitted through the funeral company to the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred (under the Ministerio de Justicia, the Spanish Ministry of Justice) within 24 hours of the death [1]. Once registered, the registry issues the burial permit (licencia de enterramiento) and the Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción, as well as the multilingual CIEC Form C certificate under the 1976 Vienna Convention when required in European signatory states) [1].
  • Hague Apostille and transcription into the Moroccan Civil Registry: Both Spain and Morocco are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, meaning the Spanish Full Literal Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) must bear the Hague Apostille (Apostilla de La Haya) issued by the justice authorities in Spain to have full legal effect in Morocco [1]. With the Spanish Full Literal Death Certificate, the deceased's Moroccan National Electronic Identity Card (Carte Nationale d'Identité Électronique - CNIE) or passport, and the family book (livret de famille), family members must complete the consular declaration or transcription of the death before the Consulate of the Kingdom of Morocco in Spain (or at the municipal civil status office in Morocco, Bureau de l'état civil de la commune, following the procedures on the Portail national de l'État civil at alhalalmadania.ma and Consulat.ma) [6][7][8].

steps.title: International repatriation to Morocco vs. local burial or cremation in Spain
steps.html:
The family must decide between repatriating the remains to the Kingdom of Morocco or carrying out local burial in Spain [2][3].

  • Repatriation of the body from Spain to Morocco: The Spanish funeral company applies to the Foreign Health department (Sanidad Exterior) of the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health, via the SISAEX system) for the international mortuary transport health authorization (autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional de cadáveres) and the mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio, in accordance with mortuary health rules and international agreements such as the Strasbourg or Berlin Agreement, as well as any applicable formalities with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, MAEC) [2][3]. To authorize entry and burial in Morocco, the Moroccan consulate in Spain (in coordination with provincial or prefectoral authorities and the Moroccan Ministry of Health) issues the consular mortuary laissez-passer (laissez-passer mortuaire) and body transfer authorization (autorisation de transfert de corps) upon presentation of the Full Literal Death Certificate, the deceased's Moroccan identity document, a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious diseases, an embalming or preservation certificate, and a certificate of placement in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc inner liner (requirements also supervised in Morocco by the municipal hygiene offices, Bureaux Municipaux d'Hygiène - BMH, for transfers or exhumations) [3][4][6].
  • Local burial in Spain (including Islamic cemetery sections) or transport of ashes: If the family chooses burial in Spain, the funeral company arranges interment at the relevant municipal cemetery (or in authorized Islamic cemeteries and cemetery sections available in various Spanish municipalities in accordance with regional mortuary health regulations) using the Civil Registry permit [1][2]. Where cremation in Spain and transport of a funerary urn is chosen, an apostilled Full Literal Death Certificate and the official cremation certificate are required [1][3].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, death grants, taxes, and probate in Morocco and Spain
steps.html:
Once the death is registered in both countries, family members or beneficiaries can initiate social security, banking, and inheritance procedures:

  • Social Security (CNSS or CMR), banks, and succession in Morocco: If the deceased contributed to or received a private-sector pension in Morocco, eligible survivors may apply to the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) (National Social Security Fund) for the death grant (allocation au décès) and the survivor pension (pension de survivants) for a surviving spouse and orphans; if the deceased belonged to the Moroccan public sector, claims are filed with the Moroccan Pension Fund (Caisse Marocaine des Retraites - CMR) [9][10]. To unfreeze bank accounts and distribute assets in Morocco, heirs must execute an Islamic deed of heirship (iratha) and estate settlement before certified notary-witnesses (adoul homologated by the family notary judge) or a Moroccan notary, submitting the transcribed or apostilled death certificate [6][8].
  • INSS benefits and probate in Spain: If the deceased worked or received a pension in Spain, beneficiaries may apply for the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and widowhood, orphan, or family member pensions (pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares) from the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) (National Institute of Social Security), totalizing contribution periods in both countries where applicable under the bilateral Social Security Agreement between Spain and Morocco [11][12]. For assets located in Spain, once 15 business days have passed since the death, heirs apply to the Ministerio de Justicia (using Modelo 790) for the Certificate of Last Will (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Life Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento) [13]. With these certificates, heirs go to a notary public of the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of Notaries) to obtain a copy of the will or process an intestate declaration of heirs (acta de declaración de herederos abintestato) and inheritance deed [14]. Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within 6 months of the death (extendable by another 6 months if requested within the first 5 months) [13][14].

closingQuestion: To help tailor the next steps to your situation: 1. In which municipality in Spain did the death occur, and to which city or province in Morocco do you wish to transport the body (or do you prefer local burial in Spain)? 2. Did your family member have active bank repatriation coverage or funeral insurance, and did they leave assets or social security contributions in Spain, in Morocco, or in both countries?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre España y Marruecos: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre España y Marruecos: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho el fallecimiento de su familiar en España. A continuación le detallamos en orden los cinco pasos oficiales para gestionar la certificación médica y registral en España, la coordinación funeraria y consular con el Reino de Marruecos, el traslado internacional o la sepultura local, y los trámites posteriores de seguridad social y sucesiones en ambos países.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción y autorización forense o judicial en España
steps.html:
Toda gestión registral y sanitaria en España se inicia con el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial del Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos, indispensable para inscribir el fallecimiento y obtener la licencia de enterramiento o traslado [1][2].

  • Fallecimiento en hospital o centro sanitario: Cuando el deceso ocurre por causas naturales bajo atención médica (por ejemplo, en hospitales públicos o privados de Madrid, Cataluña o Andalucía), el facultativo tratante expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción, habilitando a la empresa funeraria para trasladar el cuerpo al tanatorio [1][2].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Debe llamarse de inmediato al teléfono único de emergencias 112. Si el médico de urgencias constata una muerte natural documentada, puede firmar el certificado; si el fallecimiento es súbito, violento o sin causa clínica establecida, intervienen las fuerzas policiales y el Juzgado de Guardia, que ordena el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses correspondiente para practicar la autopsia judicial antes de autorizar la entrega del cuerpo y la inscripción en el Registro Civil [1][2].
  • Plazos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria: Conforme a la normativa sanitaria española y los reglamentos autonómicos de sanidad mortuoria, con carácter general no puede practicarse la inhumación, cremación ni el cierre definitivo del féretro antes de transcurridas 24 horas desde el fallecimiento, y el destino final o las prácticas de conservación o embalsamamiento deben realizarse habitualmente dentro de las 48 horas [2][3].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriación, designación de funeraria en España y Marruecos, y asistencia consular
steps.html:
Antes de contratar servicios funerarios por cuenta propia, verifique si la persona fallecida contaba con una póliza de decesos o un seguro bancario de repatriación (como los contratos de asistencia suscritos a través de entidades bancarias marroquíes o españolas), ya que la aseguradora designa y cubre directamente a las empresas funerarias en ambos países [2][4].

  • Coordinación funeraria en España y Marruecos: Si no interviene una aseguradora, la familia puede designar una empresa funeraria habilitada en España a través del directorio de la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF) para que gestione el tanatorio, el acondicionamiento sanitario y los trámites registrales [5]. En caso de repatriación a Marruecos, dicha empresa se coordina con una empresa de pompas fúnebres y transporte funerario internacional autorizada en Marruecos (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc), que se encarga de la recepción en el aeropuerto o puerto marroquí (por ejemplo, en Casablanca, Tánger, Nador o Marrakech) y del traslado hasta la comuna de inhumación [4]. Clarvia proporciona estas referencias institucionales únicamente con fines informativos y de orientación, y no recomienda, respalda ni clasifica a operadores concretos.
  • Asistencia consular de Marruecos en España: Debe notificarse el deceso al Consulado General del Reino de Marruecos competente según la demarcación en España (Madrid, Barcelona, Sevilla, Algeciras, Almería, Bilbao, Valencia, Palma de Mallorca, Tarragona, Girona, Murcia o Las Palmas) a través del portal consular oficial Consulat.ma [6][7]. El consulado inscribe la defunción en el estado civil marroquí, tramita la autorización de traslado del cuerpo hacia Marruecos y, cuando se trata de residentes marroquíes en el extranjero en situación acreditada de indigencia o vulnerabilidad sin cobertura de seguro, evalúa el programa estatal de apoyo a la repatriación de restos mortales gestionado por el Ministerio encargado de los Marroquíes Residentes en el Extranjero [4][6].

steps.title: Inscripción de la defunción en el Registro Civil en España y validez documental en Marruecos
steps.html:
La inscripción en el Registro Civil español es obligatoria para obtener la licencia de sepultura o traslado y las certificaciones oficiales necesarias para las autoridades marroquíes [1].

  • Registro Civil en España (plazo de 24 horas): La declaración del fallecimiento se presenta habitualmente por medio de la empresa funeraria ante el Registro Civil del municipio donde ocurrió el deceso (dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia) dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al fallecimiento [1]. Practicada la inscripción, se expide la licencia de enterramiento y el Certificado Literal de Defunción (además del certificado plurilingüe Fórmula C del Convenio de Viena de 1976 cuando se requiera en Estados europeos parte) [1].
  • Apostilla de La Haya y transcripción en el Estado Civil marroquí: Tanto España como Marruecos son Estados parte del Convenio de La Haya de 1961, por lo que el Certificado Literal de Defunción español debe contar con la Apostilla de La Haya expedida por las autoridades de justicia en España para surtir plenos efectos en Marruecos [1]. Con el Certificado Literal de Defunción español, la Carte Nationale d'Identité Électronique (CNIE) o pasaporte marroquí y el libro de familia de la persona fallecida, los familiares deben realizar la declaración o transcripción consular del fallecimiento ante el Consulado del Reino de Marruecos en España (o ante la oficina del estado civil de la comuna en Marruecos, Bureau de l'état civil de la commune, conforme a los procedimientos del Portail national de l'État civil en alhalalmadania.ma y consulat.ma) [6][7][8].

steps.title: Repatriación internacional a Marruecos frente a inhumación o cremación local en España
steps.html:
La familia debe decidir entre repatriar los restos al Reino de Marruecos o realizar la sepultura en España [2][3].

  • Repatriación del cuerpo desde España hacia Marruecos: La empresa funeraria española tramita ante el área de Sanidad Exterior del Ministerio de Sanidad (mediante el sistema SISAEX) la autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional de cadáveres y el salvoconducto mortuorio (conforme a las normas de policía sanitaria mortuoria y acuerdos internacionales como el Acuerdo de Estrasburgo / Berlín, así como las gestiones pertinentes ante el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores (MAEC) cuando procedan) [2][3]. Para autorizar la entrada e inhumación en Marruecos, el consulado marroquí en España (en coordinación con las autoridades provinciales o prefectorales y el Ministerio de Salud marroquí) expide el salvoconducto mortuario consular (laissez-passer mortuaire) y la autorización de transferencia de cuerpo, previa presentación del Certificado Literal de Defunción, documento de identidad marroquí del difunto, certificado médico de ausencia de enfermedades infectocontagiosas, certificado de embalsamamiento o conservación y acta de acondicionamiento en féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada (requisitos que en Marruecos también supervisan las oficinas municipales de higiene, BMH, para traslados o exhumaciones) [3][4][6].
  • Inhumación local en España (incluidos recintos islámicos) o traslado de cenizas: Si la familia opta por el enterramiento en España, la empresa funeraria gestiona la inhumación en el cementerio municipal correspondiente (o en los cementerios y parcelas islámicas habilitadas en diversos municipios españoles conforme a la normativa autonómica de sanidad mortuoria) con la licencia del Registro Civil [1][2]. En caso de que se optase por la cremación en España y el traslado de la urna funeraria, esta requiere el Certificado Literal de Defunción apostillado y el certificado oficial de cremación [1][3].

steps.title: Prestaciones de supervivencia, subsidios por defunción, impuestos y sucesión en Marruecos y España
steps.html:
Una vez inscrito el fallecimiento en ambos países, los familiares o derechohabientes pueden iniciar los trámites de seguridad social, banca y herencia:

  • Seguridad Social (CNSS o CMR), bancos y sucesión en Marruecos: Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o era pensionista del sector privado en Marruecos, los derechohabientes pueden solicitar ante la Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) el subsidio por fallecimiento (allocation au décès) y la pensión de supervivencia (pension de survivants) para cónyuge y huérfanos; si pertenecía al sector público marroquí, la gestión se realiza ante la Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR) [9][10]. Para el desbloqueo de cuentas bancarias y la adjudicación de bienes en Marruecos, los herederos deben tramitar el acta de herederos (iratha) y la liquidación de la sucesión ante adules (adoul homologados por el juez de familia notarial) o ante un notario marroquí, aportando el certificado de defunción transcrito o apostillado [6][8].
  • Prestaciones del INSS y herencia en España: Si la persona fallecida trabajaba o percibía pensión en España, los beneficiarios pueden solicitar el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS), pudiendo totalizar períodos cotizados en ambos países al amparo del Convenio bilateral de Seguridad Social entre España y Marruecos [11][12]. Para los bienes situados en España, transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la defunción se solicita al Ministerio de Justicia (mediante el Modelo 790) el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [13]. Con dichos certificados se acude a una notaría del Consejo General del Notariado para obtener copia del testamento o tramitar la declaración de herederos y la escritura de herencia [14]. El Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones en España debe presentarse dentro del plazo de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (prorrogable por otros 6 meses si se solicita dentro de los primeros 5 meses) [13][14].

es.closingQuestion: Para orientar mejor los pasos según su situación: 1. ¿En qué municipio de España ocurrió el fallecimiento y a qué ciudad o provincia de Marruecos desean trasladar el cuerpo (o prefieren la inhumación en España)? 2. ¿Contaba su familiar con un seguro bancario o póliza de repatriación activa, y dejó bienes o cotizaciones a la seguridad social en España, en Marruecos o en ambos países?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in Morocco: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in Morocco: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Spain dies in Morocco: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Morocco, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Spain and Morocco.
introHtml:
Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person holding Spanish nationality or habitual residence in Spain dies in Morocco, the required procedures are coordinated between the local Moroccan authorities (attending physician, Municipal Hygiene Office, municipal civil registry, and prefecture or province) and the Spanish institutions (Spanish consulate in Morocco, External Health services, civil registry, and social security and tax bodies) [1][2].

Below are the five main official steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and legal clearance in Morocco
steps.html:
The first step is to obtain the medical certificate of death (certificat médical de constatation de décès) in Morocco to allow civil registration and funeral arrangements [3][4]:

  • Death in a healthcare facility (clinic or hospital): The attending physician or head of department directly issues the medical certificate of death confirming that the death resulted from natural causes and is free of any contagious disease that would prevent transport or burial [3][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: You should immediately alert emergency medical services (SAMU at 141) as well as the Police (19 in urban areas) or the Royal Gendarmerie (Gendarmerie Royale, 177 outside urban areas). A physician from the local Municipal Hygiene Office (Bureau municipal d'hygiène - BMH) of the municipality or district (for example, the BMH in Casablanca, Rabat, or Marrakesh) performs the forensic medical examination on site to issue the medical death certificate [3].
  • Forensic hold (sudden, suspicious, or unnatural death): If the circumstances of death are undetermined or accidental, the judicial police notify the King's Prosecutor (procureur du Roi) at the competent court. The body is transferred to the morgue or forensic institute, and no coffining, burial, or departure from Moroccan territory may take place until the King's Prosecutor issues formal authorization [3].

steps.title: Insurance, appointing a funeral director, and Spanish consular assistance
steps.html:
Before incurring personal expenses, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, repatriation insurance, or a Spanish funeral insurance policy (seguro de decesos) [1][2]:

  • Coordination by the insurer or funeral directors: If an insurance policy covers death abroad, contact its assistance helpline as soon as the medical certificate is issued; the insurer appoints the funeral providers directly and handles the technical formalities. Where no insurance applies, the family appoints an authorized international funeral and mortuary transport company in Morocco (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc), working in coordination with a licensed funeral provider (empresa funeraria habilitada) in Spain for airport reception and final burial or cremation [1][5]. You can identify a licensed funeral operator in Spain through the professional directory of the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (National Association of Funeral Services - PANASEF, telephone: +34 91 576 31 55, email: info@panasef.com) [5]. These examples from public sources are provided for general guidance only; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank any provider.
  • Contacting the Spanish Consulate in Morocco: Promptly notify the territorially competent Spanish consular post in Morocco according to the place of death, operating under the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation - MAEC), such as the Consulado General de España en Rabat (Consulate General of Spain in Rabat, email: cog.rabat@maec.es, civil registry: cog.rabat.reg@maec.es) or the Consulate General of Spain in Casablanca (cog.casablanca@maec.es) [1][2]. Eligibility for consular protection depends on the deceased holding Spanish nationality: the consulate guides the family, registers the death in the consular civil registry, and issues the mortuary laissez-passer, although the Spanish government does not pay funeral or repatriation expenses [1][2].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Morocco, apostille, and registration in the Spanish Registro Civil
steps.html:
The death must first be registered with the local Moroccan civil registry and then transcribed into the Spanish civil registry to have full legal effect in Spain [1][3]:

  • Municipal registration in Morocco: The death declaration is filed with the civil registry office (Bureau de l'état civil) of the municipality where the death occurred in Morocco (documented via the Portail national de l'État civil at alhalalmadania.ma and the consular portal Consulat.ma), usually by a relative or the authorized funeral director presenting the medical death certificate and the deceased's identity documents [3][4]. The municipal office issues full copies (copies intégrales) and extracts of the Moroccan death record.
  • Hague Apostille and translation: Because both Morocco and Spain are parties to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, the local Moroccan death certificate must bear the Apostille issued by the competent Moroccan authorities (court of first instance or prefectural/provincial authority) and be accompanied by a sworn translation into Spanish if written in Arabic or French [1][2].
  • Transcription into the Spanish Registro Civil: Presenting the apostilled Moroccan death certificate, the medical certificate of death, and the deceased's Spanish passport or national identity card (DNI), you apply for free registration of the death with the Spanish consular civil registry (Registro Civil consulaire) in Morocco (or directly with the municipal civil registry of the deceased's domicile in Spain under the Ministerio de Justicia, Ministry of Justice) [1][2][6]. Once the death is entered in the Spanish registry (note that for a death occurring on Spanish soil, registration with the municipal Registro Civil takes place within 24 hours), the Ministerio de Justicia issues the Certificado Literal de Defunción (full literal death certificate) as well as, upon request, the multilingual extract (Certificado Plurilingüe Fórmula C) under the 1976 Vienna Convention [6][7].

steps.title: Repatriation of the body or ashes to Spain versus local burial or cremation in Morocco
steps.html:
The family chooses between international transfer to Spain and local funeral arrangements in Morocco, with the coordinated funeral director handling the technical permits with health and prefectural authorities [1][8]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Spain: International transfer of a body from Morocco requires: 1) a body transfer authorization (autorisation de transfert de corps) issued by the prefectural or provincial authorities at the place of death in Morocco and the Moroccan Ministry of Health services; 2) embalming/preservation care (thanatopraxie) and placement in a hermetically sealed coffin containing a soldered zinc liner, carried out under the supervision of the Municipal Hygiene Office (BMH) and the police, who affix official seals; 3) the consular mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio) issued by the Spanish consulate in Morocco in accordance with international agreements (Berlin and Strasbourg Agreements) after verifying the medical and sanitary certificates; and 4) border health inspection upon entry into Spanish territory by External Health (Sanidad Exterior) under the Ministerio de Sanidad (Ministry of Health) before transport to the municipality of burial or cremation in Spain [1][2][8].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes to Spain: If cremation is arranged beforehand, the sealed cinerary urn may be transported to Spain accompanied by the cremation certificate, the transcribed or apostilled death certificate, and the consular and sanitary authorization for transporting ashes [1][8].
  • Local burial or cremation in Morocco: If the family opts for a local funeral in Morocco, the burial permit (permis d'inhumer) is issued by the municipal authorities and the local BMH upon presentation of the medical certificate of death, without requiring a hermetically sealed zinc coffin for local burial [3][4].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, tax filings, and estate administration in Spain and Morocco
steps.html:
Once the Spanish death certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) and the Moroccan death certificate have been obtained, eligible family members can initiate social security, banking, notarial, and tax procedures in both countries:

  • Social Security benefits in Spain (INSS): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension from the Spanish system, eligible survivors may apply to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (National Institute of Social Security - INSS, information line: +34 91 541 25 30, via the Sede Electrónica or CAISS service centers) for the funeral grant (auxilio por defunción, subject to a 5-year limitation period) as well as survivor pensions (pensión de viudedad for the surviving spouse or registered partner and pensión de orfandad for children) [9][10].
  • Will search, notary, and inheritance tax in Spain: After a statutory waiting period of 15 working days from the date of death, request the certificate from the General Registry of Last Wills (Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad, using official form Modelo 790) from the Ministerio de Justicia to verify whether a will was executed in Spain and identify the officiating notary, together with the certificate of life/death insurance contracts [11][12]. Declaration and acceptance of the inheritance are then completed before a Spanish notary's office (notaría), which can be located through the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of Notaries) [13]. For tax purposes, Inheritance and Gift Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within 6 months of the date of death (extendable by an additional 6 months if the extension request is submitted within the first 5 months) with the tax authority of the competent autonomous community or, where the deceased or heirs are non-residents, with the Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency) [14].
  • Social security benefits, banks, and probate in Morocco: If the deceased was insured or received a pension in Morocco, eligible survivors can apply for the death grant (allocation au décès) and survivor's pension (pension de survivants) from the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (National Social Security Fund - CNSS, Allo Damane call center: +212 5 22 48 89 19 or 080 203 33 33) for the private sector, or from the Moroccan Pension Fund (Caisse Marocaine des Retraites - CMR) for the public sector [15][16]. You should also notify Moroccan banks where the deceased held accounts and settle the succession of assets located in Morocco before a Moroccan notary or adouls in accordance with applicable jurisdiction rules.

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre Maroc et Espagne : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre Maroc et Espagne : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml:
Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne ayant la nationalité espagnole ou sa résidence habituelle en Espagne décède au Maroc, les démarches s'organisent entre les autorités locales marocaines (médecin, Bureau municipal d'hygiène, état civil communal et préfecture ou province) et les institutions espagnoles (consulat d'Espagne au Maroc, Sanidad Exterior, état civil et organismes sociaux et fiscaux) [1][2].

Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles dans l'ordre chronologique.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et autorisations légales au Maroc
steps.html:
La première démarche consiste à obtenir le certificat médical de constatation de décès au Maroc afin de permettre l'enregistrement civil et les opérations funéraires [3][4] :

  • Décès en établissement de santé (clinique ou hôpital) : Le médecin traitant ou le chef de service établit directement le certificat médical de constatation du décès précisant que la mort est naturelle et exempte de maladie contagieuse faisant obstacle au transport ou à l'inhumation [3][4].
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Il convient d'alerter immédiatement les secours médicaux (SAMU au 141) ainsi que la Police (19 en zone urbaine) ou la Gendarmerie Royale (177 hors zone urbaine). Le médecin du Bureau municipal d'hygiène (BMH) de la commune ou de l'arrondissement (par exemple le BMH de Casablanca, de Rabat ou de Marrakech) procède au constat médico-légal à domicile ou sur place pour délivrer le certificat médical de décès [3].
  • Obstacle médico-légal (mort soudaine, suspecte ou non naturelle) : Si les circonstances du décès sont indéterminées ou accidentelles, la police judiciaire informe le procureur du Roi près le tribunal compétent. Le corps est transféré à la morgue ou à l'institut médico-légal, et aucune mise en bière, inhumation ni sortie du territoire marocain ne peut avoir lieu avant la délivrance de l'autorisation du procureur du Roi [3].

steps.title: Assurance, choix de l'opérateur funéraire et assistance consulaire d'Espagne
steps.html:
Avant d'engager des frais à titre personnel, vérifiez si la personne décédée disposait d'une assurance voyage, d'une assurance rapatriement ou d'une police espagnole d'assurance obsèques (seguro de decesos) [1][2] :

  • Coordination par l'assureur ou les pompes funèbres : Si un contrat d'assurance couvre le décès à l'étranger, contactez son plateau d'assistance dès le constat médical ; l'assureur mandate directement les opérateurs funéraires et prend en charge les formalités techniques. En l'absence d'assurance, la famille mandate une société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc, qui travaille en coordination avec une entreprise funéraire habilitée (empresa funeraria habilitada) en Espagne pour la réception à l'aéroport et l'inhumation ou la crémation finale [1][5]. Vous pouvez identifier un opérateur funéraire en Espagne via l'annuaire professionnel de l'Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF, téléphone : +34 91 576 31 55, courriel : info@panasef.com) [5]. Ces exemples issus de sources publiques sont mentionnés à titre d'orientation ; Clarvia n'approuve, ne cautionne ni ne classe aucun prestataire.
  • Saisine du consulat d'Espagne au Maroc : Informez rapidement la représentation consulaire espagnole territorialement compétente au Maroc selon le lieu du décès, relevant du Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (MAEC), telle que le Consulado General de España en Rabat (courriel : cog.rabat@maec.es, état civil : cog.rabat.reg@maec.es) ou le Consulat général d'Espagne à Casablanca (cog.casablanca@maec.es) [1][2]. L'éligibilité à la protection consulaire dépend de la nationalité espagnole de la personne décédée : le consulat oriente la famille, enregistre le décès au registre civil consulaire et délivre le laissez-passer mortuaire, mais l'administration espagnole ne prend pas en charge les frais funéraires ni les coûts de rapatriement [1][2].

steps.title: Déclaration d'état civil au Maroc, apostille et transcription au Registro Civil espagnol
steps.html:
Le décès doit d'abord être enregistré auprès de l'état civil local marocain, puis transcrit dans l'état civil espagnol pour produire ses pleins effets juridiques en Espagne [1][3] :

  • Enregistrement communal au Maroc : La déclaration de décès s'effectue auprès du Bureau de l'état civil de la commune du lieu de décès au Maroc (accessible et documenté via le Portail national de l'État civil alhalalmadania.ma et le portail consulaire Consulat.ma), généralement par l'intermédiaire d'un proche ou du mandataire funéraire muni du certificat médical de décès et des pièces d'identité de la personne décédée [3][4]. Le bureau communal délivre les copies intégrales et extraits de l'acte de décès marocain.
  • Apostille de La Haye et traduction : Le Maroc et l'Espagne étant tous deux parties à la Convention de La Haye de 1961, l'acte de décès local marocain doit être revêtu de l'Apostille délivrée par les autorités marocaines compétentes (tribunal de première instance ou autorité préfectorale/provinciale) et accompagné d'une traduction assermentée en espagnol s'il est rédigé en arabe ou en français [1][2].
  • Transcription dans le Registro Civil espagnol : Muni de l'acte marocain apostillé, du certificat médical de décès et du passeport ou DNI espagnol de la personne décédée, vous demandez la transcription gratuite du décès auprès du Registro Civil consulaire espagnol au Maroc (ou directement auprès du Registro Civil du domicile en Espagne relevant du Ministerio de Justicia) [1][2][6]. Une fois le décès inscrit au registre espagnol (notez que pour un décès survenu sur le sol espagnol, la déclaration au Registro Civil municipal se fait dans les 24 heures), le Ministerio de Justicia délivre le Certificado Literal de Defunción ainsi que, sur demande, le Certificado Plurilingüe Fórmula C régi par la Convention de Vienne de 1976 [6][7].

steps.title: Rapatriement du corps ou des cendres vers l'Espagne ou inhumation et crémation au Maroc
steps.html:
La famille choisit entre le transfert international vers l'Espagne et les obsèques locales au Maroc, l'opérateur funéraire coordonné se chargeant des démarches techniques auprès des autorités sanitaires et préfectorales [1][8] :

  • Rapatriement du corps vers l'Espagne : Le transfert international d'un corps depuis le Maroc requiert : 1) l'autorisation de transfert de corps délivrée par les autorités préfectorales ou provinciales du lieu de décès au Maroc et les services du ministère de la Santé marocain ; 2) les soins de conservation (thanatopraxie) et la mise en bière dans un cercueil hermétique comportant un caisson métallique en zinc scellé, effectuée sous le contrôle du Bureau municipal d'hygiène (BMH) et de la police qui apposent les scellés officiels ; 3) le laissez-passer mortuaire consulaire (salvoconducto mortuorio) délivré par le consulat d'Espagne au Maroc conformément aux règles internationales (Accords de Berlin et de Strasbourg) après vérification des certificats médicaux et sanitaires ; et 4) le contrôle sanitaire à l'entrée sur le territoire espagnol par les services de Sanidad Exterior relevant du Ministerio de Sanidad avant l'acheminement vers la commune d'inhumation ou de crémation en Espagne [1][2][8].
  • Rapatriement des cendres vers l'Espagne : Si la crémation est organisée au préalable, l'urne cinéraire scellée peut être transportée vers l'Espagne accompagnée du certificat de crémation, de l'acte de décès transcrit ou apostillé et de l'autorisation consulaire et sanitaire de transport de cendres [1][8].
  • Inhumation ou crémation locale au Maroc : Si la famille opte pour des obsèques sur place au Maroc, le permis d'inhumer est délivré par les autorités communales et le BMH du lieu de décès sur présentation du certificat médical de constatation du décès, sans qu'un cercueil hermétique en zinc soit requis pour une inhumation locale [3][4].

steps.title: Prestations de survie, formalités fiscales et règlement de la succession en Espagne et au Maroc
steps.html:
Une fois l'acte de décès espagnol (Certificado Literal de Defunción) et l'acte marocain obtenus, les ayants droit peuvent engager les démarches sociales, bancaires, notariales et fiscales dans les deux pays :

  • Prestations de la Sécurité sociale en Espagne (INSS) : Si la personne décédée cotisait ou percevait une retraite du système espagnol, les ayants droit peuvent solliciter auprès de l'Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS, téléphone d'information : +34 91 541 25 30, via la Sede Electrónica ou les centres CAISS) l'allocation pour frais funéraires (auxilio por defunción, prescrite après 5 ans) ainsi que les pensions de survie (pensión de viudedad pour le conjoint ou partenaire enregistré survivant et pensión de orfandad pour les enfants) [9][10].
  • Testament, notaire et fiscalité successorale en Espagne : Après un délai légal de 15 jours ouvrables à compter de la date du décès, demandez le certificat du Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (au moyen du formulaire officiel Modelo 790) auprès du Ministerio de Justicia afin de vérifier l'existence d'un testament en Espagne et d'identifier le notaire dépositaire, ainsi que le certificat des contrats d'assurance décès [11][12]. La déclaration et l'acceptation de la succession s'effectuent ensuite devant une étude notariale espagnole (notaría), identifiable via le Consejo General del Notariado [13]. Sur le plan fiscal, l'Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones doit être déclaré dans un délai de 6 mois à compter du décès (prorogeable de 6 mois supplémentaires si la demande de prorogation est déposée dans les 5 premiers mois) auprès de l'administration fiscale de la communauté autonome compétente ou, lorsque le défunt ou les héritiers sont non-résidents, auprès de l'Agencia Tributaria [14].
  • Prestations sociales, banques et succession au Maroc : Si la personne décédée était affiliée ou pensionnée au Maroc, les ayants droit peuvent demander l'allocation au décès et la pension de survivants auprès de la Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS, centre d'appel Allo Damane : +212 5 22 48 89 19 ou 080 203 33 33) pour le secteur privé, ou auprès de la Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR) pour le secteur public [15][16]. Il convient également de notifier le décès aux banques marocaines où la personne décédée détenait des comptes et de régler la dévolution successorale des biens situés au Maroc devant un notaire marocain ou des adouls conformément aux règles de compétence applicables.

fr.closingQuestion: Pour vous apporter des précisions adaptées à votre situation : 1. Dans quelle ville ou province du Maroc le décès est-il survenu, et dans quelle municipalité ou communauté autonome d'Espagne souhaitez-vous organiser le rapatriement ou régler la succession ? 2. La personne décédée possédait-elle la nationalité espagnole (ou une double nationalité hispano-marocaine) et bénéficiait-elle d'une assurance rapatriement ou obsèques ?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Morocco Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Morocco Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Morocco dies in Italy: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Italy, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Morocco and Italy.
introHtml:
Please accept our heartfelt condolences on the loss of your family member. When a person holding Moroccan citizenship or residence ties dies in Italy, the required procedures involve the Italian health and municipal authorities (local health authority medical examiner, Municipal Civil Registry Office, and Prefecture) alongside the consular and administrative network of the Kingdom of Morocco [1][2].

Below are the five main official steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death, necroscopic certificate, and judicial clearance in Italy
steps.html:
The first requirement is the medical verification of death in Italy in accordance with the Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria, Presidential Decree D.P.R. 285/1990), which is essential for civil registration and funeral transport [1][3]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The hospital medical management draws up the preliminary death verification (constatazione di decesso), the ISTAT cause-of-death statistical form (scheda ISTAT), and the internal necroscopic examination, transmitting the death notice directly to the Municipal Civil Registry Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) [3][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: You must immediately call the single emergency number 112 (or emergency medical services at 118) or the attending physician to issue the preliminary verification of death and the ISTAT form. Subsequently, the medical examiner (medico necroscopo) appointed by the territorially competent Local Health Authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) conducts the mandatory necroscopic examination between 15 and 30 hours after death to issue the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico) [3][4].
  • Sudden, violent, or suspicious death (Judicial Authority): If the death occurs in a public place, without medical attendance, or from unnatural causes, law enforcement and the duty prosecutor at the Public Prosecutor's Office (Procura della Repubblica) intervene. The body remains at the disposal of the Judicial Authority (Autorità Giudiziaria) for a diagnostic examination or forensic autopsy, and neither sealing the coffin nor burial or repatriation may take place until the Public Prosecutor's Office issues formal clearance (nulla osta alla sepoltura or transport clearance) [1][3].

steps.title: Insurance, appointing a funeral director, and Moroccan consular assistance
steps.html:
Before making direct financial commitments, check whether the deceased held a travel or repatriation insurance policy (often taken out through Moroccan banks or assistance companies) [2][5]:

  • Appointing a funeral director in Italy and Morocco: If repatriation insurance is active, contact the insurer's assistance center immediately so that it can appoint its contracted providers. Without insurance coverage, the family authorizes a licensed funeral company in Italy (impresa funebre autorizzata) to handle municipal, health, and airport formalities, working in coordination with an authorized international funeral and mortuary transport company in Morocco (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc) that will receive the coffin at the arrival airport [1][5]. You can locate a licensed operator in Italy through national trade associations such as the Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (National Federation of Funeral Enterprises - FENIOF, telephone: +39 051 291 0710, email: info@feniof.it) or FederCoFIt (Federation of the Italian Funeral Sector, telephone: +39 051 417 2051, email: segreteria@federcofit.it) [5][6]. These references from public sources are provided for general guidance only; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank any provider.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate of Morocco in Italy: Promptly notify the Consulate General of the Kingdom of Morocco responsible for the Italian district where the death occurred (for example in Rome, Embassy telephone: +39 06 85508001, Consulate General in Rome: +39 06 45674180, or in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Verona, Naples, or Palermo), operating under the Ministère des Affaires Étrangères, de la Coopération Africaine et des Marocains Résidant à l'Étranger (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates) and the official portal Consulat.ma [2][7]. Eligibility for consular assistance depends on the deceased holding Moroccan citizenship: the consulate issues the mortuary laissez-passer (laissez-passer mortuaire, clearance for the body to enter Morocco), transcribes the death, and, in cases of proven financial hardship where the family has no insurance, can process an application for the competent Moroccan authorities to cover repatriation costs [2][7].

steps.title: Civil death registration in Italy, legalization, and transcription in Morocco
steps.html:
Registering the death record in Italy within the statutory deadline is the prerequisite for having the death recognized in Morocco as well [3][8]:

  • Death declaration at the Italian municipality (within 24 hours): The declaration of death (denuncia di morte) must be submitted within 24 hours of death to the Civil Registry Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian municipality where the death occurred (for example, the civil registry offices of the Comune di Milano or Roma Capitale), normally through the funeral company authorized by the family or the hospital administration [3][4]. The civil registrar records the death deed (atto di morte), issues the burial permit (permesso di seppellimento), and provides death certificates and extracts, including the multilingual death extract on Form C (estratto dell'atto di morte plurilingue su Modello C) under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 (to which both Italy and Morocco are contracting states, making it exempt from translation and legalization) [1][8].
  • Apostille and consular or municipal transcription in Morocco: If a full literal copy of the Italian death record (copia integrale dell'atto di morte) is required for specific procedures, it is affixed with a Hague Apostille at the competent Prefecture (Prefettura - Ufficio Territoriale del Governo) [8]. The death record is then transcribed into the Moroccan civil status registers at the Moroccan Consulate in Italy (by submitting the Italian death certificate, the medical death certificate, and the deceased's Moroccan National Electronic Identity Card - CNIE or passport for cancellation) or at the municipal civil registry office (Bureau de l'état civil) of the municipality of origin or residence in Morocco, whose procedures are detailed on the Portail national de l'État civil (alhalalmadania.ma) and Consulat.ma [2][7][9].

steps.title: Repatriation of the body or ashes to Morocco versus local burial or cremation in Italy
steps.html:
The family decides whether to transfer the body (or ashes) to Morocco or arrange burial in Italy; the appointed funeral company coordinates the technical permits between the municipality, the ASL, and the consulate [1][10]:

  • Repatriation of the body from Italy to Morocco: Because Morocco is not a party to the 1937 Berlin International Convention, issuance of the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) by the Italian municipality of death (in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale - MAECI, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, as illustrated in the service guides of the Comune di Milano) requires: 1) the death certificate extract and burial permit; 2) an ASL certificate confirming compliance with health and sanitary regulations (anti-putrefactive preservation treatment, absence of endemic infectious diseases, and enclosure in a double coffin with a hermetically soldered zinc liner pursuant to Articles 30 and 32 of D.P.R. 285/1990); and 3) clearance for entry of the remains (nulla osta all'introduzione della salma / autorisation de transfert de corps / laissez-passer mortuaire) issued by the Consulate of Morocco in Italy after verifying the airport of entry, the municipality of burial in Morocco, and authorization from the Moroccan prefectural/provincial authorities and Ministry of Health [1][2][10][11]. Upon arrival in Morocco, the coffin is received by the local funeral operator under the supervision of border health services and the Municipal Hygiene Office (Bureau municipal d'hygiène - BMH).
  • Transport of ashes or local burial in Italy: In the case of cremation (which requires a testamentary provision by the deceased or a declaration by the surviving spouse or closest relatives before the civil registrar), the municipality issues a mortuary passport for transporting the sealed cinerary urn accompanied by the cremation record (verbale di cremazione) [10][11]. If local burial in Italy is chosen instead (including burial in Islamic cemetery sections available in many Italian municipalities), the funeral company coordinates directly with municipal cemetery services using the burial permit [3][4].

steps.title: Survivor benefits, tax filings, and estate administration in Morocco and Italy
steps.html:
With the Italian and Moroccan death certificates in hand, eligible family members can initiate pension, banking, tax, and succession procedures in both countries:

  • Social security, banks, and probate in Morocco: If the deceased was insured or received a private-sector pension in Morocco, eligible survivors may claim the funeral grant (allocation au décès) and survivor's pension (pension de survivants) from the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (National Social Security Fund - CNSS, contact center: +212 5 22 48 89 19), enclosing the death certificate and the deed of heirship (acte d'hérédité / Adad) [12][13]; for Moroccan public-sector employees, claims are submitted to the Moroccan Pension Fund (Caisse Marocaine des Retraites - CMR). You must also notify Moroccan banks of the death and formalize the inheritance of assets located in Morocco before adouls (traditional notaries for Moroccan family and succession law) or a Moroccan notary.
  • Survivor's pension in Italy (INPS): If the deceased worked or received a pension in Italy, the surviving spouse and eligible family members can submit an online claim for a survivor's pension (pensione ai superstiti, either pensione di reversibilità or pensione indiretta) and accrued unpaid pension installments to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (National Social Security Institute - INPS, contact center: 803 164 from Italian landlines or +39 06 164 164 from mobile phones and abroad), either directly using SPID/CIE credentials or through an accredited patronato assistance office [14].
  • Inheritance tax return and will search in Italy: If the deceased resided in Italy or owned real estate or financial assets in Italy, the heirs must file an inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Revenue Agency) within 12 months of the date of death (via the Successioni OnLine electronic service or an authorized intermediary) [15]. To check whether a will exists in Italy through the General Registry of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti), publish a will, or execute a sworn deed of heirship (atto di notorietà) to release Italian bank accounts, you can consult an Italian notary through the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato (National Council of Notaries) [16].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more targeted guidance, in which Italian municipality did the death occur, in which city or province of Morocco do you plan to arrange repatriation or succession formalities, and did the deceased hold solely Moroccan citizenship (or dual Italian-Moroccan citizenship) and have repatriation insurance coverage?

it.title: Cosa fare in caso di decesso tra Italia e Marocco: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso tra Italia e Marocco: certificato medico di morte, impresa funebre autorizzata, registrazione allo Stato Civile, pratiche consolari e rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri, e pensione di reversibilità e successione.
it.introHtml:
Vi porgiamo le nostre più sentite condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona con cittadinanza o legami di residenza in Marocco decede in Italia, la procedura coinvolge le autorità sanitarie e comunali italiane (medico necroscopo della ASL, Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune e Prefettura) e la rete consolare e amministrativa del Regno del Marocco [1][2].

Di seguito sono illustrati in ordine i cinque passaggi ufficiali principali.

steps.title: Constatazione medica del decesso, certificato necroscopico e nulla osta in Italia
steps.html:
Il primo adempimento consiste nell'accertamento medico della morte in Italia secondo il Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria (D.P.R. 285/1990), indispensabile per la denuncia di stato civile e per il trasporto funebre [1][3]:

  • Decesso in ospedale o struttura sanitaria: La direzione sanitaria dell'ospedale redige la constatazione di decesso, la scheda ISTAT sulle cause di morte e l'accertamento necroscopico interno, trasmettendo direttamente l'avviso di morte all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune [3][4].
  • Decesso a domicilio, in hotel o in luogo pubblico: Occorre chiamare immediatamente il numero unico di emergenza 112 (o il soccorso sanitario 118) o il medico curante per il certificato di constatazione del decesso e la scheda ISTAT. Successivamente, il medico necroscopo nominato dall'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) territorialmente competente effettua la visita necroscopica obbligatoria tra le 15 e le 30 ore dal decesso per rilasciare il certificato necroscopico [3][4].
  • Morte improvvisa, violenta o sospetta (Autorità Giudiziaria): Se il decesso avviene in luogo pubblico, senza assistenza medica o per cause non naturali, intervengono le forze dell'ordine e il magistrato di turno presso la Procura della Repubblica. La salma resta a disposizione dell'Autorità Giudiziaria (per l'eventuale riscontro diagnostico o autopsia medico-legale) e né la chiusura del feretro né la sepoltura o il rimpatrio possono avvenire prima del rilascio del formale nulla osta alla sepoltura (o al trasporto) della Procura della Repubblica [1][3].

steps.title: Assicurazione, scelta dell'impresa funebre e assistenza consolare del Marocco
steps.html:
Prima di assumere impegni economici diretti, verificate se la persona deceduta disponeva di una polizza assicurativa di viaggio o di rimpatrio salma (spesso sottoscritta tramite banche marocchine o compagnie di assistenza) [2][5]:

  • Incarico all'impresa funebre in Italia e in Marocco: Se è attiva una copertura assicurativa per il rimpatrio, contattate subito la centrale operativa dell'assicurazione affinché incarichi gli operatori convenzionati. In assenza di copertura, la famiglia conferisce mandato a un'impresa funebre autorizzata in Italia per curare il disbrigo delle pratiche comunali, sanitarie e aeroportuali, operando in coordinamento con una società di pompe funebri e di trasporto funebre internazionale abilitata in Marocco (société de pompes funèbres et de transport funéraire international agréée au Maroc) che prenderà in carico il feretro all'aeroporto di arrivo [1][5]. Potete individuare un operatore abilitato in Italia tramite le associazioni nazionali di categoria come la Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (FENIOF, telefono: +39 051 291 0710, email: info@feniof.it) o FederCoFIt (telefono: +39 051 417 2051, email: segreteria@federcofit.it) [5][6]. Questi riferimenti tratti da fonti pubbliche sono forniti a scopo puramente orientativo; Clarvia non approva, non raccomanda e non classifica alcun operatore.
  • Contatto con l'Ambasciata o il Consolato del Marocco in Italia: Informate tempestivamente il consolato generale del Regno del Marocco competente per la circoscrizione italiana del decesso (ad esempio a Roma, telefono dell'Ambasciata: +39 06 85508001, Consolato Generale a Roma: +39 06 45674180, oppure a Milano, Torino, Bologna, Verona, Napoli o Palermo), facente capo al Ministère des Affaires Étrangères, de la Coopération Africaine et des Marocains Résidant à l'Étranger e al portale ufficiale Consulat.ma [2][7]. L'idoneità all'assistenza consolare dipende dalla cittadinanza marocchina della persona deceduta: il consolato rilascia il laissez-passer mortuaire (nulla osta all'ingresso della salma in Marocco), trascrive il decesso e, in caso di comprovata indigenza della famiglia priva di assicurazione, può istruire una richiesta di presa in carico delle spese di rimpatrio da parte delle autorità marocchine competenti [2][7].

steps.title: Registrazione dello stato civile in Italia, legalizzazione e trascrizione in Marocco
steps.html:
La formazione dell'atto di morte in Italia entro i termini di legge è il presupposto per il riconoscimento del decesso anche in Marocco [3][8]:

  • Denuncia di morte presso il Comune italiano (entro 24 ore): La dichiarazione di morte deve essere presentata entro 24 ore dal decesso all'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano in cui è avvenuta la morte (ad esempio presso gli uffici di stato civile del Comune di Milano o di Roma Capitale), di norma tramite l'impresa funebre delegata dalla famiglia o la direzione sanitaria ospedaliera [3][4]. L'ufficiale di stato civile registra l'atto di morte, rilascia il permesso di seppellimento e fornisce i certificati ed estratti di morte, incluso l'estratto dell'atto di morte plurilingue su Modello C ai sensi della Convenzione di Vienna dell'8 settembre 1976 (di cui sia l'Italia sia il Marocco sono Stati contraenti, esente da traduzione e legalizzazione) [1][8].
  • Apostille e trascrizione consolare o comunale in Marocco: Qualora per specifiche procedure venga richiesta la copia integrale dell'atto di morte italiano, questa viene munita di Apostille dell'Aia presso la Prefettura - Ufficio Territoriale del Governo competente [8]. L'atto di morte viene quindi trascritto nei registri di stato civile marocchini presso il consolato del Marocco in Italia (presentando l'atto di morte italiano, il certificato medico di morte e la Carte Nationale d'Identité Électronique - CNIE o il passaporto marocchino della persona deceduta per l'annullamento) oppure presso il Bureau de l'état civil del comune di origine o di residenza in Marocco, le cui procedure sono descritte sul Portail national de l'État civil (alhalalmadania.ma) e su Consulat.ma [2][7][9].

steps.title: Rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri verso il Marocco oppure sepoltura e cremazione in Italia
steps.html:
La famiglia decide se trasferire la salma (o le ceneri) in Marocco oppure procedere alla sepoltura in Italia; l'impresa funebre incaricata coordina le autorizzazioni tecniche tra Comune, ASL e Consolato [1][10]:

  • Rimpatrio della salma dall'Italia al Marocco: Poiché il Marocco non aderisce alla Convenzione Internazionale di Berlino del 1937, il rilascio del Passaporto Mortuario da parte del Comune italiano di decesso (secondo le direttive del Ministero dell'Interno e del Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale - MAECI, come illustrato ad esempio nelle schede del Comune di Milano) richiede: 1) l'estratto dell'atto di morte e il permesso di seppellimento; 2) il certificato dell'ASL attestante l'osservanza delle prescrizioni igienico-sanitarie (trattamento conservativo antiputrefattivo, assenza di malattie infettive endemiche e chiusura in doppia cassa con cofano metallico di zinco saldato ermeticamente ai sensi degli artt. 30 e 32 del D.P.R. 285/1990); e 3) il nulla osta all'introduzione della salma (autorisation de transfert de corps / laissez-passer mortuaire) rilasciato dal Consolato del Marocco in Italia previa verifica dell'aeroporto di ingresso, del comune di inumazione in Marocco e dell'autorizzazione delle autorità prefettizie/provinciali e del Ministero della Salute marocchino [1][2][10][11]. All'arrivo in Marocco, il feretro è preso in carico dall'operatore funebre locale sotto la vigilanza dei servizi sanitari di frontiera e del Bureau municipal d'hygiène (BMH).
  • Trasporto di ceneri o sepoltura locale in Italia: In caso di cremazione (che richiede una disposizione testamentaria della persona deceduta o la dichiarazione del coniuge o dei parenti più prossimi davanti all'ufficiale di stato civile), il Comune rilascia il passaporto mortuario per il trasporto dell'urna cineraria sigillata accompagnata dal verbale di cremazione [10][11]. Se invece si sceglie l'inumazione in Italia (inclusa l'eventuale sepoltura nei reparti cimiteriali islamici presenti in diversi comuni italiani), l'impresa funebre coordina direttamente i servizi cimiteriali comunali con il permesso di seppellimento [3][4].

steps.title: Prestazioni ai superstiti, adempimenti fiscali e successione in Marocco e in Italia
steps.html:
Con i certificati di morte italiani e marocchini, i familiari aventi diritto possono avviare le pratiche previdenziali, bancarie, fiscali e successorie nei due Paesi:

  • Previdenza, banche e successione in Marocco: Se la persona deceduta era assicurata o pensionata in Marocco nel settore privato, gli aventi diritto possono richiedere l'assegno funerario (allocation au décès) e la pensione ai superstiti (pension de survivants) presso la Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS, centro di contatto: +212 5 22 48 89 19), allegando l'atto di morte e l'atto di notorietà ereditaria (acte d'hérédité / Adad) [12][13]; per i dipendenti pubblici marocchini la domanda va rivolta alla Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR). Occorre inoltre notificare il decesso agli istituti bancari marocchini e formalizzare la devoluzione ereditaria dei beni situati in Marocco dinanzi agli adouls (notai tradizionali di diritto di famiglia e successorio marocchino) o a un notaio marocchino.
  • Pensione ai superstiti in Italia (INPS): Se la persona deceduta lavorava o percepiva una pensione in Italia, il coniuge e i familiari aventi diritto possono presentare domanda telematica di pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità o pensione indiretta) e di liquidazione dei ratei maturati e non riscossi all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, contact center: 803 164 da rete fissa in Italia o +39 06 164 164 da cellulare e dall'estero), direttamente con SPID/CIE o tramite un ente di patronato [14].
  • Dichiarazione di successione e verifica testamentaria in Italia: Se il defunto era residente in Italia o possedeva beni immobili o attività finanziarie in Italia, gli eredi devono presentare la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data del decesso (tramite il servizio telematico Successioni OnLine o un intermediario abilitato) [15]. Per verificare l'esistenza di un testamento in Italia tramite il Registro Generale dei Testamenti, pubblicare un testamento o redigere l'atto di notorietà per lo sblocco dei conti bancari italiani, è possibile rivolgersi a un notaio italiano tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato [16].

it.closingQuestion: Per fornirvi indicazioni ancora più mirate: 1. In quale Comune italiano è avvenuto il decesso e in quale città o provincia del Marocco intendete organizzare il rimpatrio o le pratiche ereditarie? 2. La persona deceduta possedeva esclusivamente la cittadinanza marocchina (o anche quella italiana) ed era coperta da un'assicurazione per il rimpatrio della salma?
