title: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Portugal Dies in Spain: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Portugal dies in Spain: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Spain, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Portugal and Spain.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Portuguese citizenship or residence ties in Portugal dies in Spain, the initial medical certification, the civil registration of the death, and the public health departure clearance are handled in the Spanish municipality where the death occurred, while the reception of the coffin or urn, the consular or civil registry transcription, and survivor benefits or succession formalities are coordinated between the authorities of Portugal and Spain [1][4][6]. Below are the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical certification of death and medico-legal clearance in Spain
steps.html:
Before registering the death, arranging funeral services, or initiating cross-border repatriation to Portugal, a licensed physician or the competent judicial authority must certify the death in Spain [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or care facility: The attending physician issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Certificado Médico de Defunción) of the General Council of Official Medical Associations (Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos, in paper or electronic format), which is required for registration at the Civil Registry [1][2]. Provide your family member's Portuguese identity card (Cartão de Cidadão or Bilhete de Identidade) or passport, as well as their Foreigner Identity Number (Número de Identidad de Extranjero - NIE) if they resided in Spain, so that personal details match Portuguese records exactly [1][4].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call the single emergency number 112 so emergency medical services can attend and verify the death [1][2]. If the death results from known natural causes and a physician has access to the medical history, they may issue the Certificado Médico de Defunción [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or judicial death and Institute of Legal Medicine: If the cause of death is sudden, accidental, violent, or cannot be certified as natural, the police and the duty court (Juzgado de Guardia) of the relevant judicial district intervene, ordering the removal of the body and its transfer to the Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses, for example in Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Vigo, or Badajoz) for a judicial autopsy [1][2]. No burial, cremation, or repatriation to Portugal may take place until the court issues the burial license or transfer authorization [1].
  • Regional mortuary health regulations (24 to 48 hours): Under the regional mortuary health regulations (Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria) of the Spanish autonomous communities, burial, cremation, or preservation/embalming procedures for international transfer normally take place between 24 and 48 hours after death (unless judicial intervention applies) [2][6].

steps.title: Repatriation insurance, appointing funeral directors in Spain and Portugal, and Portuguese consular contact
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international medical assistance, bank-card coverage, or a funeral or repatriation insurance policy [2][4]. If coverage exists, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance center first so that it directly appoints and coordinates the Spanish and Portuguese funeral providers.

  • Licensed funeral director in Spain: If no insurer is involved, the family may appoint a legally licensed funeral company (empresa funeraria habilitada) in the Spanish municipality of death, represented by the national funeral sector association Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (National Association of Funeral Services - PANASEF, telephone +34 91 576 31 55, email info@panasef.com) [2].
  • Receiving funeral agency in Portugal: For overland or air transport to Portugal (for example to Lisbon, Porto, Braga, Coimbra, or Faro), the Spanish funeral company coordinates with a legally licensed funeral agency in Portugal (agência funerária habilitada), supervised by the Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (Directorate-General for Economic Activities - DGAE, integrated into the official portal gov.pt) and represented in Portuguese sector associations such as the Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, telephone +351 218 687 978) or the Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro (AAFC) [3]. Clarvia provides references to public registries and professional associations solely for informational guidance and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific operators.
  • Portuguese consular assistance in Spain: Notify the Portuguese consular network in Spain according to territorial jurisdiction - the Consular Section of the Embajada de Portugal en Madrid (Embassy of Portugal in Madrid, Consular Service Center telephone in Spain: +34 91 789 05 00; email: sconsular.madrid@mne.pt), the Consulates General of Portugal in Barcelona and Seville, or the Vice-Consulate in Vigo - operating under the Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MNE, which also maintains the 24-hour Consular Emergency Office, Gabinete de Emergência Consular, at +351 217 929 714 and gec@mne.pt) [4]. Death registration and mortuary transfer documentation are urgent consular acts that do not require an ordinary prior online appointment [4].

steps.title: Registering the death with the Civil Registry in Spain (24 hours) and civil registry recognition in Portugal
steps.html:
A death occurring in Spain must first be registered with the Civil Registry of the Spanish municipality where the death took place before its transcription or recognition in Portugal [1][4][5]:

  • Municipal Civil Registry in Spain (24-hour timeframe): The declaration is normally submitted within 24 hours of death to the municipal Civil Registry (Registro Civil) under the Spanish Ministerio de Justicia (Ministry of Justice, citizen service telephone: +34 91 837 22 95) [1]. In practice, the Spanish funeral director submits the Certificado Médico de Defunción and the deceased person's identity documents to obtain the burial or cremation permit and request the official certificates [1][2].
  • Full Death Certificate and Multilingual Extract (CIEC Form C of the 1976 Vienna Convention): Request several copies of the Full Death Certificate (Certificado Literal de Defunción) and the Multilingual Death Certificate (Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción - Fórmula C) issued under ICCH/CIEC Convention No. 16 signed in Vienna on 8 September 1976 [1]. Because both Spain and Portugal are party to the 1976 Vienna Convention and also apply Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 on public documents, the multilingual Form C certificate is exempt from the Hague Apostille and sworn translation between the two countries [1][5].
  • Transcription and civil registration in Portugal (Conservatória do Registo Civil / Consulate): Whereas a death occurring inside Portugal must be declared within 48 hours before any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (Institute of Registries and Notary Services - IRN / Justiça.gov.pt, Linha Registos telephone: +351 211 950 500) to issue the free death record (Assento de Óbito) and, where needed, the Vienna Convention multilingual certificate (certidão plurilingue) [5], the death of a Portuguese citizen occurring in Spain must be registered in the Portuguese legal order by transcription at the Consulate of Portugal in Spain or at any Conservatória do Registo Civil in Portugal upon presentation of the Spanish death certificate (Form C or full extract) and the deceased person's Cartão de Cidadão [4][5].

steps.title: Choosing between international repatriation from Spain to Portugal and local burial or cremation in Spain
steps.html:
The funeral directors in Spain and Portugal jointly manage the public health and cross-border permits according to the option chosen by the family [2][4][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body in a coffin from Spain to Portugal: Both countries are signatories to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement and the 1937 Berlin International Convention on the international transport of corpses [6]. The Spanish funeral director performs the statutory preservation or embalming procedures, places the deceased person in a hermetically sealed coffin with a soldered zinc liner (féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada / caixão de zinco selado), and processes electronically through the SISAEX system of Sanidad Exterior (Foreign Health Inspection, under the Spanish Ministry of Health) the public health authorization for international transfer and the mortuary laissez-passer (salvoconducto mortuorio / livre-trânsito mortuário or alvará de trasladação), in coordination with the Portuguese consular authorities and in line with consular guidance from the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAEC) and the Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MNE) [4][6]. Given the geographic proximity on the Iberian Peninsula, transport between Spain and Portugal is frequently carried out overland in an approved hearse as well as by air [2][6].
  • Transport of cremated ashes to Portugal: If the family chooses cremation in Spain, the sealed cinerary urn may be transported to Portugal accompanied by the Multilingual Death Certificate (Form C) and the official cremation certificate issued by the Spanish crematorium [2][6].
  • Local burial or cremation in Spain: If the burial or cremation takes place entirely in the Spanish municipality where the death occurred, the burial or cremation license issued by the Spanish Civil Registry and compliance with regional sanitary timeframes are sufficient [1][2].

steps.title: Survivor pensions, funeral grants, tax filings, and estate administration in Portugal and Spain
steps.html:
With the Multilingual Death Certificate (Form C) and the Portuguese Assento de Óbito, family members or heirs can initiate social security, tax, and probate procedures in both states:

  • Procedures in Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças, and Stamp Duty):
    • Portuguese Social Security benefits: If your family member contributed to or received a pension in Portugal, apply to Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, telephone +351 210 545 400 or +351 300 502 502; or via Segurança Social Direta) for the lump-sum death grant (Subsídio por Morte, within 180 consecutive days from the date of death), the reimbursement of funeral expenses (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, within 90 days for the person who paid the funeral costs when no relatives qualify for the Subsídio por Morte), and the monthly survivor pension (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [7].
    • Declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and 3-month tax filing: The head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) can visit the one-stop service desks of Espaço Óbito or the Balcão das Heranças (Inheritance Desk) of the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado to process the formal declaration of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) and the division of estate assets in Portugal [5][8]. In addition, where assets exist in Portugal, the cabeça-de-casal must file the death notification and inventory of assets (Participação do Imposto do Selo - Modelo 1) with the Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority - AT / Portal das Finanças, telephone +351 217 206 707) by the end of the third month following the month in which the death occurred (even when direct forced heirs are exempt from payment) [8].
  • Procedures in Spain (Social Security, Registry of Last Wills, notary, and Inheritance Tax):
    • Spanish Social Security benefits: If the deceased person worked, resided, or paid contributions in Spain, check with the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (National Institute of Social Security - INSS, telephones +34 901 16 65 65 / +34 91 542 11 76) regarding entitlement to the funeral grant (auxilio por defunción) and survivor pensions (pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares), noting that contribution periods in Spain and Portugal may be aggregated under EU social security coordination regulations [9].
    • Registry of Last Wills, notary, and Inheritance Tax within 6 months: If your family member left bank accounts, real estate, or habitual residence in Spain, once 15 working days have elapsed since the death, request the Certificate of Last Wills (Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad) and the Certificate of Life/Death Insurance Contracts (Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento) using Modelo 790 from the General Registry of Last Wills of the Ministerio de Justicia [10]. With those certificates, contact a Spanish notary through the Consejo General del Notariado (General Council of Notaries) to execute the declaration of heirs or deed of acceptance and distribution of the estate [11], and file the Spanish Inheritance and Gift Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) within 6 months of the date of death (extendable by an additional 6 months if requested within the first 5 months).

closingQuestion: Which municipality and autonomous community in Spain did the death occur in, what municipality or district in Portugal is your family member connected to, and are you planning to repatriate the body or ashes to Portugal or arrange a local burial or cremation in Spain?

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre España y Portugal: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre España y Portugal: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos sinceramente el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con ciudadanía portuguesa o vínculos de residencia en Portugal fallece en España, la certificación médica inicial, la inscripción civil del óbito y la autorización sanitaria de salida se tramitan en el municipio español del fallecimiento, mientras que la recepción del féretro o de la urna, la transcripción consular o registral y las prestaciones o trámites sucesorios se coordinan entre las autoridades de Portugal y de España [1][4][6]. A continuación se detallan los cinco pasos oficiales en orden.

steps.title: Certificación médica de la defunción e intervención médico-legal en España
steps.html:
Antes de inscribir el fallecimiento, organizar el servicio funerario o iniciar el traslado transfronterizo hacia Portugal, un médico colegiado o la autoridad judicial competente debe certificar el deceso en España [1][2]:

  • Fallecimiento en hospital, clínica o centro sociosanitario: El médico facultativo que atendió a la persona fallecida expide el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial del Consejo General de Colegios Oficiales de Médicos (en formato impreso o electrónico), requisito imprescindible para la inscripción en el Registro Civil [1][2]. Entregue el documento de identidad portugués (Cartão de Cidadão o Bilhete de Identidade) o el pasaporte de su familiar, así como su Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE) si residía en España, para que los datos filiatorios coincidan exactamente con los registros portugueses [1][4].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio, hotel o vía pública: Llame de inmediato al teléfono único de emergencias 112 para que los servicios médicos de urgencia acudan a constatar el óbito [1][2]. Si el fallecimiento responde a causas naturales conocidas y un facultativo dispone de la historia clínica, podrá emitir el Certificado Médico de Defunción [2].
  • Muerte súbita, accidental o judicial e Instituto de Medicina Legal: Si la causa de la muerte es repentina, accidental, violenta o no puede certificarse como natural, intervienen las fuerzas policiales y el Juzgado de Guardia del partido judicial correspondiente, que ordena el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado al Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses (por ejemplo, en Madrid, Barcelona, Sevilla, Vigo o Badajoz) para practicar la autopsia judicial [1][2]. Ninguna inhumación, cremación ni repatriación a Portugal puede llevarse a cabo hasta que el juzgado emita la licencia de enterramiento o autorización de traslado [1].
  • Plazos autonómicos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria (24 a 48 horas): Conforme a los reglamentos de Policía Sanitaria Mortuoria de las comunidades autónomas españolas, la inhumación, cremación o aplicación de técnicas de conservación/embalsamamiento para el traslado internacional suele realizarse entre las 24 y las 48 horas posteriores al fallecimiento (salvo intervención judicial) [2][6].

steps.title: Seguro de repatriación, designación de funerarias en España y Portugal, y contacto consular portugués
steps.html:
Antes de firmar un contrato funerario de forma independiente, verifique si su familiar disponía de un seguro de viaje, asistencia médica internacional, cobertura asociada a tarjeta bancaria o póliza de seguro de decesos o repatriación [2][4]. Si existe cobertura, comuníquese primero con la central de asistencia 24 horas de la aseguradora para que designe y asuma directamente la coordinación entre la funeraria española y la funeraria portuguesa.

  • Empresa funeraria habilitada en España: Si no media una aseguradora, la familia puede designar a una empresa funeraria legalmente habilitada en el municipio español del fallecimiento, agrupada en la patronal nacional del sector, la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (PANASEF, teléfono +34 91 576 31 55, correo electrónico info@panasef.com) [2].
  • Agencia funeraria receptora en Portugal: Para el traslado terrestre o aéreo hacia Portugal (por ejemplo, a Lisboa, Oporto, Braga, Coímbra o Faro), la funeraria española se coordina con una agencia funeraria legalmente habilitada en Portugal (agência funerária habilitada), supervisada por la Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas (DGAE, integrada en el portal oficial gov.pt) y representada en asociaciones sectoriales portuguesas como la Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, teléfono +351 218 687 978) o la Associação de Agentes Funerários do Centro (AAFC) [3]. Clarvia facilita referencias de registros públicos y asociaciones profesionales únicamente a título orientativo y no recomienda, avala ni clasifica a operadores concretos.
  • Asistencia consular de Portugal en España: Notifique el fallecimiento a la red consular portuguesa en España según la demarcación territorial -la Sección Consular de la Embajada de Portugal en Madrid (teléfono del Centro de Atención Consular en España: +34 91 789 05 00; correo electrónico: sconsular.madrid@mne.pt), los Consulados Generales de Portugal en Barcelona y Sevilla o el Viceconsulado en Vigo-, dependientes del Portal das Comunidades Portuguesas del Ministerio de Negocios Extranjeros (MNE, que cuenta además con el Gabinete de Emergência Consular 24 horas en el +351 217 929 714 y gec@mne.pt) [4]. La inscripción de óbito y la tramitación mortuoria figuran entre los actos consulares urgentes que no requieren cita ordinaria previa en línea [4].

steps.title: Inscripción de la defunción en el Registro Civil en España (24 horas) y reconocimiento registral en Portugal
steps.html:
El fallecimiento ocurrido en territorio español debe inscribirse primero en el Registro Civil del municipio español donde se produjo el deceso antes de su transcripción o reconocimiento en Portugal [1][4][5]:

  • Registro Civil municipal en España (plazo de 24 horas): La declaración se presenta habitualmente dentro de las 24 horas siguientes al fallecimiento ante el Registro Civil municipal dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia (teléfono de atención ciudadana: +34 91 837 22 95) [1]. En la práctica, la empresa funeraria española presenta el Certificado Médico de Defunción y la documentación de identidad de la persona fallecida para obtener la licencia de enterramiento o incineración y solicitar los certificados oficiales [1][2].
  • Certificado Literal de Defunción y Certificado Plurilingüe (Fórmula C del Convenio de Viena de 1976): Solicite al Registro Civil español varios ejemplares del Certificado Literal de Defunción y del Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C) conforme al Convenio n.º 16 de la CIEC de Viena de 8 de septiembre de 1976 [1]. Dado que tanto España como Portugal son Estados parte del Convenio de Viena de 1976 y aplican además el Reglamento (UE) 2016/1191 sobre documentos públicos, la certificación plurilingüe Fórmula C está exenta de Apostilla de La Haya y de traducción jurada entre ambos países [1][5].
  • Transcripción y registro civil en Portugal (Conservatória do Registo Civil / Consulado): Mientras que una defunción ocurrida dentro de Portugal debe declararse en el plazo de 48 horas ante cualquier Conservatória do Registo Civil del Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN / Justiça.gov.pt, teléfono Linha Registos: +351 211 950 500) para extender el Assento de Óbito gratuito y, cuando se precise, la certidão plurilingue de la Convención de Viena [5], el fallecimiento de una persona de nacionalidad portuguesa ocurrido en España es de inscripción obligatoria en el ordenamiento portugués mediante transcripción ante el Consulado de Portugal en España o ante cualquier Conservatória do Registo Civil en Portugal presentando la certificación española (Fórmula C o literal) y el Cartão de Cidadão de la persona fallecida [4][5].

steps.title: Elección entre repatriación internacional de España a Portugal e inhumación o cremación local en España
steps.html:
Las empresas funerarias de España y Portugal gestionan conjuntamente los permisos sanitarios y fronterizos según la modalidad elegida por la familia [2][4][6]:

  • Repatriación del cuerpo en féretro desde España hacia Portugal: Ambos países son signatarios del Acuerdo de Estrasburgo de 1973 y del Convenio Internacional de Berlín de 1937 sobre traslado internacional de cadáveres [6]. La empresa funeraria española realiza las prácticas de conservación o embalsamamiento reglamentarias, acondiciona a la persona fallecida en un féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada (caixão de zinco selado) y tramita electrónicamente a través del sistema SISAEX de Sanidad Exterior (dependiente del Ministerio de Sanidad de España) la autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional y el salvoconducto mortuorio (laissez-passer / livre-trânsito mortuário o alvará de trasladação), en coordinación con las autoridades consulares portuguesas y con referencia a las orientaciones consulares del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (MAEC) y del Ministerio de Negocios Extranjeros portugués (MNE) [4][6]. Debido a la proximidad geográfica ibérica, el traslado entre España y Portugal se realiza con frecuencia por vía terrestre en vehículo funerario homologado, además de por vía aérea [2][6].
  • Traslado de cenizas a Portugal: Si la familia opta por la cremación en España, la urna cineraria sellada puede trasladarse a Portugal acompañada del Certificado Plurilingüe de Defunción (Fórmula C) y del certificado oficial de cremación expedido por el crematorio español [2][6].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en España: Si el entierro o la cremación se celebra íntegramente en el municipio español donde ocurrió el deceso, bastará con la licencia de enterramiento o incineración emitida por el Registro Civil español y el cumplimiento de los plazos sanitarios autonómicos [1][2].

steps.title: Pensiones de supervivencia, auxilio por funeral, impuestos y sucesiones en Portugal y en España
steps.html:
Con el Certificado Plurilingüe (Fórmula C) y el Assento de Óbito portugués, los familiares o herederos pueden iniciar las gestiones de seguridad social, fiscalidad y adjudicación hereditaria en ambos Estados:

  • Trámites en Portugal (Segurança Social, Espaço Óbito / Balcão das Heranças e Imposto do Selo):
    • Prestaciones de la Seguridad Social portuguesa: Si su familiar cotizaba o percibía pensión en Portugal, solicite ante la Segurança Social (teléfono +351 210 545 400 o +351 300 502 502; o a través de Segurança Social Direta) el subsidio único por defunción (Subsídio por Morte, dentro del plazo de 180 días consecutivos desde el fallecimiento), el reembolso de gastos funerarios (Reembolso de Despesas de Funeral, en el plazo de 90 días para quien sufragó el funeral cuando no existan familiares con derecho al Subsídio por Morte) y la pensión mensual de supervivencia (Pensão de Sobrevivência) [7].
    • Habilitação de herdeiros y declaración tributaria en 3 meses: El administrador de la herencia (cabeça-de-casal) puede acudir a las ventanillas únicas de Espaço Óbito o del Balcão das Heranças del Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado para tramitar la declaración formal de herederos (habilitação de herdeiros) y la partición de bienes en Portugal [5][8]. Asimismo, cuando existan bienes en Portugal, el cabeça-de-casal debe presentar la declaración del fallecimiento y la relación de bienes (Participação do Imposto do Selo - Modelo 1) ante la Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (AT / Portal das Finanças, teléfono +351 217 206 707) hasta el final del tercer mes siguiente al mes en que se produjo el fallecimiento (incluso cuando los herederos legitimarios directos estén exentos de pago) [8].
  • Trámites en España (Seguridad Social, Últimas Voluntades, notaría e Impuesto sobre Sucesiones):
    • Prestaciones en España: Si la persona fallecida trabajaba, residía o cotizaba en España, consulte ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS, teléfonos +34 901 16 65 65 / +34 91 542 11 76) el derecho al auxilio por defunción y a las pensiones de viudedad, orfandad o en favor de familiares (pudiendo totalizarse periodos cotizados entre España y Portugal conforme a los Reglamentos europeos de coordinación de Seguridad Social) [9].
    • Últimas Voluntades, notaría e Impuesto sobre Sucesiones en 6 meses: Si su familiar dejó cuentas bancarias, inmuebles o residencia habitual en España, una vez transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la defunción solicite el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento (mediante el Modelo 790) ante el Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad del Ministerio de Justicia [10]. Con dichos certificados, acuda a una notaría española localizable a través del Consejo General del Notariado para formalizar la declaración de herederos o la escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia [11], y presente la autoliquidación del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones en el plazo de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (prorrogable por otros 6 meses si se solicita dentro de los primeros 5 meses).

es.closingQuestion: Para ofrecerle indicaciones más precisas según su situación: 1. ¿En qué municipio y comunidad autónoma de España ocurrió el fallecimiento, y con qué municipio o distrito de Portugal tiene vínculos su familiar? 2. ¿Tienen previsto realizar la repatriación del cuerpo o de las cenizas a Portugal, o prefieren organizar la inhumación o cremación local en España?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Austria Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Austria Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Austria dies in Turkey: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Turkey, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Austria and Turkey.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Austrian citizenship or residence ties in Austria dies in Turkey, the issuance of the medical death certificate, civil registration, and border health transit permits are carried out by the competent authorities in Turkey, while consular support, reception of the remains in Austria, pension notifications, and probate proceedings (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) are coordinated between Austrian and Turkish institutions [1][2][4]. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Death Certificate (ÖBS) and Forensic Clearance in Turkey
steps.html:
The first step for official civil registration, local burial, or international repatriation is the issuance of an electronic Medical Death Certificate (Ölüm Belgesi / Defin Ruhsatı) by the authorized physician or judicial authority according to where the death occurred [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: If the death occurred in a hospital from natural causes, the attending hospital physician issues the electronic Death Certificate via the Ministry of Health Death Notification System (Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi - ÖBS) [1]. Provide the deceased person's Austrian passport (Reisepass) or identity card (Personalausweis) - along with any Turkish foreigner identity number, T.C. Kimlik Kartı, or Mavi Kart - to the hospital administration so that personal details match Austrian records exactly [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: For deaths occurring outside a hospital, call the 112 Emergency Call Center (112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi) immediately or contact the relevant municipal physician (belediye tabibi) or community health center physician (toplum sağlığı merkezi hekimi) [1]. If the medical examination confirms natural causes, the physician issues the Death Certificate (Burial Permit) through the ÖBS system [1].
  • Suspicious, sudden, or forensic deaths: If the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or involves a traffic accident or suspicious circumstances, the Police (155 / 112) or Gendarmerie (156 / 112) are notified and the case is referred to the duty Public Prosecutor's Office (Cumhuriyet Savcılığı) [1][2]. Where deemed necessary by the prosecutor, an autopsy is performed by the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tıp Kurumu); the body cannot be released or repatriated abroad until the prosecutor's office issues a written burial or transfer permit [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing Funeral Directors, and Austrian Consular Support
steps.html:
Before signing an individual funeral or air cargo contract, check whether an existing insurance policy or mutual aid fund covers the arrangements, and appoint licensed funeral service providers to coordinate between both countries [2][3]:

  • Checking travel insurance and funeral mutual aid funds (Cenaze Fonu): Check whether the deceased person held international travel health/assistance insurance (Auslandsreiseversicherung), automobile club coverage, or membership in a funeral mutual aid fund operating in Austria (such as Diyanet / ATİB or other Cenaze Fonu foundations cited as publicly known orientation examples) [2]. If an insurance assistance unit or funeral fund applies, it directly appoints its contracted funeral transfer provider in Turkey and Austria.
  • Selecting licensed funeral providers in Turkey and Austria: In Turkey, municipal funeral services (ALO 188, such as the Cemeteries Directorates of the Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, or Antalya Metropolitan Municipalities) handle local funeral procedures, while an international funeral repatriation company (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) is appointed for air repatriation to Austria [1][3][5]. That provider coordinates with a licensed Austrian funeral director (konzessioniertes Bestattungsunternehmen) that will receive the coffin in Austria (for example in Vienna, Graz, Linz, Salzburg, or Innsbruck); licensed providers in Austria can be found through the official professional association Wirtschaftskammer Österreich - Bundesinnung der Rauchfangkehrer und Bestatter (Austrian Federal Economic Chamber - WKO Fachverband der persönlichen Dienstleister / Bestatter directory) [2][4]. Clarvia provides these directories and institutional references solely for guidance and does not endorse, recommend, or rank any commercial operator.
  • Austrian missions in Turkey and consular support: If the deceased person was an Austrian citizen, you may contact the Austrian Embassy in Ankara (Österreichische Botschaft Ankara, email ankara-ob@bmeia.gv.at) or the Austrian Consulate General in Istanbul (Österreichisches Generalkonsulat Istanbul, email istanbul-gk@bmeia.gv.at) according to consular jurisdiction, as well as Austria's central Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten (Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs - BMEIA, Citizens' Service line +43 1 90115 3775, 24/7 emergency duty line +43 1 90115 4411) [2][6]. Consular offices provide guidance on local procedures and assist with passport cancellation and coordination of transfer documents, but do not pay funeral or repatriation expenses [2][6].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Turkey (Form C) and Document Recognition in Austria
steps.html:
Before burial, international transfer from Turkey, or official administrative steps in Austria can proceed, the death must first be registered in the civil registry in Turkey [1][3]:

  • District Civil Registry notification and Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C): Under Population Services Law No. 5490, the death certificate issued via ÖBS is recorded within 10 days at the District Civil Registry Directorate (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü) of the place of death, under the central authority Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs, domestic call center ALO 199, international telephone +90 312 591 21 00) [1]. The authorized funeral company or family member should request multiple wet-signed originals of the multilingual death extract under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) from the İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü [1][3]. Information on Turkish consular procedures is also available 24/7 from the Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi (Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Call Center, telephone +90 312 292 29 29) [3].
  • Recognition of Formül C in Austria and Standesamt (ZPR) registration: Because both Turkey and Austria are party to the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention, the Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C) issued in Turkey is directly valid in Austria without an Apostille or additional translation [1][2][7]. Whereas deaths occurring inside Austria must be reported by the next working day to the local civil registry office (Standesamt / Personenstandesbehörde) for entry in the Central Civil Status Register (Zentrales Personenstandsregister - ZPR, as explained on the official government portal oesterreich.gv.at) and issuance of the Austrian death certificate (Sterbeurkunde and CIEC-Formblatt C), the death of an Austrian citizen in Turkey is likewise recorded in the ZPR system by presenting the Formül C certificate to the competent Austrian Standesamt or Austrian diplomatic mission [2][7].

steps.title: International Repatriation from Turkey to Austria or Local Burial in Turkey
steps.html:
Depending on the family's decision, the deceased person may be repatriated to Austria or buried locally in Turkey [2][5]:

  • Coffin repatriation from Turkey to Austria (Sargüberführung): The international funeral provider arranges mandatory embalming (tahnit / Einbalsamierung) in Turkey and obtains the embalming report, places the body in a hermetically sealed soldered zinc liner (lehimli çinko tabut) inside an outer wooden transport coffin meeting international air transport and Berlin/Strasbourg treaty standards, obtains the municipal or provincial/district health directorate Road Transit Permit (Yol İzin Belgesi), and completes the international Mortuary Laissez-Passer (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi) clearance through the border health inspection unit at the departure airport under the Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Health for Borders and Coasts - THSSGM) [3][5].
  • Entry into Austria, Leichenpass, and cremation/urn rules: Under the rules of the Austrian authorities (the relevant district administrative authority, Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde / Magistrat, and the Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten), the coffin is transported to the destination municipality in Austria accompanied by the international mortuary laissez-passer (Leichenpass / Laissez-Passer) and the Formül C death certificate [2][6][7]. (For transfers in the reverse direction from Austria or when shipping a cinerary urn, Urnenversand, after cremation in a third country, the Austrian district authority Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde / Magistrat requires an österreichischer Leichenpass and cremation certificate [2][7].)
  • Local burial in Turkey and cremation availability: If local burial in Turkey is chosen, grave allocation and interment are carried out through the municipal cemeteries directorate (ALO 188) using the ÖBS burial permit [1]. Because there is no operating crematorium in Turkey, if cremation (Feuerbestattung) is desired, the body must be repatriated to Austria [2].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Funeral Grants, Taxes, and Probate (*Verlassenschaftsverfahren*) in Austria and Turkey
steps.html:
Once the multilingual Formül C death certificate has been obtained, social security, tax, and inheritance procedures are initiated in both countries:

  • Pension notifications (PVA / ÖGK) and automatic probate (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) in Austria:
    • Austrian pension and health insurance: If the deceased person was insured or received a pension in Austria, notify the Austrian Pension Insurance Institution Pensionsversicherungsanstalt (PVA, telephone +43 50303) and the Austrian Health Insurance Fund (Österreichische Gesundheitskasse - ÖGK) to apply for survivor pensions (Hinterbliebenenpensionen: widow/widower pension Witwen-/Witwerpension or orphan pension Waisenpension; if claimed within 6 months of death, the pension is payable retroactively from the day following the date of death) [8].
    • Automatic Austrian probate procedure (Verlassenschaftsverfahren): Under Austrian law, estate proceedings are conducted ex officio under court supervision [9]. Once the death is recorded in the Austrian civil register (ZPR) or assets in Austria are reported, the competent district court (Bezirksgericht) assigns the file to the competent notary acting as court commissioner (Gerichtskommissär, organized under the official chamber Österreichische Notariatskammer, the Austrian Chamber of Civil-Law Notaries); the notary conducts the initial death record (Todesfallaufnahme) and the formal transfer of the estate (Einantwortung) [9].
  • SGK entitlements, certificate of inheritance, and inheritance tax in Turkey:
    • SGK funeral grant and survivor pension: If the deceased person had social security coverage or pension rights in Turkey, eligible family members may apply to the provincial/central directorates of the Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (Social Security Institution - SGK, helpline ALO 170) or online via the official government portal e-Devlet Kapısı for the lump-sum funeral grant (cenaze ödeneği) and survivor pension (ölüm aylığı / widow-orphan pension) [10][11].
    • Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) and Inheritance Tax (4 months): For bank accounts or real estate (Tapu) located in Turkey, heirs must obtain a Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) from a Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) or from a notary office under the Türkiye Noterler Birliği (Union of Notaries of Turkey, telephone +90 312 218 80 00) (where foreign citizenship or a will is involved, the certificate must be obtained from the Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [12]. In addition, for assets in Turkey, an Inheritance and Transfer Tax return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) must be filed with the competent Tax Office (Vergi Dairesi) of the Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (Turkish Revenue Administration, helpline ALO 189) within 4 months following the date of death (or within the extended statutory deadlines under Law No. 7338 where heirs reside in Austria) [13].

closingQuestion: Which province or district in Turkey did the death occur in, which federal state (Bundesland) or city in Austria has residence or burial ties, and are you planning to repatriate the body to Austria or arrange a local burial in Turkey?

tr.title: Türkiye ve Avusturya Arasında Vefat Durumunda Yapılması Gerekenler: 5 Adımlı Resmi Rehber
tr.cardSummary: Türkiye ile Avusturya arasında gerçekleşen bir vefat sonrasında 5 adımlı resmi rehber: tıbbi ölüm belgesi, yetkili cenaze firması, nüfus müdürlüğü tescili ve çok dilli Formül C belgesi, konsolosluk işlemleri ve cenaze nakli (Leichenpass) veya yerel defin, dul/yetim aylığı ve veraset işlemleri.
tr.introHtml: Aile yakınınızın vefatı nedeniyle başsağlığı dileriz. Avusturya vatandaşlığı veya Avusturya'da ikamet bağı bulunan bir kişinin Türkiye'de vefat etmesi halinde, tıbbi ölüm belgesinin düzenlenmesi, nüfus tescili ve sınır sağlık nakil izinleri Türkiye'deki yetkili makamlarca yürütülürken; konsolosluk desteği, cenazenin Avusturya'da teslim alınması, emeklilik bildirimleri ve tereke (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) işlemleri Avusturya ve Türkiye kurumları arasında koordine edilir [1][2][4]. Aşağıda 5 ana resmi adım sırasıyla açıklanmıştır.

steps.title: Türkiye'de Tıbbi Ölüm Belgesi (ÖBS) ve Adli İnceleme Süreci
steps.html:
Resmi nüfus tescili, yerel defin veya uluslararası cenaze nakli için ilk adım, vefatın gerçekleştiği yere göre yetkili hekim veya adli makam tarafından elektronik Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) düzenlenmesidir [1][2]:

  • Hastanede veya sağlık kuruluşunda vefat: Vefat bir hastanede doğal nedenlerle gerçekleşmişse, ilgili hastane hekimi Sağlık Bakanlığı Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) üzerinden elektronik Ölüm Belgesi düzenler [1]. Kimlik bilgilerinin Avusturya kayıtlarıyla birebir örtüşmesi için vefat eden kişinin Avusturya pasaportunu (Reisepass) veya kimlik kartını (Personalausweis) ve varsa Türkiye'deki yabancı kimlik numarasını, T.C. Kimlik Kartı ya da Mavi Kart belgesini hastane idaresine teslim edin [1][2].
  • Evde, otelde veya kamusal alanda vefat: Hastane dışında meydana gelen ölümlerde derhal 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi aranmalı veya ilgili belediye tabibi ya da toplum sağlığı merkezi hekimine başvurulmalıdır [1]. Hekim muayenesi sonucunda ölümün doğal nedenlerden kaynaklandığı tespit edilirse ÖBS üzerinden Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) düzenlenir [1].
  • Şüpheli, ani veya adli vaka niteliğindeki ölümler: Ölümün nedeni bilinmiyorsa, ani gerçekleşmişse veya trafik kazası ya da şüpheli bir durum söz konusuysa Polis (155 / 112) veya Jandarma (156 / 112) birimlerine haber verilir ve süreç nöbetçi Cumhuriyet Savcılığı tarafından devralınır [1][2]. Cumhuriyet Savcısı gerekli gördüğünde Adli Tıp Kurumu tarafından otopsi işlemi yapılır; savcılığın yazılı defin veya nakil izni düzenlenmeden cenaze teslim alınamaz ve yurt dışına çıkarılamaz [1][2].

steps.title: Seyahat Sigortası, Cenaze Nakil Firmalarının Görevlendirilmesi ve Avusturya Konsolosluk Desteği
steps.html:
Bireysel olarak cenaze veya kargo sözleşmesi imzalamadan önce mevcut bir sigorta veya yardımlaşma fonu kapsamını kontrol edin ve iki ülkede koordineli çalışacak yetkili cenaze hizmet sağlayıcılarını belirleyin [2][3]:

  • Seyahat sigortası ve cenaze yardımlaşma fonu (Cenaze Fonu) kontrolü: Vefat eden kişinin yurt dışı seyahat sağlık/asistans sigortası (Auslandsreiseversicherung), otomobil kulübü güvencesi veya Avusturya'da faaliyet gösteren bir cenaze yardımlaşma fonu (örneğin Diyanet / ATİB veya diğer cenaze fonu vakıfları gibi kamuya açık bilgi amaçlı örnekler) üyeliği bulunup bulunmadığını kontrol edin [2]. Sigorta asistans birimi veya cenaze fonu mevcutsa, Türkiye ve Avusturya'daki anlaşmalı cenaze nakil firmasını doğrudan görevlendirir.
  • Türkiye ve Avusturya'da yetkili cenaze firması seçimi: Türkiye'de yerel cenaze işlemleri için belediye cenaze hizmetleri (ALO 188; örneğin İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir veya Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi Mezarlıklar Müdürlükleri) hizmet verirken, Avusturya'ya hava yoluyla nakil için uluslararası cenaze nakil firması görevlendirilir [1][3][5]. Bu firma, Avusturya'da (örneğin Viyana, Graz, Linz, Salzburg veya Innsbruck'ta) cenazeyi teslim alacak yetkili bir Avusturya cenaze firması (konzessioniertes Bestattungsunternehmen) ile koordineli çalışır; Avusturya'daki ruhsatlı firmalara resmi meslek kuruluşu Wirtschaftskammer Österreich - Bundesinnung der Rauchfangkehrer und Bestatter (WKO Fachverband der persönlichen Dienstleister / Bestatter rehberi) üzerinden ulaşılabilir [2][4]. Clarvia bu rehber ve kurum bilgilerini yalnızca yönlendirme amacıyla paylaşır; herhangi bir ticari firmayı onaylamaz, önermez veya sıralamaz.
  • Türkiye'deki Avusturya temsilcilikleri ve konsolosluk desteği: Vefat eden kişinin Avusturya vatandaşı olması halinde, vefat yerinin bağlı olduğu görev bölgesine göre Ankara'daki Avusturya Büyükelçiliği (Österreichische Botschaft Ankara, e-posta ankara-ob@bmeia.gv.at) veya İstanbul'daki Avusturya Başkonsolosluğu (Österreichisches Generalkonsulat Istanbul, e-posta istanbul-gk@bmeia.gv.at) ile ve Avusturya'daki merkezi dışişleri bakanlığı Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten (BMEIA, vatandaş hizmet hattı +43 1 90115 3775, 7/24 acil nöbetçi hattı +43 1 90115 4411) ile iletişime geçebilirsiniz [2][6]. Konsolosluk birimleri yerel prosedürler hakkında rehberlik sağlar ve pasaport iptali ile nakil belgelerinin koordinasyonuna yardımcı olur; ancak cenaze ve nakil giderlerini karşılamaz [2][6].

steps.title: Türkiye'de Ölümün Nüfusa Tescili (Formül C) ve Avusturya'da Belge Geçerliliği
steps.html:
Cenazenin defnedilmesi, Türkiye'den nakledilmesi veya Avusturya'daki resmi işlemlerin başlatılabilmesi için vefatın önce Türkiye'de nüfus kütüğüne tescil edilmesi zorunludur [1][3]:

  • İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü bildirimi ve Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi (Formül C): 5490 sayılı Nüfus Hizmetleri Kanunu uyarınca ÖBS üzerinden düzenlenen ölüm belgesi, vefat yerindeki İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü (merkezi idare kurumu Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, yurt içi çağrı merkezi ALO 199, yurt dışı telefon +90 312 591 21 00) kayıtlarına 10 gün içinde işlenir [1]. Yetkilendirilen cenaze firması veya aile yakını, İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü'nden 1976 Viyana CIEC Sözleşmesi kapsamındaki çok dilli ölüm kayıt örneğini (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) birden fazla ıslak imzalı nüsha olarak talep etmelidir [1][3]. Türkiye'nin dış temsilcilik ve konsolosluk prosedürleri hakkında Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi (7/24 telefon +90 312 292 29 29) üzerinden de bilgi alınabilir [3].
  • Avusturya'da Formül C belgesinin tanınması ve Standesamt (ZPR) kaydı: Hem Türkiye hem de Avusturya 1976 Viyana CIEC Sözleşmesi'ne taraf olduğundan, Türkiye'de düzenlenen Formül C Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi Avusturya'da Apostil şerhi veya ek tercüme aranmaksızın doğrudan geçerlidir [1][2][7]. Avusturya sınırları içinde gerçekleşen ölümlerde bildirim bir sonraki iş günü içinde ölüm yerindeki nüfus birimine (Standesamt / Personenstandesbehörde) yapılarak Merkezi Nüfus Sicili (Zentrales Personenstandsregister - ZPR, resmi devlet portalı oesterreich.gv.at üzerinden açıklandığı üzere) kaydı ve Avusturya ölüm belgesi (Sterbeurkunde ve CIEC-Formblatt C) düzenlenirken; Türkiye'de vefat eden bir Avusturya vatandaşının ölümü de Formül C belgesi ibraz edilerek Avusturya'daki yetkili Standesamt veya Avusturya temsilciliği aracılığıyla ZPR sistemine işlenir [2][7].

steps.title: Türkiye'den Avusturya'ya Uluslararası Cenaze Nakli veya Türkiye'de Yerel Defin
steps.html:
Ailenin kararına göre cenaze Avusturya'ya nakledilebilir veya Türkiye'de yerel olarak defnedilebilir [2][5]:

  • Türkiye'den Avusturya'ya cenaze nakli (Sargüberführung): Uluslararası cenaze nakil firması, Türkiye'de zorunlu tahnit (Einbalsamierung / ilaçlama) işlemini yaptırıp tahnit raporunu alır, cenazeyi uluslararası hava taşımacılığı ve Berlin/Strazburg anlaşmaları standartlarına uygun sızdırmaz lehimli çinko tabut ve ahşap dış tabut içerisine yerleştirir, ilgili belediye veya il/ilçe sağlık müdürlüğünden Yol İzin Belgesi alır ve çıkış yapılacak havalimanındaki sınır sağlık denetim birimi (yetkili genel müdürlük Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) üzerinden uluslararası Cenaze Nakil Belgesi (Laissez-Passer) onayını tamamlar [3][5].
  • Avusturya'ya giriş, Leichenpass ve kremasyon/urne kuralları: Avusturya makamları (ilgili bölge idare makamı Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde / Magistrat ve dışişleri bakanlığı Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten) kapsamında uluslararası cenaze geçiş belgesi (Leichenpass / Laissez-Passer) ve Formül C ölüm belgesi ile cenaze Avusturya'daki hedef belediyeye ulaştırılır [2][6][7]. (Ters yönde Avusturya'dan yapılan nakillerde veya üçüncü bir ülkede kremasyon sonrası kül kavanozu Urnenversand gönderimlerinde Avusturya bölge idaresi Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde / Magistrat tarafından österreichischer Leichenpass ve kremasyon belgesi aranır [2][7].)
  • Türkiye'de yerel defin ve kremasyon durumu: Türkiye'de yerel defin tercih edilirse, ÖBS defin ruhsatı ile ilgili belediye mezarlıklar müdürlüğü (ALO 188) üzerinden mezar yeri tahsisi ve defin işlemi gerçekleştirilir [1]. Türkiye'de faal bir krematoryum bulunmadığından, kremasyon (Feuerbestattung) istenmesi halinde cenazenin Avusturya'ya nakledilmesi gerekir [2].

steps.title: Avusturya ve Türkiye'de Dul/Yetim Aylığı, Cenaze Ödeneği, Vergi ve Miras (*Verlassenschaftsverfahren*) İşlemleri
steps.html:
Çok dilli Formül C ölüm belgesi alındıktan sonra her iki ülkedeki sosyal güvenlik, vergi ve miras işlemleri başlatılır:

  • Avusturya'da emeklilik bildirimleri (PVA / ÖGK) ve otomatik tereke süreci (Verlassenschaftsverfahren):
    • Avusturya emeklilik ve sağlık sigortası: Vefat eden kişinin Avusturya'da emeklilik veya sosyal güvenlik kaydı varsa, Avusturya emeklilik kurumu Pensionsversicherungsanstalt (PVA, telefon +43 50303) ve ilgili sağlık sigortası kurumu (Österreichische Gesundheitskasse - ÖGK) bilgilendirilerek hak sahipleri için dul/yetim aylığı (Hinterbliebenenpensionen: Witwen-/Witwerpension veya Waisenpension) başvurusu yapılır (vefattan itibaren 6 ay içinde yapılan başvurularda aylık ölüm gününü izleyen günden itibaren bağlanır) [8].
    • Avusturya'da otomatik miras/tereke prosedürü (Verlassenschaftsverfahren): Avusturya hukukunda miras işlemleri mahkeme denetiminde re'sen yürütülür [9]. Vefat Avusturya nüfus sistemine (ZPR) işlendiğinde veya Avusturya'daki malvarlığı bildirildiğinde, yetkili bölge mahkemesi (Bezirksgericht) dosyayı mahkeme komiseri (Gerichtskommissär) sıfatıyla görev yapan yetkili notere (resmi meslek odası Österreichische Notariatskammer bünyesindeki noterlik) tevdi eder; noter Todesfallaufnahme (ölüm tutanağı) işlemini ve mirasın devrini (Einantwortung) yürütür [9].
  • Türkiye'de SGK hakları, mirasçılık belgesi ve veraset vergisi:
    • SGK cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı: Vefat eden kişinin Türkiye'de sigortalılık veya emeklilik kaydı bulunuyorsa, hak sahipleri resmi kurum Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, danışma hattı ALO 170) il/merkez müdürlüklerine veya resmi dijital kapı e-Devlet Kapısı üzerinden başvurarak cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı (dul/yetim aylığı) talep edebilir [10][11].
    • Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı) ve Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi (4 ay): Türkiye'de bulunan banka hesapları veya taşınmazlar (Tapu) için mirasçılar, Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi'nden veya resmi meslek kuruluşu Türkiye Noterler Birliği (telefon +90 312 218 80 00) bünyesindeki noterliklerden Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı) almalıdır (yabancı vatandaşlık veya vasiyetname bulunması halinde belge Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi'nden alınır) [12]. Ayrıca Türkiye'deki malvarlığı için ilgili Vergi Dairesi'ne (merkezi vergi idaresi Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, danışma hattı ALO 189) ölüm tarihini takip eden 4 ay içinde (mirasçıların Avusturya'da ikamet etmesi halinde 7338 sayılı Kanun uyarınca tanınan ek yasal süreler dahilinde) Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi verilmelidir [13].

tr.closingQuestion: Durumunuza özel daha net bilgi verebilmemiz için: 1. Vefat Türkiye'nin hangi il veya ilçesinde gerçekleşti ve Avusturya'da hangi eyalet (Bundesland) veya şehirle ikamet ya da defin bağlantısı bulunuyor? 2. Cenazenin Avusturya'ya naklini mi yoksa Türkiye'de yerel defin işlemini mi planlıyorsunuz?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Turkey Dies in Austria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Turkey Dies in Austria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Turkey dies in Austria: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Austria, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Turkey and Austria.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Turkish citizenship or residence ties to Turkey dies in Austria, the medical post-mortem examination (Totenbeschau), initial registration in the Central Civil Status Register (Zentrales Personenstandsregister - ZPR), and issuance of the Austrian mortuary passport (Leichenpass) take place at the place of death in Austria, while the consular transfer permit, import clearance, and pension and estate procedures are coordinated between the Austrian and Turkish authorities [1][3][5].

steps.title: Medical Post-Mortem Examination (*Totenbeschau*) and Notification of Death in Austria
steps.html:
Before any transfer or burial can take place in Austria, an official medical post-mortem examination (Totenbeschau) must by law be carried out by an authorized physician and the official notification of death (Anzeige des Todes, including the medical death certificate) must be issued [1]:

  • Death in a hospital or care home: The medical management of the Austrian hospital arranges the Totenbeschau directly within the facility and transmits the Anzeige des Todes to the civil registry office (Standesamt) [1]. Have the deceased person's Turkish passport, national identity card (T.C. Kimlik Kartı or Mavi Kart), and any Austrian residence permit ready [1][3].
  • Death at home, in accommodation, or in a public place: Immediately notify the ambulance service on emergency number 144 (or the European emergency number 112) as well as the local municipality or city magistrate (Gemeinde / Magistrat) [1]. Depending on the Austrian federal state (Bundesland), the district or municipal physician (Sprengel- or Gemeindearzt) - or in Vienna, Municipal Department 15 - Public Health Services of the City of Vienna (MA 15) - performs the Totenbeschau and releases the body for collection by a funeral director [1].
  • Unnatural or unclear cause of death: In the event of an accident, sudden unexpected death, or indications of third-party involvement, the Austrian Police (emergency number 133) must be called in immediately [1]. In such cases, the body may neither be transferred nor buried until the police and public health investigations - or a judicial autopsy ordered by the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) - have been completed [1][3].

steps.title: Checking Insurance and Funeral Mutual Aid Funds, Appointing Funeral Directors, and Contacting the Turkish Consulate
steps.html:
Before commissioning a funeral provider independently, check whether insurance or mutual aid coverage is already in place for the deceased person [2][3]:

  • Funeral mutual aid fund (Cenaze Fonu) or travel insurance: If the deceased person held international travel health or repatriation insurance, or membership in a Turkish funeral mutual aid association (Cenaze Fonu or support foundation such as ATİB, DİTİB, or IGMG UKBA as publicly known orientation examples), contact their 24-hour emergency helpline first; these organizations directly appoint their contracted funeral provider and manage the repatriation to Turkey or local burial.
  • Licensed funeral director in Austria and receiving services in Turkey: If no such coverage applies, appoint a licensed funeral director in Austria (konzessioniertes Bestattungsunternehmen) listed through the statutory professional body (Wirtschaftskammer Österreich - Bundesinnung der Rauchfangkehrer und Bestatter, within the Austrian Federal Economic Chamber WKO Fachverband der persönlichen Dienstleister / Bestatter) [2]. In Turkey, the Austrian funeral director or international funeral transport company (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) coordinates collection at the destination airport as well as the municipal funeral services of the relevant city administration (belediye cenaze hizmetleri, reachable nationwide via ALO 188, for example in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, or Antalya) [3][4]. Clarvia provides these directories solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank individual commercial providers.
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate General of the Republic of Turkey in Austria: For consular death registration and the mortuary transit permit, the funeral director or family members contact the Turkish diplomatic or consular mission in Austria responsible for the place of death (Consulates General in Vienna, Salzburg, or Bregenz, or the Embassy of the Republic of Turkey in Vienna), operating under the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı, 24-hour Consular Call Center Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi at +90 312 292 29 29) [3].

steps.title: Registration at the Austrian Civil Registry (*Standesamt* / ZPR / CIEC Form C) and Registration for Turkey
steps.html:
• Civil Registry Office of the place of death in Austria (Zentrales Personenstandsregister - ZPR): The death is reported on the next working day to the Standesamt (Personenstandsbehörde) (Civil Registry Office) of the place of death in Austria (e.g., in Vienna, Graz, Linz, Salzburg, Innsbruck, or Bregenz) and recorded in the Central Civil Status Register (ZPR), as detailed on the official Austrian government portal (oesterreich.gv.at) [1]. In practice, the appointed Austrian funeral director submits the medical Anzeige des Todes, the passport or identity card (T.C. Kimlik Kartı), and birth and, where applicable, marriage certificates [1][3].
  • Multilingual CIEC Form C (1976 Vienna Convention): Alongside the standard Austrian death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), explicitly request several multilingual extracts from the death register on Form C (CIEC-Formblatt C / Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention from the Austrian Standesamt [1][4]. Because both Austria and Turkey are contracting states to this Convention, the multilingual Form C is recognized directly by Turkish consulates, civil registries, courts, and social security institutions without an Apostille and without additional translation [3][4].
  • Civil status registration in Turkey (MERNİS / ÖBS): To record the death in the Turkish civil registry maintained by the central Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, telephone Alo 199 or +90 312 591 21 00 from abroad), the death is either reported through the competent Turkish Consulate General in Austria or registered in Turkey within 10 days at the District Civil Registry Directorate (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü, complementing electronic registration in the ÖBS reporting system) upon presentation of Form C [3][4].

steps.title: Choosing Between International Repatriation to Turkey and Local Burial in Austria
steps.html:
• Coffin repatriation from Austria to Turkey (österreichischer Leichenpass and Cenaze Nakil Belgesi): For cross-border transport, the competent Austrian district administrative authority (Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde - the Bezirkshauptmannschaft or, in statutory cities such as Vienna, Graz, or Salzburg, the Magistrat) issues an Austrian mortuary passport (österreichischer Leichenpass) upon application by the funeral director [1][5]. This requires a medical certificate of freedom from contagious disease, an embalming certificate (tahnit raporu), and placement in a hermetically soldered zinc coffin (lehimli çinko tabut) inside a transport coffin [3][5]. Using these documents, the funeral director obtains the consular mortuary transit permit (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer) from the Turkish Consulate General in Austria [3]. General consular guidance is also published by the Austrian Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs (Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten - BMEIA, Citizens' Service +43 1 90115 3775, 24-hour emergency line +43 1 90115 4411) [5][6]. Upon arrival at the destination airport in Turkey, the Turkish Directorate General of Health for Borders and Coasts (Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) inspects the accompanying documents for import clearance, while the municipal cemetery or health authority (belediye / sağlık müdürlüğü, ALO 188) issues the domestic road transport permit (Yol İzin Belgesi) to the burial location [3][7].
  • Cremation and urn transport: If cremation takes place in Austria and the urn is transported, the death certificate (Form C), the cremation certificate, and the transport documents must accompany the urn [1][5].
  • Local burial in Austria: If the family wishes to arrange burial in Austria, the Austrian funeral director organizes the interment in accordance with the funeral law of the relevant Austrian federal state (many municipal cemeteries in Austria, such as in Vienna, Graz, Linz, or Salzburg, maintain dedicated Islamic burial sections) [1][2].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Funeral Grants, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Turkey and Austria
steps.html:
With the Austrian death certificate and the multilingual CIEC Form C, you can initiate social security, tax, and inheritance procedures in both countries:

  • Benefits and estate administration in Turkey:
    • SGK funeral grant and survivor pension: If the deceased person held social security coverage or received a pension in Turkey (including under the bilateral Austro-Turkish Social Security Agreement), eligible beneficiaries can claim the lump-sum funeral grant (cenaze ödeneği) and survivor pension (ölüm aylığı / dul-yetim aylığı) from the Turkish Social Security Institution (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK, information line ALO 170); applications can also be submitted online via the official Turkish e-Government portal (e-Devlet Kapısı) [8][9].
    • Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi) and inheritance tax return (4 months): For bank accounts and real estate (Tapu) in Turkey, heirs require a Turkish Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı), requested from a Turkish Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) or - where no foreign element or will requires court jurisdiction - from a Turkish notary office via the Union of Notaries of Turkey (Türkiye Noterler Birliği, telephone +90 312 218 80 00) (the deadline to renounce an inheritance in Turkey, reddi miras, is 3 months) [10]. For assets in Turkey, an Inheritance and Transfer Tax return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) must be filed with the competent Tax Office (Vergi Dairesi) of the Turkish Revenue Administration (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, helpline ALO 189) (standard deadline 4 months; for a death occurring abroad such as in Austria, statutory deadlines of 4, 6, or 8 months apply under Law No. 7338 depending on the heirs' place of residence) [11].
  • Benefits and automatic probate proceedings (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) in Austria:
    • Austrian survivor pensions (PVA / ÖGK): If the deceased person held health or pension insurance in Austria (e.g., with the Austrian Health Insurance Fund - ÖGK), survivors should check entitlement to widow, widower, or orphan pensions or lump-sum payments with the Austrian Pension Insurance Institution (Pensionsversicherungsanstalt - PVA, telephone +43 50303; if claimed within 6 months of the date of death, the pension is awarded retroactively from the day after death) [12].
    • Automatic probate procedure (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) through the court commissioner: The Austrian Standesamt automatically forwards every death certificate to the competent Austrian district court (Bezirksgericht), which initiates probate proceedings (Verlassenschaftsverfahren) ex officio and appoints a competent notary as court commissioner (Gerichtskommissär, organized under the Österreichische Notariatskammer, the Austrian Chamber of Civil-Law Notaries) to record the death (Todesfallaufnahme) and administer the estate [1][13].

closingQuestion: Which Austrian federal state (Bundesland) or municipality did the death occur in, what province or city in Turkey is your family member connected to, and are you planning a repatriation to Turkey or a local burial in Austria?

de.title: Todesfall in Österreich (Türkei): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Österreich und Türkei: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Wenn eine Person mit Staatsangehörigkeit oder Wohnsitzbezügen zur Türkei in Österreich verstirbt, erfolgen die ärztliche Totenbeschau, die Erstbeurkundung im Zentralen Personenstandsregister (ZPR) und die Ausstellung des österreichischen Leichenpasses am Sterbeort in Österreich, während die konsularische Überführungsgenehmigung, die Einfuhrfreigabe und die Renten- sowie Nachlassabwicklung zwischen den österreichischen und türkischen Behörden koordiniert werden [1][3][5].

steps.title: Ärztliche Totenbeschau und Anzeige des Todes in Österreich
steps.html:
Vor jeder Überführung oder Bestattung muss in Österreich gesetzlich eine amtliche Totenbeschau durch eine hierzu ermächtigte Ärztin oder einen ermächtigten Arzt durchgeführt und die amtliche Anzeige des Todes (samt Todesbescheinigung) ausgestellt werden [1]:

  • Sterbefall im Krankenhaus oder Pflegeheim: Die ärztliche Leitung der österreichischen Krankenanstalt veranlasst die Totenbeschau direkt in der Einrichtung und übermittelt die Anzeige des Todes an das Standesamt [1]. Halten Sie den türkischen Reisepass, den Personalausweis (T.C. Kimlik Kartı bzw. Mavi Kart) und einen etwaigen österreichischen Aufenthaltstitel der verstorbenen Person bereit [1][3].
  • Sterbefall zu Hause, in einer Unterkunft oder im öffentlichen Raum: Verständigen Sie umgehend die Rettung unter der Notrufnummer 144 (oder den Euro-Notruf 112) sowie die zuständige Gemeinde bzw. den Magistrat [1]. Je nach österreichischem Bundesland führt die Sprengel- bzw. Gemeindeärztin oder der Gemeindearzt - in Wien die Magistratsabteilung 15 - Gesundheitsdienst der Stadt Wien (MA 15) - die Totenbeschau durch und gibt den Leichnam zur Abholung durch ein Bestattungsunternehmen frei [1].
  • Unnatürliche oder ungeklärte Todesursache: Bei einem Unfall, einem plötzlichen unerwarteten Tod oder Hinweisen auf Fremdverschulden ist sofort die österreichische Polizei (Notruf 133) beizuziehen [1]. In diesem Fall darf der Leichnam bis zum Abschluss der polizeilichen und amtsärztlichen Erhebungen bzw. einer durch die Staatsanwaltschaft angeordneten gerichtlichen Obduktion weder überführt noch bestattet werden [1][3].

steps.title: Versicherungen und Bestattungshilfeverein prüfen sowie Bestattungsunternehmen und türkisches Konsulat einschalten
steps.html:
Prüfen Sie vor einer eigenständigen Beauftragung, ob für die verstorbene Person bereits eine Versicherung oder Vereinsvorsorge besteht [2][3]:

  • Bestattungshilfeverein (Cenaze Fonu) oder Reiseversicherung: Verfügte die verstorbene Person über eine Auslandsreisekranken- oder Rückholversicherung oder über eine Mitgliedschaft in einem türkischen Bestattungshilfeverein (Cenaze Fonu bzw. Unterstützungsstiftung wie ATİB, DİTİB oder IGMG UKBA als öffentlich bekannte Orientierungsbeispiele), kontaktieren Sie zuerst deren 24-Stunden-Notfallnummer; diese Einrichtungen beauftragen das Vertragsbestattungsunternehmen direkt und übernehmen die Organisation der Überführung in die Türkei oder der Bestattung vor Ort.
  • Konzessioniertes Bestattungsunternehmen in Österreich und Empfangsstellen in der Türkei: Besteht kein solcher Schutz, beauftragen Sie ein konzessioniertes Bestattungsunternehmen in Österreich, das über die gesetzliche Berufsgruppenvertretung (Wirtschaftskammer Österreich - Bundesinnung der Rauchfangkehrer und Bestatter, im Rahmen des WKO-Fachverbands der persönlichen Dienstleister / Bestatter) gelistet ist [2]. In der Türkei koordiniert das österreichische Bestattungsunternehmen bzw. die internationale Überführungsfirma (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) die Abholung am Zielflughafen sowie die kommunalen Bestattungsdienste der jeweiligen Stadtverwaltung (belediye cenaze hizmetleri, landesweit erreichbar über die Rufnummer ALO 188, beispielsweise in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir oder Antalya) [3][4]. Clarvia stellt diese Verzeichnisse ausschließlich zur Orientierung bereit und spricht keine Empfehlung, Bestätigung oder Einstufung einzelner Anbieter aus.
  • Kontakt zur Botschaft oder zum Generalkonsulat der Republik Türkei in Österreich: Für die konsularische Sterbefallregistrierung und das Leichenbegleitdokument wenden sich das Bestattungsunternehmen oder die Angehörigen an die nach dem österreichischen Sterbeort zuständige türkische Auslandsvertretung in Österreich (Generalkonsulate in Wien, Salzburg oder Bregenz bzw. Botschaft der Republik Türkei in Wien), die dem türkischen Außenministerium (T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı, 24-Stunden-Konsular-Callcenter Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi unter +90 312 292 29 29) untersteht [3].

steps.title: Beurkundung beim österreichischen Standesamt (ZPR / CIEC-Formblatt C) und Registrierung für die Türkei
steps.html:
• Standesamt des österreichischen Sterbeortes (Zentrales Personenstandsregister - ZPR): Der Sterbefall wird am nächsten Werktag beim Standesamt (Personenstandsbehörde) des österreichischen Sterbeortes (z. B. in Wien, Graz, Linz, Salzburg, Innsbruck oder Bregenz) angezeigt und im Zentralen Personenstandsregister (ZPR) beurkundet, worüber das offizielle österreichische Behördenportal (oesterreich.gv.at) informiert [1]. In der Praxis legt das beauftragte österreichische Bestattungsunternehmen hierfür die ärztliche Anzeige des Todes, den Reisepass oder Personalausweis (T.C. Kimlik Kartı) sowie Geburts- und gegebenenfalls Heiratsurkunden vor [1][3].
  • Mehrsprachiges CIEC-Formblatt C (Wiener Übereinkommen von 1976): Beantragen Sie beim österreichischen Standesamt neben der österreichischen Sterbeurkunde ausdrücklich mehrere mehrsprachige Auszüge aus dem Sterbeeintrag auf Formblatt C (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) gemäß dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen von 1976 [1][4]. Da sowohl Österreich als auch die Türkei Vertragsstaaten dieses Übereinkommens sind, wird das mehrsprachige Formblatt C von den türkischen Konsulaten, Personenstandsbehörden, Gerichten und Sozialversicherungsträgern direkt ohne Apostille und ohne zusätzliche Übersetzung anerkannt [3][4].
  • Personenstandsregistrierung in der Türkei (MERNİS / ÖBS): Für die Eintragung im türkischen Personenstandsregister der zentralen Personenstandsbehörde (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, Rufnummer Alo 199 bzw. aus dem Ausland +90 312 591 21 00) wird der Tod entweder über das zuständige türkische Generalkonsulat in Österreich gemeldet oder in der Türkei innerhalb von 10 Tagen beim zuständigen Bezirksstandesamt (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü, ergänzend zur elektronischen Erfassung im Meldesystem ÖBS) unter Vorlage des Formblatts C registriert [3][4].

steps.title: Wahl zwischen internationaler Überführung in die Türkei und lokaler Bestattung in Österreich
steps.html:
• Sargüberführung von Österreich in die Türkei (österreichischer Leichenpass und Cenaze Nakil Belgesi): Für den grenzüberschreitenden Transport stellt die zuständige österreichische Bezirksverwaltungsbehörde (Bezirkshauptmannschaft bzw. in Statutarstädten wie Wien, Graz oder Salzburg der Magistrat) auf Antrag des Bestattungsunternehmens einen österreichischen Leichenpass aus [1][5]. Hierfür werden die medizinische Infektionsfreiheitsbescheinigung, der Einbalsamierungsnachweis (tahnit raporu) und die Einsargung in einem luftdicht verlöteten Zinksarg (lehimli çinko tabut) innerhalb eines Transportsarges benötigt [3][5]. Das Bestattungsunternehmen holt damit beim türkischen Generalkonsulat in Österreich das konsularische Leichenbegleitdokument (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer) ein [3]. Allgemeine konsularische Informationen veröffentlicht zudem das österreichische Außenministerium (Bundesministerium für europäische und internationale Angelegenheiten - BMEIA, Bürgerservice +43 1 90115 3775, 24-Stunden-Notruf +43 1 90115 4411) [5][6]. Bei der Ankunft am türkischen Zielflughafen prüft die türkische Grenz- und Küstengesundheitsbehörde (Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) die Begleitpapiere für die Einfuhrfreigabe, während die kommunale Friedhofs- bzw. Gesundheitsbehörde (belediye / sağlık müdürlüğü, ALO 188) den innerstaatlichen Transportschein (Yol İzin Belgesi) bis zum Bestattungsort ausstellt [3][7].
  • Feuerbestattung und Urnenversand: Falls eine Einäscherung in Österreich stattfindet und die Urne transportiert wird, sind die Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C), die Kremationsbescheinigung sowie die Transportdokumente mitzuführen [1][5].
  • Lokale Bestattung in Österreich: Wünscht die Familie eine Erdbestattung in Österreich, organisiert das österreichische Bestattungsunternehmen die Beisetzung nach dem jeweiligen österreichischen Landes-Bestattungsgesetz (auf zahlreichen kommunalen Friedhöfen in Österreich, etwa in Wien, Graz, Linz oder Salzburg, bestehen eigene islamische Grabfelder) [1][2].

steps.title: Hinterbliebenenpensionen, Bestattungsgeld, Steuern und Nachlass in der Türkei und in Österreich
steps.html:
Mit der österreichischen Sterbeurkunde und dem mehrsprachigen CIEC-Formblatt C leiten Sie die sozialversicherungs-, steuer- und erbrechtlichen Schritte in beiden Staaten ein:

  • Leistungen und Nachlassabwicklung in der Türkei:
    • SGK-Bestattungsgeld und Hinterbliebenenrente: Bestand eine Versicherung oder ein Rentenbezug in der Türkei (auch unter Berücksichtigung des österreichisch-türkischen Abkommens über soziale Sicherheit), können Berechtigte bei der staatlichen Sozialversicherungsanstalt (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK, Informationslinie ALO 170) das einmalige Bestattungsgeld (cenaze ödeneği) sowie die Hinterbliebenenrente (ölüm aylığı / dul-yetim aylığı) beantragen; Anträge sind auch elektronisch über das offizielle Staatsportal (e-Devlet Kapısı) möglich [8][9].
    • Erbschein (Mirasçılık Belgesi) und Erbschaftsteuererklärung (4 Monate): Für Bankkonten und Immobilien (Tapu) in der Türkei benötigen die Erben einen türkischen Erbschein (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı), der beim türkischen Friedensgericht (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) oder - sofern kein Auslands- oder Testamentsbezug eine gerichtliche Zuständigkeit erfordert - bei einem türkischen Notariat über den Berufsverband (Türkiye Noterler Birliği, Telefon +90 312 218 80 00) beantragt wird (die türkische Erbausschlagungsfrist reddi miras beträgt 3 Monate) [10]. Für Vermögen in der Türkei ist beim zuständigen Finanzamt (Vergi Dairesi) der türkischen Steuerverwaltung (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, Rufnummer ALO 189) die Erbschaft- und Übertragungssteuererklärung (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) einzureichen (Grundfrist 4 Monate; bei Tod im Ausland wie Österreich gelten je nach Wohnsitz der Erben nach Gesetz Nr. 7338 Fristen von 4, 6 oder 8 Monaten) [11].
  • Leistungen und automatisches Verlassenschaftsverfahren in Österreich:
    • Österreichische Hinterbliebenenpensionen (PVA / ÖGK): War die verstorbene Person in Österreich kranken- oder pensionsversichert (z. B. bei der Österreichischen Gesundheitskasse - ÖGK), prüfen Hinterbliebene Ansprüche auf Witwen-, Witwer- oder Waisenpensionen bzw. Abfindungen beim österreichischen Pensionsversicherungsträger (Pensionsversicherungsanstalt - PVA, Telefon +43 50303; bei Antragstellung binnen 6 Monaten nach dem Todestag erfolgt die Zuerkennung rückwirkend ab dem Folgetag des Todes) [12].
    • Automatisches Verlassenschaftsverfahren durch den Gerichtskommissär: Das österreichische Standesamt übermittelt jede Sterbeurkunde automatisch an das zuständige österreichische Bezirksgericht, das von Amts wegen ein Verlassenschaftsverfahren einleitet und eine zuständige Notarin oder einen Notar als Gerichtskommissär (organisiert über die Standesvertretung Österreichische Notariatskammer) mit der Todesfallaufnahme (Todesfallaufnahme) und Nachlassabwicklung beauftragt [1][13].

de.closingQuestion: Um Ihnen noch gezielter weiterhelfen zu können: 1. In welchem österreichischen Bundesland (bzw. welcher Gemeinde) ist der Sterbefall eingetreten, und in welche Provinz oder Stadt in der Türkei bestehen Bezüge? 2. Planen Sie eine Überführung in die Türkei oder eine lokale Bestattung in Österreich?
