title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in Turkey: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in Turkey: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in Turkey, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and Turkey.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with French citizenship or residence ties in France dies in Turkey, the issuance of the medical death certificate, civil registration, and border health departure permits are handled by the competent authorities in Turkey, while consular death registration (transcription), reception of the remains in France, social security notifications, and estate administration (succession) are coordinated between French and Turkish institutions [1][2][7]. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Death Certificate (ÖBS) and Forensic Clearance in Turkey
steps.html:
The first step for official civil registration, local burial, or international repatriation is the issuance of an electronic Medical Death Certificate (Ölüm Belgesi / Defin Ruhsatı) by the authorized physician or judicial authority according to where the death occurred [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: If the death occurred in a hospital from natural causes, the attending hospital physician issues the electronic Death Certificate via the Ministry of Health Death Notification System (Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi - ÖBS) [1]. Provide the deceased person's French passport (passeport) or national identity card (carte nationale d'identité), family record book (livret de famille) if available, and any Turkish foreigner identity number, T.C. Kimlik Kartı, or Mavi Kart to the hospital administration so that personal details match French civil records exactly [1][2].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: For deaths occurring outside a hospital, call the 112 Emergency Call Center (112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi) immediately or contact the relevant municipal physician (belediye tabibi) or community health center physician (toplum sağlığı merkezi hekimi) [1]. If the medical examination confirms natural causes, the physician issues the Death Certificate (Burial Permit) through the ÖBS system [1].
  • Suspicious, sudden, or forensic deaths: If the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or involves an accident or suspicious circumstances, the Police (155 / 112) or Gendarmerie (156 / 112) are notified and the case is taken over by the duty Public Prosecutor's Office (Cumhuriyet Savcılığı) [1][2]. Where deemed necessary by the prosecutor, an autopsy is performed by the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tıp Kurumu); the body cannot be released or repatriated abroad until the prosecutor's office issues a written burial or transfer permit [1][2].

steps.title: Travel Insurance, Appointing Funeral Directors, and French Consular Support
steps.html:
Before signing an individual funeral or air cargo contract, check whether an existing insurance policy or mutual aid fund covers the arrangements, and appoint licensed funeral service providers to coordinate between both countries [2][3]:

  • Checking travel insurance and funeral mutual aid funds (Cenaze Fonu): Check whether the deceased person held international travel health/repatriation insurance (assurance voyage / rapatriement), bank-card assistance coverage, a French funeral insurance policy (assurance obsèques), or membership in a funeral mutual aid fund (such as Diyanet / DİTİB or other Cenaze Fonu foundations cited as publicly known orientation examples) [2]. If an insurance assistance unit or funeral fund applies, it directly appoints its contracted funeral transfer provider in Turkey and France.
  • Selecting licensed funeral providers in Turkey and France: In Turkey, municipal funeral services (ALO 188, such as the Cemeteries Directorates of the Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, or Antalya Metropolitan Municipalities) handle local funeral procedures, while an international funeral repatriation company (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) is appointed for air repatriation to France [1][3][8]. That provider coordinates with a prefecture-licensed French funeral operator (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) that will receive the coffin in France (for example in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Strasbourg, or Bordeaux); licensed providers in France can be found through the national professional federations Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (National Funeral Federation - FNF, telephone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) and Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (French Federation of Funeral Directors - FFPF, telephone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [4][5][7]. Clarvia provides these directories and institutional references solely for guidance and does not endorse, recommend, or rank any commercial operator.
  • French missions in Turkey and consular support: If the deceased person was a French citizen, you may contact the French Embassy in Ankara or the French Consulate General in Istanbul according to consular jurisdiction (diplomatic network Ambassade de France en Turquie, Ankara consular switchboard +90 312 455 45 45, emergency duty phone +90 533 721 50 91, email admin-francais.ankara-amba@diplomatie.gouv.fr; as well as the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie) [2]. Consular offices provide guidance on transcribing the death into the French civil registry (transcription) and issuing mortuary transit authorizations, but do not pay funeral or repatriation expenses [2].

steps.title: Civil Registration of the Death in Turkey (Form C) and Document Recognition in France
steps.html:
Before burial, international transfer from Turkey, or official administrative steps in France can proceed, the death must first be registered in the civil registry in Turkey [1][2]:

  • District Civil Registry notification and Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C): Under Population Services Law No. 5490, the death certificate issued via ÖBS is recorded within 10 days at the District Civil Registry Directorate (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü) of the place of death, under the central authority Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs, domestic call center ALO 199, international telephone +90 312 591 21 00) [1]. The authorized funeral company or family member should request multiple wet-signed originals of the multilingual death extract under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) from the İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü [1][2]. Information on Turkish consular procedures is also available 24/7 from the Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi (Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Call Center, telephone +90 312 292 29 29) [3].
  • Validity of Formül C in France and consular transcription (transcription): Because both Turkey and France are party to the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention, the Multilingual Death Certificate (Formül C) issued in Turkey is directly valid in France without an Apostille or additional translation [1][2]. Whereas a death occurring inside France must be declared within 24 hours (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the town hall of the place of death (mairie du lieu de décès, as explained on the official French public portal Service-Public.fr, telephone 3939 or +33 1 73 60 39 39 from abroad) to obtain the full death certificate (acte de décès intégral) and multilingual Formule C, the death of a French citizen in Turkey is transcribed into the French civil registry (transcription de l'acte de décès) before the Ambassade de France en Turquie (Embassy in Ankara or Consulate General in Istanbul) upon presentation of the Formül C certificate and French identity/birth records [2][6].

steps.title: International Repatriation from Turkey to France or Local Burial in Turkey
steps.html:
Depending on the family's decision, the deceased person may be repatriated to France or buried locally in Turkey [2][7][8]:

  • Coffin repatriation from Turkey to France (rapatriement du corps): Turkey and France apply the provisions of the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement (Accord de Strasbourg) and the 1937 Berlin Agreement (Arrangement de Berlin) on the international transport of corpses [7][8]. The appointed international funeral repatriation company arranges mandatory embalming (tahnit / soins de conservation) in Turkey and obtains the embalming report, places the body in a hermetically sealed soldered zinc coffin (lehimli çinko tabut / cercueil hermétique), obtains the municipal or provincial/district health directorate Road Transit Permit (Yol İzin Belgesi), and completes the international Mortuary Laissez-Passer (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer mortuaire) clearance through the border health inspection unit at the departure airport under the Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Health for Borders and Coasts - THSSGM) and the consulate [2][3][8].
  • Entry into France and prefectural transfer permits (arrêté préfectoral): The receiving funeral operator in France collects the coffin at the arrival airport in France using the international Laissez-Passer and Formül C death certificate and transports it to the municipality of burial or cremation (conversely, for outbound transfers of a coffin or cinerary urn from France abroad, the prefecture, préfecture, of the place where the coffin is sealed issues an arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) [6][7].
  • Local burial in Turkey and cremation availability: If local burial in Turkey is chosen, grave allocation and interment are carried out through the municipal cemeteries directorate (ALO 188) using the ÖBS burial permit [1]. Because there is no operating crematorium in Turkey, if cremation (crémation) is desired, the body must be repatriated to France [2][7].

steps.title: Death Grants, Survivor Pensions, Taxes, and Estate Administration (*Succession*) in France and Turkey
steps.html:
With the multilingual Formül C death certificate and the French consular death transcription (transcription), social security, tax, and inheritance procedures can be initiated in both countries:

  • Social security (CPAM), pensions (CNAV / Agirc-Arrco), tax, and notary (Notaires de France) procedures in France:
    • French health insurance and death grant (capital décès): If the deceased person was affiliated with French social security, notify the French health insurance fund Assurance Maladie (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM / Ameli.fr, telephone 3646 within France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad) to close the file and apply for the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès) for eligible beneficiaries [9].
    • French pension funds (caisses de retraite): If the deceased person received a French pension or worked in France, notify the general pension scheme Assurance Retraite (CNAV, telephone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) and the supplementary pension fund (Agirc-Arrco) to claim the survivor pension (pension de réversion) for the surviving spouse [10].
    • Tax filing and estate settlement through a notary in France (règlement de la succession): For bank accounts, real estate, or last habitual residence in France, appoint a French notary through the official notarial network Notaires de France (High Council of the Notariat - Conseil supérieur du notariat, telephone +33 1 44 90 30 00) to draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and file the inheritance tax declaration (déclaration de succession) with the French tax authorities (impôts) within 12 months when the death occurred outside France in Turkey (compared with 6 months when death occurs in France) [6][11].
  • SGK entitlements, certificate of inheritance, and inheritance tax in Turkey:
    • SGK funeral grant and survivor pension: If the deceased person had social security coverage or pension rights in Turkey (including entitlements under the bilateral Franco-Turkish Social Security Convention), eligible family members may apply to the directorates of the Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (Social Security Institution - SGK, helpline ALO 170) or via e-Devlet for the funeral grant (cenaze ödeneği) and survivor pension (ölüm aylığı / widow-orphan pension) [12].
    • Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) and Inheritance Tax (4 months): For bank accounts or real estate (Tapu) in Turkey, heirs must obtain a Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) from a Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) or from a notary office under the Türkiye Noterler Birliği (Union of Notaries of Turkey, telephone +90 312 218 80 00) (where foreign citizenship or a will is involved, the certificate is obtained from the Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) [13]. In addition, for assets in Turkey, an Inheritance and Transfer Tax return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) must be filed with the competent Tax Office (Vergi Dairesi) of the Turkish Revenue Administration (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, helpline ALO 189) within 4 months following the date of death (or within the extended statutory deadlines under Law No. 7338 where heirs reside in France) [14].

closingQuestion: Which province or district in Turkey did the death occur in, which municipality (commune) or region in France has residence or burial ties, and are you planning to repatriate the body to France or arrange a local burial in Turkey?

tr.title: Türkiye ve Fransa Arasında Vefat Durumunda Yapılması Gerekenler: 5 Adımlı Resmi Rehber
tr.cardSummary: Türkiye ile Fransa arasında gerçekleşen bir vefat sonrasında 5 adımlı resmi rehber: tıbbi ölüm belgesi, yetkili cenaze firması, nüfus müdürlüğü tescili ve çok dilli Formül C belgesi, konsolosluk işlemleri ve cenaze nakli (Leichenpass) veya yerel defin, dul/yetim aylığı ve veraset işlemleri.
tr.introHtml: Aile yakınınızın vefatı nedeniyle başsağlığı dileriz. Fransa vatandaşlığı veya Fransa'da ikamet bağı bulunan bir kişinin Türkiye'de vefat etmesi halinde, tıbbi ölüm belgesinin düzenlenmesi, nüfus tescili ve sınır sağlık çıkış izinleri Türkiye'deki yetkili makamlarca yürütülürken; konsolosluk ölüm tescili (transcription), cenazenin Fransa'da teslim alınması, sosyal güvenlik ve miras (succession) işlemleri Fransa ve Türkiye kurumları arasında koordine edilir [1][2][7]. Aşağıda 5 ana resmi adım sırasıyla açıklanmıştır.

steps.title: Türkiye'de Tıbbi Ölüm Belgesi (ÖBS) ve Adli İnceleme Süreci
steps.html:
Resmi nüfus tescili, yerel defin veya uluslararası cenaze nakli için ilk adım, vefatın gerçekleştiği yere göre yetkili hekim veya adli makam tarafından elektronik Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) düzenlenmesidir [1][2]:

  • Hastanede veya sağlık kuruluşunda vefat: Vefat bir hastanede doğal nedenlerle gerçekleşmişse, ilgili hastane hekimi Sağlık Bakanlığı Ölüm Bildirim Sistemi (ÖBS) üzerinden elektronik Ölüm Belgesi düzenler [1]. Kimlik bilgilerinin Fransız resmi kayıtlarıyla birebir örtüşmesi için vefat eden kişinin Fransız pasaportunu (passeport) veya kimlik kartını (carte nationale d'identité), varsa aile cüzdanını (livret de famille) ve Türkiye'deki yabancı kimlik numarasını, T.C. Kimlik Kartı ya da Mavi Kart belgesini hastane idaresine teslim edin [1][2].
  • Evde, otelde veya kamusal alanda vefat: Hastane dışında meydana gelen ölümlerde derhal 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi aranmalı veya ilgili belediye tabibi ya da toplum sağlığı merkezi hekimine başvurulmalıdır [1]. Hekim muayenesi sonucunda ölümün doğal nedenlerden kaynaklandığı tespit edilirse ÖBS üzerinden Ölüm Belgesi (Defin Ruhsatı) düzenlenir [1].
  • Şüpheli, ani veya adli vaka niteliğindeki ölümler: Ölümün nedeni bilinmiyorsa, ani gerçekleşmişse veya kaza ya da şüpheli bir durum söz konusuysa Polis (155 / 112) veya Jandarma (156 / 112) birimlerine haber verilir ve süreç nöbetçi Cumhuriyet Savcılığı tarafından devralınır [1][2]. Cumhuriyet Savcısı gerekli gördüğünde Adli Tıp Kurumu tarafından otopsi işlemi yapılır; savcılığın yazılı defin veya nakil izni düzenlenmeden cenaze teslim alınamaz ve yurt dışına çıkarılamaz [1][2].

steps.title: Seyahat Sigortası, Cenaze Nakil Firmalarının Görevlendirilmesi ve Fransa Konsolosluk Desteği
steps.html:
Bireysel olarak cenaze veya kargo sözleşmesi imzalamadan önce mevcut bir sigorta veya yardımlaşma fonu kapsamını kontrol edin ve iki ülkede koordineli çalışacak yetkili cenaze hizmet sağlayıcılarını belirleyin [2][3]:

  • Seyahat sigortası ve cenaze yardımlaşma fonu (Cenaze Fonu) kontrolü: Vefat eden kişinin yurt dışı seyahat sağlık/asistans sigortası (assurance voyage / rapatriement), banka kartına bağlı asistans güvencesi, Fransa'da cenaze sigortası (assurance obsèques) veya bir cenaze yardımlaşma fonu (örneğin Diyanet / DİTİB veya diğer cenaze fonu vakıfları gibi kamuya açık bilgi amaçlı örnekler) üyeliği bulunup bulunmadığını kontrol edin [2]. Sigorta asistans birimi veya cenaze fonu mevcutsa, Türkiye ve Fransa'daki anlaşmalı cenaze nakil firmasını doğrudan görevlendirir.
  • Türkiye ve Fransa'da yetkili cenaze firması seçimi: Türkiye'de yerel cenaze işlemleri için belediye cenaze hizmetleri (ALO 188; örneğin İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir veya Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi Mezarlıklar Müdürlükleri) hizmet verirken, Fransa'ya hava yoluyla nakil için uluslararası cenaze nakil firması görevlendirilir [1][3][8]. Bu firma, Fransa'da (örneğin Paris, Lyon, Marsilya, Strazburg veya Bordeaux'da) cenazeyi teslim alacak valilik ruhsatlı bir Fransız cenaze operatörü (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) ile koordineli çalışır; Fransa'daki yetkili firmalara ulusal meslek federasyonları Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, telefon +33 1 55 43 30 00, e-posta contact@federation-fnf.fr) ve Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, telefon +33 1 46 60 24 24) üzerinden ulaşılabilir [4][5][7]. Clarvia bu rehber ve kurum bilgilerini yalnızca yönlendirme amacıyla paylaşır; herhangi bir ticari firmayı onaylamaz, önermez veya sıralamaz.
  • Türkiye'deki Fransa temsilcilikleri ve konsolosluk desteği: Vefat eden kişinin Fransa vatandaşı olması halinde, vefat yerinin bağlı olduğu görev bölgesine göre Ankara'daki Fransa Büyükelçiliği veya İstanbul'daki Fransa Başkonsolosluğu (diplomatik ağ Ambassade de France en Turquie, Ankara konsolosluk santrali +90 312 455 45 45, acil nöbetçi telefon +90 533 721 50 91, e-posta admin-francais.ankara-amba@diplomatie.gouv.fr; ayrıca Fransa Avrupa ve Dışişleri Bakanlığı Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie) ile iletişime geçebilirsiniz [2]. Konsolosluk birimleri ölüm kaydının Fransız nüfusuna tescili (transcription) ve cenaze nakil izni süreçlerinde rehberlik sağlar; ancak cenaze ve nakil giderlerini karşılamaz [2].

steps.title: Türkiye'de Ölümün Nüfusa Tescili (Formül C) ve Fransa'da Belge Tanınması
steps.html:
Cenazenin defnedilmesi, Türkiye'den nakledilmesi veya Fransa'daki resmi işlemlerin başlatılabilmesi için vefatın önce Türkiye'de nüfus kütüğüne tescil edilmesi zorunludur [1][2]:

  • İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü bildirimi ve Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi (Formül C): 5490 sayılı Nüfus Hizmetleri Kanunu uyarınca ÖBS üzerinden düzenlenen ölüm belgesi, vefat yerindeki İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü (merkezi idare kurumu Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, yurt içi çağrı merkezi ALO 199, yurt dışı telefon +90 312 591 21 00) kayıtlarına 10 gün içinde işlenir [1]. Yetkilendirilen cenaze firması veya aile yakını, İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü'nden 1976 Viyana CIEC Sözleşmesi kapsamındaki çok dilli ölüm kayıt örneğini (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) birden fazla ıslak imzalı nüsha olarak talep etmelidir [1][2]. Türkiye'nin konsolosluk prosedürleri hakkında Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi (7/24 telefon +90 312 292 29 29) üzerinden de bilgi alınabilir [3].
  • Fransa'da Formül C belgesinin geçerliliği ve konsolosluk tescili (transcription): Hem Türkiye hem de Fransa 1976 Viyana CIEC Sözleşmesi'ne taraf olduğundan, Türkiye'de düzenlenen Formül C Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi Fransa'da Apostil şerhi veya ek tercüme aranmaksızın doğrudan geçerlidir [1][2]. Fransa sınırları içinde gerçekleşen bir ölümün hafta sonu ve resmi tatiller hariç 24 saat içinde ölüm yerindeki belediyeye (mairie du lieu de décès, Fransız resmi kamu portalı Service-Public.fr, telefon 3939 veya yurt dışından +33 1 73 60 39 39 üzerinden açıklandığı üzere) bildirilerek tam ölüm kayıt örneği (acte de décès intégral) ve çok dilli Formule C belgesi alınması gerekirken; Türkiye'de vefat eden bir Fransa vatandaşının ölümü de Formül C belgesi ve Fransız kimlik/doğum belgeleriyle birlikte Ambassade de France en Turquie (Ankara Büyükelçiliği veya İstanbul Başkonsolosluğu) nezdinde Fransız nüfus kütüğüne tescil ettirilir (transcription de l'acte de décès) [2][6].

steps.title: Türkiye'den Fransa'ya Uluslararası Cenaze Nakli veya Türkiye'de Yerel Defin
steps.html:
Ailenin kararına göre cenaze Fransa'ya nakledilebilir veya Türkiye'de yerel olarak defnedilebilir [2][7][8]:

  • Türkiye'den Fransa'ya cenaze nakli (rapatriement du corps): Türkiye ve Fransa, cenazelerin uluslararası nakline ilişkin 1973 Strazburg Anlaşması (Accord de Strasbourg) ve 1937 Berlin Anlaşması (Arrangement de Berlin) hükümlerini uygular [7][8]. Görevlendirilen uluslararası cenaze nakil firması, Türkiye'de zorunlu tahnit (soins de conservation / ilaçlama) işlemini yaptırıp tahnit raporunu alır, cenazeyi sızdırmaz lehimli çinko tabut (cercueil hermétique) içerisine yerleştirir, ilgili belediye veya il/ilçe sağlık müdürlüğünden Yol İzin Belgesi alır ve çıkış yapılacak havalimanındaki sınır sağlık denetim birimi (yetkili genel müdürlük Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) ile konsolosluk üzerinden uluslararası Cenaze Nakil Belgesi (Laissez-Passer mortuaire) onayını tamamlar [2][3][8].
  • Fransa'ya giriş ve valilik nakil izinleri (arrêté préfectoral): Fransa'daki alıcı cenaze operatörü, uluslararası Laissez-Passer ve Formül C ölüm belgesi ile cenazeyi Fransa'daki varış havalimanından teslim alarak defin veya kremasyon yapılacak belediyeye ulaştırır (ters yönde Fransa'dan yurt dışına yapılan cenaze veya kül kavanozu çıkışlarında ise tabutun kapatıldığı yerin valiliği préfecture tarafından arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire düzenlenir) [6][7].
  • Türkiye'de yerel defin ve kremasyon durumu: Türkiye'de yerel defin tercih edilirse, ÖBS defin ruhsatı ile ilgili belediye mezarlıklar müdürlüğü (ALO 188) üzerinden mezar yeri tahsisi ve defin işlemi gerçekleştirilir [1]. Türkiye'de faal bir krematoryum bulunmadığından, kremasyon (crémation) istenmesi halinde cenazenin Fransa'ya nakledilmesi gerekir [2][7].

steps.title: Fransa ve Türkiye'de Ölüm Yardımı, Emeklilik, Vergi ve Miras (*Succession*) İşlemleri
steps.html:
Çok dilli Formül C ölüm belgesi ve Fransız konsolosluk ölüm tescili (transcription) ile her iki ülkedeki sosyal güvenlik, vergi ve miras işlemleri başlatılır:

  • Fransa'da sosyal güvenlik (CPAM), emeklilik (CNAV / Agirc-Arrco), vergi ve noter (Notaires de France) işlemleri:
    • Fransız sağlık sigortası ve ölüm yardımı (capital décès): Vefat eden kişinin Fransa'da sosyal güvenlik kaydı varsa, Fransız sağlık sigortası kurumu Assurance Maladie (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM / Ameli.fr, Fransa içinden 3646, yurt dışından +33 1 84 90 36 46) bilgilendirilerek dosya kapatılır ve hak sahipleri için capital décès (ölüm yardımı) başvurusu yapılır [9].
    • Fransız emeklilik sandıkları (caisses de retraite): Vefat eden kişi Fransa'dan emekli aylığı alıyorsa veya Fransa'da çalışmışsa, genel emeklilik kurumu Assurance Retraite (CNAV, telefon 3960 veya yurt dışından +33 9 71 10 39 60) ve tamamlayıcı emeklilik sandığı (Agirc-Arrco) bilgilendirilerek geride kalan eş için dul aylığı (pension de réversion) talep edilir [10].
    • Fransa'da vergi bildirimi ve noter aracılığıyla miras (règlement de la succession): Fransa'da bulunan banka hesapları, taşınmazlar veya son ikametgah için resmi noterlik ağı Notaires de France (Conseil supérieur du notariat, telefon +33 1 44 90 30 00) üzerinden bir Fransız noteri görevlendirilerek mirasçılık senedi (acte de notoriété) düzenlenir ve Fransız vergi idaresine (impôts) miras vergisi beyannamesi (déclaration de succession; vefat Fransa dışında Türkiye'de gerçekleştiğinde 12 ay, Fransa'da gerçekleştiğinde 6 ay içinde) sunulur [6][11].
  • Türkiye'de SGK hakları, mirasçılık belgesi ve veraset vergisi:
    • SGK cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı: Vefat eden kişinin Türkiye'de sigortalılık veya emeklilik kaydı bulunuyorsa (Türkiye-Fransa Sosyal Güvenlik Sözleşmesi kapsamındaki haklar dahil), hak sahipleri resmi kurum Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK, danışma hattı ALO 170) müdürlüklerine veya e-Devlet üzerinden başvurarak cenaze ödeneği ve ölüm aylığı (dul/yetim aylığı) talep edebilir [12].
    • Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı) ve Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi (4 ay): Türkiye'deki banka hesapları veya taşınmazlar (Tapu) için mirasçılar, Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi'nden veya resmi meslek kuruluşu Türkiye Noterler Birliği (telefon +90 312 218 80 00) bünyesindeki noterliklerden Mirasçılık Belgesi (Veraset İlamı) almalıdır (yabancı vatandaşlık veya vasiyetname bulunması halinde belge Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi'nden alınır) [13]. Ayrıca Türkiye'deki malvarlığı için ilgili Vergi Dairesi'ne (merkezi vergi idaresi Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, danışma hattı ALO 189) ölüm tarihini takip eden 4 ay içinde (mirasçıların Fransa'da ikamet etmesi halinde 7338 sayılı Kanun uyarınca tanınan ek yasal süreler dahilinde) Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi verilmelidir [14].

tr.closingQuestion: Durumunuza özel daha net bilgi verebilmemiz için: 1. Vefat Türkiye'nin hangi il veya ilçesinde gerçekleşti ve Fransa'da hangi belediye (commune) veya bölgeyle ikamet ya da defin bağlantısı bulunuyor? 2. Cenazenin Fransa'ya naklini mi yoksa Türkiye'de yerel defin işlemini mi planlıyorsunuz?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Turkey Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Turkey Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Turkey dies in France: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in France, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Turkey and France.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a person with Turkish citizenship or residence ties to Turkey dies in France, the medical certification of death, the civil status declaration at the town hall (mairie) within 24 hours, and the issuance of the prefectural mortuary laissez-passer take place in France, while the consular transport authorization (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi), border health clearance upon arrival, and pension and estate formalities are coordinated between France and Turkey [1][3][6]. Below are the five main official steps in order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Medico-Legal Clearance in France
steps.html:
Before any declaration at the town hall, funeral operation, or repatriation procedure can proceed, a physician must officially verify the death in France and issue the medical death certificate (certificat médical de décès, on a paper Cerfa form or electronically via the CertDc application) [1]:

  • Death in a healthcare or care facility (hospital, clinic, EHPAD): The attending ward physician verifies the death and completes the medical death certificate directly [1]. The facility arranges temporary preservation in the hospital mortuary and returns personal effects; prepare the deceased person's Turkish passport, Turkish identity card (T.C. Kimlik Kartı or Mavi Kart), and, where applicable, French residence permit (titre de séjour) [1][6].
  • Death at home, in a hotel, or in a public place: Immediately call SAMU (15), the European emergency number (112), or an on-call doctor so that a physician can attend to verify the death and issue the medical certificate [1]. If transporting the body to a funeral home prior to coffining is desired, the funeral operator submits the prior declaration to the town hall and the transfer must take place within 48 hours of death [3].
  • Medico-legal obstacle (sudden, accidental, or suspicious death): If the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or suspicious, the physician ticks the "medico-legal obstacle" (obstacle médico-légal) box on the certificate [1]. The police or gendarmerie and the public prosecutor (procureur de la République) then take charge of the investigation (forensic examination or judicial autopsy): no coffining, burial, cremation, or repatriation to Turkey may take place until the burial permit or judicial authorization is issued by the prosecutor's office [1][3].

steps.title: Checking Insurance or Mutual Aid Funds, Appointing Funeral Operators, and Turkish Consular Contact
steps.html:
Before signing an individual funeral estimate, check whether the deceased person held coverage that directly arranges and pays for repatriation or funeral expenses [3][6]:

  • Travel/repatriation insurance or Turkish funeral mutual aid fund (Cenaze Fonu): If the deceased person held travel or repatriation insurance, bank-card assistance coverage, a pre-paid funeral contract, or membership in a Turkish funeral mutual aid fund (Cenaze Fonu / community foundations such as DİTİB, Millî Görüş / UKBA, or other organizations cited as publicly known orientation examples), contact their 24/7 helpline immediately so that they can directly appoint their partner funeral operator.
  • Licensed funeral operator in France and receiving provider in Turkey: In the absence of prior coverage, appoint a prefecture-licensed funeral operator (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture) in France [1][3]. Clarvia provides these official and associative directories solely for informational guidance and does not recommend, endorse, or rank any commercial provider. You can consult official guidance via Service-Public.fr (telephone 3939 from within France or +33 1 73 60 39 39 from abroad) [1] as well as the national professional federations: the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (National Funeral Federation - FNF, telephone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (French Federation of Funeral Directors - FFPF, telephone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. In Turkey, the French company or international funeral transport provider (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) coordinates with the municipal funeral services of the destination city (belediye cenaze hizmetleri, reachable nationwide across Turkey via the official number ALO 188, for example at the metropolitan municipalities of Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, or Antalya) [6][7].
  • Contacting the Embassy or Consulate General of Turkey in France: The appointed funeral operator or the family contacts the Consulate General of Turkey territorially responsible for the place of death in France (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Strasbourg, Bordeaux, or Nantes) or the Embassy of Turkey in Paris, operating under the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı, Consular Call Center Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi reachable 24/7 at +90 312 292 29 29 or from France at +33 1 80 14 63 35) [6].

steps.title: Declaring the Death at the Town Hall in France (Within 24 Hours) and Registration for Turkey
steps.html:
• Town hall of the place of death in France (24-hour timeframe): In accordance with civil status rules detailed on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical verification (excluding weekends and public holidays) before the civil status officer at the town hall of the place of death (mairie du lieu de décès) [1]. In practice, the appointed funeral operator most often completes this step upon presentation of the medical death certificate and identity documents (T.C. Kimlik Kartı, passport, birth or marriage certificate / livret de famille) [1].
  • Full death certificate and multilingual Form C extract (1976 Vienna Convention): Request from the French town hall several copies of the full death certificate (acte de décès intégral) as well as several multilingual death extracts on Form C (extrait d'acte de décès plurilingue Formule C / Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) issued under the CIEC Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 [1][6][7]. Because both France and Turkey are states party to the 1976 Vienna Convention, the multilingual Form C extract is directly recognized by Turkish consulates, civil registries, courts, and social security bodies in Turkey without an Apostille or additional sworn translation [6][7].
  • Civil status registration in Turkey (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü): Recording the death in the central Turkish civil register maintained by the Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, telephone in Turkey Alo 199 or +90 312 591 21 00 from abroad) is carried out either through the Consulate General of Turkey in France when issuing the funeral transfer permit, or at the District Civil Registry Directorate in Turkey (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü, where deaths occurring in Turkey are otherwise declared within 10 days via the electronic ÖBS system) upon presentation of the multilingual Form C extract [6][7].

steps.title: Choosing Between International Repatriation to Turkey and Local Burial or Cremation in France
steps.html:
• International repatriation of the body or ashes from France to Turkey:
    • Prefectural mortuary laissez-passer in France: France and Turkey apply the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement as well as the 1937 Berlin International Arrangement on the transport of corpses [3][6]. The French funeral operator arranges embalming/preservation care (soins de conservation / tahnit raporu), places the body in a statutory hermetically sealed coffin (cercueil hermétique) fitted with a soldered zinc liner (lehimli çinko tabut), and obtains a prefectural mortuary laissez-passer (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) from the prefecture of the French department where the coffin is sealed (alongside general consular guidance from the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs - MEAE / France Diplomatie) [3].
    • Consular Cenaze Nakil Belgesi and border health inspection in Turkey (THSSGM): Upon presentation of the death certificate (Form C), medical certificate of non-contagion, embalming certificate, and French prefectural laissez-passer, the Consulate General of Turkey in France issues the consular mortuary transit permit (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer) [6]. Upon arrival at the airport in Turkey, the Turkish Directorate General of Health for Borders and Coasts (Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) inspects the documents to authorize entry into the country, and local municipal or health services (belediye / sağlık müdürlüğü, ALO 188) issue the domestic road transport permit (Yol İzin Belgesi) to the place of burial [6][8]. If cremation has taken place in France, transporting the cinerary urn requires the French prefectural authorization to transport ashes, the cremation certificate, and the death certificate extract [3].
  • Local burial or cremation in France: If the family chooses funeral services in France, burial (including in an Islamic denominational section of a municipal cemetery where available) or cremation must take place no earlier than 24 hours after death and no later than 14 calendar days following the day after death (unless a prefectural extension is granted), upon authorization by the mayor of the municipality of death [2].

steps.title: Survivor Pensions, Death Grants, Taxes, and Estate Administration in Turkey and France
steps.html:
With the French death certificate and the multilingual Form C extract, initiate social security, tax, and estate procedures in both countries:

  • Procedures in Turkey (SGK, Certificate of Inheritance Mirasçılık Belgesi, and inheritance tax):
    • Funeral grant and survivor pension (SGK): If the deceased person was covered by Turkish social security or received a pension in Turkey (including under the Franco-Turkish Social Security Convention), eligible beneficiaries can claim the lump-sum funeral grant (cenaze ödeneği) and survivor pension (ölüm aylığı / dul-yetim aylığı) from the Turkish Social Security Institution (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK, helpline ALO 170) or directly online via the official portal of the Turkish State (e-Devlet Kapısı) [9][10].
    • Certificate of Inheritance (Veraset İlamı) and tax filing within 4 months: To release bank accounts or transfer real estate (Tapu) in Turkey, heirs must obtain a Turkish Certificate of Inheritance (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) from a Turkish Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) or, where no foreign element or will requires court proceedings, from a Turkish notary belonging to the Union of Notaries of Turkey (Türkiye Noterler Birliği, telephone +90 312 218 80 00) (the deadline to renounce an inheritance in Turkey, reddi miras, is 3 months) [11]. In addition, heirs must file the inheritance and transfer tax return (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) with the competent tax office (Vergi Dairesi) under the Turkish Revenue Administration (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, helpline ALO 189) within a base period of 4 months following death (which may be extended to 6 or 8 months depending on the place of death abroad and the heirs' country of residence under Turkish Law No. 7338) [12].
  • Procedures in France (CPAM, pension funds, taxes, and notary):
    • Health insurance and death grant (CPAM): If the deceased person was insured in France, notify Assurance Maladie (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM / Ameli.fr, telephone 3646 from France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad) to close the file and check eligibility for the lump-sum death grant (capital décès) [13].
    • French pension funds (CNAV and Agirc-Arrco): Report the death to Assurance Retraite (CNAV, telephone 3960 or +33 9 71 10 39 60 from abroad) as well as the supplementary pension fund Agirc-Arrco to process the surviving spouse's entitlement to a survivor pension (pension de réversion) [14].
    • Taxes and estate settlement by a notary: Notify the French tax authorities (impôts) and, if the deceased person owned real estate, bank accounts, or had their habitual residence in France, instruct a notary through the official network of Notaires de France (High Council of the Notariat - Conseil supérieur du notariat, telephone +33 1 44 90 30 00) to draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and file the inheritance tax declaration within the statutory 6-month deadline (for a death occurring in metropolitan France) [1][15].

closingQuestion: Which French municipality (commune) or department did the death occur in, what province or city in Turkey had ties to your family member, and are you considering repatriating the body to Turkey or arranging a local burial or cremation in France?

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre France et Turquie : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre France et Turquie : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml: Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne ayant la nationalité turque ou des liens de résidence avec la Turquie décède en France, la constatation médicale, la déclaration d'état civil en mairie dans les 24 heures et la délivrance du laissez-passer mortuaire préfectoral s'effectuent en France, tandis que l'autorisation consulaire de transport (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi), la réception sanitaire à l'arrivée ainsi que les démarches de pension et de succession sont coordonnées entre la France et la Turquie [1][3][6]. Voici les cinq grandes étapes officielles dans l'ordre.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et certificat médical en France
steps.html:
Avant toute déclaration en mairie, opération funéraire ou procédure de rapatriement, un médecin doit constater officiellement le décès en France et établir le certificat médical de décès (sur formulaire papier Cerfa ou par voie électronique via l'application CertDc) [1] :

  • Décès en établissement de santé ou médico-social (hôpital, clinique, EHPAD) : Le médecin du service constate le décès et rédige directement le certificat médical de décès [1]. L'établissement assure la conservation du corps en chambre mortuaire et remet les effets personnels ; préparez le passeport turc, la carte d'identité turque (T.C. Kimlik Kartı ou Mavi Kart) et, le cas échéant, le titre de séjour français de la personne décédée [1][6].
  • Décès à domicile, à l'hôtel ou sur la voie publique : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU (15), le numéro d'urgence européen (112) ou un médecin de garde afin qu'un praticien se déplace pour constater le décès et établir le certificat médical [1]. Si un transport du corps avant mise en bière vers une chambre funéraire est souhaité, l'opérateur funéraire effectue la déclaration préalable auprès de la mairie et le transfert doit intervenir dans les 48 heures suivant le décès [3].
  • Obstacle médico-légal (décès soudain, accidentel ou suspect) : Si la cause du décès est inconnue, soudaine ou suspecte, le médecin coche la case « obstacle médico-légal » sur le certificat [1]. Les services de police ou de gendarmerie ainsi que le procureur de la République prennent alors la direction des opérations (examen médico-légal ou autopsie judiciaire) : aucune mise en bière, inhumation, crémation ni aucun rapatriement vers la Turquie ne peut avoir lieu avant la délivrance du permis d'inhumer ou de l'autorisation judiciaire du parquet [1][3].

steps.title: Vérification des assurances ou caisses d'entraide, choix des opérateurs funéraires et contact consulaire turc
steps.html:
Avant de signer un devis à titre individuel, vérifiez si la personne décédée bénéficiait d'une couverture prenant directement en charge l'organisation et les frais de rapatriement ou d'obsèques [3][6] :

  • Assurance voyage/rapatriement ou fonds d'entraide funéraire (Cenaze Fonu) : Si la personne décédée disposait d'une assurance voyage ou rapatriement, d'une assistance liée à une carte bancaire, d'un contrat de prévoyance obsèques ou d'une adhésion à une caisse d'entraide funéraire turque (Cenaze Fonu / fondations associatives telles que DİTİB, Millî Görüş / UKBA ou autres organismes cités à titre d'exemples publics d'orientation), contactez immédiatement leur permanence 24h/24 afin qu'ils mandatent directement leur opérateur funéraire partenaire.
  • Opérateur funéraire habilité en France et prestataire récepteur en Turquie : En l'absence de prise en charge préalable, mandatez en France un opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture [1][3]. Clarvia fournit ces répertoires officiels et associatifs uniquement à titre d'orientation et ne recommande, ne cautionne ni ne classe aucun prestataire commercial. Vous pouvez consulter les informations officielles via Service-Public.fr (téléphone 3939 depuis la France ou +33 1 73 60 39 39 depuis l'étranger) [1] ainsi que les fédérations professionnelles nationales : la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, téléphone +33 1 55 43 30 00, courriel contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] et la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, téléphone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. En Turquie, l'entreprise française ou la société internationale de transport funéraire (uluslararası cenaze nakil firması) se coordonne avec les services funéraires municipaux de la ville de destination (belediye cenaze hizmetleri, joignables dans toute la Turquie via le numéro officiel ALO 188, par exemple auprès des municipalités métropolitaines d'Istanbul, d'Ankara, d'Izmir ou d'Antalya) [6][7].
  • Contact avec l'Ambassade ou le Consulat général de Turquie en France : L'opérateur funéraire mandaté ou la famille saisit le Consulat général de Turquie territorialement compétent pour le lieu du décès en France (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Strasbourg, Bordeaux ou Nantes) ou l'Ambassade de Turquie à Paris, rattachés au ministère turc des Affaires étrangères (T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı, Centre d'appel consulaire Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluk Çağrı Merkezi joignable 24h/24 au +90 312 292 29 29 ou depuis la France au +33 1 80 14 63 35) [6].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès à la mairie en France (dans les 24 heures) et enregistrement pour la Turquie
steps.html:
• Mairie du lieu de décès en France (délai de 24 heures) : Conformément aux règles d'état civil détaillées sur Service-Public.fr, le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures suivant sa constatation (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès de l'officier d'état civil de la mairie du lieu de décès [1]. En pratique, l'opérateur funéraire mandaté effectue le plus souvent cette démarche sur présentation du certificat médical de décès et des pièces d'identité (T.C. Kimlik Kartı, passeport, acte de naissance ou de mariage / livret de famille) [1].
  • Acte de décès intégral et extrait plurilingue Formule C (Convention de Vienne de 1976) : Demandez à la mairie française plusieurs copies de l'acte de décès intégral ainsi que plusieurs extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues sur Formule C (Çok Dilli Ölüm Belgesi - Formül C) établis en application de la Convention CIEC de Vienne du 8 septembre 1976 [1][6][7]. La France et la Turquie étant toutes deux États parties à la Convention de Vienne de 1976, l'extrait plurilingue Formule C est directement reconnu par les consulats turcs, l'état civil, les tribunaux et les organismes sociaux en Turquie sans apostille ni traduction assermentée supplémentaire [6][7].
  • Enregistrement à l'état civil en Turquie (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü) : L'enregistrement du décès dans le registre central turc de l'état civil géré par la Direction générale de l'état civil et de la citoyenneté (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, numéro d'appel en Turquie Alo 199 ou +90 312 591 21 00 depuis l'étranger) s'effectue soit par l'intermédiaire du Consulat général de Turquie en France lors de la délivrance du permis de transfert funéraire, soit auprès de la direction de l'état civil du district en Turquie (İlçe Nüfus Müdürlüğü, où les décès survenus en Turquie sont par ailleurs déclarés dans un délai de 10 jours via le système électronique ÖBS) sur présentation de l'extrait plurilingue Formule C [6][7].

steps.title: Choix entre le rapatriement international vers la Turquie et l'inhumation ou la crémation en France
steps.html:
• Rapatriement international du corps ou des cendres de la France vers la Turquie :
    • Arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire en France : La France et la Turquie appliquent l'Accord de Strasbourg de 1973 ainsi que l'Arrangement international de Berlin de 1937 sur le transport des corps [3][6]. L'opérateur funéraire français fait réaliser les soins de conservation (tahnit raporu / thanatopraxie), procède à la mise en bière dans un cercueil hermétique réglementaire comportant un caisson intérieur en zinc soudé (lehimli çinko tabut) et obtient un arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire auprès de la préfecture du département français où a lieu la fermeture du cercueil (ainsi que les informations consulaires générales du Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères - MEAE / France Diplomatie) [3].
    • Cenaze Nakil Belgesi consulaire et contrôle sanitaire en Turquie (THSSGM) : Sur présentation de l'acte de décès (Formule C), du certificat médical de non-contagion, du certificat de soins de conservation et du laissez-passer préfectoral français, le Consulat général de Turquie en France délivre le laissez-passer mortuaire consulaire (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi / Laissez-Passer) [6]. À l'arrivée à l'aéroport en Turquie, la Direction générale turque de la santé des frontières et des côtes (Türkiye Hudut ve Sahiller Sağlık Genel Müdürlüğü - THSSGM) contrôle les documents pour autoriser l'entrée sur le territoire, et les services municipaux ou sanitaires locaux (belediye / sağlık müdürlüğü, ALO 188) délivrent le permis de transport intérieur (Yol İzin Belgesi) jusqu'au lieu d'inhumation [6][8]. Si une crémation a eu lieu en France, le transport de l'urne cinéraire requiert l'autorisation préfectorale française de transport de cendres, le certificat de crémation et l'extrait d'acte de décès [3].
  • Inhumation ou crémation locale en France : Si la famille choisit des obsèques en France, l'inhumation (y compris dans un carré confessionnel musulman d'un cimetière communal lorsque disponible) ou la crémation doit intervenir au plus tôt 24 heures après le décès et au plus tard dans un délai de 14 jours calendaires suivant le lendemain du décès (sauf dérogation préfectorale), sur autorisation du maire de la commune du décès [2].

steps.title: Pensions de survivant, capital décès, fiscalité et succession en Turquie et en France
steps.html:
Muni de l'acte de décès français et de l'extrait plurilingue Formule C, engagez les démarches sociales, fiscales et successorales dans les deux pays :

  • Démarches en Turquie (SGK, certificat d'hérédité Mirasçılık Belgesi et impôt sur les successions) :
    • Allocation funéraire et pension de survivant (SGK) : Si la personne décédée relevait de la sécurité sociale turque ou percevait une pension en Turquie (y compris dans le cadre de la convention franco-turque de sécurité sociale), les ayants droit peuvent demander l'allocation funéraire (cenaze ödeneği) et la pension de survivant (ölüm aylığı / dul-yetim aylığı) auprès de l'institution de sécurité sociale turque (Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu - SGK, ligne d'information ALO 170) ou directement en ligne via le portail officiel de l'État turc (e-Devlet Kapısı) [9][10].
    • Certificat d'hérédité (Veraset İlamı) et déclaration fiscale dans les 4 mois : Pour débloquer des comptes bancaires ou transférer des biens immobiliers (Tapu) en Turquie, les héritiers doivent obtenir un certificat d'hérédité turc (Mirasçılık Belgesi / Veraset İlamı) auprès du tribunal de paix civil turc (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) ou, lorsqu'aucun élément d'extranéité ou testament n'impose la voie judiciaire, auprès d'un notaire turc membre de l'Union des notaires de Turquie (Türkiye Noterler Birliği, téléphone +90 312 218 80 00) (le délai de renonciation à une succession en Turquie, reddi miras, est de 3 mois) [11]. En outre, les héritiers doivent déposer la déclaration de droits de succession (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi beyannamesi) auprès du centre des impôts compétent (Vergi Dairesi) relevant de l'administration fiscale turque (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, ligne d'information ALO 189) dans un délai de base de 4 mois suivant le décès (ce délai pouvant être porté à 6 ou 8 mois selon le lieu du décès à l'étranger et le pays de résidence des héritiers conformément à la loi turque n° 7338) [12].
  • Démarches en France (CPAM, caisses de retraite, impôts et notaire) :
    • Assurance maladie et capital décès (CPAM) : Si la personne décédée était affiliée en France, informez l'Assurance Maladie (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM / Ameli.fr, téléphone 3646 depuis la France ou +33 1 84 90 36 46 depuis l'étranger) pour clôturer le dossier et vérifier l'ouverture du droit au capital décès [13].
    • Caisses de retraite françaises (CNAV et Agirc-Arrco) : Déclarez le décès à l'Assurance Retraite (CNAV, téléphone 3960 ou +33 9 71 10 39 60 depuis l'étranger) ainsi qu'à la caisse de retraite complémentaire Agirc-Arrco afin d'instruire les droits à pension de réversion du conjoint survivant [14].
    • Impôts et règlement de la succession par un notaire : Informez l'administration fiscale française (impôts) et, si la personne décédée possédait un bien immobilier, des comptes bancaires ou sa résidence habituelle en France, saisissez un notaire via le réseau officiel des Notaires de France (Conseil supérieur du notariat, téléphone +33 1 44 90 30 00) pour établir l'acte de notoriété et déposer la déclaration de succession dans le délai légal de 6 mois (pour un décès survenu en France métropolitaine) [1][15].

fr.closingQuestion: Afin de vous orienter plus précisément selon votre situation : 1. Dans quelle commune ou quel département français le décès est-il survenu, et avec quelle province ou ville de Turquie votre proche avait-il des attaches ? 2. Envisagez-vous un rapatriement du corps vers la Turquie ou des obsèques locales en France ?
